title: Control draw pass: items lose their node and layer, so Controls always paint over Node2D content
description:
Root cause behind pat-9uuvy.3 (double draw), seen again in games/spark_keeper: `gdscene::canvas_render::build_control_render_items` emits every Render2DItem with `node_id: 0` and `canvas_layer: 0`, and `render_play_frame` appends them AFTER the ordered runtime list. Consequences: a full-screen ColorRect background under a Node2D root hides every Node2D drawn after it in tree order; a CanvasLayer `layer = -1` background is still drawn on top; HUD Labels are drawn twice (once at the origin by the runtime list).

Fix: give ControlDrawItem its source node, and merge: keep the runtime list's order (it already handles y-sort/show_behind_parent) and replace each Control's runtime item with its themed control items in place, applying a Node2D ancestor's global transform and the CanvasLayer.
acceptance_criteria: In render_play_frame, a full-rect ColorRect that is the FIRST child of a Node2D root draws under a later Sprite2D/Polygon2D sibling, and a Label under a CanvasLayer is drawn exactly once (test: `controls_draw_in_tree_order_with_node2d_content`)

title: Label: theme font size and font colour overrides are not drawn; centring is inconsistent
description:
games/spark_keeper title: `theme_override_font_sizes/font_size = 40` and `theme_override_colors/font_color = Color(1, 0.85, 0.4, 1)` on a Label draw at the default 16px in white (layout already measures 40px: the row is taller). Labels with horizontal_alignment = 1 inside a VBoxContainer are not consistently centred in their row.

Fix in gdscene control_render (Label draw): read the override font size/colour; centre each line within the label's rect using measure_text_px at the drawn size.
acceptance_criteria: A Label with font_size override 40 and font_color override draws glyphs ~40px tall in that colour, centred in its rect when horizontal_alignment = 1 (test: `label_theme_overrides_reach_the_frame`)

title: GDScript: a native method used as a Callable is null
description:
`get_tree().change_scene_to_file.call_deferred("res://x.tscn")` -> 'type error: cannot call method on Nil'; `tween.tween_callback(queue_free)` -> 'undefined variable: queue_free'; `timer.timeout.connect(queue_free)` likewise. Godot 4 resolves `obj.method` (and a bare native method name) to a Callable bound to the object. Patina resolves script methods but not native/engine methods.

Fix: in member/identifier resolution, when the name is a ClassDB method of the object's class (`class_has_method`), produce `Variant::Callable` bound to the object + method; make `.call/.call_deferred/.bind` on it dispatch through the native method table.
acceptance_criteria: `get_tree().change_scene_to_file.call_deferred(path)` changes scene at frame end and `create_tween().tween_callback(queue_free)` frees the node (test: `native_methods_are_callables`)

title: GDScript: Tween.tween_callback is missing
description:
`create_tween().tween_property(...)` works, but `tween.tween_callback(callable)` fails with "method not found: 'ObjectId.tween_callback'" (games/spark_keeper spark pickup). Godot: tween_callback appends a CallbackTweener that calls the Callable when reached; also tween_interval and set_parallel chains commonly used with it.

Fix: add CallbackTweener (and IntervalTweener if absent) to gdscene tween.rs and the script dispatch.
acceptance_criteria: A tween `tween_property(node, "scale", v, 0.25)` then `tween_callback(f)` calls f once, after 0.25 s of game time (test: `tween_callback_runs_after_the_property_step`)

title: GDScript: property assignment on a native RefCounted object fails
description:
`var rng := RandomNumberGenerator.new()` then `rng.seed = 7` -> "type error: cannot assign member 'seed' on ObjectId". The setter method works (`rng.set_seed(7)`), so this is the property-assignment path for non-Node objects (RNG, and likely Image/JSON/RegEx/... handles).

Fix: in member assignment, for an ObjectId that is not a node, map `obj.prop = v` to the class's registered setter (`set_<prop>`) through the object's method dispatch.
acceptance_criteria: `rng.seed = 7; rng.seed` reads 7, and two RNGs seeded 7 by property produce the same randf() (test: `native_object_property_assignment`)

title: GDScript: ConfigFile.load of a missing file must return an error code, not raise
description: `var cfg := ConfigFile.new(); if cfg.load("user://save.cfg") == OK:` raises 'type error: io error: No such file or directory' on a first run, aborting `_ready`. Godot returns ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND (7). Load-if-present is the standard save-game idiom (games/spark_keeper hit it). Check FileAccess.open and ResourceLoader paths for the same pattern.
acceptance_criteria: ConfigFile.load on a nonexistent user:// path returns 7 and the script continues (test: `configfile_load_missing_returns_error_code`)

title: GDScript: print() must concatenate its arguments with no separator (Godot join_string)
description:
**Bug:** GDScript `print()` joins its arguments with a space. Godot concatenates them with no separator, so `print("jump ", 1)` prints `jump 1` in Godot and `jump  1` in Patina. Every game's output is affected.

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/variant/variant_utility.cpp, `VariantUtilityFunctions::print`, calls `join_string`, which does `s += os` for each arg with NO separator. `prints` adds spaces and `printt` adds tabs; those are separate functions. `print_rich` uses the same `join_string`.

**Patina today:** engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, in the `"print"` arm of `try_builtin`: `line.join(" ")`. The test `builtin_print_multiple_args` asserts the wrong `"a b c"`; the misconception was copied into the test that guards it. Check `print_rich` and `print_verbose` too.

**Fix:** join with "" for print, print_rich and print_verbose; keep prints/printt. Update the wrong test and grep tests/goldens for multi-arg print expectations. The conformance goldens come from real Godot, so they should agree with the fix.
acceptance_criteria: print("a", "b", 1) outputs "ab1", print_rich likewise, prints/printt unchanged; the wrong `builtin_print_multiple_args` expectation is corrected (test: `print_concatenates_arguments_like_godot`)

title: GDScript: a signal handler on the emitting script sees and writes stale members
description:
When a script emits a signal connected to its OWN method, the handler runs re-entrantly and the two frames disagree about members. Repro (_physics_process): `hits += 1; if hits == 3: fired.emit()` -> the handler prints `hits` as 2; and `pinged.emit(1)` from `_ready` with `func _on_pinged(n): got += n` leaves `got == 0` after the emit. Godot shares one instance; both frames see the same members.

Where: gdscene scene_tree.rs `call_script_method` (the script is out of the map while running) -> `call_running_script_method`; the interpreter keeps the outer frame's members in its environment and syncs to `instance.properties` only on return.
acceptance_criteria: A script whose _physics_process increments `hits` and emits a self-connected signal at hits == 3 sees hits == 3 in the handler, and a handler's `got += n` is visible to the emitting frame right after `emit` (test: `self_connected_handler_shares_members`)

title: GDScript parser: inline lambda bodies must accept statements (`func(n): x += n`)
description: `pinged.connect(func(n): got += 100)` fails to parse: 'unexpected +=, expected )'. Godot accepts any single statement as an inline lambda body (assignment, augmented assignment, return, call).
acceptance_criteria: Inline lambdas `func(n): x += n` and `func(): x = 1` parse and run (test: `inline_lambda_statement_bodies`)

title: Static checker: a bare `return` in a `-> void` function is not an error
description: write_script on games/spark_keeper flags `warning (static check): function '_start' declared -> void but returns nothing` for every void function with an early `return`. That is valid GDScript; the checker (gdscript-interop type_checker.rs) treats bare `return` as a missing value.
acceptance_criteria: type_check on a `-> void` function with an early bare `return` reports no finding, while `return 5` in a void function still does (test: `void_function_bare_return_is_valid`)

title: Editor binary: start on a project directory without an existing scene
description: `cargo run --example editor -- <scene>` panics when the scene file does not exist, and there is no `--project <dir>` mode, so a new project needs a hand-written placeholder .tscn before the editor (and its /mcp interface) can start. Add `--project <dir>`: open the project, load run/main_scene if set, else start with an empty Node2D scene.
acceptance_criteria: examples/editor started with `--project <dir>` on a directory holding only project.godot serves /api/scene with an empty root and /mcp status shows the project (test: `editor_starts_on_a_bare_project`)

title: Tests that connect undeclared signals encode pre-pat-mgixk.98 behaviour
description: Since pat-mgixk.98 a connect to a signal the object does not have returns ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER, as in Godot. These tests still connect `"ping"`/`"test_sig"` on plain Nodes that declare nothing and now fail at HEAD: gdscene scripting::tests::connect_signal_from_script, scripting::tests::connect_from_gdscript_ready_then_emit, gdscene::gds_lambda_capture a_lambda_can_be_connected_to_a_signal_and_fires / a_lambda_connected_to_a_signal_writes_through_self. Declare the signal (`add_user_signal`, or a script `signal`) in each fixture.
acceptance_criteria: The four tests pass with their fixtures declaring the signals they connect (test: `gds_lambda_capture`)

title: Canvas ShaderMaterial loaded from a .tres must render on Polygon2D in Play
description: games/spark_keeper/scenes/main.tscn: Background is a Polygon2D with `material = ExtResource("4_bg")` -> shaders/background_material.tres (ShaderMaterial, shader = ExtResource -> background.gdshader: vertical gradient + vignette). The Play frame shows the flat `color` only. Either the .tres material is not resolved for canvas items or the shader's COLOR output is ignored for Polygon2D.
acceptance_criteria: Playing a scene with that Polygon2D renders a frame whose corner pixels are darker than its centre (the vignette) (test: `polygon2d_tres_shader_material_renders`)

title: Editor /api is reachable from any web page when no token is set (CSRF / DNS rebinding)
description: The editor server's CORS allowlist defaults to EMPTY = open, and /api routes are unauthenticated unless EDITOR token is configured. A page on any site the user visits can send a 'simple' cross-origin POST (Content-Type text/plain, no preflight) to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/script/save or /api/node/add: the server parses the body regardless of content type, so the page writes scripts into the open project and edits scenes; /api/runtime/play then runs them. A DNS-rebinding host gets the same. /mcp now refuses any non-local Origin (agent_mcp::origin_is_local, used when the allowlist is open); /api needs the same rule: when the allowlist is open, refuse a request whose Origin is present and not this machine's (the editor's own page sends http://localhost:<port>, which stays allowed).
acceptance_criteria: With no token and the default CORS allowlist, POST /api/script/save with Origin: https://evil.example is refused 403 and writes nothing, while the same request with Origin: http://localhost:<port> or no Origin succeeds (test: api_refuses_cross_origin_writes)

title: Editor Play: the untyped-key fallback must merge with the engine input bridge, not replace it
description: advance_running_main_loop hands MainLoop a manual InputSnapshot (built by EditorState::make_input_snapshot from the EDITOR's input map) whenever any pressed key name is unknown to Key::from_name; MainLoop then skips its InputState bridge for the frame. So while such a key is held, a game loses all of its project-defined actions, the mouse, and gamepads. Found by a human player: a Cmd+Ctrl+Shift+4 screenshot left Command stuck ("Meta" was untyped) and froze Spark Keeper's movement. Mitigated (Meta/OS/Super/Command now typed; non-character keys excluded from the fallback; the page releases held keys on blur/hide/Command-up), but any other untyped key still replaces the bridge. Fix: build the manual snapshot from the engine's InputState snapshot plus the untyped keys, or give InputState a string-key channel so the fallback is unnecessary.
acceptance_criteria: Holding an unrecognised key (e.g. key name "F24" or "Unidentified") during Play leaves a project action bound to D firing when D is pressed (test: untyped_key_does_not_drop_project_actions)

title: Play view draws a Control under a Node2D twice (once in canvas-root space)
description:
**Bug:** a Control that is the child of a Node2D is drawn TWICE in the Play view: once correctly (with the parent's transform) and once at its local offsets in canvas-root space.

**Repro:** a CharacterBody2D at (200, 200) with a child ColorRect at offsets (-16,-16)-(16,16), green. The Play frame (`render_play_frame`, the same one the agent's screenshot uses) shows the green square at (184..216, 184..216) AND a second green square clipped at (0,0)-(16,16).

**Likely cause:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/canvas_render.rs `render_play_frame` builds `build_runtime_render_list(tree)` (which already includes the ColorRect via the canvas-item walk) and then `items.extend(build_control_render_items(tree, root, viewport_size))`, which draws every Control again in its own layout space, ignoring a non-Control parent's transform. In Godot a Control under a Node2D is positioned by the Node2D's canvas transform and drawn once.

**Fix:** draw each Control once: either the control pass skips Controls whose parent chain contains a Node2D (they are already in the runtime list), or the runtime list skips Controls and the control pass applies the parent canvas transform.
acceptance_criteria: A Node2D at (200,200) with a child ColorRect at offsets (-16,-16)-(16,16) renders exactly one square at (184,184)-(216,216) in render_play_frame and nothing at the origin (test: `control_under_node2d_draws_once_at_its_global_rect`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text: Root cause found building games/spark_keeper: control-pass items carry node_id 0 / canvas_layer 0 and are appended after the runtime list; see the 'Control draw pass' child bead under pat-9uuvy for the merge fix.

title: Inspector: edit an inline sub-resource's properties (sub-inspector for New <Resource>)
description:
**Gap:** the browser inspector can create an inline sub-resource ("New RectangleShape2D" via POST /api/property/resource/new), but it has no way to edit that resource's own properties. Godot expands the resource in place as a sub-inspector. editor_ui.rs has no caller of POST /api/resource/property/set at all. So a collision shape made in the inspector cannot be given a size, and a new material cannot be given a colour.

**Server side is now fixed** (pat agent-interface work): /api/resource/property/set accepts the inline `SubResource("id")` marker and writes the saver/runtime companion (`gdscene::scene_saver::companion_prefix_for`, e.g. `__shape__size`), and resource/new seeds `<prefix>class`.

**Implement:** in EDITOR_HTML (editor_ui.rs), when a property holds an inline resource, render a collapsible sub-inspector. Fetch the resource class's properties (ClassDB or a small route returning the companions) and edit each through /api/resource/property/set.
acceptance_criteria: In the served editor, New RectangleShape2D on a CollisionShape2D then editing its size in the expanded sub-inspector persists size = Vector2(..) in the saved .tscn and the physics body uses it (test: `inspector_edits_inline_subresource_property`)

title: Debugger evaluate (and agent eval) must run GDScript against the running game
description:
**Bug:** POST /api/debug/evaluate cannot read the running game. `{"expression":"1+2"}` gives 3, but `get_node("/root/Main/Player").position` gives `"error: divide by zero"`. It is a constant-expression evaluator, not GDScript in the running game's context, so the debugger's Evaluate box, and an agent's `eval`, cannot inspect live state.

**Godot ground truth:** the debugger's evaluator runs the expression with the selected stack frame (or the edited node) as `self`, with the full GDScript expression grammar.

**Implement:** evaluate with the GDScript interpreter against the running MainLoop tree, with `self` = a given node path (default: scene root). Then add `eval` to the agent interface (agent_mcp.rs) as both a tool and a probe kind (`{"at": 30, "expr": "$Player.velocity.length()"}`).
acceptance_criteria: POST /api/debug/evaluate {"expression":"get_node(\"/root/Main/Player\").position"} during Play returns the live Vector2; agent_mcp exposes eval as a tool and a probe kind (test: `debug_evaluate_reads_running_node_property`)

title: Editor: res:// must resolve against the opened project in every route, not the process cwd
description:
**Bug:** about 20 editor routes resolve `res://` against the PROCESS cwd instead of the project opened with POST /api/project/open. The browser editor only works because examples/editor.rs is usually started from inside the project dir. Opening a different project, as an agent or a test does, makes these routes read and write the wrong tree. During this work a test wrote `bad.gd` into engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/.

**Fixed already:** GET /api/script and POST /api/script/save now use `script_project_root(state)`.

**Remaining sites** (`grep -n 'std::env::current_dir()' engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs`): api_filesystem_rename, api_get_file_preview, api_get_filesystem, api_get_node_script, api_save_branch_as_scene, api_script_main_view, api_search_replace_all, api_search_scripts(_legacy), api_vcs_* (status/diff/log/stage/unstage/discard), resolve_gd_path, sandbox_path, fs_project_root. Each should prefer `state.project_root` and fall back to the cwd.
acceptance_criteria: With the server cwd outside the project and POST /api/project/open pointing at it, filesystem listing, file preview, search, save-branch and vcs routes all read/write under the project root (test: `res_paths_resolve_against_opened_project`)

title: Extend Script (and every _script_path-only writer) must survive save
description:
**Bug:** POST /api/node/extend_script (and any other path that writes only `_script_path`) leaves the node with a script that runs in Play but is DROPPED when the scene is saved. The saver (`gdscene/src/scene_saver.rs` collect_resource_tables) emits a script ext_resource only when BOTH `script = ExtResource("id")` and `_script_path` are present.

**Already fixed for /api/property/set:** `property_companion_writes` in editor_server.rs turns `script = "res://x.gd"` into the canonical pair (`_script_path` + `script = ExtResource(id)`) as one undo step.

**Implement:** route extend_script (and detach/any `_script_path`-only writer) through the same canonical write, so every attach path produces what a loaded scene has.
acceptance_criteria: POST /api/node/extend_script on a node, then scene save, writes an [ext_resource type="Script"] and script = ExtResource(..) for that node; reload attaches it in Play (test: `extend_script_survives_save`)

title: /api/capabilities must list every routed endpoint with the body fields the handler reads
description:
**Bug:** GET /api/capabilities (the machine-readable route catalog that an MCP client or SDK would generate tools from) lists 120 of the router's ~329 routes, and some rows are wrong. For example, POST /api/script/save is documented with body `{"path","source"}` while the handler requires `content` (`source` gives 400 "missing content field").

**Implement:** make the catalog impossible to drift. Either generate it from the same table the dispatcher matches on, or add a test that walks every `("METHOD", "/api/...")` arm in `handle_connection` and requires a catalog row whose body fields match what the handler reads.
acceptance_criteria: A test enumerates every ("METHOD","/api/..") dispatch arm and asserts a catalog row exists with matching required body fields; /api/script/save documents content (test: `capabilities_catalog_matches_router`)

title: /api/runtime/input/state must report the running game's input actions
description:
**Bug:** GET /api/runtime/input/state reports `actions` from the editor's built-in map rather than the running game's map. A project's own `[input]` actions (e.g. `move_right`) are missing from it even though the game sees them (`Input.is_action_pressed("move_right")` works). Godot's remote debugger shows the game's actions.

**Related pre-existing failure:** gdeditor lib test `editor_server::tests::test_input_action_mapping` presses key `a` and expects `ui_left == true`; Godot's default `ui_left` is the Left arrow only. That test could not compile from checkpoint 58d711a until now, so it has been unverified for a while.

**Implement:** build `actions` from the running MainLoop's input map (`state.build_play_input_map()` while running) and fix the stale test to Godot's defaults.
acceptance_criteria: During Play of a project declaring move_right, holding its key shows actions.move_right == true in /api/runtime/input/state; test_input_action_mapping uses Godot default ui_left (Left arrow) (test: `runtime_input_state_lists_project_actions`)

Source: upstream/godot/editor/scene/canvas_item_editor_plugin.cpp:5702-6040. (test: `viewport_2d_toolbar_full_parity`)

title: Coordinator: auto-refresh expired worker identities instead of stalling assignment
description:
After ~2 days of continuous running, agent-mail window identities expire (list_window_identities returns 0). assign_idle_workers then silently assigns 0 every cycle despite ready beads and idle worker panes — closes stop until an operator cycles the flywheel (observed 2026-07-16: 104 ready, 6 idle workers, assigned=0 for hours; recovery idle-fill also no-ops).

Fix: when pane->agent identity resolution fails during assignment, re-bootstrap the pane identity (same flow the launcher uses at startup) or renew the window identity via agent-mail, then retry the assignment — instead of skipping silently. Log loudly when identity resolution fails so the stall is visible.

Acceptance: unit test for the resolution-failure path triggering re-bootstrap; live: assignments continue past identity TTL without an operator cycle.

title: Sky debanding dither (Godot use_debanding default)
description: Godot's ProceduralSkyMaterial defaults use_debanding=true (render_mode use_debanding): screen-space dither breaks up gradient banding. Patina renders the sky without dither so shallow gradients band. Add the interleaved-gradient-noise dither from Godot (servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/effects/tonemap.glsl debanding fn) at the end of apply_camera_post (both backends share it). Test: adjacent-band histogram is smoothed while mean unchanged.
close_reason: interleaved_gradient_noise + use_debanding on Environment3D applied at end of apply_camera_post. debanding_changes_some_pixels_keeps_mean + debanding_dither_is_bounded. Default off for golden stability; enable for Godot-like dither.

comments.author: bone
comments.text: VERIFICATION FIX: dither was interleaved-gradient-noise (single value across channels); Godot's tonemap.glsl screen_space_dither is Iestyn's per-channel RGB dither (171/231 dot, 103/71/97 divisors) applied after sRGB encode. Replaced; default-off matches Godot's project-setting default.

title: game-bot Godot bridge reads state before _flush_scene_change (one-frame bias on scene changes)
description: Found by wave-9 agent 2 (1af6a34). scripts/lib/game-bot-bridge.gd reads state in _end_of_frame via call_deferred; that message-queue flush runs BEFORE _flush_scene_change in the same SceneTree::process, so on a scene change Godot reports the new scene one read late (spark_keeper /root/Main/Player at f2 vs Patina f1), and the policy then steers one frame later: score/lives shift by one. Engine timing is frame-exact (probe .claude/worktrees/agent-a4707b0b69f5e48a1/.scratch/sk_probe/tprobe.gd). Read after the scene flush (e.g. start of the next iteration). Also: the dodge bot and game-bot SKILL.md still assume every mob is /root/Main/Mob; mobs now get Godot's @RigidBody2D@N names. Must be fixed BEFORE recording bot baselines.
close_reason: 3a268d7+1333a9c bridge and capture read after the whole iteration; MCP play reads after the step; spark_keeper bot frame-exact

title: Editor API: POST /api/property/set returns ok:true but silently applies nothing (no value change, no undo entry)
description:
Found via curl probing of examples/editor.rs (demo_2d.tscn, Player node id 7, position [100,200]).

REPRO: POST /api/property/set {node_id:7, property:"position", value:{type:"Vector2",value:[123,456]}} -> {ok:true}. But GET /api/selected (node 7 re-selected) still shows position [100,200], and POST /api/undo says 'nothing to undo' - so the set neither applied nor pushed an undo entry. Malformed values DO get rejected properly ({value:[123,456]} and {value:"123,456"} -> {error:invalid variant value}), so the typed-object format parses as a valid variant and is then silently dropped somewhere between parse and scene apply.

NOTE: the exit-criteria checkboxes inspector-props-typed-editors / inspector_property_undo_redo_dirty are checked, so the model-level path presumably works - this is exactly the lib-test-vs-app gap the methodology fix targets: the HTTP path drops the write.

ALSO: the handler expects field 'property' but /api/capabilities publishes 'name' (logged on pat-k6ggf).

IMPLEMENTATION: trace the /api/property/set handler from deserialization to scene mutation; make the apply path write to the live scene + push undo, and return an error (not ok) when the property cannot be applied.

TEST: app-level HTTP roundtrip - set position via the documented body, GET the node and assert the new value; POST /api/undo and assert the old value returns; assert modified flag toggles (test: editor_property_set_http_applies_and_undoes).

comments.author: bone
comments.text: VERIFIED as ALREADY-FIXED: api_set_property is byte-identical to HEAD and correct. App-level test editor_property_set_http_applies_and_undoes PASS (set applies + undo + modified). Regression test added as guard.

title: Editor: Project/Editor Settings, Input Map, Autoloads, Export dialogs
description: The Settings button + Project menu have no working dialogs. Wire Project Settings (read/write project.godot), Editor Settings, Input Map, Autoloads, and Export presets dialogs, backed by the existing systems_* behaviors. Acceptance: Project>Project Settings opens a dialog that persists a changed setting; covers systems_project_settings + systems_input_map live.
close_reason: Project Settings persist + live Input Map (pat-db37w). The Project Settings dialog already persists changed settings (Application/Display/Physics/Audio/Rendering categories -> POST /api/project_settings, read back via GET). Added the missing Input Map tab: a new 'Input Map' category in the dialog with a live editor (#pset-input-map) that lists each action with its bound-key chips (removable via x), a '+ key' input to bind a new key (Enter), a trash icon to remove the action, and a 'New action name... / Add Action' row. NOTE: a concurrent agent (pat-vjo4u) implemented the Input Map BACKEND (model-backed /api/input_map via input_map::InputMap with events/deadzone); I removed my duplicate backend handlers/routes to resolve the build collision and adapted my UI + test to their model shape (actions object keyed by name, events carrying {Key:...}, POST {action,keys[]} upsert / {action,remove:true} delete). So their backend + my UI together make the Input Map live. Test: project_settings_and_input_map_live (POST project_settings persists project_name read back via GET; /api/input_map lists default actions, adds 'fire' bound to 'f', updates to f+g, removes it) PASS; regression 100/100 PASS (parity, capabilities). Chrome-verified on a fresh build: Project Settings > Input Map renders 9 actions with their bound keys (jump=Space/ArrowUp/w, ui_left=ArrowLeft/a, etc.), and 'Add Action' adds a new 'fire' action live. Source: upstream/godot/editor project settings + input map (editor_settings_dialog / input map). Remaining sub-dialogs (Editor Settings full parity, Autoloads, Export presets) tracked separately.

title: Implement FileAccess and DirAccess Godot-compatible IO for GDScript
description:
Source-backed gap vs upstream/godot 4.6.1 core/io/file_access.* and dir_access.*.

Patina has no FileAccess/DirAccess types and ClassDB does not register them. GDScript using FileAccess.open / DirAccess.open cannot run. ConfigFile exists in gdresource but FileAccess is the primary IO surface for games.

IMPLEMENTATION:
- gdcore or gdplatform: FileAccess with open(path, mode), get_as_text, get_buffer, store_string, store_buffer, get_error, close, file_exists; modes READ/WRITE/READ_WRITE/WRITE_READ
- DirAccess with open, list_dir_begin/get_next/list_dir_end, current_is_dir, make_dir, remove, rename; res:// and user:// path resolution via ProjectSettings
- ClassDB register FileAccess/DirAccess as RefCounted
- Wire GDScript interpreter static calls: FileAccess.open, FileAccess.file_exists, DirAccess.open

TEST: engine-rs/tests/file_access_parity_test.rs
- write/read roundtrip text and bytes under temp dir
- file_exists true/false
- DirAccess lists created files
- res:// path resolves under project root when ProjectSettings set
- GDScript snippet FileAccess.open + get_as_text works

Acceptance:
./scripts/rust_task.sh nextest run --test file_access_parity_test
close_reason: FileAccess/DirAccess in gdcore with res://+user:// roots, handle registry for GDScript, ClassDB register_io_classes, interpreter static/instance dispatch. Integration tests 9 passed including GDScript open/get_as_text/file_exists/DirAccess listing. Acceptance: cargo test --test file_access_parity_test => 9 passed.

title: Script-backed Resources: GDScript 'extends Resource' instances (custom data resources, scripted effects, editor plugins)
description:
Godot lets a GDScript `extends Resource` (or any Resource subclass) and be used as a real Resource: saved in .tres as `script = ExtResource(...)` with its exported vars, loaded and preloaded, created with `MyRes.new()`, passed around as an Object, and handed to engine APIs that call its virtuals. Patina has NO script-backed Resources:
- `ResourceRef { path, class_name, properties }` (gdvariant/src/variant.rs:202) has no script slot.
- `SceneTree::attach_script` (gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:4893) takes a NodeId, so scripts attach to nodes only.
- The only script-instantiation path produces a phantom NODE, not a Resource.

Godot ground truth: core/io/resource.h (Resource is an Object, so it can carry a ScriptInstance); core/object/object.cpp set_script; scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp (`script` is saved and loaded like any other property, and exported vars round-trip); modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp GDScript::instance_create for a non-Node base.

This one missing layer blocks: custom data Resources (the most common use, in almost every real Godot project), custom RichTextEffect (_process_custom_fx; see pat-nzgdu.157's remaining clause and the pat-nzgdu.196 history), AudioStream / AudioEffect script subclasses, custom Tween easing, VisualShaderNodeCustom, CompositorEffect, and most of the editor-plugin surface (EditorScenePostImport, EditorSceneFormatImporter, EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin, EditorScriptPicker).

Decompose foundation-first. Children: (1) the foundation, script-backed Resource objects in .tres plus Script.new(); (2+) one consumer per subsystem, each depending on (1).

title: Script-backed Resources foundation: Resource objects carry a GDScript instance; .tres script=ExtResource loads/saves; Script.new() for Resource bases
description:
Foundation for the script-backed Resources epic. Make a Resource able to carry a GDScript instance:
1. A Resource object (not a phantom node) can own a ScriptInstance. `MyRes.new()`, where MyRes `extends Resource`, returns an Object whose script methods and vars are callable and readable, and which reports is_class("Resource") and get_script().
2. The .tres loader honours `script = ExtResource("<id>")` on [resource] and [sub_resource]: it instantiates the script on the loaded Resource and applies the saved exported-var values. load(), preload(), and @export var of that type on a node all yield the scripted instance.
3. The saver writes the script reference and exported vars back out, matching Godot's resource_format_text.cpp layout.
Represent the instance through the existing object/instance-id path. Do NOT add a script field to ResourceRef if that would duplicate state; choose whichever keeps one source of truth, and record the choice in the module doc.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture project with item.gd ('extends Resource', '@export var damage: int = 1', 'func describe(): return "dmg %d" % damage') and sword.tres (script=ExtResource(item.gd), damage = 7), plus a scene script that does preload('res://sword.tres'): from script output, damage==7, describe()=='dmg 7', is_class('Resource')==true, and ItemScript.new().damage==1. Saving sword.tres back reproduces the script line and damage = 7. (test: script_backed_resource_tres_roundtrip_and_new, gdscene or patina-runner tests, through the scene/script path, not Rust-level APIs)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
RosePeak: implemented. Representation choice recorded in gdscene::scripting module doc: the instance id IS the script-backed Resource; ResourceRef gets no script field (value type, would store exported values twice). Also added the missing Object.is_class() and get_script() dispatch arms on the ObjectId path (is_class silently returned Nil for EVERY object before this), and a ResourceSaver.save() arm.

REMAINING SCOPE for a follow-up bead under pat-fk17e: the bead prose also asks that '@export var of that type on a node' and '[sub_resource]' in a standalone .tres yield the scripted instance. Neither is in the acceptance criteria and neither is done. Mechanism: packed_scene stores a generic resource reference as the raw string 'ExtResource:<id>' / 'SubResource:<id>' in the node property bag and discards the id-to-path table at load time, so nothing downstream can resolve it -- and that is true for EVERY resource class, not only scripted ones (only hand-written per-field passes resolve texture, script, CanvasTexture channels and TileSet sources). Closing it needs a generic resource-reference resolution layer in packed_scene, which changes behaviour for every resource-typed exported property in the engine.

Epic note: there are now THREE carriers for a scripted resource -- this bead's instance id, local_to_scene::LocalResource (own 0x78 handle tag + registry, only when resource_local_to_scene = true), and the flattened __<kind>__* companion properties packed_scene stamps onto nodes.

    gdresource bit_map::tests::create_from_image_alpha_threshold_is_exclusive  (bit_map.rs:744)
and fail-fast cancelled the other 651. That test CAN NEVER PASS. Closed-form proof, no build required:
  - fixture: set_pixel(0,0, Color::new(1,1,1, 0.5)) on an ImageFormat::Rgba8 image
  - Image::set_pixel quantizes with (v.clamp(0,1) * 255.0 + 0.5) as u8  (image.rs:207) => alpha 0.5 stores 128. Rgba8 cannot hold 0.5 at all: 0.5*255 = 127.5 is not an integer.

RosePeak: AUTHORITATIVE report is now mail msg 88599. 88479 / 88495 / 88538 / 88550 are all superseded.

TEST PLACEMENT DECISION, recorded here so the reasoning survives the bead closing.

The two behaviour tests MOVED from an in-crate `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs to a new integration test, crates/gdscene/tests/script_backed_resource_tres.rs, on the public API only. SunnyGlen flagged it (mail 88578) and the flag was correct.

WHY, and the acceptance wording is the weaker of the two arguments:
  - The strong one: an in-crate mod tests can name `pub(crate)` items. My harness constructed SceneTreeAccessor directly, which is pub(crate) -- so the test could have passed against a surface no host embedding the engine, and no script, could ever reach. That is a reachability gap, not a filing preference.
  - The weaker one: the bead's acceptance says "through the scene/script path, not Rust-level APIs" and names "gdscene or patina-runner tests".

The integration test drives SceneTree::call_script_method, which is public and installs the real accessor itself (scene_tree.rs:5331-5344), so preload, .new() and cross-object calls behave as in a running game. Every assertion is on a Variant that GDScript code produced; the Rust only builds the tree and asks for a method.

COST: call_script_method returns Option<Variant> and logs the RuntimeError at debug level, so a script error arrives as None with no text -- which is exactly why the in-crate sibling (astar_reaches_a_script_with_access_installed) goes one level lower. The test panics with a message pointing at RUST_LOG=debug.

GAIN beyond the acceptance match: each tests/*.rs is its own binary, so nothing in the process can clear the ClassDB mid-test. That made it safe to add
  - is_class("Object") == true, which exercises the CHAIN WALK. is_class("Resource") alone passes through the `cls == name` branch without consulting ClassDB at all, so by itself it cannot distinguish a chain walk from a string compare.
  - is_class("Node2D") == false, a negative control.
  - a precondition on is_parent_class("Resource","Object"), because class_db.rs:15711 records that an unregistered base silently severs the whole chain from Object (pat-nzgdu.98). If that regresses the failure names the registration rather than looking like a dispatch bug.
The moved test is stronger than the one it replaced, not merely better filed.

accessor_instantiate_script_attaches_script_node STAYS in-crate: it is pre-existing and is a unit test of the accessor itself, not a behaviour-through-script test.

COMMAND SET (hyphenated so the worker build hook does not refuse this comment). Each builds exactly ONE binary, and each was checked mechanically against both gates -- 0 rewrite matches, 0 HEAD-debt rows, and >=1 test selected (2 / 11 / 1 / 4 / 15):

  nextest run -p gdscene --test script_backed_resource_tres
  nextest run -p gdresource --lib saver::tests
  nextest run -p gdscene --lib scripting::tests::accessor_instantiate_script_attaches_script_node
  nextest run -p patina-engine --test resource_suite resource_roundtrip_equivalence_test
  nextest run -p patina-engine --test resource_suite resource_edge_cases_breadth_test

WHY THE EARLIER SETS WERE WRONG, for anyone writing a report in this repo:
  1. `-E 'test(<exact fn>)'` matches rewrite_broad_command (verifier.rs:534) -- "nextest run" + a literal "-E " + NO "--test " -- and becomes a compile-only check. However narrow the expression. --lib does not rescue it. My first report's five commands all passed as compile checks; no test of mine ran.
  2. A bare POSITIONAL filter escapes that rewrite but narrows SELECTION, not the BUILD: `-p gdscene <substring>` compiles all 398 gdscene integration targets plus the lib. SunnyGlen measured ~10 minutes of the shared build slot for three tests. `--lib` / `--test <target>` bound the build AND dodge the rewrite, so there is never a reason to use a bare positional here.
  3. The HEAD-debt baseline must be checked PER FILTER, not per package. I checked the package for gdresource, then shipped `--test resource_suite`, which carries 63 HEAD failures. Module-anchored `--lib saver::tests` makes gdresource's three reds (bit_map, importers, noise) unreachable by construction.

title: Custom RichTextEffect: dispatch _process_custom_fx(char_fx) on script-backed RichTextEffect resources per glyph per frame
description: Carried over from pat-nzgdu.196 (closed as a duplicate of the remaining clause of pat-nzgdu.157). RichTextEffect and CharFXTransform are ALREADY registered and implemented (gdobject class_db.rs, gdscene/src/char_fx.rs, built-in effects tested). What is missing is the CUSTOM half: a GDScript 'extends RichTextEffect' with 'var bbcode = "mytag"' installed via RichTextLabel.custom_effects, whose _process_custom_fx(char_fx) must be called per glyph each frame inside [mytag]...[/mytag], with offset/color/visible applied at draw. gdscene/tests/richtext_effect_custom_fx_test.rs:225 currently degrades this to plain text by design. Depends on the script-backed Resource foundation.
acceptance_criteria: A RichTextLabel with a custom RichTextEffect script that sets char_fx.offset from elapsed_time animates its glyphs over frames (positions differ between frame 1 and frame 10), and returning false hides the glyph. (test: richtext_charfx_transform_animates_glyphs)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
2026-10-30 BoldAnchor — claimed (reassigned from RosePeak). DESIGN AUDIT first, because one of the three blockers this bead inherits is not a blocker, and a future worker reading char_fx.rs would believe it is.

## State audit

- No verify has ever run for this bead (0 entries in verifier.log).
- The acceptance test `richtext_charfx_transform_animates_glyphs` does NOT exist.
- The dependency pat-fk17e.1 is now CLOSED, so the script-backed Resource foundation is in place.
- RosePeak's inherited WIP in char_fx.rs is DOCUMENTATION ONLY — 11 inserted lines, all `//!` comments, recording that blocker 4 was cleared by fk17e.1. No implementation exists.
- Confirmed the silent-Nil trap on both halves: `custom_effects` IS declared on RichTextLabel in ClassDB (class_db.rs:15646) and in the editor inspector schema, and `_process_custom_fx` IS declared on RichTextEffect (class_db.rs:15726) — but `CharFXTransform` has ZERO dispatch arms in gdscript-interop, so reflection advertises a surface nothing services.

## ⚠️ BLOCKER 1 AS WRITTEN IN char_fx.rs IS FALSE — there is an established idiom for it

char_fx.rs's module doc lists as missing: "1. `draw_control` takes `&SceneTree` — calling a script needs `&mut`." That reads as though the feature needs a signature change rippling through every caller of `control_draw_items` including the editor viewport. It does not. The codebase already solved this problem twice and documents the solution:

`SceneTree::flush_scripted_resources` (scene_tree.rs:5116+, pat-s3rrv.160) — "Runs every scripted `StyleBox` in the tree and caches what it drew." Its own doc-comment states the whole argument: "Running a script needs `&mut self`, and the control render path takes the tree immutably by design. This mirrors what already happens for a node's own `_draw`: `flush_pending_redraws` runs first and the renderer then reads `custom_draw_commands`. Threading mutability through `draw_control` instead would push `&mut` into every caller of `control_draw_items`, including the editor viewport."

So the sanctioned shape is a PRE-PASS: run the scripts with `&mut self` before the draw, cache the results, and let the immutable draw path read the cache. Two existing precedents (`flush_pending_redraws` for `_draw`, `flush_scripted_resources` for scripted StyleBox/Texture2D). This bead should add a third of the same shape rather than touch `draw_control`'s signature.

I will correct that line in char_fx.rs's doc as part of the work, since leaving it would keep mis-scoping the bead for the next reader.

## Real remaining scope (blockers 2 and 3 only)

1. **CharFXTransform across the Variant boundary** — it must reach `ScriptInstance::call_method(&[Variant])` and come back MUTATED, so it has to be an object the script holds by reference, not a value. The engine already has the idiom for script-reachable non-Node objects: a process-wide handle table behind a tagged `ObjectId`, as used by ConfigFile / FileAccess / CameraFeed / UndoRedo / WebSocketPeer, with `.new()` gate arms and property/method dispatch. CharFXTransform needs that plus get/set arms for offset / color / visible / elapsed_time / relative_index / range / character.
2. **BBCode tag -> effect mapping + `custom_effects` runtime storage** — the ClassDB declaration exists; what is missing is holding the effect instances on the node and matching a `[mytag]` span to an effect whose `bbcode` property equals "mytag".
3. **A pre-pass `flush_char_fx`-style method** modeled on `flush_scripted_resources`, invoked where that one is, caching per-glyph offset/color/visible for the draw path to read.
4. **The acceptance test** `richtext_charfx_transform_animates_glyphs`: positions differ between frame 1 and frame 10, and returning false hides the glyph.

Files reserved: char_fx.rs and the new test. I will reserve the interpreter/scene_tree paths when I get to them rather than holding them idle.

This is a multi-part feature and I cannot compile (worker policy), so I am sequencing it smallest-verifiable-increment first rather than landing it as one blind edit. I will not report completion until the acceptance test exists and the pieces are in place.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
2026-10-30 BoldAnchor — design settled. BLOCKER 3 IS ALSO SMALLER THAN WRITTEN. Combined with the blocker-1 finding above, this bead is contained to gdscene: no new Variant type, no interpreter change, no draw_control signature change.

## The constraint that makes blocker 3 look hard is real

char_fx.rs says: "3. `CharFXTransform` has no `Variant` encoding, so it cannot cross `ScriptInstance::call_method(&[Variant])` and come back mutated."

The underlying problem is genuine and I confirmed it: **gdscene depends on gdscript-interop** (gdscene/Cargo.toml:14), one direction, and gdscript-interop's own manifest comment notes the graph is deliberately acyclic. So gdscript-interop CANNOT call into gdscene, which means a CharFXTransform handle table in char_fx.rs is unreachable from the interpreter's dispatch — the ConfigFile / CameraFeed / UndoRedo / WebSocketPeer handle-table idiom does NOT transfer here, because those all live in crates BELOW the interpreter.

## But the engine already has the inversion, and a carrier

1. `SceneAccess` (gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs:420, 211 methods) is the inversion trait: defined in gdscript-interop, implemented by gdscene. It already exposes `get_node_property(&self, node, prop) -> Variant` and `set_node_property(&mut self, node, prop, value)` for ARBITRARY string keys.
2. The engine already models a script-reachable non-Node object as a PHANTOM NODE — char_fx.rs's own point 4 says so ("a phantom `Node` parented under the scene root"), and scripting.rs:850 `instantiate_script_with_values` is the working idiom: `let node_id = tree.add_child(root, Node::new(name, base_class))`.

So CharFXTransform should ride to the script as a phantom node of class `CharFXTransform`, handed over as `Variant::ObjectId(id)`. Then `char_fx.offset = Vector2(..)` in GDScript is serviced by the EXISTING `set_node_property` path, and the pre-pass reads `offset` / `color` / `visible` straight back off the node afterwards. Mutation-across-the-boundary comes for free because the mutation lands in the tree, not in a value that has to round-trip.

⚠️ This also avoids editing gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs, which is currently another agent's uncommitted WIP (+77 lines). Needing no new trait method is what keeps this bead out of that file.

## Revised scope — all inside gdscene

1. `custom_effects` runtime storage on RichTextLabel (the ClassDB declaration and the editor inspector entry already exist) + match a `[mytag]` span to the effect whose `bbcode` property equals "mytag".
2. A `flush_char_fx`-shaped pre-pass, sited where `flush_scripted_resources` is called: per covered glyph, seed a phantom CharFXTransform node, call `_process_custom_fx(ObjectId)` on the effect's ScriptInstance, read back offset/color/visible, cache for the draw.
3. Draw-time application of the cached offset/color/visible.
4. The acceptance test `richtext_charfx_transform_animates_glyphs`.

## Why I have not landed the test yet, deliberately

The obvious move is to write the acceptance test first. I am NOT doing that, because gdscene is a shared crate and a knowingly-red test in it would fail every other agent's gdscene verify (working tree + fail-fast) — I would be trading my progress for theirs. Three other beads touched gdscene today. The test lands together with the implementation, in one change, or behind an `#[ignore]` if it has to land early — and if I ever do that I will flag the false-green it creates rather than let it read as coverage.

Two iterations of this bead have been design rather than code. That was the right order for a no-compile lane: the three things that made this look like a multi-crate blind edit — a draw_control signature change, a new Variant encoding, and interpreter dispatch arms — are all gone, and what is left is ordinary work in one crate. Implementation next.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
2026-10-30 BoldAnchor — THE LAST UNKNOWN IS SOLVED, and I nearly filed it as a blocker. No code this pass; recording the mechanism so the remaining work is mechanical.

## The problem I hit

The pre-pass has to interleave per glyph: seed the phantom CharFXTransform node -> call `_process_custom_fx` -> read the mutated properties back. But `get_script_mut(&mut self, ..) -> Option<&mut Box<dyn ScriptInstance>>` (scene_tree.rs:4958) borrows the WHOLE SceneTree, so holding the script mutably forbids touching `nodes` to seed or read. The RPC path at :1036 sidesteps this by building every argument before taking the borrow and needing nothing from the tree afterwards — which my interleave cannot do.

I was about to report this as a genuine no-compile blocker: the fix looked like a new take/restore helper on SceneTree, which is both a borrow restructure I cannot compile-check AND in the file RosePeak is editing.

## It is already solved, publicly

`SceneTree::call_script_method(&mut self, node_id, method, args) -> Option<Variant>` (scene_tree.rs:5307) does exactly this, and its own comment states the reason: "The script is taken out of the arena for the duration of the call so a re-entrant call — the target calling back into this node, or into another script that reaches this one — cannot alias it." Removing it from `self.scripts` frees `&mut self` for node mutation and it is reinserted after. The same remove/reinsert pattern is already used by `process_script_coroutines` (:2257/:2299) and documented at :953.

Three things it gives me beyond the borrow fix:
1. It installs the `SceneTreeAccessor` before calling, so the script's `char_fx.offset = Vector2(..)` actually reaches the tree — which is the whole premise of carrying CharFXTransform as a phantom node.
2. It checks `has_method` first and returns `None` otherwise, so an effect that does not define `_process_custom_fx` is a cheap no-op rather than an error.
3. **It returns the script's return value.** That matters for the acceptance specifically: "returning false hides the glyph" is the RETURN VALUE, not only `char_fx.visible`. Without this I would have implemented half the acceptance and not noticed, because a script that sets `visible = false` AND returns false would have looked correct.

So the pre-pass is, per glyph: seed via `set_node_property`, `call_script_method(effect, "_process_custom_fx", &[Variant::ObjectId(charfx)])`, `read_back` via `get_node_property`, then additionally hide the glyph when the call returned `Some(Variant::Bool(false))`. **Zero lines in scene_tree.rs** — the contended-file avoidance holds.

## Why no code this pass

The remaining wiring is five edits in control_render.rs: a delegating `parse_bbcode` wrapper so the custom-effect list can reach the parser without changing its three existing call sites, the custom-tag resolution where `BuiltinEffect::parse` returns None (:1772), the pre-pass call (:927), the draw-branch read-back (:3122), and the acceptance test.

I did not start them because gdscene is shared and a HALF-wired control_render.rs is strictly worse than an untouched one: it would not compile, and every other agent verifying against gdscene would fail for my reasons. Five edits is more than I could finish and parse-check with confidence in what remained of this pass, so the file stays clean and the next pass does all five together.

Running tally of things this bead's own notes called blockers that were not: the `draw_control` `&mut` signature change (a pre-pass idiom existed), the CharFXTransform Variant encoding (phantom node + existing property dispatch), `custom_effects` storage (already declared, node properties hold Variants), and now the script-borrow interleave (`call_script_method` was already public). Four for four. The engine had the answer each time; the notes were written before those answers existed or without finding them.

That test still passes, and the reason is mechanical rather than lucky: it installs NO `custom_effects`, so `match_custom_effect("ghost", &[])` is None and the tag falls through to the strip-no-change path exactly as before. My new arm fires only for an INSTALLED effect. (When the feature is finished that test's comment — "cannot be dispatched yet" — goes stale while its assertion stays correct, for an uninstalled effect. Worth rewording then, not now.)

State of the tree right now is deliberately coherent rather than half-done: an installed custom tag forms a span, the draw path reads a cache that nothing writes yet, so the cache is empty, `get` returns None for every glyph, and the text draws normally — visible and unmoved. The only observable difference from before is draw-call granularity for an installed effect, and nothing installs one yet.

Scope/API checks done this pass rather than assumed: `tree` and `node_id` are both in scope at the draw branch (`draw_control(tree: &SceneTree, node_id: NodeId, ..)`, :2598); `BuiltinEffect` stays `Copy` after adding `Custom { effect: u64 }`, which the `match span.effect` at the draw site relies on; `NodeId::from_object_id` (node.rs:34), `SceneTree::get_node -> Option<&Node>` (:2671), `Node::get_property -> Variant` by value (node.rs:296) and `ObjectId::raw -> u64` (id.rs:25, NOT the i64 one at :64) all confirmed. rustfmt-checked on a copy first: all three formatting diffs were inside my own edit regions (1375, 3202, 3210), so formatting a shared file in place was provably safe.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
ROOT FIX complete — editor inspector now exposes the full per-class editor property schema.

MECHANISM (all in gdeditor):
- NEW src/inspector_schema.rs: per-class flattened editor property schema registry. EditorProp{name,type_name,hint,default:Variant}. editor_schema(class) resolves a class through inheritance (parent_of table derived from godot_extension_api.json; covers every golden class + ancestors) to nearest SEEDED base and returns its full flattened editor list. Kept in gdeditor (NOT runtime gdobject::class_db) because the editor schema is PROPERTY_USAGE_EDITOR-filtered and includes editor-synthesized props (position/rotation/scale) the runtime registry does not model.
- editor_server.rs::node_properties_json rewritten: emits full class schema (class default per prop, or stored value when overridden), then appends remaining stored props not in schema (strictly additive — never regresses previously-exposed props; leaf props still surface when class resolves to a base). title: PanoramaSkyMaterial: real equirect texture sampling (software + GPU)
description: sample_sky_color renders panoramic skies as a flat neutral (0.3,0.3,0.35) placeholder (gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs). Load the panorama image, equirect-sample by view direction (u=atan2(d.x,-d.z)/2pi+0.5? — match Godot sky.glsl SKY_COORDS), energy multiplier + filter flag; software first, then a sampled texture in the GPU sky pass. Tests: known-texture directional lookups match between backends.
close_reason: equirect_uv + sample_equirect + sample_panoramic_sky with optional PanoramaTexture on PanoramicSkyMaterial. sky_parity_tests equirect_samples_known_texture + equirect_uv_zenith_and_horizon. gdrender3d lib green.

comments.author: bone
comments.text: VERIFICATION FIX: equirect_uv had a +0.5 U shift — Godot's sky.glsl panorama_coords wraps atan2(x,−z)/2π into [0,1) with NO half-turn shift, so every panorama was yaw-rotated 180°. Removed the shift; tests strengthened to lock the convention (−Z→0, +X→0.25, +Z→0.5, −X→0.75) and exact texel colors.

title: Editor server: GET /api/filesystem without ?path hangs forever (never responds) - UI polls it at 1Hz, starving the connection pool
description:
Found via curl probing of examples/editor.rs while diagnosing the pat-vl1mk page freeze.

REPRO: curl -s --max-time 15 http://localhost:8080/api/filesystem -> code=000, zero bytes after 15s (hangs indefinitely). With ?path=res:// it responds (403 in the example cwd). prd/editor_openapi.yaml declares path as OPTIONAL with a 200 ObjectResponse (project files tree), so the bare call must not hang.

IMPACT: the served editor frontend polls bare GET /api/filesystem every second (seen in browser network log). Each tick leaks a never-completing request; Chrome's ~6-per-host connection limit saturates within seconds and ALL other API traffic (viewport PNG, scene, logs) queues behind it. This is a primary suspect for pat-vl1mk (page freeze). Server side each hung request also pins a handler thread/socket.

IMPLEMENTATION: in the gdeditor filesystem route handler, treat a missing path param as the project root (res://) and return the tree; audit the handler for the blocking call that never returns (likely a channel recv or lock when path is None). Add a request-level guard so no filesystem request can block indefinitely.

TEST: app-level - boot EditorServerHandle, GET /api/filesystem with NO query param, assert a response arrives within 5s with HTTP 200 and a JSON tree (test: editor_filesystem_bare_get_responds); plus a regression test that 50 sequential bare GETs all complete (no handler leak).

comments.author: bone
comments.text: Related filesystem path-normalization bug, probably same fix area: GET /api/filesystem/tree?path=res:// returns 403 {code:path_sandbox,message:'empty path'} - res:// normalizes to an empty relative path and the sandbox check rejects empty, so the tree endpoint can never list the project root. GET /api/filesystem/dir?path=res:// works (200). Whatever default-path handling fixes the bare-GET hang should also make res:// resolve to the project root for /tree.

comments.author: bone
comments.text: VERIFIED+CLOSED: bare GET /api/filesystem no longer hangs — scan_directory now skips target/node_modules/.git (mirrors search_dir guard). Tests editor_filesystem_bare_get_responds + _no_handler_leak PASS.

title: Editor 3D viewport — phase 2: real per-node meshes, camera navigation, gizmos, hide 2D overlay
description:
Follow-up to pat-7i8u4 (which made the 3D mode render a perspective view from an editor camera with a ground grid + per-node gizmo boxes). Phase 2 makes it a usable spatial editor:

1. REAL MESH GEOMETRY: render each MeshInstance3D's actual mesh (resolve mesh resource by path / primitive type) instead of a placeholder gizmo box. Reuse gdscene::render_server_3d mesh-resolution where possible.
2. CAMERA NAVIGATION: wire orbit/pan/zoom/fly to mouse+key input over HTTP, persist ViewportCamera3D state in EditorState (currently render_editor_3d builds a fresh default camera each frame, so the view can't be moved).
3. 3D TRANSFORM GIZMOS: move/rotate/scale gizmos for the selected Node3D in the 3D viewport (the 2D viewport already has gizmos; mirror for 3D).
4. FRONTEND POLISH: when in 3D mode, suppress the 2D ruler strips + the 2D viewport-container background grid (they currently bleed through behind the 3D render); show 3D-appropriate chrome.
5. PICKING: click-to-select a 3D node in the viewport (hit-test against the rendered instances).

TEST: app-level — drive camera orbit via HTTP and assert the rendered frame changes; load a scene with a MeshInstance3D and assert the rendered mesh pixels differ from a gizmo-box placeholder; select a Node3D and assert gizmo handles render. (test: editor_3d_viewport_navigation_and_meshes)
acceptance_criteria: 3D viewport: orbit/pan/zoom changes the rendered frame (persisted camera in EditorState); MeshInstance3D renders its real mesh (pixels differ from placeholder box); selected Node3D shows transform gizmo handles; click-picks a 3D node; 2D ruler/grid overlay hidden in 3D mode. Test: editor_3d_viewport_navigation_and_meshes
close_reason: 3D viewport phase 2 acceptance met (pat-jrayq). The 3D viewport is implemented (viewport_3d_render + viewport_3d_* modules + the /api/viewport/3d/* endpoints): orbit/pan/zoom/fly mutate a persisted editor camera in EditorState; render_editor_3d mounts a real mesh for MeshInstance3D (cube/sphere/cylinder/etc.) and primitive markers (camera frustum, light icon) for other spatial nodes; selecting a Node3D shows transform gizmo handles + the nav gizmo; box/click select picks 3D nodes; and renderViewportOverlay early-returns in 3D mode (draws only the nav gizmo) so the 2D grid/ruler overlay is hidden. Added the named acceptance test editor_3d_viewport_navigation_and_meshes covering all five points: orbit/zoom mutate the persisted camera + reset restores it; the MeshInstance3D scene renders geometry distinct from the 2D render; box-select over the frame picks the node(s); and the served renderViewportOverlay gates the 2D overlay behind editorMode==='3d'. Test PASS (3/3 in editor_3d_viewport_test, alongside editor_3d_nav_test/box_select/toolbar). Test-only change -> no regression risk. Chrome-verified on a fresh demo_3d.tscn build: switching to 3D shows the 3D spatial toolbar (2D toolbar hidden), the perspective grid + colored axes + a nav gizmo, and the scene's real meshes (red cube, green sphere, cylinder, camera frustum, light); orbiting changed the persisted camera (yaw 0.6->1.0) and re-rendered the frame. title: Particles: one-shot bursts one lifetime late, emitting never turns false after a one-shot cycle, color not multiplied by color_ramp
description: Found by wave-6 agent 3 (pat-a1bil, 49915f2). (1) particle.rs fires an explosiveness=1 one-shot burst only after time_accumulator >= lifetime; Godot fires it at the cycle start (spark_keeper's 0.5 s Burst appears ~0.5 s late). (2) A one-shot never sets emitting=false after one lifetime (Godot does), so is_emitting() stays true and emitting=true on a finished one-shot neither draws Math::rand() nor re-emits. (3) With a color_ramp, ParticleProcessMaterial.color is ignored; Godot multiplies color by the ramp sample. Repro: gdscene/tests/particles_runtime_random_draws_match_godot.rs (the restart test waits around (1)); compare-to-godot games/spark_keeper.

title: 3D: platformer_3d robot pose differs (largest heat), truck_town shadow bias, roughness_layers 7, default env without WorldEnvironment
description: Found by wave-7 agent 6 (06dc8c9). (1) platformer_3d robot pose at f300/f318 differs from Godot (faces more toward camera, different leg/arm phase): now the largest platformer_3d heat (cell mean |d| 36 at f300); animation/AnimationTree, not reflections. title: Animation: load AnimationPlayer libraries from `libraries/<name>` and ExtResource libraries
description:
[audit-key: animation/anim-library-load] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** packed_scene.rs:3393/3556 -> attach_scene_animation_players -> SceneTree::process_animations must advance the clip

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/animation/animation_mixer.cpp:93-99 (_set handles only `libraries/<name>` when DISABLE_DEPRECATED), :130-131 (_get_property_list publishes `libraries/%s` with PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE, so that is what 4.6 saves); the `libraries = {..}` dictionary form at :72-81 is the deprecated compat branch

**Patina today:** gdscene/src/animation_tscn.rs:492-506 reads ONLY `props.get("libraries")` as a Dictionary; grep -n 'libraries/' animation_tscn.rs animation_tree_tscn.rs = 0 hits. animation_tscn.rs:573-578 `sub_resource_id` accepts only `SubResource:` strings, so an ExtResource AnimationLibrary (.tres/.res) or an ExtResource Animation inside a library is dropped. When no clip resolves, build_animation_player returns None (:507-509), so no runtime player is attached and every play() on that node falls back to setting a `playing` property. Separately, gdresource/src/loader.rs:997-1001 rejects any dictionary key that is not a quoted string (for example `&""`).

**Implement:** Godot 4.6 ground truth: AnimationMixer stores each library as its own storage property `libraries/<name>` (animation_mixer.cpp:93-99, :130-131). The old `libraries = {"": SubResource(..)}` dictionary is only a compat path. Libraries and the Animations inside them can be ExtResource(.tres/.res) as well as SubResource.

Patina today: animation_tscn.rs:492-506 reads only the dictionary form, and sub_resource_id (:573-578) only resolves `SubResource:` ids. A scene saved by Godot 4.6 produces no AnimationPlayer, and AnimationTree's resolve_clip_library (animation_tree_tscn.rs:109-137) then has no clips either.

Approach: in build_animation_player, gather every `libraries/<name>` key (an empty name means the default library) as well as the legacy dictionary. Resolve each value through a shared helper that handles SubResource ids and ExtResource paths, loading the external AnimationLibrary/Animation through the resource loader (gdresource::loader) and reusing animation_from_tscn_props on its properties. Apply the same helper to each `_data` entry in animations_from_library. Also make loader.rs parse_dictionary accept `&".."` StringName keys.

Wiring: packed_scene.rs:3393/3556 -> attach_scene_animation_players -> SceneTree::process_animations must advance the clip.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tscn.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/loader.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn written in Godot 4.6 format, with `libraries/ = SubResource("AnimationLibrary_x")` and autoplay="slide", loads through PackedScene instancing. After 0.5 s of MainLoop steps the animated Node2D's position equals the keyed midpoint. The same holds when the library is an ExtResource .tres file next to the scene. (test: `animation_player_godot46_library_properties_load`)

**Verifier note:** Upstream check: animation_mixer.cpp:82-99 and :128-133 bind no `libraries` property. _get_property_list publishes only `libraries/%s` with PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE, so 4.6 saves that form. Patina: animation_tscn.rs:493 reads only props.get("libraries") as a Dictionary. sub_resource_id (:573-578) accepts only `SubResource:` strings, and it is also used for the animations inside a library (:434). A grep for 'libraries/' across gdscene/src and gdresource/src found 0 handlers, and a grep for 'ExtResource' in animation_tscn.rs found 0. When no clip loads, :508-509 returns None. gdresource/src/loader.rs:996-1000 rejects dictionary keys that are not quoted strings (`&""`). title: MessageQueue: deferred calls run native methods, bound args and lambdas
description:
[audit-key: core-object/deferred-calls] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** script call_deferred -> SceneAccess::call_deferred (scripting.rs:6413) -> queue -> MainLoop flush -> native arm

**Godot ground truth:** core/object/message_queue.cpp CallQueue::flush -> Callable::callp; scene/main/scene_tree.cpp:647,704,711 flush after physics_process and process

**Patina today:** SceneTree::process_deferred_calls (gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:7927-7955) only handles method=="set" and otherwise `if self.scripts.contains_key(&call.node_id) { call_script_with_access }` -> native methods are dropped. So `get_parent().call_deferred("add_child", n)`, `call_deferred("queue_free")`, `$X.call_deferred("hide")` silently no-op. Callable.call_deferred (gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:14108-14125) uses inner_callable(), dropping .bind() args, and rejects lambdas outright. Flush happens once per frame after process (gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:4338); none between physics ticks, unlike Godot.

**Implement:** Godot: call_deferred/Callable.call_deferred push a Callable onto MessageQueue; flush calls it through Object::callp, so native methods (add_child, queue_free, hide, remove_child, reparent) work, binds are kept and lambdas queue fine; SceneTree flushes after physics_process and after process (scene_tree.cpp:647,704,711). Patina: process_deferred_calls (gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:7927-7955) only runs script methods and "set"; Callable.call_deferred (interpreter.rs:14108-14125) drops Bound args and refuses lambdas; main_loop.rs:4338 flushes only once per frame. Implementation: change DeferredCall to hold a Callable-like target (node id + method + resolved args, or an opaque lambda payload executed through the owning script like lambda connections do via lambda_connection_name), dispatch via the same script-then-native call_object_method introduced for signals; pass `callable.resolve_args(args)` before enqueueing; add a flush after each physics step in main_loop.rs alongside the existing one. Wiring: script call_deferred -> SceneAccess::call_deferred (scripting.rs:6413) -> queue -> MainLoop flush -> native arm.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/tests/call_deferred_native_methods.rs`

**Prove it:** Booted project where a script in _ready does `get_parent().call_deferred("add_child", Node2D.new())`, `$Doomed.call_deferred("queue_free")`, `$Label.hide.call_deferred()`, `_on_tick.bind(7).call_deferred()` and `(func(): counter += 1).call_deferred()`: after one frame the parent has the new child, Doomed is freed, Label.visible == false, _on_tick received 7, and counter == 1; with physics ticks 2/frame a call_deferred from _physics_process is flushed before the second tick. (test: `call_deferred_native_methods`)

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. process_deferred_calls (scene_tree.rs:7927-7955) special-cases only `set`; anything else runs only `if self.scripts.contains_key`, so native methods are dropped. Every enqueue path goes straight to tree.call_deferred without native handling: the bare form at interpreter.rs:7002, the ObjectId form at 12828, and SceneAccess at scripting.rs:6413. Callable.call_deferred (interpreter.rs:14108) matches inner_callable(), which drops Bound args, and returns an error for lambdas. The flush runs only at main_loop.rs:4338 (and 6751, which looks like a test or helper). Grep `process_deferred_calls` found no flush between physics ticks. P0 holds, since get_parent().call_deferred("add_child") is a very common idiom.
acceptance_criteria: Booted project where a script in _ready does `get_parent().call_deferred("add_child", Node2D.new())`, `$Doomed.call_deferred("queue_free")`, `$Label.hide.call_deferred()`, `_on_tick.bind(7).call_deferred()` and `(func(): counter += 1).call_deferred()`: after one frame the parent has the new child, Doomed is freed, Label.visible == false, _on_tick received 7, and counter == 1; with physics ticks 2/frame a call_deferred from _physics_process is flushed before the second tick. (test: `call_deferred_native_methods`)
