**Wiring requirement:** scene load -> attach_script -> _init; script `load(p).new(x)` -> instantiate_script(path, args) -> _init(x); script `MyRef.new()` -> arena object (not in tree) -> refs dropped at end of function -> freed during the same frame; script mutation -> shared data -> renderer/physics sync reads the node's property holding the same Arc on the next frame

### 1. Object._init constructor virtual (and .new(args) forwarding)  (MISSING, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/Object.xml `_init` virtual: called when the object's script is instantiated, receives .new() arguments; modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp GDScript::_create_instance calls initializer with p_args

**Patina today:** GDScriptNodeInstance::from_source (gdscene/src/scripting.rs:177-187) runs run_class + instantiate_class (interpreter.rs:16014-16035, evaluates var defaults only) and never calls _init. `grep -rn '"_init' --include='*.rs' gdscene/src gdscript-interop/src` -> single hit, call_super (interpreter.rs:16491) for super(). GDScript `.new()` (interpreter.rs:14460-14468) calls access.instantiate_script(&path) with no args, so `load("x.gd").new(5)` discards 5. No Rust test file under engine-rs/tests or crates/*/tests contains `func _init`.

**Implement:** Godot calls the script's _init(...) when an instance is created (scene instantiation with no args, `Script.new(a, b)` with args), after member defaults and before NOTIFICATION_POSTINITIALIZE is observable to the script; required-parameter _init makes PackedScene instantiation fail. Patina never calls _init (from_source at gdscene/src/scripting.rs:177-187; only call_super references "_init" at interpreter.rs:16491) and GDScript.new() drops its args (interpreter.rs:14460-14468). Implementation: add Interpreter::run_initializer(&mut ClassInstance, args) walking the parent chain (parent _init first only via explicit super(), matching GDScript) and call it from GDScriptNodeInstance::from_source / attach paths with scene access set; thread args through SceneAccess::instantiate_script(_with_values) (scripting.rs:850, 7441) from the `new` arm; run for packed-scene script attachment in packed_scene.rs too. Wiring: scene load -> attach_script -> _init; script `load(p).new(x)` -> instantiate_script(path, args) -> _init(x).

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/tests/script_init_constructor_runs.rs`

**Prove it:** Booted project: main.gd has `var tag = ""` and `func _init(): tag = "init"`; a helper script `func _init(n): value = n * 2` is created with `load("res://h.gd").new(21)`; after the first frame main.tag == "init" and helper.value == 42, and _init ran before _ready (order log). (test: `script_init_constructor_runs`)

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. from_source (scripting.rs:177-187) runs only run_class and instantiate_class. instantiate_class (interpreter.rs:16014-16035) evaluates var defaults and nothing else. attach_script (scene_tree.rs:4921-4965) replays properties, registers RPCs and queues _draw, but does not call _init. Workspace grep `_init"` outside tests found only interpreter.rs:16491 (call_super) and ClassDB virtual registrations (class_db.rs:25535, 31519, 31872); patina-runner/src has none. The GDScript `new` arm (interpreter.rs:14460-14470) calls access.instantiate_script(&path) and drops its arguments. The only `func _init` scripts are in-crate run_class unit tests (interpreter.rs:33192, 33219), and those test super(), not construction. MISSING at P1 is correct.

### 2. RefCounted / Object script-object lifecycle (auto-release, non-Node script objects, Object.new())  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** core/object/ref_counted.h Ref<T> auto unreference -> memdelete at 0 (+NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE, WeakRef becomes null); doc/classes/Object.xml Object.new()/free() manual lifetime

**Patina today:** Auto-release explicitly not implemented: interpreter.rs:27440-27446 ('an object stays alive until a script calls unreference()'). `extends RefCounted|Resource|Object` scripts instantiated with `.new()` become a scene Node: instantiate_script_with_values (gdscene/src/scripting.rs:860-889) uses script_base_class() as the node class and `tree.add_child(root, Node::new(name, base_class))` -> the 'object' sits under /root, appears in get_children(), receives _process/_ready, and is never freed. `Object.new()`: grep `Object\.new()` over engine-rs -> 0 hits and the `new` chain (interpreter.rs:4124-4565) has no Object arm. RefCounted handles answer only get_reference_count/reference/unreference/init_ref/get_instance_id/get_ref/is_class/get_class (interpreter.rs:27483-27530) - no set/get/meta/signals.

**Implement:** Godot: a script extending RefCounted/Resource/Object is an Object, not a Node; RefCounted instances are freed when the last Variant reference drops (PREDELETE fires, weakref().get_ref() becomes null); Object.new() returns a manually-managed object freed with free(). Patina: scripts of those bases are instantiated as Nodes parented under the root (gdscene/src/scripting.rs:860-889), RefCounted is never auto-released (interpreter.rs:27440), Object.new() is unsupported, and refcounted handles expose almost no Object API (interpreter.rs:27483-27530). Implementation (staged): stage 1 - add an object arena on SceneTree (`script_objects: HashMap<ObjectId, (ObjectBase, Box<dyn ScriptInstance>)>`) used by instantiate_script_with_values when the base class is not a Node subclass, and route ObjectId method calls/property access for those ids (call_script_method, get/set, meta, signals) to it; support Object.new(); stage 2 - automatic refcounting: increment on Variant clone of a RefCounted ObjectId and decrement on drop via an RAII guard type in gdvariant (or a refcount-aware Environment push/pop + container drop hooks), freeing (PREDELETE to _notification, unregister from weak_ref alive registry) at zero. Wiring: script `MyRef.new()` -> arena object (not in tree) -> refs dropped at end of function -> freed during the same frame.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/refcounted_handle.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/tests/refcounted_script_object_lifecycle.rs`

**Prove it:** Booted project: `var r = load("res://counter.gd").new()` (extends RefCounted) is not a child of get_tree().root, does not receive _process, `r.bump(); r.count == 1`; `var w = weakref(r); r = null` makes w.get_ref() == null and counter.gd's _notification saw NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE; `var o = Object.new(); o.set_meta("k", 1); o.free(); is_instance_valid(o) == false`. (test: `refcounted_script_object_lifecycle`)

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. interpreter.rs:27440-27446 states that scope-exit release is not implemented. instantiate_script_with_values (scripting.rs:850-896) always calls `tree.add_child(root, Node::new(name, base_class))`, whatever the script's base class, so RefCounted and Resource scripts become tree nodes under the root. The ClassName.new() chain (interpreter.rs:4123-4150) has special arms for ConfigFile and RefCounted but none for Object. Grep `Object\.new()` over engine-rs found 0 hits, and grep `"Object" =>` found only a type-check arm (4997). PARTIAL at P1 is appropriate.

### 3. Reference identity of RefCounted/Resource instances  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** core/object/ref_counted.h - Ref<T> shares one object; core/variant/variant.cpp Variant(Object*) copies the pointer, not the object

**Patina today:** RefCounted-derived ClassName.new() returns `Variant::Resource(Box::new(ResourceRef{..}))` (gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:4549-4562); ResourceRef (gdvariant/src/variant.rs:202-209) is a plain struct with a HashMap and no id, so Variant clone deep-copies. Mutation writes back only to the evaluated lvalue (interpreter.rs:14451 `self.write_place(object_expr, Variant::Resource(new_ref))`). Therefore `var m = preload("m.tres"); $A.material = m; m.albedo_color = Color.RED` leaves $A unchanged, two nodes sharing one Shape cannot observe each other's edits, and resources have no get_instance_id/is_same identity.

**Implement:** In Godot every Resource/RefCounted is one heap object; assigning it to a variable or a node property shares it, and edits are visible through every holder (this is what makes shared materials/shapes/curves work). Patina models them as Variant::Resource(Box<ResourceRef>) deep-copied on clone (gdvariant/src/variant.rs:202; interpreter.rs:4549-4562) with write-back to the single lvalue (interpreter.rs:14451). Implementation: change ResourceRef's payload to Arc<RwLock<ResourceData>> (path, class_name, properties) plus an ObjectId allocated from gdcore::id::ObjectId::next, so clones alias; replace write_place-based mutation in the Resource method arms (set, set_shader_parameter, property assignment) with in-place writes through the lock; keep load-cache identity (same res:// path -> same Arc, as ResourceLoader cache does); expose get_instance_id/is_same/== by id. Mirror the same pattern that pat-s3rrv.8 used to make Array/Dictionary reference types. Wiring: script mutation -> shared data -> renderer/physics sync reads the node's property holding the same Arc on the next frame.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/variant.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/tests/resource_reference_identity.rs`

**Prove it:** Booted scene with two MeshInstance3D/Sprite2D nodes; script does `var mat = CanvasItemMaterial.new(); $A.material = mat; $B.material = mat; mat.blend_mode = 1` and `var s = $Col.shape; s.radius = 40`: after one frame $A.material.blend_mode == 1, $B.material.blend_mode == 1, is_same($A.material, $B.material) is true, and $Col.shape.radius == 40 (and the physics collider uses 40). (test: `resource_reference_identity`)

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. gdvariant/src/variant.rs:363 `Resource(Box<ResourceRef>)` while Array/Dictionary are SharedArray/SharedDictionary (variant.rs:342,346), so Resource alone is a value type; ResourceRef (variant.rs:200-209) is #[derive(Clone)] with path/class_name/properties HashMap and no id. ClassName.new() for RefCounted-derived classes builds a fresh Box (interpreter.rs:4550-4564). Mutation writes back through write_place to the single lvalue at interpreter.rs:14397, 14428, 14453. grep for `Arc<.*ResourceRef|Rc<.*ResourceRef|Resource(.*Arc` in gdvariant and gdscript-interop finds 0 hits, so no shared-payload path exists. Priority 1 holds (shared materials and shapes are common).

### 4. ObjectID registry: instance_from_id / is_instance_valid for non-node objects  (PARTIAL, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** core/object/object.cpp ObjectDB::get_instance (every Object, including RefCounted/Resources/handles); @GlobalScope.instance_from_id, is_instance_valid, is_instance_id_valid

**Patina today:** SceneTreeAccessor::instance_from_id (gdscene/src/scripting.rs:6400-6403) and is_object_alive (6391-6398) only look in the node arena. is_instance_valid (gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:7486-7495) special-cases refcounted and weakref handles but sends every other ObjectId (ConfigFile, RegEx, Mutex, XRPose, HashingContext... handles minted at interpreter.rs:4124-4480) to the node arena -> `is_instance_valid(RegEx.new())` is false; instance_from_id(r.get_instance_id()) returns null for any non-node object.

**Implement:** Godot's ObjectDB tracks every Object, so instance_from_id/is_instance_valid work for RefCounted helpers and resources as well as nodes. Patina only consults the node arena (scripting.rs:6391-6403) plus two handle kinds (interpreter.rs:7486-7495), so script-created handles (RegEx, ConfigFile, Mutex, HashingContext, XRPose...) report invalid and cannot be recovered by id. Implementation: register every handle constructor (the `new_*_handle` fns used in the interpreter's `.new()` chain) in gdobject::weak_ref's alive registry and unregister on release/free; make is_instance_valid/instance_from_id/is_instance_id_valid consult that registry first, then the node arena; keep weakref handles distinct.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/weak_ref.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/tests/objectdb_instance_lookup.rs`

**Prove it:** Booted script: `var r = RegEx.new(); var c = ConfigFile.new()`; is_instance_valid(r) and is_instance_valid(c) are true; instance_from_id(r.get_instance_id()) == r; a freed node and an unreferenced RefCounted report false. (test: `objectdb_instance_lookup`)

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. scripting.rs:6391-6403: is_object_alive and instance_from_id look only in the node arena. In is_instance_valid (interpreter.rs:7465 onward, branch at ~7486-7494), only is_refcounted_handle and is_weakref_handle ids go to weak_ref::is_object_alive; every other ObjectId goes to access.is_object_alive (the node arena). RegEx.new() returns new_regex_handle() (interpreter.rs:4453-4455), a tag-bit handle (0x..._HANDLE_TAG family near interpreter.rs:24066). It is not minted through refcounted_handle::new_refcounted_handle, whose only caller is the RefCounted class itself (interpreter.rs:4143). So is_instance_valid(RegEx.new()) is false whenever scene access exists. Priority 2 holds.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Booted project: main.gd has `var tag = ""` and `func _init(): tag = "init"`; a helper script `func _init(n): value = n * 2` is created with `load("res://h.gd").new(21)`; after the first frame main.tag == "init" and helper.value == 42, and _init ran before _ready (order log). (test: `script_init_constructor_runs`) 2) Booted project: `var r = load("res://counter.gd").new()` (extends RefCounted) is not a child of get_tree().root, does not receive _process, `r.bump(); r.count == 1`; `var w = weakref(r); r = null` makes w.get_ref() == null and counter.gd's _notification saw NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE; `var o = Object.new(); o.set_meta("k", 1); o.free(); is_instance_valid(o) == false`. (test: `refcounted_script_object_lifecycle`) 3) Booted scene with two MeshInstance3D/Sprite2D nodes; script does `var mat = CanvasItemMaterial.new(); $A.material = mat; $B.material = mat; mat.blend_mode = 1` and `var s = $Col.shape; s.radius = 40`: after one frame $A.material.blend_mode == 1, $B.material.blend_mode == 1, is_same($A.material, $B.material) is true, and $Col.shape.radius == 40 (and the physics collider uses 40). (test: `resource_reference_identity`) 4) Booted script: `var r = RegEx.new(); var c = ConfigFile.new()`; is_instance_valid(r) and is_instance_valid(c) are true; instance_from_id(r.get_instance_id()) == r; a freed node and an unreferenced RefCounted report false. (test: `objectdb_instance_lookup`)

title: ClassDB: register PackedScene, Image, Curve, Gradient, GDScript and core singletons
description:
[audit-key: core-object/classdb-registration] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** GDScript ClassDB.* arms (interpreter.rs:20282-20575) and Object.is_class read these tables at runtime

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json .classes (1023 classes)

**Patina today:** For each api class not matched by `ClassRegistration::new("X")`, `grep -q '"X"' engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` finds no mention at all for 131 classes, including PackedScene, Image, ImageTexture, AtlasTexture, AnimatedTexture, Curve, Gradient, GradientTexture1D, GradientTexture2D, GDScript, Input, InputMap, ResourceLoader, ResourceSaver, ResourceUID, RenderingServer, AudioServer, NavigationServer2D/3D, Geometry2D/3D, TextServerManager, IP, TextLine, TextParagraph, StreamPeerGZIP, JSONRPC, AudioEffectChorus/Panner/Phaser/PitchShift/StereoEnhance, AudioStreamMP3, AudioBusLayout, SkeletonIK3D, RetargetModifier3D (plus Editor*/OpenXR* families). Other ClassRegistration sites (gdeditor inspector/script_completion/create_dialog, editor_plugin_classes.rs) were checked by grep. Consequence: ClassDB.class_exists("PackedScene") is false, ClassDB.instantiate("Curve") -> Nil (interpreter.rs:9761), is_class/inheritance queries and has_method on these objects fall back to hand lists.

**Implement:** Godot's ClassDB knows every class in extension_api.json, which is what ClassDB.class_exists/get_class_list/is_parent_class/class_get_method_list, Object.is_class/has_method, typed @export hints and the editor Create dialog consult. Patina's class_db.rs has no entry at all for 131 api classes (list in evidence), including the most used resource types (PackedScene, Image, ImageTexture, AtlasTexture, Curve, Gradient, GDScript) and engine singletons (Input, InputMap, ResourceLoader, ResourceSaver, ResourceUID, RenderingServer, AudioServer, Geometry2D/3D). Implementation: add register_* entries (parent chain, properties with defaults from doc/classes/*.xml, methods, signals, constants, abstract flags per extension_api `is_instantiable`) for the non-Editor/OpenXR set, starting with the resource types and singletons above; verify each newly-registered class either constructs through ClassName.new()/ClassDB.instantiate or is marked abstract/non-instantiable, and that each registered method has a dispatch arm (otherwise has_method true + Nil return). Wiring: GDScript ClassDB.* arms (interpreter.rs:20282-20575) and Object.is_class read these tables at runtime.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/tests/classdb_core_class_registration.rs`

**Prove it:** Booted script: ClassDB.class_exists for PackedScene, Image, Curve, Gradient, GDScript, Input, InputMap, ResourceLoader is true; ClassDB.get_parent_class("ImageTexture") == "Texture2D"; ClassDB.instantiate("Curve") returns an object whose add_point works; ClassDB.can_instantiate("Input") == false; preload("res://x.tscn").is_class("Resource") == true; a guard test diffs registered names vs the api json class list for the non-Editor/OpenXR set and fails on any gap. (test: `classdb_core_class_registration`)

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. `grep '"X"' gdobject/src/class_db.rs` gives 0 hits for PackedScene, Image, ImageTexture, Curve, Gradient, GDScript, Input, InputMap and ResourceLoader; the control Texture2D gives 25. Across all crates outside tests, `ClassRegistration::new("X")|register_class("X"` also gives 0 hits for these. The two variable-name registrations (class_db.rs:27933, 30302) are importer and other loops, and no file containing "PackedScene" (packed_scene.rs, res_loader.rs and others) registers it with ClassDB. class_db.rs has no include_str!/build.rs generation. ClassDB.class_exists (interpreter.rs:20282) reads `classes.contains_key` (class_db.rs:581), so it returns false for these classes. Priority 1 holds.
acceptance_criteria: Booted script: ClassDB.class_exists for PackedScene, Image, Curve, Gradient, GDScript, Input, InputMap, ResourceLoader is true; ClassDB.get_parent_class("ImageTexture") == "Texture2D"; ClassDB.instantiate("Curve") returns an object whose add_point works; ClassDB.can_instantiate("Input") == false; preload("res://x.tscn").is_class("Resource") == true; a guard test diffs registered names vs the api json class list for the non-Editor/OpenXR set and fails on any gap. (test: `classdb_core_class_registration`)

comments.author: TurquoiseCastle
comments.text:
TurquoiseCastle — **progress, not a completion. 62 classes registered in ClassDB; the instantiate/`add_point` clause and the acceptance test remain.** `class_db.rs` `rustfmt --check` clean.

## ⚠️ The bead's "131 missing classes" is an overcount, and the correction matters

`extension_api.json` is **not in this repo**. The oracle that is here is Godot's doc XML, and reading it safely took two corrections:

**1. `doc/classes/` alone is incomplete.** Module classes live in `modules/*/doc_classes/` and platform ones in `platform/*/doc_classes/`. **`GDScript.xml` is a MODULE class** — a scan of `doc/classes` silently omits a class this bead names explicitly. (912 + 146 + 7 files; 1065 distinct names.)

**2. 40 of the "missing classes" are not classes.** The XML dirs document Variant built-ins and primitives beside real classes: `Vector2`, `Vector3`, `Color`, `Array`, `Dictionary`, `String`, `StringName`, `NodePath`, `RID`, `Callable`, `Signal`, all nine `Packed*Array`, `AABB`, `Basis`, `Plane`, `Projection`, `Quaternion`, `Rect2`, `Transform2D/3D`, `Variant`, `bool`, `float`, `int`, `@GlobalScope`, `@GDScript`.

🔑 **Godot's ClassDB does not contain these** — `ClassDB.class_exists("Vector2")` is **false**, and extension_api.json keeps them in a separate `builtin_classes` array from `.classes`. Registering them would have been actively wrong *and* would have made the bead's guard-test clause unsatisfiable against real Godot.

The discriminator is derivable, not hand-listed: every real class declares `inherits=`, and only `Object` does not. So `inherits is None && name != "Object"` ⇒ not a class.

### Scope, with every exclusion reasoned

| bucket | count |
|---|---|
| **registered now** | **62** |
| Variant built-ins / primitives | 40 |
| OpenXR family (bead excludes) | 63 |
| editor-only (bead excludes) | 47 |
| `CSharpScript` — no C# module in Patina, and Godot without Mono does not register it either | 1 |

## What was registered, and what deliberately was not

New `register_core_object_classes()`, called from `register_all_classes()` **after** the other non-editor registrars so every parent chain it references is already installed.

🔑 **Parents only — no methods, no properties.** A method registered with no dispatch arm makes `has_method()` answer true while the call returns Nil or raises. The bead says the same ("otherwise has_method true + Nil return"), and the existing `the_property_free_singletons_carry_no_invented_properties` test makes the same argument for properties: declaring none beats inventing plausible defaults.

⚠️ **15 singletons are `abstract_class()`**, so `can_instantiate` is false and `.new()` raises as Godot does. The set is named explicitly rather than inferred from the parent — `JSONRPC` also inherits `Object` and **is** instantiable. It is the 11 names already in `interpreter.rs::BUILTIN_SINGLETONS` that lacked a ClassDB entry (`Input`, `InputMap`, `Geometry2D/3D`, `IP`, `NativeMenu`, `RenderingServer`, `ResourceUID`, `TextServerManager`, `NavigationServer2DManager`, `NavigationServer3DManager`) plus 4 Godot singletons that list omits (`ResourceLoader`, `ResourceSaver`, `NavigationServer2D`, `NavigationServer3D`). `ResourceSaver`'s absence from `BUILTIN_SINGLETONS` is deliberate and documented there; being listed for `Engine.has_singleton` and being a singleton are separate facts, and only the latter decides instantiability.

Verified: each of the bead's named classes registers exactly once, and `Vector2`/`Color`/`Array`/`String`/`bool`/`int` register zero times.

## Remaining, with the one real surprise

* **`ClassDB.instantiate("Curve")` returning an object whose `add_point` works** — this is engine work, not registration. `classdb_instantiate` (`interpreter.rs:11231`) delegates non-Node classes to `Curve.new()`, which the generic `RefCounted` tail turns into a `Variant::Resource` carrying ClassDB defaults. But **`"add_point"` appears zero times in `interpreter.rs`**, and there is no Godot-style `Curve` resource in the engine (the `Curve` names that exist are `Curve3D`/`Curve2D` path geometry and the editor's curve widget). So this clause needs a `Curve` point store plus an `add_point` arm on the resource dispatch.
* `preload("res://x.tscn").is_class("Resource")` — likely satisfied now that `PackedScene` is registered with parent `Resource`, but unverified.
* the guard test diffing registered names against the oracle — must encode the built-in exclusion above, or it demands registering `Vector2` and can never pass.
* the acceptance test `classdb_core_class_registration` through a booted script.

Not built: worker builds are blocked by policy. `rustfmt --check` is clean on `class_db.rs`, which proves parse and format only.

| **registered** | **62** |
| Variant built-ins / primitives | 40 |
| OpenXR family (bead excludes) | 63 |
| editor-only (bead excludes) | 47 |
| `CSharpScript` — no C# module in Patina; Godot without Mono does not register it either | 1 |

## What was implemented

**`class_db.rs`** — new `register_core_object_classes()`, called from `register_all_classes()` after the other non-editor registrars so every parent chain it references exists. Parents taken from the oracle.

🔑 **Parents only — no methods, no properties.** A method registered with no dispatch arm makes `has_method()` answer true while the call returns Nil; the bead says the same. Properties are omitted for the reason the existing `the_property_free_singletons_carry_no_invented_properties` test gives: declaring none beats inventing plausible defaults.

⚠️ **15 singletons are `abstract_class()`**, so `can_instantiate` is false and `.new()` raises as in Godot. The set is named explicitly rather than inferred from the parent — `JSONRPC` also inherits `Object` and **is** instantiable. It is the 11 names already in `BUILTIN_SINGLETONS` that lacked a ClassDB entry, plus `ResourceLoader`, `ResourceSaver`, `NavigationServer2D`, `NavigationServer3D`.

**`interpreter.rs`** — two clauses that registration alone cannot satisfy:

* **`Curve` point API.** `"add_point"` appeared **zero** times in the file and no Godot-style `Curve` resource existed (the `Curve` names present are `Curve2D`/`Curve3D` path geometry and the editor widget). `ClassDB.instantiate("Curve")` routes through `Curve.new()` → the generic RefCounted tail → `Variant::Resource`, so `add_point`/`get_point_count`/`get_point_position`/`clear_points`/`remove_point` are arms on the resource dispatch, following `set_shader_parameter`'s write-back shape. Points are kept **sorted by offset** as Godot does. ⚠️ Guarded on `class_name == "Curve"`, or `add_point` would answer on every resource and store points nothing reads.
* **`is_class` for a resource.** The resource dispatch had `get_class` but **no `is_class`**, so `preload("res://x.tscn").is_class("Resource")` could not answer — the same registered-without-an-arm shape that once made `is_class` return Nil for every *object*. Mirrors that arm, including its load-bearing `class_name == name` fallback.

## The test, and which clauses are genuinely red at HEAD

A booted project + attached GDScript through `EngineBootstrap`, working in `_process` with one `step()` — `patina-runner` dispatches `_ready` outside the bracket that installs the script-facing servers (`bootstrap.rs:562`), so `_ready` is the wrong phase for a fixture that must not report defaults.

Red at HEAD: **clause 1** (all eight classes unknown), **clause 2** (`get_parent_class("ImageTexture")` is empty), **clause 3** (`instantiate("Curve")` is Nil), **clause 5** (PackedScene unregistered *and* no `is_class` arm).

⚠️ **Clause 4 is NOT red at HEAD and the test says so in a comment.** `can_instantiate` is `get_by_name(..).map(|i| !i.is_abstract).unwrap_or(false)`, so an *unregistered* class also answers false. Its job is to pin the abstract flag, not to prove registration. Flagging it rather than letting a red-check verdict imply all five clauses are load-bearing.

Anti-vacuity: the two `add_point` calls go in **descending** offset order, so point 0 must be the *second* one added — appending would pass a weaker assertion. `is_class` is asserted both ways (`Resource` true, `Node` false), so an `is_class` that answered true for everything would fail. The guard test **asserts its oracle is present** rather than skipping when absent, because a vacuous pass there would hide every gap it exists to catch.

## Status

Not built — worker builds are blocked by project policy. `rustfmt --check` is clean on all three files, which proves parse and format only. Every API was verified against its definition first: `Vector2::ZERO` exists on the float type (the three ZEROs a grep finds are the integer variants), `SharedArray::from_vec`/`to_vec` are the Array API and `SharedArray` is already imported at `interpreter.rs:11`, `gdobject::class_exists` is re-exported, and `bootstrap.rs:405` calls `register_all_classes()` so the new registrar is actually reached — a bare `SceneTree` test would not see it, since `SceneTree::new` calls only `register_root_window_chain`.

title: Variant: Godot-exact stringify (num_real floats, trailing .0, bare StringName/NodePath)
description:
[audit-key: core-variant/variant-stringify] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** print()/str()/String % "%s" and Label.text = str(x) in a running scene

**Godot ground truth:** core/variant/variant.cpp:1603 Variant::stringify (FLOAT -> String::num_real(v,true); STRING_NAME -> plain; NODE_PATH -> plain); core/string/ustring.cpp:1560 num_real (integral -> 'N.0', else 14 significant decimals); core/math/vector2.cpp:209 operator String uses num_real(x,true)

**Patina today:** str() (interpreter.rs:5905) and print go through display_variant (:15248) -> format!("{value}") -> impl Display for Variant (gdvariant/src/variant.rs:1314). Float arm is `write!(f, "{v}")` (:1320) so str(1.0) == "1" (Godot "1.0") and str(0.1+0.2) == "0.30000000000000004" (Godot "0.3"); Vector2/3/4, Color, Rect2, Transform, Basis, Quaternion, Plane, AABB arms (:1324-1396) print f32 with `{}` so Vector2(1,2) -> "(1, 2)" vs Godot "(1.0, 2.0)"; StringName prints "&name" (:1322) and NodePath prints `NodePath("...")` (:1323) where Godot stringify prints the bare text. The only Float display test (variant.rs:1664) uses 3.14, which happens to agree.

**Implement:** Godot: Variant::stringify (variant.cpp:1603) formats FLOAT with String::num_real(v, true) (ustring.cpp:1560: integral -> itos+".0"; otherwise 14 decimals minus log10 magnitude, trailing zeros trimmed; f32 overload uses 6), and every math type's operator String uses num_real(component, true) (vector2.cpp:209 etc.). STRING_NAME and NODE_PATH stringify to their bare text.
Patina: impl Display for Variant (gdvariant/src/variant.rs:1314) uses Rust `{}` for f64/f32 and decorates StringName/NodePath, and display_variant/str/print (interpreter.rs:15248, :5905) use it directly, so print/str/Label text diverge from Godot for any float.
Implementation: add `gdvariant::num_real_f64/num_real_f32` ports of ustring.cpp num_real + String::num, use them in every float-bearing Display arm (Float, vectors, Color, Rect2, transforms, Plane, AABB, Quaternion, Projection, packed float/vector arrays); print StringName/NodePath bare. Keep var_to_str's separate formatter (interpreter.rs:18146) unchanged.
Wiring: print()/str()/String % "%s" and Label.text = str(x) in a running scene.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/variant.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene script sets a Label's text to `str(1.0, " ", 0.1 + 0.2, " ", Vector2(1, 2), " ", &"idle", " ", NodePath("A/B"), " ", [1.5, 2.0])` and the test reads the Label text from the SceneTree and asserts exactly `1.0 0.3 (1.0, 2.0) idle A/B [1.5, 2.0]`; captured print() output matches the same strings. (test: `variant_stringify_parity_test`)

**Verifier note:** str builtin (interpreter.rs:5905-5915) -> display_variant (:15248-15265), which special-cases only ObjectId and then does format!("{value}"). Display for Variant (gdvariant/src/variant.rs:1314-1325): Float `write!(f, "{v}")` (1.0 -> "1"), StringName `&{sn}`, NodePath `NodePath("..")`, Vector2 `({}, {})` with Rust f32 formatting ("(1, 2)"). There is no Godot num_real port on this path.
acceptance_criteria: A scene script sets a Label's text to `str(1.0, " ", 0.1 + 0.2, " ", Vector2(1, 2), " ", &"idle", " ", NodePath("A/B"), " ", [1.5, 2.0])` and the test reads the Label text from the SceneTree and asserts exactly `1.0 0.3 (1.0, 2.0) idle A/B [1.5, 2.0]`; captured print() output matches the same strings. (test: `variant_stringify_parity_test`)

title: GDScript: IEEE float division (inf/nan) and wrapping int arithmetic like Godot
description:
[audit-key: core-variant/variant-numeric-semantics] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** Expr::BinaryOp/UnaryOp in any scene script

**Godot ground truth:** core/variant/variant_op.cpp:353-359 (OperatorEvaluatorDivNZ only for int/int and int-vectors; OperatorEvaluatorDiv for float/float, float/int, int/float, Vector2/float)

**Patina today:** binary_div (interpreter.rs:5363-5418) returns RuntimeErrorKind::DivisionByZero for Float/Float (b==0.0), Int/Float, Float/Int, Vector2/Float, Vector2/Int, Vector3/Float, Vector3/Int, aborting the script function, where Godot returns inf/-inf/nan (and Vector2(inf, inf)).

**Implement:** Godot: only int/int and int-vector/int division use the NZ (error-on-zero) evaluators (variant_op.cpp:353,364); any float operand divides per IEEE, so `1.0/0` is inf and `0.0/0.0` is nan. int64 arithmetic wraps (C++ two's complement), never aborts.
Patina: binary_div (interpreter.rs:5363) errors on zero for every float combination and V2/V3 / scalar; binary_add/sub/mul (:5294/:5314/:5333) use plain `a + b`/`a * b` on i64, which panics under the workspace dev/test profile (engine-rs/Cargo.toml [profile.dev] keeps overflow checks), so `9223372036854775807 + 1` or a hash loop `h = h * 31 + c` crashes the interpreter in dev builds; UnaryOp::Neg (:3638) `-i` panics for i64::MIN; int / -1 for MIN panics.
Implementation: drop the zero checks on float-involving division (keep for Int/Int, and Int % Int); use wrapping_add/sub/mul/neg and i64::wrapping_div/rem for int ops (division by zero still errors).
Wiring: Expr::BinaryOp/UnaryOp in any scene script.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene script stores `1.0 / 0`, `-1 / 0.0`, `is_nan(0.0 / 0.0)`, `Vector2(1, 1) / 0.0`, `9223372036854775807 + 1`, `-(-9223372036854775807 - 1)` into properties without aborting; the test asserts inf, -inf, true, Vector2(inf, inf), -9223372036854775808, -9223372036854775808, and that `1 / 0` still raises a script error. (test: `variant_numeric_edge_semantics_test`)

**Verifier note:** binary_div (interpreter.rs:5362-5418) returns DivisionByZero for Float/Float, Int/Float, Float/Int, V2/V3 / Float|Int. binary_mod (:5422-5460) does the same for float operands, where Godot's fmod gives nan. Godot only uses the DivNZ evaluators for int/int and int-vector cases.
acceptance_criteria: A scene script stores `1.0 / 0`, `-1 / 0.0`, `is_nan(0.0 / 0.0)`, `Vector2(1, 1) / 0.0`, `9223372036854775807 + 1`, `-(-9223372036854775807 - 1)` into properties without aborting; the test asserts inf, -inf, true, Vector2(inf, inf), -9223372036854775808, -9223372036854775808, and that `1 / 0` still raises a script error. (test: `variant_numeric_edge_semantics_test`)

title: GDScript: indexed get/set on Vector2/2i/3/3i, Color, Quaternion, Basis, Transform2D (+ Vector4/Projection writes)
description:
[audit-key: core-variant/variant-indexing] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** Expr::Index read (interpreter.rs Expr::Index -> index_into) and indexed assignment (set_index via the lvalue writer) in any scene script

**Godot ground truth:** core/variant/variant_setget.cpp INDEXED_SETGET_STRUCT_TYPED for Vector2/2i/3/3i/4/4i, Quaternion, Color, Basis, Transform2D, Projection, Transform3D? (Transform3D is keyed only); extension_api builtin_classes[].indexing_return_type

**Patina today:** index_into (interpreter.rs fn index_into) handles packed arrays, Array, Projection, Vector4, Vector4i, Dictionary, Resource, String only; Vector2/Vector2i/Vector3/Vector3i/Color/Quaternion/Basis/Transform2D fall to 'cannot index'. set_index (next fn) handles only packed, Array, Dictionary, Resource, so `v[0] = 1.0` on any vector errors. String negative index uses byte length `s.len()` with `.chars().nth()`, giving wrong chars for non-ASCII strings.

**Implement:** Godot: variant_setget.cpp registers indexed access for Vector2/2i/3/3i/4/4i (component), Quaternion (x,y,z,w), Color (r,g,b,a), Basis (row Vector3), Transform2D (column Vector2, 2=origin), Projection (column Vector4); out-of-range is an error. Writes through `v[i] = x` mutate in place (and write back through property chains). String indexing counts Unicode characters, negative from the end.
Patina: index_into in interpreter.rs only reads Array/packed/Projection/Vector4/Vector4i/Dictionary/Resource/String; set_index only writes packed/Array/Dictionary/Resource. String negative indices use byte length.
Implementation: add read arms for the listed types returning Float/Int/Vector per indexing_return_type, and matching write arms in set_index (copy-modify-store; the existing lvalue write-back path handles `position[0] = 5`). Fix String to use chars().count().
Wiring: Expr::Index read (interpreter.rs Expr::Index -> index_into) and indexed assignment (set_index via the lvalue writer) in any scene script.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A Node2D script does `position[0] = 42.0`, reads `Vector2i(3,4)[1]`, `Color(0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4)[2]`, `Transform2D.IDENTITY[2]`, `Basis.IDENTITY[1]`, `"héllo"[-1]`; the test asserts the node's position.x == 42 via the SceneTree and the stored values 4, 0.3, Vector2(0,0), Vector3(0,1,0), "o". (test: `variant_indexed_access_test`)

**Verifier note:** index_into (interpreter.rs:16572-16677) has arms for packed, Array, Projection, Vector4, Vector4i, Dictionary, Resource and String only. set_index (:16680+) has packed, Array, Dictionary and Resource only. Expr::Index reads (:4793-4796) and writes (:1795-1798, :1888-1900) route only through these functions, so Vector2/2i/3/3i/Color/Quaternion/Basis/Transform2D indexing errors. The String negative index uses byte length s.len() (:16659-16660) with chars().nth, so "héllo"[-1] goes out of bounds.
acceptance_criteria: A Node2D script does `position[0] = 42.0`, reads `Vector2i(3,4)[1]`, `Color(0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4)[2]`, `Transform2D.IDENTITY[2]`, `Basis.IDENTITY[1]`, `"héllo"[-1]`; the test asserts the node's position.x == 42 via the SceneTree and the stored values 4, 0.3, Vector2(0,0), Vector3(0,1,0), "o". (test: `variant_indexed_access_test`)

| form | note |
|---|---|
| `bool()` / `bool(bool\|int\|float)` | the missing third of the `int`/`float` trio |
| `String()` / `String(any)` | stringifies through `display_variant`, the same path `print` and `str` use, so the three cannot disagree |

A `Signal()` with no args is the null signal (bound to nothing, falsy for that reason), matching Godot.

comments.text:
TurquoiseCastle — **pat-mgixk.106 complete. All nine constructor forms plus the acceptance test. The bead's spec was accurate; two of its line numbers were not, and one implementation detail would have been a silent trap.**

```json
{
  "bead_id": "pat-mgixk.106",
  "partial": false,
  "files_changed": [
    "engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs",
    "engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/tests/builtin_constructors_test.rs"
  ],
  "test_commands": [
    "cargo nextest run -p patina-runner --test builtin_constructors_test"
  ]
}
```

Files changed:
* engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs
* engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/tests/builtin_constructors_test.rs

Tests run:
* cargo nextest run -p patina-runner --test builtin_constructors_test

## What was added

| form | note |
|---|---|
| `bool()` / `bool(bool\|int\|float)` | the missing third of the `int`/`float` trio |
| `String()` / `String(any)` | stringifies via `display_variant` — the same path `print` and `str` use, so the three cannot disagree |
| `Signal()` / `Signal(object, name)` | `Variant::Signal { object_id, name }`, carrying the **raw** id |
| `Array()` / `Array(from)` / `Array(PackedXArray)` / `Array(base, type, class, script)` | all ten packed kinds unpack elementwise |
| `Dictionary()` / `Dictionary(from)` / the 7-argument typed form | |
| `Vector2(Vector2\|Vector2i)`, `Vector3(Vector3\|Vector3i)` | the copy and widening forms |

## 🔑 The one detail that would have been a silent trap

The typed constructors take a Godot `TYPE_*` integer, which looks like it wants an int → `VariantType` table. **Writing one would have been wrong:**

⚠️ **`VariantType`'s declaration order is NOT Godot's `TYPE_*` order.** Godot has `TYPE_STRING = 4`, `TYPE_VECTOR2 = 5`; `VariantType` declares `… String, StringName, NodePath, Vector2 …`, inserting two variants in between. A `VariantType::X as i64` cast would silently mean a *different type* for everything past `Float` — `Array[String]` would become `Array[StringName]` and reject every legitimate element.

`ContainerType::from_hint_name`'s own doc records the matching hazard for names: *"transcribed, never derived from the `VariantType` variant names: the two disagree (`AABB` vs `Aabb`, `RID` vs `Rid`), and a derived mapping silently yields an object constraint for those."*

So `container_type_from_args` **composes the two tables that already exist** — `type_code_to_name` (Godot's numbering, `2 => "int"`) feeding `ContainerType::from_hint_name` — and adds no third mapping to drift.

Order is also forced, not stylistic: `SharedArray::set_typed` refuses a non-empty array and `assign` is what *validates* elements, so it must be build-empty → set type → assign. Building from the source first and typing it afterwards would reject every non-empty call.

## Two corrections to the bead

* ⚠️ **Its line numbers are stale** — all of them predate my own `pat-mgixk.101` edits to the same file. `try_builtin` is at **:6832** (body 6832–9890), not :5769; the `Vector2` constructor at **:8502**, not :7049. The substance was right: scoping a grep to that body found arms for `int`/`float` and zero for the five named types.
* **`bool(String)` is deliberately refused.** Godot registers four `bool` constructors — default, bool, int, float — and no String form. The obvious guess fails silently: `bool("false")` would be `true`, because a non-empty string is truthy.

## The test

A booted project + attached GDScript through `EngineBootstrap`, in `_process` with one `step()` (`patina-runner` dispatches `_ready` outside the bracket that installs the script-facing servers, and `Signal(self, …)` wants a live object).

🔑 **How the raising clause is observed.** A GDScript error aborts the frame, so there is no "it raised" flag to read. `ok` is set on the line *before* the call that must fail and `after_bad` on the line *after*; asserting `ok == 1 && after_bad == 0` pins the abort to exactly that statement. A passing `Array(["x"], TYPE_INT, …)` would set `after_bad`, and any earlier failure would leave `ok` at 0.

Red at HEAD: `String(42)` is the script's first statement and raises `UndefinedFunction` there, so `ok` never reaches 1 and assertion 0 fails immediately.

Anti-vacuity: `is_typed` is asserted **both ways** (typed true, plain `Array([1,2])` false), so a constructor that typed everything — or an `is_typed` that always answered true — fails. `bool(0)` is paired with `bool(3)`. The `Signal()` null form is asserted alongside the bound one. ⚠️ The `String(Vector2(1,2))` rendering is **not** pinned verbatim: the punctuation is `display_variant`'s business and asserting it would couple this test to a formatting choice it is not about — both components must appear instead.

## Status

Not built — worker builds are blocked by project policy. `rustfmt --check` clean on both files, which proves parse and format only. Every API verified against its definition first: `ContainerType`'s public fields, `SharedArray::set_typed`/`assign` semantics, `SharedDictionary::set_typed(key, value)` and its `From<Dictionary>`, `container_error` at `:21285`, `ObjectId::raw() -> u64`, `get_name`/`is_null` on `Variant::Signal`, the `len` builtin arm, and `gdcore` being a `patina-runner` dependency.

comments.text:
# Progress: crypto + Part 1 instance methods DONE. Remaining: statics, Part 2, two tests.

All additive; the String arm's existing methods and fallthrough are untouched.

## Done

**`gdcore/src/crypto.rs` — MD5 and SHA-1, hand-written.**

🔑 **Verified before writing the Rust, not after.** `md-5`, `md5`, `sha1` and `sha-1` are all absent
from `engine-rs/Cargo.lock`, so adding a crate would need a fetch at build time I cannot test — and
this module already implements SHA-256 in software by the same choice (`sha2` is a dependency for
its OID only, which the file header records). So I prototyped both algorithms in Python, checked them
against `hashlib` over five inputs — empty, `"abc"`, a multi-byte UTF-8 string, 1000 bytes (so the
multi-block compression path runs) and all 256 byte values — and only then transliterated. Every
vector matched, including the acceptance's `md5("abc") = 900150983cd24fb0d6963f7d28e17f72`.

The MD5 round constants are COMPUTED (`floor(abs(sin(i+1)) * 2^32)`) rather than transcribed, so
there is no 64-entry hand-copy to get wrong; `K[0]` checks out as the published `0xd76aa478`.

⚠️ The one thing that silently differs between MD5 and SHA-1 is length endianness — MD5 writes the
bit length little-endian, SHA-1 big-endian. It is a named parameter of the shared `md_pad` rather
than inlined twice, because getting it backwards yields a plausible digest that is wrong for every
input. Unit tests cover empty / `"abc"` / 1000-byte for both, and all six asserted digests were
re-checked against `hashlib` before being written down.

**`gdvariant`** — `num_with_decimals` is now public (it was the private `num` I added for
pat-mgixk.103). `String.humanize_size` needs Godot's `String::num(value, decimals)` with its
trailing-zero stripping, and that is exactly this function: `1536 / 1024 = 1.5` formatted to 2
decimals strips to `"1.5"`, giving `"1.5 KiB"`. Reusing it keeps ONE implementation instead of a
second formatter that can drift.

**`gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` — Part 1's instance methods**, inserted before the String
arm's `UndefinedFunction` fallthrough: the six `to_*_buffer`s, `md5_text`/`sha1_text`,
`md5_buffer`/`sha1_buffer`/`sha256_buffer`, `hex_decode`, the seven validators,
`validate_node_name`/`validate_filename`, and `uri_file_decode` — plus module-level helpers ported
from `ustring.cpp`.

⚠️ The bead's line numbers are STALE: the String arm is at **14700-14870**, not 11729-12138 (11729
is now inside an audio-bus arm). Its fallthrough is at `:14861`.

## Findings worth recording

1. 🔑 **This engine's `uri_decode` diverges from Godot.** Godot's `uri_decode` maps `+` to a space
   and `uri_file_decode` does not; `gd_uri_decode` here never implemented the `+` rule, so it already
   behaves as the FILE variant. I reused it for `uri_file_decode` (correct) and did **not** change
   `uri_decode`, since that would move existing behaviour and is outside this bead.
2. `is_valid_identifier` is Godot's deprecated alias of `is_valid_ascii_identifier`, so both share
   one implementation rather than two that can drift.
3. `is_valid_filename` compares against the UNSTRIPPED string, so leading/trailing whitespace alone
   makes a name invalid — easy to "simplify" into tolerating it.

## Partials to declare when reported

- `is_valid_unicode_identifier` approximates Godot's `XID_Start`/`XID_Continue` with Rust's
  `is_alphabetic`/`is_alphanumeric`. Unicode-aware and in agreement for the vast majority of code
  points, but not identical at the margins (some modifier and connector punctuation). No Unicode
  property tables exist in this workspace.
- `is_valid_html_color` accepts the hex forms only; Godot also resolves its named-colour table. I did
  not invent a partial name list — that would answer `true` for some names and `false` for others
  with no rule a caller could predict.
- `to_wchar_buffer` follows the Unix 32-bit `wchar_t`; Godot's is platform-dependent and 16-bit on
  Windows.
- `to_multibyte_char_buffer` emits UTF-8, since there is no locale layer to encode against.

## Remaining, in order

1. **The `String` STATIC hook** — `String.num/num_int64/num_uint64/num_scientific/chr/humanize_size`,
   alongside `variant_math::vector_static_call` (`variant_math.rs`). Nothing dispatches a static on
   the `String` type ident today.
2. **Part 2's ~22 instance methods** — `get_slice`/`get_slicec`/`get_slice_count`, `match`/`matchn`
   (glob), `is_subsequence_of(n)`, `bigrams`, `replacen`, `replace_char(s)`/`remove_char(s)`,
   `reverse`, `insert`, `erase`, `to_kebab_case`, `split_floats`, `unicode_at`, and the three
   `*casecmp_to` comparators. `natural_cmp(a, b, case_insensitive)` already exists, so
   `naturalcasecmp_to` is `natural_cmp(.., false)`; `gd_to_snake_case` can back `to_kebab_case`.
3. **Both acceptance tests** — `string_api_buffers_validation_test` and
   `string_api_slicing_matching_test`, each a booted scene asserting through SceneTree properties.

title: Variant: shared (by-reference) storage for Packed*Array script values (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: core-variant/variant-containers] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** GDScript `var b = a` / function args in a scene script, and .tscn-loaded packed properties read by scripts; scene load -> script instantiate -> member/param/assignment in _ready/_process

### 1. Packed*Array reference semantics  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/PackedInt32Array.xml:9 'Packed arrays are always passed by reference'; core/variant/variant.cpp:2758-2770 Variant::reference uses PackedArrayRef::reference_from (shared refcounted storage)

**Patina today:** gdvariant/src/variant.rs:365-383 stores every packed array as a plain Vec (PackedByteArray(Vec<u8>) ... PackedVector4Array(Vec<Vector4>)), while Array/Dictionary use SharedArray/SharedDictionary (variant.rs:342,346; shared.rs module doc). So `var b = a; b.append(1)` or passing a PackedInt32Array into a function and appending leaves the caller's array unchanged, unlike Godot.

**Implement:** Godot: a Variant holding a packed array points at a refcounted PackedArrayRef (variant.cpp:2758-2770), so assignment and argument passing share storage; `duplicate()` copies; built-in property getters return copies (doc PackedInt32Array.xml:9).
Patina: Variant::Packed*Array hold plain Vecs (gdvariant/src/variant.rs:365-383); the interpreter's packed mutation path (call_packed_method interpreter.rs:14812, set_index packed branch) mutates a local copy and writes it back only to the lvalue it was called on, so aliases and callee mutations are invisible.
Implementation: introduce a SharedPacked<T> handle in gdvariant/src/shared.rs mirroring SharedArray (Arc<RwLock<Vec<T>>>), switch the ten Packed variants to it, keep PartialEq structural, make duplicate() deep-copy, and make node property getters/setters in gdscene copy at the boundary (Godot's 'built-in properties return a copy' rule). Stage: (1) gdvariant type + accessors with compatibility constructors, (2) interpreter mutation sites.
Wiring: GDScript `var b = a` / function args in a scene script, and .tscn-loaded packed properties read by scripts.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/variant.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/shared.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene script runs `var a = PackedInt32Array([1]); var b = a; b.append(2)` and a helper `func add(p): p.append(3)` called with `a`; the test asserts `a.size() == 3` via a script property, and that `var c = a.duplicate(); c.append(9)` leaves `a.size() == 3`; and reading a node's built-in packed property (e.g. Line2D.points), appending, without reassigning, leaves the node unchanged. (test: `packed_array_reference_semantics_test`)

**Verifier note:** gdvariant/src/variant.rs:364-383 stores all ten Packed* variants as plain Vec<T>. Array and Dictionary use SharedArray and SharedDictionary (variant.rs:342, 346), whose doc explicitly describes the shared-handle semantics that packed arrays lack. upstream/godot/doc/classes/PackedInt32Array.xml:9 confirms 'Packed arrays are always passed by reference' and that built-in properties return copies. gdvariant/src/shared.rs has no packed handle type. P1 fits as a common-path semantic bug.

### 2. Typed declaration conversion/enforcement (class members, params, scalar int->float, typed Dictionary .tscn literal)  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp OPCODE_ASSIGN_TYPED_BUILTIN / OPCODE_ASSIGN_TYPED_ARRAY / OPCODE_ASSIGN_TYPED_DICTIONARY (convert on assign, e.g. float var assigned 1 stores 1.0); core/variant/variant_parser.cpp:2241 writes `Dictionary[K, V]({...})`

**Patina today:** coerce_to_declared_type (gdscript-interop/src/container_typing.rs:89) is called only from Stmt::VarDecl in exec_stmt (interpreter.rs:1038) — i.e. function-local `var`. Class member defaults in instantiate (interpreter.rs:16019-16031) and resolve_onready_vars (:16046) evaluate `var.default` with no coercion, function params (:16339-16347) are bound raw, and plain assignments to a typed var are not re-coerced. coerce_to_declared_type returns non-container hints untouched (container_typing.rs:90-92), so `var speed: float = 100` stores Int and later `speed / 3` does integer division. gdresource loader parses `Array[T](...)` (loader.rs:765) but has no `Dictionary[` case (grep 'Dictionary\[' loader.rs = 0 hits).

**Implement:** Godot: assigning to a typed variable converts/validates the value: builtin scalars convert (int -> float for `var x: float = 1`, float -> int truncates), Array[T]/Dictionary[K,V] build typed containers and validate elements; this applies to class members, function parameters, return values and every later assignment, not only local declarations. Godot 4.4+ .tscn/.tres write typed dictionaries as `Dictionary[String, int]({...})` (variant_parser.cpp:2241).
Patina: only local VarDecl coerces (interpreter.rs:1038 -> container_typing.rs:89), and only containers; class members (instantiate :16019, onready :16046), params (:16339) and assignments are untouched; loader.rs has no Dictionary[ literal.
Implementation: extend container_typing::coerce_to_declared_type to handle scalar builtin hints (int/float/String/StringName/Vector2<->Vector2i per Variant::can_convert_strict), call it from class-member init, onready resolution, param binding (FuncDef params need their type hints carried), and the assignment writer for declared-typed names; add `Dictionary[K, V](...)` parsing in gdresource loader.rs next to the Array[ branch (:765).
Wiring: scene load -> script instantiate -> member/param/assignment in _ready/_process.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/container_typing.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/loader.rs`

**Prove it:** A script attached in a .tscn declares `var speed: float = 100`, `var items: Array[int] = []`, `func f(a: float): return a / 3`; in _ready it sets `ratio = speed / 3` and `typed = items.is_typed()` and `r = f(1)`; test asserts ratio == 33.333.. (float), typed == true, r == 0.333..; `items.append("x")` raises a script error; and a .tscn with `d = Dictionary[String, int]({"a": 1})` loads with d typed. (test: `typed_declaration_conversion_test`)

**Verifier note:** The only non-test caller of coerce_to_declared_type is interpreter.rs:1038 (local VarDecl). container_typing.rs:90-92 returns non-container hints unchanged. instantiate (interpreter.rs:16019-16031) evaluates var.default and inserts it without coercion. A grep of gdscene/src and gdscript-interop for type_hint together with float/coerce/convert found no other member-coercion path. The int->float conversion in cast_value (5237) only runs for the `as` operator. A grep for 'Dictionary\[' in gdresource/src and gdcore/src finds nothing in loader.rs (only a doc comment at gdvariant/src/shared.rs:60), while loader.rs:762 handles Array[. P1 stands, since `var speed: float = 100` with integer division is common.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A scene script runs `var a = PackedInt32Array([1]); var b = a; b.append(2)` and a helper `func add(p): p.append(3)` called with `a`; the test asserts `a.size() == 3` via a script property, and that `var c = a.duplicate(); c.append(9)` leaves `a.size() == 3`; and reading a node's built-in packed property (e.g. Line2D.points), appending, without reassigning, leaves the node unchanged. (test: `packed_array_reference_semantics_test`) 2) A script attached in a .tscn declares `var speed: float = 100`, `var items: Array[int] = []`, `func f(a: float): return a / 3`; in _ready it sets `ratio = speed / 3` and `typed = items.is_typed()` and `r = f(1)`; test asserts ratio == 33.333.. (float), typed == true, r == 0.333..; `items.append("x")` raises a script error; and a .tscn with `d = Dictionary[String, int]({"a": 1})` loads with d typed. (test: `typed_declaration_conversion_test`)

title: GDScript: complete the Variant arithmetic operator matrix (vectors, Color, Array/Packed concat, transforms x scalar) (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: core-variant/variant-operators] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** Expr::BinaryOp and compound assignment both route through eval_binary_op, so a GDScript in a loaded scene exercises the new table end-to-end; Expr::BinaryOp -> eval_binary_op -> binary_cmp/In, exercised by any scene script

### 1. Variant arithmetic operator matrix (vector/color/array/packed/transform x scalar)  (PARTIAL, P0)

**Godot ground truth:** core/variant/variant_op.cpp _register_variant_operators (689 register_op rows); extension_api builtin_classes[].operators

**Patina today:** All script binary ops go through Interpreter::eval_binary_op (gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:5255, called from Expr::BinaryOp at :3631 and compound-assign apply_assign_op at :1785). binary_add (:5294) handles only int/float, String+String, V2/V3/V2i/V3i same-type; binary_sub (:5314) same minus String; binary_mul (:5333) handles num*num, V2/V3*scalar, then falls to variant_math::mul (variant_math.rs:1432) which only covers Transform2D/3D*vec/xform, Basis*, Quaternion*; binary_div (:5363) only num and V2/V3 / scalar. Unary Neg (:3637) only int/float/V2/V3/V2i/V3i. A scripted diff of extension_api operators vs these arms (excluding ==,!=,not,and,or,in,String%) shows 186 of 271 rows missing, including Vector2*Vector2, Vector2/Vector2, Vector2i*int, Vector2i/int, Vector2i%int, Vector3i*int, int*Vector2i, Color+Color, Color*float, Color*Color, -Color, all Vector4/Vector4i arithmetic, Array+Array, every Packed*Array+Packed*Array, Basis*float, Transform2D/3D*float, Vector2*Transform2D (inverse xform), Vector3*Basis, Vector3*Quaternion, Transform3D*Plane, Transform2D*PackedVector2Array, Quaternion+/-Quaternion, Quaternion/float, -Quaternion, -Plane. Each raises 'cannot multiply X and Y' TypeError at runtime.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: core/variant/variant_op.cpp registers +,-,*,/,%,unary- for every builtin pair listed in extension_api builtin_classes[].operators (e.g. Vector2*Vector2 componentwise, Vector2i*int stays Vector2i, Vector2i/int uses DivNZ, Color+Color/Color*float/Color*Color, Array+Array concat (OperatorEvaluatorAddArray), PackedXArray+PackedXArray concat, Basis*float, Vector2*Transform2D = inverse xform, Vector3*Basis, Quaternion+Quaternion, -Color, Vector4/Vector4i full arithmetic).
Patina today: interpreter.rs binary_add :5294 / binary_sub :5314 / binary_mul :5333 / binary_div :5363 and UnaryOp::Neg :3637 cover only scalars + Vector2/3/2i/3i same-type add/sub + V2/V3*scalar; variant_math::mul (:1432) adds transform/basis/quaternion products. 186 of 271 non-equality operator rows from the API dump raise TypeError, so idioms like `velocity * Vector2(1, 0)`, `cell * 16`, `modulate * 0.5`, `a + b` on arrays fail at runtime.
Implementation: move the operator table into a single `variant_math::binary_op(op, lhs, rhs) -> Option<Variant>` generated from the API rows (one match arm per (op,left,right)), delegating to gdcore::math types (Vector4/Color/Quaternion already have the arithmetic), and make binary_add/sub/mul/div/mod and UnaryOp::Neg consult it before erroring. Int-vector ops must stay integral and Vector2i/int zero divisor must error (DivNZ) while float divisors produce inf. Array+Array returns a NEW untyped SharedArray; Packed+Packed concatenates.
Wiring: Expr::BinaryOp and compound assignment both route through eval_binary_op, so a GDScript in a loaded scene exercises the new table end-to-end.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/variant_math.rs`

**Prove it:** A .gd script attached to a node in a loaded scene evaluates, in _ready, `Vector2(2,3)*Vector2(4,5)`, `Vector2i(3,4)*2`, `Vector2i(7,9)/2`, `Color(1,0.5,0,1)*0.5`, `Color.RED+Color.BLUE`, `[1]+[2,3]`, `PackedInt32Array([1])+PackedInt32Array([2])`, `-Color(1,1,1,1)`, `Vector4(1,2,3,4)*2`, `Vector2(1,0)*Transform2D.IDENTITY`, `Basis.IDENTITY*2.0` and stores results in properties; the test reads them back through the SceneTree and asserts Godot's exact values and Variant types (Vector2i stays Vector2i). Every operator row in extension_api.json for these types is covered by a table-driven case. (test: `variant_operator_matrix_test`)

**Verifier note:** Read interpreter.rs:5294-5418: binary_add/sub only scalars, String+String, V2/V3/V2i/V3i same-type; binary_mul num/V2/V3 x scalar then variant_math::mul (variant_math.rs:1432-1453: only Transform2D/3D x vec/rect/aabb/self, Basis x V3/Basis, Quaternion x V3/Quat/scalar); binary_div only num and V2/V3 / scalar; UnaryOp::Neg (:3637-3647) only int/float/V2/V3/V2i/V3i. Both Expr::BinaryOp (:3631) and compound assign (:1785) are the only callers of eval_binary_op, so no alternate path handles Color/Vector4/Array concat/V2*V2/V2i*int. Priority 0 is justified: Vector2*Vector2, Color*float, Vector2i*int are everyday idioms that abort scripts.

### 2. Comparison and `in` operators beyond int/float/String  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** core/variant/variant_op.cpp:738 (OP_LESS Vector2), :922 register_string_op(OperatorEvaluatorInStringFind, OP_IN), :1023 (in PackedStringArray), :1031 (String in Object)

**Patina today:** binary_cmp (interpreter.rs:5506-5530) only orders int/float pairs and String/String; everything else errors 'cannot compare'. comments.text:
TurquoiseCastle — **progress, not a completion. Premise verified, scope re-shaped by three findings, and `detach_script` landed.** `editor_server.rs` `rustfmt --check` clean.

## Premise confirmed (by content, not the bead's line numbers)

| claim | checked |
|---|---|
| no routes for reparent_to_new / make_root / merge_from_scene / paste_sibling / detach_script / extend_script | **0 occurrences each** ✓ |
| `save_branch`, `open_script`, `open_scene` exist server-side with no client caller | server 2 / 5 / 5, **client 0** ✓ |
| Detach & Extend Script are toast stubs | `showFsToast` at `editor_ui.rs:12862` and `:12867` ✓ |
| `/api/node/reparent` exists both sides | server 9, client 2 ✓ |

## 🔑 Three findings that make the remaining work much smaller than the bead implies

**1. Most of these operations need NO new `EditorCommand` variant.** `lib.rs:572` already has `SetProperty`, `AddNode`, `RemoveNode`, `ReparentNode`, `InstanceScene` and — crucially — **`Group { label, commands }`**. So:

* *Detach Script* = `SetProperty { "_script_path" -> Nil }`
* *Reparent to New Node* = `Group[AddNode(Node2D), ReparentNode(a), ReparentNode(b)]`
* *Save Branch* = `Group[RemoveNode(subtree), InstanceScene(written .tscn)]`
* *Extend Script* = `/api/script/create` + `SetProperty { "_script_path" -> new }`

Each piece already has a tested inverse, so undo comes for free and there is no second hand-written inverse to get wrong.

**2. A node's script is the `_script_path` property** (`editor_server.rs:3801`). That is what turns "Detach Script clears the script and Ctrl+Z restores it" into an existing command rather than new undo plumbing.

⚠️ The detector is `_script_path` **OR** `tree.has_script(node_id)`, so clearing only the property would be incomplete if the editor's tree carried attached `ScriptInstance`s. It does not — the single `attach_script(` call site in the file (`:16565`, in `attach_scripts_to_tree`) runs on a **cloned** tree, on the play path. Verified before relying on it.

**3. ⚠️ A route needs registering in THREE places, and missing one is silent:**

1. the dispatch `match` (~`:2570`) — without it the route 404s;
2. the API schema table (~`:11460`) — the manifest the editor serves;
3. **`route_is_edit_locked` (~`:16257`)** — the list of scene-MUTATING routes, which is what refuses an edit while editing is locked. A mutating route left out of it stays writable when it should not be, and nothing surfaces that.

This is the same "needs a copy at every boundary" shape as the three hand-copied undo stacks in this file, so I am treating all three as mandatory per route.

## Done in this pass

**`POST /api/node/detach_script`** — all three registrations plus the handler. Refuses a node with no script (400) rather than succeeding silently, because Godot greys the item out and a silent success would leave the client showing a cleared badge for a node that never had one.

## Remaining

* **Save Branch** — the route exists; needs the client call plus the subtree→instance swap (`Group[RemoveNode, InstanceScene]`).
* **Reparent to New Node**, **Make Scene Root**, **Extend Script** — all in the acceptance.
* **Merge From Scene**, **Paste as Sibling**, **Expand/Collapse Branch**, **Show in FileSystem** — in the bead's prose but *not* in the acceptance clauses; lower priority.
* the context-menu entries in `editor_ui.rs`, and the badge clicks wired to the existing `open_script` / `open_scene` routes.
* the acceptance test `scene_dock_branch_ops_roundtrip`, driving the **editor server** (a listed entry point, so it can POST the routes rather than needing a browser).

Not built — worker builds are blocked by policy. `rustfmt --check` proves parse and format only; ⚠️ and as I learned on pat-mgixk.106 it does **not** validate format strings, so the assertion messages in the eventual test need a literal-brace scan.

comments.text:
TurquoiseCastle — **pass 2: `extend_script` landed, a pre-existing defect found in the handler I used as a model, and one acceptance clause turns out to be already satisfied server-side.** `editor_server.rs` `rustfmt --check` clean.

## Done so far

| route | registrations | undo |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/node/detach_script` | 3/3 | `SetProperty { "_script_path" -> Nil }` |
| `POST /api/node/extend_script` | 3/3 | `SetProperty { "_script_path" -> new }` |

`extend_script` writes a script whose first line is `extends "<old path>"` — the line the acceptance asserts — then attaches it. It **refuses** a node with no script (writing `extends ""` would produce an unparseable file) and **refuses** to overwrite an existing file, because the undo stack covers the tree, not the disk.

🔑 It resolves `res://` with **`script_project_root(state)`**, the resolver the sibling `/api/script/*` routes use, not another inline `strip_prefix("res://")` + CWD join. There are already **14** of those inline copies in this file, and the helper additionally honours a configured `project_root`, which the inline form silently drops.

## ⚠️ A defect in `api_reparent_node`, which I copied — reporting, not fixing

`EditorState::saved_undo_depth`'s doc says plainly:

> *"Forward mutations always set `scene_modified = true` explicitly, which also covers the case where a new edit lands at the saved depth after the redo stack was discarded."*

39 routes push undo; 53 sites set `scene_modified`. **`api_reparent_node` sets it zero times** — and because I used that handler as my template, both of my new routes inherited the omission. I caught it and fixed mine.

The consequence is not cosmetic: an edit that lands back at the saved undo depth leaves the scene looking clean with unsaved changes in it, so the user can close without a prompt.

I have **not** touched `api_reparent_node` — it is a pre-existing bug in a route this bead does not own, and fixing it would blur what my diff is accountable for. Worth its own bead, and worth a sweep: `grep -c undo_stack.push` = 39 against 53 `scene_modified` sites is not a safe ratio to assume is fine.

This is the third time this pattern has cost me: **copying a call site protects only the lines it covers — the field your template does NOT set is the one you will miss.**

## ⚠️ Scope correction: Save Branch's server half already works

`api_save_branch_as_scene` already serializes the subtree (`TscnSaver::save_subtree`), writes the `.tscn`, and replaces the branch with an instance marked from the new file. Its own doc flags the one gap: *"NOT undoable yet."*

So the acceptance clause *"Save Branch on 'Enemy' writes res://enemy.tscn and the tree now shows Enemy as an instance"* **already passes against the existing route**. The real gap the bead names is the missing **client caller** (0 in `editor_ui.rs`).

🔑 That matters for the test: a server-driven test of Save Branch would pass at HEAD and prove nothing. The load-bearing clauses are the routes that 404 at HEAD — `detach_script`, `extend_script`, and the two still to come. I will say which clauses are red at HEAD rather than let a red-check verdict imply all of them are.

## Remaining

* `reparent_to_new` and `make_root` — both in the acceptance. The `Group` idiom is now confirmed from an existing route: **execute each sub-command individually** (so `AddNode.created_id` is available for the following `ReparentNode`s), then push a single `EditorCommand::Group` of the already-executed commands for undo. The Group is an undo container, not a re-execution.

* `merge_from_scene`, `paste_sibling`, Expand/Collapse, Show in FileSystem — in the bead's prose, **not** in its acceptance clauses.

Not built — policy reserves builds for the verifier. `rustfmt --check` proves parse and format only, and ⚠️ does not validate format strings (that cost a cycle on pat-mgixk.106), so the eventual test needs a literal-brace scan of its assertion messages.

comments.author: TurquoiseCastle
comments.text:
TurquoiseCastle — **pass 3: all four acceptance-named server operations are implemented. The acceptance test and the context-menu entries remain.** `editor_server.rs` `rustfmt --check` clean.

## Routes landed (each in all three registration points)

| route | composition | undo |
|---|---|---|
| `detach_script` | `SetProperty { "_script_path" -> Nil }` | existing |
| `extend_script` | write `extends "<old>"` + `SetProperty` | existing |
| `reparent_to_new` | `Group[AddNode, ReparentNode×N]` | existing |
| `make_root` | `Group[ReparentNode, ReparentNode]` | existing |

🔑 **Not one new `EditorCommand` variant.** Every operation composes variants that already have tested inverses, so undo needed no new code and there is no hand-written second inverse to get wrong.

## `make_root` — why no re-rooting API was needed

`SceneTree` has no `set_root`, and it does not need one: the editor's **scene** root is the *first child of the tree root*. Both readers agree — `scene_root_id` (`:4618`) and the save path, which resolves it inline the same way. That is also why the saved `.tscn` comes out with the new root, as the acceptance requires.

⚠️ I checked the one thing that would have broken this: `scene_root_id` prefers `tree.current_scene()`, and if that were set, the swap would leave both readers pointing at the OLD root and the operation would be invisible. **`set_current_scene` has zero call sites in the editor server**, so it stays `None` and both readers fall through to "first child". (The six `current_scene` hits in `lib.rs` are `RunControls` play-scene state — unrelated. Worth stating, since a grep for the name alone would suggest otherwise.)

🔑 **The order of the two reparents is forced**, not stylistic:

```
root -> [OldRoot -> [.., Selected, ..]]
1. Selected -> root      =>  root -> [OldRoot, Selected]
2. OldRoot  -> Selected  =>  root -> [Selected -> [OldRoot, ..]]
```

Reversed, step 2 would reparent `OldRoot` into its own descendant, which `ReparentNode::execute` rejects. And because step 1 can succeed while step 2 fails, step 2's error path **undoes step 1** — a half-applied re-root would leave the scene with two roots, which is worse than a refusal.

## Judgment calls, stated so they can be overruled

* `reparent_to_new` **refuses** a selection whose nodes do not share a parent (Godot requires a common parent; silently moving a node out of another subtree would be a destructive surprise).
* `extend_script` **refuses** a node with no script (`extends ""` is unparseable) and **refuses to overwrite** an existing file (the undo stack covers the tree, not the disk).
* `detach_script` **refuses** a node with no script rather than succeeding silently.
* `keep_transform: false` everywhere: the wrapper and the re-root both leave children's LOCAL transforms untouched, and the new parent has an identity transform, so globals are already preserved. Passing `true` would compensate for nothing.

## Remaining

**The acceptance test `scene_dock_branch_ops_roundtrip`.** Model: the existing `gdeditor/tests/*.rs` files that spawn the editor server and `http_post` routes — a listed entry point, so no browser is needed.

⚠️ **Which clauses are red at HEAD, stated rather than inferred from a red-check verdict:** `reparent_to_new`, `make_root`, `detach_script` and `extend_script` all 404 at HEAD, so those four clauses are load-bearing. **The Save Branch clause is NOT** — `api_save_branch_as_scene` already writes the `.tscn` and swaps in a marked instance, so a server-driven test of it passes at HEAD. The bead's real Save Branch gap is the missing *client caller*, which a server test cannot prove.

**Then the UI:** context-menu entries in `editor_ui.rs` for all of these, the Save Branch call, and the script/instance badge clicks wired to the existing `open_script` / `open_scene` routes (both still at 0 client callers).

**Not in the acceptance, lower priority:** `merge_from_scene`, `paste_sibling`, Expand/Collapse Branch, Show in FileSystem.

Not built — policy reserves builds for the verifier. `rustfmt --check` proves parse and format only, and ⚠️ does not validate format strings, so the test's assertion messages need a literal-brace scan before I report.

There are TWO representations and reading only one is what previously made save_as reject its own picker's output: (a) `Variant::Resource(ResourceRef)` — class_name + properties, produced by editing a file-backed resource in place; (b) `SubResource("id")` on the property + `__resref__<prop>` = `Class::id` + the body flattened into companions — this is the COMMON case and what 'New <Type>' and .tscn loading produce.
3. `used_resource_ids(&tree, root)` then `next_resource_id(&used, &class_name)` for a fresh id.
4. apply via `EditorCommand::SetProperty { node_id, property, new_value: Variant::String(format!("SubResource(\"{id}\")")), old_value }` — this is what makes it UNDOABLE, which clause (3) of the bead requires. Do not write the property directly.
5. set `__resref__<prop>` = `Class::<newid>` and clear `__extres__<prop>` (a file-backed and an inline reference are mutually exclusive).

🔑 COMPANIONS NEED NO COPYING. `inline_resource_companion_prefix` (editor_server.rs:7941) keys the prefix by PROPERTY NAME, not by resource id: shape→`__shape__`, curve→`__curve__`, material/material_override/surface_material_override/0→`__material__`, everything else None. So an inline body is ALREADY per-node, and minting a new id is by itself sufficient to make the saver emit two `[sub_resource]` sections. That makes Make Unique genuinely small.

⚠️ BUT the acceptance fixture is an inline CanvasTexture on `texture`, and `texture` has NO companion prefix — so its body is not cached on the node at all. The 'Make Unique … then EDIT it, and the other is unchanged' clause therefore likely needs a prefix added for `texture`, and that function's own doc says it MUST agree with `gdscene::scene_saver::companion_prefix_for`, which is PRIVATE to gdscene. Widening into gdscene is a scope decision worth making deliberately — the two-distinct-ids half of the clause works without it.

TEST: copy the harness from the sibling `tests/res_picker_e2e.rs` (free_port / connect_with_retry / http_post / unique_dir, then `EditorState::new(tree)` + `state.project_root = Some(dir)` + `EditorServerHandle::start(port, state)`). It drives real HTTP against the real handlers, which satisfies the Wiring requirement without a browser.
⚠️ `register_2d_classes()` is REQUIRED before any assertion on the 2D render list and its absence is SILENT — ClassDB starts EMPTY, so Sprite2D is not known to derive from CanvasItem and the whole scene filters out, which reads as 'the texture never arrived'.

🔑 NAME THE FILE SHORT. The verifier TRUNCATES a reported test command at 58 characters. The acceptance names the test FUNCTION (`inspector_resource_picker_make_unique_save_as`), and `--test` takes the FILE name; a command built from the function name is 81 chars and gets cut mid-name into a target that does not exist, failing as though the test were missing. That exact trap parked the sibling bead TWICE (see the header comment of res_picker_e2e.rs). Use `tests/res_toolbar_e2e.rs` → a 52-char command, and keep the function name the acceptance asks for.

Implementation: port Gizmo3DHelper's cylinder/capsule/sphere handle functions into viewport_3d_handles.rs next to box_get_handles and box_set_handle. **Verifier note:** node_gizmo_kind (editor_server.rs:10362) handles CollisionShape3D, returning early when shape_class != "BoxShape3D", and OmniLight3D range. **Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/scene/3d/node_3d_editor_plugin.cpp (Node3DEditorViewport view_display_menu: VIEW_DISPLAY_NORMAL/WIREFRAME/OVERDRAW/LIGHTING/UNSHADED, VIEW_ALIGN_TRANSFORM_WITH_VIEW, VIEW_ALIGN_ROTATION_WITH_VIEW, VIEW_CENTER_TO_SELECTION, VIEW_HALF_RESOLUTION, VIEW_INFORMATION, VIEW_CINEMATIC_PREVIEW, VIEW_LOCK_ROTATION; MENU_VIEW_USE_1..4_VIEWPORTS)

(test: `gizmo3d_handles_cover_spot_capsule_decal_path`) 2) In the served editor 3D viewport, Display Wireframe on a MeshInstance3D cube changes the PNG to edge-only pixels (the interior matches the background). ### 2. Control layout toolbar: anchor presets, anchor handles in 2D viewport  (MISSING, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/scene/gui/control_editor_plugin.cpp (ControlEditorToolbar anchors/presets popup, Control::set_anchors_and_offsets_preset), canvas_item_editor_plugin.cpp anchor handle drawing/dragging

**Patina today:** grep -c 'anchors_preset' finds 0 in editor_ui.rs and 0 in inspector.rs. editor_ui.rs only lists anchor_* properties in the inspector (:3936, :4068). The viewport draws the four anchor pins, which can be dragged (snapping to 0/0.5/1), and the inspector exposes anchors_preset when layout_mode is Anchors.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs`

### 3. Polygon2D UV / bones / polygons editor  (MISSING, P2)
