## MistyTower — scope survey before touching anything. ⚠️ This bead is THREE editor features and demands THREE tests.

Recording this first so it is not re-derived: the gate resolves **every** test a
bead demands by name, and this one names
`viewport2d_polygon_editors_cover_collision_occluder_nav`,
`control_anchor_preset_toolbar_sets_godot_offsets` and
`polygon2d_uv_editor_writes_uv_and_bone_weights`. None of the three exists, so
the bead cannot close until all three do. It is not closable incrementally.

### Clause 1 — polygon/shape editors (P1). Four parts, very different sizes

| part | state | size |
|---|---|---|
| `CollisionPolygon2D.polygon` | one arm in `point_property_for` (`editor_server.rs:18273`, currently Path2D/Polygon2D/Line2D only) | **trivial** |
| Segment / SeparationRay / WorldBoundary / Convex / Concave handles | additive arms in `api_shape_handles` (`:18452`) + `api_shape_resize`; the existing arms read flattened `__shape__<key>` companions and return `(name, local offset)` | **moderate, low risk** |
| `LightOccluder2D` | 🔑 **the companion already exists** — `packed_scene.rs:1749` flattens the sub-resource to `__occluder__*`, and `light2d_scene.rs:176` already reads `__occluder__polygon` for shadow casting. So the READ path is free; only the write + save round-trip is new | moderate |
| `NavigationRegion2D` outlines | ⚠️ **not flattened at all.** `packed_scene.rs:2025-2045` resolves `navigation_polygon` but only lifts `vertices`, as `__navmesh_vertices__`. Godot's NavigationPolygon has `vertices` AND `outlines`; the bead asks for **outline** editing, so this needs new flattening in **`gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`** — a file the bead's own Files list does NOT mention | **scope the bead understates** |

The client half (`isPointEditableSelected`, `editor_ui.rs`) should read the
server's `editable` flag — `api_shape_handles` already returns one.

### Clause 2 — Control anchor presets (P1)

Genuinely absent (`anchors_preset` greps to 0 outside the generated inspector
schema, which only lists it as an int hint — so writing it today just stores an
int with no anchor/offset math). Needs a port of Godot's
`Control::set_anchors_preset` + `set_offsets_preset` (16 presets with
keep-offset modes), a new undoable POST route, a toolbar popup, and draggable
viewport anchor pins with 0/0.5/1 snapping.

### Clause 3 — Polygon2D UV / bones / polygons editor (P2)

Entirely absent. A bottom-panel UV canvas, three new undoable routes, bone
weight painting against Skeleton2D, and an acceptance that checks a **rendered
texel in the viewport PNG**. The largest of the three.

### ⚠️ Honest assessment

This is three beads' worth of editor work bundled under one id, and each clause
has a browser/HTTP-level acceptance. I am going to work it in acceptance order
(clause 1 → 2 → 3) and report **progress, not completion**, until all three
tests exist and pass. I will not re-report the bead just because one clause
builds — that is exactly the trap pat-mgixk.82 set, where a committed test
covered half the acceptance and a re-report would have closed it with the other
half unwritten.

If the operator would rather this were split into three beads, that is a better
shape than one P1 carrying a P2 UV editor — but I do not create or close beads,
so flagging it here.

Starting on clause 1: `point_property_for` and the five missing shape-handle
sets, which are additive and fully scoped above.

## Clause 1 is now fully scoped — and much smaller than my first survey suggested

Follow-up to my previous comment, which called the LightOccluder2D/Nav parts
"scope the bead understates". For the occluder that was **wrong in my favour**:
the machinery already exists end to end. Correcting it here rather than leaving
a pessimistic note for the next reader.

### 🔑 The save path already rebuilds sub-resources from companions

`gdscene/src/scene_saver.rs:1463` — `companion_prefix_for(property)` maps a
node property to the companion prefix caching its sub-resource:

```rust
"shape" => Some("__shape__".to_string()),
"curve" => Some("__curve__".to_string()),
"material" | "material_override" | "surface_material_override/0" => Some("__material__"),
// plus indexed __surfmatN__ for surface overrides > 0
```

and `collect_sub_resource_bodies` rebuilds each `[sub_resource]` **body** from
them at save time. Its own doc records why it exists: before pat-0q2kx.77 the
section was written as a bare header with no properties, so a
RectangleShape2D's `size` was silently dropped on every save.

So "updates the OccluderPolygon2D sub-resource **in the file**" needs ONE
additive arm, `"occluder" => Some("__occluder__".to_string())`, not new
machinery. `LightOccluder2D.occluder` is confirmed as the driving property at
`packed_scene.rs:1737`.

### 🔑 And the read/write path needs no special case either

`point_property_for` returns a **node property name**, and `read_point_list` /
`commit_point_list` operate on exactly that — so because the flattener already
lifts the geometry to `__occluder__polygon` (`packed_scene.rs:1749`, read today
by `light2d_scene.rs:176` for shadow casting), the whole occluder clause is:

```rust
"CollisionPolygon2D" => Some("polygon"),
"LightOccluder2D"    => Some("__occluder__polygon"),
```

Two arms, and the existing undoable `commit_point_list` carries both.

### Concrete clause-1 plan

1. `editor_server.rs` `point_property_for` (**18273**) — the two arms above.
2. `editor_server.rs` `api_shape_handles` (**18452**) + `api_shape_resize` —
   Segment (a,b), SeparationRay (length), WorldBoundary (normal/distance),
   Convex/Concave (points), alongside the existing Circle/Rectangle/Capsule.
   Existing arms read flattened `__shape__<key>` and return
   `(name, local offset)`.
3. `scene_saver.rs` `companion_prefix_for` — the `"occluder"` arm.
   ⚠️ **One open detail:** the saver needs the sub-resource TYPE for the
   section header. Shapes carry it in `__shape__class`, which is set
   separately; the occluder flattener copies the sub-resource's own props and
   there is no `__occluder__class`. So either the flattener must also record
   the class, or the saver must default LightOccluder2D's companion to
   `OccluderPolygon2D` — which is the only type that property accepts in Godot,
   so defaulting is safe and simpler.
4. `editor_ui.rs` `isPointEditableSelected` — read the server's `editable` flag
   (`api_shape_handles` already returns one) instead of its hard-coded class
   list.
5. **NavigationRegion2D outlines remains the one genuinely larger piece**:
   `packed_scene.rs:2025` lifts only `vertices` (as `__navmesh_vertices__`),
   never `outlines`, so that needs new flattening plus its own
   `companion_prefix_for` arm. Unchanged from my earlier note.

### Routes and harness for the acceptance test (pinned, so it is not re-derived)

* `GET  /api/viewport/points?node_id=N`
* `GET  /api/viewport/shape_handles?node_id=N` → `{ok, editable, shape, handles:[{handle,x,y}]}`
* `POST /api/viewport/shape_resize`
* `POST /api/path2d/point/{add,move,remove}` — the GENERIC handlers, keyed off
  `point_property_for`, so they serve any class it maps. Body:
  `{"node_id":N,"x":f,"y":f,"index":i?}`; an out-of-range `index` appends.
  `/api/polygon2d/vertex/*` are aliases onto the same handlers.
* Harness: `EditorServerHandle::start(port, EditorState::new(tree))` with local
  `http_get`/`http_post` helpers, as in
  `gdeditor/tests/anim_tree_loads_from_the_scene.rs`.

### Status

`editor_server.rs` is exclusively leased by BlackWaterfall (to 16:35Z) and
PinkMoose (to 17:14Z); I messaged both (92578) naming the three functions and am
**not** writing into it meanwhile. Next conflict-free step is the acceptance
test itself, a new file under `gdeditor/tests/`.

title: Undo: register undoable commands for animation tracks, audio buses, theme, SpriteFrames, TileSet data, input map, signals
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-undo] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/editor_undo_redo_manager.cpp (every dock/plugin op registers do/undo methods; History dock lists them)

**Patina today:** These mutating handlers neither push undo_stack nor reference undo at all: api_add_track (editor_server.rs:14760-14833), api_audio_add_bus (:22703), api_theme_item_set (:7352), api_spriteframes_anim_add (:4083), api_tileset_tile_data (:19005-19323), api_set_input_map (:23039) and signal disconnect (:22160). By contrast, api_tilemap_paint (:18293) and api_add_keyframe do push undo.

**Implement:** Godot routes every editor mutation through EditorUndoRedoManager, so Ctrl+Z and the History dock cover audio bus edits, theme items, SpriteFrames animations, TileSet tile data, project-setting and input-map changes, and signal (dis)connections.

Patina's undo stack covers scene-tree property and node ops and tilemap paint, but not the handlers listed (editor_server.rs:14760, :22703, :7352, :4083, :19005, :23039, :22160).

Implementation: add EditorCommand variants (or a generic closure-based Do/Undo pair holding before/after snapshots of the affected store) for each store: animations, audio_bus_layout, theme_editor and the .tres, the SpriteFrames sub-resource, TileSet TileData, the input map and the signal store. Push from each handler and clear redo. Make /api/history list them with Godot-style action names.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/undo_redo.rs`

**Prove it:** In the served editor, each of these is followed by Ctrl+Z (/api/undo) and restores the prior state, both on disk where the edit persists and in the corresponding GET route: add audio bus 'Music', set theme item Button/font_color, add SpriteFrames animation 'run', set a tile's physics polygon, add input action 'jump', disconnect a signal. /api/history shows six named entries. (test: `undo_covers_audio_theme_spriteframes_tileset_inputmap`)

**Verifier note:** I checked each cited handler body with grep 'undo|history|push_|snapshot': api_add_track 14760-14840, api_audio_add_bus 22703-22760, api_theme_item_set 7352-7420, api_spriteframes_anim_add 4083-4140 and api_set_input_map 23039-23100 all have 0 hits, and the tileset range 19005-19323 has 0 undo hits. api_disconnect_signal (editor_server.rs:22129-22174) rewrites signal_connections and returns with no undo push. By contrast, api_add_keyframe right above add_track pushes EditorCommand::AnimationEdit (:14737). I found no generic undo middleware in the router. PARTIAL at P1 stands.
acceptance_criteria: In the served editor, each of these is followed by Ctrl+Z (/api/undo) and restores the prior state, both on disk where the edit persists and in the corresponding GET route: add audio bus 'Music', set theme item Button/font_color, add SpriteFrames animation 'run', set a tile's physics polygon, add input action 'jump', disconnect a signal. /api/history shows six named entries. (test: `undo_covers_audio_theme_spriteframes_tileset_inputmap`)

title: Scene menu: New Inherited Scene, Reopen Closed, Reload Saved, Clear Inheritance
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-scene-menu] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/editor_node.cpp (SCENE_NEW_INHERITED_SCENE, SCENE_OPEN_PREV, SCENE_RELOAD_SAVED_SCENE, FILE_EXPORT_MESH_LIBRARY) ; editor/docks/scene_tree_dock.h TOOL_SCENE_OPEN_INHERITED/CLEAR_INHERITANCE

**Patina today:** The Scene menu (editor_ui.rs:2000-2006) has only New, Open, Save, Save As, Close and Quit. grep finds 0 hits for 'New Inherited', 'Reload Saved' and 'Reopen Closed' in editor_ui.rs. editor_server.rs has no inherited-scene creation route (grep -i 'new_inherited|inherited_scene' finds 0).

**Implement:** Godot's 'New Inherited Scene...' creates an unsaved scene whose root instances the base scene with `[node name=X instance=ExtResource(base)]` (inherited, so children are editable-inherited). Saving writes only the overrides. 'Reopen Closed Scene' restores the last closed tab, 'Reload Saved Scene' discards edits, and 'Clear Inheritance' bakes the tree.

Patina has none of these.

Implementation: add POST /api/scene/new_inherited {base_path}, which instantiates the base as the root, marks the root's scene_file_path and inherited state, and lets TscnSaver emit the base instance header plus diff-only properties (check scene_saver's instance-diff path). Add /api/scene/reload (reload from disk with a confirm prompt), keep a closed-tab stack for reopen, and add /api/node/clear_inheritance. Add the client menu items.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_saver.rs`

**Prove it:** In the served editor: New Inherited Scene from res://base.tscn, change the root's modulate, and save as res://child.tscn. The file has `[ext_resource ... path="res://base.tscn"]`, root `instance=ExtResource(...)`, and only the modulate override. Changing base.tscn changes child in Play. Reopen Closed brings back a closed tab. (test: `scene_menu_new_inherited_scene_saves_diff`)

**Verifier note:** The served Scene menu (editor_ui.rs:2024-2031) has only New, Open, Save, Save As, Close and Quit. Grepping 'new.?inherited|reload.?saved|reopen.?closed|clear.?inheritance|closed_tab|scene/reload' over editor_ui.rs and editor_server.rs found 0 hits. The near-miss is scene_menu_commands.rs:21/:176: it has a SceneMenuAction::NewInheritedScene, but that only records `inherited_from` on a document struct and never instantiates the base. Its only references are lib.rs:121 and a doc comment in project_menu_commands.rs, and the server routes do not use it, so it is a dead bookkeeping model, not wiring. The Instantiate button tooltip (editor_ui.rs:2409) mentions inherited scenes, but its handler only calls doInstanceScene (:12838). MISSING at P1 stands.
acceptance_criteria: In the served editor: New Inherited Scene from res://base.tscn, change the root's modulate, and save as res://child.tscn. The file has `[ext_resource ... path="res://base.tscn"]`, root `instance=ExtResource(...)`, and only the modulate override. Changing base.tscn changes child in Play. Reopen Closed brings back a closed tab. (test: `scene_menu_new_inherited_scene_saves_diff`)

title: Expose EditorInspectorPlugin/EditorProperty/EditorResourceConversionPlugin to @tool scripts and wire them into the editor inspector
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/inspector-plugin-family] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/doc/classes/EditorInspectorPlugin.xml, EditorProperty.xml, EditorResourceConversionPlugin.xml; editor/inspector/editor_inspector.cpp

**Patina today:** A Rust-only trait exists: gdeditor/src/inspector.rs:794 'pub trait EditorInspectorPlugin' with InspectorPluginRegistry (:914-950), and gdeditor/src/editor_compat.rs:35 'pub type EditorProperty = CustomPropertyEditor' - not script-facing. No ClassDB registration for any of the three (only hits inspector_schema_generated.rs:4466,4472,4473). The EditorPlugin ClassDB registration (class_db.rs:29930) lists no add_inspector_plugin / add_resource_conversion_plugin; crate-wide grep for 'add_inspector_plugin', '_can_handle', '_parse_property', 'add_property_editor', 'add_resource_conversion_plugin', '_converts_to' returns 0. So a @tool addon cannot customise the inspector.

**Implement:** Register the three classes (parents RefCounted, Container, RefCounted) with Godot's virtuals (_can_handle, _parse_begin/_parse_category/_parse_group/_parse_property/_parse_end, add_custom_control, add_property_editor; EditorProperty _update_property, emit_changed, get_edited_object/get_edited_property, label/read_only/checkable; _handles/_converts_to/_convert). Add EditorPlugin.add_inspector_plugin/remove_inspector_plugin and add_resource_conversion_plugin. Bridge script plugins into InspectorPluginRegistry (inspector.rs:914) so the served inspector JSON includes custom controls/properties and edits flow back via emit_changed.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/inspector.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`

**Prove it:** ClassDB.class_exists for all three true; EditorPlugin has add_inspector_plugin. Editor-server test: a @tool plugin whose _can_handle returns true for Node2D and whose _parse_property replaces 'position' with a custom EditorProperty makes GET inspector for a Node2D report the custom editor for 'position', and calling emit_changed('position', Vector2(3,4)) updates the node. A conversion plugin converting StandardMaterial3D->ShaderMaterial appears in the resource context-menu list.
acceptance_criteria: ClassDB.class_exists for all three true; EditorPlugin has add_inspector_plugin. Editor-server test: a @tool plugin whose _can_handle returns true for Node2D and whose _parse_property replaces 'position' with a custom EditorProperty makes GET inspector for a Node2D report the custom editor for 'position', and calling emit_changed('position', Vector2(3,4)) updates the node. A conversion plugin converting StandardMaterial3D->ShaderMaterial appears in the resource context-menu list. (test: `editor_inspector_plugin_script_api_wired`)

title: GDScript: fix not-precedence and add not in, is not, %Unique, await-expr, lambda name/return type, ...args
description:
[audit-key: gdscript/gdscript-parser-exprs] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** these must work in a scene-attached script driven by the MainLoop

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/gdscript/gdscript_parser.cpp:2938 (`not` operand parsed at PREC_LOGIC_NOT, below comparison), :4223 (NOT also infix `not in` at PREC_CONTENT_TEST), parse_type_test (`is not`), parse_get_node (`%Name`), parse_await (PREC_AWAIT, any expression position), parse_lambda (optional name and `-> Type`), gdscript_parser.h:854 rest_parameter (`...args`, 4.5)

**Patina today:** parser.rs:1631-1638 parses `not` inside parse_unary, binding tighter than comparison, so `not a == b` evaluates `(not a) == b` (Godot: `not (a == b)`). parse_comparison :1495-1517 has `In` but no `Not In`. parse_type_test :1690-1701 calls parse_type_hint right after Is, so `x is not Node` fails. parse_primary :1746-1992 has no Token::Percent arm, so `%HealthBar` fails to parse (the tree side supports '%' paths at gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:3130). await only as a statement (:584, :1319-1323) or `var x = await` (:735-747); `x = await f()`, `return await f()`, `if await f():` fail. Lambda :1857-1885 requires `(` right after func (no named lambdas) and `:` right after `)` (no `-> int`). No `...` token for variadic params.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: gdscript_parser.cpp:2938 parses the operand of `not`/`!` at PREC_LOGIC_NOT (looser than comparison/content-test); NOT is also the infix `not in` operator (:4223); `is not T` negates a type test; `%Name` is get_node("%Name") shorthand; `await` is a prefix expression usable anywhere (PREC_AWAIT); lambdas may be named and carry `-> Type`; Godot 4.5 adds variadic `func f(...args: Array)`.

Patina: parser.rs:1631 binds `not` at unary level; :1495-1517 lacks `not in`; :1690-1701 lacks `is not`; :1746-1992 has no `%` arm; await restricted to :584/:735; lambda :1857-1885 rejects names/return types.

Implement: move `not` to its own level between parse_and and parse_comparison; add `Not In` peek in comparison (emit UnaryOp::Not over BinOp::In); accept optional Not after Is; add Percent-in-primary producing Expr::GetNode("%Name") (resolved by existing scene_tree.rs:3130); introduce Expr::Await evaluated through the coroutine machinery (coroutine.rs AwaitTarget) so it can appear in assignments/returns; accept an optional ident and `-> Type` in lambdas; parse `...name` as a rest param collecting extra args into an Array in call_instance_method_impl (interpreter.rs:16299). Wiring: these must work in a scene-attached script driven by the MainLoop.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/parser.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene-attached script evaluates `not 1 == 2` -> true, `3 not in [1,2]` -> true, `self is not Node2D` correctly, `%Label.text = "ok"` updates a unique-named child, `hp = await get_hp()` resumes with the value, `var f = func add(a, b) -> int: return a + b` works, and `func sum(...nums): ` sums variadic args; results asserted after frames run. (test: `gdscript_parser_expression_forms`)

**Verifier note:** `not` is parsed in parse_unary (parser.rs:1631-1638) with a parse_unary operand. That binds tighter than parse_comparison (:1495-1517), so `not a == b` becomes `(not a) == b`. The comparison op table contains In but has no Not+In peek. parse_type_test (:1690-1701) calls parse_type_hint right after Is, so `is not` fails. Token::Percent appears only as the binary Mod operator (:1607); parse_primary has no prefix arm for it. await is reached only via the statement dispatch (:584) and `var x = await` (:735). The lambda parser (:1857-1885) does expect(LParen) right after func and expect(Colon) right after `)`. There is no `...` token in tokenizer.rs. PARTIAL with P1 holds, since plain `not` and `in` do work.
acceptance_criteria: A scene-attached script evaluates `not 1 == 2` -> true, `3 not in [1,2]` -> true, `self is not Node2D` correctly, `%Label.text = "ok"` updates a unique-named child, `hp = await get_hp()` resumes with the value, `var f = func add(a, b) -> int: return a + b` works, and `func sum(...nums): ` sums variadic args; results asserted after frames run. (test: `gdscript_parser_expression_forms`)

title: GDScript: project-wide class_name registry for cross-file classes
description:
[audit-key: gdscript/gdscript-global-classes] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/config/project_settings.cpp get_global_class_list; modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp resolves identifiers against ScriptServer::get_global_class_*

**Patina today:** class_registry is a per-Interpreter HashMap (interpreter.rs:594, :908) populated only from that interpreter's own run_class (:16006-16008). Greps 'global_script_class|class_name_index|GLOBAL_SCRIPT_CLASSES|script_class_cache' over gdscript-interop/src, gdscene/src, patina-runner/src, gdresource/src: 0 hits; '"get_global_class_list"' in interpreter.rs: 0 hits. So `Enemy.new()` / `Utils.helper()` where the class_name lives in another .gd file has nothing to resolve against.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: every script with `class_name X` is registered project-wide (global_script_class_cache.cfg); any script can use X as a type, call X.new(), X.static_func(), X.CONSTANT, X.Enum, `is X`, and ProjectSettings.get_global_class_list() returns {class, base, path, language, icon}.

Patina: no registry beyond the per-interpreter map (interpreter.rs:594).

Implement: a process-wide registry (thread_local like SCRIPT_TRANSLATIONS at interpreter.rs:857) mapping class_name -> res path + base, populated at boot by scanning project .gd files for a top-level class_name (patina-runner bootstrap before scripts_to_load, and the editor project open); identifier resolution for unknown names consults it and lazily run_class-loads the file; `.new()` routes to the existing instantiate_script_with_values (gdscene/src/scripting.rs:850); implement ProjectSettings.get_global_class_list. Depends on the inheritance bead for `extends ClassName`.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs`

**Prove it:** A project with utils.gd (`class_name Utils`, `static func double(x): return x * 2`, `const MAX = 5`) and enemy.gd (`class_name Enemy extends Node`), and a scene script that prints `Utils.double(4)`, `Utils.MAX`, and `Enemy.new() is Enemy`, prints `8 5 true` when run through the runner; ProjectSettings.get_global_class_list() lists both. (test: `gdscript_global_class_name_registry`)

**Verifier note:** I grepped global_script_class|class_name_index|GLOBAL_SCRIPT_CLASSES|script_class_cache|get_global_class_list|global_class|ClassNameRegistry|class_name_registry over gdscript-interop, gdscene, patina-runner, gdresource, gdcore, gdobject and gdeditor src. The only hits are unrelated EditorPlugin virtual names at class_db.rs:25721/25726. class_registry is per-Interpreter (interpreter.rs:594, init empty at :908, insert only at :16007). The ClassName.new() path (interpreter.rs:4490-4560) consults only native ClassDB, via is_node_class_name, create_node and the RefCounted resource path. P1 is fine.
acceptance_criteria: A project with utils.gd (`class_name Utils`, `static func double(x): return x * 2`, `const MAX = 5`) and enemy.gd (`class_name Enemy extends Node`), and a scene script that prints `Utils.double(4)`, `Utils.MAX`, and `Enemy.new() is Enemy`, prints `8 5 true` when run through the runner; ProjectSettings.get_global_class_list() lists both. (test: `gdscript_global_class_name_registry`)

title: Variant: String==StringName equality and Godot StringLike key comparison for Dictionary/Array (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: core-variant/variant-stringname] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** scene load (.tscn &"x" -> StringName) -> script property read -> `==` / dict lookup in GDScript; StringName values from .tscn (loader.rs:674) and &"" literals flow into script method calls via Expr::Call -> call_method_on

### 1. String/StringName equality and Dictionary/Array key comparator (StringLikeVariantComparator)  (PARTIAL, P0)

**Godot ground truth:** core/variant/variant_op.cpp:196-201 register_string_op(OperatorEvaluatorEqual) for String<->StringName; core/variant/variant.cpp:3396 StringLikeVariantComparator::compare; dictionary.cpp:50 HashMap<..., StringLikeVariantComparator>; array.cpp:383 find uses the same comparator; variant.cpp:3172 hash_compare returns false on type mismatch (int vs float keys distinct)

**Patina today:** variant_eq (interpreter.rs:31735) unifies int/float then falls to derived PartialEq (gdvariant/src/variant.rs:278 #[derive(PartialEq)]), so Variant::String("walk") == Variant::StringName("walk") is false. The .tscn loader produces Variant::StringName for &"..." values (gdresource/src/loader.rs:674,684), so `$AnimatedSprite2D.animation == "walk"` on a scene-loaded value is false. Dictionary key_eq (gdvariant/src/dictionary.rs:48-55) unifies Int/Float (Godot keeps them distinct) and keeps String/StringName distinct (Godot unifies). Array find/has use variant_eq (interpreter.rs:11326) so `[1].has(1.0)` is true (Godot false) and `["a"].has(&"a")` false (Godot true).

**Implement:** Godot: `==`/`!=` are registered for String<->StringName both ways (variant_op.cpp:196-201,493,615), so `&"a" == "a"` is true. Dictionary keys and Array.find/has/count/erase use StringLikeVariantComparator (variant.cpp:3396): hash_compare (exact type match, so int 1 and float 1.0 are DIFFERENT keys) plus String/StringName cross-equality.
Patina: variant_eq (interpreter.rs:31735) does int/float promotion then derived PartialEq, so String vs StringName is false; this breaks every comparison against a .tscn-loaded `&"name"` value (loader.rs:674). gdvariant Dictionary key_eq (dictionary.rs:48) inverts both rules; Array find/has/rfind/count/erase in the Array arm (interpreter.rs:11322+) use variant_eq.
Implementation: add `gdvariant::string_like_eq(a,b)` implementing hash_compare + String/StringName cross case, use it in Dictionary key_eq (and hashing in hash.rs must hash String and StringName identically, which hash.rs:194 already does) and in Array find/has/count/erase/rfind and BinOp::In; keep int/float promotion only for the `==` operator, and add String<->StringName arms to variant_eq.
Wiring: scene load (.tscn &"x" -> StringName) -> script property read -> `==` / dict lookup in GDScript.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/dictionary.rs`

**Prove it:** Loading a .tscn whose AnimatedSprite2D has `animation = &"walk"`, an attached script's _ready evaluates `animation == "walk"` (true), `{"a": 1}.has(&"a")` (true), `{1: "x"}.has(1.0)` (false), `[1].has(1.0)` (false), `["a"].has(&"a")` (true); the test asserts these via script-set properties read from the SceneTree. (test: `variant_string_like_equality_test`)

**Verifier note:** variant_eq (interpreter.rs:31735-31754) unifies only Int/Float then falls to derived PartialEq (gdvariant/src/variant.rs:278 #[derive(PartialEq)]), so String vs StringName is false. gdvariant/src/dictionary.rs:48-57 key_eq unifies Int/Float and leaves String/StringName distinct, the inverse of Godot (dictionary.cpp:50 uses StringLikeVariantComparator; variant.cpp:3172-3175 hash_compare returns false on type mismatch; array.cpp:383/437/489 find/count use the same comparator). Parser &"x" -> StringName (parser.rs:1821) and loader.rs:674,684 produce StringName, so comparisons against them silently fail. Priority 0 is fair because the answer is silently wrong.

### 2. StringName method surface and operators  (MISSING, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api builtin_classes StringName: 110 methods, 58 operators (String API mirrored); variant_op.cpp:208 StringName % format, :737 StringName ordering

**Patina today:** call_method_on's top-level match (interpreter.rs:11135-14487) has arms for Signal, Array, String (:11729), Dictionary, vectors, Rid, math types, ObjectId, NodePath, Callable, Resource, packed; there is NO Variant::StringName arm, so any method on a StringName falls to `_ => Err("cannot call method on StringName")` at :14483. grep -n 'Variant::StringName(' interpreter.rs shows no method-dispatch site (only argument coercions). binary_add/binary_mod/binary_cmp have no StringName arms (String+StringName, StringName+String, StringName % args, StringName < StringName missing). StringName values reach scripts from &"..." literals (parser.rs:1821), .tscn loads (loader.rs:674) and get_typed_class_name (interpreter.rs:11403).

**Implement:** Godot: StringName exposes the String method set (110 methods in extension_api) and the full register_string_op/register_string_modulo_op rows (variant_op.cpp:196-208): +, ==, !=, <, <=, >, >=, %, in. Methods return String (not StringName) per the API return types.
Patina: no Variant::StringName arm in call_method_on (interpreter.rs:11135..14487), so `&"idle".length()`, `anim.begins_with("run")` on a scene-loaded StringName error; binary ops have no StringName rows.
Implementation: in call_method_on, add `Variant::StringName(sn)` that re-dispatches to the String arm with `Variant::String(sn.as_str().into())` (for the API methods StringName shares), and in binary_add/binary_mod/binary_cmp coerce StringName operands to String for the string rows. Keep `hash` returning the same value as for String.
Wiring: StringName values from .tscn (loader.rs:674) and &"" literals flow into script method calls via Expr::Call -> call_method_on.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene script calls `(&"idle_left").begins_with("idle")`, `(&"abc").length()`, `(&"a") + "b"`, `"%s!" % &"hi"`, `&"a" < &"b"`, and `$Sprite.animation.to_upper()` on a .tscn-loaded `&"walk"`; test asserts Godot's results through the SceneTree. (test: `stringname_methods_operators_test`)

**Verifier note:** call_method_on (interpreter.rs:10773) top-level match ends with `_ => cannot call method on` at :14483. awk over lines 10773-14487 for 'StringName' finds only argument coercions (e.g. :12611 connect signal arg) and return constructors (:11403, :12184), with no `Variant::StringName(..) =>` receiver arm. Callers at :3700/:4589 pass obj straight through with no StringName->String normalization. binary_add/mod/cmp (:5294,:5422,:5505) have no StringName arms. MISSING fits: the whole receiver surface is absent.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Loading a .tscn whose AnimatedSprite2D has `animation = &"walk"`, an attached script's _ready evaluates `animation == "walk"` (true), `{"a": 1}.has(&"a")` (true), `{1: "x"}.has(1.0)` (false), `[1].has(1.0)` (false), `["a"].has(&"a")` (true); the test asserts these via script-set properties read from the SceneTree. (test: `variant_string_like_equality_test`) 2) A scene script calls `(&"idle_left").begins_with("idle")`, `(&"abc").length()`, `(&"a") + "b"`, `"%s!" % &"hi"`, `&"a" < &"b"`, and `$Sprite.animation.to_upper()` on a .tscn-loaded `&"walk"`; test asserts Godot's results through the SceneTree. (test: `stringname_methods_operators_test`)

title: GDScript: parse all annotation placements and constant-expression annotation args (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: gdscript/gdscript-annotations] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** scene-attached scripts using these annotations must load and run; the editor inspector reads these through ScriptInstance::list_properties (gdscene/src/scripting.rs:322) and the get_property_list path (interpreter.rs:12955) — both must show the new entries

### 1. Annotations: standalone/script-level annotations (@icon, @abstract, @static_unload, @warning_ignore[_start/_restore], trailing @export_group/category) and expression arguments (negative numbers, constants)  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/gdscript/doc_classes/@GDScript.xml (annotation list); gdscript_parser.cpp parse_annotation (arguments are constant expressions; annotations may precede class_name/extends/signal/any statement)

**Patina today:** parser.rs:590-662 parse_annotated_stmt: after the annotation list only var/func/static are accepted; any other following token is an error unless one annotation is `tool` (:645). So `@icon("res://i.svg")\nclass_name Foo`, `@abstract class_name Base`, `@static_unload`, `@warning_ignore("unused_signal")\nsignal s`, and `@warning_ignore("return_value_discarded")\nfoo()` inside a body all fail to parse. Argument capture :611-630 takes ONE token per argument, so `@export_range(-10, 10)` captures "-" then leaves `10)` unconsumed -> parse error at the next token; `@export_range(0, PI * 2)` likewise. Greps for '"icon"', '"abstract"', '"warning_ignore', '"static_unload"' in interpreter.rs/parser.rs: 0 handling hits.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth (@GDScript.xml, gdscript_parser.cpp): annotations may precede class_name/extends (@icon, @abstract, @tool, @static_unload), signals, functions, vars, inner classes, and arbitrary statements (@warning_ignore); @warning_ignore_start/@warning_ignore_restore are standalone; @export_group/@export_subgroup/@export_category are standalone and may be last in a class; annotation arguments are constant expressions (negative numbers, PI*2, named constants, string concatenation).

Patina: parser.rs:635-661 rejects anything but var/func/static after annotations (except @tool); :611-630 captures one token per arg.

Implement: parse args with parse_expr and constant-fold them at run_class time (store both Expr and folded string for hint_string); allow annotations before class_name/extends/signal/class/enum/statement, attaching them to the next stmt or emitting Stmt::AnnotationStmt for standalone ones; record @abstract (class and func: instantiating an abstract class / calling an abstract method errors, per Script.is_abstract), @icon path on ClassDef, and treat @warning_ignore* as accepted no-ops for the warning system. Wiring: scene-attached scripts using these annotations must load and run.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/parser.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene-attached script beginning `@icon("res://icon.svg")\n@abstract\nclass_name Shape extends Node` is rejected for instantiation with an error, while a concrete subclass script with `@export_range(-10, 10, 0.5) var t := 0.0`, `@warning_ignore("unused_signal")\nsignal s`, and `@warning_ignore_start("unused_variable")` parses, runs _ready, and reports hint_string "-10,10,0.5" for t through get_property_list(). (test: `gdscript_annotation_placements`)

**Verifier note:** parse_annotated_stmt (parser.rs:590-662) accepts only Var, Func or Static after the annotations. Anything else errors unless one annotation is `tool` (:645-647). That covers @icon followed by class_name, @warning_ignore followed by signal or a statement, and a trailing standalone @export_group. Argument capture (:611-630) takes one token and then breaks if no comma follows. So `@export_range(-10, 10)` captures "-", leaves IntLit(10) unconsumed, skips the RParen check, and errors when the next token is matched (:634). @export_group directly before a var does work, so PARTIAL with P1 is right.

### 2. @export hint family: exp_easing, flags_2d/3d_render/physics/navigation, flags_avoidance, storage, custom, tool_button, file_path, global_dir hint, group/subgroup/category property-list entries, type-derived hints (enum/Resource/typed Array)  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/gdscript/gdscript_parser.cpp export_annotations<> table (PROPERTY_HINT_EXP_EASING=4, LAYERS_2D_RENDER=7.., LAYERS_AVOIDANCE, PROPERTY_USAGE_STORAGE, TOOL_BUTTON); groups emit PROPERTY_USAGE_GROUP/SUBGROUP/CATEGORY entries; `@export var s: MyEnum` -> PROPERTY_HINT_ENUM, `: Texture2D` -> PROPERTY_HINT_RESOURCE_TYPE, `: Array[int]` -> PROPERTY_HINT_TYPE_STRING

**Patina today:** export_hint_from_annotation interpreter.rs:775-791 maps only export, export_range, export_enum, export_flags, export_file/global_file, export_dir/global_dir (same hint 14; Godot uses GLOBAL_DIR=15/GLOBAL_FILE=16), export_multiline, export_placeholder, export_color_no_alpha, export_node_path; every other export_* returns None, so e.g. `@export_flags_2d_physics var mask` and `@export_storage var x` are NOT exported at all (run_class only pushes ExportInfo when find_map returns Some, interpreter.rs:15919-15928). export_group/subgroup/category: 0 string hits in gdscript-interop/src; group annotations are merged into the following var's annotation list and dropped. `@export` with an enum/Resource/typed-array type hint always yields PROPERTY_HINT_NONE (:778).

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: gdscript_parser.cpp registers every @export_* variant with its PROPERTY_HINT/USAGE; export_group/subgroup/category insert PROPERTY_USAGE_GROUP/SUBGROUP/CATEGORY entries (with prefix) into the script property list; plain @export derives hints from the declared type (enum -> ENUM with "A:0,B:1", Resource subclass -> RESOURCE_TYPE, Node subclass -> NODE_TYPE, Array[T] -> TYPE_STRING).

Patina: interpreter.rs:775-791 covers 11 of 31 export annotations, global_dir/global_file share non-global hints, groups vanish, and unmapped exports are silently not exported (:15919-15928).

Implement: extend export_hint_from_annotation with the full table (incl. PROPERTY_HINT_EXP_EASING, LAYERS_*, ARRAY_TYPE/TYPE_STRING, TOOL_BUTTON, export_storage usage-only, export_custom(hint, hint_string, usage)); carry PROPERTY_USAGE in ExportInfo; emit group/subgroup/category pseudo-entries in declaration order; derive hints from enum/class type hints using ClassDef.enums and gdobject::class_db. Wiring: the editor inspector reads these through ScriptInstance::list_properties (gdscene/src/scripting.rs:322) and the get_property_list path (interpreter.rs:12955) — both must show the new entries.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene-attached script with `@export_group("Stats")`, `@export_flags_2d_physics var mask`, `@export_exp_easing var e := 1.0`, `@export_storage var hidden := 1`, `@export var mode: Mode` (enum), `@export var tex: Texture2D`, `@export_tool_button("Bake") var bake = bake_fn` returns, via get_property_list() at runtime, a GROUP entry "Stats" followed by entries with hints 9 (LAYERS_2D_PHYSICS), 4, ENUM "A:0,B:1", RESOURCE_TYPE "Texture2D", and TOOL_BUTTON, and `hidden` with STORAGE-only usage. (test: `gdscript_export_hint_table`)

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. interpreter.rs:775-791 match has only export, export_range, export_enum, export_flags, export_file|export_global_file, export_dir|export_global_dir (both map to PROPERTY_HINT_DIR=14), export_multiline, export_placeholder, export_color_no_alpha, export_node_path; `_ => return None`. interpreter.rs:15919-15928 pushes ExportInfo only when find_map returns Some, so unmapped @export_* vars are not exported at all. grep -rn 'export_group|export_subgroup|export_category|export_storage|export_flags_2d|export_exp_easing|export_tool_button|export_custom' over gdscript-interop/src and gdscene/src: 0 hits. The only PROPERTY_HINT_RESOURCE_TYPE / PROPERTY_USAGE_GROUP hits are the constant tables in global_constants.rs:445,479. It is worse than the finding says: ScriptInstance::list_properties (gdscene/src/scripting.rs:322-333) hardcodes hint: 0 and hint_string empty for every property, so even the hints that are mapped never reach that path. PARTIAL at P1 is right.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A scene-attached script beginning `@icon("res://icon.svg")
@abstract
class_name Shape extends Node` is rejected for instantiation with an error, while a concrete subclass script with `@export_range(-10, 10, 0.5) var t := 0.0`, `@warning_ignore("unused_signal")
signal s`, and `@warning_ignore_start("unused_variable")` parses, runs _ready, and reports hint_string "-10,10,0.5" for t through get_property_list(). (test: `gdscript_annotation_placements`) 2) A scene-attached script with `@export_group("Stats")`, `@export_flags_2d_physics var mask`, `@export_exp_easing var e := 1.0`, `@export_storage var hidden := 1`, `@export var mode: Mode` (enum), `@export var tex: Texture2D`, `@export_tool_button("Bake") var bake = bake_fn` returns, via get_property_list() at runtime, a GROUP entry "Stats" followed by entries with hints 9 (LAYERS_2D_PHYSICS), 4, ENUM "A:0,B:1", RESOURCE_TYPE "Texture2D", and TOOL_BUTTON, and `hidden` with STORAGE-only usage. (test: `gdscript_export_hint_table`)

title: GDScript: class-shared static vars and _static_init
description:
[audit-key: gdscript/gdscript-static] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** two scene nodes with the same script loaded by the runner share the value

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp (static_variables live on the GDScript, shared by all instances; _static_init runs once on script load); tests at upstream/godot/modules/gdscript/tests/scripts/runtime/features/static_variables.gd

**Patina today:** interpreter.rs:15852-15856 comment: `static var` is stored like an ordinary instance var (`is_static: _`), 'full class-shared-across-instances semantics is a follow-up'. grep 'static_init|_static_init' over gdscript-interop/src and gdscene/src: 0 hits. Combined with per-node Interpreters (scripting.rs:178), two nodes with the same script do not share a static counter.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: `static var` storage belongs to the script (shared across all instances and accessible as ClassName.var); `static func _static_init()` runs once when the script is first loaded, before any instance; @static_unload controls release.

Patina: static vars are per-instance copies (interpreter.rs:15852-15856); _static_init is never called.

Implement: a process-wide static store keyed by (script path or class name, var name), initialized once by evaluating static defaults and then calling _static_init; reads/writes of static vars from any instance or via ClassName.var route to it. Wiring: two scene nodes with the same script loaded by the runner share the value.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene with two nodes sharing a script (`static var count := 0`, `static func _static_init(): print("init")`, `func _ready(): count += 1; print(count)`) prints `init` once and then `1` and `2` when run. (test: `gdscript_static_var_shared`)

**Verifier note:** interpreter.rs:15853-15856 binds `is_static: _` with the comment that class-shared semantics is a follow-up. grep -rn 'static_init|_static_init' over gdscript-interop/src and gdscene/src: 0 hits. grep 'static_vars|static_store|STATIC_VARS' in interpreter.rs: 0 hits. is_static is parsed (parser.rs:719/768) but the interpreter drops it. Status PARTIAL and P1 stand: static counters are common in real projects.
acceptance_criteria: A scene with two nodes sharing a script (`static var count := 0`, `static func _static_init(): print("init")`, `func _ready(): count += 1; print(count)`) prints `init` once and then `1` and `2` when run. (test: `gdscript_static_var_shared`)

Patina: no harness consumes them.

Implement: an integration test in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/tests that, for each runtime/features/*.gd, runs it through Interpreter::run_class + instantiate_class + call `test`, captures print output, and diffs against the .out (normalizing the GDTEST header). Maintain an explicit allowlist file of currently-passing scripts that must stay green and a ratchet count; failures outside the allowlist are reported but do not fail until promoted. This is implementation work that makes every other gdscript bead measurable.

**Verifier note:** grep -rln -e 'GDTEST_OK' -e 'gdscript/tests/scripts' over engine-rs and tools (excluding target): 0 hits. No harness consumes the upstream .gd/.out corpus. MISSING is correct. As a task that makes the other gdscript beads measurable, P1 is reasonable.

description:

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. Use it in line_edit::handle_key instead of char_for_key. Route Ctrl+C/X/V to the DisplayServer clipboard backend. Add an undo stack on the node state. Implement TextEdit line/column caret (caret_line) with Up/Down/PageUp/PageDown. Emit the missing signals. Map handling onto InputMap ui_text_* actions rather than raw keys.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/line_edit.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/browser_input.rs`

**Verifier note:** Confirmed. gdplatform/src/input.rs:612-618: InputEvent::Key has only key/pressed/shift/ctrl/alt, and no other variant carries text (the variants listed at :612-723 have no Text/Unicode one). gdscene/src/line_edit.rs:348-363: the ctrl arm handles only A, X (deletes the selection, no clipboard) and C (swallowed, comment at :354 says 'no clipboard'). At :386-397 and :419-421, multi-line Up/Down falls through unhandled. grep '"caret_changed"|"text_change_rejected"|"editing_toggled"|"lines_edited_from"' in gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src (excluding class_db): 0 emit sites.

### 2. CodeEdit (completion, gutters for breakpoints/bookmarks/executing, folding + regions, auto-indent, brace matching, symbol lookup)  (MISSING, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** scene/gui/code_edit.cpp; doc/classes/CodeEdit.xml

**Implement:** Godot CodeEdit adds code completion (code_completion_requested, add_code_completion_option, update_code_completion_options, confirm), breakpoint/bookmark/executing gutters (breakpoint_toggled), line and region folding, auto-indent on Enter, auto brace completion, delimiters/string/comment awareness, symbol lookup (symbol_lookup/symbol_validate). Patina treats CodeEdit as a plain TextEdit. Build on the TextEdit line model from the text-editing bead: add a gutter strip + click handling, a fold model, an auto-indent rule in line_edit::handle_key for CodeEdit, a completion popup that reuses the PopupMenu modal stage, and the script method arms.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/line_edit.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`

**Prove it:** Through push_input on a focused CodeEdit: clicking the breakpoint gutter on line 2 emits breakpoint_toggled(2) and is_line_breakpointed(2)==true; Enter after 'func f():' auto-indents the next line by one tab; a script handling code_completion_requested that adds 'print' shows a popup, and Enter inserts it. (test: `code_edit_gutter_indent_completion_e2e`)

title: Editor: back the Node-dock signal connect/disconnect with real SceneTree connections
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-signals] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: STUB]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/scene/connections_dialog.cpp (ConnectDialog + ConnectionsDock); undo via EditorUndoRedoManager; persisted as [connection] by PackedScene

**Patina today:** editor_server.rs:13459 api_connect_signal ignores target_id (`let _target_raw` :13482), deferred, one_shot and binds, and only appends "sig:method" to a node property `signal_connections` (:13500-13530). It never calls SceneTree::connect_signal. scene_saver.rs:2009-2063 writes [connection] only from the tree's signal store, and is_internal_prop (scene_saver.rs:1610) does not filter `signal_connections`. So a connection made in the editor is saved as a stray `signal_connections = "..."` property, never as a [connection], and never fires in Play. The Node dock list (editor_server.rs:13402) reads only that property, so connections already loaded from a .tscn do not show. The list of available signals is a hard-coded table, signals_for_class at :13354. Disconnect (:22160-22168) splits on ';' while connect joins with ',', and it matches with `contains(&signal)`, so disconnecting one signal deletes every connection on the node. It is also not undoable. 'Go to Method' in the client is a toast (editor_ui.rs:13942) even though the route /api/signal/goto_method (:2795) exists; /api/signal/autocreate_receiver (:2796) has no client caller either.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: ConnectDialog (editor/scene/connections_dialog.cpp) creates a real Object::connect with target node, method, CONNECT_DEFERRED/ONE_SHOT flags, binds and unbinds, through EditorUndoRedoManager. The connection is saved as a [connection] section, and ConnectionsDock lists every existing connection, including ones loaded from the .tscn, plus every ClassDB and script signal of the node.

Patina today: api_connect_signal (editor_server.rs:13459) writes a string property `signal_connections` and drops target_id, flags and binds. TscnSaver writes [connection] only from the signal store (scene_saver.rs:2009-2063), so editor-made connections are lost, and the property leaks into the .tscn because is_internal_prop (:1610) does not skip it. Listing (:13402) ignores real connections and uses the hard-coded signals_for_class (:13354). Disconnect (:22160) uses the wrong separator and substring matching. The 'Go to Method' menu item is a toast (editor_ui.rs:13942).

Implementation:
(1) Replace the property model. Connect should call the SceneTree signal store (the one scene_saver reads) with the target from target_id, method, flags and binds, as an undoable EditorCommand (add ConnectSignal/DisconnectSignal variants that touch the store).
(2) Build the Node dock list from the store, and build the signals from ClassDB inheritance (gdobject class_db) plus script `signal` declarations.
(3) Make disconnect exact on (signal, target, method).
(4) Wire 'Go to Method' to POST /api/signal/goto_method and open the script at the returned line. Wire the dialog's method creation to /api/signal/autocreate_receiver when the method does not exist.
(5) Delete the `signal_connections` property path, and migrate it on load if present.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_saver.rs`

**Prove it:** In the served editor, connecting Button.pressed to a parent script method with Deferred checked and saving produces a `[connection signal="pressed" from="Button" to="." method="_on_pressed" flags=1]` line and no `signal_connections` property. Pressing Play and clicking the button runs the method. Reopening the scene lists the connection in the Node dock. Disconnecting one of two connections leaves the other. Undo restores it. (test: `editor_signal_connect_persists_and_fires_in_play`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. api_connect_signal (editor_server.rs:13459) binds `_target_raw` at :13482 and never reads it. It writes `signal:method` joined by ',' into the `signal_connections` property through EditorCommand::SetProperty (:13500-13530). The comment there says outright that it avoids SceneTree::connect_signal. Connect is undoable through SetProperty, but disconnect is not. Disconnect (:22160-22168) splits on ';', filters with `!entry.contains(&signal)`, and calls set_property directly with no undo push. I grepped `signal_connections` across crates/*.rs. The only runtime readers are the editor server's own (:3583, :13403). scripting.rs:5725, bindings.rs:467 and interpreter.rs:11220 are a separate trait method of the same name that reads the real signal store, not the property. So nothing turns the property into a live connection at Play. is_internal_prop (scene_saver.rs:1610) has no `signal_connections` case. The editor_ui.rs:4076 hit only labels the property 'Internal' in the inspector, and the saver still writes it out. signals_for_class (:13354) is a hard-coded match, used at :13400. 'Go to Method' at editor_ui.rs:13942 only shows a toast, and grep `goto_method|autocreate_receiver` in editor_ui.rs finds no fetch. Priority 0 is right: a connection made in the editor never fires and is not saved as a [connection].
acceptance_criteria: In the served editor, connecting Button.pressed to a parent script method with Deferred checked and saving produces a `[connection signal="pressed" from="Button" to="." method="_on_pressed" flags=1]` line and no `signal_connections` property. Pressing Play and clicking the button runs the method. Reopening the scene lists the connection in the Node dock. Disconnecting one of two connections leaves the other. Undo restores it. (test: `editor_signal_connect_persists_and_fires_in_play`)

comments.text:
DIAGNOSIS (BlackWaterfall) — one gap left, root-caused, and the fix is blocked
only on a file lease. Everything else in this bead is already done.

WHY IT KEEPS FAILING
The acceptance test `editor_signal_connect_persists_and_fires_in_play` gets all
the way to the Play click and then reads `hits == 0`. Latest verify:
`4 tests run: 3 passed, 1 failed` — only the Play-firing assertion fails.

ROOT CAUSE
`clone_scene_tree` (editor_server.rs:1347) copies name, class_name, properties,
groups and children — but NOT `signal_stores`. `build_play_tree` clones through
it, so every signal connection made in the editor is DROPPED the moment Play
starts. That is precisely this bead's P0 claim, and it is the last unfixed piece.

THE REST OF THE CHAIN IS INTACT (checked, so the clone fix is SUFFICIENT, not
just necessary):
- the store write works: the test's earlier assertions pass, and both the saved
  `[connection]` line and `/api/node/signals` read the editor tree's store;
- `click_at_point` emits the signal: `tree.emit_signal(hit, "pressed", &[])`
  (control.rs:1191), reached via `node_is_base_button`;
- `emit_signal` dispatches a callback-less store connection to the target's
  script: it resolves `NodeId::from_object_id(target_id)` and, for a DEFERRED
  connection (this test ticks Deferred, flags=1), queues `call_deferred`, which
  drains on the following step — and the test does step after mouse_up.

THE FIX (~25 lines, must live in `clone_scene_tree`)
It needs the source->dest NodeId map, which only that function has: the clone
allocates fresh ids via `add_child`, while `Connection.target_id` is an
`ObjectId` pointing at the EDITOR tree. So it cannot move to gdscene without
passing the map out.
- `copy_subtree` also records `src_id.raw() -> new_id`;
- after the copy, walk `source.signal_stores()`, remap each
  `conn.target_id.raw()` through that map, and `connect_signal` on the dest;
- `Connection` is NOT Clone (it can hold a closure), so rebuild each with
  `Connection::new(dest_target.object_id(), conn.method.clone())` and copy the
  public `deferred` / `one_shot` / `binds` / `unbinds` fields;
- skip a connection whose target is outside the copied subtree (the root
  `Window` is not copied) — worth a comment so it does not read as a bug.

BLOCKED ON
`RusticElk` holds an exclusive lease on editor_server.rs to 09:03Z. Asked them
(msg 90353) whether they are touching `clone_scene_tree`, offering to apply it
myself on release, to make exactly that one insertion if they are not in it, or
to let them apply it. I did not edit under their lease.

ALREADY LANDED BY ME THIS PASS
- `/api/signal/autocreate_receiver` had a route, a handler and a unit test and NO
  client caller at all — the Connect dialog connected signals to methods nobody
  had written. Wired into the dialog's confirm handler, after the connect POST
  (the receiver's script path comes from the connection's `target_script`, which
  only exists once the connection does).
- New test `connect_dialog_requests_a_receiver_stub` — PASSES. It keys on the
  call syntax `'/api/signal/autocreate_receiver', {` because both obvious
  needles are false positives: the route path also matches my own comment, and
  `path: conn.target_script` already appears earlier in the pre-existing
  "Go to Method" call, so that assertion would stay green with the wiring
  deleted.

STALE BEAD BODY — parts (1),(2),(3),(4a),(5) are all already implemented in the
tree (ConnectSignal/DisconnectSignal EditorCommands, ClassDB-driven signal list,
is_internal_prop filtering, a real goto_method POST). Only the Play-firing gap
above remains. Worth editing the body if this bounces again.

VERIFY

title: SpinBox: arrow clicks, wheel steps and typed values through push_input (+1 related)
description:

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

### 1. SpinBox interaction (arrow buttons, wheel, typing via inner LineEdit, prefix/suffix, custom_arrow_step, update_on_text_changed)  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** scene/gui/spin_box.cpp gui_input (up/down arrow press + hold repeat, wheel, drag), _text_submitted, get_line_edit

**Patina today:** SpinBox is drawn (5 refs in control_render.rs) and hit-testable (control.rs:965) but slider_axis returns None for it (range_controls.rs:31-37), so wheel_delta (:340) and drag ignore it. line_edit TEXT_INPUT_CLASSES (:51) excludes it, so it cannot be typed into. 0 references to "SpinBox" in scene_tree.rs. grep '"custom_arrow_step"|"update_on_text_changed"|"get_line_edit"' in gdscene/src: 0.

**Implement:** Godot SpinBox steps value by step (or custom_arrow_step) on an up/down arrow press with hold-to-repeat, steps on the wheel, and parses the inner LineEdit text (with prefix/suffix stripped, expressions evaluated) on submit or focus loss (update_on_text_changed for live). get_line_edit() returns the child. Patina draws a SpinBox but it is inert. Implementation: in gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs gui_input_stage, add a SpinBox branch: hit-test the arrow half (same geometry as its control_render arm), call set_range_value and emit value_changed. Extend range_controls::wheel_delta to SpinBox. Make line_edit treat a focused SpinBox as a text input over its numeric text, parse on Enter, and add get_line_edit/apply script arms.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/range_controls.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/line_edit.rs`

**Prove it:** A SpinBox(min 0, max 10, step 1, value 5) gets value 6 + value_changed(6) from a push_input click on its up arrow, 5 from a wheel-down notch, and 8 from typing '8' + Enter while focused. (test: `spinbox_arrows_wheel_typing_e2e`)

**Verifier note:** Confirmed. range_controls.rs:31-37: slider_axis covers only H/VSlider and H/VScrollBar. wheel_delta (:340-342) uses `slider_axis(&class)?`, so it returns None for SpinBox. line_edit.rs:51: TEXT_INPUT_CLASSES = LineEdit/TextEdit/CodeEdit only. SpinBox does appear in RANGE_CLASSES (range_controls.rs:400), so the script set_value/get_value methods work, and it is in FOCUSABLE_BY_DEFAULT (control.rs:3864) and the hit list (control.rs:974). grep 'SpinBox' in scene_tree.rs: 0. grep '"custom_arrow_step"|"update_on_text_changed"|"get_line_edit"' in gdscene/src: 0. A rendered SpinBox therefore has no interaction.

### 2. Range semantics: allow_greater/allow_lesser, exp_edit, rounded, share()  (PARTIAL, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** scene/gui/range.cpp set_value/_calc_ratio (exp_edit), share/unshare

**Patina today:** set_range_value (control.rs:4156-4174) always clamps to [min, max-page] and snaps to step. grep '"allow_greater"|"allow_lesser"|"exp_edit"|"rounded"' in gdscene/src: 0 files each. No share/unshare arm.

**Implement:** Godot Range::set_value skips the max clamp when allow_greater and the min clamp when allow_lesser. `rounded` rounds to an integer. exp_edit makes get_as_ratio/set_as_ratio logarithmic (used by slider drag and ProgressBar fill). share(other) links two Ranges' values. Patina's set_range_value (control.rs:4156) ignores all four. Implement them in control::set_range_value/get_range_ratio and range_controls::drag_slider_to_local, and add share/unshare to range_controls::call_range_method with a shared-value group kept on node properties.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/range_controls.rs`

**Prove it:** An HSlider(min 1, max 1000, exp_edit=true) dragged to its midpoint via push_input reports a value near 31.6 (geometric mean). A SpinBox with allow_greater accepts set_value(20) above max 10. Two shared ranges follow each other. (test: `range_exp_edit_allow_greater_share`)

**Verifier note:** Confirmed. control.rs:4155-4172: set_range_value always snaps to step and clamps to [min, max-page], with no flag checks. grep 'allow_greater|allow_lesser|exp_edit|"rounded"|"share"|"unshare"' in gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src (excluding inspector_schema): 0 hits. P2 is reasonable.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A SpinBox(min 0, max 10, step 1, value 5) gets value 6 + value_changed(6) from a push_input click on its up arrow, 5 from a wheel-down notch, and 8 from typing '8' + Enter while focused. (test: `spinbox_arrows_wheel_typing_e2e`) 2) An HSlider(min 1, max 1000, exp_edit=true) dragged to its midpoint via push_input reports a value near 31.6 (geometric mean). A SpinBox with allow_greater accepts set_value(20) above max 10. Two shared ranges follow each other. (test: `range_exp_edit_allow_greater_share`)

title: Input: route Input.get_vector through analog raw strengths with circular deadzone
description:
[audit-key: input/input-singleton-analog] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** core/input/input.cpp:548 Input::get_vector (raw strengths, optional p_deadzone, circular deadzone)

**Patina today:** interpreter.rs:9365-9385 requires exactly 4 args and calls access.get_input_vector. Only implementation is the SceneAccess DEFAULT bindings.rs:1579 (digital: is_input_action_pressed then normalize). gdscene/src/scripting.rs has no override (grep 'fn get_input_vector' across crates: only bindings.rs). gdplatform InputState::get_vector (input.rs:1983) and InputSnapshot::get_vector (:2463) are called only by tests (input.rs:4078-4308). InputState::get_vector also uses deadzone-remapped get_action_strength where Godot uses get_action_raw_strength, so the deadzone is applied twice.

**Implement:** Godot get_vector(nx,px,ny,py,deadzone=-1) builds the vector from get_action_raw_strength, takes the deadzone from the arg or the average of the four action deadzones, then applies a circular deadzone and clamps to the unit length (core/input/input.cpp:548-572). Patina: the script call (interpreter.rs:9365) rejects the 5th arg. It reaches only the digital default in bindings.rs:1579, which normalizes any pressed direction to length 1, so a half-tilted stick reads full speed. The tested InputState::get_vector (input.rs:1983) is dead. Fix: accept an optional deadzone argument. Add get_input_vector(..., deadzone) to the gdscene SceneAccess override in scripting.rs, using the snapshot's raw strengths (action_strengths pair) and per-action deadzones from the InputMap mirror. Change InputState/InputSnapshot::get_vector to use raw strength, matching Godot.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene script calls Input.get_vector('l','r','u','d') on each frame of MainLoop.step. The actions are bound to left-stick axes with deadzone 0.2. A gamepad axis event of 0.6 on X gives length ~0.5 ((0.6-0.2)/0.8), not 1.0. A 0.1 deflection gives ZERO. The 5-arg form is accepted. Test: (test: `input_get_vector_analog_test`).

**Verifier note:** The gap is real. `grep -rn 'fn get_input_vector'` over gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src finds only the default at bindings.rs:1579. That default is digital: is_input_action_pressed, then normalize. scripting.rs has no override. interpreter.rs:9365-9381 forwards exactly 4 strings. UNWIRED is accepted: the analog InputState::get_vector exists but has no runtime caller. I lowered priority to 1. Keyboard and d-pad get_vector already gives the correct normalized result, so only analog magnitude and the 5-arg deadzone form are wrong. That is a common-feature gap, not broken core.
acceptance_criteria: A scene script calls Input.get_vector('l','r','u','d') on each frame of MainLoop.step. The actions are bound to left-stick axes with deadzone 0.2. A gamepad axis event of 0.6 on X gives length ~0.5 ((0.6-0.2)/0.8), not 1.0. A 0.1 deflection gives ZERO. The 5-arg form is accepted. Test: (test: `input_get_vector_analog_test`).

title: Input: carry unicode/physical_keycode/key_label/echo/location/meta on key events end-to-end (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: input/input-event-fidelity] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

### 1. InputEventKey fidelity: unicode, key_label, physical_keycode, echo, location, meta, full Key enum  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** platform/web/display_server_web.cpp:180-210 (_key_callback sets echo=repeat, key_label, unicode, location); core/os/keyboard.h (193 Key values)

**Patina today:** InputEvent::Key carries only key/pressed/shift/ctrl/alt (gdplatform/src/input.rs:612-618). scene_tree.rs:8513-8526 hardcodes physical_keycode=key_label=keycode, unicode 0, location 0, echo false, meta false. The editor route ignores the code/location/repeat/meta that the JS sends (editor_ui.rs:12493-12500 vs editor_server.rs:17220-17271, which reads only key and shift/ctrl/alt), so a key repeat arrives as a fresh press with echo=false. The Key enum has ~81 variants vs Godot's 193 (jq .global_enums Key). No META, KP_*, F13+, NumLock, Pause, Print, or shifted symbols, so ui_accept lacks KP_ENTER (input_map.cpp:434 vs input.rs:1130). LineEdit types via a US-layout table (line_edit.rs:24-29, char_for_key :442), so non-ASCII text is impossible.

**Implement:** Godot web fills InputEventKey from the KeyboardEvent: keycode from the unshifted key, physical_keycode from code, key_label, unicode from key, echo from repeat, location, and meta (display_server_web.cpp:180-210). LineEdit inserts event.unicode. Patina's InputEvent::Key (input.rs:612) has none of these, so the payload hardcodes them (scene_tree.rs:8513). Fix: extend InputEvent::Key with physical: Key, label, unicode: u32, echo, location, meta. Grow the Key enum to Godot's full Key table (KP_*, META, F13-F35, NumLock, ScrollLock, Pause, Print, symbols), with to_godot_keycode/from_name/godot_keycode_to_key. Read code/repeat/location/meta in api_input_key_down/up (editor_server.rs:17220). Emit echo events instead of fresh presses: action state stays pressed, _input sees is_echo() true. Add KeyCombo.meta and command_or_control. Make LineEdit insert from unicode, falling back to char_for_key only when unicode is 0. Add KP_ENTER to ui_accept.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/line_edit.rs`

**Prove it:** Through POST /api/runtime/input/key_down with {key:'é', code:'Digit2', repeat:true, meta:true}, a running script's _input sees unicode==233, physical_keycode==KEY_2, echo==true, meta_pressed==true, and is_action_pressed(...) false for the echo. A focused LineEdit receives 'é'. Numpad Enter triggers ui_accept. Test: (test: `input_event_key_fidelity_test`).

**Verifier note:** InputEvent::Key has only key/pressed/shift/ctrl/alt (gdplatform/src/input.rs:612-618). scene_tree.rs:8525-8529 hardcodes physical_keycode=code, unicode 0 and echo false. input.rs:892 and :1094 note the missing Meta bit, and :1104 says KP_ENTER is dropped from ui_accept because Key lacks it. `grep KpEnter|Kp1|F13` in input.rs found no variants. Status and priority hold.

### 2. InputEventMouse fidelity (button_mask on motion, velocity, meta, wheel factor, double-click timing)  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** core/input/input.cpp (mouse_button_mask tracking, VelocityTrack for InputEventMouseMotion.velocity); InputEventMouseButton.factor; display_server_web.cpp double-click

**Patina today:** scene_tree.rs:8551-8565: MouseMotion button_mask always 0 (drag-paint code reading event.button_mask & MOUSE_BUTTON_MASK_LEFT never fires), velocity and screen_velocity always ZERO, global_position copied from position. MouseButton factor always 1.0 (:8536) although the browser wheel delta is available (editor_server.rs:17430). Mouse modifiers come from the last key event, not the mouse event (scene_tree.rs:5690-5698), and meta is always false (:8462). double_click uses a frame window DOUBLE_TAP_FRAMES (scene_tree.rs:5669-5682) instead of time and distance.

**Implement:** Godot InputEventMouseMotion carries the held button_mask and a velocity from Input's VelocityTrack. InputEventMouseButton wheel events carry factor (delta magnitude), and modifiers come from the mouse event itself. Patina hardcodes mask 0, velocity 0 and factor 1 (scene_tree.rs:8531-8565), and takes modifiers from the last key. Fix: carry the button mask from InputState (mouse_pressed set) into input_event_to_variant for motion and button events. Compute per-event velocity in InputState from timestamps (screen_velocity before the stretch inverse).
