title: Debugger: pause the GDScript interpreter at breakpoints and drive real step/stack/locals (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-debugger] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

### 1. Script debugger: breakpoints, step in/over/out, stack, locals, evaluator  (STUB, P0)

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp:3893-3924 (debug_break on breakpoint/step), editor/debugger/script_editor_debugger.cpp, core/debugger/script_debugger.cpp

**Patina today:** gdcore/src/debugger.rs:297 should_break has no caller outside its own tests and gdscript-interop/tests (I grepped `\.should_break(` across crates/). The interpreter never pauses. In editor_server.rs:~20880-20905, api_debug_step_in, step_over and step_out each just set debug_state="running". api_debug_break (:20737) pushes a fabricated frame ("_process","res://main.gd",1). debug_locals is declared (:510) and only ever cleared (:20874), never filled, so /api/debug/locals and the evaluator (which looks up names in debug_locals/debug_globals) always come back empty or 0.

**Implement:** Godot: before each statement the GDScript VM checks ScriptDebugger breakpoints and step depth (gdscript_vm.cpp:3893-3924). It then blocks in debug_break, sends the real call stack and the locals/members/globals of the chosen frame to the editor, and resumes on step_into, next (over), out or continue. The evaluator compiles and runs an Expression in that frame's context.

Patina: gdcore::debugger::Debugger::should_break (debugger.rs:297) is never called by gdscript-interop. The editor's step routes (editor_server.rs ~20880-20905) only flip a string. api_debug_break fabricates a frame (:20737). debug_locals is never written.

Implementation:
(1) In the interpreter's statement loop, call with_engine_debugger(|d| d.should_break(script, line)), passing step depth.
(2) On a hit, capture the frame stack (function, script, line) and the locals, self members and globals into a shared debugger snapshot, then block the play thread on a condvar.
(3) Make the editor routes step_in/over/out/continue set the step mode and signal the condvar. Fill debug_frames and debug_locals from the snapshot. Remove the fake frame.
(4) Evaluate /api/debug/evaluate with the interpreter's expression evaluator against the paused frame.
(5) Make breakpoints toggled in the script gutter (/api/script/breakpoint/toggle) register in the same Debugger.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/debugger.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs`

**Prove it:** Set a breakpoint on line 3 of a script whose _ready assigns `var x = 41; x += 1`, then press Play. The game pauses, and /api/debug/state reports paused at that script:line with a real stack. /api/debug/locals contains x=41. Step Over advances to the next line and x becomes 42. Continue resumes frames. Evaluating `x * 2` returns 84. (test: `debugger_breakpoint_pauses_play_and_steps`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. Grep `\.should_break(` over engine-rs/crates, excluding tests/, finds only the gdcore/src/debugger.rs unit tests (:508-522) and a doc-comment example at gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:21670. The ENGINE_DEBUGGER thread-local (interpreter.rs:21673-21788) only backs the script-facing EngineDebugger API, such as insert_breakpoint; the statement loop never consults it. api_debug_step_in (editor_server.rs:20881-20887) and step_over (:20890) only change debug_state from paused to running. Grep for `debug_locals =`, `.push` and `.extend` in gdeditor/src finds no writer. It is only declared (:510), initialized (:977), read (:20565, :20618, :20685) and cleared (:20874). P0 is fair: the routes and UI exist but are hollow.

### 2. Profiler / Visual Profiler / Video RAM fed by the running game  (UNWIRED, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/debugger/editor_profiler.cpp, editor_visual_profiler.cpp; EngineProfiler per-function script timings

**Patina today:** editor_server.rs:21212 is the only producer of profiler_frames (I grepped `ProfilerFrame {` and `profiler_frames.push`). It sits behind POST /api/profiler/record (:2772), and no client calls that route (it appears in the server-only diff of routes against fetch calls in EDITOR_HTML). Nothing in the play tick records frames, so the Profiler tab stays empty during Play. Video RAM in api_get_debug_info (~:20775) is a hard-coded literal (icon.svg 262144, font_default, viewport).

**Implement:** Godot's profiler gathers frame, process, physics and idle times plus per-script-function self/total time and call counts from the running game while profiling is on. Video RAM lists the actual loaded textures and meshes with their byte sizes.

Patina: profiler_frames is filled only by the test-only POST /api/profiler/record (editor_server.rs:2772/:21212), and nothing in the play tick records. Video RAM is a literal (~:20775).

Implementation:
(1) When /api/profiler/start has set the profiling flag, the play-loop step (the run_main_loop tick inside editor_server) times process, physics and render each frame and pushes a ProfilerFrame.
(2) Add an interpreter hook that accumulates per-function call counts and self/inclusive time per frame, and drain it into ProfilerFrame.functions.
(3) Build the video_ram list from the texture cache and mesh resources actually loaded in the running tree.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs`

**Prove it:** Start the profiler in the served editor, Play a scene whose script _process calls a function `busy()`, and stop after 30 frames. GET /api/profiler returns at least 30 frames with total_ms > 0 and a functions entry named busy with calls >= 30. /api/debug/info lists the scene's actual texture paths and none of the hard-coded icon.svg/font_default rows. (test: `profiler_records_frames_from_play_loop`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. The only push_back into profiler_frames is :21212, inside api_profiler_record (:21159). Grep `profiler/record` across engine-rs, tools, apps and scripts (rs/js/ts/gd/sh/py) finds only editor_server.rs and two gdeditor test files. The client calls only GET /api/profiler and /start, /stop and /clear (editor_ui.rs:11565, 17547, 17682, 17690). No play-loop caller exists. The Video RAM list is the literal at editor_server.rs:20770-20771.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Set a breakpoint on line 3 of a script whose _ready assigns `var x = 41; x += 1`, then press Play. The game pauses, and /api/debug/state reports paused at that script:line with a real stack. /api/debug/locals contains x=41. Step Over advances to the next line and x becomes 42. Continue resumes frames. Evaluating `x * 2` returns 84. (test: `debugger_breakpoint_pauses_play_and_steps`) 2) Start the profiler in the served editor, Play a scene whose script _process calls a function `busy()`, and stop after 30 frames. GET /api/profiler returns at least 30 frames with total_ms > 0 and a functions entry named busy with calls >= 30. /api/debug/info lists the scene's actual texture paths and none of the hard-coded icon.svg/font_default rows. (test: `profiler_records_frames_from_play_loop`)

DIAGNOSIS NARROWED TO ONE QUESTION (TurquoiseCastle). Still no code written. Everything below is static reading; nothing was executed.

=== WHAT IS NOT THE BUG ===
The pause snapshot is built CORRECTLY. `Interpreter`'s pause publisher (interpreter.rs:1098-1163) sets the innermost frame's `line` to the `line` argument — the statement about to run — and `PauseSnapshot.line` to the same value. So if the publisher is reached after the step, it reports 6. The reported 5 is therefore NOT a snapshot-construction bug, and the fix is not in that function.

=== WHAT THE SYMPTOM PINS ===
`step_over` answers `{"ok":true,"paused":true,"line":5}`. Those three together are the constraint:
- `request_resume` only sets `s.resume`; it does NOT clear `s.pause`.
- `take_resume()` is what clears it (`s.pause.take()?`), and it is consumed by the interpreter, not the HTTP handler.
- So `paused:true` + `line:5` means the OLD snapshot was still in the session when `resume_paused_game` re-read it ⇒ **nothing consumed the resume during `advance_running_main_loop`.** The step never ran; the editor is reporting the pause it already had.

That is cause (a) from my previous note, not (b). The `x == 41` vs `42` probe I proposed is no longer needed — the `paused:true` flag already discriminates, because a consumed-but-not-repaused step would have left `paused:false`.

=== THE ONE REMAINING QUESTION ===
`pump_debug_resume` (interpreter.rs:1174) is the only consumer of `take_resume`. It is correctly gated — it declines unless THIS interpreter's `coroutine_host` holds the parked coroutine, which is right, since the pause is a process global while hosts are per script instance. Its only callers are:
  interpreter.rs:1640  in `pub fn poll_coroutines(&mut self, delta: f32)`
  interpreter.rs:1662  in `pub fn tick_coroutine_frames(&mut self)`

**So: does the editor's `advance_running_main_loop` -> `MainLoop::step` reach `poll_coroutines` or `tick_coroutine_frames` on the interpreter of the script that is parked?** If it does not — or reaches them for other scripts but not the paused one — the resume is never consumed and the frame stays parked forever, which is exactly what the test sees.

⚠️ This is the SAME SHAPE as pat-mgixk.41, which I closed an hour ago: a correctly-written pump with no runtime caller on the path that matters. Worth checking that family of bugs deliberately rather than one at a time.

=== A SEPARATE REAL FINDING, CHEAP TO CONFIRM ===

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
MECHANISM IDENTIFIED (TurquoiseCastle), still no code written. Static reading only; nothing executed.

=== CORRECTION TO MY OWN PREVIOUS NOTE ===
I wrote that the resume pump might not be on the live per-frame path. **That was wrong and I checked before acting on it.** The chain is intact:

  scene_tree.rs:2447  script.poll_coroutines(delta)
  scripting.rs:409    -> interpreter.tick_instance_coroutine_frames(&mut self.instance)
  interpreter.rs:1707 -> resume_with_instance_self(instance, |i| i.tick_coroutine_frames())
  interpreter.rs:1662 -> pump_debug_resume()

So the pump IS reached every frame, with the instance bound as `self`. Had I "fixed" that, I would have added a second caller for a pump that already had one.

=== ALL FIVE PUMP GATES VERIFY STATICALLY ===
`pump_debug_resume` (interpreter.rs:1174) declines unless: the session is active; a pause exists; the snapshot carries a `coroutine` id; this host holds that coroutine; and a resume command is pending. Checked each:
- The snapshot's id is `last_call_suspended`, and `publish_debug_pause`'s doc requires `park_coroutine` to have just set it. **Every publish site is immediately preceded by a park** — 8987/8990, 17369/17370, 1869/1871. Ordering is correct.
- The `Stmt::Await` arm clears `last_call_suspended` (interpreter.rs:1511) but that is the await path, not the breakpoint path.
- `request_resume` sets the command and `take_resume` is the only consumer.
So on paper the pump should fire and re-publish line 6.

=== THE MECHANISM, AND THE TEST AUTHOR NAMED IT ===
`debugger_pause_steps.rs:25-33`, verbatim:

  "The hazard is threading, and only an end-to-end run exposes it. The pause is
   published by the thread that runs scripts (`build_play_tree`, inline on the
   connection thread serving `POST /api/runtime/play`), while the Step command
   arrives on a *different* connection thread, and the interpreter's debugger is
   a `thread_local!`. An implementation that kept the pause in that thread-local
   would compile, pass a unit test, and report 'not paused' to every route."

That is the asymmetry. `debug_session` is deliberately a process-global `Mutex<Session>` so the PAUSE crosses threads — but `with_engine_debugger` is **thread_local**, and `pump_debug_resume` calls `with_engine_debugger(|d| d.arm_step(command.step_mode(), depth))`. So the step arms the debugger belonging to whichever thread drained the resume, while `debug_break_before` on the next statement consults the debugger of whichever thread runs the script. If those are different threads, the step mode is armed on one and read from the other: the frame resumes (the BREAK_SIGNAL notify is on the shared coroutine host) and then runs on WITHOUT re-breaking, leaving the editor holding the pause it already had — `paused:true`, `line:5`, which is exactly the observed response.

⚠️ I cannot confirm which thread is which without running, so I am NOT calling this proven. It is the first hypothesis that explains all three observed values at once and it is corroborated by the author's own hazard note.

=== WHERE A FIX WOULD GO ===
Not in `editor_server.rs` (hot, shared, and the HTTP layer is not where the thread-locality lives). The candidates, cheapest first:
1. `arm_step` the step mode through the **process-global** `debug_session` rather than the thread-local debugger, so whichever thread next runs the script reads the same armed mode. `debug_session` already carries `resume`/`pause` across threads for precisely this reason.
2. Or have `pump_debug_resume` arm the debugger on the thread that will execute — i.e. arm lazily at the top of `debug_break_before` from the session state, instead of eagerly at resume time.

Option 1 keeps one source of truth and matches how the pause already crosses threads.

=== THE SEPARATE DEAD-CODE FINDING STANDS ===
`debug_session::clear_pause()` has ZERO callers workspace-wide. Under option 1 it may become the right place to clear on resume; under the current design it is vestigial. Left in place either way — deleting it would erase a clue.

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. **Godot ground truth:** core/input/input.cpp parse_input_event -> _parse_input_event_impl (updates state AND dispatches to Window/_input); InputMap.action_add_event(action, InputEvent)

**Patina today:** InputEventKey.new() yields a Variant::Resource from ClassDB defaults (interpreter.rs:4505-4518). But InputMap.action_add_event/action_erase_event accept only Int or Dictionary (event_arg, interpreter.rs:10389-10405), so a Resource argument raises TypeError. Input.parse_input_event accepts only a Dictionary of class InputEventAction (interpreter.rs:9284-9330) and only toggles action state (action_press/release). No _input, GUI or unhandled dispatch, and device events are refused. Shortcut methods matches_event/has_valid_event/get_as_text are registered (class_db.rs:29088-29090) with no dispatch arm (grep 'matches_event' in gdscript-interop/gdscene src: 0). InputEvent.accumulate is registered (class_db.rs:28676) but missing from is_input_event_method (interpreter.rs:31367-31390). No test anywhere constructs InputEvent*.new() (grep: 0).

**Implement:** Godot rebinding menus do `var e := InputEventKey.new(); e.physical_keycode = KEY_W; InputMap.action_add_event('up', e)`. Virtual-joystick and replay code does `Input.parse_input_event(ev)`, which both updates Input state and delivers the event to _input, the GUI and _unhandled_input. Patina rejects Resource events in action_add_event/erase_event (interpreter.rs:10389). parse_input_event takes only a Dictionary InputEventAction and never dispatches. Add SceneAccess::parse_input_event(Variant) that queues an InputCommand::ParseEvent. MainLoop::apply_script_input_commands converts it to gdplatform InputEvent and calls push_event, so it reaches SceneTree::push_input on the next step. Add dispatch arms for Shortcut.matches_event/has_valid_event/get_as_text and InputEvent.accumulate and as_text_location.

title: Input: Godot physics-frame vs process-frame just_pressed/just_released semantics
description:
[audit-key: input/input-frame-timing] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** core/input/input.cpp:392-414 (pressed_physics_frame vs pressed_process_frame; Engine.is_in_physics_frame)

**Patina today:** Just-pressed state lives in one per-frame set cleared once per render frame (MainLoop::step -> input_state.flush_frame at main_loop.rs:4364; InputState::flush_frame input.rs:2009). The same snapshot serves every physics tick in the step (main_loop.rs:3649-3765 builds it once before the tick loop at ~3834). A press in a render frame with 0 physics ticks (render faster than physics_ticks_per_second) is never seen by _physics_process, and a frame with 2+ ticks reports it in every tick. Godot reports it in exactly the first physics frame after the event.

**Implement:** Godot stamps each action and key transition with pressed_process_frame and pressed_physics_frame. is_action_just_pressed answers against the physics frame counter when Engine.is_in_physics_frame(), else against the process frame (input.cpp:392-414). So a jump pressed at 144 fps is seen by exactly one _physics_process call. Patina clears just_pressed at the end of each render step and shares it across all ticks of that step, so presses get lost or reported repeatedly. Fix: replace the just_* sets in InputState/InputSnapshot with per-action (and per-key, per-button) frame stamps: process frame from MainLoop.frame_counter, physics frame from the physics tick counter (main_loop.rs:641). Have the scripting accessors compare against the current frame, using gdscript_interop's in_physics_frame flag (set at main_loop.rs:3834). Stop relying on flush_frame clearing.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`

**Prove it:** With physics_ticks_per_second 60, MainLoop.step(1/240) is called 4 times after a single key press. A _physics_process counter of is_action_just_pressed('jump') ends at exactly 1. With step(1/30) (2 ticks), it is also exactly 1. _process sees it exactly once. Test: (test: `input_just_pressed_physics_frame_test`).

**Verifier note:** The script snapshot is built once per step (main_loop.rs:3649-3763). The physics tick while-loop (:3834-3835) never rebuilds or clears it. input_state.flush_frame and clear_input_snapshot run once at the end of the step (:4361-4364). `grep pressed_physics_frame|physics_frame_stamp|just_pressed_physics` in main_loop.rs, input.rs and scripting.rs: 0 hits. A step with 0 ticks therefore misses the press, and a step with N ticks reports it N times.
acceptance_criteria: With physics_ticks_per_second 60, MainLoop.step(1/240) is called 4 times after a single key press. A _physics_process counter of is_action_just_pressed('jump') ends at exactly 1. With step(1/30) (2 ticks), it is also exactly 1. _process sees it exactly once. Test: (test: `input_just_pressed_physics_frame_test`).

title: Multiplayer: per-node RPC config table and script Node.rpc_config()
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/mp-rpc-config] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** script _ready calls rpc_config('m', {...}) -> rpc('m') uses that transfer mode/channel -> the receiver applies that node's mode

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/main/node.cpp rpc_config/get_node_rpc_config; scene_rpc_interface.cpp _get_rpc_config per object+script

**Patina today:** scene_tree.rs:2057-2090 register_script_rpcs stores configs in ONE global map keyed by bare method name (MultiplayerAPI.rpc_configs, network.rs:403-406), and rpc_call_local is a global HashSet<String> (scene_tree.rs:650). If two scripts declare `func hit()` with different @rpc args, the last one loaded wins for both. Node.rpc_config(method, dict) has no dispatch: grep 'rpc_config' in gdscript-interop/src and gdscene/src finds only a comment at scene_tree.rs:2049. call_local is DEFERRED (scripting.rs node_rpc -> call_deferred), but Godot calls it synchronously inside rpc().

**Implement:** Godot keys RPC config per object: from the script's @rpc annotations plus Node.rpc_config(method, {rpc_mode, transfer_mode, call_local, channel}). get_node_rpc_config() returns the merged dictionary.

Patina keys configs by bare method name across the whole tree (scene_tree.rs:2057-2090 -> network.rs:403 rpc_configs: HashMap<String, RPCConfig>), so scripts that share a method name overwrite each other. call_local is also a global name set (scene_tree.rs:650). rpc_config() is not script-callable. call_local is queued with call_deferred instead of running synchronously.

Implementation: store RPC config per NodeId, filled at script attach (scene_tree.rs:4955) and by a new 'rpc_config' arm in the scripting.rs node-method table that parses Godot's dictionary keys. Have MultiplayerAPI::rpc/rpc_id take the RPCConfig from the caller, or look it up by (node, method). On receive, look up by the resolved node. Run call_local synchronously where re-entrancy allows; if not, document the deviation and keep same-frame ordering.

Wiring: script _ready calls rpc_config('m', {...}) -> rpc('m') uses that transfer mode/channel -> the receiver applies that node's mode.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs`

**Prove it:** Two scripts on different nodes both declare `hit` with different @rpc modes (any_peer vs authority). Each node enforces its own mode on receive. A node that calls rpc_config('ping', {'rpc_mode': MultiplayerAPI.RPC_MODE_ANY_PEER, 'call_local': true}) at runtime can then rpc('ping') successfully, and ping runs locally before rpc() returns. (test: `multiplayer_rpc_config_per_node_test`)

**Verifier note:** register_rpc (network.rs:403-405) inserts into a HashMap keyed by method name, and scene_tree.rs:2057-2090 fills it with no node key. rpc_call_local is a global HashSet<String> (scene_tree.rs:650, 2086, 2094). grep 'rpc_config|get_node_rpc_config' in gdscript-interop/src, gdscene/src and class_db.rs finds only a comment at scene_tree.rs:2049, plus class_db.rs:25338 get_rpc_config and :25520 _get_rpc_config, which belong to other classes (MultiplayerAPI/extension); Node has no dispatch arm. call_local is deferred via call_deferred at scripting.rs:6362-6363 and 6385, not run synchronously.
acceptance_criteria: Two scripts on different nodes both declare `hit` with different @rpc modes (any_peer vs authority). Each node enforces its own mode on receive. A node that calls rpc_config('ping', {'rpc_mode': MultiplayerAPI.RPC_MODE_ANY_PEER, 'call_local': true}) at runtime can then rpc('ping') successfully, and ping runs locally before rpc() returns. (test: `multiplayer_rpc_config_per_node_test`)

title: Multiplayer: install OfflineMultiplayerPeer by default so single-player is_server()==true and unique id is 1
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/mp-default-peer] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. **Patina today:** scene_tree.rs:765 builds MultiplayerAPI::new(), and network.rs:380-395 leaves peer: None. is_server() then returns false (network.rs:806-808), unique_id() returns None and scripting.rs:5827-5837 maps that to 0, and has_multiplayer_peer() returns false. **Implement:** In Godot every SceneMultiplayer starts with an OfflineMultiplayerPeer (scene_multiplayer.cpp:686). A game that never networks therefore gets multiplayer.is_server()==true, get_unique_id()==1 and has_multiplayer_peer()==true. Assigning multiplayer_peer = null also reinstalls an offline peer. Common gameplay code gates on `if multiplayer.is_server():` and so works offline.

Patina's SceneTree starts with MultiplayerAPI::new() and peer None (scene_tree.rs:765, network.rs:380), so the same script gets false/0/false and the gated code never runs.

Implementation: MultiplayerAPI::new() (or SceneTree::new) installs Box::new(OfflineMultiplayerPeer::new()). Setting the peer to null reinstalls one. Fix the interpreter fallback answers to match (true/1/true). Make sure poll_status does not emit connected_to_server for the offline peer (Godot doesn't, because it is the server). Re-check is_multiplayer_authority (scene_tree.rs:3428) so it stays true offline.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene whose script prints multiplayer.is_server(), multiplayer.get_unique_id(), multiplayer.has_multiplayer_peer() and is_multiplayer_authority() in _ready, run through MainLoop with no networking set up, prints true, 1, true, true. After `multiplayer.multiplayer_peer = null` the values are the same. No connected_to_server signal fires. (test: `multiplayer_default_offline_peer_test`)

**Verifier note:** MultiplayerAPI::new() sets peer: None (network.rs:380-382), and SceneTree uses it at scene_tree.rs:765. is_server falls back to false (network.rs:806-807). scripting.rs:5827-5837 maps a missing unique_id to 0, and has_peer answers unique_id().is_some(), i.e. false. The only non-test OfflineMultiplayerPeer::new() is multiplayer_peer_handles.rs:202, which backs the script .new(). title: MultiplayerSpawner: custom spawn(data) via spawn_function, spawned/despawned signals, live spawnable edits
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/mp-spawner] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** authority script spawner.spawn({"pos": ...}) -> outbound SPAWN -> the peer's MainLoop poll -> spawn_function runs -> the node exists at spawn_path and spawned fires

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/multiplayer/multiplayer_spawner.cpp (spawn(), _spawn_custom, spawned/despawned signals, add_spawnable_scene); doc_classes/MultiplayerSpawner.xml

**Patina today:** Auto-spawn of tracked children works: scene_tree.rs:1128-1252 register_replication_nodes reads spawn_path/spawn_limit/_spawnable_scenes, and poll_replication_spawns runs at scene_tree.rs:1985. Missing: grep 'spawn_function\|"spawned"\|"despawned"\|"spawn" =>\|"add_spawnable_scene"' in gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src -> no dispatch hits. gdscene/src/multiplayer.rs has no emit call (grep 'emit' -> only a doc comment at :105). register_replication_nodes skips already-registered nodes (scene_tree.rs:1150), so add_spawnable_scene/clear_spawnable_scenes/set_spawn_limit after enter-tree never reach the gdplatform MultiplayerSpawner.

**Implement:** Godot: MultiplayerSpawner.spawn(data) on the authority calls spawn_function(data), adds the returned node under spawn_path, and replicates the data to peers, where the same spawn_function rebuilds it. Every spawn and despawn (auto or custom) emits spawned(node)/despawned(node) on the spawner, on both sides. add_spawnable_scene, clear_spawnable_scenes and set_spawn_limit take effect at runtime.

Patina handles auto-spawn of scenes listed in the .tscn (scene_tree.rs:1128-1252), but has no spawn()/spawn_function, emits no signals, and ignores runtime edits because a registered node is never re-read (scene_tree.rs:1150).

Implementation: add scripting.rs arms for MultiplayerSpawner methods (spawn, set/get_spawn_function, add_spawnable_scene, get_spawnable_scene(_count), clear_spawnable_scenes, set/get_spawn_path, set/get_spawn_limit) that write straight into self.replication.spawners[nid]. Encode custom spawns as a SpawnPacket with the scene index set to the custom marker plus the Variant data (gdplatform network.rs:1438 encode_spawn_packet). The receiver calls the Callable through call_script_method and parents the result under spawn_path. Emit 'spawned'/'despawned' from apply_replication_packets/apply_replication_despawn and from the local auto-spawn path. Enforce spawn_limit on custom spawns.

Wiring: authority script spawner.spawn({"pos": ...}) -> outbound SPAWN -> the peer's MainLoop poll -> spawn_function runs -> the node exists at spawn_path and spawned fires.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs`

**Prove it:** With a two-tree loopback, the server script sets spawner.spawn_function = _make_player and calls spawner.spawn({'name': 'P2'}). The client tree then has a node P2 under spawn_path built by its own _make_player. 'spawned' fires once on each side (exact count == 1). Freeing the node on the server despawns it on the client and fires 'despawned'. add_spawnable_scene called at runtime makes a newly added child of that scene replicate. (test: `multiplayer_spawner_custom_spawn_test`)

**Verifier note:** grep 'spawn_function|"spawned"|"despawned"|"add_spawnable_scene"|"clear_spawnable_scenes"' in gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src finds nothing. register_replication_nodes skips already-registered ids (scene_tree.rs:1150-1152), so properties are read once. grep 'emit' in gdscene/src/multiplayer.rs finds only the doc comment at :105. Auto-spawn works through poll_multiplayer_with_delta (scene_tree.rs:1956, 1990-1994). PARTIAL at P1 stands.
acceptance_criteria: With a two-tree loopback, the server script sets spawner.spawn_function = _make_player and calls spawner.spawn({'name': 'P2'}). The client tree then has a node P2 under spawn_path built by its own _make_player. 'spawned' fires once on each side (exact count == 1). Freeing the node on the server despawns it on the client and fires 'despawned'. add_spawnable_scene called at runtime makes a newly added child of that scene replicate. (test: `multiplayer_spawner_custom_spawn_test`)

title: Navigation: persistent NavigationServer2D/3D singletons with RID maps and script-callable query API
description:
[audit-key: navigation/nav-server-singleton] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** GDScript `NavigationServer2D.map_get_path(get_world_2d().navigation_map, a, b, true)` inside a running .tscn returns the same polyline that NavigationAgent2D follows

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json singletons NavigationServer2D/NavigationServer3D; servers/navigation_2d/navigation_server_2d.h, servers/navigation_3d/navigation_server_3d.h; doc/classes/NavigationServer2D.xml

**Patina today:** gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:19606-19637 BUILTIN_SINGLETONS lists NavigationServer2DManager/3DManager and NavigationMeshGenerator but not NavigationServer2D or NavigationServer3D. grep 'NavigationServer[23]D"' across crates/*/src finds only gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4710/4712. grep 'map_get_path|map_create|region_create|agent_create|query_path' outside tests finds no implementation. gdscene/src/navigation_agents.rs:41-44 states get_rid/get_navigation_map/set_navigation_map are absent because there is 'no RID registry'. The servers in gdscene/src/navigation.rs:634/1834 are throwaway locals rebuilt every frame in main_loop.rs:2238-2249 and are reachable from nothing. NavigationPathQueryParameters/Result classes are ClassDB-registered (gdobject/src/class_db.rs:28055-28266) but cannot be constructed or used, as gdscene/tests/nav_path_query_params_and_postprocess.rs:17-23 notes.

**Implement:** Godot: NavigationServer2D/3D are script singletons that hold persistent RID-keyed maps, regions, links, agents and obstacles. Every World2D/World3D owns a default map (get_world_2d().navigation_map). Scripts call map_get_path(map, from, to, optimize, layers), map_get_closest_point(_to_segment/_owner/_normal), map_get_random_point, region_get_random_point, query_path(params, result), and await map_changed / get_tree().physics_frame for sync (navigation_server_2d.h, NavigationServer2D.xml). Patina: no NavigationServer2D/3D identifier is script-visible (interpreter.rs:19606 BUILTIN_SINGLETONS). MainLoop::process_navigation builds a new local NavigationServer2D/3D each frame (main_loop.rs:2238-2249) and drops it. Implementation, stage 1: keep one persistent NavigationServer2D and one NavigationServer3D on MainLoop with a default map per world, rebuilt only when a region/link changes (dirty flag), and expose get_world_2d().navigation_map and get_world_3d().navigation_map as stable RIDs. Add a scripting.rs singleton dispatch, mirroring how PhysicsServer2D is wired, for map_get_path, map_get_closest_point, map_get_closest_point_to_segment, map_get_closest_point_owner, map_get_random_point, map_set/get_cell_size, map_set/get_edge_connection_margin, map_set/get_link_connection_radius, map_get_iteration_id, region_create/region_set_map/region_set_transform/region_set_navigation_polygon|mesh/region_set_enabled, and query_path with NavigationPathQueryParameters*/Result* made constructible with .new(). Emit NavigationServer2D.map_changed(map) when a rebuild changes the map. Stage 2, a separate bead: agent_*, obstacle_* and link_* RID calls. Wiring: GDScript `NavigationServer2D.map_get_path(get_world_2d().navigation_map, a, b, true)` inside a running .tscn returns the same polyline that NavigationAgent2D follows.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a NavigationRegion2D (an L-shaped NavigationPolygon) and a script that, after `await get_tree().physics_frame`, calls NavigationServer2D.map_get_path(get_world_2d().navigation_map, start, end, true). The returned PackedVector2Array goes around the L corner and matches the agent's get_current_navigation_path(). map_get_closest_point snaps an off-mesh point onto the boundary. query_path with NavigationPathQueryParameters2D.new() fills NavigationPathQueryResult2D.path. map_changed fires once after the region loads. 3D equivalent with NavigationServer3D/get_world_3d() (test: `nav_server_singleton_map_get_path_from_script`).

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. A grep for '"NavigationServer2D"|"NavigationServer3D"' over crates/*/src (excluding tests) hits only gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4710/4712. A grep for 'map_get_path|region_create|"query_path"' over crates/*/src outside tests matches no files. In interpreter.rs, NavigationServer2D appears only as NavigationServer2DManager (:4019, :19624, :29158) plus a doc comment at :29197 saying a bridge 'needs' to exist. A grep for 'navigation_map' in gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src returns nothing. The servers are per-frame locals (main_loop.rs:2238 `let mut server2 = NavigationServer2D::new()`, :2246 server3). MISSING at P1 is correct.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a NavigationRegion2D (an L-shaped NavigationPolygon) and a script that, after `await get_tree().physics_frame`, calls NavigationServer2D.map_get_path(get_world_2d().navigation_map, start, end, true). title: Navigation: clamp query endpoints onto the mesh and add a 3D corridor funnel plus path_postprocessing modes
description:
[audit-key: navigation/nav-query-snapping] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** NavigationAgent2D/3D set_target_position(off-mesh point) in a .tscn -> process_navigation -> non-empty path whose last point lies on the mesh

**Godot ground truth:** modules/navigation_2d/2d/nav_mesh_queries_2d.cpp and modules/navigation_3d/3d/nav_mesh_queries_3d.cpp: begin/end polygon = closest point on any polygon (start and target are clamped onto the mesh); path ends at the closest reachable point; default PATH_POSTPROCESSING_CORRIDORFUNNEL in both 2D and 3D

**Patina today:** gdscene/src/navigation.rs:805-817 find_path returns Vec::new() when global_polygon_containing(from|to) is None (:1049-1058 is a containment test with no snapping), so click-to-move on a point slightly off the mesh, or an agent whose body center sits just outside the polygon, never moves. 3D: navigation.rs:1932-1965 find_path picks start/goal by closest CENTROID (:1956 closest_polygon), builds the path as `from`, centroids, `to`, with no string-pull, and appends the raw `to` even when it is off-mesh. find_path_linked at :1877-1929 does the same. path_postprocessing (CORRIDORFUNNEL/EDGECENTERED/NONE) is read nowhere: grep 'path_postprocessing|PATH_POSTPROCESSING' in gdscene/src returns 0.

**Implement:** Godot clamps both query endpoints to the closest point on the navmesh. An off-mesh target yields a path to the nearest reachable point, not an empty path. 3D paths are string-pulled through the polygon corridor (CORRIDORFUNNEL), and EDGECENTERED and NONE are selectable via path_postprocessing (nav_mesh_queries_2d/3d.cpp). Patina, 2D: navigation.rs:811-818 returns empty for any off-mesh endpoint. 3D: navigation.rs:1932-1965 uses centroid-nearest polygons and centroid chains and ends on the raw target. Implementation: in NavigationServer2D::find_path, replace global_polygon_containing with a closest-point search (reuse map_get_closest_point at :686 and map_get_closest_point_owner at :720) and substitute the clamped point for from/to. In NavigationServer3D, compute closest-point-on-polygon (project onto the triangle fan) instead of centroid distance, collect the shared-edge portals along the A* corridor and run a 3D funnel (port string_pull at :502 onto the polygon plane, or work in XZ with Y interpolated). Add a PathPostprocessing enum honoured by both servers and read the agent's `path_postprocessing` property in navigation_agents::sync_tuning_2d/3d. Wiring: NavigationAgent2D/3D set_target_position(off-mesh point) in a .tscn -> process_navigation -> non-empty path whose last point lies on the mesh.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation_agents.rs`

title: NavigationAgent: port Godot's _update_navigation state machine (submit gating, repath triggers, live queries, correct signals) for 2D and 3D
description:
[audit-key: navigation/nav-agent-lifecycle] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn CharacterBody2D + NavigationAgent2D + script following get_next_path_position -> signals observed by connected script handlers

**Godot ground truth:** scene/2d/navigation/navigation_agent_2d.cpp:640-930 (_update_navigation, _advance_waypoints, _transition_to_target_reached/_navigation_finished, _trigger_waypoint_reached with details Dictionary + link_reached); same structure in scene/3d/navigation/navigation_agent_3d.cpp

**Patina today:** (1) Godot does nothing until target_position_submitted. Patina main_loop.rs:2214-2218 reads target_position (default ZERO) for every agent and paths toward the world origin, and an agent standing near the origin fires target_reached/navigation_finished with no target set (:2341-2347). (2) Repath happens only when the target moved more than 0.01 (main_loop.rs:2328). There is no path_max_distance check, no map-change repath, and re-calling set_target_position with the same value does not repath. grep 'path_max_distance' in gdscene/src returns 0. (3) get_next_path_position returns a value published by process_navigation, which runs in the IDLE phase after scripts (main_loop.rs:4219), so _physics_process reads last frame's waypoint, and a set_target_position+get_next_path_position pair in one call returns stale data (navigation_agents.rs:229-238). (4) navigation.rs:1244-1270: when get_next_path_position consumes the last waypoint it sets finished_emitted=true and queues TargetReached/NavigationFinished. drain_and_emit_2d skips both (navigation_agents.rs:441-446) and main_loop's `arrived_now && !finished_emitted` (:2343) is then false, so with path_desired_distance >= target_desired_distance neither signal ever fires. When the target is unreachable Patina emits target_reached anyway (:2345-2347). Godot emits only navigation_finished. (5) is_target_reachable = path non-empty (navigation_agents.rs:417), whereas Godot uses final_position within target_desired_distance of target. (6) NavigationAgent3D has no pending_signals (main_loop.rs:2416-2419 comment), so path_changed/waypoint_reached never fire in 3D. (7) waypoint_reached is emitted with no details Dictionary (navigation_agents.rs:430-436) and link_reached is absent (grep 'link_reached' in src returns 0). (8) path_height_offset and path_metadata_flags are unsynced (navigation_agents.rs:366-371).

**Implement:** Port navigation_agent_2d.cpp:732-930 as a single state machine shared by NavigationAgent2D and NavigationAgent3D in gdscene/src/navigation.rs. Fields: target_position_submitted, navigation_finished, target_reached, last_waypoint_reached. Behaviour: no path query until set_target_position is called. Repath when the path is empty, when the map iteration changes, when the origin is >= path_max_distance from the current segment, and on every set_target_position call even with the same value. _advance_waypoints uses '<' path_desired_distance. Inside target_desired_distance emit target_reached then navigation_finished. When the last waypoint is reached and the target is unreachable, emit navigation_finished only. is_target_reachable means final_position within target_desired_distance of the target. Replace the published-state getters in navigation_agents.rs (get_next_path_position, is_navigation_finished, is_target_reachable, get_final_position) with live calls into MainLoop's agent map, running _update_navigation with the parent's current global position, so a _physics_process call sees this frame's answer. That needs a SceneAccess route from scripting.rs into MainLoop::nav_agents_2d/3d. Delete the duplicate emitters in main_loop.rs:2341-2385 and drain_and_emit_2d's skip list so each signal has exactly one source. Add pending_signals to NavigationAgent3D. Emit waypoint_reached(details) with position, plus type/rid/owner per path_metadata_flags, and link_reached(details) for link waypoints. Sync path_max_distance, path_height_offset and path_metadata_flags in sync_tuning_2d/3d. Wiring: .tscn CharacterBody2D + NavigationAgent2D + script following get_next_path_position -> signals observed by connected script handlers.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation_agents.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn script-driven body with path_desired_distance=20 and target_desired_distance=10 reaches its target and receives exactly one target_reached and one navigation_finished. An agent whose target was never set emits nothing and get_next_path_position() returns the parent's global position. An unreachable target yields navigation_finished without target_reached and is_target_reachable()==false. Calling set_target_position then get_next_path_position in the same _physics_process returns a waypoint on the new path. Teleporting the body more than path_max_distance away triggers path_changed. NavigationAgent3D emits path_changed and waypoint_reached, and waypoint_reached's handler receives a Dictionary with 'position' (test: `nav_agent_state_machine_matches_godot`).

**Verifier note:** Spot-checked items 1, 2 and 7. A grep for 'target_position_submitted|map_changed|path_max_distance|link_reached' in gdscene/src returns 0. main_loop.rs:2324 repaths only when the path is empty or the target moved more than 0.01, and target_position falls back to Vector2::ZERO (:2219-2222), so an untargeted agent paths toward the origin. :2350-2356 plus :2374-2376 emit target_reached and navigation_finished together on arrival, with no reachability distinction. The 3D loop (:2392-2420) has no drain/emit of milestone signals. PARTIAL at P1 is correct.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn script-driven body with path_desired_distance=20 and target_desired_distance=10 reaches its target and receives exactly one target_reached and one navigation_finished. An agent whose target was never set emits nothing and get_next_path_position() returns the parent's global position. An unreachable target yields navigation_finished without target_reached and is_target_reachable()==false. Calling set_target_position then get_next_path_position in the same _physics_process returns a waypoint on the new path. Teleporting the body more than path_max_distance away triggers path_changed. NavigationAgent3D emits path_changed and waypoint_reached, and waypoint_reached's handler receives a Dictionary with 'position' (test: `nav_agent_state_machine_matches_godot`).

title: NavigationRegion: place regions by global transform and accept ExtResource and script-assigned navmesh resources
description:
[audit-key: navigation/nav-region-sources] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn with a rotated, offset-parented region and an ExtResource navmesh -> process_navigation -> agent path inside the transformed area

**Godot ground truth:** scene/2d/navigation/navigation_region_2d.cpp: region_set_transform(region, get_global_transform()) on ENTER_TREE/TRANSFORM_CHANGED; set_navigation_polygon() re-uploads on assignment; scene/3d/navigation/navigation_region_3d.cpp same

**Patina today:** main_loop.rs:2068 `origin = node2d::get_position(&self.tree, id)` with polygons translated only by `verts[i] + origin` (:2073); 3D at :2129-2134 the same. A region under a moved parent, or rotated or scaled, lands in the wrong place. patina-runner/src/navigation_debug.rs:23-28 documents this as a known open bug. packed_scene.rs:1938-1947 resolves only `SubResource:` navmesh references (`s.strip_prefix("SubResource:")`), so `navigation_mesh = ExtResource("…nav.tres")` contributes nothing. The __navmesh_* companions are written only by packed_scene and nav_bake. grep '"NavigationPolygon"|"NavigationMesh"' in gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src returns 0, so `region.navigation_polygon = load(...)` or a NavigationPolygon.new() built in script never reaches the map.

**Implement:** Godot uploads each region with its GLOBAL transform and re-uploads when navigation_polygon/navigation_mesh is assigned (navigation_region_2d.cpp, navigation_region_3d.cpp). Patina translates region vertices by the LOCAL position only (main_loop.rs:2068, :2129) and resolves only SubResource navmeshes (packed_scene.rs:1938-1947). Implementation: in process_navigation, transform each vertex by node2d::get_global_transform / node3d::get_global_transform. Change nav_bake::bake_region_3d (nav_bake.rs:166-170) to store region-local vertices via the inverse global transform, and fix navigation_debug.rs to compose. In packed_scene, also resolve `ExtResource:` navigation_polygon/navigation_mesh by loading the .tres/.res through the resource loader and copying vertices/polygons/bake params onto the same __navmesh_* companions. In scripting.rs, handle a property set of navigation_polygon/navigation_mesh with a resource (loaded, or NavigationPolygon/NavigationMesh.new() with set_vertices/add_polygon) by refreshing the companions. Wiring: .tscn with a rotated, offset-parented region and an ExtResource navmesh -> process_navigation -> agent path inside the transformed area.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/nav_bake.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/navigation_debug.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn where NavigationRegion2D sits under a Node2D at (500,0) rotated 90 degrees, with an ExtResource NavigationPolygon .tres, yields agent paths inside the transformed polygon and none at the untransformed location. A script that assigns `$Region.navigation_polygon = load("res://nav2.tres")` at runtime makes the new area pathable on the next physics frame. The 3D equivalent works with a NavigationMesh .tres (test: `nav_region_global_transform_and_ext_resource`).

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. main_loop.rs:2068 `origin = node2d::get_position` and :2074 `verts[i] + origin` (translation only). 3D is the same at :2129/:2134. packed_scene.rs:1940-1946 resolves only the `SubResource:` prefix for navigation_polygon/navigation_mesh. A grep for '"navigation_polygon"|"navigation_mesh"' in gdscene/src/scripting.rs and gdscript-interop/src/*.rs returns 0, so script assignment never refreshes the __navmesh_* companions. PARTIAL at P1 is fine.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn where NavigationRegion2D sits under a Node2D at (500,0) rotated 90 degrees, with an ExtResource NavigationPolygon .tres, yields agent paths inside the transformed polygon and none at the untransformed location. A script that assigns `$Region.navigation_polygon = load("res://nav2.tres")` at runtime makes the new area pathable on the next physics frame. The 3D equivalent works with a NavigationMesh .tres (test: `nav_region_global_transform_and_ext_resource`).

title: Animation editor: write every clip/track/key edit through to the AnimationPlayer with undo (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-animation] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: STUB]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

### 1. Animation editor edits persist to the scene AnimationPlayer / .tscn  (PARTIAL, P0)

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/animation/animation_track_editor.cpp (every op goes through undo_redo on the Animation resource owned by the AnimationPlayer's library)

**Patina today:** write_animation_through (editor_server.rs:14394) has exactly two callers: :14391 (auto-key) and :14747 (api_add_keyframe). It is absent, and so is any scene_tree access, from api_create_animation :14589, api_delete_animation :14627, api_add_track :14760, api_delete_track :14833, api_remove_keyframe :14872, api_reorder_track :20206, api_paste_keyframes :20311 and api_set_keyframe_transition :20374. api_save_scene (:8542-8589) serializes the tree without flushing state.animations. So creating or deleting an animation, adding or removing tracks, removing keys, changing transitions, reordering and pasting are all lost on save and invisible to Play until some later keyframe-add rewrites the clip. None of these push undo either.

**Implement:** Godot edits the Animation resource held by the player's AnimationLibrary directly and undoably, so saving the scene always serializes the current clips.

Patina keeps a side copy in state.animations and writes it back (write_animation_through, editor_server.rs:14394) only from keyframe-add and auto-key. Create, delete, track add/delete/reorder, key remove, transition and paste (:14589, :14627, :14760, :14833, :14872, :20206, :20311, :20374) never reach the scene, and save (:8589) does not flush.

Implementation: after every mutating animation handler, call write_animation_through, and for delete remove the clip from the player. Also flush every dirty clip in api_save_scene before TscnSaver. Wrap each mutation in an EditorCommand that is undoable against both state.animations and the player (extend execute_animation/undo_animation, which exist at :8260/:8278).

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs`

**Prove it:** In the served editor: create animation 'walk', add a property track for position, add 2 keys, remove 1 key, change its transition, and save. The .tscn contains an Animation sub-resource 'walk' with one key and the chosen transition. Delete animation 'idle' and save: it is gone from the file. Play runs 'walk' via autoplay. Ctrl+Z after the track add removes the track from both the panel and the saved file. (test: `animation_editor_edits_persist_to_tscn`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. write_animation_through (:14394) has only two callers, :14391 and :14747. The only add_animation call in editor_server.rs is :14408, inside that function, and grep finds no remove_animation and no iteration over state.animations that could act as a flush. api_create_animation, api_delete_animation, api_add_track, api_delete_track, api_remove_keyframe, api_reorder_track, api_paste_keyframes and api_set_keyframe_transition never touch scene_tree or an animation player; I grepped each function's line range. The only undo_stack push in 14589-14940 is the AnimationEdit inside api_add_keyframe. api_save_scene (:8542-8590) dispatches the `_apply_changes` virtual to editor plugins, then runs TscnSaver::save_tree with no animation flush. P0 (silent data loss on save) is right.

### 2. Animation panel menus, onion skinning, bezier track editor, inspector key buttons  (STUB, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/animation/animation_player_editor_plugin.cpp (tool menu, onion skinning), animation_track_editor.cpp (edit menu), animation_bezier_editor.cpp, animation_library_editor.cpp; EditorInspector key buttons (EditorProperty::set_keying)

**Patina today:** ANIM_MENU_ROUTES (editor_ui.rs:15652-15660) maps only new/remove/edit-transitions/copy/paste keys/next-prev step. Every other item falls through to `logMessage('warn', 'Animation menu action not implemented yet')` at :15685: anim-library, duplicate-anim, rename-anim, open-in-inspector, apply-reset, bake/optimize/clean-up, copy/paste tracks, scale selection, ease selection, duplicate/cut keys, move key to cursor, delete selection, next/prev keyframe, add RESET (items at :3180-3260). Onion skinning only stores flags (:15620-15645), and grep -i onion in editor_server.rs/viewport_2d_render.rs finds nothing. There is no bezier curve editor (grep -i bezier finds only the keyframe-transition easing canvas at :16048-16410). There are no inspector key icons (grep 'Insert Key|insp-key' finds 0).

**Implement:** Godot's AnimationPlayer editor provides: library management, duplicate/rename, Apply RESET, Bake/Optimize/Clean Up, copy/paste tracks, scale selection, make easing, duplicate/cut/move keys to cursor, next/prev keyframe, and onion skinning (it renders past/future poses tinted in the 2D/3D viewport). The bezier track editor (animation_bezier_editor.cpp) edits per-key in/out handles. Inspector properties show a key icon that inserts a key on the current track while the animation editor is open.

Patina: these menu items are logged as unimplemented (editor_ui.rs:15685), onion skinning stores flags only, and there is no bezier editor and no key buttons.

Implementation:
(1) Add server routes for duplicate/rename/apply_reset/optimize/cleanup/tracks copy-paste/scale/ease/move keys, built on gdscene::animation, and route each menu act to them.
(2) Onion skinning: when enabled, render N past/future sampled poses with alpha modulate in viewport_2d_render/viewport_3d_render.
(3) Bezier track: draw curves with draggable handles that POST in_handle/out_handle (TrackType::Bezier already exists in gdscene/src/animation.rs:143).
(4) Inspector key button: when the anim panel is open, a key icon per animatable property POSTs /api/animation/keyframe/add.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`

Dragging a bezier handle changes the sampled value at mid-time. Clicking the inspector key icon on `position` adds a key at the playhead. (test: `animation_menu_ops_and_onion_skin_reach_server`)

Onion skinning only stores editorSettings.onion_skinning_flags (:15646). grep -i onion in editor_server.rs, viewport_2d_render.rs and viewport_3d_render.rs finds nothing. grep `Insert Key|insp-key|prop-key|key-btn` finds no inspector key icon. The only client keyframe/add caller is the timeline double-click (:15753), and auto-key (:14391) covers only part of inspector keying. P1 is reasonable, and STUB fits a bundle of placeholder menu items.
acceptance_criteria: 1) In the served editor: create animation 'walk', add a property track for position, add 2 keys, remove 1 key, change its transition, and save. The .tscn contains an Animation sub-resource 'walk' with one key and the chosen transition. Delete animation 'idle' and save: it is gone from the file. Play runs 'walk' via autoplay. Ctrl+Z after the track add removes the track from both the panel and the saved file. (test: `animation_editor_edits_persist_to_tscn`) 2) In the served editor: Edit > Scale Selection x2 doubles the selected key times. Duplicate Animation creates 'walk_copy' with identical tracks. Apply RESET writes the RESET values to the nodes. Enabling onion skinning with 1 past step changes viewport pixels at the past pose position. title: Navigation: filter by navigation_layers and weight A* by enter/travel costs, map margins and project defaults
description:
[audit-key: navigation/nav-layers-costs] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** NavigationRegion2D.xml (navigation_layers, enter_cost, travel_cost, use_edge_connections); NavigationLink2D.xml (navigation_layers, enter_cost, travel_cost); NavigationServer2D map_set_edge_connection_margin/map_set_link_connection_radius; ProjectSettings navigation/2d/default_cell_size, default_edge_connection_margin, default_link_connection_radius (and 3d equivalents)

**Patina today:** grep 'navigation_layers|enter_cost|travel_cost' over gdscene/src/navigation.rs, main_loop.rs and navigation_agents.rs matches only the layer-bit accessor at navigation_agents.rs:177. The A* cost is pure Euclidean distance between centroids (navigation.rs:278-335). main_loop.rs:2240 merges ALL 2D regions into one NavMesh2D with a hardcoded 0.5 tolerance, so NavigationServer2D::edge_connection_margin (navigation.rs:646, default 1.0) and use_edge_connections are never consulted. 3D uses a hardcoded 0.5 too (:2250). Links attach to the nearest centroid with no link_connection_radius (navigation.rs:1063-1075, :1895-1906). grep '"navigation/' over crates src finds only Performance monitor names (gdcore/src/performance.rs:199-208), no ProjectSettings reads.

**Implement:** Godot: a path query only considers regions and links whose navigation_layers intersect the query/agent navigation_layers. Edge cost = distance * region travel_cost, plus enter_cost when entering a different region. Links carry their own costs and layers. Regions are kept separate and stitched by map edge_connection_margin when use_edge_connections is set. Link endpoints connect within link_connection_radius. Map defaults come from ProjectSettings navigation/2d|3d/default_* (nav_map_2d.cpp, nav_mesh_queries_2d.cpp). Patina: all regions are merged into one mesh with a fixed 0.5 tolerance (main_loop.rs:2240, :2250), and costs and layers are ignored throughout navigation.rs. Implementation: give NavMesh2D/NavMesh3D per-region navigation_layers/enter_cost/travel_cost/use_edge_connections fields. Have process_navigation add one region per NavigationRegion node instead of merging, reading those properties. Make build_global_graph (navigation.rs:852) skip regions or links whose layers do not match the query mask and weight A* g-cost by travel_cost/enter_cost (astar_find_path at :278 needs a cost callback). Use edge_connection_margin for cross-region stitching and link_connection_radius for link attachment. Read the ProjectSettings defaults when the map is created. Pass the agent's navigation_layers through set_target_position.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation_agents.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn with two parallel corridors from A to B, where the shorter one has travel_cost=10, sends the agent down the longer corridor. Clearing the short corridor's navigation_layers bit 1 while the agent keeps mask 1 also routes it the long way, and when the long corridor is disabled is_target_reachable() is false. Two regions with a 0.8 gap stitch at the default margin of 1.0 and do not stitch when map edge_connection_margin is 0.5 (test: `nav_layers_and_costs_shape_runtime_path`).

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. title: Navigation2D: wire NavigationPolygon outline baking into NavigationRegion2D.bake_navigation_polygon and .tscn load
description:
[audit-key: navigation/nav-bake-2d] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn region with an outline plus a StaticBody2D box inside -> script calls bake_navigation_polygon() -> agent detours around the box

**Godot ground truth:** modules/navigation_2d/2d/nav_mesh_generator_2d.cpp; scene/2d/navigation/navigation_region_2d.cpp bake_navigation_polygon(on_thread) + bake_finished; doc/classes/NavigationPolygon.xml

**Patina today:** gdscene/src/nav_polygon.rs:153-284 implements NavigationPolygon with outlines, triangulate and make_polygons_from_outlines(_with_cell), but grep 'nav_polygon::|make_polygons_from_outlines|NavigationPolygon::new|triangulate(' over gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src (excluding nav_polygon.rs) matches only an unrelated delaunay_triangulate in animation_tree.rs. **Implement:** Godot: NavigationRegion2D.bake_navigation_polygon() parses source geometry under the region (StaticBody2D collision shapes and/or MeshInstance2D/Polygon2D/TileMap per parsed_geometry_type and source_geometry_mode/group), plus the NavigationPolygon's traversable outlines. It subtracts obstruction geometry inflated by agent_radius, partitions into convex polygons (convex partition or triangulate per sample_partition_type), writes vertices/polygons and emits bake_finished (nav_mesh_generator_2d.cpp). Patina: gdscene/src/nav_polygon.rs has an outline-to-polygon baker with obstruction carving and zero callers. Implementation: add ("NavigationRegion2D", "bake_navigation_polygon") to nav_bake::call_nav_region_method. Collect outlines from the __navmesh_outlines__ companion (make packed_scene copy `outlines` and the 2D bake params agent_radius, cell_size, parsed_geometry_type, source_geometry_mode, source_geometry_group_name). Gather StaticBody2D CollisionShape2D/CollisionPolygon2D world polygons as obstructions, run NavigationPolygon::make_polygons_from_outlines_with_cell, write __navmesh_vertices__/__navmesh_polygons__ in region-local space, then emit bake_finished. At load, when a NavigationPolygon has outlines but no polygons, bake once so outline-only resources are pathable. Wiring: .tscn region with an outline plus a StaticBody2D box inside -> script calls bake_navigation_polygon() -> agent detours around the box.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/nav_bake.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/nav_polygon.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn with NavigationRegion2D (a 400x400 outline, agent_radius 10) and a StaticBody2D 100x100 box at its centre: after a script calls $Region.bake_navigation_polygon() and awaits bake_finished, an agent sent across the region never enters the box inflated by agent_radius.
