title: AStarGrid2D: Godot-signature script API (Rect2i region, property assignment, enums, getters, cell_shape, partial paths)
description:
[audit-key: navigation/astar-grid] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** a GDScript in a running .tscn using only Godot-documented spellings

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/AStarGrid2D.xml; core/math/a_star_grid_2d.cpp; extension_api.json AStarGrid2D methods/properties/enums

**Patina today:** gdscene/src/scripting.rs:8253-8340 astar_call_grid: set_region takes two Vector2i (astar_v2i at :8085 maps Rect2i to (0,0)), so Godot's `grid.region = Rect2i(0,0,32,32)` / set_region(Rect2i) gives an empty grid. Property assignment on AStar handles is not routed (is_astar_handle is used only on the method-call path, interpreter.rs:10939). Missing dispatch arms (diffed against extension_api.json): get_region, get_offset, get_cell_size, set/get_cell_shape, is_jumping_enabled, get_diagonal_mode, get_default_compute/estimate_heuristic, fill_weight_scale_region, get_point_data_in_region. get_diagonal_mode/is_jumping_enabled are ClassDB-registered (class_db.rs:27969-27974), so has_method is true and the call fails. grep 'DIAGONAL_MODE_NEVER|DIAGONAL_MODE_ALWAYS|HEURISTIC_OCTILE' over crates src returns 0, so AStarGrid2D.DIAGONAL_MODE_NEVER is undefined. get_id_path ignores the allow_partial_path arg (astar.rs:824). cell_shape is absent from astar.rs.

**Implement:** Godot's idiomatic AStarGrid2D usage is `var g = AStarGrid2D.new(); g.region = Rect2i(0,0,32,32); g.cell_size = Vector2(16,16); g.diagonal_mode = AStarGrid2D.DIAGONAL_MODE_NEVER; g.update(); g.get_id_path(a, b, true)` (AStarGrid2D.xml). In Patina, set_region accepts only (Vector2i, Vector2i) (scripting.rs:8261), property writes on AStar handles are unrouted, the class enums are unregistered, and several getters and cell_shape are missing. Implementation: accept Variant::Rect2i in set_region and return Rect2i from get_region. Route `handle.prop = v` and `handle.prop` for AStar handles to set_/get_ arms in the interpreter's property set/get path, next to the method-call route at interpreter.rs:10939. Register the DiagonalMode/Heuristic/CellShape integer constants on AStarGrid2D in class_db.rs (values from extension_api.json) so class_get_integer_constant resolves them. Add the missing getters, CELL_SHAPE_ISOMETRIC_RIGHT/DOWN position mapping in get_point_position, allow_partial_path for get_id_path/get_point_path (closest reachable cell), get_point_data_in_region returning Array[Dictionary{id,position,solid,weight_scale}], and the fill_weight_scale_region arm. Wiring: a GDScript in a running .tscn using only Godot-documented spellings.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/astar.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn script, using only Godot syntax, sets `region = Rect2i(0,0,10,10)`, `cell_size = Vector2(16,16)`, `diagonal_mode = AStarGrid2D.DIAGONAL_MODE_NEVER`, calls update() and fill_solid_region(Rect2i(5,0,1,9)), and gets a get_id_path(Vector2i(0,0), Vector2i(9,0)) that routes around the wall with only orthogonal steps. get_point_path returns 16px-scaled positions. get_id_path to a walled-in cell with allow_partial_path=true returns the closest reachable path. get_region() == Rect2i(0,0,10,10). With CELL_SHAPE_ISOMETRIC_DOWN, positions follow Godot's iso mapping (test: `astar_grid_godot_signature_from_script`).

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. scripting.rs:8260-8262 calls set_region with astar_v2i(args,0) and astar_v2i(args,1). astar_v2i (:8085) maps anything that is not a Vector2i or Vector2 to (0,0). The comment says Variant does not model Rect2i, but gdvariant/src/variant.rs:307 has Variant::Rect2i, so that justification is stale and Rect2i(0,0,32,32) gives an empty grid. The astar_call_grid arm list (scripting.rs:8253-8340) has get_size but no get_region, get_offset, get_cell_size, get_diagonal_mode, is_jumping_enabled, fill_weight_scale_region, get_point_data_in_region or cell_shape. `grep -rn 'DIAGONAL_MODE_NEVER|HEURISTIC_OCTILE|CELL_SHAPE_'` over crates/ returns 0. cell_shape exists only as a bare property at class_db.rs:27982. is_astar_handle is used only at interpreter.rs:10939, on the method-call path. I found no set_/get_ fallback for property assignment on handles (grep 'set_{' / 'is_.*_handle(oid.raw())' in interpreter.rs). Priority 1 is appropriate: the idiomatic Godot usage fails.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn script, using only Godot syntax, sets `region = Rect2i(0,0,10,10)`, `cell_size = Vector2(16,16)`, `diagonal_mode = AStarGrid2D.DIAGONAL_MODE_NEVER`, calls update() and fill_solid_region(Rect2i(5,0,1,9)), and gets a get_id_path(Vector2i(0,0), Vector2i(9,0)) that routes around the wall with only orthogonal steps. get_point_path returns 16px-scaled positions. get_id_path to a walled-in cell with allow_partial_path=true returns the closest reachable path. get_region() == Rect2i(0,0,10,10). With CELL_SHAPE_ISOMETRIC_DOWN, positions follow Godot's iso mapping (test: `astar_grid_godot_signature_from_script`).

title: Expose NavigationServer2D/3D as script singletons backed by a persistent RID-based server
description:
[audit-key: navigation/navigation-server-singletons] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json .singletons includes NavigationServer2D (137 methods) and NavigationServer3D (154 methods); upstream/godot/doc/classes/NavigationServer2D.xml, NavigationServer3D.xml

**Patina today:** The singletons are absent from BUILTIN_SINGLETONS (interpreter.rs:19604-19639); only the *Manager variants are listed at :19624-19625. No dispatch arm exists: grep -rn 'NavigationServer2D\"|NavigationServer3D\"|\"NavigationServer' over gdscript-interop/src and gdscene/src/scripting.rs matches only the Manager arms (interpreter.rs:4019, 4023). grep '\"map_get_path\"|\"map_create\"' in gdscript-interop/src returns nothing. A backend does exist: gdscene/src/navigation.rs NavigationServer2D/3D structs, used by main_loop.rs:2020-2045 process_navigation. That function rebuilds a LOCAL server every frame from NavigationRegion nodes, so there is no persistent map/region/agent RID state that a script singleton could address.

**Implement:** Godot games commonly call NavigationServer2D.map_get_path(map, from, to, optimize), get_maps(), region_set_navigation_polygon(), agent_set_avoidance_callback() and map_get_closest_point(), and NavigationAgent2D.get_navigation_map() returns a map RID meant for those calls. Patina's nav server is a Rust struct rebuilt per frame inside MainLoop::process_navigation (main_loop.rs:2020), and GDScript cannot name NavigationServer2D or NavigationServer3D at all; they are not in BUILTIN_SINGLETONS and have no dispatch arm. Steps: make the server persistent across frames with map, region, link, agent and obstacle RIDs (World2D/World3D default map); add both names to BUILTIN_SINGLETONS with a dispatch table covering at least the map_*, region_*, agent_*, link_* and obstacle_* query/set methods; and route NavigationRegion/NavigationAgent nodes through those same RIDs.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** 1. In a scene with one NavigationRegion2D whose polygon is an L-shaped corridor, `NavigationServer2D.map_get_path(get_world_2d().navigation_map, a, b, true)` returns a non-empty PackedVector2Array that goes around the corner.
2. The 3D equivalent works for NavigationServer3D.
3. Engine.has_singleton("NavigationServer2D") is true.
4. Edge cases: an invalid map RID returns an empty path and does not panic; a path between disconnected regions returns empty or closest-point behavior matching Godot; the map RID is identical across two consecutive frames.
acceptance_criteria:
1. In a scene with one NavigationRegion2D whose polygon is an L-shaped corridor, `NavigationServer2D.map_get_path(get_world_2d().navigation_map, a, b, true)` returns a non-empty PackedVector2Array that goes around the corner.
2. The 3D equivalent works for NavigationServer3D.
3. Engine.has_singleton("NavigationServer2D") is true.
4. Edge cases: an invalid map RID returns an empty path and does not panic; a path between disconnected regions returns empty or closest-point behavior matching Godot; the map RID is identical across two consecutive frames. (test: `navigation_server_2d_map_get_path_from_script`)

title: Light2D: apply lights and CanvasModulate in the canvas's view space and only to their own canvas (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/light2d-canvas-space] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the Play loop in examples/editor.rs and the shared runtime builder must both call the view-aware entry point

### 1. Light2D / CanvasModulate composited in world space and over CanvasLayer/UI  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** scene/2d/light_2d.cpp, scene/2d/canvas_modulate.cpp (CanvasModulate tints only its own canvas: canvas_set_modulate on get_canvas()); renderer_canvas_cull.cpp lights are transformed by the canvas transform

**Patina today:** collect_lights_2d uses the raw global transform for light positions (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/light2d_scene.rs:106) and item_light_mask_buffer rebuilds items via collect_canvas_items with no camera view (gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:3711-3713). In Play, examples/editor.rs:316-350 applies apply_camera2d_view to the items, rasterizes them, and then calls shade_runtime_canvas(tree, fb). apply_lights_with_surfaces takes no view transform (viewport_2d_render.rs:3488). So lights and light masks sit at world coordinates on a screen-space buffer and drift as soon as the camera scrolls or zooms. CanvasModulate is applied to the whole finished frame ('tints the finished frame', viewport_2d_render.rs:3497-3500), Control/CanvasLayer HUD pixels included, because the Control pass is rasterized into the same fb first (examples/editor.rs:300-306).

**Implement:** Godot: a Light2D lives on a canvas, and the renderer moves it by that canvas's transform, so with a Camera2D the light stays on its torch. CanvasModulate calls canvas_set_modulate on its OWN canvas (canvas_modulate.cpp), so a CanvasLayer HUD and its Controls are not tinted. Light2D.range_layer_min/max limits lighting to items on those CanvasLayers. Patina: light positions are global world coordinates (light2d_scene.rs:106), and so are the light-mask bounds (viewport_2d_render.rs:3711), while the framebuffer they shade is in screen space after apply_camera2d_view (examples/editor.rs:316-350). CanvasModulate multiplies every pixel of the frame (viewport_2d_render.rs:3497). Approach: pass the active canvas view transform (camera2d_view_transform result times the stretch transform) into shade_runtime_canvas. Transform light positions, occluder polygons and range/texture_scale by it (range scales with zoom), and build item_light_mask_buffer from the already-transformed items. Composite lighting and CanvasModulate only over the default-canvas items: rasterize the world canvas, shade it, then rasterize CanvasLayer and Control items on top (split the render list on CanvasFollow::Fixed / canvas_layer != 0). Wiring: the Play loop in examples/editor.rs and the shared runtime builder must both call the view-aware entry point.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/light2d_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/examples/editor.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene with a Camera2D centred at (1000,0), a PointLight2D at (1000,0) and a CanvasModulate of black renders the lit spot at the screen centre, not at world-origin-relative pixels. A Label under a CanvasLayer in the same scene keeps its unmodulated colour. With zoom 2 the lit radius doubles on screen. (test: `light2d_camera_space_compositing_test`)

**Verifier note:** light2d_scene.rs:106 uses get_global_transform(...).origin with no canvas or camera transform. In shade_runtime_canvas_with_surfaces (viewport_2d_render.rs:3474-3501), collect_lights_2d, item_light_mask_buffer and apply_lights_with_surfaces get no view parameter. item_light_mask_buffer (:3711) calls collect_canvas_items(tree) fresh, so the items are untransformed. CanvasModulate is applied to the whole fb (:3497-3499). examples/editor.rs:292-350 adds the Control items, applies apply_camera2d_view only to the items, rasterizes, and then calls shade_runtime_canvas(tree, &mut fb). The HUD is therefore tinted and the lights drift with the camera.

### 2. Light2D z/layer ranges and DirectionalLight2D max_distance  (PARTIAL, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/Light2D.xml:50-60 (range_layer_min/max, range_z_min/max default -1024/1024), DirectionalLight2D.xml:18 (max_distance default 10000)

**Patina today:** grep 'range_z_max|range_layer_max|"max_distance"' over gdscene/src, gdrender2d/src and gdeditor/src (excluding inspector schema and tests) finds only audio and 3D probe hits. apply_common_light_props (gdscene/src/light2d_scene.rs:65-94) reads blend_mode, cull masks, shadow_color/filter/smooth and height, and none of these ranges.

**Implement:** Godot lights only affect items whose z_index is in [range_z_min, range_z_max] and whose CanvasLayer is in [range_layer_min, range_layer_max]. DirectionalLight2D shadows are cast only within max_distance. Patina reads none of these (light2d_scene.rs:65-94). Approach: add the four ranges and max_distance to gdrender2d::light2d::Light2D. Extend item_light_mask_buffer (viewport_2d_render.rs:3711) into a per-pixel record of (light_mask, z_index, canvas_layer) from the drawn items, and skip a light per pixel when the item is out of range. Clip directional-light occluder shadow length to max_distance. Builds on the view-space lighting bead (same group).

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/light2d_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/light2d.rs`

**Prove it:** A PointLight2D with range_z_max=0 does not brighten a Sprite2D with z_index=5 next to a lit z_index=0 sprite in the rasterized frame. A light with range_layer_min=1 lights items on CanvasLayer 1 only. (test: `light2d_ranges_test`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. grep 'range_z_max|range_layer_max|max_distance' over gdscene/src and gdrender2d/src hits only audio_server_bridge.rs (:586, :656) and the 3D directional_shadow_max_distance in render_server_3d.rs. Nothing on the 2D light side reads them. PARTIAL at P2 stands.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A scene with a Camera2D centred at (1000,0), a PointLight2D at (1000,0) and a CanvasModulate of black renders the lit spot at the screen centre, not at world-origin-relative pixels. A Label under a CanvasLayer in the same scene keeps its unmodulated colour. With zoom 2 the lit radius doubles on screen. (test: `light2d_camera_space_compositing_test`) 2) A PointLight2D with range_z_max=0 does not brighten a Sprite2D with z_index=5 next to a lit z_index=0 sprite in the rasterized frame. A light with range_layer_min=1 lights items on CanvasLayer 1 only. (test: `light2d_ranges_test`)

title: AnimatedSprite2D: load AtlasTexture frames, per-frame durations and external .tres SpriteFrames
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/animated-sprite-frames] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn load -> flattened companions -> process_animated_sprites each idle frame -> render_kind_for Sprite arm -> pixels

**Godot ground truth:** scene/resources/sprite_frames.cpp (frames are {texture: Texture2D, duration: float}); scene/2d/animated_sprite_2d.cpp _notification draw uses texture of any Texture2D type incl. AtlasTexture

**Patina today:** packed_scene.rs:1352-1355 only resolves `sprite_frames = SubResource(..)` (sub_ref_id), so a SpriteFrames saved as ExtResource .tres is ignored. Inside it, a frame texture must be `ExtResource:` (packed_scene.rs:1390-1398, `let Some(ext_id) = reference.strip_prefix("ExtResource:") else { continue }`), so frames whose texture is SubResource(AtlasTexture), which is what Godot's 'Add frames from sprite sheet' writes, are dropped and the animation has 0 frames and is invisible. Per-frame `duration` is never read: only paths are stored (packed_scene.rs:1405-1407), and sprite_frames_from_node rebuilds every entry with SpriteFrameEntry::new, duration 1.0 (scene_tree.rs:8240-8245, sprite_frames.rs:77-81). grep '"SpriteFrames"|__sf_anims__' over gdscene/gdresource/gdscript-interop: no loader for external .tres and no runtime path for `sprite_frames = load(...)` from script.

**Implement:** Godot: SpriteFrames.animations is a list of {name, speed, loop, frames:[{texture, duration}]}. A frame texture can be any Texture2D, and the sprite-sheet importer emits AtlasTexture sub-resources. The resource is often saved as an external .tres. A frame shows for duration/(speed*speed_scale) seconds. Patina: packed_scene.rs:1352 handles SubResource only; :1390-1398 drops every non-ExtResource frame texture; duration is never flattened (only __sf_<name>_frames paths), and scene_tree.rs:8240 rebuilds entries at duration 1.0. Approach: (1) in packed_scene, resolve `sprite_frames` given as ExtResource by loading the .tres through gdresource's loader and feeding its sub_resources and props into the same flattening. (2) For each frame, accept SubResource(AtlasTexture): resolve `atlas` to the sheet path and `region` to a rect. Publish __sf_<name>_regions (PackedVector4/float array) beside __sf_<name>_frames, plus __sf_<name>_durations. (3) sprite_frames_from_node reads the durations into SpriteFrameEntry::with_duration and the regions into the entry. process_animated_sprites (scene_tree.rs:4418) publishes the current frame's region as __atlas_region with the texture, so sprite_sheet_for (viewport_2d_render.rs:81) draws the sub-rect through the existing AtlasTexture path. Wiring: .tscn load -> flattened companions -> process_animated_sprites each idle frame -> render_kind_for Sprite arm -> pixels.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/sprite_frames.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn whose AnimatedSprite2D uses an external .tres SpriteFrames, with 4 AtlasTexture frames cut from one sheet, autoplay set and frame 2 duration 3.0, runs in MainLoop. After N frames the node's `frame` follows the per-frame durations, and the rasterized frame shows the sheet sub-rect of the current frame (not the whole sheet, not nothing). (test: `animated_sprite2d_atlas_frames_runtime_test`)

**Verifier note:** packed_scene.rs:1353 uses sub_ref_id(sprite_frames), so the SubResource is the only accepted form. :1393-1395 skips any texture without the ExtResource: prefix, so AtlasTexture frames are dropped. AtlasTexture resolution at :1527-1552 covers only the node `texture` property. The frame `duration` key is never read; :1344 mentions it only in a comment. scene_tree.rs:8240ff builds SpriteFrameEntry::new(path) from paths only. The files that read __sf_ (scene_tree, packed_scene, scripting, scene_saver, editor_server) contain no .tres loader for SpriteFrames. packed_scene.rs has no external .tres inlining: grep '\.tres|load_tres|read_to_string' finds only comments saying inline-only.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn whose AnimatedSprite2D uses an external .tres SpriteFrames, with 4 AtlasTexture frames cut from one sheet, autoplay set and frame 2 duration 3.0, runs in MainLoop. After N frames the node's `frame` follows the per-frame durations, and the rasterized frame shows the sheet sub-rect of the current frame (not the whole sheet, not nothing). (test: `animated_sprite2d_atlas_frames_runtime_test`)

title: TileMapLayer: render external TileSets, flipped/transposed alternatives, animated tiles and iso/hex shapes
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/tilemaplayer-render] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn load -> flatten -> tilemap_quads in the runtime render list -> pixels; set_cell from script must reach the same path

title: Camera2D: Godot current-camera semantics plus make_current/reset_smoothing/align/screen-center methods
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/camera2d-current] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** script -> dispatch -> tree current camera -> process_camera2d_scroll (main_loop.rs:4189) -> camera2d_view_transform in the render path

**Godot ground truth:** scene/2d/camera_2d.cpp:354-355 and :532-533 (the FIRST enabled camera entering a viewport with no camera becomes current), :584 make_current, reset_smoothing, force_update_scroll, align, get_screen_center_position, get_screen_rotation, is_current

**Patina today:** current_camera2d (gdscene/src/behavioral_2d.rs:601-621) scans the whole tree and keeps the LAST enabled Camera2D ('the LAST in top-down order wins'), the inverse of Godot's first-entered rule, and current-ness is not stored. Camera2D registration (gdobject/src/class_db.rs:13583) is properties-only. grep '"make_current"|"reset_smoothing"|"force_update_scroll"|"align"|"get_screen_center_position"' over gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src: make_current appears only in camera3d.rs:1032-1055; the rest have 0 arms. node2d::get_screen_center_position (gdscene/src/node2d.rs:925) exists but has no script dispatch. A game with two enabled Camera2Ds (player plus cutscene) gets the wrong camera and cannot switch with make_current().

**Implement:** Godot: on ENTER_TREE an enabled Camera2D calls make_current() only if the viewport has no camera yet (camera_2d.cpp:354), so the first one wins. make_current() switches through the viewport group (:584). Disabling the current camera hands off to another, and freeing it clears it. reset_smoothing() snaps the smoothed centre to the target, force_update_scroll() recomputes immediately, align() recentres drag, and get_screen_center_position()/get_screen_rotation() return the smoothed values. Patina: current_camera2d (behavioral_2d.rs:601) picks the last enabled camera on every call, and Camera2D has no method arms. Approach: store the current camera on the SceneTree/root Viewport (a `current_camera_2d: Option<NodeId>`). Set it in the enter-tree lifecycle when enabled and none is set, and on make_current(). Clear and reassign it on exit/disable. Make current_camera2d read it. Add call_camera2d_method (pattern of camera3d::call_camera3d_method, camera3d.rs:1032) to the call_node_method chain in scripting.rs:2594, with make_current, is_current, reset_smoothing (rewrite CAMERA2D_SCROLL_CENTER to the target), force_update_scroll (run the process_camera2d_scroll step now), align, get_screen_center_position (read CAMERA2D_SCROLL_CENTER), get_screen_rotation and get_target_position. Register these methods in ClassDB. Wiring: script -> dispatch -> tree current camera -> process_camera2d_scroll (main_loop.rs:4189) -> camera2d_view_transform in the render path.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/behavioral_2d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene with two enabled Camera2Ds renders through the first one in tree order. After a script calls $Cam2.make_current(), the next rendered frame is centred on Cam2 and Cam1.is_current() returns false. get_screen_center_position() returns the smoothed centre while smoothing is on, and the target right after reset_smoothing(). (test: `camera2d_current_and_methods_test`)

**Verifier note:** behavioral_2d.rs:601-621 keeps the last claiming camera found in a top-down scan, and current-ness is not stored. Its callers are parallax_runtime.rs:68, behavioral_2d.rs:243 and :638, and gdeditor's wrapper at :2392. grep '"(make_current|reset_smoothing|force_update_scroll|align|get_screen_center_position|get_screen_rotation|is_current)"' over gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src hits only camera3d.rs:1032/1055, and that dispatch requires class_name == "Camera3D" (camera3d.rs:1036).
acceptance_criteria: A scene with two enabled Camera2Ds renders through the first one in tree order. After a script calls $Cam2.make_current(), the next rendered frame is centred on Cam2 and Cam1.is_current() returns false. get_screen_center_position() returns the smoothed centre while smoothing is on, and the target right after reset_smoothing(). (test: `camera2d_current_and_methods_test`)

title: Node2D: add move_local/global_translate/apply_scale/get_angle_to and Sprite2D/RayCast2D query methods
description:

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Patina today:** Extension-API sweep: for each non-accessor method of these classes I grepped '"<name>"' over gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src excluding class_db and tests. 0 dispatch arms for Node2D move_local_x, move_local_y, global_translate, apply_scale, get_angle_to, get_relative_transform_to_parent; Sprite2D get_rect, is_pixel_opaque; RayCast2D get_collider_shape, get_collider_rid, add_exception_rid, remove_exception_rid. call_node2d_method serves only get/set_global_position (gdscene/src/node2d.rs). **Implement:** Godot: Node2D.move_local_x(delta, scaled=false) and move_local_y move along the node's own axes; global_translate(offset) shifts global_position; apply_scale(ratio) multiplies scale; get_angle_to(point) = (to_local(point)*scale).angle(); get_relative_transform_to_parent(parent). Sprite2D.get_rect() returns the region/frame/centered/offset rect (sprite_2d.cpp get_rect); is_pixel_opaque(pos) samples texture alpha. RayCast2D.get_collider_shape() returns the hit shape index and get_collider_rid() the RID; add_exception_rid/remove_exception_rid take RIDs. Add Sprite2D get_rect (reuse SpriteSheet and centered/offset logic in viewport_2d_render.rs:39-150, moved into gdscene so scripting can call it) and is_pixel_opaque (decode via the texture cache in gdresource). Extend raycast2d::force_raycast_update to publish the hit shape index and body RID, and add arms for them. Register the methods in ClassDB so has_method agrees.

**Prove it:** A GDScript on a Node2D rotated 90 degrees calls move_local_x(10); global_position moves +10 on y. get_angle_to(Vector2(0,10)) from the origin with rotation 0 returns PI/2. $Sprite.get_rect() on a 64x32 centered texture with hframes=2 returns Rect2(-16,-16,32,32). The quoted '"get_rect"' and '"get_relative_transform_to_parent"' have no arms in gdscene/src or gdscript-interop/src. The look_at/translate/rotate/to_local arms at scripting.rs:3528-3570 are a different set (Vector3, Node3D-style) and are not the claimed methods.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript on a Node2D rotated 90 degrees calls move_local_x(10); global_position moves +10 on y. get_angle_to(Vector2(0,10)) from the origin with rotation 0 returns PI/2. $Sprite.get_rect() on a 64x32 centered texture with hframes=2 returns Rect2(-16,-16,32,32). title: Input Map editor: typed event capture + deadzone, persisted to project.godot [input] through the served editor
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-project-settings] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED] [rewritten 2026-10-31: split, see the Project Settings tree bead for the old part 2]

**Goal:** an Input Map edited in the served editor is saved to project.godot `[input]` in Godot's format, survives reopening the project, and is what Play runs. project.godot `[input]` is the single source of truth, so one input-map model is left in the editor instead of three.

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/settings/action_map_editor.cpp and input_event_configuration_dialog.cpp. The dialog listens for a real event (a key with modifiers and a physical keycode, a mouse button, a joypad button, or a joypad axis), edits a per-action deadzone (default 0.2), and saves `jump={"deadzone":0.3,"events":[Object(InputEventKey,...)]}`.

**Patina today (2026-10-31):**
- `EditorState::input_map` is `HashMap<String, Vec<String>>` (editor_server.rs:453). `api_set_input_map` (~:23677) binds every chip as `InputEvent::Key(string)` through `input_map::InputMap::from_runtime_map`. A mouse or joy binding becomes a key string, the deadzone is dropped, and nothing is written to disk.
- An earlier partial added typed `input_map::InputEvent` variants and `InputMap::from_project_actions`/`to_project_actions` (gdeditor/src/input_map.rs:276-301), plus `GodotProjectFile::set_input_action` (gdresource/src/project.rs:142). **None of these have a caller outside tests.** Don't add a fourth model; wire these.
- Play is already fixed (pat-mgixk.24): `EditorState::build_play_input_map` (:1140) reads the project's `[input]` through `gdplatform::InputMap::load_from_project_godot`. Once the editor writes `[input]`, Play follows it with no extra work.
- Client: editor_ui.rs ~:16695/16753 is a free-text '+ key' box backed by `/api/input_map` `{action, keys}`.

**Implement:**
1. When a project opens, load `ProjectLoader::get_input_actions()` → `InputMap::from_project_actions` as the editor's input-map state. Replace the `HashMap<String,Vec<String>>` field, or derive it from the typed model if other readers still need strings, but there must be ONE writable model.
2. `POST /api/input_map` accepts typed events `{type: key|mouse_button|joy_button|joy_axis, keycode, physical_keycode, ctrl, shift, alt, meta, button_index, axis, axis_value}` and `deadzone`. On every change it writes through `to_project_actions` → `set_input_action` → project.godot on disk. `GET /api/input_map` returns the same typed shape.
3. Client: a listen dialog that captures keydown (with modifiers and `code` for the physical key), mousedown and Gamepad API buttons/axes; a deadzone field; and a 'Show Built-in Actions' toggle for the ui_* actions.

**Wiring requirement:** the served editor's HTTP API, then EditorState, then project.godot on disk, then Play's `build_play_input_map`. The acceptance test MUST boot the editor with `EditorServerHandle::start` on a temp project dir and drive it over HTTP, like tests/editor_play_input_map.rs and anim_tree_apply_reaches_the_runtime.rs. A test that builds `input_map::InputMap` directly does NOT satisfy this bead; that layer is already tested by input_map_project_bridge.rs.

**Prove it:** In a new `crates/gdeditor/tests/input_map_editor_persists_typed_events.rs`:
(a) boot the editor on a temp project whose project.godot binds `fire` to a mouse button;
(b) POST action `jump` with Space (physical_keycode 32) and joypad button 0 at deadzone 0.3;
(c) read project.godot from disk. It must contain `jump={"deadzone":0.3,` with an `Object(InputEventKey,` holding `physical_keycode":32` and an `Object(InputEventJoypadButton,` holding `button_index":0`, and `fire` must still be an `InputEventMouseButton`;
(d) GET /api/input_map returns jump's two typed events and deadzone 0.3;
(e) boot a second editor on the same dir: jump is still there (round trip through disk);
(f) start Play and assert through a script, the way editor_play_input_map.rs does, that `InputMap.has_action("jump")` and that `InputMap.action_get_deadzone("jump")` is 0.3.
acceptance_criteria: Driven through the served editor over HTTP on a temp project: POST action `jump` with Space (physical_keycode 32) + joypad button 0 at deadzone 0.3 writes project.godot `[input]` as `jump={"deadzone":0.3,"events":[Object(InputEventKey,...physical_keycode":32...),Object(InputEventJoypadButton,...button_index":0...)]}`; a pre-existing mouse binding stays InputEventMouseButton; GET /api/input_map returns the typed events; a second editor booted on the same dir sees `jump`; and a script in Play sees InputMap.has_action("jump") with deadzone 0.3. (test: `input_map_editor_persists_typed_events`)

comments.text:
SCOPE CORRECTION (TurquoiseCastle, 05:47Z) — SUPERSEDES my audit 3 minutes ago. That one said "make the typed InputMap the canonical thing EditorState holds" and warned about the blast radius of changing that field's type. That is NOT the work, and doing it would have been a large, risky change for nothing.

WHY: pat-mgixk.24 is ALREADY DONE and it covers the Play half of this bead's acceptance. It is wired into Play at editor_server.rs:16214 via main_loop.set_input_map(state.build_play_input_map()).

So "a script in Play sees InputMap.has_action(\"jump\") with deadzone 0.3" needs NO new Play work. It follows automatically IF the action reaches project.godot. Same for "a second editor booted on the same dir sees jump" — that is just on-disk state.

THE ACTUAL GAP, exactly three things, all inside the two HTTP handlers:
1. api_set_input_map (editor_server.rs:23677) accepts only `{"action","keys":[...],"remove"}` — plain key NAMES, so every binding becomes the lossy InputEvent::Key(String). It must also accept typed events (physical_keycode, joypad button_index, mouse index) and a deadzone. The typed model already exists: InputEvent::KeyEvent{..}, MouseButton(u32), JoyButton(u32) and Action{deadzone, events} in input_map.rs, which carries this bead's own 4 markers.
2. 🔑 THAT HANDLER WRITES NOTHING TO DISK. Verified: 0 occurrences each of project.godot / set_input_action / save / write / to_project_actions in its body. It only round-trips through the lossy string map (`s.input_map = map.to_runtime_map()`). Persistence is the whole lever of this bead, and the pieces are already there: InputMap::to_project_actions() (input_map.rs:276) plus gdresource::project::set_input_action / remove_input_action / parse_input_action / DEFAULT_DEADZONE.
3. api_get_input_map (:23662) rebuilds from the lossy map via from_runtime_map, so it can never return a physical_keycode, a joypad index or a deadzone even if one was POSTed. It must read the typed state.

Keep `s.input_map` updated exactly as now so the existing legacy readers (is_action_pressed at :1068/:1077, the seed at :952) are untouched, and ADD the write-through to project.godot plus typed handling in the two handlers. title: Line2D/Curve2D: implement point-editing and baked-sampling script methods
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/line-curve-script-api] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/Line2D.xml (add_point, remove_point, clear_points, set_point_position, get_point_count), Polygon2D.xml (add_bone, clear_bones, erase_bone, set_bone_weights), Curve2D.xml (add_point, clear_points, sample_baked, sample_baked_with_rotation, get_baked_points, get_baked_length, get_closest_offset, tessellate)

**Patina today:** The '"add_point"', '"remove_point"', '"set_point_position"' arms that exist are AStar2D/3D only (gdscene/src/scripting.rs:8102-8221, astar_call_2d/3d). '"clear_points"' has 0 arms. Line2D's ClassDB registration (class_db.rs:14424) has no methods. Curve2D: 0 hits for 'Curve2D' in gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs and 0 arms for sample_baked/get_baked_points/get_baked_length. curve2d_query::closest_offset (gdscene/src/curve2d_query.rs) is called only from gdscene/tests/curve2d_closest_offset.rs. The Path2D `curve` property stays a SubResource string with the data flattened to __curve__points (viewport_2d_render.rs:1776), so `$Path2D.curve` is not a Curve2D object in script. The common trail script (`$Line2D.add_point(pos)` each frame) does nothing.

**Implement:** Godot: Line2D.add_point(position, index=-1), remove_point(i), clear_points(), set_point_position(i,p), get_point_position(i) and get_point_count() mutate `points`, and the next draw reflects them. Path2D.curve returns a Curve2D whose add_point/clear_points/sample_baked(offset,cubic)/sample_baked_with_rotation/get_baked_points/get_baked_length/get_closest_offset/tessellate are used to build and query paths at runtime. Patina: no Line2D arms (the existing add_point arms are AStar-only, scripting.rs:8102-8221), and there is no Curve2D script object. Approach: (1) add call_line2d_method in a new gdscene module, chained into call_node_method (scripting.rs:2594), editing the node's `points` PackedVector2Array. (2) Give Curve2D a script-visible object handle backed by path3d::Curve2D, built from the flattened __curve__* companions on first access to `curve` and written back to __curve__points on mutation, so PathFollow2D (main_loop.rs:1345) and render_kind_for both see changes. Wire curve2d_query::closest_offset and Curve2D::sample_baked/sample_baked_cubic into its methods. (3) Add Polygon2D bone methods that write the skeleton weight companions read by skinned_polygon_points (viewport_2d_render.rs:1442). Register all methods in ClassDB.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/path3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`

**Prove it:** A script calls $Line2D.add_point(Vector2(50,0)) three times in _process; after 3 frames get_point_count()==3 and the rasterized frame shows the stroke. $Path2D.curve.add_point(Vector2(100,0)) at runtime moves a PathFollow2D child with progress_ratio=1.0 to (100,0) on the next frame. $Path2D.curve.get_baked_length() matches Godot for a 2-point straight curve. (test: `line2d_curve2d_script_api_test`)

**Verifier note:** The add_point/remove_point/get_point_count/get_point_position/set_point_position arms are all in the AStar section, scripting.rs:8102-8325. '"clear_points"', sample_baked, get_baked_points, get_baked_length, get_closest_offset and tessellate have 0 arms. add_bone exists only in skeleton3d.rs:1894, which is Skeleton3D. grep 'Line2D' over scripting.rs and interpreter.rs finds only a doc comment about .new(). gdscript-interop/src has 0 'Curve2D' hits. closest_offset has no caller in gdscene/src outside its own query modules. P1 is right because the Line2D trail add_point is common, even though the Polygon2D bone part is exotic.
acceptance_criteria: A script calls $Line2D.add_point(Vector2(50,0)) three times in _process; after 3 frames get_point_count()==3 and the rasterized frame shows the stroke. $Path2D.curve.add_point(Vector2(100,0)) at runtime moves a PathFollow2D child with progress_ratio=1.0 to (100,0) on the next frame. $Path2D.curve.get_baked_length() matches Godot for a 2-point straight curve. (test: `line2d_curve2d_script_api_test`)

title: Parallax2D: tile children by repeat_size and repeat_times in the canvas render list
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/parallax2d-repeat] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** build_runtime_render_list (:2056) is already on the Play path, so a scrolling Camera2D scene must show continuous coverage

**Godot ground truth:** scene/2d/parallax_2d.cpp (_update_repeat -> canvas_set_item_repeat; repeat_times draws extra copies)

**Patina today:** parallax_runtime.rs:215-223 reads repeat_size/repeat_times into gdserver2d::Parallax2D, but they only gate autoscroll wrap (gdserver2d/src/parallax.rs:390-404). The renderer's repeat pass apply_parallax_mirroring (gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:2076-2084) handles only `ParallaxLayer.motion_mirroring` (`if layer.class_name() != "ParallaxLayer" { continue; }`). grep 'repeat_size|repeat_times' in viewport_2d_render.rs returns 0. A Parallax2D background, the 4.3+ recommended node, draws once and runs out while scrolling.

**Implement:** Godot: Parallax2D with a non-zero repeat_size repeats its subtree on that axis across the viewport, and repeat_times adds extra copies each side (parallax_2d.cpp _update_repeat, canvas_set_item_repeat). Patina's scroll math already handles this (parallax_runtime.rs:166-196), but the render list only repeats ParallaxLayer.motion_mirroring (viewport_2d_render.rs:2076). Approach: generalise apply_parallax_mirroring to Parallax2D. For each Parallax2D, take items whose node is in its subtree (item_belongs_to_layer, :2146), compute the stride from repeat_size times global scale, and emit copies offset by k*stride for k in the range that covers the viewport plus repeat_times either side. Wrap the base offset by the published screen_offset/scroll_offset the same way. Wiring: build_runtime_render_list (:2056) is already on the Play path, so a scrolling Camera2D scene must show continuous coverage.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/parallax_runtime.rs`

**Prove it:** A Parallax2D with repeat_size=(256,0) holding a 256px-wide Sprite2D, under a Camera2D moved +1000px over the frames, fills the whole viewport width with sprite pixels (no clear-colour columns) in the rasterized frame. With repeat_times=2 the item count for that subtree is at least 5. (test: `parallax2d_repeat_render_test`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. build_runtime_render_list (viewport_2d_render.rs:2056-2060) calls apply_parallax_mirroring, which skips any node whose class is not "ParallaxLayer" (:2082-2084). repeat_size and repeat_times each grep to 0 in viewport_2d_render.rs. repeat_size shows up only in gdscene/src/parallax_runtime.rs (:215-223, scroll math), gdserver2d/src/parallax.rs and class_db.rs, and none of these is a render repeat. P1 fits, since Parallax2D is the node Godot 4.3+ recommends.
acceptance_criteria: A Parallax2D with repeat_size=(256,0) holding a 256px-wide Sprite2D, under a Camera2D moved +1000px over the frames, fills the whole viewport width with sprite pixels (no clear-colour columns) in the rasterized frame. With repeat_times=2 the item count for that subtree is at least 5. (test: `parallax2d_repeat_render_test`)

title: Play3D: render from the running tree's WorldEnvironment/Camera3D.environment, apply CameraAttributes, no preview sun
description:
[audit-key: nodes-3d/camera3d-environment] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** examples/editor.rs:257 -> viewport_for_scene_camera -> render_editor_3d_frame_gpu (and the software path)

**Godot ground truth:** scene/3d/world_environment.cpp, scene/3d/camera_3d.cpp (environment, attributes, PROJECTION_FRUSTUM), scene/resources/camera_attributes.cpp

**Patina today:** viewport_for_scene_camera (viewport_3d_render.rs:2572) builds Viewport3D::new, whose environment is the EnvironmentPreview3D default with procedural sky and a preview sun (viewport_3d.rs:582-604, 864). The Play path in examples/editor.rs:257 never copies the scene environment. world_environment_from_scene (editor_server.rs:8640) is applied only to state.editor_viewport_3d when a scene is opened (editor_server.rs:8851), not to the game-camera viewport. With no scene lights, setup_editor_lighting_3d (viewport_3d_render.rs:2319-2335) adds a preview sun Godot would not have. Camera3D.environment/attributes are never read (grep '"environment"|"attributes"' in camera3d.rs and viewport_3d_render.rs: none). gdrender3d/src/camera_attributes.rs (exposure, DOF) has no callers outside lib.rs:15. Frustum projection falls into Perspective (viewport_3d_render.rs:2585-2587).

**Implement:** Godot's game view uses Camera3D.environment, else WorldEnvironment.environment, else the project default (clear colour), with no editor sun. CameraAttributes drive exposure and DOF, and PROJECTION_FRUSTUM uses frustum_offset/size. Patina's Play viewport (viewport_3d_render.rs:2572) inherits the editor preview environment and sun. Implementation: in viewport_for_scene_camera, resolve the environment from the RUNNING tree (factor world_environment_from_scene to work on a SceneTree, including script-changed values), give Camera3D.environment priority, and set a game flag so setup_editor_lighting_3d adds no preview sun and editor_render_environment keeps the scene background. Thread CameraAttributes exposure_multiplier/exposure_sensitivity and DOF far/near into the renderer's post-process by calling camera_attributes::apply_exposure/dof_blur. Add an off-centre frustum projection using create_frustum (camera3d.rs:212). Wiring: examples/editor.rs:257 -> viewport_for_scene_camera -> render_editor_3d_frame_gpu (and the software path).

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs`, `engine-rs/examples/editor.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a WorldEnvironment of background_mode=Color red, a MeshInstance3D, no lights and a Camera3D: the Play frame's background pixels are red, and the mesh is unlit by any preview sun (it matches an ambient-only expectation). A CameraAttributesPractical with exposure_multiplier=2 brightens the mesh. (test: `play3d_uses_scene_environment`)

**Verifier note:** viewport_for_scene_camera (viewport_3d_render.rs:2572-2608) builds Viewport3D::new and never syncs the environment. It reads near/far/keep_aspect/h_offset/v_offset/frustum_offset, but PROJECTION_FRUSTUM still maps to Perspective at :2585-2587. The only production callers of load_from_environment/sync_environment_from_scene are editor_server.rs:8852-8856 (scene open, applied to editor_viewport_3d) and viewport_3d.rs:764 inside sync_from_scene, which has no production caller. examples/editor.rs:257-283 never copies the environment. setup_editor_lighting_3d adds the preview sun when scene_lights is empty (viewport_3d_render.rs:2319-2335). Grep for '"environment"|"attributes"' in camera3d.rs, viewport_3d.rs and viewport_3d_render.rs: no reads. `camera_attributes::` has no production users. P1 is correct.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a WorldEnvironment of background_mode=Color red, a MeshInstance3D, no lights and a Camera3D: the Play frame's background pixels are red, and the mesh is unlit by any preview sun (it matches an ambient-only expectation). A CameraAttributesPractical with exposure_multiplier=2 brightens the mesh. (test: `play3d_uses_scene_environment`)

title: MeshInstance3D: render script-assigned mesh/material resources and per-surface overrides
description:
[audit-key: nodes-3d/mesh-instance-resources] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** GDScript -> set_node_property -> node props -> build_render_list -> Play frame

**Godot ground truth:** scene/3d/mesh_instance_3d.cpp set_mesh / set_surface_override_material; geometry_instance_3d.cpp set_material_override

**Patina today:** node3d::get_mesh_path (node3d.rs:520-529) accepts only a String in `__viewport_mesh__` or `mesh`. The only writer of `__viewport_mesh__` is the .tscn loader (packed_scene.rs:1601), so a script-assigned mesh resource or ObjectId resolves to None and draws as a box marker. Materials reach the renderer only through `__material__*` companions flattened at load (render_server_3d.rs:2813 material_props_from_node, packed_scene.rs:654-870), so a runtime `material_override = StandardMaterial3D.new()` is ignored. surface_materials_for_node (render_server_3d.rs:2860) has no callers outside its module (grep 'surface_materials_for_node' across crates), so per-surface overrides beyond surface 0 never apply.

**Implement:** Godot: `var mi = MeshInstance3D.new(); mi.mesh = BoxMesh.new(); mi.material_override = mat; add_child(mi)` renders immediately, and surface_material_override/N applies per surface. Patina resolves meshes only from load-time String markers (node3d.rs:520) and materials only from load-time flattened companions. Implementation: in scripting.rs set_node_property, when `mesh` or a material property receives a script resource (ObjectId/Resource), convert it to the same representation the loader produces: set __viewport_mesh__ to a primitive:<Type>?props marker for PrimitiveMesh subclasses, or store an ArrayMesh via script_mesh::mesh_from_mesh_array, and re-flatten material properties into __material__*/__surfmat<N>__*. Also re-flatten when the resource is mutated, or resolve lazily in build_render_list from the live resource. Call surface_materials_for_node in build_render_list and give each surface its material, with material_override winning for all surfaces. Wiring: GDScript -> set_node_property -> node props -> build_render_list -> Play frame.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs`

**Prove it:** A GDScript _ready() creates a MeshInstance3D with BoxMesh(size 2) and a red StandardMaterial3D material_override and adds it under the Camera3D's view. The next render_game_3d_frame has red pixels covering a 2-unit box footprint and no grey marker. A two-surface mesh with surface_material_override/1 blue shows blue on its second surface. (test: `mesh_instance3d_runtime_resources_render`)

**Verifier note:** get_mesh_path (node3d.rs:521-530) accepts only a String in __viewport_mesh__ or mesh. material3d_for_node (render_server_3d.rs:2918) reads only __material__* companions via material_props_from_node (:2813). Grep for '__material__|__mesh__' in gdscene/src/scripting.rs and gdscript-interop/src: no hits, so nothing converts a script-assigned resource. surface_materials_for_node is called only at render_server_3d.rs:642, inside the adapter, and in a test. Viewport3D::build_render_list (viewport_3d_render.rs:119-210) does not call it.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript _ready() creates a MeshInstance3D with BoxMesh(size 2) and a red StandardMaterial3D material_override and adds it under the Camera3D's view. The next render_game_3d_frame has red pixels covering a 2-unit box footprint and no grey marker. A two-surface mesh with surface_material_override/1 blue shows blue on its second surface. (test: `mesh_instance3d_runtime_resources_render`)

title: Node3D: deliver TRANSFORM_CHANGED/LOCAL_TRANSFORM_CHANGED/VISIBILITY_CHANGED notifications and emit visibility_changed
description:

**Wiring requirement:** script write -> node3d setter -> dirty set -> MainLoop phase -> call_script_method("_notification")

**Godot ground truth:** scene/3d/node_3d.cpp _notify_dirty / _propagate_transform_changed / _propagate_visibility_changed; Node3D constants NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED=2000, LOCAL_TRANSFORM_CHANGED=44, VISIBILITY_CHANGED=43, ENTER_WORLD=41, EXIT_WORLD=42 (extension_api.json)

**Patina today:** Grep 'TRANSFORM_CHANGED|ENTER_WORLD|VISIBILITY_CHANGED' in gdscript-interop/src, gdscene/src and gdobject/src finds only comments (physics_server.rs:4826, node3d.rs:988). Grep 'visibility_changed' finds only the ClassDB signal declarations (class_db.rs:1534) and the editor signal list, with no emit. set_notify_transform and set_notify_local_transform are registered (class_db.rs:1571-1572) and never dispatched.

**Implement:** Godot: with set_notify_transform(true) a Node3D receives NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED in _notification whenever its global transform changes, including through ancestors, and LOCAL_TRANSFORM_CHANGED for local edits. Visibility toggles propagate NOTIFICATION_VISIBILITY_CHANGED and emit visibility_changed. Patina has none of this. Implementation: store notify flags as node properties via set_notify_transform/set_notify_local_transform dispatch. Mark nodes dirty in store_local_transform and the new transform-write funnel. Once per frame, after physics and before render (next to process_remote_transforms_3d at main_loop.rs:4207), deliver _notification(2000) to dirty flagged nodes and their flagged descendants. In set_visible, propagate 43 to the subtree and emit visibility_changed on the toggled node. Add the constants to the GDScript Node3D constant table. Wiring: script write -> node3d setter -> dirty set -> MainLoop phase -> call_script_method("_notification").

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn child Node3D whose script calls set_notify_transform(true) and counts what==NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED in _notification: moving its parent from another script increments the count once per frame. hide() on the parent fires the child's visibility_changed handler once. (test: `node3d_transform_and_visibility_notifications`)

**Verifier note:** Grep for 'TRANSFORM_CHANGED|VISIBILITY_CHANGED|ENTER_WORLD|\b2000\b' in gdscene/src, gdscript-interop/src and gdobject/src: only unrelated hits (scripting.rs:1589 0x2000, a fuzz seed). gdobject/src/notification.rs has no TRANSFORM, VISIBILITY or WORLD constant. 'visibility_changed' appears only in class_db.rs signal declarations and editor signals_tree.rs:300, never emitted. 'set_notify_transform' has no hits outside class_db.rs.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn child Node3D whose script calls set_notify_transform(true) and counts what==NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED in _notification: moving its parent from another script increments the count once per frame. hide() on the parent fires the child's visibility_changed handler once. (test: `node3d_transform_and_visibility_notifications`)

title: Light3D: consume PSSM split/blend, light_size soft shadows, shadow_blur, omni/directional shadow modes and projector on both 3D paths
description:

It does not read light_size, shadow_blur, omni_shadow_mode, directional_shadow_mode, light_projector or shadow_transmittance (grep in gdscene/src and gdeditor/src: omni_shadow_mode appears only in the unwired adapter, render_server_3d.rs:1743). In shadow_map.rs, generate_directional_cascades takes count from directional_shadow_mode and distances from split_1..3 * max_distance, blending across the split boundary when blend_splits. Scale the PCF kernel radius by light_size*distance and by shadow_blur. Sample light_projector in the light term for spot/omni lights on software and WGSL. Multiply the VoxelGI/ambient contribution by indirect_energy. Wiring: Play -> scene_lights -> setup_editor_lighting_3d -> renderer.

The renderer has a shadow_blur PCF field (renderer.rs:877, shadow_map.rs:1235), but no node reader feeds it. indirect_energy and blend_splits have 0 hits in gdrender3d. viewport_3d_render.rs:661-663 itself says they are not consumed.

title: CSG: torus/polygon/mesh primitives, recursive combiner evaluation, and use_collision
description:
[audit-key: nodes-3d/csg-family] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** Play -> build_render_list -> is_csg_root/evaluate_csg_tree; MainLoop physics sync -> CSG collider

**Godot ground truth:** modules/csg/csg_shape.cpp (CSGShape3D::_update_shape recursive per-child combine; CSGTorus3D, CSGPolygon3D depth/spin/path modes, CSGMesh3D, use_collision)

**Patina today:** csg_primitive_mesh (render_server_3d.rs:2032-2064) handles only CSGBox3D, CSGSphere3D and CSGCylinder3D (no cone), and returns None for the rest. gdserver3d/src/csg.rs has CSGMesh3D (line 383) but no torus or polygon. evaluate_csg_tree (render_server_3d.rs:2228-2265) walks the entire subtree flat, so a nested CSGCombiner3D's children are combined straight into the root with their own operation instead of first into the combiner. It supports CSGTorus3D (inner/outer radius, sides, ring_sides), CSGPolygon3D (polygon with mode depth/spin/path), CSGMesh3D (mesh), CSGCylinder3D.cone, and use_collision to create a static collider. Implementation: add torus and polygon (depth extrusion plus spin) generators to gdserver3d/src/csg.rs, and map CSGMesh3D's mesh via RenderServer3DAdapter::resolve_mesh. Rewrite evaluate_csg_tree as a recursive fn eval(node) -> Option<Mesh3D> that combines the children's results in order, and read numbers with float_property (Float or Int). When a CSG root has use_collision, register a concave trimesh static body in physics_server_3d sync. Wiring: Play -> build_render_list -> is_csg_root/evaluate_csg_tree; MainLoop physics sync -> CSG collider.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/csg.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs`

A CSGPolygon3D renders an extruded prism. A RigidBody3D dropped on a use_collision CSGBox3D comes to rest on it. (test: `csg_nested_torus_polygon_collision`)

**Verifier note:** csg_primitive_mesh (render_server_3d.rs:2031-2063) matches only CSGBox3D, CSGSphere3D and CSGCylinder3D, with Float-only radius/height. CSGCylinder3D::new_cone exists (gdserver3d/csg.rs:285) but is never used, since the cone property is not read. evaluate_csg_tree (:2228-2265) walks collect_subtree_top_down flat and combines each primitive straight into the root. gdserver3d/csg.rs has no Torus or Polygon type. use_collision appears only as struct fields in csg.rs, in class_db and in the inspector schema.
