title: GDScript: lexer support for ! && ||, hex/bin/exp numbers, triple/raw strings, bracket line-joining
description:
[audit-key: gdscript/gdscript-lexer] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** the change lives in the only tokenizer used by Interpreter::run_class, so a .tscn-attached script loaded by patina-runner bootstrap.rs:551 must now parse and run

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/gdscript/gdscript_tokenizer.cpp (number(): 689-814 hex/bin/exponent; string(): 859-947 raw/triple/escapes; BANG/AMPERSAND_AMPERSAND/PIPE_PIPE tokens; paren-depth newline suppression)

**Patina today:** engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/tokenizer.rs is the only lexer (interpreter.rs:996 and :15758 call it; GDScriptNodeInstance::from_source at gdscene/src/scripting.rs:177 -> run_class). Single-char table tokenizer.rs:729-756 has no '!' (falls to UnexpectedChar at :754). Two-char table :627-641 and :652-724 has no "&&" or "||" (so `a && b` lexes as Amp Amp and fails in parse_primary's &"StringName" arm, parser.rs:1816). Numbers :510-548 consume only digits/'.'/'_' so `0xFF` -> IntLit(0)+Ident(xFF), `1e3` -> IntLit(1)+Ident(e3). Strings :446-507: `\n` inside a string is an error (:490), escapes limited to n t r \\ ' " 0 (:476-487), no triple-quote/raw. Newline emission :427-443 is unconditional (grep -n 'depth' tokenizer.rs -> 0 hits) so multi-line arrays/dicts/call args fail in parse_primary (parser.rs:1939-1976 never skips Newline/Indent). Greps run: '"&&"', '"||"', "'!'", "'x'", 'is_ascii_hexdigit', 'from_str_radix', 'depth' in tokenizer.rs: all 0 hits. None of the 92 non-upstream .gd fixtures use these constructs (find ... | xargs grep -l '&&\||\|if !\|0x' -> empty), which is why tests stay green.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: gdscript_tokenizer.cpp emits BANG, AMPERSAND_AMPERSAND, PIPE_PIPE (parser rules at gdscript_parser.cpp:4224-4226 map && to PREC_LOGIC_AND, || to PREC_LOGIC_OR, ! to unary not); number() accepts 0x/0b prefixes, exponents and leading-dot floats with '_' separators; string() accepts """triple""" (multi-line), r"raw", \uXXXX/\UXXXXXX/\a\b\f\v escapes; a trailing backslash joins lines, and newlines/indent are suppressed while paren/bracket/brace depth > 0.

Patina today: tokenizer.rs:729-756 has no '!' ; :627-641 lacks && and ||; :510-548 numbers are decimal only; :446-507 strings reject embedded newlines (:490) and most escapes; :427-443 always emits Newline (no depth tracking), so `var a = [\n 1,\n 2\n]` and multi-line call args fail at parser.rs:1939-1976.

Implement: add Token::Bang/AndAnd/OrOr (or map && -> Token::And, || -> Token::Or, ! -> Token::Not directly, which reuses parser.rs:1467-1493/1631); hex/binary/exponent parsing with i64::from_str_radix; triple-quoted and raw string scanning; full escape table incl. unicode; a paren_depth counter that suppresses Newline/Indent/Dedent while >0 and a `\`+newline continuation. Wiring: the change lives in the only tokenizer used by Interpreter::run_class, so a .tscn-attached script loaded by patina-runner bootstrap.rs:551 must now parse and run.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/tokenizer.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/parser.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene whose attached script uses `if !is_ready and (a && b || c):`, `const MASK = 0xFF | 0b1010`, `var big = 1.5e3`, a multi-line array literal, a multi-line function call, a """docstring""" and r"C:\\path" loads via the runner/SceneTree, _ready runs and prints the expected values (output asserted). Unit-level token assertions alone do not satisfy this. (test: `gdscript_lexer_real_world_syntax`)

**Verifier note:** tokenizer.rs:337 tokenize() is the only lexer used (interpreter.rs:996, :15758; type_checker.rs:98). There is no preprocessing pass: I grepped preprocess|normalize_source|join_lines|"&&"|"||" across gdscript-interop/src, gdscene/src and patina-runner/src and got 0 hits. The single-char table (tokenizer.rs:731-757) has '&'->Amp and '|'->Pipe but no '!', so '!' falls through to UnexpectedChar. The two-char table (:627-724) has != but no && or ||. The number scanner (:510-548) accepts only digits, '.' and '_'. The string scanner (:446-507) errors on an embedded newline (:490), only knows the escapes n t r \\ ' " 0 (:476-487), and has no triple-quote or raw form. Newline is emitted unconditionally (:427-443) with no depth counter. The parser's only newline skipping is in block/decl contexts (parser.rs:474, 632, 849, 893, 1042, 1189, 1363), never inside array/dict/call parsing. P0 is right: these constructs are everywhere in real projects.
acceptance_criteria: A scene whose attached script uses `if !is_ready and (a && b || c):`, `const MASK = 0xFF | 0b1010`, `var big = 1.5e3`, a multi-line array literal, a multi-line function call, a """docstring""" and r"C:\\path" loads via the runner/SceneTree, _ready runs and prints the expected values (output asserted). Unit-level token assertions alone do not satisfy this. (test: `gdscript_lexer_real_world_syntax`)

comments.author: EmeraldCreek
comments.text:
## Known limitation of the bracket-depth suppression (EmeraldCreek, found while on pat-mgixk.18)

Recording this against the bead that introduced it. **Not a regression against any
existing test** — I checked — but it is a real gap and it wants its own bead.

### The gap

`bracket_depth` suppresses Newline AND Indent/Dedent while any `(`/`[`/`{` is
open. That is what makes multi-line arrays and argument lists work. But a LAMBDA
with an indented block body needs exactly those tokens to delimit it, so inside
brackets it cannot have one:

```gdscript
button.pressed.connect(func():      # <- '(' opens depth
    do_thing()                      # <- no Newline/Indent emitted here
)
```

`parse_primary`'s lambda arm (parser.rs ~1953) selects the block form with
`if self.check(&Token::Newline) || self.check(&Token::Indent)`. Under
suppression neither is present, so it falls through to the single-expression
branch and mis-parses the body. This spelling is extremely common in real Godot
projects.

### Why no test caught it

Every lambda in the repo's quoted GDScript is SINGLE-LINE inside its parens —
`func(): return i` (gds_lambda_capture.rs:126,
lambda_captures_enclosing_locals.rs:54/93, threading.rs:52/110). Those need no
newlines at all and are handled by the lambda arm's `Return` / single-expression
branches, so they are unaffected either way.

### Honest uncertainty

I have NOT verified whether the multi-line-inside-parens form worked BEFORE
pat-mgixk.17. Pre-change the Newline and Indent were emitted, so the lambda arm
would have taken the block path — but the enclosing call's argument parsing does
not skip Newline either, so it may well have failed further along for a
different reason. Workers cannot build, so I could not settle it. Treat this as
"a known hole in the new behaviour", not as "a thing that used to work".

### What a fix looks like

Godot's tokenizer tracks lambdas specially rather than suppressing blindly
(`gdscript_tokenizer.cpp` keeps a lambda/indent stack so a lambda body inside
parens still gets its INDENT). The port would be: when a `func` lambda opens a
suite while depth > 0, stop suppressing until its body closes.

title: Physics2D: sweep every collider of the moving body (offset + rotation) in move_and_slide/move_and_collide/test_move
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-kinematic-sweep] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** script -> scripting.rs arm -> PhysicsServer -> character solver with the full collider set -> node position

**Godot ground truth:** modules/godot_physics_2d/godot_space_2d.cpp GodotSpace2D::test_body_motion iterates every shape of the moving body at body_transform * shape_transform, honours collision_mask and exceptions; scene/2d/physics/physics_body_2d.cpp move_and_collide(motion, test_only, safe_margin, recovery_as_collision)

**Patina today:** physics_server.rs:3227 and :3111 build `PhysicsCharacterBody2D::new(body.position, body.shape.clone())`, which drops body.rotation, body.shape_transform (the CollisionShape2D offset, e.g. a capsule at (0,-16) on a feet-origin sprite) and body.extra_shapes. character.rs:398/430/575/614/731 place the mover at `Transform2D::translated(position)`. node_test_move and server_body_test_motion (physics_server.rs:1473-1517) pass only subject.shape at position and rotation, with no shape_transform, and test against every body without collision_mask or exception filtering (character.rs:216-240; `bodies()` is unfiltered). The scripting.rs:3051 move_and_collide arm ignores test_only, safe_margin and recovery_as_collision (it always moves). scripting.rs:3743 test_move ignores its `from` Transform2D and `collision` out-argument and takes the first Vector2 arg.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: GodotSpace2D::test_body_motion (godot_space_2d.cpp) sweeps each enabled shape of the moving body at body_xform * shape_xform. It honours collision_mask and collision exceptions, and move_and_collide supports test_only, safe_margin and recovery_as_collision.

Patina now: the character solver is built from a single shape at the body origin with no rotation (physics_server.rs:3227, 3111; character.rs:398-731 use Transform2D::translated). Collider offsets and extra shapes on the mover are therefore ignored. test_move and body_test_motion (physics_server.rs:1473-1517) skip mask and exception filtering, and move_and_collide ignores test_only.

Approach: give gdphysics2d::character::CharacterBody2D a `rotation: f32` and `shapes: Vec<ShapeOwner2D>` built from PhysicsBody2D::shape_owners() (body.rs). Replace each `Transform2D::translated(p)` in character.rs with `from_rotation_origin(rotation, p) * owner.transform` and take the deepest hit over the owners. Filter test_motion's `bodies` by mask and PhysicsBody2D::excludes as obstacle_bodies does (physics_server.rs:3032). Parse move_and_collide's test_only and safe_margin, and test_move's from and collision args, in scripting.rs.

Wiring: script -> scripting.rs arm -> PhysicsServer -> character solver with the full collider set -> node position.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/character.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`

**Prove it:** A runner-loaded scene has a CharacterBody2D at y=0 whose CollisionShape2D (16x16 rect) sits at position (0,-8) and falls onto a floor whose top is y=100. It comes to rest at body y=100, not y=92. A rotated 45-degree rectangle body stops at the rotated extent. test_move() against a body outside collision_mask returns false. move_and_collide(v, true) reports the hit without changing position. (test: `physics2d_kinematic_sweep_uses_collider_transform`)

**Verifier note:** physics_server.rs:3227 and :3111 build PhysicsCharacterBody2D::new(body.position, body.shape.clone()), which drops shape_transform, rotation and extra_shapes. character.rs:398/430/575/614/731 use Transform2D::translated. Obstacles do honour rotation and offset through shape_owners (character.rs:149-155), but the mover does not. In node_test_move and server_body_test_motion (physics_server.rs:1473-1510), world.bodies() is filtered only by id, with no mask or exception check. They pass rotation but no shape_transform. The move_and_collide arm (scripting.rs:3051-3074) reads only args[0]. The test_move arm (scripting.rs:3743-3753) takes the first Vector2 argument and ignores from and collision. P1 is fine.
acceptance_criteria: A runner-loaded scene has a CharacterBody2D at y=0 whose CollisionShape2D (16x16 rect) sits at position (0,-8) and falls onto a floor whose top is y=100. It comes to rest at body y=100, not y=92. A rotated 45-degree rectangle body stops at the rotated extent. test_move() against a body outside collision_mask returns false. move_and_collide(v, true) reports the hit without changing position. (test: `physics2d_kinematic_sweep_uses_collider_transform`)

title: CharacterBody2D: wire motion_mode/platform_on_leave and add wall_min_slide_angle, safe_margin, platform layers
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-character-params] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn property -> node -> physics_server character build -> solver

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/CharacterBody2D.xml (motion_mode MOTION_MODE_GROUNDED/FLOATING, platform_on_leave, wall_min_slide_angle=0.2618, safe_margin=0.08, platform_floor_layers, platform_wall_layers); character_body_2d.cpp _move_and_slide_floating

**Patina today:** gdphysics2d/src/character.rs:69-71 has the `motion_mode` and `platform_on_leave` fields and uses them (character.rs:361, :680), but process_character_movement (physics_server.rs:3231-3256) never reads either node property. grep -w motion_mode/platform_on_leave over gdscene/src finds only character3d.rs, so a FLOATING top-down CharacterBody2D still gets floor/wall classification. wall_min_slide_angle, safe_margin, platform_floor_layers and platform_wall_layers appear only in gdscene/src/character3d.rs, not in gdphysics2d or physics_server.rs. Their setter/getter methods (set_motion_mode, get_safe_margin, set_platform_on_leave, etc.) have no 2D dispatch arm.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: CharacterBody2D has two motion modes. FLOATING uses _move_and_slide_floating, which slides with no floor or ceiling and applies wall_min_slide_angle. platform_on_leave decides which platform velocity is kept on leaving. safe_margin is the recovery margin. platform_floor_layers and platform_wall_layers filter which colliders count as moving platforms (character_body_2d.cpp; CharacterBody2D.xml).

Patina now: the 2D solver has motion_mode and platform_on_leave (character.rs:69-71), but physics_server.rs:3231-3256 never sets them from the node. The other four properties do not exist in 2D; only character3d.rs reads them.

Approach: read `motion_mode` and `platform_on_leave` (int enums) in the character build block of process_character_movement, or its synchronous replacement from the physics2d-character-sync bead. Add `wall_min_slide_angle`, `safe_margin`, `platform_floor_layers` and `platform_wall_layers` to gdphysics2d::character::CharacterBody2D. Apply wall_min_slide_angle in the floating slide branch and safe_margin as the depenetration margin, and filter platform_velocity acquisition by layer, mirroring character3d.rs. Add the setter/getter arms in scripting.rs.

Wiring: .tscn property -> node -> physics_server character build -> solver.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/character.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`

**Prove it:** A runner-loaded scene has a motion_mode=FLOATING CharacterBody2D sliding into a wall at 30 degrees. It reports is_on_floor()==false and slides along the wall. A body on a moving AnimatableBody2D with platform_on_leave=DO_NOTHING keeps zero inherited velocity after jumping off. platform_floor_layers=0 stops the platform carrying the body. (test: `characterbody2d_motion_mode_platform_params`)

**Verifier note:** grep -rn 'motion_mode|MotionMode' over gdscene/src excluding character3d gave 0 hits. grep -rnw for platform_on_leave, wall_min_slide_angle, safe_margin, platform_floor_layers and platform_wall_layers over gdscene/src and gdphysics2d/src, excluding the 3D files, found only the gdphysics2d/src/character.rs fields at lines 69/71/296/297/361/680. The character build block at physics_server.rs:3228-3248 never sets motion_mode or platform_on_leave. UNWIRED and P1 are correct; FLOATING is the standard mode for top-down games.
acceptance_criteria: A runner-loaded scene has a motion_mode=FLOATING CharacterBody2D sliding into a wall at 30 degrees. It reports is_on_floor()==false and slides along the wall. A body on a moving AnimatableBody2D with platform_on_leave=DO_NOTHING keeps zero inherited velocity after jumping off. platform_floor_layers=0 stops the platform carrying the body. (test: `characterbody2d_motion_mode_platform_params`)

title: Physics2D: unbounded polygon shapes + convex decomposition for CollisionPolygon2D solids
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-polygon-shapes] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn CollisionPolygon2D -> register_bodies/sync_to_physics -> world narrowphase

**Godot ground truth:** scene/2d/physics/collision_polygon_2d.cpp _build_polygon: BUILD_SOLIDS uses Geometry2D::decompose_polygon_in_convex and adds one ConvexPolygonShape2D per piece; ConcavePolygonShape2D/ConvexPolygonShape2D have no vertex cap

**Patina today:** gdphysics2d/src/shape.rs:16 sets `MAX_POLY_VERTS: usize = 12`. pack_points (shape.rs:68-77) silently truncates both ConvexPolygon and ConcavePolygon, so a ConcavePolygonShape2D or CollisionPolygon2D(BUILD_SEGMENTS) terrain keeps only its first 6 segments. physics_server.rs:187-213 polygon_shape_from_node turns a BUILD_SOLIDS outline into ONE `Shape2D::convex_polygon(&points)` even when it is concave, giving a wrong hull. grep 'decompose|convex_decomp' over gdphysics2d/src and gdscene/src/physics_server.rs = 0 hits. tilemap_collision.rs:93 has the same single-convex conversion.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: polygon shapes take any number of points. CollisionPolygon2D in BUILD_SOLIDS mode decomposes a concave outline into convex pieces (Geometry2D::decompose_polygon_in_convex), each its own shape on the owner (collision_polygon_2d.cpp _build_polygon).

Patina now: shape.rs:16 caps polygons at 12 points and truncates silently (shape.rs:68). physics_server.rs:207 makes one convex hull out of a concave outline. Shape2D is Copy with fixed arrays, which is why the cap exists.

Approach:
1. Change ConvexPolygon and ConcavePolygon to hold `Arc<[Vector2]>`, dropping Copy but keeping Clone and PartialEq. Fix the call sites that rely on Copy; the physics_server.rs `sh != body.shape` compare still works.
2. Add a decompose_polygon_in_convex port (ear-clip plus Hertel-Mehlhorn merge, or port core/math/geometry_2d.cpp) to gdcore or gdphysics2d.
3. In polygon_shape_from_node, emit one ShapeOwner2D per convex piece through the extra_collision_shapes path (physics_server.rs:486), with the first piece as the primary.
4. Do the same for TileSet polygons in tilemap_collision.rs.

Wiring: .tscn CollisionPolygon2D -> register_bodies/sync_to_physics -> world narrowphase.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/shape.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/collision.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/tilemap_collision.rs`

**Prove it:** A runner-loaded scene has a StaticBody2D with a 40-point ConcavePolygonShape2D terrain. A RigidBody2D dropped over its LAST segment lands on it instead of falling through. A concave L-shaped CollisionPolygon2D (BUILD_SOLIDS) lets a small ball drop into the notch, which a single convex hull would fill. (test: `physics2d_large_and_concave_polygons`)

**Verifier note:** shape.rs:16 has MAX_POLY_VERTS=12, and pack_points (shape.rs:68-77) truncates. polygon_shape_from_node (physics_server.rs:190-213) builds concave_polygon from 2N segment points, which truncate to 6 segments, and a single convex_polygon for BUILD_SOLIDS. tilemap_collision.rs:93 is the same. grep -i 'decompose|convex_decomp|ear_clip|triangulat' over gdphysics2d/src, physics_server.rs and gdcore/src found only an unrelated geometry3d doc comment. No chunking of MAX_POLY_VERTS into extra shapes exists; grep MAX_POLY_VERTS outside shape.rs found only scripting.rs:1747. P1 is fine.
acceptance_criteria: A runner-loaded scene has a StaticBody2D with a 40-point ConcavePolygonShape2D terrain. A RigidBody2D dropped over its LAST segment lands on it instead of falling through. A concave L-shaped CollisionPolygon2D (BUILD_SOLIDS) lets a small ball drop into the notch, which a single convex hull would fill. (test: `physics2d_large_and_concave_polygons`)

title: Physics2D: re-sync body properties every tick, write back sleeping, emit sleeping_state_changed
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-live-body-props] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** script property write -> node -> sync_to_physics -> world; world sleep -> sync_from_physics -> node + signal

**Godot ground truth:** scene/2d/physics/collision_object_2d.cpp set_collision_layer/mask push to the server immediately; rigid_body_2d.cpp set_freeze_enabled/set_mass/set_gravity_scale/set_linear_damp/set_lock_rotation_enabled/set_can_sleep each call PhysicsServer2D::body_set_*; _sync_body_state emits sleeping_state_changed

**Patina today:** register_bodies skips nodes already mapped (physics_server.rs:1620-1622, `if self.node_to_body.contains_key(&node_id) { continue; }`). mass, friction, bounce, layer, mask, gravity_scale, damp, freeze, lock_rotation, can_sleep, center_of_mass and continuous_cd are read only there (physics_server.rs:1649-1746). sync_to_physics (physics_server.rs:2290-2583) re-reads only transform, velocities, _pending_*, constant_force/torque, conveyor velocities and collider geometry. A script doing `freeze = true`, `collision_layer = 2`, `gravity_scale = 0` or `mass = 5` at runtime has no effect on the solver. sync_from_physics (physics_server.rs:2753-2810) writes back position, rotation and velocities but never `sleeping`, so is_sleeping() and the `sleeping` property never reflect a solver sleep. grep '"sleeping_state_changed"' over gdscene/src = 0 hits.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: every CollisionObject2D and RigidBody2D property setter pushes to PhysicsServer2D straight away (collision_object_2d.cpp, rigid_body_2d.cpp). RigidBody2D::_sync_body_state reads `sleeping` back each step and emits sleeping_state_changed when it flips.

Patina now: register_bodies reads these properties once (physics_server.rs:1649-1746) and later skips the node (1620). sync_to_physics does not refresh them, and sync_from_physics never writes `sleeping`.

Approach: move the property read block of register_bodies into a `fn apply_body_props(tree, node_id, body: &mut PhysicsBody2D)` and call it from sync_to_physics for every mapped body before the per-type match. A cheap fingerprint, like TileMapFingerprint, can skip unchanged nodes. Do the same for Area2D layer, mask, priority and overrides. In sync_from_physics, write `sleeping` for rigid bodies and emit `sleeping_state_changed` when it differs from the last published value.

Wiring: script property write -> node -> sync_to_physics -> world; world sleep -> sync_from_physics -> node + signal.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs`

**Prove it:** A runner-loaded scene has a RigidBody2D falling under gravity. Its script sets `freeze = true` at tick 10, and the body's y stays constant from tick 11. A second body set to `collision_layer = 0` at tick 5 falls through a floor it previously rested on. A body left resting emits sleeping_state_changed exactly once, and is_sleeping() returns true afterwards. (test: `physics2d_runtime_body_property_changes`)

**Verifier note:** physics_server.rs:1620-1622 skips mapped nodes. mass, collision_layer, freeze, sleeping and gravity_scale are read only at 1649/1677/1725/1728/1736. A scan of sync_to_physics (lines 2290-2600) for get_property/_prop found only transform, velocities, _pending_*, constant_force/torque, conveyor velocities, sync_to_physics and Area monitoring/monitorable/gravity_point_center. No dirty or re-register mechanism exists: node_to_body.remove appears only at 1927, the free path. grep 'sleeping_state_changed' over gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src found only the class_db registration.
acceptance_criteria: A runner-loaded scene has a RigidBody2D falling under gravity. Its script sets `freeze = true` at tick 10, and the body's y stays constant from tick 11. A second body set to `collision_layer = 0` at tick 5 falls through a floor it previously rested on. A body left resting emits sleeping_state_changed exactly once, and is_sleeping() returns true afterwards. (test: `physics2d_runtime_body_property_changes`)

title: Physics2D: dispatch ClassDB property accessors (set_*/get_*/is_*) to node properties + *_layer_value/*_mask_value
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-accessor-methods] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: STUB]

**Wiring requirement:** GDScript method call -> call_object_method -> call_node_method fallback -> node property -> physics sync

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json CollisionObject2D (34 methods), RigidBody2D (58), Area2D (36), CollisionShape2D (10), PinJoint2D/GrooveJoint2D/DampedSpringJoint2D, PhysicsMaterial

**Patina today:** Missing from gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src as quoted strings: set_collision_layer_value, get_collision_layer_value, set_collision_mask_value, set_collision_layer, get_collision_mask, set_freeze_enabled, set_mass, set_gravity_scale, set_linear_damp, set_contact_monitor, set_max_contacts_reported, set_sleeping, set_lock_rotation_enabled, Area2D set_monitoring/set_gravity/set_priority, CollisionShape2D set_disabled/set_shape/set_one_way_collision, CollisionPolygon2D set_polygon/set_disabled, all Joint2D/PinJoint2D setters, PhysicsMaterial set_friction/set_bounce, StaticBody2D set_constant_linear_velocity, AnimatableBody2D set_sync_to_physics. Checked per class with jq + grep -F '"<name>"'. No generic set_/get_ accessor shim exists (grep 'strip_prefix("set_' and 'format!("set_' = 0 relevant hits). interpreter.rs:15666-15668 returns Ok(Nil) when node_has_method is true but no arm answers, so `body.set_collision_mask_value(2, true)` silently does nothing. Property-assignment syntax still reaches the node.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: every bound accessor of the physics classes works, e.g. set_collision_mask_value(layer, bool) (collision_object_2d.cpp) and CollisionShape2D.set_disabled.

Patina now: ClassDB registers these methods, so has_method is true, but no call arm exists. interpreter.rs:15666 then returns Nil, with no error.

Approach: add a fallback in SceneTreeAccessor::call_node_method (scripting.rs:2594), after the specific arms. Resolve `method` against gdobject::class_db::get_property_list(class) by matching each PropertyInfo.setter or .getter (class_db.rs:968-990 already stores them). A setter writes args[0] to the node property, a getter reads it. Add explicit arms for get/set_collision_layer_value and get/set_collision_mask_value (bit 1..32 on collision_layer/collision_mask). The physics2d-live-body-props bead makes these writes reach the solver.

Wiring: GDScript method call -> call_object_method -> call_node_method fallback -> node property -> physics sync.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`

**Prove it:** A runner-loaded scene has a script call `$Body.set_collision_mask_value(2, true)`; `$Body.collision_mask` then reads 3 and get_collision_mask_value(2) returns true. `$Shape.set_disabled(true)` makes a RigidBody2D fall through the floor on the next tick. `$Pin.get_softness()` returns the authored value. No physics-class method in extension_api for CollisionObject2D/RigidBody2D/Area2D/CollisionShape2D returns Nil for a property it owns. (test: `physics2d_accessor_methods_dispatch`)

**Verifier note:** grep -F for the quoted strings set_collision_layer_value, set_collision_mask_value, set_freeze_enabled, set_disabled, set_mass, set_gravity_scale, set_monitoring, set_friction and set_contact_monitor over gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src gave 0 hits for each. Grepping for strip_prefix("set_"/"get_"/"is_"), starts_with("set_") and format!("set_{ found no generic accessor fallback. class_db get_property_setter/getter (class_db.rs:967-990) is used only by the ClassDB.class_get_property_* script API (interpreter.rs:20314) and by script-defined setters. call_object_method (interpreter.rs:15646-15667) returns Ok(Nil) when responds is true. STUB and P1 are correct.
acceptance_criteria: A runner-loaded scene has a script call `$Body.set_collision_mask_value(2, true)`; `$Body.collision_mask` then reads 3 and get_collision_mask_value(2) returns true. `$Shape.set_disabled(true)` makes a RigidBody2D fall through the floor on the next tick. `$Pin.get_softness()` returns the authored value. No physics-class method in extension_api for CollisionObject2D/RigidBody2D/Area2D/CollisionShape2D returns Nil for a property it owns. (test: `physics2d_accessor_methods_dispatch`)

title: Physics2D: emit *_shape_entered/exited signals and report TileMapLayer as collider for tile bodies
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-shape-signals-tiles] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** world.step overlap and contact -> physics_server signal pass -> scene signals; slide collision -> collider node = TileMapLayer

**Godot ground truth:** scene/2d/physics/area_2d.cpp _body_inout emits body_shape_entered(body_rid, body, body_shape_index, local_shape_index) + body_entered; rigid_body_2d.cpp _body_inout same; TileMapLayer is reported as the collider (get_coords_for_body_rid)

**Patina today:** grep '"body_shape_entered"|"area_shape_entered"|"body_shape_exited"|"area_shape_exited"' over gdscene/src hits only physics_server_3d.rs. The 2D path (physics_server.rs:2844-2925, 2987-3030) emits only body_entered/area_entered. Tile bodies from register_tilemap_bodies (physics_server.rs:2072-2160) are never put into body_to_node. process_overlap_signals (2850-2853) and node_for_body (1598) therefore skip or answer None for them, so an Area2D overlapping a TileMapLayer emits nothing, and KinematicCollision2D.get_collider()/RayCast2D.get_collider() on tiles return null. grep 'get_coords_for_body_rid' outside class_db.rs = 0 hits.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: Area2D and RigidBody2D (contact monitor) emit body_shape_entered/exited(rid, body, body_shape_index, local_shape_index) and area_shape_entered/exited next to body_entered (area_2d.cpp _body_inout and _area_inout). Tile colliders belong to the TileMapLayer node, which is what get_collider() returns, and TileMapLayer.get_coords_for_body_rid(rid) maps back to the cell.

Patina now: 2D emits only the non-shape signals (physics_server.rs:2844-3030). Tile bodies have no node mapping (2072-2160), so every path that resolves body->node drops them.

Approach: carry shape indices in OverlapEvent and the contact events (gdphysics2d area2d.rs/world.rs), using ShapeOwner2D index order. Emit the *_shape_* signals before the plain ones, as Godot does. In register_tilemap_bodies, insert each tile body into `body_to_node` -> TileMapLayer node and record a body->cell map. Make sure the obstacle and ownership code (obstacle_bodies, prune_departed_nodes) tolerates many bodies per node. Add a TileMapLayer get_coords_for_body_rid arm that returns the cell for a body RID (RID = BodyId raw).

Wiring: world.step overlap and contact -> physics_server signal pass -> scene signals; slide collision -> collider node = TileMapLayer.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/area2d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/world.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`

**Prove it:** In a runner-loaded scene, an Area2D falling into a TileMapLayer's painted cell emits body_entered(TileMapLayer) and body_shape_entered with valid indices. A CharacterBody2D standing on tiles gets get_slide_collision(0).get_collider() == the TileMapLayer, and get_coords_for_body_rid(get_collider_rid()) returns the cell under it. (test: `physics2d_shape_signals_and_tile_colliders`)

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. grep 'body_shape_entered|area_shape_entered|shape_entered|shape_exited' over gdscene/src (excluding physics_server_3d) and gdphysics2d/src = 0 hits. body_to_node is inserted only at physics_server.rs:1777. register_tilemap_bodies (physics_server.rs:2072-2149) stores tile bodies only in tilemap_bodies:2147 and never in body_to_node. The only reverse use of tilemap_bodies is obstacle_bodies (physics_server.rs:3064), which is collision only and has no node mapping. node_for_body (physics_server.rs:1598) reads body_to_node alone, and script_move_and_collide's collider (physics_server.rs:3130) uses body_to_node too, so collisions with tiles report Nil. grep -rl 'get_coords_for_body_rid' over the crates = 0 hits. P1 is fair, since Area2D/RayCast2D detection of TileMapLayer is common.
acceptance_criteria: In a runner-loaded scene, an Area2D falling into a TileMapLayer's painted cell emits body_entered(TileMapLayer) and body_shape_entered with valid indices. A CharacterBody2D standing on tiles gets get_slide_collision(0).get_collider() == the TileMapLayer, and get_coords_for_body_rid(get_collider_rid()) returns the cell under it. (test: `physics2d_shape_signals_and_tile_colliders`)

title: TileMap physics: per-physics-layer tile bodies with layer/mask/material, all polygons, alt tiles + transforms
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-tile-physics] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn TileSet -> packed_scene flatten -> register_tilemap_bodies -> world

**Godot ground truth:** scene/resources/2d/tile_set.cpp TileSet physics_layer_N/collision_layer, collision_mask, physics_material; TileData get_collision_polygons_count, one_way_margin, constant_linear_velocity; scene/2d/tile_map_layer.cpp _physics_update_cell (one body per physics layer with layer/mask/material, flip/transpose transform, collision_enabled)

**Patina today:** packed_scene.rs:3056-3060 drops the alternative id ('only the default tile (alt 0) can be painted'). packed_scene.rs:3064 keeps only keys ending `/polygon_0/points`, and the flattened key (tilemap.rs:679-684) has no physics-layer index, so later layers overwrite earlier ones. tilemap_collision.rs:108-111 creates PhysicsBody2D::new(...) with default layer/mask 1/1 and sets only one_way_collision: no one_way margin, friction/bounce or constant velocity. grep 'collision_layer|collision_mask|friction|one_way_margin|flip|transpose' over tilemap_collision.rs = 0 hits. physics_server.rs:2095 uses only the TileMapLayer global position (no rotation/scale).

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: TileMapLayer::_physics_update_cell (tile_map_layer.cpp) makes, per physics layer, a static body with that layer's collision_layer, collision_mask and physics_material. It adds every collision polygon of the TileData with one_way and one_way_margin, honours the alternative tile's flip_h/flip_v/transpose and the layer's global transform, sets constant_linear/angular_velocity, and is skipped when collision_enabled=false.

Patina now: only polygon_0 of alt 0 is flattened, without a layer index (packed_scene.rs:3056-3064, tilemap.rs:679). Tile bodies get default layer/mask (tilemap_collision.rs:108), and only the global position is applied.

Approach:
1. Extend collect_tile_physics to keep `<alt>/physics_layer_<n>/polygon_<m>/{points,one_way,one_way_margin}` under keys that include alt, layer and polygon index, and flatten TileSet `physics_layer_<n>/collision_layer|collision_mask|physics_material`.
2. Decode the alt id from tile_map_data (tilemap.rs decode_tile_map_data) and apply TileSetAtlasSource transform flags.
3. Extend TileCollisionInfo and tilemap_to_physics to emit one ShapeOwner2D per polygon with the layer, mask, material and margin.
4. Apply the full global Transform2D of the layer and skip when `collision_enabled == false`.
5. Include these inputs in TileMapFingerprint.

Wiring: .tscn TileSet -> packed_scene flatten -> register_tilemap_bodies -> world.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/tilemap.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/tilemap_collision.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs`

**Prove it:** A runner-loaded scene has a TileMapLayer whose TileSet physics layer 0 has collision_layer=4. A RigidBody2D with collision_mask=1 falls through the tiles and one with mask=4 lands. A tile with two polygons blocks in both regions. A flip_h alternative tile's slope mirrors. A TileMapLayer with collision_enabled=false collides with nothing. (test: `tilemap_physics_layers_polygons_alternatives`)

**Verifier note:** packed_scene.rs:3055-3058 discards _alt with the comment 'only the default tile (alt 0) can be painted'. packed_scene.rs:3066 matches only '/polygon_0/points'. tilemap_collision.rs:108-110 builds PhysicsBody2D::new(...Static...) and sets only one_way_collision, with no layer, mask, material or margin. physics_server.rs:2096 uses get_global_position only, and the fingerprint at 2102-2107 has no transform or collision_enabled. grep 'collision_enabled' in physics_server.rs and tilemap.rs = 0. The status is PARTIAL because basic polygon_0 and one-way tiles do work. P1 is fair.
acceptance_criteria: A runner-loaded scene has a TileMapLayer whose TileSet physics layer 0 has collision_layer=4. A RigidBody2D with collision_mask=1 falls through the tiles and one with mask=4 lands. A tile with two polygons blocks in both regions. A flip_h alternative tile's slope mirrors. A TileMapLayer with collision_enabled=false collides with nothing. (test: `tilemap_physics_layers_polygons_alternatives`)

title: Physics3D: step the 3D solver after _physics_process and make move_and_slide synchronous
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/p3d-tick-order] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** main/main.cpp Main::iteration: SceneTree::physics_process (scripts) runs before PhysicsServer3D::step. scene/3d/physics/character_body_3d.cpp move_and_slide() moves the body synchronously and returns the collision result of that call

**Patina today:** crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:3862-3864 run sync_to_physics/step/sync_from_physics, and 3879 runs character3d::process_character_movement, all BEFORE the script phase at main_loop.rs:3974. The 2D twin was moved after scripts (main_loop.rs:3986-4044, pat-0q2kx.201); 3D was not. scripting.rs:3671-3681 move_and_slide only sets `_move_and_slide_requested` and returns the PREVIOUS tick's is_on_floor/wall/ceiling. character3d.rs:130-139 consumes the flag on the next tick. Result: every scripted RigidBody3D velocity and impulse is one tick late. A CharacterBody3D's position, velocity and is_on_floor() do not change during the _physics_process that called move_and_slide, and the frame rendered after that tick still shows the old position.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: Main::iteration (main/main.cpp) runs the scene tree's physics process (all _physics_process callbacks) and then PhysicsServer3D::step. CharacterBody3D::move_and_slide (scene/3d/physics/character_body_3d.cpp) performs the motion during the call: global_position, velocity, is_on_floor() and the slide collisions are updated before it returns, and it returns whether this motion collided. Patina: main_loop.rs:3862-3880 steps the 3D world and drives characters BEFORE the script phase (main_loop.rs:3974), while 2D was moved after it (main_loop.rs:3986-4044). scripting.rs:3671-3681 defers move_and_slide through a flag consumed by character3d.rs:130-139 on the next tick. Approach: (a) move the 3D sync, step, ragdoll writeback and signal block after process_physics_frame_with_scripts, keeping a sync_registrations-style pre-pass so first-tick queries still see scene-loaded bodies, as 2D does; (b) add a synchronous script entry point (a script_move_and_slide_3d on PhysicsServer3D, mirroring physics_server.rs script_move_and_collide) that runs gdphysics3d::character move_and_slide for one node against the live world and writes position, velocity, flags and _slide_collisions back immediately; dispatch move_and_slide on CharacterBody3D to it through the script_physics_server_3d binding that is already bracketed around the script phase (main_loop.rs:3970-3978). Remove the deferred pass for nodes handled synchronously.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/character3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs`

**Prove it:** In a scene-loaded CharacterBody3D script, `_physics_process` that calls `move_and_slide()` and then reads `global_position` sees the moved position in the same call, and `is_on_floor()` is true on the very tick the body first lands. A RigidBody3D whose `_physics_process` sets `linear_velocity = Vector3(5,0,0)` on tick N has moved by 5*dt by the end of tick N. Both are driven through MainLoop::step from a .tscn (test: `physics3d_tick_order_sync_move_and_slide`).

**Verifier note:** main_loop.rs:3863-3865 runs sync_to_physics/step/sync_from_physics, and main_loop.rs:3879 runs process_character_movement, both before process_physics_frame_with_scripts at main_loop.rs:3974. The 2D comment at main_loop.rs:3978+ shows only 2D was moved after the script phase. scripting.rs:3672-3681 only sets _move_and_slide_requested and returns the old is_on_floor/wall/ceiling flags, and character3d.rs:130-139 consumes the flag. grep '"move_and_slide"' over gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src finds only scripting.rs:3672, so no synchronous 3D path exists.
acceptance_criteria: In a scene-loaded CharacterBody3D script, `_physics_process` that calls `move_and_slide()` and then reads `global_position` sees the moved position in the same call, and `is_on_floor()` is true on the very tick the body first lands. A RigidBody3D whose `_physics_process` sets `linear_velocity = Vector3(5,0,0)` on tick N has moved by 5*dt by the end of tick N. Both are driven through MainLoop::step from a .tscn (test: `physics3d_tick_order_sync_move_and_slide`).

title: Physics3D: route $Body.apply_* Vector3 calls to the 3D force bridge (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/p3d-rigid-script-api] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** GDScript `$Ball.apply_central_impulse(Vector3)` -> interpreter -> node _pending_* -> PhysicsServer3D::sync_rigid_body -> world body

### 1. RigidBody3D apply_*/add_constant_* called on another node ($Body.apply_central_impulse(Vector3))  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/RigidBody3D.xml apply_central_impulse/apply_impulse/apply_force/apply_torque(_impulse)/add_constant_*; all take Vector3

**Patina today:** In the interpreter's ObjectId receiver dispatch (crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:12533 `Variant::ObjectId(oid) => match method`), the arms at interpreter.rs:13637-13730 coerce every argument through vec2_arg (interpreter.rs:139-144), so a Vector3 becomes Vector2::ZERO and is accumulated as a Vector2 onto `_pending_impulse`. I found no Vector3 guard between 12535 and 13637 (grep 'apply_\|Vector3(_)) =>' over that range). The working Vector3 path in scripting.rs:4003-4040 says itself that it is reached only 'by the bare / self. call form'. The only acceptance test, crates/gdscene/tests/physics3d_rigidbody_script_forces.rs:81-82,214, calls the bare form, so it stays green while `$Ball.apply_central_impulse(Vector3(0,10,0))` from a controller script does nothing. Static evidence only: I could not run it.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: RigidBody3D.apply_central_impulse(Vector3), apply_impulse(Vector3, Vector3), apply_force, apply_torque, apply_torque_impulse and add_constant_* work identically whether called as self.method() or through a node reference. Patina: interpreter.rs:13637-13730 handles these methods for every ObjectId receiver and reads arguments with vec2_arg (interpreter.rs:139), so a Vector3 argument from another script becomes zero and is written as a Vector2 `_pending_impulse`. The Vector3-aware implementation lives in scripting.rs:4017-4060 and is reachable only by the bare call form. Approach: in each interpreter arm, when args[0] is Variant::Vector3, decline (fall through to scene_access call_node_method so the scripting.rs arm handles it), or switch on the argument type and use accumulate on Vector3 with the 3D property keys (_pending_impulse, _pending_torque_impulse, constant_force, and so on). Keep the 2D path byte-identical. Also check set_axis_velocity (interpreter.rs:~13736), which already special-cases Vector3, for consistency. Wiring: GDScript `$Ball.apply_central_impulse(Vector3)` -> interpreter -> node _pending_* -> PhysicsServer3D::sync_rigid_body -> world body.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene with a controller Node whose script runs `$Ball.apply_central_impulse(Vector3(0, 10, 0))` in _ready lifts the sibling RigidBody3D `Ball` above its spawn height after 10 MainLoop ticks. `$Ball.apply_torque_impulse(Vector3(0, 5, 0))` gives it non-zero angular_velocity.y. A RigidBody2D called with Vector2 arguments behaves as before (test: `physics3d_node_ref_force_calls`).

**Verifier note:** The defect is real. The ObjectId receiver arm at interpreter.rs:13637-13660 calls accumulate_vec2_property with vec2_arg, and vec2_arg (interpreter.rs:139-144) maps any non-Vector2 argument to ZERO. call_method_on (interpreter.rs:10773 onward) has only handle-family early returns before the ObjectId arm at :12533. awk over that range for call_node_method found no fallback that would divert Vector3 calls. STUB is the wrong label: a working Vector3 implementation exists in scripting.rs and the bare call form reaches it, so this is a PARTIAL call-path gap. Priority 1 (a common usage silently does nothing) rather than 0, because the core feature works through the self/bare form.

### 2. PhysicsBody3D.move_and_collide / test_move  (UNWIRED, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/PhysicsBody3D.xml move_and_collide(motion: Vector3, test_only, safe_margin, recovery_as_collision, max_collisions) -> KinematicCollision3D; test_move(from: Transform3D, motion: Vector3, ...)

**Patina today:** The library implementation exists at crates/gdphysics3d/src/character.rs:582 (`pub fn move_and_collide`), and its only callers are that module's tests (character.rs:1167-1183). grep '\.move_and_collide(' over gdscene/src finds only physics_server.rs:3115, the 2D server. The script arm at crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs:3051-3055 accepts only Variant::Vector2 and returns Nil for a Vector3. test_move at scripting.rs:3743-3753 extracts only a Vector2 and calls physics2d_node_test_move. A 3D move_and_collide therefore always returns null and moves nothing.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: PhysicsBody3D.move_and_collide(motion: Vector3, test_only=false, safe_margin=0.001, recovery_as_collision=false, max_collisions=1) sweeps the body, stops at the first contact, moves it unless test_only is set, and returns a KinematicCollision3D (get_position, get_normal, get_travel, get_remainder, get_collider, get_angle) or null. test_move(from: Transform3D, motion: Vector3, ...) returns a bool without moving. Patina: gdphysics3d/src/character.rs:582 implements the sweep, but nothing outside its tests calls it. scripting.rs:3051 and 3743 are Vector2-only. Approach: add PhysicsServer3D::script_move_and_collide(tree, nid, motion, test_only) that gathers obstacles exactly as character3d.rs does, calls CharacterBody3D::move_and_collide, writes global_position, and stores a `_move_and_collide` record that the existing kinematic_collision_handle_for/MOVE_AND_COLLIDE_INDEX machinery (scripting.rs:1257-1300) exposes. Branch the scripting.rs arms on Variant::Vector3 and use the physics_3d_mut() binding (scripting.rs:934). Add test_move for Vector3 and Transform3D arguments.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs`

**Prove it:** A CharacterBody3D (or AnimatableBody3D) script that calls `var c = move_and_collide(Vector3(5,0,0))` toward a StaticBody3D wall 2 m away gets a non-null KinematicCollision3D whose get_normal() is about (-1,0,0) and whose get_collider() is the wall, and the body stops at the wall. `test_move(global_transform, Vector3(5,0,0))` returns true and leaves the position unchanged. Both run from a .tscn via MainLoop (test: `physics3d_move_and_collide_script`).

**Verifier note:** gdphysics3d/src/character.rs:582 has pub fn move_and_collide, and its only callers are that module's tests (:1167, :1176). grep 'move_and_collide' over gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src finds only the 2D bridge (physics_server.rs) and scripting.rs. scripting.rs:3051-3055 returns Nil unless args[0] is Vector2. test_move at scripting.rs:3743-3753 extracts only a Vector2 and calls physics2d_node_test_move.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A scene with a controller Node whose script runs `$Ball.apply_central_impulse(Vector3(0, 10, 0))` in _ready lifts the sibling RigidBody3D `Ball` above its spawn height after 10 MainLoop ticks. `$Ball.apply_torque_impulse(Vector3(0, 5, 0))` gives it non-zero angular_velocity.y. A RigidBody2D called with Vector2 arguments behaves as before (test: `physics3d_node_ref_force_calls`). 2) A CharacterBody3D (or AnimatableBody3D) script that calls `var c = move_and_collide(Vector3(5,0,0))` toward a StaticBody3D wall 2 m away gets a non-null KinematicCollision3D whose get_normal() is about (-1,0,0) and whose get_collider() is the wall, and the body stops at the wall. `test_move(global_transform, Vector3(5,0,0))` returns true and leaves the position unchanged. Both run from a .tscn via MainLoop (test: `physics3d_move_and_collide_script`).

title: Physics3D: re-sync body layers/mask/mass/material every tick and implement StaticBody3D conveyor velocity (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/p3d-body-props] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

### 1. Runtime changes to 3D body mass, collision_layer/mask, friction/bounce and StaticBody3D constant velocities  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** PhysicsBody3D/CollisionObject3D setters call PhysicsServer3D::body_set_* immediately (scene/3d/physics/collision_object_3d.cpp set_collision_layer, rigid_body_3d.cpp set_mass, static_body_3d.cpp set_constant_linear_velocity -> body_set_state)

**Patina today:** crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:795-860 read mass, collision_layer, collision_mask, friction, bounce and physics_material ONLY inside `if !self.node_to_body.contains_key(&nid)` (registration). The per-tick rigid sync (sync_rigid_body, physics_server_3d.rs:1618-1746) reads no mass/collision_layer/collision_mask/friction keys (grep of the string literals in that range). The static/kinematic arm (physics_server_3d.rs:908-940) copies only position and rotation. As a result `set_collision_layer_value()`, `collision_mask = 0`, or `mass = 10` at runtime never reaches the world. StaticBody3D.constant_linear_velocity/constant_angular_velocity exist as fields (gdphysics3d/src/body.rs:119-124), but grep finds no reader in world.rs, character.rs or physics_server_3d.rs (except a comment at :2022), so conveyors and turntables are inert.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: CollisionObject3D.set_collision_layer/mask, RigidBody3D.set_mass and physics_material_override changes take effect on the next step, and StaticBody3D.constant_linear_velocity/constant_angular_velocity make touching rigid and character bodies move as if on a conveyor or turntable without the static body moving (godot_body_3d.cpp: kinematic/static bodies report that velocity to contacts; character_body_3d platform velocity). Patina reads all of these only at registration (physics_server_3d.rs:795-860), and body.rs:119-124 constant_* has no reader. Approach: hoist the layer, mask, mass, friction, bounce and material reads into a per-tick block that runs for every body type (next to the shape re-seed at physics_server_3d.rs:~950); read constant_linear_velocity/constant_angular_velocity for StaticBody3D into the body; in gdphysics3d/src/world.rs contact resolution, use a static body's constant velocity as its surface velocity for friction; in character.rs, treat it as platform velocity when standing on it.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/world.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/character.rs`

**Prove it:** From a .tscn: a RigidBody3D resting on a floor falls through it on the tick after its script sets `collision_mask = 0`. A RigidBody3D box resting on a StaticBody3D with `constant_linear_velocity = Vector3(2,0,0)` gains positive x velocity and moves along +x over 60 ticks while the static body stays put. A CharacterBody3D standing on it is carried (test: `physics3d_runtime_body_props_and_conveyor`).

**Verifier note:** The mass/collision_layer/collision_mask/friction reads (physics_server_3d.rs:795, 817-818, 850) sit inside `if !self.node_to_body.contains_key(&nid)` (physics_server_3d.rs:~783). grep for '"collision_layer"|"collision_mask"|"mass"|"friction"' in physics_server_3d.rs finds no other body read: :1953-1954 are Area3D, :2875+ are tests. PhysicsBody3D::surface_velocity_at (gdphysics3d/body.rs:385) exists, but its only callers are body.rs tests (:618-639). Its own doc says 'the solver wiring is a separate step', and grep 'constant_linear_velocity' finds no node-to-body copy in gdscene, so conveyors are inert.

### 2. 3D default damping (physics/3d/default_linear_damp/angular_damp), RigidBody3D linear/angular_damp_mode, inertia and center_of_mass overrides  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** modules/godot_physics_3d/godot_body_3d.cpp:566-600 (adds the space default area damp unless an area REPLACEs, then BODY_DAMP_MODE_COMBINE/REPLACE); ProjectSettings physics/3d/default_linear_damp=0.1 and default_angular_damp=0.1; RigidBody3D.inertia, center_of_mass_mode, center_of_mass

**Patina today:** crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2658-2675 apply only physics/2d/default_*_damp. grep 'default_linear_damp' over gdscene/src and gdphysics3d/src finds no 3D reader, so every 3D rigid body runs with 0 damping where Godot uses 0.1/0.1 and drifts and spins forever. grep 'damp_mode' over physics_server_3d.rs and gdphysics3d/src returns nothing. The `inertia` override is not read by the 3D bridge: gdphysics3d/src/body.rs:538 local_inertia() derives inertia from the primary shape only. center_of_mass is read only for the _integrate_forces state (gdscene/src/integrate_forces.rs:259), not by the solver.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth (godot_body_3d.cpp:480-600): total damp is built from overlapping areas in priority order, then the space default area's damp (physics/3d/default_linear_damp 0.1, default_angular_damp 0.1) is added unless an area REPLACEd it, then the body's linear_damp/angular_damp is COMBINEd (added) or REPLACEs per linear_damp_mode/angular_damp_mode. RigidBody3D.inertia (non-zero Vector3) overrides the computed principal inertia, and center_of_mass_mode CUSTOM moves the center of mass used for torque from offset forces. Patina: main_loop.rs:2658-2675 has no 3D damp settings; no damp-mode handling exists; body.rs:538 always derives inertia from the shape. Approach: add default_linear_damp/default_angular_damp to PhysicsWorld3D, seeded from project settings in main_loop next to the 3D gravity read (main_loop.rs:2647-2656); restructure world.rs area resolution (around :1480-1530) to follow Godot's highest-first stop-on-REPLACE loop, including the default area; read linear_damp_mode/angular_damp_mode/inertia/center_of_mass_mode/center_of_mass in sync_rigid_body every tick and honour them in body.rs integrate.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/world.rs`

**Prove it:** From a .tscn with no physics settings, a RigidBody3D in zero gravity given linear_velocity (10,0,0) has slowed to roughly 10*(1-0.1*dt)^60 after 60 ticks, matching Godot within 1%. With linear_damp_mode=REPLACE and linear_damp=0 it keeps speed 10. A body with inertia=Vector3(100,100,100) spins 1/100 as fast from the same torque impulse as one with inertia (1,1,1) (test: `physics3d_damping_modes_and_inertia`).

**Verifier note:** grep 'default_linear_damp|damp_mode|"inertia"' over gdscene/src and gdphysics3d/src finds only the 2D settings read (main_loop.rs:2669-2670, physics/2d/...) and integrate_forces.rs:105, which reads inertia for the _integrate_forces state only. Nothing reads the physics/3d damping settings, no damp mode is handled, and the solver never sees an inertia override.
acceptance_criteria: 1) From a .tscn: a RigidBody3D resting on a floor falls through it on the tick after its script sets `collision_mask = 0`. A RigidBody3D box resting on a StaticBody3D with `constant_linear_velocity = Vector3(2,0,0)` gains positive x velocity and moves along +x over 60 ticks while the static body stays put. A CharacterBody3D standing on it is carried (test: `physics3d_runtime_body_props_and_conveyor`). 2) From a .tscn with no physics settings, a RigidBody3D in zero gravity given linear_velocity (10,0,0) has slowed to roughly 10*(1-0.1*dt)^60 after 60 ticks, matching Godot within 1%. With linear_damp_mode=REPLACE and linear_damp=0 it keeps speed 10. A body with inertia=Vector3(100,100,100) spins 1/100 as fast from the same torque impulse as one with inertia (1,1,1) (test: `physics3d_damping_modes_and_inertia`).

title: GDScript: parse := inference, one-line suites, ; separators, multi-line enums, typed for vars, inner-class extends
description:
[audit-key: gdscript/gdscript-parser-decls] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** run_class is what GDScriptNodeInstance::from_source uses for every scene-attached script

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/gdscript/gdscript_parser.cpp parse_variable (COLON_EQUAL inference), parse_suite (single-line suite on same line), parse_enum (newlines inside braces), parse_for (`for x: T in`), parse_class (extends on inner class)

**Patina today:** parser.rs:723-732: after `var name :` it calls parse_type_hint -> eat_ident, so `var x := 5` errors on Token::Assign (no ColonAssign token in tokenizer.rs:14-191). Same for params parser.rs:1125-1132 (`func f(x := 1)`) and const :777-782. parse_block_with_lines parser.rs:1362-1377 does skip_newlines then expect(Indent), so `if not x: return`, `func f(): pass` and one-line match arms (parse_match_branch :1222) fail. parse_for :1075-1087 expects In right after the ident (no `: int`). parse_enum_decl :963-986 never skips Newline so `enum State {\n IDLE,\n RUN\n}` fails; enum values must be an int literal (:998-1016) so `A = 1 << 2` fails. parse_inner_class :1024-1030 expects Colon right after the name. Semicolon token exists (tokenizer.rs:751) but parse_block/parse_script never consume it. Grep ':= ' over gdscript-interop/src and tests with quoted GDScript -> 0 hits.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth (gdscript_parser.cpp): `var x := expr` / `const X := expr` / `func f(a := 1)` infer the declared type from the initializer; any suite may be a single statement on the same line after ':' (if/elif/else/for/while/func/match branch/lambda); ';' separates statements on one line; enum bodies may span lines and values are constant expressions; `for i: int in range(n)` declares a typed loop var; `class Inner extends Base:` is legal.

Patina: parser.rs:723-732, :1125-1132, :777-782 reject `:=`; parse_block_with_lines :1362-1377 requires Indent; parse_for :1075-1087 rejects `: T`; parse_enum_decl :963-1022 rejects newlines and non-literal values; parse_inner_class :1024-1030 rejects `extends`; ';' unhandled.

Implement: tokenizer emits Token::ColonAssign for ':=' (or parser peeks Colon+Assign) and records an inferred type hint on the VarDecl/FuncParam (used by the typed-default bead); parse_block accepts a same-line simple statement (loop over ';'-separated stmts until Newline); enum parsing skips Newline/Indent/Dedent inside braces and evaluates values as const expressions at run_class time (interpreter.rs:15793-15822); parse_for accepts optional `: Type`; inner class accepts `extends X` and stores parent_class (interpreter.rs:15938-15951 currently hardcodes None). Wiring: run_class is what GDScriptNodeInstance::from_source uses for every scene-attached script.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/parser.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/tokenizer.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene-attached script containing `var speed := 200.0`, `func hit(dmg := 1):`, `if dmg <= 0: return`, `a = 1; b = 2`, a multi-line `enum State {\n IDLE,\n RUN = 1 << 2\n}`, `for i: int in 3:` and `class Bullet extends RefCounted:` loads through SceneTree, _ready executes and the asserted outputs match Godot (State.RUN == 4, loop sums). (test: `gdscript_parser_declaration_forms`)

**Verifier note:** The tokenizer has no ColonAssign token. In parser.rs:722-728, `var x :` goes to parse_type_hint (parser.rs:684), which calls eat_ident, so `:= 5` fails on Assign. parse_const_decl (:777-782) has the same problem. parse_block_with_lines (:1362-1377) does skip_newlines then expect(Indent), so there are no same-line suites; only lambdas special-case a single-line body (:1872). parse_for (:1075-1087) expects In right after the identifier. parse_enum_decl (:963-986) never skips newlines, and parse_enum_variant (:990-1016) accepts only an optional '-' plus an IntLit. parse_inner_class (:1024-1030) expects Colon right after the name. Semicolon is lexed (tokenizer.rs:751) but `grep -n Semicolon parser.rs` gives 0 hits.

title: Physics3D: raycast vehicle steering, per-wheel contact forces and full wheel params
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/p3d-vehicle] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** scene/3d/physics/vehicle_body_3d.cpp (_update_wheel steering rotation, _update_suspension with suspension_max_force/damping_relaxation, _update_friction with roll_influence, per-wheel engine_force/brake/steering, get_rpm/get_skidinfo); doc/classes/VehicleWheel3D.xml

**Patina today:** crates/gdphysics3d/src/vehicle3d.rs:113-114 stores `steering`, but VehicleController3D::step (vehicle3d.rs:142-264) never reads it, and `steerable` (vehicle3d.rs:63) is never consulted (grep 'steer' finds only declarations), so a VehicleBody3D cannot turn. All suspension, drive, brake and friction force is summed and applied once at the chassis centre via body.apply_force (vehicle3d.rs:262), so there is no pitch/roll torque and no per-wheel contact-point force. The bridge reads only brake, damping_compression, engine_force, steering, suspension_stiffness, suspension_travel, use_as_steering, use_as_traction, wheel_friction_slip, wheel_radius and wheel_rest_length (physics_server_3d.rs:1845-1904). grep for roll_influence, damping_relaxation, suspension_max_force and get_rpm finds nothing. Per-wheel VehicleWheel3D engine_force/brake/steering are not read.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth (vehicle_body_3d.cpp, a Bullet btRaycastVehicle port): each wheel's basis is rotated by its steering angle about the chassis up axis (steerable wheels follow VehicleBody3D.steering; VehicleWheel3D.steering/engine_force/brake override per wheel). Suspension force is clamped by suspension_max_force and damped by damping_compression when compressing and damping_relaxation when extending. Drive, brake and side friction are applied as impulses AT each wheel's contact point (yielding yaw from steering and pitch/roll from load), with roll_influence scaling the side impulse's lever arm. get_rpm(), get_skidinfo() and is_in_contact()/get_contact_body() are per wheel. Patina: vehicle3d.rs never reads steering, and step() applies one central force (vehicle3d.rs:262). Approach: rewrite VehicleController3D::step to compute per-wheel forward/side axes from steering, apply forces at contact points with PhysicsBody3D::apply_force_at_position (or impulse plus torque), add the missing params to VehicleWheel3D, and read them in sync_vehicles. Publish rpm/skidinfo in publish_wheel_state (physics_server_3d.rs:1803).

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/vehicle3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs`

**Prove it:** From a .tscn: a VehicleBody3D with 4 wheels (front use_as_steering, rear use_as_traction) on a StaticBody3D floor, with engine_force=200 and steering=0.4 from script, changes heading (its basis z rotates more than 20 degrees) within 180 ticks. With steering=0 it drives straight (heading change under 2 degrees). A wheel's get_rpm() is non-zero while driving (test: `physics3d_vehicle_steering_wheel_forces`).

**Verifier note:** In the live solver, gdphysics3d/src/vehicle3d.rs, grep 'steer' finds only the declarations (:62-63, :113-114, :86, :125). The step uses chassis rotation only to build its axes (:148-153), applies no torque or angular change, and applies one central force (:262). The bridge writes controller.steering (physics_server_3d.rs:1877), but nothing reads it. A steering-capable solver exists at gdphysics2d/src/vehicle3d.rs:266-270 (yaw from steering.tan()). The live module's header (gdphysics3d/vehicle3d.rs:10-11) says nothing constructs that solver, so it does not refute the finding. grep 'roll_influence|damping_relaxation|suspension_max_force|get_rpm' finds only a comment (physics_server_3d.rs:1889).
acceptance_criteria: From a .tscn: a VehicleBody3D with 4 wheels (front use_as_steering, rear use_as_traction) on a StaticBody3D floor, with engine_force=200 and steering=0.4 from script, changes heading (its basis z rotates more than 20 degrees) within 180 ticks. With steering=0 it drives straight (heading change under 2 degrees). A wheel's get_rpm() is non-zero while driving (test: `physics3d_vehicle_steering_wheel_forces`).

title: Physics3D: full direct-space-state params/results and Area3D hits in queries and picking
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/p3d-space-state] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D.xml (exclude, collide_with_areas, collide_with_bodies, hit_from_inside, hit_back_faces); PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D.intersect_ray returns {position, normal, collider, collider_id, rid, shape, face_index}; CollisionObject3D.input_event for Area3D via Viewport physics picking

**Patina today:** crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs:3238-3270 intersect_ray reads only from/to/collision_mask, ignores exclude, collide_with_areas, hit_from_inside and hit_back_faces, and returns only position/normal/collider (no collider_id/rid/shape/face_index). intersect_point/intersect_shape (scripting.rs:3108-3160) return only `collider`. Every query and the picking path iterate only world.bodies(). main_loop.rs:3315-3324 sets collide_with_areas=true and then calls query.intersect(self.physics_server_3d.world().bodies()), so an Area3D can never be ray-picked or receive input_event, and no script query can hit an area.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D.intersect_ray honours exclude (RID array), collide_with_bodies/areas, hit_from_inside and hit_back_faces, and returns position, normal, collider, collider_id, rid, shape and face_index. intersect_point and intersect_shape return {collider, collider_id, rid, shape}. Areas participate when collide_with_areas is set, and Viewport 3D physics picking delivers input_event and mouse_entered to Area3D. Patina: scripting.rs:3238-3270 and 3108-3160 implement a subset, and all paths (including main_loop.rs:3315-3324 picking) iterate bodies only. Approach: add an area-aware entry to gdphysics3d/src/query.rs (intersect over bodies plus world area_store using each area's shape), map exclude ObjectIds or RIDs through body_for_node/area_for_node, populate the missing result keys (shape index from extra_shapes order), and switch picking to the area-aware query gated on Area3D.input_ray_pickable.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/query.rs`

**Prove it:** A GDScript intersect_ray from (0,5,0) to (0,-5,0) with exclude=[floor_body] passes through the floor and hits a second body below it. With collide_with_areas=true it reports an Area3D placed in between, including its collider_id and shape. A mouse click through the current Camera3D over an Area3D fires that area's input_event signal, driven from MainLoop input (test: `physics3d_space_state_areas_and_exclude`).

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. gdscene/src/scripting.rs:3229-3266 (3D intersect_ray) reads only from/to/collision_mask from the params Resource and builds PhysicsRayQuery3D::new(from,to) with no exclude, collide_with_areas or hit_from_inside. It iterates world.bodies() only and returns position/normal/collider. The 2D arm at :3274-3300 does map exclude, but the 3D arm does not. intersect_point (:3108-3134) and intersect_shape (:3144-3163) return only `collider`, over bodies(). gdphysics3d/src/query.rs:900-925 has an `intersect_areas` helper for shape queries, but its only callers are in tests: grep 'intersect_areas|collide_with_areas' over gdscene/src finds it only at main_loop.rs:3319, where collide_with_areas=true is set and then query.intersect(world().bodies()) runs at :3324, so areas are never pickable. P1 is fine: raycasts, exclude-self and area picking are common.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript intersect_ray from (0,5,0) to (0,-5,0) with exclude=[floor_body] passes through the floor and hits a second body below it. With collide_with_areas=true it reports an Area3D placed in between, including its collider_id and shape. A mouse click through the current Camera3D over an Area3D fires that area's input_event signal, driven from MainLoop input (test: `physics3d_space_state_areas_and_exclude`).
