title: Engine: apply max_fps, max_physics_steps_per_frame and physics_jitter_fix from script and project settings (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: platform-os/platform-os-engine] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** script sets Engine.max_fps -> next rAF callback coalesces frames

### 1. Engine.max_fps / application/run/max_fps, Engine.max_physics_steps_per_frame, physics_jitter_fix not applied by the frame loop  (UNWIRED, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** main/main.cpp Main::iteration (max_fps frame delay, max_physics_steps_per_frame, physics_jitter_fix via MainTimerSync); core/config/engine.cpp set_max_fps/set_physics_jitter_fix

**Patina today:** Script Engine.max_fps writes ENGINE_MAX_FPS (interpreter.rs engine_max_fps/set_engine_max_fps); grep 'engine_max_fps' outside interpreter.rs finds only the re-export at gdscript-interop/src/lib.rs:38, so nothing reads it. gdscene/src/frame_driver.rs:102 FrameDriver::set_max_fps is called only from patina-web/src/engine.rs:65 / browser_runtime.rs:155 (a JS-exported setter), never from Engine.max_fps or ProjectSettings. gdcore/src/project_settings.rs:390 max_fps() has callers only in its own tests (:1142, :1162). gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:3631 writes self.max_physics_steps_per_frame (default 8, :821) into the script-visible value every step, overwriting what a script set; 'physics/common/max_physics_steps_per_frame' is never read from settings (only defaulted at project_settings.rs:606). engine_physics_jitter_fix has no reader outside interpreter/lib.rs (grep jitter_fix in gdscene/src: 0 hits).

**Implement:** Godot: Engine.max_fps (initialized from application/run/max_fps) caps the frame rate in Main::iteration; Engine.max_physics_steps_per_frame (physics/common/max_physics_steps_per_frame) bounds catch-up ticks; Engine.physics_jitter_fix (physics/common/physics_jitter_fix, default 0.5) snaps physics steps through MainTimerSync. Patina stores all three in interpreter atomics but the loop ignores them: ENGINE_MAX_FPS has no reader, FrameDriver::set_max_fps (frame_driver.rs:102) is only reachable from a JS setter, main_loop.rs:3631 overwrites the script's max_physics_steps every step, and jitter_fix has no consumer. Fix: at boot, seed Engine values from ProjectSettings (max_fps, max_physics_steps_per_frame, physics_jitter_fix); in MainLoop::step, read the script values with a generation counter (same pattern used for physics_ticks_per_second at main_loop.rs:3620) and apply them to self.max_physics_steps_per_frame and a jitter-fix accumulator in the fixed-step scheduler; in patina-web WebEngine::frame, pass gdscript_interop::engine_max_fps() to FrameDriver::set_max_fps when it changes. Wiring: script sets Engine.max_fps -> next rAF callback coalesces frames.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/engine.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/frame_driver.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene script setting Engine.max_fps = 30 in _ready makes a WebEngine driven by 60 Hz timestamps produce about 30 process frames per simulated second; a project with application/run/max_fps=20 does the same without script; Engine.max_physics_steps_per_frame = 2 set by script limits a 1-second delta to 2 physics ticks and the value still reads 2 on the next frame; physics_jitter_fix=0 vs 0.5 gives different tick counts for a jittery delta sequence (test: `engine_frame_pacing_settings_apply_to_main_loop`).

**Verifier note:** grep 'engine_max_fps|engine_physics_jitter_fix' outside interpreter.rs and tests: only the re-exports in gdscript-interop/src/lib.rs:38-44. grep 'max_fps|jitter' in patina-runner/src and gdscene/src/main_loop.rs: 0 hits. FrameDriver::set_max_fps is called outside tests only from patina-web engine.rs:65 and browser_runtime.rs:155 (the JS setter). main_loop.rs:3631 calls set_engine_max_physics_steps_per_frame(self.max_physics_steps_per_frame) unconditionally on every step, with no generation check like the one used for tps at :3619. So a value a script sets is overwritten on every step.

### 2. Engine missing methods: get_main_loop, get_physics_interpolation_fraction, get_architecture_name, get_license_info/text, get_author/copyright/donor_info, print_error_messages/print_to_stdout toggles, script-language registry, is_embedded_in_editor, get_write_movie_path; FPS is instantaneous  (PARTIAL, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** core/config/engine.cpp + doc/classes/Engine.xml

**Patina today:** Diff of extension_api.json Engine methods vs call_engine_static arms (interpreter.rs:29397-29681): 19 missing (capture_script_backtraces, get_architecture_name, get_author_info, get_copyright_info, get_donor_info, get_license_info, get_license_text, get_main_loop, get_physics_interpolation_fraction, get_script_language, get_script_language_count, get_write_movie_path, is_embedded_in_editor, is_printing_error_messages, is_printing_to_stdout, register_script_language, set_print_error_messages, set_print_to_stdout, unregister_script_language). grep for get_main_loop|get_physics_interpolation_fraction|get_architecture_name across crates (excluding tests and inspector_schema_generated.rs): 0 hits. Engine.get_frames_per_second is set to 1/last real delta (gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:3640) while Performance TIME_FPS is windowed over 1 s (performance.rs:411), so the two disagree; Godot reports the per-second frame count for both.

**Implement:** Godot's Engine exposes get_main_loop() (the SceneTree; widely used in autoloads/tool scripts), get_physics_interpolation_fraction() (fraction between physics ticks for custom interpolation), get_architecture_name() ('wasm32' on web), get_license_info/get_license_text/get_author_info/get_copyright_info/get_donor_info, set/is print_error_messages and print_to_stdout (silences push_error/print), script-language registry, is_embedded_in_editor, get_write_movie_path. Patina has none of them (interpreter.rs:29397-29681). Fix: add arms in call_engine_static; get_main_loop returns the SceneTree object handle the interpreter already uses for get_tree(); expose the main loop's physics accumulator fraction via a set_engine_physics_interpolation_fraction hook written in MainLoop::step (main_loop.rs near :3620); get_architecture_name from cfg target_arch; license/author data as static dictionaries copied from Godot's generated tables; print toggles gate the print/push_error paths; get_script_language_count = 1 (GDScript). Also report Engine.get_frames_per_second from the same 1-second window Performance uses.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene script reading Engine.get_main_loop().root gets the tree root; Engine.get_physics_interpolation_fraction() is in [0,1) and changes across steps with a 60 Hz physics / 144 Hz process delta; Engine.set_print_to_stdout(false) suppresses a following print() in captured output; get_architecture_name() is non-empty; get_license_text() contains 'MIT'; Engine.get_frames_per_second() equals Performance.get_monitor(TIME_FPS) after 2 simulated seconds (test: `engine_main_loop_and_info_methods`).

**Verifier note:** Quoted-literal grep for '"get_main_loop"', '"get_physics_interpolation_fraction"', '"get_architecture_name"', '"get_license_text"', '"is_embedded_in_editor"', '"set_print_to_stdout"' across crates (excluding tests and inspector_schema_generated.rs): 0 hits each. A bare grep 'physics_interpolation_fraction|get_main_loop' outside tests: 0 hits. main_loop.rs:3640 calls set_engine_frames_per_second(1.0 / real_delta_secs), so FPS is instantaneous as claimed. Engine.get_main_loop is common in tool and autoload scripts, so P1 could be argued, but there are workarounds (get_tree()), so P2 stands.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A scene script setting Engine.max_fps = 30 in _ready makes a WebEngine driven by 60 Hz timestamps produce about 30 process frames per simulated second; a project with application/run/max_fps=20 does the same without script; Engine.max_physics_steps_per_frame = 2 set by script limits a 1-second delta to 2 physics ticks and the value still reads 2 on the next frame; physics_jitter_fix=0 vs 0.5 gives different tick counts for a jittery delta sequence (test: `engine_frame_pacing_settings_apply_to_main_loop`). 2) A scene script reading Engine.get_main_loop().root gets the tree root; Engine.get_physics_interpolation_fraction() is in [0,1) and changes across steps with a 60 Hz physics / 144 Hz process delta; Engine.set_print_to_stdout(false) suppresses a following print() in captured output; get_architecture_name() is non-empty; get_license_text() contains 'MIT'; Engine.get_frames_per_second() equals Performance.get_monitor(TIME_FPS) after 2 simulated seconds (test: `engine_main_loop_and_info_methods`).

title: Engine: make all 39 Godot singletons script-reachable and listed by has_singleton
description:
[audit-key: platform-os/platform-os-engine-singletons] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json .singletons (39 names); core/config/engine.cpp has_singleton/get_singleton_list

**Patina today:** BUILTIN_SINGLETONS (gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:19606-19639) lists 32 names and drives Engine.has_singleton (:29497) and get_singleton_list (:29557). Missing vs jq '.singletons[].name': JavaClassWrapper, NavigationServer2D, NavigationServer3D, PhysicsServer3D, ResourceLoader, ResourceSaver, ThemeDB. ResourceSaver and JavaClassWrapper have Ident dispatch (:3990, :3955) but are deliberately unlisted. grep '"ResourceLoader"' and '"ThemeDB"' across engine-rs/crates/*.rs outside tests: hits only in gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs and gdobject/src/class_db.rs, i.e. no GDScript dispatch arm, so ResourceLoader.load()/exists() and ThemeDB.get_project_theme() have no call path; grep 'ResourceLoader\.' across engine-rs *.rs/*.gd finds no script test using it.

**Implement:** Godot registers 39 engine singletons (extension_api.json .singletons); every one answers Engine.has_singleton, appears in get_singleton_list, and is callable by bare identifier. Patina's BUILTIN_SINGLETONS (interpreter.rs:19606) has 32; ResourceLoader, ThemeDB, NavigationServer2D/3D and PhysicsServer3D have no Ident dispatch arm, so `ResourceLoader.load("res://x.tres")` fails as an undefined identifier/function. Fix: add Ident dispatch arms next to the existing ones (interpreter.rs ~3790-4110) delegating to the existing implementations: ResourceLoader.load/exists/has_cached/load_threaded_request/load_threaded_get_status/load_threaded_get (route through the same loader the global load() builtin uses; threaded variants complete synchronously with THREAD_LOAD_LOADED), ThemeDB (get_default_theme/get_project_theme/fallback_* from the theming crate), NavigationServer2D/3D and PhysicsServer3D (delegate to the server objects that gdscene already exposes, e.g. gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs), then add all seven names to BUILTIN_SINGLETONS and register them in class_db.rs so builtin_singletons_all_have_a_dispatch_arm and engine_singletons_are_classdb_classes stay true. Detailed server method coverage stays with the owning subsystems; this bead makes each name resolve and its most-used entry points work.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene script calling ResourceLoader.load on a fixture .tres gets the resource, ResourceLoader.exists is true/false correctly, ThemeDB.get_project_theme() returns without error, NavigationServer3D.map_create() and PhysicsServer3D.body_create() return valid RIDs, and for every name in extension_api.json .singletons Engine.has_singleton(name) is true and the name is in get_singleton_list() (test: `engine_all_godot_singletons_script_reachable`).

**Verifier note:** The BUILTIN_SINGLETONS list at interpreter.rs:19606-19639 has 32 entries, and ResourceLoader, ResourceSaver, ThemeDB, NavigationServer2D/3D, PhysicsServer3D and JavaClassWrapper are absent. grep -c ResourceLoader: interpreter.rs has 1 hit, a comment at :6191, and scripting.rs has 1, a doc comment. grep 'ThemeDB|NavigationServer3D' in interpreter.rs: only the NavigationServer3DManager arms (:4023, :29171). There is no Ident dispatch for ResourceLoader.load, which is a very common call. P1 could arguably be P0 given how common ResourceLoader.load is, but I am keeping P1.
acceptance_criteria: A scene script calling ResourceLoader.load on a fixture .tres gets the resource, ResourceLoader.exists is true/false correctly, ThemeDB.get_project_theme() returns without error, NavigationServer3D.map_create() and PhysicsServer3D.body_create() return valid RIDs, and for every name in extension_api.json .singletons Engine.has_singleton(name) is true and the name is in get_singleton_list() (test: `engine_all_godot_singletons_script_reachable`).

title: ProjectSettings: resolve feature-tag overrides in engine-side get()
description:

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** core/config/project_settings.h:264 `#define GLOBAL_GET(m_var) ProjectSettings::get_singleton()->get_setting_with_override(m_var)`; project_settings.cpp:410-425 resolves feature_overrides via OS::has_feature

**Patina today:** gdcore/src/project_settings.rs:205-209 ProjectSettings::get has no override resolution; every engine reader (content_scale_config :345-385, viewport_width :324, main_loop.rs:2605-2695 physics, bootstrap.rs:621 bus layout) goes through get(). get_setting_with_override_and_custom_features (:250) has zero non-test callers (grep returned only its own tests at :858-888). Script side does resolve overrides (interpreter.rs:20760-20768, 20795-20801), so script and engine disagree on e.g. display/window/size/viewport_width.web.

**Implement:** In Godot every GLOBAL_GET is get_setting_with_override, so physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second.web or display/window/stretch/mode.mobile change engine behaviour when the tag is active. Patina's ProjectSettings::get (project_settings.rs:205) ignores overrides; the override helper (:250) is only test-called. Add an active-feature list to ProjectSettings (set at boot from gdplatform::os feature tags - runner: active_feature_tags() in project_boot.rs; web: include 'web'), make get() consult `name.<tag>` first (keep a raw get_raw for the editor/saver), and set it in project_boot before configure_from_project_settings/content_scale_config read anything.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/project_settings.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs`

**Prove it:** Fixture project.godot with physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second=60 and physics_ticks_per_second.custom_tag=30 plus application/config/features containing custom_tag: booting through patina-runner yields Engine.physics_ticks_per_second == 30 and the frame driver ticks at 30 Hz; without the tag it is 60 (test: `project_settings_feature_override_engine_reads_test`).

**Verifier note:** ProjectSettings::get (project_settings.rs:205-209) checks properties and then defaults, with no override lookup. get_setting_with_override_and_custom_features (:250) is called only from its own tests (:864-888). Searching for get_with_override|with_features|active_features found no other engine path. One correction: on the script side only get_setting_with_override resolves tags (interpreter.rs:20759-20771, 20795-20801); plain get_setting reads the raw key, as Godot does. The engine-side gap is real.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture project.godot with physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second=60 and physics_ticks_per_second.custom_tag=30 plus application/config/features containing custom_tag: booting through patina-runner yields Engine.physics_ticks_per_second == 30 and the frame driver ticks at 30 Hz; without the tag it is 60 (test: `project_settings_feature_override_engine_reads_test`).

Add a wasm-safe boot entry (startProject(canvasId, pckUrl or VFS root)) that parses project.godot from the web VFS (patina-web/src/vfs.rs / web_vfs.rs), runs the same project boot used by patina-runner (move the platform-neutral parts of project_boot.rs into gdscene or a shared crate), applies ProjectSettings with the 'web' feature tag active (MainLoop::configure_from_project_settings, input map, content scale, application/run/max_fps -> WebEngine::set_max_fps, input_devices/pointing/emulate_* -> InputState), then installs the frame loop. Host-testable via WebEngine::from_project(settings_text, vfs) without a browser.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/browser_runtime.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/engine.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs`

Searching patina-web/src for project.godot|ProjectSettings|from_godot_format|configure_from|load_godot_project|boot_project found only two doc mentions of load_resource_pack (web_vfs.rs:116, vfs.rs:391). title: Render2D: drive root viewport default texture filter/repeat and clear color from ProjectSettings
description:

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** ProjectSettings.xml:3420 default_texture_filter default=1 (LINEAR), :3424 default_texture_repeat default=0; scene/main/viewport.cpp reads them into default_canvas_item_texture_filter/repeat; servers/rendering_server.cpp default_clear_color -> RenderingServer.set_default_clear_color

**Patina today:** Keys exist only in the default table (gdcore/src/project_settings.rs:686-693). gdrender2d/src/canvas_material.rs:96-99 treats unresolved TextureFilter::ParentNode as NEAREST ('Patina's project default is NEAREST'), draw.rs:168 likewise - opposite of Godot's LINEAR default, and the project value is never consulted. **Implement:** Godot resolves CanvasItem TEXTURE_FILTER_PARENT_NODE at the root to Viewport.canvas_item_default_texture_filter, seeded from rendering/textures/canvas_textures/default_texture_filter (default 1 = Linear), same for repeat; the clear color comes from rendering/environment/defaults/default_clear_color. Patina hardcodes Nearest for unresolved ParentNode (canvas_material.rs:96-99, draw.rs:168) and never reads the clear color setting. Add default_texture_filter/repeat + clear_color fields to the root gdserver2d Viewport, set them in the shared project-settings applier (map 0 Nearest,1 Linear,2 LinearMipmap,3 NearestMipmap), resolve ParentNode to the viewport default in the renderer, and add RenderingServer.set/get_default_clear_color + Viewport.canvas_item_default_texture_filter to the interpreter.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/canvas_material.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/draw.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdserver2d/src/viewport.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs`

The comment there is wrong: the table's default_texture_filter=1 (project_settings.rs:687) is LINEAR. default_clear_color() (project_settings.rs:399) is called only from tests (:1143, :1163). patina-runner/src has no clear_color reference. The other default_texture_filter hits are comments in gdeditor and gdserver2d.
acceptance_criteria: Render a fixture project (patina-runner render path) with a 2x2 checker Sprite2D scaled 8x: with no setting the sampled midpoint between texels is blended (Linear); with default_texture_filter=0 it is a hard edge; background pixels equal default_clear_color=Color(1,0,0) when set (test: `rendering_project_defaults_test`).

title: GDScript: typed vars default to the type's zero value and convert/enforce on assign
description:
[audit-key: gdscript/gdscript-typed-vars] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** instance defaults feed GDScriptNodeInstance properties that SceneTree syncs to node properties after each callback

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp / gdscript_compiler.cpp (typed members default-initialized to the type's zero value; OPCODE_ASSIGN_TYPED_BUILTIN converts int->float and errors on incompatible types)

**Patina today:** interpreter.rs:16014-16031 instantiate_class: a var with no initializer gets Variant::Nil regardless of type hint, so `var count: int` then `count += 1` operates on Nil (Godot: 0). Local VarDecl interpreter.rs:1020-1043 only calls container_typing::coerce_to_declared_type, which returns non-container values untouched (container_typing.rs:89-92), so `var speed: float = 200` stays Int and `speed / 3` integer-divides (Godot: 66.666...), and `var n: int = "x"` is accepted silently. Greps for 'fn default_for|fn zero_value_for|fn type_default|default_value_for_hint|fn typed_default' in gdscript-interop/src and gdscene/src: 0 hits; 'type_hint' in gdscene/src/scripting.rs: 0 hits.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: a member or local declared `var x: T` without an initializer starts at T's default (int 0, float 0.0, bool false, String "", Vector2(0,0), Color(0,0,0,1), Array [], Dictionary {}, Object types null); assigning to a typed slot converts compatible builtins (int->float, float->int with narrowing warning, String<->StringName) and raises a runtime error for incompatible values (gdscript_compiler.cpp typed-assign opcodes). Typed parameters are enforced the same way at call time.

Patina: interpreter.rs:16014-16031 defaults to Nil; :1020-1043 and the assignment path only handle containers via container_typing.rs:89.

Implement: a `typed_default(hint) -> Variant` and `coerce_scalar(value, hint) -> Result<Variant>` in container_typing.rs; call them from instantiate_class, Stmt::VarDecl, exec_assignment for typed members/locals (store the declared hint per slot), and for typed FuncParams in call_instance_method_impl (interpreter.rs:16299). Include inferred `:=` hints once the parser bead lands. Wiring: instance defaults feed GDScriptNodeInstance properties that SceneTree syncs to node properties after each callback.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/container_typing.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene-attached script with `var count: int`, `var speed: float = 200`, `var pos: Vector2`, `func _ready(): count += 1; print(count, " ", speed / 3, " ", pos)` prints `1 66.6666666666667 (0.0, 0.0)` when the scene runs; assigning `count = "x"` raises a runtime error reported by the runner. GDScriptNodeInstance::from_source (gdscene/src/scripting.rs:177-187) uses exactly this path. The VarDecl stored in run_class (interpreter.rs:15860-15867) copies value as-is. Local Stmt::VarDecl (interpreter.rs:1024-1043) only calls coerce_to_declared_type, which returns non-container values untouched (container_typing.rs:89-92). I grepped default_for|zero_value|type_default|typed_default|default_for_type|default_value_for in interpreter.rs, container_typing.rs and scripting.rs: 0 hits. title: ClassDB: fix gameplay-critical 3D query mask and nav-agent distance defaults
description:
[audit-key: property-defaults-and-default-theme/classdb-defaults-gameplay] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn load -> ClassDB seed -> raycast3d::get_collision_mask / navigation_agents::sync_tuning_* -> physics query / path following

**Godot ground truth:** scene/3d/physics/ray_cast_3d.h:52 and shape_cast_3d.h:52 (collision_mask = 1); doc/classes/SpringArm3D.xml collision_mask default=1; scene/2d/navigation/navigation_agent_2d.h:57 (path_desired_distance = 20.0); scene/3d/navigation/navigation_agent_3d.h:60 (target_desired_distance = 1.0)

**Patina today:** Scene load seeds every node's property bag from ClassDB defaults (gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:2691-2692; scene_tree.rs:7972-7974 create_node), so these values are live at runtime. Wrong values: gdobject/src/class_db.rs:3169 RayCast3D collision_mask=0xFFFF_FFFF, :3213 ShapeCast3D 0xFFFF_FFFF, :3250 SpringArm3D 0xFFFF_FFFF (Godot 1); :18031 NavigationAgent2D path_desired_distance=4.0 (Godot 20.0); :3431 NavigationAgent3D target_desired_distance=10.0 (Godot 1.0). Consumers read the seeded property: gdscene/src/raycast3d.rs:79-87, shapecast3d.rs:82, springarm3d.rs:86 (get_collision_mask); navigation_agents.rs:345-362 sync_tuning_2d/3d via tuned(); navigation_agents.rs:241-245 is_target_reached also falls back to 10.0 for both kinds. Found by a scripted, inheritance-aware diff of class_db.rs PropertyInfo::new defaults against every doc/classes/*.xml <member default=>: 10,799 effective (class, property) pairs compared, 10,681 matched.

**Implement:** Godot 4.6.1: RayCast3D, ShapeCast3D and SpringArm3D default collision_mask to 1 (ray_cast_3d.h:52, shape_cast_3d.h:52, SpringArm3D.xml). NavigationAgent2D.path_desired_distance defaults to 20.0 (navigation_agent_2d.h:57). NavigationAgent3D.target_desired_distance defaults to 1.0 (navigation_agent_3d.h:60). Patina: class_db.rs:3169/3213/3250 register 0xFFFF_FFFF, :18031 registers 4.0 and :3431 registers 10.0. Because packed_scene.rs:2691 seeds every node from ClassDB, any .tscn that leaves these at Godot's default (Godot omits default values when saving) gets the wrong value. Rays and spring arms then hit every layer instead of layer 1, 2D agents advance waypoints 5x too late, and 3D agents report arrival 10 m early. Fix: correct the five PropertyInfo defaults. Change the is_target_reached fallback (navigation_agents.rs:241-245) to the per-kind Godot defaults (2D 10.0, 3D 1.0). Align DEFAULT_COLLISION_MASK in raycast3d.rs/shapecast3d.rs/springarm3d.rs to 1. Check the NavigationAgent2D/3D struct defaults in gdscene/src/navigation.rs so they match. Wiring: .tscn load -> ClassDB seed -> raycast3d::get_collision_mask / navigation_agents::sync_tuning_* -> physics query / path following.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/raycast3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/shapecast3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/springarm3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation_agents.rs`

**Prove it:** Load a .tscn holding a RayCast3D with no collision_mask line and a StaticBody3D on collision_layer 2 in the ray's path, then step the SceneTree. is_colliding() is false; with the body on layer 1 it is true. Repeat for ShapeCast3D and SpringArm3D (the arm stays at full length when the obstacle is on layer 2). A NavigationAgent3D scene with no target_desired_distance reports is_target_reached() false when 5 m from the target. A NavigationAgent2D with no path_desired_distance returns 20.0 from get("path_desired_distance"). (test: `classdb_gameplay_defaults_scene_test`)

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. class_db.rs:3169/3213/3250 = Int(0xFFFF_FFFF), :18031 path_desired_distance Float(4.0), :3431 target_desired_distance Float(10.0). Godot: ray_cast_3d.h:52 and shape_cast_3d.h:52 collision_mask = 1; SpringArm3D.xml:41 default=1; navigation_agent_2d.h:57 path_desired_distance = 20.0; navigation_agent_3d.h:60 target_desired_distance = 1.0. raycast3d.rs:31 and shapecast3d.rs:26 also use DEFAULT_COLLISION_MASK 0xFFFFFFFF as the fallback, and raycast3d.rs:256 feeds it into the query. The navigation_agents.rs:241-245 is_target_reached fallback of 10.0 is confirmed, and sync_tuning_2d/3d (:343-362) read the seeded property. P1 is the right priority.
acceptance_criteria: Load a .tscn holding a RayCast3D with no collision_mask line and a StaticBody3D on collision_layer 2 in the ray's path, then step the SceneTree. is_colliding() is false; with the body on layer 1 it is true. Repeat for ShapeCast3D and SpringArm3D (the arm stays at full length when the obstacle is on layer 2). A NavigationAgent3D scene with no target_desired_distance reports is_target_reached() false when 5 m from the target. A NavigationAgent2D with no path_desired_distance returns 20.0 from get("path_desired_distance"). (test: `classdb_gameplay_defaults_scene_test`)

title: Theme: container separation constants from default theme feed layout
description:
[audit-key: property-defaults-and-default-theme/default-theme-layout-constants] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn load -> SceneTree layout pass (control::sort_container_tree / arrange_container) -> child rects consumed by control_render and input hit-testing

**Godot ground truth:** scene/theme/default_theme.cpp:1249-1268

**Patina today:** Layout reads only node overrides and defaults to 0: gdscene/src/control.rs:1421-1431 get_separation returns 0 when theme_override_constants/separation is unset. get_h_separation/get_v_separation (control.rs:1437-1458) chain to it. arrange_container (control.rs:2218-2248) passes that 0 into arrange_box/arrange_flow/arrange_grid. The SplitContainer drag hit-test (scene_tree.rs:7007) uses the same 0. Theme::default_theme (gdscene/src/theme.rs:440-600) sets no BoxContainer/GridContainer/FlowContainer/SplitContainer constants. Meanwhile control_render.rs:2209 uses theme separation with a 4 fallback, so draw and layout disagree. Every VBox/HBox/Grid without an override lays children out flush, where Godot leaves a 4 px gap.

**Implement:** Godot resolves Container spacing via get_theme_constant(), falling back to the default theme: separation=4 for Box/HBox/VBox, h/v_separation=4 for Grid and Flow, separation=12 and minimum_grab_thickness=6 for Split, margins 0 for MarginContainer (default_theme.cpp:1249-1268). Patina's layout (control.rs:1421-1458, arrange_container :2218) reads only theme_override_constants/* and defaults to 0, and Theme::default_theme (theme.rs:440) seeds none of these constants. Implementation: add the default_theme.cpp:1249-1268 constants to Theme::default_theme. Replace get_separation/get_h_separation/get_v_separation with a theme-aware lookup in this order: override, then the node's theme chain (the same node_themes resolution control_render.rs:852 uses), then ThemeDB default theme, then the Godot type fallback (HBoxContainer -> BoxContainer). Thread it into arrange_container and the SplitContainer grab test in scene_tree.rs:7007. Wiring: .tscn load -> SceneTree layout pass (control::sort_container_tree / arrange_container) -> child rects consumed by control_render and input hit-testing.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/theme.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`

**Prove it:** Load a .tscn with a VBoxContainer (no overrides) holding two 20 px-tall Controls and run the layout pass. The second child's position.y is 24. GridContainer with 2 columns gives column 2 x = col1 width + 4. An HSplitContainer with two children reserves a 12 px gap. An explicit theme_override_constants/separation = 0 still yields 0. (test: `container_default_theme_separation_test`)

**Verifier note:** control.rs:1422-1431 get_separation reads only theme_override_constants/separation and falls back to 0. h/v_separation (:1437-1458) chain to it. Every layout caller passes the result unchanged: control.rs:1959, 2228, 2245-2246, 2455, 2485 and scene_tree.rs:7007. Grepping 'BoxContainer|SplitContainer' in gdscene/src/theme.rs finds nothing. Neither class_db.rs nor packed_scene.rs seeds a 'separation' default for containers; the only match is TileSetAtlasSource at class_db.rs:20991. Godot sets these at default_theme.cpp:1249 (BoxContainer separation 4) and :1256-1257 (GridContainer 4/4). P1 stands, since every unthemed VBox/HBox is affected.
acceptance_criteria: Load a .tscn with a VBoxContainer (no overrides) holding two 20 px-tall Controls and run the layout pass. The second child's position.y is 24. GridContainer with 2 columns gives column 2 x = col1 width + 4. An HSplitContainer with two children reserves a 12 px gap. An explicit theme_override_constants/separation = 0 still yields 0. (test: `container_default_theme_separation_test`)

Check that the runtime readers (node process_mode handling in scene_tree.rs, Window/Viewport readers in viewport.rs/sub_viewport.rs) still see unset values the same way after seeding. Wiring: ClassDB -> packed_scene.rs:2691 seeding + inspector_schema ClassDB fallback + ClassDB.class_get_property_list script binding.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`

**Prove it:** From GDScript, ClassDB.class_get_property_list("Node") contains process_mode, process_priority and unique_name_in_owner, and property_get_revert returns 0/0/false. A Window node loaded from .tscn reports get("min_size") == Vector2i(0,0). **Verifier note:** grep in class_db.rs for unique_name_in_owner, process_priority, focus_neighbor_left, theme_type_variation, msaa_2d, always_on_top and angular_motion returned 0 hits each. editor_description appears only as the signal name at :1148. title: CanvasItem: make _draw texture/text/rect/circle/nine-patch commands render with Godot's parameters (+2 related)
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/r2d-draw-api] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** script _draw -> scripting.rs dispatch -> custom_draw_commands -> collect_canvas_items -> Play frame pixels; _draw -> scripting dispatch -> custom_draw_commands -> render list -> Play frame; _draw -> dispatch -> custom_draw_commands -> render list -> Play frame

### 1. _draw command conversion is lossy (texture draws, draw_string color, rect width, unfilled circle, nine-patch, Texture2D args, draw signal)  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/canvas_item.cpp draw_texture/draw_texture_rect/draw_rect/draw_circle/draw_string/draw_style_box, _redraw_callback emits NOTIFICATION_DRAW + 'draw' signal; doc/classes/CanvasItem.xml

**Patina today:** crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs draw_command_render. (1) DrawTextureRect (:1008-1020) and DrawTextureRegion (:1022-1035) become Render2DKind::Sprite with SpriteSheet::default(), which has centered=true (:66-77). So draw_texture(tex,pos) is drawn CENTRED on pos, rect.size is ignored (natural size), source_rect is ignored (the whole atlas draws) and modulate is discarded (`modulate: _`). (2) DrawString drops color (`color: _`, :1037-1049). (3) DrawRect unfilled is always width 1.0 (:910-923), because scripting.rs:4307-4317 never reads draw_rect's width. (4) draw_circle ignores filled/width (scripting.rs:4338-4348, DrawCircle has no filled field). (5) DrawNinePatch returns None (:977), so draw_style_box with a StyleBoxTexture draws nothing. (6) scripting.rs:4457-4485 draw_texture/draw_texture_rect read the texture via arg_str (scripting.rs:2875, which accepts String/StringName/NodePath only), while preload('x.png') returns Variant::Resource (interpreter.rs:6224-6226). A real Texture2D argument therefore returns None and nothing draws. (7) flush_pending_redraws (scene_tree.rs:5581-5607) never emits the 'draw' signal or NOTIFICATION_DRAW.

**Implement:** Godot (canvas_item.cpp): draw_texture places the texture's top-left at pos, tinted by modulate. draw_texture_rect stretches into rect (tile flag repeats). draw_texture_rect_region samples src_rect. draw_rect(filled=false,width) strokes at width. draw_circle(filled=false,width) strokes the circle. draw_string uses modulate and font. draw_style_box draws StyleBoxTexture as a nine-patch. After _draw the item emits NOTIFICATION_DRAW and the 'draw' signal.
Patina evidence: viewport_2d_render.rs:1008-1049 and :977, scripting.rs:4307-4348 and :4457-4485, scene_tree.rs:5581.
Implementation: in scripting.rs, accept Variant::Resource (use res.path) for every texture argument, and read the width/filled/tile/modulate args. Extend gdserver2d DrawCommand: DrawRect gets width, DrawCircle gets filled+width, DrawTextureRect gets tile. Add a Render2DKind::TextureRect { texture, rect, src_rect, modulate, tile, transpose } in viewport_2d_render.rs and rasterize it with the existing textured blit (no centring). Map DrawNinePatch onto it, or onto a new NinePatch kind that reuses gdrender2d::draw's nine-patch slicing. Carry DrawString color into the Text kind. In flush_pending_redraws, after _draw, send NOTIFICATION_DRAW and emit 'draw'.
Wiring: script _draw -> scripting.rs dispatch -> custom_draw_commands -> collect_canvas_items -> Play frame pixels.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdserver2d/src/canvas.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn Node2D at (0,0) whose script _draw calls: draw_texture(preload('res://4x4_red.png'), Vector2(10,10)); draw_texture_rect(tex, Rect2(30,0,16,16), false, Color(0,1,0)); draw_texture_rect_region(atlas, Rect2(60,0,4,4), Rect2(4,0,4,4)); draw_rect(Rect2(0,40,20,20), Color.BLUE, false, 4.0); draw_circle(Vector2(50,50), 8, Color.WHITE, false, 2.0); draw_string(font, Vector2(0,80), 'A', 0, -1, 16, Color.RED); draw_style_box(load('res://box_texture.tres'), Rect2(70,40,24,24)). Rendered via the Play-frame entry: pixel (10,10) is red and (9,9) is not (top-left, not centred). (45,15) is tinted green (stretched to 16). The region draw shows atlas cell 2 colors. (2,50) is blue but (10,50) is not (4px stroke). The circle centre is empty while its ring is white. Glyph pixels are red. Nine-patch corners are present. A connected 'draw' signal handler runs once. (test: `canvas_item_draw_params_reach_pixels`)

**Verifier note:** I spot-checked each item. (1) viewport_2d_render.rs:1008-1035: DrawTextureRect and DrawTextureRegion become Sprite with SpriteSheet::default(), which has centered:true (:63-75), and they bind `modulate: _` and `source_rect: _`. ### 2. Missing CanvasItem draw_* methods: draw_set_transform(_matrix), draw_texture_rect_region, draw_primitive, draw_mesh, draw_multimesh, per-vertex colors, textured polygons  (MISSING, P1)

**Implement:** Godot: draw_set_transform(_matrix) changes the transform of every subsequent draw_* call in the same _draw. draw_polygon/draw_primitive interpolate per-vertex colors and sample a texture with UVs. draw_mesh and draw_multimesh draw a Mesh/MultiMesh in item space. *_colors variants interpolate along the stroke.

In viewport_2d_render collect_canvas_items, fold SetTransform into a running local transform while expanding a node's custom_draw_commands. DrawPolygon fills with colors.first() (viewport_2d_render.rs:998-1006). P1 is OK.

title: Light2D: shade per item in screen space with texture-shaped point lights, z/layer ranges and light_mode
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/r2d-lighting] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** Play frame -> shade pass with view transform -> pixels

**Godot ground truth:** servers/rendering/renderer_rd/renderer_canvas_render_rd.cpp light culling (z_min/z_max, layer_min/max, item_mask), scene/2d/light_2d.cpp (PointLight2D requires texture; shadow_enabled default false per doc/classes/Light2D.xml:62), CanvasItemMaterial.light_mode

**Patina today:** gdrender2d/src/light2d.rs:1027 and :597 treat framebuffer pixel (x+0.5,y+0.5) as world space. light2d_scene.rs:106 collects light positions as global canvas transforms, with no camera or stretch applied (grep 'camera|canvas_transform|view' in light2d_scene.rs finds no matches). examples/editor.rs:316-347 applies the camera to items but then shades with world-space lights, so lights stay put on screen while the world scrolls. item_light_mask_buffer (viewport_2d_render.rs:3711-3729) starts every pixel at mask 1 and uses collect_canvas_items without the camera, so the clear background and CanvasLayer HUD pixels are lit. PointLight2D.texture is stored (light2d_scene.rs:120) but texture_path is never read in light2d.rs (grep finds only the field and its initialisers). Falloff is linear by 'range' or `1/(1+0.05d)` (light2d.rs:339-347), and Godot 4 has no 'range' property. light2d_scene.rs:115 defaults shadow_enabled to true, but Light2D.xml:62 has default=false. range_z_min/max and range_layer_min/max are never read (grep). LightMode::Unshaded/LightOnly is resolved (viewport_2d_render.rs:1209-1212) but never consumed (grep 'light_mode|LightOnly|Unshaded' finds only material.rs definitions and that resolver).

**Implement:** Godot: lights affect only canvas items (not the clear color) whose z is within [range_z_min,range_z_max], whose canvas layer is within [range_layer_min,range_layer_max] (default 0..0, so HUD layers are unlit), and whose light_mask matches. A PointLight2D's footprint is its texture scaled by texture_scale (no texture means no light), offset by offset. shadow_enabled defaults to false. CanvasItemMaterial.light_mode UNSHADED skips lighting, and LIGHT_ONLY shows only lit contribution. Everything is in canvas space, so lights move with Camera2D.
Patina evidence: see the light2d.rs:597/1027 pixel-as-world mapping, light2d_scene.rs:115/120, and viewport_2d_render.rs:1209 and :3711.
Implementation: (1) Pass the final canvas-to-screen transform (camera view x stretch) into shade_runtime_canvas_with_surfaces and transform light positions, directions and occluder polygons into screen space, scaling the footprint by the transform. (2) Replace the per-pixel mask buffer with a per-pixel item record {light_mask, z, canvas_layer, light_mode} stamped by item coverage. Background pixels get no item, so they are unlit. (3) Sample the light texture from TextureCache (alpha x color x energy), centred at position+offset and scaled by texture_scale. Drop the 'range' fallback. (4) Default shadow_enabled=false and read range_z_*/range_layer_*. (5) Honor light_mode.
Wiring: Play frame -> shade pass with view transform -> pixels.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/light2d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/light2d_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`

title: AnimationPlayer: Godot-exact play() restart, queue-clear and signal semantics
description:
[audit-key: animation/anim-player-playback] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** a GDScript `$AnimationPlayer.play("attack")` that runs twice, with the clip finishing in between, must restart the clip through interpreter.rs `play` arm -> scripting.rs animation_player_play -> process_animations

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/animation/animation_player.cpp:510-535 (same clip: rewinds to start if already at the end, returns early with no animation_started if still playing; emits current_animation_changed on clip change; clears playback_queue when not end_reached); :339-356 (animation_changed only for queue advance; current_animation_changed("") on finish)

**Patina today:** gdscene/src/animation.rs:832-840: `already_current` pushes AnimationStarted and returns without touching the position. on_animation_finished (~:1000-1020) never clears `current`. So when play("attack") runs after attack finished, the player resumes at length, the next advance() (:1183-1188) hits `position >= upper` and finishes again at once, and the clip never replays. A per-frame play("walk") emits animation_started every frame. AnimationPlayerSignal (:638-651) has no current_animation_changed. play() never clears `queue`. animation_changed is emitted on every clip switch (:870-877), where Godot emits it only when the queue advances.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth (animation_player.cpp:510-535, 339-356): calling play() on the current clip seeks to the start when the playhead is at or past the end (or to the end with from_end when it is at the start). It returns silently, with no signal, when the clip is still playing. Changing clip emits current_animation_changed(name). An explicit play() clears the queue unless end_reached. animation_changed(old,new) fires only when a queued clip takes over. A finish emits animation_finished and then current_animation_changed("").

Patina: animation.rs:832-840 resumes in place and always pushes AnimationStarted, so a non-looping clip can never be replayed by play(). This is the standard attack/jump pattern.

Approach: port the branch structure of AnimationPlayer::_play into play_ex. Add AnimationPlayerSignal::CurrentAnimationChanged and emit it in scene_tree.rs process_animations (~:4384-4400). Move AnimationChanged emission into the queue-advance path of on_animation_finished. Clear the queue in play_ex when the previous clip has not ended.

Wiring: a GDScript `$AnimationPlayer.play("attack")` that runs twice, with the clip finishing in between, must restart the clip through interpreter.rs `play` arm -> scripting.rs animation_player_play -> process_animations.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene with a 0.2 s non-looping clip moving a Sprite2D, driven by a script that calls play("attack") on two key presses 1 s apart: the sprite's x returns to the start value and re-animates after the second call. animation_started fires exactly twice. A play() each frame in _process on a looping clip emits animation_started exactly once. current_animation_changed fires with the name on start and with "" on finish. (test: `animation_player_replay_after_finish_script`)

**Verifier note:** animation.rs:836-842 (play_ex): when already_current it pushes AnimationStarted and returns without rewinding. on_animation_finished (:1021-1041) never clears `current`. advance (:1183-1187) sets playing=false at upper, so the next play(same) resumes at the end and finishes again at once. The script path scripting.rs:6457-6476 calls player.play(name) directly with no stop or rewind. AnimationPlayerSignal (:638-650) has only Started, Finished and Changed, with no CurrentAnimationChanged (grep current_animation_changed in animation.rs and scene_tree.rs: 0). AnimationChanged is pushed on every clip switch (:870+). play_ex never clears the queue; only stop (:906) and clear_queue (:937) do. Replaying attack/jump clips is a core pattern, so P0 is justified.
acceptance_criteria: A scene with a 0.2 s non-looping clip moving a Sprite2D, driven by a script that calls play("attack") on two key presses 1 s apart: the sprite's x returns to the start value and re-animates after the second call. animation_started fires exactly twice. A play() each frame in _process on a looping clip emits animation_started exactly once. current_animation_changed fires with the name on start and with "" on finish. (test: `animation_player_replay_after_finish_script`)

title: GDScript: resolve @onready initializers with scene access so $Child works
description:
[audit-key: gdscript/gdscript-onready] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** LifecycleManager (gdscene/src/lifecycle.rs:66) -> process_script_ready must be the path used by patina-runner and editor Play

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp (GDScriptInstance::notification NOTIFICATION_READY runs implicit_ready, which evaluates @onready initializers with the node in the tree, before _ready)

**Patina today:** gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:5537-5543 process_script_ready calls script.resolve_onready() and discards the Result (`let _ =`) BEFORE call_script_with_access sets a SceneTreeAccessor; scene access is only installed inside call_script_method (scene_tree.rs:5369) and cleared after every call (:5515, interpreter.rs:931-933). resolve_onready_vars (interpreter.rs:16042-16056) evaluates `$Sprite2D` via Expr::GetNode (interpreter.rs:4856-4872), which returns Err("get_node() requires scene access") with no access, aborting resolution of that and every later @onready var, leaving them Nil. The V1 gate test tests/v1_acceptance_gate_test.rs:1012-1075 only uses constant initializers (`@onready var health = 100`), and the only `@onready var x = $...` sources in the repo are parse-only/highlight tests (v1_acceptance_gate_test.rs:954, script_suite/script_editor_syntax_highlight_test.rs:39) — false-green.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: @onready member initializers are evaluated on NOTIFICATION_READY, with the node inside the tree, immediately before the user's _ready (gdscript.cpp implicit_ready). `@onready var sprite = $Sprite2D` is the canonical use.

Patina: scene_tree.rs:5537-5543 resolves @onready without a SceneTreeAccessor and swallows the error; GetNode (interpreter.rs:4856) needs scene_access, so node-reference @onready vars are Nil and the first failure aborts the rest (interpreter.rs:16042).

Implement: perform onready resolution inside the same access window as _ready — e.g. a `call_script_with_access`-style helper that removes the script from self.scripts, set_scene_access(accessor), resolve_onready(), then calls _ready, then clears access and syncs properties (mirror scene_tree.rs:5369-5380). Make resolve_onready_vars continue past a failing var and surface errors via push_error instead of `let _ =`. Wiring: LifecycleManager (gdscene/src/lifecycle.rs:66) -> process_script_ready must be the path used by patina-runner and editor Play.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** Loading a .tscn with a parent Node2D (script: `@onready var sprite = $Sprite2D` and `func _ready(): print(sprite.name)`) and a child Sprite2D through the runner/SceneTree prints `Sprite2D`; a second @onready var after a failing one still resolves. (test: `gdscript_onready_node_reference`)

**Verifier note:** process_script_ready (gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:5537-5543) runs `let _ = script.resolve_onready();` before call_script_with_access installs scene access. The resolve_onready impl (scripting.rs:363-366) just forwards to resolve_onready_vars (interpreter.rs:16042-16056) and sets no access. That function eval_expr's each default with `?`, so the first failure aborts the rest. GetNode without scene_access returns Err("get_node() requires scene access") (interpreter.rs:4870), and scene_tree.rs clears access after each call (:5376, :5472, :5515). It is the only resolve_onready call site (grep resolve_onready over gdscene/src). The only Rust/.gd sources with `@onready var x = $...|get_node|%` are tests/v1_acceptance_gate_test.rs and the syntax-highlight test; there are no .gd fixtures. The V1 gate test only uses constant initializers.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn with a parent Node2D (script: `@onready var sprite = $Sprite2D` and `func _ready(): print(sprite.name)`) and a child Sprite2D through the runner/SceneTree prints `Sprite2D`; a second @onready var after a failing one still resolves. (test: `gdscript_onready_node_reference`)

title: CanvasItem: honor project default texture filter/repeat, use_parent_material and CanvasItemMaterial particle animation
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/r2d-material-sampling] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** project.godot -> Play-frame entry -> collect_canvas_items -> blit filter

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/ProjectSettings.xml:3420 rendering/textures/canvas_textures/default_texture_filter default=1 (Linear), :3424 default_texture_repeat; scene/main/canvas_item.cpp set_use_parent_material; scene/resources/canvas_item_material.cpp particles_anim_h_frames/v_frames/loop

**Patina today:** resolve_texture_filter (crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:1233-1251) ends the parent chain with a hardcoded TextureFilter::Nearest and never reads the project setting, but Godot's default is Linear. So every unconfigured project's scaled or rotated sprites sample nearest instead of linear. resolve_texture_repeat (:1253) hardcodes Disabled the same way. use_parent_material appears only in the inspector UI JS (editor_ui.rs:3920,3978,5477), and resolve_canvas_item_material/resolve_canvas_shader_material read only the node's own properties (:1188, :1278). particles_anim appears only in class_db.rs and inspector_schema_generated.rs (grep -rln particles_anim crates/*/src).

**Implement:** Godot: a FILTER_PARENT_NODE chain that reaches the root resolves to the viewport's canvas_item_default_texture_filter, which comes from rendering/textures/canvas_textures/default_texture_filter (default 1 = Linear). Repeat resolves the same way (default 0, disabled). use_parent_material=true makes the item use its parent's material (CanvasItemMaterial or ShaderMaterial). CanvasItemMaterial.particles_animation with h/v frames and loop selects the sprite-sheet cell per particle from its anim offset/speed.
Patina: hardcoded Nearest/Disabled terminals (viewport_2d_render.rs:1250,1270). use_parent_material and particles_anim are not read by any renderer.
Implementation: thread ProjectSettings (or the resolved defaults) into collect_canvas_items via a CanvasDefaults struct, and use it as the terminal of resolve_texture_filter/repeat. In resolve_canvas_item_material and resolve_canvas_shader_material, walk to the parent while use_parent_material is true. In the particle quad path (read_particles / ParticleQuad), apply particles_anim frame selection using the existing SpriteSheet cell maths.
Wiring: project.godot -> Play-frame entry -> collect_canvas_items -> blit filter.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`

**Prove it:** A project.godot with no texture_filter setting and a Sprite2D scaled 4x of a 2x2 checker: the rendered edge pixels are interpolated (not pure checker colors), which is Linear. Setting default_texture_filter=0 makes them pure. A child Sprite2D with use_parent_material=true under a parent with CanvasItemMaterial blend_mode=ADD composites additively. A CPUParticles2D with CanvasItemMaterial particles_animation h_frames=2 draws cell 1 colors for a particle with anim_offset=0.5. (test: `canvas_default_filter_and_parent_material`)

**Verifier note:** resolve_texture_filter (viewport_2d_render.rs:1233-1247) ends in a hardcoded `TextureFilter::Nearest`. Its doc comment at :1231 says the project default is '1 = NEAREST', but ProjectSettings.xml:3420 has default=1, which is Linear in the Viewport default-filter enum, so the code misreads the enum. resolve_texture_repeat (:1253-1266) ends in a hardcoded Disabled, which matches Godot's default but ignores the setting. use_parent_material appears only in inspector_schema_generated.rs, editor_ui.rs and class_db.rs. particles_anim appears only in inspector_schema_generated.rs and class_db.rs. Neither has a renderer consumer. Priority 1 fits because every unconfigured project samples Nearest.
acceptance_criteria: A project.godot with no texture_filter setting and a Sprite2D scaled 4x of a 2x2 checker: the rendered edge pixels are interpolated (not pure checker colors), which is Linear. Setting default_texture_filter=0 makes them pure. A child Sprite2D with use_parent_material=true under a parent with CanvasItemMaterial blend_mode=ADD composites additively. A CPUParticles2D with CanvasItemMaterial particles_animation h_frames=2 draws cell 1 colors for a particle with anim_offset=0.5. (test: `canvas_default_filter_and_parent_material`)

title: CanvasItem: script-callable canvas/viewport transform queries, local mouse, viewport rect, move_to_front, instance shader params
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/r2d-canvas-queries] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** GDScript call -> scripting.rs native dispatch -> values consistent with what the Play frame draws

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/canvas_item.cpp get_canvas_transform/get_global_transform_with_canvas/get_viewport_transform/get_screen_transform/make_canvas_position_local/get_local_mouse_position/get_viewport_rect/move_to_front/set_instance_shader_parameter; scene/main/viewport.cpp canvas_transform/global_canvas_transform

**Patina today:** grep -rn --include='*.rs' '"<name>"' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdscript-interop/src (class_db excluded) returns 0 for get_canvas_transform, get_global_transform_with_canvas, get_viewport_transform, get_screen_transform, make_canvas_position_local, make_input_local, get_local_mouse_position, move_to_front, set_instance_shader_parameter, get_instance_shader_parameter, get_viewport_rect, get_canvas, get_canvas_layer_node and is_visible_in_tree (the Rust helper node2d::is_visible_in_tree at node2d.rs:300 has no script arm). call_node2d_method (node2d.rs:1557-1580) handles only get/set_global_position. grep 'canvas_transform|global_canvas_transform' in viewport_2d_render.rs, gdscene/src/viewport.rs, scene_tree.rs and examples/editor.rs finds no matches, so Viewport.canvas_transform is neither stored nor applied. Caveat: these are grep-negatives against string-literal dispatch. A generic accessor path was searched for (strip_prefix/starts_with 'get_'/'set_') and not found.

**Implement:** Godot: get_canvas_transform() is the viewport canvas transform (the Camera2D or CanvasLayer transform). get_global_transform_with_canvas() = canvas_transform * global_transform. get_viewport_transform() = viewport final transform (stretch) * canvas. get_local_mouse_position() = global inverse * global mouse. get_viewport_rect() = visible rect. move_to_front() moves the node to the last child. set_instance_shader_parameter sets a per-instance uniform. Viewport.canvas_transform is settable and drives the 2D view.
Patina: no dispatch arms exist (grep-negatives listed). Viewport.canvas_transform is absent.
Implementation: add these arms to node2d::call_node2d_method, or to a CanvasItem-level table covering Control too. Compute the canvas transform from the active Camera2D (viewport_2d_render::camera2d_view_transform logic moved to gdscene, or a published camera transform) and the CanvasLayer ancestor. Store a root Viewport canvas_transform that apply_camera2d_view writes and scripts can override. Store instance shader params as `instance_shader_parameters/<name>` properties that resolve_canvas_shader_material merges.
Wiring: GDScript call -> scripting.rs native dispatch -> values consistent with what the Play frame draws.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`

With a mouse event at window (160,90), get_local_mouse_position() = (0,-50). get_viewport_rect().size = (320,180). move_to_front() reorders the node in get_children() and in draw order. set_instance_shader_parameter('tint', Color.RED) changes the rendered pixel. (test: `canvas_item_canvas_space_queries`)

The only generic get_ prefix dispatch is navigation_agents.rs:183, which is scoped to navigation. Two related arms do exist: "get_canvas_item" (scripting.rs:3734) and Input.get_global_mouse_position (interpreter.rs:9332). They are not among the claimed-missing methods. get_local_mouse_position appears only in a doc comment (item_views.rs:501).

With a mouse event at window (160,90), get_local_mouse_position() = (0,-50). get_viewport_rect().size = (320,180). move_to_front() reorders the node in get_children() and in draw order. set_instance_shader_parameter('tint', Color.RED) changes the rendered pixel. title: Render2D: render each SubViewport's canvas offscreen and composite via SubViewportContainer/ViewportTexture
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/r2d-subviewport] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** Play frame -> offscreen SubViewport passes -> container/ViewportTexture blits -> main frame

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/viewport.cpp (each Viewport owns its World2D canvas), scene/gui/subviewport_container.cpp, scene/main/viewport.cpp ViewportTexture

**Patina today:** collect_canvas_items -> push_draw_order (crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:1060-1126) recurses through every child from tree.root_id() with no Viewport boundary. grep 'SubViewport|ViewportTexture' in viewport_2d_render.rs, texture_cache.rs and examples/editor.rs finds no matches. So a SubViewport's Node2D children are composited straight into the main frame at their own coordinates. gdscene/src/sub_viewport.rs has its own ColorBuffer (:107-162) that the canvas pipeline never fills.

**Implement:** Godot: a SubViewport has its own canvas. Its children never draw into the parent viewport. The result appears only through a SubViewportContainer (stretch/stretch_shrink) or a ViewportTexture assigned to a Sprite2D/TextureRect, and it respects render_target_update_mode and transparent_bg.
Patina: push_draw_order walks into SubViewport subtrees, so they draw into the root frame.
Implementation: in push_draw_order, stop at nodes with is_class('Viewport') (not root). Before the main raster, render each SubViewport subtree with the same entry (its own size, clear color and camera) into a FrameBuffer registered in TextureCache under `viewport://<node_id>`. Make SubViewportContainer emit a Sprite-like textured rect of that key at its rect, and resolve ViewportTexture (viewport_path) properties to that key in node2d::get_texture_path. Honor UPDATE_DISABLED/ONCE/ALWAYS.
Wiring: Play frame -> offscreen SubViewport passes -> container/ViewportTexture blits -> main frame.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/sub_viewport.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs`

In the Play-frame render, pixel (5,5) is NOT red (no leak into the root), (110,110) is red (container), and the sprite area around (300,50) is red. (test: `subviewport_canvas_renders_offscreen`)

**Verifier note:** push_draw_order (viewport_2d_render.rs:~1060) recurses through canvas_order::draw_ordered_children with no Viewport check. grep 'SubViewport|is_class("Viewport|"Viewport"' in viewport_2d_render.rs, canvas_order.rs and examples/editor.rs finds nothing. Only input forwarding and layout exist: control.rs:2293 (container sizing) and control.rs:2547 (click mapping). ViewportTexture appears only in sub_viewport.rs, lib.rs, local_to_scene.rs and class_db, never in the render path. The rendering half is genuinely missing, so the MISSING label holds.

title: Meshes: decode ArrayMesh _surfaces (all ARRAY_FORMAT bits incl. compression) and add colour/tangent/UV2 channels
description:

title: Shadows: camera-fit PSSM cascades with splits/blend, shadow_blur PCF in both pipelines
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/render3d-shadows] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** tscn DirectionalLight3D to editor/Play software and GPU frames

**Godot ground truth:** DirectionalLight3D.xml:21-24 (max_distance 100, mode PSSM4 default); Light3D.xml:116 shadow_blur default 1.0; servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/light_storage.cpp shadow cascades fit to camera frustum

**Patina today:** shadow_map.rs:16 SHADOW_MAP_SIZE 256 and :21 SHADOW_EXTENT 20; directional_light_view_matrix (:185-211) places the light at dir*-50 around the world origin, independent of camera. generate_directional_cascades (:1406) only called from tests (:1524-1585). shadow_split_1..3 and blend_splits are parsed (render_server_3d.rs:2511-2522) but no renderer reads them (grep shadow_split in gdrender3d/src: 0 non-test hits). shadow_blur never read from a node (grep shadow_blur literal in gdscene: 0) and Light3D defaults it to 0.0 (gdserver3d/src/light.rs:558,603,648). WGSL directional_shadow_factor does one textureLoad, no PCF (wgpu_pipeline.rs:386-401). directional_shadow_mode unread.

**Implement:** Godot fits directional shadows to the camera frustum up to directional_shadow_max_distance with 1/2/4 PSSM splits (directional_shadow_split_1..3, blend_splits) and softens with shadow_blur and shadow_filter_quality. Patina uses one 256px map covering +-20 m around world origin, so shadows vanish beyond 20 m and are blocky. Implement: pass camera transform/frustum into shadow generation, compute splits from the light's shadow_split values and directional_shadow_mode, call generate_directional_cascades from renderer.rs and wgpu ensure_shadow_atlas, select cascade per fragment (software shader.rs and WGSL), blend when blend_splits, read shadow_blur (default 1.0) and shadow_filter_quality in sync_light_properties and the editor SceneLight3D copy, add PCF taps in WGSL. Wiring: tscn DirectionalLight3D to editor/Play software and GPU frames.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/shadow_map.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs`

**Prove it:** A Play render with the camera and a shadow-casting cube both at x=60 shows the cube's shadow on the ground (currently none); with directional_shadow_mode 0 vs 2 the near shadow edge sharpness differs; GPU and software shadow masks agree within tolerance. (test: directional_shadow_follows_camera_cascades)

**Verifier note:** shadow_map.rs:16 sets SHADOW_MAP_SIZE to 256 and :21 sets SHADOW_EXTENT to 20.0, used in the ortho bounds at :217-220. generate_directional_cascades (:1406) is called only at :1524-1585, inside #[cfg(test)] (:1493). grep shadow_split|directional_shadow_mode in gdrender3d/src: 0 hits. The splits are copied onto Light3D (render_server_3d.rs:2511, viewport_3d_render.rs:2412-2414) but nothing renders with them. The software shader does PCF with shadow_blur (shader.rs:701-705, fed from renderer.rs:877). However Light3D always defaults shadow_blur to 0.0 (light.rs:558,603,648), and grep shadow_blur in gdscene/src and gdeditor/src (excluding the generated inspector schema) finds no reader of the node property. PARTIAL/P1 holds.

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/Environment.xml:202 reflected_light_source, :254 sky_rotation, :41 adjustment_color_correction, :180 glow_map; servers/rendering/renderer_rd/environment/sky.cpp radiance

**Patina today:** Environment3D fields (gdserver3d/src/environment.rs:190-308) and from_properties keys (:400-700) have no reflected_light_source, ambient_light_sky_contribution, sky_rotation, adjustment_color_correction, glow_mix, glow_normalized, glow_map (grep for these in gdrender3d/gdserver3d: 0 hits). **Implement:** Godot reflects the sky radiance on every surface (reflected_light_source Background/Sky), blends ambient with sky by ambient_light_sky_contribution, rotates sky lookups by sky_rotation, applies adjustment_color_correction (1D gradient or 3D LUT) after brightness/contrast/saturation, and supports glow_mix/glow_normalized/glow_map. Implement: add fields and parse keys in environment.rs; build a low-res sky radiance lookup per frame (sample_sky_color per direction with roughness-blurred mips) and use it in software pbr_shade and WGSL for the specular term; apply sky_rotation basis in pixel_view_direction and radiance sampling; add LUT step in postprocess apply_camera_post. **Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/environment.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/shader.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/postprocess.rs`

(test: environment_sky_reflections_and_lut_render)

**Verifier note:** reflected_light, sky_contribution, sky_rotation, color_correction, glow_mix, glow_normalized and glow_map have 0 hits in gdserver3d/src, gdrender3d/src and gdscene/src. environment_ambient_color (gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs:1779-1816) averages 6 sky directions into one flat colour. title: ResourceLoader: add the singleton (threaded load, exists, cache modes) and give load() Godot's cache/null semantics
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/resource-loader-api] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** scripts in a booted project

**Godot ground truth:** core/io/resource_loader.cpp; doc/classes/ResourceLoader.xml (load_threaded_request/get_status/get, exists, has_cached, get_cached_ref, get_dependencies, CacheMode)

**Patina today:** BUILTIN_SINGLETONS (interpreter.rs:19606-19640) omits ResourceLoader and ResourceSaver. `grep '"ResourceLoader"'` over gdscript-interop/src: 0 hits, and every ResourceLoader method name (load_threaded_request, load_threaded_get_status, load_threaded_get, exists, has_cached, get_cached_ref, get_dependencies) has 0 hits. ResourceSaver dispatches only 'save' (interpreter.rs:3991, 15551). The load() builtin (interpreter.rs:6160-6268) has no cache, as its own comment at :6191 notes, so two loads return distinct objects. For a missing file it returns a non-null placeholder ResourceRef, a class guessed from the extension. Sub-resources of a loaded .tres stay as strings like "SubResource:<id>" (load_text_resource, interpreter.rs:185-200, copies raw properties).

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: ResourceLoader.load(path, type_hint, cache_mode) returns the same instance for repeated loads (CACHE_MODE_REUSE) and null with an error when the file is missing. Nested SubResource/ExtResource properties come back as live Resource objects. load_threaded_request/get_status/get is the loading-screen API: status values THREAD_LOAD_IN_PROGRESS/LOADED/FAILED/INVALID_RESOURCE, plus a progress array. exists, has_cached, get_cached_ref, get_dependencies and get_recognized_extensions_for_type round out the class. ResourceSaver adds get_recognized_extensions and flags.

Patina today: there is no ResourceLoader identifier. The `load` builtin (interpreter.rs:6160) never caches, returns a placeholder for missing paths, and leaves sub-resources as "SubResource:id" strings.

Approach: add a per-interpreter (or global) resource cache keyed by the resolved res:// path, reusing gdresource::cache::ResourceCache. Make load() return Nil plus push_error for a nonexistent file and honor type_hint and cache_mode. Resolve SubResource/ExtResource values into nested Variant::Resource. Add a ResourceLoader dispatch arm and list it in BUILTIN_SINGLETONS. load_threaded_request may load synchronously on request (Godot's web build runs single-threaded loads) as long as get_status reports LOADED and fills the progress array, and load_threaded_get returns the cached instance. Add the remaining methods to the ResourceSaver arm.

Wiring: scripts in a booted project.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/cache.rs`

**Prove it:** In a booted project script: `load("res://a.tres") == load("res://a.tres")` is true. load("res://missing.tres") == null. A .tres whose property is SubResource returns an object whose .get("x") works. ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request("res://lvl.tscn") followed by polling load_threaded_get_status yields THREAD_LOAD_LOADED with progress[0] == 1.0, and load_threaded_get(...).instantiate() adds a node. ResourceLoader.exists("res://a.tres") is true and exists for a missing path is false (test: `resource_loader_singleton_threaded_and_cache`).

**Verifier note:** grep '"ResourceLoader"|load_threaded' in gdscript-interop/src: 0 hits. ResourceSaver dispatch exists only for save, is deliberately left out of BUILTIN_SINGLETONS (interpreter.rs:3981-3996), and has no Expr::Ident arm. The load() builtin requires exactly 1 arg (:6161), so a type_hint/cache_mode argument raises TypeError. Its comment admits it does no caching (:6191), and it returns a placeholder ResourceRef for missing paths (:6226-6262). P1 holds.
acceptance_criteria: In a booted project script: `load("res://a.tres") == load("res://a.tres")` is true. load("res://missing.tres") == null. A .tres whose property is SubResource returns an object whose .get("x") works. ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request("res://lvl.tscn") followed by polling load_threaded_get_status yields THREAD_LOAD_LOADED with progress[0] == 1.0, and load_threaded_get(...).instantiate() adds a node. ResourceLoader.exists("res://a.tres") is true and exists for a missing path is false (test: `resource_loader_singleton_threaded_and_cache`).

title: Image: back GDScript Image with gdresource::Image and bind its full method surface (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/image-texture-scripting] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** scripts in a booted project; script -> ImageTexture -> Sprite2D.texture -> renderer frame output

### 1. Image script surface (load_*_from_buffer, save_png/jpg/webp(_to_buffer), resize, fill(_rect), blit/blend, convert, crop, flip, rotate, mipmaps, get_region, get_used_rect)  (UNWIRED, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** core/io/image.cpp; doc/classes/Image.xml

**Patina today:** gdresource/src/image.rs implements fill (256), flip_x/flip_y (265/280), convert (302), resize with Nearest/Bilinear/Cubic/Lanczos (396/444), get_region (450), crop (462), rotate_90/180 (473-497), fill_rect (504), get_used_rect (519), blit_rect(_mask) (547/563), blend_rect(_mask) (588/603) and generate_mipmaps (691). Scripts instead get a separate IMAGES/ImageState map. call_image_static (interpreter.rs:27687) supports only create/create_empty. call_image_instance (interpreter.rs:27724+) supports get_width/get_height/get_size/premultiply_alpha/detect_alpha/get_format/is_empty/set_pixel/get_pixel. A jq diff of the 82 Image API methods against gdscript-interop/src finds ~60 absent, including resize, fill, blit_rect, load_png_from_buffer and save_png.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: Image (core/io/image.cpp) covers create/create_from_data/set_data/get_data, load/load_from_file and load_png/jpg/webp/tga/bmp/svg_from_buffer, save_png/jpg/webp/exr(+_to_buffer), resize(interpolation), resize_to_po2, crop, flip_x/y, rotate_90/180, convert, fill/fill_rect, blit_rect(_mask), blend_rect(_mask), get_region, get_used_rect, generate_mipmaps/clear_mipmaps/has_mipmaps, get_pixelv/set_pixelv, copy_from and adjust_bcs.

Patina today: the real implementation is gdresource/src/image.rs (lines 256-691), but the interpreter keeps its own ImageState map (interpreter.rs:27607-27860) that exposes about 10 methods.

Approach: replace ImageState with gdresource::Image (or wrap it) in the IMAGES handle table. Map Godot Format ints to ImageFormat and Interpolation ints to the enum. Bind every method above, with buffer decoders routed through gdresource importers (png/webp/tga/bmp/svg/hdr) and encoders through the image crate's png encoder (webp lossless via image-webp). Keep CameraFeed's use of IMAGES working.

Wiring: scripts in a booted project. The resulting Image must be consumable by ImageTexture (sibling bead).

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/image.rs`

**Prove it:** In a booted project script: Image.create_empty(4, 4, false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8), then fill(Color.RED), fill_rect(Rect2i(0,0,2,2), Color.BLUE), resize(8, 8, Image.INTERPOLATE_NEAREST), save_png_to_buffer() and Image.new().load_png_from_buffer(buf). Afterwards get_pixel(0,0) == BLUE, get_pixel(7,7) == RED and get_size() == Vector2i(8,8). blit_rect copies a region, and get_used_rect on a transparent image with one opaque pixel returns that pixel's rect (test: `image_script_surface_wired`).

**Verifier note:** An awk dump of the match arms in interpreter.rs:27687-27900 lists only create|create_empty, get_width, get_height, get_size, premultiply_alpha, detect_alpha, get_format, is_empty, set_pixel and get_pixel. Image handles route only to call_image_instance (:10839-10840). The quoted "resize" hits (:11381, :14882, :22334) are Array/PackedArray/StreamPeerBuffer resize, not Image. grep '"save_png"|"blit_rect"|"load_png_from_buffer"|"fill_rect"' got 0 hits. P1 holds.

### 2. ImageTexture class (create_from_image, update, set_image, get_image, set_size_override) and Texture2D.get_image  (MISSING, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** scene/resources/image_texture.cpp; doc/classes/ImageTexture.xml

**Patina today:** `grep -rn '"ImageTexture"'` over gdobject/src, gdscript-interop/src and gdscene/src returns 0 hits. The only matches are the editor's inspector_schema_generated.rs:4600 and editor_plugin.rs:1123, plus a test .tscn. class_db.rs registers only ImageTextureLayered/ImageTexture3D (23167-23538). `grep create_from_image` over gdscript-interop/src: 0 hits. A procedurally generated texture assigned to a Sprite2D/TextureRect cannot be created from script.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: ImageTexture.create_from_image(image) makes a Texture2D from an Image. update(image) replaces pixels at the same size and format, set_image, get_image, set_size_override and get_format complete the class, and any Texture2D.get_image() returns its pixels. Minimaps, generated noise, screenshots and downloaded avatars all go through it. In .tscn an ImageTexture sub_resource carries `image = SubResource("Image_x")`, and the Image sub_resource has `data = {"data": PackedByteArray, "format": "RGBA8", "width", "height", "mipmaps"}`.

Patina today: the class is not registered in ClassDB and there is no script dispatch for it.

Approach: register ImageTexture (parent Texture2D) in class_db.rs with its methods and properties. Add a script dispatch that converts an Image handle into a texture resource and registers its pixels with the 2D renderer's texture table under a synthetic path, the same path DrawTextureRect looks up. update() rewrites those pixels. Parse ImageTexture/Image sub_resources in packed_scene so scene-authored ImageTextures render too. Add Texture2D.get_image for loaded textures.

Wiring: script -> ImageTexture -> Sprite2D.texture -> renderer frame output.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs`

**Prove it:** A booted project script builds a 2x2 red Image, then `$Sprite2D.texture = ImageTexture.create_from_image(img)`. The rendered frame (patina-runner headless frame dump) has red pixels at the sprite position. Calling update() with a blue image turns them blue on the next frame. ClassDB.class_exists("ImageTexture") is true (test: `imagetexture_script_created_renders`).

**Verifier note:** I could not refute it. `grep -rln 'ImageTexture' --include='*.rs'` (excluding tests) finds the name only in gdeditor (inspector_schema_generated.rs:4600, editor_plugin.rs:1123, editor_ui.rs), in a comment at gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:1847, and in class_db.rs for ImageTextureLayered/ImageTexture3D (23167-23538). `grep '"ImageTexture"'` finds only the two editor files. `create_from_image` matches only BitMap.create_from_image_alpha (gdresource/src/bit_map.rs:141). `grep 'ImageTexture'` over gdscript-interop/src: 0 hits. The only `"get_image"` registration is on Noise (class_db.rs:22783), not Texture2D. Status and P1 stand.
acceptance_criteria: 1) In a booted project script: Image.create_empty(4, 4, false, Image.FORMAT_RGBA8), then fill(Color.RED), fill_rect(Rect2i(0,0,2,2), Color.BLUE), resize(8, 8, Image.INTERPOLATE_NEAREST), save_png_to_buffer() and Image.new().load_png_from_buffer(buf). Afterwards get_pixel(0,0) == BLUE, get_pixel(7,7) == RED and get_size() == Vector2i(8,8). blit_rect copies a region, and get_used_rect on a transparent image with one opaque pixel returns that pixel's rect (test: `image_script_surface_wired`). 2) A booted project script builds a 2x2 red Image, then `$Sprite2D.texture = ImageTexture.create_from_image(img)`. The rendered frame (patina-runner headless frame dump) has red pixels at the sprite position. Calling update() with a blue image turns them blue on the next frame. ClassDB.class_exists("ImageTexture") is true (test: `imagetexture_script_created_renders`).

title: GDScript: load base scripts and resolve inherited methods, vars and super calls
description:
[audit-key: gdscript/gdscript-inheritance] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]
