comments.text:
HARNESS DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED AFTER REPORTING (TurquoiseCastle, 05:39Z). Resent the completion (supersedes msg 89711).

THE DEFECT: EngineBootstrap does NOT configure res://. Only the full project_boot path calls gdcore::set_path_roots — I checked all four of bootstrap's init phases (init_core, init_resources, init_servers, init_scene) and none touches it. So load_base_class could not read res://base.gd, the base would never load, and the acceptance test would have failed showing NO INHERITANCE rather than a diagnosis. That is a property of the harness, not of the code under test.

THE FIX: the acceptance test's boot() helper now calls gdcore::file_access::set_path_roots(Some(dir.to_path_buf()), None) before booting. The identical call, for the identical reason, already exists in gltf_packed_scene_instancing_test.rs:114. A real game boot goes through project_boot, which installs the roots itself, so this only makes the harness match reality. gdcore is a normal dependency of patina-runner, so no manifest change.

HOW I NEARLY SHIPPED IT: the precedent test I copied the harness from (gdscript_onready_node_reference.rs:42) carries a comment asserting that "boot_project/EngineBootstrap install process-global res:// path roots". That claim is WRONG for EngineBootstrap, and that test passes anyway because a .tscn's ext_resource paths resolve by a different mechanism than FileAccess. I checked the claim against the source instead of inheriting it, which is the only reason this was caught before the verifier — the same environmental-failure class that cost me a verify on pat-mgixk.10, where a fixture problem looked exactly like a logic bug.

⚠️ GENERAL LESSON FOR THIS REPO: a comment in a green test is not evidence about the code it describes. It can be stale, or true only for the narrow path that test exercises. Verify the claim, especially when it is the thing standing between your fixture and the filesystem.

title: TSCN parser: any-Variant dictionary keys, typed Dictionary[K,V], RID/Signal/Callable/Resource literals
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/tscn-parser-completeness] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** scene load in patina-runner -> node property -> script reads it

**Godot ground truth:** core/variant/variant_parser.cpp:940 (RID), :964 (Signal), :979 (Callable), :1089 (Resource), :1187 (Dictionary[K,V]); VariantWriter::write :2241 writes Dictionary[ for typed dicts

**Patina today:** gdresource/src/loader.rs:987-1017 parse_dictionary rejects any key not starting with '"' (error 'dictionary key must be a quoted string'), so {1: "a"}, {&"name": v} and {Vector2i(0,0): v} fail. `grep 'Dictionary\['` over loader.rs and saver.rs: 0 hits, so the typed-dictionary literal Godot 4.4+ writes for `@export var d: Dictionary[String, int]` hits 'unrecognized value' (loader.rs:803). `grep '"RID"|"Signal"|"Callable"'` over loader.rs: 0 hits. gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:494-503 and :524-535 then drop the property with only a tracing::warn ('skipping unparseable value'), which is a silent skip at runtime.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: variant_parser.cpp parses dictionary keys as arbitrary Variants: ints, &StringName, Vector2i, and so on. Godot 4.4+ writes typed dictionaries as `Dictionary[KeyType, ValueType]({...})` (:1187, writer :2241) and typed arrays as `Array[T]([...])`. It also parses `RID()`/`RID(n)`, `Signal()`, `Callable()` and `Resource("res://path")` (:940-1089).

Patina today: parse_dictionary (loader.rs:987) requires quoted-string keys. There is no Dictionary[ handling and no RID/Signal/Callable/Resource arms, and packed_scene.rs:494-535 silently drops any property that fails to parse. An exported `Dictionary[int, String]` var, a TileSet custom-data dictionary with int keys, or a `{&"idle": ...}` dict all vanish at load.

Approach: rewrite parse_dictionary to split each entry at the top-level ':' (outside strings, brackets and parens) and parse the key with parse_variant_value. Add a `Dictionary[` arm that parses the two type names and builds a typed dictionary, using ContainerType::from_hint_name as as_typed_array does. Add RID/Signal/Callable null-literal arms and Resource("path") as an ExtResource-style path reference. Make scene_saver/saver re-emit all of these so a round-trip is lossless.

Wiring: scene load in patina-runner -> node property -> script reads it.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/loader.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/saver.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_saver.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn whose root has a script with `@export var a: Dictionary[int, String]` and `@export var b: Dictionary` sets `a = Dictionary[int, String]({1: "x", 2: "y"})` and `b = {&"k": Vector2i(1, 2), 3: [1]}`, and boots through patina-runner. In _ready, a[1] == "x" and a.is_typed() is true, b[&"k"] == Vector2i(1,2) and b[3] == [1]. Saving the scene with scene_saver and reparsing it yields identical values (test: `tscn_typed_dict_and_variant_keys_load`).

**Verifier note:** gdresource/src/loader.rs:987-1017: parse_dictionary rejects any pair not starting with '"' (the error is at :999). `grep 'Dictionary\['` in loader.rs: 0 hits. Only `Array[` is handled (:765), and the fallthrough is 'unrecognized value' (:801). `grep 'RID|Callable|Signal|"Resource'` in loader.rs: no parser arms. There is no other tscn value parser: the only parse_variant_value is loader.rs:306 (gdscript-interop parse_dict is the GDScript parser). packed_scene.rs:494-503 and :524-535 drop failed values with only a tracing::warn. PARTIAL at P1 stands.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn whose root has a script with `@export var a: Dictionary[int, String]` and `@export var b: Dictionary` sets `a = Dictionary[int, String]({1: "x", 2: "y"})` and `b = {&"k": Vector2i(1, 2), 3: [1]}`, and boots through patina-runner. In _ready, a[1] == "x" and a.is_typed() is true, b[&"k"] == Vector2i(1,2) and b[3] == [1]. Saving the scene with scene_saver and reparsing it yields identical values (test: `tscn_typed_dict_and_variant_keys_load`).

title: Add real Gradient, Curve, GradientTexture1D/2D resources: ClassDB, script API, sampling, texture baking
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/gradient-curve-resources] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/doc/classes/Gradient.xml, Curve.xml, GradientTexture1D.xml, GradientTexture2D.xml; upstream/godot/scene/resources/gradient.cpp, curve.cpp, gradient_texture.cpp

**Patina today:** No Rust type: grep 'struct Gradient' / 'struct Curve\b' in crates = 0. Only .tscn shape-sniffing: gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:1023-1056 copies offsets/colors from a color_ramp bag (GradientTexture1D->Gradient two-hop) into __color_ramp_*; :1057-1089 and :5877 bake Curve _data for scale_curve/width_curve. Own code admits the gap: gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs:1293 'Patina has no Curve resource, so the crossfade stays linear'; gdserver3d/src/primitive_mesh.rs:468 'this crate has no Curve type'. No ClassRegistration for Gradient/Curve/GradientTexture1D/GradientTexture2D (CurveTexture IS registered at class_db.rs:23378, whose 'curve' property has no backing class). Curve with points (0,0),(1,1) linear tangents: sample(0.25)==0.25 within 1e-4. A .tscn Sprite2D with GradientTexture2D (fill LINEAR, black->white, 64x64) renders a left pixel near black and a right pixel near white. title: Register Image + ImageTexture in ClassDB and expose the full Image API and ImageTexture.create_from_image to GDScript
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/image-imagetexture] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/doc/classes/Image.xml, upstream/godot/doc/classes/ImageTexture.xml; extension_api.json: Image inherits Resource (76 methods), ImageTexture inherits Texture2D (5 methods: create_from_image, get_format, set_image, update, set_size_override)

**Patina today:** class_db.rs has no '"Image"' or '"ImageTexture"' registration (only ImageTexture3D at class_db.rs:23536 and ImageTextureLayered at :23179). Scripts reach Image only through bare-identifier arms. Statics: interpreter.rs:4097 calls call_image_static at :27687, which handles only create and create_empty. Instance methods: call_image_instance at interpreter.rs:27724 handles get_width, get_height, get_size, premultiply_alpha, detect_alpha, get_format, is_empty, set_pixel and get_pixel. That makes 11/76 Godot methods reachable. The gdresource Image (crates/gdresource/src/image.rs:101-691) already implements resize, crop, rotate, fill_rect, blit_rect, blend_rect, convert and generate_mipmaps, none of them script-exposed, and the interpreter uses a separate struct (img.width / img.pixels). ImageTexture is wired nowhere: grep -rn 'ImageTexture' over gdresource/src, gdscene/src, gdscript-interop/src, gdrender2d/src and patina-runner/src (excluding the 3D/Layered variants) returns only a comment at gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:1847. grep for 'create_from_image|"set_image"|"get_image"' finds only PortableCompressedTexture2D and BitMap. As a result ClassDB.class_exists("Image") is false (ClassDB.class_exists at interpreter.rs:20282 reads gdobject::class_exists), and ImageTexture.create_from_image(img) is undefined.

**Implement:** Godot 4.6.1 Image (Resource, 76 methods) and ImageTexture (Texture2D) are the standard way to build textures at runtime: procedural generation, screenshots, minimaps, drawing tools. Patina has neither class in ClassDB. Image has 11/76 methods reachable from scripts, through a separate interpreter struct rather than gdresource::Image, which already implements most of the operations. ImageTexture does not exist at runtime at all, so ImageTexture.create_from_image(img) followed by assigning it to Sprite2D.texture or TextureRect.texture cannot work. Steps: (1) Register Image (parent Resource) and ImageTexture (parent Texture2D) in class_db.rs with their methods and properties. (2) Back the script Image handle with gdresource::Image and dispatch the remaining methods: resize, crop, fill, fill_rect, blit_rect, blend_rect, convert, flip_x/flip_y, rotate_*, get_region, get_used_rect, load_png_from_buffer/load_jpg_from_buffer/load_webp_from_buffer, save_png_to_buffer, get_data, set_data, generate_mipmaps and so on. (3) Implement ImageTexture.create_from_image, set_image, update, get_format and set_size_override, and make the result assignable to any texture property so the 2D renderer draws it. (4) Load and save .tres files with type="ImageTexture".

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/image.rs`

**Prove it:** 1. A GDScript calls `var img = Image.create(4,4,false,Image.FORMAT_RGBA8); img.fill(Color.RED); var tex = ImageTexture.create_from_image(img); $Sprite2D.texture = tex`. The rendered frame shows red pixels at the sprite's location.
2. `tex.update(img2)` changes the drawn pixels on the next frame.
3. ClassDB.class_exists("Image") and ClassDB.class_exists("ImageTexture") are true, and ClassDB.is_parent_class("ImageTexture","Texture2D") is true.
4. img.resize, crop, blit_rect and get_region match Godot's documented results on a 4x4 fixture.
5. Edge cases: an empty Image passed to create_from_image returns null with an error, as in Godot; set_pixel out of bounds raises an error and does not panic.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A GDScript calls `var img = Image.create(4,4,false,Image.FORMAT_RGBA8); img.fill(Color.RED); var tex = ImageTexture.create_from_image(img); $Sprite2D.texture = tex`. The rendered frame shows red pixels at the sprite's location.
2. `tex.update(img2)` changes the drawn pixels on the next frame.
3. ClassDB.class_exists("Image") and ClassDB.class_exists("ImageTexture") are true, and ClassDB.is_parent_class("ImageTexture","Texture2D") is true.
4. img.resize, crop, blit_rect and get_region match Godot's documented results on a 4x4 fixture.
5. Edge cases: an empty Image passed to create_from_image returns null with an error, as in Godot; set_pixel out of bounds raises an error and does not panic. (test: `image_texture_create_from_image_renders_in_sprite2d`)

title: ResourcesIO: ResourceLoader singleton (load/exists/threaded load) + full ResourceSaver + ClassDB registration of all three
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/resource-loader-saver-uid-singletons] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** a GDScript in a loaded scene calling ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request then load_threaded_get must yield a usable PackedScene that instantiates into the tree

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json .singletons (ResourceLoader, ResourceSaver, ResourceUID); upstream/godot/doc/classes/ResourceLoader.xml, ResourceSaver.xml, ResourceUID.xml; core/io/resource_loader.cpp

**Patina today:** ResourceLoader: no script dispatch at all. `grep -rn '"ResourceLoader' --include=*.rs crates` hits only gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:5021 (a generated name table); `grep -rn 'load_threaded_request|load_threaded_get' crates` = 0 hits; interpreter.rs has dispatch arms for ResourceUID (:3974) and ResourceSaver (:3991) but none for ResourceLoader. Godot's 14 methods (load, exists, load_threaded_request/get_status/get, has_cached, get_cached_ref, get_dependencies, get_recognized_extensions_for_type, list_directory, get_resource_uid, add/remove_resource_format_loader, set_abort_on_missing_resources) are absent. ResourceSaver: interpreter.rs:15541 call_resource_saver_static handles only "save" (1 of 6; set_uid/get_recognized_extensions/get_resource_id_for_path/add/remove_resource_format_saver absent); comment at interpreter.rs:3980-3990 confirms it is deliberately not a singleton nor ClassDB class. ResourceUID: interpreter.rs:28626 handles 11 methods and it is in BUILTIN_SINGLETONS (interpreter.rs:19633), but `grep -c '"ResourceUID"' crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` = 0, so ClassDB.class_exists("ResourceUID") is false. None of the three appears as a ClassRegistration::new in class_db.rs (grep for each quoted name = 0).

**Implement:** Godot 4.6.1: ResourceLoader, ResourceSaver and ResourceUID are engine singletons (extension_api.json .singletons) and ClassDB classes deriving Object (doc/classes/ResourceLoader.xml etc.). ResourceLoader.load(path, type_hint, cache_mode), exists(), load_threaded_request/get_status/get (web export runs these on the main thread but the API works), has_cached/get_cached_ref, get_dependencies, get_recognized_extensions_for_type are routinely used by loading screens and save systems. Patina: no `ResourceLoader` dispatch arm exists in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs (arms for ResourceUID at :3974 and ResourceSaver at :3991 only); ResourceSaver supports only `save` (interpreter.rs:15541); none of the three is registered in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs. **Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`

acceptance_criteria: A scene script runs `ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request("res://enemy.tscn")`, polls `load_threaded_get_status` until THREAD_LOAD_LOADED, then `add_child(ResourceLoader.load_threaded_get("res://enemy.tscn").instantiate())`, and the child node exists in the SceneTree; `ResourceLoader.exists("res://missing.tres")` is false; `ClassDB.class_exists` is true for ResourceLoader, ResourceSaver and ResourceUID and `Engine.has_singleton("ResourceLoader")` is true (test: `resource_loader_singleton_script_api`).

title: ResourcesIO: register PackedScene in ClassDB and implement PackedScene.new()/pack()/get_state() from script
description:

description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-lifecycle-signals] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** real script signal connections on a booted scene under MainLoop::step

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/node.cpp:317-333 _propagate_ready (ready_first), :335-372 _propagate_enter_tree (tree_entered, node_added(this), child_entered_tree), :~415-437 _propagate_exit_tree (children reversed, tree_exiting, node_removed, child_exiting_tree), :1687-1696 _add_child_nocheck (CHILD_ORDER_CHANGED + child_order_changed AFTER _set_tree)

**Patina today:** LifecycleManager::enter_tree (crates/gdscene/src/lifecycle.rs:31-68) calls process_script_ready for every node every time, and exit_tree sets ready=false (lifecycle.rs:119). So any reparent (scene_tree.rs:2874-2960) or remove+re-add runs _ready again, unlike Godot. collect_subtree_bottom_up (scene_tree.rs:3655) visits children forward, but Godot exits the last child first. NOTIFICATION_POST_ENTER_TREE does not exist (notification.rs). Never emitted anywhere: grep -rln 'tree_exiting\|tree_exited\|child_entered_tree\|child_exiting_tree\|child_order_changed' crates/*/src matches only class_db.rs and editor_server.rs, and grep '"ready"\|"renamed"\|"node_removed"\|"tree_changed"' crates/gdscene/src = 0. node_added is emitted once per subtree with no argument (scene_tree.rs:2741), where Godot emits it per node with the node. add_child fires CHILD_ORDER_CHANGED before the child enters (scene_tree.rs:2720-2728), where Godot fires it after.

**Implement:** Godot: _ready runs once per node unless request_ready() re-arms it (data.ready_first). Each tree entry sends NOTIFICATION_POST_ENTER_TREE (27) before READY. Exit walks children in reverse and emits tree_exiting before EXIT_TREE, node_removed, child_exiting_tree, then tree_exited after removal. Entry emits tree_entered, SceneTree.node_added(node) for every node, and child_entered_tree on the parent. add_child emits child_order_changed after the subtree has entered. Patina re-runs _ready on every re-entry and emits none of these signals except tree_entered and one argument-less node_added. Fix in lifecycle.rs and scene_tree.rs: add a ready_first flag on Node that request_ready sets and enter_tree consumes. Emit the signals in Godot order with Godot arguments (node ObjectId). Reverse the exit traversal. Emit tree_changed on add/remove/move. Emit Node.renamed from set_node_name. Wiring: real script signal connections on a booted scene under MainLoop::step.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/lifecycle.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node.rs`

**Prove it:** A booted scene where script P reparents child C from A to B in _process logs exactly: C._ready count stays 1. Order is tree_exiting(C) -> child_exiting_tree(A,C) -> tree_exited(C) -> tree_entered(C) -> child_entered_tree(B,C) -> child_order_changed(B). get_tree().node_added handler receives C. Exiting a parent with children [X,Y] calls Y._exit_tree before X._exit_tree. NOTIFICATION_POST_ENTER_TREE reaches _notification (test: `lifecycle_signals_and_ready_once_match_godot`).

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. In lifecycle.rs, enter_tree sets ready and calls process_script_ready unconditionally, and exit_tree calls set_ready(false), so _ready re-runs on reparent. POST_ENTER_TREE: grep in gdobject/src/notification.rs = 0. Signal literals outside tests and class_db: only "tree_entered" (lifecycle.rs) and an argument-less "node_added" (scene_tree.rs:2741). '"tree_exiting"', '"tree_exited"', '"child_entered_tree"', '"node_removed"', '"tree_changed"' and '"renamed"' all give 0. PARTIAL at P1 is reasonable.
acceptance_criteria: A booted scene where script P reparents child C from A to B in _process logs exactly: C._ready count stays 1. Order is tree_exiting(C) -> child_exiting_tree(A,C) -> tree_exited(C) -> tree_entered(C) -> child_entered_tree(B,C) -> child_order_changed(B). get_tree().node_added handler receives C. Exiting a parent with children [X,Y] calls Y._exit_tree before X._exit_tree. NOTIFICATION_POST_ENTER_TREE reaches _notification (test: `lifecycle_signals_and_ready_once_match_godot`).

title: Notifications: renumber NOTIFICATION_* to Godot 4.6 values and register the missing Node/WM/APPLICATION constants
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-notification-constants] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** notify_script delivers these values to a booted script's _notification

⚠️ **Unverified:** the adversarial verifier for this area did not run (usage limit). Priority is capped at P1. Re-check the evidence against the tree before implementing.

Add POST_ENTER_TREE, DISABLED, ENABLED, PATH_RENAMED, SCENE_INSTANTIATED, RESET_PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION, WM_MOUSE_ENTER/EXIT, WM_WINDOW_FOCUS_IN/OUT, WM_CLOSE_REQUEST, WM_GO_BACK_REQUEST, WM_SIZE_CHANGED, WM_DPI_CHANGE, VP_MOUSE_ENTER/EXIT and APPLICATION_*, and register them on Node/MainLoop in class_db.rs. Grep for hard-coded numeric literals that assumed the old values (trace detail tables, tests). Send DISABLED/ENABLED when a node's effective process mode becomes/leaves DISABLED. Deliver WM_SIZE_CHANGED from MainLoop::set_viewport_size and the web runtime's focus/blur/visibility events as WM_WINDOW_FOCUS_* / APPLICATION_FOCUS_*. Wiring: notify_script delivers these values to a booted script's _notification.

Node.NOTIFICATION_CHILD_ORDER_CHANGED == 24 from script (test: `notification_codes_match_godot_46`).

title: Pause: keep stepping physics while paused and filter every per-node phase by process_mode; script set_pause sends PAUSED/UNPAUSED
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-pause-model] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/scene_tree.cpp:1100 set_pause (propagates NOTIFICATION_PAUSED/UNPAUSED; physics frames keep iterating, each node filtered by can_process); scene/main/timer.cpp _notification (INTERNAL_PROCESS gated by can_process)

**Patina today:** MainLoop::step zeroes the physics accumulator while paused (main_loop.rs:3824-3829), so no physics tick runs: _physics_process of PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS/WHEN_PAUSED nodes never fires and SceneTree.physics_frame stops. The whole animation/particle/Timer/navigation block is wrapped in `if !paused` (main_loop.rs:4119-4250). Its own comment says an `Always` AnimationPlayer is not modelled, and the Timer comment claims pause menus use Always timers, but process_timer_nodes (scene_tree.rs:2312) never consults should_process_node. Script get_tree().set_pause -> SceneAccess::set_tree_paused (scripting.rs:6879) -> SceneTree::set_paused (scene_tree.rs:3680) only flips a bool. NOTIFICATION_PAUSED/UNPAUSED are sent only by MainLoop::set_paused (main_loop.rs:2718), and MainLoop.paused goes stale.

**Implement:** Godot keeps running physics frames while paused. Physics servers go inactive, but nodes whose effective process mode is ALWAYS or WHEN_PAUSED still get _physics_process, Timer, AnimationPlayer, AnimatedSprite, GPUParticles, Tween and other callbacks, because each checks can_process(). Patina skips whole phases. Fix in main_loop.rs: when paused, still run the tick loop for script/internal phases (process_physics_frame_with_scripts already filters with should_process_node) and skip only the solver steps, mirroring PhysicsServer set_active(false). Replace the `if !paused` block with per-node should_process_node filters inside process_timer_nodes, process_animations, process_animation_trees, process_animated_sprites, process_particles and the other per-node passes. Make SceneTree::set_paused the single owner of the transition: it propagates NOTIFICATION_PAUSED/UNPAUSED (to nodes whose can_process changes) and MainLoop reads tree.paused(). Depends on the process_mode property bead.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`

**Prove it:** With the tree paused from script via get_tree().paused = true, a PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS node's _physics_process count keeps rising across MainLoop::step, an Always Timer emits timeout, and an Always AnimationPlayer advances, while Pausable siblings freeze. A RigidBody2D does not move. _notification receives PAUSED once (test: `pause_filters_per_node_process_mode`).

**Verifier note:** main_loop.rs:3825-3829 zeroes physics_accumulator while paused, so no physics ticks run. main_loop.rs:4119-4252 wraps the simulation block in `if !paused`. SceneTree::set_paused (scene_tree.rs:3680-3682) only assigns the bool. PAUSED/UNPAUSED are propagated only by MainLoop::set_paused (main_loop.rs:2718-2738). One small correction: step() reads self.tree.paused() (main_loop.rs:3817), so a stale MainLoop.paused only affects set_paused's early-return check, not the gating. The finding stands.
acceptance_criteria: With the tree paused from script via get_tree().paused = true, a PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS node's _physics_process count keeps rising across MainLoop::step, an Always Timer emits timeout, and an Always AnimationPlayer advances, while Pausable siblings freeze. A RigidBody2D does not move. _notification receives PAUSED once (test: `pause_filters_per_node_process_mode`).

title: SubViewport: render the sub-scene into an offscreen target and sample it through ViewportTexture
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-subviewport] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: STUB]

**Wiring requirement:** a scene loaded and stepped through MainLoop, then rendered via the runtime render path

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/viewport.cpp (SubViewport::set_update_mode/clear_mode/size_2d_override, ViewportTexture::get_image), scene/main/viewport.cpp set_use_own_world_3d

**Patina today:** crates/gdscene/src/sub_viewport.rs implements a ColorBuffer whose 'render' helpers are fill_solid/render_color_rect_child/render_mesh_marker (sub_viewport.rs:280-310). render_subviewport_to_texture (514-530) has no caller outside the module and its lib.rs re-export (grep render_subviewport_to_texture|ViewportTexture:: across crates and tests = 0 outside sub_viewport.rs). The runtime 2D renderer (gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs, viewport_2d_render.rs) has no SubViewport branch (grep SubViewport scene_renderer.rs = 0). size_2d_override, update_mode, clear_mode and own_world_3d have no script dispatch (method sweep) and nothing consumes own_world_3d (grep own_world_3d crates/gdscene, gdrender3d = 0).

**Implement:** Godot renders each SubViewport's own canvas/world into its render target according to render_target_update_mode (DISABLED/ONCE/WHEN_VISIBLE/WHEN_PARENT_VISIBLE/ALWAYS) and clear_mode. Its children never draw into the parent canvas. size_2d_override scales the 2D canvas. ViewportTexture (TextureRect/Sprite2D texture or a SubViewportContainer) displays it. own_world_3d isolates 3D. Patina's SubViewport is a colour-fill stub with no runtime caller. Approach: in build_runtime_render_list, treat a SubViewport as a canvas boundary. Build a separate render list for its subtree (camera, CanvasLayers, stretch), rasterize it into a per-node offscreen buffer sized by `size`, applying update/clear modes and size_2d_override. Draw that buffer where a SubViewportContainer or a ViewportTexture-bearing node references it, and exclude the subtree from the parent list. Parse `ViewportTexture` sub-resources (viewport_path) in .tscn. Wiring: a scene loaded and stepped through MainLoop, then rendered via the runtime render path.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/sub_viewport.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn with SubViewportContainer > SubViewport(size 64x64) > ColorRect(red), plus a TextureRect elsewhere whose texture is ViewportTexture(viewport_path to the SubViewport), renders red pixels at both the container and the TextureRect rects and none at the ColorRect's raw canvas position. With update_mode=DISABLED the texture stays at its first-frame contents (test: `subviewport_renders_to_viewport_texture`).

**Verifier note:** grep 'SubViewport|sub_viewport|stretch_shrink' over gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs (build_runtime_render_list at :2056) and scene_renderer.rs = 0. grep SubViewport over gdserver2d, gdrender2d and patina-web src = 0. Outside sub_viewport.rs, render_subviewport_to_texture and ViewportTexture appear only in the lib.rs:142-143 re-export, ClassDB registration (class_db.rs:23080) and the inspector schema. SubViewportContainer support in control.rs (:819, :2293, :2547) covers layout and input coordinate mapping only, not rendering. STUB with priority 1 stands.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with SubViewportContainer > SubViewport(size 64x64) > ColorRect(red), plus a TextureRect elsewhere whose texture is ViewportTexture(viewport_path to the SubViewport), renders red pixels at both the container and the TextureRect rects and none at the ColorRect's raw canvas position. With update_mode=DISABLED the texture stays at its first-frame contents (test: `subviewport_renders_to_viewport_texture`).

title: Camera2D: viewport-scoped current camera with first-enter semantics and make_current/is_current from script
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-camera2d-current] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** Camera2D scroll pass (main_loop.rs ~4189) and the runtime render path both use the stored current camera

**Godot ground truth:** scene/2d/camera_2d.cpp _update_process_callback/make_current (viewport->_camera_2d_set; first enabled camera that enters becomes current)

**Patina today:** behavioral_2d::current_camera2d (crates/gdscene/src/behavioral_2d.rs:601-621) scans the whole tree and keeps the LAST enabled Camera2D in tree order, with no per-Viewport scoping. Godot keeps the first enabled camera to enter unless make_current is called. grep '"make_current"\|"is_current"' over gdscene and gdscript-interop finds only camera3d.rs:1032-1060, so `$Camera2D.make_current()` returns Nil silently via node_has_method (interpreter.rs:15666).

**Implement:** Godot: each Viewport tracks one current Camera2D. The first enabled camera to enter the tree becomes current. make_current() switches to it. Removing or disabling the current camera falls back to another enabled one. get_viewport().get_camera_2d() returns it. Patina picks the last enabled camera in global tree order. Fix: store the current Camera2D per viewport (the root, or the SubViewport ancestor via viewport::get_viewport). Set it on enter_tree when none is current or on make_current, and clear it on exit or enabled=false. Have current_camera2d read the stored id. Add Camera2D arms (make_current, is_current, get_screen_center_position, force_update_scroll, reset_smoothing) next to camera3d's in call_node_method. Wiring: Camera2D scroll pass (main_loop.rs ~4189) and the runtime render path both use the stored current camera.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/behavioral_2d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`

**Prove it:** A booted scene with two enabled Camera2D nodes A (first) and B renders through A. After a script calls `$B.make_current()` the next rendered frame is framed on B and `$A.is_current()` is false (test: `camera2d_first_enter_and_make_current`).

**Verifier note:** behavioral_2d.rs:601-621 scans the whole tree and keeps the LAST enabled Camera2D, with no viewport scoping. Its own doc comment says 'the LAST in top-down order wins'. grep '"make_current"|"is_current"' over gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src finds only camera3d.rs:1032/1055, and call_camera3d_method returns None for any class other than Camera3D (camera3d.rs:1036). No Camera2D arm exists anywhere.
acceptance_criteria: A booted scene with two enabled Camera2D nodes A (first) and B renders through A. After a script calls `$B.make_current()` the next rendered frame is framed on B and `$A.is_current()` is false (test: `camera2d_first_enter_and_make_current`).

title: Scripting: send ClassDB accessor methods and show/hide to node properties
description:
[audit-key: gui-controls/gui-script-api-accessors] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** GDScript `$X.set_text("a")` -> interpreter call_object_method -> call_node_method -> property store -> control_render draws new text

**Godot ground truth:** core/object/object.cpp Object::callp -> ClassDB::get_method; doc/classes/CanvasItem.xml show/hide; Button.xml set_text

**Patina today:** call_object_method tries script, then call_node_method, then `if responds { return Ok(Variant::Nil) }` (interpreter.rs:15662-15667). node_has_method answers from ClassDB (scene_tree.rs:5402-5411), and CanvasItem registers hide/show (class_db.rs:1554,1574), so `$Panel.hide()` silently returns Nil and changes nothing. No dispatch arm exists: grep for '"hide"', '"show"', '"set_text"', '"get_text"', 'strip_prefix("set_")', 'starts_with("set_")' in gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src found only ClassDB registrations and an unrelated virtual_keyboard_hide arm. get_property_setter/get_property_getter (class_db.rs:970-990) are only called by ClassDB.class_get_property_* script arms (interpreter.rs:20314-20325). No test or fixture in engine-rs calls .hide()/.show() (grep -rl '\.hide()' -e '\.show()' found nothing). Property syntax (`visible = false`) works; the method form is a silent no-op.

**Implement:** Godot: Object::callp resolves any bound method; property accessors (set_text/get_text, set_visible/is_visible, set_custom_minimum_size...) and CanvasItem.show()/hide() are real methods. Patina: interpreter.rs:15662 falls back to Nil when ClassDB says the method exists (scene_tree.rs:5402) but scripting.rs call_node_method (2594..4920) has no arm, so every accessor-form call and show()/hide() silently does nothing. Implementation: in SceneAccess::call_node_method (gdscene/src/scripting.rs) before the item_views fallthrough, look up the method among the class's PropertyInfo getter/setter names (gdobject::class_db::get_property_list + .getter/.setter), and map setter(v) to set_property(name, v) (going through the existing property-set path so side effects and signals run) and getter() to get_property(name) with the ClassDB default when unset. Add explicit show()/hide()/is_visible_in_tree() arms that write `visible` and call node2d::is_visible_in_tree. Wiring: GDScript `$X.set_text("a")` -> interpreter call_object_method -> call_node_method -> property store -> control_render draws new text.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene whose script calls $Label.set_text("hi"), $Panel.hide(), then reads $Label.get_text() and $Panel.is_visible() gets "hi" and false; the hidden Panel is skipped by control_at_point and is absent from build_control_render_items output. (test: `control_accessor_methods_reach_properties`)

**Verifier note:** The gap is real, but the mechanism and the status label are wrong. The cited class_db.rs:1554/1574 hide/show registrations belong to Node3D (neighbours get_world_3d, global_rotate, rotate_x). The CanvasItem registration (class_db.rs:13312-13410) has no hide/show; its methods are queue_redraw, draw_* and is_queued_for_redraw only. with_accessors (class_db.rs:81-85) only stores getter/setter strings on PropertyInfo and adds no MethodInfo, and ClassDB::has_method (class_db.rs:609-619) checks only the methods lists. There is no MethodInfo::new("set_text") anywhere. So for a Panel or Label, node_has_method (scene_tree.rs:5402) returns false and call_object_method (interpreter.rs:15662-15670) raises UndefinedFunction("ObjectId.hide"/"set_text"). That is a runtime error, not a silent Nil. No dispatch exists: grep for '"hide"', '"show"', '"set_text"', '"get_text"', '"set_visible"', '"is_visible"' across engine-rs/crates (all files) found only class_db and editor HTML strings. grep for strip_prefix("set_|get_|is_"), starts_with("set_"), format!("set_{ / get_{ / is_{ found only navigation_agents.rs:183,190, which is agent-local. Nothing was ever wired, so the label is MISSING, not UNWIRED. P0 stays because show()/hide()/set_text() are among the most common GDScript calls. The bead plan should also register hide/show/is_visible_in_tree on CanvasItem.
acceptance_criteria: A scene whose script calls $Label.set_text("hi"), $Panel.hide(), then reads $Label.get_text() and $Panel.is_visible() gets "hi" and false; the hidden Panel is skipped by control_at_point and is absent from build_control_render_items output. (test: `control_accessor_methods_reach_properties`)

title: Shaders: script-side ShaderMaterial edits reach the renderer
description:
[audit-key: shaders/shader-script-runtime] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** GDScript _process -> interpreter -> node property -> resolve_canvas_shader_material / resolve_shader_material -> frame pixels

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/ShaderMaterial.xml (set_shader_parameter, shader), doc/classes/Shader.xml (get_mode, code), doc/classes/ShaderInclude.xml (code); Resources are shared references so `material.set_shader_parameter()` changes what the next frame draws

**Patina today:** Both renderers read only FLAT node keys created at scene load: viewport_2d_render.rs:1281-1307 (`shader_code`/`shader_path`/`shader_parameter/*` on the node) and render_server_3d.rs:1580-1624; the flattening happens once in packed_scene.rs:1425-1483. The script side writes somewhere else: interpreter.rs:14379-14398 `set_shader_parameter` puts `shader_parameter/<n>` into a cloned Variant::Resource and write_place()s it back into the lvalue (the `material` value), never into the node's flat keys. `set_shader` (interpreter.rs:14421) only stores a `shader` property. grep `set_property("shader_parameter/` in non-test gdscene/gdscript-interop finds 0 hits. Shader.get_code/set_code/get_mode and ShaderInclude get_code/set_code have no dispatch arm: the Resource match (interpreter.rs:14299-14477) falls to UndefinedFunction, yet they are registered in class_db.rs:9442-9509. The test that admits this: crates/gdscript-interop/tests/shader_resource_script_api.rs:3-8 ('does NOT satisfy ... live parameter propagation').

**Implement:** Godot: ShaderMaterial is a shared Resource. `material.set_shader_parameter("tint", Color.RED)` in _process changes the pixels on the next frame, and so does `$Sprite.material = ShaderMaterial.new()` with `.shader = load("res://x.gdshader")`. Patina: the 2D and 3D renderers read only the flat node keys `shader_code`/`shader_path`/`shader_parameter/*` (viewport_2d_render.rs:1281-1307, render_server_3d.rs:1580-1624), which packed_scene.rs:1425-1483 writes once at load. The interpreter's `set_shader_parameter` (interpreter.rs:14379) writes into a cloned Variant::Resource in the `material` lvalue, and nothing copies that back to the node. Shader.get_code/set_code/get_mode and ShaderInclude.get_code/set_code have no dispatch arm, so they return UndefinedFunction. Approach: (1) when a node's `material`/`material_override` property is set to a ShaderMaterial Resource (from a script or from scene-load write_place), re-flatten it onto the node in the same place packed_scene does at load (one shared helper called from both): set shader_code/shader_path/shader_type, plus a shader_parameter/* key for each parameter, and clear stale keys. Alternatively, make both resolvers read the `material` Resource directly. (2) Make `set_shader_parameter` on a material reached through a node property route through that helper. (3) Add Resource arms for Shader get_code/set_code/get_mode (mode from the `shader_type` token) and for ShaderInclude get_code/set_code. Wiring: GDScript _process -> interpreter -> node property -> resolve_canvas_shader_material / resolve_shader_material -> frame pixels.

title: Shaders: route partially-matched spatial/sky shaders through the AST and surface compile errors
description:
[audit-key: shaders/shader-ast-routing] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn ShaderMaterial -> render_server_3d resolve_shader_material -> CustomFragmentShader::from_material -> software frame

**Godot ground truth:** servers/rendering/shader_language.cpp: the whole function body is compiled, and an unparsable statement is a compile error with a line number

**Patina today:** gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:1023-1043 falls back to shader_ast only when `instructions.is_empty() && func == "fragment"`. The line loop at shader.rs:1061-1063 silently drops any statement parse_fragment_statement_3d rejects. The 2D twin was fixed for exactly this case (gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:525-543 falls back on `skipped_any`, and its comment describes the bug), but 3D was not. Sky is excluded from the AST path entirely (shader.rs:1028-1035). Runtime compile errors are never printed: parse_fragment_body / compile_cached swallow ShaderError.

**Implement:** Godot compiles the whole stage function, and an unknown statement is a compile error. Patina's 3D line matcher (gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:1044-1066) drops unrecognised lines, and the AST fallback at :1038 runs only when NOTHING matched. So `float k = 0.5; ALBEDO = vec3(k);` keeps a matched ALBEDO whose local never resolves. Fix: mirror gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:510-543: track `skipped_any` in parse_named_body_3d_matched and fall back when it is set. Extend FragmentInstruction3D::Program to carry the entry-point name so `sky()` can use the AST too (eval_ast_fragment_3d at :1627 hardcodes "fragment"). Emit a ShaderError (line:col) into CompiledShader3D.diagnostics and push it to the runtime output/log once per shader source, the way Godot prints shader compile errors. Wiring: .tscn ShaderMaterial -> render_server_3d resolve_shader_material -> CustomFragmentShader::from_material -> software frame.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/shader.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/spatial_shader_partial_match_uses_ast.rs`

**Prove it:** A MeshInstance3D with `void fragment(){ float k = 0.25; ALBEDO = vec3(k); }` renders albedo 0.25 grey in the software 3D frame, not the matched-but-unresolved value. A sky shader using a local variable renders the evaluated colour. A syntax error is reported once with its line number in the runtime log. (test: `spatial_shader_partial_match_uses_ast`)

**Verifier note:** gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:1038 gates the fallback on `instructions.is_empty() && func == "fragment"`. parse_named_body_3d_matched (:1047-1066) drops statements it does not parse and has no skipped_any flag. The 2D twin at gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:521,538 uses `instructions.is_empty() || skipped_any`. The sky exclusion is documented in the comment at :1031-1037.
acceptance_criteria: A MeshInstance3D with `void fragment(){ float k = 0.25; ALBEDO = vec3(k); }` renders albedo 0.25 grey in the software 3D frame, not the matched-but-unresolved value. title: Shaders: AST-to-WGSL transpiler for spatial fragment() on the wgpu path
description:
[audit-key: shaders/shader-wgsl-3d] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** tscn ShaderMaterial -> GpuRenderer3D pipeline cache -> rendered GPU frame

**Godot ground truth:** servers/rendering/shader_compiler.cpp: the full fragment() is translated to the backend shading language on every renderer

**Patina today:** gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs:1507-1592 custom_spatial_module_wgsl returns None (flat albedo) when the body is AST-routed (gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:1910 `FragmentInstruction3D::Program(_) => return None`), when it reads TIME (wgpu_pipeline.rs:1527-1529), when it does not read UV (:1515), or when texture() refuses to transpile (comment at :1543). So any shader with locals, control flow or functions, which is everything the AST was built for, renders flat albedo on the web/wgpu path (patina-web uses gdrender3d wgpu, Cargo.toml:65) while software renders it. There is no WGSL for vertex(), light(), or the outputs beyond albedo/alpha.

**Implement:** Godot translates the whole fragment() to the backend language. Patina's GPU path (wgpu_pipeline.rs:1507 custom_spatial_module_wgsl) only accepts the six-instruction line matcher's output and returns None for anything AST-routed (gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:1910), anything using TIME (:1527), and texture sampling. Stage 1 of 2: add `gdresource::shader_ast::to_wgsl(program, stage_builtin_map)`, which emits WGSL for Stmt/Expr (locals, if/for/while, user functions emitted as WGSL fns, swizzles, ternary as select(), discard) and the builtin maths that call_builtin supports, plus texture()/textureLod() against the existing group-3 sampler slots (custom_sampler_fields). Feed TIME from a per-frame clock field on GpuRenderer3D, written into `custom.time` by the existing uniform packer. Replace the stmts path in custom_spatial_module_wgsl with to_wgsl, and keep the naga validation guard. Wiring: tscn ShaderMaterial -> GpuRenderer3D pipeline cache -> rendered GPU frame.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/shader_ast.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/tests/gpu_spatial_shader_ast_matches_software.rs`

**Prove it:** A MeshInstance3D whose shader uses a local variable, an if/else and `sin(TIME)` renders GPU pixels within tolerance of the software renderer for the same scene at two different times. A shader sampling a bound sampler2D matches software output. Unsupported constructs still fall back without a device validation error. (test: `gpu_spatial_shader_ast_matches_software`)

**Verifier note:** wgpu_pipeline.rs:1507-1592 returns None when there is no in.uv (:1515), when custom.time is used (:1527), when there are too many samplers, or when naga validation fails. fragment_body_to_wgsl_statements returns None for FragmentInstruction3D::Program at gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:1910. A grep for any wgsl emitter in gdresource/src found nothing, so there is no AST-to-WGSL path. The comment at wgpu_pipeline.rs:1545 says ColorExpr3D::Texture still refuses to transpile.
acceptance_criteria: A MeshInstance3D whose shader uses a local variable, an if/else and `sin(TIME)` renders GPU pixels within tolerance of the software renderer for the same scene at two different times. A shader sampling a bound sampler2D matches software output. Unsupported constructs still fall back without a device validation error. (test: `gpu_spatial_shader_ast_matches_software`)

title: Shaders: consume canvas_item WGSL in a real wgpu 2D textured-quad pipeline
