title: Shaders: real TIME, SCREEN_UV, FRAGCOORD and bound sampler2D uniforms for canvas_item (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: shaders/shader-canvas-runtime] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** tscn -> viewport_2d_render render list -> draw::*_shaded -> frame; tscn ColorRect with material=ShaderMaterial -> render list -> shaded raster -> frame

### 1. canvas_item CPU shading built-ins: TIME, SCREEN_UV, user sampler2D uniforms  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** shader_types.cpp canvas_item fragment built-ins: TIME, SCREEN_UV (= FRAGCOORD.xy * SCREEN_PIXEL_SIZE), FRAGCOORD, SCREEN_PIXEL_SIZE; a `uniform sampler2D` samples the texture bound via shader_parameter, or a default white/black texture

**Patina today:** TIME is hardcoded 0.0: viewport_2d_render.rs:3092-3100 ('an animated shader renders its t=0 frame') and gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs:653. SCREEN_UV is set to the quad-local UV, not the framebuffer position: gdrender2d/src/draw.rs:410 and :1225 `screen_uv: (u, v)`. Every non-screen sampler name samples the ITEM'S OWN texture: draw.rs:361-367 (`else { &tex }`), so `uniform sampler2D noise_tex` reads the sprite. No shader_parameter texture path is loaded for 2D (resolve_canvas_shader_material at viewport_2d_render.rs:1302-1307 copies Variants only). FRAGCOORD / SCREEN_PIXEL_SIZE / VERTEX are absent from the 2D AST builtins (gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:960-976).

**Implement:** Godot's canvas_item fragment gets an advancing TIME, SCREEN_UV = FRAGCOORD.xy / viewport size, and samples each `uniform sampler2D` from its bound texture (or the hint_default_* fallback). Patina passes TIME=0.0 (viewport_2d_render.rs:3100, gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs:653), sets SCREEN_UV to the quad UV (gdrender2d/src/draw.rs:410, :1225), and resolves every non-screen sampler to the item's own texture (draw.rs:361-367). Approach: thread a `time` argument from the scene tree's elapsed time into the render-list rasterizer entry point. Compute screen_uv = ((px+0.5)/fb.width, (py+0.5)/fb.height) and add FRAGCOORD and SCREEN_PIXEL_SIZE builtins in eval_ast_fragment (gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:949). In resolve_canvas_shader_material, load each sampler2D uniform's shader_parameter path through the texture cache, the way render_server_3d.rs:1550 bind_shader_textures does for 3D. Pass a name->Texture2D map into the Sampler closure, and when unbound, fall back to white, or black/normal per hint_default_black/hint_normal. Wiring: tscn -> viewport_2d_render render list -> draw::*_shaded -> frame.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/draw.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdserver2d/src/shader.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/canvas_item_shader_builtins_runtime.rs`

**Prove it:** A Sprite2D with `COLOR.r = fract(TIME)` renders different red values in frames rendered 0.25s apart. A small sprite at screen-right with `COLOR = vec4(SCREEN_UV.x,0,0,1)` reads ~0.9 red, not a 0..1 gradient. A shader sampling `uniform sampler2D noise_tex` set via shader_parameter to a solid-blue PNG renders blue, and with no texture bound renders white. (test: `canvas_item_shader_builtins_runtime`)

**Verifier note:** TIME is a literal 0.0 at viewport_2d_render.rs:3100 and gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs:653. draw.rs:410 and :1225 set screen_uv: (u, v), the quad-local UV. In draw.rs:361-367 the sampler closure picks the screen texture only for screen sampler names and uses `tex` (the item's own texture) for every other name. The 2D AST builtins at gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:964-976 are only COLOR, UV, SCREEN_UV, TIME and TEXTURE_PIXEL_SIZE, with no FRAGCOORD, SCREEN_PIXEL_SIZE or VERTEX.

### 2. canvas_item ShaderMaterial applied only to Sprite2D draws  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** CanvasItem.material applies to every draw command of the item (ColorRect, TextureRect, Polygon2D, TileMapLayer, Label, NinePatchRect, custom _draw)

**Patina today:** viewport_2d_render.rs: shader_program is used only in the Render2DKind::Sprite arm (:3080). ColorRect (:3157-3159 fill_rect_transformed), TileMap (:3138-3155), Polygon (:3193), PolygonTextured (:3249), Text (:3161), Particles (:3285) and Mesh (:3343) ignore it. In gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs only axis-aligned DrawTextureRect is shaded (:642). The rotated texture path (:661), DrawTextureRegion (:674) and DrawRect skip the shader. A full-screen ColorRect post-process shader is the most common Godot shader pattern, and it renders as a flat colour.

**Implement:** In Godot a CanvasItem's ShaderMaterial shades every primitive the item draws. Patina only shades the Sprite arm (viewport_2d_render.rs:3080). ColorRect, TextureRect-as-Polygon, Polygon2D, TileMapLayer cells, Label text and MeshInstance2D bypass shader_program. Approach: add `fill_rect_transformed_shaded` (COLOR = rect colour * modulate, UV = 0..1 over the rect, TEXTURE = 1x1 white) and a shaded variant of the polygon fill in polygon_raster.rs with per-vertex UV interpolation. Route the TileMap cells and the text glyph blits through draw_texture_rect_transformed_shaded_with_screen when shader_program is Some. Wiring: tscn ColorRect with material=ShaderMaterial -> render list -> shaded raster -> frame.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/draw.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/polygon_raster.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/canvas_shader_applies_to_all_item_kinds.rs`

**Prove it:** A full-screen ColorRect with `COLOR = vec4(UV.x, UV.y, 0.0, 1.0)` renders a 2D gradient, and the same shader on a Polygon2D and a TileMapLayer cell changes their pixels. A `hint_screen_texture` grayscale shader on a ColorRect over a BackBufferCopy greys the scene beneath it. (test: `canvas_shader_applies_to_all_item_kinds`)

**Verifier note:** In viewport_2d_render.rs, shader_program is used only inside the Render2DKind::Sprite arm (:3011, match at :3080; grep 'shader_program' found only :2969 and :3080). The ColorRect arm (:3157-3159) calls plain fill_rect_transformed. LineShaded (:3217) is Line2D gradient/width shading, not a ShaderMaterial. gdrender2d renderer.rs:642-653 shades only the axis-aligned DrawTextureRect, and DrawTextureRegion (:670+) uses the unshaded draw_texture_rect_transformed.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A Sprite2D with `COLOR.r = fract(TIME)` renders different red values in frames rendered 0.25s apart. A small sprite at screen-right with `COLOR = vec4(SCREEN_UV.x,0,0,1)` reads ~0.9 red, not a 0..1 gradient. A shader sampling `uniform sampler2D noise_tex` set via shader_parameter to a solid-blue PNG renders blue, and with no texture bound renders white. (test: `canvas_item_shader_builtins_runtime`) 2) A full-screen ColorRect with `COLOR = vec4(UV.x, UV.y, 0.0, 1.0)` renders a 2D gradient, and the same shader on a Polygon2D and a TileMapLayer cell changes their pixels. A `hint_screen_texture` grayscale shader on a ColorRect over a BackBufferCopy greys the scene beneath it. (test: `canvas_shader_applies_to_all_item_kinds`)

title: Shaders: execute vertex() and light() stages with interpolated varyings
description:
[audit-key: shaders/shader-stages] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** renderer.rs:1107 selects the custom vertex shader whenever the material has a `vertex` function

**Godot ground truth:** shader_types.cpp: spatial vertex (VERTEX, NORMAL, UV, COLOR, MODELVIEW_MATRIX...), light (DIFFUSE_LIGHT, SPECULAR_LIGHT, LIGHT, ATTENUATION, LIGHT_COLOR); canvas_item vertex (VERTEX, UV, COLOR) and light (LIGHT, LIGHT_COLOR, LIGHT_POSITION); varyings pass vertex->fragment, `flat` disables interpolation

**Patina today:** No renderer evaluates a vertex or light function: grep '"vertex"\|"light"' across gdserver2d/gdserver3d/gdrender2d/gdrender3d finds only gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:1381-1385, where unsupported_features REPORTS them. eval_function is called only with "fragment" (gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:987, gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:1676). shader_ast records varyings by name only (shader_ast.rs:441-443), so a varying read in fragment is undeclared. Water and wind vertex-displacement shaders do nothing.

**Implement:** Godot runs vertex() per vertex (writing VERTEX/NORMAL/UV/COLOR plus varyings, in model space unless world_vertex_coords or skip_vertex_transform is set) and light() per light per fragment. Patina runs only fragment(). Approach (3D software first): give gdrender3d::shader a CustomVertexShader that wraps StandardVertexShader and calls shader_ast::eval_function(program, "vertex") with VERTEX/NORMAL/UV/COLOR/TIME/MODEL_MATRIX builtins, before the model transform. Write varyings into a new VertexOutput.varyings Vec<f32> that VertexOutput::barycentric interpolates (flat varyings take the provoking vertex). Seed fragment's StageContext with them. Make light() replace the Lambert loop in CustomFragmentShader::process (gdrender3d/src/shader.rs:1203-1240): accumulate DIFFUSE_LIGHT/SPECULAR_LIGHT per light. Use the same pattern on 2D for the vertex pass over quad corners in viewport_2d_render. Wiring: renderer.rs:1107 selects the custom vertex shader whenever the material has a `vertex` function.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/shader_ast.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/shader.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/tests/shader_vertex_light_stages_render.rs`

**Prove it:** A MeshInstance3D plane with `void vertex(){ VERTEX.y += 1.0; }` renders displaced (silhouette moves up by the projected 1 unit) in the software 3D frame. A varying set in vertex() from VERTEX.x and output as ALBEDO forms a gradient. A light() writing DIFFUSE_LIGHT = vec3(1,0,0) tints the lit side red. A canvas_item `VERTEX.x += 10.0` shifts the sprite 10px. (test: `shader_vertex_light_stages_render`)

**Verifier note:** Non-test eval_function callers are only gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:987 and gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:1676, both with "fragment". grep '"vertex"|"light"' in gdserver2d/gdserver3d/gdrender2d/gdrender3d src finds only gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:1381,1384 (unsupported-feature reporting) and an unrelated OBJ parser hit at mesh.rs:1396. grep 'vertex_body|parse_vertex|VertexInstruction|CustomVertexShader|light_body' across crates (non-test) found 0 hits.
acceptance_criteria: A MeshInstance3D plane with `void vertex(){ VERTEX.y += 1.0; }` renders displaced (silhouette moves up by the projected 1 unit) in the software 3D frame. A varying set in vertex() from VERTEX.x and output as ALBEDO forms a gradient. A light() writing DIFFUSE_LIGHT = vec3(1,0,0) tints the lit side red. A canvas_item `VERTEX.x += 10.0` shifts the sprite 10px. (test: `shader_vertex_light_stages_render`)

title: Shaders: read back all spatial fragment outputs and light custom shaders via pbr_shade
description:
[audit-key: shaders/shader-spatial-outputs] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** renderer.rs:1107 CustomFragmentShader -> pbr_shade -> frame

**Godot ground truth:** shader_types.cpp spatial fragment outputs; scene_forward_lights_inc.glsl: custom shaders go through the same PBR light loop as StandardMaterial3D

**Patina today:** eval_ast_fragment_3d (gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:1627-1696) seeds ROUGHNESS/METALLIC but reads back only ALBEDO/ALPHA/COLOR, so shader writes to EMISSION, ROUGHNESS, METALLIC, NORMAL and NORMAL_MAP are discarded. CustomFragmentShader::process (gdrender3d/src/shader.rs:1203-1240) then applies hardcoded Lambert with `ambient = 0.15`, no attenuation and no specular, instead of pbr_shade (shader.rs:876). Emission comes from a uniform literally named `emission` (shader.rs:1238), which is a heuristic, not Godot semantics.

**Implement:** Godot: a spatial fragment() writes ALBEDO, ALPHA, EMISSION, ROUGHNESS, METALLIC, NORMAL, NORMAL_MAP(+DEPTH), AO, RIM, SPECULAR, and the result goes through the standard PBR light loop with environment ambient. Patina: eval_ast_fragment_3d returns only a Color (gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:1683-1695). CustomFragmentShader lights it with a fixed Lambert at 0.15 ambient (gdrender3d/src/shader.rs:1203-1240) and adds emission only from a uniform named `emission`. Approach: return a SurfaceOutput {albedo, alpha, emission, roughness, metallic, normal, ao, rim, specular} from eval_ast_fragment_3d, and from the matcher path too. Apply NORMAL_MAP via apply_normal_map (shader.rs:286). Build FragmentInput/ShaderUniforms from that output and call pbr_shade (shader.rs:876) so custom and StandardMaterial3D surfaces share lighting, attenuation and environment ambient. Remove the `emission` uniform heuristic. Wiring: renderer.rs:1107 CustomFragmentShader -> pbr_shade -> frame.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/shader.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/shader.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/tests/spatial_shader_outputs_feed_pbr.rs`

**Prove it:** In one lit software 3D scene, a custom shader that writes `ALBEDO = vec3(0.8); ROUGHNESS = 0.2; METALLIC = 0.0;` renders pixels within tolerance of a StandardMaterial3D with the same parameters. `EMISSION = vec3(1,0,0)` makes an unlit-side pixel red. A NORMAL_MAP write changes shading. (test: `spatial_shader_outputs_feed_pbr`)

**Verifier note:** eval_ast_fragment_3d (gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:1676-1693) reads back only ALPHA, ALBEDO and COLOR. grep '"EMISSION"|"ROUGHNESS"|"METALLIC"|"NORMAL_MAP"' finds only the seeding inserts at :1667-1668. CustomFragmentShader::process (gdrender3d/src/shader.rs:1203-1240) uses ambient = 0.15, Lambert N.L with no attenuation or specular, and emission from parameters.get("emission").
acceptance_criteria: In one lit software 3D scene, a custom shader that writes `ALBEDO = vec3(0.8); ROUGHNESS = 0.2; METALLIC = 0.0;` renders pixels within tolerance of a StandardMaterial3D with the same parameters. `EMISSION = vec3(1,0,0)` makes an unlit-side pixel red. A NORMAL_MAP write changes shading. (test: `spatial_shader_outputs_feed_pbr`)

title: Shaders: parse full render_mode tables and apply blend/cull/depth/shadow modes in both renderers
description:
[audit-key: shaders/shader-render-modes] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** tscn -> resolve_shader_material / resolve_canvas_shader_material -> rasterizer state

**Godot ground truth:** servers/rendering/shader_types.cpp:232-254 (spatial: blend_{mix,add,sub,mul,premul_alpha}, depth_draw_{opaque,always,never}, depth_prepass_alpha, depth_test_disabled, cull_{back,front,disabled}, unshaded, wireframe, diffuse_*, specular_*, skip_vertex_transform, world_vertex_coords, shadows_disabled, ambient_light_disabled, shadow_to_opacity, vertex_lighting, alpha_to_coverage, fog_disabled, ...); shader_language.cpp:11208 'Invalid render mode' error

**Patina today:** gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:375-388 models only 6 flags, and parse_render_modes (:575-596) silently ignores the rest, with a false 'Godot-compatible' comment (Godot errors at shader_language.cpp:11208). Only `unshaded` has a consumer (gdrender3d/src/shader.rs:1199). grep cull_disabled|blend_add|depth_draw_never|cull_front outside gdserver3d/src/shader.rs = 0 hits, so they are parsed and never applied (culling and blend come from Material3D, renderer.rs:1235). canvas_item render_mode (blend_*, unshaded, light_only, skip_vertex_transform, world_vertex_coords) appears nowhere in gdserver2d/gdrender2d/viewport_2d_render (grep render_mode = 0).

**Implement:** Godot validates render_mode against per-type tables (shader_types.cpp:232-254 for spatial, and the canvas_item block) and errors on unknown modes. Blend, cull, depth draw/test, unshaded, shadows_disabled, ambient_light_disabled and fog_disabled change rasterization. Patina parses 6 spatial flags (gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:575), applies only unshaded, and ignores canvas_item render_mode entirely. Approach: move the render_mode parsing to a shader_ast-level table keyed by shader_type and transcribed from shader_types.cpp, with Diagnostics for invalid or duplicate modes. Map the spatial cull/blend/depth/transparency modes onto the Material3D fields the rasterizer already honours (render_modes::should_cull, Transparency, DepthDrawMode, BlendMode in rasterizer.rs:190-206) when resolving a ShaderMaterial in render_server_3d. Honour shadows_disabled and ambient_light_disabled in the light loop. For canvas_item, map blend_* onto fb.blend_mode (viewport_2d_render.rs:2959) and unshaded/light_only onto the Light2D pass. Wiring: tscn -> resolve_shader_material / resolve_canvas_shader_material -> rasterizer state.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/shader.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/shader_render_modes_apply.rs`

**Prove it:** A spatial shader with `render_mode cull_front;` hides the camera-facing faces. `blend_add` brightens what lies under it. A canvas_item `render_mode blend_add;` sprite over grey yields additive pixels. `render_mode bogus_mode;` produces an 'Invalid render mode' diagnostic. (test: `shader_render_modes_apply`)

**Verifier note:** gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:375-388 RenderModeFlags has 6 bools. parse_render_modes at :575-596 sends unknown modes to `_ => {}` with the comment 'silently ignored (Godot-compatible)'. I grepped render_modes. and .render_modes across crates, excluding tests: the only consumer of the shader flags is `unshaded` (gdrender3d/src/shader.rs:1199, gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:836 and :1988). gdrender3d/src/render_modes.rs and the wgpu cull/depth code (wgpu_pipeline.rs:1267, 2465-2479) take Material3D enums, not the shader flags. Grepping cull_front|blend_add|depth_draw_never|cull_disabled outside gdserver3d/src/shader.rs found only unit tests in render_modes.rs. Grepping render_mode|blend_add|light_only in gdserver2d/src, gdrender2d/src and viewport_2d_render.rs found no files. P1 is correct: cull_disabled, unshaded and blend_add are common.
acceptance_criteria: A spatial shader with `render_mode cull_front;` hides the camera-facing faces. `blend_add` brightens what lies under it. A canvas_item `render_mode blend_add;` sprite over grey yields additive pixels. `render_mode bogus_mode;` produces an 'Invalid render mode' diagnostic. (test: `shader_render_modes_apply`)

title: Shaders: AST support for matrices, int/bool vectors, global consts, arrays, structs and out params (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: shaders/shader-language] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** proven through the canvas_item render path (viewport_2d_render -> eval_ast_fragment); through the canvas_item and spatial render paths

### 1. Shading language types: matrices, ivec/uvec/bvec, global const, arrays, structs, out/inout params  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** servers/rendering/shader_language.cpp (TYPE_MAT2/3/4, TYPE_IVEC*, TYPE_UVEC*, TYPE_BVEC*, const globals, arrays, structs, out/inout qualifiers)

**Patina today:** ShaderValue has only Bool/Int/Float/Vec2-4 (shader_ast.rs:39-51), so there are no matrices or int/bool vectors. Top-level `const` values are discarded: parse_program (shader_ast.rs:428-446) skips to `;` and ShaderProgram (:226-235) has no consts field, so a shader referencing a global const fails eval and the pixel is left unshaded. Struct declarations are skipped (:424-427), so struct-typed vars and returns cannot parse. is_type_token (:367-388) lacks Uint vectors and struct idents. Expr has no Index variant (:98-155), so there are no arrays. Function params are names only (:500-520), so out/inout is impossible. call_builtin constructs only vec2/3/4/float/int (:1515-1540): grep for ivec2/bvec2/uvec2/mat3/uint/bool in shader_ast.rs = 0.

**Implement:** Godot's language includes mat2/3/4 (with * against vecs), ivec/uvec/bvec, global `const` (including const arrays), local and uniform arrays with indexing, structs, and out/inout parameters. Patina's evaluator (gdresource/src/shader_ast.rs) has none of these: ShaderValue :39, consts dropped :428-446, structs skipped :424, no Index expr, params name-only :500. Stage 1 of 2: extend ShaderValue with Mat2/Mat3/Mat4, IVec(n), UVec(n), BVec(n), Array(Vec<ShaderValue>) and Struct(HashMap). Parse and evaluate global consts into ShaderProgram.consts, seeding StageContext from them. Add Expr::Index and struct field Member. Record param qualifiers and copy back out/inout. Add constructors and matrix multiplication. The 2D/3D adapters (gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:931, gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:1605) map Variant Transform/Basis/PackedArrays to the new values. Wiring: proven through the canvas_item render path (viewport_2d_render -> eval_ast_fragment).

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/shader_ast.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdserver2d/src/shader.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/shader.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/shader_language_types_render.rs`

**Prove it:** A Sprite2D shader using `const float K = 0.5;`, `mat2 r = mat2(vec2(0,1), vec2(-1,0)); vec2 p = r * UV;`, a `float w[3] = float[](0.2,0.3,0.5)` indexed in a for loop, a struct-typed helper, and a helper with an `out` param renders the expected pixels in the rendered frame, with no unshaded fallback. (test: `shader_language_types_render`)

**Verifier note:** ShaderValue at gdresource/src/shader_ast.rs:39-52 has only Bool/Int/Float/Vec2/Vec3/Vec4. A grep for mat2|mat3|ivec2|bvec2|uvec in shader_ast.rs counts 0. Structs are skipped via skip_braced_block (:424-427). Const declarations share the uniform/varying branch (:428-446), which pushes no name for const and then skip_to_semicolon, so the value is dropped. Matrices appear only in the WGSL/GPU-side files (gdserver3d/src/shader.rs, wgpu_pipeline.rs), not in the AST evaluator the finding scopes to. P1 is reasonable because global const and mat use are common.

### 2. Shading language builtin functions (texelFetch, textureSize, matrix, bit, packing, isnan/isinf, modf/frexp/ldexp, hyperbolic inverses, derivatives)  (PARTIAL, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** servers/rendering/shader_language.cpp:2419 builtin_func_defs[] (≈120 names, including texelFetch textureSize textureGrad textureProj* textureGather textureQueryLod/Levels inverse transpose determinant outerProduct matrixCompMult acosh asinh atanh fma frexp ldexp modf isinf isnan bitCount findLSB/MSB bitfield* pack*/unpack* floatBitsTo*/intBitsToFloat)

**Patina today:** For each of these names, grep -c '"<name>"' gdresource/src/shader_ast.rs returned 0: acosh asinh atanh bitCount determinant inverse transpose outerProduct matrixCompMult fma frexp ldexp modf isinf isnan packHalf2x16 unpackUnorm4x8 floatBitsToInt texelFetch textureSize textureGrad textureProj textureGather textureQueryLod. dFdx/dFdy/fwidth are stubbed to 0 (shader_ast.rs:1598), which breaks fwidth-based antialiasing and outline shaders. An unknown function errors, and the pixel is left unshaded.

**Implement:** Godot's builtin_func_defs (shader_language.cpp:2419) defines ~120 functions. Patina's call_builtin (gdresource/src/shader_ast.rs:1508-1860) lacks texelFetch, textureSize, textureGrad, textureProj*, textureGather, textureQueryLod/Levels, inverse, transpose, determinant, outerProduct, matrixCompMult, acosh/asinh/atanh, fma, frexp, ldexp, modf, isinf, isnan, the bit ops, pack/unpack, and float/int bit casts, and it stubs dFdx/dFdy/fwidth to 0. Stage 2 of 2 (after the type stage). Add these, transcribed from the builtin table's signatures. Extend Sampler with texel-fetch and size queries so texelFetch/textureSize work against the renderer's texture. Compute dFdx/dFdy by evaluating neighbouring pixels in a 2x2 quad (the software rasterizer can shade quads) or by finite difference of UV-driven expressions. Wiring: through the canvas_item and spatial render paths.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/shader_ast.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/shader_builtin_functions_render.rs`

**Prove it:** A canvas_item shader using `texelFetch(TEXTURE, ivec2(0,0), 0)`, `textureSize(TEXTURE,0)`, `fwidth(UV.x)` (non-zero), `isnan`, `packUnorm4x8` round-trip and `inverse(mat2(...))` renders the expected pixels in the frame. Each function has a scalar unit check against Godot reference values. (test: `shader_builtin_functions_render`)

**Verifier note:** In gdresource/src/shader_ast.rs, grep "texelFetch"|"textureSize"|"isnan"|"inverse"|"modf" = 0 hits. The only derivative hit is :1598 `"dFdx" | "dFdy" | "fwidth" => return unary(|_| 0.0)`, which is a stub. P2 is appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A Sprite2D shader using `const float K = 0.5;`, `mat2 r = mat2(vec2(0,1), vec2(-1,0)); vec2 p = r * UV;`, a `float w[3] = float[](0.2,0.3,0.5)` indexed in a for loop, a struct-typed helper, and a helper with an `out` param renders the expected pixels in the rendered frame, with no unshaded fallback. (test: `shader_language_types_render`) 2) A canvas_item shader using `texelFetch(TEXTURE, ivec2(0,0), 0)`, `textureSize(TEXTURE,0)`, `fwidth(UV.x)` (non-zero), `isnan`, `packUnorm4x8` round-trip and `inverse(mat2(...))` renders the expected pixels in the frame. Each function has a scalar unit check against Godot reference values. (test: `shader_builtin_functions_render`)

title: Shaders: run the preprocessor before every compile and finish #if/#elif/function macros
description:
[audit-key: shaders/shader-preprocessor] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** tscn -> shader with #include -> rendered pixels

**Godot ground truth:** servers/rendering/shader_preprocessor.cpp: runs before every shader compile; #include resolves .gdshaderinc ShaderInclude resources; supports function-like macros, #if/#elif/defined()

**Patina today:** gdresource/src/shader_preprocessor.rs:92 `pub fn preprocess` has no caller outside its module (grep 'shader_preprocessor::|preprocess(' = only the definition). The tokenizer rejects '#' as UnexpectedChar (shader_tokenizer.rs:699, test at :1513-1517). So any shader with `#define`/`#include` fails parse_shader, and shader_from_source (importers.rs:2018) extracts no type or uniforms. Function-like macros, #if/#elif and defined() are unimplemented (shader_preprocessor.rs:19-21).

**Implement:** Godot preprocesses every shader (shader_preprocessor.cpp) before compiling it, resolving #include against .gdshaderinc ShaderInclude resources. Patina has a preprocessor (gdresource/src/shader_preprocessor.rs:92) that nothing calls, and the tokenizer errors on '#'. Approach: add a single `gdresource::shader_source::resolve(source, include_loader)` that runs preprocess with a loader backed by the project res:// filesystem, and call it in shader_from_source (importers.rs:2004), in the packed_scene inline-code path (packed_scene.rs:1458), and in both renderer resolvers before parse. Map ShaderError lines back through Preprocessed::origin (:61). Implement function-like macros, #if/#elif with defined() and integer expressions, and #pragma disable_preprocessor. Wiring: tscn -> shader with #include -> rendered pixels.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/shader_preprocessor.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/shader_preprocessor_include_renders.rs`

**Prove it:** A Sprite2D shader that does `#include "res://inc/tint.gdshaderinc"` (defining `vec3 tint(){...}`) and uses `#ifdef USE_RED` / `#define USE_RED` renders the included function's colour in the frame. An error inside the include reports the include's file and line. (test: `shader_preprocessor_include_renders`)

**Verifier note:** I grepped `shader_preprocessor::|preprocess(` across crates. Outside the module's own definition (shader_preprocessor.rs:92), every hit is in gdresource/tests/shader_preproc.rs, so there is no runtime caller. The tokenizer test at shader_tokenizer.rs:1516 expects UnexpectedChar '#'. The only other #include handling is gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:1378, which only flags it as an unsupported feature string. There is no hidden directive stripping: I grepped `"#define|#include|"#ifdef|starts_with(.#` in shader-related code. P1 is fine.
acceptance_criteria: A Sprite2D shader that does `#include "res://inc/tint.gdshaderinc"` (defining `vec3 tint(){...}`) and uses `#ifdef USE_RED` / `#define USE_RED` renders the included function's colour in the frame. An error inside the include reports the include's file and line. (test: `shader_preprocessor_include_renders`)

title: glTF: instantiate .glb/.gltf as a real PackedScene (load, preload, sub-scene, generate_scene) (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: import-pipeline-and-gltf/gltf-runtime-scene] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** a .tscn with [ext_resource type="PackedScene" path="res://m.glb"] + instance=ExtResource, loaded by patina-runner, must produce the glTF subtree and render the real geometry, not a cube

### 1. glTF/GLB as a PackedScene at runtime: load()/preload().instantiate() and .tscn instance=ExtResource("x.glb")  (UNWIRED, P0)

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/import/3d/resource_importer_scene.cpp (ResourceImporterScene::import saves a PackedScene, get_resource_type()=="PackedScene"); modules/gltf/gltf_document.cpp generate_scene/_generate_scene_node; core/io/resource_importer.cpp remap

**Patina today:** importers.rs:1800-1801 registers .gltf/.glb -> import_gltf_asset (importers.rs:374) which returns Resource class "GltfDocument" (gltf_import.rs:128), not PackedScene. interpreter.rs:260-275 load_via_format_loaders copies that class_name; interpreter.rs:14354-14360 'instantiate' raises 'cannot instantiate a GltfDocument resource' for anything not PackedScene. Sub-scene path scripting.rs:7412-7437 reads every instance target with FileAccess::read_file_string + PackedScene::from_tscn, so a .glb (binary) or .gltf (JSON) sub-scene resolves to None and is dropped. patina-runner main.rs:574 / bootstrap.rs:512 / project_boot.rs:589 use add_packed_scene_to_tree (no sub-scene resolution at all). Only consumer of glTF geometry at runtime is render_server_3d.rs:1354-1361 which treats a MeshInstance3D.mesh STRING ending in .glb (not a Godot construct) and takes only the FIRST subresource (render_server_3d.rs:1848-1858). animations_from_gltf_resource (animation.rs:1944) has zero non-test callers (grep -rn animations_from_gltf_resource crates -> only gdscene/tests/gltf_anim_import.rs).

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: a .glb/.gltf is imported by ResourceImporterScene (editor/import/3d/resource_importer_scene.cpp) into a PackedScene; load("res://m.glb") returns PackedScene and instantiate() builds Node3D hierarchy with per-node transforms, MeshInstance3D nodes whose mesh is an ArrayMesh (one surface per primitive, with StandardMaterial3D from pbrMetallicRoughness/normal/emission/occlusion/alpha), Camera3D/Light3D from cameras/KHR_lights_punctual, and an AnimationPlayer holding the clips (gltf_document.cpp _generate_scene_node, _import_animation). Patina today: load returns class 'GltfDocument' (gltf_import.rs:128) and instantiate raises (interpreter.rs:14354); sub-scene resolver only parses tscn (scripting.rs:7426-7429); GLTFDocument.generate_scene (interpreter.rs:10685-10770) creates MeshInstance3D with only a 'gltf_mesh_index' property that nothing reads (grep gltf_mesh_index -> only interpreter.rs:10735) and applies NO translation/rotation/scale, so render_server_3d.rs:1408 falls back to Mesh3D::cube(1.0) for every node. Implementation: add gdscene/src/gltf_scene.rs with build_gltf_subtree(tree, parent, &Resource) that (1) creates nodes in document order with transforms from the parsed node dicts, (2) assigns each MeshInstance3D a mesh handle/resource built from ALL primitives of its mesh_index (extend mesh3d_from_gltf_resource to select by mesh_index and emit multi-surface), with material_from_gltf_resource per surface, (3) Camera3D/OmniLight3D/SpotLight3D/DirectionalLight3D with fov/near/far/color/energy/range/spot angles, (4) AnimationPlayer populated from animations_from_gltf_resource. Make importers.rs report class PackedScene for glb/gltf (keep the document on a property) so can_instantiate/instantiate pass; route scripting.rs instantiate_packed_scene and the sub-scene resolver by extension to build_gltf_subtree; make GLTFDocument.generate_scene call the same builder via SceneAccess. Wiring requirement: a .tscn with [ext_resource type="PackedScene" path="res://m.glb"] + instance=ExtResource, loaded by patina-runner, must produce the glTF subtree and render the real geometry, not a cube.

**Prove it:** A fixture project main.tscn instancing res://two_meshes.glb (two nodes, distinct translations, one with two primitives) loads through the runner path: the tree contains the glTF node names under the instance root with the authored transforms, each MeshInstance3D resolves to the glTF vertex count (not 24-vertex cube) with surface_count == primitive count, and a GDScript `var s = load("res://two_meshes.glb"); assert(s is PackedScene); add_child(s.instantiate())` yields the same subtree; GLTFDocument.append_from_file + generate_scene yields identical transforms/meshes; an animated fixture yields an AnimationPlayer whose library contains the clip. (test: `gltf_packed_scene_instancing_test`)

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. gltf_import.rs:128 Resource::new("GltfDocument"); importers.rs:1800-1801 register .gltf/.glb -> import_gltf_asset; interpreter.rs:14354-14359 rejects instantiate for any class != PackedScene. scripting.rs:7411-7437 instantiate_packed_scene and its sub-scene resolve closure both use FileAccess::read_file_string + PackedScene::from_tscn only (grep 'glb|gltf' in scripting.rs -> 0 hits). No remap handling in gdresource unified.rs/loader.rs (grep remap -> 0). grep build_gltf|gltf_scene|instantiate_gltf in non-test crates -> only gdeditor/src/import.rs (editor path). gltf_mesh_index set at interpreter.rs:10735 has no reader (grep gltf_mesh_index -> only that line); gltf_generate_scene (10692-10770) sets no transforms. animations_from_gltf_resource (animation.rs:1944) has no non-test caller. P0 justified: .glb is the default 3D asset path.

### 2. Skinned glTF: skins -> Skeleton3D + MeshInstance3D.skin binding, bone poses, skeleton-targeted animation tracks  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/gltf/gltf_document.cpp _determine_skeletons/_create_skeletons/_create_skins/_generate_skeleton_bone_attachment; skins/use_named_skins import option

**Patina today:** gltf_import.rs:1288 GltfSkin and :1426 parse_skins parse joints/inverseBindMatrices; JOINTS_0/WEIGHTS_0 read (8 hits each). No Skeleton3D is produced by any glTF consumer: grep Skeleton3D crates/gdeditor/src/import.rs -> doc/test only; interpreter.rs gltf_generate_scene (:10685-10770) creates only Node3D/MeshInstance3D; GLTFState.get_skins/get_skeletons raise via gltf_unsupported (interpreter.rs:22564, method table at :22500-22560 has no get_skins).

**Implement:** Godot converts glTF skins into a Skeleton3D (joint nodes become bones, not Node3D), binds each skinned MeshInstance3D via skin + skeleton NodePath, and retargets joint TRS channels to `Skeleton3D:bone_name` tracks (gltf_document.cpp _create_skeletons/_create_skins/_import_animation). Patina parses skins (gltf_import.rs:1426) but no consumer creates a Skeleton3D. Depends on the shared gltf scene builder from the gltf-runtime-scene bead: extend build_gltf_subtree to group joint nodes into a Skeleton3D (bone rest from node TRS, parent indices), attach Skin (bind poses from inverseBindMatrices) to skinned MeshInstance3D, convert joint-targeted animation channels to Skeleton3D bone tracks, and feed the same into import.rs's tscn writer and GLTFState.get_skins/get_skeletons.

**Prove it:** Instancing a rigged .glb fixture (2-bone arm with one animation) via load().instantiate() yields one Skeleton3D with 2 bones named after the joints, the MeshInstance3D's skeleton path points at it, and playing the AnimationPlayer clip for 0.5 s changes bone 1's pose to the keyed rotation; the editor reimport .scn contains the same Skeleton3D. (test: `gltf_skinned_import_skeleton_test`)

**Verifier note:** Skeleton3D appears in gdeditor/src/import.rs only at :272 (doc) and :2003 (test comment), and in gltf_import.rs only in comments (235, 1279, 1286, 1954). gltf_generate_scene (interpreter.rs:10692-10770) creates only Node3D/MeshInstance3D. call_gltf_state_instance method strings (22481-22564) are get_nodes/materials/textures/images/cameras/lights/root_nodes/meshes/base_path/filename/scene_name; no get_skins/get_skeletons, falling to gltf_unsupported at :22564. Parse-only with no consumer, so PARTIAL P1 holds.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A fixture project main.tscn instancing res://two_meshes.glb (two nodes, distinct translations, one with two primitives) loads through the runner path: the tree contains the glTF node names under the instance root with the authored transforms, each MeshInstance3D resolves to the glTF vertex count (not 24-vertex cube) with surface_count == primitive count, and a GDScript `var s = load("res://two_meshes.glb"); assert(s is PackedScene); add_child(s.instantiate())` yields the same subtree; GLTFDocument.append_from_file + generate_scene yields identical transforms/meshes; an animated fixture yields an AnimationPlayer whose library contains the clip. (test: `gltf_packed_scene_instancing_test`) 2) Instancing a rigged .glb fixture (2-bone arm with one animation) via load().instantiate() yields one Skeleton3D with 2 bones named after the joints, the MeshInstance3D's skeleton path points at it, and playing the AnimationPlayer clip for 0.5 s changes bone 1's pose to the keyed rotation; the editor reimport .scn contains the same Skeleton3D. (test: `gltf_skinned_import_skeleton_test`)

## WIP state (EmeraldCreek) — part 1 in progress, nothing wired yet Recording this so a peer who greps, or whoever inherits this bead, is not confused by a new file that nothing references. ### On disk now `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/gltf_scene.rs` — new, ~240 lines, with `build_gltf_subtree(tree, parent, &Resource) -> Option`: node hierarchy in document order, per-node TRS (quaternion -> Godot YXZ Euler via `Quaternion::to_euler`), MeshInstance3D / Camera3D / DirectionalLight3D / SpotLight3D / OmniLight3D class selection, and an AnimationPlayer populated from `animations_from_gltf_resource`. **It is deliberately NOT declared in `lib.rs`.** A file in `src/` with no `mod` line is not compiled, so this cannot break `gdscene` for any peer while it is half-finished. Parse- and format-checked with rustfmt on a scratch copy, and every API path it uses verified individually by reading the definition — one real error already caught that way: `Quaternion` is in `gdcore::math3d`, not `gdcore::math`. ### Triage finding: this bead is assembly, not new parsing Worth recording because the bead text reads bigger than it is. Everything needed already exists: - the importer DOES parse node hierarchy and TRS, including the `matrix` form (`gltf_import.rs` `node_trs`, written to each node dict as `translation` / `rotation` / `scale`), plus `children`, `mesh`, `camera`, `light`, `name`, and `scene_roots` for the default scene. - one subresource per primitive, keyed `mesh__prim_

` and tagged with `mesh_index` / `primitive_index` / `material_index`. - `Mesh3D` already supports multi-surface with paired per-surface materials, and `gdrender3d` already reads `Mesh3D::surfaces` (`renderer.rs:981-996`). - `animations_from_gltf_resource` and `material_from_gltf_resource` both exist. ### Remaining, in dependency order 1. declare `mod gltf_scene;` in `gdscene/src/lib.rs` (do this LAST of the source edits, once the module is known good). 2. `mesh3d_from_gltf_resource` currently takes only `subs[0]` — the whole file's first primitive, for every node. Needs a by-`mesh_index`, multi-surface variant, and `render_server_3d.rs:1350` needs to read the node's `gltf_mesh_index` (a property `generate_scene` already sets and NOTHING has ever read) instead of resolving per-file. 3. `importers.rs:1800` must report class `PackedScene` for `.glb`/`.gltf`, keeping the document on a property, so `interpreter.rs`'s `instantiate` stops raising "cannot instantiate a GltfDocument resource". 4. route `scripting.rs` `instantiate_packed_scene` (~:7412) and its sub-scene resolver by extension — both currently do `read_file_string` + `PackedScene::from_tscn` only, so a binary `.glb` resolves to `None` and is silently dropped. 5. `interpreter.rs` `gltf_generate_scene` (~:10692) should call the same builder rather than its own transform-less version. 6. fixture: `two_meshes.glb` (two nodes, distinct translations, one mesh with two primitives) + an animated one. Authoring these as real GLB binaries from Python is straightforward (12-byte header, JSON chunk, BIN chunk) and gives exact vertex counts to assert against. 7. the acceptance test `gltf_packed_scene_instancing_test`. Part 2 (skins -> Skeleton3D) is a separate P1 section with its own test and is untouched.

comments.author: EmeraldCreek
comments.text:
## Parked-bead diagnosis (EmeraldCreek) — the second failure is a ONE-LINE TEST BUG, not an implementation bug

I am not retrying this bead; it is parked and the reopen said to claim other
work. This is triage information so the operator does not have to re-derive it.

### How far it actually got

Verify 1 (exit 100) failed at test line 132: `is PackedScene` was false.
**Fixed** — cause was that `EngineBootstrap` never calls `set_path_roots`, so
`res://` could not resolve and `load()` fell through to an extension-guess chain
with no `.glb` arm.

Verify 2 (exit 100) failed LATER, at test line 150:
`MeshA must exist under the instanced glTF scene root`. So by then:

- `load("res://two_meshes.glb")` returns a resource, and
- `s is PackedScene` is TRUE — the class rename works, `can_instantiate`
  passes, and the marker printed.

Only the node PATH assertion failed.

### Cause, confirmed by reading the importer

`build_gltf_subtree` names the instanced root from `doc.get_property("scene_name")`
and falls back to the file stem. **The importer never sets `scene_name`** — the
`scenes` handler (`gltf_import.rs:471-481`) publishes ONLY `scene_roots` and
discards `scenes[i].name`.

So the root node is named from the file stem, `two_meshes`, and the real path is:

    /root/Main/two_meshes/MeshA

while the test asserts `/root/Main/TwoMeshes/MeshA` (the glTF scene's own name,
which my fixture does set to "TwoMeshes"). That is the whole failure.

### Two ways to finish it — the choice is a real one

1. **Minimal:** change the two `get_node_by_path` strings in
   `gltf_packed_scene_instancing_test.rs` from `TwoMeshes` to `two_meshes`.
   Matches the importer as it stands. One line each.
2. **Closer to Godot:** have the importer publish `scene_name` from
   `scenes[scene_idx].name` and let the builder prefer it. Godot names the
   imported scene root after the glTF scene, so this is the more faithful
   behaviour, and the builder already reads the property — it just always gets
   `None` today. Costs one `set_property` in `gltf_import.rs` and keeps the test
   asserting the authored name.

I would take (2): the builder was written expecting it, and a root named after
the file stem is wrong whenever the asset's scene is named.

### Everything else from the report still stands

The remaining scope is unchanged (the `.tscn` sub-scene path, `generate_scene`
parity, the animated fixture, and part 2's skins), and so is the recommendation
to convert the document INTO a PackedScene so one route serves the resolver,
`instantiate()` and `generate_scene`.

title: Timer: honor process_callback, process_mode under pause and ignore_time_scale
description:
[audit-key: signal-emission-sweep/timer-timeout] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/main/timer.cpp:50-70 (TIMER_PROCESS_PHYSICS ticks in INTERNAL_PHYSICS_PROCESS, idle otherwise; internal processing obeys node can_process/pause), :169-191

**Patina today:** SceneTree::process_timer_nodes (gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:2312-2377) ticks every Timer by idle delta, reads no process_callback or ignore_time_scale (grep '"process_callback"' gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs -> 0 hits), and is called only from main_loop.rs:4233 inside the `if !paused` branch (main_loop.rs:4119), so a PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS Timer never fires while the tree is paused and a physics-callback Timer ticks in the idle phase.

**Implement:** Godot Timer ticks in INTERNAL_PHYSICS_PROCESS when process_callback=PHYSICS and in INTERNAL_PROCESS otherwise (timer.cpp:50-70); it obeys the node's process_mode so an ALWAYS timer keeps firing timeout while the tree is paused, and ignore_time_scale uses unscaled delta. Patina's process_timer_nodes (scene_tree.rs:2312) is idle-only and invoked solely inside the not-paused branch (main_loop.rs:4119, :4233). title: Theme: honor theme_override_styles/font_sizes, theme_type_variation and button draw-mode styleboxes when drawing Controls
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/theme-override-render] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn-authored overrides -> scene load -> build_control_render_items -> pixels

**Godot ground truth:** scene/gui/control.cpp get_theme_stylebox/_get_theme_type_dependencies; scene/gui/button.cpp _notification(NOTIFICATION_DRAW) draw-mode stylebox selection

**Patina today:** control_render.rs reads only `theme_override_colors/font_color` and `theme_override_fonts/font` (grep `theme_override_` in control_render.rs: lines 1118-1119, 2824, 2851, 3065, 3409, 3935, 3995). `theme_override_styles/*` and `theme_override_font_sizes/*` are read NOWHERE in crates/*/src (grep `theme_override_font_sizes\|theme_override_styles` -> only container constants in control.rs). Button always draws the `normal` stylebox (control_render.rs:2809-2810); grep `"hover"\|"focus")\|"disabled")` finds no state stylebox selection even though `tree.hovered_control()` exists (control_render.rs:2885). Font size is always `theme.get_font_size("Button"/"Label",...)` (2827, 3074). `theme_type_variation` is never read in render (only control.rs:4270 resolve_theme_item, which has no callers); type names are hard-coded literals ("Button", "Label"), so `FlatButton` and base-type fallback do not work.

**Implement:** Godot resolves each item as local override -> theme chain over [type_variation chain..., class, parent classes...] (control.cpp _get_theme_type_dependencies), and BaseButton/Button choose normal/hover/pressed/hover_pressed/disabled stylebox and matching font_*_color per draw mode, drawing `focus` on top when focused (button.cpp NOTIFICATION_DRAW). Patina's control_render.rs uses hard-coded type names, reads only two override families, and always draws `normal`. Implement a single helper in control_render.rs `theme_item(tree,node,theme,kind,name)` that checks `theme_override_<kind>/<name>` (styles: resolve the SubResource StyleBox via stylebox_from_props; font_sizes: Int), then theme types derived from `theme_type_variation` (Theme::get_type_variation_base chain) and the node's ClassDB parent chain; replace the literal lookups in the Button, Label, Panel, LineEdit, CheckBox, OptionButton arms; add draw-mode selection using `disabled`, `button_pressed`, `tree.hovered_control()` and focus owner. Wiring: .tscn-authored overrides -> scene load -> build_control_render_items -> pixels.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/control_theme_overrides_and_states_render.rs`

**Prove it:** In one scene: a Button with `theme_override_styles/normal = SubResource(StyleBoxFlat bg red)` draws red; a Label with `theme_override_font_sizes/font_size = 32` draws glyphs ~2x taller than a sibling at 16; a Button with `theme_type_variation = &"FlatButton"` draws no background under a theme defining FlatButton/normal as StyleBoxEmpty; a disabled Button draws the theme's `disabled` box color, and hovering a Button (pushed mouse motion through MainLoop) switches to `hover`. (test: `control_theme_overrides_and_states_render`)

**Verifier note:** PARTIAL is right, but some evidence is overstated. The claim that `theme_override_styles`/`theme_override_font_sizes` are 'read NOWHERE' is false: (a) control.rs:3287 get_font_size reads `theme_override_font_sizes/font_size`, and the TabBar draw arm uses it (control_render.rs:4096); (b) scene_tree.rs:5176 flush_scripted_resources honours SCRIPTED `theme_override_styles/*` StyleBoxes, and the Panel arm draws them (control_render.rs:2789-2794). The core claims do hold. The Button arm always uses theme 'normal' (2809-2810). The Label arm uses theme.get_font_size("Label") or LabelSettings, not the override (3069-3076). A plain StyleBoxFlat SubResource override is never resolved for drawing. theme_type_variation is read only in the uncalled resolve_theme_item. Button hover/pressed/disabled/focus stylebox selection is absent: hovered_control is used only for the LinkButton underline (2885), and the disabled/pressed reads at 3097 are TextureButton only. P1 kept.
acceptance_criteria: In one scene: a Button with `theme_override_styles/normal = SubResource(StyleBoxFlat bg red)` draws red; a Label with `theme_override_font_sizes/font_size = 32` draws glyphs ~2x taller than a sibling at 16; a Button with `theme_type_variation = &"FlatButton"` draws no background under a theme defining FlatButton/normal as StyleBoxEmpty; a disabled Button draws the theme's `disabled` box color, and hovering a Button (pushed mouse motion through MainLoop) switches to `hover`. (test: `control_theme_overrides_and_states_render`)

description:
[audit-key: theming-text/text-shaping] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** Label text -> control_render layout -> Play rasterizer draws shaped glyph ids; scene with layout_direction=RTL -> layout -> Play pixels

### 1. TextServer shaping: ligatures, GSUB/GPOS, grapheme clusters, combining marks, script itemization  (MISSING, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** modules/text_server_adv/text_server_adv.cpp (_shape_run via HarfBuzz, ICU itemization); doc/classes/TextServer.xml shaped_text_*

**Patina today:** gdrender2d depends only on ab_glyph (gdrender2d/Cargo.toml) — no rustybuzz/harfbuzz/unicode-segmentation in any Cargo.toml (grep `rustybuzz\|harfbuzz\|unicode-bidi\|swash` -> none). TtfFont::measure_line sums per-char `advance`+`kern` (ttf_font.rs:137-148) and rasterize is per-`char` (ttf_font.rs:107), so ligatures, mark positioning, Arabic/Indic joining and multi-codepoint clusters are impossible. TextServerLite (gdrender2d/src/text_server.rs, 149 lines) exposes only get_char_advance/get_string_size/wrap/ellipsize.

**Implement:** Godot's default TextServerAdvanced shapes each run with HarfBuzz: ligatures, kerning via GPOS, mark attachment, contextual forms, and returns glyphs with cluster ranges used for caret/selection and drawing. Patina measures/draws one char at a time with ab_glyph (ttf_font.rs:107-148). Stage 1 (this bead): add rustybuzz (pure Rust, wasm-safe) to gdrender2d; add `ShapedRun { glyphs: Vec<{id, cluster, x_advance, x_offset, y_offset}> }` produced by `TtfFont::shape(text, px, features)`; segment by script (unicode-script) and grapheme clusters (unicode-segmentation); rasterize by glyph id (ab_glyph GlyphId) instead of char; make measure_line/wrap/ellipsize/draw_ttf_text_with_fallbacks and control_render::measure_text_px consume shaped advances. Wiring: Label text -> control_render layout -> Play rasterizer draws shaped glyph ids.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/ttf_font.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/text_server.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/Cargo.toml`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/label_text_is_shaped_in_play_render.rs`

**Prove it:** With a bundled test font that has an 'fi' ligature and combining-mark anchors, a Label with text "fi" renders the single ligature glyph (shaped run length 1) and "é" renders the acute positioned above the e (mark ink box overlaps base ink box horizontally) through the Play render path; an Arabic word draws joined forms (glyph ids differ from isolated forms). (test: `label_text_is_shaped_in_play_render`)

**Verifier note:** gdrender2d/Cargo.toml dependencies are gdcore, gdserver2d, gdvariant, thiserror, tracing, miniz_oxide and ab_glyph. No Cargo.toml in the workspace names rustybuzz, harfbuzz, unicode-bidi, unicode-segmentation, swash or brotli; Cargo.lock lists rustybuzz and unicode-bidi only as transitive deps of usvg (SVG), never used for text. ttf_font.rs rasterize(ch: char) (~107), and measure_line iterates text.chars() (~140). A grep for `fn shape|GlyphId|grapheme` in gdrender2d/src finds nothing. MISSING and P1 are correct.

### 2. BiDi, UAX#14 line breaking (incl. CJK), and RTL UI mirroring (layout_direction / text_direction)  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** modules/text_server_adv (ICU ubidi + ubrk line breaking), scene/gui/control.cpp is_layout_rtl, Label text_direction/structured_text_bidi_override

**Patina today:** grep -i `bidi\|is_layout_rtl\|layout_direction\|text_direction` over crates/*/src (excluding class_db/inspector schema) finds only translation.rs fake-bidi pseudolocalization and unrelated hits; `layout_direction` exists only as a ClassDB property (class_db.rs:18300,19154). TtfFont::wrap splits on ' ' only and breaks a word by char only if it overflows (ttf_font.rs:166-195), so CJK text without spaces is never broken at ideograph boundaries until overflow and no UAX#14 rules apply. Label `text_direction`, `language`, `structured_text_bidi_override` are never read (grep count 0 in control_render.rs).

**Implement:** Godot reorders mixed-direction text per UAX#9, breaks lines per UAX#14 (CJK breaks between ideographs), and mirrors Control layout (anchors, alignment, container order) when is_layout_rtl() (layout_direction RTL or locale RTL). Patina has none. Stage 2 after the shaping bead: add unicode-bidi + unicode-linebreak (wasm-safe) in gdrender2d; run bidi per paragraph (base direction from Label.text_direction / Control layout direction), shape visual runs, break lines at UAX#14 opportunities in ttf_font wrap/text_layout; in gdscene control.rs implement is_layout_rtl (layout_direction, inherited, locale-based via TranslationServer) and mirror horizontal anchors/offsets, HBox child order and Left/Right alignment. Wiring: scene with layout_direction=RTL -> layout -> Play pixels.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/ttf_font.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/text_layout.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/bidi_linebreak_and_rtl_layout_render.rs`

**Prove it:** A Label with text "abc אבג" draws the Hebrew run right-to-left (first logical Hebrew glyph rightmost); a 3-ideograph CJK Label with autowrap and width for 2 ideographs wraps into 2 lines at the ideograph boundary; an HBoxContainer with layout_direction=RTL places its first child at the right edge in the rendered frame. (test: `bidi_linebreak_and_rtl_layout_render`)

**Verifier note:** Partly refuted. RTL UI mirroring exists and is wired into container layout. control.rs:1348 implements is_layout_rtl, resolving Inherited up the parent chain, with Locale treated as LTR. arrange_container passes it to Box containers (control.rs:2232 -> arrange_box rtl) and GridContainer (2247, mirroring x at ~2201). The finder's evidence that 'layout_direction exists only as a ClassDB property' is wrong (control.rs:1326-1340 set/get_layout_direction). The rest is still missing. BiDi: `-i bidi` in gdrender2d/gdscene src finds only signal and navigation 'bidirectional' hits. UAX#14/CJK: `-i cjk|ideograph|uax` finds only a fallback comment at ttf_font.rs:367, and wrap splits on ' ' (~170). Label text_direction is never read. Anchor/offset mirroring and Left/Right alignment mirroring were not found. So the correct status is PARTIAL, not MISSING. The acceptance item about an RTL HBoxContainer may already pass at the layout level.
acceptance_criteria: 1) With a bundled test font that has an 'fi' ligature and combining-mark anchors, a Label with text "fi" renders the single ligature glyph (shaped run length 1) and "é" renders the acute positioned above the e (mark ink box overlaps base ink box horizontally) through the Play render path; an Arabic word draws joined forms (glyph ids differ from isolated forms). (test: `label_text_is_shaped_in_play_render`) 2) A Label with text "abc אבג" draws the Hebrew run right-to-left (first logical Hebrew glyph rightmost); a 3-ideograph CJK Label with autowrap and width for 2 ideographs wraps into 2 lines at the ideograph boundary; an HBoxContainer with layout_direction=RTL places its first child at the right edge in the rendered frame. (test: `bidi_linebreak_and_rtl_layout_render`)

title: Fonts: WOFF2 decode, resolve FontFile/FontVariation resources and fallbacks for drawing
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/fonts] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn Label with theme_override_fonts/font = FontVariation.tres (base .woff2) -> Play pixels

**Godot ground truth:** scene/resources/font.cpp (FontFile, FontVariation, fallbacks), modules/text_server_adv font_* (antialiasing, hinting, subpixel_positioning, msdf, oversampling, embolden, transform, spacing)

**Patina today:** woff_to_sfnt rejects WOFF2: 'WOFF2 uses Brotli compression, which this build has no decoder for' (gdresource/src/woff.rs:84-90) — Godot's own bundled fonts are .woff2. The only file-backed font load reads raw bytes from the CWD with `res://` stripped (gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:4682-4705), so a `.tres` FontFile/FontVariation path never parses and silently falls back. Fallbacks are always empty: `draw_ttf_text_with_fallbacks(..., &[], ...)` (viewport_2d_render.rs:3173-3176). FontVariation/SystemFont exist only as data models (gdrender2d/src/label_settings.rs:101-215) with no consumers (grep `FontVariation\|base_font` in render paths: only label_settings.rs). Theme `default_font` is never read (grep `default_font\|get_font(` in control_render.rs/viewport_2d_render.rs: none). Import flags antialiasing/hinting/subpixel_positioning/msdf/oversampling are copied onto the resource (gdresource/src/importers.rs:1249-1290) but no renderer reads them (grep of those keys in gdscene/gdrender2d src: none).

**Implement:** Godot loads TTF/OTF/WOFF/WOFF2 into FontFile, wraps them in FontVariation (base_font + variation_embolden/transform/opentype coords/spacing), resolves Font.fallbacks per missing glyph, and uses Theme.default_font / ThemeDB fallback font. Patina: WOFF2 rejected (woff.rs:84-90); file fonts loaded only as raw bytes relative to CWD (viewport_2d_render.rs:4682-4705); FontVariation unused; fallbacks hard-coded empty (3176); theme default_font unused. Implement: add a pure-Rust brotli decoder (e.g. `brotli-decompressor`) + WOFF2 table reconstruction (glyf/loca transform) in gdresource/woff.rs; replace with_override_font with a font resolver that resolves `res://` against the project root/PCK, parses `.tres` FontFile (data or source path) and FontVariation (base_font + embolden/spacing applied at draw: embolden via outline dilation or synthetic double-draw, spacing_glyph/space added to advances), loads `fallbacks` arrays into the slice passed to draw_ttf_text_with_fallbacks, and uses Theme.default_font when no override exists. Wiring: .tscn Label with theme_override_fonts/font = FontVariation.tres (base .woff2) -> Play pixels.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/woff.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/ttf_font.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/label_settings.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/font_resources_and_fallbacks_reach_play_render.rs`

**Prove it:** A Label whose theme_override_fonts/font is a FontVariation .tres with base_font = a .woff2 file and spacing_glyph = 4 renders with that face (ink differs from the built-in face) and with ink width larger by ~4px per glyph than the same text without spacing; a glyph missing from the primary font but present in its `fallbacks[0]` is drawn (non-empty ink in its cell); a Theme with default_font set changes all Labels. (test: `font_resources_and_fallbacks_reach_play_render`)

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. woff.rs:84-90 rejects WOFF2 with the Brotli message. with_override_font (viewport_2d_render.rs:4664-4690) reads raw bytes after stripping res://, so it does no .tres parsing. Fallbacks are hard-coded `&[]` at viewport_2d_render.rs:3176. Theme.default_font is parsed and stored (theme.rs:82, 928-930), but the grep `default_font|base_font|FontVariation` finds no reader in control_render.rs, viewport_2d_render.rs or the gdrender2d render path (renderer.rs:344 use_default_font is the builtin face, unrelated). msdf, subpixel_positioning and hinting appear only in the label_settings.rs data model. PARTIAL and P1 are correct.
acceptance_criteria: A Label whose theme_override_fonts/font is a FontVariation .tres with base_font = a .woff2 file and spacing_glyph = 4 renders with that face (ink differs from the built-in face) and with ink width larger by ~4px per glyph than the same text without spacing; a glyph missing from the primary font but present in its `fallbacks[0]` is drawn (non-empty ink in its cell); a Theme with default_font set changes all Labels. (test: `font_resources_and_fallbacks_reach_play_render`)

title: Text: draw font outline and drop shadow for Label/Button from theme and LabelSettings
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/text-effects] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn Label with LabelSettings outline -> Play render pixels

**Godot ground truth:** scene/gui/label.cpp NOTIFICATION_DRAW (shadow then outline then font passes via TextServer shaped_text_draw_outline); doc/classes/LabelSettings.xml

**Patina today:** control_render.rs consumes only `__ls__font_color` and `__ls__font_size` from LabelSettings (grep `"__ls__[a-z_]*"` over gdscene/src: 2 keys), although packed_scene.rs:1716-1719 copies every LabelSettings field. grep in control_render.rs for `outline_size`, `font_outline_color`, `font_shadow_color`, `shadow_offset`: 0 reads; default theme sets Label shadow constants (theme.rs:475-477) that nothing draws. No outline draw primitive exists in ttf_font.rs (functions listed at ttf_font.rs:48-457).

**Implement:** Godot draws text in three passes: shadow (font_shadow_color at shadow_offset, with shadow_outline_size), outline (font_outline_color, outline_size via glyph outline rasterization), then fill (label.cpp draw). LabelSettings carries outline_size/outline_color/shadow_size/shadow_color/shadow_offset. Patina draws only fill. Implement in gdrender2d/ttf_font.rs an outline rasterizer (dilate glyph coverage by outline_size px, or stroke the outline path) and a draw_ttf_text_effects(fill, outline, shadow) entry; add outline/shadow fields to the Text draw item in control_render.rs/viewport_2d_render.rs Render2DKind::Text; read theme constants/colors and theme overrides for Label/Button and the `__ls__outline_*`/`__ls__shadow_*` LabelSettings keys. Wiring: .tscn Label with LabelSettings outline -> Play render pixels.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/ttf_font.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/label_outline_and_shadow_render.rs`

**Prove it:** A Label with LabelSettings outline_size=4 outline_color=red renders red pixels in a 4px ring around white glyph ink; a Label with theme_override_colors/font_shadow_color=black and shadow offset (2,2) renders black ink offset 2px down-right of the fill ink; with neither, no extra colors appear. (test: `label_outline_and_shadow_render`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. grep `outline_size\|font_outline_color\|font_shadow_color\|shadow_offset` in gdscene/src/control_render.rs: 0 hits. grep `__ls__` over gdscene/gdrender2d/gdeditor src: the only readers are control_render.rs:3063 (__ls__font_color) and :3073 (__ls__font_size); packed_scene.rs:1719 is the writer. LabelSettings::has_outline (gdrender2d/src/label_settings.rs:75) is called only from its own tests (248, 255). Across gdrender2d/src, `fn .*outline` turns up only draw_rect_outline_blended (draw.rs:1239) and a test; there is no glyph outline rasterizer. The outline hits in gdeditor scene_renderer.rs are gizmo outlines, not text. P1 is right: outlined and shadowed labels are common in games.
acceptance_criteria: A Label with LabelSettings outline_size=4 outline_color=red renders red pixels in a 4px ring around white glyph ink; a Label with theme_override_colors/font_shadow_color=black and shadow offset (2,2) renders black ink offset 2px down-right of the fill ink; with neither, no extra colors appear. (test: `label_outline_and_shadow_render`)

title: i18n: auto-translate Control text, load project translations in every boot path, re-render on locale change
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/i18n-wiring] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** project.godot translations -> Play boot -> Label pixels change after a script calls TranslationServer.set_locale("fr")

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/node.cpp can_auto_translate/atr, scene/gui/label.cpp (xl_text = atr(text)), NOTIFICATION_TRANSLATION_CHANGED from TranslationServer::set_locale; core/string/translation_server.cpp load_translations from internationalization/locale/translations

**Patina today:** Label/Button draw `string_prop(tree,node_id,"text")` directly (control_render.rs:2819, 3041) — grep `translat` in control_render.rs/control.rs/scene_tree.rs finds no translation lookup; grep `auto_translate\|NOTIFICATION_TRANSLATION_CHANGED\|translation_changed` in crates/*/src (excluding class_db/inspector) finds only editor_ui.rs inspector JS. Project translations are loaded only by patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs:264 load_project_translations (called from boot_project, used by patina-runner main.rs:362); the editor Play path (examples/editor.rs) and patina-web never call boot_project or load translations (grep `boot_project\|load_project_translations` in crates/*/src + examples). So tr() works only after a script adds catalogs manually, and switching locale changes no UI text.

**Implement:** Godot Controls display atr(text) when auto_translate_mode resolves to ALWAYS/INHERIT (default) and re-translate on NOTIFICATION_TRANSLATION_CHANGED when TranslationServer.set_locale changes; translations listed in internationalization/locale/translations load at startup on every platform. Patina renders raw `text`, and only the desktop patina-runner loads project catalogs. Implement: move load_project_translations (project_boot.rs:264) into a shared gdscene/gdresource helper and call it from the editor Play start and the web boot; in control_render.rs resolve displayed text for Label/Button/LinkButton/CheckBox/OptionButton items/TabBar titles/placeholder via gdcore::translation::translate_with_context when the node's effective auto_translate_mode (inherit up the tree, default ALWAYS) allows; have TranslationServer.set_locale bump a translation epoch that MainLoop turns into NOTIFICATION_TRANSLATION_CHANGED (2000) to scripts and that invalidates cached label layouts. Wiring: project.godot translations -> Play boot -> Label pixels change after a script calls TranslationServer.set_locale("fr").

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/translation.rs`, `engine-rs/examples/editor.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/locale_switch_retranslates_labels_in_play.rs`

**Prove it:** A fixture project with a .po for 'fr' (msgid "HELLO" msgstr "Bonjour") listed in internationalization/locale/translations and a Label text="HELLO": rendered via the editor Play path with locale en, the Label draws 'HELLO'; after a script calls TranslationServer.set_locale("fr") the next frame's Label text layout is 'Bonjour' and the script's _notification receives 2000; a Label with auto_translate_mode=DISABLED keeps 'HELLO'. (test: `locale_switch_retranslates_labels_in_play`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. grep `load_project_translations\|boot_project` over crates/*/src and examples: only patina-runner (project_boot.rs:45, 264; bootstrap.rs:425 comments that EngineBootstrap bypasses boot_project). grep `locale/translations` outside translation.rs: only project_boot.rs:266. grep `auto_translate\|TRANSLATION_CHANGED\|translation_changed` in crates/*/src: only inspector_schema_generated.rs, editor_ui.rs and class_db.rs. grep `translat` in control_render.rs: 0 hits. P1 is right.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture project with a .po for 'fr' (msgid "HELLO" msgstr "Bonjour") listed in internationalization/locale/translations and a Label text="HELLO": rendered via the editor Play path with locale en, the Label draws 'HELLO'; after a script calls TranslationServer.set_locale("fr") the next frame's Label text layout is 'Bonjour' and the script's _notification receives 2000; a Label with auto_translate_mode=DISABLED keeps 'HELLO'. (test: `locale_switch_retranslates_labels_in_play`)

title: Particles: dispatch restart/emit_particle from scripts and let one_shot re-fire on emitting=true
description:
[audit-key: vfx-particles/particles-script-api] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: STUB]

**Wiring requirement:** GDScript call -> scripting.rs -> MainLoop particle phase -> published draw data

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/GPUParticles2D.xml restart(keep_seed), emit_particle(xform, velocity, color, custom, flags); scene/2d/gpu_particles_2d.cpp set_emitting (one_shot restarts on emitting=true)

**Patina today:** class_db.rs:14091-14095 registers restart/emit_particle/capture_rect/convert_from_particles/request_particles_process for GPUParticles2D (also CPUParticles2D ~14410), but `grep -rn '"restart"\|"emit_particle"\|"capture_rect"\|"convert_from_particles"' gdscene/src gdscript-interop/src` returns nothing: scripting.rs call_node_method (2594+) has no particle arm, so has_method is true and the call returns Nil silently. ParticleSimulator3D::restart (particle3d.rs:1046) has no non-test caller; 2D ParticleSimulator has no restart at all. Re-arm: main_loop.rs:1064 `one_shot_finished = emitter.one_shot && sim.total_emitted >= emitter.amount` and total_emitted is never reset, so a one-shot can never fire again even after a script sets emitting=false then true.

**Implement:** Godot: `$Boom.restart()` clears and re-emits; setting `emitting = true` on a finished one_shot starts a new cycle; `emit_particle(xform, velocity, color, custom, flags)` injects one particle honoring EMIT_FLAG_* bits (common for hit effects). Patina: methods registered (class_db.rs:14091-14095) with no dispatch arm in scripting.rs call_node_method; simulators live in MainLoop::particles so a script cannot reach them; one-shot completion is latched forever by total_emitted (main_loop.rs:1064, 1198). Fix: add a per-node command queue (e.g. `_particles_restart_requested` / `_particles_emit_queue` internal props, or a MainLoop-owned pending-command map like the cursor/command queues) written by a new `particles_node_call` arm in scripting.rs (before the generic table) for restart(keep_seed), emit_particle, request_particles_process, capture_rect (return the AABB of live particles), convert_from_particles (copy mapped properties); drain it at the top of process_particles: restart -> new ParticleSimulator::restart (2D) / existing restart (3D); emit -> inject_particle with position/velocity/color per flags. Track the previous `emitting` value per simulator and reset total_emitted/finished latch on a false->true edge for one_shot. Wiring: GDScript call -> scripting.rs -> MainLoop particle phase -> published draw data.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/particle.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/particles_script_restart_and_emit.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a one_shot GPUParticles2D and a GDScript that, on frame 60 (after `finished`), calls restart(): particle_count rises above 0 again and `finished` fires a second time; a second script setting emitting=false then emitting=true does the same; a script calling emit_particle(Transform2D(0, Vector2(50,0)), Vector2.ZERO, Color.RED, Color(), 1|8) on an emitting=false node yields one published red particle at x=50. (test: `particles_script_restart_and_emit`)

**Verifier note:** Grep across all crates for "restart", "emit_particle", "capture_rect", "capture_aabb", "convert_from_particles" and "request_particles_process" (excluding tests) hits only class_db.rs:14094-14098 and 14416-14418. No dispatch arm exists. `fn restart` exists only at particle3d.rs:1046, and its only caller is the test at :1479. The re-arm latch is confirmed: one_shot_finished at main_loop.rs:1064 and :1203 compares total_emitted, which is never reset, and nothing tracks an emitting false->true edge. Priority 1 is appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a one_shot GPUParticles2D and a GDScript that, on frame 60 (after `finished`), calls restart(): particle_count rises above 0 again and `finished` fires a second time; a second script setting emitting=false then emitting=true does the same; a script calling emit_particle(Transform2D(0, Vector2(50,0)), Vector2.ZERO, Color.RED, Color(), 1|8) on an emitting=false node yields one published red particle at x=50. (test: `particles_script_restart_and_emit`)

title: ParticleProcessMaterial: emission shapes, emission offset/scale, flatness and Godot default direction/gravity (+2 related)
description:
[audit-key: vfx-particles/particles-process-material-sim] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn -> flatten -> MainLoop readers -> emit_particle -> published positions; material -> readers -> simulators -> published arrays -> 2D renderers (and the 3D instance path); material -> readers -> simulators -> published positions

### 1. ParticleProcessMaterial emission shapes (point/sphere/sphere_surface/box/points/directed_points/ring) + emission_shape_offset/scale + flatness + Godot defaults for direction/gravity  (MISSING, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** scene/resources/particle_process_material.cpp _update_shader (EMISSION_SHAPE_* branches), doc/classes/ParticleProcessMaterial.xml emission_* (default direction Vector3(1,0,0), gravity Vector3(0,-9.8,0))

**Patina today:** `grep -c emission_shape main_loop.rs` = 0; neither the 2D reader (main_loop.rs:935-998) nor read_emitter_3d sets emission_shape, so every emitter emits from a point. 2D EmissionShape (particle.rs:68-81) lacks points/directed points/sphere-surface and ring height/axis; 3D EmissionShape3D (particle3d.rs:171-183) has a non-Godot Cone and lacks points/directed points/ring. `grep -c 'emission_sphere_radius\|emission_box_extents\|emission_points\|emission_ring' main_loop.rs` = 0. Defaults: 2D ParticleMaterial direction UP / gravity ZERO (particle.rs:157-161), 3D direction UP (particle3d.rs:289) vs Godot (1,0,0) and (0,-9.8,0); keys absent from a .tscn mean the Godot default, so a stock material emits the wrong way. flatness: grep count 0.

**Implement:** Godot: emission_shape 0..6 (POINT, SPHERE, SPHERE_SURFACE, BOX, POINTS, DIRECTED_POINTS, RING) with emission_sphere_radius, emission_box_extents, emission_point_texture/normal_texture/color_texture + emission_point_count, emission_ring_axis/height/radius/inner_radius/cone_angle, emission_shape_offset/scale; flatness collapses spread onto the XY plane; unset direction=(1,0,0), gravity=(0,-9.8,0) (particle_process_material.cpp). Patina: no reader sets emission_shape (main_loop.rs), enums incomplete (particle.rs:68-81, particle3d.rs:171-183), defaults wrong (particle.rs:157-161, particle3d.rs:289). Fix: extend both enums to Godot's 7 shapes (POINTS/DIRECTED_POINTS sample from flattened emission point arrays - flatten the ImageTexture point data in packed_scene.rs into __emission_points/__emission_normals); apply emission_shape_offset/scale; implement flatness in 3D perturb_direction; set ParticleMaterial/ParticleMaterial3D defaults to Godot's when the node lacks the key; read every emission_* key in both readers (CPUParticles2D/3D carry the same names on the node). Wiring: .tscn -> flatten -> MainLoop readers -> emit_particle -> published positions.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/particle.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/particle3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/particle_emission_shapes_from_tscn.rs`

**Prove it:** From a .tscn: a GPUParticles2D with emission_shape=3 (BOX) emission_box_extents=Vector3(50,10,1) publishes spawn positions spread across |x|<=50,|y|<=10 with some |x|>25; emission_shape=6 (RING) radius 40 inner 30 spawns at distances 30..40; a material with no direction/gravity keys and initial_velocity 100 moves particles along +x. (test: `particle_emission_shapes_from_tscn`)

**Verifier note:** Emission shapes are confirmed missing: `grep -n 'emission_|flatness|EmissionShape' main_loop.rs packed_scene.rs` returns 0. CPUParticles2D gets emission_shape/emission_* seeded onto the node from ClassDB (class_db.rs:14206-14240), but nothing reads them. The enum gaps are confirmed at particle.rs:68-81 and particle3d.rs:171-183. The defaults part is partly refuted. Nodes are seeded from ClassDB at instantiation (packed_scene.rs:2690-2695, scene_tree.rs:7973). CPUParticles2D therefore gets direction Vector2(1,0) and gravity (0,980) (class_db.rs:14198, 14260), which the 2D reader accepts. CPUParticles3D gets direction (1,0,0) and gravity (0,-9.8,0) (class_db.rs:5937-5944). So the wrong-default claim holds only for material-backed GPUParticles2D/3D (particle.rs:157-161, particle3d.rs:289), where Godot's documented defaults are direction (1,0,0) and gravity (0,-9.8,0) (ParticleProcessMaterial.xml:172, 239). ParticleProcessMaterial per-particle animation params: angle (+rotation rendered), angular velocity, orbit velocity, radial/tangential accel and damping (2D), linear_accel, directional_velocity, scale split XYZ / scale_over_velocity, hue_variation, color_initial_ramp, alpha/emission curves, anim_speed/anim_offset, particle_flags (align_y, rotate_y, disable_z)  (MISSING, P1)
