**Patina today:** Grep counts in gdscene/src/{main_loop,particle,particle3d}.rs: orbit_velocity 0/0/0, hue_variation 0/0/0, anim_speed 0/0/0, angle_min 0/0/0, particle_flag 0/0/0, scale_amount 0/0/0; radial_accel/tangential_accel/damping exist only in 3D (particle3d.rs:252-266) and are never read from the node (main_loop count 0 for radial/tangential, damping hit at main_loop.rs:2664 is physics). 2D angular_velocity integrates rotation (particle.rs:737) but is never read from a node and rotation is never published (main_loop.rs:1240-1252 publishes positions/colors/scales only) nor applied when drawing textures (viewport_2d_render.rs:3300-3315 centered_quad, unrotated).

**Implement:** Godot integrates per particle: initial angle + angular_velocity -> rotation, orbit_velocity (2D orbit around emitter), linear/radial/tangential accel, damping, scale over curves and per-axis split (scale_curve_x/y/z), scale_over_velocity, hue_variation, color_initial_ramp, alpha_curve, emission_curve, anim_speed/anim_offset (drives CanvasItemMaterial particles_anim frame), and particle_flag_align_y / rotate_y / disable_z (particle_process_material.cpp shader generation; cpu_particles_2d.cpp _particles_process mirrors it on CPU). **Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/particle.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/particle3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/particle_material_animation_params_from_tscn.rs`

The CPUParticles2D node carries angle_min and scale_amount_min seeded from ClassDB (class_db.rs:14131, 14363), but the 2D reader ignores them, so seeding does not fix this.

### 3. Turbulence (turbulence_enabled, noise_strength/scale/speed/speed_random, influence min/max/curve, initial_displacement)  (MISSING, P2)

title: Particles: Godot emission timing (explosiveness ratio, randomness, preprocess, amount_ratio, seed) and node defaults
description:
[audit-key: vfx-particles/particles-emission-timing] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn -> MainLoop readers -> simulators -> published counts/positions

**Godot ground truth:** scene/2d/gpu_particles_2d.cpp, scene/2d/cpu_particles_2d.cpp (_particles_process: emission phase uses explosiveness + randomness, preprocess pre-simulates); doc/classes/GPUParticles2D.xml (fixed_fps default 30, draw_order default 1)

**Patina today:** particle.rs:828-872 only distinguishes explosiveness>=1.0 vs continuous, so 0<e<1 behaves as 0. Grep counts in main_loop/particle/particle3d: preprocess 0/0/0, amount_ratio 0/0/0, use_fixed_seed 0/0/0, "seed" 0/0/0, fract_delta 0/0/0, visibility_rect 0/0/0. Defaults: Node::get_property returns Nil for unset keys (node.rs:296-298) and the 2D reader falls back to ParticleEmitter::default fixed_fps=0, draw_order=Index (particle.rs:334-335), while ClassDB registers Godot's fixed_fps 30 / draw_order 1 (class_db.rs:13983-13996) - a .tscn that omits them gets non-Godot behaviour. read_emitter_3d (main_loop.rs:381-472) reads no draw_order/fixed_fps/local_coords.

**Implement:** Godot: each of `amount` slots restarts at phase (i/amount)*(1-explosiveness) + randomness jitter; preprocess pre-simulates N seconds on first emit; amount_ratio limits active slots; use_fixed_seed+seed make emission deterministic and restart(keep_seed) replays it; fixed_fps defaults to 30 on GPUParticles2D/3D with interpolate; draw_order defaults to LIFETIME for GPUParticles2D (cpu_particles_2d.cpp _particles_process; gpu_particles_2d.cpp). Patina: binary explosiveness (particle.rs:828), none of preprocess/amount_ratio/seed/fract_delta, wrong defaults when the key is absent (particle.rs:334-335 vs class_db.rs:13983-13996), 3D reads none of draw_order/fixed_fps/local_coords. Fix: replace the accumulator emission with Godot's per-slot cycle phase model in both simulators (slot phase = i/amount*(1-explosiveness), jittered by randomness), honor amount_ratio by skipping slots >= amount*ratio, run preprocess on simulator creation in fixed 1/30 steps, seed the xorshift from `seed` when use_fixed_seed, fall back to ClassDB defaults (gdobject::get_class_info property default) when the node lacks a key, add draw_order (incl. VIEW_DEPTH for 3D) / fixed_fps / local_coords to read_emitter_3d; cull nothing but publish visibility_rect for the editor. Wiring: .tscn -> MainLoop readers -> simulators -> published counts/positions.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/particle.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/particle3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/particle_emission_timing_from_tscn.rs`

**Prove it:** From a .tscn: amount 10, lifetime 1, explosiveness 0.5 has ~5-10 particles alive at t=0.1s (vs 1 for 0.0 and 10 for 1.0); preprocess 1.0 has particle_count>=8 after the first frame; amount_ratio 0.5 caps live count at 5; two loads with use_fixed_seed=true seed=7 publish identical positions; a GPUParticles2D with no fixed_fps/draw_order keys publishes lifetime-ordered draw data. (test: `particle_emission_timing_from_tscn`)

**Verifier note:** The 2D defaults claim is refuted. Node::get_property does return Nil for unset keys, but every node loaded from a .tscn is first seeded with ClassDB defaults (packed_scene.rs:2676-2695, node_with_class_defaults; scene_tree.rs:7973 for create_node). GPUParticles2D registers draw_order Int(1) and fixed_fps Int(30) (class_db.rs:13982-13996). The 2D reader then picks them up as Variant::Int (main_loop.rs:953-959), so a .tscn that omits them already gets Godot's defaults. Drop that part of the bead. The rest is confirmed: explosiveness is binary at >=1.0 (particle.rs:828), and preprocess, amount_ratio, use_fixed_seed, "seed", fract_delta and visibility_rect all grep 0/0/0 in main_loop/particle/particle3d. read_emitter_3d (main_loop.rs:381-472) reads no draw_order, fixed_fps or local_coords, even though ClassDB seeds fixed_fps=30 on GPUParticles3D (class_db.rs:5547).
acceptance_criteria: From a .tscn: amount 10, lifetime 1, explosiveness 0.5 has ~5-10 particles alive at t=0.1s (vs 1 for 0.0 and 10 for 1.0); preprocess 1.0 has particle_count>=8 after the first frame; amount_ratio 0.5 caps live count at 5; two loads with use_fixed_seed=true seed=7 publish identical positions; a GPUParticles2D with no fixed_fps/draw_order keys publishes lifetime-ordered draw data. (test: `particle_emission_timing_from_tscn`)

title: CPUParticles2D/3D: read the node-level property surface (scale_amount, color_ramp, curves, emission)
description:
[audit-key: vfx-particles/cpuparticles-surface] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn -> flatten -> readers -> simulators -> renderers

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/CPUParticles2D.xml (70 properties incl. scale_amount_min/max, color_ramp: Gradient, color_initial_ramp, emission_shape on the node, *_curve: Curve); scene/2d/cpu_particles_2d.cpp convert_from_particles

CPUParticles2D's color_ramp is a Gradient directly on the node, but the ramp flattener only runs for `process_material` (packed_scene.rs:996-1000), and the 2D reader never reads __color_ramp_* anyway. CPUParticles' *_curve properties are Curve resources on the node - not baked anywhere. convert_from_particles has no dispatch (see script API finding).

**Implement:** Godot: CPUParticles2D/3D carry their process parameters on the node with different names from ParticleProcessMaterial (scale_amount_min/max, scale_amount_curve, color_ramp/color_initial_ramp as Gradient, *_curve as Curve, emission_* and particle_flag_* on the node), and convert_from_particles maps a GPUParticles node's material onto them (cpu_particles_2d.cpp). Patina: reads CPUParticles nodes with the GPU key list (main_loop.rs:935-998, 381-472), so scale_amount_*, node-level Gradient color_ramp and Curve properties are dropped; packed_scene.rs only bakes ramps reachable through process_material. Fix: in packed_scene.rs add a CPUParticles2D/3D pass that bakes node-level color_ramp/color_initial_ramp (Gradient sub_resource, direct offsets/colors) and every *_curve Curve into the same __*_samples keys the material path uses; in the readers alias scale_amount_min/max -> scale_min/max and scale_amount_curve -> scale_curve for CPUParticles classes. Wiring: .tscn -> flatten -> readers -> simulators -> renderers.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/cpuparticles_node_surface_from_tscn.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn CPUParticles2D with scale_amount_min=scale_amount_max=4 and color_ramp = SubResource(Gradient white->transparent) publishes _particle_scales of 4.0 and colours whose alpha falls with age; a CPUParticles3D with scale_amount_curve shrinking to 0 publishes decreasing scales. (test: `cpuparticles_node_surface_from_tscn`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. Outside class_db.rs and inspector_schema_generated.rs, no .rs file mentions scale_amount (grep -rln scale_amount crates). In packed_scene.rs:996-1000 the color_ramp/scale_curve flatten only runs on sub_resources typed ParticleProcessMaterial that hang off process_material (:1038, :1071). Nothing bakes a node-level Gradient or Curve. color_ramp_curve() (main_loop.rs:577) is read only by the 3D emitter reader (:434). main_loop.rs:859/864 groups the CPU and GPU classes together. convert_from_particles is only registered (class_db.rs:14097, 14417) and has no implementation. CPUParticles are common, so P1 stands.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn CPUParticles2D with scale_amount_min=scale_amount_max=4 and color_ramp = SubResource(Gradient white->transparent) publishes _particle_scales of 4.0 and colours whose alpha falls with age; a CPUParticles3D with scale_amount_curve shrinking to 0 publishes decreasing scales. (test: `cpuparticles_node_surface_from_tscn`)

title: Input: map pointer events through the stretch transform and the game-view scale
description:
[audit-key: input/input-coordinates] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/viewport.cpp push_input (event xformed by final/stretch transform inverse); Window content_scale

**Patina today:** gdscene/src/viewport.rs:113-125 RootWindow::window_to_canvas carries the comment 'Input MUST go through this'. Its only callers are its own tests (viewport.rs:244,250); grep 'window_to_canvas' elsewhere: 0. The renderer does apply stretch (gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs:197 apply_stretch_transform). scene_tree.rs push_input (5662) and main_loop push_event (2990) never apply an inverse. The editor game view posts raw CSS pixels (editor_ui.rs:12563-12564 clientX - rect.left) without the naturalWidth/rect.width scale that its other handlers use (editor_ui.rs:7067-7069).

**Implement:** Godot transforms every pointer event (position, relative, velocity) by the inverse of the window's content-scale transform before _input or the GUI sees it, so clicks hit what is drawn. Patina draws through RootWindow::stretch_transform (scene_renderer.rs:197) but never maps input back: window_to_canvas (viewport.rs:119) has no runtime caller. The editor game view also sends CSS-pixel coordinates without scaling to the frame's natural size (editor_ui.rs:12563). Fix: (1) In editor_ui.rs, scale game input coords by viewportImg.naturalWidth/rect.width, as the edit-mode handlers do. (2) In MainLoop::push_event (or SceneTree::push_input), apply root_window().window_to_canvas to MouseButton, MouseMotion, ScreenTouch, ScreenDrag and gesture positions, and the basis-only inverse to relative and velocity. Keep screen_relative and screen_velocity unscaled. (3) Do the same in patina-web CanvasMapping (browser_input.rs:44), which applies DPR only.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/viewport.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs`

**Prove it:** Project uses stretch mode canvas_items, base 640x360, window 1280x720. A Button at canvas (100,100)-(200,140). A mouse press posted at window (300,240) emits 'pressed', and the script's _input sees position (150,120). Test: (test: `input_stretch_coordinate_mapping_test`).

**Verifier note:** `grep -rn window_to_canvas` over gdscene/src, gdeditor/src and patina-web/src hits only viewport.rs:120 (the definition) and its tests at :231-250. MainLoop::push_event (main_loop.rs:2990-3007) and SceneTree::push_input (scene_tree.rs:5662+) apply no inverse transform. The game-view mousemove handler (editor_ui.rs:12563-12564) posts clientX-rect.left with no naturalWidth scale; the edit-mode handlers at :7067, :7962 and :8017 do scale. api_input_mouse_move takes x/y as given. P0 stands, since GUI clicks miss under any stretch.
acceptance_criteria: Project uses stretch mode canvas_items, base 640x360, window 1280x720. A Button at canvas (100,100)-(200,140). A mouse press posted at window (300,240) emits 'pressed', and the script's _input sees position (150,120). Test: (test: `input_stretch_coordinate_mapping_test`).

title: JavaScriptBridge: pump JS callbacks every frame and define the shell hooks force_fs_sync/pwa_* call
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web-js-bridge-wiring] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** a JS click handler -> created callback -> GDScript Callable on the next frame, inside a running WebEngine

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/platform/web/javascript_bridge_singleton.cpp; doc/classes/JavaScriptBridge.xml (create_callback invoked from JS, force_fs_sync, pwa_update, pwa_needs_update + pwa_update_available signal)

**Patina today:** crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:15357 pump_javascript_callbacks is the only consumer of gdplatform::js_bridge::take_callback_invocations (js_bridge.rs:455). `grep -rn pump_javascript_callbacks engine-rs` gave only its definition, doc comments, and crates/gdscript-interop/tests/javascript_bridge_wasm.rs:238-269, with no call in gdscene/MainLoop or patina-web. So a JS event that fires a created callback is queued forever. The WasmJsBackend calls globals `__patina_fs_sync` (js_bridge.rs:809-816), `__patina_pwa_update` and `__patina_pwa_update_pending` (js_bridge.rs:788-806). `grep -rn __patina` over web_export.rs, export.rs, patina-web/src and examples/web_export.rs found none of them defined, so force_fs_sync is a no-op and pwa_* always report no update. There is no pwa_update_available signal.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: a Callable wrapped by JavaScriptBridge.create_callback runs when JS invokes the returned function. force_fs_sync flushes user:// to IndexedDB. pwa_needs_update/pwa_update drive the service-worker update, and the singleton emits pwa_update_available (doc/classes/JavaScriptBridge.xml, platform/web/javascript_bridge_singleton.cpp). Patina today: the queue/pump design is in place (js_bridge.rs:417-460, interpreter.rs:15357), but no runtime path calls the pump. The JS globals the wasm backend calls are never defined by any shell. Approach: (1) call Interpreter::pump_javascript_callbacks once per MainLoop::step, at the same safe point as other deferred script drains (gdscene main_loop.rs step, after input dispatch, before _process), via whatever handle gdscene uses to reach the interpreter. (2) In DEFAULT_SHELL (gdplatform/src/web_export.rs) define window.__patina_fs_sync = () => store.drainPendingWrites(db, vfs). Register sw.js and set window.__patina_pwa_update_pending / window.__patina_pwa_update from the registration's waiting worker. (3) Emit pwa_update_available when the pending flag flips (polled per frame). Wiring requirement: a JS click handler -> created callback -> GDScript Callable on the next frame, inside a running WebEngine.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/web_export.rs`

**Prove it:** A host test installs a js_bridge backend double, boots a scene whose script calls JavaScriptBridge.create_callback(_on_js) and stores the result. It simulates JS invoking the callback (queue_callback_invocation), steps the MainLoop once through WebEngine::frame, and asserts _on_js ran exactly once with the passed args. A second assertion renders DEFAULT_SHELL and checks it defines __patina_fs_sync, __patina_pwa_update and __patina_pwa_update_pending. (test: `web_js_callback_runs_on_next_frame`)

**Verifier note:** grep 'pump_javascript_callbacks|take_callback_invocations' over crates/ and apps/ found the definition at interpreter.rs:15357, the js_bridge.rs definition and in-file tests (:455, :940, :950), and tests/javascript_bridge_wasm.rs only. No gdscene, MainLoop or patina-web caller exists, and gdscene/src does not reference js_bridge at all. grep '__patina_fs_sync|__patina_pwa' over crates, examples and apps hit only the readers at js_bridge.rs:793, 802 and 811, with no definitions in any shell. P1 stands.
acceptance_criteria: A host test installs a js_bridge backend double, boots a scene whose script calls JavaScriptBridge.create_callback(_on_js) and stores the result. It simulates JS invoking the callback (queue_callback_invocation), steps the MainLoop once through WebEngine::frame, and asserts _on_js ran exactly once with the passed args. A second assertion renders DEFAULT_SHELL and checks it defines __patina_fs_sync, __patina_pwa_update and __patina_pwa_update_pending. (test: `web_js_callback_runs_on_next_frame`)

title: Editor: make web export produce the bootable web_export bundle and add Export + Run in Browser to the UI
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web-editor-export] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** editor UI button -> /api/export/run -> bundle whose pck PckMount accepts and whose index.html calls init/WebVfs/startEngine

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/platform/web/export/export_plugin.cpp (export + 'Run in Browser' via EditorHTTPServer serving the export with COOP/COEP); platform/web/export/editor_http_server.cpp

**Patina today:** The editor route crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:12228-12290 api_export_run calls PackageExecutor::generate_web_bundle (crates/gdplatform/src/export.rs:536). That bundle writes a pack with magic `PATINA_PCK1` (export.rs:657), which PckMount rejects: gdresource/src/pck.rs:204 requires `GDPC`. Its loader export.rs:1350-1392 does `WebAssembly.instantiate(buffers[0], self.config.imports || {})` on a wasm-bindgen module with empty imports, and never calls init/WebVfs/startEngine. This is a second pipeline parallel to the working gdplatform/src/web_export.rs DEFAULT_SHELL + examples/web_export.rs (PckPacker, GDPC). The served EDITOR_HTML never calls the route: grep '/api/export' in crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs shows only presets GET/POST/delete/update (16870-16976), and there is no Run-in-Browser. Editor Play (/api/runtime/play, editor_server.rs:2593) runs the game natively on the server and never uses the wasm runtime.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: the Web export preset writes index.html + .js + .wasm + .pck (GDPC) that boots in a browser. 'Run in Browser' (remote debug button) exports to a temp dir and serves it from the editor's HTTP server with COOP/COEP headers (platform/web/export/export_plugin.cpp, editor_http_server.cpp). Patina today: the editor route uses gdplatform/src/export.rs generate_web_bundle, which writes a PATINA_PCK1 pack (export.rs:657) that gdresource PckMount cannot parse (pck.rs:204). Its loader instantiates the wasm-bindgen module with `{}` imports and never starts the engine (export.rs:1388). No editor UI calls /api/export/run (editor_ui.rs:16870-16976 only manage presets). Approach: delete the parallel shell/loader/pck writer in export.rs and have generate_web_bundle reuse gdplatform::web_export::{layout, render_html_shell, pwa_files} plus gdresource::pck::PckPacker (the same code examples/web_export.rs uses), copying the wasm-bindgen JS next to the wasm. Add an Export button to the export dialog in EDITOR_HTML that POSTs /api/export/run. Add POST /api/export/run_in_browser, which exports to a temp dir and serves it under /web-run/ with the editor's existing COOP/COEP header constant (editor_server.rs:3117). Wiring requirement: editor UI button -> /api/export/run -> bundle whose pck PckMount accepts and whose index.html calls init/WebVfs/startEngine.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/export.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/web_export.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs`

**Prove it:** An integration test runs api_export_run (through the editor HTTP router) for a Web preset on fixtures/project with a dummy wasm payload. It asserts that the emitted .pck parses with gdresource::pck::PckMount::from_bytes and contains res://project.godot, that index.html imports init/WebVfs/startEngine and fetches that exact .pck name, and that no file contains PATINA_PCK1. A second assertion greps EDITOR_HTML for a fetch to /api/export/run, and one more GETs /web-run/index.html after run_in_browser and checks the response carries Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin. (test: `editor_web_export_bundle_boots_pck`)

**Verifier note:** export.rs:657 writes the b"PATINA_PCK1" magic, while gdresource pck.rs:64 PCK_MAGIC = b"GDPC". export.rs:1389 calls `WebAssembly.instantiate(buffers[0], self.config.imports || {})`. The editor_server.rs:2891 route /api/export/run exists, but grep 'api/export' in editor_ui.rs finds only the presets GET/POST/delete/update calls (16870, 16941, 16950, 16976). grep 'export/run|exportRun' in the other gdeditor src files found no UI caller. There is no run_in_browser route. Unwired, P1.
acceptance_criteria: An integration test runs api_export_run (through the editor HTTP router) for a Web preset on fixtures/project with a dummy wasm payload. It asserts that the emitted .pck parses with gdresource::pck::PckMount::from_bytes and contains res://project.godot, that index.html imports init/WebVfs/startEngine and fetches that exact .pck name, and that no file contains PATINA_PCK1. A second assertion greps EDITOR_HTML for a fetch to /api/export/run, and one more GETs /web-run/index.html after run_in_browser and checks the response carries Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin. (test: `editor_web_export_bundle_boots_pck`)

title: Web input: deliver echo, unicode/keycode/physical_keycode and meta from DOM key events, plus IME composition
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web-input-keyboard] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** DOM keydown -> browser_input -> MainLoop::push_event -> a focused LineEdit's text

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/platform/web/dom_keys.inc + display_server_web.cpp key_callback (keycode from `key`, physical_keycode from `code`, unicode, echo=repeat, meta); ime callbacks (compositionstart/update/end)

**Patina today:** crates/patina-web/src/browser_runtime.rs:257-283: keydown with event.repeat() is dropped (`return`) instead of delivered as echo, and only event.code() + shift/ctrl/alt are passed (meta_key ignored). crates/patina-web/src/browser_input.rs:128-143 key_event maps the physical code only, with no `key`/unicode input. The InputEvent::Key variant itself has only key/pressed/shift/ctrl/alt (crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs:612-618). grep -rln compositionstart over patina-web, gdplatform/src and gdscene/src gave no hits, so there is no IME.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: DisplayServerWeb::key_callback builds InputEventKey with physical_keycode from KeyboardEvent.code, keycode/key_label from KeyboardEvent.key (dom_keys.inc), unicode from the printable key, echo = event.repeat, and meta/command modifiers. IME composition events feed DisplayServer IME text (display_server_web.cpp). Patina today: repeats are swallowed (browser_runtime.rs:262), only `code` is translated (browser_input.rs:128), meta is ignored, and the engine's InputEvent::Key cannot carry unicode/echo/meta (gdplatform/src/input.rs:612). On a non-QWERTY layout, LineEdit/TextEdit typing and key_label-based bindings cannot work in a web build. Approach: extend key_event to take (code, key, repeat, meta) and produce physical + logical keycodes, unicode for single-codepoint `key`, and echo. Add the needed fields to the InputEvent::Key path, or use the richer key event struct gdscene already dispatches to scripts if one exists; check main_loop push_event's conversion. Add compositionstart/update/end listeners on a hidden input element that forward IME text through the same path the native winit backend uses for Ime events. Wiring requirement: DOM keydown -> browser_input -> MainLoop::push_event -> a focused LineEdit's text.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/browser_input.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/browser_runtime.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs`

**Prove it:** A host test drives browser_input::key_event with (code="KeyQ", key="a", AZERTY) and asserts physical keycode KEY_Q, keycode KEY_A, unicode 'a'. A repeated keydown yields echo=true and is delivered. Pushing the translated events through WebEngine into a scene with a focused LineEdit makes its text equal 'a' after one frame. A composition-end payload "日本" appends that text to the LineEdit. (test: `web_keyboard_text_reaches_line_edit`)

**Verifier note:** browser_runtime.rs:271-273 returns early on event.repeat(), and key_event gets only code() plus shift/ctrl/alt (:274-280, no meta, no key()). gdplatform/src/input.rs:612-618 InputEvent::Key has only key/pressed/shift/ctrl/alt. The enum variants are Key, MouseButton, MouseMotion, GamepadButton, GamepadAxis, ScreenTouch, ScreenDrag, Midi, Action and MagnifyGesture, with no Text or Ime variant. grep 'composition' in patina-web and gdplatform/src found 0 hits. P1 is right, since text input fails on the web.
acceptance_criteria: A host test drives browser_input::key_event with (code="KeyQ", key="a", AZERTY) and asserts physical keycode KEY_Q, keycode KEY_A, unicode 'a'. A repeated keydown yields echo=true and is delivered. Pushing the translated events through WebEngine into a scene with a focused LineEdit makes its text equal 'a' after one frame. A composition-end payload "日本" appends that text to the LineEdit. (test: `web_keyboard_text_reaches_line_edit`)

title: Web DisplayServer: bind fullscreen, pointer lock, CSS cursor, document.title and clipboard to the canvas (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web-display-server] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** GDScript DisplayServer/Input call -> MainLoop state -> WebEngine display requests -> DOM API; GDScript call -> engine request queue -> DOM API; MIDI message -> InputEvent::Midi -> script _input

### 1. DisplayServer on web: fullscreen, pointer lock (MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED), cursor shape, window title, clipboard  (MISSING, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/platform/web/display_server_web.cpp has_feature (FEATURE_CLIPBOARD, FEATURE_CURSOR_SHAPE, FEATURE_CUSTOM_CURSOR_SHAPE, FEATURE_MOUSE, FEATURE_ICON) lines 1194-1229; js/libs/library_godot_display.js (requestFullscreen, requestPointerLock, style.cursor, document.title, navigator.clipboard)

**Patina today:** No wasm32 code paths exist in gdplatform clipboard.rs, cursor.rs, display.rs or window.rs: `grep cfg(target_arch` over gdplatform/src lists only fetch_state, fetch_web, http_request, js_bridge, lib, os, web_request_driver, websocket_peer, websocket_web, xr_web, xr. grep for requestPointerLock|requestFullscreen|navigator.clipboard|document.title|style.cursor across patina-web, gdplatform/src and gdscene/src matched only the dead model gdplatform/src/web.rs:410 WebPlatformLayer::request_fullscreen, which has no callers outside its own tests (grep 'WebPlatformLayer' has no external hits). FrameOutput carries cursor_shape 'so the host shell can set its CSS cursor' (gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:70-75), but browser_runtime.rs:520 discards the FrameOutput.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: on the web, DisplayServer.window_set_mode(FULLSCREEN) calls canvas.requestFullscreen(). Input.mouse_mode = CAPTURED calls requestPointerLock and reports relative motion. cursor_set_shape/custom image sets canvas.style.cursor. window_set_title sets document.title, and clipboard_get/set use navigator.clipboard (display_server_web.cpp:1194-1229, library_godot_display.js). Fullscreen and pointer lock are deferred until the next user gesture. Patina today: none of these have a browser binding. The only model is gdplatform/src/web.rs:359 WebPlatformLayer, which nothing calls, and the per-frame cursor_shape in FrameOutput is thrown away (browser_runtime.rs:520). Approach: after each stepped frame in install_frame_loop, apply engine-side display requests: map FrameOutput.cursor_shape -> CSS cursor, pending title, window mode, mouse mode. Do it through a small `WebDisplayRequests` struct computed in host-testable code (patina-web/src/engine.rs). The wasm side issues requestFullscreen/exitFullscreen/requestPointerLock on the next pointerdown/keydown gesture. Bind clipboard via a write-through cache (navigator.clipboard.writeText on set; readText refreshed on paste/focus events) so DisplayServer.clipboard_get stays synchronous. Remove or route WebPlatformLayer so there is one implementation. Wiring requirement: GDScript DisplayServer/Input call -> MainLoop state -> WebEngine display requests -> DOM API.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/engine.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/browser_runtime.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/web.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/clipboard.rs`

**Prove it:** A host test boots a scene whose script sets DisplayServer.window_set_mode(WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN), Input.mouse_mode = MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED, DisplayServer.window_set_title('Game') and DisplayServer.clipboard_set('x'), with a hovered Button using CURSOR_POINTING_HAND. After one WebEngine::frame, the computed WebDisplayRequests report fullscreen=true, pointer_lock=true, title='Game', css_cursor='pointer', clipboard_write='x'. With pointer lock active, a pointermove produces relative motion only. `scripts/check-wasm.sh` stays green. (test: `web_display_requests_reach_dom`)

**Verifier note:** grep 'requestPointerLock|request_pointer_lock|requestFullscreen|request_fullscreen|navigator.clipboard|set_title|style().set_property' over patina-web/src and gdplatform/src hit only the WindowManager trait/headless/winit set_title (window.rs:100,187; winit_backend.rs:206) and the dead WebPlatformLayer::request_fullscreen (web.rs:410, called only from its test at :633). grep 'cursor_shape' in patina-web/src found 0 hits, so FrameOutput.cursor_shape (main_loop.rs:77) is never consumed. MISSING at P1 is fine.

### 2. Web: TextToSpeech, virtual keyboard, gamepad rumble, Web MIDI  (MISSING, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/platform/web/display_server_web.cpp (FEATURE_TEXT_TO_SPEECH via speechSynthesis, FEATURE_VIRTUAL_KEYBOARD); js/libs/library_godot_input.js (gamepad vibrationActuator.playEffect); platform/web/webmidi_driver.cpp

**Patina today:** grep -rln 'speechSynthesis|vibrationActuator|playEffect|requestMIDIAccess|virtual_keyboard' over crates/patina-web and crates/gdplatform/src found no browser binding. The web-sys features list in crates/patina-web/Cargo.toml has no GamepadHapticActuator/SpeechSynthesis/MIDIAccess. InputEvent::Midi exists (gdplatform/src/input.rs, Midi variant) but nothing on wasm produces it.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: on the web, DisplayServer.tts_speak/stop/get_voices use window.speechSynthesis. virtual_keyboard_show focuses a hidden input on touch devices. Input.start_joy_vibration calls gamepad.vibrationActuator.playEffect('dual-rumble'). OS.open_midi_inputs uses navigator.requestMIDIAccess and emits InputEventMIDI (display_server_web.cpp, library_godot_input.js, webmidi_driver.cpp). Patina today: none are bound on wasm32. Approach: same pattern as browser_runtime/browser_input. Decision logic (request queues, MIDI byte -> InputEvent::Midi parsing, rumble magnitude/duration mapping) goes in host-testable modules, and DOM calls go in browser_runtime (enabling web-sys features). The per-frame engine requests carry tts/vibration commands, polled like the display requests. Wiring requirement: GDScript call -> engine request queue -> DOM API; MIDI message -> InputEvent::Midi -> script _input.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/browser_input.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/browser_runtime.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/Cargo.toml`

**Prove it:** Host tests: a script calling Input.start_joy_vibration(0, 0.5, 1.0, 0.2) yields one rumble request (pad 0, weak 0.5, strong 1.0, 200ms) after a WebEngine frame. DisplayServer.tts_speak('hi', voice) yields a speak request. Raw MIDI bytes [0x90, 60, 100] translated by the web MIDI decoder and pushed through WebEngine reach a script's _input as InputEventMIDI note-on pitch 60 velocity 100. `scripts/check-wasm.sh` green. (test: `web_tts_rumble_midi_requests`)

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. I ran grep -rniE 'tts|vibrat|rumble|midi|virtual_keyboard|speech' over crates/patina-web and got zero hits. The native-side support is real: TTS/start_joy_vibration in gdscene/src/scripting.rs and main_loop.rs, gdcore/src/display_backend.rs, decode_midi_message in gdplatform/src/input.rs. A browser requestMIDIAccess path does exist, but only in the editor's served client (gdeditor/tests/webmidi_client_forwards_browser_midi.rs: browser -> POST /api/runtime/input/midi to the editor-run game). That is the editor lane, not the wasm32 web export runtime. Nothing in the patina-web sources (audio, browser_input, browser_runtime, canvas, engine, lib, vfs, web_audio, web_vfs) binds speechSynthesis, vibrationActuator, a virtual keyboard or Web MIDI. P2 is right: these are uncommon features.

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/gltf/gltf_document.cpp (_import_animation creates an AnimationPlayer with an AnimationLibrary in the imported scene)

**Patina today:** gdscene/src/animation.rs:1944 `animations_from_gltf_resource` is called only from gdscene/tests/gltf_anim_import.rs (grep 'animations_from_gltf_resource' across crates excluding its definition = tests only). gdresource/src/gltf_import.rs:472-490 publishes clips on the document for the scene layer to consume, and nothing does. render_server_3d.rs:1353-1357 uses import_gltf only for meshes.

Approach: where a .glb/.gltf is instanced as a PackedScene (packed_scene.rs ext-resource instancing path, or the glTF-to-scene builder if one exists), add an `AnimationPlayer` node under the root and attach an AnimationPlayer built from animations_from_gltf_resource. Map track node_paths to the generated node and bone names (Skeleton3D:Bone for skinned joints).

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation.rs`

**Prove it:** A test .glb with one translation animation, instanced from a .tscn ExtResource: the instanced subtree contains an AnimationPlayer whose get_animation_list() contains the clip, and after play() plus 0.5 s of MainLoop steps the animated node's position matches the glTF sampler value. (test: `gltf_scene_animation_player_plays`)

**Verifier note:** Partly refuted. It is true that animations_from_gltf_resource (animation.rs:1944) has only test callers (gdscene/tests/gltf_anim_import.rs). But the finder missed a second, wired path in the editor: gdeditor/src/import.rs:1042 build_gltf_animations converts the document's clips, :1209-1211 adds an AnimationPlayer node, and imported_scene_to_tscn (:1447, :1577-1582) writes `libraries = {"": SubResource(...)}` into a .scn under .godot/imported. That runs from the editor route api_reimport (editor_server.rs:23664-23671). The gap is at runtime: a .glb ExtResource loads through importers.rs:1800-1801 import_gltf_asset as a plain Resource, and scene reimport does not write a [remap] (only textures do, editor_server.rs comment). title: Skeleton3D: implement SpringBoneSimulator3D with collisions
description:
[audit-key: animation/skeleton-spring-bone] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: STUB]

**Wiring requirement:** MainLoop -> process_skeletons_with_delta -> process_modifiers_with_delta -> spring bone -> bone_pose_array -> skinning

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/spring_bone_simulator_3d.cpp, spring_bone_collision_*_3d.cpp; doc/classes/SpringBoneSimulator3D.xml

**Patina today:** Only a ClassDB registration exists: grep -rln '"SpringBoneSimulator3D"' gdscene/src gdobject/src = gdobject/src/class_db.rs only. skeleton3d.rs process_modifiers_with_delta (:655-760) has no arm for it, and the comment at :788 notes it cannot fit the pose-pure pass. No SpringBoneCollision* handling (grep -rni 'spring_bone\|springbone' gdscene/src = 0 code hits).

**Implement:** Godot ground truth (spring_bone_simulator_3d.cpp): per setting chain (root/end bone, stiffness, drag, gravity, radius curves, center node), a Verlet-style joint simulation runs each modifier pass with the frame delta, with sphere, capsule and plane collisions from SpringBoneCollision*3D children.

Patina: the class is registered only, and process_modifiers_with_delta skips it.

Approach: add a stateful modifier in a new gdscene/src/spring_bone.rs. Keep per-node joint state (previous and current tail positions) in a SceneTree side map keyed by NodeId. Read the `settings/N/*` properties as Godot serialises them, port the _process_joints integration and collision pushes, and write bone poses back with set_bone_pose_rotation. Dispatch it from process_modifiers_with_delta with the real delta (already threaded, pat-s3rrv.158).

Wiring: MainLoop -> process_skeletons_with_delta -> process_modifiers_with_delta -> spring bone -> bone_pose_array -> skinning.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/skeleton3d.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn Skeleton3D with a 3-bone hanging chain and SpringBoneSimulator3D (gravity down), moved sideways by a script: after MainLoop steps the tail bone's global pose lags and then settles back. A SpringBoneCollisionSphere3D in the path keeps the tail outside its radius. (test: `spring_bone_simulator_chain_swings`)

**Verifier note:** grep -rni 'spring_?bone' over crates/*.rs (tests excluded) finds only class_db.rs:4768-4796 (registration), inspector_schema_generated.rs:5098-5102, and a comment at skeleton3d.rs:788 saying a time-integrating modifier like SpringBoneSimulator3D does not fit the pass. There is no dispatch arm in the modifier match (skeleton3d.rs:742-753). The upstream sources exist (scene/3d/spring_bone_simulator_3d.cpp and spring_bone_collision_*.cpp). STUB (registration only) at P2 is fair.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn Skeleton3D with a 3-bone hanging chain and SpringBoneSimulator3D (gravity down), moved sideways by a script: after MainLoop steps the tail bone's global pose lags and then settles back. A SpringBoneCollisionSphere3D in the path keeps the tail outside its radius. (test: `spring_bone_simulator_chain_swings`)

title: Skeleton3D: add TwoBoneIK3D, SplineIK3D, Jacobian solver and remaining SkeletonModifier3D classes
description:
[audit-key: animation/skeleton-modifier-family] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: STUB]

**Wiring requirement:** process_modifiers_with_delta dispatch -> bone poses -> skinning

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/two_bone_ik_3d.cpp, spline_ik_3d.cpp, jacobian_ik_3d.cpp, bone_twist_disperser_3d.cpp, limit_angular_velocity_modifier_3d.cpp, modifier_bone_target_3d.cpp, skeleton_ik_3d.cpp

**Patina today:** skeleton3d.rs:744-753 match covers IKModifier3D, FABRIK3D, CCDIK3D and JacobianIK3D. JacobianIK3D is routed to CCD and marked 'a deliberate placeholder, not parity' (:747-752). grep '"TwoBoneIK3D"\|"SplineIK3D"\|"BoneTwistDisperser3D"\|"LimitAngularVelocityModifier3D"\|"ModifierBoneTarget3D"' gdscene/src = 0 (class_db.rs registration only), and '"SkeletonIK3D"' = 0 anywhere.

**Implement:** Godot 4.6 ground truth: the SkeletonModifier3D subclasses listed in extension_api.json run in child order in the modifier pass and blend by `influence`.

Patina: only FABRIK, CCD, LookAt, Copy, Convert and Aim execute (skeleton3d.rs:655-760). JacobianIK3D silently uses CCD, and the rest are registration-only.

Approach: in ik_solver.rs add an analytic two-bone solver with pole target, a Jacobian (DLS) solver, and spline fitting along a Path3D Curve3D. In skeleton3d.rs add apply_* functions for BoneTwistDisperser3D (distribute twist along the chain), LimitAngularVelocityModifier3D (clamp the per-frame rotation delta, needs delta and state), ModifierBoneTarget3D (publish a bone transform to the node), and SkeletonIK3D (legacy FABRIK with magnet). Read each class's serialised properties as Godot names them. Honour `influence` for all of them.

Wiring: process_modifiers_with_delta dispatch -> bone poses -> skinning.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/skeleton3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/ik_solver.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn arm rig with TwoBoneIK3D targeting a Marker3D: after MainLoop steps the tip bone's global origin is within 1e-3 of the target and the elbow bends toward the pole node. A JacobianIK3D chain converges to the same target. LimitAngularVelocityModifier3D caps a 180-degree snap to max_angular_velocity*delta per frame. (test: `skeleton_modifier_family_scene`)

**Verifier note:** The runtime gap is real. skeleton3d.rs:742-753 dispatches only IK_MODIFIER, FABRIK, CCDIK and JACOBIAN_IK, with JacobianIK3D routed to CCD and labelled a placeholder at :746-751. All other classes hit `_ => continue`. But most of the family is not MISSING: grep '"<Class>"' over crates/*/src shows TwoBoneIK3D, SplineIK3D, BoneTwistDisperser3D, LimitAngularVelocityModifier3D and ModifierBoneTarget3D registered in gdobject/src/class_db.rs (plus inspector_schema_generated.rs). JacobianIK3D runs on a stand-in solver. Only SkeletonIK3D is truly absent from class_db (it appears only in inspector_schema_generated.rs). Registered with no behaviour is STUB, the same label the SpringBoneSimulator3D finding uses. Each class has a .cpp in upstream/godot/scene/3d and a doc XML.

title: Multiplayer: rpc() broadcasts to all peers, server relays, and receivers enforce @rpc mode
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/mp-rpc-core] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** a script on peer A calls rpc('m') -> interpreter.rs:6942 -> scripting.rs node_rpc -> MultiplayerAPI::rpc -> transport -> MainLoop poll (main_loop.rs:4266) on peers B and C -> the script method runs there

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/multiplayer/scene_rpc_interface.cpp (rpcp: target 0 = all peers; _process_rpc: rejects methods without rpc config, checks RPC_MODE_AUTHORITY against get_multiplayer_authority, call_remote vs call_local); scene_multiplayer.cpp server_relay

**Patina today:** gdplatform/src/network.rs:410-440 MultiplayerAPI::rpc targets `authority_map.get(&node_path).unwrap_or(PeerId::SERVER)`; authority_map is only written by set_authority, which has no non-test callers (grep '\.set_authority(' -> only network.rs:2671,2910 inside mod tests at :2404). So rpc() never broadcasts: on a server it sends to peer 1 = itself, and WebSocketMultiplayerPeer::send_packet (websocket_multiplayer.rs:541-545) returns PeerUnreachable for an id with no conn. Receive side: scene_tree.rs:2032-2042 dispatches every decoded RPC with call_script_with_access regardless of whether the method is @rpc or of RPCMode; grep 'RPCMode::' outside tests finds only the registration at scene_tree.rs:2061-2068 - mode is never checked. No server relay: grep 'relay' in network.rs/websocket_multiplayer.rs -> only a comment at network.rs:319.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: Node.rpc(method,...) sends to target peer 0 (every connected peer); on a client the server relays it to the other clients when SceneMultiplayer.server_relay is true. The receiver (scene_rpc_interface.cpp _process_rpc) drops calls to methods with no rpc config, and for RPC_MODE_AUTHORITY drops any call whose sender is not the node's multiplayer authority. call_remote (the default) does not run on the sender; call_local runs it on the sender synchronously.

Patina today: gdplatform/src/network.rs:410-440 sends rpc() only to authority_map[path] or PeerId::SERVER, and authority_map is never written outside tests, so the target is always peer 1. A server's rpc() therefore goes to itself, and the WS server transport returns PeerUnreachable (websocket_multiplayer.rs:541-545). gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:2032-2042 runs every inbound RPC without checking that the method is @rpc or that RPCMode allows the sender, which lets any peer call any script method on any node. Server relay is not implemented.

Implementation: (1) MultiplayerAPI::rpc sends to PeerId(0)/broadcast. Each NetworkPeer::send_packet (websocket_multiplayer.rs, webrtc_peer.rs:868, OfflineMultiplayerPeer network.rs:879, tcp_multiplayer.rs) must treat target 0 as all peers and a negative id as all-except. (2) Add server_relay (default true): when the server receives a broadcast RPC from a client it forwards it to the other peers, keeping the original sender id. (3) Carry RPCMode through DecodedRPC dispatch. In SceneTree::poll_multiplayer_with_delta, drop methods with no rpc config and drop RPC_MODE_AUTHORITY calls where sender != get_multiplayer_authority(node) (scene_tree.rs:3389). Push a Godot-style error for each dropped call. (4) Delete the authority_map routing (authority lives on the node).

Wiring: a script on peer A calls rpc('m') -> interpreter.rs:6942 -> scripting.rs node_rpc -> MultiplayerAPI::rpc -> transport -> MainLoop poll (main_loop.rs:4266) on peers B and C -> the script method runs there.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_multiplayer.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`

**Prove it:** Use two MockNetwork or WebSocket loopback pairs, or one server with two clients, each running a real SceneTree/MainLoop from a .gd script. (a) The server's rpc('sync_state', 5) reaches both clients. (b) A client's rpc to an any_peer method reaches the server and, through relay, the other client, and get_remote_sender_id() reports the original client. (c) A client calling an authority-only method on a server-owned node is rejected and the method does not run. (d) Calling a method without @rpc is rejected on the receiver. (e) call_remote does not run on the sender and call_local does. (test: `multiplayer_rpc_broadcast_authority_test`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. network.rs:410-440 MultiplayerAPI::rpc targets authority_map.get(..).unwrap_or(PeerId::SERVER). set_authority (network.rs:801) is called only at network.rs:2671 and :2910, both inside mod tests (:2404); grep 'set_authority(|authority_map' across crates/ finds nothing else except a comment at scene_tree.rs:1367. scripting.rs:6332-6366 node_rpc passes broadcast 0 only to the script-extension hook, then calls the built-in rpc() with no target, so there is no per-peer fan-out. websocket_multiplayer.rs:536-545 on the server role does conns.get(&to) and returns PeerUnreachable for id 1. On receive, scene_tree.rs:2032-2042 calls call_script_with_access for every decoded RPC. network.rs:497-503 poll decodes every RPC without checking rpc_configs. RPCMode appears only at registration (scene_tree.rs:2061-2068). grep 'relay' in gdplatform/src finds only network.rs:319 (a comment) and webrtc_peer.rs:405 (ICE). P0 is justified: a server rpc() never reaches clients, and any peer can call any method.
acceptance_criteria: Use two MockNetwork or WebSocket loopback pairs, or one server with two clients, each running a real SceneTree/MainLoop from a .gd script. (a) The server's rpc('sync_state', 5) reaches both clients. (b) A client's rpc to an any_peer method reaches the server and, through relay, the other client, and get_remote_sender_id() reports the original client. (c) A client calling an authority-only method on a server-owned node is rejected and the method does not run. (d) Calling a method without @rpc is rejected on the receiver. (e) call_remote does not run on the sender and call_local does. (test: `multiplayer_rpc_broadcast_authority_test`)

title: Skeleton3D: wire BoneMap/SkeletonProfile into a RetargetModifier3D runtime
description:
[audit-key: animation/skeleton-retarget] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** scene load -> process_skeletons_with_delta -> retarget -> target skeleton poses -> skinning

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/bone_map.cpp, skeleton_profile.cpp, scene/3d/retarget_modifier_3d.cpp

**Patina today:** gdscene/src/bone_map.rs implements SkeletonProfile and BoneMap, but grep -rn 'bone_map' across crates excluding bone_map.rs and tests = only `pub mod bone_map;` (lib.rs:29) and a signal name in class_db.rs:1887. The module is dead. grep '"RetargetModifier3D"' gdscene/src gdobject/src = 0, so the class is not even registered.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: RetargetModifier3D (a child of a source Skeleton3D) copies the source's poses onto child Skeleton3Ds by matching bone names through a SkeletonProfile, transferring rest-relative rotations and optionally positions and scales (retarget_modifier_3d.cpp). BoneMap and SkeletonProfile are resources loaded from scenes and import settings.

Patina: bone_map.rs exists with no callers, and RetargetModifier3D is unregistered.

Approach: register RetargetModifier3D (profile, use_global_pose, enable flags) in class_db.rs. Load the SkeletonProfile/BoneMap sub-resources into bone_map.rs types on scene load. Add apply_retarget_modifier to process_modifiers_with_delta that, for each child Skeleton3D, maps bones by profile name and writes poses with rest correction.

Wiring: scene load -> process_skeletons_with_delta -> retarget -> target skeleton poses -> skinning.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/bone_map.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/skeleton3d.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn with an animated source Skeleton3D, a RetargetModifier3D using SkeletonProfileHumanoid, and a child Skeleton3D with different rest poses but the same profile bone names: after MainLoop steps the child's `LeftUpperArm` global rotation tracks the source's within 1e-3. (test: `retarget_modifier_profile_copies_pose`)

title: AnimationPlayer: markers, auto-capture, wildcard blend times, method/discrete callback modes
description:
[audit-key: animation/anim-player-advanced] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** script/tscn -> AnimationPlayer -> process_animations

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/animation.cpp (add_marker, get_marker_time; `markers` storage), scene/animation/animation_player.cpp:470-485 (blend_times with "*" wildcards), play_with_capture/playback_auto_capture*; animation_mixer.cpp callback_mode_method (DEFERRED/IMMEDIATE) and callback_mode_discrete (DOMINANT/RECESSIVE/FORCE_CONTINUOUS)

**Patina today:** grep 'marker' gdscene/src/animation.rs animation_tscn.rs = 0 code hits (play_section_with_markers dispatch = 0). get_blend_time (animation.rs:1071) does an exact (from,to) lookup with no '*' fallback. callback_mode_method and callback_mode_discrete are registered in class_db.rs:4967-4974 but not read; method tracks always call immediately (scene_tree.rs:4299-4310). playback_auto_capture is registered (class_db.rs:5021) with no runtime effect.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: Animation keeps named markers (scene `markers = [{name,time,color}]`), and play_section_with_markers plays between two of them. playback_auto_capture plus play_with_capture blend from the current property values into the first frame. Blend times resolve (from,to), then (*,to), then (from,*). callback_mode_method=DEFERRED queues method-track calls to the end of the frame, and callback_mode_discrete picks how discrete tracks blend.

Patina: none of these exist.

Approach: parse `markers` in animation_tscn.rs and add marker storage plus play_section_with_markers and its backwards variant in animation.rs. Add wildcard lookups to get_blend_time. Implement capture by snapshotting the target values when playing with capture. In process_animations, queue method calls via the existing deferred-call mechanism when the mode is DEFERRED. Apply callback_mode_discrete in the crossfade blend.

Wiring: script/tscn -> AnimationPlayer -> process_animations.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tscn.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn clip with markers `a`(0.2) and `b`(0.6) plays only that range via `$AP.play_section_with_markers("clip","a","b")` from GDScript. set_blend_time("*","run",0.3) crossfades from any clip into run. With callback_mode_method=0 (DEFERRED), a method-track call runs after the frame's property writes. (test: `animation_player_markers_capture_wildcards`)

**Verifier note:** Every sub-claim holds. grep -rni 'marker' in gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src hits only packed_scene/sub_viewport/render_server_3d, nothing for animation; play_section_with_markers has 0 hits. play_section exists (animation.rs:959, scripting.rs:6753, interpreter.rs:13307). get_blend_time (animation.rs:1071-1076) is an exact HashMap lookup with no '*' fallback; Godot falls back to wildcards at animation_player.cpp:470-475. grep 'callback_mode_method|callback_mode_discrete|auto_capture|play_with_capture' hits only class_db.rs:4976-5054. The method track runs call_script_with_access immediately (scene_tree.rs:4310-4319). Priority should go from 3 to 2. Godot's default callback_mode_method is 0 = DEFERRED (class_db.rs:4976 registers Int(0)), and animation_mixer.cpp:1667 defers method-track calls by default. So every Godot game with method tracks gets end-of-frame call timing, and Patina gives immediate calls. That is a common-path behavior difference, not an exotic one. Auto-capture is also on by default (play() routes through play_with_capture, animation_player.cpp:402-405), though it only matters for capture-mode tracks.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn clip with markers `a`(0.2) and `b`(0.6) plays only that range via `$AP.play_section_with_markers("clip","a","b")` from GDScript. set_blend_time("*","run",0.3) crossfades from any clip into run. With callback_mode_method=0 (DEFERRED), a method-track call runs after the frame's property writes. (test: `animation_player_markers_capture_wildcards`)

title: Navigation: feed avoidance the parent body's global position instead of the agent's local position
description:
[audit-key: navigation/nav-avoidance-global-pos] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn with two CharacterBody2D each holding a NavigationAgent2D(avoidance_enabled=true) -> MainLoop physics tick -> process_navigation_avoidance -> velocity_computed(safe_velocity) emitted to a script that move_and_slide()s with it

**Godot ground truth:** scene/2d/navigation/navigation_agent_2d.cpp NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PHYSICS_PROCESS: agent_set_position(agent, agent_parent->get_global_position()); same in scene/3d/navigation/navigation_agent_3d.cpp; obstacles use get_global_position()

**Patina today:** gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:1849 `positions = agent_nodes.map(|id| node2d::get_position(&self.tree, *id))`, :1827 obstacle `node2d::get_position`, :1971 and :1951 the same for 3D via node3d::get_position. node2d.rs:27 get_position reads the node's own `position` property, which a NavigationAgent2D (extends Node) never has, so it returns ZERO. process_navigation was already switched to global position (main_loop.rs:2203-2218, pat-s3rrv.20 comment) but the avoidance pass was not. The green test gdscene/tests/navigation_avoidance_3d_velocity_computed.rs:68 sets `position` directly on the NavigationAgent3D node, a property Godot agents lack, which hides the bug.

**Implement:** Godot: every physics frame NavigationAgent2D/3D call agent_set_position(agent, agent_parent->get_global_position()), and obstacles submit their global position (navigation_agent_2d.cpp, navigation_obstacle_2d.cpp). Patina: process_navigation_avoidance (gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:1795) gathers agent positions with node2d::get_position (:1849) and obstacle positions with node2d::get_position (:1827). The 3D pass does the same at :1971/:1951. An agent is a plain Node child of a CharacterBody, so it has no `position` and every agent is solved at (0,0). ORCA then sees all agents overlapping, and velocity_computed returns garbage. The existing tests set `position` on the agent node, which a Godot scene never does. Fix: use node2d::get_global_position / node3d::get_global_transform(..).origin for agents and obstacles in both passes, the same as process_navigation at :2218. Remove `position` from the agent nodes in the avoidance tests and parent the agents under CharacterBody2D/3D nodes instead. Wiring: .tscn with two CharacterBody2D each holding a NavigationAgent2D(avoidance_enabled=true) -> MainLoop physics tick -> process_navigation_avoidance -> velocity_computed(safe_velocity) emitted to a script that move_and_slide()s with it.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/navigation_avoidance_3d_velocity_computed.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn with two CharacterBody2D bodies 40px apart, each with a child NavigationAgent2D (avoidance_enabled, radius 10) and a script that calls set_velocity toward the other body and moves with the velocity_computed payload. Over 120 physics frames the bodies never come closer than 2*radius - epsilon. The same scene in 3D with CharacterBody3D/NavigationAgent3D behaves the same way. No agent node carries a `position` property (test: `nav_avoidance_uses_parent_global_position`).

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. The finder's citations check out: main_loop.rs:1827 (obstacle2D node2d::get_position), :1849 (agent2D positions via node2d::get_position), :1951 and :1971 (3D via node3d::get_position). node2d.rs:27-34 get_position reads only the node's own 'position' property and falls back to ZERO, with no parent fallback. No runtime code writes 'position' onto agent nodes (grep set_property("position" in main_loop.rs/navigation_agents.rs: test-only hits at 5772/5780). process_navigation does use get_global_position (main_loop.rs:2218) and global_transform.origin (:2226), so the two passes disagree. The test fixture tests/navigation_avoidance_3d_velocity_computed.rs:67 sets 'position' directly on a root-child NavigationAgent3D. P0 is justified: the feature looks done (green tests) but the standard scene setup is broken.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with two CharacterBody2D bodies 40px apart, each with a child NavigationAgent2D (avoidance_enabled, radius 10) and a script that calls set_velocity toward the other body and moves with the velocity_computed payload. Over 120 physics frames the bodies never come closer than 2*radius - epsilon. The same scene in 3D with CharacterBody3D/NavigationAgent3D behaves the same way. No agent node carries a `position` property (test: `nav_avoidance_uses_parent_global_position`).

title: Object: Godot-shaped method/signal/property lists with script members and revert virtuals (+1 related)
description:

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

### 1. Object introspection shapes and script virtuals (get_method_list/get_signal_list/get_property_list, _property_can_revert/_property_get_revert/_validate_property, to_string)  (PARTIAL, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** core/object/object.cpp Object::get_method_list/get_signal_list/get_property_list include script members; MethodInfo/PropertyInfo dict shapes (name,args[dict],default_args,flags,id,return); Object.xml virtuals _property_can_revert/_property_get_revert/_validate_property; Node::to_string -> "Name:<Class#id>"

**Patina today:** get_method_list (interpreter.rs:12993-13008) returns {name, args: Int} from ClassDB only (no script methods, args not an Array of dicts, no flags/return/default_args); get_signal_list (13010-13030) ClassDB-only with args as Strings (script `signal` declarations omitted); get_property_list (12955-12991) ClassDB + _get_property_list but no script `var`s/categories; property_can_revert/property_get_revert (13032-13046, 13112-13125) consult ClassDB only - `grep '"_property_can_revert"|"_property_get_revert"|"_validate_property"'` over gdscene/gdscript-interop -> 0 hits. Explicit `obj.to_string()` arm (13959-13966) ignores a script _to_string (str()/print do honor it via display_variant at 15247) and lacks Node's 'Name:' prefix.

**Implement:** Godot's get_method_list/get_signal_list return MethodInfo dicts {name, args:[{name,type,class_name,hint,hint_string,usage}], default_args, flags, id, return} including the script's methods/signals; get_property_list includes script variables (PROPERTY_USAGE_SCRIPT_VARIABLE) and category/group entries; property_can_revert/get_revert call the script's _property_can_revert/_property_get_revert first; _validate_property lets scripts edit each PropertyInfo before it is returned; Node.to_string() is "Name:<Class#id>" unless _to_string overrides. Patina's arms (interpreter.rs:12955-13125, 13959) are ClassDB-only with simplified shapes. Implementation: build MethodInfo/PropertyInfo dicts from class_db MethodInfo arguments and the script's list_methods/list_signals/list_properties (ScriptInstance in gdscene/src/scripting.rs), append script members, call _validate_property per entry via call_script_method, consult _property_can_revert/_property_get_revert before ClassDB; make the to_string arm reuse display_variant + Node name prefix. title: GDScript Projection: full method/static/constant surface and Projection*Vector4 / *Projection (+2 related)
description:
[audit-key: core-variant/variant-builtin-tail] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** script calls on Camera3D.get_camera_projection() results and Projection literals in scene scripts; method/constant access on builtin values and type idents in scene scripts; script calls `a.is_equal_approx(b)` on builtin values

### 1. Projection builtin methods, statics, constants and operators  (PARTIAL, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api builtin_classes Projection (15 instance + 11 static methods, constants IDENTITY/ZERO, enum Planes, ops * Vector4 / * Projection); core/math/projection.cpp

**Patina today:** projection_method (gdscript-interop/src/variant_math.rs:1872-1885) implements only determinant, inverse, is_orthogonal; missing get_fov, get_z_near, get_z_far, get_aspect, get_projection_plane, flipped_y, jitter_offseted, perspective_znear_adjusted, get_viewport_half_extents, get_far_plane_half_extents, get_pixels_per_meter, get_lod_multiplier. Statics in vector_static_call cover create_perspective/orthogonal/frustum/orthogonal_aspect only (variant_math.rs:2478-2527); missing create_depth_correction, create_light_atlas_rect, create_perspective_hmd, create_for_hmd, create_frustum_aspect, create_fit_aabb, get_fovy. static_member (variant_math.rs:468) has no Projection.IDENTITY/ZERO or PLANE_* entries; variant_math::mul (:1432) has no Projection arms. gdcore::math3d::Projection (math3d.rs:860) already has get_frustum_planes, transposed, create_perspective_with_offset.

**Implement:** Godot core/math/projection.cpp: get_fov, get_z_near, get_z_far, get_aspect, get_projection_plane(plane), flipped_y, jitter_offseted, perspective_znear_adjusted, get_viewport_half_extents, get_far_plane_half_extents, get_pixels_per_meter, get_lod_multiplier, statics create_depth_correction/create_light_atlas_rect/create_perspective_hmd/create_for_hmd/create_frustum_aspect/create_fit_aabb/get_fovy, constants IDENTITY/ZERO, enum PLANE_NEAR..PLANE_BOTTOM, operators Projection*Vector4 and Projection*Projection.
Patina: variant_math.rs projection_method :1872 has 3 methods; statics :2478-2527 cover 4; no constants or mul arms.
Implementation: port the missing functions into gdcore::math3d::Projection (math3d.rs:860), expose them in projection_method / vector_static_call / static_member, add Projection arms to variant_math::mul.
Wiring: script calls on Camera3D.get_camera_projection() results and Projection literals in scene scripts.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/variant_math.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/math3d.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene script builds `Projection.create_perspective(60, 16.0/9.0, 0.1, 100)` and stores get_fov(), get_z_near(), get_z_far(), get_aspect(), `Projection.IDENTITY * Vector4(1,2,3,1)`, `Projection.get_fovy(90, 1.5)`, `Projection.PLANE_FAR`; test asserts Godot's values within CMP_EPSILON. (test: `projection_builtin_surface_test`)

**Verifier note:** projection_method (variant_math.rs:1872-1885) handles only determinant, inverse and is_orthogonal, then returns UndefinedFunction. Grepping for "get_fov", "get_z_near" and "get_fovy" across the three crates gives 0 hits. The only ("Projection", ...) static entries are 2478, 2501, 2514 and 2527 (create_perspective, create_orthogonal, create_frustum, create_orthogonal_aspect). There is no IDENTITY, ZERO or PLANE_ static_member entry. P2 stands.

### 2. Builtin method/constant tail: Vector2/Vector3 interpolation methods, Vector4/Basis/Transform3D constants, Axis enums, Array.get/set, Dictionary.set, Packed erase, Transform3D.is_finite  (PARTIAL, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api builtin_classes[].methods/.constants/.enums for Vector2, Vector3, Vector4, Vector4i, Basis, Transform3D, Array, Dictionary, Packed*Array

**Patina today:** Scripted diff vs dispatch arms: Vector2 missing cubic_interpolate, cubic_interpolate_in_time, bezier_interpolate, bezier_derivative; Vector3 missing signed_angle_to, inverse, slerp, cubic_interpolate, cubic_interpolate_in_time, bezier_interpolate, bezier_derivative, outer, octahedron_encode (+ static octahedron_decode) — although gdcore already implements Vector2/Vector3 cubic_interpolate (gdcore/src/math.rs:1085, :1330) and Vector3 inverse; Transform3D.is_finite missing from transform3d_method (variant_math.rs:1109); Array.get/set and Dictionary.set missing (Array arm interpreter.rs:11251, Dictionary arm :12139); `erase` missing for all 10 packed arrays (call_packed_method :14812); PackedByteArray.to_vector4_array missing. Constants: static_member (variant_math.rs:468) and the interpreter's vector constant table (interpreter.rs:19053-19110) lack Vector4.ZERO/ONE/INF, Vector4i.ZERO/ONE/MIN/MAX, Basis.FLIP_X/Y/Z, Transform3D.FLIP_X/Y/Z; grep '"AXIS_X"\|"FLIP_Z"' gdscript-interop/src = 0 hits, so Vector2.AXIS_X etc. are unresolvable.

**Implement:** Godot extension_api lists: Vector2 cubic_interpolate(_in_time), bezier_interpolate, bezier_derivative; Vector3 the same plus slerp, signed_angle_to, inverse, outer, octahedron_encode, static octahedron_decode; Transform3D.is_finite; Array.get/set; Dictionary.set; Packed*Array.erase(value) -> bool; PackedByteArray.to_vector4_array; constants Vector4.ZERO/ONE/INF, Vector4i.ZERO/ONE/MIN/MAX, Basis.FLIP_X/Y/Z, Transform3D.FLIP_X/Y/Z; enums Vector2/2i/3/3i/4/4i.Axis (AXIS_X..AXIS_W).
Patina: missing from vector2_method/vector3_method (variant_math.rs:1659/:2097 + interpreter inline arms :12354/:12422), static_member (:468), interpreter vector constant table (:19053), Array/Dictionary/packed arms. gdcore::math already has Vector2/3 cubic_interpolate (math.rs:1085, :1330) — expose rather than reimplement; port slerp/bezier/octahedron from core/math/vector3.cpp.
Wiring: method/constant access on builtin values and type idents in scene scripts.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/variant_math.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene script evaluates `Vector3(1,0,0).slerp(Vector3(0,1,0), 0.5)`, `Vector2(0,0).cubic_interpolate(Vector2(1,1), Vector2(-1,-1), Vector2(2,2), 0.5)`, `Vector3.UP.signed_angle_to(Vector3.RIGHT, Vector3.FORWARD)`, `Vector4.ONE`, `Basis.FLIP_X`, `Vector3.AXIS_Z`, `[1,2].get(1)`, `PackedInt32Array([1,2]).erase(2)` and asserts Godot's values through SceneTree properties. (test: `builtin_method_constant_tail_test`)

**Verifier note:** Spot checks: "slerp" exists only for Basis (variant_math.rs:1223), Quaternion (1255) and Vector2 (1800, inside vector2_method), so Vector3 has none. "cubic_interpolate" and "bezier_interpolate" exist only in vector4_method (1932) and the scalar global functions in try_builtin (7646, 7692), so Vector2/Vector3 have none. "signed_angle_to" and "AXIS_X" return 0 hits (the only AXIS_ hits are JOY_AXIS_* in global_constants.rs). The only "FLIP_X" hit is Transform2D (variant_math.rs:471). There is no Vector4 or Vector4i entry in the constant table (interpreter.rs:19052-19100 covers Vector2, Vector3, Vector2i and Vector3i). transform3d_method runs 1109-1180 with no is_finite (the 1197 hit is in basis_method). The Array arm (11251-12138) has no "get" or "set"; the Dictionary arm has "get" (12321) but no "set". call_packed_method has no "erase". P2 stands.

### 3. is_equal_approx epsilon semantics on math builtins  (PARTIAL, P3)

**Godot ground truth:** core/math/math_defs.h:50 CMP_EPSILON 0.00001; core/math/math_funcs.h Math::is_equal_approx (relative tolerance = max(CMP_EPSILON*|a|, CMP_EPSILON)); Color/Rect2/Plane is_equal_approx use per-component Math::is_equal_approx

**Patina today:** variant_math.rs:430 approx() uses 1e-6 (10x tighter than CMP_EPSILON) and backs Transform2D (:1095), Transform3D (:1174), Basis (:1233), Quaternion (:1302), AABB (:1369) is_equal_approx; Plane compares d with absolute 1e-5 (:1415); gdcore Color::is_equal_approx (gdcore/src/math.rs:2183) and Rect2::is_equal_approx (:2713) use absolute 1e-5, so large-magnitude values (e.g. Rect2 at x=100000 vs 100000.5) disagree with Godot.

**Implement:** Godot: Math::is_equal_approx(a,b) returns true if a==b, else |a-b| < max(CMP_EPSILON*|a|, CMP_EPSILON) with CMP_EPSILON=1e-5 (math_defs.h:50); every builtin is_equal_approx (Vector*, Color, Rect2, Plane, AABB, Basis, Quaternion, Transform*) composes it per component.
Patina: variant_math.rs approx() (:430) uses 1e-6; Plane d (:1415), gdcore Color (math.rs:2183) and Rect2 (math.rs:2713) use absolute 1e-5.
Implementation: one shared `gdcore::math::is_equal_approx_f32` (relative, CMP_EPSILON) used by variant_math approx/vec*_equal_approx and the gdcore Color/Rect2/Plane impls.
Wiring: script calls `a.is_equal_approx(b)` on builtin values.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/variant_math.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/math.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene script evaluates `Transform2D.IDENTITY.is_equal_approx(Transform2D(Vector2(1.000005,0), Vector2(0,1), Vector2.ZERO))` (true), `Rect2(100000,0,1,1).is_equal_approx(Rect2(100000.5,0,1,1))` (true), `Color(0.5,0.5,0.5).is_equal_approx(Color(0.50002,0.5,0.5))` (false); test asserts via SceneTree properties. (test: `builtin_is_equal_approx_epsilon_test`)

**Verifier note:** variant_math.rs:430-435 approx() is relative but uses 1e-6, while upstream/godot/core/math/math_defs.h:50 sets CMP_EPSILON to 0.00001. gdcore/src/math.rs:2183-2188 (Color) and 2713-2718 (Rect2) use an absolute 1e-5 per component, so large-magnitude Rect2 comparisons disagree with Godot. One correction to the bead: the Color acceptance case (0.5 vs 0.50002) returns false under both the old and the fixed rule, so it does not discriminate; the Rect2 and Transform2D cases do. P3 stands.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A scene script builds `Projection.create_perspective(60, 16.0/9.0, 0.1, 100)` and stores get_fov(), get_z_near(), get_z_far(), get_aspect(), `Projection.IDENTITY * Vector4(1,2,3,1)`, `Projection.get_fovy(90, 1.5)`, `Projection.PLANE_FAR`; test asserts Godot's values within CMP_EPSILON. (test: `projection_builtin_surface_test`) 2) A scene script evaluates `Vector3(1,0,0).slerp(Vector3(0,1,0), 0.5)`, `Vector2(0,0).cubic_interpolate(Vector2(1,1), Vector2(-1,-1), Vector2(2,2), 0.5)`, `Vector3.UP.signed_angle_to(Vector3.RIGHT, Vector3.FORWARD)`, `Vector4.ONE`, `Basis.FLIP_X`, `Vector3.AXIS_Z`, `[1,2].get(1)`, `PackedInt32Array([1,2]).erase(2)` and asserts Godot's values through SceneTree properties. (test: `builtin_method_constant_tail_test`) 3) A scene script evaluates `Transform2D.IDENTITY.is_equal_approx(Transform2D(Vector2(1.000005,0), Vector2(0,1), Vector2.ZERO))` (true), `Rect2(100000,0,1,1).is_equal_approx(Rect2(100000.5,0,1,1))` (true), `Color(0.5,0.5,0.5).is_equal_approx(Color(0.50002,0.5,0.5))` (false); test asserts via SceneTree properties. (test: `builtin_is_equal_approx_epsilon_test`)
