title: Runtime2D: move the scene-to-canvas builder out of gdeditor and drive it from patina-web and patina-runner
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/runtime-2d-canvas-producer] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** MainLoop::step -> shared builder -> framebuffer -> runner file / web canvas, with no gdeditor in the path

**Godot ground truth:** scene/2d/*.cpp NOTIFICATION_DRAW -> RenderingServer canvas_item_* (servers/rendering/renderer_canvas_cull.cpp); Godot web export draws the same canvas

**Patina today:** Per-class 2D draw dispatch lives only in gdeditor: render_kind_for at engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:1559 (Sprite2D 1679, Polygon2D 1690, Line2D 1723, TileMapLayer via tilemap_quads 1384), collect_canvas_items :539, rasterize_render_list :2863. Its only runtime callers are the editor binary (engine-rs/examples/editor.rs:293,331) and gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs:179. patina-web/Cargo.toml depends on gdscene/gdrender3d but NOT gdeditor or gdrender2d; its only presentation is WebRenderer::present_clear (patina-web/src/canvas.rs:146). patina-runner/src/main.rs:1-11 dumps tree JSON; grep 'gdrender2d|gdeditor|FrameBuffer|ppm|png' over patina-runner/src returns only a doc comment. So a 2D game run outside the editor Play tab draws no Sprite2D/TileMapLayer/Line2D pixels.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: each CanvasItem node draws into the RenderingServer canvas every frame in the exported game, web export included (scene/2d/sprite_2d.cpp _notification(NOTIFICATION_DRAW), renderer_canvas_cull.cpp). Patina today: the only node->draw-command producer is gdeditor::viewport_2d_render (render_kind_for :1559, collect_canvas_items :539, build_runtime_render_list :2056, rasterize_render_list :2863, shade_runtime_canvas :3464). Only the editor binary calls it (examples/editor.rs:293-350). patina-web has no dependency on gdeditor/gdrender2d and only clears the canvas (patina-web/src/canvas.rs:146); patina-runner emits JSON only. Approach: move collect_canvas_items/render_kind_for/tilemap_quads/sprite_sheet_for/camera2d_view_transform/apply_camera2d_view/apply_parallax_mirroring/rasterize_render_list(+_with_groups)/shade_runtime_canvas into a runtime crate (new module gdrender2d::scene_canvas, or gdscene::canvas_render if gdrender2d cannot depend on gdscene), and leave gdeditor re-exporting it so the editor keeps working. Then (a) patina-runner gets a `--frame-out <path.ppm>` flag that, after the last frame, builds the render list from MainLoop's tree, applies Camera2D + stretch + lights, and writes the framebuffer; (b) patina-web's per-frame loop rasterizes the same list and uploads it to the canvas surface (CPU framebuffer -> texture blit is fine for a first stage). Wiring: MainLoop::step -> shared builder -> framebuffer -> runner file / web canvas, with no gdeditor in the path.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/main.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/browser_runtime.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/canvas.rs`

**Prove it:** `patina-runner fixtures/sprite_scene.tscn --frames 2 --frame-out out.ppm` writes a PPM in which the Sprite2D texture pixels show up at the sprite's camera-relative position (not the clear color), and a TileMapLayer cell shows up at its cell position. patina-runner has no dependency on gdeditor (checked via its Cargo.toml in the test). patina-web compiles for wasm32 with the shared builder linked (cargo check gate). (test: `runner_2d_frame_output_test`)

**Verifier note:** Callers of collect_canvas_items/rasterize_render_list/shade_runtime_canvas outside tests are only gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs, gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs, examples/editor.rs (gdscene/src/node2d.rs:179 is a comment). patina-web/Cargo.toml lists gdcore, gdvariant, gdaudio, gdscene, gdresource, gdplatform and gdrender3d, with no gdeditor and no gdrender2d. canvas.rs:146 present_clear is the only draw call. patina-runner/src/render3d.rs drives RenderServer3DAdapter only, which is 3D. There is no 2D framebuffer path in the runner (grep 'FrameBuffer|ppm|png|render' over main.rs/lib.rs finds only `pub mod render3d`). gdscene depends on gdrender2d, but only for fonts, sdf and light maths, not for a canvas builder. P0 stands: 2D games draw nothing outside the editor.
acceptance_criteria: `patina-runner fixtures/sprite_scene.tscn --frames 2 --frame-out out.ppm` writes a PPM in which the Sprite2D texture pixels show up at the sprite's camera-relative position (not the clear color), and a TileMapLayer cell shows up at its cell position. patina-runner has no dependency on gdeditor (checked via its Cargo.toml in the test). patina-web compiles for wasm32 with the shared builder linked (cargo check gate). (test: `runner_2d_frame_output_test`)

comments.author: EmeraldCreek
comments.text:
EmeraldCreek — parked `needs-attention`. **This bead duplicates pat-mgixk.46, which PinkMoose holds IN_PROGRESS right now.** I am not writing its test, because doing so would duplicate their work in the same files and almost certainly fail for the same reason theirs does.

**The two acceptances are the same work:**

| | pat-mgixk.28 (this) | pat-mgixk.46 (PinkMoose) |
|---|---|---|
| runner invocation | `--frames 2 --frame-out out.ppm` | `--frames 3 --frame-out out.png` |
| pixel assertions | Sprite2D region + TileMapLayer cell | ColorRect centre + sprite region |
| no-gdeditor check | "checked via its Cargo.toml in the test" | "assert in the test by parsing Cargo.toml" |
| web side | patina-web compiles for wasm32 | host-side `WebEngine::render_frame` pixels |
| named test | `runner_2d_frame_output_test` (absent) | `runner_writes_2d_canvas_frame` (exists) |

Same path, same crate boundary, same Cargo.toml assertion — `.28` adds TileMapLayer and PPM, `.46` adds a host-side WebEngine test.

**Everything this bead asks for except its test is already in the tree**, and I verified each clause rather than counting greps:

- the shared builder moved: `gdscene/src/canvas_render.rs` exists with 30 `pub fn`s;
- `patina-runner/src/main.rs` drives it — `collect_canvas_items` (:234), `camera2d_view_transform` (:235), `apply_camera2d_view` (:241), `rasterize_render_list` (:247) — and has 16 `frame-out` references;
- **the `gdeditor` hit in `patina-runner/Cargo.toml` is a COMMENT, not a dependency.** It reads "NOTE the absence of `gdeditor`: the whole point of moving the canvas builder into `gdscene` was that a headless run must not pull the editor in, and the acceptance test asserts on this file to keep it that way." A `grep -c gdeditor` on that file returns 1 and means the opposite of what it looks like;
- the fixture exists at `engine-rs/fixtures/scenes/sprite_scene.tscn` (the acceptance's `fixtures/sprite_scene.tscn` is an approximate path);
- `patina-web` has the `gdrender2d` dependency and `WebEngine::render_2d_rgba`, both tagged `pat-mgixk.28` in their own comments — i.e. someone already did this bead's web half.

**The blocker is shared and it is not the test's absence.** `.46`'s `runner_writes_2d_canvas_frame` is currently RED (`verifier.log:13121`, exit 100): "the pixel at the ColorRect centre must be its authored colour: r was 0, expected 0.2. The whole rect being the clear colour means nothing rasterized." So the runner reaches `rasterize_render_list` and still produces clear-colour pixels. Writing `runner_2d_frame_output_test` to assert Sprite2D pixels would fail on the same mechanism, and I would be debugging the same rasterizer PinkMoose is already inside.

**Recommendation:** close `.28` as a duplicate of `.46`, or reduce it to only what `.46` does not cover — the TileMapLayer cell assertion and the wasm32 `cargo check` gate — and make it depend on `.46`. Either way it should not be worked in parallel: `canvas_render.rs` and `patina-runner/src/main.rs` are the same two files both beads must edit.

I have messaged PinkMoose and the coordinator rather than silently parking, so the duplication is visible to the person actually holding the work.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
TurquoiseCastle — ROOT CAUSE for the `100` at verifier.log:13313, handing off to RusticElk. I held this bead for one verify and have written nothing outside the test file; `main.rs` is untouched by me.

**The loose-`.tscn` entry point never seeds ClassDB, so the render list is EMPTY and every pixel is the clear colour.**

The chain, each link checked:
1. `collect_canvas_items` (`gdscene/src/canvas_render.rs:487`) filters every node on `node.is_class("CanvasItem")` at `:500` — and the gate is spelled NEGATIVELY (`if !is_class(..) { return None }`), so an unpopulated DB silently drops the whole scene instead of degrading.
2. `Node::is_class` (`gdscene/src/node.rs:351`) falls through to `gdobject::is_parent_class`, which reads the process-global ClassDB (`class_db.rs:993`).
3. `ClassDB::new()` (`class_db.rs:459`) starts with **empty** HashMaps. Nothing is pre-registered.
4. `register_all_classes()` is called in exactly two places in patina-runner — `EngineBootstrap::init_servers` (`bootstrap.rs:405`) and `boot_from_project_text` (`project_boot.rs:379`). **Both are on the `project.godot` path.** `main.rs`'s loose-`.tscn` path (`:649-721`) builds `SceneTree::new()` at `:667`, instances the scene, and calls neither — `grep -c register_all_classes main.rs` is **0**.

So `is_parent_class("Sprite2D", "CanvasItem")` is false, every node is filtered out, and `rasterize_render_list` correctly returns a frame of pure clear colour. The acceptance's 0 red pixels is that, not a rasterizer defect.

**Two independent confirmations, so this is not a lone hypothesis:**
- `bootstrap.rs:399-404` documents this very bug being fixed ONCE BEFORE, for `EngineBootstrap` only: *"This phase used to only read `class_count()` ... No caller ever was: the runner booted every game against an all-but-empty ClassDB, so scene loading seeded no class defaults at all."* The loose-`.tscn` path in `main` never got the same treatment.
- PinkMoose independently MEASURED it in `.46`'s test header (`runner_writes_2d_canvas_frame.rs:40-48`): entry by project directory renders pixels, **"0 of 9216 by loose `.tscn`"**, and they call it *"a separate defect"* and deliberately routed their own test around it by entering via a project dir.

**⚠️ `.46` IS NOT THE SAME DEFECT — do not wait on it.** It enters by project directory, so its ClassDB *is* seeded; its red is a wrong ColorRect colour (`r was 0, expected 0.2`), a different bug downstream. I said the opposite earlier from the symptom alone and it was wrong; the two only look alike. `.28` is independently fixable right now.

**Where the fix goes, and the trap in it.** The acceptance command is a LOOSE `.tscn` (`patina-runner fixtures/sprite_scene.tscn --frames 2 --frame-out out.ppm`), so making that path draw IS this bead — not scope creep, and changing the test to enter by project dir would dodge the bead's own stated acceptance.
⚠️ **But placement has a real blast radius, and it cuts both ways:**
- Registering early (next to `SceneTree::new()` at `:667`, which is where Godot does it — `register_scene_types()` during boot) is the correct fix AND seeds class property defaults at instancing. By the engine's own comment above, that *changes what scene loading produces* for **every** loose-`.tscn` test in patina-runner, several of which assert on `dump_tree_json` output. Expect collateral on currently-green tests and check them before reporting.
- Registering late (just before `write_frame_out`) makes the `is_class` filter pass with near-zero blast radius, but leaves class defaults unseeded at instancing — a knowingly partial fix.
I did not pick between these because I no longer hold the bead; the early placement is the honest one, the late one is the cheap one, and the difference is measurable rather than a matter of taste.

**What my one verify DID establish, since it is the only run of this target ever:** the target COMPILES (exit 100, not 101) and 1 of its 3 tests passed. The target has 3 tests now — I added `patina_web_links_the_shared_canvas_builder_for_wasm` (the wasm clause had nothing behind it); `runner_2d_frame_output_test` is the one that fails, on the Sprite2D pixel count. The fixtures are NOT the problem: I decoded them — `sprite_fixture.png` is 8x8 solid red (64 px, bar is 32), `tiles.png` is 32x16 with a red left half and green right half, and `tile_map_data` decodes under `decode_tile_map_data`'s own 12-byte layout to cell (0,0) source 0 atlas **(1,0)** = the green half (256 px, bar is 100). `res://` resolves to the scene's parent dir (`main.rs:675`), which is where both PNGs live.

title: GDScript: report script parse errors with res path and line instead of dropping them
description:
[audit-key: gdscript/gdscript-error-reporting] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** runner boot and SceneAccess load(x.gd).new()

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp GDScript::reload -> _err_print_error with file:line:col; core/io/resource_loader.cpp reports failed script loads

**Patina today:** patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs:551-558: `Err(_) => { // Non-fatal: script parse failure doesn't block boot. }` — no message, the node simply runs without its script. Same at gdscene/src/scripting.rs:891-893 for load(x.gd).new(). Combined with the lexer/parser gaps above, a real Godot project silently loses every script that uses unsupported syntax. (The editor tool path at gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:19641-19645 does log.)

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: a script that fails to parse emits `Parse Error: <msg>` with `res://path:line` to the error stream (and the debugger), and the scene still loads without that script.

Patina: bootstrap.rs:556 and scripting.rs:893 discard the RuntimeError.

Implement: on Err, print `SCRIPT ERROR: Parse Error: {e}` + `at: res://... :line` to stderr and push into the engine error channel (the same one push_error uses, interpreter.rs:939), and record it on the runner's boot report; ensure ParseError carries line/col (parser.rs ParseError::UnexpectedToken already has them). Wiring: runner boot and SceneAccess load(x.gd).new().

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`

**Prove it:** Running a scene whose script has a syntax error produces a stderr line containing the res:// path, line number and 'Parse Error', while the rest of the scene still runs. (test: `gdscript_parse_error_reported_at_boot`)

**Verifier note:** Partly refuted. The real runner path for a .tscn argument, patina-runner/src/main.rs:220 attach_scripts (called at main.rs:584), does report: on Err(e) it calls tracing::warn!(path, error=format!("{e:?}"), "failed to parse GDScript") at main.rs:249-255, and main.rs:491-493 sends the tracing subscriber to stderr, so the failure is not silent there. title: Containers: AspectRatioContainer layout plus script-driven sorting (sort_children, fit_child_in_rect) (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: gui-controls/gui-containers] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

### 1. AspectRatioContainer and script-defined Containers (_notification SORT_CHILDREN, sort_children signal, fit_child_in_rect, _get_allowed_size_flags_*)  (MISSING, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** scene/gui/aspect_ratio_container.cpp; scene/gui/container.cpp fit_child_in_rect/queue_sort/NOTIFICATION_SORT_CHILDREN

**Patina today:** arrange_container match (control.rs:2218-2299) covers Box/Flow/Grid/Margin/Center/Scroll/Tab/Foldable/Split/SubViewportContainer and ends `_ => {}`. is_container_class_name (:2348) returns true for any Container subclass via is_parent_class, so AspectRatioContainer and a scripted `extends Container` get treated as containers (children's anchors bypassed) but are never arranged. grep '"fit_child_in_rect"|"queue_sort"|"pre_sort_children"' in dispatch: only a doc comment (control.rs:2594). AspectRatioContainer has 0 refs in control_render.rs/scene_tree.rs/hit list.

**Implement:** Godot AspectRatioContainer fits children to `ratio` with stretch_mode (width/height controls, fit, cover) and alignment_horizontal/vertical. Any Container sends NOTIFICATION_SORT_CHILDREN / emits pre_sort_children + sort_children so scripts lay out children with fit_child_in_rect. Patina skips both, so their children collapse to (0,0). Add an AspectRatioContainer arm to control::arrange_container. For any other Container subclass, have arrange_container emit pre_sort_children/sort_children and call the script's _notification(NOTIFICATION_SORT_CHILDREN) (needs a &mut SceneTree script call, as in the render-walk flush pattern). Add fit_child_in_rect and queue_sort script arms in scripting.rs.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`

**Prove it:** An AspectRatioContainer(ratio 2, size 400x400) lays its child out at 400x200 centered. A custom Container script that calls fit_child_in_rect(child, Rect2(10,10,50,50)) in its sort_children handler leaves the child at that rect after one layout pass (test: `aspect_ratio_and_script_container_layout`)

**Verifier note:** Confirmed. The arms of control.rs arrange_container are Box(:2231), Flow(:2239), Grid(:2243), Margin(:2250), Center(:2254), Scroll(:2258), Tab(:2262), Foldable(:2267), Split(:2283/:2287) and SubViewportContainer(:2293), ending in `_ => {}` (:2299), with no AspectRatioContainer arm. AspectRatioContainer appears only in the mouse-filter IGNORE list (control.rs:623). One small correction: fit_child_in_rect does exist as a private Rust helper (control.rs:1593, used at :1774 and :2205). However, grep 'fit_child_in_rect|sort_children|NOTIFICATION_SORT_CHILDREN' in gdscript-interop/src and scripting.rs finds no script arm and no emit, so it is still MISSING from script.

### 2. ScrollContainer/SplitContainer signal + mode completeness (scroll_started/ended, touch drag-scroll, scroll_deadzone, SplitContainer drag_started/ended, collapsed, dragger_visibility, dragging_enabled)  (PARTIAL, P3)

**Godot ground truth:** scene/gui/scroll_container.cpp gui_input (touch drag, deadzone, scroll_started/ended), split_container.cpp (SplitContainerDragger, drag_started/drag_ended, dragging_enabled, touch_dragger)

**Patina today:** Wheel scrolling and divider drag exist (scroll_under_cursor, drag_split control.rs:2471, `dragged` emitted). Emit sites for scroll_started/scroll_ended/drag_started/drag_ended = 0. '"scroll_deadzone"','"dragger_visibility"','"dragging_enabled"','"touch_dragger_enabled"','"drag_area_margin_begin"' = 0 refs in gdscene/src. No press-drag-to-scroll path for ScrollContainer (Godot does this on touch/emulated touch).

**Implement:** Godot ScrollContainer drag-scrolls content on touch (and emulated touch) past scroll_deadzone, emitting scroll_started/scroll_ended. SplitContainer emits drag_started/drag_ended around `dragged`, honours dragging_enabled, collapsed, dragger_visibility (hidden/collapsed) and drag_area margins. Patina has wheel scroll and divider drag only. Add these in scene_tree.rs gui_input_stage beside scroll_under_cursor/drag_split_divider, and make arrange_split respect collapsed/dragger_visibility.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs`

**Prove it:** A push_input ScreenTouch + ScreenDrag of 50px inside a ScrollContainer with tall content moves scroll_vertical by 50 and emits scroll_started then scroll_ended. A divider drag on an HSplitContainer emits drag_started, dragged, drag_ended in order, and dragging_enabled=false blocks it. (test: `scroll_split_drag_signals_e2e`)

**Verifier note:** scroll_started, scroll_ended, drag_started, drag_ended and "dragging_enabled" have 0 hits in gdscene/src. They appear only in class_db.rs (e.g. drag_started at :16186 and :19412). drag_split (control.rs:2471-2492) emits only `dragged`, and its caller drag_split_divider (scene_tree.rs:7119-7160) adds no start or end signals. The ScreenTouch and ScreenDrag hits in scene_tree.rs:8611-8636 are event-to-Variant conversion only; no path scrolls a ScrollContainer by press-dragging. PARTIAL holds. Priority 3 is defensible (mostly signals for exotic cases), though touch drag-scroll on mobile could argue for 2.
acceptance_criteria: 1) An AspectRatioContainer(ratio 2, size 400x400) lays its child out at 400x200 centered. A custom Container script that calls fit_child_in_rect(child, Rect2(10,10,50,50)) in its sort_children handler leaves the child at that rect after one layout pass (test: `aspect_ratio_and_script_container_layout`) 2) A push_input ScreenTouch + ScreenDrag of 50px inside a ScrollContainer with tall content moves scroll_vertical by 50 and emits scroll_started then scroll_ended. A divider drag on an HSplitContainer emits drag_started, dragged, drag_ended in order, and dragging_enabled=false blocks it. (test: `scroll_split_drag_signals_e2e`)

title: Node3D: route every transform write (tween, animation, root motion, transform/basis/quaternion) through the canonical local transform (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: nodes-3d/node3d-transform-coherence] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** AnimationPlayer/Tween tick in MainLoop -> SceneTree::process_* -> node3d setter -> get_global_transform -> viewport_3d_render collect_scene_content; the .tscn `rotation_order = 0` (XYZ) plus `rotation = ...` -> render transform

### 1. Node3D transform writes from tweens, animation tracks, root motion and transform/basis/quaternion never reach the rendered transform  (UNWIRED, P0)

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/node_3d.cpp (set_position/set_quaternion/set_basis/set_transform all update one data.local_transform and mark dirty); doc/classes/Node3D.xml

**Patina today:** Canonical local transform is node3d.rs:69 local_transform_of: it returns an explicit `transform` property if present, otherwise composes position/rotation/scale. It never reads `quaternion`, `basis` or `rotation_degrees`. Only scripting.rs:2489-2501 routes Vector3 position/rotation/scale through node3d::set_* (store_local_transform, node3d.rs:94). Every other writer calls raw Node::set_property (node.rs:275, which has no hooks): tweens at scene_tree.rs:4850/4854 (process_tweens_in_mode), animation at scene_tree.rs:8367 set_animated_property_path, Rotation3D tracks writing `quaternion` at animation.rs:2022, root motion at scene_tree.rs:8389 apply_root_motion_delta. A .tscn-loaded Node3D keeps `transform =` (scripting.rs:2478 comment), so a tweened or animated `position` on it is ignored by local_transform_of, and an animated `quaternion` is ignored on every node. The test at scene_tree.rs:10564 only checks the raw properties, never get_global_transform.

**Implement:** Godot: every Node3D transform property (position, rotation, rotation_degrees, quaternion, basis, scale, transform) is a view of one local transform (node_3d.cpp). Patina: node3d.rs:69 local_transform_of prefers an explicit `transform` and ignores quaternion/basis. Tweens (scene_tree.rs:4850), animation value and 3D tracks (scene_tree.rs:8367, animation.rs:2022 `quaternion`) and root motion (scene_tree.rs:8389) write raw properties, so on any .tscn Node3D they change nothing on screen. Implementation: add `node3d::set_transform_component(node:&mut Node, prop, value) -> bool` that handles position/rotation/rotation_degrees/scale/quaternion/basis/transform, plus sub-paths such as position:x, by decomposing and calling store_local_transform. Call it from set_animated_property_path, the tween apply in process_tweens_in_mode, apply_root_motion_delta and the scripting.rs:2489 match, which it replaces, whenever the node is_class("Node3D"). Wiring: AnimationPlayer/Tween tick in MainLoop -> SceneTree::process_* -> node3d setter -> get_global_transform -> viewport_3d_render collect_scene_content.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a MeshInstance3D carrying `transform = Transform3D(...)` and an AnimationPlayer with a position_3d track and a rotation_3d track, run through MainLoop::step: node3d::get_global_transform changes on both translation and rotation, and the editor render list item's global_transform matches. A Tween on `position` of the same node does the same. (test: `node3d_tween_and_animation_drive_rendered_transform`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. node3d.rs:69-89 local_transform_of returns the explicit `transform` if present, otherwise composes position/rotation/scale. grep '"quaternion"|"basis"' in node3d.rs: 0 hits. Node::set_property (node.rs:275-292) has only a metadata/ mirror, no transform hook. Tween apply (scene_tree.rs:4840-4856), set_animated_property_path (scene_tree.rs:8367-8386, called at :4291 and :4693) and apply_root_motion_delta (scene_tree.rs:8388-8410) all call raw node.set_property. animation.rs:2021 maps glTF rotation to the `quaternion` property, which nothing reads. Only scripting.rs:2489-2501 routes Vector3 position/rotation/scale through the node3d setters. P0 is right: this is common, and on a .tscn node it silently breaks.

### 2. Node3D rotation_order and rotation_edit_mode ignored (always YXZ euler)  (STUB, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** scene/3d/node_3d.cpp set_rotation_order (EulerOrder), rotation_edit_mode (EULER/QUATERNION/BASIS)

**Patina today:** compose_basis (node3d.rs:58-65) calls Basis::from_euler (YXZ, gdcore/src/math3d.rs:240), and decompose_basis is YXZ. Basis::from_euler_order exists (math3d.rs:1296) but grep 'rotation_order|rotation_edit_mode' in gdscene/src and the gdeditor viewport/inspector code returned nothing.

**Implement:** Godot composes `rotation` with the node's rotation_order (default YXZ) and decomposes with the same order. Patina is hard-wired to YXZ (node3d.rs:58). Implementation: read the `rotation_order` Int in local_transform_of/compose_basis and in store_local_transform's decompose, using Basis::from_euler_order and a matching get_euler(order) (add one to math3d.rs if it is missing). Wiring: the .tscn `rotation_order = 0` (XYZ) plus `rotation = ...` -> render transform.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/math3d.rs`

**Prove it:** Two .tscn MeshInstance3Ds with rotation=(0.5,0.7,0) and rotation_order 2 (YXZ) vs 0 (XYZ) produce different global bases that match Basis.from_euler(rot, order) for each order, and rotation reads back unchanged after set_position. (test: `node3d_rotation_order_respected`)

**Verifier note:** The behavior gap is real: compose_basis (gdscene/src/node3d.rs:58-59) calls Basis::from_euler, which is YXZ, and decompose uses rotation.to_euler() (:54). Basis::from_euler_order (gdcore/src/math3d.rs:1296) has no caller in gdscene/src. But the finder's 'grep returned nothing' is wrong: both properties are registered in ClassDB at gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1536 (rotation_edit_mode, Int 0) and :1537 (rotation_order, Int 2). They are stored but have no effect, so STUB is the right label, not MISSING. grep 'rotation_order|rotation_edit_mode' outside class_db, tests and the inspector schema returns nothing else. P2 stands.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A .tscn with a MeshInstance3D carrying `transform = Transform3D(...)` and an AnimationPlayer with a position_3d track and a rotation_3d track, run through MainLoop::step: node3d::get_global_transform changes on both translation and rotation, and the editor render list item's global_transform matches. A Tween on `position` of the same node does the same. (test: `node3d_tween_and_animation_drive_rendered_transform`) 2) Two .tscn MeshInstance3Ds with rotation=(0.5,0.7,0) and rotation_order 2 (YXZ) vs 0 (XYZ) produce different global bases that match Basis.from_euler(rot, order) for each order, and rotation reads back unchanged after set_position. (test: `node3d_rotation_order_respected`)

FBXDocument registered in class_db.rs:26769 inherits GLTFDocument dispatch (interpreter.rs:4321) which calls the glTF parser on FBX bytes.

**Implement:** Godot 4.6 imports .fbx in-process with ufbx (modules/fbx, FBXDocument extends GLTFDocument) and .dae via editor_import_collada.cpp. Patina parses only the FBX binary node-record container (fbx_import.rs) and FbxSceneImporter returns Unsupported (import.rs:1407-1421); FBXDocument.append_from_file runs the glTF parser on FBX bytes (interpreter.rs:4321). Stage 1 (this bead): decode zlib array properties and the Objects/Connections graph (Model, Geometry vertices/PolygonVertexIndex/LayerElementNormal/UV, Material) following ufbx.c, convert to the same GltfDocument Resource shape gltf_import produces (nodes/transforms/ArrayMeshSurface subresources), wire FbxSceneImporter and FBXDocument.append_from_* to it. (test: `fbx_scene_import_test`)

**Verifier note:** My attempt to refute this failed. FbxSceneImporter::import_scene (gdeditor/src/import.rs:1409-1423) always returns EngineError::Unsupported("fbx: no FBX parser is vendored..."). gdresource/src/fbx_import.rs:1-7 says it handles only the container layer: it does not interpret Objects/Connections and does not decode the zlib arrays. I grepped for fbx_import in gdeditor/src/import.rs and the only hit is a test name at line 1996, so the container parser is not wired into the importer. default_scene_importer_registry (import.rs:1633-1638) registers only Gltf, Obj and Fbx. For Collada I grepped -niE 'collada|"dae"' across crates/*/src. The only hits are extension classification in import_settings.rs:78,116 and a doc comment at import.rs:378, so no Collada parser or importer exists. interpreter.rs:4321 routes FBXDocument through the same branch as GLTFDocument. gdobject/tests/fbx_document_import_to_scene.rs:1-20 says itself that the FBX parser is not implemented. description:

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. **Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/import/resource_importer_dynamic_font.cpp get_import_options (antialiasing, generate_mipmaps, disable_embedded_bitmaps, multichannel_signed_distance_field, msdf_pixel_range, msdf_size, allow_system_fallback, force_autohinter, modulate_color_glyphs, hinting, subpixel_positioning, keep_rounding_remainders, oversampling, Fallbacks, Compress, preload, language_support, script_support, opentype_features)

**Patina today:** apply_font_params (importers.rs ~1240-1310) copies params onto the font Resource, but grep '"antialiasing"|"hinting"|"multichannel_signed_distance_field"|"subpixel_positioning"' in crates/*/src lists only editor_server.rs, class_db.rs, importers.rs - no renderer/text-server consumer. import_font/load_source_params have no callers outside gdresource (grep 'load_source_params|import_font(' crates/*/src excluding importers.rs -> only lib.rs re-export). Dock font options are invented keys 'antialiasing' (string enum), 'msdf' (editor_server.rs:23455-23472) vs Godot multichannel_signed_distance_field (int/bool).

**Implement:** Godot's dynamic font importer writes FontFile properties (antialiasing, hinting, subpixel_positioning, multichannel_signed_distance_field, oversampling, fallbacks) that TextServer uses when rasterizing (resource_importer_dynamic_font.cpp). Patina copies them onto a Resource (importers.rs apply_font_params) but no glyph rasterizer reads them, and the dock uses non-Godot keys. Implement: plumb FontFile antialiasing (0 none/1 gray/2 LCD), hinting and fallbacks from the loaded font resource into the glyph rasterization used by Label/RichTextLabel in gdrender2d; rename dock options to Godot keys with int enums.

title: Skeleton3D: adopt Godot 4 absolute bone-pose semantics and scene pose keys
description:
[audit-key: animation/skeleton3d-pose-semantics] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** MainLoop::step -> skeleton3d::process_skeletons_with_delta -> bone_pose_array -> render_server_3d.rs:594 skin_mesh

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/skeleton_3d.cpp:1108-1116 (global_pose = parent.global_pose * pose_cache; rest is used only when the bone is disabled); :98-102/:199-201 (scene stores pose as bones/N/position, rotation, scale); reset_bone_pose (:908) sets pose = rest

**Patina today:** gdscene/src/skeleton3d.rs:378-399 composes `global * rest * pose` (Godot 3 semantics), and set_bone_global_pose (:410-431) inverts the same formula. Animation bone tracks write ABSOLUTE local values (apply_animation_bone_tracks :1785-1797 -> set_bone_pose_position), so rest is applied twice and an animated rig with non-identity rests is distorted. Pose getters default to ZERO, IDENTITY and ONE (:255-282) instead of rest. Pose keys are `bones/N/pose_position` etc. (:41-51), so a Godot-saved `bones/N/position|rotation|scale` is never read (grep 'pose_position\|bones/' packed_scene.rs = 0).

**Implement:** Godot 4 ground truth: a bone's pose is its full local transform. The rest is only the default (reset_bone_pose copies rest into pose). global_pose = parent_global * pose (skeleton_3d.cpp:1108-1116). The scene stores the pose under bones/N/position, rotation and scale.

Patina: skeleton3d.rs:378-399 composes rest*pose, pose getters default to identity (:255-282), and the pose lives in bones/N/pose_position etc. Godot 4 / glTF animation keys (absolute) therefore get rest applied a second time, and a script doing `set_bone_pose_rotation(i, get_bone_rest(i).basis.get_rotation_quaternion() * q)` double-rotates.

Approach: (1) get_bone_pose_* fall back to the rest components when unset. (2) get_bone_global_pose and get_bone_global_rest use parent_global * pose for enabled bones and parent_global * rest for disabled ones. (3) set_bone_global_pose solves pose = parent_global^-1 * global. (4) Read and write Godot's bones/N/position, rotation and scale keys directly (or alias them on scene load) so saved poses round-trip. (5) Audit the IK/LookAt/Copy/Aim modifiers in the same file and ik_solver.rs for any rest*pose assumption.

Wiring: MainLoop::step -> skeleton3d::process_skeletons_with_delta -> bone_pose_array -> render_server_3d.rs:594 skin_mesh.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/skeleton3d.rs`

**Prove it:** Load a skinned glTF-style scene whose bones have non-identity rest transforms and an AnimationPlayer clip whose keys equal the rest values. After stepping the MainLoop, the skinned vertex positions published by the render server (skinned_vertices) match the bind pose to 1e-4, with no double transform. get_bone_pose_position(i) from GDScript returns the rest origin on an unanimated bone. A saved `bones/0/rotation` is honoured on load. (test: `skeleton3d_absolute_pose_skinning_scene`)

**Verifier note:** skeleton3d.rs:394-397 composes `global * rest * pose`, and set_bone_global_pose (:428) inverts (parent_global*rest). bone_pose_array (:439-443), which feeds skinning, uses that global pose. The pose getters (:255-282) default to ZERO, IDENTITY and ONE rather than rest. The keys are bones/{idx}/pose_position|pose_rotation|pose_scale (:41-51). apply_animation_bone_tracks (:1771-1777) writes absolute sampled values through set_bone_pose_*, so rest is applied twice. I found no alias for Godot's `bones/N/position` key (grep 'bones/{.*}/position', 'strip_prefix("bones/")' in gdscene/src and gdresource/src: 0). Any imported rig with non-identity rests is distorted, so P0 stands.
acceptance_criteria: Load a skinned glTF-style scene whose bones have non-identity rest transforms and an AnimationPlayer clip whose keys equal the rest values. After stepping the MainLoop, the skinned vertex positions published by the render server (skinned_vertices) match the bind pose to 1e-4, with no double transform. get_bone_pose_position(i) from GDScript returns the rest origin on an unanimated bone. A saved `bones/0/rotation` is honoured on load. (test: `skeleton3d_absolute_pose_skinning_scene`)

comments.text:
STATUS (TurquoiseCastle, 04:22Z) — implementation + acceptance test are in the working tree, UNBUILT. Completion was mailed to PurpleDesert at 04:17:35Z (msg 89315, topic bead-complete, thread pat-mgixk.3). ⚠️ The agent-mail server has since gone DOWN (nothing listening on 127.0.0.1:8765, curl returns 000), so if that message was not consumed before it died, this bead will look unreported. Everything needed to verify is in this comment and in msg 89315.

TOP RISK I FLAGGED, NOW DISCHARGED BY DERIVATION. The four modifier frame sites (look_at / aim / ccd / fabrik) now read 'let frame = parent_basis' instead of 'parent_basis * rest.basis'. Derivation: global_basis = parent_basis * pose.basis under the new composition, and the modifier wants new_global = delta * global, so new_pose.basis = parent_basis^-1 * delta * parent_basis * pose.basis — which is exactly what the code computes. 'new_pose' deliberately keeps 'pose.origin', since rotating a bone must not move its local origin. The four sites are byte-identical in shape and all four were changed (grep 'let frame = parent_basis;' = 4; no code line still matches 'parent_basis \* rest.basis' — the 4 remaining textual hits are my own explanatory comments).

SECOND-ORDER EFFECT THAT IS A WIN, worth checking in review: animation clips often key position only. recompose_bone_pose rebuilds the full pose from the three component getters, which now fall back to the REST for any unkeyed channel instead of IDENTITY/ONE. So a position-only clip leaves rotation and scale at the rest, which is Godot 4's behaviour; previously it silently reset them.

LATENT GAP I FOUND AND DELIBERATELY DID NOT FIX (candidate follow-up bead, NOT in this bead's acceptance). set_bone_pose writes the full 'bones/N/pose' transform but does not update the 'bones/N/pose_position|pose_rotation|pose_scale' component keys. So after a MODIFIER poses a bone, get_bone_pose().origin and get_bone_pose_position() disagree: the former returns the modifier's result, the latter falls through to the rest. This divergence is PRE-EXISTING (it previously returned ZERO rather than the rest), so my change alters the wrong value rather than introducing the wrongness, and Godot would return the real pose position in both. I left it alone for three reasons: it is outside this bead's acceptance; the obvious fix (have set_bone_pose decompose into the component keys) risks mutual recursion with recompose_bone_pose, which already calls set_bone_pose; and I cannot build or run anything to check it (.claude/hooks/block_worker_cargo.sh blocks workers from the Rust toolchain). None of my three acceptance assertions touch the divergent path: test 1 reads skinned vertices and get_bone_global_pose, test 2 reads component keys straight off a .tscn, test 3 reads an unposed bone with no modifier in the scene.

FILES ARE UNTOUCHED BY ANY PEER since I wrote them (skeleton3d.rs 21:08:12, retarget test 21:08:40, acceptance test 21:14:05 PDT — all mine, all before my 21:17:35 report).

comments.text:
## Coexistence check: pat-mgixk.29 and .30 both implement basis/quaternion/rotation_degrees (EmeraldCreek)

Verified, equivalent, not a bug — recorded because two implementations of one
name is how `hide`/`show` briefly ended up implemented NOWHERE earlier today.

### The two routes

`scripting.rs::set_node_property` calls, in this order:

1. `:2546` `node3d::set_transform_component` (pat-mgixk.29) — owns every LOCAL
   transform property: position, rotation, rotation_degrees, scale, quaternion,
   basis, transform, and `position:x` sub-paths.
2. `:2561` `node3d::set_derived_property` (pat-mgixk.30) — owns the `global_*`
   names, but ALSO carries its own `basis` / `quaternion` / `rotation_degrees`
   arms.

Because (1) runs first, (2)'s three local arms are unreachable from a property
write. They ARE reachable from `call_node3d_method`'s `set_basis` /
`set_quaternion` / `set_rotation_degrees`, which call `set_derived_property`
directly. So:

- `self.basis = b` → the .29 funnel
- `node.set_basis(b)` → the .30 arm

### They agree, including the subtle part

- **basis**: .29 sets `Transform3D { basis: b, origin: current.origin }`; .30
  sets `t.basis = b` on the local transform. Same result — a basis carries its
  own scale, so both replace rotation+scale and keep the origin.
- **quaternion**: BOTH use `Basis::from_quaternion_scale(q, existing_scale)`.
  That is the easy thing to get wrong — rebuilding from the quaternion alone
  resets scale to one — and the two authors independently got it right.
- **rotation_degrees**: both convert degrees → radians and recompose against the
  current scale.

So there is no behavioural split today. The risk is drift: a later fix to one
route silently not applying to the other.

### Suggested tidy-up (not done here)

Have `set_derived_property`'s `basis` / `quaternion` / `rotation_degrees` arms
DELEGATE to `set_transform_component` rather than reimplement it, so both routes
share one body. I did not make that edit: .30's implementation is not mine, it is
currently under verification, and changing it mid-verify would invalidate the
run for no behavioural gain.

Same shape as the other redundancy on this bead: `is_visible_in_tree` is served
by both `call_node3d_method` (:2860, wins for 3D) and `core_node_methods`
(:2873, still serves 2D) — also equivalent, also worth collapsing.

title: Dispatch the 31 missing Input singleton methods (joypad info, sensors, emulation flags, by_event queries)

title: WebRTC: make WebRTCMultiplayerPeer script-constructible and adoptable as multiplayer_peer
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/mp-webrtc] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** script -> handle -> multiplayer.multiplayer_peer -> SceneTree poll -> peer_connected and rpc over data channels

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/webrtc/webrtc_multiplayer_peer.cpp (create_server/create_client/create_mesh/add_peer/remove_peer/has_peer/get_peer/get_peers); doc/classes WebRTCPeerConnection.xml initialize(configuration)

**Patina today:** gdplatform/src/webrtc_peer.rs:715-868 implements WebRTCMultiplayerPeer, including impl NetworkPeer at :868, and class_db.rs:27264-27274 registers it. But grep 'WebRTCMultiplayerPeer' in gdscript-interop/src and gdscene/src returns nothing: there is no .new() arm next to the WebSocketMultiplayerPeer one (interpreter.rs:4197), and MultiplayerPeerHandle (multiplayer_peer_handles.rs:49-55) has only Offline and WebSocket variants, so the peer cannot be assigned to multiplayer.multiplayer_peer. The WebRTCPeerConnection dispatch (interpreter.rs:2521-2700) has no 'initialize' arm.

**Implement:** In Godot a script does `var p = WebRTCMultiplayerPeer.new(); p.create_mesh(id); p.add_peer(conn, peer_id); multiplayer.multiplayer_peer = p`. The connection setup calls WebRTCPeerConnection.initialize({iceServers: [...]}).

Patina has a real WebRTCMultiplayerPeer with NetworkPeer (webrtc_peer.rs:715-868) and a ClassDB entry (class_db.rs:27264), but no constructor arm and no MultiplayerPeerHandle variant, so no script can reach it. initialize is not dispatched.

Implementation: add a MultiplayerPeerHandle::WebRTC(Box<WebRTCMultiplayerPeer>) variant and new_webrtc_multiplayer_peer_handle(); add a WebRTCMultiplayerPeer .new() arm in interpreter.rs next to :4197; add instance arms for create_server/create_client/create_mesh/add_peer(conn_handle, id, unreliable_lifetime)/remove_peer/has_peer/get_peer (returns {connection, channels, connected})/get_peers. Make the adopt path (scripting.rs:5952-5980 via take_multiplayer_peer) accept it. Add WebRTCPeerConnection.initialize(config) and store the iceServers config for the browser binding. Complete the ClassDB method list to the extension_api surface.

Wiring: script -> handle -> multiplayer.multiplayer_peer -> SceneTree poll -> peer_connected and rpc over data channels.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/multiplayer_peer_handles.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`

**Prove it:** A GDScript test scene creates two WebRTCPeerConnections, exchanges SDP and ICE through their signals in-process, adds each to a WebRTCMultiplayerPeer mesh, and assigns those peers to two SceneTrees. Both trees then emit peer_connected with the correct ids and a reliable rpc arrives on the other tree. initialize({}) returns OK. (test: `webrtc_multiplayer_peer_script_test`)

**Verifier note:** The gap is real. grep -rl 'WebRTCMultiplayerPeer' over crates/ hits only gdplatform/src/{lib,webrtc_peer}.rs, a gdplatform test, class_db.rs, inspector_schema_generated.rs and tests/classdb_parity_test.rs. Nothing in gdscript-interop/src or gdscene/src. MultiplayerPeerHandle (multiplayer_peer_handles.rs:49-55) has only Offline and WebSocket variants. The only 'initialize' arm in interpreter.rs is :2830, which belongs to iface (an XR interface), not WebRTCPeerConnection. UNWIRED is correct. Priority goes down to 2: WebRTC mesh multiplayer is uncommon next to ENet/WebSocket, and finding 5 shows that without a browser binding it only reaches peers in the same process.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript test scene creates two WebRTCPeerConnections, exchanges SDP and ICE through their signals in-process, adds each to a WebRTCMultiplayerPeer mesh, and assigns those peers to two SceneTrees. title: WebRTC: bind WebRTCPeerConnection/DataChannel to the browser RTCPeerConnection on wasm32
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/mp-webrtc-browser] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** script WebRTCPeerConnection.new() in the browser runtime (patina-web) -> JS RTCPeerConnection -> session_description_created/ice_candidate_created signals fire from poll()

title: MultiplayerSynchronizer: synchronized/delta_synchronized/visibility_changed signals, delta_interval, visibility update modes
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/mp-synchronizer] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** a .tscn synchronizer on the server -> MainLoop poll -> the client applies the values and its script's synchronized handler runs

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/multiplayer/multiplayer_synchronizer.cpp (synchronized, delta_synchronized, visibility_changed signals; delta_interval; VISIBILITY_PROCESS_IDLE/PHYSICS/NONE; update_visibility(for_peer)); scene_replication_interface.cpp _send_delta

**Patina today:** Interval sync, watch (ON_CHANGE) properties and visibility filters exist (scene_tree.rs:1184-1252, 3446-3557; scripting.rs:2961-3010 set_visibility_for/is_visible_to/add/remove_visibility_filter). grep 'delta_interval\|visibility_update_mode\|update_visibility\|"get_visibility_for"\|"set_replication_config"\|"synchronized"\|"delta_synchronized"\|"visibility_changed"' in gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src -> no hits. So watch properties go out on replication_interval rather than delta_interval, no signal fires after a sync is applied, and the config is only read once at registration (scene_tree.rs:1150).

**Implement:** Godot: when a peer applies a sync it emits synchronized, and for ON_CHANGE (delta) state it emits delta_synchronized. A change in visibility for a peer emits visibility_changed(for_peer). ON_CHANGE properties use their own delta_interval clock. visibility_update_mode (IDLE/PHYSICS/NONE) decides when filters re-run, and update_visibility(peer) forces a re-run. set_replication_config swaps the config at runtime. get_visibility_for(peer) reads the per-peer override.

Patina has interval sync, watch properties and filters, but none of the above (see grep evidence).

Implementation: in gdplatform MultiplayerSynchronizer (network.rs:1823-2120) add a delta_interval_ms clock for watch properties and a 'last applied kind' result from apply_sync_packet. In scene_tree.rs apply_replication_packets, emit 'synchronized'/'delta_synchronized' on the synchronizer node. Add scripting.rs arms for set/get_delta_interval, set/get_replication_interval, set/get_root_path, set/get_replication_config (a handle from network.rs:2179-2206), set/get_visibility_update_mode, update_visibility, get_visibility_for. Have the outbound pass compare the previous per-peer visibility and emit visibility_changed. Honor update mode NONE by evaluating filters only on update_visibility.

Wiring: a .tscn synchronizer on the server -> MainLoop poll -> the client applies the values and its script's synchronized handler runs.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs`

**Prove it:** With a two-tree loopback: a client script connected to synchronized sees it fire after the server changes a synced position. A watch-mode property set on the server is sent according to delta_interval, not replication_interval, and fires delta_synchronized. Toggling a visibility filter result and calling update_visibility(2) emits visibility_changed(2) exactly once. A replication_config swapped at runtime takes effect on the next tick. (test: `multiplayer_synchronizer_signals_test`)

**Verifier note:** grep '"delta_synchronized"|"synchronized"|"visibility_changed"|delta_interval|visibility_update_mode|"update_visibility"|"get_visibility_for"|set_replication_config' in gdscene/src, gdscript-interop/src and gdplatform/src finds nothing. Registration reads the config once (scene_tree.rs:1139-1152). PARTIAL at P2 is reasonable.
acceptance_criteria: With a two-tree loopback: a client script connected to synchronized sees it fire after the server changes a synced position. A watch-mode property set on the server is sent according to delta_interval, not replication_interval, and fires delta_synchronized. Toggling a visibility filter result and calling update_visibility(2) emits visibility_changed(2) exactly once. A replication_config swapped at runtime takes effect on the next tick. (test: `multiplayer_synchronizer_signals_test`)

title: Multiplayer: speak Godot 4.6 SceneMultiplayer wire format (path cache + method index) on the live RPC path
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/mp-wire-protocol] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** script rpc() -> the codec used by MultiplayerAPI::rpc -> the bytes on the transport match Godot's

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/multiplayer/scene_cache_interface.cpp + scene_rpc_interface.cpp (_send_rpc: NETWORK_COMMAND_REMOTE_CALL with node-id compression flags, method index into rpc list, NodePath strings in SIMPLIFY_PATH); scene_multiplayer.h:68-76 NetworkCommands

**Patina today:** network.rs:1066 encode_rpc_call and RpcPathCache (network.rs:964-1050) are called only from gdplatform/tests/multiplayer_godot_wire_protocol.rs:41-109; grep 'encode_rpc_call\|RpcPathCache' found no other callers. The runtime MultiplayerAPI::rpc uses encode_rpc_packet (network.rs:428, a full u64 path hash plus the method NAME string) and poll uses the cache-less decode_rpc_packet (network.rs:498). Godot sends NodePath strings in SIMPLIFY_PATH and a method INDEX, so even the cache format (u64 hash) cannot interoperate with a Godot 4.6 peer. A green test named 'godot_wire_protocol' covers code the runtime never runs.

**Implement:** Godot 4.6 SceneRPCInterface packs REMOTE_CALL as a command byte with node-id/name compression flags, a node id from the SIMPLIFY_PATH/CONFIRM_PATH cache (where SIMPLIFY_PATH carries the NodePath string and a methods hash), and a method INDEX into the sorted rpc list, followed by the encoded args. A Patina web client must use this to join a Godot dedicated server over WebSocket.

Patina's live path (network.rs:410-500) sends a Patina-only frame (u64 path hash + method name). The cache code that resembles Godot's (network.rs:964-1160) only runs in gdplatform/tests/multiplayer_godot_wire_protocol.rs.

Implementation: rewrite encode/decode against scene_rpc_interface.cpp/_send_rpc and scene_cache_interface.cpp, with byte-exact compression flags. Keep a per-peer RpcPathCache inside MultiplayerAPI that sends SIMPLIFY_PATH with the real NodePath and resolves CONFIRM_PATH. Compute the method index from the target node's sorted RPC method list (this needs the per-node config from the mp-rpc-config bead). Point MultiplayerAPI::rpc/rpc_id/poll at the new codec and remove the rpc_path_hash routing from scene_tree.rs:31/node_for_rpc_hash. Spawn/sync framing should follow scene_replication_interface.cpp in a later stage.

Wiring: script rpc() -> the codec used by MultiplayerAPI::rpc -> the bytes on the transport match Godot's.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`

**Prove it:** A golden-bytes test captures the frames from two SceneTrees running a .gd script that calls rpc('take_damage', 5) on /root/Main/Player, including the first SIMPLIFY_PATH and the follow-up REMOTE_CALL after CONFIRM_PATH. The bytes must equal Godot 4.6.1 output for the same scene (transcribed from the upstream encoder, with the derivation recorded in the test). The receiving tree still dispatches the call. (test: `multiplayer_godot_wire_live_path_test`)

**Verifier note:** UNWIRED is confirmed. grep 'encode_rpc_call|RpcPathCache' over engine-rs/crates and engine-rs/tests, outside network.rs, finds only gdplatform/tests/multiplayer_godot_wire_protocol.rs:12-109. The live poll uses decode_rpc_packet (network.rs:498), and rpc() uses encode_rpc_packet (network.rs:428). Priority goes down to 2: byte-level interop with a stock Godot server is an uncommon need, since Patina-to-Patina RPC works over its own framing and the GDScript surface does not depend on the wire bytes. The broadcast and authority bugs in mp-rpc-core matter more and stay at P0.
acceptance_criteria: A golden-bytes test captures the frames from two SceneTrees running a .gd script that calls rpc('take_damage', 5) on /root/Main/Player, including the first SIMPLIFY_PATH and the follow-up REMOTE_CALL after CONFIRM_PATH. The bytes must equal Godot 4.6.1 output for the same scene (transcribed from the upstream encoder, with the derivation recorded in the test). The receiving tree still dispatches the call. (test: `multiplayer_godot_wire_live_path_test`)

title: Networking: complete MultiplayerPeer/PacketPeer/WebSocketPeer script method surface
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/mp-peer-surface] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** a GDScript chat example using only WebSocketPeer.put_var/get_var runs over the WS loopback in MainLoop

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/main/multiplayer_peer.cpp _bind_methods; core/io/packet_peer.cpp (put_packet/get_packet/put_var/get_var/get_packet_error/encode_buffer_max_size); modules/websocket/websocket_peer.cpp + websocket_multiplayer_peer.cpp:76+

**Patina today:** call_multiplayer_peer_instance (interpreter.rs:25925-26015) dispatches only create_server/create_client/poll/close/get_unique_id/get_peer_address/get_peer_port/get_connection_status/is_server. These are absent: set/get_transfer_mode, set/get_transfer_channel, set_target_peer, get_packet_peer, get_packet_channel, get_packet_mode, disconnect_peer, generate_unique_id, set_refuse_new_connections, is_server_relay_supported, put_packet/get_packet/get_available_packet_count/put_var/get_var, and WebSocketMultiplayerPeer get_peer/supported_protocols/handshake_headers/buffer sizes/handshake_timeout/max_queued_packets. call_websocket_peer_instance (interpreter.rs:26018-26170) has no put_packet, put_var, get_var, get_packet_error, accept_stream, set/get_inbound_buffer_size, set/get_outbound_buffer_size, or encode_buffer_max_size.

**Implement:** Godot scripts use MultiplayerPeer as a PacketPeer: set_target_peer + put_packet / get_packet with get_packet_peer/channel/mode, and transfer_mode/channel properties. WebSocketPeer.put_packet and put_var/get_var are the usual way to send binary and Variant data, and buffer sizes and handshake_timeout are commonly set.

Patina's handle dispatch covers only setup and status (see evidence).

Implementation: extend call_multiplayer_peer_instance and call_websocket_peer_instance with the missing arms, backed by NetworkPeer methods (add target/transfer state to MultiplayerPeerHandle). put_var/get_var go through gdvariant::binary encode/decode with allow_objects=false. Expose transfer_mode/transfer_channel/refuse_new_connections as properties too. Add get_peer(id) on WebSocketMultiplayerPeer returning a WebSocketPeer handle. Bring the ClassDB method lists (class_db.rs) in line with extension_api.

Wiring: a GDScript chat example using only WebSocketPeer.put_var/get_var runs over the WS loopback in MainLoop.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/multiplayer_peer_handles.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`

**Prove it:** A .gd script: WebSocketPeer client to a native WebSocketMultiplayerPeer server. put_var({'a':1}) is received through get_var() as the equal Dictionary. put_packet sends binary. A MultiplayerPeer with set_target_peer(2) + put_packet is delivered only to peer 2, and get_packet_peer() reports the sender. Changing transfer_mode/transfer_channel round-trips through getters. (test: `multiplayer_peer_packet_surface_test`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. Function boundaries are interpreter.rs:25925 (call_multiplayer_peer_instance), 26018 (call_websocket_peer_instance) and 26201 (the next fn). The quoted arms in 25925-26017 are only create_server/create_client/poll/close/get_unique_id/get_peer_address/get_peer_port/get_connection_status/is_server. The websocket arms in 26018-26200 are connect_to_url, poll, get_ready_state, send_text, send, get_available_packet_count, get_packet, was_string_packet, close, close code/reason, requested_url, protocols, handshake headers, connected host/port, outbound_buffered_amount, no_delay, heartbeat, max_queued_packets. They do NOT include put_packet/put_var/get_var/buffer sizes. Greps across gdscript-interop/src, gdscene/src, gdplatform/src and gdobject/src: '"set_target_peer"'=0, '"get_packet_peer"'=0, '"set_transfer_mode"'=0, '"set_inbound_buffer_size"'=0. The '"put_packet"' hits (26210, 26461, 26663) belong to the WebRTC data channel, PacketPeerUDP and PacketPeerStream. The '"put_var"' hit (22208) is StreamPeerBuffer only. Priority 2 is reasonable.
acceptance_criteria: A .gd script: WebSocketPeer client to a native WebSocketMultiplayerPeer server. put_var({'a':1}) is received through get_var() as the equal Dictionary. put_packet sends binary. A MultiplayerPeer with set_target_peer(2) + put_packet is delivered only to peer 2, and get_packet_peer() reports the sender. Changing transfer_mode/transfer_channel round-trips through getters.
