title: Multiplayer: SceneMultiplayer property surface, per-branch set_multiplayer(api, path), SceneTree.multiplayer_poll
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/mp-api-surface] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** a lobby scene with its own SceneMultiplayer at /root/Lobby takes RPCs separately from the main API

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/multiplayer/scene_multiplayer.cpp _bind_methods (root_path, server_relay, allow_object_decoding, auth_timeout, max_sync_packet_size, max_delta_packet_size, poll, get_multiplayer_peer); scene/main/scene_tree.cpp set_multiplayer(api, root_path), multiplayer_poll

**Patina today:** call_multiplayer_method (interpreter.rs ~9880-10060) handles is_server, get_unique_id, has_multiplayer_peer, get_peers, get_remote_sender_id, get_authenticating_peers, send_bytes, complete_auth, set/is_refusing_new_connections, disconnect_peer, clear, set/get_auth_callback, send_auth, set_multiplayer_peer. grep 'auth_timeout\|root_path\|get_multiplayer_peer\|server_relay\|allow_object_decoding\|max_sync_packet_size' in interpreter.rs -> no multiplayer arms. The Rust side has set_auth_timeout (network.rs:718) but no script path. SceneTree.set_multiplayer ignores root_path (interpreter.rs:5616-5623 comment: 'one tree-wide API'). SceneMultiplayer.new() has no constructor arm (interpreter.rs:4185-4200 only Offline/WebSocket peers). grep 'multiplayer_poll' in gdscene/src -> no hits, so main_loop.rs:4266 always polls.

**Implement:** Godot exposes these SceneMultiplayer properties: root_path, server_relay, allow_object_decoding, auth_timeout, max_sync_packet_size, max_delta_packet_size, multiplayer_peer (getter). It also has poll(), lets you create a SceneMultiplayer and install it for a subtree with get_tree().set_multiplayer(api, ^"/root/Lobby"), and has SceneTree.multiplayer_poll=false for manual polling.

Patina has one tree-wide API, ignores root_path, has no script access to the properties listed above, has no SceneMultiplayer.new(), and always polls (main_loop.rs:4266).

Implementation: add the property getters/setters to call_multiplayer_method and the member get/set path (interpreter.rs:1904-1911). Wire allow_object_decoding to ObjectDecoding in decode (network.rs:354/1145) and auth_timeout to set_auth_timeout. Add a SceneMultiplayer handle type. Let SceneTree hold a map root_path -> MultiplayerAPI, where Node.multiplayer resolves to the nearest branch API, and poll each one in poll_multiplayer_with_delta, matching RPC paths relative to that root. Add a multiplayer_poll flag that MainLoop checks, plus a script-callable multiplayer.poll().

Wiring: a lobby scene with its own SceneMultiplayer at /root/Lobby takes RPCs separately from the main API.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs`

**Prove it:** A script sets get_tree().multiplayer_poll = false. RPCs do not arrive until it calls multiplayer.poll(), and then they do. A SceneMultiplayer.new() installed with set_multiplayer(api, ^"/root/Lobby") gives nodes under Lobby a different get_unique_id() than nodes outside it. multiplayer.allow_object_decoding = true lets an Object argument decode, and the default rejects it. auth_timeout round-trips and controls the timeout. (test: `multiplayer_scene_api_surface_test`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute, and found something that makes it worse. class_db.rs:7914-7917 registers SceneTree.multiplayer_poll with accessors is_multiplayer_poll_enabled/set_multiplayer_poll_enabled, but grep for 'set_multiplayer_poll\|is_multiplayer_poll_enabled' in gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src finds 0 hits. So the property exists in ClassDB, but setting it does nothing, and main_loop.rs:4266 calls poll_multiplayer_with_delta unconditionally. SceneMultiplayer (class_db.rs:27370-27396) registers server_relay, allow_object_decoding and auth_timeout as plain properties with no accessors or engine reads. network.rs:718 set_auth_timeout has no script caller ('set_auth_timeout' grep in interpreter = 0). '"get_multiplayer_peer"' = 0. The root_path hits are MultiplayerSpawner/Synchronizer only (scene_tree.rs:1203,1683). Priority 2 is fine. The multiplayer_poll no-op might justify 1, but the feature is uncommon.
acceptance_criteria: A script sets get_tree().multiplayer_poll = false. RPCs do not arrive until it calls multiplayer.poll(), and then they do. A SceneMultiplayer.new() installed with set_multiplayer(api, ^"/root/Lobby") gives nodes under Lobby a different get_unique_id() than nodes outside it. multiplayer.allow_object_decoding = true lets an Object argument decode, and the default rejects it. auth_timeout round-trips and controls the timeout. (test: `multiplayer_scene_api_surface_test`)

title: HTTP: fetch-backed HTTPClient on wasm32 + complete HTTPClient/HTTPRequest method surface
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/net-http] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** a script's HTTPClient in the browser runtime -> the fetch driver -> body chunks

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/platform/web/http_client_web.cpp (HTTPClient over fetch); core/io/http_client.cpp _bind_methods; scene/main/http_request.cpp (get_downloaded_bytes, get_body_size, download_chunk_size, use_threads)

**Patina today:** gdplatform/src/http_client.rs:1-17 builds HTTPClient on std::net::TcpStream with no wasm32 branch (grep 'wasm\|fetch' http_client.rs -> no cfg). The fetch driver web_request_driver.rs (a port of http_client_web.cpp) is used only by the HTTPRequest platform type (http_request.rs:206-207), so a script HTTPClient fails in the browser. call_http_client_instance (interpreter.rs:26797) lacks request_raw, is_response_chunked, get_response_headers_as_dictionary, set_http_proxy, set_https_proxy, query_string_from_dict, set/get_connection. HTTPRequest arms (scripting.rs:4509-4760) lack get_downloaded_bytes, get_body_size, set/get_download_chunk_size, set_use_threads/is_using_threads (grep returned no hits).

**Implement:** Godot's web export implements HTTPClient over fetch (platform/web/http_client_web.cpp), so the poll-driven connect_to_host/request/read_response_body_chunk works in the browser. HTTPRequest also reports progress through get_downloaded_bytes/get_body_size.

Patina's HTTPClient is TCP-only (http_client.rs:1-17), so in the browser it reports CANT_CONNECT, even though the same fetch driver (web_request_driver.rs) already backs HTTPRequest. Several methods are not dispatched (see evidence).

Implementation: give http_client_handle.rs a cfg(wasm32) backend that holds WebTransfer<WebFetchBackend> (http_request.rs:206), and map connect_to_host/request/poll/get_status/read_response_body_chunk onto WebRequestDriver (web_request_driver.rs:284-469). Add the missing HTTPClient arms. query_string_from_dict should follow http_client.cpp exactly (arrays repeat the key, null gives a bare key). Add the HTTPRequest progress getters fed from HttpRequestNode's transfer, and chunk size/use_threads (use_threads accepted, as a no-op on web like Godot).

Wiring: a script's HTTPClient in the browser runtime -> the fetch driver -> body chunks.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/http_client_handle.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/http_request_node.rs`

**Prove it:** A target-independent test drives the HTTPClient handle through a scripted FetchBackend: connect_to_host -> request -> STATUS_BODY -> read_response_body_chunk gives the full body, and is_response_chunked/get_response_headers_as_dictionary are correct. `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p gdplatform` succeeds. HTTPClient.query_string_from_dict({'a':[1,2],'b':null}) == 'a=1&a=2&b'. An HTTPRequest script polling get_downloaded_bytes during a mock transfer sees a non-decreasing sequence ending at get_body_size. (test: `http_client_web_fetch_surface_test`)

**Verifier note:** grep 'wasm\|fetch' in gdplatform/src/http_client.rs and http_client_handle.rs finds no cfg(wasm) branch. The only hits are an atomic fetch_add and a comment. The arms in call_http_client_instance (interpreter.rs:26797+) are connect_to_host, request, poll, get_status, has_response, get_response_code, get_response_headers, get_response_body_length, read_response_body_chunk, read_chunk_size, blocking_mode and close, plus Node passthroughs. There is no request_raw, is_response_chunked, get_response_headers_as_dictionary, set_http_proxy or query_string_from_dict. The Rust side exists but is not dispatched: http_client_handle.rs:243 get_response_headers_as_dictionary and http_client.rs:235 set_http_proxy. '"query_string_from_dict"' = 0 and '"get_downloaded_bytes"' = 0. scripting.rs has only get_body_size_limit (4702), with no download_chunk_size or use_threads. Priority 2 is fine.
acceptance_criteria: A target-independent test drives the HTTPClient handle through a scripted FetchBackend: connect_to_host -> request -> STATUS_BODY -> read_response_body_chunk gives the full body, and is_response_chunked/get_response_headers_as_dictionary are correct. `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p gdplatform` succeeds. HTTPClient.query_string_from_dict({'a':[1,2],'b':null}) == 'a=1&a=2&b'. An HTTPRequest script polling get_downloaded_bytes during a mock transfer sees a non-decreasing sequence ending at get_body_size. (test: `http_client_web_fetch_surface_test`)

title: Navigation3D: voxel-based NavigationMesh bake with radius erosion, climb and height, and collider source geometry
description:
[audit-key: navigation/nav-bake-3d] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn region over a floor with a wall and a 0.6m step -> bake_navigation_mesh() -> agent path keeps agent_radius from the wall and avoids a step above agent_max_climb

**Godot ground truth:** modules/navigation_3d/3d/nav_mesh_generator_3d.cpp (Recast: rcRasterizeTriangles, rcFilterWalkableLowHeightSpans, rcErodeWalkableArea, watershed/monotone/layers partition, rcBuildPolyMesh, detail mesh); doc/classes/NavigationMesh.xml

**Patina today:** gdserver3d/src/navigation.rs:300-385 bake_navigation_mesh is self-described 'simplified': it keeps triangles by slope and drops triangles whose inradius < agent_radius. It does no voxelization and no border erosion, so the navmesh edge sits at the wall face and agents clip walls. It does no height-clearance (agent_height) or climb (agent_max_climb) test and no merging into convex polygons (one polygon per source triangle, vertices duplicated at :361-367). cell_size, cell_height, region_min_size and edge_max_length are copied through and never used. nav_bake.rs:105-138 parses MeshInstance3D only (no parsed_geometry_type/static colliders, no source group mode). The on_thread argument is ignored (nav_bake.rs:189-193). gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:29189-29230 NavigationMeshGenerator.bake_from_source_geometry_data returns a Dictionary instead of filling the NavigationMesh argument (doc comment at :29191-29197).

**Implement:** Godot bakes 3D navmeshes with Recast (nav_mesh_generator_3d.cpp). It rasterizes source triangles into a heightfield at cell_size/cell_height, filters ledge, low-height (agent_height) and climb (agent_max_climb) spans, erodes walkable area by agent_radius, partitions per sample_partition_type, and builds a poly mesh limited by edge_max_length/edge_max_error/verts_per_poly plus a detail mesh. Patina's gdserver3d::bake_navigation_mesh (gdserver3d/src/navigation.rs:309) is a per-triangle slope filter. Implementation: write a pure-Rust heightfield pipeline in gdserver3d/src/navigation.rs (or a new navmesh_bake.rs in that crate): rasterize to spans, run walkable filters, a distance-field erosion by ceil(agent_radius/cell_size), monotone partition (watershed later), contour tracing with edge_max_error simplification, and polygonization into convex polys with shared vertices. Extend nav_bake::parse_source_geometry_3d to honour parsed_geometry_type (MESH_INSTANCES / STATIC_COLLIDERS / BOTH, reading CollisionShape3D box/sphere/capsule/cylinder/concave/convex shapes of StaticBody3D with collision_mask) and source_geometry_mode (root/group-with-children/group-explicit), and copy the remaining NavigationMesh params through packed_scene. Make NavigationMeshGenerator/NavigationServer3D.bake_from_source_geometry_data write vertices/polygons into the passed NavigationMesh resource. Wiring: .tscn region over a floor with a wall and a 0.6m step -> bake_navigation_mesh() -> agent path keeps agent_radius from the wall and avoids a step above agent_max_climb.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/navigation.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/nav_bake.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn NavigationRegion3D over a 20x20 floor with a 1m-high StaticBody3D wall (parsed_geometry_type=STATIC_COLLIDERS, agent_radius 0.5): after bake_navigation_mesh(), no navmesh vertex is within agent_radius - cell_size of the wall faces, the baked polygon count is far below the source triangle count (polygons merged), a 0.6m ledge with agent_max_climb 0.25 is not connected, and an agent pathing past the wall keeps at least 0.45m clearance (test: `nav_bake_3d_voxel_erosion_and_colliders`).

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. gdserver3d/src/navigation.rs:300-309 doc says the bake is a 'simplified baking pipeline' with one polygon per walkable triangle, and that 'a production implementation would use voxelization'. A grep for 'rcErode|heightfield|voxel' over gdserver3d/src and nav_bake.rs hits only unrelated gi.rs stubs. nav_bake.rs:190-193 says on_thread is accepted and ignored. interpreter.rs:29189-29197 says NavigationMeshGenerator returns a Dictionary rather than filling the NavigationMesh. The bake is wired (call_nav_region_method plus bake_finished), so PARTIAL at P2 fits.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn NavigationRegion3D over a 20x20 floor with a 1m-high StaticBody3D wall (parsed_geometry_type=STATIC_COLLIDERS, agent_radius 0.5): after bake_navigation_mesh(), no navmesh vertex is within agent_radius - cell_size of the wall faces, the baked polygon count is far below the source triangle count (polygons merged), a 0.6m ledge with agent_max_climb 0.25 is not connected, and an agent pathing past the wall keeps at least 0.45m clearance (test: `nav_bake_3d_voxel_erosion_and_colliders`).

title: NavigationObstacle: radius affects avoidance only, add vertices static avoidance and bake-time carving
description:
[audit-key: navigation/nav-obstacles] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn obstacle with vertices plus an agent with avoidance moving through it -> deflected safe velocity; rebake -> hole in navmesh

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/NavigationObstacle2D.xml: radius is for avoidance agents only; vertices + avoidance_enabled = static avoidance obstacle; affect_navigation_mesh/carve_navigation_mesh affect baking; scene/2d/navigation/navigation_obstacle_2d.cpp, modules/navigation_2d/2d/nav_mesh_generator_2d.cpp obstruction parsing

**Patina today:** main_loop.rs:2150-2166 adds every radius>0 NavigationObstacle2D to the PATH server, and NavigationServer2D::find_path routes around it (navigation.rs:936 route_around_obstacles, called at :817). A Godot path ignores obstacles and only avoidance reacts, so Patina paths diverge. grep 'carv|affect_navigation_mesh' in gdscene/src, gdserver3d/src and gdscript-interop/src finds only the comment at main_loop.rs:2143-2145, so there is no bake-time carving. The avoidance gather (main_loop.rs:1820-1838) reads only `radius`. `vertices` static obstacles are never read (grep '"vertices"' in that function returns nothing).

**Implement:** Godot: an obstacle's `radius` is a dynamic avoidance shape and never alters path queries. `vertices` with avoidance_enabled forms a static avoidance polygon that agents with matching avoidance_mask cannot enter. affect_navigation_mesh (with carve_navigation_mesh) makes the projected `vertices` an obstruction during navmesh baking (NavigationObstacle2D.xml, nav_mesh_generator_2d.cpp). Patina feeds radius obstacles into path queries (main_loop.rs:2150-2166, navigation.rs:936), never reads `vertices`, and has no carving. Implementation: remove obstacles from the path-query server (keep NavigationServer2D::add_obstacle for an explicit API only). In process_navigation_avoidance(_3d), build static ORCA obstacle lines from global-transformed `vertices` (port RVO2 obstacle segments into orca_safe_velocity's obstacle input) and honour avoidance_layers. In the 2D bake (nav_polygon.rs / nav_bake.rs) and the 3D bake, add obstacles with affect_navigation_mesh=true as obstruction outlines, inflated by agent_radius unless carve_navigation_mesh. Wiring: .tscn obstacle with vertices plus an agent with avoidance moving through it -> deflected safe velocity; rebake -> hole in navmesh.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/nav_bake.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/nav_polygon.rs`

**Prove it:** In a .tscn, an agent's get_current_navigation_path() is a straight line through a radius obstacle, matching Godot. With avoidance enabled the body (moved by velocity_computed) still never enters the radius. A square `vertices` obstacle blocks an avoidance agent from entering. With affect_navigation_mesh=true, bake_navigation_polygon() produces a navmesh hole and the path routes around it (test: `nav_obstacle_avoidance_vs_bake_carving`).

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. main_loop.rs:2150-2166 pushes every radius>0, avoidance_enabled NavigationObstacle2D into the path server's obstacles2, and navigation.rs:822/847/1033/1042 send path results through route_around_obstacles (:936). In Godot, `radius` is only an avoidance shape and does not change path queries. `grep -rn 'affect_navigation_mesh|carve_navigation_mesh'` over crates/ (tests excluded) finds only the ClassDB property registrations (class_db.rs:3627-3632, 18235-18240) and the comment at main_loop.rs:2143-2145. No bake code reads them. The avoidance gather (main_loop.rs:1819-1838) reads radius, velocity and avoidance_layers only. `grep '"vertices"'` in main_loop.rs, navigation_agents.rs and nav_*.rs returns nothing, so there are no static vertex obstacles. Priority 2 is defensible.
acceptance_criteria: In a .tscn, an agent's get_current_navigation_path() is a straight line through a radius obstacle, matching Godot. With avoidance enabled the body (moved by velocity_computed) still never enters the radius. A square `vertices` obstacle blocks an avoidance agent from entering. With affect_navigation_mesh=true, bake_navigation_polygon() produces a navmesh hole and the path routes around it (test: `nav_obstacle_avoidance_vs_bake_carving`).

title: Scripting: generic ClassDB accessor bridge so set_X/get_X/is_X calls on 3D nodes read and write their properties
description:
[audit-key: nodes-3d/node3d-accessor-bridge] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** GDScript call -> interpreter call_object_method -> SceneAccess::call_node_method -> bridge -> the property the renderer reads

**Godot ground truth:** core/object/class_db.cpp (property setters/getters are ordinary bound methods); doc/classes/*.xml for each 3D class

**Patina today:** A loop over extension_api.json methods, grepping each as a string literal in gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src, found 0 hits for: MeshInstance3D 21/21 (set_surface_override_material, set_blend_shape_value, get_active_material...), GeometryInstance3D 34/34, Light3D 31/31 (set_param, set_shadow...), Sprite3D 14/14, SpriteBase3D 34/34 (set_billboard_mode...), Label3D most of 61, PathFollow3D 19/19 (set_progress...), Decal 24/24, ReflectionProbe 30/30, RemoteTransform3D 11/11, MultiMeshInstance3D 2/2, Area3D most of 50. There is no generic accessor bridge: grep for '"set_"|strip_prefix("set_")|get_property_setter' finds only the ClassDB.class_get_property_setter reflection call (interpreter.rs:20321), even though ClassDB records accessors (class_db.rs:81 with_accessors, :968 get_property_getter). Because class_has_method is true, interpreter.rs:15666 returns Nil silently.

**Implement:** Godot: every property setter/getter is a callable bound method, so `$Light.set_param(Light3D.PARAM_ENERGY, 2)` and `$Mesh.set_surface_override_material(0, m)` work. Patina: none of these 3D accessors is dispatched (0 string-literal hits), and ClassDB registration makes the call return Nil silently (interpreter.rs:15666). Implementation: at the end of SceneAccess::call_node_method in scripting.rs, before returning None, look up the node's class property list (class_db get_property_list) for a PropertyInfo whose `setter`/`getter` equals the method. For a setter, call set_node_property(prop, args[0]) so the Node3D transform routing still applies; for a getter, call get_node_property(prop) and fall back to property_get_revert. Special-case indexed accessors: Light3D set_param/get_param (index -> light_energy and the other PARAM_* property names from Light3D.xml), set_surface_override_material(i) -> surface_material_override/i, and set_blend_shape_value(i) -> blend_shapes/<name>. Wiring: GDScript call -> interpreter call_object_method -> SceneAccess::call_node_method -> bridge -> the property the renderer reads.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene-loaded OmniLight3D whose script calls set_param(Light3D.PARAM_ENERGY, 4.0) shows energy 4 in the next Play frame's SceneLight3D. `$PathFollow3D.set_progress(2.0)` moves the follower in the next tick. `get_param` returns the stored value rather than Nil. (test: `node3d_accessor_methods_reach_properties`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. In gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src, grep 'strip_prefix("set_")|strip_prefix("get_")|strip_prefix("is_")|get_property_setter|get_property_getter' found only the ClassDB reflection calls (interpreter.rs:20314-20324). grep 'starts_with("set_")|starts_with("get_")' found only navigation_agents.rs:183/190 (layer bits). grep '"set_param"|"set_progress"|"set_blend_shape_value"|"set_material_override"|"set_surface_override_material"': 0 hits. call_node_method (scripting.rs:2594-4922) ends in item_views::call_item_view_method, which returns None for non-item-view classes (item_views.rs:1314). There is no generic accessor fallback, so the call returns Nil silently (interpreter.rs:15666).
acceptance_criteria: A scene-loaded OmniLight3D whose script calls set_param(Light3D.PARAM_ENERGY, 4.0) shows energy 4 in the next Play frame's SceneLight3D. `$PathFollow3D.set_progress(2.0)` moves the follower in the next tick. `get_param` returns the stored value rather than Nil. (test: `node3d_accessor_methods_reach_properties`)

title: AStar: dispatch _compute_cost/_estimate_cost/_filter_neighbor script overrides and the neighbor filter
description:
[audit-key: navigation/astar-virtuals] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** `class_name TeleAStar extends AStar2D` with _compute_cost returning 0 for one pair -> get_id_path from a running .tscn script takes that edge

**Godot ground truth:** core/math/a_star.cpp GDVIRTUAL _compute_cost/_estimate_cost/_filter_neighbor; set_neighbor_filter_enabled (extension_api.json AStar2D/AStar3D)

**Patina today:** Diffing extension_api.json AStar2D/AStar3D methods against string arms in gdscene/src/astar.rs, scripting.rs and interpreter.rs shows _filter_neighbor, _estimate_cost, _compute_cost, set_neighbor_filter_enabled and is_neighbor_filter_enabled have 0 hits. AStarGrid2D _compute_cost/_estimate_cost are also 0. astar.rs:9-11 hardcodes Euclidean cost and estimate. AStar objects are opaque handles created by astar_new (scripting.rs:7661-7680), so a GDScript `extends AStar2D` with an overridden _compute_cost has no hook.

**Implement:** Godot lets scripts subclass AStar2D/AStar3D/AStarGrid2D and override _compute_cost(from_id,to_id), _estimate_cost(from_id,end_id) and (AStar2D/3D) _filter_neighbor(from_id,neighbor_id), which applies when set_neighbor_filter_enabled(true) (a_star.cpp GDVIRTUAL calls). Patina's solver (astar.rs) uses fixed Euclidean costs and has no callback. Implementation: make AStar::get_id_path_partial and AStarGrid2D::get_id_path generic over a cost-provider trait. When the handle was created for a script instance whose class overrides these virtuals, the scripting layer supplies a provider that calls back into the interpreter (as other script virtuals are dispatched) and falls back to the built-in costs otherwise. Add set/is_neighbor_filter_enabled arms. Wiring: `class_name TeleAStar extends AStar2D` with _compute_cost returning 0 for one pair -> get_id_path from a running .tscn script takes that edge.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/astar.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** In a running .tscn, a GDScript `extends AStar2D` whose _compute_cost makes edge 1->3 free, and whose _estimate_cost returns 0, gets get_id_path(1, 4) through point 3 even though it is geometrically longer. With set_neighbor_filter_enabled(true), a _filter_neighbor that rejects point 3 sends the path through point 2 (test: `astar_script_cost_overrides_change_path`).

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. `grep -rn '_compute_cost|_estimate_cost|_filter_neighbor|neighbor_filter'` over engine-rs/crates finds only the doc comments at astar.rs:9 and :11. There is no dispatch, no callback and no set/is_neighbor_filter_enabled arm. AStar objects are opaque handles minted by astar_new (interpreter.rs:4354), with no script instance attached. MISSING and priority 2 stand.
acceptance_criteria: In a running .tscn, a GDScript `extends AStar2D` whose _compute_cost makes edge 1->3 free, and whose _estimate_cost returns 0, gets get_id_path(1, 4) through point 3 even though it is geometrically longer. With set_neighbor_filter_enabled(true), a _filter_neighbor that rejects point 3 sends the path through point 2 (test: `astar_script_cost_overrides_change_path`).

title: Line2D/Polygon2D: honour texture modes, joint/cap variants, invert, multi-polygons, vertex colors and texture transforms
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/line-polygon-render-params] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** scene/2d/line_2d.cpp + line_builder.cpp (texture_mode NONE/TILE/STRETCH, joint_mode SHARP/BEVEL/ROUND with sharp_limit, cap BOX/ROUND, round_precision); scene/2d/polygon_2d.cpp:100-300 (offset, invert_enabled/invert_border, polygons, internal_vertex_count, vertex_colors, texture_offset/scale/rotation)

**Patina today:** Line2D arm (gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:1723-1770) reads points, width, default_color, the gradient, the width curve and ROUND caps/joints only. Polygon2D arm (:1690-1721) reads polygon, uv, color and texture only. Counts in viewport_2d_render.rs: invert_enabled 0, texture_offset 0, texture_scale 0, texture_rotation 0, vertex_colors 0, '"polygons"' 0, internal_vertex_count 0, texture_mode 0, sharp_limit 0, antialiased 0, round_precision 0. '"offset"' appears once, in the Sprite arm. Line2D `texture` is never read, so textured Line2D (ropes, lasers) draws flat. BOX cap (mode 1) is treated as NONE.

**Implement:** Godot: LineBuilder emits textured strips (TILE repeats every width*aspect, STRETCH spans the length), SHARP joints with sharp_limit fallback to BEVEL, BOX caps that extend by half-width, and round_precision. Polygon2D draws with `offset`, inverts with invert_border, splits by `polygons` index arrays with internal vertices, interpolates per-vertex `vertex_colors`, and maps UVs through texture_offset/scale/rotation (polygon_2d.cpp). Patina's arms (viewport_2d_render.rs:1690-1770) read none of these. Approach: carry texture, texture_mode, joint/cap enums and sharp_limit into Render2DKind::LineShaded (or a new LineTextured kind) and port line_builder.cpp's strip generation into gdrender2d. For Polygon2D, apply offset to the points, build the inverted outer ring when invert_enabled, triangulate each `polygons` entry, pass vertex_colors to polygon_raster for per-vertex interpolation, and build the UV transform from texture_offset/scale/rotation. The same arms feed editor viewport and Play, so no extra wiring beyond the runtime-builder bead.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/polygon_raster.rs`

**Prove it:** A Line2D with texture_mode=TILE and a 2-colour stripe texture renders alternating stripes along the stroke. A BOX-capped line extends width/2 past its endpoints. A Polygon2D with offset=(10,0) renders shifted 10px, and with invert_enabled fills outside the polygon within invert_border. vertex_colors red/green/blue produce an interpolated centre pixel. (test: `line2d_polygon2d_render_params_test`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. In crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs (4714 lines), grep -c gives 0 for each of invert_enabled, texture_offset, texture_mode, vertex_colors, "polygons", sharp_limit, antialiased. The Line2D arm (around :1724-1762) reads only points, width, default_color, __gradient_*, __width_curve_samples, begin/end_cap_mode==2 and joint_mode==2 (round only), plus closed. BOX caps (1) and SHARP/BEVEL joints are not handled, and the line texture is never read. The Polygon2D arm (:1690-1721) reads polygon, uv, color and texture only. PARTIAL at P2 stands.
acceptance_criteria: A Line2D with texture_mode=TILE and a 2-colour stripe texture renders alternating stripes along the stroke. A BOX-capped line extends width/2 past its endpoints. A Polygon2D with offset=(10,0) renders shifted 10px, and with invert_enabled fills outside the polygon within invert_border. vertex_colors red/green/blue produce an interpolated centre pixel. (test: `line2d_polygon2d_render_params_test`)

title: CanvasGroup: composite groups in the Play loop and runtime frame, not only in render_runtime_canvas
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/canvasgroup-play] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** the editor Play frame and the shared runtime builder both go through the group-aware rasterizer

**Godot ground truth:** scene/2d/canvas_group.cpp + renderer_canvas_cull canvas_group mode (subtree rendered offscreen, then composited with the group's modulate, fit_margin, clear_margin)

**Patina today:** rasterize_render_list_with_groups / collect_canvas_groups (gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:3933, :4038) are called only from render_runtime_canvas (:3879-3900). grep 'render_runtime_canvas' over the crates finds no caller outside its own doc and tests. The live Play loop calls plain rasterize_render_list (engine-rs/examples/editor.rs:331), and scene_renderer::render_runtime_frame does the same (scene_renderer.rs:198). So in Play a CanvasGroup's half-transparent modulate applies per child (overlaps double-blend) instead of to the flattened group.

**Implement:** Godot draws a CanvasGroup's subtree to a backbuffer and composites it once with the group's modulate, so overlapping translucent children do not double-blend (canvas_group.cpp). Patina implemented this in rasterize_render_list_with_groups (viewport_2d_render.rs:4038), but the frame loops that run (examples/editor.rs:331 and scene_renderer.rs:198) call rasterize_render_list. Approach: change both call sites to collect_canvas_groups(tree) + rasterize_render_list_with_groups, keeping the Camera2D view applied to the items first. Make collect_canvas_groups apply the same view to group bounds, and honour fit_margin/clear_margin. Wiring: the editor Play frame and the shared runtime builder both go through the group-aware rasterizer.

**Files:** `engine-rs/examples/editor.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`

**Prove it:** A Play-mode frame of a CanvasGroup with self_modulate alpha 0.5 holding two overlapping opaque red ColorRects (or Sprite2Ds) has the same alpha in the overlap as outside it. The same scene without the group shows a darker overlap. The check goes through the editor Play render function, not render_runtime_canvas. (test: `canvas_group_play_composite_test`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. The only callers of render_runtime_canvas or rasterize_render_list_with_groups outside tests are inside viewport_2d_render.rs itself (:3879, :3900). The two real paths, examples/editor.rs:331 (Play loop) and gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs:198 (which inlines render_runtime_canvas, comment at :175), both call plain rasterize_render_list and never call collect_canvas_groups. editor.rs:341 even notes that this path 'cannot go through render_runtime_canvas'. grep for CanvasGroup in both files returns nothing. UNWIRED at P2 stands.
acceptance_criteria: A Play-mode frame of a CanvasGroup with self_modulate alpha 0.5 holding two overlapping opaque red ColorRects (or Sprite2Ds) has the same alpha in the overlap as outside it. title: Area2D: emit body_shape_entered/exited and area_shape_entered/exited with shape indices
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/area2d-shape-signals] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** physics step -> overlap events -> MainLoop physics phase -> emit_signal -> connected GDScript handler

**Godot ground truth:** scene/2d/physics/area_2d.cpp _body_inout/_area_inout emit body_shape_entered(body_rid, body, body_shape_index, local_shape_index) and area_shape_entered

**Patina today:** process_overlap_signals and process_area_overlap_signals (gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:2844-2895) emit only body_entered/body_exited/area_entered/area_exited with a single ObjectId argument. grep 'body_shape_entered|area_shape_entered' over gdscene/src, gdphysics2d/src and gdscript-interop/src hits only gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs, so the 3D side has them and 2D does not. TileMapLayer hit detection via body_shape_entered + get_coords_for_body_rid is therefore impossible.

**Implement:** Godot's Area2D emits a *_shape_* signal per overlapping (shape, shape) pair, with (rid, node, other_shape_index, local_shape_index). The plain body_entered fires only on the first shape pair and body_exited on the last. Patina's 2D overlap events carry only area_id/body_id (physics_server.rs:2844-2895), and the 3D bridge already has the shape variants (physics_server_3d.rs). Approach: extend gdphysics2d's overlap tracking (world.rs, around :830) to record per-shape-pair enter/exit with both shape indices (shape owner order, matching collider_local_transforms). In process_overlap_signals emit body_shape_entered/exited for every pair, and body_entered/exited only on the first/last pair per body, with the same for areas. Pass a Variant RID for body_rid. title: Physics2D: Godot damp composition (area->default->body COMBINE/REPLACE), 0.1 default damp, COM and freeze modes
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-damp-modes] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn props -> physics_server body sync -> world.step damping

**Godot ground truth:** modules/godot_physics_2d/godot_body_2d.cpp:439-545: area damp overrides accumulate into total_linear_damp, then the default area is added if not done, then BODY_DAMP_MODE_COMBINE adds the body's linear_damp (REPLACE replaces); project default physics/2d/default_linear_damp=0.1; RigidBody2D center_of_mass_mode AUTO|CUSTOM, freeze_mode STATIC|KINEMATIC

**Patina today:** gdphysics2d/src/world.rs:516-525: an area damp override REPLACES the body's own linear_damp (`body.linear_damp = d`) instead of combining. Godot adds the body damp in the default COMBINE mode. SpaceParams2D defaults default_linear_damp/default_angular_damp to 0.0 (world.rs:207-208), so any project.godot that omits the key (the usual case, since defaults are not written) gets no damping where Godot uses 0.1. grep -w linear_damp_mode/angular_damp_mode/center_of_mass_mode over gdscene/src and gdphysics2d/src = 0 hits. freeze_mode appears only in physics_server_3d.rs. physics_server.rs:1729 applies center_of_mass whenever it is present, regardless of mode.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth (godot_body_2d.cpp:439-545): total damp starts at 0. Area overrides are added or replaced in priority order. The default area damp (physics/2d/default_linear_damp, 0.1 by default) is added unless an area stopped the chain. Last, the body's own damp is ADDED in DAMP_MODE_COMBINE or REPLACES the total in DAMP_MODE_REPLACE. center_of_mass is honoured only in CUSTOM mode. freeze_mode chooses static or kinematic behaviour when frozen.

Patina now: world.rs:516 replaces the body's damp with the area value, the default damp is 0.0 (world.rs:207), and none of the mode enums is read.

Approach: add `linear_damp_mode` and `angular_damp_mode` (Combine|Replace) and `freeze_mode` to PhysicsBody2D. Rework the damp swap in PhysicsWorld2D::step to follow Godot's composition, using the AreaStore override walk that already stops on Replace (area2d.rs:514-620) to yield (total, stopped). Default SpaceParams2D damp to 0.1 to match the ProjectSettings default, updating set_space_params callers in main_loop.rs:2669 accordingly. Read the modes and center_of_mass_mode in the body property sync.

Wiring: .tscn props -> physics_server body sync -> world.step damping.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/world.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/body.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs`

**Prove it:** A project with no damp keys in project.godot is loaded through the runner. A RigidBody2D with gravity_scale=0 and an initial velocity of 100 decays at Godot's 0.1 default rate. Inside an Area2D with linear_damp=2 (COMBINE), a body with linear_damp=1 gets total damp 3+default. With linear_damp_mode=REPLACE it gets exactly 1. (test: `rigidbody2d_damp_composition_modes`)

**Verifier note:** The default-damp sub-claim is refuted. ProjectSettings::get (gdcore/src/project_settings.rs:205-209) falls back to godot_default_table, which seeds physics/2d/default_linear_damp=0.1 and default_angular_damp=1.0 (lines 620-621). from_godot_format seeds that table too (lines 464-475). patina-runner/src/main.rs:434 calls configure_from_project_settings, which uses float_setting -> settings.get (main_loop.rs:781, 2669-2673). So a runner-loaded project without the keys does get 0.1/1.0; the comment at main_loop.rs:2662 is stale, and only SpaceParams2D::default (world.rs:207) is 0. The rest is real. world.rs:516-525 makes an area override replace body.linear_damp instead of combining. grep -rnw 'linear_damp_mode|angular_damp_mode|center_of_mass_mode|freeze_mode' over gdscene/src and gdphysics2d/src, non-3D files, gave 0 hits. With the most visible part gone, the remaining damp-mode, COM-mode and freeze-mode gaps are uncommon, so P2. The bead's acceptance should drop the 'decays at 0.1 default' clause, and its approach should drop the 'default SpaceParams2D to 0.1' step.
acceptance_criteria: A project with no damp keys in project.godot is loaded through the runner. A RigidBody2D with gravity_scale=0 and an initial velocity of 100 decays at Godot's 0.1 default rate. Inside an Area2D with linear_damp=2 (COMBINE), a body with linear_damp=1 gets total damp 3+default. With linear_damp_mode=REPLACE it gets exactly 1. (test: `rigidbody2d_damp_composition_modes`)

title: Physics3D: Area3D multi-shape, Godot override ordering, wind on soft bodies, reverb bus
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/p3d-area] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** modules/godot_physics_3d/godot_body_3d.cpp:486-600 (highest priority first; REPLACE/COMBINE_REPLACE stop processing, REPLACE_COMBINE continues, then adds space default); godot_area_3d.cpp:160-207 wind_*; godot_soft_body_3d.cpp:952-1000 (wind force on soft-body faces); doc/classes/Area3D.xml reverb_bus_enabled/name/amount/uniformity

**Patina today:** crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:1920-1926 gives each Area3D ONLY the first direct child's shape, with no offset or rotation (area.position is the node origin). grep for wind_force, wind_source and wind_attenuation over gdscene/src and gdphysics3d/src returns nothing, and grep 'reverb_bus' over gdscene/src and gdaudio/src returns nothing (only audio_bus_override is honoured, at physics_server_3d.rs:2302-2334). gdphysics3d/src/world.rs:1507-1521 starts from the space gravity and applies areas lowest priority first, so REPLACE_COMBINE drops lower combining areas and COMBINE_REPLACE still adds the default gravity, both diverging from godot_body_3d.cpp.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: an Area3D overlaps through all of its CollisionShape3D children, each with its own transform. Gravity and damp resolution iterates overlapping areas highest priority first and stops on REPLACE/COMBINE_REPLACE (godot_body_3d.cpp:486-600). wind_force_magnitude, wind_source_path, wind_attenuation_factor and wind_direction push SoftBody3D faces (godot_soft_body_3d.cpp:952-1000). reverb_bus_* sends AudioStreamPlayer3D audio inside the area to a reverb bus at the given amount and uniformity. Patina: single first-child shape with no offset (physics_server_3d.rs:1920-1926), inverted ordering (world.rs:1507-1521), and no wind or reverb. Approach: reuse shapes_from_body_subtree for areas and add extra_shapes to gdphysics3d Area3D; port Godot's ordering loop; add wind fields read in sync_areas and apply face wind force in SoftBody3D::step given the overlapping areas; add reverb send routing in main_loop next to audio_bus_at (main_loop.rs:2856-2861).

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/area3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/world.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/softbody3d.rs`

**Prove it:** From a .tscn: an Area3D with two CollisionShape3D children 10 m apart emits body_entered for a RigidBody3D falling through the SECOND shape. Two overlapping areas (priority 2 REPLACE_COMBINE gravity (0,-1,0); priority 1 COMBINE (0,-2,0)) give a body gravity (0,-3-9.8,0), matching Godot. A SoftBody3D cloth inside an Area3D with wind_force_magnitude=10 displaces along the wind direction (test: `physics3d_area_shapes_ordering_wind`).

**Verifier note:** physics_server_3d.rs:1919-1925 takes the first child shape through find_map and uses the node's global origin, with no shape offset or rotation. grep 'wind_|reverb_bus' over gdscene/src, gdphysics3d/src and gdaudio/src finds only unrelated 'rewind' hits. gdphysics3d/src/world.rs:1508-1521 sorts areas by ascending priority, starts from self.gravity, and never stops early: ReplaceCombine assigns and CombineReplace adds, which diverges from Godot's highest-first stop loop. grep 'gravity_space_override' finds no other 3D resolver (physics_server.rs is the 2D side). P2 is reasonable.
acceptance_criteria: From a .tscn: an Area3D with two CollisionShape3D children 10 m apart emits body_entered for a RigidBody3D falling through the SECOND shape. Two overlapping areas (priority 2 REPLACE_COMBINE gravity (0,-1,0); priority 1 COMBINE (0,-2,0)) give a body gravity (0,-3-9.8,0), matching Godot. A SoftBody3D cloth inside an Area3D with wind_force_magnitude=10 displaces along the wind direction (test: `physics3d_area_shapes_ordering_wind`).

**Patina today:** PhysicsWorld3D::step (crates/gdphysics3d/src/world.rs:750-752) calls sb.step(dt, gravity) only. softbody3d.rs has no collision code (grep 'collid|collision' finds only the collision_layer field at :83), so cloth falls through every StaticBody3D. **Implement:** Godot ground truth: SoftBody3D particles collide with bodies matching collision_mask (the godot_soft_body_3d.cpp collision callbacks push nodes out of shapes), total_mass sets per-node mass, drag_coefficient applies aerodynamic drag, pinned points may follow a spatial_attachment_path node, and set_point_pinned/is_point_pinned work at runtime. Patina: world.rs:750 steps soft bodies with no collision; the bridge reads 4 params. Approach: after SoftBody3D::step, project each non-pinned particle out of every overlapping body shape in the world with gdphysics3d collision::test_collision_rot against a small sphere, honouring layer/mask, and zero the inward normal velocity. Read total_mass, drag_coefficient and collision_layer/mask in apply_soft_body_tuning. Have pinned points with an attachment path track that node's global position each tick. Add set_point_pinned/is_point_pinned dispatch in scripting.rs that edits `_pinned_points` and the live binding.

A script calling `set_point_pinned(0, true)` mid-simulation freezes vertex 0 from then on (test: `physics3d_softbody_collision_and_pins`).

title: Physics3D: dispatch SpringArm3D excluded-object methods from scripts
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/p3d-springarm] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** scene/3d/spring_arm_3d.cpp add_excluded_object(RID), remove_excluded_object, clear_excluded_objects; doc/classes/SpringArm3D.xml

**Patina today:** The implementations exist at crates/gdscene/src/springarm3d.rs:95-113, writing `_exclusions`, which springarm3d.rs:115-129 reads during the cast. grep 'add_excluded_object|remove_excluded_object|clear_excluded_objects' over gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src finds no caller outside springarm3d.rs. The script add_exception arm (scripting.rs:3956-3985) handles only RayCast3D/ShapeCast3D. The standard third-person idiom `$SpringArm3D.add_excluded_object(get_rid())` is a silent no-op, so the arm collides with its own player and the camera sits inside the character.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: SpringArm3D.add_excluded_object(rid), remove_excluded_object(rid) -> bool and clear_excluded_objects() edit the set of bodies the arm's cast ignores (spring_arm_3d.cpp). The common use is excluding the owning CharacterBody3D via get_rid(). Patina: springarm3d.rs:95-113 implements all three and the cast honours `_exclusions`, but no script dispatch reaches them. Approach: add arms in scripting.rs (beside add_exception at :3956) gated on class SpringArm3D, accepting Variant::Rid (map RID to node through the CollisionObject3D get_rid scheme) or ObjectId, and calling springarm3d::add/remove/clear. remove_excluded_object returns whether the item was present.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/springarm3d.rs`

**Prove it:** From a .tscn: a SpringArm3D child of a CharacterBody3D, spring_length 5 and pointing back, reports get_hit_length() < 1 when not excluding (its cast hits the parent's capsule), and get_hit_length() == 5 after its script calls `add_excluded_object(get_parent().get_rid())`, advanced via MainLoop (test: `physics3d_springarm_excluded_objects`).

**Verifier note:** `grep -rln excluded_object engine-rs/crates` matches only gdscene/src/springarm3d.rs (:95, :104, :111). There is no dispatch in scripting.rs, gdscript-interop or class_db.rs. The add_exception arm at scripting.rs:3956-3988 matches only RayCast3D and ShapeCast3D and otherwise falls through to Nil. springarm3d::process does run at runtime (main_loop.rs:2518), so the exclusion state exists but scripts cannot reach it. UNWIRED/P2 is accurate; it could arguably be P1, since excluding the player is the standard third-person idiom.
acceptance_criteria: From a .tscn: a SpringArm3D child of a CharacterBody3D, spring_length 5 and pointing back, reports get_hit_length() < 1 when not excluding (its cast hits the parent's capsule), and get_hit_length() == 5 after its script calls `add_excluded_object(get_parent().get_rid())`, advanced via MainLoop (test: `physics3d_springarm_excluded_objects`).

title: Render3D Play: draw nothing for non-visual Node3D classes (drop Box markers from game frames)
description:

**Wiring requirement:** examples/editor.rs:274 game_3d_render_inputs -> strip_editor_only_items

**Godot ground truth:** scene/3d/node_3d.cpp: a plain Node3D has no visual instance; only VisualInstance3D subclasses draw

**Patina today:** primitive_for_class (viewport_3d_render.rs:600-607) maps every non-mesh, non-camera, non-light Node3D to PrimitiveShape::Box. populate_editor_scene_3d draws it as Mesh3D::cube(0.4) (viewport_3d_render.rs:2264-2272). is_editor_only_marker (viewport_3d_render.rs:2620-2627) strips only Camera, Light and Collision, and its doc comment says the generic Node3D box markers are kept in Play. Patina's Play frame keeps PrimitiveShape::Box markers (viewport_3d_render.rs:2620) for every non-mesh Node3D, so a running game shows grey cubes at pivots, bodies, markers and decals. comments.author: EmeraldCreek
comments.text:
EmeraldCreek — handing this back after two failed verifies. Working tree is REVERTED to HEAD for this bead (the peer's pat-mgixk.32 hunk in the same file is untouched). Read this before re-attempting; both obvious routes are already burned.

**THE BEAD BODY CONTRADICTS A GREEN TEST. This is the owner decision.**

The Implement line says: "... and skip it for a MeshInstance3D with no mesh."
But `crates/gdeditor/tests/play_uses_scene_camera3d.rs` builds its scene content as `Node::new("Box", "MeshInstance3D")` with NO mesh property, and asserts it IS drawn in game mode, twice:
- `:177` "game mode drops editor furniture, not scene content — the mesh node stays"
- `:201` "by default the mesh is on a layer the camera renders" (the control for the cull_mask test)

Both are green at HEAD (0 entries in docs/test-debt/2026-10-30-failing-tests-at-HEAD.txt). So the bead asks for behaviour an existing green test forbids. Someone has to choose: either the bead's "skip a mesh-less MeshInstance3D" is wrong, or that fixture must be rewritten to carry a real `mesh = "primitive:BoxMesh"` (which is what `render3d_hidden_parent_top_level.rs` does, and would make the fixture honest either way).

**ATTEMPT 1 — strip by SHAPE. Failed, caused a regression.**
Added `PrimitiveShape::Box` to `is_editor_only_marker`. This is what the bead asks for literally. It deletes the mesh-less MeshInstance3D from every game frame, so `play_uses_scene_camera3d::cull_mask_excludes_nodes_off_the_cameras_layers` went red (verifier.log:12601, exit 100). Note the doc comment I removed was WARNING about this: "box markers are kept: those stand in for scene content". It was right.

Mechanism worth keeping: `PrimitiveShape::Box` encodes TWO unrelated causes — (a) a pivot with no geometry of its own, (b) a `GeometryInstance3D` whose geometry failed to resolve. Any predicate over the shape conflates them.

**ATTEMPT 2 — split the two causes. Satisfied the green test, but my own acceptance went red.**
Added `PrimitiveShape::Marker`, chosen at classification time from the CLASS, and stripped only that. Research that is still valid and worth reusing:
- The split is Godot's own line: everything with drawable geometry descends from `GeometryInstance3D` (MeshInstance3D, MultiMeshInstance3D, CSGShape3D, SpriteBase3D, Label3D, the particle nodes); the other `VisualInstance3D` subclasses are effects/probes (Decal, FogVolume, ReflectionProbe, VoxelGI, LightmapGI, OccluderInstance3D).
- Predicate: `is_parent_class(c, "Node3D") && !is_parent_class(c, "GeometryInstance3D")`. Spell it as a POSITIVE ClassDB answer, never a bare `!is_parent_class`: with an unpopulated ClassDB both queries are false, so an unknown class keeps the old VISIBLE behaviour. The inverse spelling blanks every game frame the moment the DB is empty. `is_parent_class` IS reflexive (pinned by class_db.rs:33622 `is_parent_class_self`), so a bare `Node3D` matches itself.
- 14 classes in the gdeditor test corpus flip. I swept all ten consumers of `game_3d_render_inputs`/`render_game_3d_frame`/`strip_editor_only_items`: the five using a pivot-only class all assert on fields the strip does not reach (`env_effects`, `scene_lights`, `root_motion_grid`), on a dynamically-captured background, or on blue-pixel counts (markers are orange). GridMap flips but INERTLY — `gridmap_items` overwrites the base item's `Primitive` kind per cell via `..base.clone()`, and returns an empty vec if the mesh library fails.
- Three exhaustive `match`es on `PrimitiveShape` need a new arm (colour at ~2309, overlay gizmo at ~2556, and the in-crate test `viewport_3d_render::tests::editor3d_renders_node3d_content` which pins the old classification).

**WHY ATTEMPT 2 FAILED, and what I could not determine.** verifier.log:12653, exit 100, on my own `editor_suite_d -E 'test(/^play3d_no_marker_cubes_test::/)'`. The log's output tail is TRUNCATED from the front — only the end of a `Vec<Color>` dump survives, so the panicking assertion is not identifiable from the log. A `Vec<Color>` dump means it is one of the two frame comparisons (game frames equal / editor frames differ), not one of the render-list assertions, which carry string messages. The surviving colours (r≈0.2434, g≈0.2024, b≈0.1565, varying only in the 7th decimal) look like a smooth sky gradient rather than a shaded cube. I could not diagnose further without a build, which workers are not permitted to run.

**ARTEFACT LEFT ON DISK, deliberately untracked and NOT registered** (so it cannot break a peer's build): `crates/gdeditor/tests/editor_suite_d/play3d_no_marker_cubes_test.rs`. It loads a real `.tscn` via `PackedScene::from_tscn` + `add_packed_scene_to_tree` (this bead has a Wiring requirement — a Rust-built tree is rejected before it is built; that was the FIRST reopen). To use it, re-add `mod play3d_no_marker_cubes_test;` to `tests/editor_suite_d/main.rs`. Two traps baked into it: the fixture MUST call `register_3d_classes()` or the render list is empty and every assertion passes vacuously; and do NOT assert a marker COUNT — the scene ROOT is a `Node3D` too, so the editor list holds five, not the four authored.

**FILTER WARNING for whoever reports this:** `editor_suite_d` has two tests already red at HEAD (`editor_script_view_test::editor_script_mode_serves_script_editor_view`, `editor_smoke_test::editor_app_smoke_all_modes`), so it must never be run whole. Keep `--test editor_suite_d` AND an anchored `-E`; `-E` without `--test` silently degrades to a compile-only check and reads as a false green.

BlackWaterfall — follow-up on my own report. I filed this complete saying the verify would be its first real execution of the current test+impl pair and that a failure would "finally be diagnosable". **It failed (verifier.log:13988-13989, exit 100 panic) and it is NOT diagnosable. I was wrong about that, and here is why, because it is the thing to fix first.**

WHAT THE RUN PROVED (positive, and it is not nothing):

- `1 test run: 0 passed, 1 failed, 49 skipped` — the anchored filter worked, suite_d's two known-red tests were skipped.

WHY IT IS STILL UNDIAGNOSABLE, AND THE FIX:
The captured output tail is truncated FROM THE FRONT, so all that survives is the end of a `Vec<Color>` dump (`r: 0.2433896, g: 0.20244378, b: 0.15651318 ...`). `grep -E "assertion|left|right|panicked|\.rs:[0-9]+"` over the whole captured window returns NOTHING, and there is no fuller per-bead output on disk. An `assert_eq!`/`assert_ne!` custom message prints on the FIRST line, before the left/right dumps — so the message and the file:line scrolled out.

🔑 ROOT CAUSE: the two frame assertions compare whole `Vec<Color>`s of 96x72 = 6912 entries each. Two of those dumps is ~13800 lines of Debug output, which pushes the assertion message out of the captured tail EVERY time. That is why attempt 2 was undiagnosable too — and note the surviving colours this run (r≈0.24339, g≈0.20244, b≈0.15651) are the SAME ones EmeraldCreek recorded for attempt 2 under a completely different implementation. The log has told us the same uninformative thing three times.

CONCRETE FIX, and I would do it first before touching any engine code: make the two frame assertions summarise instead of dump. Something like
  let diff: Vec<usize> = a.iter().zip(&b).enumerate().filter(|(_, (x, y))| x != y).map(|(i, _)| i).collect();
  assert!(diff.is_empty(), "{} of {} pixels differ; first at {} ({},{}): {:?} vs {:?}", diff.len(), a.len(), diff[0], diff[0] % W as usize, diff[0] / W as usize, a[diff[0]], b[diff[0]]);
and the mirror (`assert!(!diff.is_empty(), ...)`) for the editor-frames-differ clause. That turns the next run into a one-line diagnosis: how many pixels, where, and the two colours. It is a test-only change, so it cannot affect the red check.

WHAT I DELIBERATELY AM NOT DOING: naming a cause. I will not say which assertion failed from a front-truncated tail — I did exactly that earlier today on a different crate's breaker, sent an URGENT wrong diagnosis to three agents, and had to retract it. title: Expression: honor base_instance, const_calls_only and an isolated scope in execute()
description:
[audit-key: platform-os/platform-os-expression] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** core/math/expression.cpp execute(inputs, base_instance, show_error, const_calls_only); doc/classes/Expression.xml

**Patina today:** call_expression_instance (interpreter.rs, grep 'fn call_expression_instance'): execute reads only args.first() as inputs, then self.environment.push_scope() and defines input names on top of the CURRENT environment before eval_expr, so base_instance (args[1]), show_error (args[2]) and const_calls_only (args[3]) are ignored and the expression can read the calling function's local variables, which Godot's Expression cannot.

**Implement:** Godot's Expression.execute(inputs, base_instance=null, show_error=true, const_calls_only=false) resolves bare method calls/properties against base_instance, sees only the declared inputs plus globals/builtins, and with const_calls_only rejects non-const calls (expression.cpp). Patina evaluates the parsed AST in the caller's environment with a pushed scope, ignores base_instance and const_calls_only, and leaks caller locals. Fix: in call_expression_instance's execute arm, evaluate with a fresh Environment containing only the inputs (do not inherit locals), temporarily bind the base_instance (if an ObjectId/node) as the self target for unqualified calls/identifiers, enforce const_calls_only by rejecting method calls not flagged const in ClassDB, and set has_execute_failed/get_error_text on violations.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** From a node script: `var secret = 5; e.parse("secret")` -> execute() fails (has_execute_failed true); `e.parse("get_name()")` executed with base_instance=$Child returns 'Child'; `e.parse("x * 2", ["x"])` executed with [21] returns 42; const_calls_only=true rejects a non-const call (test: `expression_execute_uses_base_instance_scope`).

**Verifier note:** interpreter.rs:3443-3471: execute reads only args.first() as inputs, then calls self.environment.push_scope(), defines the input names, runs eval_expr and pops the scope. args[1..3] (base_instance, show_error, const_calls_only) are never read, and a pushed scope keeps the caller's locals in the lookup chain. PARTIAL at P2 is right (base_instance is used often with Expression for console and command patterns).
acceptance_criteria: From a node script: `var secret = 5; e.parse("secret")` -> execute() fails (has_execute_failed true); `e.parse("get_name()")` executed with base_instance=$Child returns 'Child'; `e.parse("x * 2", ["x"])` executed with [21] returns 42; const_calls_only=true rejects a non-const call (test: `expression_execute_uses_base_instance_scope`).

Seeded values give typeof() results unlike Godot's, and integer-vs-float math (size/2) differs for unset properties.

**Implement:** Godot types each property (PropertyInfo Variant::Type), and an unset property returns its default in that type. Patina registers the 33 properties listed in evidence with the wrong Variant variant. Change each to the matching variant: Variant::StringName(StringName::new(..)), Variant::Vector2i, Variant::NodePath, Variant::PackedStringArray, Variant::PackedVector2Array. Then check that consumers that match on the old variant (e.g. bus lookup in audio, AnimatedSprite2D animation lookup, SubViewport size readers in sub_viewport.rs/viewport.rs, multiplayer root_path resolution in multiplayer.rs) accept the new one, or both. title: VisualShader: correct node property defaults and apply them when a .tres omits them
description:
[audit-key: property-defaults-and-default-theme/classdb-defaults-visual-shader] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tres VisualShader load -> visual_shader_load node mapping -> GDShader code generation -> material compile

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/VisualShaderNodeVectorBase.xml op_type=1 (OP_TYPE_VECTOR_3D); VisualShaderNodeFloatFunc.xml function=13; VisualShaderNodeIntFunc.xml function=2; VisualShaderNodeParticleEmit.xml flags=31; VisualShaderNodeParticleMeshEmitter.xml use_all_surfaces=true; VisualShaderNodeParticleMultiplyByAxisAngle.xml degrees_mode=true; VisualShaderNodeParameterRef.xml parameter_name="[None]"

**Patina today:** class_db.rs:9886 VectorBase op_type 0 (inherited by VectorOp/VectorFunc/VectorCompose/... via :9866), :10001 FloatFunc function 0, :10141 IntFunc function 0, :9662 ParticleEmit flags 0, :9690 use_all_surfaces false, :9702 degrees_mode false, :11056 parameter_name empty. The .tres loader (gdscene/src/visual_shader_load.rs:104-118) reads properties straight from the sub-resource, so these ClassDB defaults reach: script-created nodes (VisualShaderNodeVectorOp.new() gets op_type 0 = 2D, not 3D), ClassDB.class_get_property_default_value, and the editor inspector/visual-shader editor for these classes.

**Implement:** Godot saves VisualShader sub-resources without default-valued properties, so a VectorOp with op_type 3D has NO op_type line, and FloatFunc with FUNC_SIGN... (13) has no function line. Fix the ClassDB defaults listed in evidence. In visual_shader_load.rs, when node_properties() finds a property missing, fall back to class_db::property_get_revert(sub.class_name, name) instead of dropping it, so absent values resolve to Godot's defaults. Wiring: .tres VisualShader load -> visual_shader_load node mapping -> GDShader code generation -> material compile.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/visual_shader_load.rs`

**Prove it:** A VisualShader .tres saved by Godot 4.6.1 containing a VisualShaderNodeVectorOp with no op_type line generates vec3 code, not vec2. A VisualShaderNodeFloatFunc with no function line emits Godot's function-13 expression. VisualShaderNodeVectorOp.new().op_type == 1 from GDScript. (test: `visual_shader_node_defaults_test`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. class_db.rs:9886 op_type Int(0), :10001 FloatFunc function Int(0), :10141 IntFunc function Int(0), :9662 ParticleEmit flags Int(0), :9690 use_all_surfaces false, :9702 degrees_mode false, :11056 parameter_name String::new(). Upstream doc XML says 1, 13, 2, 31, true, true, "[None]". The loader story is weaker than the finder says. visual_shader_load.rs:106-112 node_properties reads properties for only 4 kinds (ColorFunc, Billboard, BooleanParameter, GlobalExpression), and VectorOp is mapped only through `operator` (:76-82). So op_type is never read from a .tres at all, and the bead's '.tres VectorOp generates vec3' acceptance also needs op_type consumption added, not just a fallback. The ClassDB-default gap is real, and P2 fits.
acceptance_criteria: A VisualShader .tres saved by Godot 4.6.1 containing a VisualShaderNodeVectorOp with no op_type line generates vec3 code, not vec2. A VisualShaderNodeFloatFunc with no function line emits Godot's function-13 expression. VisualShaderNodeVectorOp.new().op_type == 1 from GDScript. (test: `visual_shader_node_defaults_test`)

title: CanvasItem: implement clip_children as an alpha mask from the parent's drawn pixels
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/r2d-clip-children] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** Play frame -> grouped raster -> pixels

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/CanvasItem.xml clip_children (CLIP_CHILDREN_ONLY/AND_DRAW use the parent's drawn alpha as the mask); renderer_canvas_cull.cpp canvas_group/clip

**Patina today:** clip_rect_for (crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:1145-1160) uses the nearest clip_children ancestor's `size` property as an axis-aligned Rect2 at its global position, and returns None for a parent without `size` (e.g. Sprite2D, Polygon2D), meaning no clipping. Rotation and scale of the mask are ignored, and child pixels are not multiplied by the mask's alpha.

**Implement:** Godot: a CanvasItem with clip_children != DISABLED renders its subtree into a buffer and multiplies it by the parent's own drawn alpha (its texture or polygon shape, at its full transform). CLIP_CHILDREN_ONLY hides the parent itself, and AND_DRAW also draws it.
Patina: a rect derived from `size` only (viewport_2d_render.rs:1145).
Implementation: in rasterize_render_list_with_groups, treat a clip_children node like a CanvasGroup. Rasterize the mask node's own items into a scratch alpha buffer, rasterize its descendants into a second scratch buffer, multiply by the mask alpha, and composite. Reuse composite_group_buffer (:4005). Drop clip_rect for these items.
Wiring: Play frame -> grouped raster -> pixels.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`

**Prove it:** A Sprite2D using a circular-alpha texture (clip_children=CLIP_CHILDREN_ONLY), rotated 45deg, with a red ColorRect child larger than the sprite. In the Play-frame render, pixels inside the circle are red, pixels inside the rect but outside the circle keep the clear color, and the sprite's own texels are not drawn. With AND_DRAW, the sprite texels appear under the red. (test: `clip_children_alpha_mask`)

**Verifier note:** clip_rect_for (viewport_2d_render.rs:1145-1159) reads the ancestor's `size`, returns None when there is no size, and builds Rect2::new(global_position, size) with no rotation or scale. The only consumer is the rect snapshot and restore at :2946 and :3411, and there is no alpha multiply. canvas_order::clip_children_mode (:168) only reads the int. PARTIAL and priority 2 are correct.
acceptance_criteria: A Sprite2D using a circular-alpha texture (clip_children=CLIP_CHILDREN_ONLY), rotated 45deg, with a red ColorRect child larger than the sprite. In the Play-frame render, pixels inside the circle are red, pixels inside the rect but outside the circle keep the clear color, and the sprite's own texels are not drawn. With AND_DRAW, the sprite texels appear under the red. (test: `clip_children_alpha_mask`)

title: Sprite3D render: let AnimatedSprite3D through the sprite quad path (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: nodes-3d/sprite3d-label3d] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** MainLoop -> process animated sprites -> node `texture` -> build_render_list -> billboard_geometry; Play -> build_render_list -> billboard_geometry

### 1. AnimatedSprite3D never renders (class guard rejects it although the dispatcher routes it)  (UNWIRED, P0)

**Godot ground truth:** scene/3d/sprite_3d.cpp AnimatedSprite3D::_draw

**Patina today:** billboard_geometry routes "Sprite3D" | "AnimatedSprite3D" to sprite3d_geometry (sprite3d_render.rs:333), but sprite3d_geometry returns None unless class_name() == "Sprite3D" (sprite3d_render.rs:155). scene_tree.rs:4433-4500 does publish the current frame's `texture` for AnimatedSprite3D, so the texture exists but is discarded, and the node falls through to a box marker.

**Implement:** Godot draws the current SpriteFrames frame of an AnimatedSprite3D as a quad. Patina: sprite3d_render.rs:155 guards on class_name()=="Sprite3D", so the AnimatedSprite3D arm at :333 always yields None. Implementation: accept both class names in the guard. Make sure the texture published by SceneTree's animated-sprite tick (scene_tree.rs:4433) is a resolvable path string or resource that MaterialTextureCache::get_or_load understands, and handle a Variant::Resource texture. Wiring: MainLoop -> process animated sprites -> node `texture` -> build_render_list -> billboard_geometry.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/sprite3d_render.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn with an AnimatedSprite3D, a SpriteFrames of two coloured PNG frames and autoplay, run through MainLoop: render_game_3d_frame shows frame-0 colour pixels, and after advancing past the frame duration shows frame-1 colour. (test: `animated_sprite3d_renders_frames`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. billboard_geometry routes "Sprite3D" | "AnimatedSprite3D" to sprite3d_geometry (sprite3d_render.rs:333), and sprite3d_geometry returns None unless class_name() == "Sprite3D" (sprite3d_render.rs:155-157). The doc comment at :325 claims that playback reaches the viewport, which is false-done, so P0 is justified.

### 2. Sprite3D/Label3D wired render ignores billboard modes, region/hframes/vframes/frame, alpha cut/transparency/no_depth_test/fixed_size/double_sided, and Label3D outline/alignment/width/autowrap  (PARTIAL, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** scene/3d/sprite_3d.cpp (SpriteBase3D::draw_texture_rect, billboard_mode, region, frame_coords, alpha_cut), scene/3d/label_3d.cpp (outline_size/outline_modulate, horizontal_alignment, width, autowrap_mode, line_spacing, uppercase)

**Patina today:** The string-literal property reads in sprite3d_render.rs are only pixel_size, modulate, texture, text, shaded, offset, font_size, flip_h, flip_v, centered and axis. Grep for 'billboard|region_rect|hframes|outline_size|alpha_cut|fixed_size|no_depth_test' in sprite3d_render.rs found nothing. Label3D is always centered, with no outline, alignment or wrap (sprite3d_render.rs:274-318), and double_sided is forced true for Sprite3D (sprite3d_render.rs:198). Billboarding exists only in the unwired RenderServer3DAdapter (render_server_3d.rs:915 sync_sprite3d(camera_pos)) and gdserver3d/src/sprite3d.rs / label3d.rs.

**Implement:** Godot: SpriteBase3D supports billboard_mode (disabled/enabled/Y-billboard), region_enabled/region_rect, hframes/vframes/frame, alpha_cut, transparent, no_depth_test, fixed_size and double_sided. Label3D adds outline_size/outline_modulate, horizontal/vertical_alignment, width plus autowrap_mode, line_spacing and uppercase. Patina reads none of these on the wired path (sprite3d_render.rs). Implementation: pass the viewport camera transform into billboard_geometry (build_render_list has the Viewport3D) and orient the quad per billboard_mode, reusing gdserver3d sprite3d.rs/label3d.rs billboarding. Crop UVs for region and for frame_coords. Map alpha_cut and transparent onto Material3D transparency/alpha-scissor and no_depth_test onto its depth flag. Rasterize the Label3D outline as a dilated pass under the glyphs, and lay out lines with alignment and wrap at `width`. Wiring: Play -> build_render_list -> billboard_geometry.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/sprite3d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs`

**Prove it:** With the camera rotated 90 degrees about Y, a Sprite3D with billboard=1 still covers the same pixel area facing the camera, while billboard=0 is edge-on and draws about 0 pixels. A Sprite3D with hframes=2 frame=1 shows only the right half of the texture. A Label3D with outline_size=8 has outline-colour pixels around the glyphs. (test: `sprite3d_label3d_billboard_region_outline`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. grep 'billboard|region|hframes|outline|alpha_cut|fixed_size|no_depth_test|double_sided' in sprite3d_render.rs matched only the hardcoded double_sided: true (:200, :314) and the doc-comment use of the word 'billboard' (:320). No property reads exist for these. P1 status PARTIAL is right.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A .tscn with an AnimatedSprite3D, a SpriteFrames of two coloured PNG frames and autoplay, run through MainLoop: render_game_3d_frame shows frame-0 colour pixels, and after advancing past the frame duration shows frame-1 colour. (test: `animated_sprite3d_renders_frames`) 2) With the camera rotated 90 degrees about Y, a Sprite3D with billboard=1 still covers the same pixel area facing the camera, while billboard=0 is edge-on and draws about 0 pixels. A Sprite3D with hframes=2 frame=1 shows only the right half of the texture. A Label3D with outline_size=8 has outline-colour pixels around the glyphs. (test: `sprite3d_label3d_billboard_region_outline`)

title: Make AtlasTexture a real Texture2D (ClassDB + script + any texture slot); add AnimatedTexture
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/texture-subclasses-atlas-animated] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/doc/classes/AtlasTexture.xml, AnimatedTexture.xml (deprecated in 4.6.1, AnimatedTexture.xml:2)

Register AtlasTexture (parent Texture2D: atlas, region, margin, filter_clip, get_width/get_height from region) and make it a texture value usable in any Texture2D slot and from script (AtlasTexture.new(), set atlas/region at runtime updates the draw). title: Materials3D: implement rim/clearcoat/AO/heightmap/triplanar/billboard/fade/render_priority/next_pass (stage 1 of 2)
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/render3d-materials-advanced] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** tscn sub-resource to both render paths

title: ProjectSettings: apply feature-tag overrides on every engine-side setting read
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/project-settings-overrides] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** patina-runner/patina-web boot -> viewport size and main scene

**Godot ground truth:** core/config/project_settings.cpp:319-334 (feature_overrides built in _set), :410-430 get_setting_with_override; project_settings.h:264 `#define GLOBAL_GET(m) ...get_setting_with_override(m)`

**Patina today:** gdcore/src/project_settings.rs:250 implements get_setting_with_override_and_custom_features, but no non-test code calls it (grep outside project_settings.rs and tests: 0 hits). The typed accessors the runtime uses read the base key with self.get: main_scene (308), physics_ticks_per_second (316), viewport_width/height (324/332), and project_name and stretch config likewise. So `display/window/size/viewport_width.web=...` or `application/run/main_scene.web=...` is ignored by the runner. Only the script-facing ProjectSettings.get_setting_with_override applies overrides (interpreter.rs:20795).

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: engine code reads settings through GLOBAL_GET, which is get_setting_with_override (project_settings.h:264). Any `name.<feature>` key overrides `name` when OS.has_feature(feature) holds, including web, mobile, pc, debug/release, platform names and custom export tags. Web exports rely on `.web` overrides for window size, renderer and main scene.

Patina today: the override resolver exists (project_settings.rs:250) but nothing calls it. main_scene, physics ticks, viewport size and stretch all read base keys (project_settings.rs:300-340), and ProjectLoader's config().main_scene (gdresource/src/project.rs:303) does the same.

Approach: add ProjectSettings::get_with_override(path) using the active OS feature set (gdplatform::os has_feature/custom features, which project_boot already populates). Route all typed accessors and ProjectLoader::config through it. Call it after features are installed in boot_from_project_text (project_boot.rs ~415) so the web feature set wins in patina-web.

Wiring: patina-runner/patina-web boot -> viewport size and main scene.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/project_settings.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/project.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs`

**Prove it:** A fixture project.godot sets viewport_width=1152 and viewport_width.web=640, plus main_scene=res://a.tscn and main_scene.web=res://b.tscn. Booting with the web feature active (the custom feature tag `web` installed as patina-web does) instances b.tscn with a 640-wide root viewport. Booting without it yields a.tscn at 1152 (test: `project_settings_feature_override_boot`).

**Verifier note:** The finding is real. The only non-test callers of get_setting_with_override_and_custom_features are in project_settings.rs's own tests (:864-888). project_boot.rs:450 sends active_feature_tags() only to the script-side set_project_feature_tags. The runtime reads base keys only: main_scene comes from gdresource/src/project.rs:303 via project_boot.rs:487, viewport_width from project_settings.rs:324 via project_boot.rs:465 and bootstrap.rs:437/466. patina-web/src has no main_scene/viewport_width/with_override reads. Priority lowered to 2: `.feature` overrides in project.godot are an uncommon project pattern, not a common one, and the base keys still work.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture project.godot sets viewport_width=1152 and viewport_width.web=640, plus main_scene=res://a.tscn and main_scene.web=res://b.tscn. Booting with the web feature active (the custom feature tag `web` installed as patina-web does) instances b.tscn with a 640-wide root viewport. Booting without it yields a.tscn at 1152 (test: `project_settings_feature_override_boot`).

Wire radiance_hdr into load_color_texture_linear and add an EXR decoder (the `exr` crate). Add BasisU transcoding through a pure-Rust transcoder, or record a scope citation if none is viable. Expose the decoders/encoders through the Image script binding (image-texture-scripting bead).

Image.new().load_jpg_from_buffer(FileAccess.get_file_as_bytes("res://photo.jpg")) returns OK with the correct size. A PanoramaSkyMaterial with an .hdr panorama loads without error (test: `jpeg_exr_codec_scene_load`).

It is a dead file that never compiles. gdeditor/src/texture_cache.rs:118 also says .jpg is not supported. gdresource/Cargo.toml:20 enables only webp and png. importers.rs:407-412 rejects exr/hdr, ctex.rs:421-423 returns Unsupported for BasisU, and `grep 'load_jpg_from_buffer|load_png_from_buffer|save_png|save_jpg|save_webp|save_exr'` over gdscript-interop/src and gdobject/src: 0.
