title: FileAccess/ConfigFile/PCK: implement FileAccessEncrypted (AES-256-CFB + MD5 header)
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/io-encryption] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** script save-game encryption in a booted project, and booting an encrypted pck

**Godot ground truth:** core/io/file_access_encrypted.cpp; core/io/file_access_pack.cpp (PACK_DIR_ENCRYPTED / PACK_FILE_ENCRYPTED); core/io/config_file.cpp load_encrypted/save_encrypted

**Patina today:** gdresource/src/pck.rs:225-231 rejects PACK_DIR_ENCRYPTED with 'encrypted PCK directory is not supported', and the header comment at pck.rs:42 says no decryption is performed. In gdscript-interop/src, `grep "open_encrypted"|"open_encrypted_with_pass"` returns 0 hits. The jq diff of ConfigFile methods reports load_encrypted and save_encrypted absent (load_encrypted_pass/save_encrypted_pass not verified individually).

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: FileAccessEncrypted writes the magic 'GDEC', then mode, a 16-byte MD5 of the plaintext, a u64 length, a 16-byte IV, and the AES-256-CFB ciphertext padded to 16 bytes. open_encrypted_with_pass derives the key as the MD5 hex of the password, used as 32 bytes. ConfigFile.save/load_encrypted(_pass) wrap it. Encrypted PCKs use the same wrapper for the directory and per-file data, keyed by the script encryption key.

Patina today: encrypted packs are rejected (pck.rs:225-231). There is no open_encrypted and no ConfigFile encrypted variants.

Approach: add a gdcore::file_access encrypted reader/writer with pure-Rust aes and cfb-mode (wasm-safe). Bind FileAccess.open_encrypted and open_encrypted_with_pass, ConfigFile.load_encrypted/_pass and save_encrypted/_pass. Let PckMount accept an optional 32-byte key (runner CLI flag and patina-web option) and decrypt the directory and flagged files.

Wiring: script save-game encryption in a booted project, and booting an encrypted pck.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/file_access.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/pck.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/config_file.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A booted project script saves a ConfigFile with save_encrypted_pass("user://s.cfg", "pw") and reloads it with load_encrypted_pass, getting identical values. The file on disk starts with 'GDEC' and does not contain the plaintext. A Godot-4.6-produced encrypted file fixture decrypts correctly. A PCK fixture with PACK_DIR_ENCRYPTED boots when given the key (test: `encrypted_fileaccess_configfile_pck`).

**Verifier note:** The finding is partly refuted. ConfigFile.save_encrypted_pass and load_encrypted_pass do exist and are wired to script: gdresource/src/config_file.rs:122 and :144, script dispatch in gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:30718 and :30735. However, they use a format of their own, not Godot's: AES-256-CBC with PKCS7, a SHA-256 password key, an IV derived from the key, and no GDEC/MD5 header (config_file.rs:107-160 says so itself: 'not byte-identical to Godot's FileAccessEncrypted layout'). So files written by Godot cannot be read and the reverse also fails, and the bead's claim of 'no ConfigFile encrypted variants' is wrong. The bead should replace this format with FileAccessEncrypted rather than add it. The rest is confirmed: save_encrypted/load_encrypted are deliberately absent (interpreter.rs:30714), `grep open_encrypted`: 0 hits, and pck.rs:228-232 rejects PACK_DIR_ENCRYPTED.
acceptance_criteria: A booted project script saves a ConfigFile with save_encrypted_pass("user://s.cfg", "pw") and reloads it with load_encrypted_pass, getting identical values. The file on disk starts with 'GDEC' and does not contain the plaintext. A Godot-4.6-produced encrypted file fixture decrypts correctly. A PCK fixture with PACK_DIR_ENCRYPTED boots when given the key (test: `encrypted_fileaccess_configfile_pck`).

Patina: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/video_stream.rs decodes only a PATVID01 fixture; the class is unregistered. Approach: register VideoStreamTheora (parent VideoStream) in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs; add an .ogv resource loader; implement Ogg demux + Theora decode (pure-Rust port from upstream/godot/thirdparty/libtheora, or a vetted crate per THIRDPARTY_STRATEGY) producing the Vec<Image> + fps that video_stream.rs already consumes; Vorbis audio track to the existing audio stream path as a stage 2. Wiring: VideoStreamPlayer with stream = load("res://clip.ogv") renders decoded frames.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/video_stream.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene with VideoStreamPlayer(autoplay, stream=res://clip.ogv, a small checked-in Theora fixture) yields get_video_texture() frames whose pixels match reference frames decoded by Godot within tolerance at t=0 and t=0.5s, and load("res://clip.ogv").get_class() == "VideoStreamTheora" (test: `video_stream_theora_plays_ogv`).
acceptance_criteria: A scene with VideoStreamPlayer(autoplay, stream=res://clip.ogv, a small checked-in Theora fixture) yields get_video_texture() frames whose pixels match reference frames decoded by Godot within tolerance at t=0 and t=0.5s, and load("res://clip.ogv").get_class() == "VideoStreamTheora" (test: `video_stream_theora_plays_ogv`).

title: Camera3D: dispatch projection/unprojection and set_perspective/orthogonal/frustum to camera3d.rs
description:
[audit-key: nodes-3d/camera3d-script-api] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** GDScript `$Camera3D.unproject_position(p)` -> scripting.rs:2639 -> camera3d

**Godot ground truth:** scene/3d/camera_3d.cpp; doc/classes/Camera3D.xml

**Patina today:** The Rust implementations exist: camera3d.rs:816 is_position_in_frustum, :835 unproject_position, :870 project_position, :905 project_ray_origin, :936 project_ray_normal, :800 get_camera_frustum. call_camera3d_method (camera3d.rs:1024-1074) handles only make_current, clear_current and get/set_cull_mask_value. Grep for '"unproject_position"|"project_ray_origin"|"project_ray_normal"|"is_position_behind"|"set_perspective"|"get_camera_transform"|"is_position_in_frustum"|"project_position"' over gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src returned nothing. ClassDB registers the names (class_db.rs:33869-33880), so calls return Nil silently. The only runtime caller is mouse-picking at main_loop.rs:3308.

**Implement:** Godot games pick with project_ray_origin/normal and place HUD markers with unproject_position (camera_3d.cpp). Patina has the math (camera3d.rs:800-975) but call_camera3d_method (camera3d.rs:1024) has no arms for it. Implementation: add arms for unproject_position, project_position(screen, z_depth), project_ray_origin, project_ray_normal, project_local_ray_normal, is_position_behind, is_position_in_frustum, get_frustum (Array of Plane), get_camera_transform (global transform with h/v offset), get_camera_projection, and set_perspective/set_orthogonal/set_frustum (write fov|size, near, far, projection). Use tree.root_window().visible_size() for the viewport size, as visibility_3d.rs:101 does. Wiring: GDScript `$Camera3D.unproject_position(p)` -> scripting.rs:2639 -> camera3d.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/camera3d.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a Camera3D at the origin looking -Z and a 640x480 window, with a GDScript run via MainLoop: unproject_position(Vector3(0,0,-5)) returns about (320,240), project_ray_normal(Vector2(320,240)) is about (0,0,-1), is_position_behind(Vector3(0,0,5)) is true, and after set_orthogonal(10,0.1,100) the projection reads 1 (orthogonal). (test: `camera3d_script_projection_api`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. grep -rln 'unproject_position' over engine-rs .rs files (excluding tests/) found only camera3d.rs and class_db.rs. In camera3d.rs the hits are the pub fn at :835 and doc/test lines. call_camera3d_method's arms are only make_current/clear_current/get_cull_mask_value/set_cull_mask_value (camera3d.rs:1032-1068). A string-literal grep for the projection method names in gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src: 0 hits. P0 is reasonable: project_ray picking is a common Godot game pattern.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a Camera3D at the origin looking -Z and a 640x480 window, with a GDScript run via MainLoop: unproject_position(Vector3(0,0,-5)) returns about (320,240), project_ray_normal(Vector2(320,240)) is about (0,0,-1), is_position_behind(Vector3(0,0,5)) is true, and after set_orthogonal(10,0.1,100) the projection reads 1 (orthogonal). comments.author: bone
comments.text:
VIEWPORT-SIZE PLUMBING LANDED (TurquoiseCastle, 06:02Z). This was the stated blocker for the whole bead, not a side task. NOT filing a completion — the dispatch arms and the test are still to come.

THE BLOCKER, IN THE CODE'S OWN WORDS. camera3d.rs's doc comment above call_camera3d_method says only the four methods needing NO viewport were ever served, and: "The projection family (get_camera_projection, get_camera_frustum, is_position_in_frustum, project_position, unproject_position, project_ray_origin, project_ray_normal) all take explicit viewport_width/viewport_height, which Godot's script API does not pass. That size lives on MainLoop's viewport_size(), and SceneTree exposes none, so wiring them from here would mean inventing a default and returning confidently wrong projections. They stay unwired until a viewport size reaches this layer." I confirmed SceneTree still had no viewport size (0 hits) before adding one.

LANDED:
- gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs: new private field `viewport_size: (u32, u32)`, plus `viewport_size()` and `set_viewport_size(w, h)`. The setter REJECTS a zero in either axis rather than storing it, because every consumer divides by the height for an aspect ratio. Default (1152, 648) — deliberately the same value MainLoop starts with, so a tree built without a loop still projects against a sane aspect instead of dividing by zero.
- gdscene/src/main_loop.rs: MainLoop::set_viewport_size now mirrors onto the tree, beside the existing self.tree.resize_root_window(..) call that already does exactly this kind of mirroring. No change to MainLoop::new was needed: both defaults are already (1152, 648), so an un-resized loop agrees with its tree.

STRUCT-LITERAL CHECK FIRST, because adding a field is the riskiest edit without a compiler: SceneTree has exactly ONE construction site (scene_tree.rs:717, inside `new()`). The other `Self {` in that file (8784) belongs to an unrelated stylus-state struct, not SceneTree. Both files scan to brace depth 0.

REMAINING, all in camera3d.rs plus one test:
1. Dispatch arms in call_camera3d_method for the projection family. The math ALREADY EXISTS and is unchanged — get_camera_projection:756, get_camera_frustum:800, is_position_in_frustum:816, unproject_position:835, project_position:870, project_ray_origin:905, project_ray_normal:936. Each takes (tree, node_id, .., viewport_width, viewport_height), so the arms just pass tree.viewport_size(). Note the gate at the top of call_camera3d_method is a `matches!` on the four current names — it must be widened or the new names return None before reaching the table.
2. NEW: `is_position_behind`. Godot's is `eyedir.dot(p - origin) < near` where `eyedir = -basis.column(2)`. Checks out against the acceptance: camera at origin looking -Z, p = (0,0,5) gives dot = -5 < near, so true.
3. NEW: set_perspective / set_orthogonal / set_frustum. Every building block exists — set_projection_type:506, set_size:523, node3d::set_fov:610 / set_near:627 / set_far:644 — so these are compositions, not new math. ProjectionType::Orthogonal = 1, which matches the acceptance's "the projection reads 1".
4. Acceptance test camera3d_script_projection_api: a .tscn Camera3D at the origin looking -Z, 640x480, driven through MainLoop with a GDScript. ⚠️ The test MUST call MainLoop::set_viewport_size(640, 480) — the default is 1152x648, and with the wrong aspect unproject_position(Vector3(0,0,-5)) will not land on (320,240). That is the harness detail most likely to make a correct implementation look broken.

HEAT WHEN I WROTE: scene_tree.rs 22:34 (26 min quiet), main_loop.rs 22:29 (31 min), camera3d.rs 14:00 (9 hours). Both writes used an st_mtime_ns guard; neither fired.

UNBUILT: the worker build guard blocks the toolchain.

title: Timer: honour process_callback=PHYSICS and ignore_time_scale, and dispatch the setter/getter surface
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-timer] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** MainLoop::step drives both passes

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/timer.cpp (_notification INTERNAL_PROCESS/INTERNAL_PHYSICS_PROCESS, ignore_time_scale, set_timer_process_callback)

**Patina today:** process_timer_nodes (scene_tree.rs:2312-2380) runs once per idle frame from main_loop.rs ~4239 with the scaled delta. It never reads process_callback (TIMER_PROCESS_PHYSICS) or ignore_time_scale (grep 'process_callback' scene_tree.rs = 0). timer_node_call (scripting.rs:1341) serves only start/stop/is_stopped. The method sweep found no dispatch for set_wait_time, get_wait_time, set_one_shot, set_autostart, set_paused, get_time_left, set_timer_process_callback or is_ignoring_time_scale; those return Nil silently through the node_has_method fallback (interpreter.rs:15666).

**Implement:** Godot Timer counts down in INTERNAL_PHYSICS_PROCESS when process_callback=1 and in idle otherwise, uses the unscaled delta when ignore_time_scale is set, and exposes set_/get_ for wait_time, one_shot, autostart, paused, time_left and process_callback. Patina has one idle pass with the scaled delta. Fix: split process_timer_nodes into idle and physics passes (call the physics one inside the MainLoop tick loop beside process_timers_phase, main_loop.rs ~4073). Pass real_delta when ignore_time_scale is set. Extend timer_node_call with the setter/getter family. Wiring: MainLoop::step drives both passes.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`

**Prove it:** A booted scene with a Timer(process_callback=1, wait_time=0.05) under Engine.time_scale=0.5 fires timeout after the expected physics ticks, and a Timer with ignore_time_scale=true fires after 0.05 real seconds. `$T.set_wait_time(2.0)` then `$T.get_wait_time()` returns 2.0 from script (test: `timer_physics_callback_and_time_scale`).

**Verifier note:** process_timer_nodes (scene_tree.rs:2312-2340) reads only __timer_started/__timer_running/time_left/wait_time/one_shot/paused/autostart and subtracts the delta it is given. The only ignore_time_scale hits (scene_tree.rs:303-2175) belong to SceneTreeTimer, not the Timer node. grep '"set_wait_time"|"get_time_left"|"set_one_shot"' over gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src = 0. I looked for a generic set_/get_ accessor fallback (strip_prefix("set_"), "set_" literals, setter/getter in scripting.rs) and found none; the only prefix handling is in navigation_agents.rs:183. The interpreter fallback (interpreter.rs:15666) returns Nil when the method is registered.
acceptance_criteria: A booted scene with a Timer(process_callback=1, wait_time=0.05) under Engine.time_scale=0.5 fires timeout after the expected physics ticks, and a Timer with ignore_time_scale=true fires after 0.05 real seconds. `$T.set_wait_time(2.0)` then `$T.get_wait_time()` returns 2.0 from script (test: `timer_physics_callback_and_time_scale`).

title: InstancePlaceholder: dispatch create_instance/get_instance_path/get_stored_values from script
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-instance-placeholder] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** a script calls it during MainLoop::step

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/instance_placeholder.cpp create_instance(replace, custom_scene), get_instance_path, get_stored_values

**Patina today:** packed_scene.rs builds InstancePlaceholder nodes (2567-2570). placeholder_instance_path (3425), placeholder_stored_values (3444) and placeholder_create_instance (3473) have no callers outside packed_scene.rs: grep 'placeholder_create_instance\|placeholder_instance_path\|placeholder_stored_values' crates/*/src. grep '"create_instance"' in scripting.rs/interpreter.rs hits only OS.create_instance at interpreter.rs:20220, which returns -1.

That loads the scene, applies the stored overrides, adds it as a sibling (or replaces the placeholder) and returns it. Patina has the logic (packed_scene.rs:3473) but no script arm. Fix: add InstancePlaceholder arms in call_node_method that call placeholder_create_instance with a FileAccess-based resolver, attach scripts with the shared helper (instantiate bead), and when replace=true free the placeholder and keep the name and index. title: Node: dedupe sibling names on add_child like Godot (@Name@N, force_readable_name -> Name2)
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-child-name-dedup] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** script add_child of three instantiated Bullet scenes under one parent during MainLoop::step

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/node.cpp _validate_child_name / _generate_serial_child_name, add_child(force_readable_name)

**Patina today:** SceneTree::add_child (scene_tree.rs:2697-2745) inserts the node with its name unchanged. grep 'readable_name\|validate_child_name\|_generate_serial_child_name\|"@"' crates/gdscene/src finds nothing relevant (only an annotation check in autoload.rs:286). Spawning several "Bullet" instances under one parent gives duplicate sibling names, so get_node("Bullet2")-style paths, NodePath uniqueness and path-hashed RPC routing are ambiguous.

**Implement:** Godot renames a child whose name collides with a sibling to '@<Name>@<n>', or '<Name><n>' when force_readable_name=true or when the editor adds it. It also renames on a set_name collision. Patina keeps duplicates. Fix: in SceneTree::add_child and in reparent/add_sibling, check sibling names and generate Godot's serial name. Accept the second add_child argument from script. Apply the same rule to set_node_name. Wiring: script add_child of three instantiated Bullet scenes under one parent during MainLoop::step.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`

**Prove it:** After a booted script adds three `Bullet` instances to the same parent, the children's names are unique and match Godot's scheme (Bullet, @Bullet@2, @Bullet@3, or Bullet2/Bullet3 with force_readable_name), and get_node resolves each (test: `add_child_dedupes_sibling_names`).

**Verifier note:** SceneTree::add_child (scene_tree.rs:2697-2745) inserts the node with no name check. The scripting add_child (scripting.rs:6298) contains no 'name' references. grep 'readable_name|validate_child_name|unique_child_name|serial_child_name|format!("@' over gdscene/src and gdobject/src = 0. '"@"' and ''@'' hits are only autoload.rs:286 (annotation) and line_edit.rs:474 (key mapping).
acceptance_criteria: After a booted script adds three `Bullet` instances to the same parent, the children's names are unique and match Godot's scheme (Bullet, @Bullet@2, @Bullet@3, or Bullet2/Bullet3 with force_readable_name), and get_node resolves each (test: `add_child_dedupes_sibling_names`).

title: Shaders: apply uniform hints, full uniform types and global uniforms in every render path (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: shaders/shader-uniforms] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** tscn/project.godot [shader_globals] -> binding -> pixels in 2D CPU, 3D CPU and 3D GPU; script/tscn -> node props -> per-instance uniform map -> pixels

### 1. Uniform hints, uniform types, and global uniforms honoured at render time  (PARTIAL, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** shader_language.cpp uniform hints (source_color, hint_range, hint_enum, hint_default_white/black/transparent, hint_normal, hint_roughness_*, filter_*, repeat_*, hint_screen_texture, hint_depth_texture, hint_normal_roughness_texture) and uniform types (ivec/uvec/bvec, mat2/3/4, samplerCube, sampler2DArray, sampler3D, isampler/usampler, arrays); global uniforms visible to every shader type

**Patina today:** gdserver3d UniformType has 9 variants (shader.rs:37-48): no ivec/uvec/bvec, mat2/3, samplerCube, sampler3D, sampler2DArray or arrays. Hints are parsed (shader.rs:284-311) but consumed only by the inspector (editor_server.rs:3879-3887): source_color does no sRGB->linear decode in either renderer, and filter_*/repeat_* do not change sampling (2D samples with the item's filter, draw.rs:365; 3D always uses sample_bilinear, gdrender3d/src/shader.rs:1176). hint_default_black/transparent/normal have no consumer (grep = 0), and an unbound sampler is always white. Global uniforms fall through to gdvariant::shader_globals only in the 3D line matcher (gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:1494-1500). The AST adapters (gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:954-958, gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:1635-1638) and the GPU packer never consult shader_globals.

**Implement:** Godot decodes source_color uniforms from sRGB, samples per the filter_*/repeat_* hints, binds hint_default_* fallback textures for unset samplers, supports all uniform types including arrays, and resolves `global uniform` from the project store in every shader type. Patina parses hints only for the inspector (editor_server.rs:3879) and reads globals only in the 3D line matcher (gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:1494). Approach: unify uniform parsing on shader_tokenizer::extract_uniforms, which already tokenises, and drop the two line-based parse_uniforms copies. Build one resolved UniformBinding per uniform (value after the hint transform, sampler filter/repeat, and default texture), used by the 2D AST adapter, the 3D AST adapter, CustomFragmentShader and the wgpu packer (custom_uniform_fields). Look up `global` scope uniforms in gdvariant::shader_globals inside that binding. Wiring: tscn/project.godot [shader_globals] -> binding -> pixels in 2D CPU, 3D CPU and 3D GPU.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/shader_tokenizer.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/shader.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdserver2d/src/shader.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/shader.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/shader_uniform_hints_and_globals_render.rs`

**Prove it:** A `uniform vec4 c : source_color = vec4(0.5,0.5,0.5,1)` renders linear ≈0.214 before output encoding, matching Godot. `filter_nearest` on a sampler gives hard texel edges in the 3D frame. An unset `hint_default_black` sampler samples black. `global uniform vec4 g_tint;`, declared in project.godot and changed via RenderingServer.global_shader_parameter_set, recolours a canvas_item AST shader and a spatial AST shader on the next frame. (test: `shader_uniform_hints_and_globals_render`)

**Verifier note:** Excluding tests and gdvariant/src/lifecycle.rs, the only shader_globals:: reader in the render path is gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:1498 (3D line matcher). The other hits are writers: project_boot.rs:400 and the interpreter.rs:8691-8742 RenderingServer API. A grep for hint_default_black|HintDefaultBlack|DefaultBlack outside tests = 0. The source_color hits in gdrender3d/renderer.rs and wgpu_pipeline.rs are hand-coded linearization for the procedural sky and a heuristic albedo name list (wgpu_pipeline.rs:2488). That is not a general per-uniform hint transform. P2 is ok.

### 2. Instance uniforms (instance uniform + set_instance_shader_parameter)  (MISSING, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/GeometryInstance3D.xml and CanvasItem.xml set_instance_shader_parameter/get_instance_shader_parameter (both in extension_api.json); `instance uniform` qualifier in shader_language.cpp

**Patina today:** UniformScope::Instance is parsed (gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:203), but grep 'instance_shader_parameter|instance_shader_params' across crates = 0 non-test hits, and class_db.rs/interpreter.rs have no set_instance_shader_parameter. Neither renderer stores per-instance values, so every instance renders the uniform's default.

**Implement:** Godot lets each GeometryInstance3D or CanvasItem override `instance uniform` values via set_instance_shader_parameter, stored as `instance_shader_parameters/<name>` properties in .tscn. Patina parses the scope (gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:203) but has no API or storage. Approach: register set/get_instance_shader_parameter on GeometryInstance3D and CanvasItem in class_db.rs, with dispatch arms that write node property `instance_shader_parameters/<name>`. Load that key from .tscn as-is. In render_server_3d resolve_shader_material and viewport_2d_render resolve_canvas_shader_material, overlay the node's instance values on top of material parameters for uniforms whose scope is Instance. Wiring: script/tscn -> node props -> per-instance uniform map -> pixels.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/instance_shader_parameters_render.rs`

**Prove it:** Two MeshInstance3D nodes share one ShaderMaterial with `instance uniform vec4 tint`, and set_instance_shader_parameter gives them red and blue. They render different colours in one frame, and a .tscn `instance_shader_parameters/tint` value loads the same way. The same holds for two Sprite2Ds. (test: `instance_shader_parameters_render`)

**Verifier note:** grep -rln 'instance_shader_parameter' --include='*.rs' across engine-rs/crates (tests included) returned no files. That covers class_db.rs, interpreter.rs and the renderers, so there is no API or storage. MISSING/P2 is correct.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A `uniform vec4 c : source_color = vec4(0.5,0.5,0.5,1)` renders linear ≈0.214 before output encoding, matching Godot. `filter_nearest` on a sampler gives hard texel edges in the 3D frame. An unset `hint_default_black` sampler samples black. `global uniform vec4 g_tint;`, declared in project.godot and changed via RenderingServer.global_shader_parameter_set, recolours a canvas_item AST shader and a spatial AST shader on the next frame. (test: `shader_uniform_hints_and_globals_render`) 2) Two MeshInstance3D nodes share one ShaderMaterial with `instance uniform vec4 tint`, and set_instance_shader_parameter gives them red and blue. They render different colours in one frame, and a .tscn `instance_shader_parameters/tint` value loads the same way. The same holds for two Sprite2Ds. (test: `instance_shader_parameters_render`)

title: Shaders: compile VisualShader resources to code at scene load so they render
description:
[audit-key: shaders/visual-shader] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** tscn -> packed_scene -> shader_code -> existing render path

**Godot ground truth:** scene/resources/visual_shader.cpp: VisualShader is a Shader; assigning it to ShaderMaterial.shader renders the compiled graph code

**Patina today:** gdscene/src/visual_shader_load.rs converts a .tres into a graph with get_code(), but its only non-test caller is the editor preview route (editor_server.rs:11511). Scene flattening (packed_scene.rs:1452-1471) handles only an inline Shader `code` or an ext_resource path stored as `shader_path`, and both resolvers then call load_gdshader on it (viewport_2d_render.rs:1287, render_server_3d.rs:1595). For a VisualShader .tres that reads raw tres text as GDShader source, and a VisualShader sub_resource has no `code`, so it is dropped.

**Implement:** In Godot a VisualShader assigned to ShaderMaterial.shader renders like text shader code. Patina compiles VisualShader graphs only for the editor preview (editor_server.rs:11511). Scene load (packed_scene.rs:1452-1471) and the resolvers (viewport_2d_render.rs:1283-1294, render_server_3d.rs:1590-1600) treat every shader as .gdshader text. Approach: in the packed_scene flattening, when the shader sub_resource class is VisualShader, or the ext_resource path ends in .tres/.res with type VisualShader, load it with the tres loader. Then run visual_shader_load::visual_shader_from_resource(..).get_code() and store the result as `shader_code` with the right shader_type. Do the same in both resolvers' shader_path branch. Wiring: tscn -> packed_scene -> shader_code -> existing render path.

Route interpreter tr_n and translate_plural through the plural lookup with context, and add the missing method arms. Add translation_remaps lookup in the resource loader. Wiring: .po loaded by the project loader -> script tr_n.

title: Particles: run a process_material ShaderMaterial (shader_type particles) from scenes, incl. start()
description:
[audit-key: vfx-particles/particles-shader] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn -> flatten -> MainLoop -> simulator -> published draw data

**Godot ground truth:** servers/rendering/shader_types.cpp / shader_language.cpp particles stage (start(), process(), TRANSFORM/VELOCITY/COLOR/CUSTOM/ACTIVE/RESTART built-ins); doc/classes/GPUParticles2D.xml process_material

**Patina today:** ParticleSimulator::set_particles_shader (particle.rs:551) and gdserver2d particles_shader interpreter exist, but `grep -rn 'set_particles_shader\|parse_particles_shader' crates --include=*.rs | grep -v /tests/` hits only particle.rs:551-552 and the interpreter itself - MainLoop never assigns a shader from a node's process_material ShaderMaterial (packed_scene.rs process_material handling only accepts ParticleProcessMaterial at :999). run_start/has_start (particles_shader.rs:122-127) are never called from the simulator, so start() never runs. 3D simulator has no shader hook. Only gdscene/tests/particles_shader.rs, which constructs ParticleSimulator directly, exercises it.

**Implement:** Godot: a GPUParticles2D/3D whose process_material is a ShaderMaterial with `shader_type particles` runs start() at spawn and process() each step instead of ParticleProcessMaterial. Patina: interpreter + simulator hook exist (particle.rs:551-571, 754-777) with no runtime caller; start() never invoked. Fix: in packed_scene.rs, when process_material resolves to a ShaderMaterial, flatten its shader code onto the node (reuse the existing ShaderMaterial flatten that produces shader_code, packed_scene.rs ~861) under `__process_shader_code`; in MainLoop::process_particles, when that key changes call sim.set_particles_shader(code) (cache by hash) and surface `unsupported` via push_warning; call program.run_start for each newly emitted/injected particle in step_exact/inject_particle; add the same hook to ParticleSimulator3D. Also pass shader uniforms from the ShaderMaterial's shader_parameter/* keys. Wiring: .tscn -> flatten -> MainLoop -> simulator -> published draw data.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/particle.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/particle3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/particles_shader_material_from_tscn.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn GPUParticles2D with process_material = ShaderMaterial whose Shader code is `shader_type particles; void start(){ COLOR = vec4(0,1,0,1); } void process(){ VELOCITY.y += 100.0*DELTA; }` and gravity unset: after 30 MainLoop steps published colours are green and particles move +y. (test: `particles_shader_material_from_tscn`)

**Verifier note:** UNWIRED holds. Outside tests, set_particles_shader (particle.rs:551) has no caller anywhere in engine-rs (grep set_particles_shader / particles_shader:: across engine-rs). The process() hook does run inside the simulator (particle.rs:754-777) when a program is set, but nothing at runtime ever sets one. has_start/run_start (gdserver2d particles_shader.rs:122-127) are called only by that file's own tests. The packed_scene process_material flatten rejects any material that is not a ParticleProcessMaterial (packed_scene.rs:999). I lowered priority to 2: hand-written particles shaders are an uncommon workflow next to ParticleProcessMaterial.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn GPUParticles2D with process_material = ShaderMaterial whose Shader code is `shader_type particles; void start(){ COLOR = vec4(0,1,0,1); } void process(){ VELOCITY.y += 100.0*DELTA; }` and gravity unset: after 30 MainLoop steps published colours are green and particles move +y. (test: `particles_shader_material_from_tscn`)

title: CharacterBody2D: run move_and_slide synchronously inside the script call
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-character-sync] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** GDScript _physics_process -> scripting.rs move_and_slide -> PhysicsServer slide -> node state is visible on the very next script line

**Godot ground truth:** scene/2d/physics/character_body_2d.cpp CharacterBody2D::move_and_slide (moves, updates velocity/floor flags/slide collisions before returning); doc/classes/CharacterBody2D.xml move_and_slide returns true if the body collided

**Patina today:** gdscene/src/scripting.rs:3673-3682: the "move_and_slide" arm only sets `_move_and_slide_requested=true` and returns the PREVIOUS tick's is_on_floor||is_on_wall||is_on_ceiling. The actual slide runs later in PhysicsServer::process_character_movement (gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:3153-3337), called from main_loop.rs:4046, which is AFTER process_physics_frame_with_scripts (main_loop.rs:3975). Effects: position/velocity/is_on_floor()/get_slide_collision*() read right after move_and_slide() in the same _physics_process are one tick stale; a velocity written AFTER move_and_slide() (e.g. `move_and_slide(); velocity = Vector2.ZERO`) is the one used for the move; calling move_and_slide twice in one tick moves once; the return value is last tick's flags. Unscripted CharacterBody2D nodes with a velocity auto-move (physics_server.rs:3180-3197), which Godot never does. get_floor_normal/get_wall_normal/get_floor_angle have no dispatch arm (grep '"get_floor_normal"' over gdscene/src, gdscript-interop/src = 0 hits).

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: CharacterBody2D::move_and_slide (scene/2d/physics/character_body_2d.cpp) does the whole slide while the script call is running. It updates global_position, velocity, the floor/wall/ceiling flags, floor/wall normals and the slide-collision list, then returns whether anything collided. Code later in the same _physics_process sees the new state.

Patina now: the scripting.rs:3673 arm only sets the `_move_and_slide_requested` flag and returns stale flags. PhysicsServer::process_character_movement (physics_server.rs:3153) does the real slide after every script has run (main_loop.rs:4046), and unscripted bodies with a velocity move on their own (physics_server.rs:3180-3197).

Approach: add `PhysicsServer::script_move_and_slide(&self, tree, node_id, dt) -> bool`, modelled on script_move_and_collide (physics_server.rs:3099), which already reaches the server through `tree.script_physics_addr()`. Move the body-build, slide and publish code out of process_character_movement into a helper that both use. Call it from the scripting.rs move_and_slide arm with the current physics delta and return the real collided bool. Remove the auto-move for unscripted bodies and the end-of-tick deferred pass; the body position must still be written to the world body so the following sync_to_physics agrees. Add get_floor_normal, get_wall_normal and get_floor_angle(up_direction) arms that read normals the slide publishes on the node, e.g. `_floor_normal` and `_wall_normal`.

Wiring: GDScript _physics_process -> scripting.rs move_and_slide -> PhysicsServer slide -> node state is visible on the very next script line.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene loaded through the runner has a CharacterBody2D falling onto a StaticBody2D floor. Its script does `velocity.y += g*delta; var hit = move_and_slide(); log(is_on_floor(), hit, position.y)`. On the tick of landing it logs is_on_floor()==true and hit==true with position.y already on the floor, in the same callback. `move_and_slide(); velocity = Vector2.ZERO` moves the body by the pre-zero velocity. An unscripted CharacterBody2D with an authored velocity does not move. get_floor_normal() returns (0,-1) on flat ground. (test: `characterbody2d_move_and_slide_synchronous`)

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. scripting.rs:3672-3682: the arm only sets _move_and_slide_requested and returns the previous tick's is_on_floor/is_on_wall/is_on_ceiling. The real slide runs in physics_server.rs:3153 process_character_movement, called at main_loop.rs:4046, after process_physics_frame_with_scripts at main_loop.rs:3975. physics_server.rs:3188-3197 applies the request gate only when tree.has_script, so unscripted bodies auto-move; the comment there admits this. grep '"get_floor_normal"|"get_wall_normal"|"get_floor_angle"' over gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src returned 0 hits. P0 is right, since move_and_slide is the core call of most 2D games.
acceptance_criteria: A scene loaded through the runner has a CharacterBody2D falling onto a StaticBody2D floor. Its script does `velocity.y += g*delta; var hit = move_and_slide(); log(is_on_floor(), hit, position.y)`. On the tick of landing it logs is_on_floor()==true and hit==true with position.y already on the floor, in the same callback. `move_and_slide(); velocity = Vector2.ZERO` moves the body by the pre-zero velocity. An unscripted CharacterBody2D with an authored velocity does not move. get_floor_normal() returns (0,-1) on flat ground. (test: `characterbody2d_move_and_slide_synchronous`)

That is not a Patina detail to paper over — **it is a model Godot does not have.** In Godot a CharacterBody2D moves only on the frame its script calls `move_and_slide()`; velocity alone never moves it, on any frame. So that test is not merely relying on an implementation quirk, its whole premise is non-Godot. Patching it with a flag would preserve a fiction; it needs rewriting to re-assert the request each step (or to use AnimatableBody2D/StaticBody2D, whichever its intent actually was).

MY RECOMMENDATION: clause 4 is correct and should land, but it is a TEST-MIGRATION bead, not a line item on this one. Specifically:
1. Close pat-mgixk.37 on clauses 1-3 + the normals arms — already delivered and PASSED (verifier.log:12798, with a genuine `Detected("fails without the change")`).
2. Spin clause 4 into its own bead covering the 4-line engine change AND the 9-file migration, with the explicit instruction that multi-step tests be rewritten to request movement per step rather than flag-patched. Whoever takes it should expect to change test INTENT, which is why it wants an owner's sign-off rather than a worker's judgement.

I cannot create or close beads, so this is a recommendation to the coordinator (also sent by mail).

WHAT I DID NOT DO, deliberately: I did not make the 4-line engine change. On its own it turns 9 green files across 4 packages red, and I have watched a single crate break stall six beads for hours today. Landing the engine half without the migration would be strictly worse than leaving clause 4 open.

comments.text:
BlackWaterfall — FINAL assessment of clause 4. This supersedes both of my comments above; read only this one.

VERDICT: clause 4 should land, and it belongs in its own TEST-MIGRATION bead. That is the same conclusion EmeraldCreek reached, but my earlier REASON for it was wrong and so was my first correction. The accurate reason is VOLUME and per-site judgement, not impossibility.

THE ENGINE CHANGE IS TRIVIAL: physics_server.rs:3226 reads `if tree.has_script(node_id) { ...require _move_and_slide_requested... }`. Dropping the `has_script` conditionality so every CharacterBody2D requires the request is ~4 lines. Verified, not inherited.

- I then implied one line per velocity write would do. Also not quite right: the request flag is one-shot per step (:3233), so a test needing sustained motion needs it re-set per FRAME, not per velocity write. The faithful migration is therefore "re-request before each stepping call", which is exactly what a Godot script does every frame — and it preserves every existing numeric expectation, including the tolerance BANDS I found (`dx > 5.0 && dx < 15.0` in character_static_body_behavior_test.rs) that a single frame of motion would undershoot.

  character_static_body_extended_parity_test.rs          2        15          19              34

78 stepping call-sites and 42 velocity writes across 9 files in 4 packages. A blanket "re-request before every step" would touch all 78, and MOST of them are RigidBody2D cases where the flag is meaningless noise — so each site needs a judgement about whether a CharacterBody2D is actually involved. title: Web export shell: register the PWA, stream pck download progress, show Rust panics on-screen
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web-export-shell] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/platform/web/js/engine/engine.js + misc/dist/html/full-size.html (progress bar via onProgress with bytes, serviceWorker.register, manifest link, displayFailureNotice); platform/web/js/engine/preloader.js (streamed fetch progress)

**Patina today:** crates/gdplatform/src/web_export.rs:242-322 pwa_files emits manifest.webmanifest + sw.js + offline.html, but DEFAULT_SHELL (web_export.rs:425-540) has no `navigator.serviceWorker.register` and no `<link rel=manifest>` (grep -n 'serviceWorker\|manifest' web_export.rs only hits the generator lines 94,258,320). The manifest has no icons (web_export.rs:258-268). The pck is loaded with `await packed.arrayBuffer()` (web_export.rs:497-498), so the only progress is the status text 'loading assets…' and there is no byte progress. The panic hook is console_error_panic_hook only (crates/patina-web/src/lib.rs:111-113), so a Rust panic inside the rAF loop after boot never reaches the #patina-error overlay; `fail` only catches main()'s rejection (web_export.rs:453-458,539).

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: the default shell shows a byte-accurate progress bar while it streams the wasm/pck (preloader.js reads the response body incrementally). With progressive_web_app/enabled it links the manifest (with icons from the export options) and registers the service worker. Any engine crash shows a failure notice on the page (misc/dist/html/full-size.html displayFailureNotice). Patina today: sw.js/manifest are written but never registered or linked (web_export.rs DEFAULT_SHELL), the manifest has no icons, the pck fetch is a single arrayBuffer() with no progress, and a panic after boot only reaches the console (patina-web/src/lib.rs:111). Approach: in DEFAULT_SHELL, when PWA is on, add `{{PATINA_MANIFEST_LINK}}` and a guarded serviceWorker.register('./sw.js'), substituted by render_html_shell from config.pwa_enabled. Add icon entries (pwa icon paths in WebExportConfig) to pwa_files. Replace the arrayBuffer fetch with a ReadableStream reader that updates a <progress> from content-length. Install a custom panic hook in __patina_web_start that also writes the panic message to #patina-error, and stop the rAF loop.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/web_export.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/web.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/lib.rs`

**Prove it:** With pwa_enabled the rendered shell contains a manifest link and serviceWorker.register('./sw.js'), and the manifest lists at least one icon; with pwa disabled neither appears. The shell's pck loader uses response.body.getReader() and writes progress to a <progress> element. patina-web exposes a panic hook that writes the payload to the error overlay element: a host-testable formatter covers the message, and the wasm hook calls it. (test: `web_export_shell_registers_pwa_and_reports_progress`)

**Verifier note:** grep 'serviceWorker|rel="manifest"|rel=manifest|getReader|progress|icons' over gdplatform/src/web_export.rs and web.rs gave 0 hits. web_export.rs:498 uses `await packed.arrayBuffer()`. lib.rs:111-113 __patina_web_start only calls console_error_panic_hook::set_once(). PARTIAL at P2 is appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: With pwa_enabled the rendered shell contains a manifest link and serviceWorker.register('./sw.js'), and the manifest lists at least one icon; with pwa disabled neither appears. The shell's pck loader uses response.body.getReader() and writes progress to a <progress> element. patina-web exposes a panic hook that writes the payload to the error overlay element: a host-testable formatter covers the message, and the wasm hook calls it. (test: `web_export_shell_registers_pwa_and_reports_progress`)

title: WebRTC: wasm32 backend over the browser's RTCPeerConnection/RTCDataChannel
description:

There is no cfg(target_arch="wasm32") in webrtc_peer.rs, unlike websocket_peer.rs:423-653, which has a browser path.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: on the web export, WebRTCPeerConnection/WebRTCDataChannel are thin wrappers over the browser's RTCPeerConnection. session_description_created / ice_candidate_created signals come from the browser's offer/ICE callbacks, and data channels deliver packets via onmessage (modules/webrtc/library_godot_webrtc.js). Patina today: webrtc_peer.rs is an in-process loopback (lines 22-30), so a web build cannot talk to any real peer. Approach: mirror websocket_peer.rs/websocket_web.rs. Add a `webrtc_web.rs` with a handle registry of js_sys RTCPeerConnection/RTCDataChannel objects reached through Reflect (as js_bridge.rs does). Callbacks push into per-handle queues drained by WebRTCPeerConnection::poll. Behind cfg(wasm32), route create_offer/set_local_description/set_remote_description/add_ice_candidate/create_data_channel/put_packet to it, and keep loopback on native. Wiring requirement: GDScript WebRTCPeerConnection.poll() each frame -> drains browser event queue -> emits session_description_created/ice_candidate_created/data_channel_received.

A simulated browser 'offer created' event emits session_description_created on the next poll, and a simulated datachannel message is readable via get_packet. `scripts/check-wasm.sh` builds gdplatform with the new module. (test: `webrtc_web_backend_routes_events`)

title: WebXR: route is_session_supported/initialize through navigator.xr on wasm32 (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: xr-peripheral/webxr-session] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** script WebXRInterface.initialize() -> interpreter call_xr_interface_instance (interpreter.rs:2758) -> WebXrInterface::initialize -> xr_web::request_session -> browser promise -> EVENTS queue -> poll_xr_interfaces (scene_tree.rs:2250) -> pump_instance_xr_signals (scripting.rs:396) -> connected Callable; GDScript -> call_xr_interface_instance -> WebXrInterface

### 1. WebXR session request never reaches navigator.xr (browser lane unwired)  (UNWIRED, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** modules/webxr/webxr_interface_js.cpp (initialize -> godot_webxr_initialize), modules/webxr/native/library_godot_webxr.js:353-370 (requestSession + requestReferenceSpace), modules/webxr/config.py:1-2 (built for web)

**Patina today:** crates/gdplatform/src/xr_web.rs:203 is_session_supported and :231 request_session have ZERO callers: `grep -rn "xr_web" crates` matches only xr.rs:410 (drain_events). WebXrInterface::initialize (gdplatform/src/xr.rs:512-562) and is_session_supported (:491) answer purely from `self.stub`; the stub comes from default_backend() (xr.rs:375-382), and `grep -rn "set_default_backend\|WebXrBackend" crates --include=*.rs | grep -v /tests/` finds no non-test installer (only the def + lib.rs:120 re-export; the sole caller is gdscene/tests/webxr_browser_session_binding.rs:76). So on wasm32 with a WebXR-capable browser, XRServer.find_interface("WebXR") (interpreter.rs:24782) builds an interface with an empty stub: is_session_supported emits supported=false and initialize() emits session_failed('session mode ... is not supported') without ever calling navigator.xr.requestSession. Also attach_session (xr_web.rs:144) queues no SessionStarted and a rejected promise queues no SessionFailed. Green tests drive a scripted backend only.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: WebXRInterfaceJS::is_session_supported calls navigator.xr.isSessionSupported and emits session_supported asynchronously; initialize() calls navigator.xr.requestSession(mode,{requiredFeatures,optionalFeatures}), then requestReferenceSpace over requested_reference_space_types (library_godot_webxr.js:353-370), emitting session_started on success and session_failed(message) on rejection (webxr_interface_js.cpp).

Patina today: gdplatform/src/xr_web.rs has real reflective bindings (is_session_supported :203, request_session :231, attach_session :144) but nothing calls them; WebXrInterface::initialize/is_session_supported (gdplatform/src/xr.rs:491,512) decide from a WebXrStub that is empty unless a test installs a WebXrBackend (no non-test caller of set_default_backend).

Implementation: in xr.rs add a backend kind (Stub vs Browser). On wasm32 when xr_web::is_available(), is_session_supported() calls xr_web::is_session_supported(mode, sink) whose sink records a new WebXrFrameEvent::SessionSupported{mode,supported}; initialize() sets state=Requesting and calls xr_web::request_session; extend xr_web so the resolve path requests the reference space (iterate requested_reference_space_types, fall back like Godot), reads enabledFeatures, and records WebXrFrameEvent::SessionStarted{reference_space,enabled_features}; the reject path records SessionFailed(message). apply_frame_event in xr.rs maps these to WebXrSignal. Keep the stub path for native/tests. Wiring: script WebXRInterface.initialize() -> interpreter call_xr_interface_instance (interpreter.rs:2758) -> WebXrInterface::initialize -> xr_web::request_session -> browser promise -> EVENTS queue -> poll_xr_interfaces (scene_tree.rs:2250) -> pump_instance_xr_signals (scripting.rs:396) -> connected Callable.

**Prove it:** On native, a WebXrInterface constructed with a fake 'browser' backend trait object (injected the same way xr_web is selected on wasm32) receives the request_session call with the script's mode/required/optional features when a GDScript scene calls `XRServer.find_interface("WebXR").initialize()`, and the resolved promise event results in the script's session_started callback firing on the next frame with get_reference_space_type() equal to the first granted requested type; a rejection fires session_failed with the browser message. wasm32 `cargo check -p gdplatform --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` compiles the new path. (test: `webxr_initialize_calls_browser_backend`)

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed on substance. Searched with grep -rn --include='*.rs' over engine-rs/crates for 'xr_web::'; the only non-test hit is gdplatform/src/xr.rs:410 (drain_events). The public fns in xr_web.rs (is_session_supported :203, request_session :231, attach_session :144) have no callers. 'set_default_backend|WebXrBackend' outside tests matches only the definitions at xr.rs:294-327 and the lib.rs:120 re-export, so nothing installs a non-test backend. xr_find_interface (interpreter.rs:24782) builds the stub-backed interface. UNWIRED is correct. I lowered priority 1 to 2: WebXR is uncommon in Godot projects, and this is a wiring gap, not core runtime.

### 2. WebXRInterface / XRInterface script method surface  (PARTIAL, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json WebXRInterface methods (is_input_source_active, get_input_source_tracker, get_input_source_target_ray_mode, get/set_requested_reference_space_types, get/set_display_refresh_rate, get_available_display_refresh_rates) + XRInterface methods (get_capabilities, is_primary/set_primary, get_tracking_status, get_play_area(_mode), supports_play_area_mode, trigger_haptic_pulse, get_system_info, environment blend modes, passthrough)

**Patina today:** call_xr_interface_instance (gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:2794-2836) dispatches only get_name, is_initialized, get_reference_space_type, get_enabled_features, get_visibility_state, session_mode/required/optional get+set, is_session_supported, initialize, uninitialize; everything else raises 'WebXRInterface has no method'. The platform side already implements input-source and refresh-rate logic (gdplatform/src/xr.rs:642-728) that script cannot reach. Grep counts in gdscript-interop/src+gdscene/src+gdobject/src: "is_input_source_active"=0, "get_input_source_tracker"=0, "get_input_source_target_ray_mode"=0, "get_display_refresh_rate"=0, "get_play_area"=0, "get_tracking_status"=0, "get_capabilities"=0, "trigger_haptic_pulse"=0; "set_requested_reference_space_types"=1 (class_db.rs:11304 metadata only). Also class_db.rs:11292-11320 registers required_features/enabled_features etc. with Variant::String defaults, while Godot types them String (comma list) for required/optional but PackedStringArray-like returns differ; get_enabled_features returns PackedStringArray in Patina vs String in Godot.

**Implement:** Godot's WebXRInterface exposes input-source queries, requested reference space types, display refresh rate get/set + available rates, plus the XRInterface base (get_capabilities, is_primary/set_primary, get_tracking_status, play area mode/points, trigger_haptic_pulse, get_system_info, environment blend modes, passthrough queries). Note Godot's required_features/optional_features/enabled_features/requested_reference_space_types are comma-separated Strings (WebXRInterface.xml).

Patina: interpreter.rs:2794-2836 dispatches 15 names; gdplatform::WebXrInterface already implements is_input_source_active/input_source_tracker_name/input_source_target_ray_mode/display_refresh_rate (xr.rs:642-728) but they are unreachable.

title: WebXR: feed viewer/controller/hand poses and gamepad input into XR trackers each frame (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: xr-peripheral/webxr-frame] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** browser frame -> tracker registry -> gdscene update_xr_nodes (main_loop.rs:4148) moves XRController3D nodes

### 1. WebXR per-frame pose/input feed (viewer pose, controllers, gamepad, hands) into XRServer trackers  (MISSING, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** modules/webxr/native/library_godot_webxr.js:47-75 (monkey-patched requestAnimationFrame + getViewerPose), :523-600 (targetRaySpace/gripSpace poses, xr-standard gamepad buttons/axes, hand joints fillPoses); webxr_interface_js.cpp _update_input_source / process()

**Patina today:** xr_web.rs has no requestAnimationFrame, getViewerPose, getPose, gamepad or hand handling (`grep -n "requestAnimationFrame\|getViewerPose\|getPose\|gamepad\|requestReferenceSpace" crates/gdplatform/src/xr_web.rs` = 0 hits). WebXrInterface::set_input_source (xr.rs:618) only records name/target_ray_mode; it never creates an XRPositionalTracker in the interpreter's XR_TRACKER_REGISTRY, so XRController3D nodes bound to left_hand/right_hand (gdscene/src/xr_nodes.rs:144) never receive poses from a browser. No 'head' tracker exists anywhere: `grep -rn '"head"' crates/gdscene/src/xr_nodes.rs crates/gdplatform/src/xr*.rs` = 0.

**Implement:** Godot: while a session runs, the web main loop is driven by XRSession.requestAnimationFrame; each frame getViewerPose(space) gives the head pose and views, and for each inputSource getPose(targetRaySpace/gripSpace), xr-standard gamepad buttons/axes and hand joints (fillPoses/fillJointRadii) are copied into XRPositionalTracker/XRControllerTracker/XRHandTracker objects registered on XRServer as 'head', 'left_hand', 'right_hand', 'left_hand'/'right_hand' hand trackers (library_godot_webxr.js:47-75, 523-600; webxr_interface_js.cpp).

Patina: xr_web.rs only listens for session events; no frame callback, no poses. Input sources are bookkeeping only (xr.rs:618-662) and never become trackers in XR_TRACKER_REGISTRY (interpreter.rs ~2455-2500).

Implementation: add a WebXrFrameEvent::Frame{head: Transform3D, sources: Vec<SourceFrame{id, aim, grip, buttons[], axes[], hand_joints?}>} recorded from a session.requestAnimationFrame loop in xr_web.rs (reflective js_sys, same style). In xr.rs poll(), expose the latest frame; add an interpreter-side `sync_webxr_trackers()` called from poll_xr_interfaces (interpreter.rs ~24760) that creates/updates trackers named head/left_hand/right_hand with poses 'default','aim','grip' and inputs trigger/grip/primary etc. mapped from xr-standard indices as Godot does, emitting pose_changed/button_pressed. Wiring: browser frame -> tracker registry -> gdscene update_xr_nodes (main_loop.rs:4148) moves XRController3D nodes.

**Prove it:** With a scripted backend delivering Frame events (same seam as the session test), a scene containing XROrigin3D > XRController3D(tracker="right_hand") has its global transform equal to the delivered grip/default pose after one MainLoop frame, `is_button_pressed("trigger_click")` true when xr-standard button 0 is pressed, and XRServer.get_tracker("head") returns a tracker whose default pose matches the viewer pose. (test: `webxr_frame_poses_drive_xr_controller`)

**Verifier note:** Grepping crates/gdplatform/src/xr_web.rs for 'requestAnimationFrame|getViewerPose|getPose|XRWebGLLayer|requestReferenceSpace|gamepad' returns 0 hits. Its pub fns (lines 58, 70, 83, 144, 203, 231) are navigator access, events and sessions only. Nothing creates a head tracker or browser-fed controller trackers. MISSING at P2 stands.

### 2. WebXR immersive rendering: XRWebGLLayer stereo output, XRCamera3D head tracking, view transforms/projections  (MISSING, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** library_godot_webxr.js:100-110 (XRWebGLLayer + updateRenderState, framebufferScaleFactor), XRInterface.get_view_count/get_transform_for_view/get_projection_for_view (doc/classes/XRInterface.xml), scene/3d/xr/xr_nodes.cpp XRCamera3D (binds 'head' tracker)

**Patina today:** `grep -n "XRWebGLLayer\|updateRenderState\|baseLayer" crates/gdplatform/src/xr_web.rs` = 0. interpreter.rs call_xr_interface_instance (2758-2840) has no get_view_count/get_transform_for_view/get_projection_for_view/get_render_target_size arms (grep of those quoted names in gdscript-interop/src and gdscene/src: 0 hits except unrelated class_db metadata). XRCamera3D is treated as an ordinary Camera3D (gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:409-418) and update_xr_nodes only handles is_class("XRNode3D") (xr_nodes.rs:139), which XRCamera3D (parent Camera3D, class_db.rs:3369) is not, so the camera never follows the HMD.

**Implement:** Godot: when the WebXR interface is primary and initialized, XRCamera3D takes the 'head' tracker pose and the renderer draws view_count (2 for immersive-vr) views using get_transform_for_view/get_projection_for_view from XRView data, into the XRWebGLLayer framebuffer created via updateRenderState({baseLayer}) (library_godot_webxr.js:100-110).

Patina: no layer creation, no view data, XRCamera3D renders as a mono Camera3D (render_server_3d.rs:409-418) and is never posed (xr_nodes.rs:139 handles XRNode3D only).

Implementation (staged after webxr_frame_poses_drive_xr_controller): (1) xr_nodes.rs: pose XRCamera3D from the 'head' tracker like an XRNode3D; (2) xr.rs: store per-view eye transforms + projection matrices from the Frame event, expose view_count/transform_for_view/projection_for_view and add those arms to call_xr_interface_instance; (3) render_server_3d.rs: when an XR interface is initialized and primary, render the active XRCamera3D once per view with the eye offset/projection into side-by-side viewports; (4) xr_web.rs: create XRWebGLLayer(session, gl) and blit/bind its framebuffer on wasm32.

**Prove it:** With a scripted backend supplying a 2-view frame, a scene with XROrigin3D > XRCamera3D renders (headless renderer) a frame whose left and right halves come from the two eye transforms (pixel difference on an off-center object), the XRCamera3D global transform equals the head pose, and WebXRInterface.get_view_count() returns 2 from GDScript. (test: `webxr_xr_camera_renders_stereo_views`)

**Verifier note:** '"get_view_count"' and '"get_transform_for_view"' give 0 non-test, non-class_db hits, and XRWebGLLayer has 0 hits in xr_web.rs. xr_nodes.rs:139 only processes nodes where is_class("XRNode3D") is true. Outside class_db and inspector, XRCamera3D appears only in a comment in render_server_3d.rs:409-412, where it is treated as a Camera3D. So the camera is never posed from the HMD and there is no stereo output.
acceptance_criteria: 1) With a scripted backend delivering Frame events (same seam as the session test), a scene containing XROrigin3D > XRController3D(tracker="right_hand") has its global transform equal to the delivered grip/default pose after one MainLoop frame, `is_button_pressed("trigger_click")` true when xr-standard button 0 is pressed, and XRServer.get_tracker("head") returns a tracker whose default pose matches the viewer pose. (test: `webxr_frame_poses_drive_xr_controller`) 2) With a scripted backend supplying a 2-view frame, a scene with XROrigin3D > XRCamera3D renders (headless renderer) a frame whose left and right halves come from the two eye transforms (pixel difference on an off-center object), the XRCamera3D global transform equals the head pose, and WebXRInterface.get_view_count() returns 2 from GDScript. (test: `webxr_xr_camera_renders_stereo_views`)

title: XRServer: real HMD transform, world origin, interface registry and tracker signals (+1 related)
description:

The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

### 1. XRServer singleton: HMD transform, world origin, interfaces, tracker signals  (PARTIAL, P2)

**Patina today:** interpreter.rs:2423-2446 get_hmd_transform builds a FRESH gdplatform::XrServer::new() each call (session_active=false) so it always returns identity-at-origin: a STUB. interpreter.rs:2448 get_interfaces returns PackedStringArray["WebXR"] where Godot returns Array of Dictionary{id,name}; :2449 get_interface_count hardcoded 1. Signals tracker_added/tracker_removed/tracker_updated/interface_added are only declared (class_db.rs:3289-3306); grep '"tracker_added"' in gdscript-interop/src and gdscene/src = 0 emit sites. XRServer.set_world_scale (interpreter.rs:2400) writes XR_WORLD_SCALE but gdscene xr_nodes.rs:64-87 reads XROrigin3D.world_scale instead, and XROrigin3D.set_world_scale never writes XRServer, so the two disagree.

**Implement:** Godot: XRServer.get_hmd_transform reads the primary interface's 'head' tracker; world_origin is set by the current XROrigin3D each frame; world_scale is shared with XROrigin3D.world_scale (the node proxies XRServer); add_interface/remove_interface/get_interface/get_interfaces (Array of {id,name}), primary_interface, center_on_hmd(rotation_mode, keep_height) and camera_locked_to_origin exist; add_tracker/remove_tracker emit tracker_added/tracker_removed(name,type) and interface changes emit interface_added/removed (servers/xr/xr_server.cpp).

Patina: interpreter.rs:2389-2500. get_hmd_transform is a stub over a throw-away XrServer; get_interfaces wrong type; ~10 methods missing; no tracker/interface signal emission; world scale split between XR_WORLD_SCALE and the XROrigin3D property (xr_nodes.rs:64).

Implementation: make get_hmd_transform read XR_TRACKER_REGISTRY['head'] 'default' pose (fallback identity); add world_origin storage + get/set, reference frame via center_on_hmd; interface registry listing WebXR (and MobileVR if implemented) with primary selection; emit XRServer signals through a singleton signal registry like CameraServer's (interpreter.rs:16173 emit_camera_server_signal pattern); in gdscene, have XROrigin3D current/world_scale write XRServer (via a gdscript_interop setter) and have world_scale_for read XRServer's value. Delete gdplatform::XrServer mock if unused.

**Prove it:** GDScript: after creating an XRPositionalTracker named "head" with a pose and XRServer.add_tracker(it), XRServer.get_hmd_transform() equals that pose, a connected tracker_added("head", TRACKER_HEAD) callback fired once; XRServer.get_interfaces()[0]["name"] == "WebXR"; setting XROrigin3D.world_scale = 2 in a scene makes XRServer.get_world_scale() == 2 and an XRController3D child's position doubles after a frame. (test: `xr_server_hmd_transform_and_signals`)

**Verifier note:** interpreter.rs:2423-2438 get_hmd_transform constructs gdplatform::XrServer::new() on every call, so it is a throwaway stub. get_interfaces returns PackedStringArray["WebXR"] and get_interface_count is hardcoded to 1 (interpreter.rs:2448-2449). The only '"get_primary_interface"' hit (interpreter.rs:28995) belongs to the TextServerManager registry, not XRServer. '"get_world_origin"', '"center_on_hmd"' and '"tracker_added"' give 0 non-test, non-class_db hits. PARTIAL at P2 stands.

### 2. XRNode3D/XRController3D/XRAnchor3D node behaviors and signals  (PARTIAL, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** scene/3d/xr/xr_nodes.cpp (XRNode3D tracking_changed(tracking: bool), get_pose, trigger_haptic_pulse; XRController3D re-emits tracker button_pressed/button_released/input_float_changed/input_vector2_changed/profile_changed, get_tracker_hand; XRAnchor3D get_size/get_plane; XROrigin3D current)

**Patina today:** main_loop.rs:4148-4150 emits tracking_changed with NO argument (`emit_signal(id, "tracking_changed", &[])`) though Godot's signal carries `tracking: bool` (class_db.rs:3317 declares .arg("tracking")) - a handler `func _on(tracking)` gets an arity error. xr_nodes.rs call_xr_node_method (:210-246) lacks get_pose, trigger_haptic_pulse, get_tracker_hand, set_tracker/set_pose_name, get_show_when_tracked; XRAnchor3D get_size/get_plane absent. XRController3D signals: the tracker handle emits button_pressed/input_float_changed (interpreter.rs:24643-24650) but nothing in gdscene re-emits them on the bound XRController3D node (grep '"button_pressed"' in gdscene/src matches only control.rs Button property uses).

**Implement:** Godot: XRNode3D emits tracking_changed(tracking) with the new state; XRController3D connects its tracker's button_pressed/button_released/input_float_changed/input_vector2_changed/profile_changed and re-emits them on the node; XRNode3D.get_pose() returns the XRPose, trigger_haptic_pulse forwards to the interface; XRController3D.get_tracker_hand; XRAnchor3D.get_size/get_plane read the anchor tracker (scene/3d/xr/xr_nodes.cpp).

Patina: main_loop.rs:4148-4150 emits tracking_changed with empty args; no controller signal forwarding; missing method arms in xr_nodes.rs:210-246.

Implementation: pass Variant::Bool(new_state) from update_xr_nodes (return (id, bool)); add a per-frame drain in main_loop after update_xr_nodes that takes queued tracker input-change events (expose a `take_xr_tracker_input_events()` from gdscript-interop recorded where interpreter.rs:24643 queues signals) and emits them on every XRController3D whose tracker matches; add the missing method arms.

**Prove it:** A scene with XROrigin3D > XRController3D(tracker="left_hand") and a script connecting tracking_changed(tracking) and button_pressed(name): when a script sets a pose on the left_hand tracker the handler receives tracking == true exactly once; set_input("trigger_click", true) on the tracker causes the node's button_pressed("trigger_click") to fire once next frame; get_pose() returns an XRPose whose transform matches. **Verifier note:** main_loop.rs:4149 is `self.tree.emit_signal(id, "tracking_changed", &[])`, with no argument. Upstream doc/classes/XRNode3D.xml:63-64 declares the param `tracking: bool`. In gdscene/src, '"button_pressed"' matches only Button-property code in control.rs and control_render.rs, so tracker signals are never forwarded to XRController3D. '"trigger_haptic_pulse"' has 0 hits. The only '"get_pose"' hit is the tracker-handle arm at interpreter.rs:24600, not a node method. PARTIAL at P2 stands.

title: Tween: support PropertyTweener.set_custom_interpolator
description:
[audit-key: animation/tween-polish] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** GDScript create_tween().tween_property(...).set_custom_interpolator(f) -> process_tweens -> node property

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/animation/tween.cpp PropertyTweener::set_custom_interpolator (Callable remaps eased progress)

**Patina today:** grep '"set_custom_interpolator"' gdscript-interop/src gdscene/src = 0. The remaining Tween/Tweener verbs are dispatched (tween_property, from, from_current, as_relative, set_delay, set_trans, set_ease, loops, parallel, subtween, custom_step, interpolate_value: 1+ hits each).

**Implement:** Godot ground truth (tween.cpp): set_custom_interpolator(callable) replaces the ease/trans curve. Each step calls the Callable with linear progress 0..1 and uses its float return as the interpolation weight.

Patina: there is no dispatch.

Approach: store an optional Callable (script node id + method, or lambda handle) on TweenStep. In SceneTree::process_tweens_in_mode, when it is set, call it through call_script_with_access before interpolating, and add the verb next to set_trans/set_ease in scripting.rs (~:7137+).

Wiring: GDScript create_tween().tween_property(...).set_custom_interpolator(f) -> process_tweens -> node property.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/tween.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene script tweens position.x 0->100 over 1 s with set_custom_interpolator(func(t): return t*t). After 0.5 s of MainLoop steps position.x == 25. (test: `tween_custom_interpolator_script`)

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. grep -rn 'set_custom_interpolator|custom_interpolator' over engine-rs/crates finds only gdobject/src/class_db.rs:5151 (comment) and :5162 (MethodInfo::new("set_custom_interpolator", 1)). There is no dispatch in gdscript-interop or gdscene/src/scripting.rs and nothing in tween.rs. So has_method reports true but the call does nothing. The method exists upstream at tween.cpp:591/688. MISSING with priority 3 is acceptable (it could also be called STUB, since it is registered with no implementation).
acceptance_criteria: A scene script tweens position.x 0->100 over 1 s with set_custom_interpolator(func(t): return t*t). After 0.5 s of MainLoop steps position.x == 25. (test: `tween_custom_interpolator_script`)

title: RigidBody2D: call _integrate_forces whenever overridden; custom_integrator skips default integration
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-integrate-forces] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** main_loop tick -> run_integrate_forces_2d -> script -> apply_state -> sync_to_physics -> world.step honours the omit flag

**Godot ground truth:** scene/2d/physics/rigid_body_2d.cpp:163-180 _body_state_changed calls _integrate_forces whenever GDVIRTUAL_IS_OVERRIDDEN, regardless of custom_integrator; modules/godot_physics_2d/godot_body_2d.cpp integrate_forces skips gravity/damping only when omit_force_integration (custom_integrator) is set

**Patina today:** gdscene/src/integrate_forces.rs:62-75 only dispatches _integrate_forces when `custom_integrator == true`. A script that overrides _integrate_forces with the default custom_integrator=false (the usual teleport/state-write idiom) is never called. custom_integrator is never read by gdscene/src/physics_server.rs or gdphysics2d (grep -w custom_integrator: only integrate_forces.rs and physics_server_3d.rs), so turning it on does not stop gravity or damping. integrate_forces.rs:105-109 sets inverse_inertia to 1.0 when inertia==0 instead of the shape-derived value, and the node's `inertia` is never pushed into PhysicsBody2D (body.rs:516 always derives it). Contact impulse and shape indices are left at 0 (integrate_forces.rs:170-176). These state methods have no dispatch arm: get_total_gravity, get_total_linear_damp, get_inverse_mass, get_inverse_inertia, get_center_of_mass, set_sleep_state, get_space_state, get_contact_collider_object (grep over gdscript-interop/src and gdscene/src).

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: RigidBody2D::_body_state_changed (rigid_body_2d.cpp:163) calls _integrate_forces every step for any script that overrides it. custom_integrator (set_use_custom_integrator -> body_set_omit_force_integration) only stops the server from adding gravity and damping in GodotBody2D::integrate_forces (godot_body_2d.cpp:~430-560).

Patina now: integrate_forces.rs:62-75 dispatches only when custom_integrator is true, and nothing in gdphysics2d reads custom_integrator. Inverse inertia falls back to 1.0 (integrate_forces.rs:109), the authored `inertia` never reaches PhysicsBody2D, and contact impulses are 0.

Approach:
1. Filter run_integrate_forces_2d targets on 'the script defines _integrate_forces'. tree.has_script plus a has-method check on the script instance will do.
2. Add `omit_force_integration: bool` and `custom_inertia: Option<f32>` to PhysicsBody2D. Read both in register_bodies and sync_to_physics (physics_server.rs ~1649-1746). Make PhysicsWorld2D::step (world.rs ~500-530) skip integrate_forces gravity and damping when omit is set.
3. Fill inverse_inertia from body.inverse_inertia() of the registered body.
4. Report solver contact impulses through publish_body_contacts.
5. Add interpreter arms for the missing PhysicsDirectBodyState2D methods.

Wiring: main_loop tick -> run_integrate_forces_2d -> script -> apply_state -> sync_to_physics -> world.step honours the omit flag.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/integrate_forces.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/body.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/world.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** Two RigidBody2D scenes are loaded through the runner and run for 60 ticks. (1) custom_integrator=false with an _integrate_forces that sets state.linear_velocity.x=100: the callback runs every tick and the body falls under gravity while moving right. (2) custom_integrator=true with an empty _integrate_forces: the body does not fall. state.get_inverse_inertia() equals 1/inertia for an authored inertia=4. (test: `rigidbody2d_integrate_forces_dispatch_and_custom_integrator`)

**Verifier note:** integrate_forces.rs:62-75 filters targets on custom_integrator==Bool(true), and its comment wrongly says Godot does the same. In upstream rigid_body_2d.cpp:163-176, _body_state_changed calls the method whenever GDVIRTUAL_IS_OVERRIDDEN, with no custom_integrator check. grep -w custom_integrator over gdscene/src and gdphysics2d/src finds only integrate_forces.rs and physics_server_3d.rs, so 2D gravity and damping are never omitted. integrate_forces.rs:109 falls back to 1.0 inverse inertia, and lines 170-176 leave impulse and shape at their defaults. In call_direct_body_state_2d_instance (interpreter.rs:22728-22840) the method forms get_total_gravity, get_inverse_inertia, get_inverse_mass, get_center_of_mass, set_sleep_state, get_space_state and get_contact_collider_object all fall to `_ => Nil`. They are registered in class_db.rs:2571/2680/2741. The property-syntax reads at interpreter.rs:22661 do work. P0 stands, because the common override idiom silently never runs.
acceptance_criteria: Two RigidBody2D scenes are loaded through the runner and run for 60 ticks. (1) custom_integrator=false with an _integrate_forces that sets state.linear_velocity.x=100: the callback runs every tick and the body falls under gravity while moving right. (2) custom_integrator=true with an empty _integrate_forces: the body does not fall. state.get_inverse_inertia() equals 1/inertia for an authored inertia=4. (test: `rigidbody2d_integrate_forces_dispatch_and_custom_integrator`)

title: Physics2D: jitter-fix timer sync, ray-only SeparationRay contacts, mouse_shape_* signals
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-polish] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** main loop -> accumulator; narrowphase via world.step and character sweeps; picking pass -> signals

**Godot ground truth:** main/main_timer_sync.cpp (physics/common/physics_jitter_fix=0.5); modules/godot_physics_2d/godot_collision_solver_2d.cpp solve_separation_ray (pushes only along the ray, slide_on_slope); scene/2d/physics/collision_object_2d.cpp mouse_shape_entered/exited

SeparationRay is modelled as a zero-radius segment (collision.rs:220-226) with normal SAT contacts, with no ray-only separation and no slide_on_slope (grep 'slide_on_slope' in gdphysics2d = 0). grep '"mouse_shape_entered"' in gdscene/src = 0 hits; picking emits mouse_entered/input_event only (main_loop.rs:3077-3240).

**Implement:** Godot ground truth:
- MainTimerSync uses physics/common/physics_jitter_fix (default 0.5) to snap physics steps to the render rate (main_timer_sync.cpp).
- SeparationRayShape2D only ever pushes along its own ray, and slide_on_slope decides whether the push follows the surface normal (godot_collision_solver_2d.cpp solve_separation_ray).
- CollisionObject2D emits mouse_shape_entered/exited(shape_idx).

Patina now: the accumulator in main_loop.rs:3823 has no jitter fix. SeparationRay is a plain segment (collision.rs:220). There are no mouse_shape_* signals.

Approach: port MainTimerSync::advance_checked's jitter snapping into MainLoop::step, reading the project setting. Add a dedicated SeparationRay arm in collision.rs::collide that returns normal = ray direction (or the surface normal when slide_on_slope) with depth along the ray, and parse slide_on_slope in shape_from_shape_props. Emit mouse_shape_entered/exited alongside mouse_entered in physics_pick_input using the picked shape index.

Wiring: main loop -> accumulator; narrowphase via world.step and character sweeps; picking pass -> signals.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/collision.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs`

**Prove it:** With physics_jitter_fix=0.5 and a 59.9 Hz frame cadence at 60 tps, the runner executes exactly one physics tick per frame over 600 frames. A CharacterBody2D with a SeparationRayShape2D on a 30-degree slope is pushed straight up, not along the slope normal. Hovering a body's second shape emits mouse_shape_entered(1). (test: `physics2d_jitter_fix_separation_ray_mouse_shape`)

**Verifier note:** All three gaps hold. grep 'jitter' in gdscene/src/main_loop.rs = 0; the setting is only registered at gdcore/src/project_settings.rs:610. grep 'mouse_shape_entered' over gdscene/src and gdphysics2d/src = 0. gdphysics2d/src/collision.rs:220-226 turns SeparationRay into a zero-radius Rounded segment. grep 'slide_on_slope' over gdphysics2d/src = 0; it exists only in physics_server_3d.rs:514-518. I changed the status to PARTIAL rather than MISSING because the bundle mixes three features and SeparationRayShape2D does exist as a shape with segment collision, so it is approximate rather than absent. P3 stands.
acceptance_criteria: With physics_jitter_fix=0.5 and a 59.9 Hz frame cadence at 60 tps, the runner executes exactly one physics tick per frame over 600 frames. A CharacterBody2D with a SeparationRayShape2D on a 30-degree slope is pushed straight up, not along the slope normal. Hovering a body's second shape emits mouse_shape_entered(1).
