title: Physics3D: honour Godot shape defaults, WorldBoundary plane and CollisionShape3D rotation
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/p3d-shape-fidelity] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn load -> packed_scene __shape__* -> shape_from_node_3d -> world body -> MainLoop step

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/CapsuleShape3D.xml:14 and CylinderShape3D.xml:17 (height default=2.0); a .tscn omits default-valued properties

**Patina today:** crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:477-484 builds CapsuleShape/CylinderShape with num("height", 1.0). The gizmo path in crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:3121-3124 uses 2.0 for the same shapes, so the two layers disagree. gdphysics3d treats height as total height (shape.rs:14,128-132). An unedited CapsuleShape3D (the default CharacterBody3D collider, which Godot writes as a sub-resource with no height line) therefore collides as a 1 m capsule, effectively a sphere, while it renders as 2 m.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: CapsuleShape3D.height and CylinderShape3D.height default to 2.0 (doc XML), WorldBoundaryShape3D has a `plane` Plane property (default Plane(0,1,0,0)), and each CollisionShape3D's full local transform, including rotation, is that shape owner's transform (CollisionObject3D::shape_owner_set_transform). Patina: (1) physics_server_3d.rs:477-484 defaults height to 1.0, so a default capsule loaded from a .tscn is half height. (2) physics_server_3d.rs:521-524 hardcodes normal (0,1,0) and distance 0 and ignores `plane`/`__shape__plane`, so a tilted or raised world boundary is flat at y=0. (3) shapes_from_body_subtree (physics_server_3d.rs:581-584) stores only a translation offset, so a CollisionShape3D rotated 90 degrees (a cylinder on its side, a rotated wall box) collides unrotated. Approach: change the defaults to 2.0; parse a Plane (Variant::Plane, or the string form) from `__shape__plane`/`plane` into normal plus d; extend the shape tuple (and PhysicsBody3D.extra_shapes/shape_offset in gdphysics3d/src/body.rs plus shapes_world) to carry a local Quaternion composed into world rotation in the narrowphase (collision::test_collision_rot already accepts rotations). Apply the same rotation handling to Area3D shapes. Wiring: .tscn load -> packed_scene __shape__* -> shape_from_node_3d -> world body -> MainLoop step.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a CharacterBody3D whose CapsuleShape3D sub-resource omits height comes to rest at y = 1.0 above a floor, not 0.5. A RigidBody3D dropped onto a WorldBoundaryShape3D with plane Plane(0,1,0,3) stops at y of about 3. A RigidBody3D box falling onto a StaticBody3D whose CollisionShape3D is a thin BoxShape3D rotated 90 degrees about Z (a vertical wall) lands at the wall's rotated extent. All three run through MainLoop from scene load (test: `physics3d_shape_defaults_and_rotation`).

**Verifier note:** physics_server_3d.rs:477-484 uses num("height", 1.0) for both shapes. The num helper (physics_server_3d.rs:434-441) falls back to that default when neither __shape__height nor height is present, and packed_scene.rs:1654-1658 copies only the keys the sub-resource authored, so nothing fills in 2.0. The gizmo path at packed_scene.rs:3123 uses unwrap_or(2.0), so the two layers disagree. Also confirmed: the WorldBoundary arm at physics_server_3d.rs:521-524 hardcodes normal (0,1,0) and distance 0, and shapes_from_body_subtree (physics_server_3d.rs:582-584) pushes only a translation delta, with no shape rotation. P0 stands: an unedited capsule is the default collider for characters.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a CharacterBody3D whose CapsuleShape3D sub-resource omits height comes to rest at y = 1.0 above a floor, not 0.5. A RigidBody3D dropped onto a WorldBoundaryShape3D with plane Plane(0,1,0,3) stops at y of about 3. A RigidBody3D box falling onto a StaticBody3D whose CollisionShape3D is a thin BoxShape3D rotated 90 degrees about Z (a vertical wall) lands at the wall's rotated extent. All three run through MainLoop from scene load (test: `physics3d_shape_defaults_and_rotation`).

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
PARTS 1 AND 2 LANDED (TurquoiseCastle). Part 3 is mapped but NOT written. No completion filed — the acceptance test needs all three.

Both files were clean at HEAD and cold when I started (physics_server_3d.rs 14h, body.rs 2 months), no peer WIP, no mgixk.39 markers anywhere.

=== PART 1 DONE: capsule/cylinder height 1.0 -> 2.0 ===
physics_server_3d.rs. The identical line `height: num("height", 1.0),` appears TWICE (capsule arm and cylinder arm) — I replaced both with the count asserted at 2, because fixing one would leave the two shapes disagreeing, which is the same class of bug as the gizmo/physics split this bead is about.

Confirmed the semantics rather than assuming them: `gdphysics3d::shape::Shape3D::CapsuleShape` documents `height` as the TOTAL height and its `bounding_aabb` spans -height/2..+height/2, so Godot's 2.0 maps straight across with no halving. That is also why the acceptance expects a resting default capsule at y = 1.0.

=== PART 2 DONE: a real WorldBoundaryShape3D plane ===
physics_server_3d.rs. The arm hardcoded `normal (0,1,0)` and `distance 0.0` and read nothing. Replaced with a `plane("plane")` read, falling back to the shape's own `normal`/`distance` field names (what a runtime setter writes).

I checked what the .tscn reader actually PRODUCES instead of inventing a shape: `gdresource/src/loader.rs` already has a `Plane(a, b, c, d)` branch -> `Variant::Plane(Plane { normal: (a,b,c), d })`, so an authored `plane = Plane(0, 1, 0, 3)` arrives here already typed. (I briefly concluded Plane was unsupported — a too-narrow grep window. It is supported.)

Added `plane` as a closure in the same namespaced-first idiom as the existing `v3`, so `__shape__plane` from a copied sub-resource wins over a property on the node. New import: `Plane` into the `gdcore::math3d` use line — it had 0 prior occurrences in the file, so no conflict.

A zero normal falls back to +Y instead of being stored: a half-space with no orientation makes every contact test degenerate. The normal is normalized, as Godot normalizes a Plane on construction.

VERIFIED: physics_server_3d.rs scans to brace depth 0; `height: num("height", 2.0)` count = 2 and `1.0` count = 0.

=== PART 3 NOT STARTED — full site map, and a trap that matters ===
Blast radius is small and entirely in 3 files (I measured it: `shapes_world()` has only 3 call sites, `extra_shapes` has 9 in 3D; the rest of the 42 hits are the 2D twins in gdphysics2d/physics_server.rs, which must NOT be touched).

Plan: `extra_shapes: Vec<(Vector3, Shape3D)>` -> `Vec<(Vector3, Quaternion, Shape3D)>`, plus a `shape_rotation: Quaternion` beside `shape_offset` for the primary shape. The tuple is the right home for a PER-SHAPE value; a parallel `Vec<Quaternion>` could desync from the shapes it describes. Note body.rs:73-81 argues for additive fields over retyping, but that argument is about `shape` (33 readers); `extra_shapes` has 9.

Sites:
- body.rs: `shape_offset` :72, `extra_shapes` :81, inits :182-183, `world_aabb` loop :470, `shapes_world` :496-502 (compose `self.rotation * local`)
- world.rs: the shape-pair loop :845-859 destructures `for (shape_pos_a, sa)` and passes the BODY-wide `rot_a`/`rot_b` to `test_collision_rot` and to `support_point` :869-870. Those must become the per-shape composed rotation, and the `hit` tuple has to carry them because the support points are computed after the loop ends.
- physics_server_3d.rs: `shapes_from_body_subtree` :556-592 returns `Vec<(Vector3, Shape3D)>` and pushes only `inv_rot.xform(delta)`; it needs the shape's local rotation too (global shape rotation composed with the body's inverse). Plus the 4 `extra_shapes` sites, and the Area3D path.
- `collision::test_collision_rot(pos_a, rot_a, shape_a, pos_b, rot_b, shape_b)` already exists and takes rotations, as the bead says — no narrowphase maths to write.

*** THE TRAP: body.rs `world_aabb` (:465-485) would silently defeat the whole fix. ***
It builds each shape's world box as `Aabb::new(local.position + world_pos, local.size)` — the UNROTATED local AABB. The broadphase prunes candidate pairs on that box. For the acceptance's third case — a thin BoxShape3D rotated 90 degrees about Z to make a vertical wall — the unrotated box is thin in Y while the real wall is thin in X, so the falling body's pair gets pruned before the narrowphase ever runs and it passes straight through. The narrowphase fix would be perfectly correct and the test would still fail, which is the worst shape of bug to debug.

So `world_aabb` must rotate the box too. Conservative and no new maths needed: `Aabb::get_endpoint(idx: u8)` yields the 8 corners and `Aabb::expand(point)` grows to include one, so seed from corner 0 rotated by the composed rotation and expand over the other 7. `Quaternion::xform(Vector3)` exists.

=== WHAT IS NOT DONE ===
No acceptance test yet. `physics3d_shape_defaults_and_rotation` needs all three cases through MainLoop from scene load, and case 3 cannot pass until part 3 plus the `world_aabb` fix are in. Parts 1 and 2 are independently correct and independently testable, but I am not filing a partial completion for a bead whose acceptance names three cases.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
PART 3 IMPLEMENTATION LANDED (TurquoiseCastle). All three parts of the bead are now written. Only the acceptance test remains. No completion filed yet.

=== PART 3 DONE: per-shape rotation, body path ===

gdphysics3d/src/body.rs
- New `shape_rotation: Quaternion` beside `shape_offset` (IDENTITY default = old behaviour), init added in `new()`.
- `extra_shapes: Vec<(Vector3, Shape3D)>` -> `Vec<(Vector3, Quaternion, Shape3D)>`. The rotation goes IN the tuple, not in a parallel `Vec<Quaternion>`: it is a per-shape value and a second vector is one `push` away from silently rotating the wrong collider. (The field doc at :88 argues for additive fields over retyping, but that argument is about `shape`, which has 33 readers; `extra_shapes` had 9 sites, all in 2 files.)
- `shapes_world()` now returns the composed world rotation per shape: `self.rotation * local`. ORDER MATTERS and is not commutative — `body * local` applies the local rotation first, which is what nesting a rotated CollisionShape3D under a rotated body means. `local * body` agrees with the correct answer whenever EITHER is identity, so an axis-aligned test cannot tell them apart; noted in the doc so nobody "simplifies" it.

gdphysics3d/src/world.rs
- The shape-pair loop now passes the PER-SHAPE rotation to `test_collision_rot` and to `support_point`, not the body-wide `rot_a`/`rot_b`. The winning pair's rotations are carried in the `hit` tuple because the support points are computed after the loop ends and must use the same orientation the test did.
- Dropped `rot_a`/`rot_b` from the pair tuple entirely — `shapes_world` bakes the body rotation in, so binding them would leave two dead bindings. `pos_a`/`pos_b` STAY: they are the lever arms (`ra`/`rb`) for the contact impulse, a different quantity. (Checked first that warnings are not denied anywhere in the workspace, so this was a cleanup, not a fix for a hard error.)

gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs
- `shapes_from_body_subtree` returns `Vec<(Vector3, Quaternion, Shape3D)>`, computing each shape's rotation relative to its body as `body_global_basis.get_rotation_quaternion().inverse() * shape_global_basis.get_rotation_quaternion()` — the same "parent inverse * child" idiom skeleton3d.rs:1119 uses for bone poses. Taken from the GLOBAL basis so an intermediate Node3D between body and shape (which the walker explicitly supports) contributes its rotation too.
- Both consumer sites updated: initial registration sets `body.shape_rotation`, and the per-tick resync re-reads it alongside the offset, so a CollisionShape3D ROTATED after the first frame is picked up for the same reason the offset is refreshed there.

*** THE BROADPHASE TRAP, FIXED *** body.rs `world_aabb` built each shape's world box from the UNROTATED local AABB, and the broadphase PRUNES pairs on that box. The acceptance's rotated wall is thin in Y locally and thin in X once placed, so the falling body's pair would have been discarded before the narrowphase ran and the body would drop straight through a wall the narrowphase models perfectly. Now rotates all 8 corners (`Aabb::get_endpoint` + `expand`, `Quaternion::xform`) and bounds them. Conservative by construction: over-estimating costs one narrowphase test, under-estimating loses the collision.

VERIFIED: all three files scan to brace depth 0. Workspace sweep for missed tuple sites found none — every remaining `extra_shapes` hit outside these files is either the 2D twin (gdphysics2d / physics_server.rs, which uses a STRUCT not a tuple, and must not be touched) or a doc comment. `impl Mul for Quaternion` exists and body.rs:359 already used `self.rotation * dq`.

=== AREA3D ROTATION: NOT DONE, and it is bigger than the bead reads ===
The bead says "apply the same rotation handling to Area3D shapes". `gdphysics3d::area3d::Area3D` has a bare `pub shape: Shape3D` with NO offset field at all, and the overlap test is `area.shape.contains_point(point - area.position)` — position-only, no rotation parameter. So giving an Area3D a shape rotation means first giving it a per-shape TRANSFORM, which is a different and larger feature than extending an existing tuple. None of the three acceptance cases involves an Area3D, so this is a genuine follow-on rather than a gap in the acceptance. Worth its own bead.

=== STILL TO DO: the acceptance test ===
`physics3d_shape_defaults_and_rotation`. Harness is settled: copy `load`/`node_of`/`y_of`/`settle`/`STEP` from the green `physics3d_multi_shape_bodies.rs`, which drives everything through `MainLoop::step` on a parsed .tscn exactly as this bead's Wiring requirement asks.

*** A POISONED ASSERTION TO AVOID IN CASE 1. *** The acceptance says "a CharacterBody3D whose CapsuleShape3D omits height comes to rest at y = 1.0". But `body_type_for_class_3d` maps `CharacterBody3D` -> `BodyType3D::Kinematic`, and a kinematic body is script-driven, not gravity-driven: a scriptless CharacterBody3D sits where the scene put it forever, so that assertion would be RED against a perfectly correct engine. Two ways out: attach a GDScript calling `move_and_slide()` each `_physics_process` (faithful to the wording, and `character_body_3d_*.rs` tests show the chain works), or drop the capsule on a RigidBody3D, which isolates the height default with no script. Either way the discriminating number is the same: floor top at y = 0, so a 2.0-height capsule rests at y = 1.0 and the old 1.0-height one rests at 0.5 — far outside any sane tolerance.

Case 2: RigidBody3D onto a WorldBoundaryShape3D with `plane = Plane(0, 1, 0, 3)` stops at y ~= 3.
Case 3: RigidBody3D box onto a StaticBody3D whose thin BoxShape3D is rotated 90 degrees about Z; this is the case the `world_aabb` fix exists for.

title: CanvasItem: clamp accumulated z to +-4096 and stop modulate/z inheritance at top_level
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/r2d-order-polish] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** collect_canvas_items uses these for sort and modulate, so Play pixels change

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/canvas_item.cpp set_z_index (clamped to RS::CANVAS_ITEM_Z_MIN..MAX = -4096..4096), _top_level_changed (canvas_item_set_parent to the canvas, so the parent's modulate and relative z are not inherited)

**Patina today:** canvas_order::effective_z_index (crates/gdscene/src/canvas_order.rs:43-54) sums z up the parent chain with no clamp and does not stop at top_level. inherited_modulate (:59-70) multiplies through top_level ancestors. node2d.rs:156-260 handles top_level only for transforms.

**Implement:** Godot clamps z_index and the accumulated relative z to [-4096,4096]. A top_level item is reparented to the canvas root in the RenderingServer, so it does not inherit its parent's modulate or relative z.
Patina: canvas_order.rs:43-70 does neither.
Implementation: clamp in effective_z_index. Return the node's own z (no parent add) and own modulate (no parent multiply) when node2d::is_top_level is true.
Wiring: collect_canvas_items uses these for sort and modulate, so Play pixels change.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/canvas_order.rs`

**Prove it:** A parent with modulate alpha 0.5 and z_index 4000, with a top_level child ColorRect (z_index 10) and a non-top-level child (z_index 500). In the Play-frame render, the top_level child is fully opaque and sorts by z 10. The other child's effective z is 4096 (it draws above an absolute z 4095 sibling, and does not overflow). (test: `canvas_z_clamp_and_top_level_inheritance`)

**Verifier note:** canvas_order.rs:43-54 adds the parent's effective z with no clamp and no top_level check. inherited_modulate (:59-70) multiplies through every ancestor. grep top_level in canvas_order.rs finds 0 hits. node2d.rs:140-147 uses top_level only as a property for transforms. Priority 3 is acceptable.
acceptance_criteria: A parent with modulate alpha 0.5 and z_index 4000, with a top_level child ColorRect (z_index 10) and a non-top-level child (z_index 500). title: MainLoop: support application/run/main_loop_type scripts (_initialize/_process/_physics_process/_finalize)
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-custom-mainloop] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** patina-runner boot of a project with that setting

**Godot ground truth:** main/main.cpp (main_loop_type, script extending MainLoop/SceneTree); doc/classes/MainLoop.xml

**Patina today:** ClassDB registers _initialize/_finalize virtuals (class_db.rs:7883-7886). grep 'main_loop_type' crates/*/src = 0, and MainLoop::step (main_loop.rs:3613) has no hook for a script-defined loop.

**Implement:** Godot lets a project set application/run/main_loop_type to a class_name or script extending SceneTree/MainLoop, whose _initialize, _process(delta) (return true to quit), _physics_process and _finalize run around the frame loop. Patina ignores the setting. Fix: in bootstrap, read the setting, instantiate the script with the SceneTree as `self` context, and call the virtuals from MainLoop::step. A true return from _process requests quit. Wiring: patina-runner boot of a project with that setting.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`

**Prove it:** A project whose main_loop_type script prints in _initialize and returns true from _process on frame 3 boots via patina-runner, prints once, and quits after frame 3 (test: `custom_main_loop_type_drives_frames`).

**Verifier note:** I couldn't refute it. I searched engine-rs/crates (src, excluding tests) for `main_loop_type`, `mainlooptype` and `custom_main_loop` (case-insensitive) and got 0 hits. I also searched for `application/run` keys: project_settings.rs:575-588 defaults only disable_stdout/disable_stderr/flush_stdout_on_print/max_fps/low_processor_mode*, and main_loop_type is not among them. Searching for `--script`, `extends SceneTree` and `extends MainLoop` outside tests also found nothing, so the related `godot --script` SceneTree-script mode is missing too. The `"_initialize"`/`"_finalize"` string hits are only ClassDB registrations (class_db.rs:7883/7886, plus other classes' _initialize at 11762/27182/29638) and test files, with no runtime dispatcher. MainLoop::step (main_loop.rs:3613) and step_traced (:4577) have no script-loop hook. MISSING is the right status. Priority 3 is defensible because a custom main_loop_type is rare in shipped games; scripted SceneTree tooling is a little more common, but not enough to raise it.
acceptance_criteria: A project whose main_loop_type script prints in _initialize and returns true from _process on frame 3 boots via patina-runner, prints once, and quits after frame 3 (test: `custom_main_loop_type_drives_frames`).

title: Web audio: feed the MainLoop's AudioServer into the AudioWorklet instead of a private demo server
description:
[audit-key: audio/audio-web-backend] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** browser page -> WebEngineHandle frame -> MainLoop::step -> AudioServerBridge::process -> ring -> AudioWorkletProcessor

**Godot ground truth:** platform/web/audio_driver_web.cpp (AudioDriverWeb feeds the one AudioServer); servers/audio/audio_server.cpp _driver_process

**Patina today:** crates/patina-web/src/audio.rs:81-127 WebAudioEngine owns its OWN `AudioServer::with_sample_rate` separate from any MainLoop; web_audio.rs:137-147 only exposes playTone/playEncoded. crates/patina-web/src/browser_runtime.rs (Runtime{engine: WebEngine,...} lines 51-75) and engine.rs contain zero references to audio/attach_output (grep -n 'audio\|Audio' browser_runtime.rs engine.rs = 0 hits). patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs:678-681 wasm default_audio_output returns None and relies on set_audio_output, which nothing on the web path calls (grep -rln 'attach_output\|audio_bridge' crates --include=*.rs minus tests = main_loop.rs, audio_server_bridge.rs, editor_server.rs, bootstrap.rs, patina-runner main.rs only). Result: on web, AudioServerBridge::process (audio_server_bridge.rs:390-396) mixes into last_mix and discards it -> every AudioStreamPlayer in a web game is silent. Also gdaudio/Cargo.toml: minimp3 is native-only, so MP3 streams report UnsupportedFormat on wasm with no decodeAudioData fallback; sample_pool.rs (web sample-playback path) has no caller outside its module (grep 'sample_pool\|SamplePool' = lib.rs:17 only).

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: the Web export has exactly one AudioServer; AudioDriverWeb (platform/web/audio_driver_web.cpp) pulls mixed frames from it into an AudioWorklet, so every AudioStreamPlayer in a running scene is audible after the first-gesture unlock. Patina: WebAudioEngine (patina-web/src/audio.rs:81-127) constructs its own AudioServer used only by playTone/playEncoded (web_audio.rs:137-147), while the scene's MainLoop (browser_runtime.rs Runtime/WebEngine) owns a separate AudioServerBridge with no output attached, so AudioServerBridge::process (gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:390-396) writes to last_mix and drops it. Implement: (1) give WebAudioEngine a mode that wraps an AudioOutputStream ring rather than a server, i.e. implement gdaudio::AudioOutputStream for the WebAudioOutput ring producer; (2) in browser_runtime.rs, when the page starts audio, call main_loop.audio_bridge_mut().attach_output(Box::new(ring_producer)) so the bridge's mix_and_write path fills the ring the worklet drains via pullBlock; (3) honor audio/driver/mix_rate when building it; (4) on wasm, decode MP3 via a JS decodeAudioData hook or a pure-Rust decoder (e.g. a no-C mp3 crate) so AudioStreamMP3 is not silently UnsupportedFormat. Wiring requirement: browser page -> WebEngineHandle frame -> MainLoop::step -> AudioServerBridge::process -> ring -> AudioWorkletProcessor.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/audio.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/browser_runtime.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/engine.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/web_output.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene with an autoplaying AudioStreamPlayer loaded into the web runtime produces non-silent frames from the same pull function the worklet calls (pullBlock), with no playTone call; the frames come from the MainLoop's bridge (stopping the player silences them). Native test drives WebEngine + MainLoop with the attached ring and asserts non-zero RMS in pulled blocks and zero after stop (test: `web_runtime_scene_audio_reaches_worklet_ring`); plus scripts/check-wasm.sh builds.

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. grep -n -i 'audio' crates/patina-web/src/browser_runtime.rs crates/patina-web/src/engine.rs = 0 hits; WebEngine (engine.rs:23-32) owns a MainLoop with no output. WebAudioEngine::new builds a private AudioServer::with_sample_rate (audio.rs:118), and web_audio.rs:126-145 exposes only pullBlock/playTone/playEncoded. Files referencing attach_output|audio_bridge|set_audio_output outside tests: main_loop.rs, audio_server_bridge.rs, editor_server.rs, patina-runner bootstrap.rs, main.rs. None of them is in patina-web. The only JS host, crates/patina-web/web/index.html:96-108, calls startWebAudio(44100), pullBlock and playTone, so nothing routes MainLoop audio. gdaudio/Cargo.toml:24-31 gates minimp3 to non-wasm and its comment says web reports UnsupportedFormat. The only SamplePool users outside sample_pool.rs are lib.rs:17 and gdaudio/tests.
acceptance_criteria: A scene with an autoplaying AudioStreamPlayer loaded into the web runtime produces non-silent frames from the same pull function the worklet calls (pullBlock), with no playTone call; the frames come from the MainLoop's bridge (stopping the player silences them). Native test drives WebEngine + MainLoop with the attached ring and asserts non-zero RMS in pulled blocks and zero after stop (test: `web_runtime_scene_audio_reaches_worklet_ring`); plus scripts/check-wasm.sh builds.

title: OS/Time: route script clocks and randomize() through wasm-safe time sources
description:
[audit-key: platform-os/platform-os-wasm-clock] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** browser rAF -> WebEngine -> MainLoop.step -> script _process calling Time.get_ticks_msec()/randomize() must not panic

**Godot ground truth:** core/os/time.cpp (get_ticks_msec/usec, get_unix_time_from_system); platform/web/os_web.cpp (OS_Unix clock via emscripten); @GlobalScope randomize()

**Patina today:** gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:19536 imports std::time::{Instant, SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH}; :19645-19650 process_epoch()/ticks_msec() use std Instant::now; OS.get_ticks_msec/usec (:19919/:19927) and Time.get_ticks_* (:29690/:29698) go through it; Time.get_unix_time_from_system (:29706) and system_unix_seconds (:30109) use SystemTime::now; GDScript randomize() (:6730) uses std::time::SystemTime::now. The repo itself documents both panic on wasm32-unknown-unknown: gdplatform/src/os.rs:9-15 (switched to web_time for that reason) and gdcore/src/rng.rs:142. patina-web links gdscene -> gdscript-interop (gdscene/Cargo.toml:14), so this is the browser script path. Native tests are green, which hides it.

**Implement:** Godot: OS.get_ticks_msec/usec, Time.get_ticks_*, Time.get_unix_time_from_system and randomize() all work in the web export (core/os/time.cpp; emscripten clock = performance.now/Date.now). Patina: interpreter.rs:19536 imports std::time::{Instant, SystemTime}; process_epoch (:19645), Time.get_unix_time_from_system (:29706), system_unix_seconds (:30109) and randomize() (:6730) call std Instant::now/SystemTime::now, which panic on wasm32-unknown-unknown (documented in gdplatform/src/os.rs:9-15 and gdcore/src/rng.rs:142). Fix: delete the interpreter's private epoch and call gdplatform::os::get_ticks_msec/usec (already web_time based); add gdplatform::os::unix_time_secs_f64() backed by web_time::SystemTime (or js_sys::Date::now on wasm) and use it for Time.* and system_unix_seconds; make randomize() call gdcore::rng::randomize() / its wasm-safe entropy. Grep interpreter.rs for any remaining std::time::Instant/SystemTime and remove them. Wiring: browser rAF -> WebEngine -> MainLoop.step -> script _process calling Time.get_ticks_msec()/randomize() must not panic.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/os.rs`

**Prove it:** A GDScript _ready that calls randomize(), OS.get_ticks_msec(), Time.get_ticks_usec() and Time.get_unix_time_from_system() runs through MainLoop without panicking, ticks are monotonic across two steps, unix time is > 1.7e9; a source-level guard asserts interpreter.rs contains no std::time::Instant::now / SystemTime::now; and the crate still passes cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p patina-web (test: `os_time_clock_is_wasm_safe`).

**Verifier note:** I could not refute it. interpreter.rs:19536 has an unconditional `use std::time::{Instant, SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH}` with no cfg gate. :19646 is PROCESS_EPOCH.get_or_init(Instant::now). :29706 and :30109 call SystemTime::now. randomize() at :6730 calls std::time::SystemTime::now. gdplatform/src/os.rs:9-15 states that std Instant panics on wasm32 and switches that module to web_time. grep 'web_time|web-time' in the gdscript-interop, gdscene and patina-web Cargo.toml files: 0 hits. patina-web/Cargo.toml:35 depends on gdscene, and gdscene/Cargo.toml:14 depends on gdscript-interop, so this code runs on the browser path. P0 holds: common script calls crash the web runtime.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript _ready that calls randomize(), OS.get_ticks_msec(), Time.get_ticks_usec() and Time.get_unix_time_from_system() runs through MainLoop without panicking, ticks are monotonic across two steps, unix time is > 1.7e9; a source-level guard asserts interpreter.rs contains no std::time::Instant::now / SystemTime::now; and the crate still passes cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p patina-web (test: `os_time_clock_is_wasm_safe`).

title: Environment: screen-space reflections and volumetric fog in the wgpu 3D renderer
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/render3d-forward-plus-only] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

The finder marked this OUT_OF_SCOPE (Godot's web export is Compatibility-only). The verifier overturned that: no Patina scope document limits rendering to Compatibility, Patina ships desktop targets (tests/docs_suite/docs_phase7_desktop_platform_targets_test.rs) where Godot defaults to Forward+, and the wgpu 3D renderer already does Forward+-class work (a fog-volume pass in gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs). This bead was written from the finding by the audit operator, because the finder supplied no bead spec for an out-of-scope finding.

**Godot ground truth:** Environment.xml:306 (ssr_enabled, ssr_max_steps, ssr_fade_in, ssr_fade_out, ssr_depth_tolerance) and :362 (volumetric_fog_enabled, volumetric_fog_density, volumetric_fog_albedo, volumetric_fog_emission, volumetric_fog_length, volumetric_fog_anisotropy, ...). Both are Forward+ features.
**Patina today:** Environment3D (gdserver3d/src/environment.rs:190-308) has none of these. grep `ssr_|volumetric_fog` across gdserver3d/gdrender3d gives 0 hits. ClassDB Environment does not register the properties.
**Implement:** (1) Register the ssr_* and volumetric_fog_* properties on Environment with Godot defaults (doc XML). (2) Carry them into Environment3D when a WorldEnvironment loads from .tscn. (3) In the wgpu pipeline, add a screen-space reflection pass: ray-march the depth buffer, honour max_steps and depth_tolerance, fade by ssr_fade_in/out. Then add volumetric fog: a froxel or ray-marched pass using density and albedo, composited before tonemap. Reuse the existing fog-volume pass inputs where possible.
**Wiring requirement:** .tscn WorldEnvironment -> Environment resource -> Environment3D -> wgpu render frame passes.
**Prove it:** Load a 3D scene with a reflective floor, a bright cube and WorldEnvironment ssr_enabled=true. The rendered frame's floor pixels below the cube must be brighter than with ssr_enabled=false. With volumetric_fog_enabled=true and density 0.1, distant pixels must move toward the fog albedo, compared with fog off.
**SSIL and SDFGI** are deliberately left out of this bead (P3, separate).
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn 3D scene with a reflective floor, a bright cube and WorldEnvironment ssr_enabled=true renders measurably brighter floor pixels under the cube than with ssr_enabled=false; with volumetric_fog_enabled=true (density 0.1), distant pixels shift toward volumetric_fog_albedo compared with fog off. (test: `environment_ssr_and_volumetric_fog_render`)

title: FogVolume: shader_type fog shaders drive fog-volume density/albedo/emission
description:
[audit-key: shaders/shader-fog] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

The finder marked this OUT_OF_SCOPE. The verifier overturned that: Patina's wgpu renderer already implements FogVolume and FogMaterial (gdserver3d/src/fog_volume.rs:141-145; gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs:19, :2591, :3430). So a ShaderMaterial on a FogVolume is a missing part of an existing feature, and no Patina scope document exempts it. This bead was written by the audit operator, because the finder supplied no bead spec.

**Godot ground truth:** servers/rendering/shader_types.cpp, the `fog` shader type. Built-ins: WORLD_POSITION, OBJECT_POSITION, UVW, SIZE, SDF, EXTENTS, TIME. Outputs: DENSITY, ALBEDO, EMISSION. FogVolume.material accepts a ShaderMaterial with `shader_type fog`.
**Patina today:** ShaderType3D has only Spatial and Sky (gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:23-28). grep `shader_type\s+fog` over engine-rs/crates gives 0 hits.
**Implement:** Add a Fog variant to the shader type enum and parser, with the built-ins and outputs above. In the fog-volume pass, when FogVolume.material is a ShaderMaterial with shader_type fog, evaluate the shader per sample for DENSITY/ALBEDO/EMISSION, instead of using the FogMaterial constants.
**Wiring requirement:** .tscn FogVolume with material=ShaderMaterial(shader_type fog) -> fog-volume pass in wgpu_pipeline.rs.
**Prove it:** A scene with a FogVolume whose fog shader sets DENSITY = 0.0 for UVW.x < 0.5 and 1.0 otherwise. The rendered frame shows fog over only one half of the volume's screen footprint.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn scene with a FogVolume whose ShaderMaterial (shader_type fog) sets DENSITY = 0.0 where UVW.x < 0.5 and 1.0 otherwise renders fog over only one half of the volume's screen footprint. (test: `fog_volume_shader_type_fog_density`)

title: Conformance gate: run fixture projects through patina-runner and diff against headless-Godot oracle traces
description:
[audit-key: conformance/oracle-gate] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

Why: the 2026-10-30 audit found 93 UNWIRED and 19 STUB features behind beads that closed green. The `*_parity_test.rs` suites compare Patina with itself. Real Godot is installed (`/Applications/Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot`, 4.6.1), and `tools/oracle/` already has the probes (frame_trace_capture, signal_tracer, notification_tracer, render_capture, property_dumper, run_fixture.gd). What is missing is running whole PROJECTS through Patina's SHIPPING path and diffing the result against Godot, as a gate.

**Godot ground truth:** headless Godot runs each project for N frames with the tools/oracle probes as autoloads and records a JSON envelope: per-frame print/signal/notification traces, the final scene tree with properties, and optional frame captures.
**Patina today:** tools/oracle_compare.sh points at a stale Godot path (/Users/bone/Downloads/...). `fixtures/patina_outputs/` holds self-generated outputs. Nothing runs a project end to end through `patina_runner::bootstrap` and compares it.
**Implement:**
1. `engine-rs/fixtures/conformance/<name>/`: small, complete Godot projects (project.godot plus scenes and scripts). Seed them by promoting suitable `fixtures/scenes/*.tscn` and adding at least 4 game-shaped projects that hit the P0 seams of epic pat-mgixk:
   - (a) a Timer `timeout` connected in the .tscn to `queue_free` on a scriptless node, plus a Button connected to Label.hide;
   - (b) `get_parent().call_deferred("add_child", n)`;
   - (c) `@onready var x = $Child` with `!`/`&&`/`:=` syntax;
   - (d) an input action from project.godot moving a CharacterBody2D, plus a CanvasLayer HUD Label.
2. `tools/oracle/conformance_capture.py`: runs each project in headless Godot (`--headless --fixed-fps 60 --quit-after N`, probes injected as autoloads through a temporary override.cfg, never edited into the project) and writes `engine-rs/fixtures/golden/conformance/<name>.json`. It is re-run only on an explicit bless.
3. Patina side: `patina-runner` gains `--trace-out <file> --frames N`, which emits the same envelope from the real bootstrap and MainLoop path (scripts, signals and deferred calls exactly as a game runs them).
4. `engine-rs/tests/conformance_suite/` (a new grouped binary) boots every project in-process through patina_runner, diffs it against its golden (exact for traces and tree shape, tolerances for floats), and prints a per-project PASS/FAIL table. It asserts that the pass count is >= `engine-rs/fixtures/golden/conformance/baseline.json`. The baseline is a ratchet: raise it when projects start passing, and never lower it without an operator note.

title: SceneTree.reparent replays _ready(): instantiate()+add_child() runs _ready twice
description:
[review 2026-10-30] Found by /code-review on uncommitted swarm work (not yet committed when filed).

**Bug:** `reparent` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:~2971) now calls LifecycleManager::enter_tree, which re-runs READY and process_script_ready for the whole moved subtree. SceneTreeAccessor::add_child (gdscene/src/scripting.rs:~6313) routes every already-parented node through reparent, and instantiate_packed_scene parents its result under root. So `var e = scene.instantiate(); add_child(e)` fires _enter_tree and _ready a second time. Editor drag-reparent (gdeditor/src/lib.rs:829/842) also runs user callbacks.
**Godot ground truth:** Node::_propagate_ready runs _ready once per node unless request_ready() was called. Reparenting fires exit/enter tree notifications but not READY (scene/main/node.cpp).
**Fix:** on reparent, propagate EXIT_TREE/ENTER_TREE only; skip READY for nodes whose ready-once flag is set; honour request_ready(). Make PackedScene.instantiate() return a detached subtree so add_child is a plain add, not a reparent.
**Wiring requirement:** GDScript `scene.instantiate()` -> `add_child()` -> SceneTree lifecycle inside MainLoop.
**Prove it:** a .tscn whose child script counts _ready calls in a global; the parent instantiates it and add_child()s it in _ready; after 2 frames via patina_runner the count == 1. Reparenting it later also leaves the count at 1, while _enter_tree fired twice.
acceptance_criteria: Instantiating a packed scene and add_child()-ing it from GDScript, booted through patina_runner, runs the child's _ready exactly once; a later reparent fires _exit_tree/_enter_tree but not _ready again. (test: `instantiate_add_child_ready_runs_once`)

title: Interpreter: grow the stack once per segment, not on every call at depth multiples of 8
description:
[review 2026-10-30] Found by /code-review on uncommitted swarm work (not yet committed when filed).

**Bug:** gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:~8362 with_script_call_stack calls stacker::grow (a fresh 4 MiB mmap'd segment with a guard page) for EVERY script call made while call_depth % 8 == 0. A helper called in a 10k-iteration loop from depth 8 does 10k mmap/munmap round-trips.
**Fix:** use stacker::maybe_grow(STACK_RED_ZONE, STACK_GROWTH, ..), which only allocates when remaining stack < red zone, or record the depth at which the current segment was allocated. Keep max_recursion_depth and max_recursion_depth_through_an_expression_context green.
**Wiring requirement:** GDScript function calls inside MainLoop _process.
**Prove it:** a script at call depth 8 that calls a trivial helper 10,000 times completes, and a debug counter on stack-segment allocations (cfg(test) atomic) stays <= 2. The recursion-limit tests still return MaxRecursionDepth.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript loop at call depth 8 calling a helper 10,000 times allocates at most 2 stack segments (counted by a test-only counter), and runaway recursion still yields MaxRecursionDepth without aborting. (test: `script_calls_do_not_regrow_stack_per_call`)

title: JavaScriptBridge: pump JS callbacks each frame and define the PWA/fs-sync shell hooks
description:
[audit-key: platform-os/platform-os-jsbridge] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** platform/web/javascript_bridge_singleton.cpp (create_callback invokes the Callable when JS calls it; pwa_update_available signal); platform/web/os_web.cpp:258-279 (update_pwa_state_callback emits pwa_update_available, force_fs_sync, pwa_update)

**Patina today:** Interpreter::pump_javascript_callbacks defined at gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:15357; the only callers are gdscript-interop/tests/javascript_bridge_wasm.rs:238-269 (grep 'pump_javascript_callbacks' and 'take_callback_invocations' across crates: no runtime caller in gdscene/patina-web/gdeditor). So a JS function from create_callback queues invocations forever. gdplatform/src/js_bridge.rs:788-818 reads globals __patina_pwa_update_pending, __patina_pwa_update and __patina_fs_sync; grep for those names across engine-rs (*.rs, *.js, *.html) finds them only in js_bridge.rs, so the export shell (gdplatform/src/web_export.rs) never defines them. pwa_update_available is registered (gdobject/src/class_db.rs:25912) but no code emits it.

**Implement:** Godot: a Callable wrapped by JavaScriptBridge.create_callback runs when JavaScript calls the returned function (javascript_bridge_singleton.cpp); the PWA service worker triggers OS_Web::update_pwa_state_callback, which emits JavaScriptBridge.pwa_update_available (os_web.cpp:258); force_fs_sync flushes IDBFS. Patina: the queue in gdplatform/src/js_bridge.rs:447-460 is filled by the wasm closure, but Interpreter::pump_javascript_callbacks (interpreter.rs:15357) is called only from tests, so callbacks never run. The shell globals __patina_pwa_update(_pending) and __patina_fs_sync that js_bridge.rs:788-818 reads are defined nowhere. Fix: (1) call pump_javascript_callbacks for each script interpreter from MainLoop::step at the start of the process phase (gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, next to the existing per-frame script hooks), so callbacks run on the main thread at a frame boundary; (2) in web_export.rs's generated shell, define __patina_fs_sync (flush the patina-web vfs IndexedDB write-back), __patina_pwa_update (postMessage skipWaiting to the waiting service worker and reload) and set __patina_pwa_update_pending from the SW 'updatefound' event; (3) when the pending flag goes false->true, emit pwa_update_available on the JavaScriptBridge singleton.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/web_export.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** With a test JsBackend installed, a scene script that does `cb = JavaScriptBridge.create_callback(_on_js)` and then has the backend queue an invocation with args sees _on_js called with those args after one MainLoop.step, with no manual pump call; the exported index.html defines __patina_fs_sync, __patina_pwa_update and the pending flag; flipping the pending flag emits pwa_update_available to a connected script handler (test: `javascript_bridge_callbacks_fire_from_main_loop`).

**Verifier note:** grep -rn 'pump_javascript_callbacks|take_callback_invocations' across crates, excluding /tests/: the only hits are the definition (interpreter.rs:15357), doc comments in js_bridge.rs, and js_bridge.rs's own in-module test (:940). Nothing in gdscene, patina-web or patina-runner calls them. grep -rl '__patina_pwa_update|__patina_fs_sync' across engine-rs and apps: only gdplatform/src/js_bridge.rs and its rustdoc HTML copy under target/doc, so web_export.rs does not define the hooks. P0 is reasonable: create_callback is documented as working, but it silently does nothing.
acceptance_criteria: With a test JsBackend installed, a scene script that does `cb = JavaScriptBridge.create_callback(_on_js)` and then has the backend queue an invocation with args sees _on_js called with those args after one MainLoop.step, with no manual pump call; the exported index.html defines __patina_fs_sync, __patina_pwa_update and the pending flag; flipping the pending flag emits pwa_update_available to a connected script handler (test: `javascript_bridge_callbacks_fire_from_main_loop`).

comments.text:
AUDIT ONLY, NOTHING WRITTEN YET (TurquoiseCastle). The bead's three claims all check out, but part (1) as written has a correctness trap that I want to settle before touching two of the hottest files in the repo.

=== THE BEAD'S CLAIMS: ALL CONFIRMED ===
- `Interpreter::pump_javascript_callbacks` has NO runtime caller. Every hit outside its own definition is a doc comment, `js_bridge.rs`'s in-module test, or `gdscript-interop/tests/javascript_bridge_wasm.rs`. So a `create_callback` function queues invocations forever.
- ⚠️ Line numbers have DRIFTED since the audit: the fn is at `interpreter.rs:15976`, not :15357. `JS_CALLBACKS` is at :22161 and `create_callback` at :22291. Worth re-greping rather than trusting the bead's line refs.

=== FILE CONTENTION: THE TWO HOTTEST FILES IN THE REPO ===
Both of my main targets carry heavy uncommitted peer WIP right now:
- `gdscene/src/main_loop.rs` (mtime 3 min old) — SEVEN other beads in its diff: pat-0q2kx.200, mgixk.25, mgixk.27, mgixk.37, mgixk.38, s3rrv.77, s3rrv.94
- `gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` (10 min) — FOURTEEN: mgixk.10/.14/.18/.19/.20/.21/.40, nzgdu.6, s3rrv.19/.34/.57/.67/.265, z35r2.3
- `gdplatform/src/web_export.rs` (15 h) and `js_bridge.rs` (Jul 27) are cold and clean — parts (2) and (3) are uncontended.

So whatever I do in main_loop.rs must be ONE call site and nothing else, and I will guard both writes on st_mtime_ns.

=== *** THE TRAP IN PART (1): "call it for each script interpreter" IS NOT SAFE AS WRITTEN *** ===
The bead says "call pump_javascript_callbacks for each script interpreter from MainLoop::step". Three facts make a naive loop silently wrong:

1. Every `GDScriptNodeInstance` owns its OWN `Interpreter` (`scripting.rs:154`, private field).
2. The invocation queue is PROCESS-GLOBAL and `take_callback_invocations()` (`js_bridge.rs:455`) `mem::take`s the WHOLE thing. So the first interpreter pumped drains every other script's invocations too.
3. `JS_CALLBACKS` (`interpreter.rs:22161`) is a **thread_local shared by all interpreters**, so the first interpreter RESOLVES those foreign ids rather than skipping them — and then runs them via `self.invoke_callable(..)` on ITSELF.

And `CallableRef::Method { target_id, method }` documents `target_id: 0` as "for self" (`gdvariant/src/variant.rs:27-32`). `create_callback` stores `(**callable).clone()` verbatim, so a script's `create_callback(_on_js)` parks a self-relative method reference. Run it on the wrong interpreter and `_on_js` dispatches against the wrong instance — wrong member vars — and `pump_javascript_callbacks` swallows the error (`if self.invoke_callable(..).is_ok()`), so it fails SILENTLY.

Net: with two scripted nodes, script B's JS callback gets drained by script A, executed against A's instance, and either does the wrong thing or errors invisibly. A one-script acceptance test passes either way, which is what makes this worth writing down rather than discovering later.

=== WHAT I INTEND TO DO ABOUT IT ===
The pump needs per-interpreter OWNERSHIP so each drains only its own ids and LEAVES the rest queued. Neither `JS_CALLBACKS` nor `NEXT_JS_CALLBACK` records an owner today, so re-queueing alone cannot discriminate — every interpreter can resolve every id.

Cheapest correct shape, still additive and contained:
- give each `Interpreter` an identity (it may already have one — to check), record it beside the callable when `create_callback` registers the id, and
- replace the blanket drain with a take-what-I-own call in `js_bridge.rs` (e.g. `take_callback_invocations_matching(|id| ..)`, or return the unhandled remainder and push it back), so a foreign invocation stays queued for the frame's later pumps.

That keeps `main_loop.rs` to a single call site and puts the real logic in the two COLD files plus a small, local change to the pump — which is also the right split for a contended file.

I will confirm whether `Interpreter` already carries a usable id before inventing one.

=== STILL TO DO ===
(1) ownership + the MainLoop call site; (2) `__patina_fs_sync` / `__patina_pwa_update` / `__patina_pwa_update_pending` in `web_export.rs`'s generated shell (confirmed absent: the only hits across engine-rs are `js_bridge.rs:788-818` reading them); (3) emit `pwa_update_available` on the false->true edge (registered at `class_db.rs:25912`, emitted nowhere); and the acceptance test `javascript_bridge_callbacks_fire_from_main_loop`.

UNBUILT: the worker build guard blocks the toolchain; nothing written yet.

=== WHAT I FIRST THOUGHT WAS A BLOCKER, AND WHY IT IS NOT ===
`JavaScriptBridge` has NO object id: it is dispatched by name-matching on the identifier (`interpreter.rs:4271` -> `call_javascriptbridge_static(member, args)`). `connect_signal(source: u64, ..)` needs a source object id, so a script cannot connect to it through the node SignalStore, and `grep` for `emit_singleton_signal` across the workspace finds nothing. - `connect` / `disconnect` / `is_connected` arms in the STATIC dispatch that only touch the registry (`connect` returns `Int(0)`, Godot's OK),

So the pattern to copy is in-tree and proven. (This is why "trace it to the destination before naming a blocker" is worth doing: the first thing that looked like a wall had a door 25k lines away.)

=== THE DESIGN, INCLUDING THE TRAP ===
Mirror CameraServer for JavaScriptBridge:
1. `JS_BRIDGE_CONNECTIONS: RefCell<Vec<JsBridgeConnection>>` thread_local beside `JS_CALLBACKS`.
2. `connect` / `disconnect` / `is_connected` arms in `call_javascriptbridge_static`.
3. Emission from an `Interpreter` method, called once per frame.

⚠️ **THE SAME OWNERSHIP TRAP AS PART 1.** `CAMERA_SERVER_CONNECTIONS` stores only `(String, CallableRef)`. A `CallableRef::Method { target_id: 0, .. }` means "self", so a connection registered by script B and invoked by script A's interpreter runs against A's instance. CameraServer presumably has this bug today; it is not mine to fix, but I must not copy it. So each connection records the registering `current_node_id`, exactly like `JsCallbackEntry`, and each interpreter emits only to its OWN connections.

⚠️ **EDGE DETECTION MUST BE PER-INTERPRETER, NOT GLOBAL.** The pending flag is a single JS global. If the false->true edge were tracked in one thread_local, only the first interpreter to poll would see it and every other script's handler would never fire. Tracking `last_pwa_pending: bool` as a field ON the interpreter makes each one independently see the edge once and emit to its own handlers once — which IS Godot's semantics (one signal, every connected handler runs once). No cross-interpreter coordination needed.

4. Where the poll goes: the per-frame hook ALREADY EXISTS from part 1 — `ScriptInstance::pump_js_callbacks` -> `Interpreter::pump_javascript_callbacks`. The PWA edge check is the same job (browser state reaching the engine at a frame boundary), so it belongs in that same call rather than a second walk of the tree. That keeps main_loop.rs at the one statement it already has.

Adding one `bool` field to `Interpreter` is the only structural change; `Interpreter::new` looks like the sole construction site, and I will confirm that by TYPE-SPELLING grep (`Interpreter {`), not by name — the pat-mgixk.39 lesson.

The three globals (`__patina_pwa_update_pending` boolean, `__patina_pwa_update` and `__patina_fs_sync` zero-arg functions, all on `globalThis`, contract pinned at js_bridge.rs:834-863) go into `DEFAULT_SHELL` (web_export.rs:425, `<script type="module">` at :446, which already imports `WebVfs` for the fs-sync flush).

So the `updatefound` event that is supposed to SET the pending flag has no source, and the flag could never flip no matter what else is correct. Registering the worker (gated on `pwa_enabled`) has to come first. `render_html_shell` is pure `{{PATINA_*}}` substitution, so this is plain shell text and needs no new substitution key.

(a) web_export.rs: SW registration + the three globals. Cold file, no contention, self-contained.
(b) interpreter.rs: connection registry + connect/disconnect/is_connected + the per-interpreter edge poll folded into `pump_javascript_callbacks`.

title: Parser: bound unary and ternary-else recursion by MAX_EXPR_DEPTH too
description:
[review 2026-10-30] Found by /code-review on uncommitted swarm work (not yet committed when filed).

**Bug:** gdscript-interop/src/parser.rs:~1621 counts depth only in parse_expr. parse_unary recurses into itself and parse_ternary recurses for the else branch (~1457) without passing parse_expr, so `-`*5000+'1', `not not ... x`, and long `a if c else b if c else ...` chains still overflow the stack and abort the process.
**Fix:** bump and check expr_depth in parse_unary and in the ternary-else recursion (or route both through a guarded helper), returning a ParseError at the limit.
**Wiring requirement:** script source -> GDScript parser when a .gd attached to a scene loads.
**Prove it:** parsing 5000 leading `-`, 5000 `not`, and a 5000-deep ternary-else chain each returns a parse error. The test binary does not abort.
acceptance_criteria: Parsing GDScript with 5000 nested unary minus, 5000 `not`, or a 5000-deep ternary-else chain returns a parse error instead of aborting the process. (test: `parser_bounds_unary_and_ternary_depth`)

title: ClassDB: has_method excludes unimplemented virtuals (_get, _to_string, Texture2D _draw...)
description:
[review 2026-10-30] Found by /code-review on uncommitted swarm work (not yet committed when filed).

**Bug:** gdobject/src/class_db.rs:~1093 now registers _get/_set/_get_property_list/_to_string on Object, and Texture2D _get_width/_get_height/_draw_rect (~22885). class_has_method does not distinguish virtuals, so has_method('_to_string') is true for EVERY object and `obj.call('_to_string')` returns Nil silently.
**Godot ground truth:** ClassDB::get_method excludes GDVIRTUAL entries; Object::has_method is true for a virtual only when the script implements it.
**Fix:** mark virtual methods in the registration (flag), exclude them from class_has_method/has_method, and answer true only when the attached script defines them.
**Wiring requirement:** GDScript `obj.has_method()` on a scene node -> ClassDB lookup.
**Prove it:** in a booted scene, a plain Node answers has_method('_to_string') == false, a scripted node that defines _to_string answers true, and has_method('get_name') stays true.
acceptance_criteria: In a scene booted through patina_runner, has_method('_to_string') is false on an unscripted Node and true on a node whose script defines it, while has_method('get_name') stays true. (test: `has_method_excludes_unimplemented_virtuals`)

title: Post-import scripts: a runtime error in _post_import fails the import
description:
[review 2026-10-30] Found by /code-review on uncommitted swarm work (not yet committed when filed).

**Bug:** gdeditor/src/script_post_import.rs:~186 treats None from tree.call_script_method as 'not overridden', but call_script_method also returns None on a runtime error (scene_tree.rs:~5370 only logs at debug). A post-import script that errors halfway imports the unmodified scene with no error shown.
**Godot ground truth:** EditorScenePostImport failure fails the import with an error.
**Fix:** check script.has_method('_post_import') separately; when it exists and the call errors, fail the import with the script error text.
**Wiring requirement:** editor import pipeline -> post-import script -> import result surfaced by the editor server.
**Prove it:** importing a .glb whose post-import script divides by zero reports an import error naming the script, and no imported scene is written.
acceptance_criteria: Re-importing a scene whose post-import script raises a runtime error reports an import failure naming the script and writes no imported scene, while a script without _post_import imports normally. (test: `post_import_runtime_error_fails_import`)

title: Project Settings: full General tree with Advanced toggle, feature overrides, Localization and Globals tabs, persisted to project.godot
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-project-settings-tree] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL] [split from pat-mgixk.16 on 2026-10-31]

**Goal:** Project Settings shows and edits every ProjectSettings key, the way Godot's General tab does, and the edits reach both project.godot and the running game.

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/settings/project_settings_editor.cpp. The General tab is an inspector over all ProjectSettings with an Advanced filter, Add/Delete for custom properties, and feature-override rows (`key.web`). The other tabs are Localization (translations, remaps, POT), Globals (autoload, shader globals, global groups), Plugins and Import Defaults.

**Patina today:** the dialog (editor_ui.rs ~:3708-3792) holds ~20 hand-curated fields. `api_get_project_settings` (editor_server.rs ~:22454) returns fixed categories. project_settings_dialog.rs has an advanced flag and a show_advanced model, but nothing outside its own file uses `ProjectSettingsDialog`. Wire that, or delete it; don't build a second one. Nothing edits internationalization/locale/*.

**Implement:**
1. `GET /api/project_settings/all` returns every key with its type, hint, default and basic/advanced flag. Defaults come from the gdresource ProjectSettings plus Godot's doc XML ProjectSettings.xml.
2. Render a searchable, sectioned tree with the inspector's property editors. POST set, add-custom, delete and override (`key.feature`), and persist to project.godot.
3. Localization tab for translations and remaps; Globals tab for global groups and shader globals.
4. The runtime honors feature-tag overrides (`.web` on the web build) when it reads settings.

**Wiring requirement:** the served editor's HTTP API, then project.godot on disk, then the running game's settings. The test boots `EditorServerHandle::start` on a temp project and drives it over HTTP; asserting on `ProjectSettingsDialog` alone does not count.

**Prove it:** Over HTTP, search `physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second`, set it to 120, add a `.web` override of 30, and save. project.godot contains both keys. Adding translation res://t.po writes internationalization/locale/translations. Play reports Engine.physics_ticks_per_second == 120 on the native runner.
acceptance_criteria: Through the served editor over HTTP: setting physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second=120 with a `.web` override of 30 writes both keys to project.godot; adding res://t.po writes internationalization/locale/translations; Play reports Engine.physics_ticks_per_second == 120. (test: `project_settings_general_tree_persists_overrides`)

title: Runner: booting a project directory never attaches main-scene GDScripts (no _ready, no prints)
description:
[found by the conformance gate, 2026-10-31] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** running a project (`godot --path <dir>`) instances `application/run/main_scene` with every node's attached script, then runs `_enter_tree`/`_ready` and the frame loop.

**Patina today:** the project-directory boot path never attaches GDScripts to main-scene nodes.
- `project_boot::boot_project` (patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs) instances the main scene and the autoloads. Only script *autoloads* get a script.
- `run_booted_project` (main.rs:548), used for `patina-runner <project_dir>` and for a .pck at main.rs:515/539, runs `LifecycleManager::enter_tree` with no attach step.
- `conformance::capture_project` (conformance.rs:266) copies that boot, so the gate sees it too.
- Only the single-`.tscn` path calls `attach_scripts` (main.rs:338, :744). A third copy in `bootstrap.rs:~530` is not on either path.

Evidence: `cargo nextest run --test conformance_suite --no-capture` reports 0/4 projects passing. Every project prints **zero** `[T]` lines, onready_syntax's Label keeps its scene value "idle" (Godot: "tick2"), and input_action_move's Player never moves (Godot: position 12, velocity 60).

**Implement:** attach scripts in ONE place, inside `boot_project`, after the main scene is instanced and before anything runs `enter_tree`. comments.author: bone
comments.text:
CLAIMED and ANALYSED, no code written (TurquoiseCastle). Static reading only.

=== WHAT THE FAILURE RULES OUT, WHICH IS THE GOOD NEWS ===
`editor_play_honors_project_settings_test.rs:293`:
  "the body must accelerate at the project's 490 px/s^2; measured 447.6 from
   vy=223.78 over 15 ticks of 0.03333s. A value near 980 means Play kept the
   engine default and the project's `physics/2d/default_gravity` never reached
   the solver."

447.6 is **not** 980. By the test's own stated discriminator, the project's gravity IS reaching the solver — so the bead's actual feature is working. What is failing is the MEASUREMENT, by about 9%.

Also note the earlier failure (log 12922) was `101, compile-error` on a peer's `gdeditor` break (`render_canvas_from_list` missing from `crate::viewport_2d_render`). That is fixed — the fn now exists at `gdscene/src/canvas_render.rs:3852` and this run compiled. So of .44's two failures, only one is about .44.

=== THE ARITHMETIC, AND WHY IT DOES NOT CLOSE ===
vy = 223.78, dt = 1/30, so the number of gravity integrations actually reflected is
  223.78 / (490 * 0.0333333) = **13.70**
against the 15 ticks the script counted. A non-integer, which is the part I cannot explain from reading alone.

The script samples inside `_physics_process`:
```
self.ticks = self.ticks + 1
self.dt = delta
self.vy = get_node("Body").linear_velocity.y
```
If `_physics_process` runs BEFORE that tick's integration, 15 calls reflect 14 integrations → vy 228.67 and measured_g 457.3. Closer, still not 447.6, and the test's tolerance is ±25 so even 457.3 would fail.

⚠️ **A HYPOTHESIS I FORMED AND THEN REFUTED, recorded so nobody re-walks it:** I thought a default `linear_damp` of 0.1 explained the residual, and the damped series does land near 223.7. It is wrong — `gdphysics2d::body`'s `linear_damp` documents "Defaults to `0.0`", and the 0.1 I found (`physics_server.rs:1876`) is for an **Area2D**, not a body. So damping is not the explanation and I have not found what the remaining ~1.3 ticks are.

=== WHAT I DID NOT DO, DELIBERATELY ===
I did not widen the ±25 tolerance. A tolerance that cannot accommodate the real integration offset is a fixture bug, and relaxing the comparison would convert a measurement question into a permanently weaker test — the acceptance's whole point is distinguishing 490 from 980, and a tolerance loose enough to swallow 447.6 is still nowhere near 980, but widening it is the wrong lever to reach for first.

=== THE MEASUREMENT THAT WOULD SETTLE IT ===
Make the script sample a SLOPE instead of an average from zero. Record vy at two known ticks and compute `(vy_b - vy_a) / ((b - a) * dt)`. That is immune to both the off-by-one on the first integration and to any constant offset, and it is the quantity the acceptance actually cares about ("the body must accelerate at 490"). Today's `vy / (ticks * dt)` is an average that silently assumes the first tick integrated and that vy started at exactly 0.

Cheapest diagnostic if someone has a build: print `dt` at full precision and vy at two ticks. That answers in one run whether the residual is a sampling offset or a real integration shortfall.

=== INHERITED WIP ===
`gdeditor/tests/editor_play_honors_project_settings_test.rs` is **UNTRACKED** (another agent's new test, mtime 00:02, ~1 h cold). `.44`'s declared Files is only `gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, which is clean. So the test is inherited; I have not edited it.

**What I changed, and why it holds:** assertion 2's old oracle required the group overlap to EQUAL the single-child area. BlackWaterfall's diagnosis was right that the premise was unsound — a group's scratch buffer is rasterized with a TRANSPARENT clear then composited with the group tint, which is not the alpha math of a 0.5 draw over the OPAQUE runtime clear, and a PointLight2D mixed lighting into both samples. ⚠️ `modulate`, not `self_modulate`, in the variant: `modulate` propagates to children so each blends at 0.5 individually — exactly what a missing `collect_canvas_groups` produces — whereas `self_modulate` does not inherit, which would have moved BOTH samples and destroyed the differential. The ungrouped branch also asserts `source != SCENE`, so a drifted `replace()` pattern cannot silently render the grouped scene twice.

**ASSERTION 4 IS NOT THE SAME CLASS OF ERROR — it is already a differential** (hemispherical vs flat normal, same scene otherwise), which is the right shape. So "no pixel differs" is a real negative, and I checked the whole chain rather than guessing. **Every link is present:**

**So the pipeline is intact and the production refactor is NOT what is failing.** The remaining suspects are fixture geometry and lighting, which is where I would look next:
1. **the `Lamp` PointLight2D's position/range vs the sampled band.** Assertion 4 samples canvas `(200+i, 60)` for i in 0..64. If the light does not reach that row, both renders are equally unlit and identical — a normal map changes nothing where there is no light. This is the cheapest thing to check and the most likely.

title: Render2D: move the canvas render list into a runtime crate and emit 2D frames from patina-runner (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/r2d-runtime-output] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** patina-runner main -> run_main_loop -> render entry -> PNG on disk; requestAnimationFrame -> WebEngine::frame -> WebEngine::render_frame -> canvas present

### 1. No 2D frame output from patina-runner or the browser runtime  (UNWIRED, P0)

**Godot ground truth:** main/main.cpp Main::iteration -> RenderingServer::draw; platform/web/display_server_web.cpp (canvas swap)

**Patina today:** The canvas render list lives only in gdeditor (crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs). patina-runner's Cargo.toml dependencies (gdcore, gdvariant, gdobject, gdresource, gdscene, gdaudio, gdplatform, gdscript-interop) include neither gdeditor nor gdrender2d. grep 'render|rasterize|FrameBuffer' in crates/patina-runner/src/main.rs returns nothing; only a 3D helper exists (src/render3d.rs). In patina-web, browser_runtime.rs:506-543 install_frame_loop only calls engine.frame(now_ms). start_engine (:556) never calls canvas::start_canvas_renderer, and the only draw primitive there is WebRenderer::present_clear (canvas.rs:146). start_engine also builds a bare Node2D tree (:560-563). So a running 2D game (native runner or web export) produces no pixels.

**Implement:** Godot: every Main::iteration ends with RenderingServer::draw, so the root viewport's canvas is rendered each frame wherever the game runs.
Patina: the only shipping 2D canvas pipeline (collect_canvas_items, rasterize_render_list*, shade_runtime_canvas, camera2d_view_transform, apply_stretch_transform) is in crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs. patina-runner and patina-web cannot reach it because neither depends on gdeditor, and gdeditor is an editor crate. The runner is headless (main.rs has no render calls).
Stage 1 (this bead): move the tree-to-render-list-to-FrameBuffer functions, plus TextureCache, into a runtime crate with no editor dependencies (gdrender2d, or a new gdscene::canvas_render module behind gdrender2d). gdeditor re-exports them so the editor keeps compiling. Add a runner flag `--frame-out <path.png>` (and `--frame-size WxH`). After the last frame it renders the current scene through the moved entry point and writes the PNG. Load textures through gdresource so sprites draw real pixels.
Stage 2 is the follow-up bead in this group: the web canvas.
Wiring: patina-runner main -> run_main_loop -> render entry -> PNG on disk.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/main.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/Cargo.toml`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/lib.rs`

**Prove it:** Run `patina-runner fixtures/<2d scene with Sprite2D + ColorRect + Label>.tscn --frames 3 --frame-out out.png` (exercised via the runner's tests/ harness spawning the binary). It writes a PNG whose pixel at the ColorRect centre matches its color within 1/255, and whose sprite region holds texture pixels, not the clear color. patina-runner must not depend on gdeditor (assert in the test by parsing Cargo.toml). (test: `runner_writes_2d_canvas_frame`)

**Verifier note:** patina-runner/Cargo.toml [dependencies] lists gdcore, gdvariant, gdobject, gdresource, gdscene, gdaudio, gdplatform, gdscript-interop, serde_json and tracing. It has no gdeditor or gdrender2d. main.rs CLI flags are --frames, --delta, --trace-frames, --event-trace and --main-pack, with no frame-out. grep render|FrameBuffer|present|softbuffer|winit in main.rs/bootstrap.rs finds no draw path. render3d::render_scene_frame is called only from tests/runner_renders_3d_scene_frame.rs. patina-web: browser_runtime.rs:517-536 only calls engine.frame(), and start_engine (:556-569) builds a bare Node2D tree. The JS template (gdplatform/src/web_export.rs:501) calls startCanvasRenderer but never draws scene content. The only draw API is presentClear.

### 2. Browser runtime frame loop never draws the scene canvas  (UNWIRED, P0)

**Godot ground truth:** platform/web/display_server_web.cpp; doc: Exporting for the Web (canvas is the render target)

**Patina today:** crates/patina-web/src/browser_runtime.rs:517-536: the rAF callback polls gamepads and calls rt.engine.frame(now_ms), with no render or present. start_engine (:556-569) never calls crate::canvas::start_canvas_renderer (canvas.rs:156). The only output API is present_clear (canvas.rs:146-147). grep 'present_clear|start_canvas_renderer' finds no caller in patina-web/src outside the definition.

**Implement:** Godot's web export renders the root viewport into the page canvas each frame and resizes with the canvas (stretch applies).
Patina: WebEngine::frame (engine.rs:46) steps the MainLoop only, and the rAF loop (browser_runtime.rs:517) presents nothing. Depends on stage 1 of r2d-runtime-output, where the render entry moves out of gdeditor.
Implementation: add `WebEngine::render_frame(&mut self, w, h) -> FrameBuffer`, which calls the moved runtime canvas entry with root_window.size = backing size from canvas_backing_size. In install_frame_loop, after a step returns Some, blit the FrameBuffer to the canvas. Either upload it as a texture through the existing GpuSurface (canvas.rs), or use putImageData on a 2D context as a fallback. Update root_window.size whenever fit_canvas_to_display reports a resize, so stretch modes track the browser window.
Wiring: requestAnimationFrame -> WebEngine::frame -> WebEngine::render_frame -> canvas present.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/engine.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/browser_runtime.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/canvas.rs`

**Prove it:** Host-side, with no browser: build WebEngine with a tree containing a red ColorRect at (0,0) size 8x8, call frame() twice with increasing timestamps, then call render_frame(16,16). Pixel (4,4) is red and pixel (12,12) is the clear color. A second test shows that after a resize to 32x32 with stretch mode canvas_items and base 16x16, the rect covers (12,12). (test: `web_engine_renders_canvas_frame`)

**Verifier note:** Small evidence correction: start_canvas_renderer does have callers, but in JS rather than Rust. gdplatform/src/web_export.rs:501 and patina-web/web/index.html:119 call startCanvasRenderer. The only frame output is presentClear, a solid clear (canvas.rs:146), which index.html:155 calls with a pulsing colour and the export template never calls at all. The substance holds: the rAF closure (browser_runtime.rs:517-536) calls engine.frame() and engine.rs:46 frame() only steps the loop. No path rasterizes the SceneTree to the canvas. Same root cause as r2d-runtime-output; P0 stands.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Run `patina-runner fixtures/<2d scene with Sprite2D + ColorRect + Label>.tscn --frames 3 --frame-out out.png` (exercised via the runner's tests/ harness spawning the binary). It writes a PNG whose pixel at the ColorRect centre matches its color within 1/255, and whose sprite region holds texture pixels, not the clear color. patina-runner must not depend on gdeditor (assert in the test by parsing Cargo.toml). (test: `runner_writes_2d_canvas_frame`) 2) Host-side, with no browser: build WebEngine with a tree containing a red ColorRect at (0,0) size 8x8, call frame() twice with increasing timestamps, then call render_frame(16,16). Pixel (4,4) is red and pixel (12,12) is the clear color. A second test shows that after a resize to 32x32 with stretch mode canvas_items and base 16x16, the rect covers (12,12). (test: `web_engine_renders_canvas_frame`)

title: Editor2D: render the edited scene through the runtime canvas list under the editor grid and gizmos
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/r2d-editor-viewport] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** examples/editor.rs 2D edit branch -> render_scene_with_zoom_pan -> canvas list rasterize -> published editor frame

**Godot ground truth:** editor/plugins/canvas_item_editor_plugin.cpp (the edited scene renders through the real canvas in the editor viewport)

**Patina today:** examples/editor.rs:473-482 renders 2D edit mode with scene_renderer::render_scene_with_zoom_pan, which goes to render_scene_inner (crates/gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs:262-430). There, a match on class_name draws only Sprite2D (texture) and ColorRect as content. Node2D is a diamond, Label/Button/Control are placeholder rects, and every other class (Polygon2D, Line2D, TileMapLayer, MeshInstance2D, AnimatedSprite2D, NinePatchRect, Light2D effect, etc.) falls to `_ => draw::fill_circle(.., 2.0, COLOR_DEFAULT)`. Nodes are placed by global *position* only (`pos` at :318), so rotation, scale and modulate are ignored. Viewport2D::build_render_list (viewport_2d_render.rs:450) uses the real canvas list but is called only from tests (viewport_2d_render.rs:4288+).

**Implement:** Godot's 2D editor viewport shows the edited scene exactly as it will render: every CanvasItem at its full transform, with modulate, z order, textures and text. Grid, rulers and gizmos are drawn on top as overlays.
Patina: render_scene_inner (scene_renderer.rs:262) draws class icons from a hand-written match, and only Sprite2D and ColorRect show content. Polygon2D, Line2D, TileMapLayer and Label text appear as 2px dots.
Implementation: in render_scene_inner, draw the grid first. Then build `Viewport2D::build_render_list(tree)` plus build_control_render_items, apply an editor view transform (zoom * translate(offset)) to every item (as apply_camera2d_view does, but ignoring Camera2D), and rasterize with the editor TextureCache into the same FrameBuffer. Keep the selection highlight, move gizmo, labels, physics/collision/nav overlays and rulers drawn after. Keep icon glyphs only for non-visual nodes (Node2D without drawable kind, Camera2D, bodies).
Wiring: examples/editor.rs 2D edit branch -> render_scene_with_zoom_pan -> canvas list rasterize -> published editor frame.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`

**Prove it:** Load a .tscn with a Polygon2D (red triangle, rotated 90deg), a Line2D (blue, width 4) and a Label('Hi') into SceneTree. Call scene_renderer::render_scene_with_zoom_pan at zoom 1. The triangle's red pixels match the rotated geometry (a sample inside the rotated triangle is red and the same sample outside it is not). The Line2D's midpoint pixel is blue. The Label region contains non-background glyph pixels. A ColorRect with modulate alpha 0.5 blends over the grid. (test: `editor_viewport_renders_real_canvas`)

**Verifier note:** examples/editor.rs:473-482 calls scene_renderer::render_scene_with_zoom_pan. That function (:91-99) calls render_scene_inner with texture_cache=None and overlays=None. render_scene_inner (:262-438) draws the grid, then matches on class: Node2D gets a diamond, Sprite2D a texture, Label and ColorRect content, Camera2D and particles icons, and the catch-all `_ => fill_circle(pos, 2.0)` (:416). Placement uses only get_global_position (:317-318), so rotation and scale are not applied to content. No production code calls Viewport2D::build_render_list or collect_canvas_items from scene_renderer. The editor_server render_scene uses are in tests (:31118+). PARTIAL and P0 are both reasonable.
acceptance_criteria: Load a .tscn with a Polygon2D (red triangle, rotated 90deg), a Line2D (blue, width 4) and a Label('Hi') into SceneTree. Call scene_renderer::render_scene_with_zoom_pan at zoom 1. The triangle's red pixels match the rotated geometry (a sample inside the rotated triangle is red and the same sample outside it is not). The Line2D's midpoint pixel is blue. The Label region contains non-background glyph pixels. A ColorRect with modulate alpha 0.5 blends over the grid. (test: `editor_viewport_renders_real_canvas`)

- **60** files under `engine-rs/tests` + `crates/*/tests` reference `SoftwareRenderer`;
- **28** of those call `render_frame`, and the acceptance demands that NO test construct it.
