comments.text:
AUDIT COMPLETE, implementation not yet started (TurquoiseCastle). Static reading only. This bead is genuinely fresh — 0 prior verifies — and its one declared file `render_server_3d.rs` is clean, as is `packed_scene.rs`.

=== THE BUG IS WORSE THAN THE BEAD SAYS, AND IN A WAY THAT CHANGES THE FIX ===
The bead describes `material_from_path` as guessing colours from the FILENAME. For an `ExtResource` material it does not even get a filename.

`packed_scene.rs:473-483` stores an ExtResource property as the RAW REFERENCE STRING — `Variant::String("ExtResource(\"1_abc\")")` — and keeps the id -> path map separately in `ext_resources`. `node3d::get_material_override` then reads that property as a `String`, so `resolve_material` step 1 calls:

  Self::material_from_path("ExtResource(\"1_abc\")")

The substring test for `red`/`green`/`blue`/`metal`/`emissive` runs against `ExtResource("1_abc")`, matches nothing, and returns the default white. So an ExtResource `material_override` renders **white**, not "a colour guessed from the file name". The heuristic never sees the path at all.

=== AND FLATTENING ALONE WOULD NOT FIX IT ===
This is the part that changes the plan. `resolve_material` (render_server_3d.rs:1430) documents a priority chain whose step 2 is the flattened `__material__*` bag — but step 1 is:

  if let Some(override_path) = node3d::get_material_override(tree, nid) {
      return Self::material_from_path(&override_path);
  }

It returns **immediately**. So even after `packed_scene` flattens a real `__material__*` bag, `material_override` would still short-circuit into the heuristic and the authored albedo would never be read. The bead's Files list is right to include `render_server_3d.rs`; what it does not say is that the ORDER there is load-bearing, not just the heuristic's existence.

=== FEASIBILITY: ALL GREEN, AND PRECEDENTED ===
- `gdresource::loader` already parses `.tres` (`[gd_resource]`, `[ext_resource]`, `[sub_resource]`, `[resource]`), so the class and the property bag come for free.
- `gdscene` already depends on `gdresource` (Cargo.toml:13).
- `gdcore::file_access::read_file_string(path)` is `res://`-aware, and `gdscene` already reads resources that way in `animation_tscn.rs`, `script_mesh.rs` and three others — so a loader module reading a referenced file is an established pattern, not a new one.
- ⚠️ But `packed_scene.rs` itself currently reads NO files (0 hits for `file_access`/`read_to_string`/`fs::read`). Adding I/O to what is today a pure text->scene transform is the one genuine design choice here. It is what the bead asks for, and the precedent above makes it defensible, but it deserves to be a deliberate decision rather than a side effect.

=== THE PLAN ===
1. `packed_scene.rs` material pass (:867-903): when `material_override` / `material_overlay` / `surface_material_override/N` / the mesh's `material` holds an `ExtResource("id")`, resolve `ext_resources[id].path`, read it, parse it with `gdresource`, and flatten `__material__class` + `__material__{key}` exactly as the SubResource branch does. Reuse that branch's copy loop verbatim rather than writing a second one.
2. `render_server_3d.rs` `resolve_material`: consult the flattened bag BEFORE falling back to `material_from_path`, so step 2 can actually win. Then `material_from_path` becomes reachable only for a genuine path string, which is the only case it was ever meaningful for.
3. Acceptance test `ext_resource_material_renders_authored_albedo`, with the bead's own discriminator: a file named `red_but_blue.tres` whose albedo is BLUE must render blue. That single fixture kills the filename heuristic outright — no other assertion is needed to prove the heuristic is gone.

=== TWO TRAPS TO PRESERVE ===
- ⚠️ **ShaderMaterial must stay excluded.** The SubResource branch filters it deliberately and says why: its keys are `shader_parameter/*`, so giving it a `__material__*` bag holding none of the StandardMaterial3D keys would make `material3d_for_node` hand the renderer a DEFAULT material where it correctly returns `None` today — turning every shader-material mesh flat. The ExtResource branch needs the same filter or it reintroduces that regression for `.tres` shaders.
- ⚠️ **A missing or unparseable `.tres` must degrade to today's behaviour, not error.** Scenes are loaded in tests without path roots configured, so the read will legitimately fail; the pass must leave the node bag-less exactly as now.

UNBUILT: worker build guard blocks the toolchain.

title: FileAccess: bind the full typed read/write surface to GDScript (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/script-io-bindings] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** a GDScript running in a booted project (patina-runner project_boot -> SceneTree -> interpreter) must reach these through FileAccess.open("user://..."); a script running under patina-runner reaches these through the `DirAccess` identifier dispatch in interpreter.rs

### 1. FileAccess script surface (typed get/store, lines, csv, var, seek/length/eof, null-on-failure open)  (UNWIRED, P0)

**Godot ground truth:** core/io/file_access.h/.cpp; doc/classes/FileAccess.xml (68 methods in extension_api)

**Patina today:** gdcore/src/file_access.rs:884-1006 implements store_8/16/32/64/float/double, get_8..get_double, seek, get_length, eof_reached, but the only script dispatch, gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:19342-19425 call_file_access_instance, has arms only for get_as_text/get_buffer/store_string/store_buffer/close/get_error, and every other method falls through to UndefinedFunction. get_buffer returns Variant::Array instead of PackedByteArray (interpreter.rs:19369-19373). FileAccess.open propagates a runtime error (interpreter.rs:19313) where Godot returns null and sets get_open_error. ClassDB registers only open/get_as_text/get_buffer/store_string/store_buffer/get_error/close/file_exists (class_db.rs:26065+). Greps that came back empty in gdscript-interop/src: "store_line", "get_line", "store_var", "get_var" (in the FileAccess context), "get_csv_line", "eof_reached", "get_length", "store_32", "get_open_error", "create_temp", "get_md5", "get_sha256".

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: FileAccess (core/io/file_access.cpp, doc/classes/FileAccess.xml) exposes get/store_8/16/32/64/half/float/double/real, get/store_line, get/store_csv_line, get/store_var(allow_objects), get/store_pascal_string, seek/seek_end/get_position/get_length/eof_reached/is_open/get_path/get_path_absolute, flush, big_endian, get_file_as_bytes, get_md5/get_sha256, create_temp and get_open_error. FileAccess.open() returns null on failure and does not raise. Save-game code depends on store_var/get_var and store_line/get_line.

Patina today: gdcore/src/file_access.rs:884-1006 already implements the typed primitives, seek, length and eof. The script binding, interpreter.rs:19342-19425 call_file_access_instance, handles only 6 methods. get_buffer returns an Array, not a PackedByteArray. open() raises a runtime error (interpreter.rs:19313). ClassDB (class_db.rs:26065) lists the same 8 methods, so has_method answers false for everything else.

Approach: add arms in call_file_access_instance for every FileAccess method, backed by the existing gdcore FileAccess methods. Add get_line/store_line/csv/pascal/half/real to gdcore where missing. Reuse the Marshalls var_to_bytes encoder (already in interpreter.rs) for store_var/get_var. Return PackedByteArray from get_buffer. Make static open() return Nil and record a thread-local open error for get_open_error(). Add get_file_as_bytes, create_temp and get_md5/get_sha256 statics. Register the full method list in class_db.rs FileAccess.

Wiring: a GDScript running in a booted project (patina-runner project_boot -> SceneTree -> interpreter) must reach these through FileAccess.open("user://...").

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/file_access.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`

**Prove it:** A project script runs in _ready: FileAccess.open("user://save.dat", FileAccess.WRITE) followed by store_32(7), store_line("hi"), store_var({"a": [1, 2.5]}), store_double(1.5) and close. It then reopens with READ and reads every value back exactly, and eof_reached() is true at the end. FileAccess.open("user://missing", FileAccess.READ) returns null and FileAccess.get_open_error() == ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND. get_buffer returns a PackedByteArray. The test boots the project through patina-runner project_boot and asserts the printed values (test: `fileaccess_typed_io_script_roundtrip`).

**Verifier note:** Read interpreter.rs:19289-19428. The static call_file_access_static has only open/file_exists/get_file_as_string. open maps errors through engine_err_to_runtime at :19313, so it raises instead of returning null. The instance function call_file_access_instance (:19342) has only get_as_text/get_buffer/store_string/store_buffer/close/get_error, with fallthrough to UndefinedFunction. get_buffer builds a Variant::Array (:19369-19371). The only router into it is :10783. Greps for store_line/get_csv_line/eof_reached across crates/*.rs hit only gdcore/src/file_access.rs, and quoted "store_32"/"get_length"/"eof_reached"/"get_open_error" in gdscript-interop/src got 0 hits. P0 holds, because save-game line/var IO is core.

### 2. DirAccess script surface (copy, make_dir_recursive, change_dir, *_absolute statics, include_hidden, get_files_at)  (UNWIRED, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** core/io/dir_access.cpp; doc/classes/DirAccess.xml

**Patina today:** gdcore/src/file_access.rs implements copy (1482), make_dir_recursive (1506), change_dir (1442), get_current_dir (1436), set_include_hidden/navigational (1196-1201) and get_files_at/get_directories_at (1418/1427). The script binding at interpreter.rs:19430-19458 (call_dir_access_static plus call_dir_access_instance) dispatches only open, dir_exists, list_dir_begin, get_next, current_is_dir, list_dir_end, get_files, get_directories, make_dir, remove and rename. These have no arms: make_dir_recursive, make_dir_absolute, make_dir_recursive_absolute, copy, copy_absolute, rename_absolute, remove_absolute, dir_exists_absolute, file_exists, change_dir, get_current_dir, get_files_at, get_directories_at, set_include_hidden, get_space_left, get_open_error.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: DirAccess (doc/classes/DirAccess.xml) has instance methods make_dir_recursive, copy, change_dir, get_current_dir, file_exists, set_include_hidden/navigational and get_space_left. Its static helpers are make_dir_absolute, make_dir_recursive_absolute, copy_absolute, rename_absolute, remove_absolute, dir_exists_absolute, get_files_at and get_directories_at. open() returns null on failure, with get_open_error().

Patina today: gdcore/src/file_access.rs:1418-1557 implements nearly all of these. interpreter.rs call_dir_access_static/call_dir_access_instance (from line 19430) dispatches only 11 methods, so `DirAccess.make_dir_recursive_absolute("user://saves/slot1")`, the standard save-folder idiom, raises UndefinedFunction.

Approach: add arms that forward to the gdcore DirAccess methods and add the *_absolute static wrappers. Make open() return Nil on error and record the error for get_open_error(). Register the methods in the class_db.rs DirAccess registration.

Wiring: a script running under patina-runner reaches these through the `DirAccess` identifier dispatch in interpreter.rs.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/file_access.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`

**Prove it:** A booted project script calls DirAccess.make_dir_recursive_absolute("user://a/b/c"), DirAccess.open("user://a").copy("user://x.txt", "user://a/b/y.txt"), get_files_at("user://a/b") and change_dir("b") followed by get_current_dir(). Each result matches Godot: the directories exist on disk, the copied file is listed, and the current dir ends with /a/b. DirAccess.open("user://nope") returns null (test: `diraccess_script_surface_wired`).

**Verifier note:** call_dir_access_static (interpreter.rs:19430-19456) has only open/dir_exists, and open raises on error. call_dir_access_instance (:19458+) has the list_dir_* family plus get_files/get_directories/make_dir/remove/rename. Grepping quoted "make_dir_recursive"/"make_dir_recursive_absolute"/"copy_absolute"/"change_dir"/"get_files_at" in gdscript-interop/src got 0 arms. The only get_files_at use is an internal call at interpreter.rs:27364 inside an editor helper, not a DirAccess script arm. The gdcore implementation is at file_access.rs:1418.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A project script runs in _ready: FileAccess.open("user://save.dat", FileAccess.WRITE) followed by store_32(7), store_line("hi"), store_var({"a": [1, 2.5]}), store_double(1.5) and close. It then reopens with READ and reads every value back exactly, and eof_reached() is true at the end. FileAccess.open("user://missing", FileAccess.READ) returns null and FileAccess.get_open_error() == ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND. get_buffer returns a PackedByteArray. The test boots the project through patina-runner project_boot and asserts the printed values (test: `fileaccess_typed_io_script_roundtrip`). 2) A booted project script calls DirAccess.make_dir_recursive_absolute("user://a/b/c"), DirAccess.open("user://a").copy("user://x.txt", "user://a/b/y.txt"), get_files_at("user://a/b") and change_dir("b") followed by get_current_dir(). Each result matches Godot: the directories exist on disk, the copied file is listed, and the current dir ends with /a/b. DirAccess.open("user://nope") returns null (test: `diraccess_script_surface_wired`).

title: ResourceUID: populate the registry at boot and resolve uid:// main_scene/autoloads/load()
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/uid-resolution] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** patina-runner boot -> registry -> main_scene instance

**Godot ground truth:** core/io/resource_uid.cpp (load_from_cache, uid_cache.bin); editor/editor_node.cpp:2627 writes application/run/main_scene as ResourceUID::path_to_uid(...)

**Patina today:** gdresource/src/uid.rs:203 load_from_cache_bytes, :232 register_uid_sidecar and :249 load_uid_sidecar_file have no non-test callers. `grep -rn load_from_cache_bytes|load_uid_sidecar_file|uid_cache.bin` outside uid.rs matches only a test in unified.rs:259-269. Nothing calls uid::global_registry() outside uid.rs. patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs:487-491 passes main_scene straight to load_scene_into_tree, which calls FileAccess::read_file_string (project_boot.rs:585). gdcore/src/file_access.rs:467-485 resolve_path handles only res:// and user://, so a uid:// path becomes a bare relative filesystem path. The Godot 4.6 editor writes run/main_scene="uid://...", so such a project boots with no main scene.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: at startup ResourceUID loads res://.godot/uid_cache.bin (core/io/resource_uid.cpp load_from_cache), and 4.4+ projects also carry *.uid sidecars for scripts and shaders. Every path consumer resolves uid:// through ResourceUID::ensure_path: the main_scene setting, autoload paths, load()/preload() and ext_resource fallback. The 4.6 editor stores run/main_scene as a uid:// (editor/editor_node.cpp:2627).

Patina today: the registry and its parsers exist in gdresource/src/uid.rs (203, 232, 249), but no boot code calls them. resolve_path (gdcore/src/file_access.rs:467) does not understand uid://. project_boot.rs:487-491 and :585 read the main scene with FileAccess::read_file_string, so a uid main scene fails to load.

Approach: (1) In project_boot::boot_from_project_text, before any scene load, load res://.godot/uid_cache.bin through FileAccess (pack-aware) into uid::global_registry(). Also scan *.uid sidecars, for loose projects and via pack listing for packs. (2) Add a uid:// branch to gdcore resolve_path/read_file_bytes via a registered resolver hook, which avoids a gdcore->gdresource dependency. Alternatively call uid::ensure_path at each consumer: main_scene, instantiate_autoload, the interpreter's load()/preload(), and packed_scene ext_resource (prefer uid when it resolves, as Godot does). (3) ResourceUID.uid_to_path in scripts must see the same registry.

Wiring: patina-runner boot -> registry -> main_scene instance.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/uid.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/file_access.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`

**Prove it:** A fixture project has project.godot run/main_scene="uid://<id>", a .godot/uid_cache.bin mapping that id to res://main.tscn, and an autoload given as uid://. It boots with patina-runner and main_scene_root is Some with the expected root name. The autoload is reachable at /root/<Name>. A script's load("uid://<id>") returns the scene, and ResourceUID.get_id_path(ResourceUID.text_to_id(...)) == "res://main.tscn" (test: `uid_main_scene_boot_resolution`).

**Verifier note:** grep 'load_from_cache_bytes|load_uid_sidecar_file|uid_cache.bin|global_registry()' matched only gdresource/src/uid.rs and a test in unified.rs:259-269. grep 'uid::|ensure_path' in patina-runner/src, gdscene/src and gdcore/src got 0 hits. The only consumers are the ResourceUID script singleton (interpreter.rs:28624-28703) and the res_loader/saver text codec. project_boot.rs:487-491 passes main_scene to load_scene_into_tree, which does a raw FileAccess::read_file_string (:585). The interpreter load() (:6160-6262) has no uid:// branch, and its load_via_format_loaders uses importers::UnifiedLoader, not the uid-aware unified.rs loader.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture project has project.godot run/main_scene="uid://<id>", a .godot/uid_cache.bin mapping that id to res://main.tscn, and an autoload given as uid://. It boots with patina-runner and main_scene_root is Some with the expected root name. The autoload is reachable at /root/<Name>. A script's load("uid://<id>") returns the scene, and ResourceUID.get_id_path(ResourceUID.text_to_id(...)) == "res://main.tscn" (test: `uid_main_scene_boot_resolution`).

title: Export boot (1/3): read project.binary, follow .remap redirects, pack-aware .import resolution (+2 related)
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/exported-pck-boot] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** `patina-runner game.pck` -> boot_project_from_pck -> settings from project.binary -> main scene via .remap; runner boot -> load_any -> SceneTree; load_any (bead 2/3) and the interpreter load() must accept RSCC files

### 1. Godot-exported PCK boot: project.binary (ECFG), .remap redirects, pack-aware .import artifact resolution  (MISSING, P0)

**Godot ground truth:** core/config/project_settings.cpp:687,912 (_load_settings_text_or_binary, ECFG); editor/export/editor_export_platform.cpp:1643 (.remap), :1676 (project.binary); editor/register_editor_types.cpp:298 convert_text_resources_to_binary=true; core/io/resource_loader.cpp path remaps

**Patina today:** patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs:81 reads only res://project.godot from the mounted pack. `grep -rn 'project.binary|ECFG'` over engine-rs/crates: 0 non-test hits. `grep -rn '\.remap'` finds only the .import [remap] section reader in importers.rs:82-1703, with no `<file>.remap` path-redirect handling. gdresource/src/importers.rs:70-112 resolve_import_artifact uses std::fs (`sidecar.exists()`, find_project_root walking the disk for project.godot), so in a mounted .pck neither the .import sidecar nor the .godot/imported artifact is found and texture/audio imports fail. project_boot.rs:585-587 always parses scenes as text via from_tscn. A default Godot export (convert_text_resources_to_binary=true) ships main.tscn.remap -> a binary .scn, so the main scene cannot load.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: an exported PCK stores res://project.binary, which is binary ECFG: a u32 count, then for each entry a u32-length key and a u32-length marshalled Variant (project_settings.cpp _load_settings_binary). It does not store project.godot. With convert_text_resources_to_binary (default true, register_editor_types.cpp:298), each text resource is replaced by `<path>.remap`, an INI file whose [remap] path= points to the converted binary. The loader follows .remap and then .import (ResourceLoader::_path_remap).

Patina today: boot_project_from_pck (project_boot.rs:59-88) requires res://project.godot. There is no ECFG parser and no .remap following. resolve_import_artifact (importers.rs:70-112) touches only the host filesystem, so imports inside a pack are invisible.

Approach: (a) In gdcore/src/project_settings.rs add ProjectSettings::from_godot_binary(&[u8]) that decodes ECFG with the existing Marshalls/var decoder. In boot_project_from_pck, try res://project.binary first and fall back to project.godot. (b) Add a remap-resolution helper, gdresource::importers::remap_path(path) -> String, that reads `<path>.remap` and then `<path>.import` through FileAccess::read_file_string, which is pack-aware. Call it from project_boot load_scene_into_tree, instantiate_autoload, the interpreter load()/preload(), and packed_scene ext_resource loading. (c) Rewrite resolve_import_artifact to use FileAccess::file_exists and read_file_bytes plus res:// paths instead of std::fs and find_project_root, so the .godot/imported artifact loads from the mounted pack.

Wiring: `patina-runner game.pck` -> boot_project_from_pck -> settings from project.binary -> main scene via .remap.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/project_settings.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A fixture .pck built with PckPacker contains project.binary (ECFG with application/run/main_scene and display/window/size/viewport_width), main.tscn.remap pointing at a text .tscn under .godot/exported/, icon.png.import, and a .godot/imported/icon-*.ctex. It boots via boot_project_from_pck with no project.godot. The viewport width comes from project.binary, the main scene instances, and a Sprite2D's ext_resource icon.png resolves through the packed .import to a decoded texture with non-zero width (test: `exported_pck_binary_project_and_remap_boot`).

**Verifier note:** boot_project_from_pck (project_boot.rs:59-88) requires res://project.godot (:81). grep 'project.binary|ECFG' over crates excluding tests: 0 hits. grep '\.remap"|remap_path' finds only the .import [remap] handling at importers.rs:79/103. resolve_import_artifact (importers.rs:70-112) uses std::fs sidecar.exists() and find_project_root, so pack contents are invisible to it. load_scene_into_tree always calls from_tscn (project_boot.rs:587).

### 2. Binary PackedScene (.scn) instancing from _bundled (names/variants/nodes/conns/node_paths/editable_instances)  (MISSING, P0)

**Godot ground truth:** scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp SceneState::set_bundled_scene / _get_bundled_scene; core/io/resource_format_binary.cpp

**Patina today:** `grep -rn _bundled` over engine-rs/crates returns 0 hits. res_loader.rs:145-286 load_res_binary decodes a binary resource into a Resource property bag, but no code converts a PackedScene resource's _bundled dictionary into gdscene::packed_scene::PackedScene. Its only callers are importers.rs:1974 (generic resource load) and audio_server_bridge.rs:1162. Every scene instancing path uses PackedScene::from_tscn: project_boot.rs:587, bootstrap.rs:506, main.rs:537. The interpreter's load() returns only a placeholder for .scn (interpreter.rs:6219-6233).

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: a binary .scn is an RSRC resource of type PackedScene with one property, _bundled, a Dictionary with keys names (PackedStringArray), variants (Array), node_count, nodes (PackedInt32Array: parent, owner, type-name-idx, name-idx, instance, index, prop count + (name,value) idx pairs, group count + idx), conn_count, conns (from, to, signal, method, flags, unbinds, binds), node_paths, editable_instances and version (packed_scene.cpp SceneState::set_bundled_scene). Imported glTF scenes in .godot/imported and every exported text scene arrive in this form.

Patina today: res_loader.rs decodes the RSRC container, but no _bundled consumer exists (0 grep hits), and scenes are only ever parsed from text (project_boot.rs:587, bootstrap.rs:506).

Approach: add PackedScene::from_bundled(&Dictionary, sub/ext resource maps) in gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs. It decodes the node table into the same node templates and SceneConnection records from_tscn builds, including instance (ext scene) indices, groups, editable instances and node_paths flags. Add PackedScene::load_any(bytes) that sniffs RSRC/RSCC and otherwise uses text. Switch project_boot load_scene_into_tree, instantiate_autoload, the runner main.rs entry and the interpreter load()/instantiate path to it.

Wiring: runner boot -> load_any -> SceneTree.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/res_loader.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/main.rs`

**Prove it:** A binary .scn fixture is produced by Godot 4.6, checked in under fixtures/ and generated from a scene with a root Node2D, a child Sprite2D (position, texture ext_resource), a group, an instanced sub-scene and a signal connection with binds. It loads via patina-runner as the main scene. The tree has the same node names, types, positions and groups as the .tscn twin, and the connection fires its target method with the bind (test: `binary_scn_bundled_scene_boot`).

**Verifier note:** grep -rn '_bundled' over engine-rs/crates *.rs: 0 hits. load_res_binary is called at project_boot.rs:285 (generic resource) and audio_server_bridge.rs:1162. No gdscene PackedScene decoder from RSRC exists: grep 'load_res_binary|RSRC|fn from_binary' in gdscene/src and patina-runner/src found nothing beyond those calls. The interpreter's load() deliberately skips format loaders for .tscn/.scn and returns a placeholder PackedScene (interpreter.rs:6223-6262).

### 3. Compressed binary resources (RSCC) + Compression modes FASTLZ/ZSTD (FileAccess.open_compressed, PackedByteArray.compress default mode)  (MISSING, P1)

**Godot ground truth:** core/io/file_access_compressed.cpp (GCPF blocks, default MODE_ZSTD), core/io/compression.cpp, resource_format_binary.cpp:990 (RSCC via FileAccessCompressed); editor/import/3d/resource_importer_scene.cpp:3325 FLAG_COMPRESS

**Patina today:** res_loader.rs:150-153 returns Unsupported for RSCC. interpreter.rs:14990-14995 states that FASTLZ, ZSTD and BROTLI have no codec and return an EMPTY array, yet PackedByteArray.compress() defaults to mode 0 (FASTLZ), so the default call yields empty bytes. open_compressed has no hits in gdscript-interop/src. `grep -rln 'zstd|fastlz|GCPF'` over engine-rs/crates finds no decoder (only a test file name and comments). gdresource/Cargo.toml lists miniz_oxide only.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: FileAccessCompressed writes 'GCPF'-style block streams: a magic, then mode, block_size, total size, block count and per-block compressed sizes, followed by the blocks. The default mode is ZSTD. Binary resources saved with FLAG_COMPRESS use the magic RSCC around the same stream (resource_format_binary.cpp:990). Imported scenes, fonts and SVG textures use it when filesystem/on_save/compress_binary_resources is on. Compression::MODE_FASTLZ (0) is the default for PackedByteArray.compress.

Patina today: RSCC is rejected (res_loader.rs:150). FASTLZ and ZSTD are unimplemented, and compress() at its default mode returns empty (interpreter.rs:14990). There is no FileAccess.open_compressed.

Approach: add a pure-Rust FastLZ (levels 1/2, a small self-contained port of thirdparty/misc/fastlz.c) and a wasm-safe zstd decoder (ruzstd) for decode, with the ruzstd encoder or an fs-level fallback for writes. Implement a gdcore CompressedReader for the block format. Teach load_res_binary to unwrap RSCC into a plain RSRC stream. Implement pba_compress/pba_decompress for modes 0 and 2. Add FileAccess.open_compressed(path, mode, compression) in the script binding.

Wiring: load_any (bead 2/3) and the interpreter load() must accept RSCC files.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/res_loader.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/file_access.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/Cargo.toml`

**Prove it:** A Godot-4.6-produced RSCC .res fixture (zstd) loads via load() in a booted project and exposes its properties. PackedByteArray([...]).compress() followed by decompress(size) round-trips bytes in modes FASTLZ and ZSTD, and decodes Godot-produced fixture buffers byte-exact. FileAccess.open_compressed write-then-read round-trips a string (test: `rscc_and_compression_modes_roundtrip`).

**Verifier note:** res_loader.rs:137/152 returns Unsupported for RSCC. interpreter.rs:14984-14999 documents FASTLZ/ZSTD/BROTLI as having no codec and returning EMPTY, and compress defaults its mode to 0 (FASTLZ). grep 'zstd|fastlz|ruzstd' across *.rs/Cargo.toml finds only a test file, a comment in http_request_node.rs:458 and res_loader.rs. grep 'open_compressed' in gdscript-interop/src and gdcore/src: 0 hits. P1 is reasonable.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A fixture .pck built with PckPacker contains project.binary (ECFG with application/run/main_scene and display/window/size/viewport_width), main.tscn.remap pointing at a text .tscn under .godot/exported/, icon.png.import, and a .godot/imported/icon-*.ctex. It boots via boot_project_from_pck with no project.godot. The viewport width comes from project.binary, the main scene instances, and a Sprite2D's ext_resource icon.png resolves through the packed .import to a decoded texture with non-zero width (test: `exported_pck_binary_project_and_remap_boot`). 2) A binary .scn fixture is produced by Godot 4.6, checked in under fixtures/ and generated from a scene with a root Node2D, a child Sprite2D (position, texture ext_resource), a group, an instanced sub-scene and a signal connection with binds. It loads via patina-runner as the main scene. The tree has the same node names, types, positions and groups as the .tscn twin, and the connection fires its target method with the bind (test: `binary_scn_bundled_scene_boot`). 3) A Godot-4.6-produced RSCC .res fixture (zstd) loads via load() in a booted project and exposes its properties. PackedByteArray([...]).compress() followed by decompress(size) round-trips bytes in modes FASTLZ and ZSTD, and decodes Godot-produced fixture buffers byte-exact. FileAccess.open_compressed write-then-read round-trips a string (test: `rscc_and_compression_modes_roundtrip`).

title: SceneTree: gate MainLoop _process/_physics_process on set_process* and physics priority, and expose toggles to GDScript
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-process-toggles] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** a .gd script calling set_process(false) in _ready must stop its own _process across MainLoop::step frames

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/node.cpp set_process/set_physics_process; scene_tree.cpp _process_group sorts physics by process_physics_priority

**Patina today:** The gated, priority-correct dispatchers SceneTree::process_all_scripts_process / process_all_scripts_physics_process (crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:7640-7670) are called only from #[cfg(test)] code (scripting.rs:10525-11602) and the test at scene_tree.rs:9417. MainLoop::step instead calls process_frame_with_scripts (scene_tree.rs:7828) and process_physics_frame_with_scripts (scene_tree.rs:7859). Neither checks is_node_processing / is_node_physics_processing, and the physics one sorts with all_nodes_in_process_order (idle priority), not all_nodes_in_physics_process_order. Separately, SceneAccess::set_process / set_physics_process / set_process_input exist (scripting.rs:4936-4958), but the interpreter never calls them: grep 'set_process' crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs = 0 hits. So `set_process(false)` from GDScript raises UndefinedFunction.

**Implement:** Godot: Node.set_process(false) stops _process and set_physics_process(false) stops _physics_process, independently of process_mode. _physics_process runs in process_physics_priority order (scene/main/node.cpp, scene_tree.cpp _process_group). Patina: the correct filtering lives in process_all_scripts_process/_physics_process (scene_tree.rs:7640-7670), which has test-only callers. The runtime path MainLoop::step -> process_frame_with_scripts (scene_tree.rs:7828) and process_physics_frame_with_scripts (7859) skips the per-node toggle and uses idle priority for physics. The interpreter has no arms for set_process, set_physics_process, is_processing, is_physics_processing, set_process_input, set_process_unhandled_input, set_process_unhandled_key_input, set_process_shortcut_input, set_process_priority, set_physics_process_priority, can_process, get_process_delta_time or get_physics_process_delta_time. Fix: (1) make process_frame_with_scripts/process_physics_frame_with_scripts apply is_node_processing/is_node_physics_processing (the NOTIFICATION_PROCESS still fires for internal processing) and use all_nodes_in_physics_process_order for physics, then delete the duplicate test-only dispatchers or route them through the same code; (2) add try_builtin/call_node_method arms that call the existing SceneAccess methods, plus per-stage input toggles (Node currently has one is_processing_input flag gating every stage in call_input_stage, scene_tree.rs:5767). Wiring: a .gd script calling set_process(false) in _ready must stop its own _process across MainLoop::step frames.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`

**Prove it:** A scene loaded through patina-runner boot, whose script calls set_process(false) in _ready and counts _process/_physics_process calls, shows 0 _process calls and N _physics_process calls after N MainLoop::step ticks. Two nodes with process_physics_priority -1 and 1 that are siblings in reverse tree order run _physics_process in priority order. is_processing() returns false from script (test: `script_set_process_gates_mainloop_callbacks`).

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. main_loop.rs:3975 and :4298 call process_physics_frame_with_scripts / process_frame_with_scripts. scene_tree.rs:7859-7874 filters only should_process_node and sorts with all_nodes_in_process_order (idle priority). process_script_process (5546) and process_script_physics_process (5551) call the script with no toggle check. The gated dispatchers at 7640/7656 have no main_loop callers. Absence greps: '"set_process"', '"is_processing"', '\.set_process(' and '\.is_processing(' across all crate src (class_db, tests and editor_server excluded) gave 0 hits. The only hits are trait defaults at bindings.rs:1196/1199/1205 and impls at scripting.rs:4936/4941, and the interpreter never calls them. P0 is right: set_process(false) is a very common idiom.
acceptance_criteria: A scene loaded through patina-runner boot, whose script calls set_process(false) in _ready and counts _process/_physics_process calls, shows 0 _process calls and N _physics_process calls after N MainLoop::step ticks. Two nodes with process_physics_priority -1 and 1 that are siblings in reverse tree order run _physics_process in priority order. is_processing() returns false from script (test: `script_set_process_gates_mainloop_callbacks`).

title: Node: route process_mode/process_priority/process_physics_priority property writes into the Node fields
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-process-mode-property] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn load -> add_packed_scene_to_tree -> Node::set_property -> should_process_node during MainLoop::step

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/node.cpp set_process_mode (property process_mode, PROCESS_MODE_* 0..4), process_priority, process_physics_priority

**Patina today:** Node::set_property (crates/gdscene/src/node.rs:275-293) stores every key in the property bag and intercepts only metadata/*. The field read by should_process_node / effective_process_mode (scene_tree.rs:3716-3748) is set only by Node::set_process_mode, whose non-test callers are behavioral_2d.rs:372 and visibility_3d.rs:181 (VisibleOnScreenEnabler). grep '\.set_process_priority(\|set_process_physics_priority(' crates/*/src finds no callers outside node.rs. The only .tscn test (tests/scene_suite/scene_instancing_edge_cases_test.rs:320-327) checks the property bag, not the effective mode. So a pause-menu scene authored with `process_mode = 3` (ALWAYS) freezes under pause, and `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` from a script has no effect.

**Implement:** Godot stores process_mode (0 INHERIT, 1 PAUSABLE, 2 WHEN_PAUSED, 3 ALWAYS, 4 DISABLED), process_priority and process_physics_priority as real Node state, reachable from the .tscn property list and from script assignment. Patina's Node::set_property (node.rs:275) never forwards them to Node::set_process_mode / set_process_priority / set_process_physics_priority (node.rs:497-526), so should_process_node (scene_tree.rs:3736) always sees Inherit/0. Fix: in Node::set_property, map these three keys (Int, accepting Float) onto the typed fields while keeping the property row for saving, and make get_property answer from the field. Check that the ProcessMode integer order matches Godot's enum (node.rs:71). Also cover the script path, get_node_property/set_node_property in scripting.rs. Wiring: .tscn load -> add_packed_scene_to_tree -> Node::set_property -> should_process_node during MainLoop::step.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn whose Menu node has `process_mode = 3` and a _process counter keeps counting after tree.set_paused(true) across MainLoop::step, while a default sibling stops. A script that assigns `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED` stops its own _process. `process_priority = -5` from .tscn reorders _process dispatch (test: `tscn_process_mode_always_runs_under_pause`).

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. Node::set_property (node.rs:275-293) intercepts only 'metadata/'. effective_process_mode (scene_tree.rs:3716) reads the typed node.process_mode() field. all_nodes_in_process_order (3688) reads n.process_priority(), also the typed field. Absence grep: '"process_mode"|"process_priority"|"process_physics_priority"' over crate src outside tests and class_db hits only gdserver3d sky.rs and the editor inspector schema. Nothing in packed_scene.rs or scripting.rs routes them. The non-test set_process_mode( callers are behavioral_2d.rs:372, visibility_3d.rs:181 and the unrelated Tween arm at scripting.rs:7349.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn whose Menu node has `process_mode = 3` and a _process counter keeps counting after tree.set_paused(true) across MainLoop::step, while a default sibling stops. A script that assigns `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED` stops its own _process. `process_priority = -5` from .tscn reorders _process dispatch (test: `tscn_process_mode_always_runs_under_pause`).

title: GDScript: make get_tree()/get_viewport()/get_window() return real objects with SceneTree/Viewport/Window property, method and signal dispatch
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-script-handles] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** a script running under MainLoop::step must reach each of these

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/node.h get_tree/get_viewport/get_window; scene/main/scene_tree.cpp _bind_methods (paused, current_scene, root, signals process_frame/physics_frame/node_added/tree_changed); scene/main/viewport.cpp get_visible_rect/set_input_as_handled/get_mouse_position/push_input

**Patina today:** The only handling of get_tree is syntactic: interpreter.rs:4572-4585 matches the literal call form `get_tree().<method>(...)` and dispatches to try_scene_tree_method (interpreter.rs:5588-5770). A bare get_tree() call goes call_self_func_or_native (15503) -> call_node_method, and nothing answers it: grep '"get_tree"' crates/*/src matches only class_db.rs:1170 and interpreter.rs:4573. So `get_tree().paused = true` (exec_assignment, interpreter.rs:1903-1950, has no get_tree case), `get_tree().current_scene`, `get_tree().root`, `await get_tree().process_frame` (only parse-tested, tests/gdscript_suite/gdscript_v1_features_test.rs:51) and `var tree = get_tree()` all raise UndefinedFunction. grep '"get_viewport"\|"get_window"\|"get_visible_rect"\|"push_input"\|"get_mouse_position"' over interpreter.rs and scripting.rs = 0 hits, so `get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()` and `get_viewport().get_visible_rect()` fail too. Rust implementations already exist: viewport::get_viewport/get_window (viewport.rs:29-38), RootWindow::visible_size (viewport.rs:101), SceneTree::current_scene (scene_tree.rs:~2385), and signal emission on root (scene_tree.rs:2741). SceneTree methods absent from try_scene_tree_method: change_scene_to_packed, change_scene_to_node, unload_current_scene, get_frame, get_node_count_in_group, notify_group_flags, set_group_flags, queue_delete, get_processed_tweens, set/get_current_scene, set_auto_accept_quit, set_physics_interpolation_enabled, set_debug_*_hint, get_multiplayer.

**Implement:** Godot: get_tree() returns the SceneTree object. Scripts write `get_tree().paused = true`, read `.current_scene`/`.root`, `await get_tree().process_frame`, `get_tree().node_added.connect(f)`, store `var tree = get_tree()`, and call `get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()`, `get_viewport().get_visible_rect()` and `get_window().size`. In Patina only the literal call form `get_tree().m(...)` resolves (interpreter.rs:4572). Approach: (1) add a reserved SceneTree handle (like WORLD_2D_HANDLE in scripting.rs:3085) returned by a get_tree builtin; route call_method_on/MemberAccess/exec_assignment on that handle into try_scene_tree_method plus property get/set (paused via set_tree_paused, current_scene, root, physics_interpolation, auto_accept_quit) and Signal values (process_frame, physics_frame, node_added, node_removed, tree_changed, scene_changed) bound to the root signal store that MainLoop already emits on. (2) get_viewport()/get_window() return the ObjectId from viewport::get_viewport/get_window, and call_node_method gets Viewport/Window arms: get_visible_rect (RootWindow::visible_size), set_input_as_handled/is_input_handled, get_mouse_position, push_input (SceneTree::push_input), gui_get_focus_owner, get_camera_2d/3d, size/content_scale_* properties read from tree.root_window(). (3) Fill in the missing SceneTree methods listed in the evidence. Wiring: a script running under MainLoop::step must reach each of these.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`

**Prove it:** A project booted through patina-runner whose script does `var t = get_tree(); t.paused = true` pauses the tree, so a Pausable node's _process stops on the next step. `await get_tree().process_frame` resumes on the next frame. `get_tree().current_scene` is the main-scene root. `get_viewport().get_visible_rect().size` equals the configured base size under stretch. `get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()` in _input stops _unhandled_input for that event (test: `get_tree_and_get_viewport_are_live_objects`).

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. interpreter.rs:4572-4587 handles only the syntactic form get_tree().m(...) via try_scene_tree_method/try_builtin. Absence greps: '"get_tree"' outside class_db gives only interpreter.rs:4573. '"get_viewport"' and '"get_window"' give 0 across crates. 'get_viewport|"paused"|current_scene' over gdscript-interop/src gives only the reload_current_scene arm. set_input_as_handled exists only as a bare builtin (interpreter.rs:6133), and its comment says no Viewport object exists. '"change_scene_to_packed"' and '"unload_current_scene"' give 0.
acceptance_criteria: A project booted through patina-runner whose script does `var t = get_tree(); t.paused = true` pauses the tree, so a Pausable node's _process stops on the next step. `await get_tree().process_frame` resumes on the next frame. `get_tree().current_scene` is the main-scene root. `get_viewport().get_visible_rect().size` equals the configured base size under stretch. `get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()` in _input stops _unhandled_input for that event (test: `get_tree_and_get_viewport_are_live_objects`).

comments.text:
PinkMoose — the third failure is diagnosed and FIXED in the working tree. Not reclaiming (I have pat-mgixk.68 in verify); flagging so nobody redoes the diagnosis and nobody trips over my uncommitted changes.

**Progress: my first test now PASSES.** verifier.log:13573 reads `2 tests run: 1 passed, 1 failed`. `scene_tree_group_and_delete_methods_from_script` passed, so queue_delete, notify_group_flags and set_current_scene all work through the new bindings.

**What failed was my test, not the implementation.** `viewport_focus_owner_and_change_scene_to_node_from_script` panicked in my own helper with `the main scene root is in the tree` — `get_node_by_path("/root/Main")` returned None. Cause: `change_scene_to_node` calls `free_current_scene()` first (scene_tree.rs:8803), which is correct Godot behaviour — the outgoing scene is disposed of. `Main` is the node the calling script is attached to, so by the time I read its script variables they were unreachable. The test was reading a corpse.

This is the same hazard I flagged when I deliberately dropped `unload_current_scene` from the submission; it applies to `change_scene_to_node` too, just less obviously, because here the free is a side effect of a method whose stated job is installing the new scene.

**Fix applied (test-only, no implementation change):** split that test in two.
- `viewport_focus_owner_from_script` — reads the script var, because nothing frees Main.
- `change_scene_to_node_from_script` — asserts only tree state, never a script variable, and now additionally asserts that `/root/Main` is GONE while the handed-over node SURVIVES. That pair is a stronger assertion than the one it replaces: the first separates a real scene change from merely storing a pointer, and the second proves the binding's detach-before-handover worked, since the moved node outlived a free that took its old parent.

File parses and is rustfmt-clean; three test fns now. Everything else is unchanged from message 91000, including the separate finding that `.tscn`-declared groups never reach the tree-level group index (measured: `is_in_group` true, `get_nodes_in_group` 0).

There is no generic get_/set_ accessor fallback (searched strip_prefix("get_"), starts_with("get_"), trim_start_matches("get_"), getter-name lookups in scripting.rs and interpreter.rs: none). The silent path: interpreter.rs:15638 call_object_method computes `responds = access.node_has_method(..)` (scene_tree.rs:5402 -> class_db::class_has_method), call_node_method (scripting.rs:2594-4922) returns None, then interpreter.rs:15665 `if responds { return Ok(Variant::Nil) }`. So `$X.get_child(0)`, `other.set_process(false)`, `n.is_inside_tree()` return null silently. A bare self-call (`set_process(false)`) goes through call_self_func_or_native (interpreter.rs:15503), finds no arm and raises UndefinedFunction. The machinery exists but nothing calls it: SceneAccess::set_process/set_physics_process/is_processing are implemented at scripting.rs:4936-4949 and declared at gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs:1196, and SceneTree::set_node_process is unit-tested at scene_tree.rs:9457. `grep -rn 'set_physics_process\|is_processing' gdscript-interop/src` shows no caller. No test or .gd fixture calls GDScript get_child (searched engine-rs/tests, crates/*/tests and *.gd).

**Implement:** Godot: Node.get_child(idx, include_internal=false) returns the child at idx (negative counts from the end) or null with an error when out of range. get_node_or_null(path) returns null without an error. remove_child(node) detaches the node and fires exit_tree. is_inside_tree() returns a bool. set_process(bool) and set_physics_process(bool) toggle the callbacks, and is_processing / is_physics_processing read them back. Object.notification(what, reversed=false) dispatches a notification. Patina registers all of these in ClassDB (class_db.rs:1160-1176), so has_method() answers true, but neither try_builtin (interpreter.rs:5769), call_method_on (interpreter.rs:10773) nor SceneAccess::call_node_method (scripting.rs:2594) has an arm for them. call_object_method's `responds` branch (interpreter.rs:15665) then returns Nil silently. SceneAccess::set_process, set_physics_process and is_processing are already implemented (scripting.rs:4936-4949) but have no caller. Implementation: add arms to scripting.rs call_node_method's generic table so both `$X.m()` and bare `m()` resolve. get_child should use access children with negative-index wrap; get_node_or_null should reuse tree.get_node_or_null (scripting.rs:2050); remove_child should call the existing tree remove path that fires exit_tree; is_inside_tree should read node.is_inside_tree; set_process, set_physics_process, is_processing and is_physics_processing should forward to tree.set_node_process and the related calls; notification should forward to the tree's notification dispatch. Wiring: a GDScript attached to a node loaded from a .tscn and run through SceneTree/MainLoop must observe the effects.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn with Root(script) > A, B. In _ready, the script calls get_child(0).name, get_child(-1).name, $A.get_node_or_null("Nope") == null, $B.is_inside_tree(), set_process(false), and then remove_child($B). Run through MainLoop for 3 frames. Assert get_child returns A and B. Assert _process ran 0 times after set_process(false), and is_processing() returns false. Assert B fired exit_tree and the root's child count is 1. Assert none of these calls returns Nil where Godot returns a value (test: `gdscript_node_core_methods_dispatch`).

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. Searched every crate under engine-rs/crates for the quoted names "get_child", "get_node_or_null", "set_process", "is_inside_tree", "remove_child", "set_physics_process", "is_processing" and "notification". Outside tests the only hits are the registrations in gdobject/src/class_db.rs (1073 notification, 1160, 1163, 1164, 1171, 1173-1175), gdeditor/src/script_editor.rs:1176 (a completion word list) and patina-runner/src/main.rs:299 (a trace label). No crate pulls in generated dispatch code through include!. There is no generic get_/set_ prefix fallback in gdscene/src or gdscript-interop/src; the only starts_with("get_") is in navigation_agents.rs:183/190, which is specific to nav agents. Sibling methods do have arms (get_parent at interpreter.rs:6844, get_children at 6860, get_child_count at 6876), which shows these names were simply left out. I read interpreter.rs:15638-15672: it calls call_script_method, then call_node_method, and if neither answers, `if responds { return Ok(Variant::Nil) }` at 15666. P0 is right: get_child and set_process are core Node API, and has_method() returns true for them.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with Root(script) > A, B. In _ready, the script calls get_child(0).name, get_child(-1).name, $A.get_node_or_null("Nope") == null, $B.is_inside_tree(), set_process(false), and then remove_child($B). Run through MainLoop for 3 frames. Assert get_child returns A and B. Assert _process ran 0 times after set_process(false), and is_processing() returns false. Assert B fired exit_tree and the root's child count is 1. Assert none of these calls returns Nil where Godot returns a value (test: `gdscript_node_core_methods_dispatch`).

title: Node: dispatch the hierarchy/query API from GDScript to the existing SceneTree implementations (+1 related)
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-node-api] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** interpreter -> SceneAccess::call_node_method -> SceneTree mutation during a MainLoop::step script phase; script call in a booted scene

### 1. Node hierarchy/query API from GDScript (has_node, get_node_or_null, get_child, remove_child, move_child, reparent, add_sibling, replace_by, get_index, is_inside_tree, is_ancestor_of, get_path_to, find_children, find_parent, propagate_call, propagate_notification, request_ready, is_node_ready, get_owner/set_owner, get_groups, print_tree)  (UNWIRED, P0)

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/node.cpp _bind_methods; doc/classes/Node.xml

**Patina today:** For each Node method in extension_api.json I grepped the literal '"<name>"' in interpreter.rs, scripting.rs and bindings.rs. These had 0 hits: add_sibling remove_child reparent get_child has_node get_node_or_null find_children find_parent is_inside_tree is_ancestor_of is_greater_than get_path_to move_child get_groups set_owner get_owner get_index print_tree print_tree_pretty get_tree_string propagate_notification propagate_call request_ready is_node_ready replace_by set_editable_instance reset_physics_interpolation get_scene_file_path. grep -rn has_node across crates/gdscene, crates/gdscript-interop and crates/gdobject finds only class_db.rs:5276/34267. Real implementations exist on SceneTree: reparent (scene_tree.rs:2874), move_child (2984), get_index (3911), find_children (8809), is_ancestor_of (8851), add_sibling (8864), propagate_call (8889), propagate_notification (8920), replace_by (8945), get_path_to (9055), get_node_or_null (used at scripting.rs:2050), request_node_ready (~7740). A bare self call returns UndefinedFunction (call_self_func_or_native, interpreter.rs:15503). `other.has_node(x)` returns Nil silently because node_has_method is true (interpreter.rs:15646-15667).

**Implement:** Godot scripts call has_node, get_node_or_null, get_child(i), remove_child, move_child, reparent(new_parent, keep_global_transform), add_sibling, replace_by, get_index, is_inside_tree, is_ancestor_of, get_path_to, find_children(pattern,type,recursive,owned), find_parent, propagate_call, propagate_notification, request_ready, is_node_ready, get_owner/set_owner (and the owner property), get_groups and print_tree on self and on other nodes. Patina has SceneTree implementations (scene_tree.rs:2874, 2984, 3911, 8809-9055) but no call_node_method arms (scripting.rs:2594-4922). Fix: add one native table in call_node_method (so both the self path via call_self_func_or_native and the ObjectId path via call_object_method reach it), plus a self-form in try_builtin only where needed. Use the existing SceneTree functions. reparent must honour keep_global_transform. remove_child must detach without freeing, so a later add_child re-enters the node. Wiring: interpreter -> SceneAccess::call_node_method -> SceneTree mutation during a MainLoop::step script phase.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A booted scene script runs `if has_node("A"): remove_child($A)`, then `add_child` of it under B, `move_child($B/A, 0)`, `get_node_or_null("Missing") == null`, `$B.get_child(0).name == "A"`, `is_inside_tree()`, `$B.is_ancestor_of($B/A)` and `get_path_to($B/A) == NodePath("B/A")`. After one MainLoop::step the dumped tree matches Godot's resulting hierarchy and every call returned the Godot value, not Nil (test: `script_node_hierarchy_api_mutates_live_tree`).

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. Dispatch uses quoted literal arms (e.g. interpreter.rs:6844 "get_parent", 6913 "add_child", 6990 "queue_free", 12536/12768). The same literal grep over all crate src (class_db.rs, tests and editor_server excluded) gave 0 hits for has_node, get_node_or_null, get_child, move_child, reparent, is_inside_tree, get_index, get_path_to, find_children, is_node_ready and request_ready. remove_child had 1 hit, in gdeditor/src/script_editor.rs:1176, a completion list and not dispatch. call_node_method (scripting.rs:2594) delegates to per-class handlers (navigation, kinematic, xr, timer, camera3d), and none of them is generic Node hierarchy.

### 2. find_child/find_children `owned` filter  (PARTIAL, P2)

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/node.cpp find_child(pattern, recursive=true, owned=true)

**Patina today:** scripting.rs:4222-4230 reads only pattern and recursive. SceneTree::find_child (scene_tree.rs:8789) has no owner check, so a runtime-added (unowned) child is found by default, where Godot's owned=true skips nodes without an owner. find_children has no script dispatch (method sweep).

**Implement:** Godot's find_child and find_children default to owned=true and only match nodes whose owner is set, which excludes children added at runtime by add_child. Patina ignores the parameter. Fix: add an `owned` argument to SceneTree::find_child/find_children that filters on Node::owner().is_some(), and pass the third script argument (default true) from scripting.rs:4222 and the new find_children arm. Wiring: script call in a booted scene.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`

**Prove it:** In a booted scene, a child added at runtime with add_child is not returned by find_child("Spawned") but is returned by find_child("Spawned", true, false). A .tscn-authored child is returned by both (test: `find_child_owned_filter_matches_godot`).

**Verifier note:** The owned-filter gap is real: scripting.rs:4222-4229 reads only pattern and recursive. The bigger gap is that find_children has no script dispatch at all. grep 'find_children' over gdscene/src and gdscript-interop/src finds only SceneTree::find_children (scene_tree.rs:8809) and no call_node_method arm. grep 'find_child' over interpreter.rs = 0. So `find_children("*", "Enemy")` from script returns Nil or errors. That is a commonly used Node API, so priority rises from 3 to 2. The bead should add the find_children arm (pattern, type, recursive, owned), not just the owned flag.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A booted scene script runs `if has_node("A"): remove_child($A)`, then `add_child` of it under B, `move_child($B/A, 0)`, `get_node_or_null("Missing") == null`, `$B.get_child(0).name == "A"`, `is_inside_tree()`, `$B.is_ancestor_of($B/A)` and `get_path_to($B/A) == NodePath("B/A")`. After one MainLoop::step the dumped tree matches Godot's resulting hierarchy and every call returned the Godot value, not Nil (test: `script_node_hierarchy_api_mutates_live_tree`). 2) In a booted scene, a child added at runtime with add_child is not returned by find_child("Spawned") but is returned by find_child("Spawned", true, false). A .tscn-authored child is returned by both (test: `find_child_owned_filter_matches_godot`).

title: PackedScene: instantiate() returns a detached, script-attached subtree; enter/ready fire once on add_child
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-instantiate] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** script -> instantiate -> add_child -> enter_tree, all in one MainLoop::step

**Godot ground truth:** scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp SceneState::instantiate (returns detached node with scripts); scene/main/node.cpp _propagate_ready (ready_first)

**Patina today:** SceneAccess::instantiate_packed_scene (crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs:7412-7439) calls add_packed_scene_to_tree_with_subscenes(tree, root, ...), which adds each node under the live /root one at a time (packed_scene.rs:3527, 3551). Each node therefore gets ENTER_TREE/READY on insertion, before its children exist. The script's later add_child calls tree.reparent (scripting.rs:6312-6313), which runs exit_tree and enter_tree again (scene_tree.rs:2874-2960), and READY with it. No runtime path attaches the `_script_path` scripts of the spawned nodes: the only `_script_path`->attach_script loops are at boot (patina-runner/src/main.rs:220-262, bootstrap.rs:524-568) and in the editor server. grep '_script_path' crates/gdscene/src returns only scene_saver.rs and tests. So `preload("res://enemy.tscn").instantiate()` spawns nodes whose scripts never run. The acceptance test crates/gdscene/tests/gdscript_preload_instantiate_spawns_live_scene.rs uses a script-less bullet.tscn.

**Implement:** Godot: PackedScene.instantiate() builds the node graph outside the tree with every node's script instance attached and @export/property overrides applied. No _enter_tree/_ready runs until add_child puts it in a live tree, and _ready then fires once, child-first. Patina parents the instance under /root immediately (scripting.rs:7436), never attaches the nodes' scripts, and the reparent in add_child replays the lifecycle. Approach: build the instance in a detached arena state, either a SceneTree 'orphan' list or nodes with parent=None that are not inside_tree, mirroring create_node + take_node in scripting.rs:6314. Attach a GDScriptNodeInstance for each node with `_script_path`, resolved via FileAccess like instantiate_script_with_values (scripting.rs:860-895), and apply the scene's property overrides through the script setters. On add_child, insert the whole subtree and run LifecycleManager::enter_tree once on its root. Move the boot-time attach loop into one shared gdscene helper so the runner, change_scene and instantiate use the same code. Wiring: script -> instantiate -> add_child -> enter_tree, all in one MainLoop::step.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/main.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs`

**Prove it:** A main scene script that does `var e = preload("res://enemy.tscn").instantiate(); e.position = Vector2(5,5); add_child(e)` on a key press, where enemy.tscn's root has `script = ExtResource(...)` with _enter_tree/_ready counters and a _process that moves it, ends with the enemy's _ready count == 1. Its _enter_tree saw position (5,5). It is never parented under /root, and its _process advances it on later MainLoop::step frames (test: `runtime_instantiate_attaches_scripts_and_readies_once`).

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. interpreter.rs:14354-14371 -> scripting.rs:7412-7439 adds the scene under tree.root_id() via add_packed_scene_to_tree_with_subscenes and attaches no scripts. add_child (scripting.rs:6298-6319) reparents already-parented nodes. Script-attach paths that read _script_path: autoload.rs:221 attach_subtree_scripts is private and called only at autoload.rs:195, plus patina-runner main.rs/bootstrap.rs and the editor. None is on the instantiate path. LifecycleManager::rewind_for_redispatch is called only from autoload.rs:164 and editor_server.rs:15983, not from instantiate. PARTIAL at P0 is right: spawning scripted scenes is core gameplay.
acceptance_criteria: A main scene script that does `var e = preload("res://enemy.tscn").instantiate(); e.position = Vector2(5,5); add_child(e)` on a key press, where enemy.tscn's root has `script = ExtResource(...)` with _enter_tree/_ready counters and a _process that moves it, ends with the enemy's _ready count == 1. Its _enter_tree saw position (5,5). It is never parented under /root, and its _process advances it on later MainLoop::step frames (test: `runtime_instantiate_attaches_scripts_and_readies_once`).

title: SceneTree: scene change replaces only current_scene (keep autoloads), defers all variants, re-attaches scripts, emits scene_changed
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-scene-change] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/scene_tree.cpp:1647-1740 (_flush_scene_change, change_scene_to_node, unload_current_scene)

**Patina today:** SceneTree::change_scene_to_packed (scene_tree.rs:8052-8088), change_scene_to_node (8103-8133) and unload_current_scene (8166-8185) remove EVERY child of root, which deletes autoload singletons too (autoloads are root children: autoload.rs:189/203). Godot deletes only current_scene. change_scene_to_packed/node apply immediately instead of deferred, and only change_scene_to_file defers (8138). MainLoop applies the deferred change (main_loop.rs ~4363) but attaches no scripts to the new scene; the attach loop exists only at boot (patina-runner/src/main.rs:220). current_scene_id is set only by these functions (scene_tree.rs:8084, 8128), so after boot get_tree().current_scene is null and reload_current_scene fails ('No packed scene source'). The scene_changed signal is never emitted: grep '"scene_changed"' crates/gdscene/src = 0. change_scene_to_packed, change_scene_to_node and unload_current_scene have no script dispatch: grep in interpreter.rs = 0. No test combines autoloads with change_scene: grep -l change_scene tests | xargs grep -li autoload returns nothing.

**Implement:** Godot: change_scene_to_node removes current_scene from root at once and sets current_scene=null. At the next frame (_flush_scene_change) it frees the old scene, adds the new one, sets current_scene and emits scene_changed. Autoloads and other root children are untouched. unload_current_scene frees only current_scene. Boot sets current_scene to the main scene. Patina wipes all root children in three places (scene_tree.rs:8052, 8103, 8166), applies packed/node immediately, attaches no scripts for the new scene, and never sets current_scene at boot. Fix: track current_scene_id from boot (bootstrap.rs:512, main.rs:574, editor Play); make all change variants remove only current_scene_id and queue the pending node for MainLoop's deferred phase; attach scripts with the shared helper from the instantiate bead; emit scene_changed on the root store; make reload use current_scene's scene_file_path; add script arms for change_scene_to_packed(PackedScene), change_scene_to_node(Node) and unload_current_scene.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A project with an autoload Global (script var score) and main scene A, whose script calls `Global.score = 3; get_tree().change_scene_to_file("res://b.tscn")`. After two MainLoop::step frames, /root/Global still exists with score 3, /root/B's script _ready ran once, get_tree().current_scene is B, and a scene_changed handler on Global fired once. reload_current_scene() from B rebuilds B (test: `change_scene_keeps_autoloads_and_runs_new_scripts`).

title: SceneTree: deferred calls and group calls fall back to native node methods (call_deferred("add_child"), call_group(..,"queue_free"))
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-deferred-group-native] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** a script queues a deferred native call during _physics_process and MainLoop's deferred phase (main_loop.rs ~4344) executes it the same frame

**Godot ground truth:** core/object/message_queue.cpp (Object::callp on flush); scene/main/scene_tree.cpp:350 call_group_flagsp (GROUP_CALL_DEFERRED/REVERSE/UNIQUE), notify_group_flags

**Patina today:** SceneTree::process_deferred_calls (scene_tree.rs:~7925-7958) handles only method=='set' and `if self.scripts.contains_key(..) { call_script_with_access }`. call_script_with_access goes to GDScriptNodeInstance::call_method -> call_instance_method_impl, which looks only in class_def.methods (interpreter.rs:16299-16312), so native methods are MethodNotFound. call_group_flags (scene_tree.rs:9222-9235) has the same script-only branch, notify_group (9239) writes only the node notification log and never calls notify_script, and GROUP_CALL_UNIQUE is ignored. The result: `call_deferred("add_child", n)`, `call_deferred("queue_free")`, `get_tree().call_group("enemies", "queue_free")` and deferred calls on script-less nodes are dropped silently. grep for call_deferred("add_child / call_deferred("queue_free in tests and crates = 0.

**Implement:** Godot's MessageQueue flush and call_group invoke Object::callp, which tries the script and then the ClassDB native method. Patina's process_deferred_calls and call_group_flags (scene_tree.rs:~7925, 9222) only reach script-defined functions. Fix: add a SceneTree-level native dispatcher, reusing SceneTreeAccessor::call_node_method (scripting.rs:2594) and the interpreter builtins for add_child/queue_free/remove_child/set/emit_signal. Use it as the fallback when the script lacks the method or the node has no script, in both the deferred flush and call_group. Make notify_group/notify_group_flags call notify_script. Implement GROUP_CALL_UNIQUE (coalesce identical deferred group calls) and notify_group_flags/set_group_flags. Make set_group write through the script instance when the property is a script var. Wiring: a script queues a deferred native call during _physics_process and MainLoop's deferred phase (main_loop.rs ~4344) executes it the same frame.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`

**Prove it:** In a booted scene, a body_entered handler that calls `call_deferred("add_child", preload("res://fx.tscn").instantiate())` adds the node by the end of that MainLoop::step. `get_tree().call_group("enemies", "queue_free")` on three script-less enemies removes all three after the frame. `get_tree().notify_group("g", 9999)` reaches a member script's _notification(9999) (test: `deferred_and_group_calls_reach_native_methods`).

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. interpreter.rs:7002-7027 -> scripting.rs:6413 -> tree.call_deferred, which only queues. The flush, process_deferred_calls (scene_tree.rs:7927-7954), handles only 'set' and script-defined methods (`if self.scripts.contains_key`). call_group_flags (9222-9235) has the same script-only branch, ignores the UNIQUE flag, and the deferred path inherits the same limit. notify_group (9239-9245) calls only node.receive_notification and never notify_script. The interpreter's call_group/notify_group arms (5722-5763) forward straight to these.
acceptance_criteria: In a booted scene, a body_entered handler that calls `call_deferred("add_child", preload("res://fx.tscn").instantiate())` adds the node by the end of that MainLoop::step. `get_tree().call_group("enemies", "queue_free")` on three script-less enemies removes all three after the frame. `get_tree().notify_group("g", 9999)` reaches a member script's _notification(9999) (test: `deferred_and_group_calls_reach_native_methods`).

title: Node: emit ready/tree_exiting/tree_exited/child_*_tree/child_order_changed/renamed from the lifecycle paths
description:
[audit-key: signal-emission-sweep/node-lifecycle-signals] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** the end-to-end path the Prove-it test drives: from a public entry point (a .tscn/project fixture, patina_runner/MainLoop, an attached GDScript, the editor server, or the web runtime) to the new code. The acceptance test must enter there, not call the implementation directly.

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/main/node.cpp:331 (ready after _ready), :358 tree_entered, :365 parent child_entered_tree(node), :423 tree_exiting (before EXIT_TREE propagation), :433 parent child_exiting_tree(node), :401 tree_exited (after removal), :576/:1696/:1767 child_order_changed, :1462 renamed, :3246 replacing_by(node), :2669 editor_description_changed(node)

**Patina today:** All nine are registered in ClassDB (gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1239 ready, :1243 tree_exited, etc.) so connect() succeeds, but none is ever emitted. Only tree_entered is emitted (gdscene/src/lifecycle.rs:50). LifecycleManager::enter_tree READY phase (lifecycle.rs:57-67) calls process_script_ready+notify_script but no emit_signal("ready"); exit_tree (lifecycle.rs:113-131) emits nothing; SceneTree::move_child (scene_tree.rs:2984-3030) dispatches NOTIFICATION_CHILD_ORDER_CHANGED but no signal. Absence greps (non-test runtime code, class_db excluded): grep -rnE 'tree_exit|child_entered|child_exiting|child_order|"renamed"|replacing_by|"ready"' gdscene/src gdscript-interop/src patina-runner -> only test fixtures (packed_scene.rs:5739 tscn string, interpreter.rs:35848 test). Scripted scan of every emit_signal/.emit call literal confirms.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth (node.cpp): _propagate_ready emits `ready` after each node's _ready (:331); _propagate_enter_tree emits tree_entered then the PARENT emits child_entered_tree(node) (:358-365); _propagate_exit_tree emits tree_exiting top-down BEFORE NOTIFICATION_EXIT_TREE and the parent emits child_exiting_tree(node) (:423-433); tree_exited fires after the node is detached (:401); child_order_changed fires on the parent after add_child/remove_child/move_child (:576,:1696,:1767); set_name emits renamed (:1462); replace_by emits replacing_by(node) (:3246). Patina: ClassDB declares all of them (class_db.rs:1239-1250) but only tree_entered is emitted (lifecycle.rs:50). So `await ready`, `tree_exited.connect(...)`, `child_entered_tree.connect(...)` silently never fire. Implementation: in gdscene/src/lifecycle.rs enter_tree READY loop add tree.emit_signal(id, "ready", &[]) after process_script_ready; after each tree_entered emit on the parent emit child_entered_tree with Variant::ObjectId(child). In exit_tree, emit tree_exiting + parent child_exiting_tree in a top-down pre-pass before EXIT_TREE (Godot order), and emit tree_exited after the subtree is detached in SceneTree::remove_node/reparent/queue_free flush (scene_tree.rs:2793, :2874, :8015). Emit child_order_changed on the parent in add_child, remove_node and move_child (scene_tree.rs:2984). Route the script `name = x` setter and Node.set_name through SceneTree::set_node_name (scene_tree.rs:3771) and emit `renamed` on the node there. Emit replacing_by in the replace_by implementation if present.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/lifecycle.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn scene whose root script connects `ready`, `tree_exiting`, `tree_exited`, `child_entered_tree`, `child_exiting_tree`, `child_order_changed` and `renamed` on a child (and uses `await child.ready`), run through the MainLoop frame loop, records each signal exactly once with Godot's ordering (tree_exiting before _exit_tree, tree_exited after detachment; child_entered_tree carries the child node) when the script add_child()s, move_child()s, renames and queue_free()s a node. (test: `node_lifecycle_signal_emission_test`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute it. I grepped every crate (class_db and tests left out) for the quoted literals "ready", "tree_exiting", "tree_exited", "child_entered_tree", "child_exiting_tree", "child_order_changed", "renamed" and "replacing_by". The only hits are fixtures and tests: packed_scene.rs:5739, interpreter.rs:35848/35858, and editor display lists at editor_server.rs:13355 and signals_tree.rs:308. lifecycle.rs:50 emits only tree_entered. The READY loop at lifecycle.rs:57-67 and exit_tree at :113-131 call no emit_signal. I also checked the dynamic emit sites (scene_tree.rs:2030 multiplayer, navigation_agents.rs:447, scene_tree.rs:2276 timer await notifications), and none of them carries a lifecycle name. Priority 0 holds: `await ready` and tree_exited are core idioms, and because the signals are registered in ClassDB, connect() succeeds and they fail silently.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn scene whose root script connects `ready`, `tree_exiting`, `tree_exited`, `child_entered_tree`, `child_exiting_tree`, `child_order_changed` and `renamed` on a child (and uses `await child.ready`), run through the MainLoop frame loop, records each signal exactly once with Godot's ordering (tree_exiting before _exit_tree, tree_exited after detachment; child_entered_tree carries the child node) when the script add_child()s, move_child()s, renames and queue_free()s a node. (test: `node_lifecycle_signal_emission_test`)

- `scene_tree.rs`: `child_order_changed` at ALL FOUR sites that deliver `NOTIFICATION_CHILD_ORDER_CHANGED` (`add_child`, `remove_child`, `reparent`, `move_child`) — wiring only some is how a listener fires for an add but not a move; `tree_exited` AFTER detachment in `remove_child` and `remove_node`; `renamed` on the NODE in `set_node_name` (it previously emitted only the tree-level `node_renamed` on the ROOT, so `child.renamed.connect(..)` never fired).

⚠️ **`tree_exited` placement in `remove_node` is load-bearing in BOTH directions:** after the detach (a listener may read `get_parent()`), and BEFORE the loop that erases the nodes from `self.nodes` — once a node is gone `emit_signal` has no source and the signal silently vanishes.

It states signals are deliberately not rewound because nothing can be connected before a script attaches — that reasoning still holds for `ready`/`child_entered_tree`, and the comment now says so, plus what would make it wrong.

**REMAINING: the acceptance test `node_lifecycle_signal_emission_test`.** Design settled, and two of the acceptance's literal spellings are deliberately avoided:
- ⚠️ **`await child.ready` would HANG, not fail.** `ready` is emitted inside `add_child`, so by the time `await` runs the signal has already passed and the coroutine parks forever. I will cover `ready` with a connected handler instead — the same emission, observable, no timeout.
