comments.author: bone
comments.text:
TurquoiseCastle — handing off after two failed verifies. **The implementation is in and I believe it is right; what is unproven is whether a GDScript handler can receive ANY of these signals.** Read this before re-attempting — one obvious route is already burned and the second failure narrows the cause a lot.

**ATTEMPT 1 (`verifier.log:13498`) — my harness, not the engine.** `phase` was `Int(0)`: `_physics_process` raised inside phase 0. Cause: **`self.connect(..)` is not a dispatched spelling.** `connect` has no arm in `call_node_method`; it is handled only on the cross-node path. And a dot call on `self` does not stay on that path — `call_object_method` short-circuits when the target is the current node (`if current_node_id == Some(id) -> call_self_func_or_native`), so it lands on the self path, finds no arm, and raises. Fixed by moving the driver to a `Driver` CHILD and connecting cross-node with the green `signal_value_emit_connect_await.rs:101` idiom.

**ATTEMPT 2 (`verifier.log:13515`) — the informative one. `Full log: []`.**
- `phase` reached **2**, so both frames ran to completion and all four operations executed (`move_child`, `set_name`, `remove_child`, `add_child`) with **no raise** — the seven cross-node `connect(..)` calls all succeeded.
- And **not one of the seven handlers recorded anything.**

**WHAT THAT RULES OUT.** The failure is not in the emission sites, and not a store mismatch: `SceneAccess::connect_signal` (`scripting.rs:6633`) goes to `tree.connect_signal(..)` -> `signal_store_mut(source)`, and `SceneTree::emit_signal` (`scene_tree.rs:4148`) reads `self.signal_stores.get(&source)` — the SAME map. So connect and emit agree on where connections live. The gap is in DELIVERY, or in the handler's writes persisting.

🔑 **LEADING CANDIDATE, with precedent in this repo.** A signal handler invoked **without the script instance bound** cannot write `self.log` — the assignment either raises into a swallowed Result or lands on a discarded copy. That is exactly the mechanism pat-mgixk.41 hit: the JS-callback pump invoked each Callable with no instance bound, so `self.x` inside the callback raised and was swallowed by an `.is_ok()`, and it was fixed by routing through `resume_with_instance_self` (which binds `self` AND writes instance properties back). If `emit_signal`'s delivery path does the same thing, EVERY script signal handler that writes `self.*` is silently inert — far bigger than this bead.

⚠️ **I have NOT verified that, and nobody should take it as established.** I could not find a single green test anywhere that proves a GDScript handler RECEIVES a signal emitted from Rust via `tree.emit_signal`. `cross_node_and_native_method_dispatch_test.rs:115` only *emits* `tree_entered` and checks the return value; it never connects a handler. So the premise my whole test rests on is itself untested in the suite.

**THE DECISIVE NEXT EXPERIMENT, cheap and one verify slot.** Connect ONE signal and have the handler write to a NODE property (`set_meta`/`set`) instead of a script `var`, then assert from Rust. That distinguishes the two possibilities in one run:
- node property written, script var not -> the handler RUNS and `self.*` does not persist (the pat-mgixk.41 mechanism; fix is in the delivery path, not here);
- neither written -> the handler never runs at all, and the problem is connection delivery.
Do that before touching `lifecycle.rs` or `scene_tree.rs` again — both already hold the emissions.

**WHAT IS ALREADY DONE AND SHOULD NOT BE REDONE** (all swept into HEAD by `Checkpoint: auto after 11 closes`, 38fe459):
- `lifecycle.rs`: `ready` after `process_script_ready`/`notify_script`; `child_entered_tree` on the parent beside the existing `tree_entered`; a top-down `tree_exiting` + `child_exiting_tree` pre-pass BEFORE any `NOTIFICATION_EXIT_TREE` (`node.cpp:423-433`) — a separate pass on purpose, since folding it into the bottom-up loop hands listeners a subtree that has already torn down.
- `scene_tree.rs`: `child_order_changed` at **all four** sites delivering `NOTIFICATION_CHILD_ORDER_CHANGED` (`add_child`, `remove_child`, `reparent`, `move_child`); `tree_exited` after detachment in `remove_child` and `remove_node` — ⚠️ in `remove_node` it MUST sit after the detach and BEFORE the loop that erases nodes from `self.nodes`, because once a node is gone `emit_signal` has no source and the signal vanishes; `renamed` in `set_node_name`.
- `scripting.rs`: a `set_name` arm. ⚠️ Without it **a script could not rename a node by any spelling** — `Node::set_name` is reached from exactly one place (`set_node_name`), which itself had exactly one caller, a test. `renamed` was unreachable wherever it was emitted. The `name = x` PROPERTY spelling is still unrouted; follow-up.

⚠️ **A hazard documented in the code, not fixed:** `child_entered_tree` fires on the PARENT, which in the assemble-then-dispatch flows (editor Play, autoloads) is already live and may have listeners, so it can arrive TWICE for one child — once from the premature pass `add_child` triggers, once from the real dispatch after `rewind_for_redispatch`. Emissions cannot be un-emitted. Full analysis is in that function's doc comment. The pre-existing `tree_entered` has had the same shape since pat-nzgdu.84, so it is inherited rather than introduced; suppressing it needs a "premature pass" flag threaded through `add_child` -> `enter_tree`.

**Two acceptance spellings to keep avoiding.** `await child.ready` would **HANG, not fail** (`ready` is emitted inside `add_child`, so by the time a later line runs the signal has passed and the coroutine parks forever). And `.new()` is proven only for `AStar2D`; whether `Node2D.new()` yields a tree-insertable node is unverified. Neither is needed — an authored child reaches all seven signals.

`scene_tree.rs` also carries pat-mgixk.62's uncommitted work in the 8620-8826 region; all my anchors are in 2929-4126 and I verified their hunks intact after writing.

title: Theme: wire Control.theme, ancestor themes and gui/theme/custom into the Play render path

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn with `theme = ExtResource(...)` on a Panel -> scene load -> editor Play frame -> rasterized pixels of a child Button reflect the theme's StyleBoxFlat bg_color

**Godot ground truth:** scene/theme/theme_owner.cpp (theme owner chain), scene/theme/theme_db.cpp (project theme from gui/theme/custom), scene/gui/control.cpp get_theme_item

**Patina today:** The only production Control render path is examples/editor.rs:300-306 -> gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:2176 build_control_render_items, which builds `Theme::default_theme()` (viewport_2d_render.rs:2230) and calls `control_draw_items` (2231), which forwards an EMPTY node_themes map (gdscene/src/control_render.rs:231-236). render_control_tree also passes an empty map (control_render.rs:438-446). `effective_theme` (control_render.rs:1181) and `control::resolve_theme_item` (control.rs:4270) have zero non-test callers (grep `effective_theme\|resolve_theme_item` outside tests). `parse_theme_tres`/`Theme::from_tres` (theme.rs:887,1047) have no callers outside theme.rs (grep `parse_theme_tres\|Theme::from_tres`). Doc comment at control_render.rs:1166-1170 claims this was fixed; the fix only exists for callers that pass a populated map, and none do.

**Implement:** Godot: every Control resolves theme items through its own `theme`, then each ancestor's `theme` (theme_owner.cpp), then the project theme loaded from ProjectSettings `gui/theme/custom` (theme_db.cpp initialize_theme), then the default theme. Patina: `control_draw_items_themed`/`effective_theme` implement the merge (control_render.rs:249,1181) but the only runtime caller, `build_control_render_items` (viewport_2d_render.rs:2176-2231), passes `Theme::default_theme()` and an empty node_themes map via `control_draw_items` (control_render.rs:225-236). Nothing reads a node's `theme` property, nothing loads a Theme .tres for rendering (`parse_theme_tres` theme.rs:887 has no callers), and `gui/theme/custom` is never read. Implement: (1) in build_control_render_items walk the tree, for each Control whose `theme` property is an ExtResource/SubResource path load it once via gdresource + `Theme::from_tres` (cache by path) and populate node_themes; (2) load `gui/theme/custom` (and `gui/theme/custom_font`, `gui/theme/default_font_size`... at least custom) from ProjectSettings at Play start and merge over Theme::default_theme() as the base theme; (3) call `control_draw_items_themed`. Wiring requirement: .tscn with `theme = ExtResource(...)` on a Panel -> scene load -> editor Play frame -> rasterized pixels of a child Button reflect the theme's StyleBoxFlat bg_color.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/theme.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/theme_resource_chain_reaches_play_render.rs`

**Prove it:** A project whose main scene has a Panel with `theme = ExtResource("theme.tres")` (Button/normal StyleBoxFlat bg_color = pure red) and a child Button renders red button pixels through build_control_render_items + rasterize_render_list; a second project setting `gui/theme/custom="res://theme.tres"` with no node theme produces the same red pixels; removing both restores default-theme pixels. (test: `theme_resource_chain_reaches_play_render`)

**Verifier note:** Refutation failed. The only callers of control_draw_items_themed are control_draw_items (control_render.rs:231), which passes an empty HashMap, and render_control_tree (440). The only production entry point is gdeditor viewport_2d_render.rs:2176 build_control_render_items, which uses Theme::default_theme() (2230) and plain control_draw_items (2231), called from examples/editor.rs:302. Grepping `effective_theme|resolve_theme_item|parse_theme_tres|Theme::from_tres` outside /tests/ finds only their definitions (control.rs:4270, control_render.rs:1181, theme.rs:887/1047). P0 stands: the docs claim this is fixed (control_render.rs:1166-1170, 240-247) but no caller does it, so it is a false-done.

acceptance clauses are now covered.

What I added: `project_base_theme()` in canvas_render.rs, used as the base theme
in `build_control_render_items` instead of the hardcoded
`Theme::default_theme()`. It reads `res://project.godot` through FileAccess,
pulls `gui/theme/custom`, loads that .tres and merges it OVER the default.
Test: `a_project_theme_setting_reaches_play_render`, appended to the bead's test
file, renders the UNTHEMED scene so the setting is the only route to a red pixel
(the acceptance test above it already proves that scene draws zero red without
it).

=== ⚠️ `gui/theme/custom` IS IN THE DEFAULT TABLE — the empty-path filter is load-bearing ===
project_settings.rs:881 seeds `("gui/theme/custom", SettingsValue::String(""))`,
and `ProjectSettings::get()` falls back to `defaults`. So `get()` returns
`Some(String(""))` for EVERY project, including ones whose project.godot never
mentions the key. Without the `.filter(|p| !p.is_empty())` in
`project_base_theme` this would call `FileAccess::read_file_string("")` and log
a warning on EVERY FRAME of every project. Do not "simplify" that filter away.

=== 🔑 DO NOT WIRE gui/theme/custom_font OR default_font_size — THEY WOULD BE INERT ===
The bead's implement list says "(and `gui/theme/custom_font`,
`gui/theme/default_font_size`... at least custom)". I checked whether the rest
is worth doing. It is not, yet:

`gdscene::theme::Theme` has the fields (theme.rs:82-86):
    pub default_font: Option<String>
    pub default_font_size: Option<i64>
    pub default_base_scale: Option<f32>
and NOTHING READS THEM outside theme.rs's own `merge_with` (:209-211) and
`clear` (:224). Zero hits in control_render.rs, control.rs or gdrender2d.

So populating them from ProjectSettings would change ZERO pixels and could not
be tested — the "field retained for existing callers is inert" trap. The work
has to be done in the other order: give the text-drawing path a reader for
`Theme::default_font_size` FIRST, then feed it from the setting.

⚠️ Do not be misled by grep here, as I nearly was. Searching
`.default_font_size` finds ~9 hits in gdeditor/src/theme_editor.rs, which looks
like live consumers. They are fields of a DIFFERENT struct — `ThemeResource`
(theme_editor.rs:169), whose `default_font` is `Option<ThemeFont>` and
`default_font_size` is `Option<u32>`, i.e. not the same types at all. That
struct is the editor's theme-EDITING model, which the bead's own verifier note
already flagged as "feeds the theme editor, not rendering". There is exactly one
`pub struct Theme` in the workspace, so the confusion is a same-named FIELD on a
different struct, not a second Theme type.

=== STILL OPEN (optional, none in the acceptance criteria) ===
 - `gui/theme/custom_font` / `default_font_size` / `default_theme_scale`:
   blocked on the above — needs a render-side reader first.
 - `project.godot` is parsed once per `build_control_render_items` call, i.e.
   per frame. `collect_node_themes` caches only within a call too, so this
   matches the established pattern rather than making it worse, but a
   longer-lived cache keyed on the res:// root would suit both.

title: Fonts: draw default UI text with the built-in TTF face in Play render, matching measured widths
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/default-font-render] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** default-theme scene -> build_control_render_items -> rasterize_render_list -> anti-aliased TTF coverage (non-binary alpha) in the framebuffer

**Godot ground truth:** scene/theme/default_theme.cpp make_default_theme (~line 1355-1375: FontFile from _font_OpenSans_SemiBold)

**Patina today:** rasterize_render_list_with_quality creates `let font = BitmapFont::builtin();` (gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:2934) and every Render2DKind::Text without a theme_override_fonts/font path is drawn with the 5x7 bitmap `draw_string(&mut fb, &font, ...)` (viewport_2d_render.rs:3184-3190). Meanwhile layout measures with the embedded Cantarell TTF (control_render.rs:1220-1234 measure_text_px -> builtin_face), so measured and drawn widths disagree; Button centering uses the bitmap `text_width` (control_render.rs:2828-2829). TTF drawing exists and is tested (gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs:1144 draw_string_renders_ttf_when_font_set; ttf_font.rs:351 draw_ttf_text) but the Play path never uses it for default text. Patina bundles Cantarell (ttf_font.rs:58-63) while Godot bundles Open Sans SemiBold (upstream thirdparty/fonts/OpenSans_SemiBold.woff2).

**Implement:** Godot draws all theme text with a dynamic FontFile (Open Sans SemiBold, default_theme.cpp make_default_theme) and measures with the same font. Patina's Play rasterizer draws every text item that lacks an override font with BitmapFont::builtin 5x7 glyphs (viewport_2d_render.rs:2934, 3184-3190) while layout measures with TtfFont::builtin (control_render.rs:1220-1234), so wrapped/centered text is positioned for one font and drawn in another. Implement: in the Render2DKind::Text arm, when no font_path resolves, draw with a process-cached `TtfFont::builtin()` + GlyphAtlas via `draw_ttf_text_with_fallbacks` at the authored pixel size; switch Button/LinkButton centering from `text_width`/`text_scale` to `measure_text_px` (control_render.rs:2826-2835, 2857-2860). Optionally vendor Open Sans SemiBold (OFL, same as Godot) as the embedded default face for metric parity. Wiring: default-theme scene -> build_control_render_items -> rasterize_render_list -> anti-aliased TTF coverage (non-binary alpha) in the framebuffer.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/default_theme_text_renders_ttf_in_play_view.rs`

**Prove it:** A default-theme scene with a Label 'Hello' at font_size 16 rendered via the editor Play rasterizer produces glyph pixels with intermediate (anti-aliased) alpha values and an ink bounding-box width within 2px of TtfFont::builtin().measure_line("Hello",16); a centered Button label's ink box is centered within 1px of the button rect. (test: `default_theme_text_renders_ttf_in_play_view`)

**Verifier note:** The claims hold. viewport_2d_render.rs:2934 `BitmapFont::builtin()`, and the Text arm at 3161-3191 draws TTF only when `font_path` resolves through with_override_font. Otherwise it uses draw_string with the bitmap font at 3190. Layout measures with builtin_face/TtfFont (control_render.rs:1229-1236). The Button arm centres with bitmap text_scale/text_width (control_render.rs:2827-2829). Godot loads _font_OpenSans_SemiBold (upstream default_theme.cpp:1381). The label is wrong, though: the TTF rasterizer (draw_ttf_text_with_fallbacks) and the embedded face already exist and run, but the default-text path does not use them. That makes it UNWIRED, not STUB. P0 kept because every default-theme text item in Play draws with the wrong font, at widths that disagree with layout.
acceptance_criteria: A default-theme scene with a Label 'Hello' at font_size 16 rendered via the editor Play rasterizer produces glyph pixels with intermediate (anti-aliased) alpha values and an ink bounding-box width within 2px of TtfFont::builtin().measure_line("Hello",16); a centered Button label's ink box is centered within 1px of the button rect. (test: `default_theme_text_renders_ttf_in_play_view`)

title: Particles2D: read Vector3 material gravity/direction + scale/color ramps in the 2D emitter
description:
[audit-key: vfx-particles/particles2d-material-reachability] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn -> PackedScene flatten -> MainLoop::process_particles -> ParticleSimulator -> _particle_positions/_colors/_scales -> viewport_2d_render read_particles

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/ParticleProcessMaterial.xml (direction/gravity are Vector3 for both 2D and 3D emitters); scene/resources/particle_process_material.cpp; scene/2d/gpu_particles_2d.cpp

**Patina today:** packed_scene.rs:994-1013 flattens ParticleProcessMaterial gravity/direction onto the GPUParticles2D node unchanged as Variant::Vector3 (pinned by gdscene/tests/particle_process_material_flattens.rs, which asserts Variant::Vector3 on a GPUParticles2D). The 2D emitter reader main_loop.rs:977 and :991 only matches `Variant::Vector2(d)` / `Variant::Vector2(g)`, so on every real Godot GPUParticles2D scene the material's gravity and direction are silently dropped and the emitter uses Patina defaults (gravity ZERO, direction UP; particle.rs:157-161). The 2D path (main_loop.rs:935-998) also never reads the flattened scale_min/scale_max, __color_ramp_offsets/__color_ramp_colors or __scale_curve_samples; only read_emitter_3d (main_loop.rs:418-440) reads them. The flatten test checks node properties only, never simulation. Greps: `grep -n 'Vector3' main_loop.rs` inside process_particles 2D block = none; `grep -c scale_min` in 2D block = 0.

**Implement:** Godot: a GPUParticles2D's motion lives on ParticleProcessMaterial whose `direction` and `gravity` are Vector3 (the 2D emitter uses x,y), and `scale_min/max`, `color_ramp` (GradientTexture1D), `scale_curve` (CurveTexture) shape each particle over its life (particle_process_material.cpp). Patina: packed_scene.rs:994-1080 flattens these onto the node (Vector3 kept as Vector3; ramps as __color_ramp_* / __scale_curve_samples), but MainLoop::process_particles 2D block (main_loop.rs:935-998) matches only Variant::Vector2 for direction/gravity (lines 977, 991) and never reads scale_min/max or the ramp/curve keys, so every Godot-authored GPUParticles2D emits with no gravity, the wrong direction, constant scale and flat colour. Fix: in the 2D block accept Variant::Vector3 (take .x,.y) as well as Vector2 for direction and gravity; read scale_min/scale_max into ParticleMaterial.scale_min/max; add a ColorCurve/ScaleCurve to the 2D ParticleMaterial (reuse particle3d::ColorCurve/ScaleCurve and main_loop.rs color_ramp_curve/scale_curve_from_samples) and sample them in ParticleSimulator::step_exact (particle.rs:739-745) instead of start_color.lerp(end_color). Wiring: .tscn -> PackedScene flatten -> MainLoop::process_particles -> ParticleSimulator -> _particle_positions/_colors/_scales -> viewport_2d_render read_particles.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/particle.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/particles2d_process_material_motion_from_tscn.rs`

**Prove it:** Loading a .tscn with a GPUParticles2D whose ParticleProcessMaterial has gravity = Vector3(0, 400, 0), direction = Vector3(0,1,0), spread 0, scale_min=scale_max=3, and a color_ramp GradientTexture1D red->blue, then stepping MainLoop 30 frames: published _particle_positions show particles accelerating downward (+y), _particle_scales are all 3.0, and an old particle's colour is bluer than a young one's. (test: `particles2d_process_material_motion_from_tscn`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute. The flattener at packed_scene.rs:1005-1014 copies direction/gravity unchanged, as Vector3. The 2D reader only matches Variant::Vector2 (main_loop.rs:977, 991). The 2D block (main_loop.rs:935-998) never reads scale_min/max, __color_ramp_* or __scale_curve_samples. Those keys are read only by read_emitter_3d (main_loop.rs:420, 578). I checked whether ClassDB seeding (packed_scene.rs:2690-2695, node_with_class_defaults) could supply a Vector2 direction/gravity for GPUParticles2D. It cannot: the GPUParticles2D registration (class_db.rs:13963+) has neither key. The Vector2 defaults at class_db.rs:14198/14260 belong to CPUParticles2D. The only other ParticleSimulator::new caller is main_loop.rs:1060, so there is no alternate path. The process_material shader hook (gdserver2d/src/particles_shader.rs) covers shader_type particles, not ParticleProcessMaterial. Priority 0 is justified: every editor-authored GPUParticles2D is affected.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn with a GPUParticles2D whose ParticleProcessMaterial has gravity = Vector3(0, 400, 0), direction = Vector3(0,1,0), spread 0, scale_min=scale_max=3, and a color_ramp GradientTexture1D red->blue, then stepping MainLoop 30 frames: published _particle_positions show particles accelerating downward (+y), _particle_scales are all 3.0, and an old particle's colour is bluer than a young one's. (test: `particles2d_process_material_motion_from_tscn`)

title: ParticleProcessMaterial: flatten the full parameter set so sub-emitter/collision/attractor work from Godot scenes
description:
[audit-key: vfx-particles/particles-material-reachability] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn material -> flatten -> MainLoop readers -> simulators

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/ParticleProcessMaterial.xml: collision_mode, collision_friction, collision_bounce, collision_use_scale, attractor_interaction_enabled, sub_emitter_mode, sub_emitter_frequency, sub_emitter_amount_at_end/at_start/at_collision, sub_emitter_keep_velocity, lifetime_randomness, damping_*, radial_accel_*, tangential_accel_*, angular_velocity_*

**Patina today:** The flattener's key list packed_scene.rs:1005-1014 is exactly [direction, gravity, spread, initial_velocity_min, initial_velocity_max, color, scale_min, scale_max]. MainLoop reads sub_emitter_mode/sub_emitter_frequency/sub_emitter_amount_at_end/keep_velocity (main_loop.rs:885-930) and collision_mode/friction/bounce/attractor_interaction_enabled (main_loop.rs:442-470) as NODE properties, with comments claiming 'the .tscn flattener lands these on the node' - it does not. The green tests author them on the node directly: gdscene/tests/subemitter_chain.rs:47 puts `sub_emitter_mode = {mode}` on the GPUParticles2D node, gdscene/tests/particle_attractors_and_collision_in_scene.rs:248 set_property("collision_mode") on the node. A Godot editor-saved scene stores these on the [sub_resource type="ParticleProcessMaterial"], so sub-emitters, collision and attractor opt-out never engage.

**Implement:** Godot: sub-emitter trigger, collision response and attractor interaction are ParticleProcessMaterial properties (ParticleProcessMaterial.xml), saved on the material sub_resource, not on the emitter node. Patina: packed_scene.rs:1005-1014 copies only 8 keys; main_loop.rs:442-470 and :885-930 read collision_*/attractor_interaction_enabled/sub_emitter_* as node properties, so they are only ever set by tests that write them on the node (subemitter_chain.rs:47, particle_attractors_and_collision_in_scene.rs:248). Fix: replace the hard-coded 8-key list with the full ParticleProcessMaterial property list from extension_api (113 properties: emission_*, *_min/*_max params, collision_*, sub_emitter_*, attractor_interaction_enabled, lifetime_randomness, turbulence_*, particle_flag_*, flatness, hue_variation_*, anim_*), still never overwriting a node-authored key; flatten the texture-typed curve params (`*_curve`) the same two-hop way scale_curve is handled (packed_scene.rs:1059-1080) into __<name>_samples. Then read lifetime_randomness, damping, radial/tangential accel and angular_velocity in both emitter readers where the simulators already have fields (particle.rs:127-140, particle3d.rs:252-266). Wiring: .tscn material -> flatten -> MainLoop readers -> simulators.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/particle_material_params_from_godot_tscn.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn where sub_emitter_mode=2 (AT_END), sub_emitter_amount_at_end=2 sit ONLY on the parent's ParticleProcessMaterial sub_resource spawns child particles in the Sub emitter after the parent particles die; a GPUParticles3D whose material has collision_mode=1 bounces off a GPUParticlesCollisionBox3D; a material with attractor_interaction_enabled=false ignores a GPUParticlesAttractorSphere3D. None of these keys appear on the node sections. (test: `particle_material_params_from_godot_tscn`)

**Verifier note:** The key list at packed_scene.rs:1005-1014 has exactly 8 entries. A search for process_material across crates/*.rs (excluding tests and class_db) found no second flattener. main_loop.rs:887-930 reads sub_emitter_* as node properties, and its comment at :889-891 claims 'the .tscn flattener lands these on the node', which is false. That makes this a false-done, so priority 0 stands. collision_mode is read only at main_loop.rs:448, from the node. ClassDB seeding does not help: the material params live on the sub_resource, not on the node.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn where sub_emitter_mode=2 (AT_END), sub_emitter_amount_at_end=2 sit ONLY on the parent's ParticleProcessMaterial sub_resource spawns child particles in the Sub emitter after the parent particles die; a GPUParticles3D whose material has collision_mode=1 bounces off a GPUParticlesCollisionBox3D; a material with attractor_interaction_enabled=false ignores a GPUParticlesAttractorSphere3D. None of these keys appear on the node sections. (test: `particle_material_params_from_godot_tscn`)

title: Particles2D: honor collision_mode from the material and collide in canvas space
description:
[audit-key: vfx-particles/particles2d-collision] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn occluder + emitter -> MainLoop::process_particles -> step_with_sdf -> published positions

**Godot ground truth:** servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/particles.glsl (2D SDF collision branch); doc/classes/ParticleProcessMaterial.xml collision_mode; doc/classes/GPUParticles2D.xml collision_base_size

**Patina today:** main_loop.rs:1004-1048 builds a CanvasSdf and main_loop.rs:1080 calls sim.step_with_sdf, but the 2D emitter block (main_loop.rs:935-998) never sets emitter.material.collision_mode - `grep -n collision_mode main_loop.rs` hits only line 448 (the 3D reader). ParticleMaterial default is Disabled (particle.rs:171) and resolve_sdf_collisions returns immediately on Disabled (particle.rs:629-631), so the SDF is built every frame and never used. Additionally resolve_sdf_collisions samples sdf.sample(p.position) (particle.rs:639,644) with the particle's emitter-local/spawn-local position, while CanvasSdf::sample takes a canvas_point (gdrender2d/src/sdf2d.rs:171) - wrong for any emitter not at the canvas origin. collision_base_size is ignored. Only module-level tests drive it (gdscene/tests/canvas_sdf_occluders_and_particle_collision.rs builds ParticleSimulator directly, line 61-64).

**Implement:** Godot: GPUParticles2D with ParticleProcessMaterial.collision_mode RIGID/HIDE_ON_CONTACT collides against the canvas SDF built from LightOccluder2D nodes with sdf_collision=true, using collision_base_size as the particle radius (particles.glsl). Patina: the SDF is built (main_loop.rs:1004-1048) and step_with_sdf called (:1080), but collision_mode is never read for 2D (only main_loop.rs:448 for 3D) so the material default Disabled short-circuits at particle.rs:629; and positions passed to sdf.sample are emitter-local (particle.rs:644) rather than canvas space. Fix: in the 2D block read collision_mode/collision_friction/collision_bounce (after the flatten bead lands them) and collision_base_size; pass the emitter global transform into resolve_sdf_collisions and convert p.spawn_transform/emitter transform -> canvas point before sample/normal_at, then convert the push-out vector back; subtract collision_base_size*scale*0.5 from the distance. Wiring: .tscn occluder + emitter -> MainLoop::process_particles -> step_with_sdf -> published positions.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/particle.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/particles2d_sdf_collision_from_tscn.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a GPUParticles2D at position (200,100) whose material has gravity Vector3(0,600,0) and collision_mode=1, plus a LightOccluder2D floor polygon at y=300 with sdf_collision=true: after 120 MainLoop frames no published particle (converted to global) is below y=300 and some rest near it; the same scene with collision_mode=0 has particles below 300. (test: `particles2d_sdf_collision_from_tscn`)

**Verifier note:** `grep -n collision_mode main_loop.rs particle.rs` finds only main_loop.rs:448-449, the 3D reader, plus the particle.rs field and default. The 2D block never sets it, so the Disabled default (particle.rs:171) returns early at particle.rs:628-630. The CanvasSdf is still built every frame (main_loop.rs:1010-1048) and step_with_sdf is called (:1080). The coordinate-space bug is real too: sdf.sample(p.position) at particle.rs:639/644 passes spawn-local positions. The publish step at particle.rs:960 shows global = spawn_transform.xform(p.position). particle.rs:24 itself says collision_* are unhonored.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a GPUParticles2D at position (200,100) whose material has gravity Vector3(0,600,0) and collision_mode=1, plus a LightOccluder2D floor polygon at y=300 with sdf_collision=true: after 120 MainLoop frames no published particle (converted to global) is below y=300 and some rest near it; the same scene with collision_mode=0 has particles below 300. (test: `particles2d_sdf_collision_from_tscn`)

title: ClassDB: make registered-but-unimplemented native calls fail loudly + add registration-vs-dispatch sweep test
description:
[audit-key: classdb-registered-but-nil-sweep/nil-systemic-guard] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: STUB]

**Wiring requirement:** the test must go through the GDScript interpreter's call path (call_method_on -> call_object_method), not through ClassDB directly

**Godot ground truth:** core/object/object.cpp Object::callp -> ClassDB::get_method (MethodBind) - every registered method has a bind and a real call

**Patina today:** Static sweep (comments stripped; test modules excluded): 854 classes and 3298 MethodInfo registrations extracted from gdobject/src/class_db.rs and editor_plugin_classes.rs. 2206 registered non-underscore methods; 1145 have no quoted literal anywhere in gdscene/src or gdscript-interop/src, and 1131 have none anywhere in engine-rs/crates. 361 of them belong to the 264 Node-derived classes, which reach the silent `if responds { return Ok(Variant::Nil) }` at interpreter.rs:15665. Largest clusters: BoneTwistDisperser3D 34, Node3D 28, IterateIK3D 22, ConvertTransformModifier3D 20, ImporterMeshInstance3D 20, BoneConstraint3D 17, ChainIK3D 17, CopyTransformModifier3D 16, Camera3D 15, LimitAngularVelocityModifier3D 15, GridMap 14, MeshInstance3D 13, ScriptEditor 12, AimModifier3D 10, MultiplayerSynchronizer 10, EditorPlugin 9, Node 8, MultiplayerSpawner 8, OccluderInstance3D 8, RootMotionView 8. The same failure mode was fixed piecemeal at least 4 times, each with a comment confessing it (interpreter.rs:12866 is_class; camera3d.rs:1006; scripting.rs:2851 Skeleton3D; scripting.rs:4870 LineEdit), but there is still no sweep test. There are also 42 registered methods Godot does not have on that class chain (for example SurfaceTool.get_vertex_count, CanvasItem.is_queued_for_redraw, MultiplayerSynchronizer.get_net_id/set_net_id, StreamPeerBuffer.is_big_endian, 8 EditorFeatureProfile names that do not match Godot's).

**Implement:** Godot: every ClassDB-registered method has a MethodBind, so a call either does real work or raises a script error; it never returns a silent null. Patina: call_object_method (interpreter.rs:15638-15672) returns Ok(Variant::Nil) whenever node_has_method is true and no arm answered. Today that covers 361 registered methods on Node-derived classes (see evidence), which makes has_method() lie and hides every gap. Implementation: (1) replace the `responds` Nil return with a RuntimeError such as `Native method '<Class>.<method>' is registered but not implemented in Patina`. Keep Nil only for methods that legitimately return void and are explicitly allow-listed as no-ops in one table. (2) Add an integration test that walks gdobject::get_class_list(). For each non-abstract Node-derived class, create the node through a SceneTree + SceneTreeAccessor, then call every registered non-virtual method with Godot-default-shaped args. Assert the result is never the 'registered but not implemented' error unless the name is on a checked-in allowlist file, so the allowlist shrinks as the per-class beads land. (3) Delete or rename registrations that are not Godot methods: compare against extension_api.json, e.g. SurfaceTool.get_vertex_count, CanvasItem.is_queued_for_redraw, MultiplayerSynchronizer.get_net_id. Wiring: the test must go through the GDScript interpreter's call path (call_method_on -> call_object_method), not through ClassDB directly.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`

**Prove it:** A GDScript running in a SceneTree calls `$Mesh.create_outline(1.0)` (a registered method with no arm). Today it returns null silently; after the fix it raises a script error naming MeshInstance3D.create_outline. A sweep test enumerates every registered method on every instantiable Node class and fails if any method is neither dispatched nor on the allowlist, with the allowlist checked in and its size asserted <= the current count. Registered names absent from extension_api.json for that class chain are rejected by the same test (test: `classdb_registered_node_methods_have_dispatch_arms`).

**Verifier note:** The mechanism is verified at interpreter.rs:15647-15671. node_has_method answers from the registration table, and when no arm answers, the `responds` branch returns Variant::Nil. camera3d.rs:1006-1013 describes the same failure in its own comment. title: Particles3D: render draw_pass meshes per live particle and spawn from the emitter transform
description:
[audit-key: vfx-particles/particles3d-render] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn -> MainLoop particle phase -> RenderServer3D sync -> gdrender3d frame -> runner output and editor 3D viewport

**Godot ground truth:** scene/3d/gpu_particles_3d.cpp (draw_pass_1..4, draw_passes, transform_align); scene/3d/cpu_particles_3d.cpp (mesh, MultiMesh instancing); doc/classes/GPUParticles3D.xml local_coords

**Patina today:** MainLoop::process_particles steps ParticleSimulator3D and publishes _particle_positions as PackedVector3Array (main_loop.rs:1219-1238), but nothing consumes it: `grep -rn '_particle_positions' crates --include=*.rs` outside main_loop hits only gdeditor viewport_2d_render.rs:1841 and scene_renderer.rs:714, both matching PackedVector2Array. `grep -rni particle crates/gdrender3d crates/gdserver3d/src` finds only Sprite3D/Label3D billboard enums; `grep -rn draw_pass` outside class_db = none. gdserver3d/tests/single_3d_particle_implementation.rs records the old duplicate renderer-side module was deleted. Also read_emitter_3d (main_loop.rs:381-472) never reads the node transform: ParticleEmitter3D has no transform field (particle3d.rs:653-672) and EmissionShape3D::sample starts at Vector3::ZERO, so particles spawn at the world origin while colliders/attractors use global transforms (main_loop.rs:515).

**Implement:** Godot: GPUParticles3D draws draw_pass_1 (up to draw_passes) mesh once per live particle using its transform, CPUParticles3D draws `mesh` via a MultiMesh; with local_coords=false (default) particles spawn at the emitter's global transform and stay in world space. Patina: particles simulate (main_loop.rs:1186-1210) and publish world positions that no renderer reads (no PackedVector3Array consumer anywhere in gdeditor/gdrender3d/gdscene render_server_3d), and the emitter transform is never applied (particle3d.rs:653-672, 692-736), so every 3D emitter is invisible and logically at the origin. Fix: add `emitter_transform: Transform3D` + `local_coords` to ParticleEmitter3D, set from node3d::get_global_transform in read_emitter_3d, transform spawn position/velocity at emit (local_coords=false) or at draw (true). In render_server_3d.rs, for GPUParticles3D/CPUParticles3D build one instance per live particle of draw_pass_1 (resolve the mesh like MeshInstance3D.mesh incl. QuadMesh/SphereMesh; billboard when the material's billboard_mode = PARTICLES), coloured by particle colour, scaled by particle scale, through the same instance path MultiMeshInstance3D uses. Wiring: .tscn -> MainLoop particle phase -> RenderServer3D sync -> gdrender3d frame -> runner output and editor 3D viewport.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/particle3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/particles3d_render_from_tscn.rs`

(test: `particles3d_render_from_tscn`)

**Verifier note:** The only consumers of _particle_positions are gdeditor viewport_2d_render.rs:1841 and scene_renderer.rs:714, both 2D. `grep -ni particle render_server_3d.rs` finds only :1108 (BillboardMode3D::Particles). A case-insensitive particle grep over gdrender3d and gdserver3d/src finds only sprite3d.rs and label3d.rs. `grep draw_pass` outside class_db and inspector_schema returns nothing. particle_positions_3d has no callers outside main_loop. ParticleEmitter3D (particle3d.rs:652-672) has no transform field, and EmissionShape3D::Point samples Vector3::ZERO (particle3d.rs:189).

title: Resource: call setup_local_to_scene from PackedScene instancing so local_to_scene resources duplicate per instance
description:
[audit-key: virtual-callback-dispatch/resource-local-to-scene] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn load via the runner/MainLoop -> instancing -> setup pass -> _setup_local_to_scene runs once per copy

**Godot ground truth:** scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp:438 make_local_resource during SceneState::instantiate; Resource::setup_local_to_scene -> GDVIRTUAL_CALL(_setup_local_to_scene) in scene/resources/resource.cpp

**Patina today:** gdscene/src/local_to_scene.rs:140 `pub fn setup_local_to_scene(tree, scene)` contains the only runtime call of the virtual (local_to_scene.rs:229 call_instance_method("_setup_local_to_scene")). `grep -rn "setup_local_to_scene(" engine-rs --include=*.rs` finds ONLY the definition and crates/gdscene/tests/resource_local_to_scene_setup_virtual.rs:86. `wants_local_to_scene` (local_to_scene.rs:119) has no caller outside the module. packed_scene.rs has no `local_to_scene` reference. So in a real scene load (patina-runner / MainLoop / editor run), local_to_scene sub-resources stay shared across instances and the virtual never fires, while the test calling the helper directly is green.

**Implement:** Godot: SceneState::instantiate (packed_scene.cpp:438) duplicates every sub-resource with resource_local_to_scene=true per instanced scene and calls Resource::setup_local_to_scene, which dispatches GDVIRTUAL_CALL(_setup_local_to_scene). Patina: the full logic lives in gdscene/src/local_to_scene.rs:140 (setup_local_to_scene) but nothing at runtime calls it; only tests/resource_local_to_scene_setup_virtual.rs:86 does. Fix: call crate::local_to_scene::setup_local_to_scene(tree, &scene) at the end of each public PackedScene instancing entry point (the instance/add-to-tree paths used by main_loop scene load, change_scene_to_*, and script `PackedScene.instantiate()`), scoped to the newly-instanced subtree so earlier instances are not re-duplicated (add a subtree-root parameter). Wiring requirement: .tscn load via the runner/MainLoop -> instancing -> setup pass -> _setup_local_to_scene runs once per copy.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/local_to_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs`

**Prove it:** Loading a .tscn through the normal scene-load path (SceneTree/MainLoop, not by calling setup_local_to_scene directly) that instances the same sub-scene twice, with a local_to_scene resource whose script defines _setup_local_to_scene, yields two distinct resource instance ids and `ran == 1` on each; a script calling PackedScene.instantiate() at runtime also triggers it. (test: `resource_local_to_scene_wired_through_scene_load`)

**Verifier note:** Grepped `setup_local_to_scene|wants_local_to_scene|local_to_scene::` over crates/*.rs excluding tests: the only hits are the definitions in gdscene/src/local_to_scene.rs (119, 140, 229) and `pub mod local_to_scene` at gdscene/src/lib.rs:59. Grepping `local_to_scene` outside that module, class_db and tests finds only serialized `resource_local_to_scene:false` strings (project.rs, input.rs, project_boot.rs) and comments at interpreter.rs:8149/21234. packed_scene.rs instance() (:2228) and instance_with_subscenes (:2381) never call it; instance_value (:250) only makes shallow copies of Array/Dictionary. So nothing at runtime calls it. P0 holds because the module looks finished but is never called.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn through the normal scene-load path (SceneTree/MainLoop, not by calling setup_local_to_scene directly) that instances the same sub-scene twice, with a local_to_scene resource whose script defines _setup_local_to_scene, yields two distinct resource instance ids and `ran == 1` on each; a script calling PackedScene.instantiate() at runtime also triggers it. title: GDScript: for-loop over Dictionary/String/Packed arrays/Vector2i and custom _iter_init objects
description:
[audit-key: virtual-callback-dispatch/gdscript-iteration-virtuals] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** scripts attached to scene nodes in a running tree must hit this path

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/Object.xml _iter_init/_iter_next/_iter_get; modules/gdscript/gdscript_vm.cpp OPCODE_ITERATE_BEGIN_* (dictionary keys, string chars, packed arrays, float/vector ranges, object iterator)

**Patina today:** gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:1115-1133 (and HEAD:1111): Stmt::For accepts only Variant::Array and Variant::Int, everything else errors 'cannot iterate over {}'. `grep -n '_iter_init\|_iter_next\|_iter_get' crates -r` -> 0 hits. So `for k in dict`, `for c in "abc"`, `for x in PackedInt32Array`, and custom iterator objects all raise TypeError.

**Implement:** Godot's VM iterates Dictionary (keys, insertion order), String (single-char strings), all Packed*Array types, float (range), Vector2/Vector2i/Vector3/Vector3i (range(start,end[,step])) and any Object implementing _iter_init(state_arr)/_iter_next(state_arr)/_iter_get(state). Patina interpreter.rs:1123 handles only Array and Int and errors on the rest. Implement in the Stmt::For arm: build items for Dictionary (keys), String (chars), Packed arrays (elements as Variants), Vector ranges; for Variant::ObjectId resolve the script and drive the protocol lazily (call _iter_init with a one-element Array state, then loop _iter_get/_iter_next) — preserve the await ResumeFrame::For path (interpreter.rs:1621) by snapshotting or extending it with an object-iterator frame. Wiring: scripts attached to scene nodes in a running tree must hit this path.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A script attached to a node in a loaded scene runs, in _ready, `for k in {"a":1,"b":2}`, `for c in "hi"`, `for v in PackedInt32Array([3,4])`, and `for x in MyRange.new(0,3)` (custom _iter_* class) and records ['a','b','h','i',3,4,0,1,2] in order with no runtime error; an await inside the custom-iterator loop resumes correctly. (test: `gdscript_for_loop_iterables_and_iter_protocol`)

**Verifier note:** Confirmed interpreter.rs:1115-1133: Stmt::For matches only Variant::Array and Variant::Int, and anything else returns TypeError 'cannot iterate over'. Grepping `cannot iterate|Stmt::For` across crates found no second executor (the other hits are type_checker.rs and shader_ast.rs). parser.rs:1078-1085 passes the iterable through unchanged, so nothing is lowered to an Array first. `_iter_init|_iter_next|_iter_get`: 0 hits. Raised to P0: `for k in dict` and `for c in string` are core GDScript, and a runtime TypeError on them is a broken-core language feature, not just a common gap.
acceptance_criteria: A script attached to a node in a loaded scene runs, in _ready, `for k in {"a":1,"b":2}`, `for c in "hi"`, `for v in PackedInt32Array([3,4])`, and `for x in MyRange.new(0,3)` (custom _iter_* class) and records ['a','b','h','i',3,4,0,1,2] in order with no runtime error; an await inside the custom-iterator loop resumes correctly. (test: `gdscript_for_loop_iterables_and_iter_protocol`)

**I independently confirmed EmeraldCreek's call that the remaining scope is a SEPARATE feature, and the obvious reuse does NOT work.** `SceneAccess::instantiate_script(path)` is indeed argument-less (`scripting.rs:8507`), and it delegates to `instantiate_script_with_values(path, &[])` — which looks like the hook to thread `_init` args through. It is not: its parameter is `values: &[(String, Variant)]`, i.e. NAMED exported-var seeding for script-backed Resources (`instantiate_script_resource`, pat-fk17e.1), not positional constructor arguments. That is a genuine object-construction feature in a different subsystem from this bead's iteration work — which IS done and verified (`verifier.log:13572` PASS with `RED-CHECK Detected`).

**Recommendation: give the constructor-args gap its own bead and close this one.** It is worth having — right now a GDScript class cannot receive `_init` arguments by any spelling, which is broader than one iteration test — but it is not what this bead is about, and leaving `.72` open keeps a verified P0 in the ready queue where workers keep re-screening it (I am the second to do so).

title: Web runtime: boot the exported project's main scene from the mounted pck in startEngine

The export shell crates/gdplatform/src/web_export.rs:489-502 mounts the pack (`vfs.mountPack`) and then calls `startEngine("patina-canvas")`, which never reads it. The real boot logic (project.godot parse, main scene, autoloads, input map, physics config) lives only in crates/patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs:45-92 + main.rs:402-450, and patina-web does not depend on patina-runner (crates/patina-web/Cargo.toml). boot_project_from_pck also uses std::fs::read (project_boot.rs:63), which has no browser equivalent. grep -rn 'main_scene|load_scene|PackedScene|instantiate' crates/patina-web/src returned no code hits. The DEFAULT_SHELL (crates/gdplatform/src/web_export.rs:489-502) mounts the pack and then never uses it. The boot code that does all this (crates/patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs boot_project/boot_project_from_pck, and run_booted_project in patina-runner/src/main.rs:402-450: enter_tree for autoloads then main scene, configure_from_project_settings, set_input_map, register_physics_bodies, audio_bridge base dir) is in the native runner binary only, and it reads the pack with std::fs::read. Wiring requirement: DEFAULT_SHELL mountPack -> startEngine -> boot_mounted_project -> MainLoop with the project's scene, driven by the existing rAF loop.

comments.text:
## pat-mgixk.74 — delivered the presentation primitive the acceptance depends on. PROGRESS, not a completion.

Following up my re-verify ask. Rather than wait on it, I built the piece the
`void renderer` clause actually needs, and made it host-testable.

### What I added

**`engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/wgpu_surface.rs`**

* `RgbaBlit` — upload an RGBA8 image and draw it over a render target. Two
  triangles, no vertex buffer, `textureSample` with a **Nearest** sampler.
* `GpuSurface::present_rgba(&mut self, ctx, rgba, w, h)` — acquires a swapchain
  frame and blits into it. The blit is built on first use and kept, since it is
  keyed to the swapchain format and rebuilding it per frame would recompile the
  shader every animation frame. The source texture is also kept and rebuilt only
  on a size change, so a steady-state frame allocates nothing.

**`engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/tests/gpu_blit_presents_rgba_bytes.rs`** (new,
`--features gpu`, loud SKIP without an adapter).

### 🔑 Two design points the test is built to pin

**1. `RgbaBlit` is separate from `GpuSurface` on purpose.** A `GpuSurface` needs
a real canvas or window, which no host test can create — that is precisely why
the web present path had no coverage. `RgbaBlit` draws into any
`wgpu::TextureView`, so the exact pass `present_rgba` performs is rendered into
an offscreen texture and read back on the host. That turns an
untestable-by-construction path into a measured one.

**2. The source format tracks the TARGET's sRGB-ness**, which is what keeps the
blit a byte identity:

| target | source declared as | effect |
|---|---|---|
| sRGB (e.g. `Bgra8UnormSrgb`) | `Rgba8UnormSrgb` | sampler decodes, target re-encodes — they cancel |
| linear (`Rgba8Unorm`) | `Rgba8Unorm` | neither happens |

One fixed format would be wrong for one case: `Rgba8Unorm` into an sRGB target
double-encodes (a washed-out frame), `Rgba8UnormSrgb` into a linear one
double-decodes (a dark frame). The test asserts **both** branches of that
choice, because only the linear one is exercised by the pixel assertions and
getting the sRGB one wrong is exactly how a browser frame comes out wrong.

### What the test asserts

A 2x2 source of primaries blitted into a 64x2 linear target, read back and
compared **exactly** — no tolerance, which the Nearest sampler and the format
pairing above make possible. Primaries are chosen so a stray encode/decode
moves a 0 or 255 off its rail and fails loudly instead of drifting.

* each source texel owns its quadrant (uv mapping);
* 🔑 row 1 must be the source's **bottom** row — clip space is y-up and texture
  space y-down, so without the v-flip in the vertex shader the presented frame
  is upside down, the classic blit bug. That assertion names it;
* 64px wide is deliberate: 64 x 4 == 256 == the `copy_texture_to_buffer` row
  alignment, so the readback needs no padding and the test carries no
  de-padding arithmetic to get wrong;
* a second test: a buffer one byte short of its claimed size is refused, and a
  zero-sized frame is refused **before** it reaches `create_texture`, which
  panics on a zero extent.

### Verification I could do

`rustfmt --edition 2021 --emit stdout` parses both files (exit 0) with **zero**
format drift — I applied rustfmt's own wrapping. I copied every wgpu descriptor
shape from this crate rather than from memory (`TexelCopyTextureInfo`,
`TexelCopyBufferInfo`, `multiview_mask`, `depth_slice`, `PollType::Wait`), since
the type names moved in recent wgpu versions and guessing them is a compile
error.

`RgbaBlit` / `present_rgba` have **0 occurrences at HEAD**, so reverting the
non-test file leaves the test unable to build. ⚠️ That makes the red check the
weak "does not compile without the change" form rather than a behavioural
failure — unavoidable for a brand-new API, and I would rather say so than let it
read as a strong pass.

### ⚠️ This does NOT complete the bead, and I am not claiming it does

`.74`'s acceptance is `web_frame_renders_scene_pixels` (already at HEAD and, I
believe, already passing — hence my re-verify ask), plus `check-wasm.sh` green,
plus the shell losing `void renderer`. **The shell still has it.** Removing it
needs the wasm-side join: `startEngine` taking the renderer that
`startCanvasRenderer` returns (`web_export.rs:518-519`), and the rAF closure in
`browser_runtime.rs` calling `render_frame_rgba` then `present_rgba` instead of
dropping the `FrameOutput`. That is a wasm-bindgen signature change in code this
lane cannot compile, gated only by `check-wasm.sh`. It is now unblocked — the
primitive it needed exists — but I have deliberately not written it blind in the
same pass as an unverified new pipeline.

### Ask

Please spot-verify just this increment alongside the `.74` re-verify:

- `cargo nextest run -p gdrender3d --features gpu --test gpu_blit_presents_rgba_bytes`

If it is green I will take the wasm wiring next and the bead's last clause with
it. If the adapter is unavailable on the verifier host the test SKIPs loudly
rather than passing vacuously, and I would want to know that too.

title: Web audio: drain the MainLoop's AudioServer into the worklet instead of a private mixer
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web-audio-scene] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** scene AudioStreamPlayer.play() -> AudioServerBridge mix -> WebAudioOutput ring -> pullBlock served to the worklet

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/platform/web/audio_driver_web.cpp (AudioDriverWeb mixes the single AudioServer into the worklet ring); js/libs/audio.worklet.js

**Patina today:** crates/patina-web/src/audio.rs:112-131 WebAudioEngine::new constructs its own `AudioServer::with_sample_rate(mix_rate)`. The scene's audio lives in MainLoop's AudioServerBridge (crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:141 `server: AudioServer::new()`, reached via main_loop.rs:2924 audio_bridge_mut). Nothing connects the two. startWebAudio (web_audio.rs:158) takes only a mix rate, not the engine handle. The only sounds that reach the worklet are play_tone and play_encoded called from JS (web_audio.rs:133-139). The shell hardcodes startWebAudio(44100) (web_export.rs:518) rather than the project's audio/driver/mix_rate. grep -n 'audio_bridge' crates/patina-web/src -> 0 hits.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: AudioDriverWeb is the output driver of the single AudioServer, so every AudioStreamPlayer/2D/3D and every bus effect in the running scene is what the AudioWorklet plays (platform/web/audio_driver_web.cpp). Patina today: WebAudioEngine (crates/patina-web/src/audio.rs:112) owns a separate AudioServer. Scene players feed MainLoop's AudioServerBridge (gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:141), which on wasm32 has no output device (cpal is gated off), so a game's music and SFX are silent while the harness's test tone plays. Approach: make WebAudioEngine borrow the mixer through the engine. Either give WebEngine a `pull_audio_block(frames)` that mixes main_loop.audio_bridge_mut()'s server through the existing WebAudioOutput resampler/ring, or let startWebAudio take the WebEngineHandle and share the Rc<RefCell<Runtime>>. Read audio/driver/mix_rate and output latency from project settings instead of the shell's literal 44100. Report the AudioContext's baseLatency/outputLatency into AudioServer.get_output_latency. Wiring requirement: scene AudioStreamPlayer.play() -> AudioServerBridge mix -> WebAudioOutput ring -> pullBlock served to the worklet.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/audio.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/web_audio.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/engine.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/web_export.rs`

**Prove it:** A host test boots a scene with an AudioStreamPlayer (autoplay, a packed WAV) through WebEngine, steps a few frames, then pulls render quanta through the same pull entry the worklet glue calls. It asserts the pulled block is non-silent and matches the WAV's resampled samples within tolerance. Stopping the player from script makes the following blocks silent. The audio engine no longer constructs its own AudioServer. (test: `web_scene_audio_stream_player_reaches_worklet`)

**Verifier note:** audio.rs:118 constructs a private AudioServer::with_sample_rate. grep 'audio_bridge' in patina-web/src found 0 hits. gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs has no WebAudioOutput or wasm32 path (grep 'WebAudioOutput|wasm32' found 0). web_audio.rs:158 start_web_audio(mix_rate: u32) takes no engine handle, and web_export.rs:518 hardcodes startWebAudio(44100). Scene audio is silent on the web, so P0 is reasonable.
acceptance_criteria: A host test boots a scene with an AudioStreamPlayer (autoplay, a packed WAV) through WebEngine, steps a few frames, then pulls render quanta through the same pull entry the worklet glue calls. It asserts the pulled block is non-silent and matches the WAV's resampled samples within tolerance. Stopping the player from script makes the following blocks silent. The audio engine no longer constructs its own AudioServer. (test: `web_scene_audio_stream_player_reaches_worklet`)

title: AnimationTree: load Add2/Add3/Sub2/TimeScale/TimeSeek/Transition, nested trees and filters from .tscn
description:
[audit-key: animation/anim-tree-load] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** packed_scene.rs:3398 -> attach_scene_animation_trees -> SceneTree::process_animation_trees_in_mode; scripts set parameters/<node>/scale, parameters/<node>/transition_request and parameters/<node>/add_amount via scripting.rs:2452

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/animation/animation_blend_tree.cpp (AnimationNodeAdd2/Add3/Sub2/TimeScale/TimeSeek/Transition), animation_node.cpp (filters, filter_enabled); animation_blend_space_1d/2d.cpp (any AnimationRootNode as point)

**Patina today:** The evaluator HAS these nodes: gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs:195-240 (Add2, Add3, Sub2, TimeScale, TimeSeek, Transition, BlendTree with filters at :639-668). They are constructed only in tests (grep 'AnimationNode::(Add2|TimeScale|Transition|BlendTree)' outside animation_tree.rs = gdscene/tests/animation_tree_blend_tree_nodes_runtime.rs only). The scene loader rejects them: animation_tree_tscn.rs:236-241 `other => ... not supported yet` returns None, and since build_blend_tree_node (:521-523) propagates None, ONE TimeScale node makes the WHOLE tree unattached. A test pins this behaviour (:977-986 unsupported_graph_node_builds_nothing). Blend-space points holding nested nodes are skipped (:437-447). tree_root and child nodes resolve only through SubResource ids.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: an AnimationNodeBlendTree may contain any AnimationNode type, wired via node_connections. Each node has `filters` (NodePath array) and `filter_enabled`. AnimationNodeTransition has input_count, input_N/name, input_N/auto_advance, input_N/break_loop_at_end, input_N/reset, xfade_time and allow_transition_to_self. Blend-space points may be any AnimationRootNode.

Patina: the evaluator already supports these (animation_tree.rs:195-240, 545-668), but animation_tree_tscn.rs:236-241 returns None for them. The None propagates and the entire tree is dropped, so real projects using TimeScale or Transition get no AnimationTree at all.

Approach: extend build_blend_tree_node (animation_tree_tscn.rs:~480) with arms for AnimationNodeAdd2/Add3/Sub2 (inputs per animation_blend_tree.cpp), TimeScale (input 0), TimeSeek (input 0) and Transition (input_count, input names, xfade). Map nested AnimationNodeBlendTree to AnimationNode::BlendTree and populate BlendTree.filters from each node's `filters` when filter_enabled. Let blend_point_clips accept nested nodes (change BlendSpace1D/2D points to hold AnimationNode, or wrap them). Resolve ExtResource tree_root through the resource loader. Make an unsupported node degrade to a pass-through or rest instead of dropping the whole tree. Replace the unsupported_graph_node_builds_nothing test.

Wiring: packed_scene.rs:3398 -> attach_scene_animation_trees -> SceneTree::process_animation_trees_in_mode; scripts set parameters/<node>/scale, parameters/<node>/transition_request and parameters/<node>/add_amount via scripting.rs:2452.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree_tscn.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn AnimationTree whose blend tree is output <- TimeScale(scale=2) <- Add2(add_amount from parameters) <- two clips, plus a Transition node switched by `set("parameters/T/transition_request", "b")` from GDScript: after MainLoop steps the target node's property equals the Godot-computed value (double speed, additive layer, switched input). A filter on Add2 excludes one track. (test: `animation_tree_blend_tree_nodes_scene_load`)

**Verifier note:** The core claim holds: build_animation_node (animation_tree_tscn.rs:198-240) and build_blend_tree_node (:544-589) handle only Animation, StateMachine, BlendSpace1D/2D, BlendTree, Blend2, Blend3 and OneShot. Anything else reaches `other => ... not supported yet` and returns None, and the `?` propagation (:540-541, :589) drops the whole tree. A grep for AnimationNode::(Add2|Add3|Sub2|TimeScale|TimeSeek|Transition) outside animation_tree.rs and tests found no production constructor. The loader does not read filter or filter_enabled: the only 'filter' hits are filter_map calls (:662, :696). One correction: a nested AnimationNodeBlendTree DOES load. The fallback `_ => build_animation_node` (:589) reaches the "AnimationNodeBlendTree" arm (:232) and build_blend_tree (:475-513), which inlines the nested graph, so drop 'nested BlendTree' from the bead scope. UNWIRED and P1 are acceptable because the evaluator nodes exist but scenes cannot reach them.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn AnimationTree whose blend tree is output <- TimeScale(scale=2) <- Add2(add_amount from parameters) <- two clips, plus a Transition node switched by `set("parameters/T/transition_request", "b")` from GDScript: after MainLoop steps the target node's property equals the Godot-computed value (double speed, additive layer, switched input). A filter on Add2 excludes one track. (test: `animation_tree_blend_tree_nodes_scene_load`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
TurquoiseCastle — claimed; AUDIT COMPLETE, implementation not started. Static reading only (worker build guard). Recording it because the evaluator side turns out to be **entirely finished**, which makes this a loader bead plus one small gap — not the six-node-type build the Implement line reads like.

**THE EVALUATOR ALREADY HANDLES EVERY ONE OF THESE, including their runtime parameters.** `apply_named_params` (`animation_tree.rs:1733`) has live arms for:
- `Add2` / `Add3` -> `parameters/<n>/add_amount` (`:1768`)
- `Sub2` -> `parameters/<n>/sub_amount` (`:1773`)
- `TimeScale` -> `parameters/<n>/scale` (`:1778`)
- `TimeSeek` -> `parameters/<n>/seek_request` (`:1783`)
- `Transition` -> switches on request (`:1788`)
So the variants (`animation_tree.rs:198-240`) AND their parameter plumbing are done. Nothing in the evaluator needs writing.

**THE ONLY LOADER GAP, and why one node kills the whole tree.** `build_blend_tree_node` (`animation_tree_tscn.rs:521`) matches `AnimationNodeBlend2/Blend3/OneShot/...` and resolves ports through an `input(index)` closure (`:539`) that recurses. There is simply no arm for Add2/Add3/Sub2/TimeScale/TimeSeek/Transition, so they fall to `build_graph_node`'s `other =>` (`:233`) which returns `None` — and because every arm uses `input(0)?`, that `None` propagates up and the ENTIRE AnimationTree goes unattached. One `TimeScale` node and a real project gets no animation tree at all.
Adding the arms is mechanical and follows `Blend2`'s shape exactly: `base: Box::new(input(0)?)`, `add: Box::new(input(1)?)`, and the amount/scale left at its DEFAULT (0.0 / 1.0) like `Blend2` leaves `weight: 0.0`, because the parameter path above fills it at evaluation time.

⚠️ **ONE REAL GAP THE BEAD DOES NOT MENTION, and the acceptance depends on it.** The acceptance switches the Transition with `set("parameters/T/transition_request", "b")` — Godot 4's spelling, a **StringName naming the input**. The evaluator reads `parameters/<n>/current_index`, an **int** (`:1793`), and `grep -rn transition_request` over `gdscene/src` and `gdscript-interop/src` returns **0 hits**. So the acceptance's own call does nothing today.
Fortunately it is cheap: `TransitionNode.inputs` is already `Vec<(String, AnimationNode)>` (`:547`), so the names are right there — resolve the string to its index and reuse `request_switch`. I plan to keep `current_index` working alongside it rather than replace it, since it is the existing spelling and something may depend on it.

**SCOPE I EXPECT TO SPLIT.** The acceptance names TimeScale, Add2, Transition and a filter on Add2 — nothing else. The Implement line additionally asks for nested `AnimationNodeBlendTree`, blend-space points holding nested nodes (`:437-447` skips them), and resolving an `ExtResource` `tree_root`. Those are structural changes to `BlendSpace1D/2D`'s point type and the resource loader, independent of the six node arms, and none is exercised by the acceptance. I will do the arms + filters + `transition_request` + the graceful degrade, and report the structural three as remainder rather than half-build them.

**The graceful-degrade change the bead asks for** ("unsupported node degrades to a pass-through or rest instead of dropping the whole tree") is the right call and is what makes the failure mode proportionate: today an unknown type costs the project every animation, not one node. There is also an existing test pinning the old behaviour — `unsupported_graph_node_builds_nothing` (`:977-986`) — which the bead says to replace, so that is a deliberate behaviour change and not a regression.

Both files are clean and cold (`animation_tree_tscn.rs` 1076 lines, `animation_tree.rs` 3819).

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
TurquoiseCastle — IMPLEMENTATION LANDED (uncommitted), acceptance test not yet written. Recording state so it survives, plus one clause I am NOT going to guess at.

**DONE — `animation_tree_tscn.rs` (+4835 bytes) and `animation_tree.rs` (+1621), both balance to 0 on `{}`/`()`/`[]`:**
1. **Six loader arms** in `build_blend_tree_node`, following `Blend2`'s shape: `AnimationNodeAdd2` / `Add3` / `Sub2` / `TimeScale` / `TimeSeek` / `Transition`. ⚠️ Amounts are left at their DEFAULTS rather than read from the sub-resource, exactly as `Blend2` leaves `weight: 0.0` — in Godot these are per-frame PARAMETERS and `apply_named_params` writes them just before evaluation, so a value read here would be overwritten. **Two defaults are NOT 0.0 and that matters:** `TimeScale.scale = 1.0` (0.0 would freeze every tree that never sets the parameter) and `TimeSeek.seek_request = -1.0` ("no seek pending"; 0.0 is a standing request to seek to the clip start every frame).
2. **`AnimationNodeTransition`** reads `input_count` + `input_<i>/name` + `xfade_time` and carries the names into `TransitionNode.inputs`. An unnamed port falls back to its index rather than being skipped, which would silently renumber the ports after it.
3. **Graceful degrade.** The `_ =>` fallthrough no longer propagates `None`: it passes input 0 through when there is one (right for any single-input effect node), else rests with an empty-name `Animation` leaf. ⚠️ This is the deliberate behaviour change the bead asks for and it **replaces what `unsupported_graph_node_builds_nothing` (`:977-986`) pins** — that test needs replacing, not fixing.
4. **`transition_request` by NAME** (`animation_tree.rs`), with a new `EvalParams::string` accessor in the style of `float`/`vector2` that takes both `String` and `StringName`. Acted on only when the string names a real input, so a typo leaves the current input playing instead of resetting to port 0; checked before `current_index` and left non-exclusive so the integer spelling keeps working.

**⚠️ NOT DONE — the filter clause, and the reason is structural, not effort.** The acceptance wants "a filter on Add2 excludes one track". The evaluator consumes filters at `animation_tree.rs:2482` — but only `bt.filters.get(&bt.output)`, the OUTPUT node's. An inner node's filter is never consulted, so populating `BlendTree.filters` from the loader would be wired-and-dead.
Making it work needs the filter carried on the `AnimationNode::Named` wrapper (the only thing that knows a node's name at sample time) and applied in `sample_node`'s `Named` arm via the existing `filter_value_lists`. That means a new field on `Named` — and `grep -rn "AnimationNode::Named {"` finds **23 sites**, including exhaustive patterns with no `..` (e.g. `:1078`) and constructors in other crates' tests. That is the bulk-struct-literal edit that has broken multiple crates for me before, and it is a change to the evaluator's node representation rather than to this bead's loader. **Recommend it as its own bead**; I will report the rest as partial rather than half-build it.

**NEXT (my next tick):** the acceptance test `animation_tree_blend_tree_nodes_scene_load` over the clauses that now work — a `.tscn` whose blend tree is `output <- TimeScale <- Add2 <- two clips`, driven through `MainLoop`, asserting double speed and the additive layer from `parameters/<n>/scale` and `/add_amount`, plus a Transition switched with `set("parameters/T/transition_request", "b")`. ⚠️ And a case that would have been silently impossible before: a tree containing ONE unsupported node must still attach, which is the whole point of (3).

title: AnimationTree: apply bone, method, audio and root-motion tracks and emit mixer/state signals
description:
[audit-key: animation/anim-tree-mixer-output] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** MainLoop::step (main_loop.rs:3906/4124) -> process_animation_trees_in_mode -> apply_mixer_output -> skeleton3d::process_skeletons_with_delta -> render

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/animation/animation_mixer.cpp (_blend_process applies all track types for both AnimationPlayer and AnimationTree; emits animation_started/animation_finished/mixer_applied); animation_node_state_machine.cpp (AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback state_started/state_finished signals)

**Patina today:** scene_tree.rs:4648-4696 process_animation_trees_in_mode writes every sampled value with set_animated_property_path only. There is no method-call dispatch, no audio keys, no nested-player starts, no root motion and no signals (compare process_animations :4197-4402). AnimationTree::get_current_values_targeted (animation_tree.rs:1535-1543) does not carry track types, and apply_animation_bone_tracks (skeleton3d.rs:1707-1730) iterates only `get_animation_player`. A tree-driven position_3d/rotation_3d bone track is therefore written as a stray `Hips` property on the Skeleton3D and the rig never deforms. Method-track arrays and audio dicts are written as junk properties too (grep 'TrackType::\|root_motion\|signal' animation_tree.rs = 0 hits).

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: AnimationTree is an AnimationMixer. Its blended result goes through the same track application as AnimationPlayer: 3D transform tracks go to Skeleton3D bone poses, method tracks are called (honouring callback_mode_method), audio tracks start streams, root motion accumulates, and animation_started/animation_finished/mixer_applied are emitted. AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback additionally emits state_started and state_finished.
