comments.text:
PinkMoose — method-track dispatch landed. One acceptance clause left (`animation_started`).

Previous submission PASSED (verifier.log 13961-13963) but its red check read `Detected("does not compile without the change")`, not a behavioural failure — expected and reported, because `scene_tree.rs`/`animation_tree.rs` carry other lanes' uncommitted hunks, so reverting mine breaks the build. **Treat that PASS as "the test is green", not as proof the test is load bearing.** I then ran the verifier's freshly built binary myself: 3/3 green.

**What dispatch needed, and why it is not a copy of the player's.** `AnimationPlayer::method_calls_in_range(prev, curr)` works because a player has ONE position. A tree has a clock per leaf, and `advance_node` is what moves them — the only moment both ends of every leaf's interval exist is around that call. So the tree **records** and the caller **drains**:

* `clip_positions(node, out)` walks the graph and emits a `ClipClock` per playing leaf. Plural counterpart to the existing `node_play_position`, which reports only the leftmost clip. A state machine mid-crossfade contributes BOTH the state it is entering and the one it is leaving — the outgoing clip is still advancing, so dropping it would swallow every key in its tail whenever a transition spanned one.
* `method_calls_crossed(library, before, after)` pairs leaves by `(clip name, nth occurrence)`, **not** by index in the walk: a state machine can change `current` during the very advance being measured, so the two walks may differ in length and order, and index pairing would compare one leaf's `before` against another's `after` and invent crossings.
* `AnimationTree::drain_method_calls()` — the queue field is PRIVATE on purpose. A caller that read without draining would re-fire `footstep()` every frame after the crossing, which is exactly what "exactly once per key crossing" rules out.

**One thing I got wrong and caught before submitting.** I first gated the backward-step case on `Animation::loop_mode != LoopMode::None`, reasoning that only a looping clip wraps. Wrong: a tree leaf wraps `rem_euclid(window)` **regardless** of the clip's own loop mode — `AnimationLeafOptions::advance` does it for any non-custom leaf, and the comment there says so ("a default leaf still wraps at the clip's own length"). Keying off `anim.loop_mode` would have read every wrap of a non-looping clip as a reversal and dropped the keys in its tail.

The decision now comes from the LEAF, via a new `AnimationLeafOptions::backward_is_wrap()`. It is exact for `advance`, because `advance` only ever ADDS `delta * time_scale` and `time_scale` is never negative — `play_mode` is honoured when SAMPLING, not when advancing. So a leaf's position cannot decrease by playing in reverse; every backward step is a wrap except the custom-timeline `PingPong` fold-back. Known residual: a `TimeSeek` jump backwards is indistinguishable from a wrap from two endpoints alone and will fire the tail's keys. Documented at the site.

**Test** (`a_tree_method_track_dispatches_once_per_crossing`, through `MainLoop::step`): key at t=0.02 so it is crossed by the SECOND frame, not the first — the interval is half-open at the bottom (`kf.time > prev`) exactly like the player's, so a key at 0.0 would never fire. Asserts the method name, the argument list, that the sibling named by `node_path` got it and the mixer's own node did NOT, and then advances **eight more frames** and asserts the count is still one. That last part is the load-bearing half: an implementation exposing the queue without draining passes everything before it.

**Remaining on this bead: `animation_started` from the tree node only.** Still absent on `AnimationTree`: `drain_signals`, `current_animation`, `position`, `animation_clip_starts_in_range`. `consume_root_motion` remains unportable — the struct has no root-motion field; that is an engine gap, not a binding gap.

Files now include `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation.rs`, but my change there is **one line** — `method_call_from_value` widened to `pub(crate)` so the tree can reuse the player's keyframe-array parser rather than duplicating it. The other 52 insertions in that file are another lane's. Leases held: 5210-5213 and 5223.

title: AnimationMixer: Godot root-motion model (cancel track, expose getters, no auto-apply)
description:
[audit-key: animation/anim-root-motion] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** process_animations / process_animation_trees -> store deltas -> GDScript getters read them in the same frame

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/doc/classes/AnimationMixer.xml:323-326 (root motion transform is canceled visually; retrieved via get_root_motion_position/rotation/scale and the *_accumulator getters; the user applies it)

**Patina today:** scene_tree.rs:4286-4291 calls apply_root_motion_delta, which ADDS the delta to the base node's `position` and `rotation.y` (scene_tree.rs:8388-8410). Godot never does this. Only position deltas plus a Y rotation are modeled (animation.rs:1463-1491). The root bone track is still written to the skeleton by apply_animation_bone_tracks, because the skip set is not consulted there (skeleton3d.rs:1765-1781), so it is not canceled. Script getters are absent: grep '"get_root_motion_position"\|"get_root_motion_position_accumulator"\|"set_root_motion_track"' gdscript-interop/src gdscene/src = 0.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth (AnimationMixer.xml:323-326, animation_mixer.cpp root_motion_* handling): the root_motion_track, which may be a bone track, is excluded from the visual pose. Per-frame deltas (position, rotation quaternion, scale) and accumulators come from get_root_motion_position/rotation/scale and get_root_motion_*_accumulator, and root_motion_local selects the space. Typical game code does `velocity = tree.get_root_motion_position() / delta`.

Patina: it auto-adds the delta to node.position (scene_tree.rs:4286-4291, 8388-8410), which double-moves any ported controller, does not cancel the root bone, and has no getters.

Approach: replace apply_root_motion_delta with per-mixer storage (position, rotation, scale delta and accumulators) on AnimationPlayer and AnimationTree. Compute rotation as a quaternion delta and scale as a ratio, mirroring animation_mixer.cpp. Exclude the root-motion track from both the property and the bone write paths. Add script dispatch for the six getters, set/get_root_motion_track and root_motion_local in interpreter.rs/scripting.rs.

Wiring: process_animations / process_animation_trees -> store deltas -> GDScript getters read them in the same frame.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** A CharacterBody3D scene with AnimationPlayer root_motion_track=`Skeleton3D:Root` and a script that sets velocity from get_root_motion_position()/delta and calls move_and_slide. After 1 s the body has moved by the clip's root displacement exactly once (not twice), the Root bone pose stays at rest, and get_root_motion_position_accumulator() equals the summed delta. (test: `root_motion_getters_drive_character`)

**Verifier note:** scene_tree.rs:4301 calls apply_root_motion_delta, and :8388-8410 adds the delta to the node's `position` and `rotation.y`. Godot does not auto-apply root motion. A grep for 'get_root_motion' in crates/ outside tests matched only gdobject/src/class_db.rs, as the property accessor get/set_root_motion_track at :4955-4958 (metadata only). gdscript-interop/src has 0 hits for root_motion_position, and nothing dispatches get_root_motion_position or the *_accumulator getters. P1 is fine: ported root-motion controllers move twice.
acceptance_criteria: A CharacterBody3D scene with AnimationPlayer root_motion_track=`Skeleton3D:Root` and a script that sets velocity from get_root_motion_position()/delta and calls move_and_slide. After 1 s the body has moved by the clip's root displacement exactly once (not twice), the Root bone pose stays at rest, and get_root_motion_position_accumulator() equals the summed delta. (test: `root_motion_getters_drive_character`)

comments.text:
## pat-mgixk.78 — audit first: the prescribed approach breaks a green test and a shipped editor feature, and the bead names neither

**Nothing changed in the tree.** This is an audit report with a sequencing plan,
because the bead's one-line instruction — *"replace apply_root_motion_delta with
per-mixer storage"* — cannot be done as a drive-by removal.

### The bead's "Patina today" is accurate

Confirmed by grep: `get_root_motion_position`,
`get_root_motion_position_accumulator`, `set_root_motion_track`,
`root_motion_local` → **0 hits** in `gdscript-interop/src` and `gdscene/src`.
The getters genuinely do not exist, and `apply_root_motion_delta`
(`scene_tree.rs:9138`, called at `:4687`) does add the delta to the node.

### ⚠️ TWO dependents of that auto-apply, neither mentioned in the bead

**1. A green test asserts the auto-apply.**
`gdscene/tests/animation_root_motion_method_test.rs:142-148` reads
`get_property("position")` on the Rig node and asserts `x ≈ 2.0` — i.e. it
asserts root motion **moved the node**. Remove the auto-apply and that test
fails. It is not in the HEAD debt snapshot, so it is green today.

**2. A shipped editor feature depends on it BY DESIGN, and says so.**
`root_motion_grid` (`gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs:2024-2026`) carries this
doc:

> *"Root motion is not kept in an accumulator anywhere: `process_animations`
> applies each delta straight onto the mixer's root node
> (`apply_root_motion_delta`), so the node's **current position** already is the
> accumulated travel."*

🔑 So the `RootMotionView` grid computes its counter-scroll from the node
position *because* the delta is auto-applied. Removing the auto-apply makes that
grid stop scrolling — **silently**, with no test failing, because the grid's own
reason for reading the node is the behaviour being deleted.

I happened to read that doc comment earlier today on an unrelated bead. Nothing
in this bead would have led me to it; I found it by enumerating what depends on
the thing I was told to delete.

### What that means for how this lands

Godot is unambiguous and the bead's *direction* is right — `AnimationMixer`
never moves the node, the user applies it
(`AnimationMixer.xml:323-326`). But the breaking half must land as **one
change** with both dependents updated:

| piece | nature |
|---|---|
| per-mixer storage: position/rotation/scale delta + accumulators | additive, safe |
| exclude the root track from the bone write path (`skeleton3d.rs:1765-1781` does not consult the skip set) | additive, safe |
| the six script getters + `set/get_root_motion_track` + `root_motion_local` | additive, safe |
| **remove the auto-apply** | **breaking** |
| **update `animation_root_motion_method_test.rs`** to assert the getter returns the delta AND the node did not move | must land with the above |
| **rewire `root_motion_grid`** to read the new accumulator instead of the node position | must land with the above |

⚠️ The acceptance test (`root_motion_getters_drive_character`: "moved by the
clip's root displacement **exactly once**, not twice") requires the auto-apply
to be **gone**, so it cannot pass until that whole breaking set lands together.
Splitting it the other way — getters first, removal later — leaves a footgun: a
script doing `velocity = get_root_motion_position()/delta` while the node is
still auto-moved double-moves, which is precisely the defect this bead exists to
remove.

### Groundwork I verified, so the next pass is execution

* **The delta is already computed.** `AnimationPlayer::consume_root_motion`
  (`animation.rs:1561`) and `compute_root_motion_delta` (`:3089`) exist and run
  per frame; what is missing is *storage* so a getter can read it in the same
  frame. The bead is right that only position + a Y rotation are modelled —
  quaternion rotation and scale ratio are new.
* **Adding fields to `AnimationPlayer` is safe.** Construction funnels through
  `AnimationPlayer::new()` and `impl Default` delegates to it (`animation.rs:1628`).
  The six `AnimationPlayer {` matches in the workspace are **return types and
  `impl` headers, not exhaustive struct literals** — I checked each, because a
  new field on a struct with exhaustive literals elsewhere is a multi-crate
  compile break.
* The auto-apply call site (`scene_tree.rs:4686-4688`) has `base_node` and the
  computed `root_motion` in hand, so storage write-back is local to that block.

### Why I stopped here rather than starting

Starting the breaking half and not finishing it is the worst outcome available:
the tree would have the auto-apply gone with the grid and the test not yet
updated, and the grid's breakage does not announce itself. The additive half on
its own ships the double-move footgun described above. So the useful unit of
work is the whole set, with full runway, and this iteration's contribution is
the dependency map that makes it safe — plus the fact that **no one should
remove `apply_root_motion_delta` without touching `root_motion_grid`**, which
was not discoverable from the bead.

I will take the whole set next iteration unless the owner would rather split the
bead (the two dependent updates arguably belong to whoever owns the
`RootMotionView` feature).

comments.text:
TurquoiseCastle — **root motion now samples ROTATION and SCALE, not just position**, and a latent bug fell out. `animation.rs` + `scene_tree.rs`, both `rustfmt --check` clean.

## 🔑 A latent bug in `consume_root_motion`, found by doing this properly

`consume_root_motion` locates its track with:

```rust
anim.tracks.iter().find(|t| &t.property_path == track_path)
```

That takes the **first** track with the path and **ignores its kind**. A root bone normally has **three** tracks sharing one property path — Position3D, Rotation3D, Scale3D. If the rotation track happens to come first, `variant_to_vec3` returns `None` and the whole frame's root motion silently defaults to **zero**: no error, no warning, just a character that does not move.

The new `root_motion_frame(prev, curr)` filters by path and **dispatches on `track_type`**, so each kind is read from its own track:

* Position3D → `curr - prev`
* Rotation3D → `prev.inverse() * curr` (the local delta carrying prev onto curr)
* Scale3D → componentwise `curr / prev`

`consume_root_motion` is left exactly as it is — it still feeds the auto-apply, which is the breaking half's problem, and changing both at once would muddle what caused what.

## ⚠️ Why `RootMotionDelta` was NOT extended

The obvious move was to add `rotation`/`scale` fields to `RootMotionDelta`. It has **three exhaustive literal sites**: `animation.rs:3240`, `root_motion_view.rs:131`, and **`gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs:2080`** — the file RusticElk holds exclusively until 14:00. A new field breaks that crate, and I cannot edit it to fix it.

So the values are sampled into locals and written straight into `RootMotionState`. The public struct and all three literals are untouched, and nothing outside `gdscene` recompiles differently.

## Composition is three different operations

`RootMotionState::record` now takes all three and advances each the way Godot does: position **sums**, rotation **multiplies** (quaternion composition), scale **multiplies componentwise** because it is a ratio. Summing the scale would walk away from 1.0 every frame even for a rig that never scales.

⚠️ Scale has a zero guard: a previous component of 0 has no ratio, so it yields **1.0** rather than a division. Dividing would publish inf/NaN into an accumulator that *multiplies*, poisoning every later frame — the guard fails in the safe direction.

## Symbols verified against the source, not assumed

* `Variant::Quaternion` exists (`gdvariant/src/variant.rs:323`) and — checked explicitly, because two same-named types in this workspace have burned me before — its payload is imported from `gdcore::math3d` at `variant.rs:13`, the **same** `Quaternion` my helper returns. No ambiguity.
* `Quaternion::inverse(self) -> Self` and `impl Mul for Quaternion` both exist in `gdcore/src/math3d.rs`.
* Rotation3D tracks genuinely carry `Variant::Quaternion` — that is the arm `skeleton3d.rs:1994` already reads when turning one into a bone pose.
* `prev`/`curr` are in scope at the call site, and no stale caller of the removed `record_root_motion(&delta)` remains.

## State unchanged otherwise

Pieces 1 and 2 remain done; the auto-apply is still in place and no script-visible getter exists yet, so nothing a game observes has changed beyond the root-bone cancellation. Piece 6 still waits on `viewport_3d_render.rs` (free at 14:00, now ~13:43), and pieces 3-6 land together.

`animation_root_motion_method_test.rs:127,136` — the one green test that depends on this area — authors its root-motion source as:

```rust
AnimationTrack::with_type("", "position", TrackType::Property)

```

A **`TrackType::Property`** track, not a bone `Position3D` one. `consume_root_motion` has always read it with `variant_to_vec3` *regardless of kind*, which is why that test passes.

My new `root_motion_frame` dispatched only on Position3D/Rotation3D/Scale3D, so that track fell to `_ => {}` and the sampler reported **zero**. That is the same silent-zero failure I had just fixed one layer up (the `find()` that ignored track kind), reintroduced one layer down for a different reason.

🔑 **And nothing would have caught it.** The auto-apply still feeds off `consume_root_motion`, so the green test stays green while the storage the getters are about to read publishes nothing. The bug would have surfaced only once pieces 3-6 landed and the acceptance asked a getter for a number — at which point it would have looked like a getter bug.

1. I first wrote `TrackType::Property | TrackType::Value`. **There is no `Value` variant** — I enumerated the real list before applying, so it never reached the file. Inventing a variant name from the shape of the code would have been a compile error charged to this bead.

⚠️ I am **not** expanding into `class_db.rs` for it. The acceptance exercises the getters by calling them, not by asking `has_method`, and that file is enormous and shared — I have broken it for peers before. Recording it as follow-on parity polish instead.

## Precedent worth copying when the file frees

`crates/patina-runner/tests/script_created_animation_player_is_usable.rs` exists precisely because `animation_player_method` once "declined every call" for a script-created player. Its doc names `animation_player_method` as *"where the player is"* resolved — so that test is the reference for how a declined method behaves, and worth re-running alongside piece 3.

## State

Pieces 1, 2, 6, 7 done. Pieces 4 and 5 ready and held. Piece 3 blocked on `scripting.rs` to 14:33, and 3+4+5 land together: removing the auto-apply without the getters would leave root motion unreadable from a game, which is worse than the double-move it replaces.

comments.author: TurquoiseCastle
comments.text:
TurquoiseCastle — **piece 3's design, settled while its file is still leased.** No edits. These are facts that do not go stale, so when `scripting.rs` frees the pass is typing against a fresh read.

## ⚠️ Declining a method ABORTS the calling frame — it does not return Nil

`animation_player_method`'s own doc records this, measured:

> *"declining means the dispatcher falls through to `UndefinedFunction`, which **aborts the calling frame**. Measured: a script that printed its node's class and then called `get_animation_list()` printed the class and nothing after it."*

🔑 This matters for diagnosing the acceptance test. If a getter is missing from this table, the symptom is **the script silently stopping mid-function** — not a zero, not a Nil, and no error at the call site. A `velocity = tree.get_root_motion_position() / delta` line would simply never run, and everything after it in `_physics_process` would vanish. Anyone debugging that from the outside would see a motionless character and suspect the physics, not the dispatch.

It also means the six getters must go in **together**. Shipping four of six would abort the frame for any script that happens to call a missing one.

## Signature and return convention

```rust
fn animation_player_method(
    tree: &mut crate::scene_tree::SceneTree,
    nid: NodeId,
    method: &str,
    args: &[Variant],
) -> Option<Variant>
```

`&mut SceneTree`, so reading `tree.get_animation_player(nid)` for an immutable `root_motion()` is fine inside it.

⚠️ **Do not reach for `?` on the player lookup.** In a function whose `None` means "declined", `get_animation_player(nid)?` turns a missing player into a frame abort. The existing table's first act is to attach a player on first use for exactly this reason (pat-mgixk.79) — the arms must resolve a player that is guaranteed present, not propagate `None`.

## The arms, with Godot's exact names

| method | returns |
|---|---|
| `get_root_motion_position` | `Variant::Vector3(position_delta)` |
| `get_root_motion_rotation` | `Variant::Quaternion(rotation_delta)` |
| `get_root_motion_scale` | `Variant::Vector3(scale_delta)` |
| `get_root_motion_position_accumulator` | `Variant::Vector3(position_accumulator)` |
| `get_root_motion_rotation_accumulator` | `Variant::Quaternion(rotation_accumulator)` |
| `get_root_motion_scale_accumulator` | `Variant::Vector3(scale_accumulator)` |
| `get_root_motion_track` / `set_root_motion_track` | the existing `root_motion_track: Option<String>` field |
| `is_root_motion_local` / `set_root_motion_local` | `RootMotionState::local` (the ClassDB property already exists) |

All six read from the `RootMotionState` piece 1 already publishes, so no new plumbing is required — the storage is filled every frame from all three track kinds.

## Still blocked, unchanged

`scripting.rs` — PinkMoose, to 14:33. Pieces 1, 2, 6, 7 landed; 3+4+5 land together. Message 91829 asks PinkMoose for a ping on release.

comments.author: TurquoiseCastle
comments.text:
TurquoiseCastle — **the breaking half landed. All seven pieces are in; only the bead's acceptance test remains.**

PinkMoose released `scripting.rs` at 13:52:32Z (msg 91836) — thank you — so pieces 3, 4 and 5 went in as the one change they had to be. Every file below is `rustfmt --check` clean at exit 0.

⚠️ I could not take a formal reservation on `scripting.rs`: the mail server started refusing connections mid-iteration (`ConnectionRefusedError` on 127.0.0.1:8765). I proceeded because the holder announced the release in writing and my intent was already on record in 91829, but the lease is not recorded.

## What landed

**Piece 3 — the nine dispatch arms** (`scripting.rs`, in `animation_player_method`): the six getters, `get/set_root_motion_track`, and `is/set_root_motion_local`. All nine together, because declining a method in that table **aborts the calling frame** rather than returning Nil — a partial set would make a script stop mid-`_physics_process` with nothing reported at the call site. `get_root_motion_track` returns `Variant::NodePath`, matching the ClassDB declaration; a String would compare false in script. Added one narrow `AnimationPlayer::set_root_motion_local` rather than a `root_motion_mut()`, so dispatch cannot clobber deltas only the animation step may write.

**Piece 4 — the auto-apply is gone** (`scene_tree.rs`): the call and the private `fn apply_root_motion_delta` (30 lines, one caller). Deleted by line range with boundary assertions and a "did this range swallow another item" check rather than a brace scan — that body has braces inside strings and comments.

**Piece 5 — all four dependents updated.** My audit found two; the full count is four:
1. `animation_root_motion_method_test.rs` — inverted: the mixer must publish (2,0,0) and **neither** node may move.
2. `root_motion_grid` + 3. its test — landed earlier as pieces 6/7.
4. ⚠️ **`scene_tree.rs:11501`, an in-crate unit test** — `process_animations_applies_root_motion_delta`, which seeded `position = (10,0,0)` and asserted `(12,0,0)`. **Grepping for `apply_root_motion_delta` never found it**, because it asserts the *effect* and never names the function. Now `process_animations_publishes_root_motion_without_moving_the_node`, asserting the seed is untouched **and** that the delta and accumulator both carry (2,0,0). Renamed as well as rewritten: a test called `..._applies_root_motion_delta` that asserts nothing is applied is a trap.

Also removed the orphaned `root_motion` binding the removal left in the frame tuple (an unused-variable warning), and rewrote the `root_motion_grid` doc paragraph, every sentence of which had become false — "not kept in an accumulator anywhere", the auto-apply, "the node's current position already is the accumulated travel", and a claim that `root_node` defaults to `"."` when ClassDB seeds `".."`.

## Still to do: the acceptance test

`root_motion_getters_drive_character` does not exist yet. The bead carries a `Wiring requirement:`, so it needs a `tests/` file driving a `.tscn` through `patina_runner`/`MainLoop` with an attached GDScript that sets `velocity` from `get_root_motion_position() / delta` and calls `move_and_slide`, asserting the body moved **once**, the Root bone stayed at rest, and the accumulator equals the summed delta.

That is the one remaining item, and I will not report the bead complete without it.

## Coherence

The tree is at a coherent resting point: the mixer no longer moves nodes, the getters a game needs exist on every script surface, the grid reads the accumulator, and all four dependents assert the new model. What is missing is the bead's own proof, not a working feature.

comments.author: TurquoiseCastle
comments.text:
TurquoiseCastle — **the clause I reported as uncovered IS closable, and here is the exact recipe.** No edits this pass: `.78`'s verify is in flight (`verifier.log:14275`), so I left the files alone rather than change what is being tested.

## What I had said, and the correction

My completion said the "Root bone pose stays at rest" clause needs *"a `Skeleton3D` with an authored rest pose and a `position_3d` track in the `.tscn`, which is a fixture of its own size"*. The effort estimate stands, but I left it ambiguous whether a `.tscn` can author skeleton bones at all. **It can**, and three fixtures already do it.

`skeleton3d.rs` stores bones as individual node properties — `bones/{idx}/name`, `/parent`, `/rest`, `/pose`, `/pose_position`, `/pose_rotation`, `/pose_scale` — so the packed-scene loader carries them like any other property. `skeleton3d_absolute_pose_skinning_scene.rs:175-181` authors exactly that, and its first bone is even named **`"Root"`**, matching the bead's `root_motion_track = "Skeleton3D:Root"`:

```
[node name="Skeleton3D" type="Skeleton3D" parent="."]
bones/0/name = "Root"
bones/0/parent = -1
bones/0/rest = Transform3D(1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0)
bones/1/name = "Tip"
bones/1/parent = 0
bones/1/rest = Transform3D(1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0)
```

## The recipe for the third clause

Add to the acceptance fixture:

1. A `Skeleton3D` child of `Player` with `bones/0/name = "Root"`, `bones/0/parent = -1` and an identity `bones/0/rest`.
2. A second track of type `"position_3d"` whose path is `"Skeleton3D:Root"` — the loader splits that into `node_path = "Skeleton3D"` + `property_path = "Root"`.
3. `root_motion_track = NodePath("Skeleton3D:Root")`, whose `get_concatenated_subnames()` is `"Root"` — which is exactly the `property_path` the matcher compares against. 🔑 The two line up only because the loader keeps the subname of one and the subname of the other; that is the same coupling that made my first two spellings wrong, and it is why this has to be checked rather than assumed.
4. Assert the bone's pose stays at its rest value after the frames — `skeleton3d::get_bone_pose_position`, the accessor `animation_tree_bone_tracks_reach_the_skeleton.rs` uses for the same kind of claim.

That clause is what piece 2 (excluding the root track from `apply_animation_bone_tracks`) exists to make true, and it currently has **no test anywhere** — the bone exclusion is the one piece of this bead with implementation and no proof.

⚠️ It is a genuine second fixture rather than two more lines: the current acceptance drives root motion through a `Property` track, and a bone track exercises a different arm of `root_motion_frame`. Trying to serve both from one clip risks the two tracks sharing a property path and the first-match problem I fixed in `consume_root_motion` reappearing in my own fixture.

## Sequence

Waiting on the verdict at `14275` first — if the acceptance fails I want to know why before changing the fixture, and if it passes this becomes a clean additive follow-up rather than a change to something already green.

comments.author: PinkMoose
comments.text:
PinkMoose — readiness check on the third clause, done WITHOUT touching any file (`.78`'s verify is in flight at `verifier.log:14319`; TurquoiseCastle was right not to edit mid-run and I followed that).

My fix for the verify blocker is submitted separately (msg 91969): a test double answered `has_method` true for every name, so pat-mgixk.100's `_init` dispatch recorded a phantom call and every call count was off by one. Fixed in `animation_root_motion_method_test.rs` and — same latent bug — in my own `animation_tree_bone_tracks_reach_the_skeleton.rs`.

**All three preconditions for the "root bone stays at rest" clause CHECK OUT.** I verified each rather than trusting the recipe:

1. **Bones can be authored in a `.tscn`** — confirmed verbatim at `skeleton3d_absolute_pose_skinning_scene.rs:174-180`, first bone named `"Root"`, `bones/0/parent = -1`, identity rest.
2. **`"position_3d"` is a recognised track type on the scene path** — `animation_tscn.rs:203` maps it to `TrackType::Position3D`, with an in-module test at `:978`. ⚠️ Worth stating because **no existing test `.tscn` authors one**: `grep 'tracks/./type = "position_3d"'` over all test fixtures returns ZERO hits, so this spelling has never been exercised from a scene before. It is mapped; it is just untried.
3. **The engine already cancels the root-motion track from bone poses.** I expected this to be the gap and went looking for it — it is not. `apply_animation_bone_tracks` builds its skip set from `player.non_property_track_paths()`, whose own comment names exactly this case (`root_motion_track = "Skeleton3D:Root"`), and deliberately reuses the same set `consume_root_motion` is keyed to rather than re-reading `root_motion_track`, so the two cannot drift. So the clause should PASS once a fixture reaches it.

**⚠️ One correction to the recipe, and it matters.** Step 3 says set `root_motion_track = NodePath("Skeleton3D:Root")`. Do **not** do that to the existing fixture: the current `root_motion_track = NodePath(".:position")` is what clauses 1 and 2 measure (the mixer publishing `(2,0,0)` from the `:position` track, and neither node moving). Repointing it would quietly invalidate both.

So the third clause needs its **own** `.tscn` and its own test function — a `Skeleton3D` child of `Player`, a `position_3d` track at `"Skeleton3D:Root"`, `root_motion_track = NodePath("Skeleton3D:Root")` — asserting both halves: the mixer still publishes a non-zero delta AND `skeleton3d::get_bone_pose_position` is unchanged from `bones/0/rest`. Asserting only the bone would pass against a fixture where the track never loaded at all.

Not doing it in this pass: the point of the current submission is getting the seven landed pieces verified, and adding a new skeleton fixture to the same change risks a fresh failure mode and delays that.

title: AnimationPlayer: full GDScript method/property surface incl. play() args, advance() and script-created players
description:
[audit-key: animation/anim-player-script-surface] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** GDScript -> interpreter -> SceneTreeAccessor -> SceneTree animation_players -> process_animations

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json AnimationPlayer methods (play(name,custom_blend,custom_speed,from_end), play_with_capture, play_section_backwards, play_section_with_markers, set/get_blend_time, animation_set_next, set_default_blend_time, is_animation_active, set_current_animation, get_assigned_animation, get_queue, clear_queue, get_current_animation_length, set_section, reset_section, seek(seconds,update,update_only)) + AnimationMixer methods (add/remove/get_animation_library, get_animation_library_list, get_animation, has_animation_library, advance, capture, clear_caches, find_animation)

**Patina today:** interpreter.rs:13165-13201 `play` arm reads args[0] only and calls animation_player_play(id,&clip), which calls player.play(name) (scripting.rs:6457-6476). custom_blend, custom_speed and from_end are dropped even though AnimationPlayer::play_ex exists (animation.rs:828). Dispatch counts (grep '"<m>"' gdscript-interop/src gdscene/src excluding class_db) are 0 for: animation_set_next, set_blend_time, set_default_blend_time, play_with_capture, play_section_with_markers, play_section_backwards, is_animation_active, set_current_animation, get_assigned_animation, get_queue, clear_queue, get_current_animation_length, set_section, reset_section, get_section_start_time, get_animation, add_animation_library, get_animation_library, get_animation_library_list, remove_animation_library, advance, capture, find_animation, clear_caches. Property assignment is not routed into the player struct: scripting.rs set_node_property routes only AnimationTree `parameters/`, `active` (:2452), and process_animations overwrites `current_animation` every frame (scene_tree.rs:4257-4259), so `$AP.current_animation = "run"` and `$AP.speed_scale = 2.0` are silent no-ops. attach_animation_player has no caller except scene load (animation_tscn.rs:562), so AnimationPlayer.new() + add_child never animates. MANUAL callback mode cannot advance because advance() is missing.

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: the full AnimationPlayer and AnimationMixer method list in extension_api.json, plus property setters (current_animation starts that clip, assigned_animation, speed_scale, autoplay, playback_default_blend_time, active, root_node, callback_mode_*).

Patina: play() drops 3 of its 4 args (interpreter.rs:13165-13201), more than 20 methods have no dispatch, property writes never reach the AnimationPlayer struct, and a player created in code is never attached (attach only at animation_tscn.rs:562).

Approach: add a single `call_animation_player_method(nid, method, args)` table in scripting.rs (modelled on skeleton3d::call_skeleton_method), reached from interpreter.rs before the generic arms. It forwards to the existing AnimationPlayer API (play_ex, play_section, set_blend_time, animation_set_next, get_queue, clear_queue, seek, sections, default_blend_time) and adds advance(delta). advance must run the same application block as process_animations, so factor that block out. In set_node_property, route AnimationPlayer props (speed_scale, current_animation, assigned_animation, autoplay, playback_default_blend_time, active, root_node) into the struct. Attach an empty AnimationPlayer on add_child of an AnimationPlayer node so code-built players work (pairs with the Animation resource API bead).

Wiring: GDScript -> interpreter -> SceneTreeAccessor -> SceneTree animation_players -> process_animations.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`

**Prove it:** From a GDScript in a loaded scene: `$AP.play("walk", 0.3, 2.0)` runs at double speed with a 0.3 s crossfade. `$AP.speed_scale = 0.5` halves the advance. `$AP.current_animation = "run"` starts run. With callback_mode_process=MANUAL, `$AP.advance(0.25)` moves the target property to the 0.25 s sample. get_queue(), animation_set_next() and get_current_animation_length() return Godot values. (test: `animation_player_script_surface_parity`)

**Verifier note:** interpreter.rs:13175-13184 passes only args.first() to animation_player_play, which calls player.play(name) (scripting.rs:6457-6476), so custom_blend, custom_speed and from_end are dropped. A quoted-name grep in gdscript-interop/src and gdscene/src excluding class_db found 0 hits each for: animation_set_next, set_blend_time, set_default_blend_time, play_with_capture, play_section_backwards, is_animation_active, get_queue, clear_queue, get_current_animation_length, set_section, get_animation, add_animation_library, get_animation_library_list and advance. An unquoted grep for get_queue, clear_queue, animation_set_next and set_blend_time in scripting.rs, scene_tree.rs and the interpreter also found 0. seek, queue, play_backwards and has_animation do exist. The speed_scale hits in scripting.rs:6562-6610 are AnimatedSprite, not AnimationPlayer. scene_tree.rs:4258 overwrites current_animation every frame. attach_animation_player's only non-test caller is animation_tscn.rs:562. P1 is fine.
acceptance_criteria: From a GDScript in a loaded scene: `$AP.play("walk", 0.3, 2.0)` runs at double speed with a 0.3 s crossfade. `$AP.speed_scale = 0.5` halves the advance. `$AP.current_animation = "run"` starts run. With callback_mode_process=MANUAL, `$AP.advance(0.25)` moves the target property to the 0.25 s sample. get_queue(), animation_set_next() and get_current_animation_length() return Godot values. (test: `animation_player_script_surface_parity`)

title: GDScript: generic property-accessor dispatch + core Node/CanvasItem/Node2D/SceneTree methods
description:
[audit-key: classdb-registered-but-nil-sweep/core-node-method-surface] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** GDScript in a MainLoop-run scene

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/node.cpp; scene/main/canvas_item.cpp; scene/2d/node_2d.cpp; scene/gui/control.cpp; scene/main/scene_tree.cpp

**Patina today:** Against extension_api non-virtual methods with no quoted literal in gdscene/src or gdscript-interop/src: Node 99/121, CanvasItem 71/91, Node2D 22/33, Control 141/155, Viewport 125/130, SceneTree 30/47. Spot checks: `grep -rn '"hide"\|"show"\|"get_viewport"\|"move_child"\|"get_global_position"\|"change_scene_to_packed"' gdscene/src gdscript-interop/src` = 0. No accessor fallback exists (searched strip_prefix/starts_with/trim_start_matches of get_/set_ and getter-name lookups). Property syntax (`visible = false`) may work, but the method spellings raise UndefinedFunction. Some setter/getter spellings may be covered via property-style paths not enumerated here, so the counts are upper bounds on missing method spellings. Not registered, so these fail loudly rather than silently; listed here because the sweep surfaced them.

**Implement:** Godot routes every bound getter/setter method (get_global_position, set_modulate, get_rotation_degrees) to the property, and exposes core helpers (CanvasItem.hide/show/is_visible_in_tree/get_global_mouse_position/get_viewport_rect; Node.get_index/move_child/reparent/has_node/find_children/get_path_to/get_groups/get_viewport/get_window/owner/is_node_ready/propagate_call/get_process_delta_time; SceneTree.get_current_scene/change_scene_to_packed/get_node_count_in_group/get_frame). Patina has no literal arm for most of these, and no accessor fallback (verified). Implementation, stage 1: in scripting.rs call_node_method, before item_views, add a generic fallback. Resolve `get_X`/`is_X`/`set_X` via ClassDB property getter/setter names (class_db::get_property_getter/get_property_setter at class_db.rs:968/983 already store with_accessors names) to the node's property get/set, so every registered accessor works without per-method arms. Stage 2: add explicit arms for the non-accessor helpers above using the existing SceneTree functions (move_child, reparent, change_scene_to_packed at scene_tree.rs, which tests already call). Wiring: GDScript in a MainLoop-run scene.

title: Animation: Godot-exact key sampling (nearest floor, ease transitions, loop_wrap, capture)
description:
[audit-key: animation/anim-sampling-fidelity] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** animation_tscn loader -> AnimationPlayer.get_current_values_targeted -> process_animations property write

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/animation.cpp:2660-2676 (per-key `transition` applied via Math::ease; tr==0 holds the value; INTERPOLATION_NEAREST returns p_keys[idx], i.e. the floor key); :2580-2640 (loop_wrap interpolates last->first across the loop edge); :256-263 + animation.h:69-71 (update 0=CONTINUOUS,1=DISCRETE,2=CAPTURE)

**Patina today:** gdscene/src/animation.rs:421-428: Nearest switches at the MIDPOINT between keys, not at the next key. animation_tscn.rs:318-322 deliberately does not read per-key `transitions` (comment says exponent not modelled), so ease-in/out keys and transition 0 (hold) play linear. track `loop_wrap` is never read (grep 'loop_wrap' animation.rs animation_tscn.rs = 0), and sample() clamps after the last key (animation.rs:400-404) with no wrap to key 0 for looping clips. animation_tscn.rs:326-331 maps update=2 to Discrete and 3 to Capture, but in Godot 4 2 IS UPDATE_CAPTURE. Capture is not modelled at all (animation.rs:200-203).

**Implement:** Godot ground truth (animation.cpp:2580-2676): the key index is the last key <= t. NEAREST returns it. For linear and cubic the per-key `transition` is applied as c = Math::ease(c, tr), and tr == 0 holds the value. With loop_wrap (default true) on a looping animation, time before the first key or after the last interpolates between the last and first keys across the loop seam. UpdateMode is 0 continuous, 1 discrete, 2 capture. Capture blends from the property's value at play time to the first key (with playback_auto_capture defaults).

Patina: midpoint nearest (animation.rs:421-428), transitions ignored (animation_tscn.rs:318-322), no loop_wrap, update 2 misread as discrete (:326-331), and capture treated as continuous.

Approach: store `transition: f32` per KeyFrame and apply gdcore ease (port Math::ease) in sample(). Fix Nearest to floor. Add `loop_wrap: bool` to AnimationTrack (parsed from tracks/N/loop_wrap, default true) and pass the clip length and loop mode into sample so it can wrap. Fix the update-mode mapping. Implement capture: snapshot the target property on play() in AnimationPlayer and blend over the first-key interval.

Wiring: animation_tscn loader -> AnimationPlayer.get_current_values_targeted -> process_animations property write.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tscn.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn clip with keys at 0 s (value 0, transition 2.0) and 1 s (value 10), loaded and played through MainLoop: at 0.5 s the property equals 10*ease(0.5,2.0)=2.5. An interp=0 track holds 0 until t=1.0. A looping 1 s clip with keys at 0.25 (0) and 0.75 (10) samples 5.0 at t=0.0. An update=2 track is classified Capture and blends from the pre-play value. (test: `animation_key_sampling_godot_exact`)

**Verifier note:** Could not refute any part. animation.rs:421-428: TransitionType::Nearest returns a before the midpoint and b after it, so it switches halfway between keys instead of holding the floor key. animation_tscn.rs:319-322: the comment states per-key `transitions` is not read. animation_tscn.rs:326-331 maps update 1 and 2 to Discrete and 3 to Capture, but upstream animation.h:69-71 has CONTINUOUS=0, DISCRETE=1, CAPTURE=2. grep 'loop_wrap' over crates/*.rs (tests excluded) finds only the writer at scene_saver.rs:414 and an unrelated gdaudio test, so no reader exists. sample() clamps at the first and last key (animation.rs:395-404). Capture is declared at animation.rs:203 and falls through to plain interpolation (:374). P1 fits: these are common authored tracks.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn clip with keys at 0 s (value 0, transition 2.0) and 1 s (value 10), loaded and played through MainLoop: at 0.5 s the property equals 10*ease(0.5,2.0)=2.5. An interp=0 track holds 0 until t=1.0. A looping 1 s clip with keys at 0.25 (0) and 0.75 (10) samples 5.0 at t=0.0. An update=2 track is classified Capture and blends from the pre-play value. (test: `animation_key_sampling_godot_exact`)

title: Animation: load and apply blend_shape tracks from scenes
description:
[audit-key: animation/anim-blend-shape-tracks] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** scene load -> AnimationPlayer -> process_animations -> node blend_shapes/<name> -> render_server_3d morph

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/animation.cpp:228-243 (TYPE_BLEND_SHAPE keys = flat PackedFloat32Array, stride BLEND_SHAPE_TRACK_SIZE=3: time, transition, value; animation.h:133); track path `Mesh:ShapeName` addresses MeshInstance3D blend_shapes/<name>

**Patina today:** animation_tscn.rs:150-160 routes only Position3D/Scale3D/Rotation3D float arrays to fill_transform_track. blend_shape falls through to fill_dictionary_track, which returns early on a non-Dictionary (:303-305), so the track has no keys and is dropped (:162). Even if keyed, property_path would be the bare shape name (`Smile`), while the renderer reads `blend_shapes/<name>` (render_server_3d.rs:2162). The only BlendShape test hand-builds `blend_shapes/Smile` (scene_tree.rs:10596).

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: blend_shape track keys are a flat float array of (time, transition, value) triples (animation.cpp:228-243). The track path `MeshInstance3D:ShapeName` drives that instance's blend_shapes/ShapeName weight.

Patina: tscn blend_shape tracks are silently dropped (animation_tscn.rs:150-160, 303-305), and the property name convention does not match the renderer (render_server_3d.rs:2162 reads blend_shapes/<name>).

Approach: add a fill_blend_shape_track (stride 3) in animation_tscn.rs. When building a BlendShape track, set property_path to `blend_shapes/<subname>`. Also handle AnimationTree output, which uses the same property path.

Wiring: scene load -> AnimationPlayer -> process_animations -> node blend_shapes/<name> -> render_server_3d morph.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tscn.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn MeshInstance3D with a morph target `Smile` and an AnimationPlayer blend_shape track keyed 0->1 over 1 s: after 0.5 s of MainLoop steps, the node's `blend_shapes/Smile` == 0.5 and the render server's morphed vertices differ from base. (test: `blend_shape_track_scene_load_morphs`)

**Verifier note:** animation_tscn.rs:185 maps "blend_shape" to TrackType::BlendShape. The match at :156-167 sends only Position3D, Scale3D and Rotation3D to fill_transform_track; BlendShape falls to fill_dictionary_track, which returns at :303-305 on anything that is not a Dictionary. Godot saves blend_shape keys as a flat PackedFloat32Array, so the track gets no keys and is dropped at :169. No 'blend_shapes/' path is built in animation_tscn.rs (grep BlendShape there: only :185). The only BlendShape tracks are a hand-built one in a test at scene_tree.rs:10596 and the glTF converter (animation.rs:2025), which has test-only callers.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn MeshInstance3D with a morph target `Smile` and an AnimationPlayer blend_shape track keyed 0->1 over 1 s: after 0.5 s of MainLoop steps, the node's `blend_shapes/Smile` == 0.5 and the render server's morphed vertices differ from base. (test: `blend_shape_track_scene_load_morphs`)

title: AnimationTree: evaluate advance_expression and apply xfade_curve on transitions
description:
[audit-key: animation/anim-tree-expressions] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: STUB]

**Wiring requirement:** process_animation_trees -> state machine auto-advance -> expression evaluated on the base node's script and properties each frame

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/animation/animation_node_state_machine.cpp (advance_expression evaluated with Expression against advance_expression_base_node; xfade_curve shapes the crossfade weight)

**Patina today:** animation_tree_tscn.rs:306-308 parses advance_expression and :330 stores xfade_curve. animation_tree.rs:1936-1938 then `continue`s past ANY edge with an expression, so such transitions never fire. xfade_curve is only declared and defaulted (animation_tree.rs:1292-1318; grep 'xfade_curve' scene_tree.rs = 0, no reader). Expression evaluation exists in the interpreter (gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:4429, class_db.rs:6974).

**Implement:** Godot ground truth: an auto-advance transition fires when its advance_condition AND advance_expression (an Expression evaluated with AnimationTree.advance_expression_base_node as the base instance, e.g. `is_on_floor() and velocity.x > 0`) are both true. xfade_curve (a Curve resource) remaps the crossfade weight.

Patina: animation_tree.rs:1936-1938 skips every expression edge, so they never fire, and xfade_curve is never sampled.

Approach: give SceneTree::process_animation_trees_in_mode an evaluator callback, implemented via the GDScript Expression machinery against the node at `advance_expression_base_node` (read that property in build_animation_tree), that is passed into StateMachine advance. Resolve the xfade_curve SubResource to a Curve, store the sampled points, and apply curve.sample(t) to the blend factor.

Wiring: process_animation_trees -> state machine auto-advance -> expression evaluated on the base node's script and properties each frame.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs`

**Prove it:** A .tscn StateMachine idle->run whose transition has advance_mode=Auto and advance_expression="speed > 1.0", with advance_expression_base_node pointing at a node whose script exports `speed`: after a script sets speed=2 and the MainLoop steps, the playback's get_current_node() == "run". With an ease-in xfade_curve the mid-fade weight matches curve.sample(0.5). (test: `state_machine_advance_expression_fires`)

**Verifier note:** animation_tree.rs:1936-1938 does `continue` for any transition with a non-empty advance_expression, so an expression-gated Auto edge can never fire. grep 'xfade_curve' over crates/*.rs (tests excluded): animation_tree_tscn.rs:330 stores a sub-resource id, animation_tree.rs:1292-1318 declares and defaults the field, and class_db.rs:5373 notes Patina has no Curve type. Nothing samples it. grep 'advance_expression' finds no evaluator call. STUB (parsed, then ignored) and P1 are fair.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn StateMachine idle->run whose transition has advance_mode=Auto and advance_expression="speed > 1.0", with advance_expression_base_node pointing at a node whose script exports `speed`: after a script sets speed=2 and the MainLoop steps, the playback's get_current_node() == "run". With an ease-in xfade_curve the mid-fade weight matches curve.sample(0.5). (test: `state_machine_advance_expression_fires`)

comments.text:
BlackWaterfall — ⚠️ THIS BEAD'S LAST FAILURE IS STALE. Do not start by chasing it.

`verifier.log:14198-14199` failed this bead `(101, compile-error)` on `-p gdscene --test state_machine_advance_expression_fires`. The error was NOT in this bead's work or in that test: it was

    Some errors have detailed explanations: E0119, E0277.

a workspace-wide `gdscene` outage that stalled six beads (.50, .51, .74, .79, .82, .406) with six consecutive 101s. Root cause: an orphaned `#[derive(Debug, Clone)]` in `animation.rs` that had been stranded above `RootMotionState` when that struct was spliced in between `BlendState`'s attributes and its body — one accident producing all four errors (Debug/Clone derived twice on one struct, E0119 x2; `BlendState` left bare while `AnimationPlayer` holds `Option<BlendState>` and derives both, E0277 x2).

**It is FIXED** (I repaired it; see msg 91814). Evidence rather than assertion: cargo's own persisted diagnostics at `target-verifier/debug/.fingerprint/*/output-lib-gdscene` now report **0** error-level entries, and `.51`/`.79`/`.50`/`.406` have all since gone PASS.

SO: this bead's recorded 101 says nothing about its own state. Re-verify before assuming there is work to do — the implementation may already be complete. Per the orchestrator's own rule a build-only check is dropped when a test command survives, so simply re-reporting the same commands is enough to get a real verdict.

🔑 General point for whoever picks this up: a `101 compile-error` naming a file OUTSIDE the bead's own crates is almost never the bead's defect. Triage 101-vs-100 first, then grep the error's file for the bead id. And the diagnostic itself is recoverable even though workers cannot build — cargo persists full JSON diagnostics under `target-verifier/debug/.fingerprint/<pkg>-<hash>/output-lib-<crate>`, and they survive a failed build. comments.author: MistyTower
comments.text:
## MistyTower picking this up — ⚠️ HALF of this bead is done and the committed test does NOT cover the other half

BlackWaterfall's note was right that the recorded 101 was a stale `gdscene`
outage, and right to say "re-verify before assuming there is work to do". I did,
and the answer is **partly**:

| acceptance clause | state |
|---|---|
| `advance_expression` evaluated, AUTO edge fires on `speed > 1.0` | **DONE** — `crates/gdscene/src/advance_expression.rs` (190 lines) exists, `scene_tree.rs:5134-5154` reads `advance_expression_base_node`, `has_advance_expressions()` gates it, and `tests/state_machine_advance_expression_fires.rs` asserts both the closed and open gate |
| "With an ease-in `xfade_curve` the mid-fade weight matches `curve.sample(0.5)`" | **NOT DONE** — and **not asserted anywhere** |

🔑 **This is the trap: re-reporting as-is would very likely PASS and CLOSE the
bead with half its acceptance unimplemented.** The wiring gate resolves the
demanded test by NAME (`state_machine_advance_expression_fires`), that test
exists, and its body (lines 182-221) contains only the two
`current_state(&fx)` assertions — no Curve, no fade weight. So the verifier
would confirm a clause nobody wrote.

`xfade_curve` is still exactly what its own doc comment says at
`animation_tree.rs:1525-1529`: *"Stored, not applied: Patina has no `Curve`
resource, so the crossfade stays linear."* `animation_tree_tscn.rs:339` captures
the sub-resource id and nothing reads it.

### The work, scoped against the code (not guessed)

* **Insertion point is one line.** `sample_state_machine`
  (`animation_tree.rs:2919`) ends with
  `let factor = (t.elapsed / t.duration).clamp(0.0, 1.0) as f32;` →
  `blend_value_lists(&from_values, &to_values, factor)`. The curve remaps
  `factor`.
* **`ActiveTransition`** (`{from_state, from_node, elapsed, duration}`) needs to
  carry the curve; it is constructed at the travel hop (~line 1000) and in
  `advance`.
* **Parsing is available**: `build_animation_tree` already takes the
  `PackedScene`, and `scene.sub_resource_type(id)` /
  `scene.sub_resource_props(id)` are how `build_animation_node` resolves ids.
  `Variant::Array` for `_data` is already produced by the parser
  (`packed_scene.rs:1143`).
* **Godot's Curve serializes as** `_data = [Vector2(x, y), left_tangent,
  right_tangent, left_mode, right_mode, ...]` — five entries per point.
* **`Curve::sample` is a cubic Bezier**, not a lerp
  (`scene/resources/curve.cpp`, `sample_local_nocheck`): with `d = bx - ax` and
  `d2 = d/3`, control points are `yac = ay + d2*a.right_tangent` and
  `ybc = by - d2*b.left_tangent`, then
  `bezier_interpolate(ay, yac, ybc, by, local/d)`.

### ⚠️ The fixture value has to be chosen so the clause is not vacuous

A curve with points (0,0) and (1,1) and **zero** tangents samples to exactly
**0.5** at t=0.5 — identical to the linear blend it is supposed to replace. So
an "ease-in curve" fixture with default tangents would assert nothing.

Using `right_tangent = 0` at (0,0) and `left_tangent = 2` at (1,1):
`yac = 0`, `ybc = 1 - 2/3 = 1/3`, and
`B(0.5) = 0.125·0 + 0.375·0 + 0.375·(1/3) + 0.125·1 = 0.25`.

**0.25 vs the linear 0.5** — hand-computable, so the assertion is not my
implementation checked against itself.

Implementing now. Will extend `state_machine_advance_expression_fires` with the
Curve clause rather than adding a second test, since the gate judges the
bead-demanded name and a sibling file would not be checked.

title: AudioServer: bind bus sends, move_bus, effect add/remove/swap/enable/get, volume_linear and timing queries to GDScript

title: Audio bus layout: instantiate Delay, Distortion, EQ6/10/21 and SpectrumAnalyzer from .tres and honor Reverb params
description:
[audit-key: audio/audio-effect-factory] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: UNWIRED]

**Wiring requirement:** bootstrap.rs:607-640 loads audio/buses/default_bus_layout before the first frame -> mixer -> AudioServer::mix

**Godot ground truth:** servers/audio/effects/audio_effect_{delay,distortion,eq,spectrum_analyzer,reverb}.cpp; AudioBusLayout .tres effect sub_resources

**Patina today:** gdaudio/src/mixer.rs:356-520 effect_from_sub_resource matches Amplify, Capture, Record, Reverb, 8 filters, BandLimit, Compressor, Limiter, HardLimiter and returns None for everything else. DSP exists for AudioEffectDelay (effects.rs:317), AudioEffectDistortion (480, 5 modes), AudioEffectEQ (227), AudioEffectSpectrumAnalyzer (1224) but grep for their constructors outside effects.rs tests = lib.rs re-export only. comments.text:
BlackWaterfall — I independently verified EmeraldCreek's remaining-scope assessment and it is CORRECT on both counts. Adding the specifics it did not include, plus a concrete recommendation so this bead can close instead of cycling.

CLAIM 1 — "EQ6/EQ10/EQ21 factory arms need the band-count work in the audio-effect-dsp-parity bead." CONFIRMED, and the reason matters:

`AudioEffectEQ` (effects.rs:227) is a FIXED THREE-BAND effect — `low_db` (~200 Hz), `mid_db` (~1 kHz), `high_db` (~5 kHz) — with per-channel state typed `Vec<[f32; 3]>`, i.e. the band count is baked into the state array, not a parameter. Its only constructors are `flat()` and `new(low_db, mid_db, high_db)`.

Godot's AudioEffectEQ6/EQ10/EQ21 are 6, 10 and 21 INDEPENDENT bands at their own centre frequencies. So a factory arm mapping `AudioEffectEQ21` onto this struct would instantiate something that processes three bands and SILENTLY IGNORES the other eighteen — a .tscn authoring 21 band gains would load, report success, and quietly apply three of them. That is precisely the "registered but wrong" failure class this port audit exists to surface, and it would be harder to find than today's honest absence. Not implementing it is the correct call, not a shortfall.

CLAIM 2 — "Reverb `damping` cannot be mapped: AudioEffectReverb has no damping field." CONFIRMED. The struct (effects.rs:135-147) is `wet`, `dry`, `feedback`, `delay_secs` plus `delay_l` / `delay_r` / `write_pos` internals. There is no damping term in the DSP at all, so there is nothing for the property to drive. Adding a `pub damping` that no code reads would be an inert field — it would make the class LOOK compliant to an inspector or a property probe while changing no sample, which is strictly worse than leaving it absent.

RECOMMENDATION: strike both items from this bead's acceptance rather than carry them.
- The delivered scope PASSED (EmeraldCreek's report, 13:59) and covers the factory arms whose effects actually exist.
- EQ6/EQ10/EQ21 need N-band DSP, which is the `audio-effect-dsp-parity` bead's job; a factory arm cannot precede the effect it instantiates.
- Reverb `damping` needs a damping term in the reverb DSP, same bead.
Keeping them here guarantees this bead cycles through park-review forever, because no amount of work in `mixer.rs` / `effects.rs` factory code can satisfy a clause that requires a DSP that does not exist yet.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: I did not implement 6/10/21-band EQ or a reverb damping term. Both are squarely the sibling bead's scope, and implementing them here would duplicate or collide with whoever holds it. I also did not add the factory arms pointing at the 3-band struct, for the silent-fidelity-loss reason above.

I hold no leases on `effects.rs` or `mixer.rs` — nothing of mine is blocking that sibling bead.

**Wiring requirement:** GDScript -> node one-shot channel -> AudioServerBridge::process -> AudioServer voices

**Godot ground truth:** scene/audio/audio_stream_player_internal.cpp (max_polyphony voice stealing); servers/audio/audio_stream.cpp AudioStreamPolyphonic/AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic::play_stream

comments.text:
BlackWaterfall — half (a) is DONE and PASSED (verifier.log:14272-14274). This note is the design for half (b), and it CORRECTS what I wrote about it in msg 91897.

WHAT I GOT WRONG EARLIER: I said half (b) "needs id-keyed voices, which PolyphonicPlayer does not have". That is true but irrelevant — `PolyphonicPlayer` is not needed at all. `PlaybackId(pub u64)` is ALREADY the per-voice id, and `AudioServer` already offers `play_on_bus -> PlaybackId`, `is_playing(id)` and `stop(id)`. So the id registry exists; `stop_stream(id)`/`is_stream_playing(id)` are one line each against the server.

THE REAL BLOCKER, which is sharper and architectural:

`play_stream(stream, from_offset, volume_db, pitch_scale, playback_type, bus) -> id` must return its id SYNCHRONOUSLY to the calling script. Patina has two script->audio paths and neither can do that on its own:

1. The DEFERRED property channel (`__play_request__`, audio_server_bridge.rs:53). This is how `$P.play()` works: the interpreter writes a property, the bridge drains it next `process()`. The bridge owns the `AudioStreamLoader` importer and `base_dir`, so it is the ONLY side that can LOAD a stream resource. But it runs after the script returns, so it cannot hand back an id.
2. The SYNCHRONOUS script audio server (`set_script_audio_server(self.audio_bridge.server_mut())`, main_loop.rs:3057; reached in scripting.rs via `self.audio()` / `self.audio_mut()`). This can start a voice and return its `PlaybackId` immediately — but it is the bare `AudioServer`. No importer, no base_dir, so it CANNOT load the stream the call passes.

So the synchronous side cannot load, and the loading side cannot answer synchronously. That is the actual work in half (b), and it is why this is a separate bead rather than a finishing touch on (a).

THREE WAYS OUT, with the trade I see:
(a) Hand the script side a loader. Pass `&mut AudioStreamLoader` + base_dir alongside the server in `set_script_audio_server`, so `audio_player_play_stream` can resolve a `res://` path and call `play_on_bus` in one go. Smallest conceptual change; widens the script-callback audio surface, and every `set_script_audio_server` call site (main_loop.rs:3057, 4189, 4544) plus `clear_script_audio_server` has to stay paired.
(b) Pre-resolve on the bridge, play on the server. The bridge adopts a node's declared polyphonic streams into a path->AudioBuffer cache during `process()`; `play_stream` then looks the buffer up synchronously and starts the voice. Keeps the loader where it is; only works for streams the bridge has seen at least one frame earlier, which is wrong for a stream first referenced inside the same callback.
(c) Return a deferred handle. `play_stream` allocates the id itself and the bridge binds it to a real voice next frame, with `is_stream_playing(id)` false until then. Honest to the channel design but NOT Godot's semantics, where the id is live immediately.

I would take (a).

ALSO NEEDED for (b), and already scoped by (a)'s work:
- `get_stream_playback()` has ZERO dispatch arms (`grep '"get_stream_playback"'` = 0). In Godot it returns an `AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic` OBJECT whose five methods are then called. The interpreter can carry engine objects (154 `Variant::Object`/`ObjectId` sites), so the pragmatic shim is to return the PLAYER's own ObjectId and dispatch the five methods on the node — document that deviation loudly if taken, because a real Godot playback object outlives/【differs from】the node.
- ⚠️ `play_stream` IS registered in ClassDB (class_db.rs:25681, asserted :33305) with no dispatch arm, so `has_method("play_stream")` answers TRUE today and a call returns Nil silently. Same inverse-direction trap as `is_class`.
- `AudioStreamPolyphonic` exists ONLY in ClassDB (class_db.rs:17800) and the inspector schema. There is no runtime stream kind for it, so `PlayerKind::from_class`-style resolution has nothing to match.
- Voice LIFETIME is already solved by (a): `extra_voices: HashMap<NodeId, Vec<PlaybackId>>` in the bridge, drained on node-free / stream-swap / `playing = false`. A `play_stream` voice should be registered there too (e.g. appended to a `__poly_voices__` node property the bridge adopts each frame) or it will play on after its node is freed, with nothing able to stop it.

WHERE THE CODE WOULD GO: 3 default-bodied `audio_player_*_stream` methods on the `SceneTreeAccessor` trait (bindings.rs, near the existing `audio_*` block ~2011-2046 — defaults mean no other impl breaks), their impls in scripting.rs beside `audio_get_bus_count` (~6528) using `self.audio_mut()`, and sibling match arms next to `"play"` in `interpreter.rs::call_method_on` (~14298).

title: Audio import: honor loop/loop_offset/bpm from .import params and imported artifacts
description:
[audit-key: audio/audio-import-loop-metadata] [port-audit 2026-10-30] [status: PARTIAL]

**Wiring requirement:** .tscn ExtResource -> resolve_stream_path -> load_stream_buffer -> apply_stream_loop on each voice start

**Godot ground truth:** modules/vorbis/resource_importer_ogg_vorbis.cpp & modules/minimp3/resource_importer_mp3.cpp (loop, loop_offset, bpm, beat_count, bar_beats); editor/import/resource_importer_wav.cpp (edit/loop_mode, edit/loop_begin, edit/loop_end)

**Patina today:** gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:1114-1119 an import artifact (.oggvorbisstr/.mp3str/.sample) always returns loop None: 'container carries loop/loop_offset metadata that nothing parses yet'; 1150-1153 same for bpm/beat_count. Loose-file loop comes only from WAV smpl chunk / Ogg LOOPSTART comments (gdaudio/src/import.rs:261-267); the `.import` [params] loop / edit/loop_mode the Godot editor writes is never read on the runtime path (resolve_stream_path prefers the artifact at 321-322). So a music .ogg marked Loop in the import dock plays once in Patina.

**Implement:** Godot: AudioStreamOggVorbis/MP3 loop with `loop`+`loop_offset` (seconds) set in the .import [params] and serialized into the .oggvorbisstr/.mp3str artifact; AudioStreamWAV uses loop_mode/loop_begin/loop_end (frames) from edit/loop_* params into the .sample. bpm/beat_count/bar_beats drive Interactive/Playlist beat sync. Patina's bridge decodes only the artifact's `data` payload and drops every other property (audio_server_bridge.rs:1114-1119, 1150-1170). Implement: in artifact_audio_payload return the res property map too; map loop/loop_offset (Ogg/MP3 -> LoopMode::Forward, begin=loop_offset, end=length) and loop_mode/loop_begin/loop_end (WAV, frames->secs by mix_rate) into StreamLoop; for loose sources with a .import sidecar but no artifact, read the [params] block via gdresource::importers' .import parser; carry bpm/beat_count/bar_beats on the loaded stream for later consumers. Wiring: .tscn ExtResource -> resolve_stream_path -> load_stream_buffer -> apply_stream_loop on each voice start.

**Files:** `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs`, `engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/import.rs`

**Prove it:** A fixture project with music.ogg + music.ogg.import (loop=true, loop_offset=0.1) and a matching .godot/imported/*.oggvorbisstr, played by an autoplay AudioStreamPlayer through MainLoop::step for 2x the clip length, is still non-silent at the end and get_playback_position() wrapped back to >=0.1; same for a WAV whose .import sets edit/loop_mode=1. (test: `audio_import_params_loop_ogg_and_wav`)

**Verifier note:** Verified. audio_server_bridge.rs:1112-1119: when load_stream_buffer gets an artifact (.oggvorbisstr/.mp3str/.sample) it returns `(buffer, None)`, with the comment 'carries loop/loop_offset metadata that nothing parses yet'. artifact_audio_payload (1150-1170) pulls out only data/packed_data. resolve_stream_path (306-330) prefers import_artifact_for over the loose source, so an imported looping .ogg plays once. Loose files keep their loop through load_file().info.loop_points (1105-1110), so PARTIAL is the right label. P1 is right: looping music is common.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture project with music.ogg + music.ogg.import (loop=true, loop_offset=0.1) and a matching .godot/imported/*.oggvorbisstr, played by an autoplay AudioStreamPlayer through MainLoop::step for 2x the clip length, is still non-silent at the end and get_playback_position() wrapped back to >=0.1; same for a WAV whose .import sets edit/loop_mode=1. (test: `audio_import_params_loop_ogg_and_wav`)

comments.author: PinkMoose
comments.text:
PinkMoose — BLOCKED on `audio_server_bridge.rs` (BlackWaterfall, exclusive to 14:56:57Z). I wrote nothing. Recording the plan because I found that **most of this bead is already implemented in that same file and just is not reached from the artifact branch** — whoever holds the file can land it in minutes.

**The one line that causes the whole gap.** `load_stream_buffer` (`:1546`) splits on the extension. The artifact branch ends at `:1569`:

```rust
gdaudio::decode::decode_auto(&payload)
    .map(|buffer| (buffer, None))      // <- the None IS the bug
```

`LoadedStream` is `(AudioBuffer, Option<StreamLoop>)` (`:1538`), and every voice start already applies that `Option` through `apply_stream_loop` at `:1138`, `:1160` and `:1171`. So the plumbing from a `StreamLoop` to a looping voice is **complete and tested**; only the artifact branch hands it `None`.

**🔑 The `.sample` (WAV) half needs NO new mapping code.** The file already has it, for the INLINE `AudioStreamWAV` sub-resource path:

* `inline_wav_from_props(get)` (`:1374`) reads `data`, `format`, `mix_rate`, `stereo`, `loop_mode`, `loop_begin`, `loop_end` out of a property bag — Godot's own defaults, and the ⚠️ on `format` defaulting to 0 not 1 is already documented there;
* `decode_inline_wav` (`:1401`) converts frames to seconds with the mix rate and builds the `StreamLoop`: `1 => Forward, 2 => PingPong, 3 => Backward`, `begin_secs = loop_begin / rate`, and an `end_secs` guard for `loop_end <= loop_begin`.

A `.sample` artifact IS an `AudioStreamWAV` resource, so its property bag has exactly that shape. The change is to route it through those two functions instead of `decode_auto`, which also means **no guessed property names** — these are already consumed by a tested path.

**The Ogg/MP3 half is the only new mapping**, and it is small: `loop: bool` + `loop_offset: f64` (SECONDS, not frames) -> `mode: Forward`, `begin_secs: loop_offset`, `end_secs: buffer.duration_secs()` (`gdaudio::decode`, `AudioBuffer::duration_secs`, decode.rs:29). ⚠️ Compute `end_secs` from the DECODED buffer, not from a container field — the artifact has no length property, and 0.0 there would make the loop region empty.

**⚠️ Two traps for whoever writes it:**

1. **There are two `LoopMode` enums.** `StreamLoop.mode` is `crate::stream::LoopMode` (`gdaudio/src/stream.rs:19`); `gdaudio/src/sample_pool.rs:51` declares another with the same name. Use the `stream` one — the `sample_pool` one will not type-check here, and if it ever did the mapping would be silently wrong.
2. **`artifact_audio_payload` (`:1609`) currently throws the Resource away** after pulling `data`/`packed_data`. It has to return the property map (or the `res`) as well. Its own doc comment already says the container "carries `loop`/`loop_offset` and `bpm`/`beat_count` metadata which nothing consumes yet" — that comment is the spec for this change, and it should be rewritten, not deleted, once the loop half lands.

**Scope note on the acceptance.** Its first clause needs a real `.ogg` + `.oggvorbisstr` pair; the second needs a WAV whose `.import` sets `edit/loop_mode=1`. The `[params]`-only case (a loose source with a `.import` sidecar and NO artifact) is a third path — `resolve_stream_path` (`:344`) prefers the artifact — and is the piece I would split out, since it needs the `.import` parser rather than the artifact reader.

`bpm`/`beat_count`/`bar_beats` have no consumer at all yet, so carrying them is dead storage until Interactive/Playlist streams exist. I would leave them out rather than add an unread field.

Not reclaiming: the file is leased and I will not edit under it. Happy to take it back the moment it frees.
