title: Physics2D: RigidBody2D contact_monitor + body_entered/exited/shape signals
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-contacts] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth (rigid_body_2d.cpp): when contact_monitor is enabled and max_contacts_reported>0, a RigidBody2D emits body_entered(body)/body_exited(body) and body_shape_entered/body_shape_exited(rid, body, body_shape_index, local_shape_index) as contacts begin/end, exposes get_colliding_bodies()/get_contact_count(), and fires sleeping_state_changed. Patina state: only Area2D emits overlap signals (physics_server.rs:465); world.step returns CollisionEvent Entered/Persisting/Exited (world.rs:294-330) stored in last_collision_events but never routed to RigidBody2D nodes; contact_monitor/max_contacts_reported unregistered. Approach: register contact_monitor + max_contacts_reported on RigidBody2D (class_db.rs); in PhysicsServer add a process_body_contact_signals pass that maps CollisionEvent body pairs (via body_to_node) to the involved RigidBody2D nodes and emits body_entered/body_exited (and shape variants using shape indices carried from the narrowphase); call it in the MainLoop physics phase after step_physics. Wiring requirement: two RigidBody2D with contact_monitor=true that collide during MainLoop.step fire body_entered once on contact and body_exited once on separation.
acceptance_criteria: A scene-loaded RigidBody2D with contact_monitor=true fires body_entered with the other body's ObjectId when they collide during MainLoop.step and body_exited when they separate; get_contact_count()>0 while touching. (test: `rigidbody2d_contact_monitor_signals`)

title: Physics2D: honor RigidBody2D freeze/sleep/lock_rotation/CCD + damp modes
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-rigidbody-states] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]
[verify-note: ADJUSTED: Finding is real (confirmed the gap) but STUB overstates what exists; corrected to MISSING. Only `freeze` has any representation: it is a registered-but-ignored property (class_db.rs:915) - PhysicsBody2D has no freeze field and integrate (body.rs:171-198) never checks it, so a frozen body s]

Godot ground truth (rigid_body_2d.cpp): freeze halts simulation (freeze_mode STATIC keeps it immovable, KINEMATIC lets animation drive it); can_sleep + sleeping put resting bodies to sleep below linear/angular thresholds (emitting sleeping_state_changed); lock_rotation zeroes angular motion; continuous_cd (CAST_RAY/CAST_SHAPE) prevents tunnelling of fast bodies; custom_integrator hands integration to _integrate_forces; linear_damp_mode/angular_damp_mode combine vs replace the area/default damp. Patina state: freeze is a stored-but-ignored property (class_db.rs:915, no field/check in body.rs), and none of sleeping/can_sleep/lock_rotation/continuous_cd/custom_integrator/damp_mode exist. Approach: add these fields to PhysicsBody2D, gate integration on freeze/freeze_mode + sleep state in body.rs:integrate, add a sleep detector in world.step (below-threshold velocity for N steps), zero angular velocity when lock_rotation, add a swept/substep CCD path in world.step for continuous_cd bodies, and read the properties in PhysicsServer.register_bodies + sync. Wiring requirement: a scene-loaded RigidBody2D with freeze=true does not fall during MainLoop.step; a fast body with continuous_cd=true does not tunnel through a thin StaticBody2D.
acceptance_criteria: A scene-loaded RigidBody2D with freeze=true keeps its position after 60 MainLoop ticks; a body at rest on a floor has sleeping==true after settling; a fast body with continuous_cd stops at a thin wall instead of passing through. (test: `rigidbody2d_freeze_sleep_lock_states`)

title: Physics2D: expose PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D + PhysicsServer2D query API to script
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-space-state] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth (godot_space_2d.cpp): scripts run spatial queries via get_world_2d().direct_space_state.intersect_ray(PhysicsRayQueryParameters2D)/intersect_point/intersect_shape/cast_motion/collide_shape/get_rest_info, each honoring exclude, collision_mask, collide_with_bodies, collide_with_areas, hit_from_inside; PhysicsServer2D.body_test_motion tests motion for a body. Patina state: PhysicsServer2D singleton is unregistered/unreachable, World2D + PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D + all query-parameter classes are missing (unregistered.txt), and the only query is the internal, param-less world.raycast (world.rs:339). Approach: register PhysicsServer2D as a script singleton and the World2D/PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D/PhysicsRayQueryParameters2D/PhysicsPointQueryParameters2D/PhysicsShapeQueryParameters2D/PhysicsTestMotionParameters2D/Result2D classes; add query methods on PhysicsWorld2D (intersect_ray/point/shape, cast_motion, collide_shape, get_rest_info, body_test_motion) that accept exclude/mask/area+body flags/hit_from_inside; back a direct_space_state object with these and dispatch its methods from the interpreter, resolving get_world_2d() from the viewport. Wiring requirement: a GDScript in a loaded scene calling get_world_2d().direct_space_state.intersect_ray(params) returns the ObjectId + point + normal of a StaticBody2D in the ray's path.
acceptance_criteria: A scene-loaded script calling get_world_2d().direct_space_state.intersect_ray() against a StaticBody2D returns a result dict whose collider is the body's ObjectId and whose position/normal match the hit; excluding that body via the params returns an empty result. (test: `physics_direct_space_state_2d_queries`)

comments.author: GentleBadger
comments.text: PARTIAL by GentleBadger (2026-07-16, uncommitted; verify cmd in completion mail msg 54072). DONE (gdphysics2d only, additive): world.rs gains RayQuery2D (= Godot PhysicsRayQueryParameters2D: from/to/exclude/collision_mask/collide_with_bodies/collide_with_areas/hit_from_inside + chained setters) and PhysicsWorld2D::intersect_ray(&RayQuery2D) -> Option<RaycastHit>; re-exported from lib.rs. 7 tests. NOT COMPILED by me (worker build policy) — eye-verified + reviewer hand-traced ray_aabb. THIS BEAD'S STATE DESCRIPTION IS STALE: 'the only query is the internal, param-less world.raycast' is FALSE — raycast, raycast_filtered (ALREADY honors exclude + collision_mask), point_query, point_query_first and shape_cast all already exist, and RaycastHit already carries body_id/point/normal/distance (exactly the collider/position/normal the acceptance wants). ARCHITECTURAL FINDING — the bead's approach needs revision: it says to add area+body flags to PhysicsWorld2D queries, but PhysicsWorld2D owns ONLY bodies+joints; AREAS LIVE IN A SEPARATE AreaStore (gdphysics2d::area2d, own AreaId/Area2D). collide_with_areas therefore cannot be honored by a &self method on PhysicsWorld2D as written — the next slice must decide: pass &AreaStore into the query, or give World2D ownership of both. DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE: RayQuery2D::collision_mask follows GODOT (default u32::MAX; mask 0 hits NOTHING) whereas the sibling raycast_filtered treats 0 as 'every layer' (not Godot's rule). I did not change raycast_filtered (out of scope; RayCast2D-node callers may depend on it) — one test pins BOTH behaviours side by side so the divergence is visible, not latent. hit_from_inside implements Godot's rule both ways (inside ray reports at origin with zero normal when set; reports that shape NOT AT ALL when clear — no punching out the far wall); inside hits pick the lowest body id for determinism (body map unordered, BodyId is not Ord). KEEP OPEN — REMAINING: (1) ClassDB registration of PhysicsServer2D singleton + World2D/PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D/Physics*QueryParameters2D/Result2D; (2) interpreter dispatch + get_world_2d() resolution from the viewport (a PhysicsServer2D singleton arm goes next to the existing ClassDB/OS/ProjectSettings/DisplayServer arms at interpreter.rs ~:1826); (3) the acceptance test physics_direct_space_state_2d_queries DOES NOT EXIST yet — do not trust a stale-recovery close (0-match filters exit 0); (4) intersect_shape/cast_motion/collide_shape/get_rest_info/body_test_motion (shape_cast is the nearest existing primitive to build intersect_shape on); (5) collide_with_areas — blocked on the AreaStore ownership decision above.

title: Physics2D: PhysicsMaterial resource + StaticBody2D conveyor velocities + AnimatableBody2D
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-material-static] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: PhysicsMaterial (physics_material.cpp) supplies friction (+rough), bounce (+absorbent) via physics_material_override on bodies (rough friction multiplies, absorbent inverts bounce combine); StaticBody2D.constant_linear_velocity/constant_angular_velocity act as conveyor surfaces that impart velocity to bodies in contact without moving the static body; AnimatableBody2D (sync_to_physics) is a kinematic body moved by animation that pushes rigid bodies. Patina state: PhysicsMaterial unregistered, bodies read flat friction/bounce (physics_server.rs:321), no rough/absorbent, no material_override; StaticBody2D has no constant velocities (grep empty); AnimatableBody2D unregistered and unmapped in body_type_for_class (physics_server.rs:30). Approach: register PhysicsMaterial + AnimatableBody2D in class_db; parse physics_material_override (a sub-resource) into body.friction/bounce with rough/absorbent semantics in physics_server; add constant_linear_velocity/constant_angular_velocity to PhysicsBody2D and apply them as surface velocity in collision.rs:separate_bodies friction/tangent for contacting bodies; map AnimatableBody2D to a kinematic body synced from the scene each tick. Wiring requirement: a RigidBody2D resting on a StaticBody2D with constant_linear_velocity is carried horizontally during MainLoop.step; a body with a bouncy PhysicsMaterial (bounce=1) rebounds elastically.
acceptance_criteria: A scene-loaded RigidBody2D on a StaticBody2D with constant_linear_velocity=(100,0) drifts +X across MainLoop ticks; a body with a PhysicsMaterial bounce=1.0 override rebounds to near its incoming speed off a floor. (test: `physics_material_static_conveyor`)

title: Physics3D: solve 3D joints in the world step + register joint nodes + add ConeTwist and Generic6DOF
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/physics3d-joints] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: STUB]

Godot's 3D joints constrain two PhysicsBody3D each solver step (Pin ball-socket, Hinge with limits+motor, Slider prismatic, ConeTwist, Generic6DOF per-axis limits/motors/springs). Patina's gdphysics3d/joint.rs has only Pin/Hinge/Slider parameter structs + helper math and no solver — PhysicsWorld3D::step (world.rs) ignores joints entirely, no joint node classes are registered, and no gdscene bridge exists. Implementation: add a JointStore to PhysicsWorld3D and a constraint-solve pass inside step() (sequential-impulse: enforce pin equality, hinge axis + angular limit/motor, slider linear/angular limits); add ConeTwistJoint3D and Generic6DOFJoint3D structs; register Joint3D/PinJoint3D/HingeJoint3D/SliderJoint3D/ConeTwistJoint3D/Generic6DOFJoint3D node classes in class_db.rs; bridge them in physics_server_3d.rs by resolving node_a/node_b NodePaths to BodyId3D and creating joints. Wiring: joints solved each MainLoop physics sub-step so two bodies linked by a PinJoint3D stay pinned.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a StaticBody3D anchor and a RigidBody3D linked by a PinJoint3D, run through MainLoop::step under gravity, swings but keeps the pinned points coincident (distance between the two anchor points stays ~0) instead of free-falling. (test: `pin_joint_3d_constrains_bodies_via_mainloop`)

title: Physics3D: bridge VehicleBody3D/VehicleWheel3D scene nodes to the vehicle sim and tick it through MainLoop against real colliders
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/physics3d-vehicle] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot's VehicleBody3D is a RigidBody3D chassis with VehicleWheel3D children providing raycast suspension (stiffness/travel/rest_length/max_force, damping compression/relaxation), tire friction_slip, roll_influence, and use_as_traction/use_as_steering, driven by engine_force/brake/steering. Patina has the sim in gdphysics2d/vehicle3d.rs but it is dead at runtime — only re-exported (lib.rs:69), no gdscene bridge, no MainLoop tick, and it raycasts only a flat ground_y plane (vehicle3d.rs:188). The nodes expose only engine_force/brake/steering (class_db.rs:617-631). Implementation: register the full VehicleWheel3D property surface; in physics_server_3d.rs build a VehicleBody3D sim from each VehicleBody3D node + its VehicleWheel3D children (reading suspension/friction/flags), replace the flat-plane raycast with casts against the physics world's colliders, step the vehicle in the physics sub-step, and write chassis position+rotation back to the node; call it from MainLoop. Wiring: engine_force set by a script accelerates the chassis over a StaticBody3D floor through MainLoop::step.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn VehicleBody3D with 4 VehicleWheel3D children on a StaticBody3D floor, given engine_force via a script, moves forward and rests at suspension height (does not sink through the floor) after several MainLoop::step frames. (test: `vehicle_body_3d_drives_via_mainloop`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED (mail 57339): the property surface. The sim bridge is follow-up.
Do NOT let a close imply a VehicleBody3D drives.

DONE: VehicleWheel3D full 14-property surface (was 5). Added the 9 missing: wheel_roll_influence,
wheel_radius, wheel_rest_length, wheel_friction_slip, suspension_travel, suspension_stiffness,
suspension_max_force, damping_compression, damping_relaxation. Names/types/parent diffed against
extension_api.json — 14/14 exact. VehicleBody3D was ALREADY complete (3/3), contrary to the beads
implication.

*** THE FINDING THAT SHOULD SHAPE THE FOLLOW-UP: THE NODE AND THE SIM ARE DIFFERENT MODELS. ***
The bridge is a SEMANTIC MAPPING, not field copying:
  - sim (gdphysics2d/vehicle3d.rs) has ONE suspension_damping (default 500.0);
    the Godot node has the PAIR damping_compression/damping_relaxation (0.83/0.88).
  - sim suspension_stiffness is FORCE-PER-UNIT-COMPRESSION (default 5000.0);
    the Godot node value is its own unit (default 5.88).
  => copying suspension_stiffness straight across under-springs the chassis by ~3 ORDERS OF
     MAGNITUDE and THE CAR SINKS THROUGH THE FLOOR — exactly the failure the acceptance checks for.
  - names differ too: sim radius/suspension_rest_length/friction/driven/steerable vs node
    wheel_radius/wheel_rest_length/wheel_friction_slip/use_as_traction/use_as_steering.
A test now pins the nodes 5.88 and asserts it stays under 100, so the trap is loud if anyone later
"aligns" the two by pasting the sims value into the node.

DEFAULTS CAVEAT (stated plainly): property NAMES and TYPES are dump-verified, but extension_api.json
carries NO property defaults — the 9 values are Godots documented defaults, RECALLED. That is the one
part here not machine-checked; worth a spot-check against a real Godot build.

BUG I CAUGHT IN MY OWN TEST: I first asserted props("VehicleWheel3D").len() == 14. But
get_property_list walks the WHOLE CHAIN, so a wheel reports 19 (14 own + Node3Ds 5) and
VehicleBody3D reports 13, not 3. Both would have FAILED verification. Replaced with presence checks
plus a sharper pair: the chassis inherits mass (RigidBody3D), the wheel does not.

Verify: -p gdobject --test vehicle_wheel_3d_property_surface_test
        -p gdobject --lib class_db

REMAINING (the bulk): build a sim per VehicleBody3D node + its VehicleWheel3D children WITH A UNITS
MAPPING; replace vehicle3d.rs:188s flat ground_y plane with casts against the worlds colliders; step
in the physics sub-step; write chassis position+rotation back to the node; call from MainLoop. Lives
in gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs.
SCHEDULING NOTE: the acceptance test vehicle_body_3d_drives_via_mainloop needs MainLoop = gdscene,
which currently does NOT COMPILE (E0119 from GreenBadgers in-flight pat-nzgdu.116; notified in mail
57259). Whoever takes the bridge is blocked until that clears. gdobject has no gdscene dep, which is
why this delivery verifies today.

title: ProjectSettings: resolve feature-tag ('.web') setting overrides via get_setting_with_override
description:
[audit-key: project-settings-runtime-honoring-and-script-api/projectsettings-feature-override] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]
[verify-note: ADJUSTED: Finding substance CONFIRMED but status should be MISSING, not PARTIAL. Every resolution behavior is absent: get_setting_with_override = 0 hits; custom_features/feature_override = 0 runtime hits; OS.has_feature is not implemented (no has_feature in interpreter OS static call_os_static at in]

GODOT: A setting key suffixed with a feature tag (e.g. display/window/size/viewport_width.web=800) overrides the base key when OS.has_feature("web") is true. get_setting_with_override(name) applies the active OS feature tags; get_setting_with_override_and_custom_features takes an explicit tag list (upstream core/config/project_settings.cpp).

PATINA: No override resolution. GodotProjectFile stores .web keys verbatim (project.rs:32) and ProjectConfig reads only base keys (project.rs:172-215); the browser target therefore silently ignores web-specific overrides. Only the editor's project generator touches custom features (project_manager.rs:624).

APPROACH: Add override resolution to the settings store used at boot: when reading key K, if K.<feature> exists for any active OS feature tag (query gdplatform feature tags - 'web','wasm32', etc.), return that value. Expose get_setting_with_override(name) and get_setting_with_override_and_custom_features(name,features) on the store, and have the boot honoring paths (physics/display) resolve through it. WIRING: project.godot with a .web override -> web-tagged boot -> overridden value applied.
acceptance_criteria: Given project.godot with display/window/size/viewport_width=1152 and display/window/size/viewport_width.web=800, resolving through the settings store with feature tag 'web' active returns 800 (and 1152 without it); get_setting_with_override_and_custom_features(name,["web"]) returns 800. Proven via the store's public API exercised through a boot-config test. (test: project_settings_feature_override)

title: ProjectSettings: honor display/window size + default clear color (+ max_fps) from project.godot at boot
description:
[audit-key: project-settings-runtime-honoring-and-script-api/projectsettings-display-rendering-honor] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

GODOT: The runtime configures the root Window/viewport size from display/window/size/viewport_width/height, the frame cap from application/run/max_fps, and the default background from rendering/environment/defaults/default_clear_color at startup.

PATINA: None honored. BootConfig hardcodes 1152x648 (bootstrap.rs:157) with window_size() only used in tests; the 2D renderer clear color defaults to the viewport/Color::BLACK (renderer.rs:546, wgpu_backend.rs:107) rather than the project's default_clear_color (0 grep hits); max_fps has no consumer. ProjectConfig already carries viewport_width/height (project.rs) so the parse exists but is dropped.

APPROACH: In patina-runner boot, populate BootConfig/render viewport dims from ProjectConfig.viewport_width/height, read rendering/environment/defaults/default_clear_color (extend ProjectConfig or read via the settings store) and pass it as the framebuffer/wgpu clear color, and thread application/run/max_fps into the MainLoop frame cap. (Window content-scale/stretch APPLICATION is a Viewport pipeline concern tracked by scene-tree/web-runtime; this bead covers reading+applying size, clear color, and fps.) WIRING: project.godot -> render viewport dims + clear color observable in the runner's rendered output/JSON.
acceptance_criteria: Booting the runner on a project whose project.godot sets display/window/size/viewport_width=800, viewport_height=600 and rendering/environment/defaults/default_clear_color=Color(0.1,0.2,0.3,1) produces a render target of 800x600 whose cleared background pixel equals that color - via the boot path, not manual overrides. (test: project_display_settings_honored)

title: Notifications: deliver Object::notification -> _notification(int) virtual to attached GDScripts
description:
[audit-key: notification-virtual-delivery-to-gdscript/notification_virtual_delivery] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: every notification an object receives is delivered to its script's `_notification(int what)` virtual, for ALL scripts in the inheritance chain that override it (core/object/object.cpp:1010-1048 -> ScriptInstance::notification; modules/gdscript/gdscript.cpp:1917 GDScriptInstance::notification looks up the `_notification` member function and calls it with `what`). This is how PREDELETE/POSTINITIALIZE (Object) and ENTER_TREE/READY/EXIT_TREE/PAUSED/UNPAUSED/PROCESS/PHYSICS_PROCESS (Node) and all app/window notifications reach user code. Patina current state: the `ScriptInstance` trait (crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs:129) has no `notification` method, and every notification sink only appends to an internal `Vec<Notification>` log (crates/gdscene/src/node.rs:426 receive_notification; crates/gdobject/src/object.rs:211 record_notification). Scripts only ever receive the five NAMED lifecycle callbacks via crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:1410 call_script_with_access (:1465-1491). No `_notification` is ever called on a script for any code, so save-on-quit, focus-pause, re-localize, etc. are impossible. Implementation approach: (1) add `fn notification(&mut self, what: i64, reversed: bool)` to the `ScriptInstance` trait (bindings.rs) with a default no-op; (2) implement it on `GDScriptNodeInstance` (crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs) to call the `_notification` GDScript method (if defined) with `[Variant::Int(what)]` via the existing interpreter call path, wrapped in the same SceneTreeAccessor set_scene_access/clear_scene_access frame used by call_script_with_access; (3) add a `SceneTree::notify_script(node_id, what)` helper and call it from EVERY existing notification site — crates/gdscene/src/lifecycle.rs:41/54/73 (ENTER_TREE/READY/EXIT_TREE), crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:236 (PAUSED/UNPAUSED), crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:1536-1634 (PROCESS/PHYSICS_PROCESS/INTERNAL_*), and :1781 (PREDELETE) — additively alongside the existing named dispatch and the node log push. Wiring requirement: the call path Node notification -> SceneTree::notify_script -> GDScriptNodeInstance::notification -> interpreter `_notification(what)` must exist end-to-end and be driven by the MainLoop tick / LifecycleManager, not only by tests. Depends on the companion bead that adds the NOTIFICATION_* constants to the interpreter (same group_key) so `what` comparisons resolve.
acceptance_criteria: A scene-loaded node with a GDScript that overrides `func _notification(what)` and records each `what` observes, in order, NOTIFICATION_ENTER_TREE then NOTIFICATION_READY on enter, NOTIFICATION_PAUSED/UNPAUSED when MainLoop.set_paused toggles, NOTIFICATION_PROCESS each frame, and NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE on queue_free — with values matching Godot (10,13,14/15,17,1). Prove via an integration test that loads a .tscn/attaches a script, runs LifecycleManager::enter_tree + a MainLoop frame + set_paused, and asserts the script's recorded notification list. (test: `notification_virtual_delivery`)

title: ProjectSettings: retain layer_names/{2d,3d}_{physics,render} keys and expose them via get_setting + inspector layer labels
description:
[audit-key: project-settings-runtime-honoring-and-script-api/projectsettings-layer-names] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

GODOT: project.godot may name each of the 32 collision/render layers (layer_names/2d_physics/layer_1="Player", etc.). These are readable via ProjectSettings.get_setting and drive the editor's layer-grid property editor tooltips (upstream core/config/project_settings.cpp default registration).

PATINA: No support - grep for layer_names yields 0 hits. The generic settings store must retain arbitrary keys (not just the handful ProjectConfig extracts) so layer_names/* survive, and get_setting must return them; the editor inspector layer grid should label bits from these keys.

APPROACH: Ensure the runtime settings store keeps ALL parsed project.godot keys (generic retention, not just the ProjectConfig allow-list), so layer_names/2d_physics/layer_N etc. are queryable via get_setting (depends on the script-API store from projectsettings-script-api). Wire the gdeditor collision/render layer property editor to read these names for labels/tooltips. WIRING: project.godot layer name -> get_setting result and editor layer-grid label.
acceptance_criteria: After loading a project whose project.godot sets layer_names/2d_physics/layer_1="Player", ProjectSettings.get_setting("layer_names/2d_physics/layer_1") returns "Player", and the editor's 2D physics layer grid labels bit 1 as "Player". (test: project_layer_names_exposed)

title: PrimitiveMesh3D: add Prism/Torus/Text/RibbonTrail/TubeTrail/Point + fix QuadMesh orientation
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/primitive-mesh3d] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]
[verify-note: ADJUSTED: Finding is REAL (PARTIAL/2 stay) but the evidence is materially wrong on TorusMesh — the finder searched only gdserver3d/primitive_mesh.rs and missed the ACTUAL editor render path (the acceptance target). REFUTED sub-claim 'TorusMesh missing': gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs:221 has a real Mesh3D::]

Godot provides 11 primitive meshes; Patina has 5 (Box/Sphere/Capsule/Cylinder/Plane, primitive_mesh.rs). Add PrismMesh (tapered box), TorusMesh (inner/outer radius, ring/radial segments), TextMesh (font-outline extrusion), RibbonTrailMesh + TubeTrailMesh (trail geometry with section counts + curve), and PointMesh (single point), matching Godot's vertex generation and default params (primitive_meshes.cpp; per-class XML). Also make QuadMesh a distinct XY-facing quad rather than an alias to the XZ PlaneMesh (render_server_3d.rs:574), respecting its `size`/`center_offset`/`orientation`. Register all primitive mesh classes in gdobject/class_db.rs so they construct from GDScript and .tscn sub_resources and appear in the Create-Mesh flow. Wiring: a .tscn with a TorusMesh sub-resource renders torus geometry (not a fallback cube/plane) in the editor viewport.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn whose MeshInstance3D uses a TorusMesh (and separately a PrismMesh) renders the correct silhouette in the editor viewport, and a QuadMesh renders facing +Z. Verified by (test: `primitive_meshes_torus_prism_quad_render`) asserting generated vertex bounds/orientation and non-empty rendered pixels.

title: MultiMesh3D: per-instance custom data (INSTANCE_CUSTOM) + visible_instance_count
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/multimesh3d] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot MultiMesh stores per-instance transform, optional color, and optional CUSTOM vec4 (set_instance_custom_data), and visible_instance_count limits rendering to the first N instances (multimesh.cpp; MultiMesh.xml). Patina's MultiMesh3D (multimesh.rs) has only transforms + colors + an unused use_custom_data flag and no visible count. Implementation: add a `custom_data: Vec<[f32;4]>` array (allocated when use_custom_data) with set/get accessors, a `visible_instance_count` field, include custom data in flatten_instance_data + the per-instance vertex attributes (wgpu_pipeline.rs instance buffer + WGSL INSTANCE_CUSTOM), and clamp the drawn instance range to visible_instance_count in renderer.rs/wgpu draw. Wiring: a .tscn MultiMeshInstance3D with visible_instance_count < instance_count renders only the visible subset, and custom-data feeds a shader.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn MultiMeshInstance3D with 10 instances and visible_instance_count=4 renders exactly 4 instances in the editor viewport, and per-instance custom data round-trips to the instance buffer. Verified by (test: `multimesh_visible_count_and_custom_data`).

title: Resources: wire .import remap resolution (source path → .godot/imported/*.ctex) into ResourceLoader
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/import-pipeline] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot's runtime never loads source PNG/WAV files; it reads the .import sidecar's [remap] path=res://.godot/imported/xxxx.ctex and loads that compiled artifact. Patina has the parser (importers.rs parse_import_file/load_import_file + ctex.rs) but nothing calls it during loading. Wire the ResourceLoader so that when loading res://asset.png it checks for asset.png.import, follows the [remap]/path to the .ctex/.oggvorbisstr artifact under .godot/imported/, and loads that (falling back to the source when no import exists, as the editor does).
acceptance_criteria: Loading res://icon.png where icon.png.import remaps to a .godot/imported/icon-*.ctex returns a texture whose pixels come from the .ctex artifact (not a re-decode of the source), verified by dimensions/format from the ctex header. (test: `resource_loader_follows_import_remap`)

title: Resources: wire uid:// resolution (uid_cache.bin + .uid sidecars) and expose the ResourceUID singleton
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/resource-uid] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot resolves uid://… references through a registry populated from res://.godot/uid_cache.bin and per-file .uid sidecars, letting scenes reference resources by UID even when paths move. Patina parses uid= attributes but never builds or consults such a registry, so uid-only ext_resource references and load("uid://…") cannot resolve. Populate gdresource::uid::UidRegistry at boot from uid_cache.bin/.uid sidecars, have the ResourceLoader consult it for uid:// paths, and expose the ResourceUID singleton (id_to_text/text_to_id/get_id_path/has_id) to GDScript.
acceptance_criteria: With a uid_cache.bin mapping uid://abc → res://sub.tscn, load("uid://abc").instantiate() loads the same scene as load("res://sub.tscn"), and ResourceUID.get_id_path(ResourceUID.text_to_id("uid://abc")) returns "res://sub.tscn". (test: `uid_resolves_to_path`)

title: DirAccess: add get_files/get_directories(+_at), copy, change_dir/get_current_dir, drives, space, and .import filtering
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/dir-access] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

The most common DirAccess usage in games/tools is DirAccess.get_files()/get_directories() and the static DirAccess.get_files_at(path); these plus copy/change_dir/get_current_dir are missing from gdcore/file_access.rs. Implement them (get_files returns non-dir entries with Godot's default .import/.godot + hidden filtering), add copy/change_dir/get_current_dir/get_drive*/get_space_left, and expose them through the interpreter DirAccess dispatch.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript calls DirAccess.get_files_at("res://assets") and receives the file names (excluding a sibling directory and any .import sidecar), and DirAccess.get_directories() on an opened dir lists only subdirectories. (test: `dir_access_get_files_and_directories`)

title: SceneTree: call_group/notify_group/set_group broadcasts + get_first_node_in_group/get_node_count_in_group/has_group
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/groups-broadcast] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot broadcasts to a group via call_group(group, method, ...args), call_group_flags(flags, ...), notify_group/notify_group_flags(what), and set_group/set_group_flags(property, value), honoring GROUP_CALL_REVERSE/DEFERRED/UNIQUE flags; plus get_first_node_in_group, get_node_count_in_group, and tree-level has_group (scene_tree.cpp). Patina only tracks membership (scene_tree.rs:864-918) with get_nodes_in_group. Implement the broadcasts over the existing group index: iterate members in tree order (reversible), invoke the named script method / set property / send notification, honoring DEFERRED by routing through the existing call_deferred queue (scene_tree.rs:1670) and UNIQUE de-duplication; add get_first_node_in_group/get_node_count_in_group/has_group. Expose to the GDScript bridge so get_tree().call_group('enemies','explode') reaches every member's script during a frame.
acceptance_criteria: call_group('g','take_damage',10) invokes take_damage on every scripted member during a MainLoop step; call_group_flags with DEFERRED defers until the frame's deferred flush; get_first_node_in_group returns the first member in tree order and get_node_count_in_group returns the member count. (test: scene_tree_group_broadcast)

title: Node: honor set_process/set_physics_process/is_processing toggles + request_ready
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/process-toggles] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

In Godot a node's _process/_physics_process run only while set_process(true)/set_physics_process(true) (default becomes enabled once the callback is defined), toggled at runtime independently of process_mode; set_process_input/unhandled_input gate input callbacks, and request_ready re-arms _ready on the next tree-enter (node.cpp process bitflags). Patina's Node has only process_priority/process_mode (node.rs:122-126) and dispatches to every scripted node passing should_process_node (scene_tree.rs:1498/1607) — a script calling set_process(false) still receives _process. Add per-node process / physics_process / internal-process enable flags (default true) to Node, gate process_all_scripts_* and process_frame_with_scripts on them, expose set_process/set_physics_process/is_processing/is_physics_processing/request_ready to the GDScript bridge, and clear/re-arm the ready flag via request_ready.
acceptance_criteria: A scripted node that calls set_process(false) in _ready receives no further _process callbacks across subsequent MainLoop steps while still receiving _physics_process; after request_ready() and re-entering the tree, _ready runs again. (test: node_process_toggles_gate_callbacks)

comments.author: bone

title: PackedScene/Node: editable instances, InstancePlaceholder, inherited scenes, duplicate() flags
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/instancing] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot instancing supports editable children (set_editable_instance exposes an instanced scene's internal nodes and persists overrides), InstancePlaceholder (set_scene_instance_load_placeholder defers instancing; InstancePlaceholder.create_instance() realizes it), inherited scenes (a .tscn whose root instances a base scene plus property/child diffs), and Node.duplicate(flags) copying signals/groups/scripts per DUPLICATE_* flags (packed_scene.cpp). Patina's packed_scene.rs handles none of these, and duplicate_subtree (scene_tree.rs:1177) copies only properties+groups+unique_name — no signals, no script, no flags. Implement editable-instance + load-placeholder flags on Node and honor them in add_packed_scene_to_tree (packed_scene.rs), add an InstancePlaceholder node with create_instance, support instances-of-instances/inherited roots during .tscn instancing, and give duplicate() a DuplicateFlags parameter that carries groups/signals/scripts.
acceptance_criteria: Instancing a scene that marks a child sub-scene editable exposes and applies overrides to its inner nodes; a placeholder-marked instance is an InstancePlaceholder until create_instance() is called; duplicate(DUPLICATE_GROUPS|DUPLICATE_SIGNALS) copies group membership and signal connections. (test: packed_scene_editable_placeholder_and_duplicate_flags)

comments.text:
[IndigoBridge 2026-07-16] SCOPING ONLY — no code delivered this pass, deliberately. This is a 4-feature pack; I am NOT shipping a thin slice because a compile-clean partial auto-closes the whole bead and would mark 4 real parity gaps done. Handing off with a verified split.

VERIFIED STATE (greps 2026-07-16) — bead evidence is mostly right, with ONE correction:

- CORRECTION: the bead says "Patina's packed_scene.rs handles none of these". Not quite — `[editable path="..."]` IS already parsed and exposed: packed_scene.rs:115/124/230/516 collects `editable_instances`, and there's a public accessor `PackedScene::editable_instances()` (packed_scene.rs:657). It is PARSED BUT NOT HONORED: the only consumer is a test assertion (packed_scene.rs:3177). So the editable-instance work is "honor the already-parsed list during instancing", not "parse it".
- InstancePlaceholder / set_scene_instance_load_placeholder / load_placeholder: 0 hits. Genuinely missing.
- DuplicateFlags: 0 hits. Genuinely missing.
- duplicate_subtree (scene_tree.rs ~1177) copies properties + groups + unique_name only. No signals, no scripts, no flags. Confirmed.

STRUCTURAL BLOCKERS a future worker must know BEFORE starting (these are why this isn't a quick win):

1. DUPLICATE_SCRIPTS IS NOT IMPLEMENTABLE TODAY. `ScriptInstance` (gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs:135) is a trait object with NO clone/duplicate method, and scripts are held as `Box<dyn ScriptInstance>`. To copy a script on duplicate you must first add something like `fn clone_script(&self) -> Option<Box<dyn ScriptInstance>> { None }` as a DEFAULTED trait method (defaulted is mandatory — there are FIVE SceneAccess/ScriptInstance impls incl. test mocks), then implement it for GDScriptNodeInstance. That touches gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, which was exclusively reserved by GentleBadger (expires 02:22) at the time of this scoping.

2. SIGNALS CAN'T RIDE ON THE CURRENT API. `duplicate_subtree(&self, root) -> EngineResult<Vec<Node>>` returns DETACHED nodes, but signal connections live on the TREE: `SceneTree.signal_stores: HashMap<NodeId, SignalStore>` (scene_tree.rs:77). A detached Vec<Node> has nowhere to carry them. GOOD NEWS: `SignalStore` derives Clone (gdobject/src/signal.rs:282), so the copy itself is trivial ONCE the API can reach the tree. The fix is a new tree-level `duplicate_node(&mut self, root, flags) -> EngineResult<NodeId>` that inserts the clone AND clones signal_stores per old->new id mapping. Note `collect_subtree_top_down` and `duplicate_subtree` walk in the same deterministic order, so old_ids.zip(clones) gives the mapping without refactoring.

3. duplicate_subtree currently has NO production callers — only tests (packed_scene.rs:2154, :2180). So changing its behaviour is low-risk, but also means nothing in the engine actually duplicates nodes yet.

4. InstancePlaceholder needs a new node class REGISTERED in gdobject/src/class_db.rs, which was exclusively reserved by GreenBadger (expires 02:21) and GentleBadger (expires 02:16) at the time of this scoping. That file has been continuously contended for the last ~2h.

SUGGESTED SPLIT (4 beads):

a. Node.duplicate(flags) — the acceptance's third clause, and the best standalone win. Add DuplicateFlags (Godot: SIGNALS=1, GROUPS=2, SCRIPTS=4, USE_INSTANTIATION=8; default duplicate() = 1|2|4). Add tree-level `duplicate_node(root, flags) -> NodeId` that inserts the clone under the same parent, copies properties+unique_name always, groups only when GROUPS, and clones signal_stores when SIGNALS. Leave SCRIPTS unimplemented until (b) lands and say so. gdscene-only, no conflicted files. Test: duplicate with GROUPS|SIGNALS copies both; with neither copies neither.

b. DUPLICATE_SCRIPTS — add the defaulted `clone_script()` to ScriptInstance + implement for GDScriptNodeInstance. Needs interpreter.rs (contended).

c. Editable instances — honor the ALREADY-PARSED `PackedScene::editable_instances()` in add_packed_scene_to_tree: expose the named instance's inner nodes and apply overrides to them. Add a per-Node editable-instance flag. gdscene-only.

d. InstancePlaceholder + inherited scenes — new InstancePlaceholder node class + registration (needs class_db.rs, contended) + `set_scene_instance_load_placeholder` deferring instantiation + `create_instance()` realizing it; plus inherited-scene roots (a .tscn whose root instances a base scene plus diffs) during .tscn instancing.

RECOMMENDATION: (a) and (c) are clean gdscene-only beads a build-restricted worker can deliver. (b) and (d) are gated on the contended class_db.rs / interpreter.rs.

title: Shaders: execute sky/particles/fog/canvas_item shader types with per-stage built-ins
description:
[audit-key: shaders/shader-types-sky-particles-fog] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: each shader_type has its own stage functions and built-ins (shader_types.cpp) — sky shaders compute COLOR from EYEDIR/LIGHTn/radiance and drive the background; particles shaders run start()/process() writing TRANSFORM/VELOCITY/COLOR; fog shaders write DENSITY/ALBEDO/EMISSION into the volumetric fog; canvas_item shaders write COLOR from TEXTURE/SCREEN_UV in vertex/fragment/light. Patina current state: only Spatial(+a non-executed Sky enum) exists in gdserver3d; the wgpu sky is a fixed procedural shader (wgpu_pipeline.rs:330) not a user Sky ShaderMaterial; canvas_item fragment programs are parsed (gdserver2d) but never run by gdrender2d. Implementation approach: add ShaderType variants + per-stage built-in contexts for sky/particles/fog; execute a Sky ShaderMaterial to produce the background (feed from WorldEnvironment.sky), execute canvas_item fragment programs in gdrender2d's draw path, and hook particles shaders into the particle process step. Wiring requirement: a `shader_type sky` material on the environment changes background pixels, and a `shader_type canvas_item` material changes a Sprite2D's pixels, at runtime.
acceptance_criteria: A `shader_type sky` ShaderMaterial assigned to Environment/WorldEnvironment renders its computed COLOR as the viewport background, and a `shader_type canvas_item` ShaderMaterial on a CanvasItem alters its rendered pixels. (test: `sky_and_canvas_shader_types_render`)

title: Physics2D: wire RigidBody2D force/impulse/torque script API + angular dynamics
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-rigidbody-forces] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot ground truth (rigid_body_2d.cpp, RigidBody2D.xml): scripts drive rigid bodies via apply_central_impulse/apply_impulse(impulse,pos)/apply_central_force/apply_force(force,pos)/apply_torque/apply_torque_impulse/add_constant_force/add_constant_torque/set_axis_velocity, and _integrate_forces receives a PhysicsDirectBodyState2D. Positioned impulses/forces produce angular acceleration through the body's inertia; collisions impart spin. Patina state: apply_force/apply_impulse exist in body.rs:126-139 (central only) with green module tests but are UNREACHABLE — no GDScript dispatch (only physics_server.rs references those names; interpreter.rs handles only get_node/queue_free) and physics_server never calls them. No apply_torque, no positioned impulse, no inertia/center_of_mass; separate_bodies (collision.rs:209) mutates only linear_velocity so collisions never rotate bodies; sync_to_physics (physics_server.rs:359) ignores linear_velocity so script velocity writes are lost mid-sim. Approach: add rotation/torque state to PhysicsBody2D (inertia auto-computed from shape+mass, center_of_mass, accumulated_torque, apply_torque/apply_impulse_at_point), integrate angular velocity in body.rs:integrate, add angular impulse in collision.rs:separate_bodies for off-center contacts; expose apply_central_impulse/apply_impulse/apply_central_force/apply_force/apply_torque/apply_torque_impulse/add_constant_force/set_axis_velocity as node methods dispatched from the interpreter through SceneAccess to PhysicsServer -> world body; make sync_to_physics forward script-set linear_velocity/angular_velocity to the body. Wiring requirement: a GDScript in a loaded .tscn calling body.apply_central_impulse(v) during _physics_process must change the body's linear_velocity and node position on the next MainLoop.step.
acceptance_criteria: A scene-loaded RigidBody2D whose _physics_process calls apply_central_impulse and apply_torque changes both linear and angular velocity and its node position/rotation after MainLoop.step; an off-center apply_impulse imparts angular velocity. (test: `rigidbody2d_apply_impulse_script_wiring`)

title: TextServer: BiDi + complex-script shaping (HarfBuzz-class) and RTL UI mirroring
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/textserver-shaping] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot's advanced TextServer (modules/text_server_adv) uses HarfBuzz for shaping (ligatures, glyph clusters, combining marks, contextual forms) and ICU for BiDi reordering + script itemization, and mirrors the whole UI for RTL locales (Control layout_direction). Patina has none of this: TextServerLite (gdrender2d/src/text_server.rs) is LTR fixed-advance only, no shaping/BiDi crate exists (grep for harfbuzz/rustybuzz/unicode-bidi/icu is empty), and the built-in font is ASCII LTR. Implementation: add a shaping backend (e.g. rustybuzz) + a BiDi pass (e.g. unicode-bidi) into gdrender2d's text layout; produce shaped glyph runs (with cluster mapping) that the TextParagraph layout (textserver-layout bead) consumes; add Control layout_direction so an RTL Control mirrors its children and text. Wiring requirement: rendering an RTL string (e.g. Arabic/Hebrew) or a combining-mark string produces visually reordered/joined glyphs, not left-to-right codepoint order.
acceptance_criteria: Shaping an RTL string reverses visual glyph order relative to logical codepoint order and joins connected forms; a string with a base char + combining mark yields a single positioned cluster; a Control with layout_direction=RTL mirrors child positions. (test: `textserver_bidi_rtl_shaping`)

title: Font resources: LabelSettings, FontVariation, and SystemFont with Label consumption
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/font-resources] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot provides LabelSettings (a resource holding font, font_size, font_color, outline, shadow, line/paragraph spacing that a Label applies instead of theme values - scene/resources/label_settings.cpp), FontVariation (a base font + variation coords/embolden/transform/spacing/OpenType features - scene/resources/font.cpp), and SystemFont (resolves OS-installed families with fallback/AA/hinting). Patina has none: LabelSettings is only an inspector schema entry (gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:709), FontVariation/SystemFont are absent, all three unregistered in gdobject/src/class_db.rs. Implementation: add LabelSettings/FontVariation/SystemFont resource types (gdrender2d building on the font-stack bead's FontFile), register them in class_db.rs, parse them from .tres, and make the Label update path prefer a LabelSettings resource over theme values and apply FontVariation transforms. Wiring requirement: a Label with a LabelSettings resource renders with the settings' color/size (not the theme default).
acceptance_criteria: A Label carrying a LabelSettings resource (font_size=32, font_color=red) renders its text at that size and color overriding the theme; a FontVariation with embolden/spacing changes measured glyph advances; SystemFont resolves at least one requested family or falls back deterministically. (test: `label_settings_font_variation_apply`)

title: Particles3D: add GPUParticlesAttractor3D volumes and wire attractor forces into the sim
description:
[audit-key: vfx-particles/particle-attractor-collision] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: GPUParticlesAttractorBox3D/Sphere3D/VectorField3D apply a per-particle force each frame when the particle is inside the attractor's volume, scaled by strength, falling off by attenuation over the volume, biased between radial and directional by directionality, filtered by cull_mask; the vector-field variant samples a Texture3D for the force direction (scene/3d/gpu_particles_attractor_3d.cpp). ParticleProcessMaterial.attractor_interaction_enabled gates whether an emitter is affected. Patina current state: none of the four classes are registered (unregistered.txt; class_db.rs grep empty) and no simulator consumes attractor volumes. Implementation approach: (1) register the four classes in gdobject/src/class_db.rs (parents GPUParticlesAttractor3D->VisualInstance3D, shapes->GPUParticlesAttractor3D) with their properties; (2) collect active attractor nodes from the SceneTree each particle step; (3) in the 3D particle step (gdscene/src/particle3d.rs:491) apply attractor force to particles inside each volume honoring strength/attenuation/directionality/cull_mask and attractor_interaction_enabled. Wiring requirement: attractor node in the same scene as an emitter measurably deflects particle trajectories in the render output.
acceptance_criteria: A scene with a GPUParticles3D emitter and a GPUParticlesAttractorSphere3D (positive strength) placed off-axis shows particle velocities/positions in frame output bending toward the attractor center versus an identical scene without the attractor; cull_mask exclusion disables the effect. (test: `particle_attractor_pulls_particles`)

title: GPUParticles: implement trails, draw_order, sub_emitter, emit_particle(), finished signal, fixed_fps/preprocess/seed
description:
[audit-key: vfx-particles/particle-node-features] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot ground truth: GPUParticles2D/3D expose node-level behaviors beyond the process material — the `finished` signal fires when a one_shot emitter completes; emit_particle(xform,vel,color,custom,flags) manually spawns; draw_order sorts particles (INDEX/LIFETIME/REVERSE_LIFETIME/VIEW_DEPTH); trails render connected ribbon geometry (trail_lifetime/sections/subdivisions); sub_emitter spawns child particles at start/end/collision; fixed_fps + interpolate + fract_delta give a fixed simulation timestep with visual interpolation; preprocess pre-warms the sim; use_fixed_seed/seed make emission reproducible; amount_ratio/interp_to_end/visibility_rect(aabb) control count, aging, and culling; convert_from_particles() copies a GPU emitter to a CPU one (scene/2d|3d/gpu_particles_*.cpp). Patina current state: the sims omit all of these — `finished` never emitted (grep empty), emit_particle/convert_from_particles/capture_* have no node dispatch, draw order is insertion order (particle.rs:363), fixed_fps is a stored-but-ignored field (particles3d.rs:271/step:376), trails/sub_emitter/preprocess/seed absent. Implementation approach: build on the wiring beads — add a fixed-timestep accumulator to the step, emit the `finished` signal through the node's signal system on one_shot drain, sort draw output by draw_order, add preprocess warm-up on start, honor use_fixed_seed/seed, and implement trail ribbon geometry + sub_emitter spawning. Wiring requirement: these must be observable in the running scene (signal reaches a connected script; draw order changes pixel/layer order).
acceptance_criteria: A scene-loaded one_shot GPUParticles2D drains and emits `finished` to a connected script callback exactly once; setting draw_order=LIFETIME reorders the emitted draw commands by particle age; a fixed_fps value produces a deterministic per-frame particle count independent of the render delta. Verified through scene run + signal capture, not struct unit tests. (test: `particle_node_trails_and_emit_signal`)

title: JavaScriptBridge: register a script-reachable singleton with real browser bindings
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web_js_bridge] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot's web export exposes the JavaScriptBridge singleton (javascript_bridge_singleton.cpp; JavaScriptBridge.xml) so GDScript can eval() JS, get_interface() globals, create_callback()/create_object(), download_buffer() to trigger a browser download, and force_fs_sync()/PWA update callbacks — the required interop surface for a browser engine. Patina has no such singleton (absent from class_db.rs and the interpreter singleton table, interpreter.rs:6224); gdplatform/web.rs's JsBridge is a fake unwired stub. Implementation: add a JavaScriptBridge singleton registered in gdobject/class_db.rs and dispatched by the interpreter alongside OS/Engine/Time, backed by real wasm-bindgen/js-sys bindings under cfg(target_arch=wasm32) (eval, get_interface, create_callback→closure, create_object→JS constructor, download_buffer→Blob+anchor click, force_fs_sync→IDBFS sync) and returning correct 'not available' results on native, so GDScript calls resolve on both targets.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript calling JavaScriptBridge.create_object/eval/get_interface resolves through the interpreter's singleton dispatch (not an 'unknown identifier' error), and download_buffer/force_fs_sync are callable with defined native fallbacks. (test: `javascript_bridge_singleton_script_reachable`) attaches a script that references JavaScriptBridge and asserts the calls dispatch and return the defined values rather than an interpreter unknown-singleton error.

title: OS.has_feature web tags + ProjectSettings .web override resolution
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web_feature_tags] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Real Godot projects branch heavily on OS.has_feature('web'|'wasm'|'JavaScript'|'threads'|'mobile'|'editor'|'debug') and ProjectSettings resolves per-feature overrides like `display/window/size/viewport_width.web`. Patina has no has_feature at all (grep empty; interpreter OS is 4 methods, interpreter.rs:6255) and never reports the web platform because the wasm branch (interpreter.rs:6268) is dead. Implementation: add OS.has_feature to the interpreter's OS singleton dispatch and to gdplatform/os.rs, returning the platform tags (web/wasm32/JavaScript on the wasm target; desktop tags on native), build config tags (debug/release, threads/simd from the web export config), plus editor when is_editor_hint; and honor `.web`-suffixed ProjectSettings overrides during project load. Note: general OS/has_feature breadth is shared with the platform-os subsystem; this bead covers the web/wasm/browser tags and the `.web` override path specifically.
acceptance_criteria: OS.has_feature('web') and OS.has_feature('wasm') return true under the wasm build and false on native, and a ProjectSettings value with a `.web` override resolves to the web-specific value when the web feature is active. (test: `os_has_feature_web_tags`) drives a GDScript calling OS.has_feature for web/wasm/desktop tags and asserts the interpreter dispatches and returns the tag set matching the active platform.

title: Web networking: browser fetch/WebSocket/WebRTC bindings behind a transport abstraction + COOP/COEP
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web_networking] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

On the web target Godot routes HTTPClient/HTTPRequest through the browser fetch API (library_godot_fetch.js), WebSocketPeer through the browser WebSocket object, and WebRTCPeerConnection through RTCPeerConnection — because raw TCP/UDP sockets are unavailable in the browser. Patina's transports are all native sockets (http_client.rs std::net TcpStream; websocket_peer.rs native RFC6455, no wss; webrtc_peer.rs a stub) and are not exposed to GDScript. Implementation: introduce a transport abstraction so HTTPClient/HTTPRequest and WebSocketPeer select a browser-backed implementation under cfg(target_arch=wasm32) (fetch for HTTP, window.WebSocket for WS incl. wss, RTCPeerConnection/RTCDataChannel for WebRTC) while keeping the native impls for desktop; expose HTTPRequest/HTTPClient/WebSocketPeer as script-reachable classes; and have the editor server emit Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy/Embedder-Policy so a threaded web build can be previewed. Coordinate the WebSocket/WebRTC protocol surface with the multiplayer subsystem to avoid duplication.
acceptance_criteria: HTTPRequest and WebSocketPeer are constructible and callable from GDScript and dispatch to a transport chosen by target (browser fetch/WebSocket under wasm, native otherwise), and the editor server responds with COOP/COEP headers. (test: `web_http_websocket_script_reachable`) constructs HTTPRequest and WebSocketPeer from a script, asserts they resolve through the interpreter and select the correct transport, and asserts the editor server includes the cross-origin isolation headers.

title: Web I/O backends: fetch-based PCK loading, IndexedDB/OPFS user:// persistence, and AudioWorklet mixer sink
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web_assets_persistence] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot's web export fetches the .pck over HTTP with progress (preloader.js), persists user:// through emscripten IDBFS with an explicit sync (force_fs_sync), and drives audio through an AudioWorklet fed from the mixer (audio_driver_web.cpp, audio.worklet.js) unlocked on the first user gesture. Patina has none of these: no IndexedDB/OPFS/localStorage backend (grep empty; web.rs WebStorageBackend is a dead stub), no PCK-over-HTTP loader (only native pck.rs:674), and no AudioWorklet/AudioContext sink for gdaudio. Implementation (stage under cfg(target_arch=wasm32)): (1) a fetch-based ResourceLoader/PCK source that streams res:// assets over HTTP with progress into the existing loader; (2) a user:// FileAccess backend mapping to IndexedDB or OPFS with a force_fs_sync flush; (3) an AudioWorklet output that pulls the gdaudio mixer buffer (SharedArrayBuffer ring when cross-origin-isolated, message-port fallback otherwise) and resumes the AudioContext on first input. Keep the native filesystem/audio backends for desktop.
acceptance_criteria: RE-SCOPED 2026-10-30 (operator triage). The backends exist: patina-web/src/vfs.rs + web_vfs.rs (fetch-PCK res:// via WebVfs::mount_pack, IndexedDB-backed user:// write-through store with hydrate + take_pending_write), and gdaudio/src/web_output.rs audio_worklet_glue. What remains is ONE integration test, `web_pck_fetch_and_user_persistence` in crates/patina-web/tests/, driven through the browser-facing seams, not just the portable halves. It must: (1) mount a packed .pck from raw bytes via the same entry point JS fetch uses and load a res:// asset from it; (2) write user://, drain the pending persist write, simulate a reload by re-hydrating a fresh store from those writes, and assert the data survived; (3) assert the gdaudio worklet glue and the patina-web worklet glue register the SAME processor name and channel count. They are tested separately today, but nothing asserts they agree. Gates: `cargo nextest run -p patina-web --test web_pck_fetch_and_user_persistence` AND `cargo check -p patina-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`. A real in-browser run is NOT required by the verifier; an operator spot-check via scripts/web.sh --runtime (:8099) is recommended before release.

comments.author: ScarletRidge
comments.text:
2026-10-30 ~08:44Z (ScarletRidge) — RE-VERIFIED, read-only. No code, no claim, no status change. Posting because this bead's own history shows its audit going materially stale twice in nine days, and it has now been three MONTHS since the last one (TealIsland, 2026-07-27) — during which a browser lane was added to the repo. WildIsland's audit is still broadly right, but three load-bearing details have moved, one of them in the direction of MORE work, not less.

=== 1. A BROWSER LANE NOW EXISTS, AND NO PREVIOUS AUDIT COULD HAVE KNOWN IT ===

`scripts/web.sh --runtime`, added 2026-10-29 in commit `ce15f3c` ("Add scripts/web.sh to start Patina in a browser; fix wasm build"). Reading the script at HEAD:
  :6        `--runtime` selects the wasm runtime harness (plain `scripts/web.sh` runs the native editor on :8080)
  :57       serves it on :8099
  :133-135  adds the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` rustup target if missing
  :151-155  installs a `Cargo.lock`-matching `wasm-bindgen-cli` into
            `engine-rs/target/wasm-bindgen-cli/<version>` on first run, leaving the global CLI and the
            lockfile untouched

This is a REAL BROWSER serving the wasm build, so the three browser APIs this bead's acceptance names — fetch, IndexedDB/OPFS, AudioWorklet — are all actually present there. That is a different thing from a headless test runner (see §2), but it is the first time this bead's acceptance has been *observable* in this environment at all.

It also matters that CLAUDE.md already mandates browser verification for this project ("When debugging HTTP/browser issues, ALWAYS check browser console logs via Claude in Chrome ... verify in the browser with error tracking active for at least 15 seconds"). So an operator-driven browser check is an established, sanctioned lane here — it is simply not a `cargo test` the verifier can close on.

=== 2. THE HEADLESS WALL STILL STANDS — verified today, not inherited ===

  chromedriver                 ABSENT from PATH
  geckodriver                  ABSENT from PATH
  wasm-bindgen-test-runner     PRESENT at ~/.cargo/bin/wasm-bindgen-test-runner
  runner line for wasm32       ABSENT (see §3)

So WildIsland's core conclusion holds: the acceptance test `web_pck_fetch_and_user_persistence` still cannot execute under the verifier, and GentleBadger's judgment that a natively-compiling storage/transport slice would compile, pass, and FALSE-CLOSE the real web gap still stands. I did not write one.

=== 3. ⚠️ `engine-rs/.cargo/config.toml` NOW EXISTS — and it is NOT the runner line ===

WildIsland's audit explicitly recorded "engine-rs/.cargo/config.toml, which does not exist". It exists now, created by the same `ce15f3c`. Its full contents:

    [build]
    jobs = 2

    # Selects getrandom's browser backend for the web build (see gdcore/Cargo.toml).
    # Scoped to the wasm target so native builds keep their cached artifacts.
    [target.wasm32-unknown-unknown]
    rustflags = ['--cfg', 'getrandom_backend="wasm_js"']

🔑 FLAGGING THIS SPECIFICALLY so the next auditor does not see "a wasm32 section appeared in .cargo/config.toml" and conclude the runner was provisioned. It sets rustflags, NOT `runner`. The ask in §4 is unchanged by it.

(Incidental, for anyone touching the wasm build: that file is under `engine-rs/`, and cargo discovers config by walking up from the CWD — so the cfg applies to builds run from `engine-rs/` but not from the repo root, where there is no `.cargo/config.toml`. In practice harmless for getrandom 0.3.4, whose wasm32 arm selects the `wasm_js` backend on the FEATURE alone, which gdcore enables; the rustflags is belt-and-braces. Worth knowing before someone "fixes" a root-level build by duplicating the file.)

=== 4. ⚠️ THE OPERATOR ASK IS LARGER THAN "ESSENTIALLY ONE QUESTION" ===

WildIsland wrote that the ask "has gone from 3 questions to essentially one: provision a headless browser runner ... and add a wasm32 runner line", on the basis that "wasm-bindgen-test IS cached". **That claim is imprecise, and the imprecision costs a network fetch.** Checked today:

    ~/.cargo/registry/src/*/wasm-bindgen-test*        0 directories
    ~/.cargo/registry/cache/*/wasm-bindgen-test*      1 file, and it is
                                                      wasm-bindgen-test-shared-0.2.114.crate
    grep '^name = "wasm-bindgen-test"' engine-rs/Cargo.lock      0

Only `wasm-bindgen-test-SHARED` is cached — a transitive support crate, not the test harness. `wasm-bindgen-test` itself has no source in the registry and is not in the lockfile. The runner BINARY being on PATH is a separate thing from the CRATE being available to `#[wasm_bindgen_test]`-annotated code.

So GentleBadger's original question (1) — "is a network fetch permitted?" — is NOT retired. It is live again.

CONSOLIDATED ASK, in the order an operator would act on it:
  (a) permit a network fetch to add `wasm-bindgen-test` as a dev-dependency of the web crate, AND
  (b) install chromedriver or geckodriver and add a `runner` line under
      `[target.wasm32-unknown-unknown]` in `engine-rs/.cargo/config.toml` pointing at
      `wasm-bindgen-test-runner`
  — OR —
  (c) ACCEPT BROWSER VERIFICATION VIA THE EXISTING HARNESS: implement items (b)/(c)/(d) from
      GentleBadger's split, verify them by hand through `scripts/web.sh --runtime` at :8099 with
      Claude in Chrome, and re-scope the acceptance so the verifier gates on the natively-testable
      seams while the browser halves are signed off by a recorded browser session rather than by
      `cargo test`.

(c) is newly possible as of 2026-10-29 and did not exist when any previous audit was written. It is also the only option that does not require a network fetch or a new binary. The tradeoff is explicit and is the operator's to make: it trades verifier-enforced regression protection on the browser halves for the ability to finish the bead at all. Given GentleBadger's and WildIsland's shared worry is precisely a FALSE CLOSE, (c) should be taken only with the re-scope written into the acceptance, so nothing silently closes on a native-only slice.

=== 5. WHAT I DID NOT DO ===

I did not claim this bead, change its status, or write any implementation. A worker cannot reach the lane in §1 either: `.claude/hooks/block_worker_cargo.sh` matches on command text (it refuses the `cargo install`/`cargo build` inside `web.sh` just as readily as a direct invocation) and `scripts/rust_task.sh:51-57` self-gates on `AGENT_NAME ∈ {interactive, verifier}`. An interactive operator or the verifier lane can run `scripts/web.sh --runtime` unmodified; I cannot.

Related, same session: I posted the same "name the lane, not its absence" correction on pat-u3l8c.112, where I had made exactly this mistake myself twelve minutes earlier. Every `blocked` note in this web family (pat-u3l8c.111/.113/.114, pat-nzgdu.113/.149) rests on a July diagnosis, and `crates/patina-web/Cargo.toml` now carries an in-tree comment explicitly retiring its own stale predecessor — which is the fastest tell that a block note has aged out. Read that file and `scripts/web.sh` at HEAD before quoting any of those notes forward.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
2026-10-30 ~13:5xZ (ScarletRidge) — **INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION of OrangePuma's finding, plus a correction to my OWN earlier comment on this bead.** Read-only; no code, no claim, no status change. I am not the assignee and am not asking for this bead.

I audited `.149` earlier today and reached a *different* conclusion from OrangePuma's. Having checked their argument I think **they are right and my earlier framing was wrong**, and since both notes sit on this bead while an owner decides, I would rather say so explicitly than leave two conflicting notes.

## What I got wrong

My earlier comment said the remaining operator ask was "(a) permit a network fetch for the `wasm-bindgen-test` dev-dep, **and** (b) install chromedriver/geckodriver plus a `runner` line." Every fact in that sentence is still true, but it **assumed the acceptance must execute inside a browser**. That assumption is what OrangePuma correctly challenges: this lane has already accepted the native-seam + unexecuted-JS-handle split for the audio half, so demanding browser execution here is an inconsistency, not a standard.

## The precedent, verified independently (OrangePuma did not cite this)

`pat-u3l8c.112` — the AudioWorklet bead — closed **green** on a chain containing no browser execution whatsoever:

    verifier.log:11744  commands = ...rust_task.sh nextest run -p patina-web --test web_demo_shell_drives_audio
                                && ...check -p patina-web --target wasm32-unknown-unknown
                                && ...nextest run -p patina-web --test web_audio_worklet
                                && ...nextest run -p patina-web --lib
                                && ...nextest run -p gdaudio --test audio_web_backend_contract
                                && ...nextest run -p gdaudio --lib web_output
    verifier.log:11745  PASS  run_ms=54195

Native test runs plus a **compile-only** wasm32 check. No chromedriver, no `wasm-bindgen-test`, no browser. That is the precedent in the verifier's own record, and `.113` closed the same way (`:11746/11747`). So "the acceptance can be satisfied without a browser runner" is not a concession anyone needs to grant — it is the rule this family has already been closed under, three times.

## I tried to break the false-close concern and could not

The three July refusals were right to guard against a portable slice that compiles, passes, and false-closes the real web gap. So I checked whether the "browser half" is genuinely wired or just inert strings. It is wired, on **both** delivery paths:

- **Live browser runtime:** `patina-web/src/audio.rs:251-253` `WebAudioEngine::worklet_glue()` calls `gdaudio::audio_worklet_glue(PROCESSOR_NAME, self.channels)`. This is production code — the `#[cfg(test)]` module in that file does not start until `:256`.
- **Exported static site:** `gdplatform/src/export.rs:595` writes `patina.audio.worklet.js` from `gdplatform::export::web_audio_worklet_glue(web.threads_enabled)`, with the transport chosen at export time.
- **`user://` host half:** `USER_STORE_GLUE` (`patina-web/src/vfs.rs:259`) is exposed to JS as a real binding — `#[wasm_bindgen(getter, js_name = userStoreGlue)]` on `WebVfs` (`web_vfs.rs:153-156`), so the host reads it off the object rather than needing a second import.

⚠️ **Correction to my own first pass at this check:** I initially read `gdaudio::audio_worklet_glue` as having *no* production consumer, because a grep of `patina-web/src` showed only doc comments. That was a truncated-grep artifact — `head -10` cut the output before `audio.rs:251`. The call site was there all along. Flagging it because the wrong version of that claim would have been a serious accusation against a peer's work.

## One residual finding, offered as a small follow-on and explicitly NOT a blocker

There are **two independently-maintained worklet glue strings** — `gdaudio::web_output::audio_worklet_glue` (:257, live runtime) and `gdplatform::export::web_audio_worklet_glue` (:1200, exported site). Each is tested against its own expectations (`patina-web/tests/web_audio_worklet.rs:136 worklet_glue_matches_the_backend_contract`; `gdplatform/tests/web_threads_and_shared_memory_story.rs:167-205` for both threaded and plain variants). **No test asserts the two agree.** So the exported site and the live runtime could drift — e.g. on processor name or channel count — and both suites would stay green.

Be careful reading a grep here: `grep -c 'audio_worklet_glue('` matches inside `web_audio_worklet_glue(`, which makes it look like the gdplatform test covers the gdaudio glue. It does not.

That is a modest hardening item (one test asserting both glues register the same processor name and channel count), worth its own small bead. It is **not** the false-close the July notes feared, and it should not gate `.149`.

## Net

OrangePuma's conclusion holds and my earlier operator ask was over-scoped. `.149`'s remaining work is writing `web_pck_fetch_and_user_persistence` over seams that already exist and are already exercised natively — a small bead, verifiable by the same native-plus-wasm32-check pattern that closed `.112` and `.113`. The `needs-attention` flag I added for "provision a browser runner" should be read as "confirm the audio precedent applies here", which is a much cheaper decision.

Still worth honouring from the July notes, because it is about correctness rather than tooling: do not accept a diff that only touches the portable half. The guard is that the acceptance names the browser-facing seams (`mount_pack` from fetched bytes, `user://` rehydration, the worklet as the sink), not that it runs in Chrome.

Carried forward unchanged from OrangePuma's note, since I verified neither: `vfs.rs`, `web_vfs.rs` and `web_vfs_res_and_user_paths.rs` are **untracked** at HEAD `632c268` and their doc comments attribute them to `pat-u3l8c.113/.114`. Whoever closes `.149` should not claim authorship of those files.

comments.text:
BlueHill 2026-10-30: wrote the re-scoped acceptance test. FINDING worth its own bead, deliberately NOT asserted here.

ScarletRidge's 13:44 residual item is REAL and I confirmed the exact divergence:

  gdaudio::web_output::audio_worklet_glue    registers "patina-audio-out"  (live wasm runtime)
  gdplatform::export::web_audio_worklet_glue registers 'patina-audio'      (export.rs:1232 AND :1262, both variants)

title: ProjectSettings: honor physics tick rate + 2D/3D gravity from project.godot at boot
description:
[audit-key: project-settings-runtime-honoring-and-script-api/projectsettings-physics-honor] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

GODOT: At startup Godot reads physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second, physics/2d/default_gravity(+_vector) and physics/3d/default_gravity(+_vector) from project.godot and configures Engine.physics_ticks_per_second and the PhysicsServer2D/3D space gravity accordingly (upstream core/config/project_settings.cpp + physics servers). A project that sets 30 ticks or 490 gravity simulates at those values.

PATINA: The values are parsed but never honored. gdresource/src/project.rs:200-213 extracts them into ProjectConfig and ProjectLoader::load (project.rs:273) reads project.godot, but nothing in the runtime consumes ProjectConfig/ProjectLoader (grep of patina-runner/gdscene/gdscript-interop for from_project_file/ProjectLoader:: yields only defs+tests). patina-runner/src/main.rs:367 builds MainLoop::new(tree) which hardcodes 60 tps (main_loop.rs:178) and physics worlds default to (0,980)/(0,-9.8). set_physics_ticks_per_second/set_gravity are only ever called from #[cfg(test)] code.

APPROACH: In patina-runner (main.rs + bootstrap.rs BootConfig/init phases), locate project.godot via ProjectLoader::load(project_dir) (add a project_dir arg or derive from scene path), extract ProjectConfig, then: (1) pass physics_ticks_per_second into MainLoop (new ctor param or set_physics_ticks_per_second before running); (2) compute gravity = default_gravity * default_gravity_vector and forward into the internal PhysicsServer/PhysicsServer3D set_gravity via a new MainLoop::configure_from_project(&ProjectConfig). WIRING: boot(project) -> ProjectLoader -> MainLoop tick rate + physics world gravity, with NO manual setter in the test.
acceptance_criteria: Booting the runner on a project dir whose project.godot declares physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second=30 and physics/2d/default_gravity=490 yields main_loop.physics_ticks_per_second()==30, the 2D physics world gravity y==490, and a RigidBody2D falls at the project gravity (position after N frames matches 490 not 980) - all via the boot path, not a manual set_* call. (test: project_settings_physics_honored)

title: XR: WebXRInterface browser session lifecycle + stereo submit to XRWebGLLayer
description:
[audit-key: xr-peripheral/xr-webxr-binding] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: modules/webxr/webxr_interface_js.cpp implements an XRInterface over the browser navigator.xr API, registered with XRServer under the name "WebXR" (see WebXRInterface.xml codeblock). Because WebXR is callback-based, the interface is signal-driven: is_session_supported(mode) returns void and later emits session_supported(mode,supported); initialize() (from XRInterface) asynchronously requests a session and emits session_started or session_failed(message); session_ended fires on exit. Properties configure the request: session_mode ('immersive-vr'/'immersive-ar'/'inline'), required_features/optional_features, requested_reference_space_types -> resolved reference_space_type, enabled_features, visibility_state. Input sources map to selectstart/select/selectend + squeezestart/squeeze/squeezeend (each with input_source_id); get_input_source_tracker(id)->XRControllerTracker and get_input_source_target_ray_mode(id) (TargetRayMode GAZE/TRACKED_POINTER/SCREEN). display refresh rate get/set/available + display_refresh_rate_changed, reference_space_reset, visibility_state_changed. Rendering: on session_started the app sets get_viewport().use_xr=true; the browser XRSession.requestAnimationFrame drives the frame loop and each eye's XRView pose+projection is submitted into the session XRWebGLLayer framebuffer.

Patina current state: none. Grep for webxr/immersive/requestSession/navigator.xr across crates and apps is empty; WebXRInterface unregistered.

Implementation approach: depends on the XRServer scaffolding (group xr-core-scene). Add a WebXRInterface implementation with wasm-bindgen bindings to navigator.xr in the gdplatform web layer (gdplatform/src/xr.rs + a web-cfg module), registered with XRServer as "WebXR"; back the async signals with browser Promise/event callbacks; translate XRInputSource select/squeeze events into the signals and feed XRController3D via XRControllerTracker poses read from the XRFrame. When Viewport.use_xr is set, drive patina-runner's frame loop from XRSession.requestAnimationFrame and render two eyes (per-XRView projection+view) into the XRWebGLLayer through gdrender3d. On native/non-web, is_session_supported must report unsupported (correct no-op) rather than panic.

Wiring requirement (end-to-end): patina-runner boot -> script gets XRServer.find_interface("WebXR") -> is_session_supported emits session_supported -> initialize() calls navigator.xr.requestSession -> session_started -> get_viewport().use_xr=true switches the runner render loop to the XR rAF submitting stereo frames; input sources fire select/squeeze and XRController3D signals every XR frame.
acceptance_criteria: With a stubbed navigator.xr, a script obtaining XRServer.find_interface("WebXR") and calling is_session_supported("immersive-vr") receives a session_supported(mode,supported) signal; setting session_mode/required_features and calling initialize() emits session_started and flips get_viewport().use_xr to true, and a mock input-source select event emits the `select` signal with its input_source_id whose get_input_source_tracker returns an XRControllerTracker. Test proves the interface is registered, added to XRServer, and its signal/property round-trip happens from a script (not module internals) (test: `webxr_interface_session_lifecycle_signals`). Live-browser stereo submit is verified by the build/browser verifier lane.

comments.author: GentleBadger
comments.text: PARTIAL by GentleBadger (2026-07-16, uncommitted; verify cmd in completion mail msg 54934). DONE (gdplatform/src/xr.rs, additive; the file was a 57-line XrServer pose mock and the bead's 'current state: none' claim was ACCURATE — grep for webxr/navigator.xr/immersive was genuinely empty): WebXrInterface implementing WebXR's CALLBACK semantics — is_session_supported() RETURNS NOTHING and answers later via a queued session_supported(mode,supported); initialize() reports session_started OR session_failed(message); plus session_ended, visibility_state_changed, reference_space_reset.
