title: Implement SkeletonModifier3D base + IKModifier3D inverse-kinematics node
description:
[audit-key: animation/animation/skeleton-modifiers] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

Add the SkeletonModifier3D base (Node3D child of a Skeleton3D: active flag, influence, _process_modification hook invoked during the skeleton's post-pose update, signals modification_processed) and IKModifier3D, an IK solver that adjusts a chain of bones so a tip bone reaches a target Transform3D (target node/bone, chain root/tip, iterations, influence blend). Register both in class_db.rs and invoke the Skeleton3D modifier stack each frame after AnimationPlayer/Tree writes poses, so IK runs on top of animation. Solve with CCD or FABRIK over the bone chain.
acceptance_criteria: SkeletonModifier3D and IKModifier3D are ClassDB-registered with correct inheritance; adding an IKModifier3D under a Skeleton3D with a target position causes the chain tip bone's global pose to move toward the target after the skeleton update, blended by influence, without detaching intermediate bones. (test: `ik_modifier3d_drives_bone_chain_tip_toward_target`)

comments.author: RedTower
comments.text: Triage (RedTower, no-run analysis): the IK math + skeleton API already exist — gdscene/src/ik_solver.rs has solve_fabrik(joints,target,iters,tol)->Vec<Vector3>, solve_two_bone_ik, and aim_rotation(from,to)->Quaternion; gdscene/src/skeleton3d.rs has the full bone API (get_bone_count/get_bone_global_pose/set_bone_pose/get_bone_parent/get_bone_children/set_bone_pose_rotation). Remaining work is additive: (1) register SkeletonModifier3D(<-Node3D) + IKModifier3D(<-SkeletonModifier3D) in class_db.rs; (2) an IKModifier3D model (target Vector3, chain root/tip bone idxs, influence f32); (3) run it in the skeleton-update phase: read chain joints' global-pose origins, solve_fabrik, then write each solved global position back as a LOCAL bone pose via parent_global.affine_inverse()*new_global (rotation from aim_rotation toward the next joint), processed root->tip; (4) test asserting tip global pose distance-to-target decreases, blended by influence. NOT taken by a no-cargo worker: the global->local frame write-back is geometry-correctness-sensitive and can't be verified without running (a wrong Transform3D method would break the shared gdscene crate). A cargo-capable worker should take it.

comments.author: GentleBadger
comments.text: DELIVERED by GentleBadger (2026-07-16, uncommitted; verify cmds in completion mail msg 55108). ACCEPTANCE MET: SkeletonModifier3D (abstract, parent Node3D) + IKModifier3D (parent SkeletonModifier3D) ClassDB-registered next to Skeleton3D; an IKModifier3D under a Skeleton3D drives the chain tip toward its target, blended by influence, without detaching intermediate bones. The named acceptance test ik_modifier3d_drives_bone_chain_tip_toward_target NOW EXISTS (gdscene/tests/, 5 tests). This bead was flagged [unverified] (triage sweep) and its claim CHECKS OUT — skeleton3d.rs genuinely had no modifier machinery. WHY AN INTEGRATION TEST rather than '-p gdscene --lib': '--test <name>' compiles the LIBRARY WITHOUT cfg(test), so it sidesteps gdscene's unit-test target (red from foreign WIP) entirely; it is also a target selector, so it hard-errors if missing and a PASS proves it really ran. DESIGN: process_modifiers(tree, skeleton_id) runs the stack (Godot: modifiers process AFTER AnimationPlayer/Tree writes poses, so IK layers on top instead of being overwritten), skipping inactive ones; CCD solver over the chain; bone_chain() returns EMPTY when the tip does not descend from the root, so a mis-wired modifier is a no-op rather than mangling unrelated bones. 'No detaching' holds BY CONSTRUCTION: the solver only writes bone ROTATIONS and a bone's global pose is composed from its parents, so parent->child offsets are preserved automatically (test pins each bone at exactly 1.0 from its parent after 16 iterations, which also proves no scale drift through repeated basis multiplication). THE SUBTLE BIT — poses live in the bone's PARENT frame, so a skeleton-space rotation delta becomes: pose' = (parent_basis*rest_basis)^-1 * delta * (parent_basis*rest_basis) * pose. Influence scales each CCD correction angle: 0 = untouched (early return), 1 = full solve, between = partway. *** GEOMETRY GOTCHA (a reviewer caught this by NUMERICALLY SIMULATING the solver — it would have FAILED the verify): bone0 is the FIXED PIVOT at (0,1,0) because a joint's own pose rotation swings its DESCENDANTS, never itself. So a 3-bone chain with 1-unit rests has reach 2, NOT 3. My original target (3,0,0) sits ~3.16 from the pivot = unreachable; the tip converges to ~1.16 away and assert!(after < 0.1) fails. Retargeted the acceptance test to (1,1,0). *** The influence test DELIBERATELY keeps the unreachable (3,0,0): against a reachable target both influence 0.5 and 1.0 converge to ~0 and the strict full<half ordering TIES and fails — keeping it out of reach is what makes the blend observable. Documented in-place. NOT COMPILED by me (worker build policy). REMAINING (follow-ons, not acceptance blockers): (1) process_modifiers is caller-driven — it still needs invoking from the frame loop after the pose update for IK to run in a live scene; (2) the modification_processed signal is registered but never emitted (nothing emits engine->script signals yet — see pat-nzgdu.150); (3) Godot's richer surface: target NODE/BONE (I model target_position only), bone constraints/limits, FABRIK as an alternative solver (the bead allows CCD or FABRIK; I chose CCD); (4) sibling beads pat-nzgdu.182/.183 build on this base. ALSO RE-FLAGGING a pre-existing red test I do not own: tests/misc_suite_d/node3d_runtime_slice_test.rs:125 asserts class_count()==12 after register_3d_classes, which already makes 125 registrations — red long before this bead (reported on pat-nzgdu.140); my 2 new classes do not newly break a passing test.

Register all in ClassDB. The existing stream.rs AudioStreamPlayback state-machine can back the base, but must gain frame-producing mix() semantics tied to a source AudioStream.
acceptance_criteria: AudioStreamPlayback + subclasses registered in ClassDB with correct parents (Resampled between); AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback.push_buffer + mix returns the pushed frames; AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic mixes N concurrent sub-playbacks; instantiate_playback() on a WAV/Ogg AudioStream returns a playback whose output matches the decoded buffer. (test: `audiostream_playback_instances_registered_and_produce_frames`)

comments.author: GentleBadger
comments.text: PARTIAL by GentleBadger (2026-07-16, uncommitted; verify cmds in completion mail msg 55210). DELIVERED 3 of the acceptance's 4 clauses. The bead was [unverified] (triage sweep) and its 'PARTIAL' status is ACCURATE — AudioStreamGenerator + PolyphonicPlayer did already exist in gdaudio/src/decode.rs, and stream.rs's AudioStreamPlayback state machine is real; none of the family was in ClassDB. CLAUSE 1 (ClassDB family) DONE: 8 classes with Godot's real shape — AudioStreamPlayback is an abstract RefCounted, NOT a Resource (Godot separates the stream RESOURCE from the playback INSTANCE it hands out); AudioStreamPlaybackResampled sits abstract between the base and the DECODER playbacks (OggVorbis, Generator) that need rate conversion, while the CONTAINER playbacks (Polyphonic/Interactive/Playlist/Synchronized) derive the base DIRECTLY because they mix children that are already resampled. The test asserts that distinction BOTH ways (containers must NOT derive Resampled). Needed a RefCounted bootstrap guard in register_audio_classes, which only had Object/Node. CLAUSE 2 (push_buffer + mix) DONE: push_buffer is ALL-OR-NOTHING (Godot rejects an oversized push rather than partially filling — a torn push tears the signal) plus frames_available/can_push_buffer/clear_buffer. THE IMPORTANT PART: the new mix() CONSUMES. The pre-existing mix_to_buffer only PEEKS at the whole queue and leaves it in place, so a generator wired to it would replay stale audio forever instead of refilling; mix(n) drains, under-runs to silence rather than erroring. CLAUSE 3 (polyphonic) DONE: PolyphonicPlayer previously only COUNTED voices — try_play() incremented an integer and no audio was ever summed. It now holds real sub-playbacks and mix(n) sums them frame-for-frame; finished voices contribute silence for the rest of the block then are RETIRED, freeing their slot, so a finished one-shot cannot pin the pool at its limit forever. Output is deliberately NOT clamped — mixing is additive, headroom is the bus's job (Godot's mix stage). BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: new() arities unchanged; push_frame/mix_to_buffer/try_play untouched; existing generator_and_poly test still passes; nothing outside decode.rs constructs either struct with a literal, so the new private field is safe. 7 new tests. NOT COMPILED by me (worker build policy) — eye-verified + reviewer pass. KEEP OPEN — REMAINING: (1) CLAUSE 4 instantiate_playback() is BLOCKED: there is NO AudioStream resource type in the tree at all (grep empty) — only AudioBuffer + decoders. It needs the resource layer first (AudioStream + AudioStreamWAV/AudioStreamOggVorbis with instantiate_playback() returning a playback bound to the decoded buffer). That is a design step, not a slice. (2) AudioStreamPlaybackResampled does no resampling yet — registered only; server.rs's mixer resamples (mix_resamples_low_rate_stream_to_output_rate), the playback-level base does not. (3) stream.rs's AudioStreamPlayback state machine (play/pause/seek/advance) is still NOT tied to frame production — needs (1) first. (4) Interactive/Playlist/Synchronized are CLASS SURFACE ONLY — no clip switching, playlist ordering or sync logic. (5) The acceptance test audiostream_playback_instances_registered_and_produce_frames DOES NOT EXIST — do not trust a stale-recovery close (0-match filters exit 0).

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED (mail 55494). All 4 acceptance clauses met.

BLOCKER ON THE STATED APPROACH (the description is not implementable):
The bead says 'backed by / over the existing UndoRedoManager'. UndoRedoManager lives in
gdeditor/src/undo_redo.rs, and gdeditor/Cargo.toml:27 depends on gdscript-interop. So gdeditor
depends on gdscript-interop; binding the interpreter to gdeditor's UndoRedoManager would invert
that into a dependency CYCLE, which the build system hard-errors on. It cannot be done as written.

ROUTE TAKEN: interpreter-local handle mirroring the existing CameraFeed pattern (pat-nzgdu.179) —
the established precedent for Object-style script handles that are not nodes. Handle tag 0xED
(non-colliding with 0xCF ConfigFile / 0xFA FileAccess / 0xDA DirAccess / 0xCA CameraFeed).
Property writes apply through SceneAccess::set_node_property (bindings.rs:207), so commit/undo/redo
genuinely mutate the scene rather than only recording history.

CONSEQUENCE worth its own bead: there are now TWO undo/redo impls — gdeditor's UndoRedoManager
(editor-internal) and this script-visible one. Unifying needs a shared undo/redo crate BELOW both.
I did not expand scope to do it.

Files:
- engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs (UndoRedo registration in register_io_classes)
- engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs (handle + new() dispatch + instance dispatch)
- engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/tests/undoredo_class_commit_undo_redo_property.rs (NEW, 5 tests)

Verify: -p gdscript-interop --test undoredo_class_commit_undo_redo_property
        -p gdobject --lib class_db

MERGE_ENDS semantics (matches Godot undo_redo.cpp): the previous action's do-ops are REPLACED by
the new ones and the ORIGINAL undo-ops are KEPT — so undoing a merged pair returns to the state
before the FIRST action. Test asserts Move(0->10)+Move(10->20) coalesces to one entry and undo
lands on 0, not 10. The test observes the SCENE via a recording SceneAccess mock, not the history,
so it fails if ops are recorded but never applied.

DELIBERATELY NOT REGISTERED: add_do_method / add_undo_method / add_do_reference. They must invoke a
Callable, which needs re-entry into the interpreter; the op recorder is a free fn with no
&mut Interpreter. Registering them would make class_has_method() promise a method that errors on
call. Registered surface == implemented surface: 15 and 15, verified mechanically.

REMAINING (do not let a close imply these are done):
- method-ops / reference-ops (needs an interpreter-re-entrant op recorder)
- version_changed signal registered but never emitted (no engine->script signal path)
- commit_action(execute=false) honored but untested
- UndoRedo.MERGE_ENDS as a direct static-member access does NOT resolve; only the
  ClassDB.class_get_integer_constant reflection path works (which the test uses)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — COMPILE FIX (E0521) applied to my UndoRedo code; resend-worthy, please re-verify.

A verifier run on a DIFFERENT bead (pat-u3l8c.12) exposed a real compile error in MY .155 code:
  error: could not compile gdscript-interop (lib) due to 1 previous error -- E0521
The verifier builds the WORKING TREE (it compiled an untracked test file), so my uncommitted
interpreter.rs changes were in that build and broke every downstream crate's test compile.

THE BUG: my helper took  fn apply(ops: &[PropOp], access: &mut Option<&mut dyn SceneAccess>).
The field is  scene_access: Option<Box<dyn SceneAccess>>  (interpreter.rs:388). A Box<dyn Trait>
with NO enclosing reference carries an implicit '+ 'static'. Wrapping the Option in a SECOND &mut
makes its pointee INVARIANT, forcing the trait object's lifetime to unify with BOTH the reborrow of
self AND 'static -> 'self escapes' = E0521.

THE FIX: take the Option BY VALUE -> fn apply(ops: &[PropOp], access: Option<&mut dyn SceneAccess>).
The three call sites (commit_action/undo/redo) are mutually exclusive match arms, so access moves at
most once per path. The single-layer shape is proven sound by accumulate_vec2_property
(interpreter.rs:6080-6168), which already feeds the same field into &mut dyn SceneAccess and compiles
today.

RULE WORTH KEEPING: never nest &mut around an Option/struct holding a &mut dyn Trait. One layer is
fine and is the established pattern here; two layers collide with the Box's implicit 'static.

Verify (unchanged): -p gdscript-interop --test undoredo_class_commit_undo_redo_property
                    -p gdobject --lib class_db

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — CORRECTION to my previous comment; resent (mail 55918).

MY EARLIER COMMENT'S MECHANISM WAS WRONG. It blamed a nested &mut Option<&mut dyn SceneAccess> and
'fixed' it by taking the Option by value. The verifier proved that wrong — the SAME E0521 came back
and the bead pat-u3l8c.12 got PARKED as collateral. Do not follow that earlier advice.

THE ACTUAL CAUSE: an Option-wrapped trait object with an ELIDED lifetime.
  field:  scene_access: Option<Box<dyn SceneAccess>>   // Box<dyn _> with no enclosing reference
                                                       // => implicit '+ 'static'
  so:     self.scene_access.as_deref_mut()  ->  Option<&'r mut (dyn SceneAccess + 'static)>
                                                 ('r = a reborrow of self)
  param:  Option<&mut dyn SceneAccess>      ==  Option<&'x mut (dyn SceneAccess + 'x)>
Coercions do NOT reach inside a generic constructor like Option, so the types must match by
SUBTYPING. &mut is INVARIANT in its pointee => (dyn SceneAccess + 'static) must EQUAL
(dyn SceneAccess + 'x) => 'x = 'static => 'r = 'static => self escapes => E0521.

THE FIX: name the bound, which the boxed accessor genuinely has:
  access: Option<&mut (dyn SceneAccess + 'static)>
Pointees are then equal, leaving only the covariant 'r: 'x.

WHY THIS ONE IS TRUSTWORTHY (precedent, not reasoning):
  gdplatform/src/network.rs:289 — committed, clean, compiling:
    pub fn peer_mut(&mut self) -> Option<&mut (dyn NetworkPeer + 'static)> { self.peer.as_deref_mut() }
  Same field shape (Option<Box<dyn _>>), same as_deref_mut, 'static spelled out.
  And there are ZERO elided 'Option<&mut dyn Trait>' params anywhere in the workspace — exactly what
  you'd expect if the shape cannot compile.
A bare '&mut dyn SceneAccess' param IS fine (accumulate_vec2_property, interpreter.rs:38/53) because
its callers pass '&mut **access' — a fresh reborrow, which IS a coercion site. The Option wrapper is
what removes that opportunity.

TECHNIQUE WORTH KEEPING: grep for the signature shape BEFORE trusting a derivation. Two separate
code-reviewer passes got this wrong (one blessed the original; one blessed the bad fix). When you
cannot compile, only an in-repo compiling precedent counts.

Verify (unchanged): -p gdscript-interop --test undoredo_class_commit_undo_redo_property
                    -p gdobject --lib class_db

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED PARTIAL (mail 56183): 2 of 3 acceptance clauses. Do NOT let a close imply clause 3.

CLAUSE 1 DONE: ClassDB::class_exists('RichTextEffect'). Registered RichTextEffect (parent Resource)
+ CharFXTransform (parent RefCounted) in register_2d_classes. RefCounted was NOT registered anywhere
in that fn — an unregistered base silently severs the chain from Object (the pat-nzgdu.98 trap), so
I bootstrap it and the test asserts both classes reach Object, not just their immediate parent.

CLAUSE 2 DONE: [wave]...[/wave] offsets glyph positions per frame. New gdscene::char_fx module:
CharFXTransform + all six built-ins (wave/tornado/shake/fade/rainbow/pulse) as PURE functions of
(relative_index, elapsed_time). parse_bbcode gained an effect stack; effected runs draw glyph-by-glyph
with per-glyph offset/colour; untagged text keeps the single-draw fast path.

CLAUSE 3 BLOCKED — needs its own bead. A scripted RichTextEffect cannot be invoked today for FOUR
independent reasons:
  1. the render pass holds &SceneTree; calling a script needs &mut
  2. RichTextLabel has no custom_effects property, and nothing maps a bbcode tag -> an effect's bbcode
  3. CharFXTransform has no Variant encoding, so it cannot cross
     ScriptInstance::call_method(&[Variant]) and come back mutated
  4. ResourceRef { path, class_name, properties } has NO script slot; the only script-attachment path
     (instantiate_script) models a scripted 'Resource' as a phantom Node under the scene root
Any ONE blocks it. I did NOT fake a seam: [ghost] degrades to plain text (asserted) rather than
inventing a non-Godot node-based effect model that would have to be torn out later.

TEST-NAMING HONESTY: the named test richtext_effect_custom_fx_test exists and passes but covers the
REGISTRATION + BUILT-IN halves. unknown_and_custom_effect_tags_are_stripped_not_rendered asserts
today's real behaviour (ghost -> one plain run). When clause 3 lands that test must be REPLACED, not
extended — true acceptance is 3 per-glyph draws with the script invoked.

REVIEWER CAUGHT A REAL BUG PRE-SHIP: a nested tag splits an effected run into several spans
([wave]a[color=red]b[/color]c[/wave] = 3), and I computed each sub-run's range from its OWN bounds ->
relative_index restarted at 0 per piece -> glyphs bobbed in phase instead of travelling. Fixed by
backfilling each effect application's true range across all its runs; added the missing regression
test (effect_phase_continues_across_a_nested_tag). Verified numerically: split and unsplit now give
identical offsets [0, 2.397, 4.207, 4.987].

DELIBERATE DEVIATION (documented in-code): Godot phases wave/tornado by the glyph's PIXEL X
(sin(elapsed*freq + glyph_x/50)), coupling the effect to font metrics + wrapping. I phase by
relative_index — same visual, reproducible from the char index, which is what makes it assertable.
Tag names/params/defaults match Godot. [shake] hashes (time step, index) instead of an RNG so it is
stable within a step and testable.

Verify: -p gdscene --test richtext_effect_custom_fx_test
        -p gdscene --lib char_fx
        -p gdscene --lib control_render
        -p gdobject --lib class_db

REMAINING: clause 3 (above); nothing advances fx_elapsed_time — render_control_tree has NO caller in
the engine loop today (only tests + the editor), so wiring a frame driver is follow-up.

title: Rendering2D: wire SceneTree -> canvas pipeline with global transforms and z/y-sort draw order
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/canvas-pipeline-core] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot draws every CanvasItem-derived node each frame through RenderingServer canvas commands, honoring the node's GLOBAL Transform2D (position*rotation*scale composed up the parent chain), z_index+z_as_relative global ordering, y_sort_enabled cross-parent ordering, and modulate/self_modulate propagation (scene/main/canvas_item.cpp). Patina has none of this in any runtime: the canvas pipeline (gdserver2d::canvas + gdrender2d::renderer::SoftwareRenderer) has zero scene-node producers (grep 'DrawCommand::' hits only tests), patina-runner is headless (main.rs:273-397, no gdrender2d dep), and the only wired 2D surface — the editor viewport via examples/editor.rs:372 -> scene_renderer.rs:213-277 — draws icons at LOCAL position (extract_position, scene_renderer.rs:220) with no rotation/scale/parent composition and no z-order draw sort, despite gdscene::node2d::get_global_transform (node2d.rs:83) already existing. Implement a scene->canvas render bridge (new module, e.g. gdrender2d::scene_bridge with a gdscene dep, or promote the editor's renderer): walk tree in order, compute each node's global Transform2D via node2d::get_global_transform, build CanvasItems ordered by accumulated z_index (respect z_as_relative) then y_sort within a subtree then tree order, propagate modulate*self_modulate and visible/visible_in_tree, feed gdserver2d::Viewport + SoftwareRenderer::render_frame to a FrameData, and replace the schematic path in examples/editor.rs so the live editor viewport shows the real transformed/ordered scene. Expose the same entry as the public 2D render for the web runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn whose root Node2D is rotated 45deg and translated, containing a Sprite2D child plus two overlapping ColorRects with z_index 0 and 1, renders (a) the sprite pixels at the globally-rotated+translated location (not the local position) and (b) the z_index=1 rect fully on top of the z_index=0 rect. title: Register PrimitiveMesh subclasses in ClassDB (SphereMesh et al.) and implement TextMesh glyph triangulation
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/rendering-3d/primitive-mesh-family] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

[audit-key: sweep-13/rendering-3d/primitive-mesh-family] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** SphereMesh and TextMesh both inherit PrimitiveMesh (extension_api). PrimitiveMesh subclasses are ClassDB-registered Resources with configurable properties (SphereMesh: radius/height/radial_segments/rings; TextMesh: text/font/font_size/depth/pixel_size) that generate ArrayMesh surfaces. TextMesh triangulates the active font's glyph outlines into extruded 3D geometry.

**Patina today:** SphereMesh has a real impl (crates/gdserver3d/src/primitive_mesh.rs:136) that IS render-wired via string dispatch (crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:571) and parsed from .tscn sub_resources (packed_scene.rs:1126) — but it is NOT ClassDB-registered, so scripts/introspection cannot reach it. TextMesh is entirely absent (grep textmesh -> empty).

**Implement:** (1) Register SphereMesh/BoxMesh/CapsuleMesh/CylinderMesh/PlaneMesh + PrimitiveMesh base in class_db.rs, mapping properties to the existing primitive_mesh structs so the ClassDB factory and the render_server_3d generate() path share one type. (2) Add a TextMesh primitive that pulls glyph outlines from the font system (gdrender2d/src/font.rs) and triangulates/extrudes them, registered like the others and wired into render_server_3d generation.

**Wiring requirement:** A .tscn with `[sub_resource type="TextMesh"]` on a MeshInstance3D renders 3D text in the runner; ClassDB.instantiate('SphereMesh') yields an introspectable resource whose radius drives the generated mesh.

**Prove it:** App-level test loads a scene with a SphereMesh and a TextMesh MeshInstance3D, ticks a frame, asserts ClassDB.class_exists for both and that non-empty triangulated geometry is produced for the text.
acceptance_criteria: ClassDB.class_exists('SphereMesh') and class_exists('TextMesh') return true; a MeshInstance3D with a ClassDB-constructed SphereMesh renders sphere geometry and a TextMesh renders non-empty extruded glyph geometry in the runner (test: `primitive_mesh_classdb_registration_test`)

title: Add MissingNode/MissingResource to preserve unknown classes losslessly on scene round-trip
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/resources-io/missing-placeholders] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

[audit-key: sweep-7/resources-io/missing-placeholders] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** When a .tscn/.tres references a class/script the engine doesn't recognize, Godot instantiates a MissingNode/MissingResource that stores the original_class name + all raw properties, so re-saving the file preserves the data byte-for-byte instead of dropping it. doc/classes/MissingNode.xml, MissingResource.xml.

**Patina today:** neither class exists (grep matches are unrelated test names in compare3d.rs/export.rs/property_undo.rs). An unknown class today has no preservation path, risking silent data loss on load→save — exactly the failure the resources-io stones forbid ("NO silent skips of unparseable values").

**Implement:** Add MissingNode (Node) and MissingResource (Resource) holding original_class + a property bag; make the .tscn/.tres loader (gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs, gdresource/src/loader.rs) emit them for unrecognized types and the saver re-emit the stored class + properties verbatim.

**Wiring requirement:** Load a .tscn referencing an unknown class into a MissingNode and save it back with the original type string + properties intact.

**Prove it:** Round-trip a .tscn containing an unregistered node type; assert the re-saved text preserves the original class name and every property (no drops).
acceptance_criteria: Loading a scene/resource that references an unknown class produces a MissingNode/MissingResource retaining original_class + all properties, and re-saving reproduces the original type and properties losslessly (test: `unknown_class_preserved_via_missing_node_roundtrip`).

title: Resources/Boot: boot patina-runner from project.godot (main scene, autoloads, input map, ProjectSettings, res:// root)
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/project-boot] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot boots a project by parsing project.godot: it resolves application/run/main_scene, registers [autoload] scene/script singletons, installs the [input] InputMap actions, applies config/features (incl. .web overrides), and populates the ProjectSettings singleton the runtime honors (physics/rendering/audio). Patina's runner (patina-runner/src/main.rs) instead takes a raw .tscn path and ignores project.godot entirely; the parsers that exist (gdresource/src/project.rs ProjectLoader, gdcore/src/project_settings.rs ProjectSettings::load_godot_project) are library-only with no runtime caller, and gdcore::file_access::set_path_roots is never invoked so res:///user:// cannot resolve. Implement a boot path that: (1) if given a project dir/project.godot, calls ProjectLoader::load + ProjectSettings::load_godot_project, (2) calls gdcore::set_path_roots(project_root, user_root) so FileAccess res:// works, (3) resolves main_scene and loads it via the scene loader, (4) instantiates autoloads before the main scene, (5) installs the input map into gdplatform input. Wire this into patina-runner/src/main.rs and patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs init_resources()/init_main_scene().
acceptance_criteria: Running the runner against a fixtures project dir containing project.godot (with run/main_scene, an [autoload], and an [input] action) boots the declared main scene, the autoload node exists in the tree, res:// FileAccess resolves under the project root, and ProjectSettings.get_setting reflects a project.godot value. (test: `runner_boots_project_godot`)

title: Editor/Resources: lossless .tscn save — regenerate ext_resource/sub_resource tables, uid+load_steps header, and full Variant serialization
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/tscn-save] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot's text saver round-trips a scene exactly: it collects external resource references (scripts, textures, sub-scenes) into an [ext_resource] table with ids, inline sub-resources into [sub_resource] sections, writes a header with load_steps and uid=, and serializes every Variant type in canonical .tscn syntax. Patina's TscnSaver (gdscene/scene_saver.rs:134) drops ext/sub-resource sections entirely and Debug-formats unsupported Variants, so any real scene (one with a script, texture, material, shape, or instanced child) is corrupted on save. Fix: reconstruct the ext_resource/sub_resource tables from node references and __resref__ companions during save, emit the load_steps/uid header, write script/instance as unquoted ExtResource("id"), and extend format_variant_value to cover Vector2i/Vector3i/Vector4(i)/Transform3D/Basis/Quaternion/Plane/AABB/Projection/Packed* arrays.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a complex .tscn (root with a script ext_resource, a child instancing a sub-scene, a node with an inline sub_resource and a Transform3D property), saving it via TscnSaver, and re-parsing yields the same ext_resources, sub_resources, script path, instance ref, and Transform3D value as the original (round-trip diff is empty for those). (test: `tscn_save_roundtrip_ext_and_sub_resources`)

title: Add SubtweenTweener (Tween.tween_subtween) nested-tween stepping
description:
[audit-key: animation/animation/subtween-tweener] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

[audit-key: sweep-13/animation/subtween-tweener] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** Tween.tween_subtween(subtween) appends a SubtweenTweener (<-Tweener) that runs an entire nested Tween as one step of the parent sequence, blocking the parent's chain until the sub-tween finishes (respecting parallel/chain semantics).

**Patina today:** Tween is wired into the frame loop (crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:425 -> process_tweens at scene_tree.rs:1307) but the builder only supports property tweens (crates/gdscene/src/tween.rs:442 tween_property); there is no tween_subtween and no Tweener hierarchy, so a nested tween cannot be sequenced.

**Implement:** Extend the TweenStep model in tween.rs with a Subtween step holding a nested Tween, and have Tween::advance drive the nested tween to completion before advancing the parent chain; expose tween_subtween on the builder and wire it through the existing process_tweens advance.

**Wiring requirement:** From a script in a runner scene, `create_tween().tween_subtween(inner)` must run `inner` to completion at the correct point in the parent sequence, with the parent chain waiting on it.

**Prove it:** App-level test builds a parent tween that tween_subtweens an inner property tween, advances process_tweens across the combined duration, and asserts the inner property animates and the parent step after it only starts once the sub-tween finished.
acceptance_criteria: A Tween using tween_subtween runs the nested Tween to completion before its next chained step begins, and the nested property animates to its end value when process_tweens is advanced across the total duration (test: `subtween_tweener_nested_test`)

title: Register OggPacketSequence / OggPacketSequencePlayback so imported OggVorbis resources load losslessly
description:
[audit-key: audio/audio/ogg-packet-sequence] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

OggPacketSequence (inherits Resource) and OggPacketSequencePlayback (inherits RefCounted) are absent (grep 'OggPacketSequence' across engine-rs/crates → 0 hits). Patina decodes .ogg straight to PCM via lewton (engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/audio_import.rs:133 decode_ogg), so it has no representation for Godot's imported form, whose AudioStreamOggVorbis references an embedded OggPacketSequence holding the demuxed Ogg pages (packet_data arrays, sampling_rate, granule positions, loop offsets). Loading such a .oggvorbisstr/.tres currently drops the packet sequence. Register both classes in ClassDB (OggPacketSequence : Resource, OggPacketSequencePlayback : RefCounted), parse OggPacketSequence sub-resources during resource loading, and feed the reconstructed Ogg stream into the existing gdaudio decode path so imported OggVorbis streams play.
acceptance_criteria: A .tres/.oggvorbisstr containing an OggPacketSequence sub-resource loads without dropping data: ClassDB reports is_parent_class("OggPacketSequence","Resource")==true and is_parent_class("OggPacketSequencePlayback","RefCounted")==true, the loaded OggPacketSequence exposes its packet_data and sampling_rate, and an AudioStreamOggVorbis referencing it decodes to non-empty PCM via the existing gdaudio path. (test: `ogg_packet_sequence_resource_load`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — delivered. Registration + a real OggPacketSequence type with demux/decode, plus the repo's first Ogg Vorbis test fixture.

*** THE BEAD'S PREMISE CITES DEAD CODE ***
The bead says "Patina decodes .ogg straight to PCM via lewton (engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/audio_import.rs:133 decode_ogg)". THAT FUNCTION HAS NEVER BEEN COMPILED. audio_import.rs is committed (df37e87) but is NOT declared in gdresource/src/lib.rs, and nothing anywhere references it. It is doubly unwirable: it opens with `use gdaudio::import::AudioFormat` while gdaudio IS NOT A DEPENDENCY of gdresource at all. So `mod audio_import;` alone would not fix it — that needs a new crate dependency edge. Its ~10 #[cfg(test)] tests have never run.
=> The LIVE ogg path is gdaudio::decode::decode_ogg. That is why I put the new type in gdaudio, next to it.
=> RECOMMEND a separate bead: "wire or delete gdresource/src/audio_import.rs" (it also invents properties Godot doesn't have — sample_rate/channels/length_seconds/frame_count/has_samples — where Godot's AudioStreamWAV uses mix_rate/stereo and AudioStreamOggVorbis has neither).

*** THE BEAD ASKS FOR 2 CLASSES; THE GAP WAS 4 ***
Patina had registered EVERY AudioStream*Playback* class — the runtime instances — but NOT ONE of the streams they play. AudioStream and AudioStreamOggVorbis were both absent, so a stream could be played but never named. The bead's own acceptance names AudioStreamOggVorbis, so both are registered here. register_audio_classes() also guarded Object/Node/RefCounted but NEVER Resource, and every class here descends from it — the acceptance's is_parent_class("OggPacketSequence","Resource") would have failed standalone without that guard.

Registered, all diffed EXACT against extension_api.json (methods+arities, properties, parent, abstractness):
  AudioStream               6 methods, 0 props  <- Resource     (GDREGISTER_CLASS = concrete, not abstract)
  OggPacketSequence         7 methods, 3 props  <- Resource
  OggPacketSequencePlayback 0 methods, 0 props  <- RefCounted   (binds nothing; opaque handle)
  AudioStreamOggVorbis     16 methods, 7 props  <- AudioStream

*** ORACLE FINDINGS ***
- THE DUMP LIES ABOUT packet_data'S TYPE. It says `typedarray::PackedByteArray` (a flat array of byte arrays). ADD_PROPERTY at modules/ogg/ogg_packet_sequence.cpp:131 says Variant::ARRAY, and the setter takes TypedArray<Array> over `Vector<Vector<PackedByteArray>>` — an array of PAGES, each holding packets. The dump's shape would collapse the page grouping the granule positions index against. Doc XML agrees with the C++ (`Array[]`). Registered as Variant::Array.
- NAME QUIRK: the property is `granule_positions` but its accessors are `{set,get}_packet_granule_positions`, and the values are one per PAGE, not per packet (`page_granule_positions` in the header). Pinned in a test.
- bar_beats defaults to 4, NOT 0 (doc XML). A zero-default would silently mean a 0-beat bar.
- `loop` is a GDScript keyword so Godot binds has_loop/set_loop, not get_loop.
- instantiate_playback() EXISTS on the C++ OggPacketSequence but is deliberately NOT in _bind_methods — so it must NOT be registered. Pinned with a negative assertion (safe: verified `instantiate_playback` is not an Object method and OggPacketSequence's chain is Resource->Object, which excludes AudioStream).

*** IMPLEMENTATION (gdaudio/src/ogg_packet_sequence.rs, the LIVE crate) ***
Mirrors AudioStreamOggVorbis::load_from_buffer: group packets by the page they arrived in, tag each page with that page's granule, drop zero-byte packets, error when no pages are found.
- demux(&[u8]) -> OggPacketSequence   (via the `ogg` crate — ALREADY in Cargo.lock as a lewton dep, so no new version resolves; I added the lock's dependency edge by hand so a --locked build stays consistent)
- decode(&self) -> AudioBuffer        (lewton's packet-level API, not its container reader)

*** THE BUG I NEARLY SHIPPED — caught by reading lewton's source ***
I was about to assert "demux+decode == decode_ogg byte-for-byte". IT IS NOT. lewton's OggStreamReader (inside_ogg.rs:189-195) truncates the last packet against a running absgp and primes/discards the first audio packet; a raw packet decode does neither. More importantly this was a REAL CORRECTNESS BUG, not just a bad test: Vorbis decodes in fixed 2048 blocks, so the fixture's 17 audio packets yield 16x1024 = 16384 frames while the stream is only 15488 long — 896 frames (~20ms) of padding that is not audio. ffmpeg's raw decode gives exactly 16384, confirming the overshoot from a second direction; ffprobe reports duration_ts=15488 as the true length. decode() now trims to the final granule position, which is the Ogg spec's definition of stream length and where Godot's playback stops. The test asserts frame_count()==15488 and deliberately does NOT assert cross-path sample equality (documented why).

*** FIXTURE: THE REPO'S FIRST .ogg ***
There was not a single .ogg file in the tree, so gdaudio::decode::decode_ogg had ONLY ever been exercised by its error path — the happy path was untested. Added tests/fixtures/test_tone.ogg (5.1KB, 0.35s 440Hz stereo, ffmpeg native vorbis encoder; libvorbis isn't available and the native one is stereo-only). Generated ONCE and committed — no test-time ffmpeg dependency, no flake. Structure verified independently by parsing the Ogg pages in Python, so the test constants are facts about the file rather than values copied from a first run: 3 pages, granules [0,0,15488], 20 packets (1 ident + 1 comment + 1 setup + 17 audio), ident says channels=2 rate=44100.

*** BLAST RADIUS — swept with NO exclusions (the .227 lesson) ***
Last bead I filtered class_db.rs out of its own blast-radius grep and missed an in-file test. This time: every hit for OggPacketSequence/AudioStreamOggVorbis/"AudioStream" across the workspace, unfiltered. All hits are mine (4731-4830), all before the #[cfg(test)] mod at 6814. Checked class_count() assertions specifically since I add 4 classes — the exact ones (classdb_parity_test 17, node3d_runtime_slice 12) run register_core_classes/register_3d_classes, which never call register_audio_classes; nothing reachable from register_audio_classes asserts a count. The in-file tests that DO call register_audio_classes (line 6984, 6958) are positive-existence/parent checks only, which adding classes cannot break — but I am listing `--lib class_db` as a test command anyway, because that is exactly the command I failed to run last time.

*** NOT DONE — honest gap ***
The bead's "parse OggPacketSequence sub-resources during resource loading" is NOT wired end-to-end. The .tres loader ALREADY parses [sub_resource] sections and PackedByteArray()/PackedInt64Array() values generically, so such a .tres already loads into a Resource carrying the right Variants. The missing bridge (Resource's Variants -> typed OggPacketSequence) must live in gdresource, which does not depend on gdaudio — the same missing dep edge that orphans audio_import.rs, and the only consumer of that bridge would be the orphan. Adding a cross-crate dep for dead code is not a P3 call I should make unilaterally; it belongs with the audio_import bead above.

I cannot compile (worker cargo policy), so every lewton/ogg signature was verified against the vendored crate sources before use, and all 3 new/changed files are rustfmt-clean (my class_db.rs block too; the file has 111 PRE-EXISTING fmt diffs that are not mine and I did not touch).

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — SECOND submission. First one failed verification: `failed (100, panic)` on `gdaudio --test ogg_packet_sequence_demux_decode`. Root cause found and fixed WITHOUT guessing — two independent bugs, both in the fixture/decode path (the ClassDB registration and the demux structural tests were and are correct).

The verifier reported only the terse "panic" with no assertion text, and worker cargo policy means I can't run the test myself. So I diagnosed from measured facts, not hypotheses:

*** BUG 1: THE FIXTURE WAS ENCODED WITH FFMPEG'S EXPERIMENTAL NATIVE VORBIS ENCODER, WHICH LEWTON CANNOT DECODE ***
My first test_tone.ogg came from `ffmpeg -c:a vorbis -strict -2` (libvorbis is NOT installed here; the native encoder is all ffmpeg has). It emits NON-STANDARD blocksizes: bs0 == bs1 == 2048 (no short blocks). Every real libVorbis file uses 256/2048 block switching. lewton is a strict pure-Rust decoder and errors on the 2048/2048 stream -> decode().expect(...) panics.

Diagnosed by parsing the ident-header blocksize byte of my fixture vs the only real .ogg files on the box (livekit pip resources): mine = 2048/2048, all real ones = 256/2048. Confirmed by the vorbis-comment vendor string: mine said "Lavf..." (ffmpeg), real ones (and the new fixture) say "Xiph.Org libVorbis...".

FIX: I compiled a ~90-line C encoder from godot's OWN vendored libvorbis+libogg (upstream/godot/thirdparty; cc is not blocked by the no-cargo hook), generated a 0.35s 440Hz sine (OUR content -> clean license; I did NOT commit the third-party livekit audio), and encoded it with reference Xiph libVorbis at VBR q=0.4. New fixture: vendor "Xiph.Org libVorbis I 20200704", blocksizes 256/2048, 5517 bytes, 3 pages, granule 15434 = exactly 0.35s. Structure re-verified by parsing the pages (no cross-page packets, so the ogg crate groups exactly [1,2,17]).

*** BUG 2: assert_eq!(frame_count(), granule) WAS WRONG EVEN WITH A GOOD FILE ***
A Vorbis decode does NOT land on the granule. The stream opens with a short block whose leading half is decoder ramp-up, so ffmpeg decodes the NEW fixture to 15306 frames -- 128 BELOW the granule 15434 -- and a raw packet decode that keeps the priming packet lands elsewhere again. You cannot predict the exact decoded count without running the decoder. So I no longer assert an exact count: the decode tests now assert a BAND (granule - 2048 <= frames <= granule) plus non-empty / correct rate+channels / finite / audible. That proves "full-length stream" without encoding a decoder-internal number. (The decode() granule cap is unchanged and still correct -- it is an upper bound only, `if target < len`, never an extend, which is right precisely because raw decode often lands below the granule.)

Ground truth used to set the bands (not predictions): `ffprobe -show_entries stream=duration_ts` = 15434 (the granule); `ffmpeg -i test_tone.ogg out.wav` -> 15306 decoded frames.

*** WHAT DID NOT CHANGE ***
- All 4 ClassDB registrations still diff EXACT vs extension_api.json. The registration test file is untouched.
- The demux structural assertions (page_count 3, granules [0,0,15434], page_data [1,2,17], packet_count 20) are provably correct: I re-verified the ogg crate's read_packet reliably sets last_in_page/absgp_page (reading/reading.rs), and the new fixture has no cross-page continuations, so the crate's grouping equals my byte-parse.
- decode()/demux() LOGIC is unchanged; I only edited doc comments (the old ones cited the old fixture's 15488/16384/896-overshoot numbers, now false) and swapped the fixture + the test assertions.

Files (same set as before; fixture bytes replaced):
- engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs
- engine-rs/crates/gdobject/tests/ogg_packet_sequence_resource_load.rs
- engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/ogg_packet_sequence.rs
- engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/lib.rs
- engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/Cargo.toml
- engine-rs/Cargo.lock
- engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/tests/ogg_packet_sequence_demux_decode.rs
- engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/tests/fixtures/test_tone.ogg  (now Xiph libVorbis)

title: Implement EncodedObjectAsID and emit it from the Variant byte decoder
description:
[audit-key: core-variant/core-variant/encoded-object-as-id] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

Add EncodedObjectAsID (RefCounted) with an object_id property, and make bytes_to_var / the RPC-wire decoder produce it when an OBJECT is encoded as an ID and full-object decoding is disabled. Register in ClassDB.
acceptance_criteria: var_to_bytes of an object with object-as-id encoding, decoded via bytes_to_var, yields an EncodedObjectAsID whose object_id matches; ClassDB.class_exists('EncodedObjectAsID') is true. (test: `encoded_object_as_id_roundtrip`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED (mail 59116). READ THIS BEFORE TOUCHING bytes_to_var: my first cut opened a REAL SECURITY HOLE.

*** THE TRAP THIS BEAD SETS ***
The bead says "make bytes_to_var produce EncodedObjectAsID". The obvious implementation — decode
OBJECT|AS_ID to Variant::ObjectId and return it — is EXPLOITABLE IN THIS PORT.
Variant::ObjectId here is NOT an inert id: it is the SAME LIVE NODE REFERENCE get_node() returns, and
get_children() on one walks the scene tree (interpreter.rs, the Variant::ObjectId method arm). So
  bytes_to_var(untrusted_bytes).get_children()
would reach into the RUNNING SCENE — with ids that START AT 1 (gdcore/src/id.rs:20), i.e. trivially
guessable. In Godot you get an EncodedObjectAsID whose ONLY surface is object_id; turning it into a
usable object needs an EXPLICIT instance_from_id(). THAT EXTRA STEP IS EXACTLY WHAT p_allow_objects=false
BUYS. A reviewer caught this; I would have shipped it.

FIX: decoded ids are re-wrapped in a tagged INERT handle (0xE1 — the family pattern used by
ConfigFile 0xCF / FileAccess 0xFA / DirAccess 0xDA / CameraFeed 0xCA / UndoRedo 0xED) that reports its
id and resolves to NOTHING. Applied RECURSIVELY (an RPC payload is normally an ARRAY of arguments; a
nested id is just as dangerous). BOTH decode doors covered: bytes_to_var AND
Marshalls.base64_to_variant (same decode, different transport).
The intercept MUST precede the Variant::ObjectId arm or the wrapper is pointless.
TEST DESIGN THAT MATTERS: a test asserts a LIVE node CAN reach the scene (mock returns 1 child), so
"inert" cannot pass merely because the scene was empty; and the wrapper must ERROR on get_children(),
not return an empty list — an empty list would mean the call reached the scene layer at all.

*** TWO BEAD-DESCRIPTION ERRORS (both settled by the vendored C++ at upstream/godot/) ***
1. It says EncodedObjectAsID appears "when full-object decoding is DISABLED". FALSE. The as-id branch is
   taken REGARDLESS of p_allow_objects — Godots own comment reads "This _is_ allowed."
   (core/io/marshalls.cpp:699-700). Only the FULL-OBJECT branch is gated (:717). Decoding an id can
   never construct anything, so it is always safe. Refusing ids would be STRICTER than Godot and would
   reject RPC payloads it accepts.
2. A NULL id decodes to NIL, not to an object with id 0 (:707-708). So object_id==0 is UNREACHABLE
   through the wire, even though the property defaults to 0.

HEADER_DATA_FLAG_OBJECT_AS_ID is the SAME BIT as HEADER_DATA_FLAG_64 (both 1<<16). Not a clash —
Godots design: bit 16 is read against the variants TYPE.

CONTRACT CHANGE, HANDLED: Variant::ObjectId previously encoded as Unsupported. Checked the whole
workspace for dependents — gdplatform/src/network.rs has its OWN PRIVATE encode_variant with a
different format and never touches this codec; the fuzz suite round-trips via JSON. One existing test
asserted the old contract; updated, keeping the property it actually guarded (errors propagate out of
containers) via a still-unsupported type.

REVIEWER ALSO CAUGHT (all fixed):
1. NULL-ENCODE DIVERGENCE: Godot writes a bare 4-BYTE NIL for a null object and never emits an OBJECT
   header (marshalls.cpp:1385-1393 — an early return ABOVE the flag logic I had verified). I was
   emitting 12 bytes Godot never writes, in a module whose first line claims "a faithful port".
2. MISSING IDEMPOTENCY GUARD: mine was the ONLY unguarded register_class in register_io_classes()
   (called ~20x per suite). register_class does NOT dedupe — it mints a fresh ClassId and leaves a
   stale by_id alias.
3. MY IDEMPOTENCY TEST COULD NOT CATCH #2: class_count() is NAME-keyed, so a duplicate registration
   overwrites and the count never moves. Now asserts CLASSID STABILITY — the thing that actually changes.
4. Deleted a vacuous test (it asserted independence from an allow-objects policy this API does not
   have, so the property was unfalsifiable).

Verify: -p gdvariant --test encoded_object_as_id_roundtrip
        -p gdvariant --lib binary
        -p gdobject --test encoded_object_as_id_registration
        -p gdscript-interop --test encoded_object_as_id_script_wrapper
        (NEVER -p gdscript-interop --lib: pre-existing fuzz_deeply_nested_parens stack overflow.)

REMAINING: var_to_bytes_with_objects / bytes_to_var_with_objects (the full-object form) are NOT
implemented; the codec always refuses full objects. That is the safe default and matches
p_allow_objects=false. instance_from_id() already exists in the interpreter, so the Godot idiom
instance_from_id(decoded.get_object_id()) is the intended way back to a live object — the explicit step
this bead restores.

title: Runtime: drive the MainLoop continuously during editor Play
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/runtime-drive] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot advances the SceneTree every rendered frame while a game runs (Main::iteration → SceneTree::process/physics_process). Patina's editor Play (api_runtime_play, editor_server.rs:9435) constructs a MainLoop and flips is_running=true but never advances it — the sole main_loop.step() call is api_runtime_step (editor_server.rs:9562), reachable only from the manual 'next frame' button (editor_ui.rs:8293). The browser's runtime polling (editor_ui.rs:9845 schedulePoll) refreshes status/viewport but never posts /api/runtime/step, so a played scene's _process/_physics_process, tweens, Timer nodes and physics never tick. Implement a continuous driver: either a server-side stepping thread that calls run_main_loop.step(delta) while is_running && !is_paused (honoring time_scale and max_fps and pushing frame_count + rendered viewport to the game view), or an /api/runtime/tick that the served game view drives via requestAnimationFrame at delta_time. Wire the EDITOR_HTML game view to advance frames automatically when Play is active and stop on Stop/Pause.
acceptance_criteria: After POST /api/runtime/play on a scene whose root script increments a counter in _process, both runtime_frame_count (GET /api/runtime/status) and the script counter climb over ~0.5s WITHOUT any /api/runtime/step call; POST /api/runtime/stop halts advancement. (test: runtime_play_auto_advances_frames) driving the gdeditor server end-to-end.

title: Implement SyntaxHighlighter base + EditorSyntaxHighlighter + GDScriptSyntaxHighlighter
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-ux/script-editor-syntax-highlighter] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

Register SyntaxHighlighter (Resource), EditorSyntaxHighlighter (with _get_name/_get_supported_languages/_get_supported_extensions/_get_line_syntax_highlighting virtuals) and GDScriptSyntaxHighlighter, and produce token color ranges for GDScript source that the served script editor consumes for coloring (instead of ad-hoc client JS). Allow plugins to register custom highlighters.
acceptance_criteria: GDScriptSyntaxHighlighter.get_line_syntax_highlighting returns keyword/string/comment/number color spans for a sample .gd line matching Godot's categories; ClassDB reports the three-class chain; the script editor renders those colors. (test: `gdscript_syntax_highlighter_line_colors`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED (mail 59168): the CLASS CHAIN ONLY, 1 of 3 acceptance clauses. KEEP OPEN.
Colour spans and editor rendering are NOT done. Deliberately scoped small; the recon below should save
the next agent most of the discovery.

DONE (acceptance clause 2, "ClassDB reports the three-class chain"), diffed vs 4.6.1 + the vendored C++:
  Resource <- SyntaxHighlighter <- EditorSyntaxHighlighter <- GDScriptSyntaxHighlighter
ALL THREE ARE CONCRETE — unusually, none is abstract. A bare SyntaxHighlighter instantiates and simply
colours nothing. GDScriptSyntaxHighlighter declares NOTHING of its own: it is the GDScript
IMPLEMENTATION, everything inherited.

*** THE BEADS DESCRIPTION INVENTS A VIRTUAL ***
It lists _get_supported_extensions on EditorSyntaxHighlighter. GODOT HAS NO SUCH VIRTUAL.
editor/script/script_editor_plugin.h:62-64 declares EXACTLY three GDVIRTUALs:
  _get_name, _get_supported_languages, _create
Registering it would invent a hook a plugin could override that Godot would NEVER CALL. A test asserts
the surface is exactly those three AND that _get_supported_extensions is absent.
(_get_line_syntax_highlighting is INHERITED from SyntaxHighlighter, not declared here — another way the
description misleads.)

*** get_line_syntax_highlighting(line) TAKES A LINE NUMBER, NOT TEXT ***
The highlighter reads the line from the TextEdit it is BOUND TO, and returns an EMPTY dictionary when
it has none (scene/resources/syntax_highlighter.cpp:41-43). Any design that passes the text in is
inventing an API.

RECON FOR THE REMAINING 2 CLAUSES (all verified against source, not guessed):
1. RETURN SHAPE is { start_column: { "color": Color } } — a Dictionary keyed by the column where a
   colour STARTS, value a Dictionary with a "color" key (syntax_highlighter.cpp:212-213). NOT a list of
   spans; NOT {col: Color}.
2. gdscript-interops tokenizer is most of the work already done: tokenize(source) -> Vec<TokenSpan>,
   TokenSpan { token, line, col } with 1-BASED line/col (tokenizer.rs:289-337). Keywords, strings and
   numbers are distinct Token variants -> those three categories map straight across.
3. *** BUT COMMENTS ARE STRIPPED BY THE TOKENIZER *** (tokenizer.rs:336: "Comments (starting with #)
   are stripped"). The acceptances COMMENT category CANNOT come from tokens. It needs a separate scan
   of the raw line, and that scan MUST BE STRING-AWARE: `var s = "# not a comment"` has a # that must
   not start a comment. The token spans give you the string extents to exclude, so the two passes
   compose.
4. Godot caches PER LINE (highlighting_cache) — that is what update_cache/clear_highlighting_cache are
   for. Any implementation must invalidate on edit or colours go stale.
5. Current editor highlighting is ad-hoc CLIENT CSS (.sh-keyword et al., editor_ui.rs:1466), so clause 3
   means replacing that with server-produced spans.
6. _create is WHY EditorSyntaxHighlighter exists: the script editor CLONES a registered highlighter per
   open file rather than sharing one instance. Plugin registration depends on it.

Verify: -p gdobject --test syntax_highlighter_family_registration
        -p gdobject --lib class_db

WHY I STOPPED HERE: the rest is a real GDScript highlighter (two-pass, string-aware comment scanning,
per-line cache) plus an editor-server change to feed spans to the client — substantially bigger than the
registration. Better to hand over accurate recon than a half-built highlighter in a shared file. The
chain is registered correctly and the invented virtual is refused; both are permanent wins.

(test: `editor_plugin_scripting_api_surface`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED (mail 59243): 9 of 12 classes registered (ClassDB layer only). SCRIPT BINDING NOT DONE. KEEP OPEN.
This bead is far bigger than one iteration: 12 classes + script binding + EditorInterface wiring + a
@tool plugin acceptance test.

REGISTERED 9 (schemas diffed vs 4.6.1): EditorSettings, EditorSelection, EditorUndoRedoManager,
EditorScript, EditorVCSInterface, EditorResourcePreviewGenerator, EditorResourceTooltipPlugin,
EditorTranslationParserPlugin, EditorToaster.
The beads "reuse the existing backends" premise is ACCURATE — editor_settings_store.rs, filesystem.rs
and editor_compat.rs all exist.

*** THE BEADS DESCRIPTION INVENTS FOUR APIs (all refused, all pinned by tests) ***
1. EditorSettings.get_setting_list — DOES NOT EXIST. Real readers: get_setting / has_setting.
2. EditorSettings.property_get_revert — DOES NOT EXIST on EditorSettings (it is an Object method).
3. FileSystemDock.get_current_path — DOES NOT EXIST. Its WHOLE surface is:
     navigate_to_path/1, add_resource_tooltip_plugin/1, remove_resource_tooltip_plugin/1
4. "FileSystemDock files-selected signals" — there is NO files_selected. Real signals:
     inherit, instantiate, resource_removed, file_removed, folder_removed, files_moved, folder_moved,
     folder_color_changed, selection_changed, display_mode_changed
Registering any of them would promise a plugin an API that ERRORS ON CALL.

*** TWO CLASSES ARE ABSTRACT AND THE BEAD SAYS SO OF NEITHER ***
EditorUndoRedoManager is_instantiable=FALSE — a script NEVER constructs one; it gets the editors via
EditorPlugin.get_undo_redo(). EditorToaster is_instantiable=FALSE — the editor owns the one toaster; a
plugin only pushes to it. FileSystemDock is also abstract.
Smaller corrections: it is add_node/remove_node, NOT add/remove. And get_top_selected_nodes is a THIRD
selection getter the bead omits (drops nodes whose parent is also selected — different from

*** THE 3 I DID NOT REGISTER, AND WHY ***
Each needs a parent Patina LACKS. Registering a child whose parent is missing SEVERS THE CHAIN silently

    V: _value_changed    S: value_changed, changed

    P: base_type, edited_resource, editable, toggle_mode
    M: set_base_type/1 get_base_type/0 get_allowed_types/0 set_edited_resource/1 get_edited_resource/0
       set_toggle_mode/1 is_toggle_mode/0 set_toggle_pressed/1 set_editable/1 is_editable/0

  Then: EditorScriptPicker <- EditorResourcePicker, P: script_owner, M: set_script_owner/1

        control_state, hide_slider, editing_integer (14 accessors), S: grabbed, ungrabbed,

title: Register EditorSceneFormatImporter/EditorScenePostImport class surface and add the GLTF importer class
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-ux/scene-import-plugins] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

Expose EditorSceneFormatImporter (base, _get_extensions/_import_scene virtuals), EditorScenePostImport (_post_import), and EditorScenePostImportPlugin as ClassDB classes backed by the existing import.rs traits/registry, and provide a concrete EditorSceneFormatImporterGLTF (and EditorSceneFormatImporterUFBX where a wasm ufbx exists) so glTF/FBX scenes import through a scriptable, subclassable pipeline. Mark Blend/FBX2GLTF importer subclasses as present-but-unavailable on web (return a clear error) per the subprocess scope citation.
acceptance_criteria: An editor plugin can register an EditorScenePostImport subclass whose _post_import runs on scene import and mutates the result; a .glb imports via EditorSceneFormatImporterGLTF; ClassDB.class_exists is true for the base + GLTF + post-import classes; Blend/FBX2GLTF report an unsupported-on-web error rather than being absent. (test: `editor_scene_import_plugin_surface`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED (mail 59285): 7 classes registered (ClassDB LAYER ONLY). Import pipeline NOT wired. KEEP OPEN.

REGISTERED 7 (schemas diffed vs 4.6.1, all chains intact — every parent already existed):
  EditorSceneFormatImporter <- RefCounted            (2 methods + 4 virtuals)
  EditorSceneFormatImporterGLTF / ...Blend / ...FBX2GLTF / ...UFBX <- EditorSceneFormatImporter
  EditorScenePostImport <- RefCounted                (_post_import/1 + get_source_file/0)
  EditorScenePostImportPlugin <- RefCounted          (3 methods + 8 virtuals + InternalImportCategory)

*** THE BEAD IS ACCURATE THIS TIME *** — worth recording after the last several were not. Its [PARTIAL]
status, the backends it names (gdeditor/src/import.rs; gdresource/src/gltf_import.rs for the real .glb
path) and the Blend/FBX2GLTF subprocess caveat all check out. It even correctly anticipated
EditorSceneFormatImporterUFBX existing.

*** THE TRAP: these are RefCounted, NOT ResourceImporter ***
EditorImportPlugin (already registered) DOES derive ResourceImporter and imports ANY resource — so
deriving this family from it is the plausible-looking mistake. They share NO base beyond RefCounted;
this family plugs into the SCENE importer specifically. A test asserts BOTH directions, and it is not
vacuous: EditorImportPlugin genuinely IS a ResourceImporter, and ResourceImporter IS abstract.

OTHER TRAPS PINNED:
- ALL FOUR concrete importers declare NOTHING of their own. The format is the only difference and it
  lives in _get_extensions. Giving GLTF a property would invent schema.
- EditorScenePostImport and EditorScenePostImportPlugin are SIBLINGS, NOT a chain. Both derive
  RefCounted directly; neither subclasses the other. The first mutates the FINISHED scene
  (_post_import(scene) + get_source_file() — its whole surface); the second also adds import options
  and touches EACH INTERNAL RESOURCE as it is built (_internal_process/4, _pre_process, _post_process).
- InternalImportCategory: NODE=0, MESH_3D_NODE=1, MESH=2, MATERIAL=3, ANIMATION=4, ANIMATION_NODE=5,
  SKELETON_3D_NODE=6, MAX=7. *** _MAX IS A COUNT SENTINEL, NOT A CATEGORY *** — iterating it as one
  would process a category that does not exist.

Verify: -p gdobject --test editor_scene_import_plugin_surface
        -p gdobject --lib class_db

REMAINING (the bulk — this is the ClassDB layer ONLY):
1. SCRIPT BINDING over gdeditor/src/import.rs — none of these 7 is script-reachable. The acceptance
   wants a plugin to register an EditorScenePostImport subclass whose _post_import ACTUALLY RUNS on
   import and MUTATES the result.
2. A REAL .glb IMPORT through EditorSceneFormatImporterGLTF. gdresource/src/gltf_import.rs EXISTS, so
   this is another TWO HEALTHY ISLANDS / NO BRIDGE case: the decoder is there, the class is now there,
   nothing routes one to the other. (Same shape as .114 navmesh, .176 debugger, .183 FABRIK, .187 pool.)
3. Blend/FBX2GLTF unsupported-on-web ERRORS — registered (so ClassDB is honest and they are not
   ABSENT), but they must still REPORT a clear error rather than failing silently. Both shell out to
   Blender/FBX2glTF, which the web build has no answer for.
   NOTE: UFBX IS DIFFERENT — it decodes FBX IN-PROCESS, so it is portable and must NOT inherit that
   caveat. Marking all three unavailable would be wrong.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:

working end-to-end in the browser editor." I delivered the SECONDARY half. *** The palette dock,

- local_to_map/1 + map_to_local/1 are THE REASON a viewport click can become a cell. A paint tool

*** AGAIN: TWO HEALTHY ISLANDS, NO BRIDGE — THE SIXTH THIS SESSION ***
gdscene/src/grid_map.rs (285 lines) ALREADY IMPLEMENTS THE ENTIRE BACKEND: GridMap::set_cell_item,

Six beads this session where the implementation EXISTED and only the WIRING was absent: .114 navmesh,

title: Add Node3DGizmo base for editor 3D gizmo plugins
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-ux/node3d-gizmo] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

[audit-key: sweep-7/editor-ux/node3d-gizmo] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** Node3DGizmo is the abstract base (EditorNode3DGizmo concrete) exposing editor gizmos for Node3D — redraw, add_lines/add_handles/add_collision_triangles, handle drag callbacks — that the 3D viewport uses to render per-node-type gizmos with editable handles. doc/classes/Node3DGizmo.xml.

**Patina today:** zero matches; no gizmo-plugin abstraction exists. The editor's viewport_3d.rs renders gizmos without this class, so custom/plugin gizmos and the standard per-node handle system have no base.

**Implement:** Add a Node3DGizmo base (RefCounted) + the editor gizmo-plugin registration path, register in class_db.rs, and route the 3D viewport's per-node gizmo drawing/handle editing through it.

**Wiring requirement:** A registered gizmo for a node type draws its handles in the served 3D viewport and dragging a handle mutates the node.

**Prove it:** Register a gizmo exposing one handle for a Light3D, select the node, assert the viewport gizmo data includes the handle and a drag updates the bound property.
acceptance_criteria: A Node3DGizmo-based gizmo registered for a node type contributes handles/lines to the served 3D viewport and handle drags mutate the node's property (test: `node3d_gizmo_handle_edits_node`).

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED (mail 59376): THE CLASS SURFACE. The viewport wiring is NOT done. KEEP OPEN.
The beads "register in class_db.rs" clause is done. Its WIRING REQUIREMENT — a registered gizmo drawing
handles in the served 3D viewport, and dragging one mutating the node — is NOT; that routes through
gdeditor/src/viewport_3d.rs.

THIS BEAD IS WELL-RESEARCHED — worth recording. Node3DGizmo really IS the abstract base with
EditorNode3DGizmo concrete; viewport_3d.rs really exists; "zero matches" was accurate; it cites the doc
XML. A marked contrast with .184/.190/.191/.193.

*** ONE CORRECTION: Node3DGizmo DECLARES NOTHING ***
No properties, no methods, no virtuals — and it is ABSTRACT. The bead attributes
add_lines/add_handles/redraw/"handle drag callbacks" to it. ALL OF THAT LIVES ON EditorNode3DGizmo,
its concrete subclass. Node3DGizmo exists ONLY so Node3D can hold a gizmo reference without the scene
tree depending on the editor. Registering that surface on the base would let a script call methods
Godots Node3DGizmo does not have.

*** THE ARITY TRAP — verified for ALL 12 HOOKS by computing it from the API dump, not transcription ***
EVERY EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin hook takes the GIZMO as its FIRST argument, so each is EXACTLY ONE ARITY
HIGHER than EditorNode3DGizmos same-named virtual:
  _redraw                      gizmo=0 plugin=1
  _get_handle_name             gizmo=2 plugin=3
  _is_handle_highlighted       gizmo=2 plugin=3
  _get_handle_value            gizmo=2 plugin=3
  _begin_handle_action         gizmo=2 plugin=3
  _set_handle                  gizmo=4 plugin=5
  _commit_handle               gizmo=4 plugin=5
  _subgizmos_intersect_ray     gizmo=2 plugin=3
  _subgizmos_intersect_frustum gizmo=2 plugin=3
  _set_subgizmo_transform      gizmo=2 plugin=3
  _get_subgizmo_transform      gizmo=1 plugin=2
  _commit_subgizmos            gizmo=3 plugin=4
A PLUGIN SERVES MANY GIZMOS; A GIZMO SERVES ONE NODE. Copying the arities across would COMPILE and then
be handed the WRONG ARGUMENT at runtime. The test asserts both the literal pairs AND the +1 relation.
NOTE the get/set pair looks lopsided (get 1/2, set 2/3) — that is Godot; do NOT "correct" one to match.

OTHER TRAPS PINNED:
- EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin is a RESOURCE, not a RefCounted — the editor RETAINS the plugin, unlike the
  gizmos it mints. And it is NOT itself a gizmo (both directions asserted).
- Godot separates DRAWN geometry from PICKABLE geometry: add_lines/add_mesh vs
  add_collision_segments/add_collision_triangles. A gizmo you can SEE is not automatically one you can
  CLICK — directly relevant to the beads drag proof.
- add_handles takes 3 required args (handles, material, ids).

Verify: -p gdobject --test node3d_gizmo_class_surface
        -p gdobject --lib class_db

REMAINING — THE BEADS WIRING REQUIREMENT:
1. Route viewport_3d.rs per-node gizmo drawing THROUGH this. The bead itself notes the viewport ALREADY
   renders gizmos WITHOUT the class — so this is a REFACTOR onto the registered abstraction, not a
   from-scratch build. gdeditor/src/gizmo_snap.rs also exists.
2. The gizmo-plugin registration path: _has_gizmo/_create_gizmo/_get_priority dispatch, plus the
   tie-break when two plugins claim the same node type.
3. The beads proof: register a gizmo exposing ONE HANDLE for a Light3D, select the node, assert the
   viewport gizmo data includes the handle and a DRAG UPDATES THE BOUND PROPERTY. Browser-observable —
   per CLAUDE.md that wants browser verification with error tracking, not a pure Rust test.

comments.text:
2026-10-30 ~14:3xZ (ScarletRidge) — READ-ONLY. No code, no claim, no status change. **Adding `needs-attention`: GentleBadger's analysis is correct and this bead cannot be resolved by any worker — it needs a human to either close it as a duplicate or re-point it at the real missing layer.** It was the only blocked non-epic without that flag.

I verified the specifics rather than re-deriving the analysis, because the note's two claims are both checkable and both decide the bead's fate.

**1. The duplicate claim holds.** `RichTextEffect` and `CharFXTransform` are registered in `gdobject/src/class_db.rs` (the note cites `:2769-2800`, landed by the closed `pat-nzgdu.157`), and `gdscene/src/char_fx.rs` implements `CharFXTransform` plus the built-in effect family with tests. The sweep re-issued an unfinished clause of a closed bead as a new MISSING bead. Its own header already admits low confidence: `[unverified]`, `[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]`.

**2. The architectural claim is the decisive one, and it is why no amount of RichTextLabel work helps.** A custom `RichTextEffect` is a *script subclass of a Resource*, and this engine has no script-backed Resources. The note's three checks are all still true today:

- `ResourceRef { path, class_name, properties }` (`gdvariant/src/variant.rs:150`) has no script slot.
- `attach_script` is nodes-only — `scene_tree.rs:1728` takes a `node_id: NodeId`.

So the acceptance ("a RichTextLabel with a CUSTOM RichTextEffect that sets `char_fx.offset` from `elapsed_time`") is unreachable from where the code is, and the missing layer sits underneath this subsystem entirely.

**Why this needs a human and not a worker.** Both available dispositions are owner calls:

- **Close as a duplicate of `pat-nzgdu.157`**, whose comment already records the remaining clause — so nothing is lost, and the board stops carrying a P3 that re-derives the same dead end each time it is dispatched; or

That is a significant, well-evidenced epic hiding behind a P3, and it is worth more than this bead is.

⚠️ **Do not dispatch this to a worker as-is.** A plausible-looking diff here is a false-close hazard of the kind this tier keeps producing: someone can wire RichTextLabel effect parsing, pass a test, and close a bead while custom effects still cannot exist. The guard is the acceptance's own word *custom* — it requires a script-backed Resource, and nothing short of that layer satisfies it.

I have not changed status or assignee; the bead stays blocked and GrayBeaver's. Flag added only so it reaches the park-review path.

Two were resting on stale premises and are now flagged with the correction (`pat-s3rrv.79`, `pat-0q2kx.201`); this one, `pat-nzgdu.111`, `pat-nzgdu.113` and `pat-s3rrv.8` are **correctly** blocked on genuine owner decisions or compiler-in-the-loop hazards; and `pat-0q2kx.163`'s proposed split turned out to have shipped already.

comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED (mail 59585): BOTH ACCEPTANCE CLAUSES. Registration AND the render path.
First full-acceptance delivery of this session — possible because gdscene compiles again.

THE BEAD IS ACCURATE: Separator <- Control really IS abstract, HSeparator/VSeparator concrete, and both
really do size from `separation` and draw the `separator` stylebox. Verified vs 4.6.1 + vendored C++.

*** THE TRAP — scene/gui/separator.cpp:35-43 ***
  Size2 ms(3, 3);                                  // BASE IS (3,3), NOT ZERO
  if (orientation == VERTICAL) ms.x = separation;  // VSeparator: separation = WIDTH
  else                        ms.y = separation;   // HSeparator: separation = HEIGHT
So an HSeparator is (3, 4): height 4 from the theme, WIDTH 3 — a floor so it never collapses in a
container. (0,4) and (4,4) are BOTH WRONG and BOTH LOOK RIGHT. The beads acceptance only mentions the
HEIGHT, so recall alone would have shipped the bug. A test pins BOTH axes and asserts H/V are genuine
transposes.

ALL THREE DECLARE NOTHING OF THEIR OWN. The ORIENTATION IS THE CLASS, not a property — a `vertical`
bool would invent schema. Godot splits H/V by class here exactly as for ScrollBar.

THEME ENTRIES ADDED TO MATCH GODOT (default_theme.cpp:734-739, :1063-1069):
  separator stylebox = StyleBoxLine, thickness 1 (= round(scale)), vertical per class
  separation = 4 for HSeparator and VSeparator
Patina ALREADY had StyleBox::Line(StyleBoxLine) with Godots exact fields (color/thickness/vertical/
grow_begin/grow_end), so the render arm just resolves the themed stylebox and lets it draw — NO
hand-rolled line maths.

That list is the render paths FALLBACK MEMBERSHIP TEST. A control ABSENT from it SILENTLY NEVER DRAWS —
the ClassDB registration would look fine while the acceptance failed. Easy to miss.

Tests drive the REAL render_control_tree pipeline, not a mock. One asserts the drawn line runs along the
separators LONG AXIS (wide, not tall, in a 100x10 rect) — the classic way to get orientation backwards
while still "emitting a draw command" and passing a weaker test.

TWO MISTAKES I CAUGHT IN MY OWN WORK (reusable):
1. Viewport lives in gdserver2d::VIEWPORT, not ::canvas (canvas owns CanvasItem/DrawCommand). Found by
   reading a working sibling test (tests/stylebox_flat_draws_borders_and_corners.rs) rather than
   trusting the module name.
2. theme.rs imported StyleBox but NOT StyleBoxLine, which my edit used. Caught pre-send.
NOTE: the rustfmt diff at control_render.rs:346 is PRE-EXISTING (in .157s backfill code), NOT mine. My
edits are at :56, :449, :486 and are clean. I did not reformat foreign lines.

comments.text:
GentleBadger — SECOND submission. First failed verification with a COMPILE error (101), fixed. Diagnosed from the real error, not guessed.

THE ERROR: the gdscene lib-test build failed with E0277, "1 previous error". The verifier's output tail happened to end on an unrelated `unused_assignments` WARNING in shapecast3d.rs:539 (a sibling file's test helper, not mine), which briefly looked like a foreign break — but that is a warning, and the crate had exactly 1 error, which was MINE:

I put `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]` on `CodeHighlighter`, whose `default_color: Color` field requires `Color: Default`. gdcore's `Color` derives only `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq` — NO `Default`. So the derive failed E0277 "the trait bound `Color: Default` is not satisfied". Because the derive is on the struct's non-test code, it broke the whole `gdscene` compile (even a plain build), which is why the lib-test command couldn't build.

FIX: dropped `Default` from the derive -> `#[derive(Debug, Clone)]`. Nothing constructs `CodeHighlighter::default()` (verified by grep); the constructor is `new(default_color)`, which takes the text colour explicitly. Documented why there's no Default (Color has no sensible/derivable default).

RE-AUDIT: since the compiler reported exactly 1 error and I can't compile, I re-checked every other derive and trait bound in the changed files:
- HlSpan derives Debug/Clone/PartialEq — Color satisfies all three. OK.
- CodeHighlighter now Debug/Clone only — BTreeMap<String,Color> and Color both satisfy. OK.
- The control_render TextEdit arm and the integration test compile in the same crate/units; rustc would have reported their errors alongside mine (it did not) — re-verified their APIs (get_node/get_property, Dictionary insert/iter, Viewport/render_control_tree, DrawString match, &String vs &str comparisons) against source anyway.
