title: Editor: drive the running scene in real time on Play (continuous MainLoop tick)
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/editor_play_realtime] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot's Play runs the game continuously at the target framerate (game_view_plugin.cpp; SceneTree::iteration each frame); Pause+Step is only a debug affordance on top of a continuously-running loop. Patina's Play starts a MainLoop and calls _ready once (editor_server.rs:9435) but has NO real-time driver: the only main_loop.step() is api_runtime_step (editor_server.rs:9562), which returns 400 unless is_paused (editor_server.rs:9550). pollRuntimeStatus (editor_ui.rs:9122) polls status every 200ms but never advances the loop, and api_runtime_status does not step. Result: after Play, the scene is frozen post-_ready; _process/_physics_process never run and runtime_frame_count is stuck at 0 unless the user pauses and hand-clicks Next Frame. Implementation: add a runtime driver that advances run_main_loop at delta_time cadence while is_running && !is_paused — either a server-side background tick thread that locks EditorState and calls run_main_loop.step(delta) on a fixed timestep (accumulator), or a new POST /api/runtime/advance endpoint the served game view calls from a requestAnimationFrame loop (editor_ui.rs) with elapsed dt, updating runtime_frame_count and pushing per-frame input. Keep the existing pause + single-step path for debugging. Wire the game-view render refresh to the advancing frame so the browser shows motion.
acceptance_criteria: After POST /api/runtime/play WITHOUT pausing, runtime_frame_count increases over ~250ms of wall/simulated time and a scripted node's _process-incremented variable advances beyond its _ready value, observable via /api/runtime/status and the node property API. Pause still freezes advancement and Next Frame still single-steps. (test: `editor_play_advances_frames_realtime`) drives the editor server end-to-end: load a scene whose script increments a counter in _process, play without pausing, tick the driver, assert counter and frame_count both grew.

title: Web export: generate real HTML shell + engine loader + PWA/COOP-COEP config (stop faking success)
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web_export_pipeline] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: STUB]

Godot's web export (export_plugin.cpp) emits a full deployable bundle: index.html from a shell template (canvas + progress bar + error/status overlay), a <name>.js engine loader (start config, preloadFile, onProgress/onExit — engine.js), the .wasm module, the .pck data, optional .worker.js + .audio.worklet.js for threads, icons, and — when PWA is enabled — a service worker + offline page + web manifest; a `variant/thread_support` option toggles the COEP/COOP requirement, and the editor's own HTTP preview server sends `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` + `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` (editor_http_server.cpp:108-109). Patina's PackageExecutor has no 'web' generator (export.rs:479-484 falls to `_ => marker`) yet reports success and writes a text file named `<app>.web.release.wasm` (export.rs:428-435, :147). Implementation: add generate_web_bundle() dispatched for target 'web' in export.rs that writes an index.html shell (with canvas/progress/error overlay + head_include from WebExportConfig in gdplatform/web.rs), an engine-loader JS (start/preload/onProgress API), a web app manifest, and options for PWA service worker + COOP/COEP/thread toggle; bundle the project resources as a .pck. Until a real wasm payload exists (see web_wasm_runtime), do NOT report success with a bogus placeholder — either embed the provided wasm binary or return a clear PackageError. Also send COOP/COEP headers from the editor server so a threaded build could be previewed.
acceptance_criteria: Exporting a project for 'web' writes index.html containing a <canvas>, a progress element and an error/status overlay, plus an engine-loader .js exposing a start()/preloadFile API and a web manifest; enabling PWA additionally writes a service worker and offline page. When no wasm payload is supplied the pipeline returns an explicit error/warning instead of a success result carrying a non-wasm placeholder. (test: `web_export_generates_runnable_shell`) runs PackageExecutor for 'web' and asserts the shell/loader/manifest files exist with the required elements and that a payload-less run does not falsely report a runnable .wasm.

title: Animation: wire AnimationTree into the tick, add parameters/ blend system, and complete blend-tree/state-machine nodes
description:
[audit-key: animation/anim-tree] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot AnimationTree evaluates an AnimationNode graph each frame writing poses to a target skeleton/nodes, driven by `parameters/...` (float blend amounts, Vector2 blend positions, OneShot request enum, TimeSeek), with a full node set (Add2/Add3/Sub2/Blend2/Blend3/OneShot/TimeScale/TimeSeek/Transition/BlendSpace1D/2D) and a StateMachine supporting travel() Dijkstra pathfinding, transition modes (immediate/sync/at_end), auto_advance + advance conditions/expressions, and a Playback control object. Patina's animation_tree.rs is a library-only struct: it is not stored in SceneTree (no `animation_trees` map), never advanced by main_loop, not loadable from .tscn, uses a bool-only parameter map (line 207), lacks Add/Sub/TimeScale/TimeSeek/Transition nodes (enum line 19), and its state machine only supports a single bool condition with no travel/modes. Approach: add an `animation_trees` side-table + attach_animation_tree, advance it from the mixer phase, parse AnimationNodeBlendTree/StateMachine/BlendSpace sub-resources from .tscn; replace the bool parameter map with a `parameters/...` Variant map (floats/Vector2/request enums) exposed via get/set; add the missing node types; implement StateMachine travel() pathfinding, transition modes, and a playback object; register AnimationTree children of AnimationMixer. Cluster the modifier-tree math; split StateMachine.travel into a follow-up if oversized.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn AnimationTree with a BlendTree root Blend2 node driven by `parameters/blend/blend_amount` produces, after scene load and ticking, an output pose interpolated by the float parameter set from a script; and a StateMachine `travel("Run")` walks intermediate states rather than snapping (test: `animation_tree_scene_wiring`).

title: Audio: expose AudioServer singleton + load project bus layout and route solo/send/effects in the mix
description:
[audit-key: audio/audio-server-buses] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot exposes AudioServer as a global singleton (set_bus_volume_db, set_bus_mute/solo, add_bus_effect, get_bus_peak_volume_left_db, set_bus_layout) and boots the project's default_bus_layout.tres so buses like Music/SFX exist with their volumes and effect chains. Patina has none of this at runtime: no AudioServer singleton in the interpreter, the bridge starts a single Master bus (audio_server_bridge.rs:44) and never loads project buses, unknown buses mix at unity (server.rs:139), solo/send/non-Master effects are ignored in server.mix (server.rs:133,184), and bypass does not exist (bus.rs). Add an AudioServer singleton dispatch in the interpreter (like the Input singleton at interpreter.rs:1543) backed by the bridge's AudioServer; load audio/buses/default_bus_layout at boot into the mixer; and make server.mix honor per-voice bus routing including solo (mute all non-soloed when any solo is set), `send` chaining to a target bus, per-bus effect chains for all buses, and a new bypass flag on AudioBus.
acceptance_criteria: A project defining a 'Music' bus at -10 dB routes an AudioStreamPlayer on that bus at the reduced level in the runner mix (not unity), AudioServer.set_bus_volume_db from a script changes a bus's level, soloing one bus silences others, and a non-Master bus effect chain is applied. Test (test: audio_server_singleton_and_bus_layout) loads a project bus layout, plays voices on two buses, and asserts per-bus volume + solo + a non-Master effect all take effect in the mix.

title: Audio: implement the AudioEffect DSP family (filters, dynamics, modulation) and attach bus effects from scenes
description:
[audit-key: audio/audio-effects] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ships 28 AudioEffect classes (servers/audio/effects). Patina has 3 (Amplify + a non-Freeverb Reverb + a 3-band EQ) in gdaudio/src/effects.rs and registers only those (class_db.rs:805). Implement the AudioEffect trait impls + register the classes for the common tier first: the AudioEffectFilter family (Low/High/BandPass/BandLimit/Notch/AllPass/Low/HighShelf) via biquad, AudioEffectCompressor (+sidechain), Limiter/HardLimiter, Delay, and EQ6/10/21; then modulation/analysis (Chorus, Phaser, Distortion, PitchShift, StereoEnhance, Panner, SpectrumAnalyzer, Capture, Record). Wire the bus effect config from the loaded bus layout (see audio-server-buses bead) into each AudioBus's EffectChain so scene/project effects actually reach the mixer, not just the Master bus (server.rs:184). Split modulation/analysis into a follow-up staged bead if needed; this bead delivers filters + dynamics.
acceptance_criteria: A bus carrying an AudioEffectLowPassFilter measurably attenuates a high-frequency sine relative to a low one in the runner mix, and an AudioEffectCompressor reduces the gain of a loud signal above threshold. Test (test: audio_effects_dsp_chain) builds a bus with a lowpass then a compressor, mixes a known signal through the bridge, and asserts the frequency-dependent attenuation and gain reduction.

title: Audio: apply pitch_scale resampling, max_polyphony voices, and stream_paused/process-mode to AudioStreamPlayer
description:
[audit-key: audio/audio-player-props] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot's AudioStreamPlayer resamples playback by pitch_scale, spawns up to max_polyphony concurrent voices per player, and pauses with the SceneTree per its process_mode / stream_paused. Patina stores pitch_scale but never resamples (player.rs:104; server.mix reads native-rate frames at server.rs:158), cuts the previous voice on re-play so no polyphony exists (player.rs:139), and mixes every frame ignoring pause (main_loop.rs:442). Apply pitch_scale as a resample ratio in server.mix's per-stream read; give each player a voice pool honoring max_polyphony (sync it in audio_server_bridge.rs:182); gate/scale the audio phase by tree pause + the node's process_mode and stream_paused; and register the missing properties (stream_paused, max_polyphony, mix_target, volume_linear, playback_type) in class_db.rs:1093.
acceptance_criteria: Setting pitch_scale=2.0 halves the audible duration of a fixed buffer in the runner mix; triggering play() twice quickly on a player with max_polyphony=2 keeps both voices audible (summed amplitude), and pausing the tree stops a pausable player's output. Test (test: audio_player_pitch_polyphony_pause) drives all three through MainLoop and asserts duration halving, two concurrent voices, and pause silence.

title: Audio: real MP3 decode + AudioStreamWAV loop modes/ADPCM/QOA + Ogg loop metadata
description:
[audit-key: audio/audio-streams] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: STUB]

Godot decodes MP3 (minimp3), WAV with IMA-ADPCM and QOA plus forward/pingpong/backward loop modes and loop_begin/loop_end, and OggVorbis loop/loop_offset/bpm. Patina rejects real MP3 (decode.rs:295 accepts only the PATMP3 fixture), decodes WAV as plain PCM with no loop/ADPCM/QOA (wav.rs), exposes only None/Forward loop modes (stream.rs:16), and drops Ogg loop/bpm metadata (decode.rs:91). Replace decode_mp3 with a real decoder (symphonia or minimp3-rs) and register it in the importer (import.rs:55); parse WAV `smpl`/loop metadata + implement IMA-ADPCM and QOA decode; add pingpong/backward LoopMode variants and honor loop_begin/loop_end in AudioStreamPlayback::advance (stream.rs:94); parse Ogg loop/loop_offset/bpm from Vorbis comments. Looping must actually wrap in the runner mix.
acceptance_criteria: A looping WAV (loop_mode=forward, loop_begin/end set) wraps at loop_end and keeps producing audio past its nominal length in the runner mix, and a real .mp3 asset decodes to a non-silent AudioBuffer via the importer. Test (test: audio_stream_formats_loop_mp3) asserts an MP3 file decodes non-silent and a looped WAV still emits samples after exceeding its length through the bridge.

title: Autoload: instantiate project [autoload] singletons under /root at boot (runner + editor Play)
description:
[audit-key: autoload-global-singletons-runtime/autoload-runtime-boot] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

GODOT: In game mode (main/main.cpp:4367-4433) Godot reads ProjectSettings.get_autoload_list() and, in declaration order, instantiates each autoload — PackedScene.instantiate() when the path is a scene, else ResourceLoader.load() the script, verify get_instance_base_type() inherits Node, ClassDB.instantiate(base_type) and set_script — then set_name(info.name) and add each as a child of SceneTree.get_root() (added AFTER all are constructed so cross-references are valid in _ready). PATINA: [autoload] is parsed into AutoloadEntry{name,path,is_singleton} at gdresource/src/project.rs:221-330 (get_autoloads at 308), but nothing in the runtime instantiates them. `grep -rn autoload crates/patina-runner/src` returns 0; patina-runner/src/main.rs:296-397 loads a single .tscn and never opens project.godot; bootstrap.rs boot phases are Resources->SceneTree->MainScene (no autoload phase); gdeditor editor_server.rs:9413 api_runtime_play clones the scene tree into MainLoop::new with no autoload step. So /root/Global never exists. IMPLEMENTATION: (1) Load project.godot via gdresource ProjectLoader in the runner boot path. (2) Add an instantiation step that runs after the SceneTree root exists and BEFORE the main scene's enter_tree, so main-scene _ready sees autoloads: for each get_autoloads() entry in declaration order, if path ends .tscn/.scn -> PackedScene::from_tscn + add_packed_scene_to_tree(tree, root_id, &scene); else read the .gd, determine the base Node class from its `extends`, create that Node via gdscene, set node.name = entry.name, attach GDScriptNodeInstance::from_source; add under root_id and run LifecycleManager::enter_tree on the autoload subtree. (3) Wire this in all three boot sites: patina-runner/src/main.rs (accept a project dir and boot autoloads), patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs (new BootPhase::Autoloads between SceneTree and MainScene), and gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs api_runtime_play (instantiate into `cloned` before MainLoop::new). Companion beads add GDScript name resolution and declaration-order preservation.
acceptance_criteria: Booting a project whose project.godot declares Global="*res://global.gd" produces a node at /root/Global with the GDScript attached, and its _ready() side effects appear in the dumped tree; both the patina-runner boot path and the editor api_runtime_play path create it. A .tscn autoload path instantiates the scene under /root under its autoload name. (test: `autoload_instantiated_under_root` — build a temp project dir with project.godot [autoload] + a global.gd that sets a var in _ready, boot end-to-end, assert the /root/Global node exists with the mutated var in the output dump)

title: Object: wire set_meta/get_meta/has_meta + dynamic set()/get()/set_deferred + to_string into GDScript
description:
[audit-key: core-object/core-object-object-api] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth (Object.xml / extension_api.json classes[Object]): every Object exposes set_meta(name,value)/get_meta(name,default)/has_meta/remove_meta/get_meta_list, a dynamic set(property,value)/get(property) and set_indexed/get_indexed for path assignment, set_deferred(property,value) (applied at end of frame), and to_string(). These are heavily used by plugins, save systems, and generic tooling. Patina current state: the GDScript interpreter's Variant::ObjectId method dispatch (interpreter.rs:4250-4444) matches a fixed set of names and falls through to UndefinedFunction (4441); none of the meta/dynamic-set methods are present (grep 0). The SceneAccess trait (bindings.rs:172) has no meta or by-name set entry points, even though Node already stores meta (node.rs:309-333) and properties (node.rs:250-259). Implementation: add get_meta/set_meta/has_meta/remove_meta/get_meta_list, set_property_by_name/get_property_by_name(+default), set_deferred, and to_string to the SceneAccess trait; implement them in gdscene/scripting.rs against the Node's meta/property bags (set_deferred routes through the existing call_deferred/deferred queue); dispatch them in the interpreter's ObjectId arm. Wiring requirement: a GDScript running in the SceneTree must read back its own metadata and dynamically-set properties.
acceptance_criteria: A script attached to a node in a loaded scene executes `set_meta("hp", 7); assert(get_meta("hp") == 7); assert(has_meta("hp")); set("position", Vector2(3,4)); assert(get("position") == Vector2(3,4))` and the interpreter returns no UndefinedFunction; the node's stored meta and property reflect the writes after the frame. (test: `object_metadata_reflection_test`) runnable via cargo nextest --test object_metadata_reflection_test.

title: Signals: honor CONNECT_ flags + Callable connect + add disconnect/is_connected + deferred/binds dispatch
description:
[audit-key: core-object/core-object-signals] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot ground truth: connect(signal, Callable, flags:int=0) with ConnectFlags DEFERRED(1)/PERSIST(2)/ONE_SHOT(4)/REFERENCE_COUNTED(8); Signal.connect(callable, flags); Object.disconnect/is_connected; deferred connections fire on the idle MessageQueue flush; bound args (Callable.bind) append and unbind drops trailing args. Patina current state: interpreter.rs:4320 accepts only connect(String,ObjectId,String), discards any 4th flag arg; scripting.rs:352 drops flags; SceneTree.emit_signal (scene_tree.rs:1126-1139) always fires immediately (uses store.emit, never emit_collecting_deferred) and passes raw args without calling Connection::resolve_args (signal.rs:122), so binds/unbinds are ignored; disconnect/is_connected are unreachable from script. Implementation: extend SceneAccess with connect_signal(source,signal,Callable,flags), disconnect_signal, is_connected; plumb flags into gdobject Connection (one_shot/deferred already fields, signal.rs:55-62); in SceneTree.emit_signal switch to emit_collecting_deferred and enqueue deferred DeferredCalls onto the existing end-of-frame deferred queue; apply resolve_args for binds/unbinds on the callback-less script-method path; expose the ConnectFlags constants to the interpreter. Wiring requirement: a one-shot+deferred connection made in a script must fire exactly once, at frame end, with bound args.
acceptance_criteria: A scripted scene connects `sig.connect(Callable(self, "_on"), CONNECT_ONE_SHOT | CONNECT_DEFERRED)`, emits twice in one frame; `_on` runs exactly once and only after the deferred flush; `is_connected` returns false afterward; a `.bind(42)` argument arrives in `_on`; and `disconnect` removes an active connection. (test: `signal_connect_flags_deferred_test`) runnable via cargo nextest --test signal_connect_flags_deferred_test.

title: Object: make is_instance_valid consult a live-object registry + add free()/instance_from_id/weakref
description:
[audit-key: core-object/core-object-lifecycle] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: STUB]

Godot ground truth: is_instance_valid(obj) returns false after the object is freed; instance_from_id(int) resolves a live ObjectID back to the Object (null if dead); free() destroys immediately (firing NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE); weakref(obj) yields a WeakRef whose get_ref() nulls on free. Patina current state: is_instance_valid just checks non-nil (interpreter.rs:2861) so freed nodes report valid — a real correctness footgun for the ubiquitous `if is_instance_valid(x)` guard; there is no id->object registry (weak_ref.rs holds only a thread_local id set), so instance_from_id/weakref/free-immediate are unimplemented (grep 0). Implementation: back the SceneTree's node arena with an authoritative (process-global, not thread_local) alive registry keyed by ObjectId that is populated on node add and cleared on free/queue_free reap; route is_instance_valid through it via SceneAccess (add is_object_alive/instance_from_id/free_immediate to the trait, implement in scripting.rs against the arena); add weakref() returning a Variant carrying the id and a get_ref() that re-queries the registry. Wiring requirement: after a node is freed within the SceneTree, a held reference must report invalid to a running script.
acceptance_criteria: A scripted scene captures a child's reference, calls its free()/queue_free() (with a frame flush), then `assert(not is_instance_valid(ref))` and `assert(instance_from_id(id) == null)`; a weakref taken before free returns null from get_ref() after; is_instance_valid stays true while the node is alive. (test: `object_instance_validity_lifecycle_test`) runnable via cargo nextest --test object_instance_validity_lifecycle_test.

title: Variant: implement Packed*Array value types with typed methods, loader round-trip, and codec
description:
[audit-key: core-variant/variant-packed-arrays] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: 10 packed array types are the compact typed storage format for mesh data, tilemaps, and binary I/O; PackedByteArray alone has 69 methods (compress/decompress, get_string_from_utf8/ascii, encode/decode_u8..s64/float/double/var, hex_encode, slice). Patina current state: gdvariant/src/variant.rs has no Packed variant; gdresource/src/loader.rs:388-416 explicitly collapses all packed literals into Variant::Array (see comment 'Stored as Variant::Array'), so type identity, COW, and all typed methods are gone and a mesh .tres round-trips to the wrong type; gdvariant/src/binary.rs has no type codes 29-38 so binary resources/RPC with packed data fail to decode. Approach: add packed variants to the Variant enum (backed by Vec<u8>/Vec<i32>/Vec<f32>/Vec<Vector2> etc.), implement the typed method surface + typed method-dispatch arms in interpreter.rs, make loader.rs emit the correct packed variant, and add encode/decode arms 29-38 in binary.rs. Wiring requirement: a PackedVector3Array in a .tres reaches the mesh consumer as a packed type, and PackedByteArray methods are callable from a script running in the runner.
acceptance_criteria: Script `var b = PackedByteArray([72, 105]); return b.get_string_from_utf8()` returns "Hi"; a mesh resource containing PackedVector3Array loads with the packed type preserved (typeof reports the packed type, not Array); encode_variant/decode_variant round-trips a PackedInt32Array. (test: `packed_array_types_and_methods`)

title: Editor: build served TileMap paint UI wired to /api/tilemap paint/erase/fill/tileset handlers
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/tilemap-editor] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot's tiles editor (editor/plugins/tiles/) provides a TileSet atlas panel and TileMapLayer paint tools (paint/line/rect/bucket, terrains, flip/rotate). Patina already has server-side tile ops that build real EditorCommands (editor_server.rs:2223 api_tilemap_paint -> EditorCommand::TileMapPaint; erase/fill/data/resize/tileset at :2224-2228) plus a dead standalone tilemap_editor.rs (63 fns, no callers). Nothing in the served editor exposes them: EDITOR_HTML has no tile palette, no active-tile state, and issues no /api/tilemap request. Add a TileSet source/atlas panel + a paint toolbar to EDITOR_HTML that, when a TileMapLayer node is selected, GETs /api/tilemap/tileset to build the palette and POSTs /api/tilemap/paint|erase|fill on viewport interaction; render painted tiles back into the 2D viewport PNG.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a TileMapLayer in the served editor shows its tileset palette; clicking a cell in the 2D viewport paints the active tile and the change persists to .tscn and appears in the viewport render. Test asserts EDITOR_HTML references /api/tilemap/paint and /api/tilemap/tileset AND drives load-scene(with TileMapLayer) -> paint -> /api/tilemap/data returns the painted cell (test: editor_tilemap_paint_wired_test).

title: Editor: wire GDScript autocomplete + find/replace + goto into the served script editor
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/script-code-intel] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot's script editor (script_text_editor.cpp) gives inline completion, signature/hover docs, ctrl-click symbol goto, and find/replace. Patina's served script editor only loads and saves source (EDITOR_HTML calls just /api/script and /api/script/save); it has no completion (editor_ui.rs completion=0). The completion engine (script_completion.rs, 825 lines) and goto_definition.rs already exist but are only reachable through /api/script/main_view + /api/script/find + /api/script/replace, none of which EDITOR_HTML calls. Add a completion popup in the script editor that debounces on typing and POSTs to a completion endpoint (expose script_completion via /api/script/complete if a route is missing), wire Ctrl+F/Ctrl+R to /api/script/find + /api/script/replace, and Ctrl+click to /api/signal/goto_method or goto_definition.

Test asserts EDITOR_HTML references the completion endpoint and /api/script/find AND drives edit-buffer -> completion request -> non-empty candidate list for a known symbol (test: editor_script_completion_wired_test).

title: GDScript: complete the @GlobalScope + @GDScript utility-function table
description:
[audit-key: gdscript/gdscript-builtins] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot ground truth: scripts can call the full @GlobalScope utility set (extension_api.json utility_functions: ~110 fns incl. push_error/push_warning/printerr/prints/printt/printraw/print_rich/print_verbose, var_to_str/str_to_var/var_to_bytes/bytes_to_var(+_with_objects), weakref, hash, instance_from_id/is_instance_id_valid/is_same/is_finite, error_string, type_string/type_convert, randomize/seed/randfn/rand_from_seed, the typed absf/absi/floori/ceili/roundi/clampi/maxi/mini/snappedi/lerpf... family, sinh/cosh/tanh + inverse hyperbolics, wrap/rotate_toward/angle_difference/fposmod/step_decimals, cubic_interpolate*/bezier_*) plus @GDScript builtins char/ord/Color8/is_instance_of/print_debug/type_exists (gdscript_utility_functions.cpp). Patina current state: try_builtin (interpreter.rs:2158) covers ~55; the rest error as unknown functions at runtime (per-name grep confirms 0 implementations). Approach: extend the try_builtin match arms in interpreter.rs with the missing functions, delegating math to gdcore/gdvariant where those ops already exist, routing print_rich/printerr/push_error/push_warning to the same output/diagnostic sink used by `print` (so editor Output + console capture see them), and implementing var_to_str/str_to_var/var_to_bytes/bytes_to_var against the Variant codec. Wiring requirement: these must be callable from a script running in a scene, and push_error/printerr output must reach the runner's stderr/console path.
acceptance_criteria: A scripted node can call push_error("x"), printerr("y"), and set r = var_to_str([1,2]) -> "[1, 2]", s = str_to_var("42") -> 42, m = maxi(3, 7) -> 7, c = char(65) -> "A", and w = weakref(self) without runtime errors. Test: `gdscript_utility_functions_complete` (cargo nextest --test gdscript_utility_functions_complete) runs a script exercising a representative slice of the newly added builtins and asserts their return values. (test: `gdscript_utility_functions_complete`)

title: GDScript: first-class Signal values with .emit()/.connect(Callable) and Callable-based connect
description:
[audit-key: gdscript/gdscript-signals] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot ground truth: a declared `signal hit(dmg)` is accessible as a first-class Signal value; the idiomatic API is `hit.emit(10)`, `hit.connect(_on_hit)`, and `some_node.pressed.connect(callable, flags)` where the argument is a Callable (Signal.xml, Callable.xml, object.cpp connect). Patina current state: signals exist only as name strings (interpreter.rs:412); referencing a signal name does not yield a Signal value and there is no .emit/.connect method on it; connect only accepts the legacy connect(name, target_id, method_name) triplet (interpreter.rs:4320). Approach: add a Variant::Signal(object_id, signal_name) (or reuse an existing Signal variant) and make an identifier that names a declared signal on self/another object evaluate to it; in call_method_on, handle `.emit(args)` (route to SceneAccess::emit_signal) and `.connect(callable[, flags])` / `.disconnect` / `.is_connected` on a Signal value, resolving the Callable's object+method into the existing connect path (scene_tree.rs:1131 already dispatches node-method connections). Keep the legacy string form working. Wiring requirement: connecting `emitter.hit.connect(listener._on_hit)` then `emitter.hit.emit(10)` in scripts must invoke listener._on_hit(10) via the tree's signal dispatch.
acceptance_criteria: Across two scripted nodes, `emitter.hit.connect(listener.take_damage)` in _ready followed by `emitter.hit.emit(25)` results in listener.take_damage(25) running (listener.hp decremented by 25). Test: `gdscript_signal_emit_connect_callable` (cargo nextest --test gdscript_signal_emit_connect_callable) builds a two-node scene, runs the connect+emit through the SceneTree, and asserts the target method received the argument. (test: `gdscript_signal_emit_connect_callable`)

title: GDScript: global class_name registry + .new()/extends resolution for script classes
description:
[audit-key: gdscript/gdscript-classreg] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot ground truth: `class_name Enemy` registers a global script class (project.godot _global_script_classes) so `Enemy.new()` instantiates it, `extends Enemy` inherits it, and a .tscn/.gd can reference it by name; `preload("enemy.gd").new()` instantiates the script (gdscript.cpp global class handling, packed_scene.cpp). Patina current state: class_name is stored only as ClassDef.name (interpreter.rs:4654) with no registry; .new() (interpreter.rs:1567) covers only built-in Node classes + ConfigFile; .new() on a preloaded GDScript returns Nil (interpreter.rs:4547); the .tscn loader ignores custom class types (packed_scene.rs:189). Approach: build a process-wide (or SceneTree-scoped) registry mapping class_name -> script source/path, populated when a project's .gd files are scanned (patina-runner boot) and when a script with class_name is loaded. In interpreter .new() handling, when the identifier resolves to a registered script class or a preloaded GDScript ResourceRef, run_class + instantiate_class and return an object handle backed by a GDScriptNodeInstance; support `extends <ClassName>` by resolving the base through the registry. In the scene loader (packed_scene.rs / scene_tree create_node), when type= names a registered script class, create the node with its declared engine base and attach the script. Wiring requirement: instantiating a custom class from a script and from a .tscn both yield a live scripted instance.
acceptance_criteria: Given enemy.gd with `class_name Enemy` `var hp = 30`, another script doing `var e = Enemy.new()` gets an instance where e.hp == 30, and a .tscn node with type="Enemy" loads with the Enemy script attached and hp==30. Test: `gdscript_class_name_new_instantiation` (cargo nextest --test gdscript_class_name_new_instantiation) registers the class, instantiates via both .new() and a .tscn load, and asserts the scripted property. (test: `gdscript_class_name_new_instantiation`)

title: GDScript globals: add typed math variants (floori/clampi/maxf/snappedf/lerpf/wrap etc.) + variadic min/max + vector abs/clamp
description:
[audit-key: globalscope-utility-functions-completeness-diff/globalscope-typed-math] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth (core/variant/variant_utility.cpp): the *i/*f typed families force integer/float return: floori(2.7)->2(int), floorf(2.7)->2.0, ceili/ceilf, roundi/roundf, absi/absf, signi/signf, snappedi/snappedf, maxi/maxf, mini/minf, clampi/clampf, lerpf; wrap(value,min,max) is the Variant-generic wrap (wrapi/wrapf already exist). min()/max() accept 2+ args; abs/clamp/sign/snapped operate componentwise on Vector2/3/4. These typed helpers are pervasive in real 4.x scripts, so their absence throws UndefinedFunction on common code. Patina current: interpreter.rs::try_builtin has no arms for any typed variant (grep=0 each) and the generic min/max cap at 2 args (interpreter.rs:2427/2439), abs is Int/Float only (interpreter.rs:2374), clamp is float-coerced (interpreter.rs:2451). Approach: add try_builtin arms; *i variants coerce to i64 and return Variant::Int, *f return Variant::Float; wrap dispatches on operand type; fold min/max over args[..]; extend abs/clamp/sign/snapped match arms to Vector2/3/4 element-wise. Wiring: script call -> new arm -> typed Variant back to script, observable via print/return.
acceptance_criteria: GDScript through Interpreter::run yields Godot-typed results: `print(floori(2.7))`->`2`, `print(typeof(floori(2.7)))` is the INT type, `print(clampi(15, 0, 10))`->`10`, `print(maxf(1, 2.5))`->`2.5`, `print(snappedf(1.37, 0.1))`->`1.4`, `print(min(3, 1, 2))`->`1` (variadic), `print(abs(Vector2(-1, -2)))`->`(1, 2)`. (test: `globalscope_typed_math_builtins`)

title: Editor: wire scene-tree Change-Type/Make-Local/Editable-Children/%Unique/Lock/Warnings into served context menu
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/scene-tree-context-ops] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]
[verify-note: ADJUSTED: Server handlers all exist (editor_server.rs:2038 warnings, 2060 change_type, 2061 editable_children, 2064 make_local, 2065 lock, 2069 unique_name; fn bodies 3854/3957/4001/4220). title: GDScript globals: add cubic/bezier interpolation + rotate_toward/angle_difference/is_finite/step_decimals/fposmod/hyperbolics
description:
[audit-key: globalscope-utility-functions-completeness-diff/globalscope-interp-math] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth (core/variant/variant_utility.cpp, core/math/math_funcs.h): cubic_interpolate(from,to,pre,post,weight) and its _angle/_in_time/_angle_in_time forms; bezier_interpolate(start,ctrl1,ctrl2,end,t) and bezier_derivative; angle_difference(from,to) shortest signed delta; rotate_toward(from,to,delta) angle move with wraparound; is_finite(x)->bool; step_decimals(x)->count of significant decimals; fposmod(x,y) float positive modulo; hyperbolic sinh/cosh/tanh/asinh/acosh/atanh. Patina current: interpreter.rs::try_builtin has no arms for any of these (grep=0 each) so calls throw UndefinedFunction (interpreter.rs:3284); note angle_difference logic already exists as private fn interpreter.rs:5828 but is not exposed as a builtin. Approach: add try_builtin arms; reuse the existing private angle_difference; implement cubic_interpolate/bezier per math_funcs.h; step_decimals matches Godot's decimal-counting; delegate hyperbolics to f64::sinh etc. Wiring: script call -> new arm -> Float/Bool/Int Variant returned, observable via print/return.
acceptance_criteria: GDScript through Interpreter::run: `print(is_finite(1.0))`->`true` and `print(is_finite(INF))`->`false`; `print(step_decimals(0.01))`->`2`; `print(bezier_interpolate(0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0, 0.5))` returns ~0.5; `print(cubic_interpolate(0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.5))` returns 0.5; `print(rotate_toward(0.0, PI, 0.1))`->`0.1`; `print(angle_difference(0.0, PI))` returns ~PI. (test: `globalscope_interp_math_builtins`)

title: GDScript globals: add prints/printt/printerr/printraw/print_verbose/print_rich + push_error/push_warning + variadic str()
description:
[audit-key: globalscope-utility-functions-completeness-diff/globalscope-print-family] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth (core/variant/variant_utility.cpp): prints(...) joins args with spaces; printt(...) joins with tabs; printerr(...) writes to the error stream; printraw(...) writes with no trailing newline; print_verbose(...) prints only when OS verbose is on; print_rich(...) renders BBCode tags to console formatting; push_error(msg)/push_warning(msg) push into the engine error/warning channel (surfaced in the editor Output/Debugger). str() is variadic and concatenates all args. Patina current: interpreter.rs::try_builtin has only plain print (interpreter.rs:2164); the eight diagnostics builtins are absent (grep=0 each) and throw UndefinedFunction (interpreter.rs:3284); str() caps at 1 arg (interpreter.rs:2244). Approach: add try_builtin arms writing into the existing output buffer (InterpreterResult.output) with the right joiner/newline semantics; route push_error/push_warning into a diagnostics sink aligned with ScriptWarning (interpreter re-exports ScriptWarning) so the editor can display them; parse+strip (or map) BBCode for print_rich; make str() fold format!("{}") over all args. Wiring: script call -> arm -> output/diagnostics buffer observable in InterpreterResult and (for push_*) the editor error channel.
acceptance_criteria: GDScript through Interpreter::run: `prints("a", 1, true)` yields output line `a 1 true`; `printt("a", "b")` yields `a\tb`; `print(str("x", 2, "y"))` yields `x2y` (variadic str); `push_error("boom")` is observable in the run's error/warning diagnostics sink (not silently dropped); `printraw("ab")` produces no trailing newline. (test: `globalscope_diagnostics_print_builtins`)

title: Control: complete base surface — transform, stretch ratio, tooltip, theme chain, RTL, rect API
description:
[audit-key: gui-controls/gui-control-core] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Extend Patina's Control beyond anchors/offsets to match Godot's 52-property surface (doc/classes/Control.xml). Add pivot_offset/rotation/scale to the control rect + draw transform; honor size_flags_stretch_ratio in arrange_vbox/arrange_hbox (control.rs:647,677 currently divide expand space equally); implement the theme resolution chain (instance theme_override_* → nearest ancestor `theme` with theme_type_variation → ThemeDB default) as a reusable lookup used by the render bridge; add layout_direction/RTL mirroring, mouse_filter/mouse_default_cursor_shape, tooltip_text + delay, and get_rect/get_global_rect/get_minimum_size (respecting _get_minimum_size from containers/scripts). Register the new properties in class_db.rs Control.
acceptance_criteria: A scene with two HBox children having stretch ratios 1.0 and 3.0 (both Expand) arranges them 1:3 after the layout tick; a Control with rotation=90° and pivot_offset reports a rotated global rect; theme lookup returns an instance override over the ThemeDB default. (test: `control_core_surface_stretch_theme_rect`)

title: GUI Ranges: Range base (min/max/step/page/ratio) + sliders, scrollbars, SpinBox, ProgressBar fill
description:
[audit-key: gui-controls/gui-ranges] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Implement Godot's shared Range model (value clamped to [min,max], snapped to step, page, exp_edit, allow_greater/lesser, ratio, shared-range groups) with value_changed/changed signals, then derive HSlider/VSlider (tick_count, ticks_on_borders, scrollable, grab via drag), HScrollBar/VScrollBar (page paging), SpinBox (prefix/suffix, update_on_text_changed, arrow step), ProgressBar (fill_mode, show_percentage, indeterminate) and TextureProgressBar (radial + nine-patch fill). Register all in class_db.rs. Slider/scrollbar drag depends on the input-routing substrate; the render bead draws grabber/fill via ThemeDB.
acceptance_criteria: An HSlider with min=0,max=10,step=2: dragging the grabber to 55% snaps value to 6 and emits value_changed(6); setting value=999 clamps to 10; a ProgressBar with value=5,max=10 renders a fill covering half its rect. (test: `range_slider_spinbox_value_changed`)

title: Image import: rasterize SVG to a Texture2D (load_svg_from_buffer/string with scale)
description:
[audit-key: image-import-format-breadth-webp-svg-compressed/image-decode-svg] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: Image.load_svg_from_buffer(buffer, scale=1.0) and load_svg_from_string(svg_str, scale=1.0) (doc/classes/Image.xml:396-414) rasterize an uncompressed SVG at a scale factor into an RGBA8 Image; modules/svg/image_loader_svg.cpp is enabled by default and is how the entire Godot editor renders its icons and how projects use vector assets. Patina current state: no SVG rasterizer anywhere (grep for usvg/resvg/tiny-skia/load_svg across crates/ = empty); `.svg` is only ever classified as a Texture2D by extension (interpreter.rs:2405, editor filesystem/asset_drag_drop) with no pixel data. Implementation: add a pure-Rust, wasm-friendly SVG stack (usvg + resvg + tiny-skia) to gdresource/Cargo.toml; add `import_svg(path)` / `rasterize_svg_bytes(bytes, scale)` that parses the SVG, rasterizes at `scale` (rounding to ceil(width*scale) x ceil(height*scale) like Godot), and produces the standard pixel-bearing Texture2D Resource; register `.svg` in ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults. Wiring requirement: the registry must turn an .svg file into a Texture2D with decoded pixels reachable by the same load path PNG uses.
acceptance_criteria: ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults().load_resource('icon.svg') returns a Texture2D whose `pixels` array is populated and whose width/height reflect the SVG viewBox times the scale; rasterizing the same SVG at scale=2.0 yields 4x the pixel count of scale=1.0. (test: `svg_import_wiring`)

title: Image import: decode Radiance .hdr + OpenEXR .exr and feed PanoramaSkyMaterial
description:
[audit-key: image-import-format-breadth-webp-svg-compressed/image-decode-hdr-exr] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: Image.load_exr_from_buffer (doc/classes/Image.xml:359) and the HDR loader (modules/hdr/image_loader_hdr.cpp, RGBE Radiance) are default-enabled; HDR/EXR panoramas drive PanoramaSkyMaterial and lightmaps. Patina current state: no HDR or EXR decoder (grep for radiance/rgbe/exr decode across crates/ = empty); gdserver3d/src/sky.rs PanoramicSkyMaterial only holds `panorama_path` (sky.rs:114) and an unpopulated Option<PanoramaTexture> (sky.rs:120), so the sky can't sample a real equirect texture. Implementation: add HDR/EXR decode deps (e.g. `image` with `hdr` feature for Radiance, and the `exr` crate for OpenEXR) to gdresource/Cargo.toml; add `import_hdr`/`import_exr` producing a Texture2D Resource carrying float (linear RGB) pixels; register `.hdr` and `.exr` in ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults; and populate PanoramicSkyMaterial::texture (PanoramaTexture) from the decoded pixels when panorama_path resolves, so the equirect sampler in sky.rs has data. Wiring requirement: a scene with a WorldEnvironment→Sky→PanoramaSkyMaterial(panorama=res://sky.hdr) must end with a sampled sky color derived from the decoded HDR pixels.
acceptance_criteria: load_resource('sky.hdr') and load_resource('sky.exr') return a Texture2D with a populated float `pixels` array; and building a PanoramicSkyMaterial with a resolvable panorama_path yields a non-None PanoramaTexture whose equirect sample at a known direction matches the decoded pixel. (test: `hdr_exr_panorama_import`)

title: Image import: decode DDS/KTX containers + VRAM-compressed (BCn/ETC2/ASTC) .ctex to RGBA
description:
[audit-key: image-import-format-breadth-webp-svg-compressed/image-decode-gpu-container] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]
[verify-note: ADJUSTED: Absence CONFIRMED (status MISSING is right): no BCn/ETC2/ASTC/KTX/DDS decoder (grep decode_dds|decode_ktx|bcn|s3tc|etc2|astc|texture2ddecoder|bcndecode = none; ktx/dds packages absent from Cargo.lock; DDS grep hits are 'adds' substrings). ctex.rs:158-176 handles DATA_FORMAT_IMAGE only for ]

Godot ground truth: Image.load_ktx_from_buffer (Image.xml:380), load_dds_from_buffer (Image.xml:351), and Image.decompress turn GPU block-compressed payloads (S3TC/BC1-7, ETC2, BPTC, ASTC) into RGBA; the default 3D import (resource_importer_texture.cpp:234, PRESET_3D default 2 = 'VRAM Compressed') stores these Image::Formats inside .ctex DATA_FORMAT_IMAGE. Patina current state: ctex.rs:158-176 only handles uncompressed L8/LA8/RGB8/RGBA8 and returns Unsupported (ctex.rs:164-168) for any compressed Image::Format, so VRAM-compressed .ctex artifacts (the 3D default) never load; there is no `.dds` or `.ktx` loader at all (grep empty). Implementation: add a block-decompression path (e.g. `texture2ddecoder`/`bcndecode` for BCn, plus ETC2/ASTC decoders) to gdresource; extend ctex.rs's img_format match to decode BC1/BC3/BC7/ETC2/ASTC level-0 blocks to RGBA; and add `import_dds`/`import_ktx` that parse the container header, decode level 0, and register `.dds`/`.ktx` in ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults. Wiring requirement: a VRAM-compressed .ctex and a loose .dds/.ktx each load to a Texture2D with real RGBA pixels through the standard registry path.
acceptance_criteria: load_resource on a BC1/BC3-compressed .ctex (inner Image::Format S3TC) returns a Texture2D with a populated `pixels` array (not Unsupported); load_resource('tex.dds') and load_resource('tex.ktx') decode a known block-compressed reference to the expected RGBA. (test: `gpu_texture_container_import`)

title: InputMap: inject Godot's built-in ui_* default actions (with default key/joy events) at project load
description:
[audit-key: input/input-defaults] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth (input_map.cpp get_builtins/load_from_project_settings): ~28 ui_* actions with default events are registered automatically; a project.godot [input] entry overrides only the actions it names, the rest keep engine defaults. Patina current: no default set is injected at runtime (grep for ui_focus_next/ui_select/ui_text_* empty); only a 6-action editor-Play map exists (gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:880). Approach: add a builtins table to gdplatform InputMap (ui_accept=Enter/Space/pad-A, ui_cancel=Escape, ui_left/right/up/down=arrows+dpad+stick, ui_focus_next=Tab, ui_focus_prev=Shift+Tab, ui_select=Space, ui_page_up/down, ui_home/end, ui_cut/copy/paste, ui_undo/redo, ui_text_* editing set, ui_menu, ui_swap_input_direction, with per-action deadzone 0.5) and call it from the project.godot load path (load_from_project_godot) so declared actions override and undeclared built-ins remain. Wiring requirement: after MainLoop loads a project with no [input] section, Input.is_action_pressed("ui_focus_next") responds to Tab in a running scene.
acceptance_criteria: Booting a scene from a project.godot lacking an [input] section, pressing Tab makes Input.is_action_pressed("ui_focus_next") true and pressing Enter makes Input.is_action_pressed("ui_accept") true; a project that declares its own ui_accept overrides only that action while ui_cancel/ui_focus_next keep defaults (test: `default_ui_actions_e2e`).

title: Input: wire browser Gamepad source (getGamepads polling + standard mapping + joy_connection_changed + Input joy_* methods and rumble)
description:
[audit-key: input/input-web-sources] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot ground truth: on web, Godot polls navigator.getGamepads() each frame, maps the 'standard' layout to JoyButton/JoyAxis, fires joy_connection_changed on connect/disconnect, exposes is_joy_button_pressed/get_joy_axis/get_connected_joypads/get_joy_name/get_joy_guid and start_joy_vibration (navigator gamepad.vibrationActuator). Patina current: the model exists (gdplatform/src/input.rs GamepadButton/GamepadAxis + InputState tracking) but has no producer — no browser polling (grep getGamepads empty), no joy Input methods in the interpreter, joy_connection_changed unemitted. Approach: in the editor Play served JS (editor_ui.rs) poll getGamepads each rAF and POST button/axis deltas to a new /api/runtime/input/gamepad endpoint that push_event's InputEvent::GamepadButton/GamepadAxis into the MainLoop InputState with standard-mapping normalization + deadzone; add Input.is_joy_button_pressed/get_joy_axis/get_connected_joypads/get_joy_name and start_joy_vibration to the interpreter; emit joy_connection_changed. Wiring requirement: a controller press reaches Input.is_joy_button_pressed / a bound action in a running scene.
acceptance_criteria: With a simulated connected gamepad, feeding a face-button-down and a left-stick-X value through the gamepad endpoint makes Input.is_joy_button_pressed(0, JOY_BUTTON_A)==true and Input.get_joy_axis(0, JOY_AXIS_LEFT_X) return the (deadzoned) value in a running scene, and get_connected_joypads() lists device 0 (test: `gamepad_input_e2e`).

title: HTTP: wire HTTPRequest as a script node with HTTPS/TLS, gzip, request_raw, download-to-file & progress
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/multiplayer_http] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot ground truth: HTTPRequest is a Node; request(url, headers, method, body) (or request_raw with PackedByteArray) drives an internal HTTPClient over http(s), decompresses gzip when accept_gzip is set, follows redirects, enforces body_size_limit, can stream to a download_file in download_chunk_size chunks, exposes get_downloaded_bytes/get_body_size/get_http_client_status for progress, and emits request_completed(result, code, headers, body). It is polled each frame via NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PROCESS. On the web export the transport is the browser fetch/XHR (raw sockets unavailable). Patina current state: HTTPRequest (gdplatform/src/http_request.rs) is a Rust struct with a background std::thread (:305) over a native TcpStream HttpClient — not a scene node, not callable from GDScript, and https:// returns SslHandshakeError (http_client.rs:451-454; test http_request.rs:487) with gzip explicitly disabled (http_client.rs:268). Implementation approach: register HTTPRequest as a gdscene Node whose internal-process poll runs from MainLoop and emits request_completed to connected script callbacks; add a TLS backend (rustls) for https and a fetch-based transport under the wasm target; add accept_gzip decompression, request_raw, download_file/download_chunk_size, body_size_limit, and get_downloaded_bytes/get_body_size/get_http_client_status; expose request()/cancel_request() as GDScript methods. Wiring requirement: a script in a loaded scene adds an HTTPRequest node, connects request_completed, calls request(https_url), and the MainLoop frame poll delivers the decompressed body to the callback.
acceptance_criteria: A MainLoop-driven scene whose script calls HTTPRequest.request() against a loopback TLS test server (https) receives request_completed with result==RESULT_SUCCESS, the correct 200 code, and a gzip-decompressed body — with no manual poll() and no SslHandshakeError. (test: `http_request_node_e2e_test`) runnable via cargo nextest --test http_request_node_e2e_test.

title: GDScript: parse annotation arguments and carry @export hint metadata into ExportInfo
description:
[audit-key: gdscript/gdscript-grammar] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: annotations take argument lists — @export_range(min,max,step,...), @export_enum("A","B"), @export_flags(...), @export_file("*.png"), @export_node_path("Node2D"), @export_multiline, @export_group/@export_subgroup/@export_category(name), @rpc("any_peer","call_local","reliable",channel), @warning_ignore("code"), @icon("path"), @export_custom(hint, hint_string) (see gdscript_parser.cpp _parse_annotation / register_annotation). Each produces a PropertyInfo with a PROPERTY_HINT_* + hint_string that drives the inspector editor. Patina current state: parser.rs:518-538 reads only the @name token and never consumes a parenthesized arg list, so parser.rs:540 errors with 'var or func declaration after annotation' on ANY parametrized annotation — the whole script fails to parse (confirmed: no tests exercise args; parser.rs:179 Annotation is name-only; interpreter.rs:380 ExportInfo has no hint fields). Approach: extend the Annotation struct to hold Vec<Expr> args; in parse_annotated_stmt consume an optional '(' ... ')' argument list after the name (reuse parse_call_args). Extend ExportInfo (interpreter.rs:378) with hint kind + hint_string + args, populate it in run_class where @export is detected (interpreter.rs:4700), mapping export_range/enum/flags/file/dir/multiline/node_path/color_no_alpha/group/subgroup/category to Godot PropertyHint values. Store @rpc config on the FuncDef and @warning_ignore/@icon on the class. Wiring requirement: a .gd with parametrized exports must parse, attach in patina-runner attach_scripts (main.rs:186), and the resolved ExportInfo (name+hint+hint_string) must be reachable via ScriptInstance::list_properties so the editor inspector/property list can consume it.
acceptance_criteria: A scene whose node has a script using @export_range(0,100,5) var speed, @export_enum("Idle","Run") var state, @export_group("Movement"), and @rpc("any_peer") func hit() loads without a parse error, the node's script attaches, and list_properties() reports 'speed' with a range hint and hint_string '0,100,5' plus 'state' with an enum hint 'Idle,Run'. Test: `gdscript_export_annotations_wired` (cargo nextest --test gdscript_export_annotations_wired) parses+instantiates such a script end-to-end and asserts the exported property hints, not just that it parses. (test: `gdscript_export_annotations_wired`)

title: WebSocket: add wss + WebSocketMultiplayerPeer wired to MultiplayerAPI + browser transport
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/multiplayer_websocket] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot ground truth: WebSocketPeer connects to ws://wss:// (or accept_stream for server), negotiates subprotocols and handshake headers, and exposes buffer/no-delay/heartbeat knobs; WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.create_client/create_server implements the MultiplayerPeer interface so an @rpc game runs over WebSocket — this is the PRIMARY in-scope multiplayer transport on the web (Godot web export uses the browser WebSocket API). Patina current state: gdplatform/src/websocket_peer.rs is a correct native RFC6455 CLIENT (frame codec + handshake tested) but rejects wss (:364-366), has no server accept path wired, is not script-reachable, and has no WebSocketMultiplayerPeer (unregistered). Native TcpStream will not compile/run on wasm. Implementation approach: add a TLS layer (rustls) for wss and a browser-WebSocket transport under the wasm target behind the same WebSocketPeer API; add accept_stream + the missing protocol/header/buffer methods; implement WebSocketMultiplayerPeer (create_client/create_server) as a NetworkPeer/MultiplayerPeer feeding the SceneTree-owned MultiplayerAPI (from the core-wiring bead); register both classes and expose WebSocketPeer to GDScript. Wiring requirement: MultiplayerAPI.set_multiplayer_peer(WebSocketMultiplayerPeer) on both ends, MainLoop poll drives connect + packet flow, and an @rpc crosses the WS link.
acceptance_criteria: A server MainLoop with WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.create_server and a client with create_client (loopback ws, plus a wss variant against a TLS test server) reach CONNECTION_CONNECTED via frame poll, emit peer_connected, and an @rpc call from the client runs on the server node. (test: `websocket_multiplayer_e2e_test`) runnable via cargo nextest --test websocket_multiplayer_e2e_test.

comments.author: GentleBadger
comments.text: PARTIAL delivery by GentleBadger (2026-07-16, uncommitted). DONE: WebSocketMultiplayerPeer transport core — gdplatform/src/websocket_multiplayer.rs (new, no new deps; reuses existing RFC6455 codec + handshake helpers), registered in lib.rs, + tests/websocket_multiplayer_e2e_test.rs (9 tests: handshake->CONNECTION_CONNECTED, peer_connected signal, both-way packets, 70KiB extended-length frame, unknown-peer error, MultiplayerAPI both ends, distinct peer ids). NOT COMPILED (worker cargo hook blocks; verifier is first compile). KEEP OPEN — REMAINING: (1) wss:// TLS via rustls (create_client('wss://') still errors TlsUnsupported; a test pins this so it fails loudly when TLS lands); (2) browser/wasm transport (native TcpStream won't build on wasm32; env-blocked, no wasm-bindgen per pat-u3l8c.109); (3) @rpc across WS via gdscene MainLoop (gdplatform tests can't reach gdscene — dep direction); (4) WebSocketPeer.accept_stream + protocol/header/buffer knobs.

title: Camera2D: compute the active-camera canvas transform each frame (limits, smoothing, drag margins, zoom) and apply it to the rendered viewport
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/nodes2d-camera] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: STUB]

GROUND TRUTH: Camera2D sets the viewport canvas_transform: the enabled/current camera centers on its global position offset by `offset`, clamped to limit_left/top/right/bottom (with limit_smoothed), eased by position_smoothing_speed when position_smoothing_enabled, constrained by drag_left/top/right/bottom_margin when drag_*_enabled, scaled by `zoom`, per anchor_mode (Fixed TopLeft / Drag Center); processed on process_callback (idle/physics). Methods: align(), reset_smoothing(), get_screen_center_position(), force_update_scroll() (upstream/godot/scene/2d/camera_2d.cpp). PATINA STATE: Camera2D is a bare registered class (class_db.rs:726) with only zoom/current property helpers (node2d.rs:319-340); no per-frame logic and no view transform anywhere. APPROACH: Add a camera_2d step invoked from MainLoop::step (gdscene/src/main_loop.rs) that, each frame, finds the current/enabled Camera2D under the active viewport, computes the canvas transform (limits+drag+smoothing+zoom+anchor), and stores it on the viewport/tree so the render bridge (nodes2d-render-bridge) offsets drawing by it; implement align/reset_smoothing/get_screen_center_position as script-callable methods. WIRING REQUIREMENT: depends on the render bridge to have a view to move; the camera transform must reach the pixels.
acceptance_criteria: A scene with a Camera2D marked current whose global position exceeds its limit_left produces a screen-center-position clamped to the limit, and a sprite at world origin renders shifted by the camera transform in the viewport output (not at raw world coords). (test: `camera2d_scroll_and_limit_wiring`)

title: TileMapLayer: parse tile_map_data + TileSet atlas from the scene and draw tiles in the viewport
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/nodes2d-tilemap] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

GROUND TRUTH: TileMapLayer stores its cells in a `tile_map_data` PackedByteArray (per-cell: coords, source_id, atlas_coords, alternative_tile) and references a TileSet whose atlas sources map (source_id, atlas_coords) to a texture sub-rect; the layer draws every used cell at map_to_local(cell) under its transform (upstream/godot/scene/2d/tile_map_layer.cpp, scene/resources/2d/tile_set.cpp). PATINA STATE: tilemap.rs models a TileMapStore but nothing loads tile_map_data or the TileSet, and it is never rendered. APPROACH: (1) decode the tile_map_data PackedByteArray in the scene loader (or a TileMapLayer post-load hook) into TileMapStore keyed by NodeId; (2) load the TileSet + TileSetAtlasSource (texture, tile_size, region per atlas coord) from the [sub_resource type="TileSet"]; (3) in the render bridge, emit a DrawTextureRegion per used cell at map_to_local. WIRING REQUIREMENT: TileMapStore must be populated from the parsed scene and consumed by the renderer.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn with a TileMapLayer carrying a tile_map_data with 3 painted cells and an atlas TileSet populates get_used_cells() with those 3 cells and draws 3 textured tiles at their map_to_local positions in the viewport framebuffer. (test: `tilemap_layer_load_and_render_wiring`)

title: RayCast2D/ShapeCast2D: implement the 2D cast nodes and update them from the physics tick
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/nodes2d-raycast-shapecast] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

GROUND TRUTH: RayCast2D casts a segment from its origin to target_position each physics frame (when enabled), querying the 2D space with collision_mask/collide_with_areas/collide_with_bodies/hit_from_inside/exclude, exposing is_colliding/get_collider/get_collision_point/get_collision_normal and force_raycast_update(). ShapeCast2D sweeps a shape and returns up to max_results contacts (upstream/godot/scene/2d/ray_cast_2d.cpp, shape_cast_2d.cpp). PATINA STATE: entirely absent for 2D (only 3D exists in raycast3d.rs/shapecast3d.rs); classes unregistered. APPROACH: register RayCast2D/ShapeCast2D in class_db, add gdscene/src/raycast2d.rs mirroring raycast3d.rs but calling the 2D DirectSpaceState (gdphysics2d/gdscene physics_server intersect_ray/intersect_shape), and add a per-physics-frame update in MainLoop::step that refreshes enabled casts before scripts read them. WIRING REQUIREMENT: is_colliding must reflect the physics world after a MainLoop physics tick.
acceptance_criteria: A RayCast2D (enabled) aimed at a StaticBody2D in a loaded .tscn reports is_colliding()==true with the body as collider and the correct collision_point after one MainLoop physics step; aimed away it reports false. (test: `raycast2d_physics_tick_wiring`)

title: Node3D: add look_at/rotate/translate/to_local/to_global, top_level, and visible-in-tree propagation
description:
[audit-key: nodes-3d/nodes3d-node3d] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot Node3D (scene/3d/node_3d.cpp, 71 methods) provides look_at/look_at_from_position, rotate/rotate_x/y/z/rotate_object_local, translate/translate_object_local, to_local/to_global, orthonormalize, global_position/global_rotation/global_basis accessors, rotation_order (all 6 EulerOrder), quaternion/basis edit modes, top_level (ignore parent transform), visibility_parent, and NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED. Patina's node3d.rs has position/rotation/scale/transform composition and a parent-chain get_global_transform (:100) but none of these methods, no top_level handling, and is_visible (:138) checks only the local flag. Approach: add the transform methods to node3d.rs (build on gdcore Basis/Transform3D), honor a `top_level` property in get_global_transform by resetting the accumulated parent transform, add is_visible_in_tree walking parents and switch render_server_3d.rs sync_mesh_instances/sync_lights and viewport_3d.rs collect_scene_content to use it, add a `rotation_order` property consumed by get_local_transform, and register the missing Node3D properties in class_db.rs. Wiring: .tscn with `top_level=true` / hidden parent -> get_global_transform / is_visible_in_tree -> renderer draw list; a script calling look_at() rotates the node the renderer draws.
acceptance_criteria: A scene where a visible MeshInstance3D is a child of a hidden Node3D does not render the mesh (is_visible_in_tree false); a `top_level=true` child ignores parent translation; a script `node.look_at(target)` orients the node so its -Z faces the target in the rendered frame. (test: `node3d_look_at_toplevel_and_visibility_propagation_from_scene`)

title: Camera3D: compile+wire projection/frustum module and expose project_ray/unproject to GDScript
description:
[audit-key: nodes-3d/nodes3d-camera] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot Camera3D exposes project_ray_origin/project_ray_normal/project_position/unproject_position/is_position_behind/get_frustum plus keep_aspect, cull_mask, frustum_offset, orthographic `size`, and doppler_tracking (scene/3d/camera_3d.cpp). Patina has a full implementation in camera3d.rs (frustum, projection modes, keep_aspect, doppler — 37 tests) that is orphaned: it is not declared as a module (`grep 'mod camera3d'` empty), so it never compiles or runs, and the renderer instead uses node3d.rs's fov/near/far only (render_server_3d.rs build_viewport:348). Approach: declare `pub mod camera3d;` in gdscene/lib.rs, reconcile it with node3d.rs camera helpers, use camera3d projection to build the Viewport3D projection (respecting keep_aspect/frustum_offset/orthographic size), register the missing Camera3D properties in class_db.rs:431, and add scripting.rs dispatch for project_ray_origin/project_ray_normal/unproject_position/project_position/make_current. Wiring: .tscn Camera3D -> camera3d projection -> render_server_3d viewport; script project_ray_normal(mouse_pos) returns a ray usable for picking.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a scene with a Camera3D and calling project_ray_origin/project_ray_normal for a screen point returns a ray whose unproject_position round-trips a known world point back to that screen point; an orthographic Camera3D with a set `size` renders at the correct scale. (test: `camera3d_project_and_unproject_from_scene`)

title: MeshInstance3D: register GeometryInstance3D base and apply material_overlay/transparency/gi_mode/custom_aabb/surface overrides
description:
[audit-key: nodes-3d/nodes3d-geominstance] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot MeshInstance3D inherits GeometryInstance3D (material_override, material_overlay, transparency, cast_shadow enum, gi_mode, extra_cull_margin, lod_bias, visibility_range + fade mode, custom AABB) and VisualInstance3D (layers, get_aabb). Patina registers MeshInstance3D directly under Node3D (class_db.rs:441) so the entire GeometryInstance3D property surface is missing, and sync_mesh_instances (render_server_3d.rs:389) applies only material_override / surface_material_override/0. Approach: register VisualInstance3D and GeometryInstance3D in the class_db.rs 3D table and reparent MeshInstance3D/MultiMeshInstance3D/Sprite3D/Label3D/GPUParticles3D through GeometryInstance3D, add the GeometryInstance3D properties; extend sync_mesh_instances to read and apply material_overlay (as next_pass), transparency (instance alpha), a surface_override_material array (not just index 0), custom_aabb, and layer cull mask; read blend_shape/blendshape values and skin/skeleton assignment onto the render instance. Wiring: .tscn MeshInstance3D with material_overlay/transparency -> render instance -> pixels reflect the overlay/alpha.
acceptance_criteria: A scene MeshInstance3D with `transparency=0.5` renders at half opacity and with a `material_overlay` renders the overlay pass over the base material; a per-surface `surface_material_override/1` is honored for surface 1; GeometryInstance3D is present in ClassDB with MeshInstance3D inheriting it. (test: `mesh_instance3d_geometry_instance_overrides_from_scene`)

title: Physics2D: rotation-aware SAT narrowphase + capsule/segment/convex/world-boundary shapes
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-shapes] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot ground truth (godot_collision_solver_2d_sat.cpp): narrowphase is rotation-aware via SAT for all shape pairs; shapes include circle, rectangle, capsule, segment, world-boundary (infinite half-plane), separation-ray, convex-polygon, concave-polygon. Patina state: only axis-aligned circle/rect pairs collide (collision.rs:39-84, other pairs -> None); rotation is thrown away because every caller builds Transform2D::translated(pos) (world.rs:273, character.rs:83, area2d.rs:146); Shape2D lacks WorldBoundary/SeparationRay/Convex/Concave (shape.rs:11); shape sub-resources unregistered and physics_server only parses CircleShape2D/RectangleShape2D (physics_server.rs:82-116). Approach: extend Shape2D with WorldBoundary{normal,distance}, SeparationRay{length}, ConvexPolygon{points}, and give shapes a rotation; rewrite test_collision as a rotation-aware SAT solver (rect-rect OBB, capsule as segment+radius, convex GJK/SAT, world-boundary half-plane) driving the same CollisionResult; pass body.rotation into the transforms at the call sites (world.rs:273, character.rs, area2d.rs); register the *Shape2D resource classes in class_db.rs and parse CollisionShape2D.shape sub-resource + CollisionPolygon2D in physics_server shape_from_node. Wiring requirement: a .tscn with a rotated RectangleShape2D StaticBody and a CircleShape2D RigidBody, plus a WorldBoundaryShape2D floor, resolves collisions correctly through MainLoop.step.
acceptance_criteria: Scene-loaded RigidBody2D (circle) rests on a rotated RectangleShape2D ramp and slides along the incline (not on a horizontal AABB edge), and a WorldBoundaryShape2D stops a falling body at the plane; a capsule-vs-rect pair collides instead of passing through. (test: `rotation_aware_narrowphase_scene_parity`)

title: Physics2D: implement RayCast2D + ShapeCast2D nodes wired to the physics tick
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-raycast] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth (ray_cast_2d.cpp, shape_cast_2d.cpp): RayCast2D updates each physics frame (enabled), casting target_position from its transform, exposing is_colliding()/get_collider()/get_collider_shape()/get_collision_point()/get_collision_normal(), force_raycast_update(), add_exception/clear, exclude_parent, collide_with_areas/collide_with_bodies, hit_from_inside; ShapeCast2D sweeps a shape and returns multiple results + collision_count + closest fraction. Patina state: neither node exists at runtime — RayCast2D is only a class_defaults property stub (class_defaults.rs:213), not registered (class_db.rs), and world.raycast (world.rs:339-361) is internal-only with no exclusions/masks/area toggles. Approach: extend gdphysics2d world raycast to accept exclude set, collision_mask, collide_with_areas/bodies and hit_from_inside, and add a shape-sweep query; register RayCast2D/ShapeCast2D in class_db; add per-node cast state to PhysicsServer, update all enabled RayCast2D/ShapeCast2D each physics tick in step order (main_loop.rs physics phase) writing is_colliding/collider/point/normal back to node properties; dispatch get_collider/get_collision_point/force_raycast_update etc. from the interpreter. Wiring requirement: a .tscn RayCast2D pointing at a StaticBody2D reports is_colliding()==true and the correct collider ObjectId after MainLoop.step, and stops colliding when the target moves away.
acceptance_criteria: A scene-loaded RayCast2D aimed at a StaticBody2D returns is_colliding()==true, get_collider() == the body's ObjectId, and get_collision_normal() facing the ray after one MainLoop physics tick; moving the target out of range flips is_colliding() to false; a ShapeCast2D reports collision_count>0 against an overlapping body. (test: `raycast2d_shapecast2d_physics_tick`)

title: Physics2D: register + wire Joint2D nodes (pin/groove/damped-spring) from scene into world
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-joints] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot ground truth (joints/*.cpp): Joint2D subclasses resolve node_a/node_b NodePaths to two bodies and create a physics-server joint with bias, disable_collision; PinJoint2D adds softness + angular limits + motor; GrooveJoint2D constrains body_b to a groove segment on body_a; DampedSpringJoint2D has length/rest_length/stiffness/damping. Patina state: joint.rs implements Pin + DampedSpring and world.step applies them (world.rs:180-198) with green tests, but nothing creates joints from the scene — register_bodies (physics_server.rs:297) skips joints, and the joint classes are unregistered (class_db.rs). GrooveJoint2D has no implementation. Approach: register Joint2D/PinJoint2D/GrooveJoint2D/DampedSpringJoint2D in class_db with their properties (node_a, node_b, bias, disable_collision, softness, length/rest_length/stiffness/damping); implement GrooveJoint2D constraint in joint.rs; in PhysicsServer add joint registration that resolves node_a/node_b to BodyIds and calls world.add_joint, and add the jointed pair to the collision-skip set (already supported via jointed_pairs in world.rs:201). Wiring requirement: a .tscn with two RigidBody2D and a PinJoint2D between them keeps their anchor distance fixed across MainLoop.step (they swing together, not apart).
acceptance_criteria: A scene-loaded PinJoint2D between two RigidBody2D holds them at the anchor after 30 MainLoop physics ticks (distance ~constant), and a DampedSpringJoint2D converges the pair toward its rest_length. (test: `joint2d_scene_wiring_parity`)

title: GDScript: drive coroutine/await resumption from the SceneTree tick and bind awaited values
description:
[audit-key: gdscript/gdscript-coroutines] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot ground truth: 'await sig' suspends the function, returns a GDScriptFunctionState, and resumes with the signal's argument(s) when the signal emits or the awaited coroutine finishes (gdscript_vm.cpp OPCODE_AWAIT). 'await get_tree().create_timer(1.0).timeout' and 'var frame = await RenderingServer.frame_post_draw' are ubiquitous. Patina current state: the suspension machinery exists and is unit-tested but is never driven at runtime — poll_coroutines/notify_await_signal/tick_coroutine_frames (interpreter.rs:796-821) have zero callers outside interpreter.rs #[cfg(test)] (lines 9830-9935); ScriptInstance (bindings.rs:129) has no poll hook; await is statement-only (parser.rs:1030) and the resumed value is dropped (interpreter.rs:711). Approach: (1) add `poll_coroutines(&mut self, delta)` and `notify_await_signal(&mut self, name, args)` to the ScriptInstance trait (bindings.rs) and implement them on GDScriptNodeInstance (scripting.rs) by forwarding to the interpreter. (2) In SceneTree/MainLoop each frame, after process dispatch and after every emit_signal (scene_tree.rs:1102), call notify_await_signal on all attached scripts and poll_coroutines(delta); also route SceneTreeTimer timeouts (scene_tree.rs take_timeout_signals) into notify_await_signal. (3) Make `await` an expression (add to parse_unary/parse_primary in parser.rs) whose value is the resumed signal arg(s), and thread the resumed Variant back into the suspended frame's binding. Wiring requirement: the per-frame loop in patina-runner/gdscene must resume parked coroutines.
acceptance_criteria: A scripted node running under MainLoop that does `func _ready(): var t = get_tree().create_timer(0.1); await t.timeout; done = true` has `done == true` after enough frames elapse to fire the timer, and `var v = await sig` binds the emitted argument. Test: `gdscript_await_resumes_at_runtime` (cargo nextest --test gdscript_await_resumes_at_runtime) builds a SceneTree+MainLoop, attaches such a script, steps frames, and asserts the post-await statement executed and the awaited value was bound — proving resumption via the tick, not a direct interpreter poll. (test: `gdscript_await_resumes_at_runtime`)

title: Physics3D: rotation-aware GJK/SAT narrowphase pair matrix + missing shapes + layer/mask broadphase
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/physics3d-narrowphase] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot's 3D solver (godot_collision_solver_3d.cpp) collides every shape pair with orientation via GJK/EPA/SAT and filters pairs by collision_layer & collision_mask before narrowphase. Patina's solver only does axis-aligned Sphere-Sphere, Sphere-Box, Box-Box (collision.rs:161-184, `_ => NONE`); capsule/cylinder/convex/trimesh/worldboundary/heightmap never collide; box-box is AABB-only (collision.rs:112) ignoring body.rotation (body.rs:58); and world.rs:116-214 applies no layer/mask filter so all bodies collide regardless of layers. Shape3D (shape.rs:8-23) is missing HeightMapShape3D and SeparationRayShape3D; no SphereShape3D/BoxShape3D/etc. Resource classes are registered (unregistered.txt) so CollisionShape3D.shape is a bare String (physics_server_3d.rs:61-92) and convex/concave shapes carry empty geometry (physics_server_3d.rs:86-87). Implementation: extend collision.rs with an orientation-aware SAT/GJK path (feed body.rotation into a support-function based test) covering Box(OBB)/Capsule/Cylinder/Convex/Trimesh/WorldBoundary; add HeightMapShape3D + SeparationRayShape3D to Shape3D; register the Shape3D resource classes in class_db.rs and make shape_from_node_3d read real dimensions AND convex points / concave faces / heightmap data from the shape resource; add a layer&mask gate in world.rs:117-121 before test_collision. Wiring: the path must run inside PhysicsWorld3D::step which MainLoop already calls (main_loop.rs:408).
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a stack of BoxShape3D RigidBody3D on a StaticBody3D box floor, run through MainLoop::step for ~60 frames, settles resting on the floor (boxes do not interpenetrate or fall through, and an OBB rotated 45deg still collides); two rigid bodies whose collision_layer/mask do not intersect pass through each other. (test: `physics3d_box_stack_settles_via_mainloop`)

title: Physics3D: complete RigidBody3D property bridge + inertia tensor, lock_rotation, damp modes, physics material, constant force/torque, contact signals
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/physics3d-rigidbody] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot RigidBody3D exposes inertia (custom tensor), center_of_mass[_mode], lock_rotation, linear/angular_damp_mode (combine/replace), physics_material_override (friction/bounce/rough/absorbent), constant_force/constant_torque, custom_integrator via _integrate_forces(PhysicsDirectBodyState3D), continuous_cd, contact_monitor+max_contacts_reported, and emits body_entered/body_shape_entered/sleeping_state_changed. Patina registers only mass/gravity_scale/freeze (class_db.rs:523-529) and the bridge reads only mass+collision_layer (physics_server_3d.rs:181-198); angular integration fakes inertia as scalar mass (body.rs:196,215,247); there are no rotation axis locks, damp modes, physics material, constant forces, custom integrator, or contact signals. Implementation: register the missing RigidBody3D properties + PhysicsMaterial resource; extend sync_to_physics to transfer them into PhysicsBody3D; add an inertia tensor (from shape) used in apply_torque/apply_impulse_at_position and angular integration; add per-axis lock flags honored in integrate(); add constant_force/torque accumulation; compute friction/bounce from physics_material_override; add contact-signal emission in a new 3D processor called by MainLoop. (CCD swept collision may be a follow-up sub-task.) Wiring: node properties set in a .tscn must change simulated behavior through MainLoop::step, and a monitored contact must emit body_entered.
acceptance_criteria: A RigidBody3D .tscn with lock_rotation=true and a physics_material_override (bounce=0.9) dropped onto a floor via MainLoop::step bounces to ~0.9x height and never rotates, and a contact_monitor body emits body_entered on impact. (test: `rigid_body_3d_material_and_locks_via_mainloop`)

title: Physics3D: re-sync moving Static/Kinematic body transforms each frame, write rotation back, add AnimatableBody3D + StaticBody3D constant velocity
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/physics3d-kinematic-sync] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot pushes StaticBody3D/AnimatableBody3D/CharacterBody3D transforms into the physics server every frame (AnimatableBody3D with sync_to_physics moves other bodies as a platform), applies StaticBody3D.constant_linear_velocity/constant_angular_velocity as surface motion (conveyors), and reflects body rotation back to the node. Patina's bridge only registers new bodies and never updates existing ones (physics_server_3d.rs:202-203), writes back position only for Rigid bodies and never rotation (physics_server_3d.rs:232-241), lacks AnimatableBody3D (unregistered), and has no constant-velocity support.
