Implementation: in sync_to_physics, for already-tracked non-rigid bodies read the node's current global transform and update body.position AND body.rotation; register AnimatableBody3D (parent PhysicsBody3D) and treat it as a moving kinematic body that imparts velocity to contacts; add constant_linear_velocity/constant_angular_velocity fields to PhysicsBody3D applied as surface velocity in the friction/contact resolution (world.rs); in sync_from_physics write body.rotation to the node via node3d::set_rotation for rigid bodies. Wiring: driven each MainLoop physics sub-step (main_loop.rs:407-409).
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn AnimatableBody3D platform whose position is advanced by a script each frame carries a RigidBody3D resting on it (the rigid body's X tracks the platform) through MainLoop::step; a spinning RigidBody3D's node rotation updates (get_rotation changes). (test: `animatable_body_3d_platform_carries_via_mainloop`)

title: Physics3D: expose PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D to GDScript (intersect_ray/point/shape, cast_motion, collide_shape, get_rest_info) + query param classes
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/physics3d-spacestate] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot scripts query the 3D world through get_world_3d().direct_space_state with PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D/PhysicsPointQueryParameters3D/PhysicsShapeQueryParameters3D and get back Dictionaries (position, normal, collider, rid, shape). Patina exposes none of this to scripts (grep in gdscript-interop finds no intersect_ray/direct_space_state; the classes are unregistered) even though gdphysics3d/query.rs has ray + shape-overlap structs. Missing query kinds entirely: intersect_point, cast_motion, collide_shape, get_rest_info. Implementation: register PhysicsRay/Point/ShapeQueryParameters3D as script-constructible classes; add a PhysicsDirectSpaceState3D binding backed by the live PhysicsServer3D world (physics_server_3d.rs) that runs intersect_ray/intersect_point/intersect_shape/cast_motion/collide_shape/get_rest_info and returns Godot-shaped result Dictionaries with the resolving NodeId as `collider`; expose it via get_world_3d().direct_space_state (or PhysicsServer3D singleton). Add intersect_point/cast_motion/collide_shape/get_rest_info to query.rs. Wiring: a GDScript calling direct_space_state.intersect_ray during _physics_process must return the hit body from the live MainLoop scene.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript in a .tscn calls get_world_3d().direct_space_state.intersect_ray(PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D.create(from,to)) during _physics_process and receives a Dictionary whose `collider` is the StaticBody3D the ray hits, verified after MainLoop::step. (test: `direct_space_state_3d_intersect_ray_from_script`)

title: Physics3D: tick RayCast3D/ShapeCast3D/SpringArm3D each physics frame through MainLoop
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/physics3d-querynodes] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

In Godot, enabled RayCast3D/ShapeCast3D update automatically every physics frame and SpringArm3D shortens its length to the nearest obstacle; scripts read is_colliding()/get_collider()/get_collision_point() or the arm's resulting child transform. Patina implemented raycast3d::process/shapecast3d::process/springarm3d::process (gdscene) and registered the nodes (class_db.rs:556-587), but no runtime code calls the process functions (grep finds only tests) so these nodes are inert during play. Implementation: add a PhysicsServer3D-aware pass in MainLoop's physics sub-step that iterates enabled RayCast3D/ShapeCast3D/SpringArm3D nodes and calls their process() against the live physics server (respecting collision_mask, exclude_parent, collide_with_bodies/areas), caching hit results onto the nodes and applying SpringArm3D length. Wiring: called every physics tick so a script polling $RayCast3D.is_colliding() sees live results.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a RayCast3D pointing at a StaticBody3D, run through MainLoop::step, reports is_colliding()==true and get_collider() == that body without any manual force_raycast_update; moving the target out of the ray path flips is_colliding() to false the next tick. (test: `raycast_3d_is_colliding_via_mainloop`)

title: OS: implement has_feature, locale, cmdline, environment, user/config/data/cache dirs, processor/memory, delay, shell_open web surface
description:
[audit-key: platform-os/os-singleton] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot ground truth: OS is the most-called singleton in real projects — OS.has_feature("web"/"debug"/"editor"/"wasm32"/browser tags), OS.get_name() returns "Web" in the web export, OS.get_locale()/get_locale_language(), OS.get_cmdline_args()/get_cmdline_user_args() (args after --), OS.get_environment/has_environment/set_environment, OS.get_user_data_dir()/get_config_dir()/get_data_dir()/get_cache_dir() (virtual user:// on web), OS.get_unique_id(), OS.get_processor_count() (navigator.hardwareConcurrency on web), OS.get_static_memory_usage()/get_memory_info(), OS.delay_msec/usec, OS.shell_open() (window.open on web), OS.alert(); native-only OS.execute/create_process/kill return ERR_UNAVAILABLE in the web export (upstream platform/web/os_web.cpp). Patina current state: interpreter.rs:6254-6303 implements only get_name/get_ticks_msec/get_ticks_usec/is_debug_build; has_feature is absent everywhere (grep empty), so any `if OS.has_feature("web")` guard errors at runtime. gdplatform/src/os.rs has platform detection but is not script-wired. Approach: extend call_os_static in interpreter.rs with the full set; implement has_feature backed by a feature-tag set (target arch, debug/release, editor, plus project.godot feature overrides read via gdcore/src/project_settings.rs); wire cmdline args from the runner argv; map user/config/data/cache dirs to the project's user:// virtual root; return correct ERR_UNAVAILABLE-style errors for execute/create_process/kill. Wiring requirement: OS.* calls resolve through the interpreter's call_os_static in the runner MainLoop, and has_feature reflects the real build target + project feature overrides.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn script that does `visible = OS.has_feature("web")`, `loc = OS.get_locale()`, `n = OS.get_processor_count()`, and `OS.get_cmdline_user_args()` runs through the runner without UndefinedFunction, and the dumped node shows a non-empty locale, processor_count>=1, and has_feature returning a bool consistent with the build target; OS.get_name() returns "Web" under the wasm32 target build. (test: `os_singleton_feature_tags_e2e`)

title: JavaScriptBridge: real web-sys eval/get_interface/create_callback/create_object/download_buffer/force_fs_sync/pwa + script dispatch
description:
[audit-key: platform-os/js-bridge] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: STUB]

Godot ground truth: JavaScriptBridge is the required browser-integration primitive of the web export — JavaScriptBridge.eval(code, use_global_exec_context) runs JS and returns the result, get_interface(name) fetches a global (e.g. window.localStorage), create_callback(callable) returns a JS-callable proxy into GDScript, create_object(name, ...args) does `new name(...)`, download_buffer(bytes, name, mime) triggers a browser download, force_fs_sync() flushes the IDBFS/persistent user:// store, pwa_needs_update/pwa_update drive service-worker updates (upstream platform/web/javascript_bridge_singleton.cpp). Patina current state: gdplatform/src/web.rs JsBridge is a headless stub — eval() returns Undefined (web.rs:155-160), download_file only logs calls (web.rs:448), and the module explicitly says all browser calls are stubbed (web.rs:14). No web-sys/wasm-bindgen dependency exists in any Cargo.toml, and the interpreter has zero JavaScriptBridge dispatch. Approach: add wasm-bindgen + web-sys (or js-sys) as wasm32-gated deps to gdplatform, implement JsBridge::eval/get_interface/create_object/create_callback/download_buffer/force_fs_sync against real browser APIs under cfg(target_arch="wasm32") with a headless fallback for native tests, and add a `JavaScriptBridge` singleton dispatch arm in interpreter.rs routing to it. Wiring requirement: `JavaScriptBridge.eval(...)` in a scene script reaches the web-sys binding in a wasm build and the headless recorder in native tests.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn script calling `result = JavaScriptBridge.eval("1+2")` and `JavaScriptBridge.download_buffer(...)` runs through the runner: in the native/headless test the eval result and a recorded download call are observable in the dumped node/bridge log (not UndefinedFunction), proving the singleton is script-reachable end-to-end; the wasm32 target compiles with the web-sys binding gated in. (test: `javascript_bridge_eval_e2e`)

title: DisplayServer: web singleton surface — screen DPI/scale, fullscreen, clipboard, TTS, virtual keyboard, cursor shapes
description:
[audit-key: platform-os/displayserver-web] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: the web export's DisplayServer exposes screen_get_dpi()/screen_get_scale() (devicePixelRatio), window_set_mode(WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN) via the Fullscreen API, clipboard_set/clipboard_get via the async navigator.clipboard API, tts_get_voices/tts_speak/tts_pause/tts_resume/tts_stop via SpeechSynthesis (upstream platform/web/display_server_web.cpp explicitly wires TTS), virtual_keyboard_show/hide/get_height on mobile, cursor_set_shape/cursor_set_custom_image via CSS cursor, screen_get_orientation, and window_get_size from the canvas. Patina current state: DisplayServer is not script-reachable (0 dispatch in interpreter.rs), and gdplatform/src/display.rs is a native HeadlessWindow manager with get_screen_size hardcoded to 1920x1080 (display.rs:78-80) and none of the web methods; clipboard.rs is an in-memory headless stub; TTS is entirely absent (grep => 0). Approach: add a `DisplayServer` singleton dispatch arm in interpreter.rs; implement screen_get_dpi/scale, fullscreen, clipboard_get/set, tts_* (SpeechSynthesis), virtual_keyboard_* and cursor_set_shape in gdplatform against real browser APIs under wasm32 (needs the web-sys layer from the JavaScriptBridge bead) with headless fallbacks. Wiring requirement: DisplayServer.* script calls resolve through the interpreter to the gdplatform web backend in a wasm build.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn script that calls `s = DisplayServer.screen_get_scale()`, `DisplayServer.clipboard_set("hi")` then `v = DisplayServer.clipboard_get()`, and `DisplayServer.tts_speak("hello", voice)` runs through the runner without UndefinedFunction; the headless test observes clipboard round-trip ("hi") and a recorded tts_speak call in the dumped state, proving script-reachability end-to-end. (test: `display_server_web_singleton_e2e`)

title: ProjectSettings: wire GDScript singleton dispatch (get/set/has_setting, get_setting_with_override, globalize/localize_path)
description:
[audit-key: project-settings-runtime-honoring-and-script-api/projectsettings-script-api] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

GODOT: ProjectSettings is a script-reachable singleton. get_setting(name,default) returns the Variant value (or default), set_setting mutates, has_setting queries, get_setting_with_override applies feature-tag overrides, globalize_path converts res://user:// to absolute OS paths and localize_path the reverse (upstream core/config/project_settings.cpp; doc/classes/ProjectSettings.xml).

PATINA: None of it is reachable from scripts. interpreter.rs:1542-1565 dispatches Input/OS/Engine/Time/JSON/FileAccess/DirAccess but has zero ProjectSettings branch (grep count 0). globalize_path/localize_path have no implementation anywhere. The only ProjectSettings store, gdcore/src/project_settings.rs, is orphaned (no mod project_settings in gdcore - not compiled).

APPROACH: (1) Un-orphan/compile a runtime settings store: add pub mod project_settings; to gdcore/src/lib.rs (or build the store in gdscene) and widen its value type to the real gdvariant::Variant (current SettingsValue enum cannot hold arrays/dicts/PackedStringArray). Seed it from ProjectLoader at boot and hold it where the interpreter can read it. (2) Add a ProjectSettings branch in interpreter.rs singleton dispatch (mirror call_os_static) routing get_setting/set_setting/has_setting/clear/get_setting_with_override to the store. (3) Implement globalize_path/localize_path on top of gdcore::file_access::{resolve_path,project_root,user_root} (already exported). WIRING: a script calling ProjectSettings.get_setting must return the value loaded from the project's project.godot, observable in the runner JSON dump.
acceptance_criteria: A scene whose script does func _ready(): var g = ProjectSettings.get_setting("physics/2d/default_gravity", 111.0); ProjectSettings.set_setting("custom/x", 7); assert(ProjectSettings.has_setting("application/config/name")); var p = ProjectSettings.globalize_path("res://a.txt") run through the runner boot path produces g == the project's declared gravity, custom/x readable back as 7, has_setting true, and p an absolute path ending in a.txt. (test: gdscript_project_settings_singleton)

title: ProjectSettings: load InputMap actions from project.godot [input] into the runtime InputMap at boot
description:
[audit-key: project-settings-runtime-honoring-and-script-api/projectsettings-inputmap] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

GODOT: On startup InputMap::load_from_project_settings() reads every [input] action from project.godot (name, deadzone, event list) so Input.is_action_pressed("jump") works for project-defined actions (upstream core/input/input_map.cpp). Default ui_* actions are also registered from ProjectSettings.

PATINA: ProjectLoader::get_input_map() (gdresource/src/project.rs:339) parses [input] into InputMapEntry but nothing consumes it - grep shows only defs/tests. The runner never seeds an InputMap from the project; runtime action tables are hardcoded demo strings (gdscene/scripting.rs:3554, editor_server.rs:882). A project's custom actions therefore never exist at runtime.

APPROACH: At boot in patina-runner, after ProjectLoader::load, iterate get_input_map() and register each action (name + deadzone + mapped events) into the runtime InputMap used by gdplatform/src/input.rs / the SceneTree input snapshot feeding MainLoop. Ensure the default ui_* action set is registered from a canonical default table, not per-demo. WIRING: project [input] -> runtime InputMap -> Input.is_action_pressed in a script.
acceptance_criteria: Booting the runner on a project whose project.godot [input] defines jump={deadzone,events:[InputEventKey keycode Space]}, then injecting a Space key press, makes a script's Input.is_action_pressed("jump") return true and the action's deadzone match the project value - proven end-to-end through boot, not by manually populating the map. (test: project_input_map_honored)

title: GDScript: resolve @GlobalScope enum constants (KEY_*/OK/FAILED/ERR_*/MOUSE_BUTTON_*/PROPERTY_HINT_*/alignment/TYPE_*) in the VM
description:
[audit-key: globalscope-enum-constants-in-gdscript/globalscope-constants] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: @GlobalScope exposes 512 named integer constants across 22 global enums (extension_api.json .global_enums; registered in upstream/godot/core/core_constants.cpp, surfaced per core/variant/variant_utility.cpp + doc/classes/@GlobalScope.xml). GDScript references them as BAREWORDS: KEY_SPACE(32), KEY_ESCAPE(4194305), KEY_A(65), OK(0), FAILED(1), ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND(7), MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT(1), JOY_BUTTON_A(0), PROPERTY_HINT_RANGE(1), PROPERTY_USAGE_DEFAULT(6), HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER(1), VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER(1), SIDE_LEFT(0), TYPE_VECTOR2(5), etc. Enums (value counts): Key(193), Error(49), PropertyHint(45), PropertyUsageFlags(32), Variant.Type/TYPE_*(40), Variant.Operator/OP_*(26), JoyButton(24), MIDIMessage(19), InlineAlignment(13), MouseButton(10), KeyModifierMask(9), JoyAxis(9), MethodFlags(9), EulerOrder(6), MouseButtonMask(5), Side/Corner/HorizontalAlignment/VerticalAlignment(4 each), KeyLocation(3), Orientation/ClockDirection(2 each). Godot also allows the enum-qualified form (Key.KEY_SPACE, Error.OK). These appear in essentially every real script (Error returns, input keycode compares, typeof checks, Control alignment, @export hint/usage flags).

PATINA CURRENT STATE: the GDScript VM resolves NONE of them. The rvalue identifier resolver at engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:1433-1466 (Expr::Ident read arm) handles only PI/TAU/INF/NAN, then falls through to environment/self_instance.properties/node properties and returns RuntimeErrorKind::UndefinedVariable(name) at interpreter.rs:1462. try_static_member (interpreter.rs:5935-5974) only knows Vector2/Vector3/Color/FileAccess. Environment (interpreter.rs:169-206) holds only user scopes + `const`. No constants module exists in gdscript-interop; grep of all crates/ for KEY_SPACE/MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT/ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND/PROPERTY_HINT/HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT/SIDE_LEFT/JOY_BUTTON/TYPE_VECTOR2/OK/FAILED = 0 hits. Any script using a global constant halts with UndefinedVariable.

IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH: (1) New module engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/global_constants.rs exporting `pub fn global_constant(name: &str) -> Option<Variant>` returning Variant::Int for all 512 names, generated 1:1 from extension_api.json .global_enums[].values[] (value.name -> value.value); add `mod global_constants;` (or pub) to lib.rs. (2) Wire into the Ident read arm: in interpreter.rs, immediately before the Err(UndefinedVariable) at line 1462, add `if let Some(v) = crate::global_constants::global_constant(name) { return Ok(v); }`. Precedence matches Godot (user local/member/const shadow the global constant -> table is last lookup before error). (3) Add enum-qualified access in try_static_member (interpreter.rs:5935) for the 22 enum type names (Key, Error, MouseButton, JoyButton, JoyAxis, MIDIMessage, PropertyHint, PropertyUsageFlags, InlineAlignment, HorizontalAlignment, VerticalAlignment, Side, Corner, EulerOrder, KeyModifierMask, KeyLocation, MouseButtonMask, MethodFlags, Orientation, ClockDirection) delegating member -> same table so `Key.KEY_SPACE`/`Error.OK` resolve too.

WIRING REQUIREMENT (end-to-end): .tscn load -> script attached -> MainLoop/SceneTree fires _ready -> interpreter eval_expr reaches Expr::Ident("KEY_SPACE") -> global_constants table -> Variant::Int(32) with no error. Must be the real _ready/_process dispatch path used by the runner, not a standalone helper call.
acceptance_criteria: A scene whose attached script uses @GlobalScope constants during _ready resolves them to correct integers end-to-end through the real interpreter dispatch (scene-load-to-output, no UndefinedVariable). Concretely: a script `extends Node` with `func check() -> Array: return [KEY_SPACE, KEY_ESCAPE, KEY_A, OK, FAILED, ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND, MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT, HORIZONTAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER, VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT_CENTER, SIDE_LEFT, JOY_BUTTON_A, PROPERTY_HINT_RANGE, TYPE_VECTOR2, Key.KEY_SPACE]` returns [32, 4194305, 65, 0, 1, 7, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 5, 32]; and `typeof(Vector2()) == TYPE_VECTOR2` evaluates true. Add a scoped integration test (test: `globalscope_constants_resolve`) that loads/attaches such a script and asserts the returned values (proving VM wiring, not just table lookup), runnable via `cargo nextest --test globalscope_constants_resolve`.

title: ProjectSettings: instantiate [autoload] singletons at boot and resolve them by global name in GDScript
description:
[audit-key: project-settings-runtime-honoring-and-script-api/projectsettings-autoload] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

GODOT: Every [autoload] entry in project.godot is instanced as a child of the root before the main scene and registered as a global singleton; scripts reference it by name (e.g. Global.score). A * prefix marks a script/singleton autoload (upstream main/main.cpp add_autoload).

PATINA: get_autoloads() (gdresource/src/project.rs:308) parses them but nothing instances them - grep shows no runtime consumer. Bootstrap loads only the main scene (bootstrap.rs:396) and its per-node scripts (init_scripts:425); there is no autoload phase, and the interpreter cannot resolve an autoload global name.

APPROACH: Add an autoload boot phase in patina-runner/bootstrap.rs (before MainScene): for each AutoloadEntry, load the .gd/.tscn, add it under the SceneTree root with the given name, run enter_tree/_ready, and register the name in a singleton table the interpreter consults during Ident resolution (interpreter.rs). WIRING: project [autoload] -> root child + global-name binding -> script Autoload.member resolves at runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Booting the runner on a project whose project.godot has [autoload] Global="*res://global.gd" (global.gd sets var score=5) makes a main-scene script read Global.score==5 and a node named Global exist under root - observable in the runner tree/JSON dump. (test: project_autoload_singletons)

title: Rendering2D: complete the CanvasItem draw_* primitive set + honor line width
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/canvas-draw-api] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot's CanvasItem has 32 draw_* primitives backed by RenderingServer canvas_item_add_* (canvas_item_add_polyline/multiline/polygon/primitive/arc/mesh/multimesh/set_transform/...). Patina implements 7 (gdserver2d/src/canvas.rs:14-81) and draw.rs (draw.rs:47-591) has no polygon/polyline/arc/primitive/mesh rasterizer; draw_line (draw.rs:170) ignores its `_width` argument. Add DrawCommand variants and CPU rasterizers in gdrender2d/src/draw.rs for: polyline(+per-vertex colors, width, optional AA), arc/ellipse_arc (segment tessellation), polygon/colored_polygon (concave scanline fill + per-vertex color interpolation + optional uv texture sampling), primitive (2-4 vertex tri/quad with per-vertex color+uv), multiline, dashed_line, style_box (delegate to StyleBoxFlat/Texture), char/string outline, mesh/multimesh (2D array-mesh triangles), set_transform/matrix (per-command local transform stack). Fix draw_line to rasterize a `width`-thick capsule/quad. Wire each variant into SoftwareRenderer::rasterize_item (renderer.rs:296-415) and the wgpu_backend batch path.
acceptance_criteria: A CanvasItem carrying draw_polyline (width 6, 2 colors), draw_colored_polygon (concave 6-gon, per-vertex color), draw_primitive (uv-textured quad), draw_arc, and draw_dashed_line renders through SoftwareRenderer::render_frame with: a 6px-wide line (not 1px), the concave polygon interior filled with an interpolated gradient, and dashed gaps present. (test: `canvas_draw_primitives`)

title: Rendering2D: wire Light2D/LightOccluder2D/CanvasModulate into the frame + blend modes, PCF shadows, cull masks
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/canvas-lighting] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot's 2D light pass composites each Light2D (blend_mode ADD/SUB/MIX, energy, color, range, light texture) over unshaded canvas output, casts occluder shadows filtered by shadow_filter (PCF5/PCF13 + shadow_filter_smooth) tinted by shadow_color, and respects range_item_cull_mask/shadow_item_cull_mask + light_mask; CanvasModulate multiplies the whole canvas. Patina's light2d.rs has a hard-shadow point/directional slice that nothing in a runtime feeds (grep: only SoftwareRenderer, itself unwired, and the lib re-export call it). Bridge PointLight2D/DirectionalLight2D nodes -> SoftwareRenderer::set_lights and LightOccluder2D nodes -> set_occluders each frame from the scene tree (in the scene->canvas bridge), and drive it from the editor viewport render. Extend light2d.rs with per-light blend_mode (add/sub/mix compositing), light texture sampling + texture_scale, PCF soft-shadow filtering with shadow_filter_smooth and shadow_color, and item cull via light_mask vs range/shadow_item_cull_mask. Register and apply CanvasModulate (multiply final canvas by its color).
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a ColorRect (white), a PointLight2D (energy 2, range covering part of the rect) above it, and a LightOccluder2D between them renders so lit pixels near the light are brighter than unlit pixels, and pixels in the occluder's shadow are darker than surrounding lit pixels; switching the light blend_mode to SUB darkens instead of brightens; a CanvasModulate=(0.5,0.5,0.5) halves overall brightness. Prove the lights come from scene nodes, not a manual set_lights call. (test: `canvas_light2d_wired`)

title: Rendering2D: RenderingServer singleton canvas_* API + CanvasItem _draw() script callback
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/rendering-server-api] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot scripts drive custom 2D two ways: (1) overriding CanvasItem._draw() and calling draw_rect/draw_line/draw_polygon/... which queue canvas commands, re-run on queue_redraw(); (2) direct RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_* calls. Patina exposes neither — RenderingServer isn't a registered singleton (grep: 0 script-side hits) and there is no _draw dispatch. Register RenderingServer as a script-callable singleton in the GDScript interop layer, mapping the canvas_item_* subset (canvas_item_create, add_line/add_polyline/add_rect/add_circle/add_texture_rect(_region)/add_nine_patch/add_polygon/add_primitive/add_multimesh/set_transform/set_modulate/set_self_modulate/set_z_index/set_z_as_relative/set_clip/set_material/set_visible/set_light_mask) onto gdserver2d DrawCommands/CanvasItem fields. Add CanvasItem._draw virtual dispatch in the scene->canvas bridge: before rendering each CanvasItem-derived node, clear its command list, call the script's _draw (binding draw_* built-ins to the same command emitters), and mark redraw via queue_redraw semantics. Requires the scene->canvas bridge and the draw primitive set.
acceptance_criteria: A node with a GDScript `func _draw(): draw_rect(Rect2(0,0,10,10), Color.RED); draw_circle(Vector2(20,20), 5, Color.BLUE)` renders a red rect and blue circle through the pipeline into the frame; separately, a script calling `RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_line(ci, a, b, Color.GREEN, 3)` on its own canvas item draws a 3px green line. Prove the draw came from executing the script _draw / RS call, not a hardcoded command. (test: `rendering_server_canvas_api`)

title: Shadows3D: PSSM directional cascades + GPU spot/omni shadow atlas sampling + PCF
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/shadows3d] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot directional lights use PSSM (1/2/4 orthographic cascades fit to the view frustum with split blend), and omni/spot lights render into a shadow atlas (omni as dual-paraboloid or cubemap, spot as perspective), all sampled with PCF (renderer_rd shadow code; Light3D.xml). Patina's GPU pipeline (the default editor viewport render) samples only a single primary directional map (wgpu_pipeline.rs:538 shadow_map_index 0-only; WGSL directional_shadow_factor), and the directional map is a fixed half-extent frustum with no cascades (shadow_map.rs:18). Software spot/omni maps exist (shadow_map.rs) but never reach the GPU shader. Implementation: (1) compute PSSM cascade split distances + per-cascade ortho matrices for directional lights and upload a cascade array; select cascade per-fragment by view depth and blend across the split in WGSL; (2) upload spot depth maps and omni cube/paraboloid maps into a shadow atlas texture array and add spot_shadow_factor/omni_shadow_factor to SHADER_3D_WGSL keyed by GpuLightData.kind; (3) add PCF taps to all shadow samples. Wiring: a .tscn with a SpotLight3D (shadow_enabled) over a plane must render a projected shadow in the GPU editor viewport, and a large directional scene must show cascaded shadow coverage.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a shadow-casting SpotLight3D and an OmniLight3D each produce a visible cast shadow in the editor GPU viewport frame (currently absent), and a directional light shows shadow coverage across a large depth range (cascades). Verified by (test: `spot_omni_and_pssm_shadows_render_gpu`) asserting shadowed pixels appear for spot/omni and near+far directional receivers.

title: Meshes3D: ArrayMesh full vertex arrays (tangent/uv2/color/custom) + ImmediateMesh + SurfaceTool
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/meshes3d] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]
[verify-note: ADJUSTED: REFUTATION of a factual claim: the finder wrote 'there is no ArrayMesh (add_surface_from_arrays)' after grepping only mesh.rs — but ArrayMesh EXISTS at gdserver3d/primitive_mesh.rs:341-404 with add_surface_from_arrays (:365) and is re-exported in lib.rs:51. The finder's grep was scoped too]

Godot meshes carry ARRAY_VERTEX/NORMAL/TANGENT/COLOR/TEX_UV/TEX_UV2/CUSTOM0-3/BONES/WEIGHTS/INDEX with optional compression and 8/16-bit variants; ArrayMesh.add_surface_from_arrays builds surfaces from a typed Array, ImmediateMesh builds geometry per-frame (surface_begin/set_color/set_uv/add_vertex/surface_end), and SurfaceTool is the procedural builder (mesh.cpp; ArrayMesh.xml/ImmediateMesh.xml/SurfaceTool.xml). Patina's Surface3D (gdserver3d/mesh.rs) has only vertices/normals/uvs/indices and no ArrayMesh/ImmediateMesh/SurfaceTool classes. Implementation: (1) extend Surface3D with tangents, uv2, colors, and custom channels; feed color+uv2 into the render path (renderer.rs + wgpu vertex layout) so vertex colors and lightmap-uv2 work; (2) add an ArrayMesh type with add_surface_from_arrays reading the Godot ARRAY_* layout, an ImmediateMesh with the surface_begin/add_vertex API, and a SurfaceTool builder; (3) register ArrayMesh/ImmediateMesh/SurfaceTool (and the primitive/multimesh classes) in gdobject/class_db.rs so they construct from GDScript and .tscn sub_resources. Wiring: a .tscn/script building an ArrayMesh with vertex colors must render those per-vertex colors in the editor viewport.
acceptance_criteria: A scene that builds an ArrayMesh via add_surface_from_arrays (with ARRAY_COLOR + ARRAY_TEX_UV2) and assigns it to a MeshInstance3D renders per-vertex colors in the editor viewport frame, and ImmediateMesh/SurfaceTool construct geometry that renders. Verified by (test: `arraymesh_vertex_colors_and_immediatemesh_render`).

title: GeometryInstance3D: consume cast_shadow, visibility_range, material_overlay, transparency, lod_bias, extra_cull_margin in the render path
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/geometryinstance3d] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot GeometryInstance3D controls per-instance rendering: cast_shadow (On/Off/DoubleSided/ShadowsOnly), visibility_range_begin/end (+margins, +fade_mode) to LOD-hide by camera distance, material_overlay (extra pass over the surface), transparency (per-instance alpha fade), lod_bias, extra_cull_margin, custom_aabb, and gi_mode (visual_instance_3d.cpp; GeometryInstance3D.xml). Patina stores cast_shadow + visibility_range as node properties (node3d.rs) but the renderer ignores all of them (no reads in render_server_3d.rs/renderer.rs/wgpu_pipeline.rs). Implementation: in render_server_3d.rs sync, read these properties per MeshInstance3D and (a) skip shadow-map submission when cast_shadow==Off / render shadows-only when ShadowsOnly, (b) cull the instance from the draw list when the camera distance is outside [visibility_range_begin, visibility_range_end] (with fade), (c) apply per-instance transparency to albedo alpha, (d) draw material_overlay as a second pass, (e) apply extra_cull_margin/custom_aabb to visibility and lod_bias to LOD selection. Register GeometryInstance3D in class_db.rs. Wiring: a .tscn MeshInstance3D with cast_shadow=Off must produce no shadow, and one past visibility_range_end must not render.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn MeshInstance3D with cast_shadow=Off casts no shadow in the editor viewport frame (currently it does), and a mesh whose camera distance exceeds visibility_range_end is not drawn. Verified by (test: `geometryinstance_cast_shadow_and_visibility_range_consumed`) asserting shadow pixels vanish and the far mesh is absent from output.

comments.author: GreenBadger
comments.text:
[GreenBadger 2026-07-16] Handing back UNSTARTED — not deliverable by a build-restricted worker. No code written. Scoping findings (description is partly STALE, please correct):

STALE #1: "Register GeometryInstance3D in class_db.rs" is ALREADY DONE. It is registered at gdobject/src/class_db.rs:817-840 — abstract, parent VisualInstance3D — with the full property surface already present: material_override, material_overlay, transparency, cast_shadow, extra_cull_margin, lod_bias, gi_mode, ignore_occlusion_culling, visibility_range_begin/_margin, visibility_range_end/_margin. An existing test at class_db.rs:2407-2416 already asserts it. Do NOT redo this.

STALE #2: the named file paths do not exist. There is no render_server_3d.rs in gdserver3d. Real locations:
  - gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs (2300 lines) — the sync layer; consumes NONE of these properties (grep for cast_shadow / visibility_range / material_overlay / transparency / lod_bias / extra_cull_margin = zero hits).
  - gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs and gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs — the draw path; also zero hits.

CONFIRMED REAL: the gap itself is genuine. The properties are stored (gdscene/src/node3d.rs) and registered, but nothing in the render path reads them.

USEFUL HOOK POINT for whoever takes it: gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs:424 calls shadow_map::generate_shadow_maps(&self.lights, &self.instances) — a CPU-side shadow map. cast_shadow=Off / ShadowsOnly is therefore implementable by filtering the instance list feeding that call, and is assertable WITHOUT a GPU (inspect the generated ShadowMap directly), which is far cheaper than the pixel assertion the acceptance currently demands. Recommend re-writing the acceptance around that.

WHY I CANNOT DO IT:
  (a) Acceptance requires rendered-frame pixel assertions ("shadow pixels vanish", far mesh absent from output) — needs a compile plus a rendered GPU frame, which this worker lane cannot run (policy hook blocks the Rust builder; the verifier lane is the sole builder).
  (b) It requires threading new per-instance fields from gdscene into gdrender3d's instance struct — a cross-crate struct-field change whose call sites cannot be compile-checked here. That is the classic shared-crate-break cascade.
  (c) gdscene already carries foreign uncommitted work (control.rs).

DO NOT accept a "partial" here: the verifier closes beads on compile, not on the acceptance test, so a compile-clean partial would FALSE-CLOSE this P1 parity gap while the renderer still ignores every property. This needs a builder+GPU-capable worker.

comments.author: SunnyHill
comments.text:
SunnyHill 2026-07-25: CONFIRMING GreenBadger hand-back. Claimed, scoped, returned UNSTARTED. No code written.

Both blockers still hold after re-checking:

1. The cross-crate struct change is unavoidable even for the cheap subset. GreenBadger is right that cast_shadow is CPU-assertable via the instance list feeding generate_shadow_maps, no GPU needed. But gdrender3d still has to KNOW each instance cast_shadow value to filter it, and the gdscene sync layer cannot just omit the instance instead: shadows and normal drawing consume the SAME list, so omitting removes the mesh from the visible frame too. Either way a new per-instance field crosses the gdscene -> gdrender3d boundary, and a build-restricted worker cannot compile-check the call sites.

2. Acceptance still demands rendered-frame pixel assertions (shadow pixels vanish, far mesh absent from output).

RECOMMENDATION: route to a build-capable lane, or split. Worker-deliverable split: (a) rewrite the acceptance around inspecting the generated ShadowMap on the CPU per GreenBadger, (b) land the per-instance field plumbing as its own small bead verified once by a build-capable lane. After that the individual behaviours (visibility_range culling, transparency, material_overlay) become ordinary contained work.

GreenBadger STALE #1/#2 still stand: GeometryInstance3D is already registered in class_db.rs, and the file paths named in the description do not exist.

title: Resources: implement real load()/preload()/ResourceLoader.load (text .tscn/.tres/images) wired through the GDScript interpreter
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/resource-load] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]
[verify-note: ADJUSTED: STUB is overstated and one factual claim is false. TRUE: the preload/load builtin (interpreter.rs:2389-2426) returns a path-only ResourceRef with an extension-guessed class_name and properties:HashMap::new(), so load('.tres').get(prop) and image pixels are genuinely NOT loaded. FALSE: 'the]

In Godot, load("res://x.tres") reads+parses the file and returns a live Resource; load("res://x.tscn") returns a PackedScene whose instantiate() builds the real subtree; load("res://x.png") returns a Texture2D backed by decoded pixels. Patina's interpreter (interpreter.rs:2389) returns a path-only placeholder with a guessed class string and never touches the filesystem. Implement a ResourceLoader backend that resolves res:// via gdcore::resolve_path, dispatches by extension to the existing loaders (gdresource TresLoader for .tres, gdscene PackedScene::from_tscn for .tscn, gdresource::import_image/texture_import for images), caches by path (gdresource::cache::ResourceCache), and returns Variants carrying the loaded resource. Expose ResourceLoader.load/exists/get_dependencies as a script singleton and route preload/load builtins through it so preload("x.tscn").instantiate() yields the real nodes and load("x.tres").get("prop") returns parsed properties.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript that runs load("res://sub.tres") reads a real property value from the parsed .tres, and preload("res://child.tscn").instantiate() adds the child scene's actual node subtree to the tree (verified via the runner tree dump). (test: `gdscript_load_reads_real_resource`)

title: Resources: complete the .tscn/.tres variant-literal parser (int vectors, Vector4/Quaternion/Plane/AABB/Basis/Projection, StringName, typed arrays) and surface parse errors
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/tscn-parser] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot's VariantParser reads every math literal and preserves types exactly. Patina's parse_variant_value (gdresource/loader.rs:232+) coerces Vector2i/Vector3i to float vectors and cannot parse Vector4(i), Quaternion, Plane, AABB, Basis, Projection, StringName (&"..."), typed Array[T]([...]), or Object(...); packed_scene.rs then silently discards unparseable properties. Add the missing literal arms (mapping to the correct gdvariant types — requires Vector4/Quaternion/Plane/AABB/Projection Variant variants; add them if absent), preserve int-vector types, and change packed_scene.rs to propagate parse errors (or at minimum store the raw literal) instead of dropping the property.
acceptance_criteria: Parsing a .tscn node with position=Vector2i(3,4), basis-bearing transform=Transform3D(...), rot=Quaternion(0,0,0,1), and cells=PackedInt32Array(...) preserves the integer vector as an int type and round-trips the Transform3D/Quaternion values; a property with a genuinely malformed value produces a reported error rather than being silently missing. (test: `tscn_parses_intvec_and_math_literals`)

title: GDScript: expose ProjectSettings, ResourceSaver, ResourceUID, Marshalls singletons + var_to_bytes/str_to_var utilities
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/io-singletons] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot scripts constantly call ProjectSettings.get_setting/has_setting/set_setting, ResourceSaver.save, ResourceUID.id_to_text/text_to_id, Marshalls.variant_to_base64, and the @GlobalScope var_to_bytes/bytes_to_var/var_to_str/str_to_var helpers. None are reachable in Patina's interpreter. Add static-singleton dispatch arms in interpreter.rs (alongside the existing OS/Engine/Time/JSON handlers) backed by: gdcore::ProjectSettings (already has get/set/has), gdresource::ResourceSaver + saver.rs, gdresource::uid (text_to_id/id_to_text), and a new Marshalls/base64 + variant-binary codec (share the binary Variant codec with res_loader/multiplayer). Ensure ProjectSettings reads the globally-loaded settings populated at boot.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript can read ProjectSettings.get_setting("application/config/name"), round-trip Marshalls.base64_to_variant(Marshalls.variant_to_base64(v)) == v, and ResourceUID.id_to_text(ResourceUID.text_to_id("uid://abc")) == "uid://abc", all returning correct values in the runner. (test: `gdscript_reaches_io_singletons`)

title: Image import: decode WebP source + WebP-compressed .ctex (Godot default web/2D texture)
description:
[audit-key: image-import-format-breadth-webp-svg-compressed/image-decode-webp] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: WebP is decoded by Image.load_webp_from_buffer (doc/classes/Image.xml:423) via modules/webp/image_loader_webp.cpp (registered by default, register_types.cpp:45). The default texture importer (editor/import/resource_importer_texture.cpp:234, PRESET default 0=Lossless) stores imported 2D textures as WebP inside .ctex with inner DATA_FORMAT_WEBP=2 — so opening ANY real imported/exported project routes imported PNG/JPG/etc. through a WebP-in-.ctex artifact. Patina current state: no WebP decoder exists in the workspace (gdresource/Cargo.toml has only miniz_oxide; grep for decode_webp/load_webp/image-webp/libwebp across crates/ is empty). ctex.rs:152-154 returns EngineError::Unsupported('no WebP decoder in this build') for DATA_FORMAT_WEBP, and importers.rs::ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults (importers.rs:579) registers no `.webp` extension, so source .webp also cannot load. Implementation: add a pure-Rust WebP decoder dep (e.g. `image` with `webp` feature, or `image-webp`) to gdresource/Cargo.toml; add `decode_webp_bytes -> (w,h,format,pixels)` and (a) branch ctex.rs's DATA_FORMAT_WEBP to decode the embedded WebP level-0 payload into the same Texture2D Resource shape build_raw_texture/import_image_bytes produce, and (b) register `.webp` in ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults dispatching to a new import_webp producing a pixel-bearing Texture2D. Wiring requirement: ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults().load_resource(path) must decode both a loose `.webp` and a `.import`→`.ctex(WebP)` artifact (via resolve_import_artifact, importers.rs:62) end-to-end to a Texture2D whose `pixels` Variant::Array is populated — identical contract to the existing PNG path.
acceptance_criteria: ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults().load_resource('foo.webp') returns class Texture2D with a non-empty `pixels` array of the correct dimensions/colors; and load_resource on a .ctex whose inner data_format is DATA_FORMAT_WEBP (2) returns decoded pixels instead of an Unsupported error; and a source PNG with a `.import` sidecar redirecting to a WebP `.ctex` loads real pixels. (test: `webp_import_wiring`)

title: FileAccess: typed get/store (8-64/half/float/double/real/var/line/csv/pascal), endianness, compressed + encrypted modes, md5/sha
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/file-access] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Games use FileAccess for save files with typed binary reads/writes, big-endian control, compression, encryption, and hashing. gdcore/file_access.rs currently only does whole-buffer/string read/write. Implement the typed get_*/store_* family (little/big-endian aware via a big_endian flag), get_var/store_var using the binary Variant codec, get_line/get_csv_line/get_pascal_string, open_compressed (fastlz/deflate/zstd/gzip via miniz_oxide + a fastlz impl), open_encrypted(+with_pass) using gdcore::crypto AES, and get_md5/get_sha256. Expose them all through the interpreter FileAccess instance dispatch. Note the wasm user:// backend (IndexedDB/OPFS) as a follow-up so the API is web-usable.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript writes a save file with store_32/store_float/store_var, closes, reopens, and get_32/get_float/get_var read back the exact values; toggling set_big_endian(true) changes the on-disk byte order; open_compressed round-trips a buffer. (test: `file_access_typed_binary_roundtrip`)

title: Image: implement the Godot Image class (pixel API, formats, mipmaps, resize, blit/blend, load/save buffers) + ImageTexture, register + script-expose
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/image] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Image is one of the most-used data classes and is entirely absent — only scattered PNG decoders exist. Create a gdresource (or gdcore) Image type holding width/height/Format/data with the core API: create/create_empty/create_from_data, get/set_pixel(v), get_format/convert (across the L8/RGBA8/RF/RGBAF/RGBE families), get_data/get_data_size, generate_mipmaps/get_mipmap_offset, resize/crop/shrink_x2, blit_rect(+mask)/blend_rect(+mask), fill(_rect), get_used_rect/get_region, flip_x/flip_y, load_png_from_buffer/load_jpg_from_buffer + save_png(_to_buffer). Back ImageTexture (create_from_image/update) on it, register both in class_db.rs, and expose Image static/instance methods to GDScript so Image.load_png_from_buffer + ImageTexture.create_from_image drive a Sprite2D texture.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript builds an Image via create() + set_pixel, wraps it in ImageTexture.create_from_image, assigns it to a Sprite2D, and the runner reports the sprite's texture size and a queried pixel color matching what was set. (test: `image_class_pixels_to_texture`)

title: Resources: wire PCK mount + binary .scn/.res loading into the boot path (RSCC, full variant decode, binary PackedScene)
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/binary-pck] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

A real Godot web export ships a .pck of binary .scn/.res files fetched over HTTP. Patina has a complete PCK reader (pck.rs) and a partial binary .res reader (res_loader.rs) but nothing mounts a PCK or reads binary resources at boot, and there is no binary PackedScene loader. Wire a PCK mount into patina-runner boot (fetch/read bytes → PckMountManager → res:// resolves inside the pack), extend res_loader.rs to handle RSCC compression, big-endian, and the full variant set (packed arrays + objects), and add a binary PackedScene decoder that reconstructs the node-path-indexed tree. Route ResourceLoader through the mounted pack.
acceptance_criteria: Given a .pck built by PckPacker containing a binary .scn main scene, the runner mounts it and boots the scene into the tree (node count/names match the source), proving the fetch→PCK→binary-resource→scene-tree chain end to end. (test: `runner_boots_binary_scene_from_pck`)

title: SceneTree/Viewport: dispatch _input/_unhandled_input/_shortcut_input/_unhandled_key_input with push_input + set_input_as_handled
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/input-propagation] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot routes each InputEvent through Viewport::push_input in a fixed order: _input (tree order) → GUI/gui_input (focus + mouse target) → _shortcut_input → _unhandled_key_input → _unhandled_input → physics picking, with set_input_as_handled() short-circuiting later stages (viewport.cpp). Nodes opt in via set_process_input/set_process_unhandled_input/etc. Patina has none of this: MainLoop::step (main_loop.rs:344) only builds a polling InputSnapshot; there is no process_script_input path (scene_tree.rs:1465-1493 lists only ready/process/physics/enter/exit) and no set_input_as_handled. Implement SceneTree::push_input(event) that walks nodes in Godot stage order, invokes the corresponding script virtual on nodes that enabled it, honors a per-event input_handled flag, and is called from MainLoop::step for each queued InputEvent BEFORE the process phase. Add process_script_input / process_script_unhandled_input dispatch to the gdscene scripting bridge plus per-node input-enable flags, and route the editor key/mouse endpoints (editor_server.rs:10106) through push_input rather than only InputState.
acceptance_criteria: A scene whose script implements _unhandled_input(event) and sets a var flips that var when a key InputEvent is pushed and MainLoop::step runs; a node that calls set_input_as_handled() in _input prevents a sibling's _unhandled_input from seeing the same event. (test: unhandled_input_dispatched_via_main_loop)

title: SceneTree/Node: emit lifecycle + per-frame signals (process_frame, physics_frame, node_added, tree_entered, …)
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/tree-signals] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot emits SceneTree.process_frame/physics_frame each frame (immediately before _process/_physics_process) and tree-mutation signals tree_changed/node_added/node_removed/node_renamed/tree_process_mode_changed/scene_changed; Nodes emit tree_entered/tree_exiting/tree_exited/child_entered_tree/child_exiting_tree/child_order_changed/ready/renamed. Scripts routinely `await get_tree().process_frame` and `node.tree_exiting.connect(...)`. Patina emits none: MainLoop::step (main_loop.rs) has no process_frame/physics_frame emission, and add_child/remove_node/reparent/set_name + LifecycleManager (lifecycle.rs) only append notifications to the log — no signal fires. Emit these through the existing SceneTree signal store (scene_tree.rs:1102 emit_signal): emit tree-level signals inside MainLoop::step (process_frame before the process phase, physics_frame before each physics tick) and inside add_child/remove_node/reparent/set_name; emit the Node-level signals on the affected node during enter/exit/child-order transitions in LifecycleManager.
acceptance_criteria: A script connecting to get_tree().process_frame AND to a child node's tree_entered receives both callbacks when the scene is stepped once through MainLoop; node_added fires when add_child inserts a live node and node_renamed fires on set_name. (test: scene_tree_and_node_signals_fire_via_main_loop)

title: SceneTree: change_scene_to_file, unload_current_scene, quit + auto_accept_quit/quit_on_go_back, get_frame, physics_interpolation
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scenetree-scene-api] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot's most-used scene API is change_scene_to_file(path) — deferred: free current scene, load+instance the .tscn, set current_scene — plus unload_current_scene, quit(exit_code) with auto_accept_quit/quit_on_go_back semantics, get_frame() (Engine frame counter), get_processed_tweens(), and physics_interpolation toggle (scene_tree.cpp). Patina has only change_scene_to_packed/_to_node/reload (scene_tree.rs:1806-1900). Implement change_scene_to_file by loading the res:// path through the existing PackedScene loader and delegating to change_scene_to_packed with Godot's deferred timing (swap at end of frame); add unload_current_scene, a quit() path that signals the MainLoop/PlatformBackend to stop (and the editor to Stop), get_frame() returning MainLoop.frame_count, get_processed_tweens(), and a physics_interpolation flag surfaced to the renderer. Wire change_scene_to_file so a script calling get_tree().change_scene_to_file('res://next.tscn') actually swaps the running scene in patina-runner and editor Play.
acceptance_criteria: Stepping a scene whose script calls change_scene_to_file('res://b.tscn') replaces current_scene with b's root by the next frame; quit() ends patina-runner's run loop (should_quit becomes true). (test: change_scene_to_file_swaps_running_scene)

title: Node: add_sibling, wildcard find_child/find_children/find_parent, has_node, get_path_to, is_ancestor_of, propagate_call/notification
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/node-query-api] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot's Node query surface (node.cpp) includes add_sibling(node, force_readable_name), find_child(pattern, recursive, owned) and find_children(pattern, type, recursive, owned) with String wildcard matching, find_parent(pattern), has_node(path), get_path_to(node), is_ancestor_of(node), and propagate_notification(what)/propagate_call(method, args, parent_first). Patina exposes only exact-path resolution (scene_tree.rs get_node_by_path:695, find_child_by_name:711) plus get_index/node_path; the wildcard find_child/find_children, add_sibling, find_parent, get_path_to, is_ancestor_of and propagate_* are absent (0 non-test hits). Implement these on SceneTree over NodeId with Godot wildcard semantics (`*`/`?`), add_sibling inserting immediately after the node in its parent's child list (with unique-name resolution), and propagate_call/notification walking the subtree parent-first/child order. Expose them to the GDScript bridge so scripts can call node.find_child('Enemy*') and node.add_sibling(n).
acceptance_criteria: On a loaded scene, find_children('*', 'Sprite2D', true) returns every Sprite2D descendant, find_child('Ene*') matches by wildcard, add_sibling inserts a node immediately after its sibling in tree order, and propagate_call reaches all descendants. (test: node_find_and_sibling_queries)

title: SceneTree: make root a Window/Viewport with get_viewport/get_window and content-scale stretch pipeline
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/viewport-tree] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

In Godot the SceneTree root is a Window (subclass of Viewport); every Node.get_viewport()/get_window() climbs to it, and its content_scale_mode (disabled/canvas_items/viewport) + content_scale_aspect (ignore/keep/keep_width/keep_height/expand) + content_scale_factor drive the stretch transform applied to the whole canvas (window.cpp — the web-canvas resize path). Patina creates the root as a bare Node (scene_tree.rs:114) with no Viewport/Window semantics, no get_viewport/get_window, no world_2d/world_3d, and content-scale only stored as an unused project-settings string (project_settings_dialog.rs:566). Make the root a Window-class node carrying Viewport state (size, world_2d/world_3d, canvas_transform), implement Node.get_viewport()/get_window() returning it, parse display/window/stretch/{mode,aspect,scale} from project.godot, and compute+apply the content-scale transform into the 2D draw path (gdrender2d) for both patina-runner and editor Play/viewport.
acceptance_criteria: get_viewport() on any node returns the root Window; with stretch mode=canvas_items, aspect=keep and a base size, rendering a scene into a 2x window scales the emitted canvas transform / draw output by 2. (test: root_window_content_scale_stretch)

comments.author: GreenBadger
comments.text:
[GreenBadger 2026-07-16] Handing back UNSTARTED — wrong worker lane. No code written. Scoping findings for the next worker:

DESCRIPTION VERIFIED ACCURATE (unusually — no staleness found):
  - gdscene has NO get_viewport / get_window (grep 'fn get_viewport|fn get_window' across gdscene/src = zero hits). Genuinely missing.
  - content_scale has ZERO consumers anywhere in engine-rs (grep -rl content_scale = no files). Genuinely unwired.
  - Viewport IS already registered in ClassDB (gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1419) and Window is registered under it (:1435, .parent("Viewport")), with a test at :2805. So the CLASS surface exists; what is missing is making the tree ROOT actually be one, plus the stretch pipeline.

WHY THIS IS NOT DELIVERABLE IN THIS LANE:
  (a) It changes the SceneTree ROOT NODE TYPE (scene_tree.rs) — scene_tree.rs is the central file of gdscene with a very large call-site surface. Retyping the root cannot be compile-checked here (the policy hook blocks the Rust builder in this lane; the verifier lane is the sole builder), and a mistake in gdscene breaks every dependent crate for the whole swarm.
  (b) It is inherently cross-crate: gdscene (root/Viewport state) + gdresource (parse display/window/stretch/* from project.godot) + gdrender2d (apply the content-scale transform to the draw path) + patina-runner AND the editor Play viewport.
  (c) Acceptance asserts on emitted draw output ("scales the emitted canvas transform / draw output by 2") — needs a compile + a render.

SUGGESTED SPLIT (would make most of this landable, and some of it landable in a no-build lane):
  1. gdresource-only: parse display/window/stretch/{mode,aspect,scale} from project.godot into a typed struct (e.g. StretchMode/StretchAspect enums + factor) with a pure parse unit test. Self-contained, additive, no shared-crate risk — this one IS deliverable without a builder.
  2. Pure math: a `content_scale_transform(base_size, window_size, mode, aspect, factor) -> Transform2D` function with table-driven unit tests per aspect (ignore/keep/keep_width/keep_height/expand). Pure function, testable with no render.
  3. gdscene: root-as-Window + get_viewport()/get_window() (needs a builder).
  4. gdrender2d/runner: apply the transform to the draw path (needs a builder + render assertion).
Steps 1+2 are the bulk of the actual Godot semantics and carry near-zero cascade risk; 3+4 are the invasive parts. Recommend splitting into separate beads.

DO NOT accept a compile-clean "partial" against the current single bead: the verifier closes on compile rather than on the acceptance test, so a partial would FALSE-CLOSE this P1 while the root is still a bare Node and content_scale is still ignored.

title: Shaders: uniform hints + global/instance uniforms + ShaderInclude #include preprocessor
description:
[audit-key: shaders/shader-uniforms-globals-include] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: uniform hints drive semantics (source_color sRGB decode, hint_range clamps + inspector slider, filter_*/repeat_* sampler state, screen_texture/depth_texture/normal_roughness_texture bind engine buffers); `global uniform` values are stored in ProjectSettings shader_globals and set at runtime via RenderingServer.global_shader_parameter_set; `instance uniform` are per-instance overrides; ShaderInclude (.gdshaderinc) + `#include` compose sources (doc/classes/Shader.xml, ShaderInclude.xml). Patina current state: hints are opaque strings with no behavior (gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:65); no global parameter store; RenderingServer.global_shader_parameter_* unimplemented; #include/ShaderInclude absent; instance/global uniforms lexed but ignored. Implementation approach: parse the full hint grammar and apply hint semantics in the compiler/interpreter; add a global-shader-parameter registry (seeded from project.godot shader_globals, mutable via a RenderingServer surface) and resolve `global uniform` reads from it; resolve `#include`/ShaderInclude during compilation (register a .gdshaderinc loader in gdresource/importers.rs). Wiring requirement: setting a global uniform at runtime changes shaded output next frame, and a #include'd function is callable in the fragment body.
acceptance_criteria: A shader declaring `global uniform vec4 sky_tint;` renders using the value set via the global-parameter API (changing it changes output), a `source_color` hinted uniform is sRGB-decoded, and a `#include "res://lib.gdshaderinc"` function resolves and executes. (test: `shader_uniform_hints_and_globals`)

title: Theme: full default theme (55 control types), icon item type, type variations, and Control get/add_theme_* resolution API
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/theme-system] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: STUB]

Godot's Theme (api: 69 methods) stores 6 item types (color/constant/font/font_size/icon/stylebox) with type variations and base types; default_theme.cpp generates the built-in theme with 794 item assignments across 55 control types; Controls resolve theme items by walking the theme_owner parent chain and merging per-instance overrides via ~40 Control methods (get_theme_color, add_theme_stylebox_override, has_theme_font, get_theme_default_font, set_theme_type_variation, begin/end_bulk_theme_override). Patina's Theme (gdscene/src/theme.rs) is a 5-category HashMap with no Icon type, styleboxes stored as flat Variant::Color, and a default_theme() covering only Label/Button/Panel (theme.rs:186); Control has no theme-resolution API at all (grep for get_theme_color/add_theme_*_override finds nothing); nothing is registered in gdobject/src/class_db.rs. Implementation: extend gdscene/src/theme.rs with an Icon item type, type variations/base types, default font/size, merge/clear, and a get_theme_*/has_theme_*/add_theme_*_override resolution that walks the node's theme_owner chain (gdscene/src/control.rs); port default_theme.cpp coverage for the full control-type set; register Theme+ThemeDB in class_db.rs so .tscn/[gd_resource type="Theme"] loads into a usable Theme. Wiring requirement: a Control in a scene with a custom Theme and an add_theme_color_override resolves the override, then the theme, then ThemeDB default - and that resolved value feeds the render path from the text-render-wiring bead.
acceptance_criteria: A scene with a Button that has a theme_type_variation and an add_theme_color_override('font_color') resolves font_color from the override; removing it falls back to the assigned Theme, then to the default theme; the default theme exposes styleboxes/colors/constants for the full Godot control-type set (Label, Button, Panel, LineEdit, Tree, ... ) and Theme/ThemeDB are constructible via ClassDB. (test: `control_theme_override_resolution`)

title: Input singleton: add get_axis / is_action_just_released / get_action_strength + capture just_released in the snapshot + circular-deadzone get_vector/get_axis
description:
[audit-key: input/input-singleton-api] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]
[verify-note: ADJUSTED: All technical claims verified: call_input_method (interpreter.rs:3167-3287) handles exactly 6 methods (is_action_pressed/is_action_just_pressed/is_key_pressed/get_global_mouse_position/is_mouse_button_pressed/get_vector) with `other => UndefinedFunction` catch-all (3284); Input.* routes ON]

Godot ground truth (core/input/input.cpp): Input.get_axis(neg,pos)=strength(pos)-strength(neg); get_vector applies the max action deadzone to the raw vector length then renormalizes (circular deadzone); is_action_just_released mirrors just_pressed; get_action_strength/raw return analog magnitude (raw ignores deadzone). Patina current: interpreter call_input_method (gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:3167) has only 6 methods — get_axis, is_action_just_released, get_action_strength, get_mouse_position, is_physical_key_pressed are absent; the script InputSnapshot (gdscene/src/scripting.rs:167) carries no just_released_keys at all, and get_vector (gdplatform/src/input.rs:738) ignores deadzone. Approach: add a just_released_keys HashSet to gdscene InputSnapshot and populate it from InputState (flush pipeline already tracks keys_just_released); add SceneAccess methods get_input_axis, is_input_action_just_released, get_action_strength; register the corresponding names in call_input_method; port Godot's circular-deadzone get_vector/get_axis into InputState/InputSnapshot. Wiring requirement: a GDScript calling Input.get_axis(), Input.is_action_just_released(), Input.get_action_strength() during _process in a running scene returns correct values (not an error) through the editor Play snapshot bridge (editor_server.rs make_input_snapshot -> main_loop.set_input).
acceptance_criteria: A scene script that in _process records Input.get_axis("ui_left","ui_right"), Input.is_action_just_released("ui_accept"), and Input.get_action_strength("ui_right") returns -1/0/1 for get_axis across press/both/release frames, true on the exact frame ui_accept is released (and false the next), and 1.0 strength while held — with a diagonal get_vector normalized after deadzone (test: `input_singleton_polling_e2e`).

title: StyleBox: StyleBoxFlat/Texture/Line/Empty resources + bordered/rounded/nine-patch drawing wired into Control rendering
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/stylebox] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot draws Control backgrounds via StyleBox resources: StyleBoxFlat (bg_color, per-side border_width + border_color, per-corner corner_radius + corner_detail, expand_margin_*, content margins, shadow_color/size/offset, skew, anti_aliasing - 23 properties), StyleBoxTexture (nine-patch with per-axis stretch/tile/tile-fit + modulate + region), StyleBoxLine, StyleBoxEmpty (scene/resources/style_box_flat.cpp etc.). Patina has no runtime StyleBox class - none registered in gdobject/src/class_db.rs, styleboxes are stored as flat Variant::Color in gdscene/src/theme.rs:209, and nothing draws borders/corners/shadows (control.rs:1024-1059 only stores theme_override_styles/* as Variants; gdeditor/src/theme_editor.rs:85 is editor-only data). Implementation: add StyleBox resource types (gdscene or gdrender2d) parsed from .tscn/.tres sub_resources, register them in class_db.rs, and add a draw_stylebox routine in gdrender2d (rounded-rect fill + per-side borders + shadow + AA; nine-patch for StyleBoxTexture reusing draw::draw_nine_patch); consume the theme's stylebox item when rendering Panel/Button/Control backgrounds. title: TextServer: line breaking, autowrap, alignment, ellipsis, tab stops via TextParagraph/TextLine layout
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/textserver-layout] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: STUB]

Godot lays out text through TextServer + TextParagraph/TextLine: breaking lines by word/grapheme/CJK against a width, applying autowrap_mode, horizontal/vertical alignment, justification_flags, text_overrun_behavior (ellipsis/trim), and tab stops, with per-size glyph metrics (ascent/descent/advance) (servers/text/text_server.cpp; scene/resources/text_paragraph.cpp). Patina's TextServerLite (gdrender2d/src/text_server.rs) only returns a fixed per-char advance (2 methods vs 236); TextLine/TextParagraph do not exist; Label's stored autowrap_mode/horizontal_alignment (gdscene/src/control.rs:800-843) drive nothing (no layout consumer); draw_string_multiline wraps only on literal newlines (font.rs:568). Implementation: build a TextParagraph/TextLine layout module in gdrender2d that, given a string + font (from the font-stack bead) + width + alignment + wrap mode + overrun behavior, produces positioned glyph runs (line breaks, alignment offsets, ellipsis); expose glyph metrics per size on the TextServer; have the Label update path (text-render-wiring bead) request a paragraph layout and emit one DrawString per positioned run. Wiring requirement: a Label with autowrap enabled and a bounded width wraps its text across multiple lines with the chosen alignment when rendered.
acceptance_criteria: A Label with a fixed width, autowrap_mode=word and horizontal_alignment=right, given text longer than its width, renders on multiple lines each right-aligned within the rect; text_overrun_behavior=trim_ellipsis on a single-line Label produces a trailing ellipsis; tab characters advance to tab stops. (test: `label_autowrap_and_alignment_layout`)

title: i18n: TranslationServer singleton + tr()/tr_n() builtins + .po/.csv loaders + auto_translate re-render
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/i18n] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot's TranslationServer (core/string/translation_server.cpp, 35 methods) matches locales (with script/country fallback + plural rules), holds Translation catalogs loaded from .po (context + plurals) and .csv, and Object.tr()/tr_n() look up the active-locale string; auto_translate_mode makes Controls re-translate their text on locale change; pseudolocalization + number formatting round out the surface. title: ParticleProcessMaterial: register resource class and parse its full property set from .tscn/.tres
description:
[audit-key: vfx-particles/particle-process-material] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: ParticleProcessMaterial is the resource that drives GPU particles; it exposes ~120 properties and 4 enums (EmissionShape POINT/SPHERE/SPHERE_SURFACE/BOX/POINTS/DIRECTED_POINTS/RING, ParticleFlags, SubEmitterMode, CollisionMode) plus min/max + CurveTexture curve for every parameter (scene/resources/particle_process_material.cpp). A .tscn references it as `process_material = SubResource("ParticleProcessMaterial_...")`. Patina current state: the class is unregistered (unregistered.txt; class_db.rs has no entry) and gdresource has no parse path (grep empty), so the process_material is silently dropped; particle nodes fall back to ad-hoc inline material structs (gdscene/src/particle.rs:87, gdserver3d/src/particles3d.rs:110). Implementation approach: (1) register ParticleProcessMaterial (parent Material) in gdobject/src/class_db.rs with its property + enum list; (2) parse the resource from text .tscn/.tres sub-resources in gdresource (loader.rs) into a Rust struct holding the full parameter set (emission shape+params, direction/spread/flatness, gravity, per-param min/max, curves, color/color_ramp, flags, collision/sub_emitter/turbulence groups); (3) hand that struct to the particle node's simulator (the wiring bead) replacing the inline material. Wiring requirement: scene load parses the SubResource -> node.process_material is populated -> simulator reads real values (start this with emission shape + gravity + initial velocity so it is observable).
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn whose GPUParticles2D/3D has a ParticleProcessMaterial SubResource (with e.g. emission_shape=BOX, gravity, initial_velocity_min/max, spread) results in a node whose simulator uses those exact values — particles emit within the box extents and integrate under the parsed gravity — verified by inspecting frame output after scene load (not by constructing the material in Rust). (test: `particle_process_material_parses_from_tscn`)

title: Web runtime: wasm32 cdylib entry + browser boot + rAF fixed-timestep MainLoop driver
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web_wasm_runtime] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

A browser-native engine must actually run in the browser. Godot's web platform (web_main.cpp) provides an emscripten entry that acquires the canvas, initializes the GL/WebGL2 (or WebGPU) context, and installs a main-loop callback driven by the browser; engine.js/preloader.js handle async load + progress. Patina has none of this: no wasm target, no wasm-bindgen/cdylib, and patina-runner (main.rs) is a native JSON-dumping CLI with a for-loop over a fixed frame count — not a real-time rAF loop. Implementation (stage this): (1) add a wasm crate (crate-type=cdylib) with a wasm-bindgen start() entry that acquires the <canvas>, requests a WebGPU adapter/device with a WebGL2 fallback, and installs a panic hook routing to console.error + an on-screen overlay; (2) implement a fixed-timestep driver (accumulator) invoked from requestAnimationFrame that calls gdscene MainLoop::step at the physics tick rate with visibility-hidden throttling and max_fps honoring; (3) feed the existing renderer/scene-tree so a loaded PackedScene renders to the canvas. Factor the timestep accumulator so its logic is unit-testable on native. This is the foundational enabler for the rest of the web-runtime beads (export payload, JS bridge, browser input/audio, persistence).
acceptance_criteria: The engine builds for wasm32-unknown-unknown (verifier build check) with a wasm-bindgen entry point, and the fixed-timestep browser driver advances gdscene MainLoop deterministically: feeding N seconds of accumulated frame time produces the Godot-correct number of physics steps and advances a scripted _process counter. (test: `web_runtime_fixed_timestep_driver`) exercises the accumulator driving a real MainLoop over simulated elapsed time and asserts step count + a scene _process side effect, proving the driver is wired to the scene tick rather than to a fixed batch count.

comments.author: IvoryDune
comments.text:
AUTO-CLOSED BUT THE BROWSER HALF IS NOT DONE -- a game still cannot run in a browser (IvoryDune 2026-07-16). Flagging because a CLOSED status here will overstate web-runtime parity on any scorecard.

DELIVERED: gdscene/src/frame_driver.rs -- FrameDriver turns requestAnimationFrame timestamps into MainLoop::step calls (delta from successive DOMHighResTimeStamps, 0.25s max_frame_delta clamp so a backgrounded tab resuming with a multi-second jump cannot spiral, max_fps coalescing, hidden-tab throttling; skipped callbacks CARRY their delta so N seconds of browser time still yields N seconds of engine time). Pure logic over an injected timestamp, no browser types -- exactly the "factor the accumulator so it is unit-testable on native" the bead asked for. Plus gdscene/tests/web_runtime_fixed_timestep_driver.rs (the named acceptance test): 1s as 60x16.6ms -> 60 steps / 60 physics ticks / _process=60, and the same second as 20x50ms -> 20 steps but STILL 60 physics ticks. Verify with: nextest run -p gdscene --test web_runtime_fixed_timestep_driver

Deliberately did NOT duplicate the physics accumulator: MainLoop::step already banks delta and runs fixed 1/physics_ticks_per_second ticks capped by max_physics_steps_per_frame. The driver owns only the browser-side concerns.

NOT DELIVERED -- suggest splitting into new beads:
 (1) wasm entry does not acquire the <canvas>, request a WebGPU adapter/device, or fall back to WebGL2
 (2) no requestAnimationFrame callback is installed, and no on-screen panic overlay (only console_error_panic_hook, inherited from pat-u3l8c.109)
 (3) nothing feeds the renderer -- a loaded PackedScene does not draw to the canvas
 (4) max_fps is a driver setting, not yet read from Engine.max_fps / ProjectSettings

WHY THE BROWSER HALF IS BLOCKED, NOT MERELY SKIPPED: patina-web cannot depend on gdscene today -- gdscene -> gdaudio -> cpal is an unconditional native dep that breaks the wasm32 build (which is why pat-u3l8c.109 deliberately scoped patina-web to gdcore+gdvariant only). Wiring FrameDriver into patina-web's rAF entry requires the cpal cfg-gating owned by the audio web bead (pat-u3l8c.112). The driver was therefore landed in gdscene, where MainLoop lives and where it is natively provable now; the follow-up is then pure glue over an already-tested accumulator.

description:
[audit-key: autoload-global-singletons-runtime/autoload-editor-ui] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

GODOT: the editor's Project Settings -> Autoload tab lets the user add/remove/rename/reorder/enable autoloads, persisting to the [autoload] section. PATINA: a complete model exists — gdeditor/src/autoload_manager.rs AutoloadManager (add/remove/rename/move_up/move_down/set_enabled/globals/to_cfg/from_cfg) — but it is UNWIRED: no editor_server.rs route references it, project_settings_dialog.rs has 0 autoload refs, and EDITOR_HTML (editor_ui.rs) never mentions autoload. comments.author: IvoryDune
comments.text:
AUTO-CLOSED BUT ONLY ~25% DELIVERED (IvoryDune 2026-07-16).

DELIVERED: gdeditor/src/autoload_manager.rs gains to_project_godot_section() / from_project_godot_section() = REAL project.godot [autoload] INI (Name="*path", the * marks enabled exactly as Godot's Enable checkbox does, declaration-order preserving, reads only [autoload] out of a full project file) + 4 unit tests. Verify with: nextest run -p gdeditor --lib autoload_manager

WHY THAT WAS NEEDED: this bead's own plan said "persist via to_cfg", but to_cfg() is serde_json::to_string_pretty(self) -- it emits JSON despite its doc comment claiming "Serializes the [autoload] section to project-settings text". Following the bead literally would write a JSON blob into project.godot where an INI section belongs, and the acceptance (Global="*res://global.gd" present in the file) could never pass. The to_cfg/from_cfg docs are now corrected to say plainly they are JSON state snapshots, not project.godot text.

NOT DELIVERED -- suggest splitting into new beads:
 (1) hold an AutoloadManager in EditorState, loaded via from_project_godot_section at startup
 (2) editor_server.rs routes: GET list, POST add/remove/reorder/toggle-enabled, each rewriting project.godot
 (3) Autoload tab markup in EDITOR_HTML (editor_ui.rs) + project_settings_dialog.rs, guarded by an EDITOR_HTML-string test so the served JS actually calls the routes
 (4) the named acceptance test editor_autoload_tab_crud_persists

Scoped out deliberately, not overlooked: editor_server.rs is 21k lines and carries uncommitted concurrent work; a half-applied edit there breaks gdeditor for every worker in the swarm. The foundation landed above is what those routes call, so (1)-(4) are now purely additive.

SEPARATE BUG -- needs its own gdresource bead: ProjectLoader::get_autoloads (gdresource/src/project.rs ~331) ends with entries.sort_by(|a,b| a.name.cmp(&b.name)) "Sort by name for deterministic order". Godot uses DECLARATION order, and that order IS load order (an autoload may reference one declared before it). Patina therefore boots autoloads alphabetically, silently reordering _ready for any project whose declaration order is not alphabetical -- breaking the exact cross-autoload reference that pat-nzgdu.3 / pat-nzgdu.70 exist to support. Left untouched here: wrong crate for this bead, shared code, and existing tests may encode the sorted order.

title: ClassDB: expose script singleton + add signals/constants/enums to ClassInfo + instance reflection
description:
[audit-key: core-object/core-object-classdb] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot ground truth: ClassDB is a global singleton scripts call (ClassDB.class_exists, get_parent_class, get_inheriters_from_class, can_instantiate, instantiate, class_has_method, class_get_method_list, class_has_signal, class_get_signal_list, class_get_integer_constant(_list), class_has_enum/class_get_enum_list/class_get_enum_constants, class_get_property_list); and every Object answers has_method/has_signal/get_method_list/get_signal_list/get_property_list/get_instance_id. Patina current state: ClassInfo (class_db.rs:64-83) stores only properties+methods (no signals/constants/enums); PropertyInfo/MethodInfo are thin (class_db.rs:17-52); nothing exposes ClassDB or instance reflection to GDScript (grep 0). Implementation: extend ClassInfo/ClassRegistration with signals (name+arg schema), integer constants, and enums, and populate them in the register_*_classes tables; enrich PropertyInfo with type/usage/hint_string and MethodInfo with return/arg types; add a ClassDB singleton path in the interpreter that routes to gdobject::class_db; add SceneAccess reflection entry points (has_method/has_signal/get_method_list/get_signal_list/get_property_list/get_instance_id) implemented against ClassDB + the node. Wiring requirement: a script must query ClassDB and its own class metadata and get non-empty, correct results.
acceptance_criteria: A script runs `assert(ClassDB.class_exists("Sprite2D")); assert(ClassDB.get_parent_class("Sprite2D") == "Node2D"); assert(ClassDB.class_has_method("Node","get_parent")); assert(has_method("_ready")); assert(get_method_list().size() > 0)` with no UndefinedFunction, and class_get_signal_list("Node") returns a non-empty list. (test: `classdb_singleton_reflection_test`) runnable via cargo nextest --test classdb_singleton_reflection_test.

comments.author: RedTower
comments.text: Triage (RedTower, no-run analysis): the gdobject-local foundation is a clean ADDITIVE slice — extend ClassInfo + ClassRegistration with signals/integer_constants/enums (default-empty fields; ONLY ONE ClassInfo{} construction site at class_db.rs:155 to update), add builder methods + inherited query fns (class_has_signal/class_get_signal_list/class_get_integer_constant/class_get_enum_list mirroring get_property_list), populate a few signals on Node. The bead's ACCEPTANCE (classdb_singleton_reflection_test) is GDScript-driven, so it additionally needs the cross-crate interpreter part: a ClassDB singleton path in gdscript-interop + SceneAccess reflection entry points (has_method/has_signal/get_method_list/get_signal_list/get_property_list/get_instance_id).
