comments.author: GentleBadger
comments.text: PARTIAL by GentleBadger (2026-07-16, uncommitted; verify cmds in completion mail msg 53946). Followed RedTower's triage. DONE (2 crates, additive): gdobject/src/class_db.rs — SignalInfo{name,arguments} + EnumInfo{name,constants}; ClassInfo/ClassRegistration gain signals/integer_constants/enums (DEFAULT-EMPTY so all existing registrations are unaffected); builders .signal()/.constant()/.enumeration() (enum constants also register as integer constants, as Godot does); inherited query fns get_signal_list/class_has_signal/get_integer_constant_list/class_get_integer_constant/get_enum_list/class_has_enum/get_enum_constants (base-first like get_property_list; derived-first shadowing for constant lookup). title: RefCounted: attach RefCountedBase to script RefCounted/Resource instances so ref counting + auto-free work
description:
[audit-key: core-object/core-object-refcounted] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot ground truth: RefCounted.new() starts at refcount 1; sharing a reference increments and dropping decrements via reference()/unreference(); reaching 0 frees the object; get_reference_count() is script-observable; init_ref sets up first ownership. Patina current state: RefCountedBase (ref_counted.rs) is a correct-but-orphan primitive — 0 call sites outside gdobject (workspace grep) and no init_ref; script-created RefCounted objects therefore never count references or free. Implementation: give each script-instantiated RefCounted/Resource an owned RefCountedBase; increment/decrement it as the interpreter copies/drops Variant references that hold such objects; expose reference()/unreference()/get_reference_count()/init_ref() through the ObjectId (or Resource) dispatch and SceneAccess; free the backing object (and clear it from the alive registry) when the count hits 0. Also promote the WeakRef alive registry off thread_local so validity is process-global. Wiring requirement: RefCounted.new() in a script yields count 1 and its get_reference_count reflects additional references.
acceptance_criteria: A script executes `var r = RefCounted.new(); assert(r.get_reference_count() == 1); var r2 = r; assert(r.get_reference_count() == 2)` (or the engine's reference model) with no UndefinedFunction, and dropping all references invalidates a weakref taken to it. (test: `refcounted_reference_lifecycle_test`) runnable via cargo nextest --test refcounted_reference_lifecycle_test.

title: Editor: Import dock + asset import pipeline wired into FileSystem
description: No Import tab / reimport UI. Wire the import pipeline (glTF, PNG/JPEG/WebP, WAV/OGG, fonts) into the FileSystem dock with an Import settings panel and reimport-on-change. Acceptance: dropping a PNG into the project produces a usable Texture2D with import settings; covers fs_dock_import_hooks live.
close_reason: Import pipeline acceptance met: dropping a PNG into the project produces a usable Texture2D with import settings; fs_dock_import_hooks live (pat-oepf7). The import pipeline is wired into the FileSystem dock: the Import tab (#import-dock with an 'Import As:' select) populated via renderImportDock; GET /api/import_settings derives the importer from the extension (ImportResourceType::from_extension) -> a PNG reports importable=true, importer 'Texture2D', presets [Default, 2D Pixel, 2D, 3D] and 7 editable options (compression/filter/mipmaps/etc.), mirroring Godot's texture importer; POST /api/import_settings persists, POST /api/reimport reimports-on-change; and the texture decode path (TextureCache.get -> load_png -> gdrender2d::texture::decode_png, supporting RGBA + grayscale) turns a PNG into a usable Texture2D{width,height,pixels}. Added the named test fs_dock_import_hooks: /api/import_settings for a .png -> importable Texture2D with the 2D Pixel preset + compression/filter options; /api/reimport returns the path; a real PNG (encode_png of a 3x2 FrameBuffer) decode_png's back to a Texture2D with width 3/height 2 and the correct corner pixel; a .txt reports importable=false; the served dock wires /api/import_settings. Test PASS. Test-only change -> no regression risk. Chrome-verified on the running editor: the Import tab opens the dock (Import As: select present) and the served editor reads the PNG's real texture settings (Texture2D, 7 options, Godot presets). Source: upstream/godot/editor/import/resource_importer_texture.cpp + editor/import_dock.cpp.

KEY FACT (correcting a common misread): gdrender3d is a CPU SOFTWARE renderer. wgpu/pollster/bytemuck are optional=true in its Cargo.toml. FrameBuffer3D (renderer.rs:31) has set_pixel/set_depth with in-crate unit tests (:1949+). Shadow maps are CPU too (:424). So "decal projects albedo" / "fog volume density" is assertable in a PLAIN UNIT TEST on a framebuffer — no GPU, no editor, no viewport needed.

ADDITIVE-SAFE PLAN (breaks zero call sites — reflection_probes is the exact precedent):
  SoftwareRenderer3D (renderer.rs:108) holds PRIVATE Vec fields (instances, lights, reflection_probes) and BOTH constructors (new() :118, wireframe() :127) are in the SAME file. So a new private Vec field + new add_/accessor methods is purely additive.
  1. Add `fog_volumes: Vec<PlacedFogVolume>` where PlacedFogVolume{volume: FogVolume, transform: Transform3D} (transform needed: sample_density takes LOCAL space, so world->local via the inverse). Init in both ctors.

  3. Add `apply_fog_volume_pass(pixels:&mut [Color], depth:&[f32], w, h, volumes:&[PlacedFogVolume], inv_proj, camera_transform)` as a sibling static fn to apply_fog_pass (:689). Reconstruct each fragment's world pos from depth via inv_proj (apply_fog_pass already does exactly this — copy that reconstruction), map world->local per volume, sample_density, accumulate density and blend albedo + add emission.
  4. Call it from the two render entry points right next to the existing apply_fog_pass calls (:321 and :622).
  5. Tests in-crate: render a frame with a volume in front of the camera and assert the pixel shifts toward material.albedo; density=0 / volume outside the frustum leaves pixels unchanged; a point outside the shape contributes nothing (sample_density already returns 0.0 outside).
  Decal: same shape — needs a Decal type + projection math in gdserver3d first (see box_projection.rs), then a decal pass + a private Vec on SoftwareRenderer3D.

comments.author: GreenBadger
comments.text:
[GreenBadger 2026-07-16] CORRECTION to my previous comment + the real root cause of the Decal half.

I said earlier that Decal3D was "already fully implemented, just in the wrong crate". That was WRONG, and the truth is more important:

**gdscene/src/decal.rs IS DEAD CODE. It is never compiled.**
  - `grep -rn "mod decal" crates/` across the whole workspace = ZERO hits. The file is not declared by gdscene/src/lib.rs (which lists ~50 other `pub mod`s) nor by any other module.
  - Nothing anywhere references Decal3D / DecalRegistry (grep outside the file itself = zero hits).
  - It IS tracked/committed (df37e87 "Checkpoint: full engine, editor, 3D...") — so it was written, committed, and silently never wired in. 709 lines that have never been type-checked by rustc even once.

So the bead's premise ("Decal + FogVolume have math but are never called from renderer.rs/shader.rs") understates it for decals: the decal math is not merely uncalled, it is not part of any crate. Any "it's mostly done, just wire it" estimate is wrong.

Good news — it is probably close to compiling. It parses cleanly, and its entire external API surface is tiny and verified to exist: `use gdcore::math::{Color, Vector3}` + `use gdcore::math3d::Transform3D`; the only methods it calls are `.abs()` (37x), `Transform3D::xform` (2x), `Transform3D::inverse` (2x), `Color::WHITE`, `Vector3::new`. NOTHING gdscene-specific. That means it can move down the dependency graph with no import changes.

WHY IT MUST MOVE (unchanged from my last comment, and it is a hard constraint): the renderer is gdrender3d, and **gdscene depends on gdrender3d** (gdscene/Cargo.toml:19). gdrender3d can therefore never `use gdscene::decal` — dependency cycle, rejected by cargo. gdserver3d is where every other server-side render primitive lives (light.rs, reflection_probe.rs, fog_volume.rs) and gdrender3d already depends on it, and gdserver3d needs only gdcore — which is all decal.rs imports.

EXACT RECIPE for a builder-capable worker (should be quick):
  1. `git mv crates/gdscene/src/decal.rs crates/gdserver3d/src/decal.rs` — imports need NO change (gdcore only). Zero call sites to fix because there are zero callers.
  2. gdserver3d/src/lib.rs: add `pub mod decal;` (alphabetically after `csg`) + `pub use decal::{Decal3D, DecalRegistry, DecalTexture};` next to the fog_volume re-export on line 40. NOTE: this is the first time these 709 lines are ever compiled — expect to fix real rustc errors here. That is the actual work of this half.
  3. gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs: add the decal pass using the SAME additive pattern already used for fog volumes in this bead — a private `decals: Vec<PlacedDecal>` on SoftwareRenderer3D (both ctors are in that file, so zero external call sites change), `add_decal()`/`decals()` accessors, and an `apply_decal_pass(pixels, depth, w, h, decals, inv_proj, camera_transform)` sibling to `apply_fog_volume_pass`. Reconstruct the fragment world pos from depth (copy that reconstruction), then use the existing `Decal3D::sample_alpha(world_point, camera_distance) -> Option<f64>` to modulate albedo by `modulate`/`energy`. Wire at BOTH entry points.
  4. Tests: same shape as the new fog_volume_* tests (identity inv_proj + identity camera makes a fragment's world pos exactly its NDC, so expected values are hand-checkable).

I did NOT do steps 1-3: this lane is hook-blocked from the Rust builder, and declaring 709 never-compiled lines into gdserver3d — which gdrender3d, gdscene and everything above depend on — is precisely the blind cross-crate change that breaks the build for the whole swarm. It needs someone who can run the compiler.

STATUS: FogVolume half delivered (see previous comment). Decal half NOT started. Keep this bead OPEN; ideally split it, and add a separate bead for "declare + fix-compile the orphaned decal.rs into gdserver3d" since that is a real unit of work on its own.

Patina has no WebSocket implementation anywhere in engine-rs (grep websocketpeer/websocket_peer over crates returns nothing), so GDScript multiplayer/realtime code using WebSocketPeer cannot run.

IMPLEMENTATION: add WebSocketPeer with connect_to_url, send/send_text, get_available_packet_count/get_packet, poll, ready-state lifecycle (CONNECTING/OPEN/CLOSING/CLOSED) and close codes matching Godot's API, registered in class_db; client-side first, over the gdplatform TCP/TLS stack.

close_reason: WebSocketPeer (client-side) implemented over the gdplatform std::net transport with a hand-rolled RFC6455 stack (zero new runtime deps; tiny inline SHA1+base64). Files: NEW crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_peer.rs (connect_to_url, send/send_text, get_available_packet_count/get_packet/was_string_packet, poll, close(code,reason), CONNECTING/OPEN/CLOSING/CLOSED state machine matching Godot WebSocketPeer.State, get_close_code/-1 sentinel/get_close_reason; frame codec mask/unmask + text/binary/close/ping/pong + fragmentation; public helpers encode_frame/decode_frame/Frame/Opcode/parse_handshake_key/websocket_handshake_response reused by the in-process test echo server); lib.rs re-exports; gdobject/src/class_db.rs WebSocketPeer:PacketPeer:RefCounted in register_networking_classes; websocket cases appended to tests/networking_parity_test.rs. Test cases: websocket_peer_handshake_reaches_open, _text_echo_round_trip, _binary_echo_round_trip, _clean_close_with_code_and_reason, _poll_state_transitions, _rejects_wss_without_tls, _registered_in_classdb. title: Editor: Script mode shows a central script editor (currently the SCRIPT button is cosmetic; viewport stays 2D)
description:
Found via live browser inspection (localhost:8080/editor): clicking the SCRIPT main-screen mode button highlights it and opens the small bottom Script panel tab, but the CENTRAL view still shows the 2D viewport (grid + node markers). Godot's Script mode replaces the central area with a full script editor.

ROOT CAUSE (same class as pat-7i8u4 / pat-v4o3a): the frontend mode handler (editor_ui.rs setupModeButtons) for 'script' only POSTs the mode + clicks the bottom Script tab; it never swaps the central #viewport-panel for a script editor. The full script editor ALREADY EXISTS (renderScript/fetchScript/highlightGDScript/saveScript with header, line numbers, syntax highlight, auto-indent) but renders into the bottom #script-panel only. Server already exposes GET /api/script, /api/script/save, /api/script/main_view, and /api/editor/main_view returns component 'script_editor'/is_2d_viewport:false for script mode — but the frontend never renders a central script view.

SCOPE (phase 1): when editor mode is 'script', the central area shows the script editor full-size (relocate the existing #script-panel editor into a central container), not the 2D viewport; switching back to 2D/3D restores the viewport. Empty state offers a New Script action. Open-scripts list, find/replace UI, and breakpoint gutter wiring are follow-ups.

TEST (app-level): served /editor HTML has a central script-editor container and the mode handler shows it in script mode; GET /api/editor/main_view after POST /api/editor/mode {script} reports component script_editor / is_2d_viewport:false. (test: editor_script_mode_serves_script_editor_view)
acceptance_criteria: In script mode the central area shows the script editor (relocated from the bottom panel), not the 2D viewport; switching to 2D/3D restores the viewport. Served /editor HTML has a central script-editor container wired into the mode switch; GET /api/editor/main_view after POST mode script reports component script_editor / is_2d_viewport:false. Test: editor_script_mode_serves_script_editor_view

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
VERIFIED + CLOSING. Script mode now shows the script editor in the CENTRAL area instead of the 2D viewport. Implementation (editor_ui.rs): added a central #script-editor-panel + #script-main-host; new showScriptMode(on) relocates the existing #script-panel code editor into the central host in script mode and restores it + the viewport when leaving (reuses the full editor — header/Save/New, line numbers, syntax highlight, auto-indent — with no duplicate-id issues). Mode handler calls showScriptMode(mode==='script'). Test crates/gdeditor/tests/editor_script_view_test.rs::editor_script_mode_serves_script_editor_view PASSES (served HTML has the central container + wiring; /api/editor/main_view reports script_editor / is_2d_viewport:false). Verified LIVE in Chrome: clicking SCRIPT shows the central code editor, viewport gone, 'Switched to script mode' logged.

FOLLOW-UP REQUEST (selecting a node shows its script) — DONE: the selection handler already calls fetchScript(_script_path); the demo scene just had no scripts attached. examples/editor.rs now attaches fixtures/scripts/player.gd to Player and enemy_spawner.gd to Enemy (sets _script_path). Verified LIVE: selecting Player in Script mode loads player.gd into the central editor (header res://fixtures/scripts/player.gd, line-numbered source, script badge on the tree row, _script_path in the inspector). title: Verifier timeout kill misses sccache-parented rustc orphans
description:
The pat-regax process-group kill reaps the verify's bash/cargo/nextest tree on timeout, but compiles routed through RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache run as children of the long-lived sccache SERVER process (pid 1-parented), outside the verify's process group. Observed live 2026-07-14: after the platform_suite verify timed out and was group-killed, its rustc (gdrender3d) survived for 6+ min at 0 CPU, parented by sccache, holding an sccache slot.

Fix options: (a) on timeout, enumerate+kill rustc processes whose cmdline matches the verify's workspace AND whose start time falls within the verify window; (b) run verifies with RUSTC_WRAPPER unset and rely on the private target-verifier incremental cache; (c) sccache --stop-server on timeout (heavy: aborts other sessions' compiles).

Acceptance: a test in verifier.rs proving a wrapper-spawned grandchild outside the process group is reaped after timeout (analogous to verifier_timeout_kills_process_group).

title: Verifier: kill the entire process group on verify timeout (orphaned cargo-nextest survives and wedges the lane)
description:
Observed 2026-06-10: each 900s verify timeout killed the am-run/shell parent but left cargo-nextest alive as an orphan, each holding ~26 spawned test-binary children. Four generations piled up (15:48, 16:03, 16:18, 16:33 - exactly one per 15-min verify cycle), 102 hung child processes total, all stuck at _dyld_start (AMFI code-sign wedge). The orphans also held the cargo build-dir lock so every later verify spent its whole 900s waiting.

IMPLEMENTATION: in the orchestrator verifier lane, launch the verify command in its own process group (setsid/setpgid) and on timeout send SIGKILL to the negative pgid; then waitpid-reap. Also assert post-kill that no cargo-nextest/test-binary descendants survive (pgrep by pgid) and log if they do.

TEST: spawn a fake long-running command tree (sh -c 'sleep 1000 & sleep 1000') via the verifier timeout path with a 2s timeout and assert zero surviving descendants after the kill (test: verifier_timeout_kills_process_group).
close_reason: verifier.rs: bash verify child now leads its own process group (process_group(0)); on timeout SIGKILL the negative pgid (whole tree, not just bash) + surviving_group_members() post-kill assertion logs any orphans. Stops orphaned cargo-nextest from holding the build-dir lock. Test verifier_timeout_kills_process_group PASS (cargo nextest -p patina-orchestrator).

title: Editor viewport: node-name labels render as tofu/placeholder boxes for most glyphs (Player -> ??a???)
description:
Found via live browser inspection of examples/editor.rs (http://localhost:8080/editor, demo_2d.tscn).

'Enemy' and 'Ground' similar. Vertical ruler tick labels are also garbled.

ROOT CAUSE AREA: the editor overlay text path in the software renderer (gdrender2d / gdeditor viewport overlay) is drawing labels with a glyph set that covers only a small subset of ASCII (some lowercase letters work, most upper/lowercase missing). pat-04f (BitmapFont/FontFile text rendering) is closed, so either the overlay label path does not use that font system or the fallback atlas is incomplete.

IMPLEMENTATION: route editor viewport label drawing through the real font rendering path (full printable-ASCII coverage minimum) instead of the partial debug atlas; same for ruler tick labels.

TEST: render demo_2d.tscn editor frame and assert the glyph lookup used by viewport labels returns a non-placeholder glyph for every char in 'PlayerEnemyGround0123456789-' (unit), plus an app-level check that the rendered label bounding box for 'Player' is non-uniform across the 6 glyph cells (test: editor_viewport_label_glyph_coverage).
acceptance_criteria: Every char in 'PlayerEnemyGround0123456789-' resolves to a real glyph in the viewport label text path (no placeholder box); ruler tick labels legible; test editor_viewport_label_glyph_coverage passes

title: Animation: expose AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback so scripts can travel/start/stop a state machine
description:
[audit-key: animation/anim-state-machine] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/animation/animation_blend_tree.cpp + animation_node_state_machine.cpp; doc/classes/AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback.xml; extension_api.json class AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback (methods travel, travel_to_next_blend, start, next, stop, is_playing, get_current_node, get_current_play_position, get_current_length, get_travel_path, get_fading_from_node) | upstream/godot/scene/animation/animation_node_state_machine.cpp; doc/classes/AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition.xml (properties: xfade_time, xfade_curve, break_loop_at_end, reset, priority, switch_mode {IMMEDIATE,SYNC,AT_END}, advance_mode {DISABLED,ENABLED,AUTO}, advance_condition, advance_expression) | upstream/godot/editor/animation/animation_state_machine_editor.cpp, animation_blend_space_1d_editor.cpp, animation_blend_space_2d_editor.cpp, animation_blend_tree_editor_plugin.cpp

**Godot classes:** AnimationNodeStateMachine, AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback, AnimationTree, AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition, AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D, AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D, AnimationNodeBlendTree

**Patina today:**
- [animation] Patina implements the algorithm but nothing calls it: `StateMachine::travel` (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs:507), `travel_path` (:467) and `is_travelling` (:518). `grep -rn '\.travel(|is_travelling|travel_path' --include=*.rs crates/` returns ONLY those three definitions plus five `#[cfg(test)]` hits inside the same file (animation_tree.rs:2127-2187). No script path exists either: `AnimationTree::get_parameter` (animation_tree.rs:611) returns only Variants that were previously `set`, so `$AnimationTree.get("parameters/playback")` yields Nil, and `grep -rn 'parameters/playback' --include=*.rs crates/` returns 0 hits. `crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs` has `animation_player_*` hooks (lines 544-635) but no `animation_tree_*` hook at all. Registration exists as a name only: class_db.rs registers `AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback` (1 occurrence) with no methods.
- [animation] Patina's `StateTransition` carries exactly two Godot fields: `condition` and `crossfade` — /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs:525-532. The .tscn reader reads only `xfade_time` and `advance_condition` — engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree_tscn.rs:277-278. `grep -rn 'advance_expression|break_loop_at_end|auto_advance' --include=*.rs crates/` → 0 hits each; `advance_mode`/transition `priority`/`xfade_curve`/`reset` also 0 hits in the state-machine path. `SwitchMode` (animation_tree.rs:186-212) exists but is only used by `AnimationNodeTransition` (animation_tree.rs:222), not by state-machine edges. Consequence: an ADVANCE_MODE_AUTO edge (the standard "attack → idle when the clip ends" pattern) never fires.
- [editor-ux] POST /api/animation/tree/state/move, /state/remove, /transition/remove and /transition/set are all in the editor_server.rs dispatch table but have 0 references in editor_ui.rs (only /api/animation/tree, /tree/state/add and /tree/transition/add are called). So the served state-machine graph is add-only: states cannot be moved or deleted and transitions cannot be edited or removed. Blend spaces and blend trees are absent entirely: `grep -ci 'blend space\|blend_space\|blendSpace' editor_ui.rs` = 0, and no /api/animation/tree/blend* route exists.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree_tscn.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/anim_tree_graph.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: every state-machine-driven game steers the graph through the playback object — `var p = $AnimationTree.get("parameters/playback"); p.travel("Run")`. `AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback` (upstream/godot/scene/animation/animation_node_state_machine.cpp, doc/classes/AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback.xml) exposes travel(node, reset_on_teleport=true), travel_to_next_blend, start(node, reset=true), next(), stop(), is_playing(), get_current_node(), get_current_play_position(), get_current_length(), get_travel_path(), get_fading_from_node(). Nested state machines expose their own playback at `parameters/<name>/playback`.

Patina current state: the BFS travel algorithm is fully implemented and unit-tested but has ZERO runtime callers. `StateMachine::travel` engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs:507, `travel_path` :467, `is_travelling` :518 — the only call sites are the module's own `#[cfg(test)]` tests (animation_tree.rs:2127-2187). `AnimationTree::get_parameter` (animation_tree.rs:611) only returns previously-`set` Variants so `get("parameters/playback")` is Nil; `SceneAccess` (engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs:544-635) has no `animation_tree_*` method at all. A game can therefore only flip `parameters/conditions/<x>` booleans; it cannot travel.

Implementation approach: (1) add a `StateMachinePlayback` handle type in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs that addresses a `StateMachine` by its `parameters/<path>` prefix inside the attached `AnimationTree`; (2) mint an ObjectId-style handle for it in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs `get_node_property` when `prop` ends in `/playback` (mirroring the existing tween-handle pattern at scripting.rs:2943 `tween_call`); (3) add `animation_tree_playback_call(&mut self, handle: u64, method: &str, args: &[Variant]) -> Option<Variant>` to `SceneAccess` in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs and dispatch it from the ObjectId method arm in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs (next to the `animation_player_*` arms at interpreter.rs:9335-9522), routing travel/start/next/stop/is_playing/get_current_node/get_travel_path onto the StateMachine; (4) make `start(node, reset)` and `next()` real (snap current, clear travel queue / take next hop).

Wiring requirement: .tscn with AnimationTree(tree_root=AnimationNodeStateMachine) + attached GDScript → `_ready` grabs `parameters/playback` → `travel("run")` → `MainLoop::step` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2968 `process_animation_trees`) crossfades along the path → the target node's animated property reaches the "run" clip's value and `get_current_node()` reports "run".

**Merged findings (3):** AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback — the `parameters/playback` control object (travel/start/next/stop/is_playing/get_current_node/get_travel_path/get_current_play_position/get_current_length/get_fading_from_node); AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition full field surface — switch_mode, advance_mode (incl. AUTO), advance_expression, priority, xfade_curve, reset, break_loop_at_end; AnimationTree editor: state machine edit ops, blend spaces 1D/2D, blend tree graph

**Prove it:** Loading a .tscn whose AnimationTree holds a 3-state machine (idle→run→jump) with an attached script that calls `$AnimationTree.get("parameters/playback").travel("jump")` in `_ready`, then stepping MainLoop past the declared xfade times, leaves the driven node's property at the `jump` clip's sampled value and `get_current_node()` == "jump"; `get_travel_path()` returned the two-hop path before arrival. (test: `animation_tree_state_machine_playback_travel_from_script`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test animation_tree_state_machine_playback_travel_from_script`.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn whose AnimationTree holds a 3-state machine (idle→run→jump) with an attached script that calls `$AnimationTree.get("parameters/playback").travel("jump")` in `_ready`, then stepping MainLoop past the declared xfade times, leaves the driven node's property at the `jump` clip's sampled value and `get_current_node()` == "jump"; `get_travel_path()` returned the two-hop path before arrival. (test: `animation_tree_state_machine_playback_travel_from_script`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test animation_tree_state_machine_playback_travel_from_script`.

title: Editor3D: wire per-node gizmo handles end-to-end (shape/light/camera) through the served viewport
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-3d-gizmo-handles] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/scene/3d/gizmos/*_gizmo_plugin.cpp (35 plugin files: collision_shape_3d, light_3d, camera_3d, decal, fog_volume, reflection_probe, spring_arm_3d, ray_cast_3d, gpu_particles_3d, soft_body_3d, vehicle_body_3d, joint_3d, occluder_instance_3d, spring_bone_3d, ...); Gizmo3DHelper handle drag

**Godot classes:** EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin, CollisionShape3D, Light3D, Camera3D, Path3D, SpringArm3D

**Patina today:**
- [editor-ux] gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_handles.rs implements Godot's box face-handle math (box_get_handles/box_set_handle/box_handle_drag_commands) but has ZERO non-test callers: `grep -rn viewport_3d_handles --include=*.rs` returns only lib.rs:156 (mod decl) and crates/gdeditor/tests/viewport3d_gizmo_handles_e2e.rs:18. That test is named `_e2e` and its docstring says 'This wires it to the editor's undo stack', yet `grep -c 'http_post|TcpStream|editor_server'` in it = 0 — it calls the module directly and never touches the served editor. The only handle route that exists, `GET /api/viewport/shape_handles` (editor_server.rs:2430 -> api_shape_handles editor_server.rs:14014), hard-returns `{"ok":true,"editable":false,"handles":[]}` for any class != "CollisionShape2D" (editor_server.rs:14028-14031). No `/api/viewport/3d/handle*` route exists in the 288-route table. Result: in the served 3D viewport, no node type exposes draggable gizmo handles — only the shared transform gizmo (viewport_3d.rs:1953 begin_gizmo_drag) works.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_handles.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/viewport3d_gizmo_handles_e2e.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: every selected 3D node draws its own gizmo with draggable handles (upstream/godot/editor/scene/3d/gizmos/collision_shape_3d_gizmo_plugin.cpp resizes BoxShape3D/SphereShape3D/CapsuleShape3D via Gizmo3DHelper; light_3d_gizmo_plugin.cpp drags omni range and spot angle/range; camera_3d_gizmo_plugin.cpp drags FOV/size). Dragging a handle mutates the shape/light sub-resource and lands on the editor undo stack.\n\nPATINA: the math exists and is orphaned. engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_handles.rs provides box_get_handles/box_set_handle/box_handle_drag_commands with unit tests, but the only reference outside the file is lib.rs:156 (module declaration) and crates/gdeditor/tests/viewport3d_gizmo_handles_e2e.rs:18, which imports the module directly and never issues an HTTP request (0 matches for http_post/TcpStream/editor_server in that file) — so a green 'e2e' test proves nothing about the served editor. The only handle endpoint, api_shape_handles (editor_server.rs:14014), returns editable:false for every class except CollisionShape2D (editor_server.rs:14028). editor_ui.rs's 3D pointer handlers (editor_ui.rs:6167-6240) only post /api/viewport/3d/gizmo/{begin,update,end} for the transform gizmo.\n\nAPPROACH: add `GET /api/viewport/3d/handles?node_id=` + `POST /api/viewport/3d/handle/{begin,update,end}` to editor_server.rs, backed by viewport_3d_handles.rs for BoxShape3D and new sphere/capsule/cylinder handle helpers, plus OmniLight3D range and SpotLight3D angle/range handles. Project handle world positions to screen space with the existing Viewport3D camera (viewport_3d.rs) so the client can hit-test. Emit the existing EditorCommand::SetProperty pairs onto s.undo_stack so undo/.tscn persistence come for free (the __shape__* / __resref__shape companions are already saved by TscnSaver).\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: editor_ui.rs must (a) fetch handles for the selected node when the 3D viewport is active, (b) render them over #viewport-container as it already does for 2D in #shape-handle-overlay, and (c) post drag begin/update/end. Server route + Rust-level test with no EDITOR_HTML caller does not count.

**Prove it:** Loading a .tscn with a CollisionShape3D(BoxShape3D size 2,2,2) and an OmniLight3D, selecting each in the served editor, shows draggable handles; dragging the +X box handle to x=2 rewrites the shape to size.x=4 with the node re-centred, POST /api/undo restores 2, and saving the scene writes the new size into the sub-resource. `pub const EDITOR_HTML` contains a fetch of the new handle endpoints. (test: `editor_3d_gizmo_handles_served`) drives the real editor_server over TCP (like the existing http_post helpers in editor_server.rs tests) and asserts EDITOR_HTML references /api/viewport/3d/handle.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn with a CollisionShape3D(BoxShape3D size 2,2,2) and an OmniLight3D, selecting each in the served editor, shows draggable handles; dragging the +X box handle to x=2 rewrites the shape to size.x=4 with the node re-centred, POST /api/undo restores 2, and saving the scene writes the new size into the sub-resource. `pub const EDITOR_HTML` contains a fetch of the new handle endpoints. title: Physics2D: wire StaticBody2D conveyor velocities and implement AnimatableBody2D
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-staticbody-family] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/2d/physics/static_body_2d.cpp (constant_linear_velocity/constant_angular_velocity → PhysicsServer2D BODY_STATE_LINEAR_VELOCITY on a static body) and upstream/godot/scene/2d/physics/animatable_body_2d.cpp:33-66 (AnimatableBody2D extends StaticBody2D, sync_to_physics installs body_set_state_sync_callback so the body pushes the platform's motion into contacting bodies).

**Godot classes:** StaticBody2D, AnimatableBody2D

**Patina today:**
- [physics-2d] The solver fully implements surface velocity: `PhysicsBody2D::constant_linear_velocity` / `constant_angular_velocity` at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/body.rs:117-122, consumed by the friction path at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/solver.rs:341, with green tests at solver.rs:864 and the integration test /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/tests/physics2d_solver_stacking_conveyor_sleep.rs:178 — which constructs `PhysicsBody2D` structs directly and never touches a SceneTree. The scene bridge never reads the properties: `grep -rn "constant_linear_velocity|constant_angular_velocity" engine-rs/crates/gdscene/ engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/` → 0 hits; the only workspace mentions outside gdphysics2d/gdphysics3d are the editor inspector schema (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:3296-3297) and the runner's class defaults (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/class_defaults.rs:66-69). `register_bodies` (physics_server.rs:945-990) sets 16 properties, none of them these. Separately, `body_type_for_class` (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:32-39) maps only RigidBody2D/StaticBody2D/CharacterBody2D — an `AnimatableBody2D` node in a .tscn becomes NO physics body at all (no collision, no platform velocity), and `sync_to_physics` has 0 hits in gdphysics2d/gdscene.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/body.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/solver.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: StaticBody2D.constant_linear_velocity / constant_angular_velocity drag contacting bodies without moving the static body itself (upstream/godot/scene/2d/physics/static_body_2d.cpp) — conveyor belts and turntables. AnimatableBody2D (upstream/godot/scene/2d/physics/animatable_body_2d.cpp:33-66) is a StaticBody2D whose `sync_to_physics` makes the physics body follow the node's animated/tweened transform and imparts that motion to riders.

PATINA: the solver already does the work — `PhysicsBody2D::constant_linear_velocity`/`constant_angular_velocity` (engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/body.rs:117-122), surface-velocity friction (engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/solver.rs:341), green tests at solver.rs:864 and engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/tests/physics2d_solver_stacking_conveyor_sleep.rs:178 — but those tests build `PhysicsBody2D` structs by hand. The scene bridge never reads the node properties (0 hits for `constant_linear_velocity` in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/), so an authored conveyor does nothing. `body_type_for_class` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:32-39) has no `AnimatableBody2D` arm, so those nodes are not physics at all.

APPROACH: in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs, extend `body_type_for_class` with `"AnimatableBody2D" => BodyType::Kinematic` (Godot treats it as a moved static body). In `register_bodies` (~physics_server.rs:945) read `constant_linear_velocity` (Vector2) and `constant_angular_velocity` (float) onto the body next to the existing `gravity_scale`/`linear_damp` reads. Re-read them each tick in `sync_to_physics` (physics_server.rs:1288) under the Static/Kinematic arms so a script can change a belt's speed. For AnimatableBody2D honor `sync_to_physics` (default true): under the Kinematic arm, derive the body's per-tick velocity from (new_global_position - previous_global_position)/dt and store it as constant_linear_velocity so riders are carried, mirroring how CharacterBody2D's `platform_velocity` is already consumed at physics_server.rs:1794.

WIRING: MainLoop::step → PhysicsServer::sync_to_physics reads the node properties → step_physics → ContactSolver2D surface-velocity term moves the rider → sync_from_physics writes the rider's new position back to its Node2D.

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a StaticBody2D floor whose `constant_linear_velocity = Vector2(100, 0)` carries a resting RigidBody2D to the right at ~100 px/s after one second of MainLoop ticks; an AnimatableBody2D platform whose `position` is driven by a Tween/AnimationPlayer both blocks a falling body and carries it horizontally. (test: `staticbody2d_conveyor_and_animatablebody_scene`) — loads the scene through the packed-scene path, runs MainLoop::step, asserts the rider's global x displacement and that the AnimatableBody2D registered a body.

title: Physics3D: support multiple offset CollisionShape3D children per body (and CollisionPolygon3D)
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/phys3d-collision-shapes] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/collision_object_3d.cpp (shape owners: shape_owner_add_shape / shape_owner_set_transform / shape_owner_set_disabled); doc/classes/CollisionObject3D.xml; doc/classes/CollisionPolygon3D.xml

**Godot classes:** CollisionObject3D, CollisionShape3D, CollisionPolygon3D

**Patina today:**
- [physics-3d] crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:556-562 picks a single shape with `.children().to_vec().iter().find_map(|&child_id| shape_from_node_3d(tree, child_id))` — first matching DIRECT child only, defaulting to `Shape3D::Sphere { radius: 0.5 }`. `shape_from_node_3d` (:285-460) returns bare geometry and never reads the CollisionShape3D node's own transform, so a shape authored at an offset (the normal way to build a capsule-plus-feet character or an L-shaped platform) collides at the body origin. The shape is written only inside the `if !self.node_to_body.contains_key(&nid)` registration branch (:548-585), so unlike areas (which re-seed the shape every tick at :1187-1189) a body's shape is never refreshed after the first tick. CollisionPolygon3D is unsupported: crates/gdphysics3d/src/shape.rs:8-42 has no such variant, and the only implementation (crates/gdphysics2d/src/shape3d.rs:24) belongs to the orphan gdphysics2d 3D stack that no runtime path uses.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/shape.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: a CollisionObject3D owns a LIST of shapes, each with its own transform relative to the body (upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/collision_object_3d.cpp shape_owner_add_shape / shape_owner_set_transform / shape_owner_set_disabled). CollisionShape3D contributes its own node transform, so authoring a character as a capsule offset up by half its height, or a platform as two boxes, is routine. Shapes added, moved, resized or disabled at runtime take effect immediately. CollisionPolygon3D extrudes a 2D polygon by `depth` into a convex/concave shape.\n\nPATINA: crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:556-562 takes the FIRST matching direct child only and falls back to a 0.5-radius sphere; crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:285-460 (`shape_from_node_3d`) returns geometry with no transform, so every shape is centred on the body origin; and the shape is assigned only in the registration branch (:548-585), never refreshed (areas do refresh, :1187-1189). A two-box StaticBody3D platform therefore collides as one box at the origin, and an offset capsule character collides at its feet. CollisionPolygon3D has no gdphysics3d shape variant (crates/gdphysics3d/src/shape.rs:8-42).\n\nAPPROACH: (1) change gdphysics3d::PhysicsBody3D (crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs:64 `pub shape: Shape3D`) to carry `shapes: Vec<(Transform3D, Shape3D)>`, keeping a single-shape convenience constructor; update `world_aabb` (:400), the broadphase (crates/gdphysics3d/src/world.rs:619) and the narrowphase dispatch (crates/gdphysics3d/src/collision.rs:207 `test_collision_rot`) to iterate shape pairs; (2) make `shape_from_node_3d` return `(Transform3D, Shape3D)` using the CollisionShape3D node's local transform relative to its body, and walk the body's whole descendant subtree (stopping at nested CollisionObject3D nodes) instead of `find_map` over direct children; (3) re-seed the shape list every tick in `sync_to_physics` for bodies as it already does for areas; (4) add a `CollisionPolygon3D` case producing an extruded convex hull from `polygon` + `depth`.\n\nWIRING: the shape list must be rebuilt from the tree on every `sync_to_physics` call in the MainLoop physics tick (crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2840), so an editor-moved or script-moved CollisionShape3D changes collision the next tick.

**Prove it:** Driven only by MainLoop::step on a loaded .tscn: (a) a StaticBody3D with two BoxShape3D children offset to x = -2 and x = +2 stops a falling RigidBody3D dropped above EITHER box, and lets one dropped at x = 0 fall through; (b) a RigidBody3D whose single CollisionShape3D is offset upward by 1.0 comes to rest with its node origin 1.0 lower than the same body with a centred shape; (c) resizing that CollisionShape3D's shape after the first physics tick changes the resting height on a later tick. (test: `physics3d_multi_shape_bodies`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test physics3d_multi_shape_bodies`.

title: RigidBody3D: dispatch _integrate_forces with a PhysicsDirectBodyState3D and expose contact/exception APIs
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/phys3d-direct-body-state] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/RigidBody3D.xml (_integrate_forces, custom_integrator, get_colliding_bodies, get_contact_count, get_inverse_inertia_tensor, set_axis_velocity); doc/classes/PhysicsDirectBodyState3D.xml (28 methods incl. get_contact_impulse/get_contact_local_normal/get_space_state); doc/classes/PhysicsBody3D.xml (add_collision_exception_with, remove_collision_exception_with, get_collision_exceptions) | doc/classes/RigidBody3D.xml members physics_material_override, center_of_mass, center_of_mass_mode, inertia, linear_damp_mode, angular_damp_mode; doc/classes/PhysicsBody3D.xml members axis_lock_linear_*/axis_lock_angular_*; upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/rigid_body_3d.cpp

**Godot classes:** RigidBody3D, PhysicsDirectBodyState3D, PhysicsBody3D, StaticBody3D, PhysicsMaterial

**Patina today:**
- [physics-3d] `grep -rn "_integrate_forces" --include='*.rs' crates/` → 0 hits; `custom_integrator` exists only as a ClassDB property (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1837) and an inspector string (crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:2893) — nothing reads it in crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs::sync_rigid_body (:1049-1118). `grep -rn '"get_colliding_bodies"\|"get_contact_count"\|"get_inverse_inertia_tensor"' --include='*.rs' crates/` → 0 script arms, even though the data exists on the body (crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs:359 `get_contact_count`, :364 `get_colliding_bodies`, :473 `inverse_inertia_diagonal`). `set_axis_velocity` has a script arm but coerces to 2D: crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:9704-9713 writes `Variant::Vector2(vec2_arg(args, 0))` into `_pending_axis_velocity`, which only the 2D server consumes (crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:1312) — a Vector3 call collapses to zero. `grep -rn "add_collision_exception_with\|get_collision_exceptions" --include='*.rs' crates/` → 0 hits (the world's only exceptions come from joints, crates/gdphysics3d/src/world.rs:414-423).
- [physics-3d] (a) crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:578-579 reads FLAT `friction`/`bounce` properties, which Godot's RigidBody3D does not have. The PackedScene loader already flattens a real `physics_material_override` onto the node as `__physics_material__friction`/`__physics_material__bounce`/`rough`/`absorbent` (crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:548-565), and the 2D bridge consumes them (crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:958-963), but the 3D bridge never reads a `__physics_material__*` key — grep of physics_server_3d.rs for `physics_material` returns nothing. An authored PhysicsMaterial on a RigidBody3D/StaticBody3D is therefore silently ignored and every 3D body simulates at friction 0.5 / bounce 0.0. (b) `grep -rn "axis_lock_linear" --include='*.rs' crates/*/src` → 0 hits (present only in crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:2876-2881); crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs:79 has only an all-or-nothing `lock_rotation`. (c) `center_of_mass` exists in 2D (crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:974) but not in 3D — crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs:52-108 has no COM field; `inertia` appears only in the inspector schema (inspector_schema_generated.rs:2887) and crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs:435 always derives inertia from the shape. (d) linear_damp_mode/angular_damp_mode are never read by crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs::sync_rigid_body (:1066-1067 read the raw values only).

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: a RigidBody3D script can override `_integrate_forces(state: PhysicsDirectBodyState3D)`, called once per physics tick from inside the solver; with `custom_integrator = true` the built-in force integration is skipped entirely and the script owns velocity. The state object exposes the tick's contacts (get_contact_count, get_contact_local_normal/position, get_contact_impulse, get_contact_collider_object, get_contact_collider_velocity_at_position), the body's inverse inertia tensor, `set_constant_force`, `integrate_forces()` and `get_space_state()`. Separately, RigidBody3D offers `get_colliding_bodies()`, `get_contact_count()`, `get_inverse_inertia_tensor()`, `set_axis_velocity(Vector3)`, and PhysicsBody3D offers add/remove/get_collision_exceptions.\n\nPATINA: `_integrate_forces` has zero occurrences in the workspace; `custom_integrator` is only a ClassDB property (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1837) and an inspector string, never read by crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs::sync_rigid_body (:1049-1118), so a body authored with it still gets built-in gravity. No script arm exists for get_colliding_bodies/get_contact_count/get_inverse_inertia_tensor even though the data is on the body (crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs:359,:364,:473). `set_axis_velocity` exists but is hard-coded to Vector2 (crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:9704-9713) writing `_pending_axis_velocity`, consumed only by the 2D server (crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:1312). title: Physics3D: run RayCast3D/ShapeCast3D/SpringArm3D once per physics tick before the script phase
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/phys3d-query-node-timing] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/ray_cast_3d.cpp:166 `set_physics_process_internal(true)` and :200 `case NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PHYSICS_PROCESS`; shape_cast_3d.cpp:44,:78; spring_arm_3d.cpp:40,:50 | upstream/godot/scene/3d/ray_cast_3d.cpp (add_exception/add_exception_rid/remove_exception/clear_exceptions, get_collider_shape, get_collision_face_index, set_collision_mask_value) and upstream/godot/scene/3d/shape_cast_3d.cpp (get_collision_count, get_collision_point(idx), get_closest_collision_safe_fraction/unsafe_fraction, collision_result)

**Godot classes:** RayCast3D, ShapeCast3D, SpringArm3D

**Patina today:**
- [physics-3d] crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:1850 `process_queries_3d()` drives all three node types, and its only non-test caller is crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:3031 — inside the per-FRAME idle block, after the fixed-step physics `while` loop ends at :2915 and long after `process_physics_frame_with_scripts` runs at :2903. The 2D twin was already moved into the tick for exactly this reason: crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2885-2894 documents pat-0q2kx.32 ("This used to sit in the idle section after the script phase, which made is_colliding() read false for the whole first frame ... and ran it once per frame rather than once per physics tick") and calls `self.process_raycasts()` at :2895 inside the loop. The 3D path never got the same fix, so with physics_ticks_per_second > fps a RayCast3D misses ticks, and a `_physics_process` reading `is_colliding()` always sees the previous frame's cast.
- [nodes-3d] The per-frame drivers ARE wired: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:1867-1873 calls `raycast3d::force_raycast_update`, `shapecast3d::force_shapecast_update` and `springarm3d::process` every frame. The script surface is narrower than the implementation: gdscene/src/scripting.rs `call_node_method` covers only `is_colliding` (:1418), `get_collision_point` (:1419), `get_collision_normal` (:1422), `get_collider` (:1425) and `force_raycast_update` (:1434). `add_exception`/`clear_exceptions` exist in the Rust modules (4 hits each in gdscene/src/raycast3d.rs+shapecast3d.rs) but have no dispatch arm; `get_collision_face_index` and `collision_result` have 0 hits anywhere; ShapeCast3D's `get_collision_count` (2 hits) and `get_closest_collision_safe_fraction` (4 hits) exist but are not dispatched, and none of the indexed multi-result accessors are reachable.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/raycast3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/shapecast3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/springarm3d.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/raycast3d.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/shapecast3d.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: all three query nodes call `set_physics_process_internal(true)` and do their work in NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PHYSICS_PROCESS — once per fixed physics tick, dispatched before user `_physics_process` callbacks (upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/ray_cast_3d.cpp:166,:200; shape_cast_3d.cpp:44,:78; spring_arm_3d.cpp:40,:50). A script reading `is_colliding()`/`get_collider()`/`get_hit_length()` inside `_physics_process` therefore sees THIS tick's result, and at 120 physics ticks against 60 fps the cast runs 120 times, not 60.\n\nPATINA: `MainLoop::process_queries_3d` (crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:1850) does the right per-node work, but its only caller is crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:3031 — in the once-per-frame idle block, after the physics `while` loop (:2812-2915) and after `process_physics_frame_with_scripts` (:2903). So `_physics_process` reads a one-frame-stale cast, results are dropped at high tick rates, and a SpringArm3D on a moving character lags the body it follows. The 2D side already fixed this (pat-0q2kx.32, see the comment block at :2885-2894 and the `self.process_raycasts()` call at :2895).\n\nAPPROACH: move the `self.process_queries_3d()` call from crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:3031 into the physics `while` loop next to `self.process_raycasts()` (:2895) — i.e. after `physics_server_3d.sync_from_physics` (:2842) and `character3d::process_character_movement` (:2856) so the world reflects this tick, and BEFORE `self.tree.process_physics_frame_with_scripts(physics_dt)` (:2903). Keep the per-node `enabled` self-guard already in crates/gdscene/src/raycast3d.rs / shapecast3d.rs / springarm3d.rs. Remove the idle-block call so a cast is not published twice per frame.\n\nWIRING: the acceptance test must go through MainLoop::step with no manual `force_raycast_update`, proving the tick-phase placement rather than the function's internals.

**Merged findings (2):** RayCast3D / ShapeCast3D / SpringArm3D update timing — Godot runs them under NOTIFICATION_INTERNAL_PHYSICS_PROCESS (once per physics tick, before _physics_process); Patina runs them once per rendered frame, after the script phase; RayCast3D / ShapeCast3D script surface (exceptions, face index, shapecast results)

**Prove it:** With a .tscn containing a RayCast3D pointing at a StaticBody3D and a script whose `_physics_process` records `is_colliding()` on every tick: (a) the very first physics tick already records true (no one-frame delay); (b) with `physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second = 120` and a single `MainLoop::step(1.0/60.0)`, the ray publishes a fresh result for each of the two ticks (a body teleported between ticks by another `_physics_process` is seen at both positions); (c) a SpringArm3D parented to a body that moves during `_physics_process` reports a hit length computed from this tick's position. (test: `physics3d_query_nodes_physics_tick`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test physics3d_query_nodes_physics_tick`.
acceptance_criteria: With a .tscn containing a RayCast3D pointing at a StaticBody3D and a script whose `_physics_process` records `is_colliding()` on every tick: (a) the very first physics tick already records true (no one-frame delay); (b) with `physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second = 120` and a single `MainLoop::step(1.0/60.0)`, the ray publishes a fresh result for each of the two ticks (a body teleported between ticks by another `_physics_process` is seen at both positions); (c) a SpringArm3D parented to a body that moves during `_physics_process` reports a hit length computed from this tick's position. (test: `physics3d_query_nodes_physics_tick`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test physics3d_query_nodes_physics_tick`.

GODOT: the standard way a 3D game raycasts from script is `var space = get_world_3d().direct_space_state` then `space.intersect_ray(PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D.create(from, to))`, returning a Dictionary with position/normal/collider/collider_id/rid/shape or {} on a miss. title: DisplayServer: add a browser-backed DisplayBackend and the missing mouse-mode/dark-mode/vsync/IME/orientation methods
description:
[audit-key: platform-os/platform-os-displayserver] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: STUB/MISSING/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/platform/web/display_server_web.cpp; upstream/godot/servers/display_server.h; extension_api.json singletons[DisplayServer] (full method list incl. mouse_set_mode/warp_mouse/is_dark_mode/screen_get_refresh_rate/window_set_vsync_mode/ime_get_text/get_name) | upstream/godot/platform/web/os_web.cpp:54 (alert→godot_js_display_alert), :148 (get_processor_count→hw_concurrency), :194-198 (shell_open→godot_js_os_shell_open, returns OK), :200 (get_name "Web"), :214-217 (get_user_data_dir → "/userfs"), :277 (is_userfs_persistent → idb_available); upstream/godot/platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_os.js:304-323 (web_macos/web_windows/web_android/web_ios/web_linuxbsd tags) | upstream/godot/platform/web/display_server_web.cpp (canvas size/resize policy, fullscreen, cursor, clipboard via navigator.clipboard, TTS via SpeechSynthesis, virtual keyboard, screen_get_scale from devicePixelRatio) | extension_api.json classes[OS].methods (88 methods); doc/classes/OS.xml | extension_api.json classes[] contains OS/Engine/Time/DisplayServer/Performance/ProjectSettings/EngineDebugger/NativeMenu as Object-derived classes; ClassDB.class_exists("OS") is true in Godot and class_get_method_list("OS") enumerates 88 methods | upstream/godot/platform/web/os_web.cpp + display_server_web.cpp (the real platform layer these types imitate)

**Godot classes:** DisplayServer, OS, Window, Viewport, Engine, Time, Performance, ProjectSettings, EngineDebugger, NativeMenu, JavaScriptBridge

**Patina today:**
- [platform-os] The ONLY `DisplayBackend` implementation in the workspace is the in-memory headless one: `grep -rn 'impl DisplayBackend' crates/` returns exactly engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/display_backend.rs:148 (`impl DisplayBackend for HeadlessDisplayBackend`). Both runner entry points install it — engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs:298 and engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs:432 — so `DisplayServer.screen_get_scale()` is always 1.0 and `screen_get_dpi()` always 96 (display_backend.rs:68-74), never devicePixelRatio. No browser binding exists anywhere: `grep -rn 'devicePixelRatio' crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs` = 0 hits, `grep -rn 'speechSynthesis' crates/` = 0 hits (Godot's web export DOES implement TTS via SpeechSynthesis). The script method table is ~20 entries (engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:15427-15489) and everything else falls to `UndefinedFunction("DisplayServer.{other}")` at interpreter.rs:15488. Absence verified by `grep -rl '"<name>"' crates/` returning 0 for: mouse_set_mode, mouse_get_mode, mouse_get_position, is_dark_mode, get_accent_color, screen_get_refresh_rate, window_set_vsync_mode, ime_get_text, ime_get_selection, is_touchscreen_available, clipboard_get_image, get_display_safe_area, window_get_position, screen_set_orientation, cursor_get_shape, keyboard_get_keycode_from_physical, file_dialog_show, get_swap_cancel_ok. `DisplayServer.get_name()` is also unhandled, so it errors instead of returning "web". engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/clipboard.rs (403 lines, Clipboard trait + HeadlessClipboard) is dead — `grep -rn 'clipboard' crates/gdplatform/src/lib.rs crates/gdplatform/src/backend.rs crates/gdplatform/src/winit_backend.rs` yields only the `pub mod clipboard;` declaration.
- [platform-os] None of the web-specific OS behaviours are bound, even though a real js-sys backend already exists in the same crate (engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/js_bridge.rs:468+). `OS.get_locale()` reads POSIX env vars only (engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:15017-15034 `os_locale`), which are empty on wasm32-unknown-unknown, so it always returns "en" instead of navigator.languages[0]. `OS.get_processor_count()` uses `std::thread::available_parallelism()` (interpreter.rs:14707-14711), which cannot succeed on wasm32, so it returns 1 instead of navigator.hardwareConcurrency. `gdplatform::os::shell_open` explicitly returns ERR_UNAVAILABLE(46) on wasm32 (engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/os.rs:426-431) whereas Godot's web build calls window.open and returns OK. `gdplatform::os::alert` writes to stderr and returns false (os.rs:451-455) instead of window.alert. `gdplatform::os::user_data_dir` (os.rs:316-327) always builds `<data dir>/Godot/app_userdata/<name>` from HOME/USERPROFILE, which is empty on wasm → falls back to the literal "user://"; Godot web returns "/userfs/<user_dir>". `is_userfs_persistent()` hardcodes `current_platform() != Platform::Web` (os.rs:331-333), i.e. always false on the web, whereas Godot reports IndexedDB availability. The browser feature tags web_macos/web_windows/web_android/web_ios/web_linuxbsd are absent from `has_feature` (os.rs:70-107) and fall through to `has_custom_feature` → false.
- [web-runtime] `gdcore/src/display_backend.rs:3-5` documents exactly this intent ("the web build binds clipboard to `navigator.clipboard`, TTS to `SpeechSynthesis`, and window size to the canvas") but ships no web implementation: the trait's defaults are empty (tts_speak/tts_stop/tts_voices/tts_is_speaking at display_backend.rs:90-98) and the only concrete impl is a call-recording double (display_backend.rs:120-170). `rg 'target_arch' crates/gdcore/src/` returns only rng.rs — there is no wasm32 backend in that crate. On the wasm side, crates/patina-web/src/canvas.rs:44-83 does devicePixelRatio-aware backing-store sizing only; there is no Window content-scale mode/aspect handling, no `requestFullscreen`, no `requestPointerLock`, no virtual keyboard (`rg 'requestFullscreen|requestPointerLock|virtual_keyboard' --type rust crates/` → 0 hits). Godot's canvas resize policy (None/Project/Adaptive, export_plugin.cpp:379) has no equivalent (`rg 'canvas_resize' crates/gdplatform/` → 0 hits).
- [platform-os] `call_os_static` (engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:14613) falls through to `UndefinedFunction("OS.{other}")` at interpreter.rs:14871. Verified absent workspace-wide (`grep -rl '"<name>"' engine-rs/crates/` returns 0 for each): get_entropy, get_system_ca_certificates, get_processor_name, get_system_fonts, get_system_font_path, get_system_font_path_for_text, is_sandboxed, move_to_trash, get_system_dir, get_video_adapter_driver_info, is_keycode_unicode, set_thread_name, request_permission, request_permissions, get_granted_permissions, revoke_granted_permissions, set_delta_smoothing, is_delta_smoothing_enabled, is_stdout_verbose, get_version_alias, read_string_from_stdin, read_buffer_from_stdin, get_stdin_type, get_stdout_type, get_stderr_type, get_process_exit_code, execute_with_pipe, open_with_program, add_logger, remove_logger, set_restart_on_exit, is_restart_on_exit_set, get_restart_on_exit_arguments, set_use_file_access_save_and_swap, crash. `OS.get_entropy` matters directly for crypto (Godot documents it as cryptographically secure) and `OS.get_system_fonts`/`get_system_font_path` are what SystemFont resolves through.
- [platform-os] `grep -c 'ClassRegistration::new("<C>")' engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` returns 0 for OS, Engine, Time, DisplayServer, Performance, ProjectSettings, EngineDebugger and NativeMenu (JavaScriptBridge returns 1, so the pattern is used elsewhere in the same file). The audit's own sweep artifact scratchpad/port-audit-2026-07-27/unregistered.txt lists exactly these names. The interpreter reaches OS/Engine/Time/DisplayServer/EngineDebugger/ProjectSettings by matching a bare `Expr::Ident` (engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:2905-3010) and answers `Engine.has_singleton` from the hand-maintained `BUILTIN_SINGLETONS` list (interpreter.rs:14464-14484), so the reflection API and the dispatch table are two independent sources of truth. Consequence: `ClassDB.class_exists("OS")` is false, `ClassDB.class_get_method_list("DisplayServer")` is empty, and any editor/tool script that enumerates singleton classes through ClassDB sees nothing.
- [web-runtime] crates/gdplatform/src/web.rs:99-102 states the bridge "records calls and returns stubbed values", and every operation is pure in-memory state: `resume_audio` just assigns an enum (web.rs:392-407), `request_fullscreen`/`exit_fullscreen` assign a field (:410-419), `has_shared_array_buffer` returns the export flag (:433-435), `download_file` calls two recorded no-ops and comments "In reality: create blob URL, set href, trigger click, revoke URL" (:452-466). The types have zero consumers: `rg 'WebPlatformLayer|CanvasConfig|WebStorageBackend|AudioContextState|PageVisibility' --type rust crates/ | grep -v gdplatform/src/web.rs` → 0 hits. Only `JsValue`/`JsError`/`JsObjectHandle` (re-exported at crates/gdplatform/src/js_bridge.rs:36) and `WebExportConfig` (used at crates/gdplatform/src/export.rs:13) are live. The real bridge already lives in js_bridge.rs (:1-30), so this module is a superseded duplicate presenting as a platform layer.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/display_backend.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/clipboard.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/lib.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/os.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/js_bridge.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/canvas.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/display.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/web.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/export.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: `DisplayServerWeb` (upstream/godot/platform/web/display_server_web.cpp) binds the singleton to real browser APIs — `mouse_set_mode(MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED)` → `canvas.requestPointerLock()`, `MOUSE_MODE_HIDDEN` → CSS `cursor:none`; `screen_get_scale()`/`screen_get_dpi()` → devicePixelRatio; `screen_get_size()` → screen.width/height; `window_set_mode(WINDOW_MODE_FULLSCREEN)` → Fullscreen API; `clipboard_set/get` → navigator.clipboard; TTS (`tts_get_voices/tts_speak/tts_pause/tts_resume/tts_stop`) → SpeechSynthesis; `screen_get_orientation`/`screen_set_orientation` → the Screen Orientation API; `virtual_keyboard_show/hide/get_height`; `is_dark_mode()` → prefers-color-scheme; `get_name()` → "web".\n\nPATINA CURRENT STATE: the only DisplayBackend implementation is `HeadlessDisplayBackend` (engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/display_backend.rs:148), installed unconditionally by engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs:298 and bootstrap.rs:432, so DPI is a constant 96 and scale a constant 1.0 (display_backend.rs:68-74). The script table (engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:15427-15489) covers ~20 methods; everything else errors at interpreter.rs:15488. `mouse_set_mode`, `is_dark_mode`, `screen_get_refresh_rate`, `window_set_vsync_mode`, `ime_get_text`, `window_get_position`, `cursor_get_shape`, `get_name` and a dozen more return 0 grep hits workspace-wide. There is no devicePixelRatio or speechSynthesis binding anywhere (0 grep hits in engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs). engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/clipboard.rs is an unreferenced module.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION APPROACH: (1) Extend the `DisplayBackend` trait in engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/display_backend.rs with the missing surface (mouse mode get/set, mouse position, warp, dark mode, accent colour, refresh rate, vsync mode, orientation get/set, window position/mode/flags, cursor shape get, virtual keyboard height, IME text/selection, `name()`). (2) Add a `WebDisplayBackend` in engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/ (or a wasm32-gated module in gdplatform) implementing it over js-sys/web-sys the same way engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/js_bridge.rs already reaches the DOM reflectively, and install it from the wasm entry point `__patina_web_start` (patina-web/src/lib.rs:81). (3) Route the editor's served client: reuse the existing pointer-lock plumbing (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs:10551-10571 and editor_server.rs:14286) so `DisplayServer.mouse_set_mode` shares the path `Input.set_mouse_mode` already uses, and post devicePixelRatio back so scale/DPI are real. (4) Add the new arms to `call_displayserver_via_backend`/`call_displayserver_static` in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs and delete or fold engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/clipboard.rs into the backend.\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: a script in a loaded scene calls `DisplayServer.mouse_set_mode(DisplayServer.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED)`, `DisplayServer.screen_get_scale()`, `DisplayServer.get_name()` and `DisplayServer.window_set_mode(...)` and each reaches the installed backend rather than a hardcoded constant or an UndefinedFunction error.

**Merged findings (6):** DisplayServer: browser/native backend + the mouse-mode / dark-mode / vsync / IME / orientation / refresh-rate method surface; OS singleton on wasm32: locale, processor count, shell_open, alert, user data dir, userfs persistence, browser feature tags; DisplayServer on web: canvas resize policy + content scale, fullscreen, pointer lock, clipboard, TTS, virtual keyboard, screen DPI; OS singleton method coverage (~30 documented methods missing from the script dispatch table); ClassDB registration for the platform singleton classes (OS, Engine, Time, DisplayServer, Performance, ProjectSettings, EngineDebugger, NativeMenu); gdplatform::web platform layer (canvas config, audio-context state, visibility, fullscreen, storage backend, download_file)

**Prove it:** With a non-headless backend installed, a scene script calling `DisplayServer.get_name()`, `DisplayServer.mouse_set_mode(2)` then `mouse_get_mode()`, `screen_get_scale()`, `screen_get_refresh_rate()`, `is_dark_mode()`, `window_set_vsync_mode(...)`/`window_get_vsync_mode()` and `screen_get_orientation()` all return backend-supplied values with no UndefinedFunction error, and the captured mouse mode is observable in the served client payload the game view polls. (test: `display_server_backend_surface_reaches_scripts`)
acceptance_criteria: With a non-headless backend installed, a scene script calling `DisplayServer.get_name()`, `DisplayServer.mouse_set_mode(2)` then `mouse_get_mode()`, `screen_get_scale()`, `screen_get_refresh_rate()`, `is_dark_mode()`, `window_set_vsync_mode(...)`/`window_get_vsync_mode()` and `screen_get_orientation()` all return backend-supplied values with no UndefinedFunction error, and the captured mouse mode is observable in the served client payload the game view polls. (test: `display_server_backend_surface_reaches_scripts`)
