title: Platform: wire the Performance singleton — frame loop feeds the registry, scripts and the editor monitors read it
description:
[audit-key: platform-os/platform-os-performance] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json singletons[Performance]; classes[Performance] methods get_monitor/add_custom_monitor/remove_custom_monitor/has_custom_monitor/get_custom_monitor/get_monitor_modification_time/get_custom_monitor_names/get_custom_monitor_types; upstream/godot/main/performance.cpp | upstream/godot/core/core_bind.cpp / main/performance.cpp; extension_api.json Performance = 8 methods (get_monitor, add_custom_monitor, remove_custom_monitor, has_custom_monitor, get_custom_monitor, get_monitor_modification_time, get_custom_monitor_names, get_custom_monitor_types) + the Monitor enum (TIME_FPS, TIME_PROCESS, TIME_PHYSICS_PROCESS, TIME_NAVIGATION_PROCESS, MEMORY_STATIC, MEMORY_STATIC_MAX, OBJECT_COUNT, OBJECT_RESOURCE_COUNT, OBJECT_NODE_COUNT, OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT, RENDER_TOTAL_OBJECTS_IN_FRAME, RENDER_TOTAL_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME, RENDER_VIDEO_MEM_USED, PHYSICS_2D/3D_ACTIVE_OBJECTS, AUDIO_OUTPUT_LATENCY, ...) — this is what powers the editor Debugger's Monitors graphs | extension_api.json `.singletons[]` includes Performance (1 of 39); `.classes[] | select(.name=="Performance") | .enums` = Monitor + ProfilerMetric, 64 values; upstream/godot/doc/classes/Performance.xml | upstream/godot/doc/classes/Performance.xml — Object singleton, 8 methods (get_monitor, add_custom_monitor, remove_custom_monitor, has_custom_monitor, get_custom_monitor, get_custom_monitor_names, get_monitor_modification_time, get_monitor_name) and the Monitor enum (TIME_FPS … MONITOR_MAX). Listed in extension_api.json `.singletons[]`.

**Godot classes:** Performance

**Patina today:**
- [platform-os] There is a complete 432-line monitor registry at engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/performance.rs (`PerformanceRegistry` :262, `FrameMonitorFeed` :373, `global()` :429) whose only consumers are its own tests: `grep -rn 'PerformanceRegistry|performance::global|FrameMonitorFeed' crates/` outside the defining file returns only engine-rs/crates/gdcore/tests/performance_registry.rs. The singleton is not script-reachable: `Performance` is absent from `BUILTIN_SINGLETONS` (engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:14464-14484), has no `Expr::Ident` dispatch arm (`grep -rn 'Ident(n) if n == "Performance"' crates/` = 0 hits), and is listed in the sweep's unregistered.txt (no `ClassRegistration::new("Performance")` in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs). Method names are absent workspace-wide: `grep -rl '"get_monitor"' crates/` = 0, same for add_custom_monitor/remove_custom_monitor/has_custom_monitor/get_custom_monitor/get_custom_monitor_names/get_monitor_modification_time. The frame loop never feeds it — `grep -rn 'performance' crates/patina-runner/src crates/gdscene/src` returns only an unrelated doc comment (gdscene/src/lod.rs:151). The editor's `/api/monitors` route (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:16823-16918) hand-builds a monitor JSON blob from EditorState instead of reading the registry, so the two can drift. engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/memory_profiler.rs (1448 lines) has zero consumers anywhere (`grep -rn 'memory_profiler' crates/` = only `gdcore/src/lib.rs:27 pub mod memory_profiler;`).
- [singleton-dispatch-table] IMPLEMENTATION EXISTS: engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/performance.rs — `MONITOR_MAX = 59` (line 38), `ALL_MONITORS` (line 110), `MONITOR_NAMES` (line 174), `PerformanceRegistry` (line 262) with set/add/get/add_custom_monitor/remove_custom_monitor/has_custom_monitor/get_custom_monitor/custom_monitor_names, `FrameMonitorFeed` (line 373) with record_frame/fps, and a process-global `global()` (line 429). Declared at engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/lib.rs:31. NO CONSUMERS: `grep -rn 'PerformanceRegistry|FrameMonitorFeed|performance::global|gdcore::performance' engine-rs/crates/ apps/ --include='*.rs' | grep -v '^engine-rs/crates/gdcore/'` -> 0 hits; the only references anywhere are engine-rs/crates/gdcore/tests/performance_registry.rs. Nothing in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, patina-runner or gdeditor ever constructs or feeds it. NO SCRIPT PATH: `rg -c '"Performance"' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` -> 0; absent from `BUILTIN_SINGLETONS` (interpreter.rs:14464-14482); `grep -c '"Performance"' engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` -> 0. NO ENUM: `grep -c '"TIME_FPS"' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/global_constants.rs` -> 0.
- [class-scoped-enums-and-constants] The Rust implementation is complete and orphaned. /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/performance.rs:38 `MONITOR_MAX = 59`, :47 `pub enum Monitor`, :110 `ALL_MONITORS`, :174 `MONITOR_NAMES`, plus a `PerformanceRegistry`, `FrameMonitorFeed` and a `global()` accessor. Consumers outside the defining crate: NONE. `rg 'gdcore::performance|performance::' engine-rs/crates --include='*.rs'` returns only engine-rs/crates/gdcore/tests/performance_registry.rs (lines 15, 233, 280, 333, 354). `rg '"Performance"' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src` returns nothing — there is no `Performance` singleton arm in the interpreter and no `ClassRegistration::new("Performance")` in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs. `rg 'get_monitor' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` returns nothing. So `Performance.get_monitor(Performance.TIME_FPS)` — the canonical FPS read and the feed behind Godot's editor Monitors graphs — fails twice over: unknown singleton and unknown constant.
- [sweep-4] THE REGISTRY EXISTS AND NOTHING USES IT. /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/performance.rs is a complete port: :33-38 `MONITOR_MAX: usize = 59` ("Mirrors Godot's Performance::MONITOR_MAX"), :110 ALL_MONITORS, :174 MONITOR_NAMES, :286-348 PerformanceRegistry with set/add/get/add_custom_monitor/remove_custom_monitor/has_custom_monitor/get_custom_monitor/custom_monitor_names, :429-431 `pub fn global()`.
ZERO NON-TEST CONSUMERS: `rg -n 'performance::|PerformanceRegistry|add_custom_monitor|get_monitor|FrameTimer' engine-rs --glob '!gdcore/src/performance.rs' --glob '!*fixtures*'` returns only gdcore/tests/performance_registry.rs and the unrelated editor route name `api_get_monitors`.
NOT SCRIPT-REACHABLE: "Performance" is not in the interpreter's BUILTIN_SINGLETONS (interpreter.rs:14464-14483) and `rg 'ClassRegistration::new("Performance"' engine-rs apps` -> 0 hits, so `Performance.get_monitor(...)` is an unknown identifier.
A PARALLEL FAKE EXISTS: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:16823-16880 `api_get_monitors` re-derives node/draw/physics/video-memory counts by walking the scene tree with string heuristics (`c.ends_with("Body2D")`, `texture_count * 262_144`) instead of reading gdcore::performance::global() — two implementations, neither fed by the frame loop.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/performance.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/memory_profiler.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/global_constants.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: `Performance` is a global singleton (extension_api.json singletons[Performance]). `Performance.get_monitor(Performance.TIME_FPS)` returns the live frame rate; the Monitor enum covers TIME_FPS/TIME_PROCESS/TIME_PHYSICS_PROCESS/TIME_NAVIGATION_PROCESS, MEMORY_STATIC/MEMORY_STATIC_MAX/MEMORY_MESSAGE_BUFFER_MAX, OBJECT_COUNT/RESOURCE_COUNT/NODE_COUNT/ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT, RENDER_TOTAL_OBJECTS_IN_FRAME/…/RENDER_VIDEO_MEM_USED, PHYSICS_2D_ACTIVE_OBJECTS/…, AUDIO_OUTPUT_LATENCY. `add_custom_monitor(name, callable)` registers a script-provided monitor that also shows up in the editor profiler (upstream/godot/main/performance.cpp).\n\nPATINA CURRENT STATE: the registry already exists and is tested — engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/performance.rs:262 `PerformanceRegistry` with the full Monitor enum, :313 `add_custom_monitor`, :373 `FrameMonitorFeed::record_frame`, :429 process-global `global()`. Nothing outside engine-rs/crates/gdcore/tests/performance_registry.rs touches it. `Performance` is not in `BUILTIN_SINGLETONS` (engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:14464), has no dispatch arm, and is not in ClassDB (no `ClassRegistration::new("Performance")` in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs), so `Performance.get_monitor(0)` in GDScript is an undefined-identifier error. The editor's `GET /api/monitors` (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:16823) computes its own numbers independently.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION APPROACH: (1) Add a `Performance` arm to the singleton dispatch in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs next to the DisplayServer/EngineDebugger arms, add "Performance" to BUILTIN_SINGLETONS, and expose the Monitor enum constants (TIME_FPS = 0 …) so `Performance.TIME_FPS` resolves; back get_monitor/add_custom_monitor/… with `gdcore::performance::global()`, invoking script Callables for custom monitors. (2) Register `Performance` (Object base) in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs. (3) Call `FrameMonitorFeed::record_frame` from the frame tick in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs beside the existing `set_engine_frame_counters` calls (main_loop.rs:2925/3061/3135) so time/object/node counts are live. (4) Repoint engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs `api_get_monitors` at the same registry so the editor panel and scripts cannot disagree.\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: .tscn with a script → runner/editor frame tick → registry updated → `Performance.get_monitor(Performance.TIME_FPS)` returns a non-zero live value in that same script, and the editor monitors endpoint reports the same numbers.

**Merged findings (4):** Performance singleton (get_monitor + all built-in monitors + custom monitors); Performance singleton — a complete 59-monitor registry exists in gdcore with ZERO consumers outside its own tests, and no script or editor path reaches it; Performance singleton + Performance.Monitor constants (TIME_FPS, MEMORY_STATIC, OBJECT_NODE_COUNT, RENDER_TOTAL_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME, ...); Performance singleton — 59 engine monitors + custom monitors

**Prove it:** A scene whose script reads `Performance.get_monitor(Performance.TIME_FPS)` and `Performance.get_monitor(Performance.OBJECT_NODE_COUNT)` after several stepped frames gets live, non-zero values matching the tree; `add_custom_monitor("game/score", callable)` then `get_custom_monitor("game/score")` round-trips through the script Callable; and the editor monitors endpoint reports the same fps value in the same run. (test: `performance_singleton_monitors_live_from_frame_loop`)
acceptance_criteria: A scene whose script reads `Performance.get_monitor(Performance.TIME_FPS)` and `Performance.get_monitor(Performance.OBJECT_NODE_COUNT)` after several stepped frames gets live, non-zero values matching the tree; `add_custom_monitor("game/score", callable)` then `get_custom_monitor("game/score")` round-trips through the script Callable; and the editor monitors endpoint reports the same fps value in the same run. (test: `performance_singleton_monitors_live_from_frame_loop`)

Named enums are the standard GDScript state-machine idiom.
- [scene-tree] REGISTERED but never emitted. engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:726-734 registers `ready`, `renamed`, `tree_entered`, `tree_exiting`, `tree_exited`, `child_entered_tree`, `child_exiting_tree`, `child_order_changed`, `replacing_by` on Node. The editor exposes them: engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/signals_tree.rs:307-308 and engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:10974 (`vec!["tree_entered", "tree_exiting", "ready"]`). The .tscn parser accepts `[connection signal="ready" ...]` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:4085). Runtime emits only ONE of them: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/lifecycle.rs:50 `tree.emit_signal(id, "tree_entered", &[])`. Greps run over engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src: `grep -rn '"tree_exiting"|"tree_exited"|"child_entered_tree"|"child_exiting_tree"|"child_order_changed"|"replacing_by"|"node_removed"|"tree_changed"|"scene_changed"|"node_configuration_warning_changed"'` → 0 hits. An enumeration of every `emit_signal(x, "...")` literal in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/*.rs shows `tree_entered` 1, `node_added` 1 (scene_tree.rs:1036), `node_renamed` 1 (scene_tree.rs:1754), and no other tree signal. `SceneTree::remove_node` (scene_tree.rs:1088) and `replace_by` (scene_tree.rs:4711) emit nothing.
- [class-scoped-enums-and-constants] Patina HAS the data (795 integer constants in ClassDB) and NOTHING in the script runtime routes to it. `Ident.MEMBER` is dispatched at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:3222-3226 into `try_static_member` (interpreter.rs:14111). Its match arms are only Vector2/Vector3/Color/Engine/FileAccess; the `_` fallback at interpreter.rs:14157-14158 is `variant_math::static_member(...).or_else(|| global_constants::global_enum_member(...))`. `variant_math::static_member` (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/variant_math.rs:427-447) is a 9-entry Transform2D/Transform3D/Basis/Quaternion/Plane table. `global_enum_member` (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/global_constants.rs:1170-1179) only accepts the 20 @GlobalScope prefixes enumerated at global_constants.rs:607-632 (Side/Corner/Orientation/ClockDirection/HorizontalAlignment/VerticalAlignment/InlineAlignment/EulerOrder/Key/KeyModifierMask/KeyLocation/MouseButton/MouseButtonMask/JoyButton/JoyAxis/MIDIMessage/Error/PropertyHint/PropertyUsageFlags/MethodFlags) — no class names. There is NO `gdobject::class_get_integer_constant` call anywhere on this path. When `try_static_member` returns None the interpreter evaluates the base `Expr::Ident("Node")` (interpreter.rs:3228), which walks locals -> instance props -> node props -> signals -> methods -> global constants -> autoloads and ends at `UndefinedVariable` (interpreter.rs:2764). So `Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` is a hard runtime error, not a wrong value. Grep for the only production reader: `rg 'gdobject::class_get_integer_constant' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src` -> single hit at interpreter.rs:14973, inside the `ClassDB.class_get_integer_constant(...)` reflection arm (interpreter.rs:14968-14996) — a call no real GDScript writes. Grep for the natural spelling anywhere in the repo: `rg 'Tween\.TRANS_|Node\.PROCESS_MODE|Control\.PRESET_|Viewport\.MSAA_|Light3D\.PARAM_|TileSet\.TILE_SHAPE|Animation\.LOOP_|Mesh\.PRIMITIVE_' engine-rs/crates --include='*.rs'` -> zero GDScript uses; the only hits are Rust doc comments. FALSE GREEN: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/tests/tween_gdscript_wiring.rs:298-327 asserts all 16 `Tween.TRANS_*`/`EASE_*` values via `class_get_integer_constant("Tween", name)` and passes, while no script can spell `Tween.TRANS_SINE`. Same shape in gdobject/tests/camera_server_singleton_web_parity.rs:93-131, gdobject/tests/misc_canvas_nodes_register_and_wire.rs:134-172, gdresource/tests/portable_texture.rs:112, gdscene/tests/crypto_script_classes.rs:236-241 — every reader of the constant table is a test.
- [scene-tree] engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:84-88: `pub const SCRIPTS: Self = Self(4);` documented as "Accepted but **not yet honored** — `ScriptInstance` has no clone." and line 90-92 `USE_INSTANTIATION` "Accepted but not yet honored." The default at scene_tree.rs:113-117 is `Self(1 | 2 | 4)`, i.e. SCRIPTS is on by default and silently dropped. `SceneTree::duplicate_node` (scene_tree.rs:1924) and `duplicate_subtree` (scene_tree.rs:2001) never touch `self.scripts`.
- [gdscript] There is no global script-class registry anywhere: `grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'global_script_class\|script_class_cache\|GlobalScriptClass\|class_name_registry\|ScriptClassRegistry' engine-rs/crates` → 0 hits. `Interpreter::class_registry` is populated only from a `class_name` in the SAME source (engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:11530-11532) and is per-Interpreter (one per node). Method dispatch never walks a base: `call_instance_method_impl` looks up `instance.class_def.methods.get(method_name)` and errors otherwise (interpreter.rs:11764-11771); `instantiate_class` copies only the class's own `instance_vars` (interpreter.rs:11537-11556). `extends` with a path is explicitly discarded — engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/autoload.rs:374-378 asserts `base_class_from_source("extends \"res://base.gd\"") == "Node"`. `preload("res://base.gd")` returns a bare `ResourceRef{class_name:"GDScript", properties:{}}` with no compilation (interpreter.rs:4341-4399), so `const Base = preload(...)` + `extends Base` cannot work either.
- [scene-tree] engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/notification.rs assigns: PHYSICS_PROCESS=18 (Godot 16), PARENTED=20 (18), UNPARENTED=21 (19), CHILD_ORDER_CHANGED=16 (24), INTERNAL_PROCESS=35 (25), INTERNAL_PHYSICS_PROCESS=36 (26), DRAG_BEGIN=26 (21), DRAG_END=27 (22), and defines `NOTIFICATION_INSTANCED=25` — the Godot 3 name; Godot 4 has SCENE_INSTANTIATED=20. Two of these collide with real Godot codes: Patina CHILD_ORDER_CHANGED=16 == Godot NOTIFICATION_PHYSICS_PROCESS, Patina INTERNAL_PROCESS=35 == Godot CanvasItem::NOTIFICATION_LOCAL_TRANSFORM_CHANGED. These codes are what reaches scripts: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:2986 `notify_script(node_id, what)` is called with `gdobject::NOTIFICATION_PROCESS.code() as i64` (scene_tree.rs:3856) and the ENTER_TREE/READY/EXIT_TREE codes (lifecycle.rs:48,65,120). Separately, GDScript has NO notification constants at all: `grep -c NOTIFICATION engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/global_constants.rs` → 0; `grep -rn 'NOTIFICATION' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/*.rs` → 1 hit, a doc comment in bindings.rs:213. Missing constants entirely: POST_ENTER_TREE, PATH_RENAMED, SCENE_INSTANTIATED, ENABLED/DISABLED, RESET_PHYSICS_INTERPOLATION, SUSPENDED/UNSUSPENDED, all WM_* (1002-1012), all APPLICATION_*, TRANSLATION_CHANGED, TEXT_SERVER_CHANGED, CRASH, OS_MEMORY_WARNING, VP_MOUSE_ENTER/EXIT, EDITOR_PRE_SAVE/POST_SAVE.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/lifecycle.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/variant_math.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/global_constants.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/autoload.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/notification.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/parser.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/tokenizer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/type_checker.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: a named `enum Name { A, B = 5 }` becomes a class member; `Name.A` resolves inside the class, from a subclass, and as `OtherClass.Name.A` when the class has a `class_name` (gdscript_analyzer.cpp `resolve_datatype`/`reduce_identifier_from_base`). The enum name is also usable as a type hint, and the whole enum is a Dictionary-like constant.\n\nPatina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:11318-11341 parses named enums into `ClassDef::enums`, and NOTHING reads that map — `grep -n 'enums' interpreter.rs` yields only the declaration (:669), initialisers (:11293/:11465), the insert (:11335) and test assertions. `Stmt::EnumDecl` is a no-op in `exec_stmt` (interpreter.rs:1053-1056), and `call_instance_method_impl` seeds only `class_def.constants` (interpreter.rs:11811-11816). So `State.IDLE` falls through to the @GlobalScope enum-qualified resolver and errors (see tests/enum_member.rs::unknown_prefix_still_rejected).\n\nImplementation approach: in `Interpreter::call_instance_method_impl` (interpreter.rs:11758+) and `call_user_func_impl` (:6261), seed each `class_def.enums` entry as a constant Dictionary/`Variant` namespace value under its enum name, alongside the existing `define_const` loop. Add resolution in `eval_expr`'s `Expr::MemberAccess` arm (interpreter.rs:3191+) so an `Expr::Ident(prefix)` that names a class enum resolves the member (and errors with Godot's \"Cannot find member X in enum Y\" wording for a bad member, matching the membership behaviour already implemented for @GlobalScope enums). Accept the enum name as a type hint in `is_builtin_type_name`/`value_is_type` so `var s: State = State.IDLE` and `s is State` behave. Keep anonymous-enum-to-constants behaviour unchanged.\n\nWiring requirement: the resolution must happen on the same path the runner uses for `_ready`/`_process` — `run_class` → `instantiate_class` → `call_instance_method` → `eval_expr` — not via a side table only tests touch.

**Merged findings (27):** Script-declared named enums (`enum State { IDLE, RUN }` → `State.IDLE`); Node lifecycle signals (ready, renamed, tree_exiting, tree_exited, child_entered_tree, child_exiting_tree, child_order_changed, replacing_by) + SceneTree signals (node_removed, tree_changed, scene_changed, node_configuration_warning_changed); GDScript `Class.CONSTANT` / `Class.Enum.CONSTANT` static access (Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, Control.PRESET_FULL_RECT, Tween.TRANS_SINE, Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED, FileAccess.COMPRESSION_ZSTD, ...); Node.duplicate() DUPLICATE_SCRIPTS / DUPLICATE_USE_INSTANTIATION; Script inheritance: `extends "res://base.gd"`, `extends OtherClassName`, global `class_name` registry, inherited methods/vars/signals/constants; Node NOTIFICATION_* constant codes and the GDScript NOTIFICATION_* constant table; Script-level / standalone annotations (@icon, @abstract, @static_unload, @export_group, @export_subgroup, @export_category, @warning_ignore_start/restore) + negative numeric annotation args; `super` dispatch: `super.method(args)` and bare `super()` inside a non-_init method; Lexer literal forms: hex `0xFF`, binary `0b1010`, exponent `1e-5`, raw `r"..."`, multiline `"""..."""`, StringName `&"x"`, NodePath `^"x"`, `\uXXXX`/`\a\b\f\v` escapes, `\` line continuation; Scene-unique-name node access sugar `%Name` and `$%Name` / `$Foo/%Bar`; Node.set_multiplayer_authority / get_multiplayer_authority / is_multiplayer_authority; Class-qualified type annotations (`var m: Node.ProcessMode`, `func f(e: Tween.EaseType) -> Control.LayoutPreset`)

**Prove it:** A scene-attached script declaring `enum State { IDLE, RUN = 5 }` can, from `_ready`, assign `self.state = State.RUN`, compare `state == State.RUN`, iterate `State.values()`-equivalent access, and the test reads back the node property as 5 through SceneTree after a runner frame; a member that does not exist in the enum (`State.WALK`) raises a runtime error rather than resolving to a @GlobalScope constant. (test: `gds_named_enums`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscript-interop --test gds_named_enums`.
acceptance_criteria: A scene-attached script declaring `enum State { IDLE, RUN = 5 }` can, from `_ready`, assign `self.state = State.RUN`, compare `state == State.RUN`, iterate `State.values()`-equivalent access, and the test reads back the node property as 5 through SceneTree after a runner frame; a member that does not exist in the enum (`State.WALK`) raises a runtime error rather than resolving to a @GlobalScope constant. (test: `gds_named_enums`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscript-interop --test gds_named_enums`.

title: GUI: register the real property/signal tables for Button, Label, ColorRect, TextureRect and the container family
description:
[audit-key: registered-class-member-depth/classdb-depth-gui] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json: Button 13 props (text, icon, flat, alignment, text_overrun_behavior, autowrap_mode, autowrap_trim_flags, clip_text, icon_alignment, vertical_icon_alignment, expand_icon, text_direction, language); Label 22 props; RichTextLabel 30 props/138 methods/4 signals; CodeEdit 22 props/116 methods/5 signals; ColorRect {color}; TextureRect {texture, expand_mode, stretch_mode, flip_h, flip_v}; ProgressBar {fill_mode, show_percentage, indeterminate, editor_preview_indeterminate}; SplitContainer 11 props/3 signals; ScrollContainer 11 props/2 signals; GridContainer {columns}; SubViewportContainer 3 props; Container 2 signals; StyleBox 4 props; Theme 3 props/69 methods

**Godot classes:** Button, Label, RichTextLabel, CodeEdit, ColorRect, TextureRect, ProgressBar, SplitContainer, ScrollContainer, GridContainer, SubViewportContainer, Container, StyleBox, Theme

**Patina today:**
- [registered-class-member-depth] engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:7719 `if !class_exists("Button") { register_class(ClassRegistration::new("Button").parent("BaseButton")); }` and :7722 the same for Label — bare names. Also :7783 ColorRect (no `color`), :7245 TextureRect, :7228 ProgressBar, :7055 RichTextLabel, :7777 CodeEdit, :7897 SplitContainer, :7113 ScrollContainer, :7261 GridContainer (no `columns`), :7906 SubViewportContainer, :7887 Container, :5937 StyleBox, :8071 Theme, :8074 ThemeDB. The inconsistency is local and visible: class_db.rs:7791 ReferenceRect immediately after ColorRect registers border_color/editor_only in full, and class_db.rs:7734 LineEdit registers 7 properties + 2 signals. Only Button, Label, TextEdit, LineEdit, ItemList, TabBar and ScrollContainer of this set appear in the editor's 70-class inspector schema, so ColorRect/CodeEdit/SplitContainer/GridContainer selected in the editor fall back to stored-only enumeration of an empty property bag.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth (upstream/godot/scene/gui/*.cpp _bind_methods + doc XML): Button {text, icon, flat=false, alignment=CENTER, text_overrun_behavior, autowrap_mode, clip_text=false, icon_alignment, vertical_icon_alignment, expand_icon=false, text_direction, language}; Label {text, label_settings, horizontal_alignment, vertical_alignment, autowrap_mode, justification_flags, clip_text, text_overrun_behavior, ellipsis_char, uppercase, tab_stops, lines_skipped, max_lines_visible=-1, visible_characters=-1, visible_characters_behavior, visible_ratio=1.0, text_direction, language, structured_text_bidi_override(+options), paragraph_separator, autowrap_trim_flags}; ColorRect {color=Color(1,1,1,1)}; TextureRect {texture, expand_mode, stretch_mode, flip_h, flip_v}; ProgressBar {fill_mode, show_percentage=true, indeterminate=false, editor_preview_indeterminate}; GridContainer {columns=1}; SplitContainer 11 props + dragged/drag_started/drag_ended; ScrollContainer 11 props + scroll_started/scroll_ended; SubViewportContainer {stretch, stretch_shrink, mouse_target}; Container emits pre_sort_children/sort_children; StyleBox {content_margin_left/top/right/bottom}; Theme {default_base_scale, default_font, default_font_size}.\n\nPatina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:7719 Button and :7722 Label are one-line registrations; :7783 ColorRect has no `color`; :7261 GridContainer has no `columns`; :7245 TextureRect, :7228 ProgressBar, :7055 RichTextLabel, :7777 CodeEdit, :7897 SplitContainer, :7113 ScrollContainer, :7906 SubViewportContainer, :7887 Container, :5937 StyleBox, :8071 Theme, :8074 ThemeDB are all bare. ReferenceRect at class_db.rs:7791 and LineEdit at :7734 show the intended depth.\n\nImplementation: extend those registrations with `.property(PropertyInfo::new(name, default).with_hint(...).with_hint_string(...))` using doc-XML defaults (watch the non-zero ones: ColorRect.color = white, GridContainer.columns = 1, ProgressBar.show_percentage = true, Label.visible_characters = -1, Label.visible_ratio = 1.0) and add the container/split/scroll signals. Wiring requirement: the values must round-trip .tscn -> ClassDB-seeded property bag -> the control draw path in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs (ColorRect at control_render.rs:1047 already reads the node's color property).

**Prove it:** A ColorRect created in the editor (no .tscn override) reads `color == Color(1,1,1,1)` and draws white; a GridContainer defaults to `columns == 1`; a Button loaded from a .tscn exposes text/icon/flat/alignment in the inspector and from GDScript; `ClassDB.class_get_property_list("Label")` returns all 22 names. (test: `classdb_gui_control_property_tables_match_godot`) — table-driven over the 15 classes plus a scene-load-to-draw assertion that a default ColorRect emits a white rect into the 2D draw list.
acceptance_criteria: A ColorRect created in the editor (no .tscn override) reads `color == Color(1,1,1,1)` and draws white; a GridContainer defaults to `columns == 1`; a Button loaded from a .tscn exposes text/icon/flat/alignment in the inspector and from GDScript; `ClassDB.class_get_property_list("Label")` returns all 22 names. (test: `classdb_gui_control_property_tables_match_godot`) — table-driven over the 15 classes plus a scene-load-to-draw assertion that a default ColorRect emits a white rect into the 2D draw list.

title: ClassDB: complete the particle node and ParticleProcessMaterial property tables plus the finished signal
description:
[audit-key: registered-class-member-depth/classdb-depth-particles] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json: CPUParticles3D 77 properties / 90 methods / 1 signal (finished); ParticleProcessMaterial 113 properties / 1 signal (emission_shape_changed); GPUParticles2D 1 signal, GPUParticles3D 30 properties / 1 signal; CPUParticles2D 1 signal

**Godot classes:** CPUParticles3D, CPUParticles2D, GPUParticles3D, GPUParticles2D, ParticleProcessMaterial

**Patina today:**
- [registered-class-member-depth] engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:2783 registers CPUParticles3D with zero properties, methods and signals; :2662 GPUParticles3D has 3 of 30; :5670 ParticleProcessMaterial has 19 of 113 and no signal; :6453 GPUParticles2D and :6526 CPUParticles2D have no `finished`. The simulation itself reads the node property bag with its own hardcoded fallbacks — engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:652 selects the classes and read_emitter_3d/emitter config at main_loop.rs:722-760 defaults amount/lifetime/draw_order/fixed_fps/explosiveness/speed_scale in code — so the runtime works while `ClassDB.class_get_property_list("CPUParticles3D")` is empty and `has_signal("finished")` is false on every particle node.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: CPUParticles3D binds 77 properties (emitting, amount, lifetime, one_shot, preprocess, speed_scale, explosiveness, randomness, lifetime_randomness, fixed_fps, fract_delta, visibility_aabb, local_coords, draw_order, mesh, emission_shape + sphere/box/points/normals/colors/ring params, particle_flag_*, direction, spread, flatness, gravity, and the min/max/curve triples for initial_velocity, angular_velocity, orbit_velocity, linear_accel, radial_accel, tangential_accel, damping, angle, scale_amount, hue_variation, anim_speed, anim_offset, plus color, color_ramp, color_initial_ramp) and the `finished` signal; ParticleProcessMaterial binds 113; GPUParticles3D 30. Godot's doc XML carries every default.\n\nPatina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:2783 CPUParticles3D is a bare registration; :2662 GPUParticles3D has 3 of 30; :5670 ParticleProcessMaterial has 19 of 113 and no emission_shape_changed signal; :6453 GPUParticles2D and :6526 CPUParticles2D lack `finished`. The simulator duplicates the defaults in code instead — engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:722-760 hardcodes amount/lifetime/draw_order/fixed_fps/explosiveness/speed_scale fallbacks — so nothing surfaces to the inspector or to `ClassDB.class_get_property_list`.\n\nImplementation: register the full property tables (with min/max/curve triples named exactly as Godot does, e.g. initial_velocity_min/initial_velocity_max/scale_amount_curve) and the `finished` signal on all four particle nodes plus emission_shape_changed on ParticleProcessMaterial; then have main_loop.rs read defaults from the ClassDB-seeded property bag rather than its own constants. Wiring requirement: a one_shot emitter in a .tscn must emit `finished` to a connected script when its last particle dies, and the property table must feed the same values the simulator uses.

**Prove it:** A .tscn CPUParticles3D with one_shot=true emits `finished` to a script-connected handler after its lifetime elapses, `has_signal("finished")` is true on all four particle node types, and `ClassDB.class_get_property_list("CPUParticles3D")` returns all 77 Godot names with matching defaults. (test: `classdb_particle_property_tables_match_godot`)
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn CPUParticles3D with one_shot=true emits `finished` to a script-connected handler after its lifetime elapses, `has_signal("finished")` is true on all four particle node types, and `ClassDB.class_get_property_list("CPUParticles3D")` returns all 77 Godot names with matching defaults. title: ClassDB: register MultiMesh, Skin, ImmediateMesh, TextMesh and the missing PrimitiveMesh subclasses with their property surface
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/classdb-render-resources] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json classes MultiMesh, Skin, ImmediateMesh, TextMesh, TorusMesh, QuadMesh, PointMesh, RibbonTrailMesh, TubeTrailMesh; upstream/godot/scene/resources/ | upstream/godot/scene/resources/multimesh.cpp, servers/rendering/renderer_scene_cull.cpp multimesh instancing; doc/classes/MultiMesh.xml (transform_format, use_colors, use_custom_data, instance_count, visible_instance_count, set_instance_transform, set_instance_color, set_instance_custom_data, buffer)

**Godot classes:** MultiMesh, Skin, ImmediateMesh, TextMesh, TorusMesh, QuadMesh, PointMesh, RibbonTrailMesh, TubeTrailMesh

**Patina today:**
- [rendering-3d] `grep -n '"MultiMesh"|"TextMesh"|"ImmediateMesh"|"Skin"|"TorusMesh"|"QuadMesh"|"PointMesh"|"RibbonTrailMesh"|"TubeTrailMesh"' engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` returns only PrismMesh (line 4224) — none of the nine names is registered. Yet implementations exist: MultiMesh3D (gdserver3d/src/multimesh.rs:35), Skin (gdserver3d/src/skin.rs), TextMesh (gdserver3d/src/text_mesh.rs), and TorusMesh/RibbonTrailMesh/TubeTrailMesh/PointMesh/QuadMesh in gdserver3d/src/extra_meshes.rs:32-140. ImmediateMesh has no implementation at all (only gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs mentions it). A .tscn declaring `[sub_resource type="MultiMesh" …]` for a MultiMeshInstance3D, or a `Skin` for a skinned MeshInstance3D, therefore cannot resolve through ClassDB.
- [sweep-2] A real per-instance MultiMesh exists at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/multimesh.rs:33 `pub struct MultiMesh3D` with set_instance_transform(index):76, get_instance_transform(index):84, set_instance_color(index):94, set_instance_custom_data(index):154, visible_count:178, flatten_instance_data:134. The rendering server trait exposes it: gdserver3d/src/server.rs:55 `fn set_multimesh(&mut self, id: Instance3DId, multimesh: MultiMesh3D);` and BOTH renderers implement it (gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs:2043 and gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs:3112). Nothing calls it — `rg -n 'MultiMesh3D|multimesh::' -g '*.rs' crates/` outside gdserver3d/src/multimesh.rs returns only those two impls, the trait declaration, instance.rs:240 (`pub multimesh: Option<MultiMesh3D>` field) and the lib.rs re-export; zero call sites in gdscene, gdscript-interop or patina-runner. The path that IS live goes around it and is broken: gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:672-745 `sync_multimesh_instances` expands N render instances and at :729 calls `node3d::get_multimesh_instance_transform(tree, nid, i)` — whose signature at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node3d.rs:672-684 is `pub fn get_multimesh_instance_transform(tree: &SceneTree, node_id: NodeId, _index: usize)` — the index is DISCARDED and the function returns the single `instance_transform` property of the node. Same for color: node3d.rs:686-693 `get_multimesh_instance_color(..., _index: usize)` returns the single `instance_color` property. So all N instances of a MultiMeshInstance3D render at the identical transform and identical color. 'MultiMesh' is also absent from class_db.rs's string literals (MultiMeshInstance3D IS registered).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/multimesh.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/extra_meshes.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/text_mesh.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node3d.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: MultiMesh (transform_format, use_colors, use_custom_data, instance_count, visible_instance_count, mesh, buffer/transform_array/color_array/custom_data_array, custom_aabb), Skin (bind count/name/bone/pose), ImmediateMesh (surface_begin/add_vertex/surface_end), TextMesh (text, font, font_size, depth, pixel_size, curve_step, horizontal/vertical_alignment, autowrap, width, line_spacing), and the PrimitiveMesh subclasses TorusMesh (inner/outer_radius, rings, ring_segments), QuadMesh, PointMesh, RibbonTrailMesh and TubeTrailMesh (size/sections/section_length/section_rings/curve/cap_top/cap_bottom). All appear in extension_api.json.

Patina current state: none of the nine is registered — `grep -n '"MultiMesh"' engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` and the equivalents for the other eight match nothing (PrismMesh at :4224 is the only one of this family present). This blocks .tscn resolution for `[sub_resource type="MultiMesh"]` (needed by every MultiMeshInstance3D) and `[sub_resource type="Skin"]` (needed by every skinned MeshInstance3D). Implementations already exist for most of them and are simply unreachable from ClassDB: gdserver3d/src/multimesh.rs:35 (MultiMesh3D with transform_format/instance_colors/instance_custom_data/use_custom_data/visible_instance_count), gdserver3d/src/skin.rs, gdserver3d/src/text_mesh.rs, and gdserver3d/src/extra_meshes.rs:32/:136 for PrismMesh/PointMesh plus the trail meshes. ImmediateMesh has no implementation anywhere.

Implementation approach: (1) add the nine `register_class(ClassRegistration::new(...).parent(...))` entries to `register_3d_classes` in gdobject/src/class_db.rs with the full property list and Godot defaults, using extension_api.json + doc/classes/*.xml as the oracle for names, types and defaults; (2) implement `ImmediateMesh` in gdserver3d (surface_begin/set_normal/set_uv/set_color/add_vertex/surface_end appending into a `Mesh3D`); (3) hook the MultiMesh and Skin sub-resource property bags into the existing `MultiMesh3D::from_properties`-style construction so a `[sub_resource type="MultiMesh"]` in a .tscn produces a populated MultiMesh3D on the MultiMeshInstance3D node.

title: Environment3D: colour adjustments + LUT, glow map, sky rotation, ambient sky contribution and background intensity
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/environment-surface] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/environment.cpp (adjustment_*, glow_map/glow_map_strength, sky_rotation, ambient_light_sky_contribution, background_intensity, reflected_light_source, glow_normalized, glow_mix); doc/classes/Environment.xml | upstream/godot/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/effects/ss_effects.cpp (SSR/SSAO/SSIL), environment/sdfgi, environment/fog.cpp (volumetric fog); doc/classes/Environment.xml

**Godot classes:** Environment, Sky

**Patina today:**
- [rendering-3d] Environment3D (engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/environment.rs:190) has 39 fields; Godot's Environment has 94 properties (jq). Missing and confirmed by grep across all non-test Rust: `adjustment_enabled`/`adjustment_color_correction` — only gdobject/src/class_db.rs:3677 (registration) and a ClassDB test; `glow_map`/`glow_map_strength` — only class_db.rs:3754-3755; `sky_rotation`, `ambient_light_sky_contribution`, `background_intensity`, `glow_normalized`, `glow_mix`, `ssao_power`/`ssao_detail`/`ssao_horizon`/`ssao_sharpness`/`ssao_light_affect`/`ssao_ao_channel_affect` — 1 hit each (the ClassDB registration only). `reflected_light_source` — class_db.rs:3759 plus a ClassDB test. So the editor inspector will show and persist these values and the renderer will discard every one of them.
- [rendering-3d] Grepping every one of `ssr_enabled`, `ssil_enabled`, `sdfgi_enabled`, `volumetric_fog_enabled` across engine-rs/crates returns exactly two hits each: the ClassDB registration (gdobject/src/class_db.rs:3817, :3805, :3769, :3861) and a ClassDB registration test (gdobject/tests/rendering_resources.rs:181-190). `Environment3D` (gdserver3d/src/environment.rs:190) has no ssr/ssil/sdfgi/volumetric field; gdrender3d/src/postprocess.rs implements only `apply_ssao_env` (:818) and glow/tonemap. There is no reflection-ray, GI-cascade or froxel volume code anywhere. Note also `apply_ssao_env` is called only from the software renderer (gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs:529, :938); `grep -i ssao gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs` = 0, so even the SSAO that exists is absent from the default GPU path.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/environment.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/postprocess.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: Environment.adjustment_enabled gates brightness/contrast/saturation and an optional `adjustment_color_correction` (Texture2D gradient strip or Texture3D LUT) applied at the end of the post chain; glow_map + glow_map_strength modulate the glow buffer; glow_normalized and glow_mix control level normalisation and mix blending; sky_rotation (Vector3) rotates the sky basis; ambient_light_sky_contribution blends sky ambient against ambient_light_color; background_intensity scales the background in nits; reflected_light_source selects Bg/Disabled/Sky for reflections. See upstream/godot/scene/resources/environment.cpp and doc/classes/Environment.xml.

Patina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/environment.rs:190 `Environment3D` has 39 fields versus Godot's 94. Every property above is registered with a default in gdobject/src/class_db.rs (adjustment_enabled at :3677, glow_map at :3754, reflected_light_source at :3759) but has NO corresponding field on `Environment3D` and no consumer in gdrender3d/src/postprocess.rs — grep proves the ClassDB registration is the only occurrence in the codebase. The inspector therefore round-trips the value into the .tscn and the render silently ignores it.

Implementation approach: (1) add `adjustment_enabled/brightness/contrast/saturation/color_correction`, `glow_map` (+ strength), `glow_normalized`, `glow_mix`, `sky_rotation: Vector3`, `ambient_light_sky_contribution`, `background_intensity`, `reflected_light_source` and the six missing `ssao_*` knobs to `Environment3D`; (2) parse them in the WorldEnvironment resolver at gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:7701 (`environment_from…`) alongside the existing fields; (3) implement adjustments as a final stage in gdrender3d/src/postprocess.rs `apply_camera_post` (brightness/contrast/saturation in linear, then a 1D-strip or 3D LUT lookup), modulate the glow buffer by `glow_map` in `generate_glow`, and honour `glow_normalized`/`glow_mix` in `blend_glow`; (4) apply `sky_rotation` to the sky direction basis in gdserver3d/src/sky.rs and both sky passes; (5) fold `ambient_light_sky_contribution` into the ambient term in both shading paths.

Wiring requirement: WorldEnvironment -> Environment sub-resource -> `Environment3D` -> post-process/sky in both the software and wgpu paths.

**Merged findings (2):** Environment adjustments (brightness/contrast/saturation + colour-correction LUT), glow map, sky rotation, ambient sky contribution and background intensity are registered in ClassDB but have no render field; Environment screen-space effects: SSR, SSIL, SDFGI and volumetric fog have no implementation at all

**Prove it:** A .tscn WorldEnvironment with `adjustment_enabled = true, adjustment_saturation = 0.0` renders a greyscale frame (R==G==B per pixel) where the unadjusted scene is coloured; `adjustment_brightness = 2.0` raises mean luminance; a non-zero `sky_rotation` moves the procedural sky's horizon/sun in the frame; `ambient_light_sky_contribution = 0.0` with a coloured `ambient_light_color` shifts surface ambient away from the sky colour. (test: `environment_adjustments_render`) — renders each case from a .tscn string via the editor 3D render path and asserts the pixel statistics.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn WorldEnvironment with `adjustment_enabled = true, adjustment_saturation = 0.0` renders a greyscale frame (R==G==B per pixel) where the unadjusted scene is coloured; `adjustment_brightness = 2.0` raises mean luminance; a non-zero `sky_rotation` moves the procedural sky's horizon/sun in the frame; `ambient_light_sky_contribution = 0.0` with a coloured `ambient_light_color` shifts surface ambient away from the sky colour. (test: `environment_adjustments_render`) — renders each case from a .tscn string via the editor 3D render path and asserts the pixel statistics.

title: GI3D: feed VoxelGI/LightmapGI from the scene tree into the shading loop
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/gi] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/STUB]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/voxel_gi.cpp, lightmap_gi.cpp; servers/rendering/renderer_rd/environment/gi.cpp; doc/classes/VoxelGI.xml, LightmapGI.xml | upstream/godot/scene/3d/voxel_gi.cpp (subdiv, size, camera_attributes, bake -> VoxelGIData), upstream/godot/scene/3d/lightmap_gi.cpp (quality, bounces, directional, texel_scale, environment_mode, generate_probes_subdiv, bake -> LightmapGIData), upstream/godot/scene/3d/lightmap_probe.cpp

**Godot classes:** VoxelGI, VoxelGIData, LightmapGI, LightmapGIData, LightmapProbe

**Patina today:**
- [rendering-3d] engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/gi.rs is 962 lines (VoxelGI, VoxelGIId, VoxelGISubdiv, LightmapGI, LightmapGIData, LightmapBakeQuality, LightmapProbeGeneration) and is re-exported at gdserver3d/src/lib.rs:45. `grep -rn "gdserver3d::gi|VoxelGI" --include=*.rs engine-rs/crates` outside gi.rs finds only: the lib.rs re-export, gdobject/src/class_db.rs:2868 (registration), gdeditor/src/create_dialog.rs:567 (a tooltip string), and test files. `grep -ci "VoxelGI|LightmapGI"` in gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs = 0 and in gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs = 0 — neither shading loop reads a GI contribution. A VoxelGI or LightmapGI node in a .tscn changes no pixel.
- [nodes-3d] /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/gi.rs:1 is titled "Global Illumination stub nodes: VoxelGI and LightmapGI" and :11 states "`VoxelGI::bake` never voxelizes anything". More importantly there is no scene consumer at all: grep for `is_class("VoxelGI")`, `is_class("LightmapGI")` or `"LightmapProbe"` across engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src and gdeditor/src returns nothing — `scene_env_effects` (gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs:1641) collects only FogVolume, Decal, ReflectionProbe and OccluderInstance3D, so a .tscn containing a VoxelGI or LightmapGI node is read into the tree and then ignored by every render path. The classes are registered (present in patina_registered.txt) and appear in the create-node catalog (gdeditor/src/create_dialog.rs:567-568), so the editor advertises them as usable.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/gi.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: VoxelGI voxelises static geometry into a cascade (subdiv 64/128/256/512), stores it in VoxelGIData (energy, bias, normal_bias, propagation, dynamic_range, interior, use_two_bounces) and cone-traces it per fragment; LightmapGI bakes irradiance into LightmapGIData textures sampled through UV2, with LightmapProbe capture points for dynamic objects. GeometryInstance3D.gi_mode selects Disabled/Static/Dynamic participation. See upstream/godot/scene/3d/voxel_gi.cpp and lightmap_gi.cpp.

Patina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/gi.rs is a 962-line module (VoxelGI, VoxelGISubdiv, LightmapGI, LightmapGIData, LightmapBakeQuality, LightmapProbeGeneration) re-exported at gdserver3d/src/lib.rs:45 with ZERO production consumers. Outside gi.rs, the names appear only in gdobject/src/class_db.rs:2868 (registration), gdeditor/src/create_dialog.rs:567 (a tooltip), and tests. Both shading loops are GI-blind: `grep -ci VoxelGI` in gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs and gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs = 0. `gi_mode` likewise reaches only class_db.rs and the inspector schema. So authoring GI in a scene changes nothing.

Implementation approach: (1) extend `SceneEnvEffects3D` in gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs:1488 (which already snapshots FogVolume/Decal/ReflectionProbe/Occluder) with `voxel_gi: Vec<(VoxelGI, Transform3D)>` and `lightmap_gi: Vec<LightmapGI>`, parsed from the tree the same way; (2) add `add_voxel_gi`/`add_lightmap_gi` to the `RenderingServer3D` trait (gdserver3d/src/server.rs) and implement them on BOTH SoftwareRenderer3D and GpuRenderer3D — do not leave them as default no-ops, which is exactly how decals and fog volumes were lost on the GPU path; (3) implement a runtime voxelisation + cone-trace ambient term in gdserver3d/src/gi.rs's existing structures and add it to the ambient contribution in gdrender3d/src/shader.rs and the WGSL fragment stage; (4) sample LightmapGIData through the mesh's UV2 for instances whose gi_mode is Static; (5) honour GeometryInstance3D.gi_mode.

Wiring requirement: VoxelGI node in a .tscn -> render inputs -> render server -> ambient/indirect term in both pipelines.

**Merged findings (2):** VoxelGI / LightmapGI: a 962-line gi.rs module with zero production consumers; VoxelGI / LightmapGI / LightmapProbe

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a VoxelGI covering a red wall next to a white wall renders visible colour bleed onto the white wall (its pixels shift toward red) that is absent when the VoxelGI node is removed or its `gi_mode` participation is Disabled, in both the software and GPU frames. (test: `voxelgi_lightmap_scene_render`) — loads the scene from a .tscn string, renders through the editor 3D path with and without the GI node, and asserts the hue shift on the sampled wall region.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a VoxelGI covering a red wall next to a white wall renders visible colour bleed onto the white wall (its pixels shift toward red) that is absent when the VoxelGI node is removed or its `gi_mode` participation is Disabled, in both the software and GPU frames. (test: `voxelgi_lightmap_scene_render`) — loads the scene from a .tscn string, renders through the editor 3D path with and without the GI node, and asserts the hue shift on the sampled wall region.

title: Shadows3D: use the PSSM cascades, honour shadow bias/normal bias and add soft shadows + directional shadow mode
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/shadows] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/light_3d.cpp (shadow_bias, shadow_normal_bias, light_size, light_angular_distance, directional_shadow_mode/max_distance/fade_start/pancake_size, shadow_reverse_cull_face, shadow_transmittance_bias); servers/rendering/renderer_rd/ shadow atlas + PSSM

**Godot classes:** DirectionalLight3D, Light3D, OmniLight3D, SpotLight3D

**Patina today:**
- [rendering-3d] gdrender3d/src/shadow_map.rs implements the full PSSM machinery — `DirectionalCascade` (:902), `cascade_split_distances`/`_lambda` (:912/:924), `generate_directional_cascades` (:952), `select_cascade` (:1006), `cascade_index_for` (:1017) — and `grep -rn "cascade_split_distances|DirectionalCascade|generate_directional_cascade"` outside shadow_map.rs returns NOTHING: not the software renderer, not the GPU pipeline. Both callers use the single-map `generate_shadow_maps` (renderer.rs:628, wgpu_pipeline.rs:1300, :2199); `grep -n "cascade|split" gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs` = 0 hits. Separately `grep -rln` excluding tests/inspector-schema shows `shadow_bias` and `shadow_normal_bias` reach only patina-runner/src/class_defaults.rs and gdobject/src/class_db.rs; `light_size`, `directional_shadow_fade_start`, `shadow_reverse_cull_face` and `light_intensity_lumens` return NO hits anywhere; `light_negative`, `light_specular` and `light_bake_mode` hit only class_db.rs. Light3D (gdserver3d/src/light.rs:337-427) does carry shadow_split_1..3 and blend_splits, which are therefore parsed and then discarded.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/shadow_map.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/light.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: DirectionalLight3D renders 1/2/4 PSSM cascades chosen by `directional_shadow_mode`, bounded by `directional_shadow_max_distance`, faded over `directional_shadow_fade_start`, optionally blended across splits (`directional_shadow_blend_splits`); every Light3D applies `shadow_bias` (default 0.1) and `shadow_normal_bias` (default 2.0) to kill acne, and `light_size`/`light_angular_distance` widen the PCF kernel for soft shadows. See upstream/godot/scene/3d/light_3d.cpp.

Patina current state: the cascade code exists and is dead. engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/shadow_map.rs defines `DirectionalCascade` (:902), `cascade_split_distances_lambda` (:924), `generate_directional_cascades` (:952), `select_cascade` (:1006) and `cascade_index_for` (:1017) with unit tests — and has ZERO callers outside the module. Both real renderers call the single-map `generate_shadow_maps` instead (gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs:628; gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs:1300 and :2199), and `grep -n cascade gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs` returns nothing. `Light3D` (gdserver3d/src/light.rs:337-427) stores shadow_split_1..3 and blend_splits that nothing reads. Bias is worse: `shadow_bias`/`shadow_normal_bias` exist only as ClassDB defaults (gdobject/src/class_db.rs, patina-runner/src/class_defaults.rs) and `light_size` / `directional_shadow_fade_start` / `shadow_reverse_cull_face` do not exist at all.

Implementation approach: (1) add `shadow_bias`, `shadow_normal_bias`, `light_size`, `directional_shadow_mode`, `directional_shadow_max_distance`, `directional_shadow_fade_start` to `Light3D` and parse them where the other light properties are read (gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs and gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs SceneLight3D); (2) replace the single directional map with `generate_directional_cascades(..., count_from(directional_shadow_mode))` in gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs:628, selecting per-fragment with `cascade_index_for` and cross-fading when `blend_splits` is set; (3) upload the cascade array + per-cascade matrices to the WGSL shadow bind group in gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs and select in the fragment shader; (4) subtract `shadow_bias` and offset along the normal by `shadow_normal_bias` at the depth compare in the shared sampler (shadow_map.rs:213 is documented as the single chokepoint for all three map kinds); (5) scale the PCF kernel radius by `light_size`/`light_angular_distance`.

Wiring requirement: a DirectionalLight3D in a .tscn -> cascade generation -> per-fragment cascade selection in BOTH renderers.

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a DirectionalLight3D and a long ground plane renders a shadow that stays sharp at close range and remains present at far range (the far half is currently either unshadowed or heavily aliased with a single map), and `directional_shadow_mode = 2` (4 splits) produces a different, higher-resolution near shadow than mode 0. Raising `shadow_bias` removes self-shadow acne (measured as speckle pixel count on the lit side of a sphere) in both the software and GPU frames. (test: `directional_cascade_shadow_render`) — renders from .tscn strings through the editor 3D render path and asserts near/far shadow coverage and acne-pixel counts.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a DirectionalLight3D and a long ground plane renders a shadow that stays sharp at close range and remains present at far range (the far half is currently either unshadowed or heavily aliased with a single map), and `directional_shadow_mode = 2` (4 splits) produces a different, higher-resolution near shadow than mode 0. Raising `shadow_bias` removes self-shadow acne (measured as speckle pixel count on the lit side of a sphere) in both the software and GPU frames. (test: `directional_cascade_shadow_render`) — renders from .tscn strings through the editor 3D render path and asserts near/far shadow coverage and acne-pixel counts.

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

[status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** `Curve` (Resource) is a piecewise curve of points with left/right tangents and TangentMode FREE/LINEAR, `bake()`d at `bake_resolution` (default 100) and read via `sample(offset)`/`sample_baked(offset)`; domain/value are clamped to min/max_domain & min/max_value. `Gradient` (Resource) holds parallel `offsets`/`colors` arrays sampled with interpolation_mode CONSTANT/LINEAR/CUBIC in interpolation_color_space sRGB/OKLAB/LINEAR_SRGB. `GradientTexture1D` bakes a gradient into a width-wide 1D texture; `GradientTexture2D` fills a width×height texture with FILL_LINEAR/RADIAL/SQUARE between fill_from and fill_to with repeat NONE/MIRROR/REPEAT. **Prove it:** an integration test that loads such a scene, renders/steps it, and asserts (a) the rasterized Line2D pixels differ between the two ends, and (b) a particle's colour at 10% lifetime differs from its colour at 90%.

**Prove it:** Curve, Gradient, GradientTexture1D and GradientTexture2D are registered in ClassDB with Godot 4.6.1 defaults, parse from .tscn/.tres sub_resources, and drive real output: a Line2D with a gradient + width_curve rasterizes a varying stroke via draw_polyline_shaded, and a ParticleProcessMaterial color_ramp changes particle colour over lifetime. (test: `curve_gradient_resources_drive_line2d_and_particles`)

[audit-key: resources-io/texture2d-variant-resources] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

There is no sub-rect sampling path at all: `rg -i 'atlas' engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/*.rs` finds only the unrelated TTF glyph atlas (`ttf_font.rs`).

**Implement:** register all three with their exact properties/defaults in `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`. Add resource types + `.tres` load/save in `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/` (AtlasTexture holding an ext_resource reference to its atlas plus region/margin/filter_clip). In `engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs`, make texture sampling honour an AtlasTexture's region+margin (so a Sprite2D/TextureRect assigned an AtlasTexture draws only its sub-rect at the right size), tick AnimatedTexture frame advance from the same per-frame path that drives AnimatedSprite2D, and let CanvasTexture supply the normal/specular maps to the 2D lighting pass.

**Wiring requirement:** a `.tscn` Sprite2D whose `texture` is an `[ext_resource type="AtlasTexture"]` must draw the correct sub-rect in both the runner and the editor viewport; an AnimatedTexture must advance frames from the main-loop tick; a CanvasTexture's normal map must change the 2D lighting result under a Light2D.

**Prove it:** load a scene with a Sprite2D using an AtlasTexture over a known 4x4 checkerboard sheet and assert the drawn pixels equal the selected cell (and the item's rect size equals the region size); step the loop for an AnimatedTexture with two visually distinct frames and assert the drawn pixels change at the configured duration and stop after one cycle with `one_shot`; assert a CanvasTexture's normal_texture changes the lit output versus a flat normal.

**Prove it:** AtlasTexture, AnimatedTexture and CanvasTexture are registered and loadable from .tres/.tscn, a Sprite2D with an AtlasTexture draws exactly its region sub-rect at region size, an AnimatedTexture advances frames from the main-loop tick (honouring one_shot/speed_scale), and a CanvasTexture normal map changes the Light2D-lit output (test: `texture2d_variant_resources_draw`)

title: Image: complete the Format enum, script method table, encoders and buffer loaders
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/image-class-surface] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json Image has 76 methods and `Image.Format` has 48 values (L8…ASTC_8x8_HDR). Encoders: save_png/save_png_to_buffer/save_jpg/save_webp/save_exr/save_dds (+_to_buffer). Buffer loaders: load_png_from_buffer, load_jpg_from_buffer, load_webp_from_buffer, load_tga_from_buffer, load_bmp_from_buffer, load_ktx_from_buffer, load_dds_from_buffer, load_exr_from_buffer, load_svg_from_buffer/string. **Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `Image` exposes 76 script methods and 48 pixel formats (`Image.Format`). Scripts routinely do `Image.load_png_from_buffer(bytes)`, `img.resize(w,h,INTERPOLATE_LANCZOS)`, `img.convert(FORMAT_RGBA8)`, `img.generate_mipmaps()`, `img.save_png("user://shot.png")`, `img.save_webp_to_buffer()`, `img.blit_rect(src, rect, dst)`, `img.premultiply_alpha()`, `img.srgb_to_linear()` (upstream/godot/core/io/image.cpp).

No encoder is reachable from Image — the only PNG encoder is a framebuffer dump at `gdrender2d/src/export.rs:202`; `grep -rn save_webp` over the workspace is empty. No `load_*_from_buffer` is bound even though decoders exist (`gdresource/src/texture_import.rs:180 decode_png_bytes`, `:413 decode_jpg_bytes`, WebP via the `image` crate, `gdresource/src/image_tga_bmp.rs`, `gdresource/src/radiance_hdr.rs:121 decode_hdr`, `gdresource/src/image_svg.rs:40 rasterize_svg_bytes`). `generate_mipmaps` (image.rs:691) returns a detached `Vec<Image>` instead of storing levels, so `has_mipmaps`/`get_mipmap_count`/`get_mipmap_offset` cannot work.

Implementation approach: extend `ImageFormat` in `gdresource/src/image.rs` to the full 48-value Godot enum with correct ordinals, implementing pixel get/set + convert for at least the uncompressed families (8-bit, 16-bit half-float, RGBA4444/RGB565/RGBE9995) and treating compressed formats as opaque payloads with a `decompress()` entry point. Store mip levels on `Image` (data + per-level offsets) so `generate_mipmaps`/`clear_mipmaps`/`get_mipmap_offset`/`get_mipmap_count`/`has_mipmaps` behave. Add `save_png`/`save_png_to_buffer` on top of the existing `gdrender2d::encode_png` (lift it into gdresource or a shared crate to avoid the dependency inversion), plus `save_webp`/`save_jpg` via the `image` crate's encoders and `save_exr` if cheap. Add `load_{png,jpg,webp,tga,bmp,hdr,exr,svg}_from_buffer` delegating to the decoders already in `texture_import.rs`, `image_tga_bmp.rs`, `radiance_hdr.rs`, `image_svg.rs`. Then fill out `call_image_static`/`call_image_instance` in `gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:18853/18890` to the full 76-method table, returning `PackedByteArray` where Godot does.

Wiring requirement: an `Image` built or loaded from a script must be usable as a texture in a running scene (via `ImageTexture.create_from_image`, see the texture-resource-classes bead) and `save_png` must write a real file through `gdcore::FileAccess` path resolution so `user://` works.
