title: Resources-IO: implement ImageTexture/AtlasTexture/Gradient(+Textures)/Curve/NoiseTexture resources end-to-end
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/texture-resource-classes] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json classes ImageTexture (create_from_image/set_image/update/get_image), AtlasTexture (atlas, region, margin, filter_clip), Gradient (offsets/colors/interpolation modes), GradientTexture1D (width, use_hdr), GradientTexture2D (fill modes, from/to), Curve (points, bake, min/max value, domain), Noise + FastNoiseLite (noise_type, fractal, cellular, domain warp), NoiseTexture2D/3D (seamless, as_normal_map, bump strength, color_ramp). Sources: upstream/godot/scene/resources/{texture.cpp,atlas_texture.cpp,gradient.cpp,gradient_texture.cpp,curve.cpp}, modules/noise/.

**Godot classes:** ImageTexture, AtlasTexture, Gradient, GradientTexture1D, GradientTexture2D, Curve, Noise, FastNoiseLite, NoiseTexture2D, NoiseTexture3D

**Patina today:**
- [resources-io] None of these are ClassDB-registered: `grep -c 'ClassRegistration::new("<name>")' gdobject/src/class_db.rs` returns 0 for ImageTexture, AtlasTexture, Gradient, GradientTexture1D, GradientTexture2D, Curve, Noise, FastNoiseLite, NoiseTexture2D and NoiseTexture3D; all ten also appear in the audit's own `unregistered.txt`. No implementation exists either: `grep -rn '"AtlasTexture"' --include='*.rs'` over engine-rs/crates (excluding gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs) → 0 hits; the only occurrence anywhere is a string in the editor's HTML dropdown list at `gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs:5048`, i.e. the editor offers to create resource types the engine cannot construct. `grep -rn 'ImageTexture' gdscript-interop/src gdrender2d/src gdscene/src` → 0 hits, so `ImageTexture.create_from_image(img)` — the standard procedural-texture idiom — is impossible. `gdresource/src/noise.rs:78` has a working `FastNoiseLite` math struct with `bake_image_l8` (:208) but no resource class or ClassDB entry wraps it, so nothing in a `.tscn` can reach it. `Curve2D` is registered (class_db.rs) but the plain `Curve` used by particle/audio curves is not.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/noise.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `ImageTexture.create_from_image(image)` / `set_image` / `update` is how every script builds a runtime texture (upstream/godot/scene/resources/texture.cpp). `AtlasTexture` draws a `region` out of an `atlas` texture with `margin` and `filter_clip` (atlas_texture.cpp) and is the standard sprite-sheet resource. `Gradient` holds offset/color point pairs with interpolation modes (LINEAR/CONSTANT/CUBIC) and color spaces; `GradientTexture1D(width, use_hdr)` and `GradientTexture2D(fill: LINEAR/RADIAL/SQUARE, fill_from, fill_to, repeat)` bake it into pixels (gradient_texture.cpp). `Curve` (min/max value, domain, points with left/right tangents and modes, `bake_resolution`, `sample`/`sample_baked`) backs curve-driven params. `FastNoiseLite`/`NoiseTexture2D`/`NoiseTexture3D` (modules/noise/) expose noise_type, fractal params, cellular params, domain warp, `seamless`, `as_normal_map`, `bump_strength`, `color_ramp`.

Patina current state: all ten classes are unregistered — `grep -c 'ClassRegistration::new("X")' engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` is 0 for each, and each appears in the audit's `unregistered.txt`. `AtlasTexture` has no Rust code at all; its only occurrence is a string in the editor's create-resource dropdown at `gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs:5048`, so the editor advertises a type that cannot be constructed. `ImageTexture` has no occurrence in gdscript-interop/gdrender2d/gdscene. The noise math exists but is orphaned: `gdresource/src/noise.rs:78 FastNoiseLite` with `bake_image_l8` at :208 has no resource wrapper.

Implementation approach: add `gdresource/src/gradient.rs` (Gradient + GradientTexture1D/2D bake to `crate::image::Image`), `gdresource/src/curve.rs` (Curve with tangents + baking), `gdresource/src/atlas_texture.rs` (region/margin/filter_clip resolution to a source-rect), and a `NoiseTexture2D/3D` wrapper in `gdresource/src/noise.rs` that bakes through the existing `FastNoiseLite` (noise.rs:208/:221) honoring seamless/as_normal_map/color_ramp. Add an `ImageTexture` resource in `gdresource/src/image.rs` with `create_from_image`/`set_image`/`update`/`get_image`. Register all of them in `gdobject/src/class_db.rs` with correct parents (ImageTexture/AtlasTexture/GradientTexture*/NoiseTexture2D → Texture2D; NoiseTexture3D → Texture3D; Gradient/Curve/Noise/FastNoiseLite → Resource, `Noise` abstract) and their real property/method lists. Add `.new()` arms plus method dispatch in `gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` next to the existing `ConfigFile`/`XMLParser` arms (interpreter.rs:3018-3070), and teach the `.tscn` sub-resource path (`gdresource/src/loader.rs`) to build them from `[sub_resource type="Gradient"]` sections.

Wiring requirement: the 2D renderer must sample them. `gdrender2d`'s texture resolution (used by Sprite2D/TextureRect draw item generation) must resolve an `AtlasTexture` to its atlas sub-rect and a Gradient/Noise texture to baked pixels, so a `.tscn` authoring `texture = SubResource("GradientTexture2D_1")` produces the gradient in the frame buffer.

**Prove it:** A `.tscn` containing a Sprite2D whose `texture` is a `SubResource("AtlasTexture_…")` over a PNG atlas renders exactly the sub-region's pixels; a TextureRect whose texture is a `GradientTexture2D` with a two-stop Gradient renders the interpolated ramp; a `NoiseTexture2D` sub-resource renders deterministic noise for a fixed seed; and a script can do `var it = ImageTexture.create_from_image(img); $Sprite2D.texture = it` and see those pixels. Test: `texture_resource_classes_render_from_scene` — loads one fixture scene exercising AtlasTexture, GradientTexture2D, NoiseTexture2D and a script-built ImageTexture, steps a frame, and asserts the sampled framebuffer pixels at known coordinates (test: `texture_resource_classes_render_from_scene`).
acceptance_criteria: A `.tscn` containing a Sprite2D whose `texture` is a `SubResource("AtlasTexture_…")` over a PNG atlas renders exactly the sub-region's pixels; a TextureRect whose texture is a `GradientTexture2D` with a two-stop Gradient renders the interpolated ramp; a `NoiseTexture2D` sub-resource renders deterministic noise for a fixed seed; and a script can do `var it = ImageTexture.create_from_image(img); $Sprite2D.texture = it` and see those pixels. Test: `texture_resource_classes_render_from_scene` — loads one fixture scene exercising AtlasTexture, GradientTexture2D, NoiseTexture2D and a script-built ImageTexture, steps a frame, and asserts the sampled framebuffer pixels at known coordinates (test: `texture_resource_classes_render_from_scene`).

title: GUI: implement BaseButton toggle/action-mode/button-mask/group semantics and press mouse capture
description:
[audit-key: gui-controls/gui-button-semantics] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: STUB/MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/gui/base_button.cpp (`_pressed`, `_toggled`, `set_pressed`, ACTION_MODE_BUTTON_PRESS/RELEASE, `button_mask` default MOUSE_BUTTON_MASK_LEFT, ButtonGroup), upstream/godot/scene/main/viewport.cpp:1916 (`gui.mouse_focus` capture) and 2070-2075 (motion routed to mouse_focus) | extension_api.json BaseButton._pressed() / _toggled(bool toggled_on), Range._value_changed(float new_value); upstream/godot/scene/gui/base_button.cpp (`pressed` signal emission is preceded by GDVIRTUAL_CALL(_pressed)), scene/gui/range.cpp Range::_value_changed.

**Godot classes:** BaseButton, Button, CheckBox, CheckButton, ButtonGroup, OptionButton, MenuButton, Range, HSlider, VSlider, SpinBox, ProgressBar

**Patina today:**
- [gui-controls] ClassDB registers the full toggle surface — engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:7187-7192 declares `toggle_mode`, `button_pressed`, `action_mode`, `button_group` — and the renderer *reads* it (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs:1469 `bool_prop(tree, node_id, "button_pressed")` draws the checkmark). Nothing ever writes it: `grep -rn 'toggle_mode' --include=*.rs crates/` outside class_db.rs returns 0 hits, `grep -rn '"toggled"'` finds only gdeditor signal-catalog strings (signals_tree.rs:170, signal_dialog.rs:449) and no `emit_signal`. `SceneTree::gui_input_stage` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:3350-3389) is the only press handler: it emits `button_down` on press and `button_up`+`pressed` on same-target release, with no toggle, no `action_mode`, and it matches `Ev::MouseButton { pressed, .. }` for ANY button, so a right-click fires `pressed` (Godot's `button_mask` defaults to LEFT only). `keep_pressed_outside` and `ButtonGroup` have zero occurrences workspace-wide. There is also no press capture: motion during a held press is re-hit-tested rather than routed to the pressed control, so no Control can implement a drag.
- [engine-virtual-method-table] `rg -F '"_pressed"' / '"_toggled"' / '"_value_changed"' engine-rs/crates/` each return 0 hits tree-wide including tests. The engine-side state changes that would fire them exist: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs:3044-3062 `set_range_value` clamps/snaps and returns whether the value changed, with the doc comment at :3042-3043 stating "the caller emits the `value_changed` signal in that case" — the signal is emitted but the virtual is never called. BaseButton is registered at engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:7183 and Range at :7201, neither declaring any `_`-prefixed method.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/item_controls.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `BaseButton` (upstream/godot/scene/gui/base_button.cpp) tracks `pressing_inside`, honors `button_mask` (default MOUSE_BUTTON_MASK_LEFT — other buttons are ignored entirely), `action_mode` (ACTION_MODE_BUTTON_PRESS fires `pressed` on the down edge, ACTION_MODE_BUTTON_RELEASE on the up edge inside the rect), `keep_pressed_outside`, and `toggle_mode`: a toggle button flips `button_pressed` and emits `toggled(bool)` in addition to `pressed`. `ButtonGroup` makes toggles mutually exclusive (with `allow_unpress`), and `shortcut` + `shortcut_feedback` let a key event press the button. Separately, `Viewport` captures `gui.mouse_focus` on press (viewport.cpp:1916) and routes all subsequent motion and the release to that control (viewport.cpp:2070-2075), which is what makes button drag-off/drag-back and every draggable Control work.\n\nPatina current state: the properties are registered (engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:7187-7192) and `button_pressed` is drawn (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs:1467-1497) but never written by input. `SceneTree::gui_input_stage` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:3350-3389) emits only `button_down` / `button_up` / `pressed`, matches any mouse button, and drops `gui_press_target` on release without capturing motion. `toggled`, `ButtonGroup` and `keep_pressed_outside` do not exist anywhere in the workspace.\n\nImplementation approach: add a `gui_mouse_focus: Option<NodeId>` to SceneTree alongside the existing `gui_press_target` (scene_tree.rs:3350) and, while it is set, route MouseMotion and the MouseButton release to it instead of re-hit-testing. Gate the whole press block on `button_mask` (read the property, default `1 << (MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT-1)`). Add `control::button_is_toggle`, `control::set_button_pressed` in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs that flip `button_pressed` and emit `toggled`, honoring `action_mode` for which edge fires, and a `button_group` resolution pass that unpresses siblings sharing the group. Register `toggled` / `ButtonGroup` in class_db.rs.\n\nWiring requirement: the flow must be `MainLoop::step` -> `SceneTree::push_input` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2754) -> `gui_input_stage` -> property write + signal emit, observable from a GDScript handler connected in a loaded .tscn.

**Merged findings (2):** BaseButton toggle_mode / button_pressed / toggled, action_mode, button_mask, button_group, shortcut, mouse capture for drag; BaseButton `_pressed`/`_toggled` and Range `_value_changed` subclass hooks

**Prove it:** A .tscn CheckBox with `toggle_mode = true` clicked once has `button_pressed == true` and emitted `toggled(true)`; clicked again reports `toggled(false)`. A right-click on a Button emits nothing. A Button with `action_mode = 0` (BUTTON_PRESS) fires `pressed` on the down edge. Pressing a Button, moving the pointer off it, and releasing outside fires `button_up` but not `pressed`, and the intermediate motion events were delivered to the pressed control's `_gui_input`. Two CheckBoxes sharing a `button_group` are mutually exclusive. (test: `base_button_toggle_group_and_capture_semantics`)
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn CheckBox with `toggle_mode = true` clicked once has `button_pressed == true` and emitted `toggled(true)`; clicked again reports `toggled(false)`. A right-click on a Button emits nothing. A Button with `action_mode = 0` (BUTTON_PRESS) fires `pressed` on the down edge. Pressing a Button, moving the pointer off it, and releasing outside fires `button_up` but not `pressed`, and the intermediate motion events were delivered to the pressed control's `_gui_input`. Two CheckBoxes sharing a `button_group` are mutually exclusive. (test: `base_button_toggle_group_and_capture_semantics`)

title: Window: drive root-window resize through the frame loop so stretch, size_changed and get_visible_rect stay live
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/st-root-window-resize] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/STUB]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/main/window.cpp `Window::_update_viewport_size` / `_notification(NOTIFICATION_WM_SIZE_CHANGED)` recomputes the stretch transform from `content_scale_size`/`content_scale_mode`/`content_scale_aspect`/`content_scale_factor` whenever the OS window (or, on web, the canvas) changes size, then emits `size_changed`; `Viewport::get_visible_rect()` reports the new size. doc/classes/Window.xml size_changed. | upstream/godot/scene/main/scene_tree.cpp:2079-2147 (msaa_2d, snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel, snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel, sdf oversize/scale applied to the root viewport) and scene/main/window.cpp content-scale pipeline; extension_api.json Viewport.canvas_cull_mask/msaa_2d | upstream/godot/scene/gui/dialogs.cpp (AcceptDialog `popup_centered`, ok/cancel buttons, `confirmed`/`canceled` signals, `register_text_enter`, `add_button`/`add_cancel_button`, `dialog_hide_on_ok`, `dialog_close_on_escape`), file_dialog.cpp (file_mode, access, filters, options API), scene/main/window.cpp (`close_requested`, `about_to_popup`, exclusive/transient, `wrap_controls`)

**Godot classes:** Window, Viewport, SceneTree, ProjectSettings, AcceptDialog, ConfirmationDialog, FileDialog, PopupPanel, Popup

**Patina today:**
- [scene-tree] `SceneTree::resize_root_window` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:411) does the right thing — it republishes state and emits `size_changed` (scene_tree.rs:418) — but has no non-test caller. `grep -rn 'resize_root_window' engine-rs/crates` returns the definition at scene_tree.rs:411 and only engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/root_window_state_reaches_scripts.rs:149,160,194. `MainLoop::step` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2628-3145) never touches the root window; `MainLoop::set_viewport_size` (main_loop.rs:2314) only stores a tuple used for 3D pick rays and does not update `tree.root_window()`. The one production writer is boot-time only: engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs:459-469 sets `window.config = settings.content_scale_config()` and `window.size` once, then calls `publish_root_window_state()`. The editor Play loop (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:13010 `MainLoop::new`, :13228 `main_loop.step(delta)`) never resizes it. No `NOTIFICATION_WM_SIZE_CHANGED` constant exists (see the notification-codes finding).
- [rendering-2d] `apply_stretch_transform` (crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:1283-1290) and `CanvasQuality::from_project_settings` (viewport_2d_render.rs:1407-1429) both exist and are tested, but `grep -rn 'apply_stretch_transform\|CanvasQuality::from_project_settings\|rasterize_render_list_with_quality' crates/ examples/ | grep -v /tests/` shows the only production caller is crates/gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs:195 inside `render_runtime_frame`, and `render_runtime_frame` itself has no non-test caller (`grep -rn 'render_runtime_frame' crates/ examples/` → tests only). The served editor's Play loop (engine-rs/examples/editor.rs:290-345) inlines its own sequence and calls `rasterize_render_list` (the `CanvasQuality::default()` wrapper, viewport_2d_render.rs:1562-1577) with no stretch step — `grep -n 'stretch\|content_scale\|CanvasQuality' engine-rs/examples/editor.rs` returns nothing. Consequence: `display/window/stretch/*` and `rendering/2d/snap/*` / `rendering/anti_aliasing/quality/msaa_2d` from project.godot change nothing in the actual product, and `visibility_layer` never culls because the default cull mask is `u32::MAX` (viewport_2d_render.rs:1379).
- [gui-controls] engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:8544-8580 registers AcceptDialog and ConfirmationDialog with a full property table (title "Alert!", dialog_text, ok_button_text, dialog_autowrap, dialog_close_on_escape, dialog_hide_on_ok, exclusive, keep_title_visible, wrap_controls) — and nothing consumes any of it. Workspace greps return zero non-editor, non-test hits for `popup_centered`, `"confirmed"`, `"canceled"` (the only `canceled` match is engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:4434, an unrelated dictionary key), `close_requested`, `about_to_popup`, `register_text_enter`. FileDialog and PopupPanel have no `ClassRegistration::new(...)` in class_db.rs at all. Neither dialog has a draw arm in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs, engine-rs/examples/editor.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GROUND TRUTH (Godot 4.6.1, upstream/godot/scene/main/window.cpp): when the OS window — on the web export, the canvas — changes size, the root Window receives NOTIFICATION_WM_SIZE_CHANGED, recomputes the content-scale (stretch) transform from `content_scale_size`/`content_scale_mode`/`content_scale_aspect`/`content_scale_stretch`/`content_scale_factor`, updates `Viewport.get_visible_rect()`, re-lays-out anchored Controls, and emits `size_changed`.\n\nPATINA NOW: the machinery exists and is inert. `SceneTree::resize_root_window` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:411) recomputes the scale, republishes the mirrored properties and emits `size_changed` (scene_tree.rs:418) — but `grep -rn 'resize_root_window' engine-rs/crates` shows callers only in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/root_window_state_reaches_scripts.rs. The sole production writer is boot: engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs:459-469. `MainLoop::step` never touches it; `MainLoop::set_viewport_size` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2314) stores a separate tuple used only for 3D pick rays, so the two sizes can disagree. The editor Play loop (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:13010/13228) never resizes either. Net effect: after a browser/editor viewport resize the stretch transform, `get_viewport().get_visible_rect()` and Control anchoring all stay at the boot size, and `size_changed` never fires.\n\nAPPROACH: make `MainLoop::set_viewport_size` the single entry point — have it call `self.tree.resize_root_window(Vector2::new(w, h))` (which already no-ops when the size is unchanged, scene_tree.rs:411-420) in addition to updating the pick-ray tuple. Call `set_viewport_size` from the editor's runtime driver whenever the served game-view canvas size changes (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs `advance_running_main_loop`, near :13210) and from the runner's platform backend resize event in `MainLoop::run_frame` (main_loop.rs:3249). Add NOTIFICATION_WM_SIZE_CHANGED dispatch to the root node inside `resize_root_window`, and re-run the Control layout pass so anchored Controls reflow.\n\nWIRING: a resize delivered on the same path the runtime uses must be observable from a .tscn-attached script: `get_viewport().get_visible_rect().size` changes, `size_changed` fires once, and a `size_flags`-anchored Control's rect follows.

**Merged findings (3):** Root Window resize → content-scale recompute, size_changed signal, NOTIFICATION_WM_SIZE_CHANGED; Root-window content-scale (stretch) and Viewport canvas-quality settings applied to the served Play frame; Dialogs: AcceptDialog / ConfirmationDialog / FileDialog / PopupPanel runtime behavior

**Prove it:** Booting a project whose project.godot sets `window/stretch/mode="canvas_items"`, `window/stretch/aspect="keep"` and a 640×360 base, then delivering a viewport resize to 1280×720 through the runtime path, makes a script's `get_viewport().get_visible_rect().size` still report 640×360, the stretch transform report 2×, `size_changed` fire exactly once, and a full-rect anchored Control's size follow — all without the test calling `resize_root_window` directly. (test: `root_window_resize_reaches_scripts_from_the_frame_loop`)
acceptance_criteria: Booting a project whose project.godot sets `window/stretch/mode="canvas_items"`, `window/stretch/aspect="keep"` and a 640×360 base, then delivering a viewport resize to 1280×720 through the runtime path, makes a script's `get_viewport().get_visible_rect().size` still report 640×360, the stretch transform report 2×, `size_changed` fire exactly once, and a full-rect anchored Control's size follow — all without the test calling `resize_root_window` directly. (test: `root_window_resize_reaches_scripts_from_the_frame_loop`)

title: Timer: expose start/stop/is_stopped to scripts and honor process_callback
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/st-timer-node] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/main/timer.cpp — `start(time_sec = -1)`, `stop()`, `is_stopped()`, `paused`, `time_left`, `autostart`, `one_shot`, `wait_time`, and `process_callback` (TIMER_PROCESS_PHYSICS = 0, TIMER_PROCESS_IDLE = 1, default IDLE) which selects `set_process_internal` vs `set_physics_process_internal`. doc/classes/Timer.xml. | extension_api.json .classes[].signals; upstream/godot/doc/classes/*.xml <signals>. Timer.timeout, Area2D/Area3D 8 each (body_entered/exited, body_shape_entered/exited, area_entered/exited, area_shape_entered/exited), Control 9 (resized/gui_input/mouse_entered/mouse_exited/focus_entered/focus_exited/size_flags_changed/minimum_size_changed/theme_changed), CanvasItem 4 (draw/visibility_changed/hidden/item_rect_changed), RigidBody2D+3D 5 each, SceneTree 9, Window 15, Resource 2 (changed/setup_local_to_scene_requested), HTTPRequest.request_completed, AudioStreamPlayer/2D/3D.finished, GPUParticles2D/3D + CPUParticles2D/3D.finished, VideoStreamPlayer.finished, Node3D.visibility_changed, CanvasLayer.visibility_changed, Sprite2D frame_changed/texture_changed, PopupMenu 4, RichTextLabel 4, Container 2, ScrollContainer 2, SplitContainer 3, AcceptDialog 3, ColorPicker 3, MultiplayerPeer 2, MultiplayerSpawner/Synchronizer 2+3

**Godot classes:** Timer, Area2D, Area3D, Control, CanvasItem, RigidBody2D, RigidBody3D, SceneTree, Window, Resource, HTTPRequest, AudioStreamPlayer, GPUParticles2D, Node3D, PopupMenu, RichTextLabel

**Patina today:**
- [scene-tree] `SceneTree::process_timer_nodes` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:687-752) drives Timers from stashed `__timer_started`/`__timer_running` properties, honoring only `autostart`, `one_shot`, `paused`, `wait_time`, `time_left`. Nothing else writes `__timer_running`: `grep -n '"__timer_running"|"__timer_started"' engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/*.rs engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/*.rs` matches only scene_tree.rs:705,706,719,720,746. `SceneTreeAccessor::call_node_method` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs:1196) has no `"start"`/`"stop"`/`"is_stopped"` arm — `grep -n '            "start"' engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs` → 0 hits; the `"stop"` at scripting.rs:3079 is the Tween handle dispatcher. So `$Timer.start()` on a non-autostart Timer never starts it. `process_callback` is unimplemented: `grep -rn 'process_callback|TIMER_PROCESS' engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src` matches only two unrelated test function names in scripting.rs. `process_timer_nodes` is called from the idle phase only (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:3035) and does not filter by `should_process_node`.
- [registered-class-member-depth] Parsed all 680 `ClassRegistration::new("X")` blocks in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs + editor_plugin_classes.rs and joined against extension_api.json: 125 signals registered vs 366 Godot declares over the same 627 classes; 70 classes register zero while Godot declares ≥1. Registration sites: Timer class_db.rs:8057, Area2D :8021, Area3D :1354, Control :7673, CanvasItem :6065, RigidBody2D :7998, RigidBody3D :1333, SceneTree :3967, Window :8511, Resource :3538, HTTPRequest :11500, AudioStreamPlayer :10115, GPUParticles2D :6453, Node3D :978, CollisionObject2D :7912, CollisionObject3D :1317. This is load-bearing, not cosmetic: `class_has_signal` (class_db.rs:508) gates `Object.has_signal` from GDScript at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs:1641 and :2183, and `get_signal_list` (class_db.rs:496) backs `Object.get_signal_list` (engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:9213) and `ClassDB.class_get_signal_list` (interpreter.rs:14953). So `$Timer.has_signal("timeout")` and `$Area2D.get_signal_list()` answer wrong today.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GROUND TRUTH (Godot 4.6.1, upstream/godot/scene/main/timer.cpp): `Timer.start(time_sec = -1)` restarts the countdown (overriding `wait_time` when a positive value is given), `stop()` halts it and clears `time_left`, `is_stopped()` reports whether it is inactive, and `process_callback` (TIMER_PROCESS_PHYSICS = 0, TIMER_PROCESS_IDLE = 1; default IDLE) decides whether the countdown advances on the idle frame or the physics tick — Godot flips between `set_process_internal` and `set_physics_process_internal`. The node also obeys `process_mode` like any other Node, which is what makes an `ALWAYS` Timer the standard pause-menu clock.\n\nPATINA NOW: `SceneTree::process_timer_nodes` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:687-752) is the whole implementation and reads only `autostart`, `one_shot`, `paused`, `wait_time`, `time_left` via stashed `__timer_started`/`__timer_running` properties. Nothing outside that function ever sets `__timer_running` (`grep -n '\"__timer_running\"' engine-rs/crates` → scene_tree.rs only), and `SceneTreeAccessor::call_node_method` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs:1196) has no Timer arm, so `$Timer.start()` / `$Timer.stop()` / `$Timer.is_stopped()` from GDScript are silent no-ops: a Timer without `autostart = true` can never run. `process_callback` is absent entirely, and the phase is called only from the idle block at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:3035 without a `should_process_node` filter.\n\nAPPROACH: add a Timer arm to `SceneTreeAccessor::call_node_method` in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs that handles `start` (optional `time_sec` > 0 overrides `wait_time` for this run), `stop`, `is_stopped`, and `set_paused`/`is_paused`, writing the same `__timer_running`/`time_left` fields `process_timer_nodes` reads. Read `process_callback` in `process_timer_nodes` and split it into two passes — one invoked from the physics tick loop in `MainLoop::step` (before `process_physics_frame_with_scripts`, main_loop.rs:2903) for PHYSICS timers, one from the idle phase for IDLE timers — and filter both through `SceneTree::should_process_node` (scene_tree.rs:1712).\n\nWIRING: driven from a .tscn through `MainLoop::step` — a script calling `$Timer.start()` in `_ready` must see `timeout` fire after `wait_time` of game time.

**Merged findings (2):** Timer node: start()/stop()/is_stopped() from script, process_callback, process_mode gating; ClassDB signal tables: 70 registered classes declare zero of their Godot signals (125 of 366 registered overall = 34%)

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a non-autostart `Timer` (wait_time 0.5, one_shot) whose parent script calls `$Timer.start()` in `_ready` emits `timeout` once after ~30 frames of 1/60 s; `$Timer.stop()` before then prevents it and `$Timer.is_stopped()` returns true; `$Timer.start(0.25)` fires after ~15 frames. A Timer with `process_callback = 0` (PHYSICS) fires on the physics cadence when `physics_ticks_per_second` is changed to 20. (test: `timer_node_start_stop_and_process_callback`)
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a non-autostart `Timer` (wait_time 0.5, one_shot) whose parent script calls `$Timer.start()` in `_ready` emits `timeout` once after ~30 frames of 1/60 s; `$Timer.stop()` before then prevents it and `$Timer.is_stopped()` returns true; `$Timer.start(0.25)` fires after ~15 frames. A Timer with `process_callback = 0` (PHYSICS) fires on the physics cadence when `physics_ticks_per_second` is changed to 20. (test: `timer_node_start_stop_and_process_callback`)

title: Shaders: bind custom uniform buffers, samplers and TIME on the wgpu spatial pipeline; consume the canvas_item WGSL
description:
[audit-key: shaders/shader-gpu-path] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/servers/rendering/renderer_rd — a ShaderMaterial's uniform set (buffer + textures) is bound per material for both the canvas and scene pipelines | upstream/godot/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/shaders/forward_clustered/scene_forward_lights_inc.glsl — a shader's ALBEDO/ROUGHNESS/METALLIC/NORMAL feed the same Burley + Schlick-GGX light_compute as StandardMaterial3D, with per-light attenuation, spot cone and shadows, and no LDR clamp

**Godot classes:** ShaderMaterial, Shader, RenderingServer, StandardMaterial3D, OmniLight3D, SpotLight3D, DirectionalLight3D

**Patina today:**
- [shaders] 3D: crates/gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs:2243-2247 compiles the material and calls `custom_spatial_module_wgsl`, but the transpiler REFUSES any body touching a uniform, a texture or TIME — crates/gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:1497 `FloatExpr3D::BuiltinTime => return None`, :1498 `FloatExpr3D::Uniform(_) => return None`, :1541 `ColorExpr3D::Uniform(_) => return None`, :1548 `ColorExpr3D::Texture(_,_,_) => return None` — so `custom_module` is None and the draw silently falls back to flat albedo. The pipeline layout confirms it: crates/gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs:948-956 binds only camera/model/light (groups 0-2); there is no group 3, even though crates/gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:649-650 generates a `@group(3) @binding(0) var<uniform> custom: CustomUniforms;` declaration that nothing ever binds. 2D: `grep -rn generate_canvas_item_wgsl --include=*.rs crates/` shows the function (crates/gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:973) is reached only from `ShaderCompiler::compile` (crates/gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:273) and its own unit tests — and `ShaderCompiler` itself has no caller outside crates/gdserver2d/src/lib.rs:45's re-export. The 2D 'GPU' backend is a stated simulation: crates/gdrender2d/src/wgpu_backend.rs:3-7 'Internally it falls back to the software renderer to produce pixel data, simulating what a real wgpu pipeline would output', and the file contains zero occurrences of the word `shader`.
- [shaders] crates/gdrender3d/src/shader.rs:824-858: when the shader is not `unshaded`, the custom path applies a hardcoded `let ambient = 0.15;` (crates/gdrender3d/src/shader.rs:828), then a bare `normal.dot(light_dir).max(0.0)` per light with NO distance attenuation, NO spot cone, and NO shadow term (`light.evaluate` and `compute_shadow_factor` — used by every built-in shader in the same file at crates/gdrender3d/src/shader.rs:543-546 — are not called), and finally clamps every channel to 1.0 at crates/gdrender3d/src/shader.rs:854-856. That clamp contradicts the file's own HDR contract asserted for the built-in shaders (crates/gdrender3d/src/shader.rs:1015-1036 `unlit_emission_is_hdr_unclamped`), so a shader-material surface can never cross the glow HDR threshold. Roughness/metallic written by the shader are not fed back into shading because the instruction set cannot write them (crates/gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:806-820). Emission is special-cased to a parameter literally named `emission` (crates/gdrender3d/src/shader.rs:848).

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/shader.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver2d/src/shader.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/wgpu_backend.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/shader.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: a ShaderMaterial owns a uniform set — a packed uniform buffer for scalar/vector/matrix uniforms plus texture+sampler bindings for every sampler uniform — bound per material in both the canvas and scene render passes, alongside the engine's own frame/instance/light sets. TIME is a frame-global uniform available to every stage.

PATINA STATE: the 3D wgpu path deliberately declines any shader that needs these. crates/gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:1497-1498 and :1541,:1548 return None for TIME, custom uniforms and texture samples, so crates/gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs:2246 `custom_spatial_module_wgsl` yields None and the draw silently reverts to flat `model.albedo`. The pipeline layout at crates/gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs:948-956 has only groups 0-2; the `@group(3)` uniform struct generated by crates/gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:639-668 is never bound. On 2D, crates/gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:973 `generate_canvas_item_wgsl` emits a complete `fragment_main` module but has no production caller — its entry point `ShaderCompiler::compile` (crates/gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:269) is only re-exported (crates/gdserver2d/src/lib.rs:45), and crates/gdrender2d/src/wgpu_backend.rs is a documented software simulation (crates/gdrender2d/src/wgpu_backend.rs:3-7) with no shader handling at all.

APPROACH: (1) In crates/gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs, add a group-3 bind group layout (uniform buffer + N texture/sampler pairs) built from `CompiledShader3D::uniforms`, pack the material's parameter Variants into that buffer with std140-compatible offsets using crates/gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:599 `uniform_type_wgsl_size`, and upload the referenced textures. (2) Add a frame-globals uniform carrying TIME to a stable binding. (3) Remove the four `return None` bail-outs in crates/gdserver3d/src/shader.rs `float_expr_to_wgsl`/`color_expr_to_wgsl`, emitting `custom.<name>`, `textureSample(<name>, <name>_sampler, uv)` and `globals.time` instead, and extend `custom_spatial_module_wgsl` (crates/gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs:1012) to splice the generated declarations into the module. (4) Key the pipeline+bind-group cache on the shader source hash so a per-material pipeline is built once, not per frame. (5) For 2D, make the wgpu backend (crates/gdrender2d/src/wgpu_backend.rs) call `generate_canvas_item_wgsl` and create a real pipeline per material, or — if the 2D GPU path stays a simulation — delete the dead generator so it cannot read as shipped capability.

WIRING REQUIREMENT: the same .tscn must render the same shader-driven pixels on the wgpu path as on the software path (the shader is not allowed to silently fall back to flat albedo).

**Merged findings (2):** GPU (wgpu) consumption of ShaderMaterial: custom uniform buffers, sampler bindings, TIME; canvas_item WGSL pipeline; Lighting integration of a non-`unshaded` spatial ShaderMaterial

**Prove it:** Rendering a .tscn MeshInstance3D whose spatial shader is `uniform vec4 tint : source_color; void fragment() { ALBEDO = tint.rgb * UV.x; }` with `shader_parameter/tint` = red produces a red horizontal gradient on the wgpu path, matching the software path's output within tolerance (today the wgpu path returns flat material albedo); a shader sampling `texture(tex, UV)` with a bound texture returns that texture's texels on the wgpu path. (test: `gpu_shader_uniforms_and_textures_bound`)
acceptance_criteria: Rendering a .tscn MeshInstance3D whose spatial shader is `uniform vec4 tint : source_color; void fragment() { ALBEDO = tint.rgb * UV.x; }` with `shader_parameter/tint` = red produces a red horizontal gradient on the wgpu path, matching the software path's output within tolerance (today the wgpu path returns flat material albedo); a shader sampling `texture(tex, UV)` with a bound texture returns that texture's texels on the wgpu path. (test: `gpu_shader_uniforms_and_textures_bound`)

## Partial completion — bead intentionally left open

Reported by BronzeLake and verified: the delivered scope passed its tests, but the worker flagged the bead as incomplete, so it was returned to the queue instead of closed.

### Remaining scope
DIAGNOSED, NOT FIXED - supersedes all my earlier reports. CONFIRMED with precondition satisfied (rotation guard: silhouette 51 vs 53 px at yaw 0 vs 45deg): gradient -0.235 head-on, -0.297 at 45deg, negative at both and CHANGING with geometry. The software path renders UV.x BACKWARDS; the sign slides with rotation rather than jumping, so NOT a wrong-face artefact and backface culling is very unlikely to be the lever. ELIMINATED with file:line - projection has a POSITIVE X scale (gdserver3d/src/projection.rs); view matrix is a plain t.inverse() (renderer.rs:1620); screen mapping flips only Y (rasterizer.rs:59-60); vertex stage passes uv: input.uv (shader.rs:532); interpolation symmetric and perspective-correct (shader.rs:88); fragment hand-off passes UV through (shader.rs:1083). Geometry: right = -Z x +Y = +X, camera-facing +Z face has u_dir=+X (mesh.rs:747). EVERY STAGE INDIVIDUALLY CORRECT, COMPOSITE WRONG - a convention mismatch BETWEEN stages. THE PROBE IS #[ignore]d ON PURPOSE asserting the CORRECT behaviour - do NOT invert it to green, that pins the defect; REMOVE THE #[ignore] AS THE LAST LINE OF THE FIX. TWO MECHANICAL TRAPS FOUND: (1) #[ignore] on the ONLY test in a target makes it exit 4 'no tests were run' and unverifiable - hence the live companion test; (2) gpu_shader_uniforms_and_textures_bound ALSO exits 4 in the verifier lane because both its tests are GPU-gated and skip when no adapter is present, so it is unusable as a gate there even though it passes when its prebuilt binary is run directly. LOOSE END: at 45deg the silhouette widened only 51->53px where 2->2*sqrt(2) predicts ~72px. FIXTURE NEGATIVES: zero-thickness quads do not rasterize here; a cube is invariant at yaw 0/90/180 - USE AN ASYMMETRIC MESH. The GPU half of the bead already works.

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## Root cause: the software back-face cull was inverted (EmeraldIsland, 2026-08-20)

### The bead's own APPROACH was already built — do not re-do it

The four `return None` bail-outs this description names in `gdserver3d/src/shader.rs`
(TIME, uniforms, texture samples) no longer exist. `@group(3)`, `custom_uniform_fields`
("THE ONE ORDERING AUTHORITY"), the packed uniform buffer and the sampler bindings are
all present in `wgpu_pipeline.rs`. Of the acceptance's two tests,
`gpu_bound_sampler_returns_the_textures_texels` already PASSED.

### The real failure was the acceptance's own software reference

```
the software reference itself has no gradient (-0.235) — the fixture is wrong,
not the GPU path
```

The GPU assertions passed. The software path produced the same magnitude with the
opposite SIGN.

### `should_cull` read screen winding as if Y grew upward

`clip_to_screen` maps `y = (1 - ndc_y) * 0.5 * height`, so screen Y grows DOWNWARD
and handedness flips. A front face — counter-clockwise in NDC, the
OpenGL/Godot/wgpu `FrontFace::Ccw` convention — is CLOCKWISE on screen, so its
`signed_area` is NEGATIVE. `should_cull` had `Back => area <= 0.0`, so Godot's
DEFAULT cull mode culled every camera-facing face and let the far side of the mesh
draw instead.

Numerically, for `Mesh3D::cube(2.0)` at z = -4 with the default 64x64 viewport:

| face | screen signed area | old `Back` | fixed `Back` |
|------|-------------------|------------|--------------|
| +Z (near, `u_dir = +X`) | **-2652** | CULLED | kept |
| -Z (far, `u_dir = -X`)  | **+954**  | drawn  | culled |

The far -Z face carries `u_dir = -X` (`mesh.rs`), so its UV.x runs toward screen
LEFT — exactly the mirrored gradient the test measured.

### Why it survived this long

On a closed convex opaque mesh the wrong choice is nearly invisible: the silhouette
is identical, and only the shading normal and the UV direction change. It surfaces
only when something reads DIRECTION off the surface, which is what a `UV.x` shader
does. The wgpu path never had the bug (`FrontFace::Ccw` + `Face::Back`), so the two
backends silently disagreed about which side of a mesh you were looking at.

### Why the existing unit tests were green

`render_modes`' own `ccw()`/`cw()` helpers were authored in ordinary y-UP math
coordinates. They are self-consistent, so they pass under EITHER polarity — the
defect lived in the composition with `clip_to_screen`, which nothing tested.
Renamed to `screen_front()`/`screen_back()` and flipped, plus a new
`cull_matches_screen_space_winding.rs` that pins the SEAM by running real vertices
through `clip_to_screen` before asking `should_cull`.

### Things that are NOT bugs (verified, do not chase)

1. **UV evaluation** — `FloatExpr3D::UvComponent(X) => ctx.uv.0` (software) and
   `"in.uv.x"` (WGSL) are the same passthrough.
2. **Screen X orientation** — green test `skinning_render` pins world +X to screen
   right.
3. **Depth test** — `DepthBuffer::test_and_set` is nearer-wins from `f32::MAX`, and
   `depth` is OpenGL NDC z, monotonic with distance.
4. **Directional light convention** — BOTH backends negate `Light3D.direction`
   before shading (`renderer.rs:825` and `wgpu_pipeline.rs:1783`), so they agree;
   `direction` is the travel direction and `l = -direction`.

### Blast radius

`should_cull` has exactly ONE production caller (`renderer.rs:1180`). Silhouettes are
unchanged, but shading generally gets BRIGHTER (the drawn face's normal now faces the
camera) and textured surfaces stop being mirrored, so 3D tests asserting exact pixel
colours may need re-baselining. `gdeditor`'s `material_transparency_modes_render`
asserts only that Front and Back DIFFER within a backend, so it survives — and now
passes for the right reason in software.

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## Second defect: `texture(tex, UV).rgb` parses to a WHITE albedo passthrough

Follow-up to the cull diagnosis above (EmeraldIsland, 2026-08-20). Found by the
verifier run that reopened this bead — 236/237 passed, the one failure being
`custom_shader_sampler_binding_reaches_the_shader::a_bound_sampler_texture_is_sampled`
(expected `(0.2, 0.4, 0.6)`, got `(1.0, 1.0, 1.0)`).

### It was NOT a regression from the cull fix

That test's `shade()` helper calls `CustomFragmentShader::process` **directly** —
no rasterizer, no `clip_to_screen`, no `should_cull` anywhere on the path. The file
also predates the cull change (committed in `87f632f`) and had no binary in
`target-verifier`, so its failure had simply never been observed here.

### Root cause

The test's shader is `ALBEDO = texture(tex, UV).rgb`. Every branch of
`parse_color_expr_3d` is anchored on the WHOLE string:

- `strip_func_call_3d` requires `s.ends_with(')')` — `...rgb` does not;
- the bare-identifier branch requires every char be alphanumeric or `_` — `(`, `,`
  and `.` all fail it.

So the swizzled form matched nothing and fell through to the `BuiltinAlbedo`
catch-all, a silent passthrough of the material albedo. With `uniforms.albedo`
white, a correctly bound texture rendered as flat WHITE — **indistinguishable from
an unbound sampler hitting the placeholder**, which is why it reads as a binding
bug and is not one.

⚠️ `from_material` was already correct: it does `textures: Arc::new(material.textures.clone())`
with a pat-s3rrv.122 comment. The producer half is DONE. The parser was dropping
the expression on the floor.

### Fix

`strip_color_swizzle_3d` drops a trailing `.rgb` / `.rgba` before parsing, so the
swizzled form yields the identical `ColorExpr3D::Texture` node. `ColorExpr3D`
already carries RGBA, and ALPHA is a separate builtin that an ALBEDO write does not
touch, so the swizzle is dropped rather than modelled. Godot accepts both spellings,
so this is parity, not a workaround — and normalising to one AST node means both
backends get it.

Guard against inventing a node from nothing: a bare `.rgb` (empty base) is left
unchanged.

### Note for whoever writes the next fixture

Two sibling tests in this bead deliberately AVOID the swizzle and say so in their
comments ("the GDSL front end does not yet accept a swizzle ... `parse_texture_uv`
pins this form"). That is no longer true for `.rgb`/`.rgba` on a colour expression.
It IS still true for float swizzles like `tint.rgb * UV.x` inside arithmetic, which
this change does not address.

title: EditorInterface: dispatch the editor API surface @tool scripts and plugins need (currently 1 of 70 methods)
description:
[audit-key: singleton-dispatch-table/editor-interface-singleton] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

> **UNVERIFIED** — this finding's adversarial verify pass did not run (session limit during the audit). Confirm the evidence below before implementing. Capped at P1 for that reason.

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/register_editor_types.cpp:304-306 (registered with editor_only = true); extension_api.json EditorInterface = 70 methods (get_selection, get_editor_settings, get_editor_paths, get_command_palette, get_resource_filesystem, get_editor_main_screen, get_base_control, get_editor_theme, get_script_editor, get_edited_scene_root, get_open_scenes, open_scene_from_path, reload_scene_from_path, save_scene, save_scene_as, save_all_scenes, mark_scene_as_unsaved, edit_resource, edit_node, edit_script, inspect_object, select_file, get_selected_paths, get_current_directory, get_current_path, set_main_screen_editor, play_main_scene, play_current_scene, play_custom_scene, stop_playing_scene, is_playing_scene, set_movie_maker_enabled, popup_dialog(_centered/_ratio/_clamped), make_mesh_previews, restart_editor, get_editor_viewport_2d/3d, ...)

**Godot classes:** EditorInterface, EditorSelection, EditorSettings, EditorPaths, ScriptEditor, EditorFileSystem

**Patina today:**
- [singleton-dispatch-table] engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:2989 has the `Expr::Ident(n) if n == "EditorInterface"` arm, but `call_editor_interface_static` has exactly ONE match arm — `"get_resource_filesystem"` — and every other member returns `UndefinedFunction("EditorInterface.{other}")`. The follow-on `call_editor_fs_instance` covers 8 EditorFileSystem members, several of which are hard-coded no-ops (`is_scanning` -> false, `get_scanning_progress` -> 1.0, `"scan" | "scan_sources" | "update_file" | "reimport_files" => Ok(Variant::Nil)`). EditorInterface is also absent from `BUILTIN_SINGLETONS` (interpreter.rs:14464-14482), so `Engine.has_singleton("EditorInterface")` is false even in the editor, and Patina has no `editor_only` concept to filter it out at runtime the way Godot does (engine.cpp:385-395 + register_editor_types.cpp:305).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: editor/register_editor_types.cpp:304-306 registers `EditorInterface` as an editor_only singleton with 70 methods. It is the entire entry point for `@tool` scripts and `EditorPlugin`s: scene access (`get_edited_scene_root`, `get_open_scenes`, `open_scene_from_path`, `reload_scene_from_path`, `save_scene`, `save_scene_as`, `save_all_scenes`, `mark_scene_as_unsaved`), selection and inspection (`get_selection`, `edit_node`, `edit_resource`, `edit_script`, `inspect_object`), settings and chrome (`get_editor_settings`, `get_editor_paths`, `get_command_palette`, `get_base_control`, `get_editor_theme`, `get_script_editor`, `get_editor_main_screen`, `set_main_screen_editor`), the filesystem dock (`get_resource_filesystem`, `select_file`, `get_selected_paths`, `get_current_directory`, `get_current_path`), and the run bar (`play_main_scene`, `play_current_scene`, `play_custom_scene`, `stop_playing_scene`, `is_playing_scene`, `set_movie_maker_enabled`).

PATINA CURRENT STATE: the arm exists at `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:2989` but `call_editor_interface_static` has a single match arm, `"get_resource_filesystem"`; every other member falls to `UndefinedFunction("EditorInterface.{other}")`. The EditorFileSystem handle it returns is itself partly inert: `call_editor_fs_instance` answers `is_scanning` -> false, `get_scanning_progress` -> 1.0 and makes `scan | scan_sources | update_file | reimport_files` no-ops returning Nil. `EditorInterface` is also missing from `BUILTIN_SINGLETONS` (interpreter.rs:14464-14482), so `Engine.has_singleton("EditorInterface")` is false even inside the editor, and there is no `editor_only` flag to hide it at runtime the way Godot does (core/config/engine.cpp:385-395).

IMPLEMENTATION: expand `call_editor_interface_static` in `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` into an inherent `&mut self` method (it needs the edited SceneTree and the editor server's state) and back each group against what already exists in `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/`: route `get_edited_scene_root`/`get_open_scenes`/`open_scene_from_path`/`save_scene*`/`mark_scene_as_unsaved` through the editor server's scene-tab state; `get_selection` through the scene-tree dock's selection (returning an EditorSelection handle with `get_selected_nodes`/`add_node`/`clear` and the `selection_changed` signal); `edit_node`/`edit_resource`/`inspect_object` through engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/inspector.rs; `get_editor_settings` through the editor settings store; `get_editor_paths` through the existing `call_editor_paths_static` (and remove the bare `EditorPaths` global, which Godot does not have); `get_command_palette` through the existing `call_editor_command_palette_static`; the play-bar quartet through the editor server's Play route. Give the EditorFileSystem handle a real `scan`/`update_file`/`reimport_files` that actually re-walk engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/filesystem.rs and fire `filesystem_changed`/`resources_reimported`. Add "EditorInterface" to `BUILTIN_SINGLETONS` with the editor_only flag introduced by the singleton-registry work.

WIRING REQUIREMENT: a `@tool` script running inside the served editor must be able to open a scene, read `get_edited_scene_root()`, mutate it, `save_scene()`, and have the change land in the .tscn on disk that the editor then re-serves.

**Prove it:** With `Engine.is_editor_hint()` true, a @tool script can: `EditorInterface.open_scene_from_path(p)` then `get_edited_scene_root()` returns the root node of that scene and `get_open_scenes()` contains p; adding a child and calling `EditorInterface.save_scene()` writes the new node into the .tscn on disk (re-parsed and asserted); `EditorInterface.get_selection().get_selected_nodes()` reflects a selection made through the editor server route; `EditorInterface.get_editor_settings().get_setting(k)` round-trips a value set via `set_setting`; `EditorInterface.get_resource_filesystem().scan()` picks up a file created after load and `get_filesystem_path(dir)` finds it. `Engine.has_singleton("EditorInterface")` is true in the editor and the name is absent from `Engine.get_singleton_list()` when `is_editor_hint()` is false. (test: `editor_interface_singleton_surface` at engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/editor_interface_singleton_surface.rs, runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdeditor --test editor_interface_singleton_surface`)
acceptance_criteria: With `Engine.is_editor_hint()` true, a @tool script can: `EditorInterface.open_scene_from_path(p)` then `get_edited_scene_root()` returns the root node of that scene and `get_open_scenes()` contains p; adding a child and calling `EditorInterface.save_scene()` writes the new node into the .tscn on disk (re-parsed and asserted); `EditorInterface.get_selection().get_selected_nodes()` reflects a selection made through the editor server route; `EditorInterface.get_editor_settings().get_setting(k)` round-trips a value set via `set_setting`; `EditorInterface.get_resource_filesystem().scan()` picks up a file created after load and `get_filesystem_path(dir)` finds it. `Engine.has_singleton("EditorInterface")` is true in the editor and the name is absent from `Engine.get_singleton_list()` when `is_editor_hint()` is false. (test: `editor_interface_singleton_surface` at engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/editor_interface_singleton_surface.rs, runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdeditor --test editor_interface_singleton_surface`)

title: Engine: answer has_singleton/get_singleton/get_singleton_list from the real Godot 4.6.1 singleton set
description:
[audit-key: singleton-dispatch-table/engine-singleton-registry] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/config/engine.cpp:326-395 (add_singleton/get_singleton_object/has_singleton/get_singletons/is_singleton_user_created/is_singleton_editor_only), upstream/godot/core/core_bind.cpp:1980-2012; the real set is core/register_core_types.cpp:357-382 (18 core) + servers/register_server_types.cpp:152,265,279,306,320,384-402 (15 servers) + scene/register_scene_types.cpp:1486 (ThemeDB) + editor/register_editor_types.cpp:304-306 (EditorInterface, editor_only=true) + platform/android (JavaClassWrapper) = 39 in extension_api.json | extension_api.json classes[Engine].methods — get_author_info, get_copyright_info, get_donor_info, get_license_info, get_license_text, get_architecture_name, get_main_loop, is_embedded_in_editor, get_physics_interpolation_fraction, get_write_movie_path, set_print_to_stdout/is_printing_to_stdout, set_print_error_messages/is_printing_error_messages, register_script_language/unregister_script_language/get_script_language_count/get_script_language | upstream/godot/core/config/engine.cpp, servers/display_server.cpp, core/debugger/engine_debugger.cpp; extension_api.json: Engine <- Object (41 methods, 7 properties), DisplayServer <- Object (269 methods, not instantiable), EngineDebugger <- Object (23 methods). All three are entries in `.singletons`.

**Godot classes:** Engine, DisplayServer, EngineDebugger

Add the editor_only flag for EditorInterface and filter it out of `get_singleton_list` when `ENGINE_EDITOR_HINT` is false. Make `get_singleton(name)` return a singleton handle Variant for built-ins (reuse the ObjectId-handle-tag pattern already used for EditorFileSystem at interpreter.rs `EDITOR_FS_HANDLE_TAG`) so `Engine.get_singleton("OS").get_name()` dispatches to `call_os_static`. Add Godot's register/unregister guards (duplicate name, invalid identifier, non-user-created removal) returning the same push_error text. Remove the bare `EditorPaths` global and route it through `EditorInterface.get_editor_paths()`.

WIRING REQUIREMENT: the assertions must run through a script executing in a loaded scene under the runner's interpreter, not against the constant slice.

A compile-time or unit assertion pins the singleton table against the dispatch arms so the two cannot drift again. These need real algorithms (Clipper-style boolean core, ear clipping, Delaunay, monotone chain, Minkowski offsets), not wiring. Geometry3D: 10 of 15 absent — build_box/cylinder/capsule_planes, clip_polygon, compute_convex_mesh_points, get_triangle_barycentric_coords, segment_intersects_convex, segment_intersects_cylinder, tetrahedralize_delaunay; plus segment_intersects_sphere, which EXISTS in gdcore but is deliberately undispatched until it returns [point, normal] like Godot. Class-scoped enums Geometry2D.OPERATION_*/JOIN_*/END_* are still absent from global_constants.rs and try_static_member. No ClassDB registration for either name. The named acceptance test crates/gdscript-interop/tests/geometry_singletons_script_reachable.rs does NOT exist and was deliberately not created: it would be a red gate, since it requires merge_polygons/convex_hull/triangulate_polygon/offset_polygon and a scene-loaded script writing results back onto node properties. NOTE for whoever takes this: build_arc is not a Godot method at all, so the existing misc_suite_c 'parity' test is not a parity oracle.

title: ThemeDB: make the singleton real — dispatch it, own the runtime default/project theme, add the fallback chain
description:
[audit-key: singleton-dispatch-table/themedb-singleton] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: STUB]

> **UNVERIFIED** — this finding's adversarial verify pass did not run (session limit during the audit). Confirm the evidence below before implementing. Capped at P1 for that reason.

**Patina today:**
- [singleton-dispatch-table] NAME-ONLY REGISTRATION: engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:8073-8075 `if !class_exists("ThemeDB") { register_class(ClassRegistration::new("ThemeDB").parent("Object")); }` — no methods, no properties. GREEN TEST THAT ONLY PROBES THE NAME: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/control_theme_override_resolution.rs:87-88 asserts `gdobject::class_db::class_exists("ThemeDB")`. NO SCRIPT DISPATCH: `rg -c '"ThemeDB"' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` -> 0; absent from `BUILTIN_SINGLETONS` (interpreter.rs:14464-14482), so `ThemeDB.get_default_theme()` dies with UndefinedVariable at interpreter.rs:2764. REAL STRUCT, NEVER INSTANTIATED AT RUNTIME: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/theme.rs:653 `pub struct ThemeDB { default_theme: Theme }` with `new()`, `default_theme()`, `default_theme_mut()`, `set_default_theme()`, exported at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/lib.rs:118 — but `grep -rn 'ThemeDB::new|ThemeDB::default' engine-rs/crates/ --include='*.rs' | grep -v 'src/theme.rs'` returns only engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/ui_parity_test.rs:140,157. Control theme resolution (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs:3147, control_render.rs:1028) refers to it only in comments. NO FALLBACK API AT ALL: none of fallback_base_scale / fallback_font / fallback_font_size / fallback_icon / fallback_stylebox exists on the struct, and there is no get_project_theme.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/theme.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/control_theme_override_resolution.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: scene/register_scene_types.cpp:1486 registers `ThemeDB` as the singleton that owns the generated default theme and the project theme, plus the last-resort fallbacks every Control falls back to when neither its own theme nor any ancestor's supplies an item: `get_default_theme()`, `get_project_theme()`, `set/get_fallback_base_scale`, `set/get_fallback_font`, `set/get_fallback_font_size`, `set/get_fallback_icon`, `set/get_fallback_stylebox` (12 methods). A @tool script or a game that restyles UI at runtime goes through this object.

PATINA CURRENT STATE: this is registration theatre. `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:8073-8075` registers the bare name `ThemeDB` with parent `Object` and zero methods/properties, and `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/control_theme_override_resolution.rs:87-88` pins that with a green assertion on `class_exists("ThemeDB")` — which is why this reads as done. No script can touch it: zero `"ThemeDB"` in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs and it is absent from `BUILTIN_SINGLETONS` (interpreter.rs:14464-14482), so `ThemeDB.get_default_theme()` fails with UndefinedVariable at interpreter.rs:2764. A real `ThemeDB` struct does exist at `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/theme.rs:653` (holding a `Theme::default_theme()` built at theme.rs:440) and is re-exported at gdscene/src/lib.rs:118 — but `grep -rn 'ThemeDB::new|ThemeDB::default' engine-rs/crates/ | grep -v src/theme.rs` finds it only in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/ui_parity_test.rs:140,157. The runtime never constructs one; Control's theme-resolution chain (control.rs:3147, control_render.rs:1028) only mentions it in comments. None of the five fallback pairs and no `get_project_theme` exist.

IMPLEMENTATION: (a) make the SceneTree/MainLoop own one `ThemeDB` (a field beside `audio_bridge` in `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:448-451`, or a process-global mirroring `gdcore::performance::global()`), constructed at startup and loaded with the project theme named by `gui/theme/custom` in project.godot; (b) extend `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/theme.rs` with `project_theme`, `fallback_base_scale`, `fallback_font`, `fallback_font_size`, `fallback_icon`, `fallback_stylebox` and their getters/setters; (c) make Control's item lookup in `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs:3147` actually terminate at that ThemeDB instance (own overrides -> own theme -> ancestor themes -> project theme -> default theme -> fallback_*), so a `ThemeDB.set_fallback_font_size(...)` from a script visibly changes what `control_render.rs` draws; (d) add `call_themedb_static` plus an `Expr::Ident(n) if n == "ThemeDB"` arm in `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` next to the Marshalls/TranslationServer arms, returning Theme handles the existing Resource/ObjectId handle machinery can carry; (e) add "ThemeDB" to `BUILTIN_SINGLETONS` and give the ClassDB entry its 12 methods.

WIRING REQUIREMENT: `.tscn with a Label/Button -> script calls ThemeDB.get_default_theme().set_color(...) or ThemeDB.set_fallback_font_size(N) -> the next control draw uses the new value`. A test that only asserts `class_exists` must not be able to pass for this bead.

**Prove it:** A scene containing a Label and a Button is loaded and stepped; a script calls `ThemeDB.get_default_theme()` and receives a non-null Theme whose `get_color("font_color", "Label")` matches the engine default, then mutates it (or calls `ThemeDB.set_fallback_font_size(31)`) and the very next draw of the Label reports the new value through the control draw-item inspection the existing gdscene control-render tests use. `ThemeDB.get_project_theme()` returns the theme named by the project's `gui/theme/custom` setting when one is set and null when not. `Engine.has_singleton("ThemeDB")` is true and `ClassDB.class_get_method_list("ThemeDB")` lists all 12 Godot methods. title: Fonts: consume LabelSettings/FontVariation/SystemFont from scenes and apply them in the Label draw path
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/font-resources-wiring] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/LabelSettings.xml; doc/classes/FontVariation.xml; doc/classes/SystemFont.xml; scene/resources/font.cpp FontVariation::_update_base_font (embolden/transform/spacing/variation coords); scene/gui/label.cpp Label::_draw uses settings->get_font()/outline_size/shadow

**Godot classes:** LabelSettings, FontVariation, SystemFont, Label

**Patina today:**
- [theming-text] engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/label_settings.rs:1-12 states outright: "Registering the classes, parsing them from `.tres`, and applying them in the `Label` draw path are wired elsewhere." They are not. grep `LabelSettings|FontVariation|SystemFont` over engine-rs/crates returns only: the defining module, the re-export engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/lib.rs:35, the ClassDB name/property tables (engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:5816,5837,5876), and tests (gdeditor/tests/fontfile_end_to_end.rs, gdresource/tests/tscn_value_parser_fidelity.rs). The Label draw arm (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs:1156-1175) reads only `text`, `theme_override_colors/font_color` and the theme font size — grep `label_settings|outline_size|shadow_offset` over engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs, control.rs and engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs returns nothing, so `label_settings`, outline and shadow never draw. `advance_with_spacing`, `resolve_family` and `variation_coords` (label_settings.rs:143,225,153) have no callers outside the module's own tests.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/label_settings.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/ttf_font.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: a Label with a `label_settings` LabelSettings resource takes its font, font_size, font_color, outline_size/outline_color, shadow_size/shadow_color/shadow_offset, line_spacing and paragraph_spacing from that resource instead of the theme (scene/gui/label.cpp). FontVariation wraps a base font with OpenType variation coords, `variation_embolden`, `variation_transform`, `variation_face_index` and the four TextServer.SpacingType values (scene/resources/font.cpp). SystemFont resolves an OS family by name with weight/stretch/italic matching.\n\nPATINA: the resource data models exist and are tested but nothing consumes them. engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/label_settings.rs:1-12 says so in its own module doc. grep across engine-rs/crates finds these type names only in the defining module, the lib.rs:35 re-export, ClassDB property tables (engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:5816/5837/5876) and tests. The Label arm at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs:1156-1175 never reads `label_settings`, and no outline or shadow draw commands exist anywhere in the Control path.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION: (1) teach the .tscn/.tres resolution path (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs:604-613 `font_override_path` and its sub_resource/ExtResource lookup) to materialize LabelSettings/FontVariation/SystemFont into the structs in engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/label_settings.rs; (2) in the Label/Button arms of control_render.rs, prefer LabelSettings values over theme values, and emit outline + shadow text draw items (new `ControlDrawItem::Text` fields or paired items) ahead of the fill; (3) implement outline/shadow rasterization in engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/ttf_font.rs (dilate coverage by outline_size, offset copy for shadow) and consume it in engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs + engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs; (4) apply FontVariation `advance_with_spacing`, embolden and variation coords when measuring and rasterizing.\n\nWIRING: .tscn Label with `label_settings = SubResource("LabelSettings_x")` (font_size 32, outline_size 3, red outline) → control_draw_items → an outline draw item plus a fill item at 32px, both in the editor viewport and Play render.

**Prove it:** A scene-loaded Label with a LabelSettings sub-resource (font_size 32, font_color blue, outline_size 3, outline_color red, shadow_color opaque black at offset (2,2)) emits three text draw items (shadow, outline, fill) with the settings' colors and a 32px size, overriding the theme's Label/font_size; a Label whose font is a FontVariation with spacing_glyph = 4 measures 4px wider per glyph than the same text with the base font; a SystemFont with font_names = ["NoSuchFace","<builtin family>"] resolves to the builtin family.
