title: Variant codec: add Rect2i/Vector4/Vector4i/Projection/RID/Callable/Signal/PackedVector4Array to the binary encoder and fail loudly in RPC
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/variant-binary-codec-missing-types] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/io/marshalls.cpp encode_variant/decode_variant covering Variant::Type 0..38; scene_rpc_interface.cpp:288 MultiplayerAPI::decode_and_decompress_variants. Godot type ids: RECT2I=8, VECTOR4=12, VECTOR4I=13, PROJECTION=19, RID=23, CALLABLE=25, SIGNAL=26, PACKED_VECTOR4_ARRAY=38.

**Godot classes:** Marshalls, MultiplayerAPI

**Patina today:**
- [multiplayer] crates/gdvariant/src/binary.rs declares type constants at lines 84-116 and the sequence skips 8, 12, 13, 19, 23, 25, 26 and stops at 37: `grep -n 'T_RECT2I|T_VECTOR4|T_PROJECTION|T_RID|T_CALLABLE|T_SIGNAL|T_PACKED_VECTOR4' crates/gdvariant/src/binary.rs` returns ZERO matches, while T_PACKED_VECTOR2_ARRAY=35 / T_PACKED_VECTOR3_ARRAY=36 / T_PACKED_COLOR_ARRAY=37 are present (binary.rs:114-116). The RPC consequence is silent corruption: `encode_rpc_tail` at crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs:1010-1027 writes `argc` first and then does `if let Ok(bytes) = gdvariant::binary::encode_variant(a) { out.extend_from_slice(&bytes); }` (line 1021) — an unencodable arg is SKIPPED while argc still counts it, so `rpc("m", Vector4(...))` produces a packet whose declared arg count does not match its payload and the decoder (network.rs:1122-1128) reads the wrong bytes or bails.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/binary.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: upstream/godot/core/io/marshalls.cpp encode_variant/decode_variant covers every Variant::Type 0..38. The multiplayer RPC wire, `var_to_bytes`, `Marshalls.variant_to_base64`, and binary .scn all share it. RPC argument decoding goes through `MultiplayerAPI::decode_and_decompress_variants` (scene_rpc_interface.cpp:288) and a malformed packet fails the call rather than running the method with wrong values.\n\nPATINA CURRENT STATE: crates/gdvariant/src/binary.rs implements 31 of the 39 type ids. The const table at binary.rs:84-116 jumps 7→9 (no RECT2I=8), 11→14 (no VECTOR4=12, VECTOR4I=13), 18→20 (no PROJECTION=19), 22→24 (no RID=23), 24→27 (no CALLABLE=25, SIGNAL=26), and stops at T_PACKED_COLOR_ARRAY=37 (no PACKED_VECTOR4_ARRAY=38). `grep -n 'T_RECT2I|T_VECTOR4|T_PROJECTION|T_RID|T_CALLABLE|T_SIGNAL|T_PACKED_VECTOR4' crates/gdvariant/src/binary.rs` = 0 matches. Worse, the RPC tail encoder silently swallows the failure: crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs:1010-1027 writes `argc` and then, at line 1021, only appends the arg `if let Ok(bytes) = encode_variant(a)`. An unencodable arg therefore vanishes from the payload while still being counted, so the receiver's decode loop (network.rs:1122-1128) misreads subsequent args or drops the call — a wrong-value dispatch is possible.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION: (a) add T_RECT2I=8, T_VECTOR4=12, T_VECTOR4I=13, T_PROJECTION=19, T_RID=23, T_CALLABLE=25, T_SIGNAL=26, T_PACKED_VECTOR4_ARRAY=38 to the const table (binary.rs:84-116) and both the encode match (around binary.rs:420-437) and the decode match (around binary.rs:850-871), following marshalls.cpp layouts exactly (Rect2i = 4×i32; Vector4/Vector4i = 4 components; Projection = 16 floats; RID = u64; Callable/Signal encode as object id + StringName per Godot's rules). (b) change `encode_rpc_tail` (network.rs:1010-1027) to return a Result and propagate the encoding error, so `rpc()` fails with an error instead of emitting a packet whose argc lies. Cross-check with the core-variant / resources-io findings so this codec is fixed once.\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: an RPC carrying each of the eight types must round-trip through a real peer pair and arrive at the receiving script as the same Variant.

**Prove it:** `encode_variant`/`decode_variant` round-trip Rect2i, Vector4, Vector4i, Projection, RID, Callable, Signal and PackedVector4Array with byte layouts matching upstream marshalls.cpp. Over a live peer pair stepped through MainLoop, `rpc("take", Vector4(1,2,3,4), Rect2i(...), PackedVector4Array([...]))` delivers all three args as the same Variants to the receiving script, and an intentionally unencodable arg makes `rpc()` return an error rather than sending a packet with a mismatched argc. (test: `rpc_args_round_trip_every_variant_type`)
acceptance_criteria: `encode_variant`/`decode_variant` round-trip Rect2i, Vector4, Vector4i, Projection, RID, Callable, Signal and PackedVector4Array with byte layouts matching upstream marshalls.cpp. Over a live peer pair stepped through MainLoop, `rpc("take", Vector4(1,2,3,4), Rect2i(...), PackedVector4Array([...]))` delivers all three args as the same Variants to the receiving script, and an intentionally unencodable arg makes `rpc()` return an error rather than sending a packet with a mismatched argc. (test: `rpc_args_round_trip_every_variant_type`)

## EmeraldIsland — parked; the second failure was a gate that was already red, not my code

Not resubmitting: the bead is parked for operator triage. The tree is left clean, and the two failures were different in kind.

### Failure 1 — mine, fixed

Four `E0107`s. `network.rs:52` defines `pub type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, NetworkError>;` — **one** generic parameter — and I wrote `-> Result<Vec<u8>, NetworkError>` in all four signatures I changed. Corrected to the file's own form. I had checked `NetworkError`'s derives, its match sites and every call site, but not how the file spells its own return type, thirty lines above the code I was editing.

### Failure 2 — NOT mine, and a gate I should never have listed

    binary::tests::decode_unsupported_type_id_errors
    called `Result::unwrap_err()` on an `Ok` value: (PackedVector4Array([]), 8)

That test asserts `PACKED_VECTOR4_ARRAY(38)` is unsupported. The const, the encode arm and the decode arm for 38 all exist — so it decodes, and the assertion is stale. **My change never touched type 38** (`git diff` on that file has no reference to it), so this test was failing before I started.

The error is that I listed `-p gdvariant --lib` as a regression gate without checking it was green. I reasoned only about **blast radius** — I had edited a contract test in that crate, so the gate seemed justified — and never asked the separate question of whether it currently passes. Those are two different checks and I ran one.

**Corrected in the tree**, since it is a stale assertion in a file I hold and it blocks the crate's lib tests for everyone: `decode_unsupported_type_id_errors` now asserts that 38 decodes to an empty `PackedVector4Array` consuming 8 bytes, which is what the codec actually promises. The comment records the contract change, as its encode-side sibling already did for two earlier ones.

### The duty this exposed, for whoever extends this codec

`encode_unsupported_variant_types_error` and `decode_unsupported_type_id_errors` assert in **opposite directions**, and adding a type obliges you to update both. Whoever added type 38 updated neither. I found the encode-side one by grepping `VariantType::Callable`; I missed the decode-side one because it keys on a **numeric id**, not a type name. Grep the id as well as the name.

### State of the work

All four files are in the tree with both fixes applied. The substance is unchanged from my reports:

- `Callable` (25) and `Signal` (26) added to the codec — the only two of the bead's eight types that were genuinely absent; the other six already had constants, encode arms and decode arms.
- `encode_rpc_tail` no longer writes an `argc` that counts an argument it then skips; it returns `NetworkError::UnencodableArgument { index, source }`.
- ⚠️ A `Callable` encodes as its header alone and decodes back empty, per `marshalls.cpp:1817-1818` / `:788-790`. It deliberately does not round-trip to itself; a test pins that, because making it an encode error would reintroduce the argc bug.

  binary — which is ALSO from 21:28, so it is listed for a real run rather than
  presented as a current verdict.

### Both contract tests now agree with the codec

`encode_unsupported_variant_types_error` claims only `Resource` is unsupported,
matching the encoder's final arm; the decode-side test no longer claims 38.

⚠️ Standing hazard for the next person to extend this codec: the two tests assert
in OPPOSITE directions, and the decode-side one keys on a NUMERIC ID rather than a
type name. Grepping `VariantType::Callable` finds the encode-side test and misses
the decode-side one entirely. **Grep the id as well as the name.**

### The mistake that caused the park, stated plainly

"My change's blast radius touches this crate, so this gate is justified" and "this
gate currently passes" are two different checks. I ran the first and listed the
gate on the strength of it.

title: SceneMultiplayer: complete the script surface (auth callback, relay, root_path, packet caps) and bind multiplayer.<signal>.connect
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/multiplayer-scenemultiplayer-surface] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json SceneMultiplayer methods (set_root_path/get_root_path/clear/disconnect_peer/get_authenticating_peers/send_auth/complete_auth/set_auth_callback/get_auth_callback/set_auth_timeout/set_allow_object_decoding/set_server_relay_enabled/send_bytes/get_max_sync_packet_size/set_max_sync_packet_size/get_max_delta_packet_size/set_max_delta_packet_size) and MultiplayerAPI methods (object_configuration_add/remove, get_multiplayer_peer, set_default_interface/create_default_interface) + signals peer_connected/peer_disconnected/connected_to_server/connection_failed/server_disconnected on the API object; upstream/godot/modules/multiplayer/scene_multiplayer.cpp.

**Godot classes:** SceneMultiplayer, MultiplayerAPI

**Patina today:**
- [multiplayer] ClassDB advertises a surface the runtime cannot serve. crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:11618-11645 registers SceneMultiplayer with methods send_bytes, set_auth_callback, get_auth_callback, send_auth, complete_auth, get_authenticating_peers, disconnect_peer, clear and properties server_relay, allow_object_decoding, auth_timeout — but `call_multiplayer_method` (crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:7266-7370) implements only 10 methods and returns `UndefinedFunction("multiplayer.{other}")` at line 7369 for set_auth_callback / get_auth_callback / send_auth / disconnect_peer / clear / set_root_path / get_root_path / set_allow_object_decoding / set_server_relay_enabled / the packet-size accessors / object_configuration_add / object_configuration_remove. On the Rust side `grep -n 'server_relay|max_sync_packet|max_delta_packet|send_auth|auth_callback|root_path' crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs` finds none of them in MultiplayerAPI (the only root_path hits are on MultiplayerSynchronizer at network.rs:1582-1675); the struct fields (network.rs:167-195) are peer/rpc_configs/authority_map/inbound_rpcs/peers/events/last_status/refuse_new_connections/remote_sender_id/auth_required/pending_auth/auth_timeout. Signals are also misplaced: crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:487 emits peer_connected/peer_disconnected/connected_to_server/connection_failed/server_disconnected/peer_packet/peer_authenticating/peer_authentication_failed on the scene ROOT node, and the interpreter treats `multiplayer` only as a method-call receiver (interpreter.rs:2894), so the canonical `multiplayer.peer_connected.connect(cb)` — which the code comment at scene_tree.rs:451 claims to support — has no binding path (`grep -rn 'peer_connected' crates/gdscript-interop/src` = 0).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH (upstream/godot/modules/multiplayer/scene_multiplayer.cpp, extension_api.json): SceneMultiplayer exposes set_root_path/get_root_path, clear, disconnect_peer, send_auth, set_auth_callback/get_auth_callback, set_auth_timeout, set_allow_object_decoding/is_object_decoding_allowed, set_server_relay_enabled/is_server_relay_enabled, and get/set_max_sync_packet_size + get/set_max_delta_packet_size. MultiplayerAPI adds object_configuration_add/remove (how Spawner/Synchronizer register) and get_multiplayer_peer. All five connection signals (peer_connected, peer_disconnected, connected_to_server, connection_failed, server_disconnected) plus SceneMultiplayer's peer_packet/peer_authenticating/peer_authentication_failed live on the API object, so `multiplayer.peer_connected.connect(_on_peer)` is the standard idiom.\n\nPATINA CURRENT STATE: ClassDB registers the full method list (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:11618-11645, including set_auth_callback/send_auth/disconnect_peer/clear and the server_relay + allow_object_decoding properties) but the interpreter's `call_multiplayer_method` (crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:7266-7370) implements only 10 methods and errors `UndefinedFunction` at line 7369 for all the rest. Nothing behind them exists either: `grep -n 'server_relay|max_sync_packet|max_delta_packet|send_auth|auth_callback|root_path' crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs` finds no MultiplayerAPI fields; the struct at network.rs:167-195 has no relay, no packet caps, no root path, no auth callback. Signals are emitted on the wrong object: crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:487 emits all eight on the scene ROOT node, and interpreter.rs:2894 only recognizes `multiplayer` as a method-call receiver, so `multiplayer.peer_connected.connect(...)` — which the comment at scene_tree.rs:451 claims works — cannot bind (grep for 'peer_connected' in crates/gdscript-interop/src = 0 hits).\n\nIMPLEMENTATION: (a) add the missing fields to MultiplayerAPI in crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs:167-195 — `server_relay: bool` (default true), `allow_object_decoding: bool` (default false), `root_path: String` (default "/root"), `max_sync_packet_size: i32` (1350), `max_delta_packet_size: i32` (1350), `auth_callback: Option<CallableRef>` — with getters/setters, and implement `clear()` (drop peers, caches, pending auth) and `disconnect_peer(id)` delegating to MultiplayerPeerState::disconnect_peer (crates/gdplatform/src/multiplayer_peer_state.rs:83). (b) implement `send_auth(id, data)` emitting an auth packet and route inbound auth data into the registered auth callback before completing the handshake in `poll_auth` (network.rs:688-706). (c) extend `SceneAccess` (crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs:1077-1127) and `call_multiplayer_method` (interpreter.rs:7266-7370) with the full method list so ClassDB no longer advertises anything uncallable. (d) introduce a script-visible `multiplayer` object handle (an ObjectId like the existing WebSocketPeer handles) so `multiplayer.peer_connected` resolves to a Signal value and `.connect(cb)` works; keep emitting on it from `poll_multiplayer_with_delta` (scene_tree.rs:454-501) instead of, or in addition to, the root node.\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: a GDScript in a loaded scene must connect `multiplayer.peer_connected` and see the callback fire when a peer joins during MainLoop frames, and must be able to set `multiplayer.server_relay = false` / call `multiplayer.disconnect_peer(2)` without an UndefinedFunction error.

**Prove it:** A scene script doing `multiplayer.peer_connected.connect(_on_peer)` in `_ready()` receives `_on_peer(id)` when a second tree connects, driven only by MainLoop frames. `multiplayer.set_auth_callback(cb)` + a peer joining routes the auth payload through the script callback before `peer_connected` fires. Every method registered on SceneMultiplayer in class_db.rs:11618-11645 returns a value rather than UndefinedFunction when called from GDScript, and `multiplayer.disconnect_peer(2)` removes the peer from `multiplayer.get_peers()`. (test: `scene_multiplayer_signals_and_full_method_surface_from_script`)
acceptance_criteria: A scene script doing `multiplayer.peer_connected.connect(_on_peer)` in `_ready()` receives `_on_peer(id)` when a second tree connects, driven only by MainLoop frames. `multiplayer.set_auth_callback(cb)` + a peer joining routes the auth payload through the script callback before `peer_connected` fires. Every method registered on SceneMultiplayer in class_db.rs:11618-11645 returns a value rather than UndefinedFunction when called from GDScript, and `multiplayer.disconnect_peer(2)` removes the peer from `multiplayer.get_peers()`. (test: `scene_multiplayer_signals_and_full_method_surface_from_script`)

title: Navigation: runtime + scripted navmesh baking, source-geometry parsing, and obstacle carving
description:
[audit-key: navigation/nav-baking] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json NavigationServer3D.parse_source_geometry_data / bake_from_source_geometry_data / bake_from_source_geometry_data_async / is_baking_navigation_mesh / source_geometry_parser_create / source_geometry_parser_set_callback, NavigationServer3D.region_bake_navigation_mesh, NavigationRegion3D.bake_navigation_mesh(on_thread) + bake_finished signal, NavigationRegion2D.bake_navigation_polygon; NavigationObstacle2D/3D.affect_navigation_mesh / carve_navigation_mesh / vertices; NavigationMesh bake params (cell_size, cell_height, agent_max_climb, region_min_size, region_merge_size, edge_max_length, edge_max_error, detail_sample_distance/max_error, filter_low_hanging_obstacles, filter_ledge_spans, filter_walkable_low_height_spans, sample_partition_type)

**Godot classes:** NavigationMesh, NavigationPolygon, NavigationRegion2D, NavigationRegion3D, NavigationObstacle2D, NavigationObstacle3D, NavigationMeshSourceGeometryData2D, NavigationMeshSourceGeometryData3D

**Patina today:**
- [navigation] A 3D baker exists and has no runtime caller: engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/navigation.rs:309-382 `bake_navigation_mesh` (plus NavigationMesh3D at :31-274 and NavigationRegion3D at :393-470); `grep -rn "bake_navigation_mesh|BakeSourceGeometry3D|NavigationMesh3D" engine-rs/ ` finds only the definitions, the re-export at engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/lib.rs:58, and test files. The 2D outline baker engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/nav_polygon.rs:92-284 has exactly one caller, the editor route at engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:4296 — nothing in the runtime. No node method or server method is registered for baking: NavigationRegion2D/3D registrations (class_db.rs:7525-7542, :1515-1527) declare zero `.method(...)`, so `region.bake_navigation_polygon()` from a script is an UndefinedFunction. The baker itself ignores nearly all Godot params — it does a slope test plus an inradius test only (gdserver3d/src/navigation.rs:313-358), while class_db.rs:12074-12190 registers cell_size, cell_height, agent_max_climb, region_min_size, region_merge_size, edge_max_length, edge_max_error, detail_sample_distance, detail_sample_max_error, filter_* and sample_partition_type. Obstacles: `grep -rn "add_obstacle" engine-rs/` shows `NavigationServer2D::add_obstacle` (navigation.rs:694) is called only from navigation.rs:2691 (unit test) and engine-rs/tests/broader_suite/broader_integration_audio_nav_ui_test.rs:323 — MainLoop::process_navigation (main_loop.rs:1661-1678) never populates `server2.obstacles`, so the obstacle-detour logic at navigation.rs:863-909 is dead at runtime. `carve_navigation_mesh` / `affect_navigation_mesh` / obstacle `vertices` are registered (class_db.rs:7649-7670, :1619-1640) with 0 readers in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/navigation.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/nav_polygon.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `NavigationRegion2D.bake_navigation_polygon()` / `NavigationRegion3D.bake_navigation_mesh(on_thread)` rebake a region at runtime and emit `bake_finished`; `NavigationServer2D/3D.parse_source_geometry_data()` walks the scene into a `NavigationMeshSourceGeometryData2D/3D` honoring `parsed_geometry_type`, `parsed_collision_mask` and `source_geometry_mode`/`source_geometry_group_name`, and `bake_from_source_geometry_data(_async)` turns it into polygons using the NavigationMesh/NavigationPolygon params (cell_size, cell_height, agent_radius/height/max_climb/max_slope, region_min_size, region_merge_size, edge_max_length, edge_max_error, detail_sample_*, filter_low_hanging_obstacles, filter_ledge_spans, filter_walkable_low_height_spans, sample_partition_type). NavigationObstacle2D/3D with `affect_navigation_mesh`/`carve_navigation_mesh` punch their `vertices` outline out of the baked mesh.\n\nPatina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/navigation.rs:309-382 implements a fan-triangle baker with only a slope test and an inradius test, and has ZERO non-test callers (`grep -rn bake_navigation_mesh engine-rs/` = definition, re-export at engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/lib.rs:58, and tests). The 2D outline baker engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/nav_polygon.rs:92-284 is called only from the editor route at engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:4296. No bake method is registered on NavigationRegion2D/3D (class_db.rs:7525-7542, :1515-1527 have zero `.method(...)`), so scripts cannot bake. Obstacles never reach the path query: `NavigationServer2D::add_obstacle` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation.rs:694) has no runtime caller, leaving the detour code at navigation.rs:863-909 dead, and `carve_navigation_mesh`/`affect_navigation_mesh`/`vertices` (class_db.rs:7649-7670, :1619-1640) have 0 readers in gdscene/src.\n\nImplementation approach: (1) register `bake_navigation_polygon`/`bake_navigation_mesh` methods and the `bake_finished` signal on NavigationRegion2D/3D and dispatch them from engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs; (2) add a `parse_source_geometry` pass that walks the subtree collecting MeshInstance3D surfaces and StaticBody3D collision shapes (2D: Polygon2D/CollisionPolygon2D/TileMapLayer) into the NavigationMeshSourceGeometryData containers already registered at class_db.rs:12169-12204, honoring parsed_geometry_type/collision_mask/source_geometry_mode; (3) extend engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/navigation.rs `bake_navigation_mesh` to honor cell_size/cell_height voxelization, agent_max_climb, region_min_size/merge_size, edge_max_length/error, detail sampling and the three filter flags, and to merge coplanar triangles per sample_partition_type instead of one polygon per triangle; (4) carve obstacle outlines out of the baked polygons using the existing clipping in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/nav_polygon.rs; (5) in `MainLoop::process_navigation` (main_loop.rs:1498) gather NavigationObstacle2D/3D nodes and call `server2.add_obstacle(...)` so the detour path at navigation.rs:863-909 becomes live.\n\nWiring requirement: .tscn → MainLoop::step → a script calling `$NavRegion.bake_navigation_mesh()` produces polygons an agent can path over in the same run; an obstacle placed on the corridor makes the agent's runtime path route around it.

**Prove it:** A loaded 3D scene whose NavigationRegion3D has an empty NavigationMesh plus MeshInstance3D floor geometry, after a script call to `bake_navigation_mesh()`, yields a region an agent can path across end-to-end in the same run and emits `bake_finished`; raising `agent_max_slope` admits a ramp that a lower value rejects; a NavigationObstacle2D with `radius` on the straight corridor makes the runtime agent path bend around it (path length grows, no waypoint enters the obstacle radius). (test: `nav_runtime_bake_and_obstacle_carving`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test nav_runtime_bake_and_obstacle_carving`.
acceptance_criteria: A loaded 3D scene whose NavigationRegion3D has an empty NavigationMesh plus MeshInstance3D floor geometry, after a script call to `bake_navigation_mesh()`, yields a region an agent can path across end-to-end in the same run and emits `bake_finished`; raising `agent_max_slope` admits a ramp that a lower value rejects; a NavigationObstacle2D with `radius` on the straight corridor makes the runtime agent path bend around it (path length grows, no waypoint enters the obstacle radius). (test: `nav_runtime_bake_and_obstacle_carving`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test nav_runtime_bake_and_obstacle_carving`.

title: Navigation: path query parameter/result objects, postprocessing + simplify honored, 3D corridor funnel
description:
[audit-key: navigation/nav-path-query] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json NavigationPathQueryParameters2D/3D (RefCounted: map, start_position, target_position, navigation_layers, pathfinding_algorithm, path_postprocessing, metadata_flags, simplify_path, simplify_epsilon, excluded_regions, included_regions, path_return_max_length/radius, path_search_max_polygons/distance) and NavigationPathQueryResult2D/3D (path, path_types, path_rids, path_owner_ids); NavigationServer2D/3D.query_path and simplify_path; PATH_POSTPROCESSING_CORRIDORFUNNEL is the default | upstream/godot/doc/classes/NavigationPathQueryParameters2D.xml / 3D / NavigationPathQueryResult2D.xml / 3D. extension_api.json: NavigationPathQueryParameters2D inherits RefCounted, instantiable, 30 methods / 15 properties (map:RID, start_position, target_position, navigation_layers, pathfinding_algorithm, path_postprocessing, metadata_flags, simplify_path, simplify_epsilon, excluded_regions, included_regions, path_return_max_length, path_return_max_radius, path_search_max_polygons, path_search_max_distance); NavigationPathQueryResult2D 11 methods / 5 properties (path, path_types, path_rids, path_owner_ids, path_length). These are the argument/out types of NavigationServer2D/3D.query_path().

**Godot classes:** NavigationPathQueryParameters2D, NavigationPathQueryParameters3D, NavigationPathQueryResult2D, NavigationPathQueryResult3D

**Patina today:**
- [navigation] None of the four classes are registered — they appear in the sweep's unregistered.txt and `grep -rn "NavigationPathQuery" engine-rs/crates/` matches only a doc comment at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/nav_simplify.rs:4,14. The agent-side knobs ARE registered but read by nobody: engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:7566-7585 (2D) and :1549-1568 (3D) declare `pathfinding_algorithm`, `path_postprocessing`, `path_metadata_flags`, `simplify_path`, `simplify_epsilon`, `path_max_distance`, `path_return_max_length`, `path_return_max_radius`, `path_search_max_polygons`, `path_search_max_distance`, while `grep -rn "path_postprocessing|path_metadata_flags|simplify_epsilon|path_max_distance|path_search_max" engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/` returns 0 hits. The RDP simplifier exists and is dead: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/nav_simplify.rs:23 `simplify_path_2d` / :37 `simplify_path_3d` have no callers (`grep -rn "simplify_path_2d|simplify_path_3d" engine-rs/crates/` = definitions and their own tests only). 3D paths never funnel — engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation.rs:1840-1845 and :1812-1817 push `positions[pi]`, i.e. polygon CENTROIDS, so a 3D path zig-zags where Godot's default CORRIDORFUNNEL would give a taut line (the 2D side does funnel, navigation.rs:429-498).
- [sweep-3] Patina's own source names them as explicitly NOT done: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/nav_simplify.rs:9-15 — "# Scope / remaining work (pat-u3l8c.66, a nav pack) … the rest of the pack — … honoring `navigation_layers` bitmasks and `enter_cost`/`travel_cost` in the search, and the `NavigationPathQueryParameters`/result objects — is not implemented here." Only `simplify_path_2d`/`simplify_path_3d` (the RDP reduction behind simplify_epsilon) exist there.
ABSENCE, exact greps run from /Users/bone/dev/games/patina: `rg -n 'NavigationPathQuery' --glob '!target*' --glob '!upstream/**' -g '*.rs' .` returns exactly three kinds of hit — engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/nav_simplify.rs:4 and :14 (doc comments), and engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4703-4706 (the generated (class,parent) string table used only by `generated_parent_of`, inspector_schema.rs:191 — no methods, no properties, no ClassDB entry). `rg -n 'NavigationPathQuery' engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` → 0 hits; `register_navigation_resource_classes()` (class_db.rs:12001) registers only NavigationPolygon, NavigationMesh and the two SourceGeometryData classes. No struct, no property table, no script constructor anywhere.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/nav_simplify.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/nav_simplify.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `NavigationServer2D/3D.query_path(parameters, result)` takes a `NavigationPathQueryParameters2D/3D` (map, start/target, navigation_layers, pathfinding_algorithm, path_postprocessing CORRIDORFUNNEL|EDGECENTERED|NONE, metadata_flags, simplify_path + simplify_epsilon, included/excluded regions, path_return_max_length/radius, path_search_max_polygons/distance) and fills a `NavigationPathQueryResult2D/3D` (path, path_types, path_rids, path_owner_ids). The same knobs exist as properties on NavigationAgent2D/3D and shape the path the agent follows. CORRIDORFUNNEL is the default postprocessing in both dimensions.\n\nPatina current state: all four classes are unregistered (sweep unregistered.txt; `grep -rn NavigationPathQuery engine-rs/crates/` matches only comments in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/nav_simplify.rs:4,14). The agent properties are registered at engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:7566-7585 and :1549-1568 but `grep -rn "path_postprocessing|path_metadata_flags|simplify_epsilon|path_max_distance|path_search_max" engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/` = 0 readers — every one is inert. The RDP simplifier engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/nav_simplify.rs:23/:37 has zero callers. 3D paths are centroid chains, not funnelled: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation.rs:1840-1845 and :1812-1817 push polygon centroids, while the 2D funnel at navigation.rs:429-498 exists and works.\n\nImplementation approach: (1) register NavigationPathQueryParameters2D/3D and NavigationPathQueryResult2D/3D in class_db.rs with their full property sets and add RefCounted `.new()` handles + method dispatch in gdscript-interop (same pattern as the AStar binding bead); (2) refactor `NavigationServer2D::find_path` / `NavigationServer3D::find_path` (navigation.rs:732, :1825) to take a parameters struct and produce path + path_types/rids/owner_ids; (3) port the 2D portal-funnel string-pull (navigation.rs:429-498) to 3D by projecting each shared-edge portal onto the travel plane, and add the EDGECENTERED mode; (4) call `nav_simplify::simplify_path_2d/3d` on the result when `simplify_path` is set, using `simplify_epsilon`; (5) enforce `path_search_max_polygons`/`path_search_max_distance` in the A* loop and truncate to `path_return_max_length`/`path_return_max_radius`; (6) read all of these off the agent node each tick in `MainLoop::process_navigation` (main_loop.rs:1708-1741) the way AvoidanceNodeParams reads avoidance knobs.\n\nWiring requirement: a .tscn agent with `simplify_path = true`/`simplify_epsilon = 8.0` yields a shorter waypoint list at runtime; a script calling `NavigationServer2D.query_path(params, result)` gets `result.path` plus populated `path_types`.

**Merged findings (2):** NavigationPathQueryParameters2D/3D + NavigationPathQueryResult2D/3D, path_postprocessing (corridorfunnel/edgecentered), path_metadata_flags, simplify_path/simplify_epsilon, path_max_distance, path_search_max_polygons/distance, path_return_max_length/radius; and 3D corridor funnelling; Navigation path-query parameter/result objects

**Prove it:** A GDScript constructs `NavigationPathQueryParameters2D.new()`, sets map/start/target/simplify_path/simplify_epsilon, calls `NavigationServer2D.query_path()` and reads a non-empty `result.path` plus `result.path_types`; a NavigationAgent3D crossing an L-shaped 3D navmesh produces a funnelled path whose interior waypoints sit on portal edges (not polygon centroids) and is strictly shorter than the centroid chain; setting `simplify_epsilon` on an agent in a .tscn reduces its runtime path length. (test: `nav_path_query_params_and_postprocess`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test nav_path_query_params_and_postprocess`.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript constructs `NavigationPathQueryParameters2D.new()`, sets map/start/target/simplify_path/simplify_epsilon, calls `NavigationServer2D.query_path()` and reads a non-empty `result.path` plus `result.path_types`; a NavigationAgent3D crossing an L-shaped 3D navmesh produces a funnelled path whose interior waypoints sit on portal edges (not polygon centroids) and is strictly shorter than the centroid chain; setting `simplify_epsilon` on an agent in a .tscn reduces its runtime path length. (test: `nav_path_query_params_and_postprocess`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test nav_path_query_params_and_postprocess`.

## EmeraldIsland — blocked on the navigation.rs lease; and this bead is six beads

### The bead's claims check out

Unusually, all of them. Verified independently:

- `NavigationPathQuery*` in `class_db.rs` → **0 hits**. All four classes genuinely unregistered.
- `simplify_path_2d` / `simplify_path_3d` (`nav_simplify.rs:23`, `:37`) → **zero callers** outside their own tests. Implemented, tested, dead.
- `simplify_epsilon` readers under `gdscene/src/` → none outside `nav_simplify.rs` itself. (A naive `grep -c` counts that file, because its function names contain the string; the reader count really is zero.)
- The named acceptance test does not exist.

### Why nothing landed this cycle

**`navigation.rs` is held by MagentaBrook** (reservation, expires 05:21Z), and every clause of this bead needs it:

- **Clause 1** — `NavigationServer2D.query_path()` is the server, in `navigation.rs`.
- **Clause 2** — the 3D corridor funnel replaces the centroid pushes at `navigation.rs:1812-1817` and `:1840-1845`, porting the working 2D funnel at `:429-498`.
- **Clause 3** — the simplifier has to be applied where the path is produced: `NavigationAgent2D::set_target_position` (`:1196`) and the 3D twin (`:1634`), and the knobs need fields on the agent structs (`:1086`+).

I hold `navigation_agents.rs`, but `sync_tuning_2d`/`sync_tuning_3d` there can only copy a scene value onto a **field that does not exist yet**. Adding the sync without the field is not a partial increment, it is a compile error.

I tried the lease, saw the conflict, and released my duplicate row rather than leave a second HELD row.

### The scoping problem, stated plainly

This is six features behind one acceptance test: two new class families with `.new()` and method dispatch, a server API change to parameter/result objects, a 3D funnel port, A* search limits and result truncation, the simplifier wiring, and per-tick agent reads. Its own "Implementation approach" is numbered (1) through (6).

**The most valuable piece is also the smallest**, and it is clause 3: `nav_simplify` is complete, tested, and has no callers — the "implemented but unreachable" shape. Wiring it is roughly two struct fields, two `sync_tuning` lines and two call sites. That would be a good bead on its own, and it is what I would take first when the file frees.

**Clause 2 is the highest user-visible value**: 3D paths currently chain polygon centroids, so they visibly zig-zag where Godot's default CORRIDORFUNNEL gives a taut line. The 2D funnel already exists and works, so it is a port rather than a design.

I would rather this were split than attempt all six blind in one pass — I have just had two beads parked, and both were cases where breadth outran what I could verify without a compiler.

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## EmeraldIsland — step 1 (registration) landed; steps 2-6 still blocked on navigation.rs

### Landed

The four classes are registered in `class_db.rs` with their complete documented property sets, plus five tests in `gdobject/tests/nav_path_query_classes_registered.rs`.

Every name, default and accessor pair was **transcribed** from `doc/classes/NavigationPathQuery{Parameters,Result}{2D,3D}.xml`, not derived. That mattered immediately:

⚠️ **The getter is `get_simplify_path`, NOT `is_simplify_path`.** Godot uses the `is_` prefix for a great many bool getters — `is_editable`, `is_allow_unpress`, `is_showing_hidden_files` — and does not use it here. Deriving from the convention gives a plausible, wrong string. There is a test pinning it with that reasoning.

Two defaults that would fail *silently* if copied wrong, both now asserted:

- **`navigation_layers = 1`**, not 0. A zero mask matches no region, so every query through a default-constructed parameters object returns an empty path — which reads as a pathfinding bug, not a default.
- **`path_search_max_polygons = 4096`**, not 0. Zero means "no limit" for the three neighbouring caps (`path_return_max_length/radius`, `path_search_max_distance`), but this one is a real budget and 0 would refuse every search.

There is also a control test: the 2D/3D assertions run in a shared loop, which would pass if 3D had been registered as a copy of 2D, so one test asserts they differ exactly where Godot says — `Vector2`/`Vector3` and `PackedVector2Array`/`PackedVector3Array`.

### ⚠️ Finding for whoever does the rest of step 1

**ClassDB registration alone does NOT make these constructible from a script.** `Interpreter::classdb_instantiate` (`gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:8635`) branches:

- `is_parent_class(class, "Node")` → `scene_access.create_node`;
- **every non-Node class → it delegates to the expression `ClassName.new()`**, i.e. to the interpreter's ~30 bespoke handle arms, deliberately (pat-s3rrv.57 comment: "a bare refcounted handle would be worse than the Nil this used to return: an object that exists and answers nothing").

So `NavigationPathQueryParameters2D.new()` needs a real arm in `interpreter.rs`; the registration is the introspection half only. The Rust-side `class_db::instantiate` *does* build a `GenericObject` from the property table, which is what my test exercises — the two paths are different and it is easy to conclude from the Rust one that the script one works.

### Still blocked

Steps 2-6 all live in `navigation.rs`, held by MagentaBrook since 04:31 and unreleased. I asked for a ping when they drop it and explicitly told them not to release on my account — they are mid-edit, which is when a file should be left alone. I have released every duplicate row I took rather than leave a second HELD row.

The two pieces I would take first, in order: wiring `nav_simplify` (dead tested code, two fields plus two call sites), then the 3D corridor funnel (a port of the working 2D funnel at `:429-498`, replacing the centroid pushes at `:1812-1817` and `:1840-1845`).

title: AnimatedSprite2D: backwards playback, pause/set_frame_and_progress, and the animation_looped/animation_changed signals
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/animated-sprite-2d] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/2d/animated_sprite_2d.cpp; extension_api.json AnimatedSprite2D methods play(name, custom_scale, from_end)/play_backwards/pause/stop/set_frame_and_progress/get_playing_speed and signals animation_changed/animation_looped/animation_finished/frame_changed/sprite_frames_changed

**Godot classes:** AnimatedSprite2D, SpriteFrames

**Patina today:**
- [nodes-2d] `crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:2360-2450 process_animated_sprites` covers autoplay, `speed_scale`, `frame`, `frame_progress`, `frame_changed` and `animation_finished`. It does not cover: backwards playback — `AnimatedSpritePlayback::advance` at `crates/gdscene/src/sprite_frames.rs:256-290` only ever increments (`self.frame + 1`) and multiplies `dt * self.speed_scale` without handling a negative scale, so `play_backwards()` / `from_end` cannot work; `animation_looped` and `animation_changed` are declared in ClassDB (`crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1248-1250`, `:6206-6208`) but never emitted (`grep -rn 'animation_looped' crates/gdscene/src` = 0); `set_frame_and_progress` and `get_playing_speed` have no binding (`grep -rn 'set_frame_and_progress' crates/` = 0); `pause()` (which freezes without resetting, unlike `stop()`) has no script binding.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/sprite_frames.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: `AnimatedSprite2D.play(name, custom_scale, from_end)` and `play_backwards(name)` run a clip in reverse (negative effective speed, wrapping from frame 0 to the last frame). `pause()` freezes on the current frame and progress without resetting; `stop()` resets. `set_frame_and_progress(frame, progress)` sets both atomically. `get_playing_speed()` returns the signed effective speed. The node emits `animation_looped` each time a looping clip wraps and `animation_changed` when the selected animation switches (upstream/godot/scene/2d/animated_sprite_2d.cpp).

PATINA: `crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:2360-2450` already handles autoplay, `speed_scale`, `frame`, `frame_progress`, `frame_changed` and `animation_finished`. Missing: `crates/gdscene/src/sprite_frames.rs:256-290 AnimatedSpritePlayback::advance` only ever does `self.frame + 1` and accumulates `dt * speed_scale` with no negative-direction branch, so reverse playback is impossible; `animation_looped` and `animation_changed` are declared at `crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1248-1250` and `:6206-6208` but never emitted (`grep -rn 'animation_looped' crates/gdscene/src` = 0); `set_frame_and_progress`, `get_playing_speed` and `pause` have no script bindings anywhere (`grep -rn 'set_frame_and_progress' crates/` = 0).

APPROACH: give `AnimatedSpritePlayback` a signed direction: let `speed_scale` be negative and, in `advance`, step `frame - 1` when negative, wrapping to `count - 1` on a looping clip and stopping at frame 0 otherwise; return an enum/flag distinguishing 'wrapped' from 'finished'. In `scene_tree.rs::process_animated_sprites`, emit `animation_looped` on the wrap flag and `animation_changed` when the resolved `animation` differs from the previous frame's. Add `play`/`play_backwards`/`pause`/`stop`/`set_frame_and_progress`/`get_playing_speed` bindings to `crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs` alongside the AnimationPlayer bindings at `scripting.rs:2740`.

WIRING: `.tscn` with an AnimatedSprite2D and a script -> `MainLoop::step` -> `process_animated_sprites` -> `frame` and `texture` published -> `build_runtime_render_list` draws the reversed frame; signals reach connected script methods.

**Prove it:** A .tscn AnimatedSprite2D whose script calls `play_backwards("walk")` in `_ready()` shows a strictly DECREASING `frame` across successive `MainLoop::step` calls and wraps from 0 to the last frame on a looping clip, with the node's published `texture` matching the reversed frame each tick. A looping clip emits `animation_looped` exactly once per wrap to a connected script method. `pause()` freezes `frame` and `frame_progress` across further steps while `stop()` resets them. `set_frame_and_progress(2, 0.5)` is reflected in both properties on the next tick. (test: `animated_sprite_2d_backwards_and_signals`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test animated_sprite_2d_backwards_and_signals`.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn AnimatedSprite2D whose script calls `play_backwards("walk")` in `_ready()` shows a strictly DECREASING `frame` across successive `MainLoop::step` calls and wraps from 0 to the last frame on a looping clip, with the node's published `texture` matching the reversed frame each tick. A looping clip emits `animation_looped` exactly once per wrap to a connected script method. `pause()` freezes `frame` and `frame_progress` across further steps while `stop()` resets them. `set_frame_and_progress(2, 0.5)` is reflected in both properties on the next tick. (test: `animated_sprite_2d_backwards_and_signals`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test animated_sprite_2d_backwards_and_signals`.

title: Canvas2D: implement CanvasGroup compositing, BackBufferCopy screen texture, and MultiMeshInstance2D
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/canvas-compositing-2d] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/2d/canvas_group.cpp, back_buffer_copy.cpp, multimesh_instance_2d.cpp; extension_api.json CanvasGroup{fit_margin, clear_margin, use_mipmaps}, BackBufferCopy{copy_mode, rect}, MultiMeshInstance2D{multimesh, texture}

**Godot classes:** CanvasGroup, BackBufferCopy, MultiMeshInstance2D

**Patina today:**
- [nodes-2d] All three are registered in `crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` but have zero behavior: `rg -n 'CanvasGroup|BackBufferCopy|MultiMeshInstance2D' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdeditor/src crates/gdrender2d/src crates/patina-runner/src` (excluding the generated inspector schema) returns NOTHING. They are absent from the render-kind dispatch at `crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:677-798`, so each one falls through to `Render2DKind::Marker` and draws an editor placeholder glyph at runtime. Godot uses CanvasGroup for grouped alpha/outline compositing and BackBufferCopy to feed `SCREEN_TEXTURE` to canvas_item shaders — with no BackBufferCopy, no 2D shader can read the screen behind it.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: `CanvasGroup` renders its whole CanvasItem subtree into an offscreen buffer (grown by `fit_margin`, cleared by `clear_margin`, optionally mipmapped) and composites that buffer once, so `modulate`/alpha applies to the group rather than per child and shaders can operate on the flattened result. `BackBufferCopy` copies the current framebuffer region (`rect`, or the whole screen when `copy_mode = VIEWPORT`) into the back buffer that a canvas_item shader samples as `SCREEN_TEXTURE`. `MultiMeshInstance2D` draws a `MultiMesh` (per-instance transform/colour/custom data) with one `texture`, in a single batch.

PATINA: all three classes are registered in `crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` and have NO implementation anywhere — `rg -n 'CanvasGroup|BackBufferCopy|MultiMeshInstance2D' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdeditor/src crates/gdrender2d/src crates/patina-runner/src` returns nothing outside the generated inspector schema. The render-kind dispatch at `crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:677-798` has no arm for them, so each falls into the `Render2DKind::Marker` catch-all at `:796` and shows an editor placeholder in the running game. Without BackBufferCopy no 2D shader can read `SCREEN_TEXTURE` even though the canvas shader stack is otherwise wired (`crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs:126` / `crates/gdserver2d/src/shader.rs`).

APPROACH: (1) In `build_runtime_render_list`, tag items whose ancestor is a CanvasGroup with a group id; in `rasterize_render_list`, rasterize each group into its own `FrameBuffer` sized by the group's item bounds grown by `fit_margin`, then blit that buffer once with the group node's `modulate`. (2) Add a `Render2DKind::BackBufferCopy { rect, copy_mode }` that, at its position in the sorted draw list, snapshots the framebuffer into a screen-texture slot the canvas shader path samples. (3) Add a `Render2DKind::MultiMesh { texture, instances: Vec<(Transform2D, Color)> }` fed from the `multimesh` sub-resource (flatten it in `crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs` alongside the existing `__viewport_mesh__` pass) and rasterize each instance through `gdrender2d::polygon_raster::fill_polygon_textured`.

WIRING: `.tscn` -> `build_runtime_render_list` -> `rasterize_render_list` -> a CanvasGroup with `modulate.a = 0.5` shows uniform half-alpha over overlapping children (not doubled alpha at overlaps), a BackBufferCopy makes SCREEN_TEXTURE non-black for a shader below it, and a MultiMeshInstance2D draws N quads.

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a `CanvasGroup` (modulate alpha 0.5) over two overlapping opaque children renders the overlap region at the SAME alpha as the non-overlap region (proving one composite, not two blends). A .tscn with a `BackBufferCopy` above a red ColorRect and a canvas_item ShaderMaterial sampling SCREEN_TEXTURE renders a non-black sampled colour. A `MultiMeshInstance2D` with 3 instance transforms produces 3 drawn quads at the expected positions instead of a marker glyph. (test: `canvas_group_backbuffer_multimesh_2d_render`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test canvas_group_backbuffer_multimesh_2d_render`.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a `CanvasGroup` (modulate alpha 0.5) over two overlapping opaque children renders the overlap region at the SAME alpha as the non-overlap region (proving one composite, not two blends). A .tscn with a `BackBufferCopy` above a red ColorRect and a canvas_item ShaderMaterial sampling SCREEN_TEXTURE renders a non-black sampled colour. A `MultiMeshInstance2D` with 3 instance transforms produces 3 drawn quads at the expected positions instead of a marker glyph. (test: `canvas_group_backbuffer_multimesh_2d_render`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test canvas_group_backbuffer_multimesh_2d_render`.

title: Node2D: compose skew into the local transform and honor CanvasItem.top_level in the global walk
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/node2d-transform-parity] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/main/canvas_item.cpp `CanvasItem::get_global_transform` (top_level breaks the parent chain), scene/2d/node_2d.cpp `Node2D::_update_transform` (skew shears the Y basis: `Transform2D(angle, scale, skew, pos)`)

**Godot classes:** Node2D, CanvasItem

**Patina today:**
- [nodes-2d] `crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs:86-98 get_local_transform` composes only `translate * rotate * scale` — `skew` is never read, even though it is registered as a Node2D property at `crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:5947` and `gdcore::math::Transform2D::from_rotation_scale_skew_origin` already exists (`crates/gdcore/src/math.rs:674`) and is used by `crates/gdscene/src/canvas_layer.rs:179`. `crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs:102-120 get_global_transform` walks EVERY ancestor unconditionally; it never checks `top_level`, which is registered as a CanvasItem property at `crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:6094` and asserted by `crates/gdobject/tests/canvas_item_classdb_properties.rs:30`. The 3D side does honor it (`crates/gdscene/src/node3d.rs:279 get_global_transform_top_level`), so this is a 2D-only omission: `grep -rn 'top_level' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs crates/gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs` yields hits only in `node3d.rs`. A `top_level = true` sprite (the standard 'detach from the parent's transform' idiom, e.g. for projectiles) still inherits its parent's transform, and a skewed Node2D draws unskewed.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/canvas_order.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: `Node2D::_update_transform` builds the local matrix as `Transform2D(rotation, scale, skew, position)` — `skew` shears the Y basis relative to X (upstream/godot/scene/2d/node_2d.cpp). `CanvasItem::get_global_transform` stops climbing at any node whose `top_level` is set: that node's local transform IS its global transform, which is how detached projectiles, screen-space effects and parented-but-world-space nodes work (upstream/godot/scene/main/canvas_item.cpp).

PATINA: `crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs:86-98 get_local_transform` composes only `translated * rotated * scaled` and never reads `skew`, although the property is registered (`crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:5947`) and `gdcore::math::Transform2D::from_rotation_scale_skew_origin` already exists at `crates/gdcore/src/math.rs:674` (used by `crates/gdscene/src/canvas_layer.rs:179`). `crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs:102-120 get_global_transform` multiplies through the entire ancestor chain with no `top_level` check, while the 3D sibling `crates/gdscene/src/node3d.rs:279 get_global_transform_top_level` does implement it. So both properties round-trip through .tscn and the inspector but change nothing on screen.

APPROACH: read `skew` in `get_local_transform` and build the matrix via `Transform2D::from_rotation_scale_skew_origin(rotation, scale, skew, position)`, preserving the existing CanvasLayer-identity short-circuit at `node2d.rs:87-92`. Add `is_top_level_2d(tree, id)` and make `get_global_transform` break the ancestor walk at the first `top_level` node exactly as `node3d.rs:279-297` does. Sweep the derived helpers in the same file so they stay consistent: `get_global_rotation` (`:148`), `get_global_scale` (`:159`), `set_global_position` (`:126`), `set_global_rotation` (`:172`), plus `crates/gdscene/src/behavioral_2d.rs:78 global_scale_of`.

WIRING: `.tscn` -> `PackedScene` -> `build_runtime_render_list` (which calls `node2d::get_global_transform` at `crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:362`) -> rasterized item transform.

**Prove it:** A .tscn where a Sprite2D with `top_level = true` sits under a Node2D at `position = Vector2(500, 500)` renders at world (0,0), while its `top_level = false` sibling renders at (500,500); the same sprite's `get_global_position()` read from a GDScript returns (0,0). A Node2D with `skew = 0.5` produces a rendered item transform whose basis is sheared (the y-column x-component is non-zero) and whose corner positions differ from an unskewed node. (test: `node2d_skew_and_top_level_affect_scene_transform`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test node2d_skew_and_top_level_affect_scene_transform`.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn where a Sprite2D with `top_level = true` sits under a Node2D at `position = Vector2(500, 500)` renders at world (0,0), while its `top_level = false` sibling renders at (500,500); the same sprite's `get_global_position()` read from a GDScript returns (0,0). A Node2D with `skew = 0.5` produces a rendered item transform whose basis is sheared (the y-column x-component is non-zero) and whose corner positions differ from an unskewed node. (test: `node2d_skew_and_top_level_affect_scene_transform`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test node2d_skew_and_top_level_affect_scene_transform`.

title: Skeleton2D: add a 2D bone phase that poses Bone2D chains and skins Polygon2D
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/skeleton2d] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/2d/skeleton_2d.cpp, polygon_2d.cpp (bone weights); extension_api.json Skeleton2D{get_bone/get_bone_count/get_skeleton/set_modification_stack/execute_modifications}, Bone2D{rest, get_index_in_skeleton, apply_rest, get_skeleton_rest, set_autocalculate_length_and_angle, ...}, SkeletonModification2D + CCDIK/FABRIK/Jiggle/LookAt/PhysicalBones/StackHolder/TwoBoneIK, SkeletonModificationStack2D | upstream/godot/scene/2d/skeleton_2d.cpp, scene/2d/polygon_2d.cpp (`bones`, `skeleton`, `add_bone`, `internal_vertex_count`), scene/resources/skeleton_modification_2d*.cpp; doc/classes/Skeleton2D.xml, Bone2D.xml, Polygon2D.xml

**Godot classes:** Skeleton2D, Bone2D, SkeletonModificationStack2D, SkeletonModification2DTwoBoneIK, SkeletonModification2DLookAt, SkeletonModification2DCCDIK, SkeletonModification2DFABRIK, SkeletonModification2DJiggle, Polygon2D

**Patina today:**
- [nodes-2d] No runtime pose system exists. `crates/gdscene/src/ik_solver_2d.rs` (solve_two_bone_ik_2d) is referenced only by its `pub mod` at `crates/gdscene/src/lib.rs:46` — `rg --type rust -l -F 'ik_solver_2d::' crates examples` is empty. `crates/gdrender2d/src/polygon_raster.rs:290-360` defines `Bone2D`, `Skeleton2D::skinning_transforms` and `deform_polygon_vertices`, none of which has a caller outside `crates/gdrender2d/tests/line_shading.rs` (verified with `rg --type rust -l -F deform_polygon_vertices crates examples`). The MainLoop skeleton phase is 3D-only: `crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2986 crate::skeleton3d::process_skeletons` — there is no 2D equivalent. `Polygon2D`'s `bones`/`skeleton` properties are never read (`grep -rn '"bones"' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdeditor/src` = 0). `SkeletonModification2D`, `SkeletonModification2DCCDIK/FABRIK/Jiggle/LookAt/PhysicalBones/StackHolder/TwoBoneIK` and `SkeletonModificationStack2D` are not registered at all (`grep -c 'ClassRegistration::new("SkeletonModification2D")' crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` = 0), so a .tscn referencing them loses the nodes.
- [animation] The deformation math exists as a library-only module: `Bone2D`, `Skeleton2D`, `skinning_transform`, `skinning_transforms`, `deform_polygon_vertices` at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/polygon_raster.rs:290-370. Its `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` begins at polygon_raster.rs:373 and every `deform_polygon_vertices` call site is inside it (lines 541, 560, 585, 604, 625); `grep -rn 'deform_polygon_vertices|skinning_transforms|polygon_raster::Skeleton2D' --include=*.rs crates/` finds no caller outside that file. `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/ik_solver_2d.rs` (135 lines, the SkeletonModification2DTwoBoneIK core) has exactly one workspace reference — its own `pub mod ik_solver_2d;` at gdscene/src/lib.rs:46. There is no `Polygon2D` node implementation in gdscene at all (`grep -rn 'Polygon2D' crates/gdscene/src` matches only CollisionPolygon2D in physics_server.rs). Skeleton2D/Bone2D are registered in class_db.rs but the nine `SkeletonModification2D*` classes plus `SkeletonModificationStack2D` are unregistered (verified: `grep -c '"SkeletonModification2D"' crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` → 0).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/ik_solver_2d.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/polygon_raster.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/lib.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: `Skeleton2D` collects its `Bone2D` descendants, holds their `rest` transforms, and each frame produces skinning transforms (`bone_pose * rest.affine_inverse()`) that a `Polygon2D` with a `skeleton` NodePath and per-vertex `bones` weights uses to deform its vertices (upstream/godot/scene/2d/skeleton_2d.cpp, polygon_2d.cpp). A `SkeletonModificationStack2D` assigned to the skeleton runs `SkeletonModification2D*` entries (TwoBoneIK, LookAt, CCDIK, FABRIK, Jiggle, PhysicalBones, StackHolder) after animation, in stack order, via `execute_modifications`.

PATINA: nothing runs. `crates/gdscene/src/ik_solver_2d.rs` (`solve_two_bone_ik_2d`) is only `pub mod`-declared at `crates/gdscene/src/lib.rs:46` and never called. `crates/gdrender2d/src/polygon_raster.rs:290-360` already has `Bone2D`, `Skeleton2D::skinning_transforms()` and `deform_polygon_vertices()` — all dead outside `crates/gdrender2d/tests/line_shading.rs`. The MainLoop's skeleton phase at `crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2986` calls only `skeleton3d::process_skeletons`. `Polygon2D.bones`/`skeleton` are read nowhere. The whole `SkeletonModification2D*` family and `SkeletonModificationStack2D` are unregistered in `crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`, so those nodes vanish on scene load.

APPROACH: add `crates/gdscene/src/skeleton2d.rs` with `process_skeletons_2d(tree)`, modelled on `crates/gdscene/src/skeleton3d.rs`: walk each `Skeleton2D`, gather its `Bone2D` children with their `rest` and current `position/rotation/scale`, run the node's modification stack (call `ik_solver_2d::solve_two_bone_ik_2d` for TwoBoneIK; add LookAt and CCDIK inline), write the resulting poses back to the Bone2D nodes, and publish the skinning transforms on the Skeleton2D as an internal property. Call it from the skeleton phase in `main_loop.rs:2986`, right after `skeleton3d::process_skeletons`. In `crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, when a Polygon2D names a `skeleton`, run `polygon_raster::deform_polygon_vertices` over the published transforms before emitting `Render2DKind::Polygon`. **Prove it:** A .tscn with `Skeleton2D > Bone2D > Bone2D` and a `Polygon2D` bound to that skeleton with per-vertex weights renders polygon vertices at their rest positions on frame 0; after a script rotates the root Bone2D by 45 degrees and one `MainLoop::step` runs, the emitted `Render2DKind::Polygon` points have moved by the corresponding skinning transform. comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## Extra mesh surfaces now RENDER with their own overrides (EmeraldIsland, 2026-08-20)

### ⚠️ The bead description is badly stale — do not work from it

It claims 0 repo hits for four symbols. Actual non-test counts today:

| symbol | bead says | actual |
|---|---|---|
| `sorting_offset` | 0 | **19** |
| `sorting_use_aabb_center` | 0 | **16** |
| `visibility_parent` | 0 | **22** |
| `gi_mode` | 0 (registration only) | **17** |
| `instance_shader_parameter` | 0 | 0 (still genuinely absent) |

Sorting, the GI properties and per-surface LOADING were all delivered by an earlier
pass. That author left an unusually good scope note in the acceptance test's header
naming exactly what they had NOT done — read it before this description.

### The one real gap: nothing ever DREW the extra surfaces

`gdrender3d` had **zero** references to `Mesh3D::surfaces`. Both backends iterated
only the top-level `vertices`/`indices`, i.e. the primary surface.

Meanwhile the data was fully plumbed and inert: `packed_scene` flattens
`surface_material_override/N` onto the node as `__surfmat<N>__*`, `scene_saver`
filters and rewrites them — and **nothing in between ever read them**. A complete
round trip that never reached a pixel.

### Why the diff is additive rather than a loop rewrite

`DrawEntry` is a FUNCTION-LOCAL struct in the draw-list builder. So each additional
surface is promoted to a standalone `Mesh3D` and pushed as one more draw entry. The
draw loop is **untouched**, and culling, depth, shadows, transparency sorting and
the overlay pass all apply to the extra surfaces for free.

Restructuring the loop to iterate surfaces inline would have meant rebuilding a
20-field `ShaderUniforms` literal per surface inside the crate's hottest function.

⚠️ The surface meshes are built BEFORE `entries` and never mutated afterwards —
the entries borrow from that vec, so building them lazily inside the push loop
would not compile.

### 🔑 The index is off by one against Godot's property names

`Mesh3D::surfaces` holds the surfaces BEYOND the primary one, so `surfaces[i]` is
Godot's `surface_material_override/{i + 1}`. Override 0 is the primary surface and
still arrives as the instance material. `surface_materials_for_node` therefore
skips companion 0 — `packed_scene` already skips it on the way in, for the same
reason.

Two tests pin this instead of trusting it:
- one authors at companion **2** leaving 1 absent, so a gap-collapsing
  implementation puts the material at the wrong index and fails;
- one asserts companion 0 never appears in the extra-surface list.

### Trait change is defaulted on purpose

`RenderingServer3D::set_surface_materials` has a default no-op body, so neither
backend breaks and wgpu simply ignores the data until it grows a per-surface draw
loop. Only the software renderer overrides it. `Instance3D` has exactly ONE
constructor, so the new field needed no struct-literal sweep.

### Still open (follow-ups, not this clause)

1. The wgpu backend does not draw extra surfaces — default no-op.
2. `instance_shader_parameter` is still genuinely unimplemented.

title: Register the Shape2D resource subtree in ClassDB (WorldBoundaryShape2D and its 8 siblings)
description:
[audit-key: physics/physics-2d-shape2d-resource-classdb] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/2d/world_boundary_shape_2d.h + the Shape2D subtree; doc/classes/WorldBoundaryShape2D.xml — inherits Shape2D, members `normal: Vector2` default Vector2(0,-1) and `distance: float` default 0.0. Godot registers Shape2D, CircleShape2D, RectangleShape2D, CapsuleShape2D, SegmentShape2D, SeparationRayShape2D, ConvexPolygonShape2D, ConcavePolygonShape2D and WorldBoundaryShape2D in scene/register_scene_types.cpp

**Godot classes:** WorldBoundaryShape2D

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-7] Behaviour exists, registration does not. Implementation: engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/shape.rs:48 defines the infinite half-plane and gdphysics2d/src/world.rs:1060 raycasts it; engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:313-317 constructs it from a .tscn sub-resource by matching the literal "WorldBoundaryShape2D" and reading normal (default Vector2(0,-1)) and distance (default 0.0). Registration absence: `grep -x` against the 4186 literals extracted from engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs = 0 hits for EVERY 2D shape resource — Shape2D, CircleShape2D, RectangleShape2D, CapsuleShape2D, SegmentShape2D, SeparationRayShape2D, ConvexPolygonShape2D, ConcavePolygonShape2D, WorldBoundaryShape2D — while the 3D twins ARE registered (Shape3D, BoxShape3D, SphereShape3D, CapsuleShape3D, CylinderShape3D, ConvexPolygonShape3D, ConcavePolygonShape3D, HeightMapShape3D, SeparationRayShape3D, WorldBoundaryShape3D). Consequences: `ClassDB.class_exists("WorldBoundaryShape2D")` false (interpreter.rs:14922); `WorldBoundaryShape2D.new()` from GDScript errors because interpreter.rs falls through to `is_node_class_name` (interpreter.rs:21256, a hardcoded node-name list that contains no shape resources) and then raises; the ClassDB-driven editor create/inspector paths (gdeditor/src/create_dialog.rs) cannot offer the resource. Scene loading itself still works because gdscene/src/physics_server.rs matches the resource class STRING rather than consulting ClassDB.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/shape.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

[status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** Godot 4.6.1 registers the whole 2D shape resource subtree: Shape2D (abstract, Resource) -> CircleShape2D (radius 10.0), RectangleShape2D (size Vector2(20,20)), CapsuleShape2D (radius 10.0, height 40.0), SegmentShape2D (a Vector2(0,0), b Vector2(0,10)), SeparationRayShape2D (length 20.0, slide_on_slope false), ConvexPolygonShape2D (points), ConcavePolygonShape2D (segments), WorldBoundaryShape2D (normal Vector2(0,-1), distance 0.0). Defaults from upstream/godot/doc/classes/*.xml.

**Patina today:** the physics behaviour is implemented and consumed — gdphysics2d/src/shape.rs:48 (half-plane), gdphysics2d/src/world.rs:1060 (ray vs half-plane), gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:313-317 (constructs from a .tscn sub-resource by matching the class STRING and reading normal/distance) — but NOT ONE of the nine classes is in ClassDB (0 hits each against class_db.rs's string literals), while every 3D twin is registered. So `ClassDB.class_exists("CircleShape2D")` is false, `ClassDB.instantiate` on any of them fails, `WorldBoundaryShape2D.new()` from GDScript errors (interpreter.rs falls through to the hardcoded node-name list at interpreter.rs:21256), and the ClassDB-driven editor create/inspector paths (gdeditor/src/create_dialog.rs) cannot offer a shape resource. This is rung (a) missing beneath working rungs (b)-(c).

**Implement:** register the subtree in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs's 2D block (`register_2d_classes()` at class_db.rs:5732), mirroring the existing 3D shape registrations: Shape2D `.abstract_class()` with parent Resource plus `custom_solver_bias`, then the eight concrete leaves with their doc-XML property defaults. Then make script construction work: extend the GDScript `.new()` path in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs so a registered Resource class name yields a Variant::Resource with the ClassDB defaults, instead of falling through `is_node_class_name` (interpreter.rs:21256) to an error.

**Wiring requirement:** a script in a loaded scene can build `var s = RectangleShape2D.new()`, set its size, assign it to a CollisionShape2D and have gdscene/src/physics_server.rs produce the same collider it produces from a .tscn sub-resource; ClassDB introspection reports the full subtree; the editor's resource-creation path lists the shapes.

**Prove it:** an app-level test that both loads a .tscn using a WorldBoundaryShape2D sub-resource AND builds one from script, asserting identical physics behaviour and full ClassDB introspection.

**Prove it:** ClassDB reports Shape2D as abstract with parent Resource and reports CircleShape2D, RectangleShape2D, CapsuleShape2D, SegmentShape2D, SeparationRayShape2D, ConvexPolygonShape2D, ConcavePolygonShape2D and WorldBoundaryShape2D with parent Shape2D and their doc-XML property defaults (WorldBoundaryShape2D.normal == Vector2(0,-1), distance == 0.0); and a GDScript that does `WorldBoundaryShape2D.new()`, sets normal/distance and assigns it to a CollisionShape2D produces the same collision result as the equivalent .tscn sub-resource (test: `shape2d_resource_classes_registered`)

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## Diagnosis from a no-build lane (EmeraldIsland, 2026-08-20)

I claimed this, could not solve it, and **released it unchanged** — the tree is
byte-identical to how I found it. Handing over the elimination work.

### ⚠️ The bead title no longer describes what is left

"Register the Shape2D resource subtree in ClassDB" is **done**. All nine 2D shape
classes are registered with correct parents and defaults, and that half of the
test passes. What fails is the *script-construction* half — a scripting/runtime
bug, not a ClassDB one. Re-scoping the title would stop the next worker starting
where I did.

### The failure

`shape2d_resource_classes_registered.rs:168` — after running:

```gdscript
var s = WorldBoundaryShape2D.new()
s.normal = Vector2(0, -1)
s.distance = 25.0
var col = get_node("FromScript/Col")
col.shape = s
```

`/root/World/FromScript/Col`'s `shape` is not a `Variant::Resource`.

### The failure is CURRENT, not a stale binary

- binary built **08-20 05:45:16**; the test file it runs is **05:38:19** (older)
- both halves of the relevant code — the `WorldBoundaryShape2D` registration and
  the RefCounted `.new()` branch — landed in commit `f8986b8` at **08-19 20:23
  UTC**, well before that build

### Links I verified as CORRECT (do not re-check these)

1. **ClassDB registration + parent chain** — `WorldBoundaryShape2D.parent = Shape2D`,
   and `Shape2D -> Resource -> RefCounted -> Object` is complete, so
   `is_parent_class(.., "RefCounted")` holds.
2. **Abstractness** — `Shape2D` is abstract (correct); the leaves are not, so the
   abstract guard ahead of the constructor is not firing.
3. **ClassDB seeding in the test** — `register_all_classes()` is the test's first
   line, so this is not the pat-s3rrv.220 trap.
4. **`.new()` on a RefCounted class** returns `Variant::Resource` seeded from
   ClassDB defaults (`interpreter.rs:4436`).
5. **Member WRITE on a resource** — this was my hypothesis and it is **wrong**.
   `try_exec_value_member_assignment` handles only Vector2/Vector3/Color, which is
   what misled me, but the generic tail of the same branch does
   `set_index(container, String(member), val)` and `set_index` inserts into a
   `ResourceRef`'s property bag (`interpreter.rs:16312`). I wrote a fix for this,
   disproved it, and reverted.
6. **Member READ on a resource** works (`interpreter.rs:4638`).
7. **`col.shape = s` where `col` is a local holding a node ObjectId** routes to
   `set_property_with_virtual` (`interpreter.rs:2019`).
8. **Relative `get_node("FromScript/Col")`** — `get_node_relative`
   (`scene_tree.rs:3097`) splits on `/` and walks segment by segment via
   `find_child_by_name` (`:3131`), which iterates **direct children only**. So the
   two same-named `Col` nodes under different parents cannot be confused, and the
   name-only fallbacks in `ScriptAccess::get_node` never fire for a multi-segment
   path.

### What disproved the obvious hypothesis

Three existing tests already do exactly the operations I thought were broken, all
green: `physics3d_direct_space_state_script` (7 passed —
`PhysicsRayQueryParameters3D.new()` plus property writes),
`script_built_shape_reaches_the_body` (3 passed — `$Col.shape = CircleShape2D.new()`),
`physics2d_shape_resources_classdb_instantiate` (3 passed).

### Cheapest next step

One instrumented run asserting on **`FromScene/Col`'s** shape as well as
`FromScript/Col`'s. That separates "the script aborted partway" from "the shape
landed on the wrong node" in a single execution, and every remaining hypothesis
falls on one side or the other.

title: Navigation: bind AStar2D/AStar3D/AStarGrid2D to GDScript and complete their method surface

**Godot classes:** AStar2D, AStar3D, AStarGrid2D

**Patina today:**
- [navigation] A complete, tested implementation exists: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/astar.rs:53-756 (`AStar<V>` for Vector2/Vector3 with weight scales, disabled points, bidirectional connect/disconnect, partial paths at :249, closest point at :329; `AStarGrid2D` at :471-755 with diagonal modes, dual heuristics, jumping/collinear compression at :714, solid+weight region fills). - [sweep-0] CORRECTION to the mechanical diff: both ARE registered — /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:11929 `for name in ["AStar2D", "AStar3D"]` registers them (parent RefCounted, 19 methods each) at :11932-11955; they were missed because the sweep's registration extractor only sees literal `ClassRegistration::new("Name")`. The runtime also exists: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/astar.rs:1-23. What is missing is the script constructor: `rg -n 'AStar' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/` returns ZERO hits. The interpreter's `.new()` path (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:3014-3155) is a hardcoded allowlist of RefCounted handle types (ConfigFile, RefCounted, XR trackers, XMLParser, ZIPReader/Packer, PCKPacker, CameraFeed, WebSocketPeer, UndoRedo, StreamPeerBuffer, RandomNumberGenerator, Expression, Thread, Mutex, Semaphore, RegEx, HashingContext, AESContext, Crypto) followed by `is_node_class_name` (:21256, itself a hardcoded node list) — AStar2D/AStar3D/AStarGrid2D are in neither, so `AStar2D.new()` errors and the pathfinder is unreachable from any game script.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/astar.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/astar.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GDScript cannot even create one: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:3014-3160 has no `.new()` arm and interpreter.rs:21256-21285 `is_node_class_name` excludes them, so `AStar2D.new()` is a TypeError. This is dead, tested code behind a green suite.\n\nImplementation approach: (1) add a handle registry (mirroring the `new_rng_handle` / `new_expression_handle` pattern already used in interpreter.rs:3103-3120) that owns `gdscene::astar::AStar<Vector2>`, `AStar<Vector3>` and `AStarGrid2D` instances keyed by ObjectId; (2) add `AStar2D`/`AStar3D`/`AStarGrid2D` arms to the `.new()` chain returning those handles; (3) add a `call_astar_method` dispatcher covering every ClassDB-registered method plus the ones listed above, converting Variant↔Vector2/Vector2i/Vector3/PackedVector2Array; (4) fill the gaps in astar.rs: `get_available_point_id`, `reserve_space`/`get_point_capacity`, `get_closest_position_in_segment`, AStarGrid2D `cell_shape`, `size`, `is_dirty`, `clear`, `get_point_data_in_region`, and make `update()` (astar.rs:544) actually rebuild after a dirty region change; (5) extend the ClassDB registrations so the missing method names exist for reflection.\n\nWiring requirement: a GDScript attached to a node in a .tscn runs `var g = AStarGrid2D.new(); g.region = Rect2i(...); g.update(); g.set_point_solid(...); var p = g.get_id_path(a, b)` under MainLoop::step and the returned PackedVector2iArray reaches the script.

**Merged findings (3):** AStar2D / AStar3D / AStarGrid2D reachable from GDScript; AStar2D/AStar3D/AStarGrid2D cost virtuals `_estimate_cost`, `_compute_cost`, `_filter_neighbor`; AStar2D / AStar3D not constructible from GDScript (registered + implemented, but no .new())

**Prove it:** A GDScript in a loaded scene constructs `AStar2D.new()`, adds and connects weighted points, and `get_point_path()` returns the expected PackedVector2Array; a second script constructs `AStarGrid2D.new()`, sets a region, marks solid cells, and `get_id_path()` routes around them honoring `diagonal_mode` and `jumping_enabled`; both round-trip through the interpreter (no UndefinedFunction / TypeError). (test: `astar_classes_reachable_from_gdscript`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscript-interop --test astar_classes_reachable_from_gdscript`.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript in a loaded scene constructs `AStar2D.new()`, adds and connects weighted points, and `get_point_path()` returns the expected PackedVector2Array; a second script constructs `AStarGrid2D.new()`, sets a region, marks solid cells, and `get_id_path()` routes around them honoring `diagonal_mode` and `jumping_enabled`; both round-trip through the interpreter (no UndefinedFunction / TypeError). (test: `astar_classes_reachable_from_gdscript`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscript-interop --test astar_classes_reachable_from_gdscript`.

The IMPLEMENTATION IS COMPLETE AND COMMITTED AT HEAD. Do not rewrite it. Verified by reading, end to end:
