Only the TEST file (gdscene/tests/astar_from_gdscript.rs) is uncommitted WIP; all src is HEAD.

### The failing signal, and four hypotheses ELIMINATED by source reading
Latest verify: stage=0, expected 19. The earlier direct-call error TypeError('undefined variable: AStar2D') is a HARNESS ARTEFACT — the .new() arm needs scene_access to be Some, and ScriptInstance::call_method leaves it None. process_script_ready -> call_script_with_access -> call_script_method DOES install SceneTreeAccessor (scene_tree.rs:3390/3411), so the tree path is correct.

stage=0 means statement 1 ('stage = 1') never executed. Eliminated:
1. 'bare assignment makes a local' — NO. exec_assignment (interpreter.rs:1636) treats a declared var as an instance prop, and the else branch is environment.set, which never defines a local.
2. 'the write is rolled back when _ready raises' — NO. Environment::set (interpreter.rs:~382) walks inner->outer and writes IN PLACE; list_properties reads scopes[0]; call_script_method has no snapshot/restore.
3. 'typed class vars (var stage: int = 0) mis-parse' — NO. parser.rs:679 parse_var_decl_with_annotations handles the hint. Also stage reads back as its initialiser 0, so the VarDecl ran.
4. 'astar_new is an inherent method, so the trait default None runs' — NO, see above.

### The surviving hypothesis
_ready parses to an EMPTY/TRUNCATED body: that alone fits all three observations at once — has_method('_ready') true, the call does NOT raise (ran.is_some() passes), and zero statements execute so stage keeps its initialiser. NEXT STEP is empirical and needs a compiler: print script.list_methods() and the parsed body length for _ready, or run one statement at a time. Do NOT spend another cycle on the AStar plumbing.

### Genuine defect found in passing (report separately, do not fix under this bead)
interpreter.rs:6523 'self.exec_stmt(&body[i])?' returns early on a raise WITHOUT self.environment.pop_scope(), while every other exit path pops. A script error therefore leaks its function scope for the life of the instance, so later calls see stale locals and is_shadowed_in_inner_scope can wrongly report a class var as shadowed.

gdscene/src is mid-refactor by another agent RIGHT NOW: scene_bridge.rs is a STAGED DELETION (pat-s3rrv.22) alongside modified lib.rs/scene_tree.rs/main_loop.rs/packed_scene.rs and a new untracked navigation_agents.rs. title: Area2D: route audio_bus_override to the mixer when a player enters the area

SliderJoint3D adds `linear_motion/*`, `linear_ortho/*`, `angular_motion/*`, `angular_ortho/*` softness-restitution-damping triples. PhysicalBone3D chooses its parent constraint via `joint_type` (PIN/CONE/HINGE/SLIDER/6DOF) with `joint_constraints/*` sub-properties, which is what makes an elbow bend one way and a shoulder swing in a cone.\n\nPATINA: crates/gdphysics3d/src/joint.rs:492-496 states plainly that motors and springs are absent; `AxisLimit` (:374-381) carries only enabled/lower/upper. 2. `a_hinge_bone_is_constrained_where_the_pin_fallback_is_not` failed its own

- (b) linear spring — `linear_spring*` / `equilibrium_point` present;
- (c) per-bone ragdoll `joint_type` — `physics_server_3d.rs:1012` reads it and

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## ROOT CAUSE FIXED: spring damping erased the spring's own correction

EmeraldIsland, 2026-08-20. **Correcting my own comment above**, which said this
bead was a stale verdict already finished by a peer. It was not.

⚠️ Mail server was down when this landed (`Too many open files`), so the
completion message may not have reached the coordinator. **The code change IS in
the tree.** Gate: `-p gdscene`, test `physics3d_joint_motors_and_springs`.
Changed file: `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/world.rs`.

### How I got it wrong

I ran the binary found by `ls | grep | head -1`. There were **two** binaries for
this target — 08-19 23:07 and 08-20 11:30 — and `head -1` handed me the stale one
while my freshness check used `max(mtime)` on the other. I compared a fresh
timestamp against a stale binary's OUTPUT and concluded "stale verdict".

The newest binary says **3 passed, 1 failed**. My call was half right, which is
what made it seductive: the hinge failure really was stale and now passes. I
generalised from that one clause to the whole bead.

🔑 **When a target has more than one binary, `head -1` is a coin flip.** Sort by
mtime and run the NEWEST, or the verdict you read belongs to code that no longer
exists.

### The defect

`damp_linear_axis` computed

    lambda = (-relative / k) * damping.clamp(0.0, 1.0)

treating Godot's `damping` as *the fraction of relative velocity to erase*. It
runs immediately after the spring solve, which sets the relative velocity to
exactly the corrective value the positional bias asks for.

So at Godot's **default `damping = 1.0`** the damper erased **100% of the spring's
own correction, every tick**. The spring computed a perfect answer and the damper
threw it away before it could move anything.

Symptom: `got y = 0.5` — the bob sitting at its authored start position to the
digit. That is indistinguishable from the spring parameters never reaching the
solver, which is why it survived a `stiffness` that plainly WAS arriving. The
solver's own comment even predicts this exact shape ("neither drifts nor sags but
stays at its start value to the last digit") for a DIFFERENT cause that had
already been fixed — so the tell pointed at an already-closed bug.

### The fix

`damping` is a RATE, not a fraction, so scale it by `dt`:

    lambda = (-relative / k) * (damping * dt).clamp(0.0, 1.0)

At 60 Hz a damping of 1.0 now bleeds ~1.7% per step; the spring dominates and a
heavier damping still saturates safely at the clamp. Applied identically to the
angular twin.

### Simulated against the real constants

stiffness 100, damping 1.0, dt 1/60, start y = 0.5:

| | y after 240 ticks |
|---|---|
| before | **0.5** — reproduces the observed failure EXACTLY |
| after | ~0 (0.193 → 0.074 → 0.029 by tick 3, under the 0.05 tolerance) |

Reproducing the failure value to the digit is what makes this a confirmed model
rather than a plausible story. The spring converges without oscillating because
the bias is a position-level ERP, not an accumulating force.

### Blast radius and test choice

`damp_linear_axis`/`damp_angular_axis` have exactly TWO call sites, both inside
the 6DOF spring block, and the only test file in the workspace touching
`linear_spring`/`angular_spring` is this bead's own acceptance test.

No new test file, deliberately: the acceptance test already catches this defect —
it is red right now *because* of it — and it is an integration target inside my
blast radius. A unit test on `damp_linear_axis` could only live in `world.rs`'s
own `#[cfg(test)]` block (both the fn and `JointBody` are private), reachable only
via `-p gdphysics3d --lib`, whose binary is from **07-26** so its greenness cannot
be shown — and it would land ungated, the anti-pattern removed on pat-s3rrv.195.

⚠️ `world.rs` is not rustfmt-clean at HEAD (10-line pre-existing diff). The change
leaves it at exactly 10, so the delta is zero.

title: Physics3D: drive VehicleBody3D/VehicleWheel3D from the scene tree into the real 3D world
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/phys3d-vehicle] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/vehicle_body_3d.cpp; doc/classes/VehicleBody3D.xml, VehicleWheel3D.xml; extension_api.json classes VehicleBody3D (parent RigidBody3D), VehicleWheel3D (parent Node3D)

**Godot classes:** VehicleBody3D, VehicleWheel3D

**Patina today:**
- [physics-3d] A complete raycast-vehicle solver exists at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/vehicle3d.rs (VehicleBody3D::step applies gravity, suspension, drive, brake, steering; add_wheel at :136) and is exported at crates/gdphysics2d/src/lib.rs:77. Both classes are registered in ClassDB with full property surfaces (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1641 VehicleBody3D parent RigidBody3D, :1661 VehicleWheel3D) and the editor inspector lists them (crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:5194-5195), and crates/gdobject/tests/vehicle_wheel_3d_property_surface_test.rs passes green on the property defaults. But NOTHING outside the module constructs one: `grep -rn "vehicle3d\|VehicleBody3D\|VehicleWheel3D" --include='*.rs' crates/` returns only crates/gdphysics2d/src/vehicle3d.rs, its own test crates/gdphysics2d/tests/vehicle3d_drive.rs, class_db.rs and inspector_schema_generated.rs. The scene bridge crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs::body_type_for_class_3d (:37) does not know the class, so a .tscn VehicleBody3D registers as a plain body (or not at all) and its wheels are inert. It also builds on a second, parallel 3D world (crates/gdphysics2d/src/world3d.rs, body3d.rs, shape3d.rs, collision3d.rs) that no runtime path uses, not on gdphysics3d::PhysicsWorld3D.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/vehicle3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: VehicleBody3D is a RigidBody3D whose VehicleWheel3D children raycast down `wheel_rest_length + wheel_radius` each physics tick; the suspension spring (suspension_stiffness, suspension_travel, suspension_max_force, damping_compression, damping_relaxation) pushes the chassis up, `engine_force`/`brake` drive the contact patch, `steering` rotates the front wheels, and `wheel_friction_slip`/`wheel_roll_influence` shape the tire model (upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/vehicle_body_3d.cpp `_update_suspension`/`_resolve_single_bilateral`/`_update_friction`). Wheels expose is_in_contact(), get_contact_body(), get_skidinfo(), get_rpm().\n\nPATINA: the solver already exists — crates/gdphysics2d/src/vehicle3d.rs (VehicleBody3D::new :115, add_wheel :136, step applies gravity/suspension/drive/brake) — and both classes are in ClassDB (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1641, :1661) with an inspector schema (crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:5194). Nothing constructs it at runtime: the class is absent from `body_type_for_class_3d` (crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:37) and from every call site outside crates/gdphysics2d/tests/vehicle3d_drive.rs. It is also built on the orphan gdphysics2d::world3d/body3d/shape3d stack, not gdphysics3d::PhysicsWorld3D, so it cannot interact with the bodies a scene actually contains.\n\nAPPROACH: (1) move the vehicle model into crates/gdphysics3d/src/vehicle3d.rs and re-express the wheel raycast on gdphysics3d::query::PhysicsRayQuery3D against PhysicsWorld3D bodies, so wheels ride real StaticBody3D/trimesh ground; (2) in crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs add a `sync_vehicles` pass alongside `sync_areas`/`sync_joints` (called from `sync_to_physics`, :635-639) that registers each VehicleBody3D as a Rigid body and reads its VehicleWheel3D children's authored props (engine_force, brake, steering, wheel_radius, wheel_rest_length, suspension_*, damping_*, wheel_friction_slip, wheel_roll_influence, use_as_traction, use_as_steering); (3) apply the per-wheel suspension/traction impulses to the chassis body inside PhysicsWorld3D::step (crates/gdphysics3d/src/world.rs:569) before contact resolution; (4) publish `_wheel_*` results back onto each wheel node in `sync_from_physics` (:1442) so is_in_contact()/get_skidinfo() are script-readable.\n\nWIRING: MainLoop physics tick (crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2840-2842 sync_to_physics -> step -> sync_from_physics) must drive it end to end, so a .tscn with a VehicleBody3D + 4 VehicleWheel3D children over a StaticBody3D floor drives forward when a script sets engine_force.

title: Crypto: implement RSA/X509 (keys, self-signed certs, sign/verify/encrypt/decrypt), construct CryptoKey/X509Certificate/HMACContext, and back generate_random_bytes with a CSPRNG
description:
[audit-key: platform-os/platform-os-crypto] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: STUB/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json classes[Crypto,CryptoKey,X509Certificate,HMACContext]; upstream/godot/core/crypto/crypto.cpp + crypto_core.cpp (mbedTLS CTR_DRBG backs Crypto::generate_random_bytes) | doc/classes/AESContext.xml + upstream/godot/core/crypto/aes_context.cpp — update() requires a multiple of 16 bytes, adds NO padding, chains CBC IV state across calls, and get_iv_state() returns the current chained IV

**Godot classes:** Crypto, CryptoKey, X509Certificate, HMACContext, AESContext

**Patina today:**
- [platform-os] engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:17092-17094 stubs the entire asymmetric half: `"generate_rsa" | "generate_self_signed_certificate" => Ok(Variant::Nil)`, `"sign" | "encrypt" | "decrypt" => Ok(Variant::PackedByteArray(Vec::new()))`, `"verify" => Ok(Variant::Bool(false))`. CryptoKey, X509Certificate and HMACContext ARE registered in ClassDB (engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:10899 HMACContext, :10926 CryptoKey, :10937 X509Certificate) so `ClassDB.class_exists` reports true and the inspector schema lists them, but none is constructible: `grep -c 'class_name == "HMACContext"|class_name == "X509Certificate"|class_name == "CryptoKey"' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` = 0, while Expression/Thread/Mutex/Semaphore/RegEx/HashingContext/AESContext/Crypto all have handle constructors at interpreter.rs:3113-3141. Separately `Crypto.generate_random_bytes` is not cryptographically secure: engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/crypto.rs:413-421 draws from `crate::rng::randi()`, a wall-clock-seeded xorshift (engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/rng.rs:128-131), and the doc comment at crypto.rs:405-412 admits it — Godot backs the same call with mbedTLS CTR_DRBG.
- [platform-os] engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/crypto.rs:260-268 documents the divergence in-tree: "Godot's `AESContext.update()` does *no* padding: it requires the input to be a multiple of 16 and returns the raw blocks. This pads with PKCS7 on encrypt and strips it on decrypt." The CBC path (crypto.rs:280-311) constructs a fresh `cbc::Encryptor` from `self.iv` on every call, so two successive `update()` calls both start from the original IV instead of chaining — different ciphertext from Godot for any multi-call stream. `finish()` (crypto.rs:367-372) is a no-op that leaves state usable. The script binding compounds it: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:17050 returns `"get_iv_state" => Ok(Variant::PackedByteArray(Vec::new()))`, so a ported script that saves and restores the IV state gets nothing back. Ciphertext produced by a Godot project therefore will not decrypt here and vice versa.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/crypto.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/rng.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/config_file.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: `Crypto.generate_rsa(bits)` returns a CryptoKey; `generate_self_signed_certificate(key, issuer_name, not_before, not_after)` returns an X509Certificate; `sign(hash_type, hash, key)` / `verify(hash_type, hash, signature, key)` / `encrypt(key, plaintext)` / `decrypt(key, ciphertext)` do RSA over that key. `CryptoKey.save/load/save_to_string/load_from_string/is_public_only` and `X509Certificate.save/load/save_to_string/load_from_string` handle PEM. `HMACContext.start/update/finish` is the streaming HMAC. `Crypto.generate_random_bytes` is a CSPRNG (mbedTLS CTR_DRBG, upstream/godot/core/crypto/crypto_core.cpp).\n\nPATINA CURRENT STATE: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:17092-17094 returns Nil / empty PackedByteArray / false for the whole asymmetric family. HMACContext, CryptoKey and X509Certificate are registered in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs (:10899, :10926, :10937) but have no handle constructor in the `.new()` dispatch at interpreter.rs:3113-3141, so a script that does `X509Certificate.new().load(path)` gets an object with no working methods — registration without construction. `gdcore::crypto::generate_random_bytes` (engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/crypto.rs:413) pulls from the xorshift in engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/rng.rs:128-131 seeded from SystemTime, so keys/nonces/session ids generated by a ported project are predictable.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION APPROACH: (1) Swap `generate_random_bytes` in engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/crypto.rs onto `getrandom` (native) / crypto.getRandomValues (wasm) — the doc comment at crypto.rs:405-412 states this is the whole fix and needs no call-site changes — and expose the same source as `OS.get_entropy`. (2) Add RSA (rsa/rustcrypto) + X509 (x509-cert / rcgen) behind `gdcore::crypto`, implementing key generation, PEM save/load and PKCS#1v15 sign/verify/encrypt/decrypt. (3) Add handle constructors and instance dispatch for CryptoKey, X509Certificate and HMACContext in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs alongside the existing HashingContext/AESContext handles, and have `Crypto.generate_rsa`/`generate_self_signed_certificate` hand back those handles. (4) Keep the existing ClassDB registrations in sync with the real method arities.\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: a script in a loaded scene must be able to run the full Godot idiom — `var c = Crypto.new(); var k = c.generate_rsa(2048); var cert = c.generate_self_signed_certificate(k, "CN=patina"); var sig = c.sign(HashingContext.HASH_SHA256, hash, k); c.verify(...)` — and `k.save_to_string()` / `CryptoKey.new().load_from_string(pem)` must round-trip.

**Merged findings (2):** Crypto: RSA/X509 half (generate_rsa, generate_self_signed_certificate, sign/verify/encrypt/decrypt), CryptoKey/X509Certificate/HMACContext construction, and CSPRNG-backed generate_random_bytes; AESContext: block semantics diverge from Godot (PKCS7 padding added, no IV chaining across update(), get_iv_state empty)

**Prove it:** A scene script generates a 2048-bit RSA key, signs a SHA-256 digest and verifies it (true), verifies a tampered digest (false), round-trips the key and a self-signed certificate through save_to_string/load_from_string, and drives HMACContext start/update/finish to the same digest as `Crypto.hmac_digest`; two consecutive `Crypto.generate_random_bytes(32)` calls differ and do not repeat across a process restarted with the same wall clock. (test: `crypto_rsa_x509_and_csprng_reachable_from_script`)
acceptance_criteria: A scene script generates a 2048-bit RSA key, signs a SHA-256 digest and verifies it (true), verifies a tampered digest (false), round-trips the key and a self-signed certificate through save_to_string/load_from_string, and drives HMACContext start/update/finish to the same digest as `Crypto.hmac_digest`; two consecutive `Crypto.generate_random_bytes(32)` calls differ and do not repeat across a process restarted with the same wall clock. (test: `crypto_rsa_x509_and_csprng_reachable_from_script`)

verifier lane, which a worker cannot perform or even test. Hand-rolling RSA plus

* **(b)** **split the bead** — bank the AES-semantics and CSPRNG findings as

  RSA/X509 bead parked on the dependency question.

I cannot create or split beads; that is the coordinator's call. I have raised the
dependency question twice without an answer, so I am naming the lever rather than
re-asking the question.

  rsa::rand_core        public re-export at rsa/src/lib.rs:226, of rand_core 0.6.4

  rsa::sha2             real re-export, gated `#[cfg(feature = "sha2")]` (lib.rs:242-243) — gdcore

                        `features = ["oid"]` (Cargo.toml:164-168), so

                        AssociatedOid` bound (pkcs1v15.rs:74-77)
  offline resolvability rsa 0.9.10 is in engine-rs/Cargo.lock AND vendored in the registry, with
                        sha2, num-bigint-dig, pkcs1, pkcs8, der, spki all in the lock

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## STALE VERDICT — proven by content, not by mtime. Needs a re-run, not a fix.

Audit from a no-build lane (EmeraldIsland, 2026-08-20). **No code changed** — the
tree is byte-identical to how I found it. Released for a lane that can build.

### The recorded failure is from a test that NO LONGER EXISTS

The prebuilt binary panics with:

    AudioEffectReverb has exactly 8 parameters upstream, got [...11 names...]

**That string does not appear anywhere in the current test source** (`grep -c` = 0).
The live assertion reads "AudioEffectReverb declares exactly 8 parameters of its
own upstream…" and subtracts `Resource`'s members before counting:

```rust
let base = get_property_list("Resource") ... collect();
let own  = reverb.iter().map(|p| &p.name).filter(|n| !base.contains(*n)) ...;
assert_eq!(own.len(), 8, ...);
```

Binary 08-19 23:29, test source 08-19 23:30 — one minute newer. Someone hit this
exact failure and fixed the ASSERTION (correctly: `get_property_list` walks the
inheritance chain, so a bare `len() == 8` would assert the class has no ancestors).

⚠️ Content beats mtime as staleness evidence. A panic message that cannot be found
in the file it names is proof; an mtime is only a hint. I have twice today drawn
the wrong conclusion from mtimes alone (`.203`, `.206`).

### What the failing run nevertheless PROVES about the implementation

The panic came from the COUNT assertion, which sits AFTER the per-parameter loop.
So the run got through all eight of:

    predelay_msec 150.0 | predelay_feedback 0.4 | room_size 0.8 | damping 0.5
    spread 1.0 | hipass 0.0 | dry 1.0 | wet 0.5

each asserted to be a `Variant::Float` within 1e-6 of the doc-XML default. **All 8
reverb parameters and their defaults are already correct.** The reported 11 names
were the 8 plus `Resource`'s `resource_local_to_scene` / `resource_name` /
`resource_path`, which is the inheritance chain behaving properly.

### `finished` is registered on all three players

`AudioStreamPlayer` (24809), `AudioStreamPlayer2D` (24847) and
`AudioStreamPlayer3D` (24899) each carry `.signal(SignalInfo::new("finished"))`.

Each is registered EXACTLY ONCE, so although each sits behind
`if !class_exists(..)`, no earlier registrar can win the race and skip it — the
guarded-duplicate trap does not apply here.

### Not verified by me

Clause 1 of the acceptance — a script connected to `$AudioStreamPlayer.finished`
receiving the callback when the stream ends — sits AFTER the count assertion, so
the recorded run never reached it. The sibling test
`a_finished_player_reports_itself_stopped` passes, which is adjacent evidence but
not the same claim. **A re-run is the cheapest way to settle the whole bead.**

### ⚠️ Unrelated finding for whoever owns class_db.rs

Two comments in this file contradict each other about `register()`:

* `class_db.rs:~7109` — "`register()` mints a fresh ClassId on every call and
  overwrites `classes[name]` … so an unguarded registration is not idempotent."
* `class_db.rs:~12650` — "`register()` merges by member name, so running unguarded
  is additive and idempotent instead."

I read the implementation (`fn register`, ~496): when the class exists it KEEPS
`existing.class_id` and merges properties, methods, signals, constants and enums,
deduplicating by name. **The second comment is right and the first is wrong.**

This matters because the first comment is the stated justification for guarding
registrations with `if !class_exists`, and guarding is precisely what makes a later,
richer registration vanish — the failure mode `Resource` is unguarded to avoid,
with ten bare registrations competing. Worth correcting under a bead that owns
this file.

title: Finish the PrimitiveMesh family: PointMesh/QuadMesh/RibbonTrailMesh + fix the QuadMesh-is-PlaneMesh alias
description:

**Godot classes:** PointMesh, QuadMesh, RibbonTrailMesh

**Patina today:**

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/extra_meshes.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/primitive_mesh.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

ClassDB registers 6 of Godot's 12 PrimitiveMesh subclasses (class_db.rs:4199-4225: Box/Sphere/Capsule/Cylinder/Plane/Prism). PointMesh, QuadMesh and RibbonTrailMesh are unregistered, and the way QuadMesh is currently faked produces wrong geometry for two classes at once.

Godot's PlaneMesh has `orientation` (FACE_Y default), `center_offset`, `subdivide_width` and `subdivide_depth`; QuadMesh overrides `orientation` to FACE_Z and `size` to Vector2(1,1). A third asserts a MeshInstance3D whose mesh is a PointMesh resolves to a single-vertex mesh rather than the default cube, and that a MeshInstance2D with a PlaneMesh draws at 2x2 not 1x1 (test: `primitive_mesh_family_quadmesh_orientation_and_pointmesh_routing`)

title: Import dock: persist import options to .import sidecars and run a real reimport
description:
[audit-key: asset-import-pipeline/import-dock-persist] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: STUB/MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/docks/import_dock.cpp (_update_options, _reimport_attempt/_reimport_and_cleanup) + editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp (reimport_files); options come from ResourceImporter::_get_import_options and persist into the asset's .import [params] section | upstream/godot/editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp (`_reimport_file`, `_save_filesystem_cache`, `.godot/imported/` naming = `<basename>-<md5(path)>.<save_extension>`), editor/import/resource_importer_texture.cpp (`_save_ctex`), core/io/resource_uid.cpp (uid_cache.bin / `.uid` sidecars)

**Godot classes:** EditorFileSystem, ResourceImporter, EditorImportPlugin, ResourceImporterTexture, ResourceUID

**Patina today:**
- [asset-import-pipeline] engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:19192-19197 — `api_set_import_settings` body is literally `let _ = parse_json_body(body); send_json(stream, r#"{\"ok\":true}"#)` with the comment "persisting to a `.import` sidecar is future work". engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:19199-19226 — `api_reimport` validates the extension and echoes `{"ok":true,"reimported":"<path>"}`; no importer runs, no artifact is written, the TextureCache is never invalidated. engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:19050-19180 — `api_get_import_settings` returns a hardcoded option list per extension (compression="VRAM Compressed", mipmaps=true, …); it never opens the asset's `.import` file, so the dock can never show what an option is actually set to. engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs:9996-10050 — the served JS renders the options and POSTs every change to the discarding endpoint; the Preset menu only relabels the button client-side. This is behind GREEN tests: engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/editor_suite_b/editor_import_hooks_test.rs:74-125 asserts `importable`, preset names and that reimport "reports the path" for `res://hero.png` — a file that is never created on disk.
- [asset-import-pipeline] Grep for any writer of a `.import` sidecar or a `.godot/imported/` artifact across `engine-rs/crates/*/src` — patterns `godot/imported`, `write.*\.import`, `generate_import`, `\[remap\]` — returns ONLY readers/tests: engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs:62-100 (`resolve_import_artifact` reads a sidecar), importers.rs:643-676 (accessors), and test fixtures. Nothing constructs one. The FileSystem dock never scans for importable sources: engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/filesystem.rs only mentions "import" as a file-icon category (filesystem.rs:314) and as a directory to skip (filesystem.rs:178). engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/fs_import_pipeline.rs is a status-bookkeeping model whose `reimport()` (lines 145-155) sets `imported_version` and increments a counter without touching the filesystem, and it has zero callers (`grep -rn fs_import_pipeline crates/ --include=*.rs` → only `lib.rs:68 pub mod fs_import_pipeline;`). Consequence: a project authored in Patina has no `.import`, no `.ctex`, no `uid://` — Godot cannot open it, and Patina's own remap resolution only ever works on projects a real Godot editor imported.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/import_settings.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/filesystem.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/fs_import_pipeline.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/ctex.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/uid.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `ImportDock::_update_options` reads the selected asset's `.import` file, asks the matching `ResourceImporter` for its option list/defaults/visibility, and shows the CURRENT values; `_reimport_and_cleanup` writes the edited values back into the `.import` `[params]` section and calls `EditorFileSystem::reimport_files`, which re-runs the importer, rewrites `.godot/imported/<name>-<md5>.<ext>`, and reloads every in-memory reference (upstream/godot/editor/docks/import_dock.cpp, editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp).\n\nPatina current state: `api_get_import_settings` (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:19050-19180) synthesises a hardcoded option list from the file extension and never opens the asset's `.import`; `api_set_import_settings` (editor_server.rs:19192-19197) drops the body on the floor with the comment "persisting to a `.import` sidecar is future work"; `api_reimport` (editor_server.rs:19199-19226) validates the extension and echoes the path. The served dock JS (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs:9996-10050) is fully built and calls all three, so the UI looks live and changes nothing. `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/fs_import_pipeline.rs:145-155` `reimport()` only flips an `ImportStatus` enum.\n\nImplementation approach: add a typed import-option model in `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs` (extend `ImportFile` with a parsed `[params]` map keyed by importer, plus a writer that serialises an `ImportFile` back to Godot's INI form). In `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs`: have `api_get_import_settings` load `<source>.import` through `gdresource::load_import_file` and overlay the stored `[params]` on the importer defaults; have `api_set_import_settings` write the edited key into `[params]` and mark the asset stale via `fs_import_pipeline::ImportPipeline::set_setting`; have `api_reimport` invoke the real importer (see the artifact-generation bead), rewrite the `.import` `[remap] path`/`uid`, drop the `state.texture_cache` entry for that path, and return the new artifact path.\n\nWiring requirement: EDITOR_HTML dock → POST /api/import_settings → `.import` file on disk → POST /api/reimport → importer runs → `.godot/imported/*` artifact rewritten → texture cache invalidated → next GET /api/import_settings reports the persisted value.

**Merged findings (2):** Editor Import dock: option persistence + real reimport (ImportDock/EditorFileSystem::reimport_files); Import artifact generation: `.import` sidecars, `.godot/imported/` outputs, `.uid` sidecars on filesystem scan

**Prove it:** Starting the assembled editor server on a temp project containing a real `hero.png`: (1) GET /api/import_settings?path=res://hero.png reports the values currently stored in `hero.png.import` (not hardcoded defaults); (2) POST /api/import_settings with `{"option":"mipmaps","value":false}` causes `hero.png.import` on disk to contain `mipmaps=false` under `[params]`; (3) POST /api/reimport regenerates the artifact named by `[remap] path` (file mtime/content changes) and a subsequent GET reports `mipmaps=false`. (test: `import_dock_persists_options_and_reimports`)
acceptance_criteria: Starting the assembled editor server on a temp project containing a real `hero.png`: (1) GET /api/import_settings?path=res://hero.png reports the values currently stored in `hero.png.import` (not hardcoded defaults); (2) POST /api/import_settings with `{"option":"mipmaps","value":false}` causes `hero.png.import` on disk to contain `mipmaps=false` under `[params]`; (3) POST /api/reimport regenerates the artifact named by `[remap] path` (file mtime/content changes) and a subsequent GET reports `mipmaps=false`. (test: `import_dock_persists_options_and_reimports`)

The parent CharacterBody is never moved. Additionally, `process_navigation` (main_loop.rs:1688-1741) reads ONLY `target_position` (:1643) off the node — `path_desired_distance`, `target_desired_distance`, `max_speed`, `radius`, `path_height_offset` are never synced from the scene (AvoidanceNodeParams::apply, main_loop.rs:224-256, runs only in the avoidance phase and only when `avoidance_enabled` is true), so a .tscn tuning those values is ignored by path following.
- [navigation] Patina computes these milestones but never emits them. engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation.rs:1019-1031 defines `NavAgentSignal::{PathChanged, WaypointReached, TargetReached, NavigationFinished, VelocityComputed}`; they are pushed at :1149 (PathChanged), :1163 (WaypointReached), :1174-1176 and :1282 — and drained only by `NavigationAgent2D::drain_signals` (navigation.rs:1299). `grep -rn "drain_signals" engine-rs/crates/ | grep -i nav` returns 0 non-navigation.rs hits (the matches are AnimationPlayer at scene_tree.rs:2206 and the multiplayer peers). The runtime emits only three signals by hand: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:1749-1750 (`target_reached`, `navigation_finished`), :1787-1788 (3D twin) and :1363-1364 (`velocity_computed`). `link_reached` has no producer anywhere (`grep -rn "link_reached" engine-rs/crates/` matches only the class_db signal declarations). All six signals ARE declared in ClassDB (engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, NavigationAgent2D block at :7634-7639 and NavigationAgent3D at :1604-1609), so `connect("waypoint_reached", …)` succeeds and then never fires. NavigationAgent3D does not even maintain a pending-signal list (navigation.rs:1334-1395 has no `pending_signals` field).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/class_defaults.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth (upstream/godot/doc/classes/NavigationAgent2D.xml:7-10, NavigationAgent3D.xml): NavigationAgent2D/3D inherit `Node`, have no transform, and NEVER move anything. The canonical usage is `var next = agent.get_next_path_position(); velocity = (next - global_position).normalized() * SPEED; move_and_slide()` inside `_physics_process`. The agent exposes 20 methods (get_next_path_position, is_navigation_finished, is_target_reached, is_target_reachable, distance_to_target, get_current_navigation_path, get_current_navigation_path_index, get_current_navigation_result, get_final_position, get_path_length, get_rid, set_velocity, set_velocity_forced, get/set_navigation_map, get/set_navigation_layer_value, get/set_avoidance_layer_value, get/set_avoidance_mask_value).\n\nPatina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:7544-7645 (2D) and :1529-1618 (3D) register properties+signals and ZERO methods. No dispatch arm exists in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs (node method table, :1242-1916) or in gdscript-interop, so a script call lands on engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:11209-11218 and throws `UndefinedFunction`. Meanwhile engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:1742-1747 and :1780-1785 integrate the agent and write `position` back onto the NavigationAgent node itself (given a position only by engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/class_defaults.rs:222), so the character body a Godot project actually parents the agent to never moves. `process_navigation` also reads only `target_position` (main_loop.rs:1643) — `path_desired_distance`, `target_desired_distance`, `max_speed`, `path_height_offset` set in a .tscn are inert during path following.\n\nImplementation approach: (1) register the full method list on both classes in class_db.rs next to the existing property/signal builders; (2) add a `navigation_agents` dispatch module reachable from `SceneAccess::call_node_method` in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs that resolves the node's backing `NavigationAgent2D`/`3D` in `MainLoop::nav_agents_2d/3d` (main_loop.rs:507-511) and answers each method, including path recomputation on `get_next_path_position` when the target moved; (3) split `process_navigation` (main_loop.rs:1498) into a *path maintenance* pass (rebuild map, recompute path, advance waypoint index, publish `next_path_position`) and REMOVE the `set_position` writes at :1743 and :1781 so the agent stops teleporting itself; (4) sync `path_desired_distance`, `target_desired_distance`, `max_speed`, `path_height_offset`, `navigation_layers` from the node each tick the same way AvoidanceNodeParams does (main_loop.rs:186-256).\n\nWiring requirement: .tscn with NavigationRegion2D + CharacterBody2D whose child NavigationAgent2D has a script calling `get_next_path_position()` in `_physics_process` → MainLoop::step → interpreter dispatch → real Vector2 → `move_and_slide()` moves the BODY across the navmesh; the agent node's own transform must not change.

**Merged findings (2):** NavigationAgent2D/3D script API (get_next_path_position, is_navigation_finished, is_target_reached/reachable, distance_to_target, get_current_navigation_path[_index], get_final_position, get_path_length, set_velocity[_forced], get/set_navigation_map, get_rid, get/set_navigation_layer_value, get/set_avoidance_layer/mask_value, get_current_navigation_result) + the "agent does not move anything" contract; NavigationAgent2D/3D signals path_changed, waypoint_reached, link_reached (and per-frame ordering of target_reached vs navigation_finished)

**Prove it:** Loading a .tscn where a CharacterBody2D's child NavigationAgent2D is driven by a GDScript `_physics_process` that calls `get_next_path_position()` and `move_and_slide()` moves the CharacterBody2D from start to target across a NavigationRegion2D, while the NavigationAgent2D's own `position` stays at its authored value; `is_navigation_finished()` returns false mid-route and true on arrival; `distance_to_target()` decreases monotonically; the same script pattern works for CharacterBody3D/NavigationAgent3D. (test: `nav_agent_script_api_moves_parent_body`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test nav_agent_script_api_moves_parent_body`.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn where a CharacterBody2D's child NavigationAgent2D is driven by a GDScript `_physics_process` that calls `get_next_path_position()` and `move_and_slide()` moves the CharacterBody2D from start to target across a NavigationRegion2D, while the NavigationAgent2D's own `position` stays at its authored value; `is_navigation_finished()` returns false mid-route and true on arrival; `distance_to_target()` decreases monotonically; the same script pattern works for CharacterBody3D/NavigationAgent3D. (test: `nav_agent_script_api_moves_parent_body`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test nav_agent_script_api_moves_parent_body`.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
AmberForge handoff — I briefly held this bead, made ONE substantive fix, then it was reassigned
away mid-work. The change is already in the working tree (uncommitted). Do not redo it; do not be
surprised by it.

DONE (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, both the 2D and 3D agent update blocks):
  Stopped the NavigationAgent node teleporting itself.

  Before: each tick ran `agent.step(current, dt, &others)` - an internal simulation of the agent
  walking its own path - then wrote that simulated point onto the agent node via
  node2d::set_position / node3d::set_position, and derived `next_path_position` from the SIMULATED
  point.

  Two bugs from that one line:
   (a) the agent node teleported away from its authored position and away from its parent body;
   (b) `next_path_position` advanced on the simulation's schedule, not as the body actually moved.

  After: no self-simulation and no write to the agent's transform. `next` is now
  `agent.get_next_path_position(*current)` - the agent's REAL position. That function already
  contains the whole mechanism (it consumes waypoints against the position handed to it and pushes
  WaypointReached), so feeding it the real position makes progress follow the body, which is
  Godot's passive-agent behaviour. The blocks now publish `next_path_position` only.

  rustfmt clean; `agent.step` has no remaining callers on these paths.

NOT DONE (the rest of the bead):
 1. ClassDB method surface. NavigationAgent2D (class_db.rs:7918) and NavigationAgent3D (:1632) are
    registered with PROPERTIES AND SIGNALS ONLY - zero `.method(..)` entries (verified: 0 hits).
    SceneTree's script dispatch gates on class_has_method, so get_next_path_position(),
    is_navigation_finished(), distance_to_target() etc. are ALL unreachable from GDScript. This is
    the same shape as pat-s3rrv.23 slice 1, which I closed green - see that registration for the
    pattern.
 2. Node-method dispatch arms in gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs + gdscene/src/scripting.rs.
 3. NavAgentSignal milestones are computed but never emitted: navigation.rs:1019-1031 defines
    PathChanged/WaypointReached/TargetReached/NavigationFinished/VelocityComputed and they are
    pushed at :1149/:1163/etc, but nothing drains pending_signals into emit_signal.
 4. Sync path_desired_distance / target_desired_distance / max_speed / path_height_offset /
    navigation_layers from the node each tick (the bead suggests mirroring AvoidanceNodeParams).
 5. The acceptance test itself.

⚠️ The acceptance is runtime movement over frames (body crosses a NavigationRegion2D while the
agent's own position stays authored). Useful prior: a body sitting at EXACTLY its spawn position
means the update loop never ran for it, not that the movement maths is subtly wrong - check
registration/dispatch first.

title: Honor MeshInstance3D.skin: load the Skin resource's binds instead of always synthesizing a rest skin
description:
[audit-key: rendering/rendering-3d-skin-resource-binds] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/skin.cpp + scene/3d/skeleton_3d.cpp (register_skin/SkinReference); doc/classes/Skin.xml; extension_api.json Skin(Resource, 11 methods), SkinReference(RefCounted, 2 methods)

**Godot classes:** Skin, SkinReference

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-6] The skinning MATH is real and wired: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/skin.rs:60 `pub struct Skin` + `skin_matrices`/`skin_mesh`, consumed each frame by /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:565 `gdserver3d::skin::skin_mesh(base, &skin, &poses)`. But the Skin RESOURCE is never read: `resolve_skin` at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:661-670 unconditionally rebuilds a default skin from the skeleton rest (`for (bone, rest) in skeleton3d::bone_rest_array(...) { skin.add_bind_from_rest(bone, rest) }`) — it never looks at the MeshInstance3D's `skin` property. `Skin` and `SkinReference` are absent from the 638-name `ClassRegistration::new` list, so `[sub_resource type="Skin"]` in a .tscn cannot resolve; `class_db.rs:1086` only declares a `skin` PropertyInfo of `Variant::Nil` on the node. Consequence: any imported rig whose Skin carries non-rest inverse-bind matrices or name-based bone remapping (the normal glTF/Blender case) deforms with the wrong bind poses, silently.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/skin.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

**Godot ground truth:** `Skin : Resource` holds an ordered bind list — `add_bind(bone, pose)`, `add_named_bind(name, pose)`, `set_bind_pose`/`get_bind_pose`, `set_bind_bone`/`get_bind_bone`, `set_bind_name`/`get_bind_name`, `clear_binds` (11 methods). `MeshInstance3D.skin` selects it; when null the skeleton supplies `create_skin_from_rest_transforms()`. `Skeleton3D.register_skin(skin)` returns a `SkinReference` (RefCounted) holding the resolved bone indices and the live bind matrix array. Source: `upstream/godot/scene/resources/skin.cpp`, `scene/3d/skeleton_3d.cpp`.

**Patina today:** the math is present and driven every frame — `crates/gdserver3d/src/skin.rs:60 Skin` with `skin_matrices`/`skin_mesh`, called at `crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:565`. But the resource is ignored: `resolve_skin` (`render_server_3d.rs:661-670`) always rebuilds a default skin from `skeleton3d::bone_rest_array` and never reads the MeshInstance3D's `skin` property. `Skin` and `SkinReference` are not in ClassDB (absent from the 638 registrations; `class_db.rs:1086` only declares a `skin` PropertyInfo of `Variant::Nil`), so `[sub_resource type="Skin"]` in a .tscn cannot resolve at all. Any imported rig whose Skin carries non-rest inverse-bind matrices or name-based bone remapping — the normal glTF/Blender case — therefore deforms with wrong bind poses and does so silently, since the rest-derived fallback always renders *something*.

**Implement:** register `Skin` (Resource) and `SkinReference` (RefCounted) in `class_db.rs`. Teach `resolve_skin` to take the MeshInstance3D node id, read its `skin` property (SubResource copy or `Variant::Resource`), and build the `gdserver3d::skin::Skin` from the resource's `bind/N/bone`, `bind/N/name` and `bind/N/pose` entries — resolving named binds against `Skeleton3D` bone names — falling back to the rest-derived skin only when `skin` is null. Add a `SkinReference` handle so `Skeleton3D.register_skin` is script-callable.

**Wiring requirement:** the per-frame 3D sync path must build its skin from the MeshInstance3D's Skin resource, so a .tscn rig with explicit binds renders with those binds in the runner and the editor viewport.

**Prove it:** an app-level test loading a .tscn with a Skeleton3D, a skinned MeshInstance3D and a `[sub_resource type="Skin"]` whose bind poses are deliberately NOT the rest inverses (e.g. one bind offset by a known translation), ticking a frame, and asserting the deformed vertex positions match the explicit-bind expectation and differ from the rest-derived fallback — the assertion must fail if `resolve_skin` reverts to the rest path. Also assert a named bind resolves to the right bone index.

**Prove it:** A .tscn MeshInstance3D with an explicit `[sub_resource type="Skin"]` whose bind poses differ from the skeleton rest inverses deforms its mesh using those binds after one frame (vertex positions match the explicit-bind expectation and differ measurably from the rest-derived fallback), and a named bind resolves to the correct Skeleton3D bone index (test: `mesh_instance_skin_resource_binds_drive_deformation`)
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn MeshInstance3D with an explicit `[sub_resource type="Skin"]` whose bind poses differ from the skeleton rest inverses deforms its mesh using those binds after one frame (vertex positions match the explicit-bind expectation and differ measurably from the rest-derived fallback), and a named bind resolves to the correct Skeleton3D bone index (test: `mesh_instance_skin_resource_binds_drive_deformation`)

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## The implementation was already delivered — the missing piece was the SEAM test

EmeraldIsland, 2026-08-20.

### ⚠️ The description is stale

It claims `Skin`/`SkinReference` are "absent from the 638-name registration list"
and that `resolve_skin` "never looks at the MeshInstance3D's `skin` property".
Both are false today:

- `Skin` at class_db.rs:1734, `SkinReference` at :1755 (with its two upstream
  methods `get_skeleton` / `get_skin`);
- `resolve_skin` takes `mesh_node` and tries `authored_skin` FIRST, falling back
  to the rest-derived skin only on `None`;
- `packed_scene` flattens the sub-resource to `__skin__*`; `scene_saver` filters
  it back out.

None of that needed redoing.

### 🔑 The real gap: each half was tested, the composition was not

`skin_resource_binds.rs` split the feature down the middle and never joined it:

- `an_inline_skin_sub_resource_reaches_the_node` stops once the `__skin__*`
  companions land on the node;
- every deformation test starts from `rig()`, a tree built by hand with `set()`.

So a break in the seam between "the companions arrived" and "the companions were
read" left the entire file GREEN. The acceptance asks for exactly the joined path:
a `.tscn` skin deforming the mesh after a frame.

### ⚠️ Why the existing `SCENE` fixture cannot be reused for it

Two independent reasons, recorded so nobody tries:

1. its `Skel` declares **no bones at all**;
2. its two bind poses **are** the rest inverses — the coincidence point where a
   correct engine and one ignoring the skin both return the identity.

That is the same trap `rig()`'s own doc warns about ("the bone rests must not be
identity").

### The new fixture distinguishes THREE answers

Authored entirely in `.tscn`, bones included as `bones/{idx}/name|parent|rest`
node properties — what Godot writes, and what `get_bone_count` infers from when a
scene-loaded skeleton has no `_bone_count`.

The bind names `b1`, leaves `bind/0/bone` at Godot's `-1` default, identity pose.
With `deformed = global_rest(bone) * bind_pose * vertex`:

| engine behaviour                      | vertex   |
|---------------------------------------|----------|
| resolves the NAME to bone 1 (correct)  | (5,0,0)  |
| ignores the skin, rest-derived fallback| (0,0,0)  |
| trusts `bone = -1`, clamps to bone 0   | (0,3,0)  |

Three DISJOINT coordinates, so a failure names the defect instead of merely
reporting one — and the acceptance's two clauses (binds drive deformation; a named
bind resolves correctly) stay separated rather than conflated.

Paired with a differential control that strips ONLY the `skin` reference from the
same fixture, and asserts the strip actually happened so it cannot decay into a
copy of the test it controls for. A bone-count precondition is asserted FIRST, so
`(0,0,0)` can never be misread as "skin ignored" when the cause is "zero bones".

### Still open, outside the acceptance

`Skeleton3D.register_skin` is NOT script-callable — the name appears only in a
comment (class_db.rs:1748) and is registered nowhere.

⚠️ Do not "quickly add" it to ClassDB: a registration with no dispatch arm yields
`has_method("register_skin") == true` and a call that returns `Nil` silently, which
is worse than the honest absence. Doing it properly means constructing a
`SkinReference` Variant in the interpreter. Worth its own bead.

title: Make SurfaceTool script-callable and complete its 33-method surface
description:
[audit-key: rendering/rendering-3d-surface-tool] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/surface_tool.cpp; doc/classes/SurfaceTool.xml; extension_api.json SurfaceTool(RefCounted, 33 methods)

**Godot classes:** SurfaceTool

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-6] A `SurfaceTool` exists in Rust — /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs:41-130 (`begin`, `add_vertex`, `add_index`, `commit`), re-exported at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/lib.rs:55 — but nothing script-facing can reach it: `SurfaceTool` is absent from the 638-name `ClassRegistration::new` list, and `rg -n 'SurfaceTool' crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` returns zero hits, so `SurfaceTool.new()` and `ClassDB.instantiate("SurfaceTool")` both fail (the interpreter's only `instantiate` arm, interpreter.rs:10219, rejects everything except PackedScene). Coverage is 5 of Godot's 33 methods: no `set_normal`/`set_uv`/`set_uv2`/`set_color`/`set_tangent`/`set_bones`/`set_weights`/`set_custom`/`set_smooth_group`, no `add_triangle_fan`, no `generate_normals`/`generate_tangents`/`generate_lod`, no `index`/`deindex`/`optimize_indices_for_cache`, no `append_from`, no `create_from`/`create_from_arrays`/`create_from_blend_shape`, no `commit_to_arrays`, no `set_material`/`set_skin_weight_count`/`set_custom_format`.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

**Godot ground truth:** `SurfaceTool : RefCounted` is the procedural mesh builder scripts use — `begin(primitive)`, per-vertex attribute setters applied before `add_vertex` (`set_normal`, `set_tangent`, `set_color`, `set_uv`, `set_uv2`, `set_bones`, `set_weights`, `set_custom`, `set_smooth_group`), `add_vertex`, `add_index`, `add_triangle_fan`, `index`/`deindex`, `generate_normals(flip)`, `generate_tangents`, `generate_lod`, `optimize_indices_for_cache`, `append_from(mesh, surface, transform)`, `create_from(mesh, surface)`, `create_from_arrays`, `create_from_blend_shape`, `set_material`, `set_custom_format`, `set_skin_weight_count`, `commit(existing, flags) -> ArrayMesh`, `commit_to_arrays`, `clear` (33 methods total). Source: `upstream/godot/scene/resources/surface_tool.cpp`.

**Patina today:** a Rust `SurfaceTool` exists at `crates/gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs:41-130` with 5 operations (`begin`, `add_vertex`, `add_index`, `commit`) and is re-exported at `gdserver3d/src/lib.rs:55` — but no script can reach it. `SurfaceTool` is not in ClassDB (absent from the 638 `ClassRegistration::new` names) and appears nowhere in the GDScript interpreter (`rg -n 'SurfaceTool' crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` = 0 hits); the interpreter's only `instantiate` arm (`interpreter.rs:10219`) rejects every class except PackedScene. So `SurfaceTool.new()` fails and procedural mesh generation from GDScript — a very common game pattern — is impossible.

**Implement:** register `SurfaceTool` (parent RefCounted) in `class_db.rs`. Extend the Rust struct in `mesh.rs` with the staged per-vertex attribute setters, index/deindex, `generate_normals`/`generate_tangents`, `append_from`/`create_from`, `set_material` and `commit_to_arrays`, producing an `ArrayMesh`-compatible surface. Add an interpreter object type (mirroring how another RefCounted handle is already exposed) so `SurfaceTool.new()` returns a live handle whose method calls mutate it and whose `commit()` returns a Mesh resource assignable to a MeshInstance3D's `mesh`.

**Wiring requirement:** a GDScript in a played scene must be able to build a mesh with SurfaceTool, assign `commit()` to a MeshInstance3D's `mesh`, and have the 3D render pass draw it that frame.

**Prove it:** an app-level test whose script begins a TRIANGLES surface, sets normals/UVs/colors per vertex, adds a two-triangle quad, calls `generate_normals`, commits to a MeshInstance3D, ticks a frame, and asserts the render instance carries 6 vertices with the expected UVs, per-vertex colors and the generated face normal.

**Prove it:** A GDScript in a played scene calls `SurfaceTool.new()`, builds a two-triangle quad with per-vertex normals/UVs/colors, calls `generate_normals()` and assigns `commit()` to a MeshInstance3D's `mesh`; after one frame the 3D render instance carries 6 vertices with the expected UVs, per-vertex colors and generated face normal (test: `surface_tool_builds_mesh_from_script`)
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript in a played scene calls `SurfaceTool.new()`, builds a two-triangle quad with per-vertex normals/UVs/colors, calls `generate_normals()` and assigns `commit()` to a MeshInstance3D's `mesh`; after one frame the 3D render instance carries 6 vertices with the expected UVs, per-vertex colors and generated face normal (test: `surface_tool_builds_mesh_from_script`)

title: Rendering2D: BackBufferCopy node + SCREEN_TEXTURE sampling in canvas_item shaders
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/backbuffer-screen-texture] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: STUB]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/2d/back_buffer_copy.cpp; RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_copy_to_backbuffer; canvas_item shader `hint_screen_texture` / SCREEN_TEXTURE + SCREEN_UV

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## ROOT CAUSE: `parse_uniforms` scanned LINES, and a `.tscn` shader is ONE line

EmeraldIsland, 2026-08-20. Correcting my own comment above.

### ⚠️ My previous comment was wrong

I wrote that the implementation was complete and only the test coverage was
missing. I had verified the `hint_screen_texture` handling EXISTS in all three
crates and inferred it worked. **Existence is not composition** — the trap I had
been flagging on other beads the same day. The first real run of this file
disproved it.

### The defect

`gdserver2d::shader::parse_uniforms` iterated `source.lines()` and required
`trimmed.starts_with("uniform ")`.

A `.tscn` stores a shader as a single `code = "..."` string, so the entire program
arrives on **ONE line, beginning with `shader_type`**. The scan therefore found
**zero uniforms** in any scene-authored shader — not just screen textures, every
uniform default too.

Consequence for this bead: `screen_uniforms` was empty, so `is_screen_sampler`
(`gdrender2d/src/draw.rs:307`) never matched `screen_tex`, and the sampler fell
through to the sprite's own white texture. A sprite sampling itself, which is
precisely the failure mode the test's message describes.

🔑 Only the hint spelling broke, because the legacy `texture(SCREEN_TEXTURE, …)`
needs no uniform DECLARATION. The bug was invisible to every path that did not
need a declared uniform — which is why `.183` looked complete.

### The fix

Strip `//` comments, then normalise `;`, `{` and `}` to newlines before scanning.
Strictly a SUPERSET of the old behaviour: line breaks survive the normalisation,
so every declaration the old scan found is still found, plus those sharing a line.

### ⚠️ My first fix was wrong — simulation caught it before submitting

Splitting on `;` alone breaks `parse_multiple_uniforms`:

    uniform float speed = 2.0;
    uniform int count = 5;
    void fragment() {}          <-- NO semicolon
    uniform bool enabled = true;

`void fragment() {}` carries no `;`, so the following `uniform bool enabled` is
absorbed into that segment and the count silently drops 3 -> 2. **Braces are
statement separators too.**

I re-ran every existing `parse_uniforms` case by hand against the corrected
version — `parse_uniform_float`, `_with_hint`, `_no_default`,
`parse_multiple_uniforms`, `canvas_item_wgsl_mix_expression` — all unchanged.

### The composition, verified link by link this time

    resolve_canvas_shader_material   viewport_2d_render.rs:1301
      -> Shader::new(CanvasItem, src)
      -> parse_uniforms(source)      shader.rs:78  (fills .uniforms)
      -> hint_screen_texture filter  viewport_2d_render.rs:2993
      -> is_screen_sampler           draw.rs:307

No literal `Shader { … }` construction bypasses `new` on that path.

### Note on coverage

Fail-fast cancelled after the first failure, so **3 of the 4 tests in the gdeditor
file have still never executed**, including the SCREEN_UV shift test I added last
pass.

## Diagnosis from a no-build lane (EmeraldIsland, 2026-08-20)

I did NOT claim this bead — no code changed. Handing over the elimination work so
whoever takes it starts seven links further along.

### The failure is structural, not a shading tolerance

Both failing assertions report the normal-mapped and flat values as **identical
to the last digit**:

```
a_right_facing_normal_darkens_a_pixel...   got bumpy=0.94600755 flat=0.94600755
a_flat_normal_map_...has_far_less_variation  got bumpy=0.05399245 flat=0.05399245
```

Bit-identical means the normal map contributes **nothing** — `canvas_surface_buffer`
is almost certainly returning an all-`None` buffer, so every pixel takes the flat
path. This is not a "shading is slightly off" bug; some link returns empty.

### Links I verified as CORRECT (do not re-check these)

1. **The fixture's `.tscn`** declares `[sub_resource type="CanvasTexture"]` with
   `normal_texture = ExtResource("1_n")`, and the Sprite2D's
   `texture = SubResource("CanvasTexture_1")`.
2. **The flatten guard** (`gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:1817`) requires the
   sub-resource's class to be exactly `"CanvasTexture"` — the fixture satisfies it.
3. **ExtResource resolution** (`packed_scene.rs:1834-1840`) rewrites
   `"ExtResource:1_n"` into `Variant::String(<path>)`, so the flattened key is a
   real path string and not an unresolved id.
4. **The consumer** (`gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:3638`) reads
   `__canvas_texture__normal_texture` and requires `Variant::String` non-empty —
   which item 3 produces.
5. **The cache** is populated: the test injects `res://wall_d.png` and
   `res://wall_n.png` via `TextureCache::insert`, and passes `Some(&mut cache)`.
6. **The wiring** in `render_runtime_canvas` (`viewport_2d_render.rs:3804-3807`)
   builds the surface buffer BEFORE the cache moves into the rasterizer and then
   calls `shade_runtime_canvas_with_surfaces(tree, &mut fb, &surfaces)`. There is
   even a comment explaining the reborrow ordering.
7. **No `__`-prefix filtering** exists on instantiation, so the flattened keys

The remaining candidates all need one execution to separate, and all of them
produce exactly the observed all-`None` buffer:

**One print settles it**: log `node.get_property("__canvas_texture__normal_texture")`

title: Decals3D: sample the decal albedo/normal/orm/emission textures during projection
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/decal-textures] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/decal.cpp — texture_albedo/normal/orm/emission are projected onto geometry with albedo_mix, normal_fade, emission_energy and modulate

**Godot classes:** Decal

**Patina today:**
- [rendering-3d] gdserver3d/src/decal.rs:260 `sample_alpha` computes `vertical_fade * distance_fade * albedo_mix` from the projected point and returns a scalar — it never indexes any texture. The software decal pass (gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs:1081 `apply_decal_pass`) blends `decal.modulate` by that alpha, so the four texture channels are decoded, transported and discarded. The GPU path drops decals entirely (see the wgpu trait-gap finding).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/decal.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: a Decal projects `texture_albedo` (blended by albedo_mix and modulate), `texture_normal` (blended by normal_fade against the surface normal), `texture_orm` (AO/roughness/metallic override) and `texture_emission` (scaled by emission_energy) onto every surface inside its oriented box, with upper/lower fade and distance fade. See upstream/godot/scene/3d/decal.cpp and doc/classes/Decal.xml.

Patina current state: only the box test and the fades are implemented. engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/decal.rs:260 `sample_alpha` returns `vertical_fade * distance_fade * albedo_mix` — a scalar computed from geometry alone, with no texture lookup anywhere in the function. The software pass gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs:1081 `apply_decal_pass` then blends the decal's flat `modulate` colour by that alpha. So `texture_albedo` is parsed off the node, decoded, carried into the renderer, and never read. (The GPU path is worse — it drops decals entirely; that is tracked separately as the wgpu RenderingServer3D trait-gap bead, which this one depends on for the GPU half.)

Implementation approach: (1) change `Decal3D::sample_alpha` into `sample(world_point, camera_distance) -> Option<DecalSample>` returning the projected (u,v) plus the sampled albedo RGBA, normal, ORM and emission from the decal's `TextureImage` channels, still folded with the fades and `albedo_mix`; (2) in `apply_decal_pass` blend the sampled albedo (times modulate) over the fragment, perturb the shaded normal by the sampled normal map weighted by `normal_fade`, override roughness/metallic from ORM, and add emission * emission_energy; (3) mirror the same sampling in the GPU decal pass added by the trait-gap bead so both backends agree.

Wiring requirement: Decal node with texture_albedo in a .tscn -> decal snapshot -> decal pass -> the texture's pattern visible on the receiving surface.

**Prove it:** A .tscn Decal with a two-colour checker `texture_albedo` projected onto a white floor renders that checker pattern on the floor (two distinct colours inside the decal footprint), where today the footprint is a single flat colour. An emission texture brightens only its lit texels. (test: `decal_texture_projects_pixels`) — loads the scene from a .tscn string, renders through the editor 3D render path, and asserts at least two distinct colours inside the decal footprint and one outside.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn Decal with a two-colour checker `texture_albedo` projected onto a white floor renders that checker pattern on the floor (two distinct colours inside the decal footprint), where today the footprint is a single flat colour. An emission texture brightens only its lit texels. (test: `decal_texture_projects_pixels`) — loads the scene from a .tscn string, renders through the editor 3D render path, and asserts at least two distinct colours inside the decal footprint and one outside.

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## The decal projection is CORRECT — the test's screen-axis expectation is wrong

Diagnosis from a no-build lane (EmeraldIsland, 2026-08-20). I did NOT claim this
bead — no code changed.

### The failing assertion

`the_projection_uses_both_uv_axes`:

> a texture varying in v must split the footprint near-to-far, i.e. top-to-bottom
> on screen; centroids at y=77.8 and y=77.9

The **u** half of the same test passes.

### `project_point` is right

`gdserver3d/src/decal.rs:226` maps

```
u <- local.x     v <- local.z     w <- local.y   (the projection depth axis)
```

That is Godot's decal convention: the box projects along local -Y with X/Z as the
UV plane. Nothing here needs changing.

### 🔑 The expectation is unsatisfiable under the camera this path actually uses

`render_editor_3d_frame` draws from the **Viewport3D orbit camera**, whose default
is `yaw: FRAC_PI_4` — **45 degrees** (`gdeditor/src/viewport_3d.rs:114`). At 45
degrees the camera's right vector is `(cos45, 0, -sin45)`, so:

- world **+X projects to screen RIGHT**
- world **+Z projects to screen LEFT**

Both are **horizontal**, with opposite sign, and neither has a vertical
component. A v-varying texture (v <- `local.z`) therefore cannot split
top-to-bottom on screen — the two centroids land at the same y, which is exactly
the 77.8 / 77.9 the test reports.

⚠️ This is a known trap in this codebase: the editor 3D frame ignores the scene's
`Camera3D` and renders from the orbit camera. The assertion was written expecting
scene-camera semantics.

### The robust replacement

Do not assert an absolute direction — assert the two axes against **each other**:

```
sign(dx of the 2x1 u-texture centroids) == -sign(dx of the 1x2 v-texture centroids)
```

i.e. both split horizontally, in OPPOSITE order.

Why this is the right shape:

- It still catches a transposed UV, which is the whole point of the guard — a u/v
  swap flips the sign relationship.
- It does not depend on which side is near or far, so it survives any yaw the
  default camera later adopts.
- Neither half can pass vacuously, because each is checked against the other
  rather than against a constant.

⚠️ **Keep** the existing "the other axis stays put" assertions — they are correct,
and they are what stops a single-colour footprint passing.

### Why this was handed over rather than fixed

The replacement is a render assertion and I cannot run a renderer to confirm the
centroids separate far enough to be measurable. The diagnosis above is verified
against source; the edit is a few minutes for a lane that can run the test once.

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## Fixed — and ⚠️ my own earlier recommendation above was WRONG

EmeraldIsland, 2026-08-20. Follow-up to my 15:59 diagnosis. The diagnosis held; the
REPLACEMENT ASSERTION I proposed in it did not, and would have quietly destroyed
the guard.

### The diagnosis, re-verified against the current tree

- `render_editor_3d_frame` renders "from the editor camera"
  (`viewport_3d_render.rs`), NOT the scene's `Camera3D`. The test's own doc
  comment said "with the camera on the +z axis looking down -z", describing the
  scene camera — that premise was the bug.
- `ViewportCamera3D::right() = (cos yaw, 0, -sin yaw)`; default yaw `FRAC_PI_4`
  (`viewport_3d.rs`). So world **+x → screen RIGHT**, world **+z → screen LEFT**.
  Both horizontal, no vertical component ⇒ "v splits top-to-bottom" is
  unsatisfiable for ANY correct projection. Observed centroids 0.1px apart in y.

### 🔑 Why "assert the two axes are opposite" was the wrong fix

That was my recommendation. It does NOT catch a u/v transpose:

    correct:    sign(u split) = -,  sign(v split) = +   -> opposite
    transposed: sign(u split) = +,  sign(v split) = -   -> STILL opposite

Swapping u and v flips BOTH signs, so the relationship survives the exact bug the
test exists to catch. The test header calls itself "🔑 The transpose guard".
Landing my own suggestion would have left it green and blind.

**Lesson worth generalising: a purely RELATIONAL assertion between two quantities
is invariant under swapping them.** If the bug you are guarding against IS the
swap, at least one endpoint must be pinned absolutely.

### What landed

- both axes split horizontally, neither splits vertically (all this camera can
  show);
- plus ONE absolute claim, which is the transpose catcher:
  **`u`'s low texel must land LEFT of its high texel** (`urx < ugx`).

Derivation: `texture_file` writes texel 0 at x=0; `u = (local.x/he.x)*0.5 + 0.5`
increases with `local.x`; `DECAL_HEAD` carries no `transform` so local IS world;
+x projects screen-right. Under a transpose the low texel tracks world z, which
runs the other way, and this flips.

⚠️ `v`'s absolute direction is deliberately NOT asserted: whether the sampler
treats texture row 0 as `v=0` or flips it is the one inference I could not settle
from source, and `u` alone suffices. One claim I can fully derive beats two where
one is a guess.

⚠️ `urx < ugx` is DERIVED, not observed — the u half passed, so no centroid values
were ever printed. The failure message prints both, so a wrong sign is a one-line
fix on the next run.

### Interference check with pat-s3rrv.122 (my own earlier change)

This test's binary (01:17) PREDATES the `should_cull` wiring (renderer.rs 01:31),
so the recorded failure came from a build with no face culling at all. The floor
is a single-sided `PlaneMesh`; viewed from above its winding is clockwise on
screen = front-facing, so the corrected `CullMode::Back` KEEPS it. No regression.
(The old inverted rule would have culled it — incidental extra evidence that fix
was right.)
