- [vfx-particles] All 8 classes are ClassDB-registered but have no simulation whatsoever: `grep -rn 'GPUParticlesAttractor|GPUParticlesCollision|attractor' /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/ /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/ /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver2d/src/` returns only two unrelated hits in gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:1421,1423 about Area2D point gravity. The simulators have no collider or attractor input at all — `ParticleSimulator::step_exact` (particle.rs:647-796) applies only gravity, and `grep -c 'collision_mode\|collision_friction\|collision_bounce\|particle_flag' gdscene/src/main_loop.rs` = 0. The module doc at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/particle.rs:20-24 states it: "This module has no collider input at all: a particle's only per-step force is gravity, so particles pass through every body in the scene. collision_mode/collision_friction/collision_bounce are unhonored." The tests confirm registration-only scope: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/tests/particle_attractor_classes_test.rs:3-6 ("The simulator half ... is follow-up") and /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/tests/particles_collision.rs:12-14 ("SCOPE: registration only ... attractor forces and box/sphere bounce in the CPU sim, wired through process_particles — NOT delivered").

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/particle.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/particle3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: GPUParticlesAttractor3D nodes pull or push particles within their volume — `strength` (negative repels), `attenuation` (falloff exponent over the normalized distance), `directionality` (0 = radial toward the attractor center, 1 = along the attractor's -Z axis), `cull_mask` (matched against the emitter's layers). Shapes: Box3D (`size`), Sphere3D (`radius`), VectorField3D (`size` + a `texture` of per-cell directions). Attractors only affect emitters whose material has `attractor_interaction_enabled`. GPUParticlesCollision3D nodes stop particles: Box3D/Sphere3D analytic volumes, HeightField3D, SDF3D baked field. The response is chosen by ParticleProcessMaterial.collision_mode — COLLISION_DISABLED(0), COLLISION_RIGID(1) which bounces using `collision_bounce` and `collision_friction`, COLLISION_HIDE_ON_CONTACT(2) which kills the particle — with `collision_use_scale` scaling the particle's collision radius by its scale. See upstream/godot/scene/3d/gpu_particles_attractor_3d.cpp and gpu_particles_collision_3d.cpp.\n\nPATINA CURRENT STATE: all eight classes are registered in ClassDB and instantiate with the right properties, but nothing simulates them. `grep -rn 'GPUParticlesAttractor|GPUParticlesCollision|attractor' gdscene/src/ gdserver3d/src/ gdserver2d/src/` returns only two unrelated Area2D point-gravity comments (gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:1421,1423). `ParticleSimulator::step_exact` (gdscene/src/particle.rs:647-796) applies gravity and nothing else — there is no collider or attractor input parameter on the function at all. main_loop.rs never reads collision_mode/collision_friction/collision_bounce/attractor_interaction_enabled (all grep counts 0). The module doc at particle.rs:20-24 admits particles "pass through every body in the scene". The tests are explicit about being registration-only: gdobject/tests/particle_attractor_classes_test.rs:3-6 and gdobject/tests/particles_collision.rs:12-14.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION — STAGE THIS BEAD; stage 1 covers attractors + analytic box/sphere collision (VectorField, HeightField and SDF are follow-ups): (1) Define a `ParticleField` input struct in gdscene/src/particle3d.rs holding the frame's attractor volumes (global transform, shape, strength, attenuation, directionality, cull_mask) and collider volumes (global transform, shape, cull_mask), plus the emitter's collision_mode/friction/bounce/use_scale. (2) Change `ParticleSimulator3D::step` to accept `&ParticleField` and, inside the integration loop, add each in-range attractor's acceleration before the position update, then resolve collisions after it: for COLLISION_RIGID reflect the velocity about the contact normal scaled by `collision_bounce` and damp the tangential component by `collision_friction`, pushing the particle back out of the volume; for COLLISION_HIDE_ON_CONTACT mark the particle dead. (3) In gdscene/src/main_loop.rs `process_particles` (:645), collect GPUParticlesAttractor*3D and GPUParticlesCollision*3D nodes from the tree in the same pass that collects emitters (:662-673), build the `ParticleField` from their global transforms, and pass it to each 3D simulator step at :915-925. (4) Mirror a 2D subset (circle/rect attractors and colliders) into gdscene/src/particle.rs, which is the path 2D emitters use, so the feature is not 3D-only. (5) Record AT_COLLISION sub-emitter events at the contact point, which makes `SubEmitterMode::AtCollision` (already defined at particle.rs:395-397 and currently inert) live.\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: a plain `.tscn` containing an emitter plus an attractor/collider sibling → MainLoop::step → the published particle positions bend toward the attractor and stop at the collider surface.

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a GPUParticles3D firing straight up and a GPUParticlesAttractorSphere3D offset to one side bends the cloud toward the attractor, while the identical scene with `strength` negated bends it away — and with the attractor deleted the cloud stays straight. A GPUParticlesCollisionBox3D placed in the fall path of a gravity-driven emitter stops the particles at its surface instead of letting them pass through. Test `particle_attractors_and_collision_in_scene` (cargo nextest --test particle_attractors_and_collision_in_scene) loads each scene, steps MainLoop 90 frames, reads MainLoop::particle_positions_3d, and asserts (a) mean particle x is displaced toward the attractor by more than one attractor radius vs the no-attractor control, (b) the negated-strength case is displaced the opposite way, (c) with a collider at y = -50 and COLLISION_RIGID, no particle's y goes below -50 minus the collision radius, whereas the collision-disabled control has particles well below it, and (d) COLLISION_HIDE_ON_CONTACT drops the live count to zero after contact (test: `particle_attractors_and_collision_in_scene`)

A GPUParticlesCollisionBox3D placed in the fall path of a gravity-driven emitter stops the particles at its surface instead of letting them pass through. Test `particle_attractors_and_collision_in_scene` (cargo nextest --test particle_attractors_and_collision_in_scene) loads each scene, steps MainLoop 90 frames, reads MainLoop::particle_positions_3d, and asserts (a) mean particle x is displaced toward the attractor by more than one attractor radius vs the no-attractor control, (b) the negated-strength case is displaced the opposite way, (c) with a collider at y = -50 and COLLISION_RIGID, no particle's y goes below -50 minus the collision radius, whereas the collision-disabled control has particles well below it, and (d) COLLISION_HIDE_ON_CONTACT drops the live count to zero after contact (test: `particle_attractors_and_collision_in_scene`)

title: Web: threaded export variant — worker-backed WorkerThreadPool, honest has_feature("threads"), SAB audio ring
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web-threads] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/platform/web/detect.py (thread_support build variant) + platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_audio.js (SAB ring for the audio worklet) + Godot docs "Exporting for the Web" cross-origin isolation section | extension_api.json classes[Thread,Mutex,Semaphore,WorkerThreadPool]; upstream/godot/core/object/worker_thread_pool.cpp (real task threads when THREADS_ENABLED); Godot's web export supports threads under cross-origin isolation

**Godot classes:** Thread, Mutex, Semaphore, WorkerThreadPool, OS

**Patina today:**
- [web-runtime] crates/gdplatform/src/thread.rs contains no target gating at all (`rg 'target_arch|wasm' crates/gdplatform/src/thread.rs` → 0 hits), so the Thread/Mutex/WorkerThreadPool surface is plain std::thread with no browser Worker path and no single-thread fallback scheduler. `OS.has_feature("threads")` is hardcoded to false on web regardless of the export variant: crates/gdplatform/src/os.rs:92-93 `"threads" => platform != Platform::Web`. The audio worklet uses main-thread message-port block passing only (crates/gdaudio/src/web_output.rs:310-315 `this.port.postMessage("need-block")` / node.port.onmessage), never a SharedArrayBuffer ring, even though cross-origin isolation is already available in the editor dev server (crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:2973). The export's threads flag only emits an HTML comment and a message (crates/gdplatform/src/export.rs:632-639, 1227-1232) — no actual threaded build variant exists.
- [platform-os] engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:17417-17432 states the design: Thread/WorkerThreadPool Callables run inline on the calling thread, so a task is complete before its id is returned, `wait_*` is a no-op and `Semaphore.wait()` cannot block. engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/thread.rs (615 lines: GodotThread, GodotMutex, GodotSemaphore, WorkerThreadPool with real `std::thread`) has ZERO non-test consumers — `grep -rn 'gdplatform::thread' crates/` outside the defining file returns only a test doc-comment (engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/tests/threading.rs:12) and the explanatory comment at interpreter.rs:17424. Nothing in the engine itself (resource loading, navmesh baking, rendering) uses the pool either. Notably the cross-origin isolation half IS done — engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:2973 serves `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` + `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` — so `crossOriginIsolated`/SharedArrayBuffer is reachable and only the thread side is missing. `Thread.set_thread_safety_checks_enabled` is absent (the Thread dispatch covers start/get_id/is_started/is_alive/wait_to_finish/is_main_thread only).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/thread.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/os.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/web_output.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/export.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GROUND TRUTH — Godot ships a `thread_support` web build variant (platform/web/detect.py) that requires COOP/COEP cross-origin isolation; with it, Thread/WorkerThreadPool run on real Web Workers, `OS.has_feature("threads")` is true, and the audio driver feeds the worklet through a SharedArrayBuffer ring instead of message passing (platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_audio.js). Without it the engine runs single-threaded and the feature tag is false. PATINA — engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/thread.rs has no target gating whatsoever (`rg 'target_arch|wasm' crates/gdplatform/src/thread.rs` → 0 hits), so there is neither a worker path nor a documented single-thread fallback; `OS.has_feature("threads")` is hardcoded false on web (crates/gdplatform/src/os.rs:92-93) so a threaded export could never report itself; the audio worklet is message-port only (crates/gdaudio/src/web_output.rs:310-315) despite the editor already serving COOP/COEP (crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:2973); and the export's `threads_enabled` flag emits only an HTML comment and a log line (crates/gdplatform/src/export.rs:632-639, 1227-1232). APPROACH — (1) make `has_feature("threads")` read a runtime capability set by the wasm entry from `self.crossOriginIsolated`, not the target; (2) give crates/gdplatform/src/thread.rs a wasm32 path with a cooperative single-thread fallback scheduler (tasks drained on the frame tick) so `WorkerThreadPool` group tasks complete deterministically without threads, and a worker-backed path behind the threaded variant; (3) add a SharedArrayBuffer ring to crates/gdaudio/src/web_output.rs's worklet glue, used when isolated and falling back to the current postMessage path otherwise. WIRING — required path: script calls `WorkerThreadPool.add_group_task(...)` in a scene under the wasm engine handle; the tasks complete and `wait_for_group_task_completion` returns on both the isolated and non-isolated paths.

**Merged findings (2):** Threads on web: SharedArrayBuffer / wasm-threads WorkerThreadPool, has_feature("threads"), SAB audio ring; Threading: Thread/WorkerThreadPool run Callables inline; gdplatform::thread (real OS threads) has no call path; Thread.set_thread_safety_checks_enabled missing

**Prove it:** With cross-origin isolation reported off, `OS.has_feature("threads")` is false, `WorkerThreadPool` group tasks still all complete via the cooperative scheduler within the frame tick, and the audio worklet glue uses the message-port path; with it reported on, the feature tag is true and the emitted worklet glue uses a SharedArrayBuffer ring. Test: `web_threads_and_shared_memory_story`, runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdplatform --test web_threads_and_shared_memory_story` (test: `web_threads_and_shared_memory_story`)
acceptance_criteria: With cross-origin isolation reported off, `OS.has_feature("threads")` is false, `WorkerThreadPool` group tasks still all complete via the cooperative scheduler within the frame tick, and the audio worklet glue uses the message-port path; with it reported on, the feature tag is true and the emitted worklet glue uses a SharedArrayBuffer ring. Test: `web_threads_and_shared_memory_story`, runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdplatform --test web_threads_and_shared_memory_story` (test: `web_threads_and_shared_memory_story`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
DEFECT FOUND IN CLOSED WORK — triage only, no code, no status change (OrangePuma, 2026-10-30 13:50 UTC).
Reopening is the coordinator's/owner's call; I have not touched the status. This is not a criticism of
the close: both this bead and pat-u3l8c.112 passed their stated acceptance. The acceptance simply never
required the exported site to LOAD the worklet, so a green suite and a silent export are consistent.

THE EXPORTED WEB BUILD EMITS AN AUDIO WORKLET THAT IS NEVER LOADED OR INSTANTIATED.

export.rs:593-597 writes `patina.audio.worklet.js` from web_audio_worklet_glue(web.threads_enabled).
That module ends in:
    export.rs:1232  registerProcessor('patina-audio', PatinaAudio);   // threaded branch
    export.rs:1262  registerProcessor('patina-audio', PatinaAudio);   // non-threaded branch

Nothing in the exported site ever consumes it. Verified by elimination, with a positive control so the
absence is not a truncated-grep artifact:

  - `audioWorklet` / `addModule` across gdplatform/src, patina-web/src, patina-web/web, gdaudio/src
    (tests excluded): exactly ONE hit, gdaudio/src/web_output.rs:309 — and that is inside the OTHER
    glue string, the live-runtime one.
  - `AudioWorkletNode` constructions: exactly ONE, gdaudio/src/web_output.rs:310, same string.
  - fn web_engine_loader_js (export.rs:1348, 47 lines extracted): ZERO hits for audio|worklet.
    Control on the same extraction: 4 hits for canvas|wasm, so the range captured real content.
  - fn web_index_html (export.rs:1270, 74 lines extracted): ZERO hits for audio|worklet.

So the file is written beside the loader and no loader line references it. An AudioWorklet module that
is never passed to audioWorklet.addModule() and never fronted by an AudioWorkletNode produces no sound
at all. The exported game is silent.

THE TWO GLUE PATHS ALSO DISAGREE ON THE PROCESSOR NAME, which means a host page cannot rescue it by
wiring the runtime's name by hand:
    live runtime : patina-web/src/audio.rs:47  PROCESSOR_NAME = "patina-audio-out"
                   -> gdaudio/src/web_output.rs:306/310 register AND construct from the same
                      ${PATINA_PROCESSOR} placeholder, so that path is self-consistent by construction.
    exported site: export.rs:1232/1262 hardcode 'patina-audio'.
"patina-audio-out" != "patina-audio". The doc comment at export.rs:1195-1197 warns about exactly this
class of failure ("if the loader references it throws on load and the page gets no audio at all").

WHY THE SUITE IS GREEN. The only test touching this glue is
gdplatform/tests/web_threads_and_shared_memory_story.rs:166-205, and it calls web_audio_worklet_glue()
DIRECTLY and asserts on the returned string (transport follows the threaded flag; the non-isolated
variant must not reference SharedArrayBuffer). Those are good assertions about the generator. None of
them asserts the exported SITE loads the module. Testing a string producer in isolation cannot see a
missing call site — the helper is called, and the feature still does not work.

MEASUREMENT TRAP, carried from ScarletRidge who found the two-glue seam: `grep -c 'audio_worklet_glue('`
also matches inside `web_audio_worklet_glue(`, so the gdplatform test looks like it covers the gdaudio
glue. It does not. They are two independent implementations with different signatures —
audio_worklet_glue(processor_name, channels) vs web_audio_worklet_glue(threads_enabled) — and nothing
asserts they agree.

SUGGESTED FIX, smallest first:
  1. Have web_engine_loader_js() call `context.audioWorklet.addModule('patina.audio.worklet.js')` and
     construct an AudioWorkletNode, resumed on the first user gesture (Godot unlocks on first input).
  2. Make the name one constant shared by both paths instead of two literals, so a future rename cannot
     split them again.
  3. Add the assertion that is missing rather than another string assertion: the exported folder's
     loader must reference the worklet filename AND the processor name it registers. That is checkable
     natively from the export output — no browser needed — and it is the assertion that would have
     caught this.

Credit: ScarletRidge spotted that two glue strings exist and are separately tested (their msg 88241); I
followed that to the call site and found the exported one has no consumer. Their framing was "they could
drift while both suites stay green" — the stronger finding is that the exported path is not connected at
all, so there is nothing to drift from.

title: WebXR: bind WebXrInterface to navigator.xr and pump session/input events from the web frame loop
description:

**Patina today:**

There is no real `navigator.xr` here'. The browser bindings (wasm32) would drive the same state machine". engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/lib.rs declares only `canvas`, `audio`, `web_audio` — there is no xr module and no wasm-bindgen WebXR code anywhere. In scope per the taxonomy scope anchor (WebXR named explicitly as in-scope for the browser port).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/xr.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/lib.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: WebXR ships in Godot's web export (upstream/godot/modules/webxr/config.py:1-2). `WebXRInterfaceJS` calls `navigator.xr.isSessionSupported(mode)` and `navigator.xr.requestSession(mode, {requiredFeatures, optionalFeatures})` through godot_webxr.h, then per frame `process()` (webxr_interface_js.cpp:602) reads the XRFrame: view transforms/projections (`get_transform_for_view` :457, `get_view_count` :280), the reference-space pose (`get_camera_transform` :439), and input-source connect/disconnect + selectstart/selectend/squeezestart/squeezeend events which it forwards as Godot signals and as XRControllerTracker updates on XRServer.\n\nPatina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/xr.rs:254-580 already models this state machine correctly (feature resolution, reference-space fallback, session_failed, input sources, refresh rates) and gdplatform is natively tested. But nothing drives it from a browser. Its only input is `WebXrStub` (xr.rs:243-252) set via `set_stub` (xr.rs:294), whose only non-test caller is the `_set_test_stub` seam at engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:2280-2300 — explicitly documented there as not a Godot method. `rg 'navigator\.xr|requestSession' crates/ apps/` finds no browser code; `rg -l 'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")' crates/gdplatform/src/` lists only js_bridge.rs and os.rs. The browser-event entry points (set_input_source, on_input_event, set_visibility_state, notify_reference_space_reset, set_available_display_refresh_rates) have no non-test callers, so an actual headset session is impossible.\n\nImplementation: add a `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]` backend module beside engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/xr.rs (mirroring the pattern in engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/js_bridge.rs) that (1) resolves `navigator.xr`, (2) fulfils `is_session_supported` from `isSessionSupported`, (3) issues `requestSession` and resolves it into `WebXrInterface::initialize`'s existing success/fail paths, (4) subscribes to session `end`, `visibilitychange`, reference-space `reset`, `inputsourceschange`, `selectstart`/`selectend`/`squeezestart`/`squeezeend` and calls the matching `WebXrInterface` methods, and (5) exposes a `poll()` that the web frame loop calls each tick. Keep `WebXrStub` as the non-wasm/test backend behind the same trait so the native tests still run. Then call `poll()` + `drain_xr_signals` from the runtime frame tick (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs frame step, reached by engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/lib.rs) so signals reach scripts every frame instead of only synchronously inside a script's own `initialize()` call — today the drain happens only at interpreter.rs:2325.\n\nWiring requirement: with a session running, a browser `selectstart` must reach a script's connected Callable through the frame loop with no script-side method call in between.

**Merged findings (3):** WebXR has no browser binding — the session state machine is driven only by a non-Godot `_set_test_stub`, never by navigator.xr; WebXRInterface script surface: input-source, refresh-rate, reference-space and all XRInterface base methods missing (platform code exists, no binding); WebXRInterface: unregistered and backed by a test stub instead of navigator.xr

**Prove it:** With the stub backend installed as the platform backend (not via the `_set_test_stub` script method), a loaded scene whose script connects `session_started`, `selectstart` and `session_ended` on `XRServer.find_interface("WebXR")` receives all three callbacks purely by advancing the MainLoop frame tick — proving the drain runs from the frame loop, not from the script's own call. `_set_test_stub` is removed from the script-visible method table. On wasm32 the module compiles against web-sys/js-sys `navigator.xr`. (test: `webxr_browser_session_binding`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test webxr_browser_session_binding`.
acceptance_criteria: With the stub backend installed as the platform backend (not via the `_set_test_stub` script method), a loaded scene whose script connects `session_started`, `selectstart` and `session_ended` on `XRServer.find_interface("WebXR")` receives all three callbacks purely by advancing the MainLoop frame tick — proving the drain runs from the frame loop, not from the script's own call. `_set_test_stub` is removed from the script-visible method table. On wasm32 the module compiles against web-sys/js-sys `navigator.xr`. (test: `webxr_browser_session_binding`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test webxr_browser_session_binding`.

title: XR nodes: drive XRNode3D/XRController3D/XROrigin3D transforms from XRServer trackers each frame
description:
[audit-key: xr-peripheral/xr-nodes] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/xr/xr_nodes.cpp:246-260 (_bind_methods), :329 (set_show_when_tracked), :373-401 (_bind_tracker / pose_changed connect), :426 (_pose_changed applies the pose), :215-228 (XRCamera3D connects tracker_added/updated/removed on XRServer); extension_api.json XRNode3D/XRController3D/XRAnchor3D/XROrigin3D

**Godot classes:** XRNode3D, XROrigin3D, XRCamera3D, XRController3D, XRAnchor3D

**Patina today:**
- [xr-peripheral] Registration exists and is otherwise correct: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1484-1506 (XROrigin3D world_scale/current, XRNode3D tracker, XRController3D, XRAnchor3D, XRCamera3D). Behaviour is absent everywhere: `rg -n 'XR' crates/gdscene/src` -> only 3 comment lines at crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:405-408; `rg -n 'world_scale|world_origin|reference_frame' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdrender3d/src crates/gdserver3d/src crates/patina-runner/src` -> 0 hits, so XROrigin3D.world_scale is inert; `rg -n 'is_button_pressed|get_has_tracking_data|get_is_active|show_when_tracked|get_pose\b|trigger_haptic_pulse' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdscript-interop/src` -> 0 hits, so none of XRNode3D's 10 methods, XRController3D's 5 methods + 5 signals, or XRAnchor3D's get_size/get_plane are dispatchable. XRNode3D is missing the `pose` and `show_when_tracked` properties in ClassDB (only `tracker` is registered, class_db.rs:1502). No per-frame XR update exists in crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs (`rg 'XR' crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs` -> 0 hits). The only green XR node test, crates/gdscene/tests/xr_camera_active.rs, asserts registration + that XRCamera3D is picked by the 3D camera lookup — nothing about tracking.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth (upstream/godot/scene/3d/xr/xr_nodes.cpp): XRNode3D holds a `tracker` StringName + `pose` name + `show_when_tracked`. On entering the tree it binds the tracker from XRServer and connects `pose_changed` (:373-401); `_pose_changed` (:426) writes the pose's transform into the node's local transform, scaled by XRServer world_scale, and toggles visibility when `show_when_tracked` is set. It exposes get_is_active/get_has_tracking_data/get_pose/trigger_haptic_pulse and emits `tracking_changed`. XRController3D adds is_button_pressed/get_input/get_float/get_vector2/get_tracker_hand and the button_pressed/button_released/input_float_changed/input_vector2_changed/profile_changed signals, all fed from the bound XRPositionalTracker's input map. XROrigin3D's `world_scale` writes XRServer::set_world_scale and `current` selects the active origin. XRCamera3D connects XRServer tracker_added/updated/removed in its constructor (:215-228) and takes the head pose.\n\nPatina current state: the classes are registered (engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1484-1506) and nothing else. `rg 'XR' crates/gdscene/src` returns only three comment lines in crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:405-408. No method of any XR node is dispatchable (`rg 'is_button_pressed|get_has_tracking_data|show_when_tracked' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdscript-interop/src` -> 0 hits), XROrigin3D.world_scale reaches nothing (`rg 'world_scale' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdrender3d/src crates/gdserver3d/src crates/patina-runner/src` -> 0 hits), and crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs has no XR step. The existing green test crates/gdscene/tests/xr_camera_active.rs only checks registration and camera selection.\n\nImplementation: add engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/xr_nodes.rs providing `update_xr_nodes(tree, delta)`: walk nodes whose class inherits XRNode3D, resolve `tracker` against the XRServer tracker registry (today engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:17213 XR_TRACKER_REGISTRY — lift it into a shared store gdscene can read, or expose a gdplatform-level registry both crates use), read the named pose, and write `transform = world_scale * pose.transform` onto the node via the existing Node3D transform path (crates/gdscene/src/node3d.rs); apply `show_when_tracked` visibility and emit `tracking_changed` on transitions. Call it from the frame tick in crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs immediately before the render publish, in the same place skeleton modifiers run (main_loop.rs:2982). Add the XRNode3D/XRController3D/XRAnchor3D/XROrigin3D method dispatch to the node method table used by GDScript, and add the missing `pose`/`show_when_tracked` properties to class_db.rs:1500.\n\nWiring requirement: loading a .tscn containing XROrigin3D > XRController3D(tracker="left_hand"), registering a tracker with a pose on XRServer, and stepping the MainLoop must move the controller node in the scene — no Rust helper call in between.

**Prove it:** A .tscn with XROrigin3D > XRCamera3D + XRController3D(tracker="left_hand", show_when_tracked=true) is loaded; a script registers an XRControllerTracker named "left_hand" with a pose at (0.3, 1.2, -0.4); after one MainLoop frame step the XRController3D's global transform origin equals (0.3, 1.2, -0.4), and with XROrigin3D.world_scale = 2.0 it equals (0.6, 2.4, -0.8). Before any pose exists the node is hidden (show_when_tracked) and `get_has_tracking_data()` is false; after the pose arrives `get_is_active()` is true and `tracking_changed` fired exactly once. `XRController3D.is_button_pressed("trigger")` reflects the tracker's input map. (test: `xr_nodes_track_pose_from_server`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test xr_nodes_track_pose_from_server`.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with XROrigin3D > XRCamera3D + XRController3D(tracker="left_hand", show_when_tracked=true) is loaded; a script registers an XRControllerTracker named "left_hand" with a pose at (0.3, 1.2, -0.4); after one MainLoop frame step the XRController3D's global transform origin equals (0.3, 1.2, -0.4), and with XROrigin3D.world_scale = 2.0 it equals (0.6, 2.4, -0.8). Before any pose exists the node is hidden (show_when_tracked) and `get_has_tracking_data()` is false; after the pose arrives `get_is_active()` is true and `tracking_changed` fired exactly once. `XRController3D.is_button_pressed("trigger")` reflects the tracker's input map. (test: `xr_nodes_track_pose_from_server`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test xr_nodes_track_pose_from_server`.

title: Canvas2D: collapse the dead gdscene::scene_bridge onto the shipped viewport_2d_render path
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/scene-bridge-dead-path] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/MISSING/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/main/canvas_item.cpp — there is exactly one canvas draw path in Godot; a second divergent one is a parity hazard | upstream/godot/scene/main/canvas_item.cpp (NOTIFICATION_DRAW / `queue_redraw` → `_draw` → item command list); extension_api.json CanvasItem._draw + queue_redraw | upstream/godot/platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_webgl2.js + servers/rendering canvas renderer running unchanged under the web export | extension_api.json CanvasItem methods — 32 `draw_*` entries; upstream/godot/doc/classes/CanvasItem.xml | upstream/godot/servers/rendering/renderer_canvas_cull.cpp:110-181 (`_collect_ysort_children`/`_count_ysort_children` flatten the WHOLE subtree of a `sort_y` item) and :437-458; extension_api.json CanvasItem.top_level + ClipChildrenMode (CLIP_CHILDREN_DISABLED/ONLY/AND_DRAW); RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_canvas_group_mode | upstream/godot/editor/plugins/canvas_item_editor_plugin.cpp — the 2D editor renders the live canvas through the same RenderingServer viewport as the game, with editor overlays composited on top | upstream/godot/servers/rendering/renderer_canvas_render.cpp — a CanvasItem's material shader runs for every primitive the item emits (rects, textured rects at any transform, polygons, lines, circles, glyphs), not only axis-aligned textured rects

**Godot classes:** CanvasItem, Sprite2D, Node2D, Control, RenderingServer, Viewport, CanvasGroup, CanvasLayer, ShaderMaterial, ColorRect, Polygon2D, Line2D, Label

**Patina today:**
- [nodes-2d] `crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs` documents itself as THE scene->canvas bridge ('nothing connected a live SceneTree to a Viewport of CanvasItems', `:1-35`) and implements `build_canvas_viewport` / `render_scene_to_frame`. It has NO production caller: `rg --type rust -l -F 'scene_bridge::' crates examples` returns nothing outside `crates/gdscene/tests/*` (canvas_item_material_blend_in_play.rs, particle_2d_scene_renders_moving_particles.rs, gdscript_draw_api_renders_pixels.rs, script_draw_and_gui_input_virtuals.rs, canvas_item_shader_scene_pixels.rs). The real path is `gdeditor::viewport_2d_render::build_runtime_render_list` (called from `crates/gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs:177` and `engine-rs/examples/editor.rs`). The two have already diverged: `scene_bridge.rs:287-311 draw_commands_for` handles only Sprite2D/AnimatedSprite2D/ColorRect/TextureRect/GPUParticles2D/CPUParticles2D and its `sprite_commands` (`:317-341`) ignores `region_enabled`/`region_rect`/`hframes`/`vframes`/`frame`/`flip_h`/`flip_v`, all of which `viewport_2d_render::sprite_sheet_for_node` (`:83-117`) does support; it also has no Line2D/Polygon2D/TileMapLayer/Path2D/Label arms. Tests that 'prove' 2D features end-to-end through `scene_bridge` therefore prove nothing about the shipped renderer.
- [rendering-2d] GDScript `draw_rect/draw_line/...` land in `SceneTree::push_draw_command` (crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs:1669-1875) and are stored in `SceneTree::custom_draw_commands` (crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:255,3070-3101), flushed each frame by `MainLoop` (crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:3117). The ONLY consumer in the whole workspace is `crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs:310` (`grep -rn 'custom_draw_commands' crates/ examples/` returns exactly that one non-definition hit). `scene_bridge::build_canvas_viewport` / `render_scene_to_frame` have ZERO production callers (`grep -rn 'build_canvas_viewport\|render_scene_to_frame'` → only crates/gdscene/tests/*). The served editor's Play loop is examples/editor.rs:290-345, which calls `gdeditor::viewport_2d_render::build_runtime_render_list` → `collect_canvas_items` (crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:334-447); that walk never reads `custom_draw_commands`. Ironically the RenderingServer script items ARE merged there (viewport_2d_render.rs:403-441), so `RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_rect` draws but `_draw` does not. The green test `crates/gdscene/tests/gdscript_draw_api_renders_pixels.rs:67` asserts pixels through the dead `build_canvas_viewport` path, so the gap is invisible to CI.
- [web-runtime] The wasm build has no 2D renderer. crates/patina-web/Cargo.toml:41-45 pulls in gdrender3d (with the `webgl` feature) and nothing else render-side; gdrender2d and gdserver2d are absent. The only draw operation exposed to JS is a clear: crates/patina-web/src/canvas.rs:145-148 `present_clear(&self, r, g, b) -> bool`, driven by the harness at crates/patina-web/web/index.html:128. gdrender2d is a CPU rasterizer that emits BMP frames over HTTP for the editor preview (crates/gdrender2d/src/frame_server.rs:1-5, 290-300), i.e. a server-side path with no browser-canvas consumer. `rg 'gdrender2d|gdserver2d' crates/patina-web/` → 0 hits.
- [rendering-2d] Patina's dispatch table (crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs:1675-1875) implements 14 names: draw_rect, draw_line, draw_circle, draw_polyline(+_colors), draw_multiline(+_colors), draw_dashed_line, draw_arc, draw_polygon, draw_colored_polygon, draw_texture, draw_texture_rect, draw_string. Absent (grep for each literal across crates/ returns nothing outside class_db/inspector schema): draw_ellipse, draw_ellipse_arc, draw_texture_rect_region, draw_msdf_texture_rect_region, draw_lcd_texture_rect_region, draw_style_box, draw_primitive, draw_string_outline, draw_multiline_string, draw_multiline_string_outline, draw_char, draw_char_outline, draw_mesh, draw_multimesh, draw_set_transform, draw_set_transform_matrix, draw_animation_slice, draw_end_animation. Parameters are dropped even on implemented calls: `draw_rect` ignores `width` for unfilled rects (scripting.rs:1675-1685); `draw_circle` ignores `filled`, `width`, `antialiased` (1706-1716); `draw_polyline_colors`/`draw_multiline_colors` collapse to the first colour (1725-1755, and the DrawCommand has one colour: crates/gdserver2d/src/canvas.rs:67-86); `draw_polygon` drops `uvs`+`texture` and per-vertex colours (1801-1819, canvas.rs:125-130); `draw_texture_rect` drops `tile` and `transpose` (1838-1849); `draw_string` drops `font`, `alignment` and `width` by its own comment (1850-1875). `DrawCommand` has only 11 variants (canvas.rs:42-182) — no mesh, multimesh, primitive, stylebox or set-transform representation exists.
- [rendering-2d] Y-sort: `canvas_order::draw_ordered_children` (crates/gdscene/src/canvas_order.rs:93-111) sorts only the DIRECT children of a `y_sort_enabled` parent; each child's own subtree still emits contiguously in `push_draw_order` (crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:522-534). Godot instead flattens every descendant reachable through non-y-sorted children into ONE list and sorts them by their composed ysort transform. top_level: `node2d::get_global_transform` (crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs:102-120) multiplies the whole ancestor chain with no `top_level` check — the flag is implemented for 3D only (crates/gdscene/src/node3d.rs:254-317); `grep -rn 'top_level' crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs crates/gdscene/src/canvas_order.rs crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs` returns nothing. clip_children: `clip_rect_for` (crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:543-556) treats any non-zero mode identically, requires the ancestor to have a `size` property (so a Sprite2D/Node2D clip parent yields None), and clips to an axis-aligned rect rather than the parent's drawn alpha; the rasterizer implements it by snapshot-and-restore (viewport_2d_render.rs:1639). CLIP_CHILDREN_ONLY (parent used as mask, not drawn) is not distinguished from CLIP_CHILDREN_AND_DRAW. `CanvasGroup` is registered with its properties (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:6374-6380) but has no compositing anywhere (`grep -rn 'CanvasGroup' crates/ --include='*.rs'` → class_db + tests + create-dialog catalog only). In the `scene_bridge` path `clip_rect` is never set at all (crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs:116-136).
- [rendering-2d] The edit-mode viewport is a third, independent renderer: `scene_renderer::render_scene_inner` (crates/gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs:222-330+) walks nodes, sorts them by `effective_z_index` only, and draws per-class glyphs/markers, positioning each node with `node2d::get_global_position(...) * zoom + offset` — a translation-and-uniform-scale, so a rotated or non-uniformly scaled node draws axis-aligned. `grep -n 'collect_canvas_items\|build_render_list\|Render2DItem' crates/gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs` returns nothing, so the edit view shares no code with the Play render list. `draw_sprite2d_with_texture` (scene_renderer.rs:693-760) reads only the node's OWN `modulate` (line 720-723), not `canvas_order::effective_modulate`, and applies no rotation. CanvasLayer ordering, `show_behind_parent`, Y-sort, clip_children and the 2D light pass are all absent from this path (they exist only in viewport_2d_render.rs).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs, engine-rs/examples/editor.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-web/Cargo.toml, engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/canvas.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/frame_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver2d/src/canvas.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/canvas_order.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/draw.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: there is exactly one canvas draw path — the scene tree feeds `RenderingServer` canvas items once per frame. Two divergent Rust implementations guarantee they drift and let green tests certify the wrong one.

PATINA: `crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs` presents itself as the scene->canvas bridge and is exercised by five integration tests (`crates/gdscene/tests/canvas_item_material_blend_in_play.rs`, `canvas_item_shader_scene_pixels.rs`, `particle_2d_scene_renders_moving_particles.rs`, `gdscript_draw_api_renders_pixels.rs`, `script_draw_and_gui_input_virtuals.rs`), but nothing in `src/` or `examples/` calls it (`rg --type gust -l -F 'scene_bridge::' crates examples` -> only tests). The shipped path is `gdeditor::viewport_2d_render::build_runtime_render_list` + `rasterize_render_list`, invoked from `crates/gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs:177-201` and `engine-rs/examples/editor.rs`. They have already diverged: `scene_bridge.rs:287-311` handles six classes and its `sprite_commands` at `:317-341` ignores region/hframes/vframes/frame/flip entirely, while `viewport_2d_render.rs:83-117` handles all of them; `scene_bridge` has no Line2D/Polygon2D/TileMapLayer/Path2D/Label arms at all.

APPROACH: pick `viewport_2d_render` as the single canvas path. Move the features `scene_bridge` uniquely carries — the CanvasItemMaterial/ShaderMaterial resolution at `scene_bridge.rs:126-282` and the `custom_draw_commands` append at `:310` — into `viewport_2d_render::render_kind_for`/`rasterize_render_list` if they are not already there, then delete `crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs` and repoint the five test files at `build_runtime_render_list`/`rasterize_render_list`. If the crate layering forbids `gdscene` depending on `gdeditor`, move `viewport_2d_render`'s collection half down into `gdscene` (it only needs `gdscene` + `gdrender2d`) and have `gdeditor` re-export it, so there is one collection function and one rasterizer.

WIRING: after the change, every 2D pixel test drives the same `.tscn -> collect -> rasterize` path the Game view and the editor example use; no second bridge exists to drift.

**Merged findings (7):** gdscene::scene_bridge — a second, dead scene-to-canvas 2D render bridge; CanvasItem `_draw` custom draw commands reaching the frame; 2D canvas rendering on the web target (CanvasItem draw commands reaching the browser canvas); CanvasItem draw_* script API surface; Y-sort across the full subtree, CanvasItem.top_level, clip_children modes / CanvasGroup; Editor 2D edit-mode viewport drawing real CanvasItem content (WYSIWYG with Play); canvas_item ShaderMaterial applied to every CanvasItem draw kind

**Prove it:** `rg --type rust -F 'scene_bridge' engine-rs/crates engine-rs/examples` returns no hits (the module is gone), and the five former scene_bridge tests pass against `build_runtime_render_list` + `rasterize_render_list`. A regression test loads a .tscn Sprite2D with `hframes = 4, frame = 2, flip_h = true` and asserts the SAME sampled sub-rect and mirroring through the one remaining path — the case the old bridge silently got wrong. A canvas_item ShaderMaterial and a script `_draw()` both still reach pixels through that path. (test: `single_canvas_path_renders_sprite_sheet_and_shader`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test single_canvas_path_renders_sprite_sheet_and_shader`.
acceptance_criteria: `rg --type rust -F 'scene_bridge' engine-rs/crates engine-rs/examples` returns no hits (the module is gone), and the five former scene_bridge tests pass against `build_runtime_render_list` + `rasterize_render_list`. A regression test loads a .tscn Sprite2D with `hframes = 4, frame = 2, flip_h = true` and asserts the SAME sampled sub-rect and mirroring through the one remaining path — the case the old bridge silently got wrong. A canvas_item ShaderMaterial and a script `_draw()` both still reach pixels through that path. (test: `single_canvas_path_renders_sprite_sheet_and_shader`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test single_canvas_path_renders_sprite_sheet_and_shader`.

## Lead from AmberForge (pat-s3rrv.28 owner) — the failure is NOT in the render list

I do not own this bead and have not edited anything. Flagging because .22 blocks .28's remaining scope and I had the files open.

### Failing assertion
`canvas_item_shader_material_still_reaches_pixels` — 'a materialled ColorRect must still produce a render item' (single_canvas_path_renders_sprite_sheet_and_shader.rs:191), exit (100, panic).

### What is PROVEN by reading
The `"ColorRect"` arm of `render_kind` (gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:1078) is UNCONDITIONAL — it always returns `Render2DKind::ColorRect { size, color }`. There is no early-out, no material check, and no size guard that could suppress it. Therefore `items.is_empty()` CANNOT be caused by the render list failing to carry a material. The ColorRect node is not reaching `build_runtime_render_list` at all.

So the fault is UPSTREAM of the render path: either `PackedScene::from_tscn` or `add_packed_scene_to_tree` is dropping the node.

### HYPOTHESIS (not confirmed — needs a compiler)
The only unusual thing in that scene is an EMPTY sub-resource: `[sub_resource type="ShaderMaterial" id="Mat_1"]` with no body, referenced as `material = SubResource("Mat_1")`. gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:507-508 says the ShaderMaterial pass 'deliberately filters `material` to `ShaderMaterial`', and :725 filters sub-resource ids by type == "ShaderMaterial". A property-less sub-resource is the natural edge case for that filter. Worth checking whether the node survives instantiation when `material` resolves to an empty ShaderMaterial.

⚠️ packed_scene.rs is itself part of this bead's uncommitted WIP, so check it in the WORKING TREE, not HEAD — the verifier builds the working tree.

### Cheapest next step
Assert on the TREE, not the render list: after `add_packed_scene_to_tree`, check the Rect node exists and its `size`/`color` survived. That splits 'the node was dropped at load' from 'the node exists but produced no item' in one run, instead of re-guessing at the render layer.

### Scope warning for whoever finishes this
.22 and .28 overlap. .22's acceptance needs material/shader to reach pixels through the single path, which is substantially .28's feature; meanwhile .28 needs new fields on `Render2DItem`, and this bead currently has +311 uncommitted lines in viewport_2d_render.rs including new `Render2DItem { .. }` construction sites that would all break with E0119/E0063 if fields were added underneath them. Land .22 FIRST, then re-scope .28. The four resolvers .28's description tells you to reuse are gone with scene_bridge.rs — recover them from `git show HEAD:engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs`.

comments.text:
## ROOT CAUSE FOUND (AmberForge) — missing ClassDB registration in the new tests, NOT an engine bug

Follow-up to my earlier lead. I have now CONFIRMED the cause by reading, and corrected one claim I made before.

### The cause
`collect_canvas_items` (gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:346) filters EVERY node through:

    if !node.is_class("CanvasItem") { return None; }

`Node::is_class` (gdscene/src/node.rs:315) falls through to `gdobject::is_parent_class`, i.e. a **ClassDB lookup**. ClassDB is NOT auto-populated in tests. With it empty, `ColorRect` is not known to inherit `CanvasItem`, so every node is filtered and `build_runtime_render_list` returns EMPTY — which is exactly the failing assertion 'a materialled ColorRect must still produce a render item'.

### Proof by reference test
Green gdeditor tests that use `build_runtime_render_list` all register first:
- crates/gdeditor/tests/camera2d_drives_runtime_canvas_transform.rs:62 -> `gdobject::class_db::register_2d_classes();`
- crates/gdeditor/tests/camera2d_scroll_drives_runtime_canvas.rs:32 -> same, and its comment even says it mirrors 'the register_*_classes() calls that the editor/runner make at startup'.

The new crates/gdeditor/tests/single_canvas_path_renders_sprite_sheet_and_shader.rs registers NOTHING (its `load()` helper is from_tscn + add_packed_scene_to_tree only).

### THE FIX
Add `gdobject::class_db::register_2d_classes();` to the test's `load()` helper (and to any test in that file that builds a tree directly). This is a HARNESS fix — the .22 implementation may be entirely correct and has never been fairly exercised.

### ⚠️ Two more files have the same latent fault
`canvas_item_material_blend_in_play.rs` and `canvas_item_shader_scene_pixels.rs` were MOVED into crates/gdeditor/tests/ and now call `build_runtime_render_list` with **0** registration calls. On the old scene_bridge path they never hit the `is_class` filter; on the surviving path they do. Expect them to fail the same way — fix all three together.

### CORRECTION to my earlier note
I previously wrote that those two material tests were 'deleted'. **That was wrong** — `git status` reports them as `RM` (renamed) from crates/gdscene/tests/ to crates/gdeditor/tests/. They exist and are the right starting point; do not rewrite them from scratch.

### Hypotheses I ELIMINATED so nobody repeats them
1. 'The render list drops materialled items' — NO. The `\"ColorRect\"` arm of `render_kind` (viewport_2d_render.rs:1078) is unconditional: no material check, no size guard, no early-out.
2. 'The empty `[sub_resource type=\"ShaderMaterial\"]` swallows the following [node] lines' — NO. packed_scene.rs routes property lines to `current` (the node) BEFORE `current_sub`, so node properties land correctly.
3. 'Visibility filtering drops it' — NO. `node2d::is_visible(` defaults to TRUE when the property is absent/Nil (node2d.rs:201).

comments.text:
## Handoff (EmeraldIsland): 5 of 6 green, and the last red is a SECOND real product bug — flip_h displaces an uncentred sprite

The bead was parked after two verifies, but it advanced a long way in them. Latest run: **6 tests, 5 passed, 1 failed.** Do not restart from the top.

### DONE and confirmed working — do not redo
1. **ClassDB registration in all five canvas tests.** AmberForge's root cause was right and their five-file scope correction was right. `single_canvas_path…`, `gdscript_draw_api_renders_pixels` and `script_draw_and_gui_input_virtuals` now call `gdobject::class_db::register_2d_classes()` before every `SceneTree::new()` (2, 2 and 10 sites); `canvas_item_material_blend_in_play` and `canvas_item_shader_scene_pixels` were fixed earlier under .28. PROOF: `script_draw_reaches_pixels_on_the_shipped_path` and `canvas_item_shader_material_still_reaches_pixels` both PASS now, where they previously saw an empty render list.
2. **`frame_coords` precedence bug — FIXED.** `packed_scene::node_with_class_defaults` seeds every ClassDB default before the scene values land, and Sprite2D registers `frame_coords` default `Vector2i(0,0)` (class_db.rs:6701). `sprite_sheet_for_node` treated mere PRESENCE as "authored", so the seeded default beat the authored `frame` and pinned every sheet to cell 0 in any real project (the editor and runner both register at startup). Now only a NON-ZERO cell wins. Three regression tests cover it, all green.

### THE REMAINING RED — a genuine defect, not a test bug
`single_canvas_path_renders_sprite_sheet_and_shader.rs:125` — the PIXEL half. Got `Color { r: 0, g: 0, b: 0 }`, i.e. the BACKGROUND. Note the assert message guesses "draws the red first cell instead" — that guess is wrong and will mislead you: nothing is drawn at that pixel at all.

**Cause: `flip_h` mirrors about the NODE ORIGIN instead of about the sprite rect.** In `rasterize_render_list_with_quality`'s Sprite arm the flip is `Transform2D::scaled((-1, 1))` composed as `xform * flip`. With `centered = false` the local rect is `(0,0)..(4,4)`, so the mirror maps it to `(-4,0)..(0,4)` and the quad lands at screen x in [12,16) — the test samples (18,10), which is now background.

Godot never moves the destination: `Sprite2D::_get_rects` flips the SOURCE/UV and leaves the dest rect in place. A CENTRED sprite hides this completely, because its rect is symmetric about the origin — which is why this has survived until an uncentred fixture existed.

**Suggested fix** (mirror in place; identical behaviour for centred sprites):

    let c = rect.position + rect.size / 2.0;   // rect centre, local space
    let flip = Transform2D::translated(c)
        * Transform2D::scaled(Vector2::new(if flip_h {-1.0} else {1.0},
                                           if flip_v {-1.0} else {1.0}))
        * Transform2D::translated(-c);

For a centred sprite `c` is the origin, so this reduces to the current transform and cannot move an existing pixel. Add an uncentred `flip_v` case too — it has the same bug on the Y axis and nothing covers it.

### Housekeeping on the bead itself
- **The Acceptance line's command is broken:** the suggested invocation omits `-p gdeditor`, so it dies at cargo target resolution (exit 101, nothing compiled, no information). Always pass `-p gdeditor`. Please fix the bead text; agents keep copying it.
- **The `rg 'scene_bridge' returns no hits` criterion cannot be met literally.** It returns 5 hits, ALL prose — doc comments explaining the collapse, plus this bead's own test header asserting "the bridge is gone (rg scene_bridge returns no hits)", which is itself a hit. There are ZERO code references (no `use`, no `mod`, no `::scene_bridge`) and the module file is a staged deletion. That is a wording fix, not a code change.
- Never run green: `canvas_item_material_blend_in_play` and `canvas_item_shader_scene_pixels`. Worth running each with `-p gdeditor --test <name>` once this closes.

All my file reservations are released.

comments.text:
BronzeBridge — respecting the park (05:10 today, "do NOT retry"). NOT requesting a re-run: I tried that on pat-s3rrv.30, also parked, and the request was never dispatched. Leaving the diagnosis instead, because the failure message is pointing the next worker in the wrong direction.

THE ERROR MESSAGE CONTRADICTS THE OBSERVED VALUE. The assertion at single_canvas_path_renders_sprite_sheet_and_shader.rs:125 says:

    "frame = 2 of a 4-frame sheet must sample the BLUE cell, got Color { r: 0.0, g: 0.0, b: 0.0, a: 1.0 } - a path that ignores `frame` draws the red first cell instead"

The message predicts RED for the failure mode it describes. The value is BLACK (0,0,0,1) - the clear colour. So the sampled pixel is NOT the wrong cell, it is NOT COVERED AT ALL. `frame` handling is not implicated by this evidence, and the five other tests in the file pass.

Note the other assertions in the same test already PASS: hframes == 4 and frame == 2 both reach the render item. So the field plumbing is fine; only the pixel is missing.

WHERE TO LOOK. The fixture is `position = Vector2(16, 8)` with `centered = false`, and the test samples (18, 10) on the comment "the drawn cell occupies x in [16,20), y in [8,12)". That comment is an ASSUMPTION about placement, and it is the thing to check first:

  1. Does the Sprite2D's `position` reach the render item's rect? `Render2DKind::Sprite` (viewport_2d_render.rs:1253) carries texture/offset/flip_h/flip_v/sheet and NO position - placement comes from the item's rect via `base * Transform2D::translated(rect.position)` (viewport_2d_render.rs:855, :870). If `rect.position` is not fed from the node's `position` property, the cell draws at [0,4)^2 and (18,10) reads the clear colour, which is exactly the observed BLACK.
  2. A Sprite2D draws at TEXTURE size, not FRAME size. The sheet here is 4 cells wide, so a texture-sized draw at (16,8) would cover x in [16,32) and (18,10) WOULD be inside - so this alone does not explain BLACK, but it changes which pixels are safe to sample if (1) turns out fine.

I did NOT confirm (1) - I stopped at the park rather than chase it into an engine fix. But BLACK vs RED is solid, and it is worth more than the error message: it redirects from "the path ignores frame" to "nothing is drawn where the test looks".

SEPARATE, AND IT AFFECTS THE FIRST ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE. The acceptance requires `rg -F 'scene_bridge'` to return NO hits. It currently returns 5, in 4 files:
  crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs
  crates/gdrender2d/src/draw.rs
  crates/gdeditor/tests/canvas_item_material_and_sampling_in_play_frame.rs
  crates/gdeditor/tests/single_canvas_path_renders_sprite_sheet_and_shader.rs
Two are in SOURCE. Whoever picks this up should check whether those are live references or only comments - if the module is already gone and these are prose mentions, the clause is satisfiable by an edit to the bead text rather than by code, and that is worth settling before anyone re-attempts the pixel work.

EmeraldIsland — measured this bead's remaining items at HEAD rather than trusting the text. One
is STALE and should be struck; two are confirmed live. No code changed this pass.

I did this because the bead text has already proved stale once on this bead (the scene_bridge
grep clause) and three more times today on other beads, and the next worker should not re-derive
it.

STALE — strike this item:

  "top_level is implemented for 3D only; `grep -rn 'top_level' crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs`
   returns nothing."

  Not true at HEAD. node2d.rs has 15 occurrences, including `set_top_level` (:107),
  `is_top_level` (:118) and — the part that matters — an explicit check inside
  `get_global_transform` that ENDS the ancestor walk, commented "pat-s3rrv.22: `top_level` ends
  the walk." It is stored under the plain `top_level` node property, the same key the .tscn
  parser writes, and ClassDB registers it. This item is done.

CONFIRMED LIVE — both still exactly as described:

  Y-SORT. `canvas_order::draw_ordered_children` (:93-110) collects `tree.children` of the parent
  and sorts THAT list only. No subtree flattening anywhere. Godot instead flattens every
  descendant reachable through non-y-sorted children into one list and sorts by composed ysort
  transform (renderer_canvas_cull.cpp:110-181).

  CLIP_CHILDREN. `canvas_order::clip_children_mode` does return Godot's 0/1/2, but
  viewport_2d_render.rs:926 tests it with `!= 0`, so CLIP_CHILDREN_ONLY and
  CLIP_CHILDREN_AND_DRAW remain indistinguishable. CanvasGroup: `grep -c CanvasGroup
  crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs` = 0, so still no compositing.

SIZING NOTE for whoever takes the Y-sort item — it is not a local edit:

  `draw_ordered_children` has ONE production caller, `push_draw_order`
  (viewport_2d_render.rs:903), which recurses into each child itself. If
  `draw_ordered_children` starts returning a FLATTENED subtree, `push_draw_order` must stop
  recursing into those same nodes or every descendant lands in the draw list twice. Duplicated
  entries do not necessarily change any pixel — a node drawn twice at the same transform looks
  identical — so the existing pixel tests can stay green while the list is wrong. Whoever does it
  should assert the draw list's LENGTH and node-id multiset, not just the resulting image.

  Two tests exercise this ordering directly and must keep passing:
  gdeditor/tests/canvas_order_effective_z_modulate_ysort_runtime.rs and
  gdeditor/tests/play_canvas_inheritance_semantics.rs, plus two in-file tests at
  canvas_order.rs:197 and :216.

I did not attempt it: changing the draw walk blind, with a failure mode the pixel tests would not
catch, is the wrong shape for the no-cargo lane. It wants someone who can run those four tests.

title: Add SkeletonProfile/SkeletonProfileHumanoid and the BoneMap retargeting path
description:
[audit-key: animation/animation-skeleton-retargeting-profiles] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/skeleton_profile.cpp + skeleton_profile_humanoid.cpp; doc/classes/SkeletonProfile.xml; extension_api.json SkeletonProfile(Resource, 29 methods, 4 props), SkeletonProfileHumanoid(SkeletonProfile)

**Godot classes:** SkeletonProfile, SkeletonProfileHumanoid

**Patina today:**

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

**Godot ground truth:** `SkeletonProfile : Resource` names a canonical bone set for retargeting — `bone_size`, `root_bone`, `scale_base_bone`, `group_size`, and per-bone `set_bone_name`/`set_bone_parent`/`set_bone_tail`/`set_reference_pose`/`set_handle_offset`/`set_group`/`set_required`, plus `find_bone`/`get_bone_name`/`is_required` (29 methods). `SkeletonProfileHumanoid` is the preset filling that table with Godot's 56-bone humanoid rig (Hips, Spine, Chest, UpperChest, Neck, Head, per-side Shoulder/UpperArm/LowerArm/Hand + 15 finger bones, UpperLeg/LowerLeg/Foot/Toes). `BoneMap : Resource` pairs a profile with a source skeleton's bone names and is what `RetargetModifier3D` and the glTF/FBX importer consume. Source: `upstream/godot/scene/resources/skeleton_profile*.cpp`.

**Patina today:** nothing exists. Grepping `SkeletonProfile|BoneMap|retarget` over `engine-rs/crates/**/*.rs` (excluding the generated inspector schema table) finds only two comments saying so: `crates/gdscene/src/ik_solver.rs:21` and `crates/gdscene/tests/skeleton_modifiers.rs:23-25`, the latter stating verbatim that `RetargetModifier3D`, `BoneMap` and `SkeletonProfile*` are 'registered nowhere, asserted nowhere'. **Wiring requirement:** a `.tscn` referencing a `SkeletonProfileHumanoid` sub-resource must load with a populated 56-bone table, and applying a BoneMap to a differently-named source rig must produce Skeleton3D bone poses the 3D render pass consumes.

**Prove it:** an app-level test loading a .tscn with a Skeleton3D whose bones use non-Godot names plus a BoneMap onto a SkeletonProfileHumanoid, asserting the humanoid profile reports 56 bones with `Hips` as root and `find_bone("LeftUpperArm")` resolving, then asserting a pose applied through the map lands on the correct source bone and the resulting global pose matches the expected transform.

description:
[audit-key: core-variant/core-variant-hash] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/variant/variant.cpp `Variant::hash()` / `recursive_hash()` hashes every Variant type — NODE_PATH via its string hash, TRANSFORM2D/BASIS/TRANSFORM3D/PROJECTION component-wise, RID/OBJECT by pointer/id, CALLABLE/SIGNAL via their own hash().

**Godot classes:** Variant, Dictionary, Array

**Patina today:**
- [core-variant] engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/hash.rs:186-378 covers 25 kinds (Nil, Bool, Int, Float, String, StringName, Vector2/2i, Vector3/3i, Rect2, Aabb, Plane, Quaternion, Color, Array, Dictionary, and the 9 packed arrays) and line 379 is `_ => 0` — the comment at 370-378 admits the fallback. So NodePath, Transform2D, Transform3D, Basis, ObjectId, Resource, Callable and Signal all hash to 0. A parallel test file records the same gap (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/vhash_parity.rs:22 lists exactly these types as not covered). Because Dictionary key lookup uses this notion of hashing, a Dictionary keyed by NodePath or Transform degenerates to a single bucket and `Array.hash()`/`Dictionary.hash()` are additionally not even exposed to GDScript (absent from the Array/Dictionary method tables at interpreter.rs:7800-8126 / 8537-8671).

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/hash.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: `upstream/godot/core/variant/variant.cpp::Variant::recursive_hash()` produces a hash for EVERY Variant type — NodePath via the string hash of its path, Transform2D/Basis/Transform3D/Projection by hashing each component with `hash_murmur3_one_real`, RID/Object by id, Callable/Signal via their own `hash()`. `Array::hash()` and `Dictionary::hash()` are bound methods.

PATINA CURRENT STATE: engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/hash.rs:186-378 handles 25 kinds and then falls back to `_ => 0` at line 379; the comment at 370-378 states outright that the remaining types are not covered, and engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/vhash_parity.rs:22 records the same list. NodePath, Transform2D, Transform3D, Basis, ObjectId, Resource, Callable and Signal therefore all hash to 0, which collapses any Dictionary keyed by those types into one bucket and makes cross-engine hash parity wrong. `Array.hash()` and `Dictionary.hash()` are also not callable from GDScript — neither name appears in the Array table (interpreter.rs:7800-8126) or the Dictionary table (interpreter.rs:8537-8671).

IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH: extend `recursive_hash` in gdvariant/src/hash.rs with the remaining arms, reading the exact murmur3 sequence from variant.cpp (the file already has `hash_murmur3_one_double`/`hash_murmur3_one_float`/`hash_fmix32` helpers and golden constants in its tests — add golden values for each new type computed from the C++). Remove the `_ => 0` catch-all so a future new Variant kind is a compile error rather than a silent zero. Add `"hash"` arms to the Array and Dictionary method tables in interpreter.rs delegating to `gdvariant::hash::godot_hash` (already used for the global `hash()` at interpreter.rs:13780).

WIRING REQUIREMENT: a script in a scene keys a Dictionary by NodePath and by Transform2D and the lookups must resolve distinctly; `arr.hash()` must return Godot's value.

**Prove it:** A scene script builds `{^"A": 1, ^"B": 2}` and a Transform2D-keyed dictionary, reads both keys back distinctly, and `[1,2,3].hash()` / `{"a":1}.hash()` return the values Godot produces; `godot_hash` has no catch-all arm. (test: `variant_hash_full_type_coverage_from_scene`)
acceptance_criteria: A scene script builds `{^"A": 1, ^"B": 2}` and a Transform2D-keyed dictionary, reads both keys back distinctly, and `[1,2,3].hash()` / `{"a":1}.hash()` return the values Godot produces; `godot_hash` has no catch-all arm. (test: `variant_hash_full_type_coverage_from_scene`)

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## Implemented and composed — never built. Needs a run, not a worker.

EmeraldIsland, 2026-08-20. **No code changed.** Released.

The acceptance test `variant_hash_full_type_coverage_from_scene` exists
(`crates/gdscene/tests/`) but has **no binary in `target-verifier`** — it has
never been built here, so there is no verdict to be stale or current.

### Verified the whole chain, not just that the symbols exist

This is the check I got wrong on pat-s3rrv.202, so each link was opened:

| link | state |
|---|---|
| `godot_hash` exhaustive, no catch-all | ✅ zero `_ =>` arms; exhaustiveness is compiler-enforced |
| NodePath arm | ✅ `hash.rs:194` region |
| Transform2D arm | ✅ `hash.rs:402`, with the COLUMNS note |
| `^"A"` literal | ✅ parses as a **NodePath** literal (`parser.rs:1678`) — correct Godot semantics; `&"..."` is the StringName form, and the test's `np_a`/`np_b` naming confirms NodePath is intended |
| `Transform2D(x, y, origin)` | ✅ 3-arg arm in `variant_math::construct` |
| `Array.hash()` / `Dictionary.hash()` | ✅ `interpreter.rs:11057` / `:11924` → `variant_hash` → **`gdvariant::hash::godot_hash`** (a one-line wrapper, so no second implementation to drift) |
| dictionary keying by those types | ✅ `key_eq` falls back to structural `a == b`; `key_hash` buckets by discriminant and `key_eq` separates within the bucket — distinct keys stay distinct, and nothing panics on an exotic key |

### Nothing worth adding to the test

Six tests already cover: all fourteen previously-zero kinds hash nonzero; they do
not collide with each other; a Basis differs from its transpose; NodePath hashes
as its string; the script keys a dictionary by NodePath and Transform2D; and
`Array`/`Dictionary` hash match the Godot goldens.

🔑 Worth noting the golden provenance, because it is the trap
[[a_round_trip_proves_agreement_not_correctness]] warns about: the file records
that `{"a":1} = 120477264` had previously been *calibrated* against a number this
repo already asserted — so the assertion restated its own input. Both goldens have
since been re-derived from the vendored C++ (`hashfuncs.h`, `array.cpp`,
`dictionary.cpp`, `variant.h` ordinals) without consulting `gdvariant`. That makes
them parity evidence rather than self-agreement. Do not "simplify" that derivation
back to a recorded constant.

title: PackedByteArray: add compress/decompress(+dynamic) and the UTF-16/32/wchar string decoders
description:
[audit-key: core-variant/core-variant-packed-compress] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json PackedByteArray → 69 methods; missing here are compress(mode), decompress(size, mode), decompress_dynamic(max, mode), get_string_from_utf16, get_string_from_utf32, get_string_from_wchar, get_string_from_multibyte_char, to_vector4_array. Upstream core/variant/variant_call.cpp `func_PackedByteArray_compress` + core/io/compression.cpp (FASTLZ/DEFLATE/ZSTD/GZIP/BROTLI).

**Godot classes:** PackedByteArray

**Patina today:**
- [core-variant] engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:10677+ `call_packed_method` implements size, is_empty, get, set, append/push_back, resize, clear, slice, to_byte_array, duplicate, has, get_string_from_utf8, get_string_from_ascii, hex_encode, sort, bsearch, find, rfind, count, reverse, fill, insert, remove_at, append_array and the to_*_array converters, and interpreter.rs:10372-10520 `call_pba_codec` adds the full decode_*/encode_* family. `compress`/`decompress`/`decompress_dynamic`/`get_string_from_utf16`/`get_string_from_utf32`/`get_string_from_wchar`/`get_string_from_multibyte_char`/`to_vector4_array` appear nowhere in engine-rs/crates (grep of each quoted name → 0 hits).

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: extension_api.json binds 69 PackedByteArray methods. Missing here: `compress(compression_mode)`, `decompress(buffer_size, mode)`, `decompress_dynamic(max_output_size, mode)` — modes FASTLZ/DEFLATE/ZSTD/GZIP/BROTLI per `upstream/godot/core/io/compression.cpp` and the `FileAccess.CompressionMode` enum — plus `get_string_from_utf16`, `get_string_from_utf32`, `get_string_from_wchar`, `get_string_from_multibyte_char`, and `to_vector4_array`.

PATINA CURRENT STATE: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:10677+ (`call_packed_method`) covers the container surface and interpreter.rs:10372-10520 (`call_pba_codec`) covers the full decode_*/encode_* binary codec — good work, but the compression and wide-encoding entry points do not exist anywhere in engine-rs/crates.

IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH: add `"compress"`, `"decompress"`, `"decompress_dynamic"` arms to `call_packed_method` for the PackedByteArray receiver, backed by codec helpers in engine-rs/crates/gdcore (the FileAccess compressed-file support in gdcore/src/file_access.rs is the natural home — reuse whatever deflate/zstd/gzip implementation it already carries so the two paths agree, and note Godot's mode integer ordering is FASTLZ=0, DEFLATE=1, ZSTD=2, GZIP=3, BROTLI=4). `decompress` must fail (returning an empty array) when the output exceeds `buffer_size`, matching Godot. Add the UTF-16/UTF-32/wchar decoders alongside the existing `get_string_from_utf8` arm, honouring a BOM the way Godot's `String::parse_utf16` does, and `to_vector4_array` once PackedVector4Array exists.

WIRING REQUIREMENT: reachable from a script in a scene — e.g. compress a save blob, write it via FileAccess, read it back and decompress — so the codepath is exercised through the runtime, not a Rust unit test.

**Prove it:** A scene script round-trips a PackedByteArray through compress()/decompress() in DEFLATE, GZIP and ZSTD modes and recovers the original bytes, decompress with too small a buffer returns empty, and get_string_from_utf16/utf32 decode a BOM-prefixed buffer to the expected string. (test: `packed_byte_array_compression_and_wide_decoders`)
acceptance_criteria: A scene script round-trips a PackedByteArray through compress()/decompress() in DEFLATE, GZIP and ZSTD modes and recovers the original bytes, decompress with too small a buffer returns empty, and get_string_from_utf16/utf32 decode a BOM-prefixed buffer to the expected string. (test: `packed_byte_array_compression_and_wide_decoders`)

title: Implement editor feature profiles (EditorFeatureProfile + Manage dialog)
description:
[audit-key: editor/editor-ux-feature-profiles] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: STUB]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/editor_feature_profile.cpp; extension_api.json (editor api): EditorFeatureProfile <- RefCounted, 11 methods — set/is_disabled_class, set/is_disabled_class_editor, set/is_disabled_property, set/is_disabled_feature (Feature enum: 3D, SCRIPT, ASSET_LIB, SCENE_TREE, NODE_DOCK, FILESYSTEM_DOCK, IMPORT_DOCK, HISTORY_DOCK, GAME), get_feature_name, save_to_file, load_from_file.

**Godot classes:** EditorFeatureProfile

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-1] The menu entry exists and does nothing: engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_menu.rs:497-499 maps `MenuAction::EditorFeatureProfile` to `MenuActionResult::OpenDialog("Manage Feature Profiles")` — a bare string. `rg -in 'feature_profile|featureprofile' crates/` matches only that menu file and the generated inspector schema table; there is no profile resource, no .profile save/load, no class/property/feature disabling anywhere. `rg -n 'ClassRegistration::new("EditorFeatureProfile")' crates/` → 0 hits, and no editor-server route serves the dialog.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_menu.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

[status: STUB]

**Godot ground truth:** `EditorFeatureProfile <- RefCounted` stores which editor features, classes, class-editors and properties are hidden: `set_disabled_class`/`is_disabled_class`, `set_disabled_class_editor`, `set_disabled_property`, `set_disabled_feature` over the Feature enum (FEATURE_3D, FEATURE_SCRIPT, FEATURE_ASSET_LIB, FEATURE_SCENE_TREE, FEATURE_NODE_DOCK, FEATURE_FILESYSTEM_DOCK, FEATURE_IMPORT_DOCK, FEATURE_HISTORY_DOCK, FEATURE_GAME), plus `get_feature_name`, `save_to_file(path)` and `load_from_file(path)` (.profile JSON). The Editor > Manage Editor Features dialog creates/imports/exports profiles and applies the current one, hiding the disabled docks, main screens, classes in Create Node, and properties in the inspector. (upstream/godot/editor/editor_feature_profile.cpp)

**Patina today:** a dead menu entry. `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_menu.rs:497-499` returns `MenuActionResult::OpenDialog("Manage Feature Profiles")` and nothing consumes that string; `rg -in 'feature_profile|featureprofile' crates/` finds no implementation outside that file and the generated inspector schema table; `rg -n 'ClassRegistration::new("EditorFeatureProfile")' crates/` → 0 hits; no editor-server route serves the dialog.

**Implement:** register `EditorFeatureProfile` (parent RefCounted) with all 11 methods and the Feature enum in `class_db.rs`; add a profile store in gdeditor that persists .profile JSON alongside EditorSettings and loads the currently-selected profile at editor start; add editor-server routes (list/create/select/import/export a profile, set disabled classes/features/properties) and the Manage Editor Features dialog in EDITOR_HTML wired to them; then honour the active profile where it matters — filter disabled classes out of the ClassDB-driven Create Node list (`engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/create_dialog.rs`), hide disabled properties in the inspector payload, and hide disabled docks/main screens in the served UI.

**Wiring requirement:** selecting a profile that disables FEATURE_3D and the class `Sprite2D` must make the served editor omit the 3D main screen and omit Sprite2D from Create Node — and the setting must survive an editor restart via the saved .profile file.

**Prove it:** an editor-server test that creates a profile disabling one class and one feature, selects it, and asserts the Create Node listing omits that class and the UI payload omits that feature's screen; then reloads the profile from disk and re-asserts.

**Prove it:** EditorFeatureProfile is registered in ClassDB with its 11 methods and Feature enum, profiles save/load as .profile files, and selecting a profile that disables a class and a feature removes that class from the ClassDB-driven Create Node list and that feature's screen from the served editor UI, persisting across reload. (test: `editor_feature_profile_disables_class_and_feature`)
acceptance_criteria: EditorFeatureProfile is registered in ClassDB with its 11 methods and Feature enum, profiles save/load as .profile files, and selecting a profile that disables a class and a feature removes that class from the ClassDB-driven Create Node list and that feature's screen from the served editor UI, persisting across reload. (test: `editor_feature_profile_disables_class_and_feature`)

title: Register FileSystemDock (parent now exists) and emit its file-operation signals

[status: MISSING]
