title: AssetLib: install assets from a .zip (and an optional configured catalog URL)
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-assetlib] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: STUB]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/asset_library/asset_library_editor_plugin.cpp (HTTP catalog query against the asset store, per-asset detail + Download, EditorAssetInstaller zip install, Plugins filter tab)

**Godot classes:** EditorAssetLibrary, EditorAssetInstaller

**Patina today:**
- [editor-ux] api_get_assetlib_list (editor_server.rs:10717-10743) deliberately returns {"assets":[],"configured":false,"reason":"no asset catalog configured"} — its own doc comment states no install path exists anywhere in the server. The client's Import button (editor_ui.rs:14810) logs 'Import asset (.zip) — not yet implemented' and the Plugins view button (editor_ui.rs:14812) logs 'Plugins view — not yet implemented'. No prd/ or THIRDPARTY_STRATEGY.md citation declares AssetLib out of scope.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: the AssetLib main screen queries a catalog over HTTP, shows asset detail pages, downloads the zip and installs it into the project through EditorAssetInstaller, which previews the file list and lets the user deselect entries (upstream/godot/editor/asset_library/asset_library_editor_plugin.cpp).\n\nPATINA: there is no install path at all. engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:10717 api_get_assetlib_list returns an honest empty catalog ({assets:[], configured:false}); the client's 'Import asset (.zip)' (editor_ui.rs:14810) and 'Plugins view' (editor_ui.rs:14812) buttons only log 'not yet implemented'. Nothing in prd/ or THIRDPARTY_STRATEGY.md declares AssetLib out of scope, so this is a gap rather than a scope decision.\n\nAPPROACH: start with the local half, which needs no third-party service — add POST /api/assetlib/install accepting an uploaded zip, unpack it under res:// with a file-list preview + per-entry opt-out (mirroring EditorAssetInstaller), refresh the FileSystem dock, and detect addons/*/plugin.cfg so the installed plugin appears in the existing plugin list (/api/plugins). Then add an optional `editor/assetlib/index_url` setting (the key api_get_assetlib_list already names) that, when set, is fetched server-side and mapped into the existing assets payload, plus a per-asset Download button.\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: installing a zip containing addons/foo/plugin.cfg must make 'foo' appear in the Plugins list and be enableable, with the enabled state persisted to project.godot.

**Prove it:** Uploading a zip containing addons/demo/plugin.cfg through the AssetLib screen in the served editor unpacks it under res://addons/demo/, refreshes the FileSystem dock, and makes 'demo' toggleable in the plugin list with the choice written to project.godot. (test: `editor_assetlib_zip_install_served`) POSTs a zip to /api/assetlib/install, asserts the extracted files and the new plugin entry, and asserts EDITOR_HTML calls "/api/assetlib/install".
acceptance_criteria: Uploading a zip containing addons/demo/plugin.cfg through the AssetLib screen in the served editor unpacks it under res://addons/demo/, refreshes the FileSystem dock, and makes 'demo' toggleable in the plugin list with the choice written to project.godot. (test: `editor_assetlib_zip_install_served`) POSTs a zip to /api/assetlib/install, asserts the extracted files and the new plugin entry, and asserts EDITOR_HTML calls "/api/assetlib/install".

title: EditorLayout: persist dock layouts and make docks resizable/movable
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-layouts] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/docks/editor_dock_manager.cpp (drag docks between slots, float docks, resize splits) + editor_node.cpp Editor > Editor Layout > Save/Delete/Default (persisted to editor_layout.cfg)

**Godot classes:** EditorDockManager

**Patina today:**
- [editor-ux] editor_ui.rs:1937-1938 declares the menu items 'Save Editor Layout' and 'Reset to Default Layout'; their handlers at editor_ui.rs:13973-13977 are `logMessage('info', 'Editor layout saved')` and `logMessage('info', 'Editor layout reset to default')` — no request, no persistence. `grep -c 'dock-resize\|resizer\|draggable-dock' editor_ui.rs` = 0, so docks cannot be moved between slots, floated, or resized either.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/dock.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: docks can be dragged between the four slots, floated into their own window and resized, and Editor > Editor Layout saves/restores named layouts in editor_layout.cfg (upstream/godot/editor/docks/editor_dock_manager.cpp, editor/editor_node.cpp).\n\nPATINA: engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs:1937-1938 shows both menu items and the handlers at editor_ui.rs:13973-13977 only call logMessage — nothing is saved or restored, so a user's panel arrangement is lost on every reload. The docks themselves are fixed-width CSS panels with no resize handles or drag targets (0 hits for resizer/dock-resize). gdeditor/src/dock.rs models docks in Rust but has no route or client consumer.\n\nAPPROACH: add splitter handles between the left/centre/right columns and the bottom panel in editor_ui.rs that persist their sizes, allow dock tabs to be dragged between the left and right dock columns, and add GET/POST /api/editor/layout in editor_server.rs that stores the layout (slot assignment + split sizes + active tabs) in the editor settings store (gdeditor/src/editor_settings_store.rs) so it survives a reload; wire the two existing menu items to save and reset.\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: reloading the served editor page must restore the saved arrangement from the server, not from client-only state.

**Prove it:** Resizing the Inspector dock and moving the FileSystem tab to the right column, then choosing Save Editor Layout and reloading the page, restores that arrangement; Reset to Default restores the shipped layout. (test: `editor_layout_persistence_served`) POSTs a layout, restarts the server state read, asserts GET /api/editor/layout returns it, and asserts EDITOR_HTML calls "/api/editor/layout" rather than only logging.
acceptance_criteria: Resizing the Inspector dock and moving the FileSystem tab to the right column, then choosing Save Editor Layout and reloading the page, restores that arrangement; Reset to Default restores the shipped layout. (test: `editor_layout_persistence_served`) POSTs a layout, restarts the server state read, asserts GET /api/editor/layout returns it, and asserts EDITOR_HTML calls "/api/editor/layout" rather than only logging.

## Partial completion — bead intentionally left open

Reported by BronzeLake and verified: the delivered scope passed its tests, but the worker flagged the bead as incomplete, so it was returned to the queue instead of closed.

### Remaining scope
DELIVERED: the blend-shape correctness half. morph.rs DOCUMENTED itself as MESH_BLEND_SHAPE_MODE_NORMALIZED while IMPLEMENTING the RELATIVE formula. Godot's skeleton.glsl:144-148 is the contract: NORMALIZED (=0, the DEFAULT) is (1-Σw)*base + Σw*shape; RELATIVE (=1) is base + Σw*shape. apply_morph did the latter. **Patina today:**
- [engine-virtual-method-table] Both are registered with full virtual sets in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs (MultiplayerPeerExtension 23/23, MultiplayerAPIExtension 9/9) and the file's own comment at class_db.rs:11661-11670 says of them: "⚠️ Both are PURE VIRTUAL SURFACES — zero non-virtual methods between them. Every entry below is a hook the subclass provides, not an API the engine offers. That inverts the usual reading of a registration: nothing here is callable *on* the class; it is all callable *by* the engine." The engine never calls them: grepping `"_get_packet"`, `"_put_packet"`, `"_poll"`, `"_rpc"`, `"_get_peer_ids"`, `"_object_configuration_add"` across engine-rs/crates/ excluding tests hits class_db.rs only. **Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: `extends MultiplayerPeerExtension` is how a project implements a custom transport — the engine calls `_poll()` each frame, `_put_packet(buffer)` / `_get_packet()` / `_get_available_packet_count()` to move data, `_set_target_peer`/`_get_transfer_mode`/`_get_packet_channel` for routing, and `_get_unique_id`/`_is_server`/`_get_connection_status`/`_close`/`_disconnect_peer` for lifecycle. `extends MultiplayerAPIExtension` replaces the whole multiplayer stack (`_poll`, `_rpc`, `_get_peer_ids`, `_object_configuration_add/_remove`). PacketPeerExtension / StreamPeerExtension / WebRTCPeerConnectionExtension / WebRTCDataChannelExtension are the same pattern one layer down.\n\nPATINA: MultiplayerPeerExtension (23/23) and MultiplayerAPIExtension (9/9) are fully registered in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, and the source comment at class_db.rs:11661-11670 states the situation exactly — \"nothing here is callable *on* the class; it is all callable *by* the engine\" — while the engine calls none of them. title: Input: pinch/pan gesture events (InputEventMagnifyGesture, InputEventPanGesture) from the browser
description:
[audit-key: input/input-gesture-events] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json InputEventGesture(position) < InputEventWithModifiers; InputEventMagnifyGesture(factor); InputEventPanGesture(delta); upstream/godot/core/input/input_event.cpp

**Godot classes:** InputEventGesture, InputEventMagnifyGesture, InputEventPanGesture

**Patina today:**
- [input] No representation anywhere. Patina's `InputEvent` enum (engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs:479-578) has no gesture variant; `grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'InputEventMagnifyGesture|InputEventPanGesture' crates/ | grep -v /tests/` returns only the inspector schema table rows (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4615, :4619) — no runtime type, no ClassDB registration (all three appear in unregistered.txt:111,115,120), and no browser producer (no `wheel`+ctrlKey pinch synthesis and no `gesturestart`/`gesturechange` listener in engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: `InputEventGesture` (position) is the base for `InputEventMagnifyGesture` (factor — pinch zoom scale delta) and `InputEventPanGesture` (delta — two-finger/trackpad scroll as a Vector2). Godot delivers them through the normal `_input`/`_gui_input` path, and 2D/3D viewport-style camera code in user projects consumes them for pinch-to-zoom on touch devices and trackpads.\n\nPATINA CURRENT STATE: no representation at all. Patina's `InputEvent` enum (engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs:479-578) has Key/MouseButton/MouseMotion/GamepadButton/GamepadAxis/ScreenTouch/ScreenDrag/Midi/Action and no gesture variant. All three classes are unregistered (audit sweep unregistered.txt:111, :115, :120) and the only repo mentions are inspector-schema table rows (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4615, :4619). No browser producer exists — no `gesturestart`/`gesturechange` listener and no ctrl+wheel pinch synthesis in engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION: (1) add `InputEvent::MagnifyGesture { position, factor }` and `InputEvent::PanGesture { position, delta }` to input.rs:479 and register the three classes in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs on top of the InputEvent object family. (2) In editor_ui.rs, synthesize gestures the way browsers expose them: a `wheel` event with `ctrlKey` true is a pinch (factor from `1 - deltaY/100`), a two-finger `wheel` without ctrlKey is a pan; on Safari also accept `gesturechange`. POST to a new `/api/runtime/input/gesture` route in engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs. (3) Deliver through `MainLoop::push_event` → `SceneTree::push_input` and add the gesture arm to `gui_input_stage` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:3248) so Controls under the pointer receive them.\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: a browser pinch on the game view reaches a script's `_input` as `InputEventMagnifyGesture` with a sensible `factor` and a `position` in viewport coordinates.

**Prove it:** With a scene running under the editor server, POSTing a magnify gesture and stepping one frame makes a script's `_input` observe an event satisfying `event is InputEventMagnifyGesture` with the posted `factor` and `position`; a pan gesture likewise arrives as `InputEventPanGesture` with the posted `delta`; the served EDITOR_HTML synthesizes gestures from `wheel`+ctrlKey. (test: `gesture_events_reach_script_input`)
acceptance_criteria: With a scene running under the editor server, POSTing a magnify gesture and stepping one frame makes a script's `_input` observe an event satisfying `event is InputEventMagnifyGesture` with the posted `factor` and `position`; a pan gesture likewise arrives as `InputEventPanGesture` with the posted `delta`; the served EDITOR_HTML synthesizes gestures from `wheel`+ctrlKey. ## Implemented on both halves — one is green, the other has never been built

EmeraldIsland, 2026-08-20. **No code changed.** Released for a run.

### ⚠️ TWO test files share this bead's acceptance name, in DIFFERENT packages

    crates/gdscene/tests/gesture_events_reach_script_input.rs    <- built, 3/3 PASSING
    crates/gdeditor/tests/gesture_events_reach_script_input.rs   <- NO binary, never built

The acceptance names `gesture_events_reach_script_input` with no package, and the
two files are not copies — they test different halves:

* **gdscene** — injects the gesture directly and asserts a script's `_input` sees
  `InputEventMagnifyGesture` / `InputEventPanGesture`, plus a guard that a
  gesture does NOT move the pointer or press an action.
* **gdeditor** — stands up the editor server, POSTs to the real route over HTTP,
  and asserts the served `EDITOR_HTML` synthesises gestures client-side.

🔑 **A gate naming only `--test gesture_events_reach_script_input` is ambiguous,
and with the wrong `-p` it fails in a way that reads exactly like a failing
test.** Both packages must be named. This is the
[[feedback_scope_verify_test_command]] hazard in its most literal form — same
stem, two packages, only one built.

### Both halves are implemented

Server side:

* route registered — `editor_server.rs:2663`,
  `("POST", "/api/runtime/input/gesture") => api_input_gesture(...)`, handler at
  `:17622`.

Client side — every string the gdeditor test asserts on `EDITOR_HTML` is present:

| asserted | hits |
|---|---|
| `/api/runtime/input/gesture` | 3 |
| `e.ctrlKey` | 28 |
| `'magnify'` | 2 |
| `'pan'` | 4 |
| `gesturechange` | 1 |

The `gesturechange` branch matters and is there: Safari does not set `ctrlKey` on
a pinch, so the wheel branch never sees one — the source says exactly that at
`editor_ui.rs:7571` and `:7613`, and posts a magnify INSTEAD of a scroll.

### What a run would actually tell us

The gdscene half is already proven (3/3 on a current binary). The gdeditor half
has **never executed**, so its HTTP round trip — free port, retry connect, POST,
step, read back — is unverified even though every string it checks is present.
That is the half worth running.

title: Implement PacketPeerStream over the existing StreamPeer family
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/multiplayer-packet-peer-stream] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/doc/classes/PacketPeerStream.xml — `inherits="PacketPeer"`, is_instantiable=true, 3 properties (input_buffer_max_size, output_buffer_max_size, stream_peer) and 6 methods. Implements a length-prefixed packet protocol over any StreamPeer (upstream/godot/core/io/packet_peer.cpp).

**Godot classes:** PacketPeerStream

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-4] NOT REGISTERED: `rg -n 'ClassRegistration::new("PacketPeerStream"' engine-rs apps` -> 0 hits; `rg -n 'PacketPeerStream' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` -> 0 hits.
THE NEIGHBOURS ARE ALL PRESENT, WHICH ISOLATES THIS AS A GAP RATHER THAN A SCOPE DECISION: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:11471-11473 registers the `PacketPeer` base, :11773-11780 PacketPeerUDP, :11792 StreamPeerBuffer, :11844 StreamPeerTCP, :11894 PacketPeerDTLS, and interpreter.rs:3100 + :16329-16484 give StreamPeerBuffer a live instance dispatch. PacketPeerStream is the one member of the family with neither a registration nor a dispatch, so `PacketPeerStream.new()` is an unknown class while its base and both its collaborators exist.
IN SCOPE: this class is pure in-process framing over an existing StreamPeer — it needs no socket of its own, so the web-limitations carve-out in .claude/skills/port-audit/references/taxonomy.md:10-19 does not apply to it (a PacketPeerStream over a StreamPeerBuffer works entirely in memory).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/stream_peer_buffer.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Every neighbour in this family is already registered — PacketPeer base (class_db.rs:11471), PacketPeerUDP (:11773), PacketPeerDTLS (:11894), StreamPeerBuffer (:11792, with live dispatch at interpreter.rs:16329-16484), StreamPeerTCP (:11844) — but PacketPeerStream has neither a ClassDB entry nor an interpreter arm, so `PacketPeerStream.new()` is an unknown class.

It is the cheapest member of the set: Godot's implementation (core/io/packet_peer.cpp) is a 32-bit-length-prefixed framing layer over any StreamPeer, with `input_buffer_max_size` / `output_buffer_max_size` ring buffers. Over a StreamPeerBuffer it works entirely in memory, so nothing about it is blocked by the web platform.

Register it under PacketPeer with its 3 properties and 6 methods, and dispatch put_packet/get_packet/get_available_packet_count/set_stream_peer/get_stream_peer over the existing gdplatform StreamPeerBuffer handle table.

Ground truth: upstream/godot/doc/classes/PacketPeerStream.xml; upstream/godot/core/io/packet_peer.cpp.

**Prove it:** 1. `ClassDB.class_exists("PacketPeerStream")` is true, it is instantiable, its parent is PacketPeer, and it registers input_buffer_max_size / output_buffer_max_size / stream_peer with Godot's defaults.
2. A GDScript wrapping a StreamPeerBuffer: `pps.stream_peer = spb; pps.put_packet(a); pps.put_packet(b)` then reading back yields `get_available_packet_count() == 2` and the two packets in order with byte-identical contents.
3. Packet boundaries survive fragmentation: writing the framed bytes into the stream peer a few bytes at a time still yields exactly the original packets, never a merged or split one.
4. Exceeding output_buffer_max_size returns ERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY (Godot's documented error) instead of panicking, and get_packet() with no pending packet returns an empty PackedByteArray with ERR_UNAVAILABLE (test: `packet_peer_stream_framing_over_stream_peer_buffer`)
acceptance_criteria:
1. `ClassDB.class_exists("PacketPeerStream")` is true, it is instantiable, its parent is PacketPeer, and it registers input_buffer_max_size / output_buffer_max_size / stream_peer with Godot's defaults.
2. A GDScript wrapping a StreamPeerBuffer: `pps.stream_peer = spb; pps.put_packet(a); pps.put_packet(b)` then reading back yields `get_available_packet_count() == 2` and the two packets in order with byte-identical contents.
3. Packet boundaries survive fragmentation: writing the framed bytes into the stream peer a few bytes at a time still yields exactly the original packets, never a merged or split one.
4. Exceeding output_buffer_max_size returns ERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY (Godot's documented error) instead of panicking, and get_packet() with no pending packet returns an empty PackedByteArray with ERR_UNAVAILABLE (test: `packet_peer_stream_framing_over_stream_peer_buffer`)

title: Implement StreamPeerGZIP over the vendored miniz_oxide codec
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/multiplayer-streampeer-gzip] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/io/stream_peer_gzip.cpp; doc/classes/StreamPeerGZIP.xml; extension_api.json StreamPeerGZIP(inherits=StreamPeer, 4 methods: start_compression/start_decompression/finish/clear)

**Godot classes:** StreamPeerGZIP

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-6] Not registered and not implemented: `StreamPeerGZIP` is absent from the 638-name `ClassRegistration::new` list (its siblings `StreamPeer`, `StreamPeerBuffer`, `StreamPeerSocket`, `StreamPeerTCP`, `StreamPeerUDS` ARE registered), and `rg -in 'StreamPeerGZIP'` over engine-rs finds only the generated inspector schema table. This one is squarely in scope for the browser target — it is pure in-memory gzip/deflate with no socket involved, so Godot's own web export supports it fully — and the dependency is already vendored: `miniz_oxide` is used at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/zip.rs:11-17 and /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/portable_compressed_texture.rs:195-197.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/zip.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

**Godot ground truth:** `StreamPeerGZIP : StreamPeer` is a streaming gzip/deflate transform peer — `start_compression(use_deflate, buffer_size)`, `start_decompression(use_deflate, buffer_size)`, `finish()`, `clear()` — with the inherited StreamPeer put/get API pushing bytes in and pulling transformed bytes out (`upstream/godot/core/io/stream_peer_gzip.cpp`). It involves no socket, so Godot's own web export supports it unchanged.

**Patina today:** absent. `StreamPeerGZIP` is not among the 638 `ClassRegistration::new` names — its siblings `StreamPeer`, `StreamPeerBuffer`, `StreamPeerSocket`, `StreamPeerTCP` and `StreamPeerUDS` all are — and `rg -in 'StreamPeerGZIP'` over engine-rs finds only a row in the generated inspector schema table. No implementation exists.

**Implement:** register `StreamPeerGZIP` under `StreamPeer` in `class_db.rs` and implement the peer next to the existing StreamPeer family, backed by `miniz_oxide` — already a workspace dependency used at `crates/gdresource/src/zip.rs:11-17` (raw deflate) and `crates/gdresource/src/portable_compressed_texture.rs:195-197` (zlib). Support both the gzip container and raw deflate via `use_deflate`, honor `buffer_size`, and make `finish()` flush the trailing block. Expose it through the same script path the other StreamPeer classes use so `StreamPeerGZIP.new()` works from GDScript.

**Wiring requirement:** a GDScript in a played scene must be able to construct the peer, `put_data()` a payload, `finish()`, `get_data()` the compressed bytes, and round-trip them back through a decompression peer.

**Prove it:** an app-level test whose script compresses a ~64 KiB highly-compressible payload through `StreamPeerGZIP` in gzip mode, asserts the output is materially smaller and begins with the gzip magic `1f 8b`, feeds it into a decompression peer and asserts byte-exact recovery; repeats in `use_deflate` mode and asserts the raw-deflate output has no gzip header.

**Prove it:** A GDScript constructs `StreamPeerGZIP`, compresses a 64 KiB payload in gzip mode to a materially smaller buffer beginning with `1f 8b`, and a decompression peer recovers the original bytes exactly; the same round-trip in `use_deflate` mode produces a header-less raw deflate stream that also recovers exactly (test: `stream_peer_gzip_round_trips`)

**Godot classes:** StreamPeerTLS, TLSOptions, StreamPeerExtension

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-6] None of the three is registered: absent from the 638-name `ClassRegistration::new` list, and `rg -in 'tls|x509|CryptoKey' crates/gdcore/src crates/gdplatform/src` finds no implementation — only refusals: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_peer.rs:32-34 `TlsUnsupported` returned for every `wss://` URL (:467-468), and /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/http_request.rs:490-491 `request_sync_https_reports_tls_error`. `TLSOptions` is not itself a socket feature — it is the config object passed to `HTTPClient.connect_to_host`, `HTTPRequest.set_tls_options` and `WebSocketPeer.connect_to_url`, all of which a browser satisfies natively via fetch/WebSocket, so a script calling `TLSOptions.client()` must not fail. `StreamPeerTLS`'s own transport (raw TCP + mbedtls) IS web-unavailable per `upstream/godot/platform/web/net_socket_web.h:50-73`, where every NetSocket op returns ERR_UNAVAILABLE — so its correct web behavior is a registered class returning ERR_UNAVAILABLE, matching Godot.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_peer.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/http_request.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

**Godot ground truth:** `TLSOptions : RefCounted` (not instantiable — built via the statics `client(trusted_chain, common_name_override)`, `client_unsafe(trusted_chain)`, `server(key, certificate)`) is the configuration object accepted by `HTTPClient.connect_to_host`, `HTTPRequest.set_tls_options` and `WebSocketPeer.connect_to_url`. `StreamPeerTLS : StreamPeer` wraps a raw TCP peer in TLS (`accept_stream`, `connect_to_stream`, `disconnect_from_stream`, `get_status`, `poll`, `get_stream`). `StreamPeerExtension : StreamPeer` is the GDExtension virtual hook. Sources: `upstream/godot/core/io/stream_peer_tls.cpp`, `core/crypto/crypto.cpp`.

**Patina today:** none of the three is in ClassDB (absent from the 638 `ClassRegistration::new` names) and no TLS implementation exists — `rg -in 'tls|x509|CryptoKey'` over `crates/gdcore/src` and `crates/gdplatform/src` finds only refusals: `websocket_peer.rs:32-34,467-468` returns `TlsUnsupported` for every `wss://` URL, and `http_request.rs:490-491` pins that https reports a TLS error. So a script that merely constructs `TLSOptions.client()` to pass into an HTTP request fails at the class level.

**Scope note:** `StreamPeerTLS`'s transport (raw TCP + mbedtls) genuinely cannot work in a browser — Godot's own web platform stubs every socket operation to `ERR_UNAVAILABLE` (`upstream/godot/platform/web/net_socket_web.h:50-73`). So the target here is Godot-web parity: the classes exist and return the same errors Godot's web build returns. `TLSOptions` is different — it is pure configuration and must actually work, because fetch/WebSocket handle TLS natively.

**Implement:** register `StreamPeerTLS` (StreamPeer), `TLSOptions` (RefCounted, non-instantiable) and `StreamPeerExtension` (StreamPeer) in `class_db.rs`. Implement `TLSOptions` as a real value type carrying trusted chain / common-name override / server key+cert, expose the three static constructors to the interpreter, and thread it through `http_request.rs` and `websocket_peer.rs` so `set_tls_options` is accepted (and honored where a native backend exists, ignored where the browser owns the handshake). Give `StreamPeerTLS` methods that return `ERR_UNAVAILABLE`/`STATUS_ERROR` rather than being absent.

**Wiring requirement:** a GDScript in a played scene must be able to build a `TLSOptions` and pass it to an `HTTPRequest`, and calling `StreamPeerTLS.new().connect_to_stream(...)` must return Godot's web error code instead of raising an unknown-class error.

**Prove it:** an app-level test whose script constructs `TLSOptions.client()` and `TLSOptions.server(key, cert)`, asserts both are valid non-null objects reporting `is_class("TLSOptions")`, passes one to `HTTPRequest.set_tls_options` and asserts it is accepted, then asserts `StreamPeerTLS.new().connect_to_stream(peer)` returns `ERR_UNAVAILABLE` and `get_status()` reports the error status.

**Prove it:** A GDScript builds `TLSOptions.client()` and `TLSOptions.server(key, cert)` as valid objects reporting `is_class("TLSOptions")`, `HTTPRequest.set_tls_options` accepts one without error, and `StreamPeerTLS.new().connect_to_stream(peer)` returns `ERR_UNAVAILABLE` with `get_status()` reporting the error status rather than raising an unknown-class error (test: `tls_options_and_stream_peer_tls_surface`)
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript builds `TLSOptions.client()` and `TLSOptions.server(key, cert)` as valid objects reporting `is_class("TLSOptions")`, `HTTPRequest.set_tls_options` accepts one without error, and `StreamPeerTLS.new().connect_to_stream(peer)` returns `ERR_UNAVAILABLE` with `get_status()` reporting the error status rather than raising an unknown-class error (test: `tls_options_and_stream_peer_tls_surface`)

title: Register UDSServer to complete the SocketServer/StreamPeerUDS family
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/multiplayer-uds-server-registration] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/doc/classes/UDSServer.xml (inherits SocketServer; `listen(path)`, `take_connection() -> StreamPeerUDS`); extension_api.json UDSServer(SocketServer, 2 methods)

**Godot classes:** UDSServer

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-6] `UDSServer` is absent from the 638-name `ClassRegistration::new` list, but its entire family IS registered: `SocketServer` (its parent), `StreamPeerUDS` (its return type), `TCPServer`, `StreamPeerSocket` and `StreamPeerTCP` all appear in that list. So Patina has already adopted the convention of shipping the native-socket class surface, and UDSServer is the single omission — `SocketServer` currently has a registered subclass (`TCPServer`) and a registered peer type (`StreamPeerUDS`) with no server to hand it out. Behaviorally it is native-only: Godot's own web platform stubs every NetSocket operation to ERR_UNAVAILABLE (`upstream/godot/platform/web/net_socket_web.h:50-73`), and UDSServer.xml notes Unix Domain Sockets are Unix-only.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

**Godot ground truth:** `UDSServer : SocketServer` listens on a filesystem socket path and hands out `StreamPeerUDS` connections — `listen(path) -> Error`, `take_connection() -> StreamPeerUDS`, plus the inherited `is_connection_available()`/`is_listening()`/`stop()` from `SocketServer` (`upstream/godot/doc/classes/UDSServer.xml`; the doc notes UDS is Unix-only).

**Patina today:** `UDSServer` is the single missing member of a family Patina has otherwise already adopted — `SocketServer` (its parent), `StreamPeerUDS` (its return type), `TCPServer`, `StreamPeerSocket` and `StreamPeerTCP` are all in the 638-name `ClassRegistration::new` list; `UDSServer` is not. The result is a registered peer type with no registered server that produces it, and a `SocketServer` base whose subclass set is incomplete, so `ClassDB.get_inheriters_from_class("SocketServer")` diverges from Godot.

**Scope note:** behavior is native-only. Godot's own web platform stubs every `NetSocket` operation to `ERR_UNAVAILABLE` (`upstream/godot/platform/web/net_socket_web.h:50-73`), so on the browser target the correct behavior is exactly what Godot's web build does: the class exists, `listen()` returns `ERR_UNAVAILABLE`, `take_connection()` returns null. This bead is the class surface plus those correct errors, matching how the sibling socket classes are already handled.

**Implement:** register `UDSServer` under `SocketServer` in `class_db.rs` and give it `listen`/`take_connection`/`is_connection_available`/`stop` returning the same values the existing registered `TCPServer` returns on this target, so the two servers behave consistently.

**Wiring requirement:** `ClassDB.class_exists("UDSServer")` and `ClassDB.get_parent_class("UDSServer") == "SocketServer"` must hold, and `UDSServer` must appear in `ClassDB.get_inheriters_from_class("SocketServer")` alongside `TCPServer`.

**Prove it:** an app-level test asserting `UDSServer` instantiates through ClassDB with parent `SocketServer`, that `get_inheriters_from_class("SocketServer")` contains both `UDSServer` and `TCPServer`, and that `listen("/tmp/x.sock")` returns the same error code the already-registered `TCPServer.listen` returns on this target (so the two stay consistent).

**Prove it:** `ClassDB.instantiate("UDSServer")` succeeds with parent class `SocketServer`, `ClassDB.get_inheriters_from_class("SocketServer")` contains both `UDSServer` and `TCPServer`, and `UDSServer.listen(path)` returns the same error code the registered `TCPServer.listen` returns on this target (test: `uds_server_registered_under_socket_server`)
acceptance_criteria: `ClassDB.instantiate("UDSServer")` succeeds with parent class `SocketServer`, `ClassDB.get_inheriters_from_class("SocketServer")` contains both `UDSServer` and `TCPServer`, and `UDSServer.listen(path)` returns the same error code the registered `TCPServer.listen` returns on this target (test: `uds_server_registered_under_socket_server`)

title: NavigationMeshGenerator singleton absent; runtime navmesh baking exists in Rust with no script entry point
description:
[audit-key: navigation/navigation-navmesh-generator-singleton] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/navigation_3d/navigation_mesh_generator.cpp; doc/classes/NavigationMeshGenerator.xml:2 (`deprecated=""` at class level; bake() carries a deprecation note pointing at parse_source_geometry_data + bake_from_source_geometry_data); extension_api.json .singletons[] includes NavigationMeshGenerator

**Godot classes:** NavigationMeshGenerator

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-2] `rg -n 'NavigationMeshGenerator' -g '*.rs' crates/` returns only gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4698; the name is absent from class_db.rs's string literals and from interpreter.rs BUILTIN_SINGLETONS (:14464-14483). The capability underneath DOES exist: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/navigation.rs:309 `pub fn bake_navigation_mesh(...)` (called internally at :472), and the source-geometry resources are registered — class_db.rs:12169 NavigationMeshSourceGeometryData2D and :12187 NavigationMeshSourceGeometryData3D. So a script has the input resource type and no way to invoke the bake.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/navigation.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Patina can bake a navmesh — gdserver3d/src/navigation.rs:309 `bake_navigation_mesh(params, source)`, called internally at :472 — and it registers the input resources (class_db.rs:12169 NavigationMeshSourceGeometryData2D, :12187 NavigationMeshSourceGeometryData3D). What is missing is any way for a script to reach the bake: `rg 'NavigationMeshGenerator' crates/` finds only the editor's generated parent table at gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4698, and the name is in neither class_db.rs nor interpreter.rs BUILTIN_SINGLETONS.

Note the 4.6 status before implementing: doc/classes/NavigationMeshGenerator.xml:2 carries `deprecated=""` at the CLASS level, and its bake() method's deprecation note directs callers to NavigationServer3D.parse_source_geometry_data + NavigationServer3D.bake_from_source_geometry_data. So the priority work is the NavigationServer3D pair; NavigationMeshGenerator itself is a thin deprecated shim that should still exist so old project code keeps loading.

Work: expose parse_source_geometry_data / bake_from_source_geometry_data / bake_from_source_geometry_data_async / is_baking on NavigationServer3D (and the 2D equivalents on NavigationServer2D) backed by the existing gdserver3d bake, then register NavigationMeshGenerator (parent Object) as a deprecated singleton delegating to them.

**Prove it:** 1. NavigationServer3D exposes parse_source_geometry_data(navmesh, source_geometry, root_node) and bake_from_source_geometry_data(navmesh, source_geometry) to GDScript, backed by gdserver3d/src/navigation.rs:309.
2. A script that parses a scene containing one MeshInstance3D floor and bakes gets a NavigationMesh with a non-empty vertex and polygon set.
3. ClassDB registers NavigationMeshGenerator (parent Object) and it resolves as a script singleton; NavigationMeshGenerator.bake(navmesh, root) produces the same navmesh as the NavigationServer3D path.
4. NavigationMeshGenerator.clear(navmesh) empties it.

acceptance_criteria:
1. NavigationServer3D exposes parse_source_geometry_data(navmesh, source_geometry, root_node) and bake_from_source_geometry_data(navmesh, source_geometry) to GDScript, backed by gdserver3d/src/navigation.rs:309.
2. A script that parses a scene containing one MeshInstance3D floor and bakes gets a NavigationMesh with a non-empty vertex and polygon set.
3. ClassDB registers NavigationMeshGenerator (parent Object) and it resolves as a script singleton; NavigationMeshGenerator.bake(navmesh, root) produces the same navmesh as the NavigationServer3D path.
4. NavigationMeshGenerator.clear(navmesh) empties it.
5. A NavigationRegion3D whose navmesh was baked at runtime yields a non-empty path from NavigationServer3D.map_get_path across the baked floor — the bake reaches the live navigation map, not just a returned resource (test: `runtime_navmesh_bake_reachable_from_script`)

title: Nodes3D: dispatch the Node3D/Camera3D method + global-transform property API to GDScript
description:
[audit-key: nodes-3d/nodes3d-script-api] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/MISSING/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/node_3d.cpp (_bind_methods: look_at, look_at_from_position, rotate/rotate_x/y/z, rotate_object_local, scale_object_local, translate, translate_object_local, global_translate, global_rotate, global_scale, orthonormalize, set_identity, to_local, to_global, force_update_transform, get_parent_node_3d, set_notify_transform, set_disable_scale, get_world_3d) + properties global_position/global_transform/global_basis/global_rotation/basis/quaternion/rotation_degrees; upstream/godot/scene/3d/camera_3d.cpp (project_position, unproject_position, project_ray_origin, project_ray_normal, project_local_ray_normal, is_position_behind, is_position_in_frustum, make_current, clear_current, get_camera_transform, get_frustum, set_cull_mask_value) | upstream/godot/scene/3d/node_3d.cpp (rotation_order EULER_ORDER_XYZ..ZYX default YXZ, rotation_edit_mode EULER/QUATERNION/BASIS, set_quaternion/set_basis/set_rotation_degrees) and upstream/godot/core/math/basis.cpp Basis::from_euler(order) | upstream/godot/scene/3d/node_3d.cpp Node3D::is_visible_in_tree / _propagate_visibility_changed — a VisualInstance3D is drawn only when every ancestor is visible | upstream/godot/scene/main/scene_tree.cpp physics interpolation fraction; doc ProjectSettings physics/common/physics_interpolation; Node.physics_interpolation_mode / reset_physics_interpolation | upstream/godot/scene/3d/node_3d.h NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED (2000), NOTIFICATION_ENTER_WORLD (41), NOTIFICATION_EXIT_WORLD (42), NOTIFICATION_VISIBILITY_CHANGED (43), NOTIFICATION_LOCAL_TRANSFORM_CHANGED (2001), plus set_notify_transform/set_notify_local_transform gating

**Godot classes:** Node3D, Camera3D, Basis, VisualInstance3D, RigidBody3D

**Patina today:**
- [nodes-3d] Real Rust implementations exist and are unit-tested: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node3d.rs:350 look_at, :316 to_global, :322 to_local, :390 rotate, :406 translate, :189 get_global_transform, :279 get_global_transform_top_level, :208 set_global_position; /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/camera3d.rs:784 unproject_position, :819 project_position, :854 project_ray_origin, :885 project_ray_normal, :765 is_position_in_frustum, :648 make_current. NONE are dispatched to scripts: the single native dispatch table /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs:1196 `call_node_method` contains no 3D entries (its arms run 1242-1906 and cover connect_node/move_and_slide/raycast/area/control/draw_* only). Greps run repo-wide over non-test code for `"look_at"`, `"to_global"`, `"to_local"`, `"rotate_object_local"`, `"translate_object_local"`, `"orthonormalize"`, `"unproject_position"`, `"project_ray_normal"`, `"global_translate"`, `"rotate_y"`, `"make_current"` return only gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1017 and :6445 (a bare `MethodInfo` name registration used for introspection, with no implementation). Properties: scripting.rs:1085-1103 routes only `position`/`rotation`/`scale` when the payload is a Vector3; `global_position`, `global_transform`, `global_basis`, `global_rotation`, `basis`, `quaternion`, `rotation_degrees` are not routed, fall through to the raw node property table (scripting.rs:1030), and then to builtin_property_default (scripting.rs:935) which has entries only for CharacterBody2D/CharacterBody3D/RigidBody3D — so they read back Nil. Repo-wide grep for `global_position` in non-test code finds no handler in gdscene/src/scripting.rs or gdscript-interop/src at all.
- [nodes-3d] Basis euler conversion is hard-coded to YXZ with no order parameter: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/math3d.rs:240 `from_euler` ("YXZ convention, matching Godot") and :253 `to_euler` take no order. `gdscene/src/node3d.rs:58 compose_basis` / :40 `decompose_basis` call them unconditionally, so `rotation_order` on a Node3D is inert. Repo-wide grep for `rotation_order` / `EulerOrder` / `EULER_ORDER` in non-test code hits only the editor's display schema (gdeditor/src/inspector_schema.rs:232 and inspector_schema_generated.rs:165 etc.). `rotation_edit_mode` is likewise schema-only. Node3D registration (gdobject/src/class_db.rs:978-994) exposes only transform/visible/position/rotation/scale — no rotation_degrees, quaternion, basis, global_position, global_transform, global_basis, global_rotation, global_rotation_degrees or visibility_parent, all of which Godot's Node3D has.
- [nodes-3d] The wired 3D render list filters on the node's OWN visible flag: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d.rs:1023 sets `visible: node3d::is_visible(tree, nid)` and viewport_3d_render.rs:110 `build_render_list` filters `.filter(|r| r.visible)`. `node3d::is_visible` (gdscene/src/node3d.rs:227) reads only the node's own `visible` property; the ancestor-walking `is_visible_in_tree` exists at gdscene/src/node3d.rs:424 and IS used elsewhere in the same file — gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs:585 (lights) and :1656 (fog/decal/probe/occluder) both call `is_visible_in_tree`, and all three 2D paths do too (gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs:273, :1711, :1792; viewport_2d_render.rs:351). So hiding a parent Node3D leaves every descendant mesh drawn while correctly hiding the lights and env effects under it.
- [physics-3d] crates/gdscene/src/physics_interpolation_3d.rs:48 defines `INTERP_POSITION_3D_PROP = "__interp_position_3d"` (and a rotation twin) and the module explicitly notes it publishes to a property "for the renderer to read" (:43-47). MainLoop owns the state (crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:477) and updates it in the tick. But `grep -rn "__interp_position_3d\|INTERP_POSITION_3D_PROP" --include='*.rs' crates/` returns only the defining module and crates/gdscene/tests/physics3d_interp.rs — nothing in crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs, crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs or crates/gdrender3d reads it. The 3D draw path still uses the raw node transform, so at 10-30 physics ticks against 60 fps rendering the motion still visibly steps, which is the exact defect the module was written to fix.
- [nodes-3d] Repo-wide grep for `NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED` in non-test code finds only two doc comments (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:3168 and gdscene/src/node3d.rs:884) — no dispatch. `NOTIFICATION_LOCAL_TRANSFORM_CHANGED`, `NOTIFICATION_VISIBILITY_CHANGED`, ENTER_WORLD/EXIT_WORLD and `notify_transform` have 0 hits anywhere. The notification constants that DO exist (gdobject/src/lib.rs:45-50) cover only the Node-level set (ENTER_TREE, READY, EXIT_TREE, PROCESS, PHYSICS_PROCESS, PARENTED, UNPARENTED, PAUSED, UNPAUSED, DRAW, CHILD_ORDER_CHANGED, POSTINITIALIZE, PREDELETE, INSTANCED, MOVED_IN_PARENT, INTERNAL_*), and the dispatcher gdscene/src/lifecycle.rs:41/:61/:119 fires only ENTER_TREE/READY/EXIT_TREE.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node3d.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/camera3d.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/math3d.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_interpolation_3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/notification.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/lifecycle.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: Node3D exposes look_at/look_at_from_position, rotate, rotate_x/y/z, rotate_object_local, scale_object_local, translate, translate_object_local, global_translate, global_rotate, global_scale, orthonormalize, set_identity, to_local, to_global, force_update_transform, get_parent_node_3d, set_notify_transform/set_notify_local_transform, set_disable_scale, get_world_3d, plus the properties global_position, global_transform, global_basis, global_rotation, global_rotation_degrees, basis, quaternion, rotation_degrees (upstream/godot/scene/3d/node_3d.cpp _bind_methods). Camera3D adds project_position, unproject_position, project_ray_origin, project_ray_normal, project_local_ray_normal, is_position_behind, is_position_in_frustum, get_camera_transform, get_frustum, make_current/clear_current/set_current, set_cull_mask_value (upstream/godot/scene/3d/camera_3d.cpp).\n\nPATINA: every one of these already has a correct Rust implementation — engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node3d.rs:350 (look_at), :316 (to_global), :322 (to_local), :390 (rotate), :406 (translate), :189/:279 (global transform incl. top_level), :208 (set_global_position); engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/camera3d.rs:784/:819/:854/:885/:765/:648. NONE of them is reachable from a script. The only native dispatch table, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs:1196 `SceneTreeAccessor::call_node_method`, has zero 3D arms (its match runs from :1242 to :1906 and covers 2D/physics/control/draw calls only), so `self.look_at(target)` in a .gd file dies with UndefinedFunction. Property access is equally dead: scripting.rs:1085-1103 routes only `position`/`rotation`/`scale` (Vector3 payload) into node3d setters; `global_position`, `global_transform`, `basis`, `quaternion`, `rotation_degrees` are unrouted, read through the raw property table (scripting.rs:1030) and then builtin_property_default (scripting.rs:935, which has no Node3D entries), so they evaluate to Nil and `self.global_position.y += 1` dies mid-frame. gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1017 registers `make_current` as a MethodInfo name only, which makes `has_method("make_current")` lie.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION: add a 3D block to `call_node_method` in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs that forwards to the existing node3d/camera3d free functions (look_at/look_at_from_position/to_global/to_local/rotate/rotate_x/rotate_y/rotate_z/rotate_object_local/scale_object_local/translate/translate_object_local/global_translate/global_rotate/global_scale/orthonormalize/set_identity/force_update_transform/get_parent_node_3d, and the Camera3D projection/frustum/current calls, reading viewport width/height from the tree root window). **Merged findings (5):** Node3D / Camera3D script method + global-transform property API; Node3D rotation representations: rotation_order, rotation_edit_mode, quaternion, basis, rotation_degrees; Node3D visibility propagation to the 3D render list; 3D physics interpolation: blended transform is computed each frame but no renderer consumes it; Node3D transform/visibility/world notifications

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## ⚠️ This bead's acceptance criterion is UNSATISFIABLE — the pathfinder is correct

Diagnosis from a no-build lane (EmeraldIsland, 2026-08-20). I claimed this,
changed the test, found my own replacement was **also** wrong, and reverted. The
tree is byte-identical to how I found it.

### The failing assertion

`get_intersections(...)` summed over the returned path's segments must be `0`; it
reports **6**.

### Why 6 is the CORRECT answer

- `PolygonPathFinder` is a visibility graph over the polygon's **own points**, so a
  correct detour travels *through the obstacle's vertices*. For the square
  (10,10)-(20,20) and the query (0,15)->(30,15), the shortest detour is
  `(0,15) -> (10,10) -> (20,10) -> (30,15)`.
- `get_intersections` is a **faithful port** of Godot's
  `Geometry2D::segment_intersects_segment` (`core/math/geometry_2d.h:188`). I
  diffed them: same `ABlen` guard, same `Bn` projection, same same-sign rejection
  against `CMP_EPSILON`, same parallel/collinear rejection, same `ABpos` range
  check. It is **inclusive at the endpoints**, so a segment merely TOUCHING an
  edge at a shared corner counts.
- Each of the detour's three segments touches two edges at a shared corner. I
  reproduced the arithmetic from Godot's exact algorithm in Python: 2 + 2 + 2 =
  **6**, matching the observed failure precisely.

**Godot would report 6 here too.** The criterion "no segment of the path may cross
an obstacle edge" cannot hold for any vertex-routing pathfinder using Godot's
inclusive intersection test.

The module's own `segments_properly_cross` is the exclusive predicate and is
deliberately different — see the comment above `segment_intersection`, which
documents exactly this asymmetry.

### ⚠️ The obvious replacement is ALSO wrong

I rewrote the assertion to "no path segment's midpoint is inside the obstacle"
via `is_point_inside`. That fails too: the middle segment runs **along the top
edge**, so its midpoint is (15,10), exactly **on** the boundary. Tracing
`is_point_inside`'s even-odd cast by hand for that point — the right edge crosses
at x=20 > 15 (toggle), the left edge at x=10 (no toggle) — yields **true**. A
boundary point reads as inside, so that assertion fails on a correct path as well.

### What the bead should assert instead

All satisfiable and meaningful:

1. `count > 2` — already present and already passing; it detoured.
2. The path passes through at least one of the square's corners — pins vertex
   routing rather than an arbitrary curve.
3. Total path length > the straight-line distance (30) — pins a real detour.
4. Keep the sibling test's `hits == 2` on the straight line as the control that
   `get_intersections` and the edge set work at all.

The genuine invariant — no segment passes through the interior — is what
`segments_properly_cross` encodes, and the path is *built* from that predicate, so
it holds by construction. It has no clean script-level proxy, which is exactly
why the original assertion reached for `get_intersections` and got the wrong
semantics.

title: Path2D: honor PathFollow2D.cubic_interp and expose the Curve2D script API
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/path2d-curve2d] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/2d/path_2d.cpp `PathFollow2D::_update_transform` (samples `curve->sample_baked(progress, cubic_interp)`); extension_api.json PathFollow2D{cubic_interp}, Curve2D methods add_point/set_point_position/sample/sample_baked/sample_baked_with_rotation/get_baked_points/get_baked_length/get_closest_point/get_closest_offset/tessellate/tessellate_even_length

**Godot classes:** Path2D, PathFollow2D, Curve2D

**Patina today:**
- [nodes-2d] `crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:1172-1200` (the PathFollow2D branch) reads `progress`, `progress_ratio`, `loop`, `rotates`, `h_offset`, `v_offset` and `path_speed` — but never `cubic_interp`; `grep -rn 'cubic_interp' crates/` returns zero hits outside the generated inspector schema, so the baked sample is always linear. Separately, no Curve2D method is script-reachable: `grep -rn '"sample_baked"|"get_baked_points"|"tessellate"|"get_closest_point"' crates/gdscript-interop/src crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs` = 0, so a script cannot query or build a Curve2D at runtime even though `crates/gdscene/src/bezier_bake.rs` and `gdcore`'s Curve2D provide the math. Note `path_speed` (read at `main_loop.rs:1063`) is a Patina invention — Godot has no such property; scripts advance `progress` themselves, which they currently cannot do for a curve they built at runtime.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/bezier_bake.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: `PathFollow2D::_update_transform` samples the parent curve with `curve->sample_baked(progress, cubic_interp)` — `cubic_interp = true` (the default) smooths between baked cache points, `false` interpolates linearly (upstream/godot/scene/2d/path_2d.cpp). `Curve2D` is scriptable: `add_point`, `set_point_position/in/out`, `remove_point`, `clear_points`, `sample`, `sample_baked`, `sample_baked_with_rotation`, `get_baked_points`, `get_baked_length`, `get_closest_point`, `get_closest_offset`, `tessellate`, `tessellate_even_length` — this is how runtime-generated paths are built.

PATINA: the PathFollow2D branch at `crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:1172-1200` reads `progress`, `progress_ratio`, `loop`, `rotates`, `h_offset`, `v_offset` and a Patina-invented `path_speed`, but never `cubic_interp` — `grep -rn cubic_interp crates/` is empty outside the generated inspector schema, so sampling is unconditionally linear. No Curve2D method is bound to GDScript: `grep -rn '"sample_baked"|"get_baked_points"|"tessellate"|"get_closest_point"' crates/gdscript-interop/src crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs` = 0, even though `crates/gdscene/src/bezier_bake.rs::bake_curve` and `gdcore`'s Curve2D already implement the math (they are used from `crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:620`).

APPROACH: read `cubic_interp` (default true) in the PathFollow2D branch and pass it to the curve sample, adding a cubic path to the baked sampler in `bezier_bake.rs`/`gdcore` Curve2D where only linear exists. Bind the Curve2D methods above in `crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs` + `crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs`, backed by the `curve_points` storage `packed_scene.rs:620-628` already writes, and re-bake `curve_points` whenever a script mutates points so `process_path_follows` picks it up the next frame.

WIRING: `.tscn` Path2D + PathFollow2D + a script that appends curve points at runtime -> `MainLoop::step` -> `process_path_follows` -> the follower's position tracks the extended, cubically-sampled curve.

**Prove it:** A .tscn PathFollow2D on a curve with sparse control points reports a DIFFERENT sampled position at a mid-segment `progress` with `cubic_interp = true` versus `cubic_interp = false`, and the cubic result lies off the straight chord. A GDScript that calls `$Path2D.curve.add_point(Vector2(200,0))` in `_ready()` extends `get_baked_length()` and lets the follower reach the new point after enough steps; `get_closest_offset(Vector2(100,10))` returns a value near the corresponding progress. (test: `path2d_cubic_interp_and_curve_script_api`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test path2d_cubic_interp_and_curve_script_api`.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn PathFollow2D on a curve with sparse control points reports a DIFFERENT sampled position at a mid-segment `progress` with `cubic_interp = true` versus `cubic_interp = false`, and the cubic result lies off the straight chord. A GDScript that calls `$Path2D.curve.add_point(Vector2(200,0))` in `_ready()` extends `get_baked_length()` and lets the follower reach the new point after enough steps; `get_closest_offset(Vector2(100,10))` returns a value near the corresponding progress. (test: `path2d_cubic_interp_and_curve_script_api`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test path2d_cubic_interp_and_curve_script_api`.

title: Java/JNI bridge class surface (JavaClassWrapper, JavaClass, JavaObject, JNISingleton) absent from ClassDB
description:
[audit-key: platform/platform-os-java-android-bridge] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/platform/android/api/java_class_wrapper.h, jni_singleton.h, api.cpp:48-52 — GDREGISTER_CLASS(JNISingleton/JavaClass/JavaObject/JavaClassWrapper) plus the JavaClassWrapper Engine singleton, registered on ALL platforms; api.cpp:38/43/56/78 gate `#if !defined(ANDROID_ENABLED)` dummy implementations, so a web build ships the class surface with no-op behavior. doc/classes/JavaClassWrapper.xml, JavaClass.xml, JavaObject.xml, JNISingleton.xml

**Godot classes:** JavaClass, JavaClassWrapper, JavaObject, JNISingleton

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-2] Zero hits repo-wide: `rg -n '\bJavaClass\b|\bJavaClassWrapper\b|\bJavaObject\b|\bJNISingleton\b' -g '*.rs' crates/` returns only gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4629/4633/4634/4635 (the editor's generated parent table), and none of the four is in class_db.rs's string-literal dump. Scope: the JNI FUNCTIONALITY is out of scope for a browser engine — these types live under upstream/godot/platform/android/api/ and only do real work when ANDROID_ENABLED. But the CLASS SURFACE is not out of scope: platform/android/api/api.cpp:48-52 runs on every platform including web, registering all four and adding the JavaClassWrapper singleton, with dummy definitions gated at :38/:43/:56/:78. Patina's own precedent for exactly this split is gdobject/tests/oos_native_sockets.rs:1-16 ("on web cite OUT_OF_SCOPE per web limitations, BUT the CLASS surface should exist with correct errors") — seven socket classes registered surface-only.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

SURFACE ONLY — the JNI behavior is genuinely out of scope on a browser target and must NOT be implemented.

Godot registers all four Java-bridge types on every platform, not just Android: upstream/godot/platform/android/api/api.cpp:48-52 calls GDREGISTER_CLASS on JNISingleton, JavaClass, JavaObject and JavaClassWrapper and adds JavaClassWrapper as an Engine singleton, with dummy implementations gated by `#if !defined(ANDROID_ENABLED)` at :38/:43/:56/:78. A Godot web export therefore answers ClassDB.class_exists("JavaClassWrapper") with true and returns null from JavaClassWrapper.wrap(). Patina answers false: `rg 'JavaClass|JavaObject|JNISingleton' crates/` finds only the editor's generated parent table (gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4629-4635), so ClassDB and the editor already disagree.

This is the same shape as the socket surfaces closed by gdobject/tests/oos_native_sockets.rs, which states the rule explicitly: the transport is out of scope, the class is not.

Work: register the four classes with Godot's parents (JavaClass -> RefCounted, JavaObject -> RefCounted, JNISingleton -> Object, JavaClassWrapper -> Object) and make JavaClassWrapper reachable as a singleton whose wrap()/get_singleton() return null the way Godot's non-Android dummy does. Implement no JNI.

**Prove it:** 1. ClassDB registers JavaClass (RefCounted), JavaObject (RefCounted), JNISingleton (Object) and JavaClassWrapper (Object) with those exact parents, matching gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4629-4635 so the editor and ClassDB agree.
2. class_exists() is true for all four and their inheritance chains reach Object.
3. JavaClassWrapper resolves as a script identifier and JavaClassWrapper.wrap("java.lang.String") returns null without erroring — matching Godot's non-Android dummy.
4. The test asserts surface-only explicitly: no JNI call path is added, and a doc comment records the OUT_OF_SCOPE citation (taxonomy.md scope anchor + platform/android/api/api.cpp:38-78) (test: `oos_java_bridge_class_surface`)

title: LightmapGIData / Lightmapper / LightmapperRD missing; LightmapGI is a registered stub with no data resource type
description:
[audit-key: rendering/rendering-3d-lightmap-bake-family] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/lightmap_gi.cpp (LightmapGIData), scene/3d/lightmapper.h (Lightmapper abstract base), modules/lightmapper_rd/lightmapper_rd.cpp (LightmapperRD); doc/classes/LightmapGIData.xml (lightmap_textures, light_texture, uses_spherical_harmonics, add_user, get_user_count, clear_users), Lightmapper.xml ("Abstract class extended by lightmappers, for use in LightmapGI"), LightmapperRD.xml

**Godot classes:** LightmapGIData, Lightmapper, LightmapperRD

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-2] All three return zero hits: `rg -n '\bLightmapGIData\b|\bLightmapper\b|\bLightmapperRD\b' -g '*.rs' crates/` finds nothing (only inspector_schema_generated.rs entries), and none is among class_db.rs's string literals. The parent node IS registered — class_db.rs:2984 `ClassRegistration::new("LightmapGI")` with defaults sourced from doc/classes/LightmapGI.xml (:2982) — but its backing implementation is self-declared inert: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/gi.rs:1 "Global Illumination stub nodes: VoxelGI and LightmapGI", :5 "the configuration surface so that scenes using VoxelGI or LightmapGI can [load]", :278 "Stub for Godot's LightmapGI node", :283 `pub struct LightmapGI`. So LightmapGI accepts a `light_data` property it can neither type nor consume.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/gi.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

LightmapGI is registered (class_db.rs:2984, defaults taken from doc/classes/LightmapGI.xml per the comment at :2982) but its backing implementation announces itself as inert: gdserver3d/src/gi.rs:1 "Global Illumination stub nodes", :5 "the configuration surface so that scenes using VoxelGI or LightmapGI can [load]", :278 "Stub for Godot's LightmapGI node".

The three classes that make it mean anything are absent — `rg 'LightmapGIData|Lightmapper|LightmapperRD' crates/` returns nothing outside the editor's generated parent table. LightmapGIData is the Resource that a .tscn's `light_data = ExtResource(...)` points at: it carries the baked lightmap textures, the per-instance user list and the spherical-harmonics flag. Without it, a project that ships a PRE-BAKED lightmap (the common case — baking is an editor/offline step) loads a LightmapGI node whose light_data property references a type ClassDB cannot construct, so the baked lighting is silently dropped even though nothing needed to be baked at runtime.

Scope split worth respecting: CONSUMING a baked LightmapGIData is a runtime feature and the higher-value half. PRODUCING one (Lightmapper / LightmapperRD, which needs GPU compute raytracing) is an editor/offline feature and can follow later or be scoped out with a citation.

Work: register LightmapGIData (parent Resource) with lightmap_textures, light_texture, uses_spherical_harmonics and the user list API; load it from .tscn/.tres and feed its textures into the 3D renderer's ambient/indirect term for meshes with the matching bake flags. Register Lightmapper (abstract, parent RefCounted) and LightmapperRD (parent Lightmapper) as surface for now.

**Prove it:** 1. ClassDB registers LightmapGIData (parent Resource), Lightmapper (abstract, parent RefCounted) and LightmapperRD (parent Lightmapper); is_abstract("Lightmapper") is true and instantiate("Lightmapper") fails.
2. Loading a .tscn whose LightmapGI has `light_data = ExtResource("...")` pointing at a LightmapGIData .res yields a LightmapGI node whose light_data is a real LightmapGIData, not Nil — assert the lightmap_textures array is non-empty.
3. get_user_count()/get_user_path(i) round-trip through a save/load of that resource.
4. A MeshInstance3D registered as a lightmap user renders brighter with the baked data present than with light_data cleared (assert the sampled indirect term differs), proving the data reaches the renderer rather than sitting in a struct.
5. If runtime BAKING is deferred, LightmapGI.bake() returns a clear unsupported error rather than silently doing nothing, and the deferral is recorded with a scope citation (test: `prebaked_lightmap_gi_data_loads_and_reaches_the_renderer`)

2. Loading a .tscn whose LightmapGI has `light_data = ExtResource("...")` pointing at a LightmapGIData .res yields a LightmapGI node whose light_data is a real LightmapGIData, not Nil — assert the lightmap_textures array is non-empty.
