title: Rendering2D: generate the canvas SDF from occluders and expose it to particles + shaders
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/canvas-sdf] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/servers/rendering (canvas SDF generation from LightOccluder2D with sdf_collision), Viewport.sdf_oversize/sdf_scale, LightOccluder2D.sdf_collision, RenderingServer.canvas_light_occluder_set_as_sdf_collision, canvas_item shader builtins `texture_sdf`/`texture_sdf_normal`/`sdf_to_screen_uv`/`screen_uv_to_sdf`

**Godot classes:** LightOccluder2D, Viewport, GPUParticles2D

**Patina today:**
- [rendering-2d] `CanvasQuality` stores `sdf_oversize`/`sdf_scale` with an explicit comment that they are "parsed and carried but **not yet consumed**" (crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:1364-1370). `LightOccluder2D.sdf_collision` is never read (crates/gdscene/src/light2d_scene.rs:146-155 reads only `polygon`/`light_mask`), and `canvas_light_occluder_set_as_sdf_collision` is absent from the RenderingServer dispatch (crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs has no `canvas_light_*` arms at all). The `texture_sdf` shader vocabulary is registered in ClassDB for VisualShader (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:5618) with no SDF buffer behind it; `grep -rn 'sdf_texture\|texture_sdf' crates/gdrender2d crates/gdserver2d` returns nothing.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/light2d_scene.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/light2d.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: occluders marked `sdf_collision` are rasterized into a signed-distance-field texture sized by the viewport's `sdf_oversize`/`sdf_scale`; GPUParticles2D collision samples it, and canvas_item shaders reach it through `texture_sdf`, `texture_sdf_normal`, `sdf_to_screen_uv` and `screen_uv_to_sdf` (upstream/godot/servers/rendering; extension_api.json Viewport.sdf_oversize/sdf_scale, LightOccluder2D.sdf_collision, RenderingServer.canvas_light_occluder_set_as_sdf_collision).

PATINA NOW: nothing generates an SDF. `CanvasQuality` carries `sdf_oversize`/`sdf_scale` with the comment "parsed and carried but **not yet consumed**" (crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:1364-1370). `LightOccluder2D.sdf_collision` is never read (crates/gdscene/src/light2d_scene.rs:146-155). The `texture_sdf` builtins are registered for VisualShader (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:5618) with no buffer behind them, and there is no `canvas_light_occluder_*` arm in the RenderingServer dispatch. Consequently 2D particle collision against level geometry is impossible.

APPROACH: add an SDF module to gdrender2d that, given the frame size, `sdf_oversize` and `sdf_scale`, rasterizes every `sdf_collision` occluder polygon into a coverage buffer and runs a jump-flood (or 8SSEDT) pass to a signed distance buffer. Build it once per frame in the Play assembly, keyed off `CanvasQuality`. Read `sdf_collision` in `collect_occluders_2d` (crates/gdscene/src/light2d_scene.rs). Feed the buffer to the 2D particle step (crates/gdscene/src/particle.rs) so `collision_mode` particles bounce/stop against it, and bind it in the canvas shader evaluator for the `texture_sdf*` builtins with the `sdf_to_screen_uv`/`screen_uv_to_sdf` conversions.

WIRING: the SDF must be produced inside the served Play frame assembly and consumed by the particle phase in the same tick.

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a LightOccluder2D (sdf_collision = true) forming a floor and a GPUParticles2D emitting downward with collision enabled shows particles accumulating at the occluder line instead of passing through; a canvas_item shader sampling `texture_sdf(screen_uv_to_sdf(SCREEN_UV))` returns near-zero distance on the occluder edge and increasing values away from it. (test: `canvas_sdf_occluders_and_particle_collision`)
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a LightOccluder2D (sdf_collision = true) forming a floor and a GPUParticles2D emitting downward with collision enabled shows particles accumulating at the occluder line instead of passing through; a canvas_item shader sampling `texture_sdf(screen_uv_to_sdf(SCREEN_UV))` returns near-zero distance on the occluder edge and increasing values away from it. (test: `canvas_sdf_occluders_and_particle_collision`)

title: Compositor3D: invoke CompositorEffect callbacks at the render pass boundaries
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/compositor] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/servers/rendering/storage/compositor_storage.* and scene/resources/compositor.cpp — CompositorEffect._render_callback fires at EFFECT_CALLBACK_TYPE_PRE_OPAQUE / POST_OPAQUE / POST_SKY / PRE_TRANSPARENT / POST_TRANSPARENT with RenderData

**Godot classes:** Compositor, CompositorEffect

**Patina today:**
- [rendering-3d] gdserver3d/src/compositor.rs (196 lines) defines Compositor, CompositorEffect and EffectCallbackType and is re-exported at gdserver3d/src/lib.rs:39; its own doc comment (compositor.rs:7) says a WorldEnvironment/Camera3D references a Compositor to inject effects. `grep -rn "gdserver3d::compositor|CompositorEffect" --include=*.rs engine-rs/crates` outside the file finds only the lib.rs re-export, gdobject/src/class_db.rs:4169-4171 (registration), class_db.rs:9767 (per-frame render-data object registration) and test files. Neither gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs nor gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs mentions a compositor or invokes a callback at any pass boundary, and there is no `compositor` field on Viewport3D (gdserver3d/src/viewport.rs:9).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/compositor.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/viewport.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: a WorldEnvironment or Camera3D references a Compositor holding an ordered `compositor_effects` list; each CompositorEffect declares an `effect_callback_type` (PRE_OPAQUE, POST_OPAQUE, POST_SKY, PRE_TRANSPARENT, POST_TRANSPARENT) and `_render_callback(effect_callback_type, render_data)` runs at that point in the frame with access to the render buffers. See upstream/godot/scene/resources/compositor.cpp and servers/rendering/storage/compositor_storage.*.

Patina current state: the data model exists and nothing calls it. engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/compositor.rs (196 lines) defines `Compositor`, `CompositorEffect` and `EffectCallbackType`, and its own header comment (:7) describes the intended WorldEnvironment/Camera3D wiring. Outside that file the only references are the lib.rs re-export (:39), the ClassDB registration (gdobject/src/class_db.rs:4169) and the per-frame render-data class registrations (class_db.rs:9767) — plus tests. Neither renderer mentions a compositor, and `Viewport3D` (gdserver3d/src/viewport.rs:9) has no `compositor` field, so there is no place for the list to live.

Implementation approach: (1) add `compositor: Option<Compositor>` to `Viewport3D` and resolve it from the WorldEnvironment / Camera3D in the same place `Environment3D` is resolved (gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:7701 and gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs); (2) define the render-data handle the callback receives (colour buffer, depth buffer, view/projection, size) as a concrete struct in gdserver3d/src/compositor.rs; (3) invoke the callbacks in frame order at each of the five boundaries in gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs and at the equivalent points in gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs; (4) route script-defined effects through the gdscript-interop bridge so a CompositorEffect subclass with a `_render_callback` runs. Keep the callback list ordered and skip disabled effects.

Wiring requirement: WorldEnvironment.compositor in a .tscn -> Viewport3D.compositor -> callback invoked mid-frame with a real buffer it can mutate.

**Prove it:** A .tscn WorldEnvironment referencing a Compositor with one effect registered at POST_TRANSPARENT causes that effect's callback to run exactly once per rendered frame and its mutation of the colour buffer (e.g. tinting the frame) to appear in the output; removing the effect restores the untinted frame. (test: `compositor_effect_runs_in_frame`) — registers a Rust test effect through the Compositor on a scene loaded from a .tscn string, renders one frame through the editor 3D render path, and asserts both the invocation count and the pixel change.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn WorldEnvironment referencing a Compositor with one effect registered at POST_TRANSPARENT causes that effect's callback to run exactly once per rendered frame and its mutation of the colour buffer (e.g. tinting the frame) to appear in the output; removing the effect restores the untinted frame. (test: `compositor_effect_runs_in_frame`) — registers a Rust test effect through the Compositor on a scene loaded from a .tscn string, renders one frame through the editor 3D render path, and asserts both the invocation count and the pixel change.

title: JSON and Marshalls are implemented and dispatchable but unknown to ClassDB; JSON is modelled as a singleton, not a class
description:
[audit-key: resources/resources-io-json-marshalls-classdb-registration] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/io/json.cpp (JSON is a RefCounted CLASS with static parse_string/stringify/from_native/to_native, NOT a singleton), core/io/marshalls.cpp (Marshalls IS an Object singleton); doc/classes/JSON.xml, Marshalls.xml; extension_api.json .singletons[] contains Marshalls but not JSON

**Godot classes:** JSON, Marshalls

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-2] Both are fully implemented in the interpreter and both are missing from ClassDB. JSON: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:20581 `fn call_json_static` handles new/parse/parse_string/stringify/from_native/to_native; :20301 `fn call_json_instance` handles get_data (:20339), get_error_line (:20340), get_error_message (:20341), get_parsed_text (:20344); :20289 creates the `JSON.new()` handle; :20354 json_from_native and :20405 json_to_native; :20508 the stringify serializer. Marshalls: interpreter.rs:2947 intercepts `Marshalls.<member>` and routes to `call_marshalls_static`. Both names are in BUILTIN_SINGLETONS (interpreter.rs:14473 "JSON", :14475 "Marshalls"). Neither name is among class_db.rs's string literals (verified via the full literal dump). Note the modelling error too: Godot's JSON is a RefCounted class, not a singleton (it is absent from extension_api.json's .singletons list), so Patina reaching it only through an `Expr::Ident("JSON")` interception (interpreter.rs:2920, and see the comment at :20583-20584) means ClassDB.instantiate("JSON") and a typed `var j: JSON` cannot work even though `JSON.new()` does.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Both classes have real, thorough implementations in the GDScript interpreter and neither exists in ClassDB.

JSON: interpreter.rs:20581 call_json_static covers new / parse / parse_string / stringify (with indent, sort_keys, full_precision) / from_native (:20354) / to_native (:20405); interpreter.rs:20301 call_json_instance covers get_data, get_error_line, get_error_message, get_parsed_text; interpreter.rs:20508 is the Godot-compatible serializer. Marshalls: interpreter.rs:2947 routes Marshalls.<member> to call_marshalls_static. Both are listed in BUILTIN_SINGLETONS (interpreter.rs:14473, :14475). Neither name appears in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs.

There is also a modelling error. Godot's JSON is a RefCounted CLASS (core/io/json.cpp) — it is NOT in extension_api.json's .singletons list; Marshalls is. Patina reaches JSON only by intercepting the bare identifier `JSON` in eval_expr (interpreter.rs:2920, acknowledged in the comment at :20583-20584). So `JSON.new()` works by luck while ClassDB.instantiate("JSON") fails, a typed `var j: JSON = JSON.new()` has no type to bind to, a `@export var cfg: JSON` gives the inspector nothing, and a .tres holding `Object(JSON, ...)` cannot load.

Work: register JSON (parent RefCounted, with its static and instance methods and the `data` property) and Marshalls (parent Object, singleton) in ClassDB from doc/classes/JSON.xml and Marshalls.xml. Route JSON construction through ClassDB.instantiate so both spellings reach the same implementation.

**Prove it:** 1. ClassDB registers JSON with parent RefCounted (NOT Object/singleton) and Marshalls with parent Object; class_exists() is true for both.
2. ClassDB.instantiate("JSON") returns a working instance whose parse()/get_data()/get_error_line() behave the same as the existing `JSON.new()` path.
3. class_has_method("JSON","stringify"), class_has_method("JSON","parse_string"), class_has_method("JSON","from_native") and class_has_method("Marshalls","variant_to_base64") are all true.
4. A typed declaration `var j: JSON = JSON.new()` type-checks.
5. The BUILTIN_SINGLETONS-vs-ClassDB guard test (see the Input/InputMap bead) passes for both names (test: `json_and_marshalls_registered_and_instantiable`)
acceptance_criteria:
1. ClassDB registers JSON with parent RefCounted (NOT Object/singleton) and Marshalls with parent Object; class_exists() is true for both.
2. ClassDB.instantiate("JSON") returns a working instance whose parse()/get_data()/get_error_line() behave the same as the existing `JSON.new()` path.
3. class_has_method("JSON","stringify"), class_has_method("JSON","parse_string"), class_has_method("JSON","from_native") and class_has_method("Marshalls","variant_to_base64") are all true.
4. A typed declaration `var j: JSON = JSON.new()` type-checks.
5. The BUILTIN_SINGLETONS-vs-ClassDB guard test (see the Input/InputMap bead) passes for both names (test: `json_and_marshalls_registered_and_instantiable`)

title: Resources-IO: bind the remaining nine ResourceUID singleton methods to GDScript
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/resource-uid-script] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json ResourceUID: id_to_text, text_to_id, create_id, create_id_for_path, has_id, add_id, set_id, get_id_path, remove_id, uid_to_path, path_to_uid, ensure_path (12).

**Godot classes:** ResourceUID

**Patina today:**
- [resources-io] `gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:19413 fn call_resourceuid_static` binds exactly three: `id_to_text`, `text_to_id`, `has_id`. The engine-side registry already implements more than is bound — `gdresource/src/uid.rs:163` provides `get_id_path`, and uid.rs:190-230 loads `uid_cache.bin` and `.uid` sidecars — so `create_id`, `create_id_for_path`, `add_id`, `set_id`, `get_id_path`, `remove_id`, `uid_to_path`, `path_to_uid` and `ensure_path` are unreachable from GDScript despite the backing store existing.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/uid.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `ResourceUID` exposes 12 methods — `id_to_text`, `text_to_id`, `create_id`, `create_id_for_path`, `has_id`, `add_id`, `set_id`, `get_id_path`, `remove_id`, plus the 4.5/4.6 additions `uid_to_path`, `path_to_uid` and `ensure_path` (extension_api.json). Tooling scripts and `@tool` plugins use them to mint and resolve UIDs when creating or moving resources.

Patina current state: `gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:19413 call_resourceuid_static` binds only `id_to_text`, `text_to_id` and `has_id`. The backing registry is richer than the binding — `gdresource/src/uid.rs:163` already implements `get_id_path`, and uid.rs:190-230 populates the registry from `uid_cache.bin` and `.uid` sidecars — so the remaining nine methods are unreachable purely for lack of dispatch arms.

Implementation approach: add the missing registry operations to `gdresource/src/uid.rs` (`create_id` using Godot's random-with-high-bit scheme, `create_id_for_path` deterministic from the path, `add_id`, `set_id`, `remove_id`, and the `uid_to_path`/`path_to_uid`/`ensure_path` conveniences that fall back to the path when no UID is registered), then extend the match in `gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:19413` to cover all 12 with Godot's return types and error codes (`add_id` returns Error, `get_id_path` returns String, `has_id` bool).

Wiring requirement: the methods must operate on the same process-global registry the `.tscn` loader consults for `uid://` ExtResource references (`gdresource/src/loader.rs:228 parse_uid_string` → `gdresource::uid::text_to_id`), so a script that adds a UID mapping makes a later `uid://` resource reference in a loaded scene resolve.

**Prove it:** From a script in a running scene, `ResourceUID.create_id()` returns a distinct valid id each call, `add_id(id, "res://a.tres")` then `get_id_path(id)` returns that path and `has_id(id)` is true, `remove_id(id)` clears it, `path_to_uid`/`uid_to_path` are inverse for a registered pair, and after `add_id` a scene referencing that `uid://` ExtResource loads to the mapped file. Test: `resource_uid_script_registry_resolves_uid_refs` — exercises all 12 methods from GDScript and then loads a fixture `.tscn` whose ExtResource is a `uid://` reference registered at runtime (test: `resource_uid_script_registry_resolves_uid_refs`).
acceptance_criteria: From a script in a running scene, `ResourceUID.create_id()` returns a distinct valid id each call, `add_id(id, "res://a.tres")` then `get_id_path(id)` returns that path and `has_id(id)` is true, `remove_id(id)` clears it, `path_to_uid`/`uid_to_path` are inverse for a registered pair, and after `add_id` a scene referencing that `uid://` ExtResource loads to the mapped file. Test: `resource_uid_script_registry_resolves_uid_refs` — exercises all 12 methods from GDScript and then loads a fixture `.tscn` whose ExtResource is a `uid://` reference registered at runtime (test: `resource_uid_script_registry_resolves_uid_refs`).

title: XMLParser: add open(path), get_node_offset, get_current_line and get_named_attribute_value_safe
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/xmlparser-surface] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json XMLParser: read, get_node_type, get_node_name, get_node_data, get_node_offset, get_attribute_count, get_attribute_name, get_attribute_value, has_attribute, get_named_attribute_value, get_named_attribute_value_safe, is_empty, get_current_line, skip_section, seek, open, open_buffer (17). | upstream/godot/doc/classes/XMLParser.xml — XMLParser inherits RefCounted, registered in core; NodeType enum NODE_NONE..NODE_UNKNOWN plus open/open_buffer/read/get_node_type/get_node_name/get_node_data/get_attribute_count/get_attribute_name/get_attribute_value/has_attribute/get_named_attribute_value(_safe)/get_node_offset/seek/skip_section

**Godot classes:** XMLParser

**Patina today:**
- [resources-io] `gdcore/src/xml_parser.rs` implements read (:61), node_type (:81), node_name (:86), node_data (:91), is_empty (:96), attribute_count (:101), attribute_name (:106), attribute_value (:111), has_attribute (:116), named_attribute_value (:122), open_buffer (:358), seek (:367), skip_section (:385) and cursor (:401) — 13 of 17. Absent: `open(path)` (load from a file rather than a buffer), `get_node_offset`, `get_current_line`, and `get_named_attribute_value_safe` (the non-erroring variant). `grep -n 'fn open\b\|get_current_line\|node_offset\|_safe' gdcore/src/xml_parser.rs` returns no matches for those four.
- [sweep-7] Implemented and script-reachable, but absent from ClassDB. Implementation: engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/xml_parser.rs (pull parser + handle registry at :303-311). Script reachability is a hardcoded branch, not ClassDB: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:3054 `if class_name == "XMLParser" { return Ok(Variant::ObjectId(gdcore::xml_parser::XmlParser::new_handle())) }`, with instance dispatch at interpreter.rs:20876-20983. Registration absence: `grep -x XMLParser` against the 4186 literals extracted from engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs = 0 hits (ConfigFile IS there). So `ClassDB.class_exists("XMLParser")` is false (interpreter.rs:14922) and `ClassDB.instantiate("XMLParser")` cannot work, and the editor's ClassDB-driven create dialog (gdeditor/src/create_dialog.rs) does not know it. gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:5410 has the ("XMLParser","RefCounted") row but that file makes 0 register_class calls.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/xml_parser.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/xml_parser.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `XMLParser` exposes 17 methods (extension_api.json). Beyond the pull-parsing core, `open(path)` loads a document straight from a `res://`/`user://` file, `get_node_offset()` reports the byte offset of the current node (used with `seek()` to revisit a position), `get_current_line()` reports the 1-based line for error messages, and `get_named_attribute_value_safe(name)` returns an empty string instead of erroring when the attribute is missing.

Patina current state: `gdcore/src/xml_parser.rs` implements 13 of 17 — read (:61), node_type (:81), node_name (:86), node_data (:91), is_empty (:96), attribute_count (:101), attribute_name (:106), attribute_value (:111), has_attribute (:116), named_attribute_value (:122), open_buffer (:358), seek (:367), skip_section (:385), plus `cursor` (:401). Grepping the file for `fn open`, `get_current_line`, `node_offset` and `_safe` returns nothing, so the four remaining methods are absent from both the Rust type and the script dispatch.

Implementation approach: track a per-node start offset and a running line counter inside the tokenizer in `gdcore/src/xml_parser.rs`, exposing `node_offset()` and `current_line()`; add `named_attribute_value_safe(name) -> &str` returning `""` for a missing attribute; add `pub fn open(path: &str) -> EngineResult<Self>` reading through `gdcore::FileAccess::read_file_bytes` so packs and `user://` work. Then add the four dispatch arms alongside the existing XMLParser handle methods in `gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` (the `XMLParser` handle is constructed at interpreter.rs:3055-3059).

Wiring requirement: `XMLParser.new().open("res://data.xml")` must succeed from a script running in a booted scene, including when the file lives only inside a mounted pack, and `seek(get_node_offset())` must return the parser to the same node.

GODOT: the canonical script physics query is `var q = PhysicsRayQueryParameters2D.create(from, to); var hit = get_world_2d().direct_space_state.intersect_ray(q)`, returning a Dictionary with position/normal/collider/collider_id/rid/shape. PATINA: none of it exists. `get_world_2d` has 0 hits across engine-rs; `World2D.direct_space_state` is registered as `Variant::Nil` (engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:4011); the parameter resource classes are unregistered; `intersect_ray` has 0 hits in gdscript-interop and gdscene/src/scripting.rs. (2) Add a `get_world_2d` arm plus a `direct_space_state` handle to the node method table in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs, alongside the existing `test_move`/`is_colliding` arms (scripting.rs:1367-1440), returning an object whose method calls route back into the SceneAccess bridge. (3) Add `physics2d_intersect_ray/intersect_point/intersect_shape/cast_motion/collide_shape/get_rest_info` to the SceneAccess trait in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs next to the existing `physics2d_body_test_motion` (bindings.rs:883) and implement them in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs over `PhysicsWorld2D`. (4) Add `intersect_shape`/`collide_shape`/`get_rest_info`/`cast_motion` to engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/world.rs on top of the existing `collision::test_collision` narrowphase; `cast_motion` can bisect using the swept helpers already in engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/ccd.rs. Results must be Dictionaries with Godot's exact keys.

WIRING: script `_physics_process` → MainLoop's script phase (main_loop.rs:2903, which already binds the physics server via `set_script_physics_server`) → SceneAccess → PhysicsWorld2D query → Dictionary back into the interpreter.

**Merged findings (2):** PhysicsDirectSpaceState2D script API (intersect_ray / intersect_point / intersect_shape / cast_motion / collide_shape / get_rest_info) and World2D.direct_space_state; PhysicsDirectSpaceState 2D/3D query API + query-parameter resources

title: CameraFeed: add YCbCr setters, format selection and emit frame_changed/format_changed
description:
[audit-key: xr-peripheral/camera-feed] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/servers/camera/camera_feed.cpp (set_ycbcr_image / set_ycbcr_images / set_format / get_formats / get_texture_tex_id, emit_signal("frame_changed") on each set_*_image, "format_changed" on set_format); upstream/godot/servers/camera/camera_server.cpp (camera_feeds_updated)

**Godot classes:** CameraFeed, CameraServer

**Patina today:**
- [xr-peripheral] /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:18398-18512 `call_camera_feed_instance` implements get_id/get_name/set_name/get_position/set_position/is_active/set_active/get_transform/set_transform/set_rgb_image/set_external/get_external_size/get_datatype, then hardcodes `get_formats -> Array::new()` (interpreter.rs:18506), `set_format -> Bool(false)` (:18507) and `get_texture_tex_id -> Int(0)` (:18508); `set_ycbcr_image` and `set_ycbcr_images` are absent entirely and error. The `frame_changed` and `format_changed` signals are registered at engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:9275-9276 but never emitted — `rg 'frame_changed|format_changed|camera_feeds_updated' crates/gdscript-interop/src` -> 0 hits (only camera_feed_added/removed are emitted, interpreter.rs:11654,11660). Note this is low impact: Godot's own web export has no camera driver (`ls upstream/godot/platform/web/` contains no camera_*.cpp; drivers exist only under platform/{macos,windows,linuxbsd,android,ios}), so only script-fed feeds matter.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth (upstream/godot/servers/camera/camera_feed.cpp): `set_rgb_image`, `set_ycbcr_image` and `set_ycbcr_images(y_image, cbcr_image)` each install pixels, set the matching FeedDataType (FEED_RGB=1, FEED_YCBCR=2, FEED_YCBCR_SEP=3) and emit `frame_changed`. `get_formats()` returns the device's supported format dictionaries and `set_format(index, parameters)` selects one, returning true and emitting `format_changed` on success. `CameraServer` emits `camera_feeds_updated` when the feed list is re-enumerated.\n\nPatina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:18398-18512 covers the RGB/external half well, but `set_ycbcr_image`/`set_ycbcr_images` are missing (any call errors), and `get_formats` (interpreter.rs:18506), `set_format` (:18507) and `get_texture_tex_id` (:18508) return hardcoded empty/false/0. `frame_changed` and `format_changed` are registered as signals at engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:9275-9276 but never emitted (`rg 'frame_changed|format_changed|camera_feeds_updated' crates/gdscript-interop/src` -> 0 hits), so a script that connects to `frame_changed` to react to new pixels never wakes up. Scope note: Godot's own web export has no camera device driver, so this bead is about the script-fed path only — a game feeding frames from an Image (e.g. decoded video or a canvas capture) into a CameraFeed for a CameraTexture.\n\nImplementation: add `set_ycbcr_image` and `set_ycbcr_images` arms mirroring the existing `set_rgb_image` handle plumbing (interpreter.rs:18450-18470), setting datatype 2 and 3 respectively; store per-feed a format list that `set_format` selects from, returning true and recording the selection. Emit `frame_changed` from every set_*_image and `format_changed` from a successful set_format through a per-feed signal registry modelled on CAMERA_SERVER_CONNECTIONS (interpreter.rs:19148-19176) — the emission needs the interpreter to invoke the Callable, so it belongs on `Interpreter` beside `emit_camera_server_signal` (interpreter.rs:11676). Emit `camera_feeds_updated` from CameraServer whenever the feed list changes.\n\nWiring requirement: a script connecting `feed.frame_changed` must receive the callback when another script pushes an Image into the feed.

**Prove it:** A GDScript script creates a CameraFeed, connects a Callable to `frame_changed`, then calls `set_rgb_image(img)` and `set_ycbcr_images(y, cbcr)`: the callback fires twice and `get_datatype()` reads FEED_RGB then FEED_YCBCR_SEP. `set_format(0, {})` returns true, emits `format_changed` once, and a second call with an out-of-range index returns false and emits nothing. `CameraServer.add_feed(feed)` emits both `camera_feed_added` and `camera_feeds_updated`. (test: `camera_feed_ycbcr_and_signals`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscript-interop --test camera_feed_ycbcr_and_signals`.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript script creates a CameraFeed, connects a Callable to `frame_changed`, then calls `set_rgb_image(img)` and `set_ycbcr_images(y, cbcr)`: the callback fires twice and `get_datatype()` reads FEED_RGB then FEED_YCBCR_SEP. `set_format(0, {})` returns true, emits `format_changed` once, and a second call with an out-of-range index returns false and emits nothing. `CameraServer.add_feed(feed)` emits both `camera_feed_added` and `camera_feeds_updated`. (test: `camera_feed_ycbcr_and_signals`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscript-interop --test camera_feed_ycbcr_and_signals`.

title: MovieWriter: bind add_writer to GDScript and drive _write_begin/_write_frame/_write_end from the frame loop
description:
[audit-key: xr-peripheral/movie-writer] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json .classes[MovieWriter] (_get_audio_mix_rate, _get_audio_speaker_mode, _handles_file, _write_begin, _write_frame, _write_end, add_writer); upstream/godot/servers/movie_writer/movie_writer.cpp

**Godot classes:** MovieWriter

**Patina today:**
- [xr-peripheral] /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/movie_writer.rs:27-53 implements add_writer/registered_writers/writer_count/clear_writers over a OnceLock<Mutex<Vec<_>>>. Non-test callers: none. `rg --glob '!**/tests/**' 'movie_writer|add_writer|write_frame|write_begin|write_end' crates/` returns only crates/gdobject/src/lib.rs:22 (`pub mod movie_writer;`), the MethodInfo declarations at crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:12800-12803, a doc comment at crates/gdobject/src/weak_ref.rs:32, and unrelated TCP framing in crates/gdplatform/src/tcp_multiplayer.rs. The string "add_writer" never appears as a dispatch arm in the interpreter (`rg '\"add_writer\"' crates/` -> class_db.rs:12803 only), so `MovieWriter.add_writer(w)` from GDScript raises. No frame-capture path calls _write_begin/_write_frame/_write_end. The module's own test (movie_writer.rs:60-89) calls the Rust functions directly, so it is green while the feature is script-unreachable.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/movie_writer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `MovieWriter` (upstream/godot/servers/movie_writer/movie_writer.cpp) is an abstract Object whose static `add_writer(writer)` registers a candidate encoder. When movie-write mode is on, Godot picks the first registered writer whose `_handles_file(path)` returns true, calls `_write_begin(movie_size, fps, base_path)`, then `_write_frame(frame_image, audio_frame_block)` once per rendered frame, then `_write_end()`.\n\nPatina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/movie_writer.rs holds a process-global registry (add_writer at :33, registered_writers at :42, writer_count at :47) with zero non-test callers — `rg --glob '!**/tests/**' 'movie_writer|add_writer'` finds only the module declaration at crates/gdobject/src/lib.rs:22 and the MethodInfo entries at crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:12800-12803. `"add_writer"` is never a dispatch arm in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, so a script calling `MovieWriter.add_writer(self)` errors. Nothing calls _write_begin/_write_frame/_write_end.\n\nImplementation: add a `MovieWriter` static-singleton arm in the interpreter's `Expr::Ident` dispatch chain (beside the CameraServer arm at interpreter.rs:2992) handling `add_writer(writer)` — record the writer's script class name plus its ObjectId so its virtuals can be invoked. Add a movie-capture step to the frame tick in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs: when capture is enabled (an Engine/ProjectSettings flag, since the web target has no `--write-movie` CLI), select the first registered writer whose `_handles_file` accepts the output path, call `_write_begin` once, `_write_frame` with the published frame image each tick, and `_write_end` on shutdown. Frame pixels come from the same publish the renderer already produces.\n\nWiring requirement: a GDScript class `extends MovieWriter` that registers itself must have its `_write_frame` virtual invoked once per MainLoop frame while capture is on.

**Prove it:** A GDScript class extending MovieWriter registers itself via `MovieWriter.add_writer(self)` in `_ready`, `_handles_file` returns true for the configured output path, and after enabling capture and stepping the MainLoop 3 frames the script observes `_write_begin` once, `_write_frame` exactly 3 times with a non-empty image, and `_write_end` once on shutdown. With capture off, none of the three virtuals is called. (test: `movie_writer_script_registry`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test movie_writer_script_registry`.
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript class extending MovieWriter registers itself via `MovieWriter.add_writer(self)` in `_ready`, `_handles_file` returns true for the configured output path, and after enabling capture and stepping the MainLoop 3 frames the script observes `_write_begin` once, `_write_frame` exactly 3 times with a non-empty image, and `_write_end` once on shutdown. With capture off, none of the three virtuals is called. (test: `movie_writer_script_registry`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test movie_writer_script_registry`.

title: XR: implement XRHandModifier3D/XRBodyModifier3D/XRFaceModifier3D on the SkeletonModifier3D phase
description:
[audit-key: xr-peripheral/xr-modifiers] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/xr/xr_hand_modifier_3d.cpp (drives a Skeleton3D's bones from an XRHandTracker's 26 joints each frame), xr_body_modifier_3d.cpp, xr_face_modifier_3d.cpp (drives blend shapes on a MeshInstance3D target); upstream/godot/servers/xr/xr_vrs.cpp (make_vrs_texture)

**Godot classes:** XRHandModifier3D, XRBodyModifier3D, XRFaceModifier3D, XRVRS

**Patina today:**
- [xr-peripheral] Registered with properties and enums at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:5560 (XRHandModifier3D), :5572 (XRBodyModifier3D), :5588 (XRFaceModifier3D), :5596 (XRVRS). Zero implementation anywhere: `rg -n 'hand_tracker|body_tracker|face_tracker|vrs_min_radius|vrs_strength|make_vrs_texture' crates/ --glob '!**/class_db.rs' --glob '!inspector_schema_generated.rs'` returns 0 hits. Patina does have a SkeletonModifier3D phase to hang these off (crates/gdscene/src/skeleton3d.rs:559-640, run from crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2982), so the hook exists and is unused.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/skeleton3d.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `XRHandModifier3D` (upstream/godot/scene/3d/xr/xr_hand_modifier_3d.cpp) is a SkeletonModifier3D that, each frame, reads the named XRHandTracker from XRServer and writes its 26 HandJoint transforms into the parent Skeleton3D's matching bones, honouring `bone_update` (FULL vs ROTATION_ONLY) and skipping joints whose HAND_JOINT_FLAG_*_VALID bits are clear. `XRBodyModifier3D` does the same for XRBodyTracker joints with `body_update` (UPPER_BODY/LOWER_BODY/HANDS flags) and `bone_update`. `XRFaceModifier3D` (a Node3D, not a modifier) copies an XRFaceTracker's blend-shape weights onto the `target` MeshInstance3D's blend shapes by name. `XRVRS` produces the variable-rate-shading density texture from vrs_min_radius/vrs_strength/vrs_render_region.\n\nPatina current state: all four are ClassDB entries only — engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:5560, :5572, :5588, :5596 — with correct parents, properties and enum constants and zero behaviour. `rg 'hand_tracker|body_tracker|face_tracker|vrs_min_radius|make_vrs_texture' crates/` outside class_db.rs and the generated inspector schema returns nothing. The SkeletonModifier3D process phase that these belong in already exists and runs each frame: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/skeleton3d.rs:559-640, invoked from engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2982.\n\nImplementation: add engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/xr_modifiers.rs registering hand/body modifier handlers into the existing SkeletonModifier3D stack in skeleton3d.rs (same `active`/`influence` contract as the IK modifiers), resolving the tracker name through the XRServer tracker registry and mapping HandJoint/Joint indices to Skeleton3D bone names using Godot's canonical joint-to-bone name table. Handle XRFaceModifier3D as a plain per-frame Node3D update writing blend shapes onto the `target` NodePath's MeshInstance3D. XRVRS can stay registration-only for now (VRS has no render-pipeline consumer) — scope this bead to the three modifiers.\n\nWiring requirement: loading a .tscn with Skeleton3D > XRHandModifier3D(hand_tracker="left_hand") and stepping the MainLoop must move the skeleton's bones from the tracker's joint data.

**Prove it:** A .tscn with Skeleton3D (hand bone chain) > XRHandModifier3D(hand_tracker="left_hand", bone_update=BONE_UPDATE_FULL) is loaded; a script registers an XRHandTracker named "left_hand" with HAND_JOINT_WRIST and HAND_JOINT_INDEX_FINGER_TIP transforms and the POSITION_VALID|ORIENTATION_VALID flags set; after one MainLoop frame the corresponding Skeleton3D bone poses equal those transforms, and a joint whose valid flags are clear is left at its rest pose. Setting `active = false` on the modifier leaves the skeleton untouched. (test: `xr_modifiers_drive_skeleton`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test xr_modifiers_drive_skeleton`.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with Skeleton3D (hand bone chain) > XRHandModifier3D(hand_tracker="left_hand", bone_update=BONE_UPDATE_FULL) is loaded; a script registers an XRHandTracker named "left_hand" with HAND_JOINT_WRIST and HAND_JOINT_INDEX_FINGER_TIP transforms and the POSITION_VALID|ORIENTATION_VALID flags set; after one MainLoop frame the corresponding Skeleton3D bone poses equal those transforms, and a joint whose valid flags are clear is left at its rest pose. Setting `active = false` on the modifier leaves the skeleton untouched. (test: `xr_modifiers_drive_skeleton`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test xr_modifiers_drive_skeleton`.

title: Multiplayer: wasm32 browser-WebSocket backend for WebSocketPeer + WebSocketMultiplayerPeer client role
description:
Split from pat-s3rrv.79 (operator triage 2026-10-30). Covers that bead's parts (a) and (c) only; the native wss:// part (b) stays on .79, blocked on a rustls dependency decision.

Godot ground truth: upstream/godot/modules/websocket/emws_peer.cpp + library_godot_websocket.js. Godot's web build binds the browser WebSocket API, so ws:// and wss:// both work in the browser, since the browser does TLS. websocket_multiplayer_peer.cpp: on web only the client role works, and create_server returns ERR_UNAVAILABLE (platform/web/net_socket_web.h:51-60).

Patina today: crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_peer.rs:510 connect_to_url is native TCP only (to_socket_addrs + TcpStream). There is no cfg(target_arch = "wasm32") backend.

Implement, under #[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")] in gdplatform:
1. A browser WebSocket transport behind WebSocketPeer. Construct the browser WebSocket through js_sys::Reflect (get the global WebSocket constructor, then Reflect::construct), following the pattern in crates/gdplatform/src/js_bridge.rs:497-525 and :630. Set binaryType to arraybuffer, queue onmessage packets (text and binary), map readyState to READY_STATE_*, and support close(code, reason). Both ws:// and wss:// go through the browser.
2. WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.create_client uses that transport on wasm32. create_server returns ERR_UNAVAILABLE on wasm32, matching Godot.

Dependencies: none new. wasm-bindgen and js-sys are already in gdplatform/Cargo.toml:28-30 under the cfg(target_arch = "wasm32") target table. Do NOT add web-sys (the manifest comment at :23-27 deliberately keeps this to js-sys only).

Native behaviour must not change.
acceptance_criteria: (1) `cargo check -p gdplatform --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds with the browser backend compiled in. The verifier replays this command; it passed for pat-u3l8c.115 and genuinely fails on compile errors. (2) A native test covers the portable logic, factored out so it runs without a browser: readyState mapping, text/binary packet framing in the receive queue, and create_server returning ERR_UNAVAILABLE on the wasm path (test: websocket_wasm_backend_contract). (3) The existing native suite still passes: `cargo nextest run -p gdplatform --test websocket_multiplayer_e2e_test`.

title: Typed containers from declarations: var a: Array[int] = [] creates a typed SharedArray and enforces element type; const arrays are read-only
description: Follow-up to pat-s3rrv.8 (Array/Dictionary are now shared handles carrying typed and read-only state). What is still missing is CREATING typed containers. The parser keeps `Array[int]` / `Dictionary[String, int]` hints as strings only (parser.rs parse_type_hint), so every container is untyped and is_typed() is always false. Godot: assigning to a typed variable or member converts the value to a typed array (gdscript_vm.cpp OPCODE_ASSIGN_TYPED_ARRAY) and every later write is type-checked; a mismatch is a runtime error. Also Godot makes `const` arrays and dictionaries read-only (make_read_only), so `DIRS.append(x)` errors. SharedArray::typed / set_typed / make_read_only already exist and are tested, and the interpreter's container_error path already surfaces refused writes. Wire: (1) typed hints on var/member/param declarations set the type on assignment; (2) const container values are made read-only; (3) the .tscn loader's typed Array[T](...) literals (loader.rs parse_variant_value_typed) produce typed arrays.
acceptance_criteria: GDScript: 'var a: Array[int] = []; a.append("x")' raises a runtime error; 'a.is_typed()' is true and 'a.get_typed_builtin() == TYPE_INT'; 'const C = [1]; C.append(2)' raises; a .tscn 'Array[int]([1, 2])' property loads typed. (test: typed_containers_from_declarations)

comments.author: BlueHill
comments.text:
BlueHill 2026-10-30: implemented. Two notes for whoever reads this next.

== CORRECTION to this bead's own premise ==

"SharedArray::typed / set_typed / make_read_only already exist and are tested, and the interpreter's container_error path already surfaces refused writes."

The first half is true. The second half is true for ReadOnly and FALSE for TypeMismatch, so clause 1 of the acceptance would have failed even with the array correctly typed.

Mechanism: `Interpreter::array_mutate` does not call `SharedArray::push`. It snapshots with `to_vec()`, mutates a plain `Vec`, and stores back through `SharedArray::with_mut`, which checks ONLY `body.read_only` -- it never consults `body.typed`. So every array mutation reachable from GDScript (append, push_front, insert, sort, reverse, ...) bypassed the element check. `a.append("x")` on an `Array[int]` would have succeeded silently.

Fixed by storing through `assign` instead, which performs the same write plus the per-element validation, and which is a no-op for untyped arrays (`ContainerType::accepts` returns true when `builtin` is None). This is the widest-blast-radius part of the change -- it is on the write path of every array mutation in the interpreter -- so the reported gates include a package-wide `-p gdscript-interop` run, not only the named acceptance test.

Also worth recording: NO parser change was needed. This bead says the parser "keeps hints as strings only", which is accurate but reads as though the parser must be taught to keep the type. It already does: `parse_type_hint` returns `format!("{name}[{params}]")`, so `"Array[int]"` carries the element type and recovering it from the string is sufficient. parser.rs is untouched.

== RESIDUAL, deliberately not fixed here ==

`SharedDictionary::merge` (interpreter.rs, the `merge` arm) and `get_or_add` reach the map through `with_mut`, so they bypass the key/value type check in exactly the way `array_mutate` did. They INTRODUCE entries, so on a typed dictionary they can seat a value the type forbids.

Not fixed because: (a) it is outside this bead's acceptance, which names only arrays and const; (b) the ordinary `d[k] = v` path goes through `set_index` -> `SharedDictionary::insert`, which DOES validate both key and value, so typed dictionaries are enforced where scripts actually write them; (c) interpreter.rs is being live-edited by a peer for pat-fk17e.1 and widening the diff there has a real conflict cost.

The two other `with_mut` sites in the dictionary arm (`sort`) and the array arm (`sort_custom`) only REORDER existing elements, so they need no validation and were left alone.

Suggested follow-up bead: "typed Dictionary: merge and get_or_add bypass the element check" -- a two-line change of the same shape as the array_mutate fix (compute the new map, then store through `assign`).

comments.text:
BlueHill 2026-10-30 ~17:05Z: the verify FAILED but NOT on this bead's work, and the blocker is now fixed. Reassigned to BoldAnchor after the fail; full handoff sent as mail 88555. Recording here because mail is not durable and the next holder reads this.

== COMMANDS 1-4 PASSED, INCLUDING THE ACCEPTANCE ==

verifier.log:11829-11830. Seven commands joined by && run in order and stop at the first failure. It stopped at command 5, so:

  1. nextest -p gdscript-interop --test typed_containers_from_declarations  PASS  <- THE ACCEPTANCE
  2. nextest -p gdscript-interop --test container_typed_and_read_only       PASS  <- pat-s3rrv.8 regression gate
  3. nextest -p gdscript-interop --lib container_typing                     PASS
  4. nextest -p gdvariant --lib                                            PASS
  5. nextest -p gdresource --lib loader                                     FAIL (100, panic)

The feature compiles and the bead's own acceptance is green. Do NOT re-implement.

== WHAT COMMAND 5 FAILED ON ==

Ran the verifier's own fresh binary (target-verifier/debug/deps/gdresource-81efc09a7510b797, mtime 09:57):

  test importers::tests::format_loader_with_defaults ... FAILED
  panicked at crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs:2528: assertion `left == right` failed
    left: 25, right: 19
  test result: FAILED. 108 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 384 filtered out

That is `assert_eq!(rfl.extension_count(), 19)` -- a hardcoded count of extensions registered by ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults(). Proof it is foreign to this bead:

- extension_count() is `self.loaders.len()`, and with_defaults' body contains ZERO references to parse_variant_value or loader:: -- the function this bead changed is unreachable from it.
- importers.rs was UNMODIFIED in the working tree; the last commit touching it (2fdb6ef, pat-s3rrv.8) made only mechanical .into()/.to_vec() SharedArray edits there, not list or count changes.
- loader.rs's own unit tests, including parse_typed_array_value, are among the 108 that PASSED.

== THE TRAP, WHICH WILL RECUR ==

`--lib loader` is a SUBSTRING FILTER ON THE TEST NAME, and `importers::tests::format_loader_with_defaults` contains "loader". So anyone who reports a `--lib loader` gate inherits a red test from a different module. The test's own comment records it going stale twice before ("it read 12 while with_defaults registered 14 -- so it was red at HEAD").

Narrower gate that gates only the changed module: `nextest run -p gdresource --lib 'loader::tests::'`.

== FIX APPLIED (foreign to this bead; add importers.rs to files-changed if kept) ==

with_defaults registers 25 extensions (counted from source; runtime agrees -- `left: 25`), so 19 was simply stale. Rather than bump the integer and leave the trap armed a fourth time, the bare count is replaced with an explicit list: a new `EXPECTED_DEFAULT_EXTENSIONS` const (the 25 actual extensions) plus a `can_load` assert per entry and a count assert against the list length. A registration added or dropped now names itself in the diff instead of printing two integers.

The test is self-validating: a wrong entry in the list fails naming that extension, and a 26th registration trips the count. importers.rs parses; the edited region is formatter-clean (its 3 formatting diffs at lines 425/740/1583 are pre-existing).

!! The old comment pointed at `format_loader_covers_source_asset_extensions` as "pinning the full list". THAT TEST DOES NOT EXIST -- only six format_loader* tests are in the file. Nothing was pinning the list, which is how it drifted. The dangling reference is removed.

== STILL UNPROVEN ==

Commands 6 and 7 never ran, so neither is verified yet: `-p gdresource --test tscn_value_parser_fidelity` and the package-wide `-p gdscript-interop`. The package-wide run is the one that matters -- this change routes every interpreter array mutation through the element check.

comments.author: BlueHill
comments.text:
BlueHill 2026-10-30 ~17:2xZ — MEASURED EVIDENCE for BoldAnchor, plus a corrected gate list. Read-only; no code changes in this pass, no claim, no status change. The bead is BoldAnchor's.

The reopen (msg 88531) fired on a foreign failure and fail-fast cancelled 97 of 109 tests, so most of what my report claimed went UNVERIFIED rather than failing. I have now measured it by running the verifier's own binaries directly, which needs no build. Numbers below are observed, not inferred.

== MEASURED: all green ==

Binaries from target-verifier/debug/deps, each checked for staleness with `find <srcdir> -name '*.rs' -newer <binary>` before trusting it:

  typed_containers_from_declarations-777790ca30af7988   17 passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored   <- THE ACCEPTANCE
  container_typed_and_read_only-<...>                    9 passed / 0 failed               <- pat-s3rrv.8 regression gate
  backtrace-<...>                                        6 passed / 0 failed
  midi_ports-<...>                                       6 passed / 0 failed
  gdresource-81efc09a7510b797  filter 'loader::tests'    57 passed / 0 failed               <- was in the cancelled 97
  tscn_value_parser_fidelity-78b1f0943d542dd4             2 passed / 0 failed               <- command 6, never ran

The 57 include `loader::tests::parse_typed_array_value`, which is the one I was most worried about: it compares a typed `Array[int]([1,2,3])` against the plain `[1,2,3]`, and it stays green because SharedArray's PartialEq is Godot's structural `recursive_equal` and does not consider the element type.

Staleness caveat, stated rather than hidden: the only source file newer than those binaries is `crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs`, my later fix. It lives in a `#[cfg(test)]` module, which is not compiled into the rlib dependents link, so it cannot affect the gdscript-interop results above.

== CORRECTED GATE LIST ==

Two of my seven commands were wrong. Replacements, with every target cross-checked against docs/test-debt/2026-10-30-failing-tests-at-HEAD.txt (0 known-red rows each):

  1  nextest -p gdscript-interop --test typed_containers_from_declarations     [measured 17/0]
  2  nextest -p gdscript-interop --test container_typed_and_read_only          [measured  9/0]
  3  nextest -p gdscript-interop --lib container_typing                        [verifier PASS 17:0x]
  4  nextest -p gdvariant --lib                                               [verifier PASS 17:0x]
  5  nextest -p gdresource --lib 'loader::tests'          <- NARROWED          [measured 57/0]
  6  nextest -p gdresource --test tscn_value_parser_fidelity                   [measured  2/0]
  7  nextest -p gdscript-interop --test container_custom                      <- replaces the package-wide run
  8  nextest -p gdscript-interop --test packed_array_methods_parity            <-  "
  9  nextest -p gdscript-interop --test lambda_captures_enclosing_locals       <-  "
 10  nextest -p gdresource --lib 'importers::tests::format_loader'             <- gates MY importers fix; UNVERIFIED, see below

WHY 5 CHANGED: nextest's bare positional is a SUBSTRING FILTER ON THE FULL TEST NAME, not a module selector. `--lib loader` also selected `importers::tests::format_loader_with_defaults`, which contains "loader" and is one of three gdresource tests already red at HEAD. Anchoring on `loader::tests` selects 0 importers tests — I verified that with `--list`, not by assuming.

WHY 7 CHANGED, and this is the one that would have failed the re-report again: a package-wide `-p gdscript-interop` CANNOT PASS at HEAD. The debt file lists three red tests in that package's LIB target:

    gdscript_interop::canvas_server::tests::create_parent_add_and_clear
    gdscript_interop::editor_commands::tests::registration_order_is_preserved
    gdscript_interop::editor_commands::tests::remove_reports_whether_it_removed_anything

⚠️ I nearly missed these and told you the package was debt-free: I had grepped `^gdscript-interop::` with a HYPHEN, and the file uses the Rust crate path with an UNDERSCORE (`gdscript_interop::`). The hyphen grep returns 0, the underscore grep returns 3. Check both spellings for any package whose name has a dash.

Commands 7-9 are the replacement blast-radius gate. They matter because the change routes EVERY interpreter array mutation through the element check (see the correction note above): `array_mutate` previously stored via `with_mut`, which checks only `read_only` and never `typed`. I picked those three by counting array-mutation calls across all 93 gdscript-interop test targets; they are the highest-scoring ones with no debt rows. This is narrower than a package-wide run and I would rather say so than imply equivalence — a package-wide run would be better coverage if the three red lib tests were fixed first.

== STILL UNVERIFIED, HONESTLY ==

1. My `importers.rs` fix (the stale extension count, 19 -> 25 replaced by an explicit list). NO binary includes it — every gdresource binary predates it — so it has never been executed. Command 10 gates it. If you would rather not carry a foreign fix, drop importers.rs from the files list and command 10 with it; the bead's own acceptance does not need it, but then command 5 must stay narrowed or the red test returns.

2. The package-wide run. 90 of 93 gdscript-interop test binaries exist locally but 86 are OLDER than my interpreter.rs edit, so running them would be a FALSE GREEN rather than evidence. I did run the 4 that are current — backtrace, container_typed_and_read_only, midi_ports, typed_containers_from_declarations: 38 passed, 0 failed between them.

== ONE DRIFT IN THE DEBT FILE WORTH KNOWING ==

docs/test-debt/2026-10-30-failing-tests-at-HEAD.txt (generated 08:11 today) lists three `backtrace::*` rows as red. I ran that target's current binary: 6 passed, 0 failed. So the file is already partly stale — treat a row in it as "check this" rather than "this is red", and re-measure before quoting it as a reason.

title: Debugger: attach EngineDebugger to the editor Play session and drain its messages/breaks over a WebSocket transport

**Patina today:**

Consequence: `EngineDebugger.is_active()` is permanently false in the runner and during editor Play, `EngineDebugger.debug()` is inert (interpreter.rs:16166-16171 only fires when a session is attached, and none ever is), and `EngineDebugger.send_message()` pushes onto a thread-local `DEBUG_MESSAGES` (interpreter.rs:16152) that nothing reads. Separately `engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/debug_protocol.rs` (869 lines: DebugCommand/DebugEvent/DebugServer/DebugClient) has zero call sites — `grep -rn 'debug_protocol' crates/ apps/` returns only `gdcore/src/lib.rs:16 pub mod debug_protocol;` and two doc-comments — and it is built on `std::net::TcpListener/TcpStream` (debug_protocol.rs:34), which cannot run in a browser at all; Godot's web export uses the WebSocket remote-debugger peer.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/debug_protocol.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/debugger.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: when a game runs from the editor, `EngineDebugger::initialize()` installs a RemoteDebugger and `EngineDebugger.is_active()` returns true for the whole session (core/debugger/engine_debugger.cpp). `EngineDebugger.send_message(name, data)` is delivered to the editor's registered capture; `EngineDebugger.debug(can_continue, is_error_breakpoint)` actually suspends script execution and hands the editor a stack; profiler frame data queued with `profiler_add_frame_data` reaches the editor's profiler panel. On the web export the transport is the WebSocket peer (core/debugger/remote_debugger_peer_websocket.cpp), not TCP.\n\nPATINA CURRENT STATE: the script surface is complete (23/23 methods dispatched, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:15817-16258) and there is a real breakpoint/stack model in engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/debugger.rs — but nothing connects them to the product. `engine_debugger_attach()` (interpreter.rs:15879), `drain_engine_debugger_messages()` (interpreter.rs:15918) and `take_engine_debugger_break()` (interpreter.rs:16258) are called only from engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/tests/engine_debugger_singleton_script_reachable.rs; `grep -rn 'engine_debugger' engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src` returns nothing. So `EngineDebugger.is_active()` is false even while the editor is running the scene with its own breakpoints set, `debug()` never pauses, and `send_message()` fills a thread-local Vec nobody drains. engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/debug_protocol.rs (869 lines) is dead code and is TCP-only (debug_protocol.rs:34 `use std::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream}`), unusable from a browser.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION APPROACH: (1) In engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, call `gdscript_interop::interpreter::engine_debugger_attach()` when `POST /api/runtime/play` starts a session and `engine_debugger_detach()` on `/api/runtime/stop`, and mirror the panel's skip-breakpoints toggle through `engine_debugger_set_skipping_breakpoints`. title: Rendering2D: carry material, blend mode and texture filter/repeat into the Play rasterizer
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/play-raster-material-state] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json CanvasItemMaterial (blend_mode, light_mode, particles_animation, particles_anim_h_frames/v_frames/loop) + CanvasItem.material/use_parent_material/texture_filter/texture_repeat; upstream/godot/servers/rendering/renderer_canvas_render.cpp | extension_api.json CanvasItemMaterial: particles_animation, particles_anim_h_frames, particles_anim_v_frames, particles_anim_loop; LightMode NORMAL/UNSHADED/LIGHT_ONLY

**Godot classes:** CanvasItemMaterial, ShaderMaterial, CanvasItem

**Patina today:**
- [rendering-2d] The feature-complete rasterizer `gdrender2d::SoftwareRenderer::rasterize_item` honours per-item blend mode, texture filter, clip scissor and shader material (crates/gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs:388-436, and `CanvasItem` carries material/canvas_material/texture_filter/texture_repeat/clip_rect at crates/gdserver2d/src/canvas.rs:207-237). Its only feeder is `gdscene::scene_bridge` (crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs:126-135, 163-236), which has no production caller. The served Play path instead uses `gdeditor::viewport_2d_render::Render2DItem` (crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:246-289) — that struct has NO material, filter or repeat field at all — and `rasterize_render_list_with_quality` (viewport_2d_render.rs:1591-1704) does plain source-over blending. Its texture blit `draw::draw_texture_rect_transformed` (crates/gdrender2d/src/draw.rs:77-127) hardcodes nearest sampling and clamps UVs to 0..1 (no repeat/mirror). `grep -n 'material\|shader\|texture_filter\|CanvasQuality' engine-rs/examples/editor.rs` returns nothing. Green tests crates/gdscene/tests/canvas_item_material_blend_in_play.rs and canvas_item_shader_scene_pixels.rs assert on the dead `scene_bridge` path.
- [rendering-2d] `gdserver2d::material::CanvasItemMaterial` has exactly two fields — `blend_mode` and `light_mode` (crates/gdserver2d/src/material.rs:172-177) — so the four particles-animation properties cannot be represented at all; `grep -rn 'particles_anim' crates/ --include='*.rs'` returns nothing. `light_mode` is parsed but explicitly unused: crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs:182-183 says "Carried through so the lighting pass can gate on it; nothing here consumes it yet", and the live Play shading pass `shade_runtime_canvas` (crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:1904-1926) has no material input at all, so UNSHADED and LIGHT_ONLY items are shaded like NORMAL ones.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/draw.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver2d/src/material.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: every canvas item carries a material (CanvasItemMaterial → blend_mode MIX/ADD/SUB/MUL/PREMULT_ALPHA + light_mode NORMAL/UNSHADED/LIGHT_ONLY, or a ShaderMaterial whose canvas_item `fragment()` rewrites COLOR) and a resolved texture_filter/texture_repeat inherited from the parent chain (extension_api.json CanvasItem/CanvasItemMaterial; upstream/godot/servers/rendering/renderer_canvas_render.cpp).

PATINA NOW: two 2D pipelines exist and the wrong one is live. `gdrender2d::SoftwareRenderer::rasterize_item` (crates/gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs:388-436) already implements blend mode, filter, clip scissor and shader evaluation, fed by `gdscene::scene_bridge` (crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs:126-135, 163-282) — but `scene_bridge` has zero production callers. The served editor Play loop (engine-rs/examples/editor.rs:290-345) uses `gdeditor::viewport_2d_render`, whose `Render2DItem` (crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:246-289) has no material/filter/repeat fields, and whose blit `gdrender2d::draw::draw_texture_rect_transformed` (crates/gdrender2d/src/draw.rs:77-127) is nearest-only with clamped UVs. So an authored CanvasItemMaterial composites as plain Mix, a `.gdshader` on a Sprite2D does nothing, and `texture_filter = LINEAR` / `texture_repeat = ENABLED` are inert in the running game.

APPROACH: add `canvas_material: Option<gdserver2d::material::CanvasItemMaterial>`, `shader_material: Option<gdserver2d::shader::ShaderMaterial>`, `texture_filter` and `texture_repeat` to `Render2DItem`; populate them in `collect_canvas_items` by reusing the already-written resolvers `scene_bridge::resolve_canvas_item_material`, `resolve_canvas_shader_material`, `resolve_texture_filter`, `resolve_texture_repeat` (move them into a shared module, e.g. `gdscene::canvas_order`, so both feeders share one implementation). In `rasterize_render_list_with_quality`, set `fb.blend_mode`/`fb.texture_filter` around each item exactly as `SoftwareRenderer::rasterize_item` does, restore them afterwards, and route textured draws through a shaded blit when a ShaderMaterial is present (`draw::draw_texture_rect_shaded` already exists at crates/gdrender2d/src/draw.rs:820). Teach `draw_texture_rect_transformed` to take filter + repeat (bilinear sample; wrap/mirror UVs instead of `continue`ing outside 0..1).

WIRING: no change needed in examples/editor.rs — the Play loop already calls `build_runtime_render_list` + `rasterize_render_list`; after this bead an authored material must change the pixels it produces.

**Merged findings (2):** CanvasItemMaterial blend/light modes, canvas_item ShaderMaterial, and texture_filter/texture_repeat in the running frame; CanvasItemMaterial particles animation + light_mode consumption

**Prove it:** A .tscn with two overlapping ColorRects where the top one has `material = SubResource(CanvasItemMaterial)` with `blend_mode = 1` (ADD) renders a brighter sum in the Play frame than with MIX; a Sprite2D with a `.gdshader` setting `COLOR.rgb = vec3(0,1,0)` renders green in the Play frame; a Sprite2D with `texture_filter = 2` (LINEAR) produces intermediate-value pixels along a scaled-up texture edge where NEAREST produces only source values. (test: `canvas_item_material_and_sampling_in_play_frame`) — drives `.tscn` → `PackedScene::from_tscn` → `add_packed_scene_to_tree` → `gdeditor::viewport_2d_render::build_runtime_render_list` → `rasterize_render_list` and asserts pixels.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with two overlapping ColorRects where the top one has `material = SubResource(CanvasItemMaterial)` with `blend_mode = 1` (ADD) renders a brighter sum in the Play frame than with MIX; a Sprite2D with a `.gdshader` setting `COLOR.rgb = vec3(0,1,0)` renders green in the Play frame; a Sprite2D with `texture_filter = 2` (LINEAR) produces intermediate-value pixels along a scaled-up texture edge where NEAREST produces only source values. (test: `canvas_item_material_and_sampling_in_play_frame`) — drives `.tscn` → `PackedScene::from_tscn` → `add_packed_scene_to_tree` → `gdeditor::viewport_2d_render::build_runtime_render_list` → `rasterize_render_list` and asserts pixels.
