comments.author: bone
comments.text:
## ⚠️ CORRECTION to my own previous comment — do NOT `#[derive(Default)]` here (AmberForge)

In my last comment I suggested, as a risk reduction before adding fields:

  'Add `#[derive(Default)]` to `Render2DItem` FIRST (check `Transform2D`/`Color`/`Rect2`/`Option<Rect2>` all impl Default — they should)'

**They do not, and the obvious way to make them would introduce a severe silent bug. Ignore that advice.**

Verified just now:
- `gdcore::math::Transform2D` derives only `(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)` — **no `Default`**.
- No manual `impl Default` for `Transform2D`, `Rect2` or `Color` either.

So `#[derive(Default)]` on `Render2DItem` simply will not compile. **The trap is the fix someone would reach for next:** adding `#[derive(Default)]` to `Transform2D` in gdcore. A derived Default is all-ZEROS — `x = (0,0)`, `y = (0,0)`, `origin = (0,0)` — which is a DEGENERATE transform that collapses every point to the origin, NOT `Transform2D::IDENTITY`. Nothing would fail to compile; 2D rendering would just silently collapse, and the cause would be nowhere near the symptom. Do not do that to gdcore.

### The safe version of the same idea
Write a MANUAL impl on `Render2DItem` with semantically correct defaults, in its own behaviour-preserving commit:

    impl Default for Render2DItem {
        fn default() -> Self {
            Self {
                node_id: 0,
                global_transform: Transform2D::IDENTITY,   // NOT derived
                modulate: Color::WHITE,                    // NOT Color::default()
                z_index: 0,
                canvas_layer: 0,
                clip_rect: None,
                ..                                          // remaining fields explicit
            }
        }
    }

Then convert the 9 literals to `..Default::default()`, then add the new fields. Each step is separately verifiable and none of them can silently change a pixel.

The 9 construction sites and the rest of the plan are in my previous comment and still stand — only the derive advice was wrong.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
## Note on step 1 of my proposed sequence — `Render2DItem` is not Default-shaped (AmberForge)

I re-examined whether step 1 (a manual `impl Default for Render2DItem`) could be landed NOW as a provable no-op, independently of .22. It CAN — a new trait impl touches no construction site and cannot conflict. But two things are worth knowing before anyone does it:

**1. Nine of the ten fields have obvious defaults; `kind` does not.**

    node_id: 0 | global_transform: Transform2D::IDENTITY | modulate: Color::WHITE
    z_index: 0 | canvas_layer: 0 | clip_rect: None
    light_mask: 1 | visibility_layer: 1        (Godot's default layer, NOT 0)
    canvas_follow: CanvasFollow::DefaultCanvas
    kind: ???

`Render2DKind` has **no `#[default]` variant** and no meaningful 'empty' one. Any Default must INVENT a kind (e.g. `Marker { class: String::new() }`). That is fine in the `..Default::default()` idiom because all 9 construction sites set `kind` explicitly — but it means Default is a construction convenience, not a semantic default, and `Render2DItem::default()` on its own yields a meaningless item. Document it as such if you add it.

⚠️ Note `light_mask`/`visibility_layer` default to **1**, not 0. A derived Default would give 0 = 'on no layer', which silently means the item is culled and never lit. That is the same class of trap as the zero-`Transform2D` one I flagged above.

**2. I did NOT land it, deliberately.** It delivers nothing on its own: the step it enables (converting the 9 literals to `..Default::default()`) is the one that touches .22's uncommitted construction sites, so it stays blocked either way. Adding public API to a struct that .22's collapse may restructure would be churn with no consumer. If .22 lands and `Render2DItem` survives in this shape, do step 1 then — it is a 15-minute, zero-risk change at that point.

title: Rendering3D: implement GeometryInstance3D settings, decals, fog volumes and occluders in the wgpu RenderingServer3D impl
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/gpu-render-server-trait-gaps] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/visual_instance_3d.cpp (GeometryInstance3D cast_shadow/visibility_range/transparency/material_overlay), scene/3d/decal.cpp, scene/3d/fog_volume.cpp, scene/3d/occluder_instance_3d.cpp; extension_api.json GeometryInstance3D/Decal/FogVolume properties

**Godot classes:** GeometryInstance3D, Decal, FogVolume, OccluderInstance3D

**Patina today:**
- [rendering-3d] `impl RenderingServer3D for GpuRenderer3D` at engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs:3081 implements only create_instance/free_instance/set_mesh/set_material/set_shader_material/set_multimesh/clear_multimesh/set_transform/set_visible/add_light/remove_light/update_light/add_reflection_probe/update_reflection_probe (verified by listing every `fn` in 3081-3160). It does NOT override `set_geometry_instance_settings`, `add_fog_volume`, `add_decal` or `add_occluder`, all of which are DEFAULT NO-OPS on the trait (gdserver3d/src/server.rs:73, :106, :110, :116). The software renderer implements all four (gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs:2011, :2086, :2091, :2095) and its tests pass. The shipped editor uses the GPU path: gdeditor/Cargo.toml:14 `default = ["gpu-render"]`, and examples/editor.rs:359 and :508 call `render_editor_3d_frame_gpu` for both the Play frame and the editor viewport. `grep -ci decal gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs` = 0; `grep -ci FogVolume` = 0. So in the default build, a .tscn Decal/FogVolume changes nothing, and cast_shadow=Off / visibility_range_end / GeometryInstance3D.transparency / material_overlay / extra_cull_margin / custom_aabb are all ignored.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: GeometryInstance3D.cast_shadow (Off/On/DoubleSided/ShadowsOnly), visibility_range_begin/end (+ margins, fade mode), transparency, material_overlay, extra_cull_margin and custom_aabb affect every renderer (upstream/godot/scene/3d/visual_instance_3d.cpp); Decal projects its albedo/normal/orm/emission maps onto geometry inside its oriented box (scene/3d/decal.cpp); FogVolume injects local density into the fog pass (scene/3d/fog_volume.cpp).

Patina current state: the trait declares these as DEFAULT NO-OPS — gdserver3d/src/server.rs:73 (`set_geometry_instance_settings`), :106 (`add_fog_volume`), :110 (`add_decal`), :116 (`add_occluder`). SoftwareRenderer3D implements all four (gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs:2011, 2086, 2091, 2095) and has passing tests. GpuRenderer3D does NOT: `impl RenderingServer3D for GpuRenderer3D` (gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs:3081) stops at `update_reflection_probe` (:3158). Because gdeditor's default feature is `gpu-render` (gdeditor/Cargo.toml:14) and examples/editor.rs:359/:508 both call `render_editor_3d_frame_gpu`, the SHIPPED editor viewport and Play frame silently drop all four. gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs:1889 calls `set_geometry_instance_settings` and `populate_editor_scene_3d` feeds `inputs.env_effects` through the trait — the producer side is correct; the GPU consumer is missing.

Implementation approach: (1) add fields for `geometry: HashMap<Instance3DId, GeometryInstanceSettings>`, `decals: Vec<Decal3D>`, `fog_volumes: Vec<(FogVolume, Transform3D)>`, `occluders: Vec<OccluderInstance3D>` to `GpuRenderer3D` and clear them in `reset_scene`; (2) implement the four trait methods on wgpu_pipeline.rs:3081's impl block; (3) honour geometry settings at instance-submit time (skip instances outside visibility range, exclude cast_shadow=Off from the shadow pass, draw ShadowsOnly only into shadow maps, apply per-instance transparency and material_overlay); (4) run a decal projection pass and a fog-volume density pass on the linear HDR target before `apply_camera_post` in `render_editor_color_bgra`, reusing the existing math from renderer.rs `apply_decal_pass` / `apply_fog_volume_pass` rather than duplicating it; (5) make the trait methods non-defaulted (or add a `debug_assert`) so a future backend cannot silently drop them again.

Wiring requirement: .tscn with Decal/FogVolume/MeshInstance3D(cast_shadow=Off) -> `editor_3d_render_inputs` -> `render_editor_3d_frame_gpu` -> GpuRenderer3D -> pixels, with the GPU frame matching the software frame.

**Prove it:** Loading a .tscn containing a Decal, a FogVolume and a MeshInstance3D with cast_shadow=Off / visibility_range_end set produces the same observable pixel differences through `render_editor_3d_frame_gpu` as through `render_editor_3d_frame` (software), instead of an unchanged frame. Concretely: the decal tints its footprint, the fog volume raises density in its box, the cast_shadow=Off mesh casts no shadow, and a mesh beyond visibility_range_end is not drawn. (test: `gpu_env_effects_render_from_scene`) — loads the scene from a .tscn string, renders once via the GPU entry point and once via the software entry point, and asserts both differ from a control frame with the effects removed and agree with each other within tolerance; skips cleanly when no GPU adapter is present.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn containing a Decal, a FogVolume and a MeshInstance3D with cast_shadow=Off / visibility_range_end set produces the same observable pixel differences through `render_editor_3d_frame_gpu` as through `render_editor_3d_frame` (software), instead of an unchanged frame. Concretely: the decal tints its footprint, the fog volume raises density in its box, the cast_shadow=Off mesh casts no shadow, and a mesh beyond visibility_range_end is not drawn. (test: `gpu_env_effects_render_from_scene`) — loads the scene from a .tscn string, renders once via the GPU entry point and once via the software entry point, and asserts both differ from a control frame with the effects removed and agree with each other within tolerance; skips cleanly when no GPU adapter is present.

title: Scene import: real glTF→PackedScene importer with node suffixes, materials and collision
description:
[audit-key: asset-import-pipeline/scene-import-to-packedscene] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: STUB]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/import/3d/resource_importer_scene.cpp — 108 import options, `_pre_fix_node`/`_post_fix_node` name-suffix handling (-col/-convcol/-colonly/-convcolonly/-navmesh/-occ/-vehicle/-rigid/-noimp), material extraction, LOD generation, shadow meshes, physics body creation, BoneMap retarget, `save_to_file` per-subresource; produces a `.scn` PackedScene

**Godot classes:** ResourceImporterScene, EditorSceneFormatImporterGLTF, EditorScenePostImport, PackedScene

**Patina today:**
- [asset-import-pipeline] engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/import.rs:477-547 — `GltfSceneImporter::import_scene` reads the file bytes and then FABRICATES output: `// Stub: create a mesh child to represent imported geometry` (line 517) pushes one `MeshInstance3D` named `<stem>_Mesh`, and `// Stub: detect animations from file content length as a placeholder` (line 531) emits an animation named "default" when `content.len() > 100`. engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/import.rs:605-676 — `FbxSceneImporter` fabricates a `MeshInstance3D` + `Skeleton3D` + an "idle" animation from ANY bytes. engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/import.rs:558-600 — `ObjSceneImporter` likewise. These are behind green tests that pin the fabrication: import.rs:879-893 writes `"x".repeat(200)` to a `.gltf` and asserts `mesh_count == 1` and `animations[0].name == "default"`; import.rs:939-961 writes `b"FBX binary data stub"` and asserts a Skeleton3D child. The whole registry is also UNWIRED: `grep -rn SceneFormatImporterRegistry crates/ --include=*.rs` outside its own file returns only the re-export at engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/lib.rs:207 — no editor route, no runner call. No PackedScene/.scn is ever produced from any 3D source asset.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/import.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/gltf_import.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `ResourceImporterScene` runs an `EditorSceneFormatImporter` to get a Node tree, then applies `_pre_fix_node`/`_post_fix_node` — name suffixes `-col`/`-convcol`/`-colonly`/`-convcolonly` create StaticBody3D + CollisionShape3D, `-noimp` drops the node, `-vehicle`/`-rigid` change the body type — extracts materials, generates LODs and shadow meshes, builds an AnimationPlayer from the document's animations, and saves the result as a `.scn` PackedScene under `.godot/imported/` (upstream/godot/editor/import/3d/resource_importer_scene.cpp).\n\nPatina current state: `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/import.rs` contains three FAKE importers. `GltfSceneImporter::import_scene` (import.rs:477-547) reads the bytes then invents a single `MeshInstance3D` child (line 517, comment `// Stub: create a mesh child…`) and invents an animation when `content.len() > 100` (line 531). `FbxSceneImporter` (import.rs:605-676) and `ObjSceneImporter` (import.rs:558-600) do the same. Tests pin the fabrication (import.rs:879-893, import.rs:939-961). None of it is reachable — `SceneFormatImporterRegistry` is only re-exported at `gdeditor/src/lib.rs:207`. Meanwhile `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/gltf_import.rs` has a REAL glTF/GLB parser (nodes, meshes, materials, cameras, KHR_lights_punctual, `parse_animations` at gltf_import.rs:1410) that this code never calls.\n\nImplementation approach: delete the three fabricating importers and reimplement `GltfSceneImporter::import_scene` on top of `gdresource::import_gltf_bytes`, walking the parsed `nodes` array into `ImportedSceneNode`s (Node3D/MeshInstance3D/Camera3D/OmniLight3D/DirectionalLight3D per node dict), honoring the `-col`/`-colonly`/`-convcol`/`-noimp` name suffixes by emitting StaticBody3D+CollisionShape3D children, and converting `gltf_import::parse_animations` output into an AnimationPlayer node (reusing `gdscene::animation`'s `animations_from_gltf_resource`). Add a serialiser from `ImportedScene` to a `.tscn`/`.scn` via `gdscene::scene_saver`, and register the whole flow behind the editor reimport route so a `.glb` in the project yields `.godot/imported/<name>-<md5>.scn`.\n\nWiring requirement: a real `.glb` on disk → importer → PackedScene file → `gdscene::PackedScene::from_tscn`/binary load → instanced node tree with the glTF's real node names, mesh count and animation names.

**Prove it:** Importing a real 2-node `.glb` fixture (one mesh named `Body-col`, one animation named `Walk`) yields a PackedScene whose instanced tree contains a node named `Body`, a StaticBody3D+CollisionShape3D child created by the `-col` suffix, an AnimationPlayer holding an animation named `Walk` (NOT "default"), and whose mesh count equals the glTF's real primitive count; feeding the same importer 200 bytes of non-glTF data returns an error instead of a fabricated scene. (test: `gltf_scene_import_produces_packed_scene`)
acceptance_criteria: Importing a real 2-node `.glb` fixture (one mesh named `Body-col`, one animation named `Walk`) yields a PackedScene whose instanced tree contains a node named `Body`, a StaticBody3D+CollisionShape3D child created by the `-col` suffix, an AnimationPlayer holding an animation named `Walk` (NOT "default"), and whose mesh count equals the glTF's real primitive count; feeding the same importer 200 bytes of non-glTF data returns an error instead of a fabricated scene. (test: `gltf_scene_import_produces_packed_scene`)

title: Materials3D: wire transparency, blend, cull and depth-draw modes from .tscn into both render pipelines
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/material3d-render-modes] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/MISSING/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/material.cpp (BaseMaterial3D::Transparency, BlendMode, CullMode, DepthDrawMode, alpha_scissor_threshold, alpha_hash_scale, alpha_antialiasing_mode); doc/classes/BaseMaterial3D.xml | upstream/godot/scene/resources/material.cpp BaseMaterial3D feature flags FEATURE_EMISSION..FEATURE_DETAIL; doc/classes/BaseMaterial3D.xml; extension_api.json BaseMaterial3D has ~135 properties | upstream/godot/scene/resources/material.cpp (uv1_scale/offset/triplanar/world_triplanar, billboard_mode + keep_scale + particles anim frames, grow/grow_amount, fixed_size, use_point_size/point_size, proximity_fade, distance_fade_mode, render_priority, Material::next_pass); doc/classes/BaseMaterial3D.xml | extension_api.json: BaseMaterial3D 131 properties / 154 methods (albedo_color, albedo_texture, metallic, roughness, emission*, normal*, rim*, clearcoat*, anisotropy*, ao*, heightmap*, subsurf_scatter*, backlight*, refraction*, detail_*, uv1_*/uv2_*, transparency, blend_mode, cull_mode, depth_draw_mode, shading_mode, diffuse_mode, specular_mode, billboard_mode, grow, point_size, proximity_fade_*, distance_fade_*); Material {render_priority, next_pass}; Mesh {lightmap_size_hint}; ArrayMesh {blend_shape_mode, custom_aabb, shadow_mesh}; PrimitiveMesh {material, custom_aabb, flip_faces, add_uv2, uv2_padding}; SphereMesh/PlaneMesh/PrismMesh 5 each; CylinderMesh 7

**Patina today:**
- [rendering-3d] gdrender3d/src/render_modes.rs (170 lines: CullMode, Transparency, DepthDrawMode, should_cull, alpha_scissor_discard, writes_depth, back-to-front sort) has ZERO consumers outside itself — `grep -rn "render_modes::|should_cull|alpha_scissor_discard|writes_depth" --include=*.rs engine-rs/crates` returns only its own file plus an unrelated shadow test name. StandardMaterial3D (gdserver3d/src/material.rs:211) has no `transparency`, `blend_mode`, `depth_draw_mode`, `alpha_scissor_threshold` field — only `double_sided: bool`. The .tscn parser `standard_material_from_props` (gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:2090-2141) reads 11 keys and maps cull_mode ONLY as `double_sided: matches!(props.get("cull_mode"), Some(Variant::Int(2)))` (:2139); `transparency` and `blend_mode` are never read (`grep -n '"transparency"' gdscene/src gdserver3d/src gdrender3d/src` -> only GeometryInstance3D.transparency at render_server_3d.rs:1857). A second dead copy with the right enums exists in gdserver2d/src/material.rs:47-87 with zero consumers (only re-exported at gdserver2d/src/lib.rs:27).
- [rendering-3d] gdserver3d/src/material.rs:211-235 defines StandardMaterial3D with exactly 13 fields (albedo_color/texture, metallic(+tex), roughness(+tex), normal_enabled/texture/scale, emission, shading_mode, double_sided). Godot's BaseMaterial3D exposes ~135 properties (jq '.classes[]|select(.name=="BaseMaterial3D").properties[].name' | wc -l). Grepping each feature flag across all of engine-rs/crates excluding tests finds hits ONLY in gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs (a UI schema table): rim_enabled, clearcoat_enabled, anisotropy_enabled, heightmap_enabled, subsurf_scatter_enabled, backlight_enabled, refraction_enabled, detail_enabled, vertex_color_use_as_albedo, diffuse_mode, specular_mode, shadow_to_opacity, disable_receive_shadows, stencil_mode. `ao_enabled` matches only Environment SSAO code, not material AO. - [rendering-3d] `grep -rln` across engine-rs/crates excluding tests: `uv1_scale`, `uv1_triplanar`, `billboard_mode` (material — the only hit is Sprite3D's own billboard in gdserver3d/src/sprite3d.rs), `proximity_fade_enabled`, `grow_amount`, `use_point_size` all resolve exclusively to gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs. `next_pass` appears ONLY in inspector_schema_generated.rs — no ClassDB registration, no render struct. `render_priority` appears in gdserver3d/src/sprite3d.rs and class_db.rs but is not used in any draw-order sort. Material distance-fade math exists in gdserver3d/src/material_math.rs but is referenced from light/decal code, not from a material path (StandardMaterial3D has no distance_fade field, gdserver3d/src/material.rs:211-235).
- [registered-class-member-depth] engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:5658 BaseMaterial3D, :5662 StandardMaterial3D, :5663 ORMMaterial3D, :3553 Material, :3604 Mesh, :4225 ArrayMesh, :4199 PrimitiveMesh, :4221 SphereMesh, :4222 CylinderMesh, :4223 PlaneMesh, :4224 PrismMesh, :4283 ShaderInclude — all registered with zero properties/methods/signals. StandardMaterial3D IS in the editor's 70-class generated schema (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs) so the editor panel looks populated, but ClassDB — which backs `ClassDB.class_get_property_list`, `Object.get_property_list` (engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:9195+), `property_get_revert` (class_db.rs:466) and the .tscn default seeding at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:1549 — has nothing. That is a textbook false green: the inspector sample class passes while the base that declares all 131 properties is empty.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/render_modes.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/material.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver2d/src/material.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/shader.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/material_math.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: BaseMaterial3D.transparency (Disabled/Alpha/AlphaScissor/AlphaHash/DepthPrePass), alpha_scissor_threshold (default 0.5), alpha_hash_scale, alpha_antialiasing_mode/edge, blend_mode (Mix/Add/Sub/Mul/PremultAlpha), cull_mode (Back/Front/Disabled), depth_draw_mode (OpaqueOnly/Always/Never), no_depth_test — see upstream/godot/scene/resources/material.cpp and doc/classes/BaseMaterial3D.xml. Transparent materials are drawn back-to-front after opaques and by default do not write depth.

Patina current state: the decision logic already exists, fully tested, and is dead. engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/render_modes.rs defines CullMode/Transparency/DepthDrawMode plus `should_cull`, `alpha_scissor_discard`, `writes_depth` and a back-to-front sort — and has zero call sites outside the module. The material type has no fields to carry the modes (gdserver3d/src/material.rs:211-235 — only `double_sided`), and the .tscn reader ignores them: gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:2090 `standard_material_from_props` maps cull_mode only to `double_sided` at :2139 and never reads `transparency` or `blend_mode`. Result: an alpha-blended or alpha-scissored material authored in Godot renders fully opaque in Patina.

Implementation approach: (1) add `transparency: Transparency`, `alpha_scissor_threshold: f32`, `alpha_hash_scale: f32`, `blend_mode: BlendMode`, `cull_mode: CullMode`, `depth_draw_mode: DepthDrawMode`, `no_depth_test: bool` to `StandardMaterial3D` and `Material3D` in gdserver3d/src/material.rs, moving the enums out of gdrender3d/src/render_modes.rs into gdserver3d so both backends share them (and delete the duplicate dead copy in gdserver2d/src/material.rs:47-87); (2) parse all of them in `standard_material_from_props` (gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:2090) and in the editor's material resolution path; (3) consume them in SoftwareRenderer3D (call `should_cull` per triangle, `alpha_scissor_discard` per fragment, `writes_depth` on the depth store, and sort transparent draws back-to-front); (4) in wgpu_pipeline.rs map them onto the wgpu `PrimitiveState.cull_mode`, `DepthStencilState.depth_write_enabled` and `ColorTargetState.blend`, splitting the draw list into an opaque pass and a depth-sorted transparent pass.

Wiring requirement: .tscn StandardMaterial3D sub-resource -> material resolution -> both renderers -> visibly blended/discarded/back-face pixels.

**Merged findings (4):** Material transparency / blend / cull / depth-draw modes never reach either render pipeline; StandardMaterial3D advanced PBR channels (rim, clearcoat, anisotropy, AO, heightmap/parallax, subsurface, backlight, refraction, detail) entirely absent; StandardMaterial3D UV1/UV2 transforms, triplanar, billboard, proximity/distance fade, grow, point size, next_pass and render_priority absent; Material and mesh resource shells: BaseMaterial3D registers 0 of 131 properties; Material, Mesh, ArrayMesh, PrimitiveMesh, SphereMesh, PlaneMesh, PrismMesh, CylinderMesh all bare

**Prove it:** A .tscn with two overlapping quads whose StandardMaterial3D sets `transparency = 1` (Alpha) with albedo alpha 0.5 renders the far quad's colour through the near one; a material with `transparency = 2` (AlphaScissor) and `alpha_scissor_threshold = 0.5` discards sub-threshold texels leaving background pixels; a material with `cull_mode = 1` (Front) shows the far side of a cube rather than the near side. All three hold in the software renderer AND in the wgpu renderer. (test: `material_transparency_modes_render`) — loads each case from a .tscn string via the editor 3D input builder and asserts specific pixel colours in the rendered frame, not just the parsed material struct.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with two overlapping quads whose StandardMaterial3D sets `transparency = 1` (Alpha) with albedo alpha 0.5 renders the far quad's colour through the near one; a material with `transparency = 2` (AlphaScissor) and `alpha_scissor_threshold = 0.5` discards sub-threshold texels leaving background pixels; a material with `cull_mode = 1` (Front) shows the far side of a cube rather than the near side. All three hold in the software renderer AND in the wgpu renderer. (test: `material_transparency_modes_render`) — loads each case from a .tscn string via the editor 3D input builder and asserts specific pixel colours in the rendered frame, not just the parsed material struct.

comments.text:
BronzeLake: ROOT CAUSE FOUND. The renderer is innocent. Fix applied; bead reassigned away from me before I could resend.

THE DIAGNOSTIC ANSWERED IT. I added an assertion on the intermediate state (Render3DItem.material) ahead of the pixel comparisons, precisely because "0 pixels differed" cannot distinguish "no material reached the renderer" from "the renderer ignored transparency" - opposite fixes. The verify returned:

    left: None    right: Some(Alpha)

None = NO render item carried a material at all. So the break is upstream of the renderer entirely.

ROOT CAUSE: the test never populated ClassDB. It called no register_*_classes(). Viewport3D::build_render_list collects only **Node3D-derived** nodes, which is a class-chain query, and with an empty registry is_class("Node3D") is false for every node - so the render list is EMPTY, nothing carries a material, and both frames come back identical and blank. That presents as "an alpha-blended quad renders identically to an opaque one", which points at the renderer and is completely misleading.

The proof is the sibling: crates/gdscene/tests/material_resource_to_pixels.rs uses the SAME surface_material_override/0 = SubResource(..) shape and works - because line ~59 calls gdobject::class_db::register_3d_classes() before parsing. Same trap the gdeditor canvas tests document for CanvasItem/2D.

FIX APPLIED (one line, in load()): gdobject::class_db::register_3d_classes(), with a comment explaining why so nobody deletes it as redundant. gdobject is already a gdeditor dependency and the fn exists.

ALSO FIXED EARLIER IN THIS BEAD, and still correct even though it was not the cause: the three fixtures attached their material as a bare `material = SubResource(..)` on a MeshInstance3D. Godot has no such property - doc/classes/MeshInstance3D.xml lists only mesh, skeleton, skin; overriding is GeometryInstance3D.material_override or per-surface surface_material_override/N. packed_scene resolves __material__* from surface_material_override/0 or the MESH sub-resource's own material, so a bare `material` key resolves to nothing. Now switched to surface_material_override/0.

THE IMPLEMENTATION IS NOT AT FAULT - I traced every link before touching anything: packed_scene flattens the material's full property bag verbatim (no allowlist); material_props_from_node strips the prefix; standard_material_from_props reads transparency/cull_mode/depth_draw_mode/alpha_scissor_threshold; to_material3d() maps all four EXPLICITLY with a comment warning that ..default() would drop them; renderer.rs calls should_cull with entry.material.cull_mode and passes entry.material.transparency into rasterize_triangle_with_modes, which blends src-over when is_transparent. Every render_modes helper now has real callers in renderer.rs, rasterizer.rs and wgpu_pipeline.rs.

NEXT STEP: just re-verify. If it now passes, done. If item_transparency still reports None, the remaining suspects are narrow: whether the .tscn parser preserves the slash-bearing key surface_material_override/0, and whether mesh = "primitive:PlaneMesh" (a raw string, vs the sibling's mesh = SubResource(..)) is accepted by the editor's 3D builder. If it reports Some(Disabled), transparency is lost between the .tscn and StandardMaterial3D. The assertion messages spell all three out.

STILL OPEN regardless: (1) material_override carrying a plain StandardMaterial3D never flattens - packed_scene handles material_override only in the ShaderMaterial pass, so a 3D node overriding that way renders unmaterialed; same class of bug, own bead. (2) render_modes::sort_back_to_front has ZERO callers workspace-wide; not needed by these fixtures since the far quad is declared first, but any scene where a transparent surface precedes what is behind it composites wrongly. (3) The wgpu half is skipped without a GPU adapter, so it may be unproven regardless.

Needs the GPU worktree.
(b) alpha_hash_scale, alpha_antialiasing_mode/edge and no_depth_test are REGISTERED now but still unparsed by the .tscn material reader — registration and parsing are separate halves and only the first is done.
(c) The BaseMaterial3D feature flags are named in ClassDB but never read by pbr_shade: rim, clearcoat, anisotropy, heightmap, subsurf_scatter, backlight, refraction, detail, vertex_color_use_as_albedo, diffuse_mode, specular_mode, uv1_*/uv2_*, billboard_mode, proximity_fade, distance_fade, grow, point_size, render_priority, next_pass.

title: Rendering3D: resolve glTF and ArrayMesh mesh resources into the editor viewport and Play frame
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/mesh-asset-pipeline] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/mesh.cpp (ArrayMesh surfaces), modules/gltf/ (GLTFDocument import to ImporterMesh/ArrayMesh); a Godot 3D project references meshes as ExtResource("…glb::Mesh_…") or [sub_resource type="ArrayMesh"] with `_surfaces` | upstream/godot/scene/resources/mesh.cpp Mesh::ARRAY_VERTEX/NORMAL/TANGENT/COLOR/TEX_UV/TEX_UV2/CUSTOM0..3/BONES/WEIGHTS/INDEX + ARRAY_FORMAT_* flags and blend-shape arrays; doc/classes/ArrayMesh.xml

**Godot classes:** ArrayMesh, ImporterMesh, MeshInstance3D, GLTFDocument, Mesh

**Patina today:**
- [rendering-3d] The editor's only file-backed mesh loader is `mesh_from_file` at gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs:472-480: it early-returns None unless the path ends in `.obj`, then calls `Mesh3D::from_obj`. `grep -n "gltf|glb|ArrayMesh" gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs` returns nothing but that .obj branch. Everything else resolves through `split_mesh_marker` (:421) which only understands `primitive:BoxMesh|…` markers. A real glTF importer exists (gdresource/src/gltf_import.rs) and a converter `mesh3d_from_gltf_resource` exists at gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:1547, but its only caller is line 1116 inside `RenderServer3DAdapter::render_frame` — and `RenderServer3DAdapter` has NO production callers at all (`grep -rn RenderServer3DAdapter` outside its defining file returns only gdscene/tests/*, gdeditor/tests/probe_decal.rs). There is no ArrayMesh `_surfaces` byte-array decoder anywhere (`grep -rn "_surfaces|ARRAY_FORMAT|surface_get_arrays"` -> no production hits).
- [rendering-3d] gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs:29-39 `Surface3D` holds only vertices, normals, uvs, indices, primitive_type. `Mesh3D` (:138-170) adds `surfaces`, `bone_weights`, `bone_indices` — still no tangents, no colours, no UV2, no custom arrays, no blend-shape targets. `ArrayMesh::add_surface_from_arrays` (gdserver3d/src/primitive_mesh.rs:367) takes exactly (primitive_type, vertices, normals, uvs, indices) — five of Godot's thirteen array slots. `grep -rn "ARRAY_CUSTOM"` across engine-rs = 0 hits. Blend shapes: gdrender3d/src/morph.rs (181 lines of morph-target math) has ZERO consumers — `grep -rn "gdrender3d::morph|morph::"` outside the file returns nothing, and `grep -ci blend_shape` in both renderer.rs and wgpu_pipeline.rs = 0. Because normal mapping needs tangents and none are carried, `normal_texture` shading cannot be correct.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/gltf_import.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/primitive_mesh.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/morph.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: a MeshInstance3D's `mesh` is an ArrayMesh (inline `[sub_resource type="ArrayMesh"]` with a `_surfaces` array of packed vertex/index byte buffers) or an ExtResource pointing into an imported .glb/.gltf/.obj scene (`res://model.glb::Mesh_xyz`). See upstream/godot/scene/resources/mesh.cpp and modules/gltf/.

Patina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs:472 `mesh_from_file` accepts ONLY `.obj` — every other path returns None and the viewport falls back to a placeholder cube. The primitive path (`split_mesh_marker`, :421) covers only Box/Sphere/Capsule/Cylinder/Plane/Prism/Torus markers. A working glTF converter already exists at gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:1547 (`mesh3d_from_gltf_resource`, plus `material_from_gltf_resource` at :1636), but its only caller is the test-only `RenderServer3DAdapter` (render_server_3d.rs:1116) which nothing in production constructs. Consequence: importing a real Godot 3D project into Patina shows grey placeholder boxes.

Implementation approach: (1) extend `mesh_from_file` in gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs to dispatch on extension — `.obj` (existing), `.glb`/`.gltf` via `gdresource::import_gltf`/`import_gltf_bytes` then `gdscene::render_server_3d::mesh3d_from_gltf_resource`, and the `path::SubresourceName` suffix form Godot writes for imported scenes; (2) add an ArrayMesh `_surfaces` decoder in gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs that reads Godot's packed vertex/attribute/index byte layout out of a `[sub_resource type="ArrayMesh"]` property bag and fills `Surface3D`; (3) resolve `ExtResource`/`SubResource` mesh references through the existing resource companion mechanism rather than raw strings; (4) memoize decoded meshes in a cache keyed by resource path, mirroring `MaterialTextureCache` (gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:2156), so the per-frame render does not re-decode; (5) also pull the glTF material through `material_from_gltf_resource`.

Wiring requirement: .tscn -> MeshInstance3D.mesh ExtResource(.glb) or inline ArrayMesh -> `editor_3d_render_inputs` -> `render_editor_3d_frame_gpu` -> mesh triangles on screen.

**Merged findings (2):** Mesh assets: only primitive markers and .obj reach the 3D viewport — glTF/ArrayMesh/.mesh resources never render; Mesh vertex format: no tangents, vertex colours, UV2, custom arrays, or blend shapes; per-surface materials are structural only

**Prove it:** A .tscn whose MeshInstance3D references a small .glb (or an inline ArrayMesh sub-resource) renders that model's actual silhouette in the editor 3D viewport and in the Play frame, instead of the placeholder cube. Observable: the rendered frame differs from the frame produced for the same scene with the mesh reference removed, and its filled-pixel count matches the model's projected area rather than the 0.4-unit marker cube. (test: `gltf_mesh_renders_in_viewport`) — writes a minimal .glb + .tscn to a temp dir, loads via PackedScene, renders through `editor_3d_render_inputs` + `render_editor_3d_frame`, and asserts the triangle geometry reached the frame.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn whose MeshInstance3D references a small .glb (or an inline ArrayMesh sub-resource) renders that model's actual silhouette in the editor 3D viewport and in the Play frame, instead of the placeholder cube. Observable: the rendered frame differs from the frame produced for the same scene with the mesh reference removed, and its filled-pixel count matches the model's projected area rather than the 0.4-unit marker cube. (test: `gltf_mesh_renders_in_viewport`) — writes a minimal .glb + .tscn to a temp dir, loads via PackedScene, renders through `editor_3d_render_inputs` + `render_editor_3d_frame`, and asserts the triangle geometry reached the frame.

title: Rendering3D: drive a per-frame 3D scene render from patina-runner and the patina-web canvas
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/runtime-3d-render-path] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/platform/web/ + servers/rendering/renderer_scene_render.cpp — Godot's web export renders the 3D scene each rAF frame into the canvas | upstream/godot/scene/main/viewport.cpp — a Viewport owns a render target updated per `render_target_update_mode` (DISABLED/ONCE/WHEN_VISIBLE/WHEN_PARENT_VISIBLE/ALWAYS) with `render_target_clear_mode`; upstream/godot/scene/gui/sub_viewport_container.cpp draws the child SubViewport's ViewportTexture and forwards input via `_notification`/`unhandled_input` scaled by `stretch_shrink`. doc/classes/SubViewport.xml, SubViewportContainer.xml. | upstream/godot/scene/main/viewport.cpp (scaling_3d_mode/scale, fsr_sharpness, use_taa, msaa_3d, screen_space_aa, use_debanding, use_hdr_2d, mesh_lod_threshold); doc/classes/Viewport.xml | upstream/godot/scene/main/viewport.cpp `Viewport::find_world_2d()` / `find_world_3d()` walk up to the nearest viewport that owns a world; `SubViewport::set_use_own_world_3d` gives a sub-viewport an isolated World3D (its own physics space + environment). extension_api.json Viewport properties: `own_world_3d`, `world_3d`, `world_2d`. doc/classes/Viewport.xml, World2D.xml, World3D.xml.

**Godot classes:** Viewport, Camera3D, RenderingServer, SubViewport, SubViewportContainer, ViewportTexture, World2D, World3D

**Patina today:**
- [rendering-3d] engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/main.rs:1-11 documents itself as the "Patina headless runner" that "dumps the final tree state as JSON to stdout"; `grep -rn "gdrender3d|gdrender2d|SoftwareRenderer" engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/` returns NOTHING, and patina-runner/Cargo.toml has no dependency on either render crate. patina-web's entire render surface is engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/canvas.rs:146 `present_clear(r,g,b)` — a solid-colour clear; there is no scene submission, no camera, no instance list. The only real 3D frame producer in the repo is gdeditor's server-side `render_editor_3d_frame_gpu` (examples/editor.rs:359, :508), which renders on the host and streams BMP to the editor page.
- [scene-tree] The implementation exists but nothing in the frame loop calls it. `render_subviewport_to_texture` is defined at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/sub_viewport.rs:514 and re-exported at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/lib.rs:122; `grep -rn 'render_subviewport_to_texture' engine-rs` returns only the definition, its own in-module test (sub_viewport.rs:603) and engine-rs/tests/misc_suite_f/subviewport_viewport_texture_test.rs:118. `grep -rn 'SubViewport' engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src` matches only two rows of engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:5124-5125. `MainLoop::step` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2628-3145) has no sub-viewport phase. The container-side coordinate mapping `subviewport_container_to_viewport_coord` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs:2028) has no caller: `SceneTree::gui_input_stage` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:3245-3380) hit-tests with `control::control_at_point` and never descends into a SubViewport; `grep -rn 'subviewport_container_to_viewport_coord' engine-rs/crates` finds only control.rs and engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/subviewport_container_composite_and_input.rs. Related gap in the same area: Viewport's `world_2d`, `world_3d` and `own_world_3d` have zero implementation — `grep -rn 'own_world_3d|\bworld_2d\b|\bworld_3d\b' engine-rs/crates --include='*.rs'` matches only the unrelated `PhysicsWorld2D`/`PhysicsWorld3D` type names, and World2D/World3D are registered as Nil-property Resource stubs at engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:4000-4010.
- [rendering-3d] `grep -rln` across engine-rs/crates excluding tests: `scaling_3d_mode`, `fsr_sharpness`, `use_taa`, `screen_space_aa` each hit ONLY gdobject/src/class_db.rs (ClassDB registration). `msaa_3d` hits gdcore/src/project_settings.rs:699 (a default value put into the settings map) and class_db.rs — with no consumer. `use_hdr_2d` returns NO hits anywhere. The render-side viewport type gdserver3d/src/viewport.rs:9 `Viewport3D` has exactly six fields (width, height, camera_transform, fov, near, far, environment) — no anti-aliasing, no resolution scale, no render layers. So a project that sets MSAA 4x or FSR upscaling in project.godot or on a SubViewport gets an unfiltered, unscaled frame. (`use_debanding` IS implemented — Environment3D.use_debanding + gdrender3d/src/postprocess.rs `screen_space_dither`.)
- [scene-tree] `grep -rn 'own_world_3d' engine-rs/crates --include='*.rs'` → 0 hits. `grep -rn 'world_2d|world_3d' engine-rs/crates --include='*.rs'` matches only the unrelated `PhysicsWorld2D`/`PhysicsWorld3D` struct names in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs and physics_server_3d.rs. World2D/World3D exist as registration stubs only: engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:4000-4010 registers `World2D` with `canvas`/`space`/`navigation_map` as Nil because Patina has no RID Variant. `crate::viewport` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/viewport.rs) implements `get_viewport`/`get_window` climbing and the root window content scale but has no world concept; `MainLoop` holds exactly one `PhysicsServer` and one `PhysicsServer3D` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2085-2100), so there is one global space with no per-viewport partition.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/main.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/canvas.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/lib.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/sub_viewport.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/viewport.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/project_settings.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/viewport.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: the runtime renders the active Viewport's 3D world every frame from the current Camera3D through the rendering server, and Godot's web export does exactly this into the HTML canvas (upstream/godot/platform/web/, servers/rendering/).

Patina current state: there is no runtime 3D render at all. engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/main.rs:1 declares a "headless runner" that dumps tree JSON; the crate does not even depend on gdrender3d/gdrender2d (`grep -rn gdrender3d engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/` -> no hits). engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/canvas.rs exposes only `WebRenderer::present_clear` (:146), a flat clear + present — proof that surface/device/swapchain work, but nothing draws a scene. All actual 3D pixels in the project come from the editor host process (examples/editor.rs:359/:508). So "the runner renders what the editor shows" is not true for any 3D feature in this subsystem.

Implementation approach: (1) add gdrender3d + gdserver3d to patina-runner and give it an optional `--render <w>x<h> --out frame.png` mode that, after each frame's lifecycle tick, builds render inputs from the SceneTree (reuse the collection logic in gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs rather than duplicating it — promote `RenderServer3DAdapter` from test-only to a real production entry point) and renders via SoftwareRenderer3D; (2) in patina-web, add a `renderFrame` binding on `WebRenderer` that takes the tree's render inputs and submits them to `gdrender3d::wgpu_pipeline::GpuRenderer3D` against the live `GpuSurface` instead of clearing; (3) drive it from the rAF loop so the browser runtime shows the scene.

Wiring requirement: `patina-runner scene.tscn --render` must emit a frame whose pixels come from Camera3D + MeshInstance3D in the .tscn, and the same input path must be callable from patina-web.

**Merged findings (4):** No 3D render path in the runtime: patina-runner is headless JSON, patina-web can only clear the canvas; SubViewport render target + SubViewportContainer composite/input forwarding; Viewport 3D quality settings: scaling_3d_mode (bilinear/FSR), TAA, MSAA 3D, screen_space_aa and HDR-2D are registered but have no render field or effect; Viewport World2D / World3D and SubViewport own_world_3d

**Prove it:** Running the runner on a .tscn containing a Camera3D and a lit MeshInstance3D produces a frame buffer with non-background pixels where the mesh projects, and an empty scene produces a uniform background frame. The frame-producing entry point is the same one patina-web's canvas render calls. (test: `runner_renders_3d_scene_frame`) — invokes the runner's render entry point in-process on a .tscn string and asserts coverage > 0 for the mesh scene and == 0 for the camera-only scene.
acceptance_criteria: Running the runner on a .tscn containing a Camera3D and a lit MeshInstance3D produces a frame buffer with non-background pixels where the mesh projects, and an empty scene produces a uniform background frame. The frame-producing entry point is the same one patina-web's canvas render calls. (test: `runner_renders_3d_scene_frame`) — invokes the runner's render entry point in-process on a .tscn string and asserts coverage > 0 for the mesh scene and == 0 for the camera-only scene.

A second, duplicate implementation lives in engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/project_settings_dialog.rs:511-720 with the same invented keys plus `application/project_name`, `display/resolution_w`, `physics/fps`, `rendering/renderer`; `grep -rn ProjectSettingsDialog` outside that file returns only its own tests, so it is dead code, and its backing store engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/project_settings_store.rs:70-72 `to_godot()` emits `serde_json::to_string_pretty`, i.e. JSON, while its doc comment claims "project.godot contents".

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/file_access.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/main.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/project_settings_dialog.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/project_settings_store.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/input_map.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/content_scale.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/export.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/pck.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-web/build-web.sh

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `PackedData` (upstream/godot/core/io/file_access_pack.cpp) registers `FileAccessPack`/`DirAccessPack` as the process-wide FileAccess/DirAccess backends. Consequently after `ProjectSettings.load_resource_pack()` — or when a game boots from an exported `.pck` — every `res://` read is served from the pack transparently: scene loading, `load()`/`preload()`, `FileAccess.open`, `DirAccess.list_dir_begin`, `FileAccess.file_exists`. `replace_files` controls whether pack entries shadow disk; `offset` supports packs embedded in a host binary.

Patina current state: the pack VFS is real and tested (`gdcore/src/file_access.rs:115 mount_pack`, `:177 read_from_packs`, `:332 read_file_bytes`, `gdresource/src/pck.rs` PCK V2/V3 reader) but almost nothing calls it. Grepping the whole workspace for `read_from_packs|read_file_bytes|read_file_string` outside gdcore and tests finds only `gdresource/src/pck.rs:923` and `patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs:81,420`. The hot paths bypass it: `gdscene/src/scripting.rs:3112` (`preload(x).instantiate()`) uses `std::fs::read_to_string`; `gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:152` (`load()` of a `.tres`) uses `std::fs::read_to_string`; `gdcore/src/file_access.rs:282 FileAccess::open` opens a real `std::fs::File` and its doc at :326 concedes it "cannot serve a pack". And no boot path mounts a pack: `grep -n pck patina-runner/src/main.rs patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs` → 0 hits.

Implementation approach: (1) in `gdcore/src/file_access.rs`, give `FileAccess` an internal backing enum `{ Os(File), Packed { bytes: Vec<u8>, pos: u64 } }` so `FileAccess::open` on a `res://` path that `pack_has_file` serves an in-memory reader supporting seek/read/get_length/eof — write mode on a pack path returns ERR_FILE_CANT_WRITE like Godot. (2) Make `DirAccess::open`/`list_dir_begin`/`get_files`/`get_directories` merge mounted-pack directory entries with disk entries, honoring removal entries. (3) Replace the raw `std::fs::read_to_string` at `gdscene/src/scripting.rs:3112` (and its sub-scene `resolve` closure at :3115) and at `gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:152` with `gdcore::FileAccess::read_file_bytes`. (4) In `patina-runner/src/main.rs`, accept a `.pck` path argument (and a `--main-pack` flag): mount it via `gdresource::pck::load_resource_pack`, then read `res://project.godot` and the main scene through the pack-aware path already present in project_boot.rs.

Wiring requirement: after `patina-runner <game.pck>` the frame loop must be driving nodes that came out of the pack, with zero loose files on disk; and a script running in that scene must be able to `FileAccess.open("res://data.txt", READ).get_as_text()` and `preload("res://sub.tscn").instantiate()` against pack-only content.

**Merged findings (28):** PCK-mounted `res://` overlay reaching the runtime read paths (scene load, script `load()`, `FileAccess.open`); Editor "Project Settings" dialog: real Godot keys + persistence to project.godot; Editor Project Settings ▸ Input Map tab reads/writes the project's [input] section; Editor Play honors project.godot ProjectSettings (physics, gravity, script-visible settings); display/window/stretch/* content scale and audio/buses/default_bus_layout applied on the real runner boot path; Exported web bundle actually boots (loader instantiates the module and hands it the data pack); Binary .scn / PackedScene `_bundled` unbundling (SceneState reconstruction); Feature-tag overrides (`setting.web`, `.mobile`, `.debug`, `.editor_hint`) resolved on every setting read; project.godot value types: Dictionary / Array / PackedStringArray / int-vector settings, and lossless save round-trip; Scene tree dock context menu: Save Branch as Scene / Open Scene / Open Script / Add to Group; Export dialog: running an export (Export Project / Export All); Web export preset options reach the generated bundle (thread support, PWA, head include, canvas resize policy, icon, VRAM compression)

**Prove it:** `patina-runner path/to/game.pck` boots the project's main scene with no loose project files present; inside that run a script's `FileAccess.open("res://data.txt", FileAccess.READ).get_as_text()` returns the packed bytes, `DirAccess.open("res://").get_files()` lists packed entries, and `preload("res://sub.tscn").instantiate()` returns a non-null node. Test: `pck_only_project_boots_and_serves_all_reads` — packs a fixture project with PCKPacker into a temp `.pck`, deletes the source tree, boots the runner from the pack, and asserts main-scene node names, a script-side FileAccess read, a DirAccess listing, and a runtime `preload().instantiate()` all resolve from the pack (test: `pck_only_project_boots_and_serves_all_reads`).
acceptance_criteria: `patina-runner path/to/game.pck` boots the project's main scene with no loose project files present; inside that run a script's `FileAccess.open("res://data.txt", FileAccess.READ).get_as_text()` returns the packed bytes, `DirAccess.open("res://").get_files()` lists packed entries, and `preload("res://sub.tscn").instantiate()` returns a non-null node. Test: `pck_only_project_boots_and_serves_all_reads` — packs a fixture project with PCKPacker into a temp `.pck`, deletes the source tree, boots the runner from the pack, and asserts main-scene node names, a script-side FileAccess read, a DirAccess listing, and a runtime `preload().instantiate()` all resolve from the pack (test: `pck_only_project_boots_and_serves_all_reads`).

title: SceneTree: advance SceneTreeTimers once per frame and honor create_timer's process flags
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/st-scene-tree-timer] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: STUB/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/main/scene_tree.cpp `SceneTree::create_timer(double p_delay_sec, bool p_process_always=true, bool p_process_in_physics=false, bool p_ignore_time_scale=false)` and `SceneTree::process_timers(double p_delta, bool p_physics_frame)` — timers are advanced exactly once per iteration, in the idle pass unless `process_in_physics`. doc/classes/SceneTree.xml `create_timer`. | upstream/godot/scene/main/scene_tree.cpp `SceneTree::_notification` — on NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST it calls `get_root()->propagate_notification(NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST)` and, if `auto_accept_quit`, `quit()`; on NOTIFICATION_WM_GO_BACK_REQUEST it does the same for `quit_on_go_back`. Both default true. doc/classes/SceneTree.xml auto_accept_quit / quit_on_go_back. | upstream/godot/scene/main/scene_tree.cpp — `multiplayer_poll` gates the per-frame MultiplayerAPI::poll; `SceneTree::set_multiplayer(Ref<MultiplayerAPI>, NodePath root_path)` and `get_multiplayer(NodePath)` let a subtree run its own MultiplayerAPI; doc/classes/SceneTree.xml.

**Godot classes:** SceneTree, SceneTreeTimer, Node, MultiplayerAPI

**Patina today:**
- [scene-tree] DOUBLE ADVANCE: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:3837 — `process_frame_with_scripts` begins with `self.process_timers(delta);` — and engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:629 — `process_script_coroutines` begins with `self.process_timers(delta as f64);`. engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:3076 calls `self.tree.process_frame_with_scripts(delta_secs);` and main_loop.rs:3084 calls `self.tree.process_script_coroutines(delta_secs as f32);` in the same `step()`. Every SceneTreeTimer therefore loses 2×delta per frame, so `await get_tree().create_timer(1.0).timeout` resumes after ~0.5 s of game time. MISSING FLAGS: `SceneTree::create_timer` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:568) takes only `seconds: f64`; the script bridge mirrors that (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs:2662, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs:467) — no `process_always`, `process_in_physics` or `ignore_time_scale`.
- [scene-tree] Registered with correct defaults but no runtime path: engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:3972-3974 registers `auto_accept_quit` and `quit_on_go_back` as `Variant::Bool(true)`, and engine-rs/crates/gdobject/tests/scene_main_classes.rs:105 asserts those defaults — while the same test file states at lines 11-15 that "The bead also asks for a runtime `auto_accept_quit` path — a close-request delivering `NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST` and ending the loop — which lives in `gdscene/src/main_loop.rs` plus the runner/editor stop path. Not delivered". `grep -rn 'auto_accept_quit|quit_on_go_back|NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST|WM_GO_BACK' engine-rs/crates --include='*.rs'` finds only class_db.rs:3970-3974 and that test file — nothing in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src or engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src. The NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST constant itself does not exist (engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/notification.rs has no WM_* block).
- [multiplayer] `multiplayer_poll` is registered as a SceneTree property defaulting to true (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:3974) and asserted by crates/gdobject/tests/scene_main_classes.rs:105, but nothing reads it: `grep -rn 'multiplayer_poll' crates/ --include='*.rs'` matches only those two sites plus a comment at class_db.rs:3971. The MainLoop polls unconditionally at crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:3051 (`self.tree.poll_multiplayer_with_delta(delta_secs as f32);`) with no gate. Per-branch multiplayer is absent: the SceneTree owns exactly one `multiplayer: MultiplayerAPI` field (crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:231) with only `get_multiplayer()`/`get_multiplayer_mut()` accessors (scene_tree.rs:426-433); `grep -rn 'fn set_multiplayer\b' crates/` = 0.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GROUND TRUTH (Godot 4.6.1): `SceneTree::process_timers` runs once per idle iteration (and once per physics tick for timers created with `process_in_physics = true`); `create_timer(delay, process_always = true, process_in_physics = false, ignore_time_scale = false)` — a `process_always = false` timer stops while the tree is paused, and `ignore_time_scale = true` uses the unscaled delta (upstream/godot/scene/main/scene_tree.cpp, doc/classes/SceneTree.xml).\n\nPATINA NOW: timers are advanced TWICE every frame. `SceneTree::process_frame_with_scripts` opens with `self.process_timers(delta)` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:3837) and `SceneTree::process_script_coroutines` opens with `self.process_timers(delta as f64)` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:629); `MainLoop::step` calls both, at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:3076 and :3084. Net effect: `await get_tree().create_timer(1.0).timeout` fires after roughly half a second, and every timed gameplay beat runs at double speed. `SceneTree::create_timer` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:568) also drops all three Godot flags, as do engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs:2662 and engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs:467.\n\nAPPROACH: remove the `process_timers` call from `process_frame_with_scripts` (the coroutine pass at scene_tree.rs:629 is the one that also drains `take_timeout_signals`, so it is the correct single owner) — or hoist a single call into `MainLoop::step` between the process phase and the coroutine phase. Extend `SceneTreeTimer` with `process_always`, `process_in_physics`, `ignore_time_scale`; extend `SceneTree::create_timer` and the two bridge signatures to take them (defaulting to Godot's defaults when a script passes fewer args); skip non-`process_always` timers when `SceneTree::paused()`; advance `process_in_physics` timers from the physics tick loop in `MainLoop::step` instead of the idle pass; feed `ignore_time_scale` timers the unscaled `real_delta_secs` already computed at main_loop.rs:2652.\n\nWIRING: the fix must be observable from a .tscn-attached GDScript running under `MainLoop::step` — the frame loop, not a direct `process_timers` unit call.

**Merged findings (3):** SceneTreeTimer (`get_tree().create_timer()`) tick rate and constructor flags; SceneTree.auto_accept_quit / quit_on_go_back and the NOTIFICATION_WM_CLOSE_REQUEST path; SceneTree.multiplayer_poll honoured; per-branch SceneTree.set_multiplayer/get_multiplayer(root_path)

**Prove it:** A .tscn-attached script doing `await get_tree().create_timer(1.0).timeout` then setting a flag resumes on the frame nearest 60 steps of 1/60 s (±1 frame), not ~30. A timer created with `process_always = false` does not advance while `get_tree().paused = true`; one created with `process_in_physics = true` advances on physics ticks (verified by changing physics_ticks_per_second); one created with `ignore_time_scale = true` is unaffected by `Engine.time_scale = 0.5`. (test: `scene_tree_timer_advances_once_per_frame_with_flags`)
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn-attached script doing `await get_tree().create_timer(1.0).timeout` then setting a flag resumes on the frame nearest 60 steps of 1/60 s (±1 frame), not ~30. A timer created with `process_always = false` does not advance while `get_tree().paused = true`; one created with `process_in_physics = true` advances on physics ticks (verified by changing physics_ticks_per_second); one created with `ignore_time_scale = true` is unaffected by `Engine.time_scale = 0.5`. (test: `scene_tree_timer_advances_once_per_frame_with_flags`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
FuchsiaDeer, parked-bead diagnosis (NOT a retry; leaving it for operator triage).

Last failure was "got 0" from scene_tree_timer_advances_once_per_frame_with_flags. That is NOT the double-advance. 0 means the script variable frames was still 0 when the await resumed -- i.e. the scripts _process(_d) never ran, so the in-script frame counter I used as the measuring instrument never incremented. The other 3 tests in the binary passed, including the paused/process_always and ignore_time_scale flag semantics, so the flag work itself is exercised and green.

Likely cause: the test builds the scene with add_packed_scene_to_tree + attach_script + process_script_ready but never runs the enter_tree lifecycle, so the node is not process-enabled. The engine change is probably fine; the test measures the wrong thing.

Suggested fix: drop the in-script counter and measure in Rust -- step one frame at a time and record the loop index at which the scripts post-await flag flips. That removes any dependence on _process being wired.

Correction to my own earlier report on this thread: I claimed the acceptance test had passed in the prior run. nextest had reported "3/4 tests run" and I inferred which two passed from declaration order, which is not how it numbers them -- it may never have run. What both runs DO establish is that the implementation compiles (exit 100 = test panic, not 101 = compile error), covering gdscene, gdscript-interop and the test target.

comments.text:
FuchsiaDeer, slice-2 findings before implementing (sequencing matters here).

1. MISSING DEPENDENCY EDGE. The approach says to make gdserver2d/gdserver3d thin adapters over gdresource::shader_ast, but NEITHER server crate depends on gdresource today -- they are siblings, both on gdcore+gdvariant only. So item 3/4 starts with adding `gdresource = { path = "../gdresource" }` to gdserver2d/Cargo.toml and gdserver3d/Cargo.toml. I checked this is NOT a cycle: gdresource -> {gdcore, gdvariant, gdobject}, and none of those depend on either server crate. Safe, but it is an unstated prerequisite.

2. ORDERING HAZARD -- do the sampler plumbing BEFORE the routing. My instinct was to route parse_fragment_body/execute_fragment through the AST first and plumb textures after. That is backwards and would REGRESS visible output. execute_fragment receives only (instructions, ctx, uniforms) and FragmentContext carries no texture, so an AST-routed fragment() would evaluate texture(TEXTURE, UV) as transparent black (the no-sampler default I added in slice 1). For outline.gdshader that yields alpha 0 everywhere -- the sprite DISAPPEARS, which is worse than the current unshaded-sprite behaviour. Plumb the sampler through to execute_fragment first, then flip the routing.

3. SUGGESTED SHAPE for the routing, to keep the public signatures the bead requires: add a FragmentInstruction::Program(Arc<ShaderProgram>) variant so parse_fragment_body(source) -> Vec<FragmentInstruction> can carry the whole parsed program, and have execute_fragment match on it. That preserves both signatures so gdrender2d/src/draw.rs:875 keeps compiling, which is what the bead asks for.

4. SAMPLER PLUMBING OPTIONS. Adding `sampler: Option<gdresource::shader_ast::Sampler>` to FragmentContext is the natural home, but note there are ~16 FragmentContext literal sites and only 13 use ..Default::default() -- the other ~3 are full literals that would need editing. The lower-risk alternative is a new execute_fragment_with_sampler(instructions, ctx, uniforms, sampler) with execute_fragment delegating to it with None, leaving the struct and every construction site untouched.

Slice 1 (the Sampler hook in shader_ast) is already on disk and is the prerequisite for all of the above.

comments.text:
FuchsiaDeer, follow-up: a flaw in the Sampler API I shipped in slice 1, found by reading the actual call site (gdrender2d/src/draw.rs:979).

LIFETIME PROBLEM. I typed Sampler as Arc<dyn Fn(&str,[f32;2])->[f32;4] + Send + Sync>, which implies + `static. The renderer call site has `texture: &Texture2D` -- a BORROW -- and everything it needs to sample is already in scope there (canvas_material::sample_texture(texture, u, v, tex_filter, tex_repeat) two lines above). A closure capturing that borrow is not `static, so `Sampler::new(...)` will not accept it as written.

Three ways out, in my order of preference:

(a) Clone the texture into the closure ONCE per draw call, before the pixel loop:
      let tex = texture.clone();
      let sampler = Sampler::new(move |_name, uv| { let c = canvas_material::sample_texture(&tex, uv[0], uv[1], tex_filter, tex_repeat); [c.r, c.g, c.b, c.a] });
    Texture2D is #[derive(Clone)] over a Vec<Color> (gdrender2d/src/texture.rs:10), so this copies the whole pixel buffer -- but once per draw call, not per pixel. Simplest, no API change.

(b) Give Sampler a lifetime parameter and hold a borrowed trait object. Cheapest at runtime, but the lifetime propagates into StageContext and would cost it the Debug/Clone/Default derives that other code relies on.

(c) Have the renderer hand ownership via Arc<Texture2D> instead. Cleanest long-term, but Texture2D is not currently stored behind an Arc anywhere, so it is the largest change.

I would take (a) unless profiling says otherwise -- it is contained to the call site and changes no public type.

ALSO NOTE: Texture2D lives in gdrender2d, NOT gdserver2d. So gdserver2d::execute_fragment can never name the texture type at all; the sampler MUST arrive as a caller-supplied closure from gdrender2d. That confirms the closure shape is right even though its lifetime bound is wrong.

comments.author: bone
comments.text: FuchsiaDeer, correcting my own wording in the previous comment: I called this "a flaw in the Sampler API", which overstates it. Option (a) needs NO API change -- an owning closure (move a cloned Texture2D in) satisfies Send + Sync + `static perfectly well. The constraint is on the CALLER (it must own, not borrow, its texture data), not a defect in the type. Options (b) and (c) are only worth considering if the per-draw-call clone shows up in profiling.

`shader_ast` has 28 refs, not 2. Both renderers route through it: `gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs:440` and
`gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:2261` both call `parse_fragment_body`, which falls through to

The acceptance test EXISTS: `gdeditor/tests/shader_language_frontend_drives_scene_pixels.rs`, with 3
tests covering acceptance clauses 1 and 3.

## THE UNCOVERED CLAUSE IS 2 — "a syntax error yields a ShaderDiagnostic naming the line"

Two independent gaps, both confirmed:

1. `parse_fragment_body_checked` (gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:526) is the reporting variant, and it has
   **ZERO production callers** — its only callers are in `gdserver2d/tests/gdshader_parse_diagnostics.rs`.
   Both render paths use the lossy `parse_fragment_body`, so a broken shader renders unshaded and silent.
2. `validate_shader_source` (gdeditor/src/shader_editor.rs:492) **never runs the AST parse** —
   `grep -c shader_ast crates/gdeditor/src/shader_editor.rs` = **0**. It does a lex pass, a
   `shader_type` presence check, an undefined-function pass and an unused-uniform heuristic. So a
   shader that lexes cleanly, declares `shader_type`, and contains a genuine SYNTAX error validates as
   `ok: true`: the editor says the shader is fine while the renderer silently drops it.

## ⚠️ THE TRAP: DO NOT GATE VALIDATION ON `parse_shader` WITHOUT BOUNDING FALSE POSITIVES

The obvious fix — call `shader_ast::parse_shader` inside `validate_shader_source` and report its
`ShaderError` — is a REGRESSION RISK, because `parse_program` (shader_ast.rs:371) errors on any
top-level construct it does not model. That has already bitten once: the file's own comment at :391-400
records that `ShaderToken::Struct` had no arm, so **a shader declaring any struct failed to parse in its
entirety, taking its `fragment()` body with it**. `render_mode`/`group_uniforms`/`struct` are tolerated
today; anything else added to GDShader is not.

Gating the editor's validator on that parser would report a fabricated syntax error for every valid
shader using an unmodelled construct — turning a silent-failure bug into a false-alarm bug. Whoever
takes this should either (a) make `parse_program` tolerant-by-default for unknown top-level items, then
gate on it, or (b) gate the diagnostic on `parse_fragment_body` ALSO being empty (the
`parse_fragment_body_checked` semantics), which cannot false-positive on a shader that actually renders.
I did not attempt either blind: `semantic_pass_accepts_builtins_constructors_and_user_functions`
(shader_editor.rs:1260) is a live gate that a false positive would flip.

## ALSO: there is no 2D diagnostics channel to surface into

`gdserver2d::CompiledShader` (shader.rs:220) has **no diagnostics field**, unlike
`gdserver3d::CompiledShader3D` which carries `diagnostics: Vec<ShaderDiagnostic>`. And gdserver2d's
`ShaderCompiler` has zero production callers. So "surface a diagnostic from the 2D path" needs a channel
built first — that is the real cost of clause 2, not the parse call.

Note `ShaderDiagnostic` is TWO different types: gdserver3d's (`line`, `severity`, `message`, zero-based)
and gdeditor's (`line`, `col`, `message`, **1-based** — see the `shader_type` case using `line: 1`).
Do not cross them without converting.

## DELIVERED THIS PASS

`parse_shader` discarded the lexer's position: it mapped every `ShaderLexError` into
`ShaderError { line: 0, col: 0 }` even though all three lex variants carry `line`/`col` and their
`Display` prints them. Line 0 is out of range for a 1-based field, so no editor could highlight it.
Fixed with a wildcard-free or-pattern (mirroring `shader_lex_error_pos` in gdeditor), so a future lex
variant fails to compile here rather than silently regressing to 0. Two tests added asserting the real
line for an unexpected character and for an unterminated block comment (which correctly reports the line
it OPENED on, `start_line`, not the end-of-input line).

The same question needs asking of the enclosing functions for emit sites 1193, 1299 and 1324 — I confirmed `font_size` is in scope at the ten `let scale = text_scale(font_size)` bindings, but did NOT confirm that each of those bindings is in the same function as the emit site it feeds. I assumed proximity implied scope. That assumption is what made my estimate too low.

Also note :1000 computes `line_height = (GLYPH_H + GLYPH_GAP) * scale`, so line height is on the same parameter and moves with it.

TRACK RECORD, so this is weighted properly: this is the third estimate of mine on this bead that came in low — "58 sites across the codebase" (actually ~49, one crate), then "~6 edits" (actually 6 plus at least one signature change and its callers). Each was derived from greps plus inference about scope rather than from reading the enclosing functions. Whoever takes this should re-derive the count by reading the four emit sites` enclosing functions top to bottom, not from my numbers.

WHAT IS SOLID and worth keeping from my comments: the atomicity constraint (measurement and hit-testing share tab_spans, so families must convert together); the ordering constraint (family (c) before (a)/(b), else the box/glyph mismatch just moves); that ControlDrawItem::Text.font_size can stay u32; and that no existing test pins font_size, though label_text_layout.rs does pin POSITION and will move when family (b) lands. Slice 1 (measure_text_px / line_height_px + metrics test) is on disk, additive, and currently unwired.

Each ControlDrawItem::Text emit site paired with the `let scale = text_scale(X)` binding that feeds it, derived by walking the file with awk rather than by eyeballing proximity (line numbers post-slice-2a):

  emit 1053  <- binding  987   X = font_size

NINE of twelve bind from a local named `font_size`, so those are one-line edits: `font_size: scale` -> `font_size: font_size.max(1) as u32`. Scope is safe: `scale` is visibly in scope at each emit (the code compiles today), and `font_size` is declared immediately before `scale` in the same block, so it is in scope wherever `scale` is.

THREE inline their expression and bind no local — 1663, 1725, 1808. Hoist first, e.g. `let font_px = crate::control::get_font_size(tree, node_id);` then `let scale = text_scale(font_px);`, then emit `font_px.max(1) as u32`.

  - gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:1378 — same
