title: GLTFDocument/GLTFState: dispatch append_from_* and generate_scene to the real parser
description:
[audit-key: asset-import-pipeline/gltf-runtime-api] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/gltf/gltf_document.cpp + gltf_state.cpp; extension_api.json: GLTFDocument 6 properties / 23 methods, GLTFState 31 properties / 71 methods, FBXDocument/FBXState inherit them — this is the runtime glTF load path scripts use (`GLTFDocument.new().append_from_file(path, state)` → `generate_scene(state)`) | upstream/godot/modules/gltf/gltf_document.cpp (`_parse_accessors` incl. sparse, `_parse_skins`/`_create_skeletons`/`_create_skins`, `_parse_meshes` morph targets + `KHR_mesh_quantization`, `_parse_images` bufferView + `data:` URI decode, `_parse_materials` KHR_materials_{emissive_strength,unlit,specular,ior,clearcoat,transmission,volume}, KHR_texture_transform)

**Godot classes:** GLTFDocument, GLTFState, FBXDocument, FBXState, GLTFDocumentExtension, GLTFAccessor, GLTFSkin, GLTFSkeleton, GLTFMesh, GLTFTexture

**Patina today:**
- [asset-import-pipeline] engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:11071-11122 registers `GLTFDocument` with six properties and 23 method NAMES (append_from_file/append_from_buffer/append_from_scene/generate_scene/generate_buffer/write_to_filesystem/…), class_db.rs:11331 registers `GLTFState`, class_db.rs:11433-11444 registers `FBXDocument`/`FBXState`. Nothing dispatches any of them: `grep -rn 'GLTFDocument|GLTFState|append_from_buffer|generate_scene' crates/gdscript-interop/src crates/gdobject/src crates/gdscene/src --include=*.rs` excluding class_db.rs returns exactly ONE hit, a comment at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation.rs:1726. The registration's own test file admits the gap: engine-rs/crates/gdobject/tests/gltf_runtime_class_family_test.rs:1-8 — "The runtime API itself — constructing them from GDScript, routing `gdresource`'s `gltf_import.rs` parser through `GLTFDocument.append_from_buffer`, and `generate_scene` — is follow-up". So a registered, introspectable, method-listing class family that no script call can ever reach.
- [asset-import-pipeline] engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/gltf_import.rs:14-19 — the module's own "Unsupported (documented)" list: "Morph targets, sparse accessors, Draco/meshopt compression", "Skinned mesh skinning matrices / animation playback", "Image / texture sampling (albedo texture URI is recorded but not decoded)", "Multiple scenes (only default / first scene is imported)". gltf_import.rs:596-610 — `resolve_texture_uri` returns `None` for GLB `bufferView`-backed images, which is how virtually every real `.glb` stores its textures, so material texture maps silently vanish. gltf_import.rs:492-497 — the `unsupported_extensions` list only reports KHR_draco_mesh_compression, KHR_materials_transmission, KHR_materials_volume, KHR_animation_pointer; the other KHR material extensions are neither parsed nor reported. `parse_skins` (gltf_import.rs:1362) and `parse_animations` (gltf_import.rs:1410) exist, and JOINTS_0/WEIGHTS_0 are read (gltf_import.rs:229-239), but no skin binding is produced for the renderer.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/gltf_import.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: the runtime glTF path is `var doc = GLTFDocument.new(); var state = GLTFState.new(); doc.append_from_file(path, state); var node = doc.generate_scene(state)` — `append_from_buffer(bytes, base_path, state, flags)` and `generate_scene(state, bake_fps, trimming, remove_immutable_tracks)` (upstream/godot/modules/gltf/gltf_document.cpp). `GLTFState` then exposes the parsed document (31 properties, 71 methods: nodes, meshes, materials, animations, skins, buffers, json, …). `FBXDocument`/`FBXState` inherit this surface.\n\nPatina current state: the whole family is ClassDB-registered with correct names, parents, properties and method arities — engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:11071-11122 (GLTFDocument), :11331 (GLTFState), :11433-11444 (FBXDocument/FBXState) — but nothing dispatches a single method. `grep -rn 'GLTFDocument|append_from_buffer|generate_scene' crates/gdscript-interop/src crates/gdobject/src crates/gdscene/src --include=*.rs` (excluding class_db.rs) yields one unrelated comment at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation.rs:1726. The registration's own test file states the runtime API is "follow-up" (engine-rs/crates/gdobject/tests/gltf_runtime_class_family_test.rs:1-8). A real, working parser already exists at `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/gltf_import.rs`.\n\nImplementation approach: add a handle-backed `GLTFDocument`/`GLTFState` pair in `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` following the existing ConfigFile handle pattern (interpreter.rs ~20750): `GLTFState` holds the `Arc<Resource>` produced by `gdresource::import_gltf_bytes` plus the source base path; `append_from_buffer(bytes, base_path, state, flags)` and `append_from_file(path, base_path, state, flags)` run the parser and store the result into the state handle; `generate_scene(state, bake_fps, trimming, remove_immutable_tracks)` converts the document into a live node tree via the scene-import path (shared with the glTF→PackedScene bead) and returns the root's ObjectId. Expose the GLTFState getters that the parser can actually answer (json, nodes, meshes, materials, animations, root_nodes, base_path, scene_name) and return an explicit unsupported error for the rest rather than silently returning defaults.\n\nWiring requirement: a `.gd` script executed by the runner must be able to load a `.glb` with GLTFDocument and add the generated node to the tree.

**Merged findings (2):** GLTFDocument / GLTFState runtime scripting API (append_from_file/buffer/scene, generate_scene, generate_buffer, GLTFState accessors); glTF import fidelity: skinning, morph targets, sparse accessors, embedded (bufferView) images, KHR material extensions

**Prove it:** A GDScript snippet that does `var d = GLTFDocument.new(); var s = GLTFState.new(); d.append_from_file("res://cube.glb", s, 0, ""); var n = d.generate_scene(s); add_child(n)` results in a node in the SceneTree whose name and child MeshInstance3D count match the GLB fixture's real contents, and `s.get_meshes().size()` equals the fixture's mesh count. (test: `gltf_document_append_and_generate_scene_from_script`)
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript snippet that does `var d = GLTFDocument.new(); var s = GLTFState.new(); d.append_from_file("res://cube.glb", s, 0, ""); var n = d.generate_scene(s); add_child(n)` results in a node in the SceneTree whose name and child MeshInstance3D count match the GLB fixture's real contents, and `s.get_meshes().size()` equals the fixture's mesh count. (test: `gltf_document_append_and_generate_scene_from_script`)

title: Audio: resolve res:// stream paths against the project root in the runner boot
description:
[audit-key: audio/audio-runtime-wiring] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/io/resource_loader.cpp + ProjectSettings::globalize_path — `res://` always resolves against the project root, never the process CWD | upstream/godot/scene/audio/audio_stream_player_internal.cpp (set_stream stops+reloads; play() always starts a NEW playback and trims to max_polyphony); doc/classes/AudioStreamPlayer.xml (max_polyphony default 1) | extension_api.json AudioStreamPlayer (11 properties / 28 methods), AudioStreamPlayer2D (14/32), AudioStreamPlayer3D (23/44); doc/classes/AudioStreamPlayer*.xml

**Godot classes:** AudioStreamPlayer, AudioStreamPlayer2D, AudioStreamPlayer3D, AudioListener2D, AudioListener3D

**Patina today:**
- [audio] `AudioServerBridge::resolve_stream_path` (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:148-154) strips `res://` and joins `self.base_dir`, falling back to `PathBuf::from(stripped)` (CWD-relative) when `base_dir` is None. `set_base_dir` (same file line 123) is never called by the runner: `grep -rn "set_base_dir" crates/ --include="*.rs"` returns ONLY two call sites, both in a test (crates/gdscene/tests/audio_tscn_stream_resource_plays.rs:120,150). crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs:580-638 (`init_running`) loads the bus layout and attaches the output sink but never sets the bridge's base dir, and patina-runner never chdirs (`grep -rn "set_current_dir" crates/patina-runner/src/` → no hits; main.rs:236-255 has its own separate `resolve_res_path` helper the bridge does not use).
- [audio] crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:405-411 reads the node's `stream` property ONLY as `Variant::String` (or the `__extres__stream` companion). But `load("res://sfx.wav")` in GDScript returns `Variant::Resource(ResourceRef{class_name:"AudioStream"})` — crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:4369-4394 — so `$Player.stream = load(...)` yields an empty path and silence. The stream is also imported only once: audio_server_bridge.rs:467 `if first_sight && !player.has_stream()`, so re-assigning `stream` mid-game (music track swap) never reloads. Finally, `play()` on an already-playing node is a no-op: the interpreter sets `playing = true` (interpreter.rs:9335-9377) and the bridge's branch chain (audio_server_bridge.rs:493-512) only starts a voice when `playing_prop && !voice_alive`, so a rapid-fire SFX retrigger is swallowed. `max_polyphony` appears nowhere: `grep -rn "max_polyphony" crates/ --include="*.rs"` → no hits.
- [audio] crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:10113-10170 registers only stream/volume_db/pitch_scale/autoplay/bus/playing (+ max_distance/attenuation/panning_strength for 2D, + max_distance/unit_size/attenuation_model/max_db/panning_strength for 3D) and only three methods (play/stop/is_playing). Missing everywhere: `stream_paused` (which the bridge nonetheless reads at crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:427), `max_polyphony`, `mix_target`, `playback_type`, `volume_linear`, `area_mask`; missing on 3D: `emission_angle_enabled`, `emission_angle_degrees`, `emission_angle_filter_attenuation_db`, `attenuation_filter_cutoff_hz`, `attenuation_filter_db`, `doppler_tracking`. Missing methods: `seek`, `get_playback_position`, `set_stream_paused`/`get_stream_paused`, `has_stream_playback`/`get_stream_playback`. Separately, `AudioListener2D/3D.make_current()/clear_current()` are registered in ClassDB (class_db.rs:1013-1020, :6441-6449) but the interpreter never dispatches them — `grep -n "make_current" crates/gdscript-interop/src/*.rs` returns no hits, so `$Listener.make_current()` raises UndefinedFunction.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/player.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: every `res://` path resolves against the project directory (the folder holding project.godot), independent of the process working directory (core/io/resource_loader.cpp, ProjectSettings::globalize_path). Launching the game from any cwd loads the same assets.\n\nPATINA: crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:148-154 `resolve_stream_path` joins `self.base_dir` when set and otherwise returns a bare relative path, i.e. CWD-relative. `set_base_dir` (audio_server_bridge.rs:123) has ZERO production callers — `grep -rn "set_base_dir" crates/` matches only crates/gdscene/tests/audio_tscn_stream_resource_plays.rs:120 and :150. crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs:580-638 builds the MainLoop, loads the bus layout from `self.config.project_dir`, and attaches the audio sink, but never passes `project_dir` to the bridge. Result: a project launched from anywhere but its own directory silently loads no audio at all — the stream load fails and only logs `tracing::warn!` (audio_server_bridge.rs:474-478), which the runner does not surface.\n\nAPPROACH: in `EngineBootstrap::init_running` (crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs, right after `MainLoop::new(tree)` at line 586) call `main_loop.audio_bridge_mut().set_base_dir(self.config.project_dir.clone())`. Also make the bridge fall back to the same ancestor-walk `resolve_res_path` uses in crates/patina-runner/src/main.rs:236-255 so loose-file layouts still work, and promote the stream-load failure from `warn!` to a runner-visible error line.\n\nWIRING: boot -> bridge.base_dir set -> `sync_player_node` first-sight import -> `AudioStreamLoader::load_buffer(project_dir/sfx/beep.wav)` -> non-silent mix on the first frame.

**Merged findings (3):** res:// audio stream path resolution in the runner; Runtime `stream` assignment, retrigger, and max_polyphony on AudioStreamPlayer*; ClassDB surface for AudioStreamPlayer*/AudioListener* (properties + methods)

**Prove it:** Booting a project whose scene has an autoplaying `AudioStreamPlayer` with `stream = "res://sfx/beep.wav"` from a working directory OUTSIDE the project directory produces a non-silent mix within the first few frames (bridge `last_mix()` has samples above the noise floor); the same boot with a missing file logs a visible error rather than silence. (test: `audio_res_path_resolves_from_project`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p patina-runner --test audio_res_path_resolves_from_project`.
acceptance_criteria: Booting a project whose scene has an autoplaying `AudioStreamPlayer` with `stream = "res://sfx/beep.wav"` from a working directory OUTSIDE the project directory produces a non-silent mix within the first few frames (bridge `last_mix()` has samples above the noise floor); the same boot with a missing file logs a visible error rather than silence. (test: `audio_res_path_resolves_from_project`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p patina-runner --test audio_res_path_resolves_from_project`.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/image_svg.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: each `ResourceImporter` declares its options in `_get_import_options` and the chosen values are persisted per-asset in the `.import` file's `[params]` section; the importer then applies them when producing the artifact (upstream/godot/editor/import/resource_importer_texture.cpp — 26 options; resource_importer_wav.cpp — 10; resource_importer_svg.cpp — 4). Project-wide defaults live in ProjectSettings under `importer_defaults/<importer_name>`.\n\nPatina current state: `.import` `[params]` IS parsed but immediately orphaned — `ImportFile::other_sections` (engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs:641-649, populated at importers.rs:712-719) has zero readers outside its own module (verified by `grep -rn other_sections crates/ apps/ --include=*.rs`). The values are raw strings, so even a reader could not distinguish `true` from `\"true\"` from `1`. `import_svg` hardcodes `1.0` (engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/image_svg.rs:114-121); `import_wav` (importers.rs:487-548) ignores every loop/trim/normalize/force option; `import_image` (importers.rs:44-52) ignores size limit, mipmaps and alpha processing. `importer_defaults/*` does not exist anywhere.\n\nImplementation approach: in `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs`, add `ImportParams` that parses `[params]` values into `Variant` via the existing `gdresource::loader::parse_variant_value`, and expose `ImportFile::params()`. Give each importer entry point an `_with_params` variant: `import_image_with_params` (apply `process/size_limit` by downscaling, `mipmaps/generate`, `process/premult_alpha`, `process/fix_alpha_border`, `process/normal_map_invert_y`, `process/channel_remap/*`), `import_wav_with_params` (apply `force/mono`, `force/8_bit`, `force/max_rate_hz`, `edit/trim`, `edit/normalize`, and store `edit/loop_mode`/`loop_begin`/`loop_end` onto the AudioStreamWAV resource so `gdaudio::stream` honors them), `import_svg_with_params` (`svg/scale`, `base_scale`, `saturation`). Have `ResourceFormatLoader::load_resource` look for `<source>.import` and pass the parsed params through. Add `importer_defaults/<name>/<option>` lookup in `gdresource::project` as the fallback.\n\nWiring requirement: a loose source file plus a sibling `.import` with non-default `[params]` must load DIFFERENTLY through `UnifiedLoader::load` than the same file with default params — end-to-end, no direct call into the option struct.

**Prove it:** Loading `res://icon.svg` through `UnifiedLoader` with a sibling `icon.svg.import` containing `[params] svg/scale=2.0` yields a Texture2D with 4x the pixel count of the same file with `svg/scale=1.0`; loading `res://tone.wav` with `[params] force/mono=true` on a stereo source yields `channels=1`; loading `res://big.png` with `[params] process/size_limit=16` on a 64x64 source yields `width==16`. (test: `import_params_change_loaded_resource`)
acceptance_criteria: Loading `res://icon.svg` through `UnifiedLoader` with a sibling `icon.svg.import` containing `[params] svg/scale=2.0` yields a Texture2D with 4x the pixel count of the same file with `svg/scale=1.0`; loading `res://tone.wav` with `[params] force/mono=true` on a stereo source yields `channels=1`; loading `res://big.png` with `[params] process/size_limit=16` on a 64x64 source yields `width==16`. (test: `import_params_change_loaded_resource`)

title: Resource loaders: compile the orphaned import modules and register jpg/tga/bmp/hdr/ogg/obj/gltf
description:
[audit-key: asset-import-pipeline/loader-registry-extensions] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/io/image_loader.cpp + modules/{jpg,tga,bmp,hdr,svg,webp}/ register loaders for every source image format; editor/import/resource_importer_texture.cpp accepts bmp/dds/exr/hdr/jpg/jpeg/png/svg/tga/webp; modules/{minimp3,vorbis} for audio; modules/gltf/ for .gltf/.glb | extension_api.json ResourceFormatLoader (11: _get_recognized_extensions, _recognize_path, _handles_type, _get_resource_type, _get_resource_script_class, _get_resource_uid, _get_dependencies, _rename_dependencies, _exists, _get_classes_used, _load), ResourceFormatSaver (5), ImageFormatLoaderExtension (2); upstream/godot/core/io/resource_loader.cpp ResourceLoader::_load which walks the registered loaders.

**Godot classes:** ResourceFormatLoader, Image, ImageTexture, ResourceImporterTexture, ResourceImporterOBJ, ResourceFormatSaver, ImageFormatLoaderExtension, ResourceLoader, ResourceSaver

**Patina today:**
- [asset-import-pipeline] `ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults` registers exactly 14 extensions — .png .webp .svg .ctex .wav .ttf .otf .tres .tscn .res .scn .vs .gdshader .gdshaderinc (engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs:755-771). Missing: .jpg/.jpeg/.tga/.bmp/.hdr/.exr/.ogg/.mp3/.gltf/.glb/.obj/.fbx/.csv/.glsl/.dds/.ktx. A unit test even pins the gap: `assert!(!rfl.can_load(".jpg"))` (importers.rs:1413). The decoders exist but are unreachable: (a) `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/texture_import.rs` (785 lines, hand-rolled PNG+JPEG decoder) and `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/audio_import.rs` (401 lines, WAV+OGG→Resource) are ORPHANED MODULES — neither appears in the `pub mod` list at engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/lib.rs:23-50 and `grep -rn 'mod texture_import|mod audio_import' crates/` returns nothing, so rustc has never compiled them; this is independently documented at engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/portable_compressed_texture.rs:237-242 ("25 KB never declared in lib.rs, so the compiler has never seen it"). (b) `image_tga_bmp::decode_bmp`/`decode_tga` (engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/image_tga_bmp.rs:33,83) and `radiance_hdr::decode_hdr` (radiance_hdr.rs:121) compile but have ZERO consumers. (c) `gdserver3d::mesh::Mesh3D::from_obj` (engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs:713) has no callers outside its own module. The editor's own doc comment claims otherwise: engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/texture_cache.rs:107-114 says "This is what makes `.webp`, `.svg`, `.jpg` and `.ctex` render in the editor viewport".
- [engine-virtual-method-table] All 18 virtuals ARE declared — engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:10707-10714 (ImageFormatLoaderExtension), :10731-10746 (ResourceFormatLoader), :10748-10758 (ResourceFormatSaver) — and the file's own comment at class_db.rs:10725-10730 states the gap outright: "⚠️ SCOPE: this registers the class surface so `extends ResourceFormatLoader` resolves. The runtime *dispatch* — `ResourceLoader.add_resource_format_loader` plus a `load()` that invokes a script subclass's `_load` — is a separate, larger gdscript-interop feature (no ResourceLoader singleton/registry exists in the interpreter yet) and is NOT wired here." Grepping `"_load"`, `"_save"`, `"_recognize_path"`, `"_get_recognized_extensions"` over engine-rs/crates/ (tests excluded) returns class_db.rs only.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/lib.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/texture_import.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/audio_import.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/image_tga_bmp.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/radiance_hdr.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/loader.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: every source asset extension Godot's importers accept (bmp, dds, exr, hdr, jpg, jpeg, png, svg, tga, webp for textures; wav, ogg, mp3 for audio; gltf, glb, obj, fbx for scenes) resolves through a registered loader, so `load()`/the editor/the renderer all agree (upstream/godot/core/io/image_loader.cpp, modules/{jpg,tga,bmp,hdr,minimp3,vorbis,gltf}).\n\nPatina current state: `ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults` (engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs:755-771) registers 14 extensions and none of jpg/jpeg/tga/bmp/hdr/exr/ogg/mp3/gltf/glb/obj; a test asserts the JPEG gap (importers.rs:1413). Real decoders sit unreachable: `texture_import.rs` (785 lines incl. a JPEG decoder) and `audio_import.rs` (401 lines) are NOT declared in engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/lib.rs:23-50, so they are dead files rustc never compiles — confirmed in prose at engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/portable_compressed_texture.rs:237-242. `image_tga_bmp::decode_bmp`/`decode_tga` (image_tga_bmp.rs:33,83), `radiance_hdr::decode_hdr` (radiance_hdr.rs:121) and `gdserver3d::mesh::Mesh3D::from_obj` (engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs:713) compile with zero consumers.\n\nImplementation approach: (1) add `pub mod texture_import;` and `pub mod audio_import;` to engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/lib.rs and fix whatever fallout compiling them produces (they were written against an older `Resource` API). (2) In `with_defaults`, register `.jpg`/`.jpeg` → the JPEG path, `.tga`/`.bmp` → thin wrappers over `image_tga_bmp::decode_tga/decode_bmp` producing the same pixel-bearing Texture2D shape as `import_image_bytes`, `.hdr` → `radiance_hdr::decode_hdr`, `.ogg`/`.mp3` → an `AudioStream*` Resource built from `gdaudio::decode`, `.gltf`/`.glb` → `gltf_import::import_gltf`, `.obj` → a wrapper over `Mesh3D::from_obj`. (3) Delete the `assert!(!rfl.can_load(\".jpg\"))` assertion and replace it with positive coverage. (4) Correct the stale doc at engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/texture_cache.rs:107-114.\n\nWiring requirement: every added extension must load through `UnifiedLoader::load(\"res://…\")` (the path the editor texture cache and — once its own bead lands — the interpreter take), not just through a direct module call.

**Merged findings (2):** ResourceFormatLoader extension coverage: .jpg/.jpeg/.tga/.bmp/.hdr/.exr/.ogg/.mp3/.gltf/.glb/.obj + orphaned decoder modules; ResourceFormatLoader / ResourceFormatSaver / ImageFormatLoaderExtension virtuals registered but never dispatched

**Prove it:** For a temp project containing real `a.jpg`, `b.tga`, `c.bmp`, `d.hdr`, `e.ogg` and `f.obj` fixtures, `UnifiedLoader::load` returns for each a Resource of the right class with real data (images: correct `width`/`height` and a `pixels` array of exactly w*h entries; ogg: non-zero `length_seconds`; obj: a Mesh with the fixture's real vertex count), and `ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults().can_load(".jpg")` is true. (test: `format_loader_covers_source_asset_extensions`)
acceptance_criteria: For a temp project containing real `a.jpg`, `b.tga`, `c.bmp`, `d.hdr`, `e.ogg` and `f.obj` fixtures, `UnifiedLoader::load` returns for each a Resource of the right class with real data (images: correct `width`/`height` and a `pixels` array of exactly w*h entries; ogg: non-zero `length_seconds`; obj: a Mesh with the fixture's real vertex count), and `ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults().can_load(".jpg")` is true. (test: `format_loader_covers_source_asset_extensions`)

description:

title: Audio3D: match Godot's attenuation math and wire emission cone, distance lowpass, and doppler
description:
[audit-key: audio/audio-spatial-3d] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/audio_stream_player_3d.cpp:232-259 (_get_attenuation_db) and :444-465 (max_distance rolloff, attenuation_filter highshelf, emission cone)

**Godot classes:** AudioStreamPlayer3D, AudioListener3D

**Patina today:**
- [audio] Formula mismatch: Godot's inverse-distance gain is `linear_to_db(1/((d/unit)+CMP_EPSILON))` and inverse-square is `1/((d/unit)^2+eps)`, logarithmic is `-20*ln(d/unit+eps)` (upstream audio_stream_player_3d.cpp:235-247). Patina uses entirely different curves: `unit/(unit+d)`, `u^2/(u^2+d^2)`, `1/(1+log2(1+d/unit))` (crates/gdaudio/src/spatial.rs:181-198). Godot additionally multiplies by `max(0, 1 - d/max_distance)` when max_distance>0 (upstream :445-447); Patina hard-cuts to 0 past max_distance (spatial.rs:176-179). The cone/filter/doppler fields are declared but dead: `emission_angle_degrees`, `emission_angle_filter_attenuation_db`, `emission_angle_enabled`, `attenuation_filter_cutoff_hz`, `attenuation_filter_db`, `doppler_tracking` (crates/gdaudio/src/spatial.rs:79-97) are never read by `compute_spatial` (spatial.rs:204-231), and `grep -rn "doppler_pitch_scale\|emission_angle\|attenuation_filter" crates/ --include="*.rs" | grep -v spatial.rs` returns ZERO hits. The scene bridge's `read_spatial_3d` (crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:319-346) mirrors only volume_db/unit_size/max_distance/max_db/panning_strength/attenuation_model.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/spatial.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT (scene/3d/audio_stream_player_3d.cpp): `_get_attenuation_db(d)` returns `linear_to_db(1/((d/unit_size)+CMP_EPSILON))` for INVERSE_DISTANCE, `linear_to_db(1/((d/unit_size)^2+eps))` for INVERSE_SQUARE, `-20*ln(d/unit_size+eps)` for LOGARITHMIC, 0 for DISABLED; it then adds `volume_db` and clamps at `max_db`. `_update_panning` (:444-465) multiplies by `max(0, 1 - d/max_distance)` when max_distance>0, derives `db_att = (1-min(1,multiplier)) * attenuation_filter_db`, subtracts `emission_angle_filter_attenuation_db` when the listener is outside the emission cone, and feeds the result to `set_playback_highshelf_params(linear_attenuation, attenuation_filter_cutoff_hz)`. `doppler_tracking` shifts pitch from relative velocity.\n\nPATINA: crates/gdaudio/src/spatial.rs:181-198 implements three DIFFERENT curves (`unit/(unit+d)`, `u^2/(u^2+d^2)`, `1/(1+log2(1+d/unit))`) and hard-cuts at max_distance (:176-179) instead of the linear rolloff. `emission_angle_*`, `attenuation_filter_*`, `doppler_tracking` are struct fields (spatial.rs:79-97) that `compute_spatial` (:204-231) never reads, and `doppler_pitch_scale` (spatial.rs:339) has no callers anywhere. The bridge's `read_spatial_3d` (crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:319-346) never mirrors them, and crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:10148-10170 does not register them as properties.\n\nAPPROACH: (1) rewrite `compute_attenuation` in crates/gdaudio/src/spatial.rs to Godot's dB formulas, add the `max(0, 1 - d/max_distance)` factor, and clamp `att + volume_db` at `max_db`; (2) implement the emission-cone test against the source's -Z basis column and the high-shelf filter (reuse crates/gdaudio/src/biquad.rs) applied per-voice; (3) add a per-voice high-shelf slot on the server voice (crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs `stream_mut`) so `SpatialAudioResult` can carry `(highshelf_gain, cutoff_hz)`; (4) implement doppler by tracking the previous frame's source and listener global positions in the bridge and calling `doppler_pitch_scale`, gated on `doppler_tracking` (idle vs physics step); (5) extend `read_spatial_3d` to mirror all six properties and register them on `AudioStreamPlayer3D` in crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs.\n\nWIRING: Node3D global transform each frame -> read_spatial_3d -> compute_spatial -> voice gain/pan/high-shelf/pitch -> mixed output.

**Prove it:** For a source at distance d with unit_size u, the mixed gain matches Godot's `db_to_linear(linear_to_db(1/(d/u)) )` within 1e-3 for all three attenuation models; a listener placed outside a 30-degree emission cone hears the source attenuated by `emission_angle_filter_attenuation_db` relative to on-axis; a source moving toward the listener with `doppler_tracking` enabled raises the mixed playback rate. (test: `audio3d_attenuation_cone_doppler`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test audio3d_attenuation_cone_doppler`.
acceptance_criteria: For a source at distance d with unit_size u, the mixed gain matches Godot's `db_to_linear(linear_to_db(1/(d/u)) )` within 1e-3 for all three attenuation models; a listener placed outside a 30-degree emission cone hears the source attenuated by `emission_angle_filter_attenuation_db` relative to on-axis; a source moving toward the listener with `doppler_tracking` enabled raises the mixed playback rate. (test: `audio3d_attenuation_cone_doppler`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test audio3d_attenuation_cone_doppler`.

BronzeLake: diagnosis after three verify rounds. The cone clause of the acceptance CANNOT pass as written. Read this before touching the test.

WHAT NOW PASSES (verifier log, run 3): all three attenuation models. Getting there took two fixes, both mine:
1. `peak(&mix)` is NOT the gain. Panning is equal-power (compute_spatial uses angle.cos()/angle.sin()), so a centred source puts gain/sqrt(2) in EACH channel. Use sqrt(L^2+R^2), valid at any pan since cos^2+sin^2==1. The tell was the ratio 0.176776/0.25 = 0.70711 exactly.
2. Godot's LOGARITHMIC attenuation is `-20 * Math::log(d/u)` and Math::log is the NATURAL log (scene/3d/audio_stream_player_3d.cpp:243). Not log10. At d/u=4 that is -27.7 dB, not -12.0 dB. Expected values now: 0.250000 / 0.062500 / 0.041087, the last matching the engine to six decimals.

WHAT STILL FAILS, and why it is not a test bug: `on 1.412538 vs off 1.412538`. Two facts.

(a) 1.412538 = 10^(3/20) exactly — both runs are pinned at max_db, whose Godot default is 3.0 dB. With unit_size 100 and distance 10 the raw gain is +20 dB, so the clamp flattens everything. Any cone fixture must keep the pre-clamp gain below max_db or set max_db high.

(b) THE REAL ISSUE: the cone is not a gain cut. compute_spatial does
      let highshelf_db = distance_filter_db + self.emission_cone_db(to_source);
    so emission_cone_db feeds the HIGH-SHELF, never volume_linear. That is CORRECT Godot behaviour - `emission_angle_filter_attenuation_db` is a filter attenuation, an HF rolloff, not a broadband cut. And apply_spatial (audio_server_bridge.rs) consumes only volume_linear and the pan pair, so highshelf_db is computed and then dropped on the floor.

    Net: the cone currently has ZERO audible effect, and no amplitude-based assertion can ever detect it. Worse, a DC or constant test signal has no high-frequency content, so even once the filter IS applied, a peak/energy comparison would barely move. A future test needs broadband content (noise or a high-frequency tone) to see an HF rolloff at all.

    The cone properties themselves ARE wired: read_spatial_3d reads emission_angle_enabled / _degrees / _filter_attenuation_db at audio_server_bridge.rs:513-523. So this is purely the missing filter application.

ALSO WRONG IN MY FIXTURE, fix it while you are there: the source's forward defaults to -Z, so a source at (0,0,-10) with the listener at the origin has the listener 180 degrees BEHIND it. My "on-axis" run was fully off-axis; both runs were outside the cone, which is the other reason they matched. Set the source's rotation/forward explicitly, or place the listener along the source's actual forward axis.

SUGGESTED NEXT STEP, pick one: (i) apply highshelf_db to the voice - needs a per-voice filter slot on the playback stream, and then assert the cone with broadband content; or (ii) assert the cone where it is observable today, on SpatialAudioResult.highshelf_db (needs a small bridge accessor), and move "hears the source attenuated" to remaining scope until the filter lands. (i) is what the bead actually asks for.

NOT AT FAULT: the Doppler wiring in apply_spatial. It has never executed - fail-fast cancels after the attenuation/cone assertions, which run first - so its correctness is still unknown, not disproven. Consider running with --no-fail-fast once to get all the signal in one round.

The cone/filter/doppler properties are not registered on AudioStreamPlayer3D in gdobject/src/class_db.rs. read_spatial_3d reads them off the node so authored scenes work, but they are missing from reflection and the inspector. doppler_tracking should be registered as an enum-typed int with DISABLED 0 / IDLE_STEP 1 / PHYSICS_STEP 2.
DopplerTracking::PhysicsStep is not distinguished from IdleStep. Both enable tracking, but Godot samples velocity on a different step for each, so a physics-driven source reads its velocity one frame out of phase. The mapping is in place; the two-clock behaviour is not.
The 2D spatial path (compute_spatial_2d) has no filter or Doppler equivalent and has not been checked against audio_stream_player_2d.cpp.
PATTERN worth a sweep: this bead has now produced THREE registered-but-inert properties at different layers - the cone was computed and dropped by the mixer, doppler_tracking was never read from the node at all, and the filter fields before that were struct fields nothing wrote. When auditing a subsystem, grep each declared property for a WRITE from the scene side and a READ on the consumer side separately; either half missing makes the feature silently inert while looking fully wired.

title: Audio: carry loop_mode/loop_begin/loop_end from stream resources into playback
description:
[audit-key: audio/audio-stream-loop] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/audio_stream_wav.cpp (loop_mode LOOP_DISABLED/FORWARD/PINGPONG/BACKWARD + loop_begin/loop_end), modules/vorbis/audio_stream_ogg_vorbis.cpp (`loop`, `loop_offset`), modules/minimp3/audio_stream_mp3.cpp (`loop`, `loop_offset`) | upstream/godot/modules/minimp3/audio_stream_mp3.cpp + resource_importer_mp3.cpp — .mp3 is a first-class importable stream on every export target including web | upstream/godot/scene/resources/audio_stream_wav.cpp — FORMAT_8_BITS / FORMAT_16_BITS / FORMAT_IMA_ADPCM / FORMAT_QOA; upstream/godot/modules/interactive_music + thirdparty/misc/qoa.h | extension_api.json: AudioStreamWAV : AudioStream, AudioStreamMP3 : AudioStream, AudioStreamGenerator : AudioStream, AudioStreamPolyphonic : AudioStream; upstream/godot/doc/classes/AudioStreamWAV.xml (data, format, loop_mode, loop_begin/end, mix_rate, stereo, save_to_wav)

**Godot classes:** AudioStreamWAV, AudioStreamOggVorbis, AudioStreamMP3, AudioStreamGenerator, AudioStreamPolyphonic

**Patina today:**
- [audio] The loop engine is implemented and unit-tested — crates/gdaudio/src/stream.rs:19-35 (LoopMode None/Forward/PingPong/Backward), :135-220 (advance with ping-pong reflection and loop window), and the mixer honours it (crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs:420-455 direction/window read cursor). But `set_loop_mode` / `set_loop_begin` / `set_loop_end` have no caller outside gdaudio: `grep -rn "set_loop_mode\|set_loop_begin\|set_loop_end" crates/gdscene/src crates/gdresource/src crates/patina-runner/src` → zero hits for the audio types (all matches are `gdscene/src/animation*.rs`, a different LoopMode). The scene bridge never touches loop state (crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:389-547) and the WAV importer records no loop fields (crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs:536-546 sets only sample_rate/channels/bit_depth/audio_format/length_seconds). The 'green' test crates/gdaudio/tests/audio_stream_formats_loop_mp3.rs:26-52 drives `AudioStreamPlayback` directly, proving module math, not wiring.
- [audio] `decode_mp3` and `is_mp3` are implemented and tested (crates/gdaudio/src/decode.rs:263-300, crates/gdaudio/tests/audio_stream_formats_loop_mp3.rs, crates/gdaudio/tests/mp3_decode_test.rs) but the loader the scene bridge actually uses cannot reach them: `AudioFormat` has exactly two variants, Wav and OggVorbis (crates/gdaudio/src/import.rs:44-51), `from_extension` matches only "wav"/"ogg" (:55-61), `from_header` only RIFF/OggS (:64-74), and `decode_audio_data` dispatches only those two (:233-238). `AudioServerBridge::sync_player_node` calls `self.importer.load_buffer(&path)` (crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:472), so an `.mp3` stream returns `ImportError::UnsupportedFormat` and the player is silent. crates/gdresource/src/audio_import.rs:55-56,127-136 has the same two-format table. On wasm the decoder is not even compiled: crates/gdaudio/Cargo.toml:28-31 gates `minimp3` to `cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))`.
- [audio] crates/gdaudio/src/ima_adpcm.rs is a complete, tested IMA-ADPCM decoder whose ONLY reference in the workspace is the `pub mod ima_adpcm;` line at crates/gdaudio/src/lib.rs:10 — `grep -rn "ima_adpcm" crates/ --include="*.rs"` returns exactly that one hit outside the file itself. Its own header (ima_adpcm.rs:19-27) admits 'Wiring this decoder into wav.rs's format dispatch is also left to the owner of that (contended) file'. crates/gdaudio/src/wav.rs:137-141 still rejects anything but audio_format 1 and 3, so format tag 0x11 returns `WavError::UnsupportedFormat`. QOA is absent entirely: `grep -rin "qoa" crates/` → no hits.
- [sweep-0] register_audio_classes registers the PLAYBACK halves but not the resources: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:10061 AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback, :10077 AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic, :10089 AudioStreamPlaybackInteractive, :10099 AudioStreamPlaybackPlaylist, :10104 AudioStreamPlaybackSynchronized — and on the resource side only AudioStream (:10186), OggPacketSequence, OggPacketSequencePlayback and AudioStreamOggVorbis (:10233). Decoders exist: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/wav.rs (decode_wav/parse_wav_header), /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/decode.rs (decode_mp3, is_mp3, AudioStreamGenerator, PolyphonicPlayer) — all re-exported at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/lib.rs:25-27. The importer already stamps the Godot class name: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/audio_import.rs:55 `AudioFormat::Wav => "AudioStreamWAV"` and /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs:536 `Resource::new("AudioStreamWAV")`, and .tscn fixtures reference `[ext_resource type="AudioStreamWAV"]` (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:4104). Absence grep: `rg -n 'ClassRegistration::new("AudioStream' engine-rs/crates` returns no WAV/MP3/Generator/Polyphonic entry; `rg -n 'AudioStreamMP3' engine-rs/crates` -> only inspector_schema_generated.rs:4307.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/import.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/stream.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/decode.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/audio_import.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/Cargo.toml, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/ima_adpcm.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/wav.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: `AudioStreamWAV` exposes `loop_mode` (Disabled/Forward/PingPong/Backward) plus `loop_begin`/`loop_end` in FRAMES (scene/resources/audio_stream_wav.cpp); `AudioStreamOggVorbis` and `AudioStreamMP3` expose `loop` + `loop_offset` (seconds). The importer writes these from the .import preset and the playback honours them, so background music authored as looping keeps playing forever.\n\nPATINA: the runtime half is complete and tested — crates/gdaudio/src/stream.rs:19-35 and :135-220 implement all four loop modes with a `[loop_begin, loop_end]` window and the mixer's read cursor respects direction and window (crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs:420-455). Nothing ever calls `set_loop_mode`/`set_loop_begin`/`set_loop_end` from a scene or resource: those setters have no callers outside gdaudio. `AudioStreamImport`/`AudioStreamInfo` (crates/gdaudio/src/import.rs:80-107) carries no loop metadata, the WAV `smpl` chunk is never parsed (crates/gdaudio/src/wav.rs:90-133 reads only the fmt chunk), and crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs:536-546 stores no loop fields on the `AudioStreamWAV` resource. Consequence: every looping music track plays once and stops.\n\nAPPROACH: (1) parse the WAV `smpl` chunk in crates/gdaudio/src/wav.rs and add `loop_mode`/`loop_begin`/`loop_end` to `WavHeader`; (2) extend `AudioStreamInfo`/`AudioStreamImport` (crates/gdaudio/src/import.rs:80-107) with loop metadata and populate it for WAV and Ogg (Vorbis comment `LOOPSTART`/`LOOPLENGTH` plus the resource's `loop`/`loop_offset`); (3) in `AudioServerBridge::sync_player_node` (crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:458-481) push that metadata plus any node/resource-level override onto the voice via `self.server.stream_mut(pid)`; (4) resolve loop props off the `.tres`/`__extres__` companion so `[sub_resource type="AudioStreamWAV"] loop_mode = 1` in a .tscn takes effect.\n\nWIRING: .tscn/.wav on disk -> importer metadata -> bridge -> AudioStreamPlayback::set_loop_mode -> mixer read cursor wraps -> audio still non-silent past the stream's nominal length.

**Merged findings (4):** Stream loop modes / loop points from the authored resource; MP3 playback from a scene (AudioStreamMP3); WAV IMA-ADPCM and QOA sample formats; AudioStream resource classes with existing decoders (WAV / MP3 / Generator / Polyphonic) unregistered while their *Playback companions are registered

**Prove it:** A scene loading a 0.2 s WAV whose resource declares forward looping, stepped for 1.0 s of simulated time, still produces a non-silent mix at t=0.9 s and reports `playback_position` inside the loop window; the same scene with looping disabled goes silent after 0.2 s and emits `finished` exactly once. (test: `audio_stream_loop_from_resource`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test audio_stream_loop_from_resource`.
acceptance_criteria: A scene loading a 0.2 s WAV whose resource declares forward looping, stepped for 1.0 s of simulated time, still produces a non-silent mix at t=0.9 s and reports `playback_position` inside the loop window; the same scene with looping disabled goes silent after 0.2 s and emits `finished` exactly once. (test: `audio_stream_loop_from_resource`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test audio_stream_loop_from_resource`.

## Measured: deriving property accessors from naming convention does NOT work (51.7%)

Follow-up to my status comment. `class_get_property_getter` / `class_get_property_setter` are two of the three remaining ClassDB methods, and both are blocked on `PropertyInfo` having no accessor fields — a `class_db.rs` change, still leased.

Before accepting that, I checked whether they could be answered **without** the struct change, from the interpreter alone: derive `get_<prop>` / `is_<prop>` / `has_<prop>` and `set_<prop>`, and return it only if that method is actually registered on the class. That would have been checkable rather than invented, and needed no leased file.

**It does not hold up.** Godot's own doc XML carries exact `getter=` / `setter=` attributes on every `<member>`, so the convention is directly measurable across all 5371 documented properties:

```
getter matches get_/is_/has_ convention:  2777 / 5371  (51.7%)
setter matches set_ convention:           4483 / 5371  (83.5%)
```

**A derived getter would be wrong for nearly half of all properties.** The mismatches are not exotic — many properties share one accessor pair covering several members:

| class | member | real getter |
|---|---|---|
| PhysicsBody3D | `axis_lock_angular_x` (and 5 siblings) | `get_axis_lock` |
| SpriteBase3D | `alpha_antialiasing_mode` | `get_alpha_antialiasing` |
| SpriteBase3D | `alpha_cut` | `get_alpha_cut_mode` |

Six `axis_lock_*` members all map to a single `get_axis_lock`, so no per-name rule can recover them.

Shipping that heuristic would produce a confidently wrong answer for half the API, and this codebase's own rule is that a wrong registration is worse than a missing one — `class_exists` still answers true, so the caller has no way to tell. **Declining it is the correct outcome, and it is now measured rather than assumed.**

### What this means for the remaining work
The accessor names must be STORED, not derived. The doc XML is the natural source (it has them exactly), so whoever unblocks `class_db.rs` should add `getter`/`setter` to `PropertyInfo` and populate from `doc/classes/*.xml` rather than by hand or by rule. That is a generated-table job, not a heuristic.

comments.text:
## Merged finding 7: method flags populated (EmeraldIsland)

### ⚠️ I repeated a stale claim in my own remaining_scope an hour ago
My last payload said "MethodInfo has no flags field". **It does** — `is_virtual`, `is_static`, `is_const`, `is_vararg`, `arguments`, `returns`, and a `godot_flags()` that maps to Godot's exact bit values; `class_get_method_list` already emits the key. I took that line from the bead description instead of re-measuring, which is the same trap I had just finished documenting for everyone else. Measuring first would have cost one grep.

**The real gap was POPULATION, not structure:** of 1901 registered methods only 48 carried `.virtual_method()`, 39 `.const_method()`, 1 `.vararg_method()`, and **zero** were marked static. A caller could read `flags` and learn nothing — the editor's Override-Virtual-Method dialog, which upstream builds by filtering this list on `METHOD_FLAG_VIRTUAL`, would have shown an empty list for `Node`.

### Delivered
**786 methods flagged**, generated from the `qualifiers=` attribute on `<method>` in `upstream/godot/doc/classes/*.xml`:

| flag | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `virtual_method()` | 48 | **317** |
| `const_method()` | 39 | **706** |
| `static_method()` | **0** | **19** |
| `vararg_method()` | 1 | 6 |

317 is exactly the number of virtual-qualified methods the XML has for classes Patina registers — the before/after arithmetic (48 + 269 added) lands on the independent count, which is the cross-check that the transformation neither missed nor invented any.

The pass is **chain-aware**: it walks the existing builder chain after each `MethodInfo::new(...)` and skips a flag already present, so the 69 sites that were already correct were left untouched rather than double-appended.

⚠️ Flags come from the documented qualifiers, never from name shape. `Tween.interpolate_value` carries no underscore and IS static; `Object.get_class` carries no underscore and is `const`, not virtual. A leading-underscore rule gets both wrong — which is why static sat at zero.

### Test
`crates/gdscene/tests/classdb_method_list_reports_godot_flags.rs`, using the **existing** scene-probe harness from `classdb_method_list_reports_return_type.rs` rather than the ad-hoc one I first wrote — same layer, proven to iterate `class_get_method_list` from GDScript.

It asserts both halves: `_ready` IS virtual and `add_child` is NOT. Asserting only the first would pass against an implementation that flagged everything, which is exactly as useless to the dialog as flagging nothing. The virtual count is a lower bound, not an exact number, so adding a virtual later does not break it.

comments.author: MagentaBrook
comments.text:
MagentaBrook - CORRECTION to this bead's remaining scope, item (ii). No code change; this unblocks work that is currently being deferred for a reason that no longer holds.

THE STALE PREMISE: 'Resource and 8 other multiply-registered classes are excluded because run order decides which of several guarded registrations wins - that duplication should be collapsed first.' I repeated a version of this in my pat-s3rrv.71 report. It is obsolete.

WHAT I CHECKED. Surveying all 740 registration sites in class_db.rs, 13 classes are registered more than once (RefCounted x13, Resource x10, SpriteFrames x2, Viewport/Window x2, ...). Resource looked like a live bug: ONE of its ten registrations carries the three real members (resource_local_to_scene, resource_name, resource_path) and the other nine carry none - and the property-less one in register_viewport_classes executes FIRST.

Then I read Registry::register() before claiming anything. It MERGES rather than overwrites:
  - members union BY NAME, first registration winning (deliberately: get_property_list concatenates the chain without deduping, so appending would surface a doubled inspector row);
  - a real parent is never clobbered by an empty one;
  - is_abstract is sticky-true.

Its own doc says merging was introduced precisely to remove 'the ordering hazard behind 86 classes carry zero properties'. And the Resource block carries a comment saying it is DELIBERATELY UNGUARDED for exactly this reason - a class_exists guard there would reintroduce the race.

So Resource does get its three properties. No defect, and multiple registrations are additive by design.

THE DISTINCTION THAT ACTUALLY MATTERS is guarded vs unguarded, not duplicated vs not:
  - UNGUARDED duplicates MERGE - additive, idempotent, order-independent. Metadata added in a later pass lands.
  - GUARDED (if !class_exists(..)) duplicates skip the later block entirely, so an EDIT landing in a skipped block is silently inert. That is the real trap, and it is the one that made me skip Slider during the signal pass on this bead rather than risk editing the wrong copy.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS: item (ii) does not need 'collapse the duplication first'. Bulk-adding properties/methods/signals to Resource and the other multiply-registered classes can be done now, in any registrar, PROVIDED THE ADDITION IS UNGUARDED. That is what the merge is for.

WARNING for whoever does it: add metadata unguarded, exactly as the Resource block does, and say so in a comment. Wrapping a metadata pass in if !class_exists(..) is what makes it a no-op - the exact failure this design already fixed once.

SELF-CORRECTION: my pat-s3rrv.71 report framed duplicate registrations as a run-order hazard in general. The narrower statement above is the accurate one. The three GUARDED blocks I deleted there (Slider, SpinBox, TextureProgressBar) were independently verified to be strict subsets, so that change stands and was behaviour-preserving - but the general warning I attached to it was too broad.

- `lightened` and `darkened` are NOT mirrors: one moves toward white (`c + (1-c)*a`), the other scales toward black (`c * (1-a)`).

## Method/member/constant count audit — the open question from the last partial is closed

The previous partial left one thing unresolved: "the bead says 26 methods and I counted 17 instance plus 8 statics, which is 25, so one name may still be unaccounted for." Answered by enumerating both sides mechanically rather than by counting by hand.

**Godot side** — upstream/godot/doc/classes/Color.xml: 26 <method> names, 14 <member> names, 146 <constant> names.

**Patina side** — parsed out of variant_math.rs / gdcore::math:
- color_method dispatches **17** instance methods
- vector_static_call dispatches **9** statics (the 8 counted before, plus the from_string that partial delivered)
- member_get / member_set carry **14** members
- Color::named covers all **146** constants

Set difference both ways: Godot - Patina = [] and Patina - Godot = []. **26/26, 14/14, 146/146.** The missing 26th was from_string itself, so the implementation half of this bead is complete.

## What was actually left, and what this pass delivers

The bead's acceptance has a wiring clause the existing tests never touched:

> the path is .tscn -> node with a Color property (e.g. modulate) -> attached script mutates it -> the property read-back reflects the new value after a frame

gdscript-interop/tests/color_builtin_surface_from_scene.rs drives a bare Interpreter — no scene, no node, no frame — and every one of its member assertions is a **read**. Two things only the scene layer can catch:

1. **The write half of the members.** Godot's Color members are read-WRITE. The write path is a different function (member_set) reached through a different interpreter branch, so a read-only bridge passes every existing assertion and still drops `modulate.a8 = 128` on the floor.
2. **The seed.** A bare `modulate = ...` writes the *node* property only when that property is already non-Nil — the interpreter uses "reads back non-Nil" as its test for "this name is a node property". An unpopulated ClassDB seeds nothing, so the whole script runs clean and changes nothing at all. The new test asserts that precondition explicitly so a seeding regression names itself instead of looking like a Color bug.

New file: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/color_members_reach_a_scene_node.rs — four tests over a real .tscn (Node2D root, Sprite2D child), script attached, enter_tree, one step: the darkened-yellow read-back (the acceptance clause), the 8-bit write landing on the node property, the HSV write re-deriving the channels via `self.<var>.h = 0.5`, and the member reads off the node property.

Thresholds are derived, not picked: darkened(0.2) scales by (1 - amount) so YELLOW lands on 0.8; a8 = 128 stores 128/255 = 0.50196 and must round-trip back to **128, not 127**; yellow's hue is **1/6** because Godot normalises hue to 0..1 (a bridge handing back degrees produces a wildly wrong colour that still looks like a colour).

No engine source changed this pass — the implementation was already complete, the proof was not.

title: Variant: add the six missing builtin kinds (Vector4, Vector4i, Rect2i, Projection, RID, PackedVector4Array) end-to-end
description:
[audit-key: core-variant/core-variant-missing-types] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json `.builtin_classes` lists 38 builtins; Vector4 (32 methods), Vector4i (16), Rect2i (13), Projection (26), RID (2), PackedVector4Array (23) are all absent from Patina's Variant. Upstream types: core/math/vector4.h, vector4i.h, rect2i.h, projection.h, core/templates/rid.h. | upstream/godot/scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp `VariantParser` handles every builtin literal; `Vector4`, `Vector4i`, `Rect2i`, `Projection` and `PackedVector4Array` are first-class Variant types (extension_api.json `builtin_classes`) that appear in real scenes — e.g. `Projection` on Camera3D-adjacent resources and `Rect2i` on TileSet/atlas region properties.

**Godot classes:** Vector4, Vector4i, Rect2i, Projection, RID, PackedVector4Array

**Patina today:**
- [core-variant] engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/variant.rs:164-205 (`VariantType`) and :209-291 (`Variant`) enumerate 34 kinds with no Vector4/Vector4i/Rect2i/Projection/RID/PackedVector4Array. The .tscn loader knows they exist and deliberately smuggles them through as tagged dictionaries: engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/loader.rs:235-241 `UNPARSED_BUILTINS = ["Vector4i","Vector4","Rect2i","Projection","PackedVector4Array"]` and :638-665 wrap the literal in a Dictionary with `__gd_unparsed_type__`/`__gd_unparsed_literal__` keys. The GDScript constructor table has no arms for them (engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:5180-5360 covers Vector2/2i/3/3i/Color/Rect2/AABB/Plane/Quaternion/Basis/Transform2D/Transform3D/Callable/Array/Dictionary and 9 Packed arrays — PackedVector4Array is absent at 5324-5358). The binary codec cannot encode them either (engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/binary.rs:238-472). `RID` exists nowhere as a type (grep `struct Rid|type Rid` across engine-rs/crates → 0 hits; the only `"RID"` strings are a syntax-highlight keyword list at gdeditor/src/gdscript_highlight.rs:52 and a type-name table at interpreter.rs:13961).
- [resources-io] `gdresource/src/loader.rs:235-241 pub const UNPARSED_BUILTINS: &[&str] = ["Vector4i", "Vector4", "Rect2i", "Projection", "PackedVector4Array"]` — these five literals are preserved as a marker `Variant::Dictionary` carrying `__gd_unparsed_type__` / `__gd_unparsed_literal__` / `__gd_unparsed_args__` (loader.rs:243-266) rather than becoming real values. The root cause is upstream in the Variant type: `gdvariant/src/variant.rs:164-204 pub enum VariantType` has no `Vector4`, `Vector4i`, `Rect2i`, `Projection` or `PackedVector4Array` arms. Text round-trip is therefore lossless, but any consumer that reads such a property (node property sync, inspector, script `get()`) receives a Dictionary where Godot yields a math type, so comparisons, arithmetic and typed assignment all fail. The binary loader is worse — `gdresource/src/res_loader.rs:135-138` documents that these same types return `EngineError::Unsupported`, so one such property aborts the whole binary resource load.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/variant.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/loader.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/binary.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/res_loader.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: Godot 4.6.1 has 38 Variant builtins (extension_api.json `.builtin_classes`). Six have no Variant kind in Patina: Vector4 (32 methods, 3 constants), Vector4i (16, 4), Rect2i (13), Projection (26 methods, 2 constants — the camera/XR projection matrix), RID (2 methods — every *Server API returns one), PackedVector4Array (23 methods, Godot 4.3+, used by skin weights and shader data). Upstream: core/math/vector4.h, vector4i.h, rect2i.h, projection.h, core/templates/rid.h.

PATINA CURRENT STATE: engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/variant.rs:164-205 and 209-291 have 34 kinds and none of these six. The .tscn loader already flags the gap: engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/loader.rs:235-241 keeps a `UNPARSED_BUILTINS` list and :638-665 stores each literal as a Dictionary tagged `__gd_unparsed_type__`/`__gd_unparsed_literal__` so the saver can re-emit the text — data is preserved but nothing can READ these values. GDScript cannot construct them (no arms in the constructor table at engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:5180-5360; PackedVector4Array is missing from the packed block at 5324-5358), the binary codec cannot encode them (engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/binary.rs:238-472), and `RID` has no Rust type at all.

IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH: (1) add `Vector4`/`Vector4i` to engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/math.rs, `Rect2i` next to `Rect2`, `Projection` to engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/math3d.rs (a Projection type already exists in gdscene/src/camera3d.rs:100 and gdserver3d/src/projection.rs — consolidate rather than duplicate), and a newtype `Rid(u64)` in gdcore; (2) add the six `Variant`/`VariantType` variants in gdvariant/src/variant.rs and sweep every exhaustive match (variant.rs Display/variant_type/is_packed_array, binary.rs, serialize.rs, hash.rs, conversion.rs, plus gdresource/src/{loader,saver,res_loader}.rs and gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs — a `..`-free enum means the compiler enumerates the work); (3) give binary.rs the correct Godot type ids (Rect2i=6? use the table at interpreter.rs:13940-13980 as the id oracle: Rect2i=8, Vector4=12, Vector4i=13, Projection=19, RID=23, PackedVector4Array=38); (4) delete the `UNPARSED_BUILTINS` path in loader.rs so these literals parse into real values, keeping the saver byte-identical; (5) add GDScript constructors, members, methods and constants for each.

WIRING REQUIREMENT: a .tscn carrying `Vector4(1,2,3,4)`, `Rect2i(0,0,16,16)`, `Projection(...)` and `PackedVector4Array([...])` properties must load into real typed values, be readable and writable from an attached script, and re-save byte-identically.

**Merged findings (2):** Missing Variant builtin types: Vector4, Vector4i, Rect2i, Projection, RID, PackedVector4Array; .tscn/.tres math literals Vector4 / Vector4i / Rect2i / Projection / PackedVector4Array

**Prove it:** A .tscn with Vector4 / Vector4i / Rect2i / Projection / PackedVector4Array property values loads into real Variant kinds (no `__gd_unparsed_type__` dictionaries anywhere in the loaded scene), a script attached to the node reads `.x/.w`, `.size`, indexes the projection and appends to the packed array, and re-saving the scene reproduces the original text. (test: `missing_variant_builtins_tscn_roundtrip_and_script_access`)

Three traps are now pinned by tests: posmod is Math::fposmod whose result takes the sign of the DIVISOR (fposmod(5,-3) = -1 where Rust rem_euclid says 2, agreeing only for positive divisors); snapped is floor(v/step + 0.5)*step, round-half-UP, so -2.5 snaps to -2 where round() gives -3; inverse is the component-wise reciprocal, not a negation or a normalise. Also: Vector4i::snappedi promotes to DOUBLE because Godot has only one Math::snapped taking doubles, so snappedi(-5,10) is 0 not -10, and the promotion uses f64 since an i32 past 2^24 is not exact in f32; distance_squared_to returns an Int matching Godot's int64_t. STILL OPEN from the recorded list: Vector4/Vector4i cubic_interpolate and cubic_interpolate_in_time; Projection's six remaining statics (create_for_hmd, create_perspective_hmd, create_depth_correction, create_light_atlas_rect, create_fit_aabb, create_frustum_aspect) - only create_perspective_with_offset has a gdcore counterpart, the rest need gdcore work first; Projection's derived getters (get_fov, get_fovy, get_aspect, get_z_near, get_z_far, get_lod_multiplier, get_pixels_per_meter, get_viewport_half_extents, get_far_plane_half_extents, get_projection_plane, flipped_y, jitter_offseted, perspective_znear_adjusted), with get_fovy already transcribed inline in variant_math as a reference to lift; Rect2i grow_individual and grow_side are not in gdcore::Rect2i; and scripts_read_the_new_builtins_off_a_node remains a self.<ad-hoc .tscn property> interpreter bug rather than a Variant one, keeping a red test in gdscene/tests and deserving its own bead.

GODOT: `AudioServer` is a global singleton (extension_api.json `.singletons[]`, servers/audio/audio_server.cpp) with 57 bound methods. Games routinely call `AudioServer.get_bus_index("Music")`, `set_bus_volume_db`, `set_bus_mute`, `set_bus_solo`, `set_bus_bypass_effects`, `add_bus_effect`/`remove_bus_effect`/`swap_bus_effects`/`set_bus_effect_enabled`, `get_bus_effect_instance` (music visualizers), `get_bus_peak_volume_left_db/right_db` (VU meters), `set_playback_speed_scale`, `get_mix_rate`, `get_output_latency`, `set_bus_layout`/`generate_bus_layout`.\n\nPATINA: the Rust half is already implemented and unit-tested — crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs:109 (playback_speed_scale), :124-129 (peak meters), :598 (get_bus_effect_instance), :615 (bus_effect_magnitude), and crates/gdaudio/src/mixer.rs:22-88 (add/remove/move/get_bus_by_name) — but nothing script-facing reaches it. crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:14464 `BUILTIN_SINGLETONS` omits "AudioServer" and there is no `Ident("AudioServer")` dispatch arm anywhere in the interpreter. ClassDB does not register the class either (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs has no `ClassRegistration::new("AudioServer")`).\n\nAPPROACH: (1) add "AudioServer" to `BUILTIN_SINGLETONS` and add an `AudioServer.*` dispatch function in crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs alongside the existing `PhysicsServer2D`/`RenderingServer` arms; (2) route the calls to the live mixer owned by `gdscene::MainLoop`'s `AudioServerBridge` (crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:107-114 already exposes `server()`/`server_mut()`) — extend the `SceneAccess` trait with audio-server accessors rather than creating a second AudioServer; (3) register the class + methods in crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs so the inspector/ClassDB reflection sees it; (4) add the missing server methods that back the API (`get_bus_index`, `get_bus_name`, `set_bus_name`, `add_bus_effect`, `swap_bus_effects`, `set_bus_effect_enabled`, `get_output_latency`, `get_mix_rate`).\n\nWIRING: script call -> interpreter AudioServer arm -> SceneAccess -> MainLoop::audio_bridge_mut().server_mut() -> AudioMixer, observable in the very next `MainLoop::step` mix output.

**Merged findings (9):** AudioServer singleton (script-reachable bus/effect/peak API); Web (wasm) audio: scene players feeding the AudioWorklet; NavigationServer2D / NavigationServer3D script-reachable singletons (map/region/link/agent/obstacle RID API, query_path, closest-point and random-point queries, simplify_path, get_process_info); AudioServer script singleton (57 methods) — the mixer runs every frame but no script can address a bus, effect or volume; NavigationServer2D / NavigationServer3D / NavigationMeshGenerator script singletons (137 + 154 + 4 methods); PhysicsServer3D script singleton (175 methods) — PhysicsServer2D is dispatched with 94 arms, its 3D twin has none; physics/3d space + solver ProjectSettings (default_linear_damp, default_angular_damp, solver/solver_iterations, sleep thresholds / time_before_sleep) never reach PhysicsWorld3D; AudioServer singleton (script-unreachable); NavigationServer2D/3D script singletons + RID API (incl. NavigationServer2DManager/3DManager)

**Prove it:** A scene whose script runs `AudioServer.set_bus_volume_db(AudioServer.get_bus_index("Music"), -80.0)` in `_ready()` makes a player routed to the Music bus mix to silence on the next frame, while a second player on Master stays audible; `AudioServer.get_bus_peak_volume_left_db(0, 0)` returns a finite dB value that rises when audio plays; `AudioServer.set_playback_speed_scale(2.0)` doubles the rate a stream's playback_position advances. title: String: implement Godot's full `%` sprintf (specifiers, flags, width, precision, error strings)
description:
[audit-key: core-variant/core-variant-string-format] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/string/ustring.cpp `String::sprintf()` — supports %d/%i/%o/%x/%X/%f/%F/%e/%E/%g/%G/%s/%c/%v/%%, the `-`/`+`/space/`0` flags, explicit and `*` (argument-supplied) width, `.precision`, and returns diagnostic strings such as "not enough arguments for format string" (ustring.cpp:5206-5413) rather than dropping the specifier. | extension_api.json String → 116 methods, StringName → 110 (StringName exposes the whole String surface). upstream/godot/core/string/ustring.cpp + core/variant/variant_call.cpp bind list.

**Godot classes:** String, StringName

**Patina today:**
- [core-variant] engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:14022-14076 `string_format` handles only `%%`, `%s`, `%d`, `%f` (hard-coded `{:.6}`) and `%v`; every other specifier falls to `_ => result.push('%')` at 14069, which emits a bare `%` and leaves the letter as literal text. Width, precision, flags and `*` are unimplemented, so `"%.2f" % x`, `"%04d" % n`, `"%x" % n`, `"%c" % 65`, `"%-10s" % s` are all wrong. When arguments run out the code silently emits nothing (`if idx < values.len()` at 14035/14042/14053/14064) instead of returning Godot's error string.
- [core-variant] engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:8127-8536 is the String method table: 66 of 116 arms. Missing (diffed against extension_api.json): match, matchn, get_slice, get_slicec, get_slice_count, split_floats, replacen, replace_char, replace_chars, remove_char, remove_chars, to_kebab_case, unicode_at, chr, num, num_int64, num_uint64, num_scientific, humanize_size, bigrams, is_subsequence_of(n), naturalcasecmp_to, filecasecmp_to, filenocasecmp_to, md5_text, sha1_text, md5_buffer, sha1_buffer, sha256_buffer, hex_decode, uri_file_decode, validate_node_name, validate_filename, is_valid_identifier, is_valid_ascii_identifier, is_valid_unicode_identifier, is_valid_hex_number, is_valid_html_color, is_valid_ip_address, is_valid_filename, to_ascii_buffer, to_utf8_buffer, to_utf16_buffer, to_utf32_buffer, to_wchar_buffer, to_multibyte_char_buffer, erase, insert, reverse. None of these appear anywhere in engine-rs/crates (grep of each quoted name across the tree → 0 hits). Separately, `Variant::StringName` has NO arm in `call_method_on` (arm list: interpreter.rs:7690/7800/8127/8537/8672/8736/8801/8813/10001/10165/10345), so `&"Foo".to_lower()` falls to "cannot call method on StringName" at interpreter.rs:10348 although Godot binds the entire String surface onto StringName.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: `upstream/godot/core/string/ustring.cpp::String::sprintf()` (lines ~5150-5450) defines the `%` operator: specifiers %d %i %o %x %X %f %F %e %E %g %G %s %c %v %%; flags `-` (left justify), `+` (force sign), space, `0` (zero pad); a width that may be a literal or `*` (taken from the argument list); `.precision` likewise; and error RETURN VALUES that become the resulting string — "not enough arguments for format string" (ustring.cpp:5210, 5280, 5325, 5395, 5413), "unsupported format character", "too many decimal points in format". `register_string_modulo_op` in core/variant/variant_op.cpp:205-210 registers `%` for String AND StringName against every Variant type, so `"%s" % Vector2(1,2)` works.

PATINA CURRENT STATE: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:14022-14076 is a 55-line loop that understands `%%`, `%s`, `%d`, `%f` (fixed at six decimals, line 14055) and `%v`. Anything else hits `_ => result.push('%')` (14069) and the specifier letter survives as literal text. There is no width, precision, flag or `*` handling at all, and running out of arguments silently emits nothing (the `if idx < values.len()` guards at 14035/14042/14053/14064) where Godot returns the diagnostic string. `"%.2f" % 3.14159`, `"%04d" % 7`, `"%x" % 255`, `"%c" % 65` and `"%-8s|" % "a"` are therefore all wrong.

IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH: replace `string_format` with a faithful port of `String::sprintf` in a new module (e.g. engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/format.rs so the .tscn/resource layer can share it), driven by a small state machine mirroring ustring.cpp's `in_format`/`left_justified`/`pad_with_zeros`/`show_sign`/`min_chars`/`min_decimals` variables. Return `Result<String, String>` where the Err payload is Godot's exact diagnostic text, and have the `%` operator surface it as the result string. Wire it from interpreter.rs's `binary_mod` (interpreter.rs:3684-3690) for both `Variant::String` and `Variant::StringName` left-hand sides.

WIRING REQUIREMENT: a script in a scene formats a Label's text with `%` and the rendered/stored text must match Godot character-for-character.

**Merged findings (2):** String `%` format operator (sprintf); String method surface (and StringName as a method receiver)

**Prove it:** A scene script setting a Label's `text` via `"%s scored %04d (%.2f%%) hex=%x chr=%c |%-6s|" % [name, 7, 12.3456, 255, 65, "ab"]` produces exactly Godot's output, and `"%d %d" % [1]` yields "not enough arguments for format string". (test: `string_percent_format_parity_from_scene`)

(test: `string_percent_format_parity_from_scene`)

title: AnimationPanel: implement onion skinning ghosts and auto-key, and add a bezier track editor

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/animation/animation_track_editor.cpp (AnimationBezierTrackEdit, auto-key toggle, AnimationTrackEditTypeAudio waveform preview, method track argument dialog) + canvas_item_editor_plugin.cpp onion skinning

**Godot classes:** AnimationTrackEditor, Animation

comments.text:
## Handoff (EmeraldIsland): auto-key is WIRED; one real parity gap found; onion untouched

### DONE — auto-key now records
`editor_server.rs` gained `auto_key_property(...)`, called from `api_set_property`. The flag already existed (`AnimationPlaybackState::recording`, set by `POST /api/animation/record`, reported in `/api/animation/status`, read by the panel) but **nothing consumed it** — arming auto-key flipped a boolean and recorded nothing. An armed edit now writes a keyframe at the playhead and pushes the clip through to the AnimationPlayer, exactly as an explicit keyframe add does.

Test: `crates/gdeditor/tests/editor_autokey_records_keyframe.rs`, driving the real HTTP surface. It asserts the **disarmed** case first — without that control the test would pass even if auto-key recorded on every edit regardless of the toggle — and asserts the key lands at the PLAYHEAD, not at 0.

### 🔴 REAL PARITY GAP the test exposed — worth its own bead
**A clip can only become "current" by PLAYING it.** The one and only setter of `AnimationPlaybackState::animation_name` is `api_play_animation` (editor_server.rs:12937), which also forces `playing = true` and resets `current_time = 0.0`. There is no "select clip without playing".

Consequence: a user arms auto-key, drags a node, and gets **nothing** unless they have played the clip first. Godot's auto-key writes into the clip SELECTED in the animation panel and does not require playback (`editor/animation/animation_track_editor.cpp`). My first test run failed exactly this way (`got []`) and I fixed the TEST to select via `play`, because that is the only mechanism available — but the underlying coupling is a genuine defect, not a test artifact. A `POST /api/animation/select` (or letting `create` select) would close it.

### 🔴 BEAD DESCRIPTION IS STALE — please correct
It claims gdscene "has no Bezier and no Animation track". **`TrackType::Bezier` already exists** (pat-s3rrv.44): `in_handle`/`out_handle` on keyframes, `KeyFrame::bezier(...)`, parsing in `animation_tscn.rs`, saving in `scene_saver.rs`, exposure in `editor_server.rs`, and a round-trip test `bezier_and_animation_tracks_from_tscn_drive_properties.rs`. The other two claims I re-verified and they hold: onion is decorative (8 hits, all the button), auto-key was absent (0 hits).

### NOT DONE — onion skinning, and why it needs a decision not just effort
1. `GET /api/viewport` serves a **cached** BMP from `ViewportCache`; the render loop that fills it lives in `engine-rs/examples/editor.rs`, **outside this bead's stated file list**. Compositing N ghost renders at t±step needs a call on whether that happens in the render loop or on demand in the handler. `EditorState` already has the playhead to anchor it.
2. The acceptance also needs `EDITOR_HTML` to post an onion parameter instead of only calling `logMessage` (editor_ui.rs:12291-12296). That file was under continuous edit by another agent while I worked, so I left it alone.

I deliberately did **not** create the acceptance-named test `editor_animation_onion_autokey_served` — it must fail until onion lands, and a knowingly-red test in a shared crate's `tests/` is a fail-fast hazard for every other bead in that suite. My test is named for what it actually covers.

### Also separable
`crates/gdeditor/src/anim_track_types.rs` has its OWN `TrackType` enum (Value/Transform/MethodCall/Audio/Animation) that diverges from gdscene's in both directions — it lacks Bezier, gdscene lacks Animation. Reconciling the two models is its own piece of work.

### Trap for whoever edits `api_set_property`
`let prop_name = property.clone(); let mut cmd = EditorCommand::SetProperty {` appears **twice** in `editor_server.rs` (two similar handlers). A patch asserting a unique match will correctly refuse; target the FIRST occurrence, which is the one inside `api_set_property` (~7057-7205).

All my file reservations are released.

The verifier built the tree as it stood at 06:26, which was BEFORE I added the `play` call to `open_clip`. The failing assertion it reported sits at line 211; in the current file it is at line 234. So that half was already closed — the reopen was diagnosing a stale tree.

### Cause 2 — the real bug, found while confirming the above
`auto_key_property` derived the track path with `absolute_node_path`, which returns `/root/Main/Sprite2D`. **Animation track paths are RELATIVE to the AnimationPlayer's `root_node`** — `apply_animation_preview` and `SceneTree::process_animations` both resolve them with `get_node_or_null(base, &track.node_path)` where `base` is the player's `root_node` (`".."` by default, i.e. the player's PARENT). The existing test at editor_server.rs:25689 asserts `node_path == "Player"`, confirming the convention.

So auto-key stored a track addressing a path nothing resolves against, and one that does not match how Godot writes tracks to `.tscn`. It would have looked wired and been inert.

### Fix
- Extracted the base computation out of `apply_animation_preview` into `animation_track_base()`, and pointed BOTH the resolver and the new writer at it, so the two cannot drift apart — the drift is exactly what caused this.
- Added `relative_node_path(tree, base, node_id)`, returning the path relative to the base, an empty string when the node IS the base (which the resolver already treats as the base), and `None` when the base is not an ancestor. `None` logs a warning and skips rather than inventing a path that silently resolves to nothing.

### Test hardening
The failure mode cost a full verify round trip because "no track written" and "track written under the wrong path" both surface as `got []`. The test now checks the track's `(node_path, property)` pair FIRST and prints every track on the clip when it does not match, so a future path regression names itself instead of looking like a dead flag.

Still not done, unchanged from my previous comment: onion skinning (needs a decision on where compositing happens — the render loop lives in `examples/editor.rs`, outside this bead's file list), the `EDITOR_HTML` onion parameter, and the "select a clip without playing it" parity gap.
