## Increment (EmeraldIsland): the server half — template registry, generation, validation

Picking up BronzeBridge's partial. They fixed `doAttachScript` to use the node's class; the remaining scope was the dialog, the templates, and built-in scripts. I took the part that is provable without a browser.

### 🔴 A SECOND hardcoded literal they missed
`createNewScript()` (editor_ui.rs:12634) had its **own** `extends Node2D` literal and attached the result to the selected node — the exact bug the bead describes, in a sibling function. Fixing only `doAttachScript` left the Script-panel "new script" path still producing Node2D scripts for every node. Both now go through the server.

### Delivered
**`crates/gdeditor/src/script_templates.rs` (new module)** — registry + renderer, ported from the vendored Godot tree rather than the docs:
- `render()` implements `GDScriptLanguage::make_template`'s substitutions: `_BASE_`, `_CLASS_SNAKE_CASE_`, `_CLASS_`, `_TS_`.
  ⚠️ **Order is load-bearing**: `_CLASS_` is a PREFIX of `_CLASS_SNAKE_CASE_`, so substituting it first corrupts the longer key into `MyNodeSNAKE_CASE_`. Pinned by its own test.
- `parse_template()` mirrors `ScriptCreateDialog::_parse_template`: `# meta-name:` / `# meta-description:` / `# meta-space-indent:` are metadata not body, leading indentation folds back to `_TS_`, leading blank lines are stripped, and the name falls back to the file stem capitalized (`basic_movement` → `Basic Movement`).
- `templates_for()` walks the **whole ancestor chain** via ClassDB, project templates before built-ins — Godot's `_update_template_menu` → `_get_hierarchy`. Exact-class matching would offer a Sprite2D nothing at all.
  ⚠️ ClassDB is empty until seeded, so an unknown/unregistered class falls back to the `Node` → `Object` spine instead of returning an empty dropdown.
- Built-in content is the vendored `Object/empty`, `Node/default`, `CharacterBody2D/basic_movement`, run through the same parser as project templates rather than hand-transcribed a second time.

**`editor_server.rs`** — `GET /api/script/templates?base_class=X` and `POST /api/script/create`, plus CAPABILITIES entries. Generation happens server-side, which is what the bead's APPROACH asked for. Validation runs BEFORE touching disk and returns which rule broke (Godot validates live and shows the reason); an existing file is reused rather than clobbered.

**`editor_ui.rs`** — both `doAttachScript` and `createNewScript` now POST `/api/script/create` with `base_class`. No script body is built in the browser any more.

### Divergence I chose, flagged rather than buried
`DEFAULT_INDENT` is **4 spaces**, not Godot's tab. Every script Patina writes today is space-indented and its GDScript fixtures assume that; the `_TS_` placeholder is what carries the parity, and the width stays a parameter.

### NOT delivered (unchanged from BronzeBridge's list)
The modal Create-Script dialog itself — Inherits picker, Class Name field, Template dropdown, Built-in Script toggle, live validation display. `editor_ui.rs` still has no modal helper to build on, and that scaffolding wants a browser to verify. ### 🔴 The "BLOCKED on pat-s3rrv.59" note is STALE
The previous remaining_scope said Rect2i / Vector4 / Vector4i have no Variant kind (`grep -c '    Rect2i(' variant.rs -> 0`) so `from_json` rejects them, and a guard test enforced their absence. That is no longer true: all three now have **both** a `Variant` kind and a `from_json` arm (serialize.rs — `"Vector4"` decodes a flat 4-array, `"Vector4i"` the same as ints, `"Rect2i"` an object of `{position:[2], size:[2]}`). Re-measuring the claim cost one grep and unblocked three types. Worth doing before deferring anything to .59 — that bead is still open and `needs-attention`, but the parts this bead needed have landed.

### Delivered — the Packed* family (the named remaining scope)
A resizable indexed list per `editor_properties_array_dict.cpp`: per-element inputs, add, and remove, for **all ten** Packed types `from_json` can decode (Byte/Int32/Int64/Float32/Float64/String/Vector2/Vector3/Vector4/Color).

⚠️ **The wire shape is ONE FLAT ARRAY, never an array of elements.** `from_json` decodes PackedVector2Array by chunking a flat list in pairs and **rejects an odd length outright**; Vector3 chunks in threes. Emitting `[[x,y],[x,y]]` would be refused by the server and the edit would vanish — the same silent discard this bead exists to fix, one layer down. A `stride` per type drives both the layout and the commit, and remove splices a whole ELEMENT so the length stays a valid multiple.

⚠️ **PackedByteArray is the one CLAMPED type.** Its decoder is `u8::try_from(x.as_u64()?)`, so a single negative or >255 entry makes the conversion fail and **the whole array is rejected**, not just that element. The editor clamps to 0..=255 in both the input bounds and the coercion. That is load-bearing, not cosmetic.

### Also corrected: a test with a FALSE justification
My own new guard initially asserted RID must be absent "because from_json cannot decode it". It can (`"RID" => Variant::Rid(...)`). RID does stay read-only, but the real reason is that it is an opaque runtime handle Godot exposes no editor for either. Fixed — a wrong reason in a test misleads the next reader as much as a wrong assertion.

### NOT delivered, with the detail needed to finish it
**Projection.** It decodes, so leaving it read-only is a genuine remaining gap — but its shape is a **flat 16-element array** (`arr.len() != 16` then `m[i/4][i%4]`), which is neither the compound object-of-arrays nor the strided list. ## Projection delivered — the remaining scope from my previous comment is closed

Supersedes the `remaining_scope` I filed minutes ago: it named Projection as the one decodable Variant type still stuck read-only. It is now editable, so that note is spent — don't carry it forward.

title: TileSet: add an atlas-source TileSet editor (tile selection, per-tile collision/nav/custom data) served from the editor
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-tileset] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/scene/2d/tiles/tile_set_editor.cpp, tile_set_atlas_source_editor.cpp, tile_data_editors.cpp, tile_set_scenes_collection_source_editor.cpp

**Godot classes:** TileSet, TileSetAtlasSource, TileData, TileMapLayer

**Patina today:**
- [editor-ux] The only tileset endpoint is GET /api/tilemap/tileset (editor_server.rs:2547 -> api_tilemap_tileset, editor_server.rs:15248-15262), which serialises a flat {id,name,color,collision} per tile from state.tile_grid_store.tileset (seeded by TileGridStore::new_with_defaults(), editor_server.rs:905). There is no route that creates or edits a TileSet: no atlas source, no per-tile collision polygon, navigation polygon, occlusion, custom data layer, terrain set/peering bits, alternative tile or animation frame endpoint exists in the 288-route table. The client's tilemap palette (editor_ui.rs ~2355-2385) only lists those flat tiles for painting.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/tilemap.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: the TileSet editor (upstream/godot/editor/scene/2d/tiles/tile_set_editor.cpp + tile_set_atlas_source_editor.cpp) lets you add a TileSetAtlasSource from a texture, slice it into tiles, and paint per-tile data with the TileData editors (tile_data_editors.cpp): collision polygons per physics layer, navigation polygons per navigation layer, occlusion, custom data layers, terrain set + peering bits, z-index/y-sort offset, alternative tiles and animation frames.\n\nPATINA: no TileSet authoring exists. The single endpoint GET /api/tilemap/tileset (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:15248) emits {id,name,color,collision} triples from a default-seeded TileGridStore (editor_server.rs:905 TileGridStore::new_with_defaults()); painting works (/api/tilemap/paint..line, wired) but the tiles themselves cannot be defined, and none of the TileData surface is representable. Loading a real Godot project's .tres TileSet therefore cannot round-trip through the editor.\n\nAPPROACH (stage 1 of the family — atlas + collision + custom data): extend gdscene's TileSet model to carry atlas sources (texture path, texture_region_size, separation, margins) and per-tile TileData (collision polygons per layer, custom data values); add GET/POST /api/tileset/source, /api/tileset/tile and /api/tileset/tile/data to editor_server.rs that read/write the TileSet resource of the selected TileMapLayer and save it into the .tres/.tscn; add a TileSet editor bottom panel in editor_ui.rs showing the atlas texture (served via /api/preview/file), a tile grid selector, and a per-tile data pane. Terrains, alternative tiles and animation frames are a follow-up bead under the same group_key.\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: editing a tile's collision polygon must persist into the TileSet resource on disk and be honoured by the runtime (the TileMapLayer static-collision path already consumes tile collision, see crates/gdscene/tests/tilemap_tiles_provide_static_collision.rs).

**Prove it:** In the served editor, selecting a TileMapLayer opens a TileSet panel where an atlas texture can be assigned, tiles selected, and a collision rect set on tile (0,0); the change is written to the TileSet resource file and a body placed on that tile in the runner collides with it. (test: `editor_tileset_atlas_tiledata_served`) drives editor_server, POSTs the atlas source + tile collision, asserts the saved resource text, and asserts EDITOR_HTML contains "/api/tileset/tile".

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## `custom_data_layer_<i>/type` now round-trips (EmeraldIsland, 2026-08-20)

Picked up the item the 13:10 comment named as still open. The two later comments
dropped it from their remaining-scope lists, so it was re-checked against source
rather than trusted either way — it was still missing.

### The gap

`packed_scene.rs` read `custom_data_layer_<i>/name` only. The saver can only write
back what the loader kept, so a `.tscn` authored in real Godot came out of Patina
with every custom data layer's TYPE declaration stripped, and Godot reopening it
saw untyped layers.

### ⚠️ The existing "never guess a type" decision was KEPT

`scene_saver.rs:1105` and `packed_scene.rs:2772` both argue that a guessed type is
worse than an absent one: it silently coerces the value on load, whereas an absent
type leaves the Variant as authored. **That reasoning is correct and nothing here
touches it.** No type is ever inferred from a value.

The fix is narrower: a type the FILE ITSELF DECLARED is no longer thrown away.
Preserving a declared type violates nothing the original comment was protecting —
the two concerns only looked like one.

### Shape

- `tilemap.rs`: `TILE_CUSTOM_DATA_TYPES = "__tile_custom_data_types__"`, a
  `PackedInt32Array` parallel to `TILE_CUSTOM_DATA_LAYERS`, `-1` = "declared with
  no type" so the index mapping cannot collapse.
- `packed_scene.rs`: collected in lockstep with the names, stored ONLY if the file
  typed at least one layer — so an editor-authored TileSet is byte-for-byte
  unchanged.
- `scene_saver.rs`: emits `custom_data_layer_<i>/type` only for entries `>= 0`.

Already covered by `is_internal_prop`'s existing `TILE_CUSTOM_DATA_PREFIX` filter.
Nothing SCANS that prefix — per-tile keys are always built by
`tile_custom_data_key` — so there is no parser for the new key to confuse.

### The test that carries the weight

`an_untyped_layer_still_emits_no_type`. The fixture's two values are obviously an
Int and a String, so that assertion is precisely what fails on a "just write the
value's type" implementation. `an_untyped_layer_does_not_shift_a_later_layers_type`
puts the UNTYPED layer first, which is what catches walking names and types with
independent counters.

The Godot-authored fixture is built by injecting `/type` lines into the saver's own
output, not hand-authored: a hand-authored `.tscn` that failed to parse for an
unrelated reason would look identical to the feature being broken.

### Scope note for the coordinator

The bead's approach note scopes it to "stage 1 of the family — atlas + collision +
custom data", naming terrains/alternative tiles/animation frames as a FOLLOW-UP
BEAD under the same group_key. Stage 1 is now complete: atlas source, per-tile
collision, custom data (incl. this), navigation, occlusion and the atlas grid UI.
The acceptance `editor_tileset_atlas_tiledata_served` passes (3/3 on the prebuilt
binary).

Remaining items in the newest comment are the deferred Stage 2, atlas-grid zoom,
and a standing note that the editor_server tileset handlers were checked NLL-clean
by inspection only. None of those is Stage 1.

## Two acceptance clauses delivered (EmeraldIsland) — lease freed mid-block

I reported this bead blocked at 07:17 with both files leased. **BronzeLake released `editor_server.rs` shortly after**, so I re-checked the reservations rather than trusting my own earlier "blocked until 08:05" note, and took the two acceptance clauses that were measuring zero.

### Delivered
- **`_apply_changes` on scene save** — dispatched to EVERY enabled plugin, **before** `TscnSaver::save_tree`. Godot's `EditorNode::_save_scene` runs `apply_changes_in_editors()` first precisely so a plugin can flush pending edits into the scene and have them land in the file; calling it after serialisation would be inert.
- **`_forward_canvas_gui_input` on viewport click** — offered to plugins **before** the editor's own select tool. A truthy return consumes the event: the handler returns early, the hit-test never runs, and the selection is left alone.

Both go through one new helper, `dispatch_plugin_virtual(state, method, args, stop_at_first_claim)`, which copies `notify_plugins_of_selection`'s take-map / call / restore / log borrow dance rather than reinventing it.

⚠️ **`stop_at_first_claim` is load-bearing, not a convenience.** Input forwarding must STOP at the first plugin returning true — that plugin consumed the event, and continuing would let two plugins act on one click. Lifecycle broadcasts like `_apply_changes` must reach EVERY plugin; a truthy return there does not mean "handled", and stopping would silently skip the rest.

### 🔴 A trap for anyone editing the viewport routes
The prologue of `api_viewport_click`

```
let mut state = state.lock().unwrap();
let vw = state.viewport_width;   ... let hit = hit_test_with_zoom_pan(...)
```

is **byte-identical in `api_viewport_drag_start`** (lines 8175 and 8218). A first-occurrence string replace happens to hit the right one today, but only by luck — any reordering moves the edit into the wrong handler. I spliced by position (locate `fn api_viewport_click(`, take the first hit after it, assert it falls before the next `fn api_`) and verified afterwards that the forward is present in the click handler and absent from drag_start.

### Tests
`apply_changes_fires_once_per_scene_save` COUNTS occurrences rather than checking presence — a hook wired into a helper the save path calls twice would still "contain" the line once — saves twice to prove it is per-save rather than one-shot, and asserts the .tscn still exists so the hook is shown to precede the save rather than replace it.

`a_plugin_can_consume_a_viewport_click` asserts the consuming case AND the declining control. It deliberately does **not** pin the post-click selection value in the control: whether (10,10) hits a textureless Sprite2D depends on hit-test geometry, and pinning it would make the test fail for reasons unrelated to plugin dispatch. `consumed_by` appears exactly once in the whole server — only in the consume branch — so its absence is sufficient proof the editor's own path ran.

Items (c) overlay draw, (e) state/layout, (h) `api_select_multi`, most of (d) (`_save_external_data`, `_get_unsaved_status`, `_build`, `_get_breakpoints`, `_clear`, `_run_scene`), the 3D input forward, and (f) the main-screen tab. ## Item (h) + `_save_external_data` (EmeraldIsland)

### 🔑 The doc XML changed where one of these goes
I was about to put `_save_external_data` next to `_apply_changes` — one tidy call site before the write. The doc is explicit and **opposite**:

- `_apply_changes` — "called when the editor is **about to save**… to apply any pending state changes"
- `_save_external_data` — "called **after** the editor saves the project or when it's closed… to save edited external scenes/resources"

So they straddle the write: apply → `atomic_write` → external. Pairing them would have looked neat and put one on the wrong side of the file being written, which is unobservable in a smoke test and wrong for any plugin that actually writes companion resources. Reading the description, not just the method list, is what caught it.

### Item (h): multi-select dispatch — **two** exit paths, not one
`api_select_multi` sets the selection and dispatched to nobody, so a plugin's panel went stale the moment a user extended a selection. It has **two** exit paths and both needed it:
1. the explicit `node_ids` array, and
2. the `mode` path (`add`/`remove`/`toggle`/`range`) — which is what ctrl-click and shift-click actually send.

Fixing only the first would pass any test that used the array form. The test exercises both and counts dispatches, so a one-path fix fails it.

Both dispatch on the FIRST selected object (Godot's rule); an empty selection passes `None`, which hides every plugin via `_make_visible(false)`.

`save_external_data_runs_after_apply_changes` asserts the ORDER by log position, not just that both fired — the ordering is the whole contract, and two hooks in the wrong order still both "appear in the logs". DELIVERED: item (d)'s headline virtual `_build` gating Play, and item (e)'s per-scene `_get_state`/`_set_state` round-trip.
DESIGN NOTE — `_build` is the INVERSE of dispatch_plugin_virtual's stop_at_first_claim, not another case of it. That helper stops at the first TRUTHY return; `_build` must stop at the first FALSE one ('the run is aborted immediately, so this also prevents all other plugins' _build methods from running'). Reusing it would have let one approving plugin short-circuit the sweep and skip a later refuser — a veto silently ignored. Hence plugin_build_refusal is its own function. title: GDScript: capture enclosing locals and self into lambdas at creation time
description:
[audit-key: gdscript/gdscript-lambda] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/gdscript/gdscript_lambda_callable.cpp + gdscript_function.h (GDScriptFunction::captures, GDScriptLambdaCallable holds captured Variants); doc @GDScript.xml "Lambda functions"

**Godot classes:** Callable, @GDScript

**Patina today:**
- [gdscript] engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:3409-3416 builds `CallableRef::Lambda { params, body }` — params and an Arc'd statement list ONLY, no captured environment and no `self`. `CallableRef` in engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/variant.rs:30-36 has no capture field. Invocation (interpreter.rs:11238-11263) pushes a fresh scope onto whatever environment is current at CALL time and binds only the parameters. `grep -rn 'capture' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/*.rs` finds only coroutine/backtrace uses, nothing about lambda captures. Consequence: the canonical Godot pattern `for i in n: cbs.append(func(): total += i)` or `tween.tween_callback(func(): label.text = msg)` reads whatever `i`/`msg` happens to be in scope when the callable is finally invoked (typically undefined → RuntimeError, or a stale value). Lambda parameter defaults are also unsupported (params carry no defaults).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/variant.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: a lambda captures every enclosing local it references BY VALUE at the moment the `func(...)` expression evaluates, plus `self`; modules/gdscript/gdscript_lambda_callable.cpp stores those captures in the GDScriptLambdaCallable and rebinds them on every invocation, so a lambda stored in an Array/Timer/Tween/signal connection still sees the values from where it was written.\n\nPatina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:3409-3416 constructs `CallableRef::Lambda { params, body }` with no environment snapshot; engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/variant.rs:30-36 has no capture field; engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:11238-11263 invokes the body against the CURRENT environment with only the parameters bound. `grep -rn 'capture' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/` shows no lambda-capture code.\n\nImplementation approach: extend `CallableRef::Lambda` in engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/variant.rs with `captures: Arc<HashMap<String, Variant>>` and `self_id: u64`. At lambda construction (interpreter.rs:3409) walk the body's free identifiers (a small `collect_free_idents(&[Stmt]) -> HashSet<String>` helper over the existing `Expr`/`Stmt` trees in parser.rs) and snapshot each one that resolves in the current `Environment` plus the current `self_instance` properties. In `invoke_callable` (interpreter.rs:11238) push a scope seeded with the captures BEFORE binding parameters, and restore `self_instance` from `self_id`. Add lambda parameter defaults by reusing `FuncParam`'s default expression slot.\n\nWiring requirement: prove it through a stored-then-later-invoked callable driven by the SceneTree — a lambda connected to a node signal or passed to `create_tween().tween_callback(...)` inside `_ready`, invoked on a later frame of the runner loop.

**Prove it:** A scene-attached script whose `_ready` does `var msg := \"hi\"` then connects a node signal to `func(): self.result = msg` produces `result == \"hi\"` when the signal is emitted on a LATER frame of the runner loop (not the same call frame); and a loop that appends three lambdas each capturing the loop variable yields 0/1/2 when invoked afterwards. (test: `gds_lambda_capture`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test gds_lambda_capture`.

comments.text:
## Triage note from EmeraldIsland — root cause of the 2nd verify failure is FOUND and is one line

Not retrying (bead is parked). Recording the diagnosis so triage does not have to rediscover it.

### Where it stops

`hits == 0` after the emit means the connected lambda never ran. Dispatch bails BEFORE reaching the new intercept:

  gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs, `call_script_method`:
      if !script.has_method(method) { self.scripts.insert(node_id, script); return None; }

  gdscene/src/scripting.rs:290 (the `ScriptInstance` impl `call_script_method` actually calls):
      fn has_method(&self, name: &str) -> bool { self.instance.class_def.methods.contains_key(name) }

The synthetic connection name `__lambda_connection_N` is deliberately NOT in `class_def.methods`, so `has_method` answers false and the emit path returns early. `Interpreter::call_instance_method` — where the intercept lives — is never entered.

### The fix

`has_method` must also answer true for a registered lambda-connection name. `LAMBDA_CONNECTIONS` is private to gdscript-interop, so expose a predicate there and consult it in gdscene:

1. gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs — next to the existing private `lambda_connection`:
       pub fn is_lambda_connection_name(name: &str) -> bool { lambda_connection(name).is_some() }
2. gdscene/src/scripting.rs — BOTH `has_method` bodies (the inherent one at :160 and the trait impl at :290):
       self.instance.class_def.methods.contains_key(name)
           || gdscript_interop::interpreter::is_lambda_connection_name(name)

Note it is a free fn, not a method: the registry is a thread-local, so no `&self` is needed.

### State of the rest

Everything else in the chain is verified working by this run:
- the Rust compiles (both failures were runtime, not build);
- `connect()` with a lambda no longer raises — `ran == true` proves `_ready` ran to completion, which it could not do while `callable_target` returned None;
- the fixture parses (the 1st failure, `unexpected token +=`, is fixed — a single-line lambda body is ONE EXPRESSION, so `func(): self.x = v` is not valid; the fixture uses `func(): self._note_msg(msg)`).

Unverified beyond that point: whether `self` resolves inside the lambda body and whether `resume_with_instance_self` writes the mutation back. Those are what the two tests assert once dispatch reaches them.

### Separate gap this surfaced (not this bead)

A single-line lambda body is parsed as one expression with an implicit return (parser.rs, `Token::Func`), so a statement body — `func(): self.result = msg`, which is this bead's own literal acceptance wording and is legal GDScript — does not parse. The multi-line `parse_block()` branch exists but has no fixture anywhere in the repo. Worth its own bead.

title: Register CheckButton and CenterContainer in ClassDB — both render and lay out but cannot be created in the editor
description:
[audit-key: gui/gui-controls-checkbutton-centercontainer-registration] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json: CheckButton : Button (no own members; the toggle-switch themed variant of CheckBox) and CenterContainer : Container (use_top_left, bool default false); upstream/godot/scene/gui/check_button.cpp, scene/gui/center_container.cpp

**Godot classes:** CheckButton, CenterContainer

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-0] Both are fully implemented on the gdscene side: CheckButton at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs:825 (control-class list), :865 (button list), :2756, and drawn at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs:67, :1467 (`"CheckBox" | "CheckButton" =>` draw arm), with theme styleboxes at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/theme.rs:593. CenterContainer at control.rs:848 (container list), :1737 (`"CenterContainer" => arrange_center(...)`), :2305, control_render.rs:80. Neither is in ClassDB: grep of registered names from /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs shows CheckBox, Button, BaseButton, OptionButton, MenuButton, Container, MarginContainer, GridContainer, HBoxContainer, VBoxContainer, ScrollContainer, PanelContainer, TabContainer, SubViewportContainer, Split/HSplit/VSplitContainer — but no CheckButton and no CenterContainer. Because the editor's Create Node dialog enumerates `class_db::get_class_list()` (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/create_dialog.rs:1050, :934) neither can be added to a scene from the editor, and `node.is_class("Button")`/`is_class("Container")` fall back to hardcoded name lists (control.rs:848-865) rather than the inheritance chain.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/create_dialog.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

[audit-key: gui-controls/checkbutton-centercontainer-registration] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** `CheckButton : Button` — no own members; it is the toggle-switch themed variant of CheckBox, drawn with the `checked`/`unchecked` icons and the `normal`/`pressed`/`hover`/`disabled` styleboxes registered for the `CheckButton` theme type (`upstream/godot/scene/gui/check_button.cpp`, and the theme entries in `scene/theme/default_theme.cpp`). `CenterContainer : Container` with `use_top_left` (bool, default false — when true children are centered around the container's top-left instead of inside it) (`upstream/godot/scene/gui/center_container.cpp`).

**Patina today:** both behave correctly at runtime but neither exists in ClassDB. CheckButton: `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs:825` (control-class list), `:865` (BUTTON_CLASSES), `:2756`; drawn at `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs:67` and `:1467` (`"CheckBox" | "CheckButton" =>` arm); theme styleboxes at `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/theme.rs:593`. CenterContainer: `control.rs:848` (container list), `:1737` (`"CenterContainer" => arrange_center(tree, &children, total)`), `:2305`, `control_render.rs:80`. But the registered-name set extracted from `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` contains CheckBox, Button, BaseButton, OptionButton, MenuButton, Container, MarginContainer, GridContainer, H/VBoxContainer, ScrollContainer, PanelContainer, TabContainer, SubViewportContainer and the Split containers — and neither CheckButton nor CenterContainer. Consequences: the editor's Create Node dialog enumerates `class_db::get_class_list()` (`engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/create_dialog.rs:1050`, `:934`), so neither node can be added to a scene from the editor at all; and `is_class("Button")`/`is_class("Container")` only work via the hardcoded fallback lists in `control.rs:848-865` instead of the real inheritance chain.

**Implement:** register `CheckButton` with parent `Button` and `CenterContainer` with parent `Container` (property `use_top_left`, default false) in `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` next to the existing CheckBox (`:7230`) and MarginContainer (`:7263`) entries. Honour `use_top_left` in `arrange_center` (`engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs:2305`). Then delete the now-redundant hardcoded membership so `control.rs`'s container/button detection resolves through the ClassDB chain (keeping the list only as the documented fallback for an unpopulated ClassDB).

**Wiring requirement:** both must appear in the editor's Create Node dialog under their correct base types, instantiate into the scene tree, persist to `.tscn`, and then draw/lay out through the existing canvas pipeline; `node.is_class("Button")` on a CheckButton and `is_class("Container")` on a CenterContainer must resolve through ClassDB inheritance.

**Prove it:** assert the Create-dialog class list contains both under Button/Container; instantiate a CenterContainer with a fixed-size child and assert the child's rect is centered (and, with `use_top_left = true`, centered on the top-left corner); instantiate a CheckButton, assert `is_class("Button")`/`is_class("BaseButton")` via ClassDB, click it and assert `toggled`/`pressed` fires and the drawn glyph state flips.

**Prove it:** CheckButton (parent Button) and CenterContainer (parent Container, with use_top_left) are ClassDB-registered, both appear in the editor Create Node dialog and instantiate into a scene, CenterContainer centers a child (and respects use_top_left), and CheckButton resolves is_class("Button") through ClassDB while still emitting pressed/toggled (test: `checkbutton_centercontainer_registered_and_behave`)
acceptance_criteria: CheckButton (parent Button) and CenterContainer (parent Container, with use_top_left) are ClassDB-registered, both appear in the editor Create Node dialog and instantiate into a scene, CenterContainer centers a child (and respects use_top_left), and CheckButton resolves is_class("Button") through ClassDB while still emitting pressed/toggled (test: `checkbutton_centercontainer_registered_and_behave`)

title: Implement the Range control family: Slider/HSlider/VSlider, SpinBox, TextureProgressBar
description:

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/gui/{slider,spin_box,texture_progress_bar}.cpp; doc/classes/{Slider,SpinBox,TextureProgressBar}.xml; extension_api.json Slider(inherits=Range,10 methods,5 props), SpinBox(Range,18,8), TextureProgressBar(Range,26,16)

- [sweep-6] NOT registered anywhere: `rg -o 'ClassRegistration::new\("([A-Za-z0-9_]+)"\)'` across all `crates/**/src/**` yields 638 names; `Slider`, `HSlider`, `VSlider`, `SpinBox`, `TextureProgressBar`, `ScrollBar`, `HScrollBar`, `VScrollBar` are all absent (only `Range` at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:7201 and `ProgressBar` are present). The default theme DOES ship their styleboxes (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/theme.rs:570 `("SpinBox","normal")`, :587-589 `("HScrollBar","scroll")`,`("HSlider","slider")`,`("VSlider","slider")`) and hit-testing accepts them (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs:832-838 CONTROL_HIT_CLASSES lists HSlider/VSlider/SpinBox/ProgressBar/ScrollBar) — so an authored slider is clickable and focusable (control.rs:2751 FOCUSABLE_BY_DEFAULT) but renders nothing and has no grab/drag/value behavior. No `fn *slider*`/`spin_box`/`texture_progress`/`radial_fill` implementation exists: `rg -in 'slider|spin_box|spinbox|texture_progress|radial_fill' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdrender2d/src` only hits SliderJoint3D physics.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/theme.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

**Godot ground truth:** `Slider` (abstract, `Range` subclass) with `editable`, `scrollable`, `tick_count`, `ticks_on_borders`, drag-grab on the grabber and page-step on the track (`upstream/godot/scene/gui/slider.cpp`); `H/VSlider` differ only by axis + theme item. `SpinBox` (`Range`) with `prefix`/`suffix`/`custom_arrow_step`/`alignment`/`editable`/`select_all_on_focus`/`update_on_text_changed`, an embedded LineEdit and up/down arrow buttons (`spin_box.cpp`). `TextureProgressBar` (`Range`) with `fill_mode` (9 modes incl. 4 radial), `texture_under/over/progress`, `tint_*`, `radial_initial_angle`, `radial_center_offset`, `nine_patch_stretch` + `stretch_margin_*` (`texture_progress_bar.cpp`). Signatures: `extension_api.json` Slider 10 methods/5 props, SpinBox 18/8, TextureProgressBar 26/16.

**Patina today:** none of these are in ClassDB — the full registration list (`rg -o 'ClassRegistration::new\("([A-Za-z0-9_]+)"\)' crates/**/src/**` = 638 names) contains `Range` (class_db.rs:7201) and `ProgressBar` but no `Slider`/`HSlider`/`VSlider`/`SpinBox`/`TextureProgressBar`/`ScrollBar`. `control_render.rs:1039 draw_control` matches on exact class name and has no arm for any of them (grep count 0). **Implement:** register the classes with Godot's property defaults in `class_db.rs` (Slider abstract under Range, HSlider/VSlider under Slider, SpinBox under Range, TextureProgressBar under Range). Add a `slider`/`spinbox`/`texture_progress` behavior module under `crates/gdscene/src/` holding grabber geometry, page/step arithmetic, tick positions, radial and nine-patch fill geometry. Add `draw_control` arms in `control_render.rs` that pull the existing theme styleboxes (`slider`, `grabber`, `grabber_area`, `normal`, `up`/`down`) plus the texture properties. **Wiring requirement:** a `.tscn` containing an `HSlider`, a `SpinBox` and a `TextureProgressBar` loaded by the SceneTree must produce draw commands in the runner's `render_control_tree` pass, and a drag on the slider grabber routed through `control::click_at_point`/drag must move `value` and emit `value_changed` to a connected script Callable.

**Prove it:** A .tscn with HSlider, SpinBox and TextureProgressBar loads with all three resolving through ClassDB to `Range` -> `Control`, each renders draw commands in the runner's control render pass using the default theme styleboxes, and dragging the HSlider grabber to 75% of its track sets `value` to 75.0 and emits exactly one `value_changed(75.0)` to a connected script callback (test: `range_control_family_renders_and_drags`)
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with HSlider, SpinBox and TextureProgressBar loads with all three resolving through ClassDB to `Range` -> `Control`, each renders draw commands in the runner's control render pass using the default theme styleboxes, and dragging the HSlider grabber to 75% of its track sets `value` to 75.0 and emits exactly one `value_changed(75.0)` to a connected script callback (test: `range_control_family_renders_and_drags`)

comments.text:
BronzeLake — triage note. NOT retrying (respecting the park). The second failure is diagnosed and the fix is one line in the TEST FIXTURE, not in the implementation.

STATUS: exit 100 (test panic), so everything COMPILES. 4 of the 5 tests that ran passed. The single failure is the acceptance test:

    left: Some(100.0)   right: Some(75.0)

ROOT CAUSE. `drag_slider_to_local` reads the control's extent via `control::get_size`, which (control.rs:466) reads the stored `size` PROPERTY and returns Vector2::ZERO when it is absent:

    tree.get_node(node_id).map(|n| match n.get_property("size") {
        Variant::Vector2(v) => v, _ => Vector2::ZERO })

My fixture sets only anchors and offsets — `apply_anchor_preset` + `set_offset_right/bottom` — and `set_offset_right` (control.rs:423) writes ONLY `offset_right`. Nothing derives `size` from offsets. So size was (0, 0), and the arithmetic follows exactly:

    track_length((0,0), Horizontal) = max(0 - 10, EPSILON) = EPSILON
    ratio = (72.5 - 5) / EPSILON = enormous -> clamp(0,1) -> 1.0
    value = 0 + 100 * 1.0 = 100.0

which is precisely the observed `Some(100.0)`. The implementation is correct; it was handed a zero-sized control.

THE FIX (one line, in the fixture only): in `control_node` in crates/gdscene/tests/range_control_family_renders_and_drags.rs, add

    control::set_size(&mut tree, id, Vector2::new(w, h));

`control::set_size` already exists at control.rs:459 and writes the `size` property directly. Keep the anchor/offset calls or drop them; they are not what `get_size` reads.

A REAL QUESTION FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP, worth more than the fixture fix. `render_control_tree` reads the SAME `control::get_size` (control_render.rs:473). So if nothing in the runtime populates the `size` property, a production slider is zero-sized on the render path too, not just in my fixture — every Range control would draw into a zero rect and every drag would clamp to max. I did not chase where (or whether) layout writes `size` back; `gdeditor::control_binding::invalidate_layout` looked like the place and does not obviously do it. If it turns out nothing writes it, that is a Control-layout bug well outside this bead and should get its own, because it would affect every Control, not just the Range family.

UNCHANGED AND STILL TRUE from my completion report: the registration of all five classes (defaults extracted by script from doc/classes/<Class>.xml), the shared `range_controls` geometry module, the four draw arms, and the VSlider inversion / `step` override / change-only-emission traps each pinned by their own test. The three geometry tests that need no SceneTree (`a_vertical_slider_has_its_minimum_at_the_bottom` among them) are unaffected by the size bug.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
BronzeBridge — picked this up, applied the fixture fix, and ANSWERED the open question.

1. DIAGNOSIS CONFIRMED, implementation untouched. My diff is 121 insertions in the test file and zero lines of implementation. BronzeLake's arithmetic was exact: get_size (control.rs:466) returns Vector2::ZERO for an absent `size` property, track_length collapses to EPSILON, and the drag clamps to max = 100.0.

2. THE OPEN QUESTION IS ANSWERED: THERE IS NO PRODUCTION LAYOUT BUG. Nothing needs its own bead.

`control::resolve_control_layout` (control.rs:1291) IS the offset -> size derivation, and it ends with `set_position` + `set_size` (control.rs:1360-1361). The render pass calls it: control_render.rs:472, `control::resolve_control_layout(tree, node_id, parent_size)`, guarded only by `!parent_is_container` (a container-managed child gets its rect from fit_child_in_rect instead). gdeditor/src/control_binding.rs:51 calls it too.

So a production slider is correctly sized on the render path. This is also exactly why 4 of 5 tests passed and only the drag failed: `draw()` goes through render_control_tree, which derives `size` itself, while `drag_slider_to_local` was called directly on a tree where nothing had.

3. THE FIX I APPLIED IS resolve_control_layout, NOT set_size. Both work, but calling the same function the render pass calls keeps the fixture honest — the drag is now measured against the rect production actually computes, and the anchor/offset setup stays meaningful instead of being dead code beside a hardcoded size. With the TopLeft preset every anchor is 0.0, so the parent size cancels and the rect is exactly (w, h); a debug_assert_eq! in the fixture pins that, so if layout ever stops deriving size this fails loudly in the fixture rather than silently as a bogus value 100.0.

Hand-traced: track = 100 - 10 = 90, ratio = (72.5 - 5)/90 = 0.75 exactly (all values binary-exact), value = 0 + 100*0.75 = 75.0, step defaults to 1.0 (control.rs get_range_step) so the snap is a no-op, page = 0 so effective_max = 100. Second drag: old == 75.0, so set_range_value returns false -> None.

4. I ADDED THE MISSING HALF OF THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION. The criterion says the drag must "emit exactly one value_changed(75.0) to a connected script callback". The existing test asserts the RETURN VALUE of drag_slider_to_local, which pins the arithmetic but bypasses the input path entirely and cannot show any callback was ever invoked. A slider that moves silently is as broken as one that does not move.

New test `a_dragged_slider_emits_value_changed_to_a_connected_callable` connects a recorder Callable to `value_changed` and pushes a real InputEvent::MouseButton through SceneTree::push_input, which reaches scene_tree.rs:4317 `self.emit_signal(hit, "value_changed", ...)` via drag_range_control. It asserts value == 75.0 and the callback received exactly [75.0], then re-presses the same point and asserts nothing further is emitted.

The slider is deliberately placed at (20, 30), NOT the origin: drag_range_control converts viewport space to control-local via get_global_position, and a control at (0,0) makes the two spaces identical, so the test would pass whether or not that conversion happened.

Unchanged and still true: registration of all five classes, the range_controls geometry module, the four draw arms, and the VSlider-inversion / step / change-only-emission traps.

title: Slider/ScrollBar family: unregistered, never drawn, and the Range value model has no runtime caller
description:
[audit-key: gui/gui-controls-slider-scrollbar-family] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/gui/slider.cpp, scene/gui/scroll_bar.cpp, scene/gui/range.cpp; doc/classes/HSlider.xml, VSlider.xml, Slider.xml, HScrollBar.xml, VScrollBar.xml, ScrollBar.xml, Range.xml

**Godot classes:** HScrollBar, HSlider, VScrollBar, VSlider, Slider, ScrollBar

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-2] ClassDB: `Range` IS registered (class_db.rs:7214 declares its `value_changed` signal) but Slider, HSlider, VSlider, ScrollBar, HScrollBar, VScrollBar are ALL absent — verified against the full string-literal dump of /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs. Rendering: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs:42-87 `const CONTROL_CLASSES` (the draw-pass membership list) contains ProgressBar, CheckBox, ItemList, TabBar, Separator/HSeparator/VSeparator ... and NO slider or scrollbar entry; `rg '"HSlider"|"HScrollBar"' control_render.rs` returns nothing, so a standalone HSlider/HScrollBar node never draws. Value model is dormant: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs:3044 `pub fn set_range_value(...)` whose doc says "the caller emits the `value_changed` signal in that case (Slider drag, SpinBox typing, etc.)" has ZERO callers outside tests — `rg -n 'set_range_value' -g '*.rs' crates/` returns only the definition at control.rs:3044 plus lines 3424/3427/3429/3431/3442/3450, all inside `mod tests` (the test module starts at control.rs:3410), plus crates/gdscene/tests/range_slider_spinbox_value_changed.rs which computes a fake `dragged_to_55_percent` number rather than pushing an event. Corroborating: `rg -n '"value_changed"' -g '*.rs' crates/ | grep -v /tests/` returns exactly ONE line — class_db.rs:7214, the signal DECLARATION — so nothing in the engine ever emits it. Theme entries exist but have no consumer for a standalone node: gdscene/src/theme.rs:585-588 registers ("HScrollBar","scroll"), ("VScrollBar","scroll"), ("HSlider","slider"), ("VSlider","slider") styleboxes. Hit-test/focus lists DO include them (control.rs:832-838 CONTROL_HIT_CLASSES, control.rs:2761-2762 FOCUSABLE_BY_DEFAULT), so the node is clickable and tab-focusable but invisible and inert.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/theme.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot's Range subclass tree is Range -> Slider -> {HSlider, VSlider} and Range -> ScrollBar -> {HScrollBar, VScrollBar}. Patina registers Range in ClassDB but none of the six subclasses (verified against the complete string-literal set of engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs).

Three distinct failures compound:

(1) NOT REGISTERED. ClassDB.class_exists("HSlider") is false, ClassDB.instantiate("HSlider") fails, the editor Create Node dialog cannot offer them, and inheritance queries only work through the hardcoded fallback lists.

(2) NEVER DRAWN. control_render.rs:42-87 CONTROL_CLASSES — the membership list that gates the draw arm — has no slider or scrollbar entry. gdscene/src/theme.rs:585-588 already registers the "slider"/"scroll" styleboxes for all four concrete classes, so the theme data exists with no consumer. A .tscn containing an HSlider renders nothing.

(3) VALUE MODEL UNWIRED. control.rs:3044 set_range_value() exists with correct step-snapping and [min, max-page] clamping, and its own doc comment names its intended callers ("Slider drag, SpinBox typing") — but it has zero callers outside test modules. And `value_changed` appears exactly once in non-test source: class_db.rs:7214, the signal declaration. Nothing in the engine emits it. So dragging a slider grabber, paging a scrollbar, or arrow-keying a focused slider changes nothing and notifies no one.

Work: register Slider (abstract), ScrollBar (abstract), HSlider, VSlider, HScrollBar, VScrollBar with Godot's properties (Slider: editable, scrollable, tick_count, ticks_on_borders; ScrollBar: custom_step; plus inherited Range min_value/max_value/step/page/value/exp_edit/rounded/allow_greater/allow_lesser). Add draw arms in control_render.rs for the slider track+grabber and the scrollbar track+grabber sized from Range page/max (control_render.rs:508-590 already does exactly this for ScrollContainer's internal bars — reuse it). Route _gui_input mouse-press/drag and focused arrow keys into set_range_value() and emit `value_changed`.

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `PopupMenu` (upstream/godot/scene/gui/popup_menu.cpp) is a Popup<-Window that draws above everything, grabs input while open, highlights on hover, activates on release, and emits `id_pressed(id)`/`index_pressed(idx)`; it supports checkable/radio/multistate items, separators with labels, submenus opened on hover, accelerators and `Shortcut`s, `hide_on_item_selection`/`hide_on_checkable_item_selection`, and incremental search. `MenuBar` (menu_bar.cpp) draws a title strip from its child PopupMenus and switches menus on hover while one is open. `MenuButton` (menu_button.cpp) opens its child PopupMenu below itself on press. `OptionButton` (option_button.cpp) calls `show_popup()` on press and emits `item_selected(idx)` when an entry is chosen.\n\nPatina current state: both logic layers exist and neither is reachable. engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/popup.rs (items, separators, checkables, `activate_item` -> id) has zero non-test callers; engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/menu.rs (`MenuBarModel` open/hover state) has zero callers at all — its own doc comment at menu.rs:8-13 records that it was written to fix exactly this for PopupMenu and then repeated the pattern. `SceneTree::gui_input_stage` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:3248) has no popup branch, and `item_views::item_view_click` returns false for OptionButton at item_views.rs:770-774 with a TODO comment.\n\nImplementation approach: add an open-popup slot to SceneTree next to `hovered_control`/`gui_press_target` (scene_tree.rs, near line 3350) holding `(owner NodeId, PopupMenu model, screen rect)`. comments.text:
## Popup geometry landed in the model; the wiring is lease-blocked. Completion HELD.

### The bead's claims are ACCURATE — unusual, and worth saying
I measured before building, as several recent beads had stale descriptions. This one checks out: `popup::` has exactly one hit workspace-wide (a doc comment in `menu.rs:8`), `menu::` has **zero** callers, and `gui_input_stage` has no popup branch. Both logic layers really are unreachable.

### Delivered (in the free file, `popup.rs`)
The geometry the wiring needs, which the bead's own approach calls for ("map y to an item index using a shared row-height constant"):

- **`PopupMenu::ROW_HEIGHT`** — ONE constant shared by the hit-test and the draw pass. If the height used to map a click differs from the one used to lay rows out, every click below the first row lands on the wrong item, and it looks correct until you click the last one.
- **`height()`** — panel height for the current items.
- **`index_at(local_y)`** — the row under an offset, `None` outside the panel.
- **`is_activatable(idx)`** — the activation rule *without* mutating.

⚠️ **`index_at` deliberately answers for separators and disabled rows.** Refusing them would silently turn a click on a disabled row into a click on whatever sits *underneath* the popup — the opposite of modal. Activation is the gate, and `activate_item` already returns `None` for disabled / separator / submenu rows (that acceptance clause is satisfied at the model level today).

⚠️ **`is_activatable` must not mutate**, and a test pins that: asking whether a checkbox can be activated must not toggle it. `activate_item` toggles as a side effect, so the read-only twin is what the input layer needs when deciding whether a release should close the popup.

⚠️ Divergence recorded in the code: Godot derives row height from the theme and draws separators SHORTER than normal rows. Patina has no popup theme, so rows are uniform. When theme metrics arrive, `index_at` and the draw pass must change **together**.

### Blocked: the actual wiring
`scene_tree.rs` — which needs the open-popup slot and the modal branch in `gui_input_stage` — is leased to BronzeLake until 09:50. `control_render.rs` is free, but a draw arm with no open-popup state to read would be inert, so it waits for the same file.

### Completion HELD, deliberately
Every `-p gdscene` target compiles the whole crate, and `gdscene/src` was being edited **26 seconds** before I checked (09:03:06, with `scene_tree.rs` at 09:00:18). That in-flight state is what produced the E0308 that reopened pat-s3rrv.57 and .66 at 07:58. I am not spending a verify cycle into an active sweep; I will report once `gdscene/src` goes quiet.

title: RichTextLabel: register the real class surface and extend BBCode to url/img/font/outline/bgcolor/indent/list/align
description:
[audit-key: gui-controls/gui-richtextlabel] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/gui/rich_text_label.cpp + doc/classes/RichTextLabel.xml (bbcode_enabled, text, ~40 push_* methods, append_text, add_text/add_image, `meta_clicked`/`meta_hover_started`, visible_characters/visible_ratio + VisibleCharactersBehavior, fit_content, scroll_active/scroll_following, threaded, selection_enabled, tab_size, get_parsed_text)

**Godot classes:** RichTextLabel, RichTextEffect, CharFXTransform

**Patina today:**
- [gui-controls] engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:7054-7056 registers RichTextLabel as `ClassRegistration::new("RichTextLabel").parent("Control")` — no properties, no methods, no signals. The BBCode parser at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs:695-791 recognises only `[color=...]`/`[/color]` and the six built-in effect tags; its own doc comment (control_render.rs:690-694) says `[b]/[i]/[u]/[s]` are stripped and "Unknown `[...]` tags are dropped". `grep -rn 'append_text\|push_color\|push_bold\|add_text\|meta_clicked\|visible_characters\|visible_ratio\|fit_content\|scroll_following' --include=*.rs crates/` returns zero hits outside the unrelated JSON `get_parsed_text` in gdscript-interop. Script-defined `RichTextEffect` dispatch is documented as impossible in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/char_fx.rs:19-33.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/char_fx.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `RichTextLabel` (upstream/godot/scene/gui/rich_text_label.cpp) declares `bbcode_enabled`, `text`, `fit_content`, `scroll_active`, `scroll_following`, `selection_enabled`, `visible_characters` + `visible_characters_behavior`, `visible_ratio`, `tab_size`, `threaded`, `custom_effects`, plus `append_text`, `add_text`, `add_image`, `newline`, `clear`, `get_parsed_text`, `get_total_character_count` and the whole push/pop stack (`push_bold`, `push_italics`, `push_underline`, `push_strikethrough`, `push_color`, `push_bgcolor`, `push_fgcolor`, `push_outline_size`, `push_outline_color`, `push_font`, `push_font_size`, `push_paragraph`, `push_indent`, `push_list`, `push_table`/`push_cell`, `push_meta`, `push_hint`, `push_dropcap`, `push_customfx`, `pop`, `pop_all`). BBCode tags map onto those, and `[url=...]` emits `meta_clicked`/`meta_hover_started`.\n\nPatina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:7054-7056 registers a bare `RichTextLabel` under Control with no properties, methods or signals, so `has_signal("meta_clicked")` is false and no property round-trips through the inspector. The parser at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs:695-791 handles only `[color]` plus the six native effect tags; its doc comment at control_render.rs:690-694 states that `[b]/[i]/[u]/[s]` and unknown tags are simply stripped. `append_text`, the push/pop API, `meta_clicked`, `visible_characters`, `visible_ratio`, `fit_content` and `scroll_following` do not exist anywhere.\n\nImplementation approach: fill in the class registration in class_db.rs with the properties above and the `meta_clicked`/`meta_hover_started`/`meta_hover_ended`/`finished` signals. Extend `parse_bbcode` in control_render.rs from a colour-only stack into a general span attribute stack (bold/italic/underline/strikethrough, bgcolor/fgcolor, font_size, outline size+colour, indent level, list bullet/number, paragraph alignment `[center]`/`[right]`/`[fill]`, `[url=...]` meta, `[img]`), and give `TextSpan` those fields so the draw loop can honour them. Add a `meta` hit region list so `gui_input_stage` can emit `meta_clicked` for a click inside a `[url]` span. Implement `visible_characters`/`visible_ratio` as a trim on the emitted glyph count and `fit_content` as a minimum-size contribution. Route `append_text`/`add_text`/`clear`/`push_*`/`pop` through engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs alongside the existing LineEdit routes (scripting.rs:1882-1900), building the same span list the parser produces.\n\nWiring requirement: `.tscn` text or a script `append_text` -> spans -> `control_draw_items` -> Play-frame draw items, and a click on a `[url]` span -> `push_input` -> `gui_input_stage` -> `meta_clicked` in a GDScript handler.

**Prove it:** A .tscn RichTextLabel with `bbcode_enabled = true` and text `[b]bold[/b] [center]mid[/center] [url=go]link[/url]` produces draw items where the "bold" run carries the bold attribute, "mid" is horizontally centred in the rect, and clicking the "link" run's rect emits `meta_clicked("go")` to a connected GDScript handler. ## STALE — word wrapping is DONE

The remaining-scope note says "NOT done: word wrapping ... the gap is that richtext_placements ignores
autowrap_mode, and the fix is to REUSE break_lines_word". At HEAD that is implemented:
`control_render.rs:1934` calls `gdrender2d::text_layout::break_lines_word(&widths, space_w, rect.size.x)`
inside the richtext path, `autowrap_mode` is read at :1829 (defaulting to 3, matching the ClassDB
default), and the word splitter accumulates pieces ACROSS run boundaries carrying `(run_index, piece,
piece_start)` — which is exactly the char_offset preservation the note asked for so `[wave]` does not
desync. Strike that item.

## THE REAL GAP NOBODY HAS RECORDED: RichTextLabel has ZERO methods in ClassDB

Measured against `doc/classes/RichTextLabel.xml`:

    properties  32/32   ✓
    signals      4/4    ✓
    methods      0/78   ✗

So `ClassDB.class_get_method_list("RichTextLabel")` is empty for a class whose whole point is its method
API, and `class_has_method("RichTextLabel", "append_text")` answers false for a call the engine services
today. The bead's acceptance names `append_text` explicitly.

**FIVE methods are implemented AND script-dispatched right now** — all guarded by
`is_rich_text_label` in `gdscene/src/scripting.rs:2943+`. Register exactly these, with the arities and
qualifiers taken from the doc XML:

```rust
.method(MethodInfo::new("append_text", 1))
.method(MethodInfo::new("add_text", 1))
.method(MethodInfo::new("clear", 0))
.method(MethodInfo::new("get_parsed_text", 0).const_method())
.method(MethodInfo::new("get_total_character_count", 0).const_method())
```

⚠️ **DO NOT register the other 73.** Nothing implements them, and `class_has_method` answering true for
a method that raises on call is the same lie inverted — the shape this audit keeps finding.

⚠️ **AND DO NOT TRUST A BARE NAME GREP HERE.** Searching the scene/script layers for the 78 documented
names returns EIGHT hits, but three are other classes' methods: `select_all` is guarded by
`is_text_input` (LineEdit/TextEdit) at scripting.rs:3007, not by `is_rich_text_label`, and `deselect` /
`get_selected_text` are the same family. Only the five above are behind the RichTextLabel guard. A
name-collision over-report is exactly how unbacked methods get registered by accident.

## ALSO CORRECTED: `[fgcolor]` is NOT an alias for `[color]`

I was about to implement it as one — it is the cheapest-looking remaining tag and the span model already
has a colour stack. It is not: `RichTextLabel::_find_fgcolor` (rich_text_label.cpp:3693-3705) walks the
item parent chain and defaults to **transparent** `Color(0,0,0,0)`, i.e. it is a separate overlay
concept drawn over the glyphs, not the glyph colour. Implementing it as an alias would have silently
changed text colour where Godot draws an overlay. It needs per-run rect draw support, the same blast
radius as `[bgcolor]`.

EmeraldIsland — triage note for the park. NOT a retry; leaving this bead alone as instructed.

## The park was earned by TWO pre-existing red tests in one file, neither caused by the reported work

`gdobject/tests/richtextlabel_and_codeedit_carry_godot_properties.rs` had two failing assertions.
nextest cancels on the first failure, so fixing #1 merely revealed #2 and spent the second strike.

**#1 — `codeedit_carries_its_twenty_two_members` (FIXED, and it was red at HEAD).**
`own_count("CodeEdit")` is 24 at HEAD and 24 after my change — identical, so nothing I did moved it.
24 is the CORRECT value: `doc/classes/CodeEdit.xml` documents exactly 24 `<member>` entries. The
assertion and the test's name were simply left behind when someone completed the surface. Corrected
to 24 and renamed.

**#2 — `no_member_is_declared_twice_along_the_chain` (STILL RED, and I believe the TEST is wrong).**

    `clip_contents` appears more than once in RichTextLabel's property list — left: 2, right: 1

This is not a duplicate-by-accident. `clip_contents` is declared SIX times across the file, and every
one of them is deliberate:

    Control          clip_contents = false   (class_db.rs:14168)  <- the base default
    RichTextLabel    clip_contents = true    (:12391)
    ScrollContainer  clip_contents = true    (:12534)
    ItemList         clip_contents = true    (:12590)
    GraphEdit        clip_contents = true    (:13335)
    Tree             clip_contents = true    (:16869)

Those five subclasses OVERRIDE Godot's base default of `false` with `true`, which matches Godot. Our
ClassDB has no separate "override" concept — an override IS a re-declaration — and
`get_property_list` concatenates the chain base-first **without deduping** on purpose, with
`property_get_revert` taking `.next_back()` so the most-derived value wins.

So a property appearing twice along a chain is the DESIGNED representation of an override, and this
test asserts an invariant the design deliberately violates. It will fail for ScrollContainer,
ItemList, GraphEdit and Tree too, for the same reason, the moment anyone adds them to its loop.

⚠️ Do NOT "fix" it by deleting the subclass re-declarations — that would silently revert five widgets
to `clip_contents = false` and change rendering. The test is the thing that is wrong.

Suggested fix for whoever triages: make the assertion tolerate a duplicate whose DEFAULT VALUE
differs from the earlier one (a genuine override) and fail only on an exact repeat, which is the
real defect it was presumably written to catch. That keeps its value while matching how overrides
are modelled.

## Also corrected: an earlier figure of mine on this bead was wrong

I previously reported RichTextLabel at "32/32 properties". The verifier disproved it: the sibling
assertion `own_count("RichTextLabel") == 30` PASSES, so the real own-count is 30 against 32
documented `<member>` entries — RichTextLabel is short 2 properties, not complete. That figure came
from a textual parser over class_db.rs which over-counts; the signal and method figures in the same
report share that provenance and should be re-measured against a running ClassDB before use.

title: Web input: mouse wheel, X-buttons, double-click and pen fields end-to-end into the running game
description:
[audit-key: input/web-pointer-event-coverage] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json .global_enums MouseButton (WHEEL_UP=4, WHEEL_DOWN=5, WHEEL_LEFT=6, WHEEL_RIGHT=7, XBUTTON1=8, XBUTTON2=9) and MouseButtonMask; InputEventMouseButton.factor/double_click/canceled; InputEventMouseMotion.velocity/screen_velocity/pressure/tilt/pen_inverted; upstream/godot/platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_input.js wheel handler

**Godot classes:** InputEventMouseButton, InputEventMouseMotion, InputEventMouse

**Patina today:**
- [input] CONSUMER EXISTS, PRODUCER DOES NOT. `MouseButton::WheelUp/WheelDown` are declared (engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs:288-294) and consumed for ScrollContainer scrolling at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:3332-3340, but: `grep -rn --include='*.rs' "input/wheel|mouse_wheel|\"wheel\"" crates/gdeditor/src/ crates/gdplatform/src/` returns 0; the editor routes are only key_down/key_up/mouse_move/mouse_down/mouse_up/gamepad/midi/clear_frame/mouse_mode/state (editor_server.rs:2518-2537); `WindowEvent` (engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/window.rs:25-52) has no wheel or touch variant. Both mouse-button routes reject anything above 2: editor_server.rs:14356-14362 and :14400-14406 `Some(b) if b <= 2`, and `push_mouse_button_event` (editor_server.rs:14380-14391) maps only 0/1/2. No `double_click` field exists on `InputEvent::MouseButton` (input.rs:489-493); `gdscene::control::double_click_at_point` (control.rs:904) has no caller outside crates/gdscene/tests/item_views_scene_wiring.rs:181. `Input.get_mouse_button_mask` only ORs buttons 1..=3 (interpreter.rs:6838-6852), never XBUTTON masks 128/256. `InputEvent::MouseMotion` (input.rs:495-498) carries only position+relative — no velocity/screen_velocity/pressure/tilt/pen_inverted/button_mask/global_position.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: Godot's web layer turns a `wheel` event into `InputEventMouseButton` with `button_index = MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT` and a `factor` from the normalized delta (deltaMode 0/1/2 must be normalized), turns `mousedown` buttons 3/4 into XBUTTON1/XBUTTON2, sets `double_click` from the platform double-click window, fills `button_mask` from the currently held buttons and `global_position`, and fills `InputEventMouseMotion.velocity`/`screen_velocity` plus pen `pressure`/`tilt`/`pen_inverted` from PointerEvents (upstream/godot/platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_input.js, display_server_web.cpp).\n\nPATINA CURRENT STATE: scroll handling is already implemented and waiting — engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:3332-3340 routes `MouseButton::WheelUp/WheelDown` to ScrollContainer — but nothing ever produces one. There is no `wheel` listener in the served EDITOR_HTML (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs, 0 grep hits), no `/api/runtime/input/mouse_wheel` route (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:2518-2537), and `WindowEvent` (engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/window.rs:25-52) has no wheel variant. Both mouse-button routes hard-reject button > 2 (editor_server.rs:14356 and :14400) and `push_mouse_button_event` (editor_server.rs:14380) maps only left/middle/right. `InputEvent::MouseButton` (engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs:489) has no `double_click`, and `control::double_click_at_point` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs:904) is only ever called from a test. `Input.get_mouse_button_mask` (interpreter.rs:6838) covers only buttons 1..3.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION: (1) add `wheel` + `contextmenu` listeners on the game view in editor_ui.rs, normalizing `deltaMode` and posting `{axis, delta, x, y, modifiers}`. (2) Add `POST /api/runtime/input/mouse_wheel` in editor_server.rs that pushes `InputEvent::MouseButton{WheelUp|WheelDown|WheelLeft|WheelRight, factor}` press+release pairs. (3) Widen the button routes to 0..=4 and add `MouseButton::WheelLeft/WheelRight/XButton1/XButton2` to input.rs:288. (4) Add `double_click`, `factor`, `button_mask`, `global_position` to `InputEvent::MouseButton` and `velocity`/`screen_velocity`/`pressure`/`tilt`/`pen_inverted` to `MouseMotion`, computing double_click in `InputState` the way `DOUBLE_TAP_FRAMES` (input.rs:1418) already does for touch. (5) Widen `get_mouse_button_mask` to the full MouseButtonMask set.\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: a browser wheel event must scroll a ScrollContainer in a played scene and reach a script's `_input` as an `InputEventMouseButton` with `button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_DOWN`.

**Prove it:** With a scene containing a ScrollContainer running under the editor server, POSTing a wheel-down event and stepping one frame advances the container's scroll offset AND a script's `_input` observes `button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_DOWN`; two mouse-down events inside the double-click window deliver a second event with `double_click == true`; the served EDITOR_HTML registers a `wheel` listener (assert on `pub const EDITOR_HTML`). comments.text:
MagentaBrook — correction to my own sizing in the block report (msg 79672), because it would send the next worker down a path that does not work.

I wrote that velocity/screen_velocity are 'derivable from the position delta and frame timing' inside push_input. The first half is right, the second is NOT: I checked, and `SceneTree::push_input(&mut self, event: &InputEvent)` takes no delta and SceneTree holds no wall-clock or per-frame time — every delta on SceneTree arrives as a parameter to a process_* method (process_timers, process_script_coroutines, process_video_players), none of which is on the input path. push_input only has trace_frame, a counter.

So velocity is NOT computable where double_click is computed. Godot builds it in the OS layer from event timestamps. Whoever takes this needs a transport decision, not a derivation:
  (a) stamp arrival time in the route (editor_server has a clock) and carry it, or
  (b) have InputState track it across MouseMotion events and expose a getter, then pass it into input_event_to_variant the way double_click is passed — note this needs MainLoop, which owns both InputState and the tree, since SceneTree deliberately cannot see InputState (scene_tree.rs:389).

Option (b) is the same shape as the emulate_mouse_from_touch work in pat-s3rrv.77: the decision is made in MainLoop because it is the only place that holds both halves.

button_mask IS derivable without timing — it is the set of currently-held buttons, which push_input can track the same way it tracks last_mouse_press_frame. That part of my note stands.

Unchanged and still the key warning: do NOT widen InputEvent::MouseMotion. 41 construction sites workspace-wide, and this bead family already chose the computed-flag route for double_click for exactly that reason (71 sites on MouseButton, per the comment at scene_tree.rs:4340).

title: Web input: touch pipeline (touchstart/move/end → ScreenTouch/ScreenDrag) + honor emulate_* project settings
description:
[audit-key: input/web-touch-pipeline] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json InputEventScreenTouch/InputEventScreenDrag; Input.set_emulate_mouse_from_touch/set_emulate_touch_from_mouse; ProjectSettings input_devices/pointing/emulate_mouse_from_touch|emulate_touch_from_mouse; upstream/godot/platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_input.js touch handlers

**Godot classes:** InputEventScreenTouch, InputEventScreenDrag, TouchScreenButton

**Patina today:**
- [input] IMPLEMENTED BUT UNREACHABLE. `InputEvent::ScreenTouch`/`ScreenDrag` with double_tap/canceled/pressure/tilt exist at engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs:511-535; `InputState` tracks `touch_positions`, `touch_last_press_frame`, `mouse_from_touch_index`, `emulate_mouse_from_touch`, `emulate_touch_from_mouse` (input.rs:1381-1408) with `DOUBLE_TAP_FRAMES` (input.rs:1418). But `grep -rn 'touchstart|touchmove|touchend|TouchEvent' crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs crates/gdplatform/src/export.rs` returns 0 hits, and there is no touch route among editor_server.rs:2518-2537. `grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'touchstart|input/touch|ScreenTouch' crates/gdeditor/src/` finds only the inspector schema table entry (inspector_schema_generated.rs:4621). The project settings exist only as defaults — engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/project_settings.rs:738,742 declare `input_devices/pointing/emulate_touch_from_mouse` and `emulate_mouse_from_touch`, and grepping for consumers outside gdplatform/gdcore returns 0, so setting them in project.godot has no effect on `InputState`. Consequence: a phone or tablet cannot play a Patina game, and `TouchScreenButton` routing (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2770) can only ever be driven by a real mouse.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/project_settings.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: Godot's web platform registers `touchstart`/`touchmove`/`touchend`/`touchcancel` on the canvas and emits `InputEventScreenTouch` (index, position, pressed, double_tap, canceled) and `InputEventScreenDrag` (index, position, relative, velocity, pressure, tilt) per finger (upstream/godot/platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_input.js). `ProjectSettings.input_devices/pointing/emulate_mouse_from_touch` (default true) makes the first finger drive `InputEventMouseButton`/`MouseMotion` so Controls and Buttons respond to touch; `emulate_touch_from_mouse` (default false) does the inverse for desktop testing.\n\nPATINA CURRENT STATE: the whole engine-side model already exists and is tested — `InputEvent::ScreenTouch`/`ScreenDrag` at engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs:511-535, per-finger tracking, Godot's `mouse_from_touch_index` first-finger rule and double-tap window at input.rs:1381-1418 — but there is NO producer. The served EDITOR_HTML (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs) has zero touch listeners and engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs has no touch route (routes end at editor_server.rs:2537). The two project settings are declared as defaults in engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/project_settings.rs:738,742 and read by nobody, so `InputState::emulate_mouse_from_touch` keeps its hard-coded value regardless of project.godot.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION: (1) add passive-false `touchstart`/`touchmove`/`touchend`/`touchcancel` listeners on the game view in editor_ui.rs, posting the changed-touches array `[{identifier, x, y, force, tiltX, tiltY}]` with a `phase` field. (2) Add `POST /api/runtime/input/touch` in editor_server.rs that pushes `InputEvent::ScreenTouch`/`ScreenDrag` through `MainLoop::push_event`. (3) At boot in both engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/main.rs:366 and editor_server.rs:13011, read `input_devices/pointing/emulate_mouse_from_touch` / `emulate_touch_from_mouse` from the booted ProjectSettings and apply them to `InputState`. (4) Route ScreenTouch/ScreenDrag into `SceneTree::gui_input_stage` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:3248) — today only MouseButton/MouseMotion/Key take a branch there.\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: a touchstart on the game view must press a Button in a played scene (via mouse emulation) AND reach a script's `_input` as an `InputEventScreenTouch`.

**Prove it:** With a scene containing a Button running under the editor server, POSTing a touchstart at the Button's rect and stepping one frame emits `pressed` on the Button and a script's `_input` observes an `InputEventScreenTouch` with `index == 0` and `pressed == true`; a project.godot setting `emulate_mouse_from_touch=false` suppresses the Button press while the ScreenTouch still arrives; the served EDITOR_HTML registers a `touchstart` listener. (test: `touch_events_reach_running_game`)
acceptance_criteria: With a scene containing a Button running under the editor server, POSTing a touchstart at the Button's rect and stepping one frame emits `pressed` on the Button and a script's `_input` observes an `InputEventScreenTouch` with `index == 0` and `pressed == true`; a project.godot setting `emulate_mouse_from_touch=false` suppresses the Button press while the ScreenTouch still arrives; the served EDITOR_HTML registers a `touchstart` listener. (test: `touch_events_reach_running_game`)
